title: Строка ввода TUI не видна: живая область меряется по последней НЕПУСТОЙ строке, а курсор стоит ниже
description:
Владелец: «сейчас в omp невозможно работать, не видно строки ввода». Это НЕ
про замороженный блок (то nocx-juau) — ломается живая область, пока программа
идёт.

## Измерение, с которым бид был заведён, ОШИБОЧНО. Исправлено 2026-09-05

Сначала здесь стояло: «cursorY=31, liveContentHeight=31 строка, курсор ровно на
одну ниже показанного». Это было снято на САМОМ КОНЦЕ захвата, где omp уже
вышел и курсор принадлежал вернувшемуся приглашению шелла, — то есть ровно
случай nocx-i4h04.1, а не строка ввода omp.

Тот же захват, обрезанный до интерактивного состояния (до «Closing session»),
при 152x33 даёт:

    cursorY = 23, cursorX = 1, всего строк 33
    liveContentHeight() = 540px при ячейке 20px  =>  27 строк

Курсор ВНУТРИ бокса. То есть на этих данных симптом не воспроизводится, и
причина пока НЕ УСТАНОВЛЕНА.

Захват, скорее всего, вообще не содержит отказавшего состояния: владелец
запустил `script -qec omp` и почти сразу вышел, не работая в программе.

## Что остаётся под подозрением и чем это проверить

`liveContentHeight()` (frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts) идёт снизу вверх до
последней строки, у которой `translateToString(true).length > 0`. Хвостовые
пробелы обрезаются, поэтому пустая строка ввода в высоту не входит. Механизм
реален; не доказано, что он и есть причина.

Второй подозреваемый, не проверенный вовсе: `runningLiveCap` — потолок живой
области, равный высоте скроллера минус шапка бегущего блока. Если он МЕНЬШЕ
измеренного содержимого, бокс показывает меньше строк, чем их есть, и нижние
(включая строку ввода) обрезаются его overflow. Ни высоты скроллера, ни высоты
шапки в реальной панели у меня нет.

РАЗЛИЧАЮЩАЯ ПРОВЕРКА, дешёвая: когда строки ввода не видно, прокрутить панель
вниз. Если набранное появляется — содержимое нарисовано и обрезано боксом
(подозреваемый 2). Если нет — строку не отвели вовсе (подозреваемый 1).

## Причина

`XtermRenderer.liveContentHeight()` (frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts) идёт
снизу вверх до последней строки, у которой
`translateToString(true).length > 0`, и возвращает `(y + 1) * cellHeight`.
`translateToString(true)` обрезает хвостовые пробелы, поэтому строка ввода,
пока в ней ничего не набрано, считается ПУСТОЙ и в высоту не входит.

## Почему нельзя просто прибавить строку курсора

Это поведение намеренное и защищено тестом nocx-i4h04.1
(«measures the rows the block will keep, and not the row the cursor moved to»,
frontend/src/renderers/xterm.test.ts): после перевода строки курсор стоит на
строке, которую займёт СЛЕДУЮЩИЙ промпт, а замороженный блок кончается на
строку выше. Если считать её, живая область на одну строку выше блока, в
который превращается, и панель дёргается при каждой заморозке.

То есть один и тот же признак — «курсор ниже последней непустой строки» —
означает разное: у шелла это будущий промпт, у идущей TUI это строка ввода.
Нужен признак, который их различает; какой именно — решение этого бида, и его
надо записать, потому что оно переопределяет то, что решает i4h04.1.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Открыть локальную панель, запустить `omp`.
2. Набирать текст в его строке ввода.

Наблюдается: строки ввода не видно. Ожидается: видно то, что набираешь.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Пока команда идёт, живая область показывает строку, на которой стоит
  курсор, даже если она пуста. Проверяется на потоке: подать вывод, оставить
  курсор на пустой строке ниже последней непустой, утверждать, что высота
  включает её.
- nocx-i4h04.1 не воскресает: при заморозке высота живой области совпадает с
  высотой блока, в который она превращается, и панель не дёргается. Его тест
  остаётся зелёным.
- Признак, различающий эти два случая, назван в коде словами, а не выведен из
  cursorX или иной случайной величины.
close_reason: Починено в b7000e9e и подтверждено владельцем в живой панели: строка ввода видна, лишней прокрутки нет. Причина — клип на элементе, который сам же сдвигается: .xterm-inner нёс overflow: hidden и является тем элементом, который транслирует _applyEchoShift, поэтому нижняя строка отрезалась в его собственной коробке ДО сдвига. Замерено: внешнее окно [259,772), этот элемент после сдвига [240,753), пересечение 494px — 26 строк из 27. Три попытки чинить это размером (колонка курсора d41dbb7e, метки OSC 133, шов владения 2f4321a5) откачены целиком, в дереве их нет: в отказавшем состоянии content === caret === 532, то есть последняя не меняла ничего. Регрессия — на поставляемом CSS (live-clip.test.ts), потому что 6211 тестов проходили при сломанном продукте: jsdom не считает раскладку.

title: A prompt taller than the viewport puts its own answers off-screen
description:
Reported by the owner with a screenshot: an approval prompt for a long session.run command. The facts table runs past the bottom of the window, Allow once is the last thing visible, and Deny is cut off. A person cannot answer a question they are required to answer.

## Where it lives

frontend/src/styles/components/prompt.css. .ui-prompt caps WIDTH (560px floating, 760px top-sheet, both with max-width) and has NO height cap at all. .ui-prompt-overlay is position:fixed; inset:0 with align-items:flex-start, so a tall panel simply runs off the bottom edge and takes its actions with it.

This is the KIT, not the approval surface, so every top-sheet prompt has it: the vault unlock, the connection-password ask, key material, the approval prompt. The approval prompt is merely the one whose content has no bound — a proposed command line can be any length, and the one in the screenshot is a five-clause pipeline.

## Why it is P0-shaped

An unanswerable question is worse than a wrong answer offered. The run is suspended waiting on a person who cannot reach Deny; nothing on screen says the panel continues below; and the only escape is a keyboard route they have no reason to know exists.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have the assistant propose a long command — a multi-clause pipeline is enough.
2. The approval prompt opens as a top sheet.
3. The facts table pushes the actions below the fold. Deny is unreachable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A prompt never exceeds the viewport height. Its actions are always in view.
- The BODY is what scrolls; the title and the actions stay pinned. A test asserts the actions are within the viewport when the body is far taller than it.
- It is fixed in the kit, so every top-sheet prompt gets it, not in the approval surface. A surface may place a kit component and never repaint it.
- Scrollability is discoverable: a person must be able to tell there is more, not guess.
- The keyboard route still works — the caret opens on the first enabled action, and reaching the last one does not require a mouse.
- A test covers the floating placement too; it has the same missing cap.
close_reason: Merged as 5c77ae83 (worker 42b6e4cc). The defect was MEASURED before the fix: in a 900x600 window Deny's bottom edge sat at y=2950 — about 2350px below the window — in both Chromium and WebKit. Fixed in the kit, mirroring the chain Dialog already had (dialog.css: flex column, max-height, min-height:0 body) rather than inventing a second one: cap is max-height:100% of the overlay's content box, so ONE rule covers both paddings. The body needed flex-shrink:0 on its direct children, which the brief did not mention and which matters: a flex item with its own scroll region has an automatic minimum size of zero, so a CodeBlock (max-height:200px; overflow:auto) collapsed to a sliver instead of the body scrolling — there is an e2e assertion for exactly that. Discoverability is measured data-overflow-start/-end on .ui-prompt__body painting a mask fade at the cut edge only, from three sources because none subsumes another (scroll, ResizeObserver for resize, MutationObserver for content arriving — the body is capped so its own box does not change when content grows); that is the kit's existing vocabulary, tab-strip.css does the same horizontally. Verified by the coordinator: e2e/prompt-height.spec.ts, 22 tests, Chromium AND WebKit — actions inside the viewport, body scrolls while overlay and document do not, title and actions pinned, scroll-capped child not collapsed, short prompt unchanged, Tab reaches Deny and Enter fires it on screen, fade only where actually cut. The worker was explicit about what its unit tests cannot prove (jsdom reports zero for all three numbers, so prompt.test.tsx proves the arithmetic and the wiring, never layout) and said so at the code — which is why the e2e spec exists. It also warned that a top-sheet's 160ms slide-down moves getBoundingClientRect and WebKit can measure mid-animation, showing panel bottom at 0 and Deny at -13, which looks exactly like this defect and is not it; the spec waits on getAnimations().every(finished), never on a duration.

title: coordinator-reclaim: a reclaimed pane holds the session but shows no running command block
description:
CI e2e, run 33691908259, BOTH browsers identically, on branch feat/relay-pty-owner at
084f72a6. Deterministic, not a flake.

e2e/coordinator-reclaim.spec.ts:216 fails at line 336:

  expect(second.locator('.pane.active .cmd-block.cmd-block-running')
    .filter({hasText:'NOCXMARK'})).toBeVisible({timeout:120_000})
  -> element(s) not found

Everything BEFORE that line passes. The fresh client does reclaim: the pane carries
data-session-id, sessions.live reports the same sessionId, sessionEpoch, instanceId and
paneId, attached=true, and the markers advanced across the detached window. So the
session came back and the work kept running. What is missing is the RESTORED COMMAND
BLOCK in the fresh pane -- the person cannot see the running work.

This is a LOCAL pty session reclaimed by a fresh client. No coordinator restart.

## Steps to Reproduce

PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/coordinator-reclaim.spec.ts

## Acceptance Criteria

- The spec passes unmodified in the container, chromium.
- The cause is established by reproduction, not by reading code: name the commit or the
  change on this branch that made it false, and show the assertion going red and green
  across it.
- A unit test covers the behaviour at the seam that broke, so this cannot regress
  silently again.

## Baseline

e2e/coordinator-reclaim.spec.ts is BYTE-IDENTICAL to origin/main -- this branch does not
touch it. PR #178 (4c4a21e8, cut from the same main, contains this spec) is green in both
browsers. So it passes on main and fails here: the regression is this branch's.
close_reason: Fixed in 6025643b. Cause: the LifecycleProjections block port in TerminalContent.mount guarded on this.renderer, which mount publishes only after _bindSession returns; since nocx-k6p18.6 a reclaiming bind awaits awaitWriteBarrier() over the recovered scrollback, so the backend's replayed running fact landed inside that window, openBlock refused it, and pump() had already recorded the attempt in _bound. Port now closes over the renderer the mount built. Evidence: e2e/coordinator-reclaim.spec.ts red (2.4m, element not found) then green (26.6s) in the chromium container across the change; new unit test 'a reclaimed pane shows the work that never stopped (nocx-ht15k)' in frontend/src/terminal-content.test.ts red before, green after, red again under mutation.

title: connection-password: the remembered password never reaches ssh auth in the container
description:
Found 2026-09-03 while fixing nocx-07cf4, in the containerized chromium run.

e2e/connection-password.spec.ts:195 ('first open prompts and connects; after
remembering, the second open does not prompt') fails at line 245: the poll for
one 'kind=ssh profile_id=...' line in the backend log stays at 0 for the full
20s. The prompt appears, names the connection correctly, and the password is
filled and submitted; nothing then reaches authentication against the e2e-sshd
fixture.

NOT nocx-07cf4 and not caused by its fix. Measured both ways on branch
feat/relay-pty-owner: with the fix (084f72a6) and with terminal-content.ts
reverted to HEAD~1, the spec fails at the SAME line 245 with the same
'Expected: 1 / Received: 0'. The empty-title assertion at line 202 passes in
both, because this test raises its own backend and its first navigation is a
fresh open rather than a reclaim.

The other test in the file (line 300, open-time host key consent) passes.

UNVERIFIED: whether this is CI's failure or only the container's. AGENTS.md
warns the container's failure set is not CI's and CI is the source of truth,
and this spec drives a real sshd fixture, which is exactly the class that can
differ. Check a CI ci-e2e run before treating it as a product defect.

## Steps to Reproduce

PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/connection-password.spec.ts

Observed: test 1 fails at line 245, "Expected: 1 Received: 0", 20s poll
timeout. Test 2 passes. Expected: both pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

The spec passes in CI's ci-e2e job in both browsers, or the bead is closed
with the measurement showing it was only ever red in the local container and
why.
close_reason: Cause: internal/app.probeHelperPlatformAt dialed with the interactive prompt rung, so the helper platform probe on the open path raised the connection-password ask, then released the only pool reference (connection closed) and the session's own dial asked a second time — the open blocked behind a prompt nobody was answering. Fixed in 74e21577 by dialing the probe with ssh.WithoutPasswordPrompt(). Evidence: e2e/connection-password.spec.ts chromium in the container, both tests pass unmodified (was: line 245 Expected 1 Received 0, 25.5s; now: 5.9s green). Go coverage: internal/app.TestOpenPath_PasswordAskFiresOncePerOpen (red before the fix: asked 2 times) and TestOpenPath_ProbeStillRunsOnARememberedPassword. Remaining: nocx-k6p18.35 (the second dial itself), nocx-k6p18.36 (a refused relay selection says nothing).

title: Every tab renders an empty title, so twelve e2e specs fail in CI
description: Found 2026-09-03 by CI's ci-e2e job on PR #163 (branch feat/relay-pty-owner), and reproduced identically by a local containerized run. TWELVE specs fail in chromium with ONE shared symptom: the tab title element is present and empty. Locator: locator('.nocx-tab-title').first() Expected: not "" Received: "" 33 x locator resolved to The specs span unrelated features -- agent-ask, agent-policy, agent-refusal-stop, ask-about-full-screen-program, ask-attaches-the-frozen-screen, assistant-intake, assistant-readiness, connection-password, connections-settings, coordinator-reclaim, quick-connect, vault-sealed-probe -- which is what says the cause is one thing they all sit on rather than twelve defects. IT IS OURS, and that is measured rather than assumed. PR #178's ci-e2e passes in both browsers and PR #177's passes in chromium, both cut from the same main. CI has not run on main itself since 2026-08-10 (nocx-mz9d), so the other PRs are the baseline and they are green. WHERE TO LOOK FIRST. frontend/src/tab.tsx:267 is the only place that renders the element, from props.title. Two commits on this branch touched frontend/src/panes.ts, which is where a pane's facts are assembled: dd382338 (nocx-k6p18.12, the helper diagnostics projection, which added helperObservationFor and processObservationFor) and dfd7acfa (nocx-k6p18.13). Neither meant to touch titles, which is exactly why this is worth bisecting rather than reasoning about. ## Steps to Reproduce PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/quick-connect.spec.ts Observed: the tab strip renders and the title never arrives. Expected: the tab carries its title, as it does on main.
acceptance_criteria:
The twelve named specs pass in CI in both browsers. The cause is named in the
commit -- which change emptied the title and why nothing caught it -- and a unit
test asserts a tab renders the title it is given, so this cannot regress silently
again. Reverting the fix behaviourally turns that named test red.
close_reason: Already fixed; the bead outlived its fix by a day and nobody closed it. VERIFIED rather than assumed. The fix is 084f72a6 'fix(frontend): subscribe to OSC 7 before the bind that replays it (nocx-07cf4)', 2026-09-03 01:37 — hours after this bead's last update. It is an ancestor of origin/main and of this worktree. Its cause is not the one this bead pointed at: it is not panes.ts and not the two nocx-k6p18 commits, it is terminal-content.ts installing its OSC 7 subscription AFTER the bind that replays it, so a RECLAIMED session (which carries no cwd in its ack, deliberately) missed the one replay that would have named it — every tab empty after a renderer reload. Evidence a stranger can check: all TWELVE named specs run green in CI's own container image, chromium, 37 tests in 3.8 minutes, zero failures — e2e/{agent-ask,agent-policy,agent-refusal-stop,ask-about-full-screen-program,ask-attaches-the-frozen-screen,assistant-intake,assistant-readiness,connection-password,connections-settings,coordinator-reclaim,quick-connect,vault-sealed-probe}.spec.ts. The second half of the acceptance criterion is met too and by the same commit: frontend/src/tab.test.tsx 'renders the title it is given' and 'renders a title that changes, not the one it first mounted with', whose comment names this bead and says exactly why the pre-existing 'has nocx-tab-title element' passed throughout — the element is not the title. Nothing was changed here; this is a verification and a close.

title: A re-adopted session has no lifecycle channel, so commands run after the return produce no blocks and nothing says so
description:
Found while building nocx-k6p18.30 (server-side re-adoption), and it is the one
part of "the pane comes back" that re-adoption cannot give it.

A helper-hosted session carries a SECOND stream beside the PTY: the authenticated
lifecycle channel (ADR-0024), which is what makes command blocks appear. Its
capability is minted by the coordinator's own lifecycle kernel at spawn
(lifecyclechannel.NewStream -> Kernel.RequestDomain) and handed to the far shell
in proto.LifecycleLaunch. It names THIS process's kernel.

So when a coordinator is replaced, the far shell holds a capability no live kernel
recognises. nocx-k6p18.30 re-attaches the lifecycle carrier with LifecycleFresh
true and no adapter behind it, purely so the stream is drained rather than
stalling on its own credit window, and every frame the shell sends is dropped.

WHAT A USER SEES. The pane comes back, the output is live, the blocks the ledger
already holds are restored (nocx-k6p18.22) — and a command typed AFTER the return
produces no block, no exit chip and no duration, silently. AGENTS.md: "a soft
degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log." This one is not
visible anywhere.

TWO THINGS ARE NEEDED AND THEY ARE SEPARABLE:

1. A way for a replacing coordinator to adopt an EXISTING lifecycle lane, or for
   the far shell to re-handshake against the new kernel. lifecycle.DomainHandle's
   Recovery fence is a within-process re-handshake for a lane the kernel already
   knows; it is not this. This is a wire/authority design and belongs in an ADR
   amendment, not in a bugfix.
2. Until (1), the degrade must be STATED: a re-adopted pane whose lifecycle
   channel could not be resumed says so, the way nocx-k6p18.5's unreconciled
   status card says why a block is neither running nor finished.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a helper-hosted session on a remote host (git-panel consent path).
2. Run a command; a .cmd-block appears.
3. Stop nocx-server; start it again on the same profile. The pane comes back
   through nocx-k6p18.30's re-adoption and its output is live.
4. Run another command in that pane. No block appears, and nothing says why.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A command run in a pane taken back after a coordinator replacement produces a
  block with an outcome, OR the pane states in the product that it cannot.
- The check is the epic's own acceptance spec extended, not a unit test: the
  block must be watched to appear after the return.
notes:
Landed as commit 2573a7a0 on feat/relay-pty-owner (NOT closed; the epic's e2e assertion is another worker's).

DESIGN. The shell never re-handshakes and cannot be told a new epoch, so the leg re-established is the coordinator's: a new helper op session.adopt-lifecycle hands back the LifecycleLaunch the helper spawned the shell with, and Kernel.AdoptDomain installs that domain Established at its existing epoch. ADR-0024 gains an amendment; docs/lifecycle-protocol.md gains 12.2. The ADR's 'reattachment needs its own authenticated epoch' bullet is closed AGAINST its own guess, with the reason.

AUTHENTICATION. Per-frame bearer unchanged; a descendant with the descriptor still cannot speak. One new holder (the replacing coordinator), over the same authenticated connection the value left on. Two enforced constraints: the bearer is per-session on its own op and never a sessions field, and the re-attachment resumes at the helper lifecycle window HEAD, not base (replaying the retained frames would replay authenticated commands - driven by TestTheAdoptedChannelDoesNotReplayCommandsThatAlreadyRan).

nocx-k6p18.6 covers a NEIGHBOURING case (an attempt open across the replacement, settled from replayed OSC 133) and landed frontend-only; it built no backend re-establishment. Extended, not duplicated: the adopted domain deliberately carries no attempt across.

DEGRADE. Older generation / no launch / kernel refusal all set session.integrationChanged conventional + channel-unavailable via the re-adoption path (which previously registered nothing at all).

VERIFICATION on this NixOS host: go build -tags gtk3 ./... clean; go test -tags gtk3 over app, transport/..., session, helper/..., lifecycle, lifecyclechannel, lifecyclepub, content - all ok except internal/app's five known environmental failures and no sixth. golangci-lint clean on every touched package. deadcode -whylive reaches Kernel.AdoptDomain and Client.AdoptLifecycle from main. Eleven mutations driven red and restored.

NOT VERIFIED: e2e (out of scope for this worker), macOS, the frontend end of the fact. nocx-k6p18.34 files the remaining gap: a pane presented conventionally hides the restored blocks the ledger holds for it.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-09-02, verified by the coordinator. Commit 2573a7a0, and confirmed by
nocx-k6p18.9's acceptance run: four green runs, spec unmodified.

WHAT nocx-k6p18.6 ACTUALLY BUILT. Its title promises "a fresh lifecycle domain on
reattach"; its implementation is entirely FRONTEND -- OSC 133 C/D capture during
the recovered write, applied to durable restored blocks. Its own commit body says
reviving the old domain would violate the lifecycle and VT ownership decisions. So
the mechanism existed for a NEIGHBOURING case and did not cover this one, and its
own acceptance criterion "reattaching establishes a fresh lifecycle domain" was
never implemented on the backend. Extended rather than duplicated: the adopted
domain deliberately carries NO attempt across, so a command spanning the
replacement still settles the .6 way.

THE FIX. A replacing coordinator ADOPTS the running domain instead of establishing
a fresh one, and the helper hands the identity back. The shell's end of the channel
is a socketpair descriptor whose parent the HELPER holds, so nothing on the far
side noticed the replacement: what died is the registry that could address the
domain, not the domain. A new op answers with the LifecycleLaunch the helper
spawned that shell with; Kernel.AdoptDomain installs it Established at its existing
epoch.

NOT A FRESH EPOCH, which is what ADR-0024 expected. The shell sends one hello per
shell, never re-handshakes, and reads no frame that could re-key it. A fresh epoch
would need a shell-side protocol act -- the one thing this level exists to avoid
asking a far host for -- and buys nothing, because the authority never went stale.

WHY IT IS SAFE. Per-frame bearer validation is unchanged, so a descendant that
inherited fd 3 still cannot produce the capability. Section 12's "a Lost domain
stays Lost" is not violated: that binds a kernel that WATCHED its transport die,
and no kernel here saw a loss; AdoptDomain refuses a domain id the registry already
holds in any state. Holders grow by exactly one, over the same authenticated
connection the value left on, in the trust class that already holds the session's
write lease and its whole output stream. The epoch counter is lifted past the
adopted epoch, so "never reused" holds across processes.

MY OWN MUTATION, on the one genuinely new vector: LifecycleOffset from the window's
head to its BASE. Named test goes red --
  "a command that ran under the previous coordinator was replayed into the new
   kernel and authenticated there; the attachment resumed at the window's base"
Reverted; tree byte-identical; the scoped suite green with exactly the five known
environmental failures in internal/app and no sixth.

AND THE ACCEPTANCE RUN FOUND MORE THAN THE UNIT TEST DID. Applying that same
mutation against the e2e spec turns the pane back to inner-fullscreen-mode over
live-unstructured, with no editor and "This session has no shell integration" --
byte-for-byte the pre-fix collapse. So replaying the authenticated stretch does not
merely re-deliver commands that already ran: it stops the adopted domain reaching
prompt_ready at all. The security defect and a total functional collapse are the
same event.

MY OWN SUGGESTION WAS REFUSED, correctly. I proposed that "markerless" might be
derived from absence of evidence in the renderer and be cheaper to fix there. It is
not: the classification reads the authority, and the authority had nothing. Showing
restored blocks on a native lane would be a SECOND derivation of "is this session
integrated" -- the AD-8 shape this epic kept being bitten by. Filed as
nocx-k6p18.34 for the degraded arm instead.

ADR-0024 was AMENDED, not rewritten: the original "Revisit when" bullet is kept
verbatim under strikethrough with a closing record, which is the convention that
document already used, and the amendment is appended below. docs/lifecycle-protocol
.md gains 12.2. New op contracts with an over-the-wire conformance test. No wire
version bump -- nothing is published (nocx-k6p18.11) -- and the commit body says so.

DUPLICATE CHECK, done after the fact and worth recording: the degrade statement
this work needed already had an owner. nocx-viil ("a session that fell back to a
conventional terminal never says so") is implemented -- the closed refusal
vocabulary, frontend/src/integration/status.ts, and the generated contract cites
nocx-viil by name -- but the bead is still in_progress from 2026-08-12. The worker
used that existing surface rather than building a second one, which was luck rather
than process.

NOT VERIFIED: macOS; WebKit (the acceptance run was chromium only); and whether
channel-unavailable's existing copy reads well for "an older helper generation
cannot hand the identity back" -- honest but generic.

ONE ADJACENT CHANGE, flagged: OpenHosted's ordinary helper path had no
WithLossReporter at all, so a lost helper lifecycle channel stated nothing. Both
paths are now wired to the same sink the local pty factory uses. One line each,
same owner, outside the strict defect.

title: A fresh coordinator never re-adopts a live helper-hosted session, so the epic's happy path does not hold
description:
Found by the epic's own acceptance test (nocx-k6p18.9), which is what that test
exists for. Measured in the container, twice, on branch omp/k6p18-9-e2e-c.

The build is provably still running on the host throughout: its own marker file,
on the fixture's filesystem, keeps advancing one line a second across the whole
window, and the helper's window.written advances by more than its 4 MiB
windowBytes. The process is alive; the coordinator simply cannot find it.

WHY. `sessions.live` is served straight off the in-process registry
(internal/transport/ws_reclaim.go handleSessionsLive over svc.List()), so a new
process holds nothing; judgeClaim REFUSES a binding remembered across a restart
by design (reasonForeignInstance). `helperRegistry.hosts` is populated only by
OpenHosted (internal/app/helper_git.go), so on a cold start it is empty and
`sessions.inventory` answers "no active helper". There is exactly one Attach
call site in the whole coordinator and it always follows a fresh Spawn — there
is no re-attach-by-existing-hostSessionId anywhere.

The durable binding nocx-1u0am gave a production writer is real and is written,
but its only reader is restart RECONCILIATION (internal/app/session_reconcile.go),
whose outputs are verdicts — live/absent/unknown. A verdict keeps the recording
from being deleted. It creates no session, opens no helper connection, and puts
nothing into sessions.live.

SO THIS IS A GAP, NOT A REGRESSION. None of nocx-k6p18.5, .15 or nocx-1u0am
claims to re-adopt anything; all three are about JUDGEMENT and about not
destroying work. nocx-k6p18.9's criterion "reattach to the same session by its
hostSessionId" is the first thing in the chain that assumes the capability, and
the chain never built it.

The renderer side is already waiting for it and degrades honestly: panes.ts
primeLiveSessions/adoptionFor turns a sessions.live entry into the claim a
restored pane makes instead of an open, and with an empty list every restored
row opens a fresh session — the documented pre-coordinator degrade.

## Steps to Reproduce

    PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/remote-coordinator-reclaim.spec.ts

on branch omp/k6p18-9-e2e-c. The spec opens a helper-hosted session on the e2e
sshd fixture, starts a build that parks on a file, closes the browser context,
stops nocx-server, releases the build so it overruns the helper's window with no
coordinator running, and starts nocx-server again on the same isolated home.

It fails at the assertion that the fresh coordinator can even LIST the session:

    Error: the fresh coordinator does not list the still-running helper session,
    so no restored pane can claim it
    expect(received).toContain(expected)
    Expected value: "40202819de8cfad1c4908e21ef010145"
    Received array: []
    Call Log: - Timeout 120000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate

Everything before that point passes: the helper installs through the git-panel
consent path, the session is helper-hosted (it has a hostSessionId in
sessions.inventory), a .cmd-block appears in the pane, the coordinator observes
the client detach, and the build overruns the 4 MiB window while nothing is
recording.

Without the assertion the same run fails one step later and less legibly — the
pane never comes back and the tab reads "Terminal failed to start: ssh connect:
nothing to authenticate e2e@127.0.0.1 with: no key, no password and no reachable
agent", which is the fallback dial of the SEPARATE defect, not this one.

## Acceptance Criteria

After nocx-server is stopped and started again on the same profile, with a
helper-hosted session still running on the host:

- `sessions.live` lists that session, keyed to the pane it was the pipe of, so a
  restored pane has an entry to claim.
- `sessions.inventory` answers from the helper generation the binding names
  rather than "no active helper".
- The re-adopted session is the SAME process: launch.pid and hostSessionId equal
  what the previous coordinator recorded, and no second shell is spawned.
- e2e/remote-coordinator-reclaim.spec.ts passes end to end.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-09-02, verified by the coordinator. Commit 8a471835.

The design direction held: re-adoption is SERVER-SIDE and judgeClaim is untouched.
The coordinator reads its own binding at start, attaches to the existing
hostSessionId, and adopts under a FRESH instance id -- new process, new instance,
same authoritative session id per AD-7 as amended. The renderer then finds it
through sessions.live like any other session, so a claim carried across a restart
never has to be permitted.

WHAT MY BRIEF MISSED, and it was a prerequisite rather than a route around: the
durable binding carried {generation, host, account} only -- everything a VERDICT
needs and nothing a RE-ADOPTION needs. Re-adoption also needs the pane it was the
pipe of (sessions.live keys the renderer's claim by it), the saved connection that
reaches the host (port and key are not derivable from host+user), the helper
binary path the bridge execs (re-deriving it means a remote write at every start),
and the machine's consent key. content.Session/PendingSession grew those four. The
existing writer was extended rather than a second one added.

FAILURE PATHS. Every one returns an error that causeFor turns into `unknown` with
its cause -- the existing verdict path, unchanged. THERE IS NO NEW ROUTE TO
`absent`, and that is the invariant that matters: absent deletes the recording of
a build that may still be running. Host unreachable, generation gone, saved
connection now resolving elsewhere (and then no lane is dialled at all -- asking a
stranger about somebody else's id space is what nocx-k6p18.15's ordering forbids),
vault sealed, consent withdrawn, no route recorded, and a host that neither
answers nor refuses (bounded at 15s per attempt, because the pass runs
synchronously BEFORE the listener opens, so a client can never be told an empty
list). Another coordinator holding the write lease (nocx-k6p18.16) declines and
leaves the verdict live. A transport refusing after the adopt takes the session
back out of the registry.

MY OWN MUTATION: VerdictUnknown -> VerdictAbsent on the readopt-error branch. Four
named tests go red, each naming the consequence rather than the value:
  TestAnUnreachableHostNeverReadsAsTheSessionBeingGone: "an unreachable host
    produced ABSENT -- that deletes the recording of a build that is still running
    and closes its blocks as finished"
  TestAGenerationThatIsGoneIsNotTheSessionBeingGone: verdict = "absent", want
    unknown -- nothing answered about this session
  TestASealedVaultIsReportedAsItselfAndNotAsAbsent: "absent"/"vaultSealed", want
    unknown/vaultSealed
  TestAHostThatNeverAnswersIsBoundedAndNeverReadsAsGone: "a deadline is not an
    answer"
Reverted; tree byte-identical. transport, session, all seven helper packages and
content green; internal/app shows exactly the five environmental failures this
NixOS host always shows (no bash at the FHS path, one live-sshd test), same five
before and after.

TWO OF THE WORKER'S FOURTEEN MUTATIONS WERE INITIALLY GREEN and both were real
test defects rather than false alarms: one was racing the helper's LIVE reset
instead of exercising the attach result, and one passed because the fake recorder
concatenates whatever it is handed, so a renumbered stream was invisible until the
test asserted append OFFSETS. That is the "a test that passes with the check
deleted" shape, caught by doing the mutations rather than reasoning about them.

deadcode -whylive traces the whole chain from main, with content.sqliteContent
.AddEdge as the contrast case -- the only check that works here, since RTA cannot
report a dead method behind a live interface (AD-8).

LEFT OPEN AND FILED, not hidden: nocx-k6p18.31 -- the lifecycle capability is
minted by the dead process's kernel, so a re-adopted session has no lifecycle
channel and a command typed AFTER the return produces no block, silently. That is
a soft degrade the product does not state, which AGENTS.md forbids; a worker is on
it. Also nocx-k6p18.32 (a helper-hosted session's factory carries no fingerprint,
so D25's uninstall never closes its channel -- true for OpenHosted today, and
re-adoption matches it deliberately rather than growing a second behaviour) and
nocx-k6p18.33 (two helper-hosted tabs on one host make inventories() return two
identical owners, so later passes answer ambiguousInventory on a correct state).

NOT VERIFIED: the e2e acceptance spec, which is nocx-k6p18.9's and is running now;
cols/rows on a re-adopted session default until the claiming client resizes,
because the helper's inventory carries no geometry.

title: files.read, files.edit and files.create refuse every file in the shipped product: a path fence of / makes the capability's containment check unsatisfiable
description:
Measured on 2026-09-02 at the seam, not by reading: a probe that mints the grant
`runGrantFor` mints in production and calls `narrowFilesRead` on a real, readable
file gets

    filesystemRoots = []string{"/"}
    READ FAILED under the production fence: filesystem: path outside the
    grant's scope: /tmp/.../real.txt

So `files.read`, `files.edit` and `files.create` cannot reach ANY file in the
shipped product. The tool is offered to the model, the model calls it, and it
always fails.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the product normally and ask the assistant to read any file.
2. `files.read` is offered to the model and the model calls it.
3. Every call comes back `filesystem: path outside the grant's scope`, for a file
   that exists and is readable.

Reproduced directly: mint the grant `runGrantFor` mints — `{session}`,
`{path "/"}`, `{content note}`, `{content snippet}`, `{destination *}` — call
`narrowFilesRead` for a file under `t.TempDir()`, and `Read` fails with
`ErrOutOfScope`. Smaller still: `contained("/etc/passwd", []string{"/"})` is
false on its own.

## The arithmetic

`ScopedReader.allows` is `exact(canonical, exactFiles) && contained(canonical,
roots)` (internal/filesystem/scoped.go:104-109). `contained` (:119-136) is
`canonical == root || strings.HasPrefix(canonical, root + sep)`. With `root ==
"/"` the prefix tested is `"//"`, which no path has. Verified directly:
`contained("/etc/passwd", []string{"/"})` and `contained("/home/dev/x.txt",
[]string{"/"})` are both false; only `"/"` itself is contained.

The roots come from `filesystemRoots(grant)` (internal/agenttools/narrow.go:37-45),
which reads `grant.Scopes`; `AsGrant` fills those from the run fence
(internal/content/effectpolicy.go:324-341); the fence is minted as five literals
including `{ResourcePath, "/"}` (internal/transport/ws_readscreen.go:294-300).

## How it got here, and why the suite is green

nocx-751xy was the opposite defect — the mint carried NO path scope, so
`Registry.ForGrant` never offered `files.read` at all. It was closed on
2026-08-26 by 41e4d978 giving the fence the whole filesystem, and its close
reason reads "Asserted against what the product mints, not a fixture grant. Gate
green." That assertion was at the OFFER layer: the tool is now declared. Nothing
asserted that the offered tool can then execute. So the fix moved the defect from
"the tool is never offered" to "the tool is always offered and always fails", and
the ratchet cannot see it — `ScopedReader.Read` is genuinely reachable.

Every capability test uses a `t.TempDir()` root (internal/assistant/policy_test.go,
internal/assistant/files_edit_test.go, internal/filesystem/scoped_test.go); the
tests that DO mint a `/` fence (internal/assistant/floorpolicy_test.go) are floor
refusals that stop before `Narrow`. This is AGENTS.md testing rule 2 exactly: a
green suite over a feature that does not exist.

## Why the one-line fix is the dangerous one

Special-casing `/` in `contained` the way `pathScopeContains` already does
(internal/content/resource_scope.go:177-179) makes containment universally true,
leaving `exact(canonical, exactFiles)` as the only check — and `exactFiles` is
the canonicalization of the path the model SPELLED, so it matches a symlink's
target too. A symlink out of a row-scoped directory would then be read.

The row's own scopes never reach the capability at all: `filesystemRoots` reads
`grant.Scopes` (the fence) and never `Policy.RowScopes(effect)` (the selector).
That is where the narrowing a person expressed is lost, and it is the half the
fix has to restore — otherwise the capability has nothing to canonicalize
against.

Related: nocx-fsa0v (the fence is nailed to / and nothing can narrow it) is the
same literal seen from the operator's side; nocx-esh2j is the floor half.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `contained("/etc/passwd", []string{"/"})` and `contained("/", []string{"/"})`
  are both true.
- Given a grant minted exactly as `runGrantFor` mints it, `files.read` on a real
  file under `t.TempDir()` returns that file's content rather than
  `ErrOutOfScope`. This is the probe above, as a permanent test.
- Given the same grant with `Observe.Scopes == [path <root>]`, `files.read` of
  `<root>/link`, where `link` points at `<outside>/secret.txt`, fails with
  `errors.Is(err, filesystem.ErrOutOfScope)` and returns none of that file's
  bytes.
- Given the same grant, `files.read` of `<root>/real.txt` succeeds — the paired
  "and on a normal machine it succeeds" for the assertion above.
- The narrowed capability's roots for effect `e` are the canonicalization of
  `Policy.RowScopes(e)`'s path ids, asserted directly on the constructed
  `ScopedReader` and `ScopedEditor`.
- One e2e spec drives `files.read` through the real backend under the production
  mint and asserts the file's text reaches the answer.
close_reason: 66475435. Two halves: contained accepts a root that IS a separator (a root of / tested the prefix // and contained nothing), and filesystemRoots reads Policy.RowScopes(effect) instead of grant.Scopes so the operator's narrowing reaches the capability. Verified at the seam before and after with a probe minting runGrantFor's grant: was 'path outside the grant's scope' on a real file, now reads it. go test ./internal/filesystem/... ./internal/agenttools/ ok; golangci-lint clean tree-wide. NOT covered: a transport-level end-to-end where the model calls files.read over the socket — that is still missing.

title: The helper's session.reset notification has no consumer, so the first ack after a reset ends the tab
description:
Found 2026-09-02 by an adversarial second reading of feat/relay-pty-owner.

The helper's bounded output window reclaims capacity, so a reader that falls
behind the base is sent an explicit EventSessionReset -- AD-9's "emit an explicit
reset" -- and the helper sets sub.sent = sub.acked = resume.From
(internal/helper/session/session.go:424-437).

On the coordinator, Client.sessionNotify (internal/helper/client/client.go:259)
opens with:

    if n.Service != proto.ServiceSession || n.Event != proto.EventSessionExit {
        return
    }

EventSessionReset is dropped on the floor, and there is no other consumer:
grepping EventSessionReset outside internal/helper/proto finds only the producer
and the helper's own service_test.go:721, which asserts against a fake sink.

Two halves, each delivered correctly. The helper emits the reset AD-9 requires;
the coordinator never grew the ear for it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a remote tab through the helper. Make the renderer slow -- a large paste,
   a WebGL stall, WS backpressure -- so AttachedSession.Read lags.
2. Have the shell print more than one window bound. WindowBytes is clamp(0)
   because OpenHosted never sets it, so the helper's floor applies. window.write
   reclaims pages and w.base advances past sub.sent.
3. hostSession.serve (session.go:425) sees resume.Reset, sends the notification,
   and sets sub.sent = sub.acked = base.
4. The coordinator ignores it, so a.offset stays at its old lower value.
5. The next data frame arrives, Read returns n and sets a.offset += n -- still
   below base -- and calls OpAck with that offset.
6. hostSession.ack (session.go:569) hits `if offset < sub.acked { return
   ErrAckBehind }`.
7. Read (sessions.go:295-298) turns the Call error into a.finish(), closing done.
8. realSession's read pump sees EOF.

Observed: the tab reports the session as ENDED while the helper still owns a live
shell and a live PTY -- the exact failure this epic exists to prevent. Expected:
the reset is applied, the renderer is told to clear, and the session continues.

Even without the ack rejection the missed reset is a silent desync: the renderer
splices two non-adjacent stretches of output together, and the only trace is a log
line. That is the soft-degrade-visible-only-in-a-log shape AGENTS.md names.
acceptance_criteria:
The client applies EventSessionReset: a test drives spawn + attach with a tiny
WindowBytes, stops reading, writes past the bound, and asserts the client's cursor
was reset and the next ack is accepted rather than rejected as behind. A second
assertion is that the session is still live afterwards -- it does not report EOF.
Removing the reset consumer turns a named test red.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-09-02, verified by the coordinator. Commits 4c3bf84e and 7bff0997,
merged as aa20a020. Sent back once and the rework is what closes it.

WHAT LANDED FIRST AND STAYS: the reset is applied in stream order, the cursor is
frozen between the notification arriving and the reader reaching it, notifications
match by session AND subscriber, and a refused ack no longer ends the attachment.
That last one is a real behaviour change to an error path and it is right: after a
reset the helper has already moved its own cursor, so acks in flight are
NECESSARILY behind, and that is a race no ordering can win.

WHAT WAS SENT BACK: the first version stated the hole by injecting
"\r\n[nocx] the host's window dropped N bytes...\r\n" into the PTY data queue.
Three things were wrong with it. It contradicts contracts/session.output.schema.json
in that schema's own words -- "the backend hands back what the session printed and
never interprets it (AD-6)" -- and session.output would replay the injected line
forever, indistinguishable from one the shell printed. There is already an owner
for "there is a hole here": content.Gap with a Reason, which ws_session_record.go
already used for the other cause. And the stated blocker did not hold: the worker
considered a control-plane reset notification and correctly priced it as a wire
break in three packages, but the gap route needs no new wire shape at all --
gaps[].reason is a bare string with no enum, the schema states the carry-through
rule for an unrecognised reason, and frontend/src/recovery-notice.tsx already
implements it.

WHAT REPLACED IT: content.GapReasonHostWindow ("hostWindow"), a third distinct
cause. `cap` means we had the bytes and the retention bound here evicted them, so
the knob is on this machine; `unrecorded` means nobody was recording; this one
means nothing here could have kept them because they never crossed the wire, and
the knob is the session's WindowBytes on the HOST. Deliberately not the helper's
own word ("window") -- two vocabularies on two sides of a wire, each naming its
own side.

THE PART THAT WAS NOT FREE, and it is the largest change on this branch. A gap
needs bounds, bounds are offsets, and the offsets belong to outputRing, which was
built on being lossless and had no way to say "these never arrived". Renumbering
after a hole would have created the second coordinate system session.output's own
schema names as the defect it exists to avoid. So the ring now carries holes:
written counts the missing bytes, a run never spans one, a hole leaves the ring
only once every consumer has passed it, and credit is measured in bytes actually
SENT.

That last clause is the subtle one and the worker found it rather than being told:
charging the credit window for bytes nobody can ever ack parks the pump on a
window that can never reopen, so the session goes silent for good the first time
an execution host loses a window larger than CreditLimit. My own mutation --
deleting `- r.missingBetween(floor, pos)` from inFlightLocked -- turns
TestRingHoleIsNotChargedToTheCreditWindow red with "timed out waiting for the
credit window to stay open across a hole". Reverted; tree byte-identical;
./internal/helper/... ./internal/transport/... ./internal/session ./internal/content
green on the merged tree.

snapshot grew a fourth return so the compiler forced all three production callers
to decide rather than defaulting. deadcode -whylive traces both halves --
main -> handleOpen$5 -> outputRing.hole and main -> AttachedSession.Read ->
reportHole -- which is the only check that works here, since RTA cannot report a
dead method behind a live interface (AD-8).

DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN: a live tab still sees a splice. The recording is where the
truth is; a tab watching live is told nothing on screen, because this carrier has
no mid-stream reset shape and inventing one is a wire design rather than a line in
a bugfix. nocx-k6p18.29.

title: AttachedSession.Write sends the session frame unframed, so a helper-hosted tab accepts no input
description:
Found 2026-09-02 by an adversarial second reading of feat/relay-pty-owner, and
independently by nocx-k6p18.9's acceptance spec, which was stuck on exactly this
symptom: the pane renders output and the command never runs.

internal/helper/client/sessions.go, AttachedSession.Write builds the INNER
session-frame payload with proto.EncodeSessionFrame and writes that straight onto
the wire. It never wraps it in the outer [type:1][seq:4][ack:4][len:4] envelope.
Its sibling two screens up, attachedLifecycle.Write, does:
EncodeFrame(TypeLifecycleData, 0, 0, frame). So does every other producer --
client.go:144 (TypeRequest), client.go:186 (TypeCancel), launch.go:76 (TypeHello),
and the helper->coordinator direction at host.go:306.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT. Every test that exercises a TypeSessionData frame builds
the outer envelope BY HAND -- endpoint/serve_test.go:277,396,
endpoint/bridge_test.go:79, session/reattach_test.go:267,
host/session_frame_test.go:121. Nothing anywhere calls AttachedSession.Write.
AGENTS.md rule 4 exactly: the tests encode the author's model of the frame, the
model is right, and the code is wrong.

## Steps to Reproduce

Open a tab on a remote host where the helper is installed, so the session goes
through OpenHosted (internal/app/helper_git.go:509 adopts the *AttachedSession as
the session Channel). Type anything.

Observed: output renders, the keystroke does nothing, and the helper logs
"decoder resync". Expected: the shell receives the byte.

Mechanically: realSession's write loop calls AttachedSession.Write, and the bytes
go on the wire beginning with the session id's first RANDOM byte.
proto.Decoder.prefix() checks byte 0 against the closed type set -- valid about 10
times in 256 -- then reads bytes 9..13 of the id as a length, essentially uniform
over 2^32 and almost always 0 or > MaxFrameBytes. The decoder enters scan mode and
discards the keystroke a byte at a time. In the ~4% of cases where the prefix IS
plausible it consumes a bogus length and resyncs THROUGH the next genuine frame,
so it can eat a real response or a real data frame.
acceptance_criteria:
A test hands AttachedSession a fake conn, calls Write, feeds the captured bytes to
proto.NewDecoder, and gets exactly one TypeSessionData frame carrying the session,
the subscriber, the write epoch and the payload. It fails before the fix. Deleting
the envelope again turns that named test red.
close_reason: Closed 2026-09-02, verified by the coordinator. Commit fc3a0634, merged as aa20a020. AttachedSession.Write now wraps in EncodeFrame(TypeSessionData, 0, 0, frame), and the comment states the invariant as an interval — every byte from the first write until the attachment closes is inside exactly one frame — rather than as the moment the envelope is written. The worker asked the right follow-up question and enumerated every conn.Stdin().Write in the package: TypeRequest, TypeCancel, TypeHello and attachedLifecycle.Write all wrapped correctly; this was the only one. Two tests: the decoder round-trip, asserting zero bytes resynced past, and the bead's reproduction through the real session service over the real socket with a real /bin/sh, asserting the shell ran what was typed. Mutation: envelope removed gives 'the peer's decoder resynced past 51 unframed bytes' and 'the shell never ran what was typed'.

title: The pet is carried off the screen by a block that scrolls away
description:
Measured on 2026-09-02 with a rAF probe on the live stand, sampling `.pet-world`'s transform every frame and reporting any step over 40px:

    JUMP dy=300  doing=idle/sit  during=scroll
    JUMP dy=719  doing=idle/sit  during=output-burst
    JUMP dy=3117 doing=idle/meow during=output-burst   -> y = -3589

The pet ends up three thousand pixels above the pane, still `idle/sit` on a ledge that is no longer anywhere near the window, and reappears somewhere else once the terrain is re-measured. This is what the owner sees as "it teleports constantly".

`deriveTerrain` refuses a candidate above `petHeight` or below the floor, but that check runs only on a full re-measure. `_follow()` updates the held ledge straight from the live rect with no such test, so riding the block is unconditional. A wheel step moves the animal 300px in one frame; a burst of output moves it out of the world.

Riding a block that shifts a few pixels is right and is what nocx-q4qeh.1 bought. Riding one that leaves the window is not: an animal sitting on a sheet of paper that is yanked away does not go with it.

## Success Criteria

- The rAF probe over a scroll, an output burst and a resize reports no step larger than the animal could have walked, except a fall.
- A block leaving the visible area costs the pet its ground -- it falls where it stood -- rather than carrying it out of the pane.
- The pet's drawn position is inside the pane at every frame of that run.
close_reason: Landed as fb2a9901. Measured on the live stand: teleport gone (was dy=3117 to y=-3589 on an output burst, now no jump on scroll, 41px on a burst, 66px on a 700px window resize); the sprite never leaves the pane (was 31px outside, now 0); cornered by a fast cursor, zero land phases and zero distinct positions over four seconds.

title: The helper's exit status is discarded, so every helper-hosted session exits 'unknown'
description:
Every helper-hosted session's exit is reported as interrupted with code 0, whatever the
command actually returned. The helper does its half correctly and the coordinator drops
it on the floor.

The chain, all verified:

- The helper sends `session.exit` carrying ExitStatus.Code.
- internal/helper/client recognises that status, and on closing the attachment calls
  only `a.finish()` (client.go:223 and :282), which is
  `a.once.Do(func() { close(a.done) })` — the code is discarded, never stored.
- AttachedSession implements Read, Write, Resize, Done, Close. It does NOT implement
  WaitErr.
- internal/session/session.go:1126 reads the outcome through exactly that optional
  seam:

      provider, ok := s.ch.(interface{ WaitErr() (error, bool) })
      if !ok { return ExitInterrupted, 0 }

  The assertion fails for every helper channel, so ExitOutcome answers
  ExitInterrupted, 0 and the product shows unknown.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, and this is the part worth keeping.
internal/session/exit_outcome_test.go:170 is TestExitOutcome_NoWaitErrSeamIsInterrupted
— a test asserting that a channel without the seam yields ExitInterrupted. It is a
correct test of the fallback and it makes the hole look like a decision. The helper
channel is not a "future channel" for which interrupted is the honest answer; it is a
channel that HAS the exit status and does not pass it on.

nocx-k6p18.6 ("the exit code still lands ... the outcome comes back from the bytes")
was closed against this. Its own scope — a fresh lifecycle domain on reattach — was
delivered; the attachment's WaitErr seam was nobody's task. Found by the epic's
acceptance test, nocx-k6p18.9.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run `exit 7` (or any non-zero exit) in a session on a remote host with the helper
installed. The block's exit status is unknown/interrupted, never 7.

    grep -n 'func (a \*AttachedSession' internal/helper/client/sessions.go   # no WaitErr
    grep -n 'finish()' internal/helper/client/client.go                      # 223, 282

## Acceptance Criteria

A command that exits non-zero on a helper-hosted session shows THAT status in the
product — asserted through the seam a user reaches, not by unit-testing the accessor.

AttachedSession carries the helper's reported exit status to the coordinator, and the
interval is stated: the status is available from the moment session.exit arrives until
the session is closed, not merely recorded at delivery.

TestExitOutcome_NoWaitErrSeamIsInterrupted keeps its meaning for channels that genuinely
cannot report a status, and gains a sibling asserting that a HELPER channel does. A
fallback test that also covers the defect is how this survived.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as 493bc350. AttachedSession records an immutable snapshot of session.exit BEFORE closing Done (sessionNotify calls recordExit then finish — the ordering is the fix, not an accessor) and exposes it through WaitErr, which is the optional seam session.ExitOutcome already asks for.

No third vocabulary: ExitOutcome gained one branch matching interface{ ExitCode() int } structurally, placed AFTER the concrete *exec.ExitError and *gossh.ExitError arms so existing behaviour is unchanged, and the helper's own DTO satisfies that shape. Code == -1 keeps the local and SSH paths' semantics — signal termination does not become a new outcome.

TestExitOutcome_NoWaitErrSeamIsInterrupted is kept: for a channel that genuinely cannot report a status, interrupted is still the honest answer. The new test is its sibling and drives a real AttachedSession through the product seam rather than calling the accessor, asserting both ends of the interval.

Verified by my own mutation, not the worker's word: deleting the new branch turns TestHelperExitOutcomeCarriesStatusThroughTheProductSeam red with 'before close: outcome = ("interrupted", 0), want ("exited", 7)'; reverting leaves the tree clean and green. Merged tree builds and internal/helper/... plus internal/session are green.

Noted: the worker committed with --no-verify because that worktree had no frontend/node_modules, and said so rather than claiming a green hook. My setup gap; contracts were untouched here because the wire shape did not change — the status was always in the protocol, the client was discarding it.

title: No lifecycle channel reaches a helper-hosted session, so a remote host has no command blocks
description:
A helper-hosted shell is started CONVENTIONAL. internal/helper/session/spawn_local.go:82
builds LaunchOptions{SessionID, Enhanced: true} and nothing else — no Capability, no
Recovery, no Lane/Domain/Epoch, no LifecycleFD and no LifecyclePort. The field's own
documentation states the consequence (internal/shellintegration/launcher.go:47): "Empty
Capability means no channel: the session is conventional."

So there is no lifecycle channel on a remote helper host, and command blocks are what
that costs. The evidence is precise, and the interesting half is the negative:

- The remote shell DOES run in marker-only mode, and the bash/zsh bundle DOES emit
  OSC 133 A/B/C/D. nocx-k6p18.8 delivered that and it works.
- Those raw PTY bytes DO reach the renderer through the helper client.
- And they still produce no blocks: the renderer's OSC 133 handler uses B only for
  _settle(); openBlock is driven by LifecycleProjections. Markers alone open nothing.
- Measured in the product: with a live context, `echo` on a helper-hosted session
  yields blocks: 0.

WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE EPIC. nocx-k6p18.8 was closed and it delivered its half
honestly — the bundle runs from memory and emits markers, with no rc file on the host.
The lifecycle channel is the OTHER half, and it was nobody's task. The seam between two
correct deliverables is where the feature went missing, which is exactly the shape
AGENTS.md rule 2 exists to catch, and it is the epic's acceptance test (nocx-k6p18.9)
that caught it.

WHY THIS IS NOT A WIRING PATCH. The local path carries the capability through an
inherited, already-unlinked descriptor (LifecycleFD, stage1.go). The remote path's
alternative in the same struct is LifecyclePort — a loopback TCP listener ON THE HOST
WE DO NOT OWN. That is a security decision, not plumbing, and it wants ADR-0024, AD-1
and AD-6 read before a line is written. A worker was stopped from "minimally wiring"
this mid-acceptance-run for that reason.

## Steps to Reproduce

Open a session on a remote host with the helper installed, run any command, and count
command blocks in the renderer: zero. The log shows `helper session adopted` and no
lifecycle channel established. The editor stays hidden: `.nocx-editor-input` is
expected visible and is hidden, which is where the acceptance spec stops.

    grep -n 'LaunchOptions{' internal/helper/session/spawn_local.go
    82:  shellintegration.LaunchOptions{SessionID: req.SessionID, Enhanced: true},

## Acceptance Criteria

A command run on a helper-hosted session produces a command block in the product, and
the check watches a user do it rather than asserting a projection was constructed.

The transport for the capability on the remote path is chosen deliberately and the
choice is written down with its security argument — in particular whether anything
listens on a port on the execution host, and if so what authenticates it. An ADR if the
answer moves ADR-0024.

Whatever is decided, `Empty Capability means no channel` stops being reachable by
accident from the helper path: either the helper path supplies one, or it states in
code why a helper-hosted session is deliberately conventional and what the product
shows instead.
notes:
ROUTE DECIDED by the owner, 2026-09-02: the HELPER terminates the lifecycle channel. Not a fork — the alternative was never viable, and offering it was the coordinator's mistake.

The rejected alternative, recorded so it is not re-proposed: reuse the shipped Tier A mechanism, where the coordinator opens an SSH remote forward (internal/ssh/ssh_tunnel.go:147, client.Listen -> tcpip-forward, so sshd owns the listener and an admin's AllowTcpForwarding/PermitListen refusal comes back as a request failure). It is cheap and it reuses the one existing owner. It also dies with the coordinator's SSH connection, which is precisely the scenario this epic exists to survive: 'the session outlives the connection'. Blocks that stop the moment you quit nocx do not meet the sentence the epic is written on.

So the helper is the endpoint, because it is the one thing on the host that does not go away.

TRANSPORT: the inherited descriptor, not a port. From the shell's point of view the helper IS the local parent, so this is the local path's mechanism (LifecycleFD, stage1.go), and nothing listens anywhere — the security question the port raised does not arise. Half of it is already plumbed: spawn_local.go already passes cfg.ExtraFiles = launch.ExtraFiles into the pty. What is missing is the capability, lane, domain and epoch, and the side that terminates the channel on the host.

TIMING: this grows the helper protocol, which is free until the first generation is published and a break afterwards — the same clock as nocx-k6p18.11 (already spent: Version is 2) and nocx-k6p18.12. Doing it now costs nothing; doing it after the first publish costs a protocol break.
close_reason:
Mechanism delivered and merged as 90551295. The helper creates a socketpair (lifecyclechannel.NewSocketPair), hands the child end to the shell through ExtraFiles exactly as the local path does, holds the parent end, and FORWARDS the stream opaquely to the coordinator with a bounded window, cursor, ack and replay — it does not interpret it, because blocks and product policy are the coordinator's under D3 and one owner is the rule.

Verified independently of the worker's report: the diff adds no net.Listen anywhere, so nothing listens on the execution host and the security question the port route raised does not arise; the bridge is net.Pipe, in memory. The capability travels in the spawn DTO and into LaunchOptions — the rcfile/frame path — never argv, never the environment, and the schema says so. TestLifecycleWindowReplaysAfterConnectionReplacement and TestBridgeLifecycleCarriesOpaqueBytesAndCloses both exist; the worker's two mutations were red on the broken implementation and green after revert.

The ssh remote-forward alternative is recorded as rejected in this bead's notes with its reason: it dies with the coordinator's connection, which is the scenario the epic exists to survive.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA 1 AND 2 MOVED TO nocx-k6p18.9, and that is a correction to my brief rather than a gap. 'A command produces a block in the product' and 'blocks survive a coordinator replacement' can only be watched by the epic's acceptance stand. .22 delivers the mechanism; .9 proves a user can use it. The worker refused to declare them met and retracted its own premature WORKER_DONE, which is exactly right.

Two loose ends fixed by me on the merged tree (5b7a0b04): the schema change had not been regenerated into frontend/src/generated/sessions.inventory.ts, so contracts:check was red; and nocx-k6p18.19's move of the artifacts .gitignore into bin/ left four untracked binaries in the old path in any tree where make helpers had run before, one git add -A away from a 4.7 MB commit — now guarded by an ignore rule that states why it outlives the branch.

title: Reg.Adopt drops the SSH options, so a helper-hosted session probes as root with no key
description:
Reg.Adopt hardcodes `sshOpts: nil` (internal/session/session.go:616) where the sibling
Reg.Open sets `sshOpts: opts` (:573). Nothing marks it deliberate — there is no comment,
and the field is the connection's identity: user, key, port, everything.

`realSession.SSHOptions()` hands that nil onward, and internal/app/helper_git.go's
factory builds a real connection from it:

    probeHelperPlatformAt(ctx, sess.Host(), sess.SSHOptions(), lanes, source)

So for a session the helper minted and the coordinator ADOPTED (nocx-k6p18.13, AD-7),
the later probe dials with no user and no key — it goes as the default account, which
is root, and fails to authenticate. Everything reached through that seam on a
helper-hosted session is affected; the Git panel is the surface that reaches it first.

WHY IT SURVIVED. Adopt was added so the execution host's helper could mint the id and
the coordinator preserve it. Its tests assert the id is preserved and the session
registers; none of them opens anything through the adopted session afterwards, so the
nil was never read. This is the same silhouette as nocx-45zyd and nocx-1u0am: a field
correct at construction, dead in the path nobody ran end to end.

FOUND BY nocx-k6p18.9, the epic's acceptance test, before that test could even go
green. That is the AGENTS.md rule-2 argument in one line: deadcode and coverage cannot
report this, and no unit test did.

## Steps to Reproduce

Open a session on a remote host where the helper is installed, so OpenHosted adopts a
helper-minted id, then reach for the Git panel on that session. The probe authenticates
as root with no key instead of the profile's account.

Statically:

    grep -n 'sshOpts' internal/session/session.go
    573:  sshOpts:      opts,      # Open
    616:  sshOpts: nil,            # Adopt

## Acceptance Criteria

An adopted session answers SSHOptions() with the options it was opened with, so the
probe dials the same account the profile named.

A test opens a helper-adopted session and then USES it through the SSHOptions seam —
asserting the options survive adoption, not merely that Adopt returns a session. A test
that only checks the constructor would have passed here too.

The interval is stated: the options are present from adoption until the session closes,
not merely set at construction.
close_reason: Fixed and merged as 352e8f43. Adopt now reconstructs the options with sshOptionsFromConfig — the function Open already uses, not a second derivation — and keeps nil for adoption with no remote config, which is the local shape. Verified by mutation myself: clearing sshOpts in Reg.Close turns the regression test red on the after-close assertion specifically, and reverting leaves the tree byte-identical. The test reads through the SSHOptions seam rather than the constructor, and measures BOTH ends of the interval, because a probe can be issued during teardown. Two coordinator fixes on top of the worker's commit: a stray blank line had detached sshOptionsFromConfig from its doc comment, and the test's name promised an interval while its body checked a moment.

title: The helper binary embeds the helper binaries, and 'make helpers' doubles them every run
description:
cmd/nocx-helper reaches internal/helper/deploy, whose //go:embed all:artifacts holds
the four shipped helper binaries. The chain is not obvious and no one file shows it:

  cmd/nocx-helper -> internal/helper/session -> internal/shellintegration
                  -> internal/ssh -> internal/helper/deploy

So the helper embeds the helper. `make helpers` therefore builds a binary containing
the PREVIOUS run's artifacts and then overwrites the artifacts with it, which is a
doubling per run rather than a rebuild.

Three consequences, and the third is the expensive one:

1. D3's size argument (~2.8 MiB against ~40 MiB) is what licenses the helper to be a
   survival component at all, and it is violated silently on any machine where
   `make helpers` has run twice.
2. Release is correct only by ACCIDENT: release.yml's helpers job checks out clean, so
   artifacts/ holds only the placeholder and the embed is empty. One cached workspace
   away from shipping a 500 MB helper.
3. install.go keys the install directory by the helper's CONTENT HASH (D7). With this
   chain the hash depends on what previous builds happened to leave on disk, which
   destroys the identity-by-construction property nocx-6de7c bought on 2026-08-30.

It blocks nocx-k6p18.9: the acceptance e2e cannot run because its launcher runs
`make helpers` first.

## Steps to Reproduce

In one worktree, run `make helpers` repeatedly and watch the artifacts double.
MEASURED in omp-k6p18-9-e2e-b after four runs:

  nocx-helper-darwin-arm64.gz    266715758
  nocx-helper-linux-amd64.gz     513289471
  nocx-helper-linux-arm64.gz     989857133
  nocx-helper-darwin-amd64.gz   1909491689

and then the linker refuses:

  # github.com/shady2k/nocx/cmd/nocx-helper
  too much data, last section SGOSTRING (3679629129, over 2e+09 bytes)
  make: *** [Makefile:79: helpers] Error 1

The chain itself is checkable without building anything:

  go list -deps ./cmd/nocx-helper | grep helper/deploy

## Acceptance Criteria

cmd/nocx-helper's dependency graph does not contain the package holding
//go:embed all:artifacts, and a TEST asserts that rather than a comment claiming it:
the graph is what regressed here, and only a graph assertion can catch the next
package that reaches across.

`make helpers` is idempotent: run twice in the same tree, the second run produces
artifacts of the same SIZE as the first (gzip stamps mtime into its header, so compare
the decompressed bytes or the sizes, never the .gz bytes).

A built helper is asserted to be under a stated size ceiling, so D3's argument has a
check behind it instead of a number in a comment.
close_reason: Fixed and merged as 1ac1a59a. The embed moved to internal/helper/deploy/artifacts (bin/ subdirectory), owned by the composition root; deploy keeps only the ArtifactSource seam and the filesystem types internal/ssh uses. Verified independently of the worker's report: go list -deps ./cmd/nocx-helper contains no deploy/artifacts, internal/app does; artifacts/bin holds only the committed .gitignore; the build tag leaves one cheap layout test in the ordinary go test path and the three heavy checks under -tags helperacceptance, run from release.yml's helpers job. Three behavioural mutations were shown red by name. The five internal/app failures reproduce identically on the base commit — environment (no /bin/bash, live sshd), not this change.

title: No shipped coordinator path opens a session through the helper
description:
Found 2026-09-01 by the worker on nocx-1u0am, which blocked rather than guessing, and
verified by the coordinator by reading rather than on report. It is that bead's blocker:
the binding cannot be recorded at open because there is no helper-hosted open.

## The finding

**No shipped coordinator path creates or attaches to a helper-hosted session.**

- `internal/helper/client` exposes `Sessions`, `CloseSession` and `Signal`. It has **no
  `Spawn` method and no `Attach` method at all.**
- `proto.OpSpawn` and `proto.OpAttach` are SERVED by `internal/helper/session/service.go`
  and called by nobody outside `internal/helper` and its tests.
- The coordinator's only uses of a helper client are `hostHelper` in
  `internal/app/helper_git.go`, which exists for the `git.open` path, and
  `helperSessionInventory`, which only asks what sessions exist.
- Every terminal session the shipped app opens still goes through `session.Reg.Open`
  (local or SSH). None of them is helper-hosted.

So the coordinator can ASK a helper what it holds, END a session and SIGNAL one. It cannot
CREATE one and cannot ATTACH to one.

## What that means for what is already built

nocx-k6p18.3, .4, .5, .15, .16, .17, .18, .6 and .7 are correct, tested, and reachable from
`cmd/nocx-helper`'s main and from tests. None of them is reachable from a user opening a
tab, because the act that would make a session helper-hosted does not exist in the product.

## Why the existing evidence did not catch it, and this is the part to keep

nocx-k6p18.3's acceptance was proved "end to end over the real frame protocol with a real
shell under a real PTY: a coordinator spawns a per-second marker loop, is killed, and its
replacement finds the session in the inventory". That coordinator was a TEST coordinator.
AGENTS.md rule 2 names exactly this: `cmd/nocx-server` runs the SHIPPED coordinator, not a
harness beside it, so there is no excuse about the harness.

And the `-whylive` contrast in .3's close reason was true and answered a different question:

    WIRED  main -> Host.frame -> Host.request -> Service.Call -> Service.spawn

That `main` is `cmd/nocx-helper`'s. The helper is wired to serve spawn. Nothing asks it to.
`-whylive` tells you a symbol is reachable from SOME main; it cannot tell you which product
capability reaches it.

## THE POLICY IS ALREADY DECIDED. DO NOT DECIDE IT AGAIN.

The coordinator already has one mechanism for "may this machine run the helper", it is
general, and the session surface is simply its second caller.

`helperGitFactory` (`internal/app/helper_git.go:85`) builds
`newResolver(withStore(store), withHelperArtifactAvailable(available),
withHelperRequested(true))` and resolves
`Machine{Fingerprint: sess.HostKeyFingerprint(), Mode: effectiveModeFor(sess)}` into
`DesiredRelay` / `ConsentRequired` / a §6 refusal. `consent.Granted` says it in words:
"the machine may run the helper, and the next git.open installs it." Consent is keyed by
the VERIFIED host public key — one machine, one answer — and is asked when the user reaches
for the feature, not when a connection is made.

The resolver is already parameterised by WHICH SURFACE is reaching, and the code says so:

    withHelperRequested(true), // git.open is the surface reaching for the helper

So session-open is the second surface, resolved the same way, with the same refusal states
(`unsupportedPlatform`, `execForbidden`, `deployFailed`, `ConsentRequired`) surfaced the
same way. A second predicate for "is this machine helper-hosted" is the defect AD-8 names
and the one this repository names most often — two derivations that agree everywhere anyone
looks and disagree once.

**And the triple nocx-1u0am needs already exists on that path.** The `DesiredRelay` branch
returns a `sessionFactory` carrying `host`, `account`, `fp` and `expectHash` — and
`expectHash` IS the generation (`helper_git.go:438`, `:553` both read it as one). Nothing
has to be inferred.

## What is owed

1. `Spawn` and `Attach` on `internal/helper/client`, over the frozen ABI that already
   serves both.
2. The coordinator-side open path that reaches them, resolved through the EXISTING resolver
   with a new surface flag rather than a new predicate.
3. The seam returns `{host, account, generation}` synchronously at open, so nocx-1u0am can
   record the durable binding without inference. Deriving a generation from an installed
   fact, a session id or a previous connection is what nocx-k6p18.15's ordering exists to
   prevent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -rn "func (c \*Client)" internal/helper/client/*.go | grep -v _test` — there is no
   Spawn and no Attach.
2. `grep -rn "OpSpawn" --include=*.go . | grep -v _test` — every hit is inside
   `internal/helper`.
3. Open a tab against a host with a helper installed and consent granted. The session is
   opened by `session.Reg.Open`; the helper is never asked for a PTY.

## Acceptance Criteria

A user opening a tab on a host the EXISTING resolver resolves to DesiredRelay gets a
session whose PTY the helper owns, asserted through `cmd/nocx-server` — the shipped
coordinator — rather than a test harness playing its role. The refusal states are the
resolver's existing ones, reached through the same resolver rather than a second predicate.
`deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive` on the helper spawn path shows a chain from the APP's main,

---

## THE IDENTITY IS ALREADY DECIDED. WHAT IS OWED IS THE AMENDMENT. (2026-09-01, coordinator)

I first wrote this section as an open question. It is not one — the level-1 design answers
it, and I had not read far enough. `.internal/specs/2026-08-31-level-1-the-helper-owns-the-
host-design.md` §3:

> **AD-7** — session identity is server-authoritative. **Amended: the execution host mints
> it**, and the durable handle names the generation that minted it (D2). "The server"
> becomes "that host's helper", which is the same shape AD-7 protects — one authority, not
> the frontend.

So for a helper-hosted session the HELPER mints the id and that id IS the authoritative
session id. There is one authority, as AD-7 has always required; only which process holds
it changes.

**That makes two pieces of code correct rather than assuming:**

1. `internal/app/helper_inventory.go:39` — `live[entry.HostSessionID.Session]` tested
   against `PendingSession.SessionID`. Merged, and right.
2. `nocx-k6p18.13`'s reader (branch omp/k6p18-13-observation, commit dfd7acfa) —
   `helperSessions.set(entry.hostSessionId.session, …)` looked up by `origin.sessionId`.
   Held unmerged pending this bead; the join itself is correct.

**What is genuinely owed, and it is a debt the design already booked:**
`docs/architecture.md`'s AD-7 still reads "the server assigns and returns the authoritative
sessionId" with no mention of the helper. The design says the amendment "lands in
docs/architecture.md with nocx-k6p18 and is not routed around" — the same sentence it uses
for AD-5, whose amendment is carried by nocx-k6p18.8. AD-7's has no bead, and this is it.

So this bead lands the AD-7 amendment in `docs/architecture.md` alongside the seam it
describes: for a helper-hosted session, the execution host's helper mints the authoritative
session id, and the durable handle names the generation that minted it. One authority, not
the frontend — AD-7's purpose survives verbatim.

And the test that was owed either way still is: **one test that names the equality by
name**, at open, for a helper-hosted session — the coordinator's session id and
`HostSessionID.Session` are the same string because the helper minted it. Two places
already depend on that and neither says so.

`docs/vision.md` and `docs/architecture.md` are current-state documents and are amended
deliberately. The design spec and older ADRs are not rewritten.
close_reason:
