The other fifteen rows keep their finite deadlines. supervise runs the INT-TERM-KILL ladder on caller cancellation and on the broker's ErrRequestDisconnected/ErrRequestUndelivered, so a bound that ends a run no longer leaves the command executing. The fork this bead posed was answered by measurement first: the deadline is anchored at RESUME, not at the original call, so it was never charging the person's reading time.

title: An unrecognised passphrase typed into the composer reaches durable history in the clear
description:
Found 2026-08-30 by the worker on nocx-25k9.25 while establishing whether a mistyped passphrase could persist. It was asked to REPORT, not to fix, so this is the finding as a task.

The trace it produced, in order of durability:

1. Before submission, switching targets stores the raw draft in TargetState.drafts and restores it later in the same renderer session. In memory only.
2. On submission, terminal-content.ts stores the raw document in TargetState.historyByTarget, and recall returns that raw session-history text.
3. Submission opens a CommandLedger record containing the raw command.
4. If the command completes, history-client.ts sends the raw command through history-outbox.ts. The backend runs MaskWithSegments before RecordCompleted writes the durable history intent.
5. A submitted command is also sent to the PTY and may appear in xterm scrollback if the shell echoes it. Not verified against a live PTY for a particular shell.

THE GAP IS AT STEP 4, AND IT IS NOT A BUG IN THE MASKER. MaskWithSegments redacts what the DETECTOR RECOGNISES. A vault passphrase is an arbitrary string with no recognisable shape — no prefix, no charset signature, no length rule — so the detector does not recognise it and nothing masks it. There is no separate password-field protection on this path, because on this path the text never went through a password field: it went into the ordinary composer, because the unlock prompt did not hold the keyboard (nocx-25k9.25).

So the composer's protection is shape-based, and the one secret guaranteed to have no shape is a passphrase. ADR-0021 and the masking work assume a detector can find the secret; that assumption holds for tokens and keys and fails exactly here.

nocx-25k9.25 closes the door that let the passphrase in. This bead is about what the room already contains: text that reached durable history before the door was fixed, and any future path that puts unrecognised secret text in the composer.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT: it is not 'improve the detector'. Widening a shape-based detector to catch arbitrary strings makes it match ordinary commands. The question to answer is what the composer should do about text that CANNOT be recognised — whether a submission made while a passphrase prompt was open is recorded at all, whether the ledger and the session-history copies are in scope alongside the durable store, and whether anything already written can be found and removed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have the assistant run something whose result needs vault screening, so the unlock dialog opens.
2. On a build without nocx-25k9.25's fix, start typing: the characters land in the composer instead of the passphrase field.
3. Press Enter. The raw text goes to TargetState.historyByTarget, to the CommandLedger, and through history-outbox to durable history, where MaskWithSegments does not recognise it and does not mask it.

## Notes

Reported by the nocx-25k9.25 worker, 2026-08-30, as a required deliverable of that bead rather than as a discovery in passing. The bead asked it to say whether the text could persist and it answered with the path. Verified by reading; a live PTY echo check was not run and is listed as not verified.
acceptance_criteria: A passphrase mistyped into the composer while an unlock prompt was open does not reach durable history, the CommandLedger, or the recall corpus; the decision about which of the three are in scope is recorded with its reason; the fix does not work by widening the shape detector; a test drives a submission made while a vault prompt is open and asserts what is and is not recorded; and the bead records whether anything already written to a developer's or the owner's store needs finding and removing, with the answer either way.

title: The assistant never calls a tool: it plans a command, then asks the person to run it, and nothing says why
description:
Owner, 2026-08-30, screenshot. He asked 'Расширь файловую систему, я в proxmox увеличили диск'. The model's own thinking names the tools it needs and ends 'Start by running lsblk and df -h'. The visible answer then PIVOTS to asking the person: 'чтобы я мог составить план действий, мне нужно увидеть текущую структуру дисков и разделов'. No tool call was made. The block header says completed, 22.4s, green. The turn looks successful and the product did nothing.

The model reasoned about lsblk/df -h from general knowledge, then found no run tool in front of it and asked the human instead. That is what an assistant with an empty or crippled tool set does.

FOUR CANDIDATE CAUSES, all traced in code today, all producing this exact symptom, none distinguishable from the UI. MEASURE BEFORE EDITING.

1. NO POLICY AT ALL. runGrantFor (internal/transport/ws_readscreen.go:250) opens with 'if s.agentPolicy == nil { return nil }'. Its own comment: 'Unset, the run carries no grant — the model is offered no tools, which is the state before readScreen AND the deliberate production state until a policy is named.' On a stand with no agent policy named the assistant has ZERO tools BY DESIGN, and the UI says nothing at all.

2. DESTRUCTIVE REFUSED KILLS ALL RUNNING, INCLUDING READS. session.run declares Effect: content.EffectMutateDestructive (internal/agenttools/registry.go:293-306). PermittedEffects (internal/content/effectpolicy.go:274) admits an effect unless its decision is DecisionRefuse, and ForGrant (registry.go:589) drops any tool whose declared effect is not permitted. So an operator who refuses mutate-destructive — a reasonable, cautious setting — removes the ability to run ANYTHING, lsblk and df -h included. The per-command lowering that would make lsblk observe (commandEffect, kernel.go:495) runs at EXECUTION time, long after the tool was filtered at OFFER time. The filter uses the declared worst case; the real effect is only knowable per call.

3. LAZY PRESENTATION HIDES IT. defaultEssentialTools (internal/agenttools/presentation.go:16) is exactly {files.read, session.read}. session.run is NOT essential. When Project() goes lazy (schema tokens over the limit) only essential + explicitly loaded tools are Visible; the rest move to a hidden Catalog the model must SEARCH for. A model that does not search sees no way to run a command. This fits the screenshot best: session.read being visible explains why it could speak about the session at all.

4. THE CALL WAS EMITTED AND DROPPED between the model and execution.

WHAT IS COMMON TO ALL FOUR AND IS THE REAL DEFECT: the tool set the model actually received is invisible — to the person and in the log. The turn reports completed and green while the assistant cannot act. AGENTS.md: a soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log; a silent degrade the UI contradicts is how a feature that does not exist survives a release.

INSTRUMENT PROBLEM: the recorded request WOULD name the offered tools, but the model dump is a 200px unformatted window over a megabyte (nocx-0mvpy.9), so the one diagnostic that answers this in a minute is unusable. Fix or use that first.

MAY BE ONE CAUSE WITH nocx-a7mw7.8. That bead is 'a marked block tells the model nothing'. A worker measured the whole frontend path on 2026-08-30 and found it CORRECT — the mark reaches grantedBlocks, survives to submit, and appears in the captured agent.ask payload. If the model is offered no tools, it also cannot call session.read, which is exactly what the attached-content pointer instructs it to do. One empty tool set explains BOTH of the owner's reports. Test that hypothesis first; it is cheaper than either bead alone.

RELATED, NOT DUPLICATE: nocx-klqjo is the same filter dropping notes.*/snippets.* for missing resource SCOPES; this is the EFFECT arm of the same seam, plus presentation. nocx-4h0m7.3 is the declared-versus-derived asymmetry at execution time; this is that same asymmetry at OFFER time.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a pane and ask the assistant something that requires looking at the machine, e.g. 'Расширь файловую систему, я в proxmox увеличили диск'.
2. The model's thinking names lsblk and df -h and says it will start by running them.
3. No tool call is made. The answer asks the PERSON to supply the disk layout. The block header reads completed, green, 22.4s.
Owner screenshot 2026-08-30.
acceptance_criteria: The offered tool set is observable: a person can see which tools the assistant has in this run, and the recorded request names them. When the assistant has no run capability the product SAYS so at the moment the person asks — not only in a log — and names which cause it is: no policy named, the effect refused, the tool unloaded in lazy presentation, or the call dropped. A test drives an ask under a policy that refuses mutate-destructive and asserts the person is told the assistant cannot run commands, rather than the model being left to improvise a request for help. A test asserts a read-only command is runnable under a policy that permits observe, whatever the declared worst case of session.run is — or, if that is deliberately not so, the code says why at the filter.
notes:
DESIGN LINE, from the second session's reading (2026-08-30), before anyone is dispatched:

A filter that decides on a DECLARATION cannot represent a tool whose real effect is
PER-CALL. session.run declares EffectMutateDestructive; commandEffect lowers per
command at execution time (kernel.go:495). So the offer-time filter can only ever
see the declared worst case, and an operator who refuses mutate-destructive — the
cautious, correct-seeming setting — silently loses lsblk and df -h along with rm.
The failure is invisible in exactly the way the owner's screenshot shows: not a
refusal a person can read, but a model behaving as though no such tool exists.

So the fix is probably NOT 'widen the grant'. It is: the offer-time filter admits a
tool whose effect is knowable only per call, and the per-call decision stands where
it already stands. Whoever takes this should state which of the two they chose and
why, in the code, at the filter.

ORDER OF WORK: check the trivial arm FIRST — is an agent policy named on the owner's
stand at all? runGrantFor returns nil without one and the model is then offered
nothing. That is one question to the owner, not an investigation. If it is nil, all
of the above is still true and is simply not what bit him today, and the product's
real defect is that it said nothing.

DO NOT DISPATCH THIS WHILE A WORKER IS IN internal/transport/ws_readscreen.go —
nocx-cmj11/nocx-klqjo is in that file now and two workers in it is how today's only
merge conflict happened. That worker has been asked to print the actual minted grant
and the actual ForGrant tool list, which answers the first acceptance criterion here
as a side effect.

=== 2026-08-30, OWNER'S CONFIGURATION: THREE OF THE FOUR CAUSES ARE DEAD ===

The owner sent his Settings -> Agent policy page. It shows three rows — 'Read and
inspect', 'Make changes that can be undone', 'Make changes that cannot be undone' —
and ALL THREE READ 'Ask every time'.

That eliminates, with evidence rather than argument:

  CAUSE 1 (no policy named) — DEAD. A policy is named, so runGrantFor does not
  return nil and the run carries a grant.

  CAUSE 2 (destructive refused) — DEAD. 'Ask every time' is DecisionAsk.
  PermittedEffects admits an effect unless its decision is DecisionRefuse, so
  observe, mutate-reversible AND mutate-destructive are all permitted, and
  session.run's declared EffectMutateDestructive passes the effect arm.

  CAUSE 3 (lazy presentation) — DEAD, ruled out independently earlier the same
  day: assistant.Params.Presentation has no production caller, so Project's lazy
  branch never runs and Visible is always exactly ForGrant(g).

WHAT REMAINS IS CAUSE 4: session.run was offered, and the call was either never
emitted or was emitted and dropped. Under his configuration the tool should have
been in front of the model.

AND THE SHARPEST FORM OF THE QUESTION IS NOW THIS: with 'Read and inspect' set to
'Ask every time', even lsblk must raise an approval prompt. The owner saw NO
prompt, and the block reported completed and green at 22.4s. So either the model
never emitted the call, or a call was emitted and the approval path swallowed it
without ever reaching a surface. Those two need opposite fixes, and the recorded
request separates them in one look — which is why nocx-0mvpy.9 (the model dump is
a 200px unformatted window) is the instrument to fix or use first.

NOTE THE DESIGN ANALYSIS ABOVE IS STILL TRUE AND STILL WORTH FIXING — a filter
that decides on a declaration cannot represent a tool whose real effect is
per-call, and an operator who sets mutate-destructive to Refuse still silently
loses lsblk and df -h. It is simply not what bit the owner today. Keep it in
scope; do not let the elimination above delete it.

SEPARATE, FROM THE SAME SCREENSHOT: the owner observed 'тут очень мало всего' —
three rows where the matrix has seven. That is DELIBERATE today: LiveEffects()
(internal/agenttools/registry.go:661) returns only effects a declared tool
actually carries, and privilege-change, disclose, cross-boundary and delegate have
nothing behind them yet. nocx-4h0m7.3 seats Delegate (execute) and CrossBoundary
(network) and makes those rows appear. Not a bug; filed here so the next reader
does not re-derive it.

A REGRESSION RISK IS OPEN AGAINST THE FIX IN FLIGHT: the nocx-cmj11 worker's
intersectScopeSet drops a selector whose KIND has no fence entry, so an operator
who sets a path scope on every row loses session and content coverage from
Grant.Scopes and ForGrant then drops session.run AND every notes/snippets tool —
this bug, caused a new way. Sent back to that worker to verify and fix; not yet
confirmed by running it.

=== 2026-08-31: A DETERMINISTIC UNIT-TEST REPRODUCTION OF THE MECHANISM ===

Found while reviewing the nocx-cmj11 worker's diff, and confirmed by measuring the
baseline it had not measured.

internal/transport/TestAssistant_LooksAtPaneDespiteOperatorSessionScope:

  on fix/assistant-panel-wave1   ok, 3.033s
  on the worker's branch         FAIL — 'the run reached completed before the screen
                                 was ever asked for; the model called readScreen with
                                 "" — the id it found in the system prompt'

Green before the change, red after, so it is attributable. What the failing run logged
is the point:

  agent ask: the stream ended run=1 elapsed=97ms reasoning=0 answer=26
             calls=0 outcome=answered

THAT IS THIS BEAD'S SIGNATURE. calls=0 outcome=answered, produced deterministically,
by a grant that failed to cover a tool's ResourceKinds. The model was offered no
usable tool and answered with text instead of calling one — which in the product is
the assistant planning a command in its thinking and then asking the person to run it.

The mechanism, precisely: the worker replaced the union in EffectPolicy.WithRunScopes
with an intersection (correct, and what nocx-cmj11 asked for), but intersectScopeSet
drops a selector whose KIND finds no match in the run fence. A row with a stated
selector therefore ends up carrying fewer resource kinds than the fence, Grant.Scopes
is the union of row scopes, and Registry.ForGrant then drops every tool whose
ResourceKinds are not covered. The test's own name says what it guards:
LooksAtPane DESPITE OperatorSessionScope.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH:

  DOES: a scope narrowing that removes a tool's resource kind produces exactly this
  bead's symptom, deterministically, with a named test that fails on it. Any future
  fix to the grant path has a regression test waiting for it.

  DOES NOT: explain the owner's own instance. His agent-policy has all seven rows at
  'ask' with NO scopes at all, so no narrowing is in play on his stand and this
  mechanism is not what bit him. His cause remains open and is the reason
  instrumentation was commissioned.

=== WHY 'calls' IN THE LOG CANNOT ANSWER THIS, AND WHAT WAS BUILT INSTEAD ===

A wrong reading was published in this session and is corrected here, because the
correction is the useful part. It was claimed that the owner's turn failed to call a
tool because of the MODEL: one run on google/gemma-4-26b-a4b logged calls=0 where
qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b had been calling tools.

The owner rejected it — different models cannot behave identically — and he was right.
The full evening's table shows EVERY first stream segment logging calls=0, in all 25
segments, across three models (tiel-coder-35b-a3b-mlx-oq4e, qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b,
google/gemma-4-26b-a4b). calls=1 appears only on a RESUMED segment.

The cause is that toolCalls++ (internal/transport/ws_agent.go:1199) counts the
assistant.AskToolCall EVENT — an execution — and a call that needs approval aborts the
stream with ApprovalRequestedError before that event fires. So 'calls' never counted
what the model REQUESTED, and calls=0+answered is indistinguishable in the log from
'no tool was offered'. That ambiguity is why two sessions argued from code reading and
both were partly wrong.

Commissioned as a result (worker w2instr, instrumentation only, no behaviour change):
one INFO line per run naming the offered tool set, the grant scopes and the permitted
effects; a per-segment split of REQUESTED versus EXECUTED tool calls plus first-run
versus resume; and NOCX_WIRE_LOG reaching the stand the owner actually runs, since
scripts/dev-web.sh sets it by default and 'wails dev' does not — which is why no dump
of the failing turn exists.

=== AND WHY THE UI SHOWS NO TOOL CALLS (the owner's own question) ===

contracts/agent.runToolCall.schema.json states the notification is 'sent once per
execution, immediately before the tool runs: a call that was refused, malformed or
ESCALATED has not happened, and an escalated one already has a surface of its own
(agent.approvalRequested), which is why this is not sent for it.'

The owner's policy is ask-everything, so EVERY call is escalated, so the
pre-execution announcement is suppressed for all of them by design. The render path
itself is healthy and was not touched by this branch: agent-ask.ts:208 subscribes,
blocks.ts:367 draws the call as a child of the turn, and blocks.test.ts covers it at
:1989, :2044, :2132, :2384, :2397 and :3436.

Whether an APPROVED call is announced on the resumed segment is being measured by
w2instr. If it is not, then under a policy of 'ask about everything' the product shows
no tool activity at all, and that is a separate bead to file.

=== PRECISION NOTE on reading 'calls=0' (2026-08-31) ===

A reviewer cautioned that the reproduction above leans on calls=0, and that calls=0
is also what an escalated-and-pending call prints — so it cannot by itself mean 'no
usable tool was offered'. The caution is right about calls=0 ALONE and wrong about the
PAIR, and the difference is worth stating because both readings will recur.

askOutcome (internal/transport/ws_agent.go:2382):

    err == nil                                   -> "answered"
    ApprovalRequestedError / EgressRequestedError -> "suspended"
    anything else                                 -> "failed"

So an escalated call logs outcome=suspended, never outcome=answered. The pair
calls=0 + outcome=ANSWERED therefore excludes escalation: the stream ended with a nil
error, no approval was raised, and nothing executed. calls=0 + outcome=suspended is
the escalation case and means nothing on its own.

READ THE PAIR, NEVER THE COUNTER. calls=0 by itself is compatible with an escalated
call, a failed call and a text-only answer, and reading it alone is the error already
corrected once in this bead.

The reproduction's load-bearing evidence remains, in this order: green before the
scope change and red after, on a test purpose-built to guard that scope
(TestAssistant_LooksAtPaneDespiteOperatorSessionScope); the model calling readScreen
with an EMPTY id — the one it found in the system prompt rather than one a tool gave
it; and only then the calls=0/outcome=answered pair as corroboration.

--- 2026-08-31, instrumentation landed (claude-panel2, commit 279e6477 on fix/assistant-panel-wave1) ---

The log can now tell the two hypotheses apart, which it could not before:
  agent ask: tools offered  run= count= tools=[...] effects=[...] scopes=[...]
  agent ask: the stream ended  run= toolCallsRequested= toolCallsExecuted= resume= suspensionTool= suspensionEffect= outcome=
The old line had only calls=, which counted EXECUTIONS, so an offered-and-escalated
call and an offer the model ignored both read as calls=0. requested vs executed is
the distinction; suspensionTool names the gate that stopped it.

RENDERER FINDING from the same worker, measured against a scripted provider, NOT yet fixed:
  - the escalated first segment emits NO agent.runToolCall at all (as contracts/agent.runToolCall.schema.json says it deliberately does not);
  - after approval the renderer gets agent.runRequest, then the approved execution emits agent.runToolCall, agent.runDelta, agent.runState;
  - session.run declares opensBlock: true, so scrollback draws the COMMAND BLOCK rather than a tool-call child.
So with the owner's ask-everything policy every call is escalated and the announcement
never fires: that is the visibility defect, and it is in the notify path, not the model.
2026-08-31, RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT — the tool call fires. This bead's premise no longer
holds and it should close.

The owner ran the instrumented stand. backend.log, two runs:

  run=117  tools offered  count=15  tools=[files.read session.list session.read session.run
           files.edit files.create notes.* snippets.*]
           effects=[observe mutate-reversible mutate-destructive privilege-change disclose
           cross-boundary delegate]
           scopes=[session:571d9df2..., path:/, content:content]
  run=117  the stream ended  toolCallsRequested=1 toolCallsExecuted=0 outcome=suspended
           suspensionTool=session.run suspensionEffect=observe
  run=117  the stream ended  toolCallsRequested=1 toolCallsExecuted=1 resume=true outcome=completed

So all three forks this bead was opened to separate are answered, and all three answer in
the product's favour: the tools ARE offered (15 of them, with effects and scopes), the
model DOES call one, the approval IS raised, and after approval the call EXECUTES. In the
panel the owner saw exactly that — 'df -h' ran, was announced with an agent chip, and
came back ok in 25 ms.

The instrumentation is what settled it, and it stays: toolCallsRequested vs
toolCallsExecuted, plus the suspending tool and effect, is the pair that makes this class
of report answerable from a log rather than from a screenshot.

What the same session DID find is a different defect, already filed: nocx-tz0rt — the run
dies of session.run's own 30 s deadline and leaves the command executing. That is where
the 'the tool did not work' experience now lives.

Close this as answered, not as fixed: nothing was wrong in the path this bead names.
close_reason: Answered by measurement rather than fixed — the premise did not hold. The owner ran the instrumented stand: tools ARE offered (run=117, count=15 with effects and scopes), the model DOES call one (toolCallsRequested=1), approval IS raised, and after approval the call EXECUTES (toolCallsExecuted=1, outcome=completed). df -h ran and came back ok in 25ms. All three forks this bead was opened to separate answer in the product's favour. The instrumentation that settled it shipped in PR #157 and stays: toolCallsRequested vs toolCallsExecuted, plus the suspending tool and effect, makes this class of report answerable from a log instead of a screenshot. What the same session found instead is nocx-tz0rt and nocx-wnun2, where the 'the tool did not work' experience actually lives.

title: Attaching a block tells the model nothing: the ask arrives with no attached content
description:
The owner marked a block with the block menu's 'Ask about this block' and
asked a question about it. The model knew nothing about the block. He reports
the same for the frozen full-screen capture (nocx-7l4ex.16), and concludes:
attachments do not work at all right now.

THE PLUMBING IS ALL THERE, which is why this needs measuring rather than
building. Traced 2026-08-30:

  - the block menu's mark: blocks.ts:1090 ('Ask about this block' / 'Unmark');
  - the marks are held in TerminalContent.grantedBlocks (terminal-content.ts:
    682), mutated at :5531-5566 and cleared wholesale at :5570;
  - they reach the ask through the seam grants: () => this.grantedBlocks
    (terminal-content.ts:1939);
  - AgentAsk.submit maps them into attachedContent — itemId, command, state
    and the row window, NOT the text (agent-ask.ts:82);
  - the transport validates the array and refuses a malformed one
    (ws_agent.go:2171, cap of 32 at :61);
  - it becomes SystemPromptFacts.AttachedContent (ws_agent.go:656) and is
    rendered into the prompt's 'Terminal content' section
    (systemprompt.go:112-117) as 'id: …; state: …; command: …'.

So a pointer — not the bytes — is what the model is meant to get, and then it
reads the item with session.read. That design is right and is NOT what this
bead changes.

WHAT TO MEASURE FIRST, in this order, before editing anything:
  1. does the mark reach grantedBlocks at all? The composer chip in every one
     of the owner's screenshots reads 'marked for the question · 0', including
     after he used the menu. If the count is 0, nothing downstream matters.
  2. if it is held, does it survive to submit? Note :3181 reassigns
     grantedBlocks from another source and :5570 clears it wholesale — either
     could fire between the mark and the send.
  3. if it reaches the wire, is the rendered prompt section actually present in
     the request? Read the recorded request in the model dump (nocx-0mvpy) and
     quote the 'Terminal content' section verbatim.

The answer is one of those three, and the fix is whichever it turns out to be.
Do not rebuild the path.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run a command, open the block's ⋮ menu, choose 'Ask about this block', then ask
about that block. The model answers as though it had never been given
anything, and the composer chip reads 'marked for the question · 0'. Owner,
2026-08-30.
acceptance_criteria: Marking a block with 'Ask about this block' shows a non-zero count in the composer chip and the ask carries that item in attachedContent; the recorded request's 'Terminal content' section names the item's id, state and command, quoted in the bead; the model can then read that item; a test drives mark → ask → request and asserts the item is in it, and a second test asserts an unmarked block is not.
notes:
COORDINATOR REVIEW 2026-08-31: the branch w2-attach (0fe56263, unmerged) is NOT an answer to this bead. It adds 44 lines of frontend test and no production change, asserting that agent.ask carries the right attachedContent and that an unmarked neighbour stays out. That is the half nearest the worker.

Both halves already had tests before it: systemprompt_test.go, ws_agent_grant_test.go and ws_agent_systemprompt_test.go cover attachedContent reaching SystemPromptFacts and the prompt's 'Terminal content' section. So every unit is green in both directions and the owner still reports the model knowing nothing — the AGENTS.md rule-1 shape exactly: units correct, the person's task impossible.

Therefore the defect is in the JOIN nothing watches, and the next step is rule 2: ONE check that follows a marked block from the gesture to what the model actually receives, through cmd/nocx-server rather than a harness beside it. Candidates it would separate, none of which any current test can distinguish: the itemId the frontend sends is not the id session.read resolves; the grant is cleared before submit reaches the transport; the prompt section renders but the model is never told it may read those ids.

Do not take this bead as a test-coverage task. The measurement comes first and it is the whole bead.

It adds 44 lines of frontend test and no production change, asserting that agent.ask carries the right attachedContent and that an unmarked neighbour stays out. That is the half nearest the worker.

MEASURED, 2026-08-31, branch w8-attach, commit 7056a662. The marked-block path
WORKS end to end, and this time the check is worth its verdict: it follows the
real gesture through block marking, the attached item id appearing in the
model's system prompt, a dynamic session.read using that exact id, and an answer
derived ONLY from the tool result. The unmarked neighbour is absent from both
the initial and the post-tool prompt. Ran green under chromium.

The seams, for whoever comes next: frontend/src/agent-ask.ts:82-95 sends
attachedContent; internal/transport/ws_agent.go:2250-2281 maps the wire grant to
AttachedContentItem.ItemID; internal/assistant/systemprompt.go:112-122 renders
the session.read id; internal/assistant/blocks.go:242-275 resolves it.

THE MEASUREMENT DEFECT IS NAMED, and it is the reason this bead survived two
rounds of green tests: the previous e2e assertion found the marker in the
COMMAND LABEL, not in a tool result. It could pass while the attachment did
nothing. That is the whole shape of this bead — every unit green, the person's
task impossible — and it is now closed by deriving the answer from the actual
session.read result instead.

SO WHAT REMAINS IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. The owner reported the model knowing
nothing about a marked block, and the path he used now demonstrably works. Do
not close this on the evidence above alone: ask him what the conditions were —
which provider, whether the block was still running, whether the mark survived
a tab change. The cause is outside the attachment join and nobody has named it.

title: The vault unlock prompt does not take the keyboard, and the passphrase goes into the composer
description:
When the assistant needs the vault to screen a tool result, the unlock prompt
opens but the caret stays in the composer: the owner types the passphrase into
the terminal composer instead of the field. It happens sometimes, not always.

A passphrase typed into the composer is a secret written into a place that
keeps text, so this is a leak, not only an annoyance — check whether what was
typed can persist (draft restore, history, scrollback) and say so in the bead.

## Steps to Reproduce

Have the assistant run something whose result needs vault screening. The unlock
dialog appears; start typing — sometimes the characters land in the composer.
Owner screenshot 2026-08-30.
acceptance_criteria: The unlock prompt holds the keyboard from the moment it opens, every time, including when it opens while the composer had focus; a test asserts focus is in the passphrase field on open and cannot be lost to the composer while it is up; the bead records whether anything typed by mistake could have been persisted.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/assistant-panel-wave1 as 6a3b0491 (worker branch w2-vault-focus, reviewed and verified; merge pending). Prompt is now the keyboard owner while it is the top overlay: a capture-phase focusin guard reclaims focus that pane activation steals in the same turn that raised the prompt, gated on the overlay stack's topOverlay() so ownership is named by position rather than by evaluation order. Fix is in the kit (ui/prompt.tsx, +23), not in the surface. dispatcher.ts was deliberately untouched — another session is rewriting it. vault/dialog/prompt specs 154/154, both tsconfigs clean. The required persistence finding is filed as its own P0, nocx-41azr: an arbitrary passphrase is not recognised by the detector, so MaskWithSegments does not mask it and it reaches durable history in the clear.

title: The answer is painted over the frozen screen instead of beside it
description:
Asking a question while a full-screen program is frozen paints the assistant's
text ON TOP of the program's rows: the two texts overlap character by character
and neither is readable.

Two surfaces are writing into the same rows. Decide which owns them for the
span of the ask — an overlay with its own ground over the frozen capture, or
the answer written outside the pane — and make the other one stop.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run top, freeze the screen with an ask, and let the assistant answer: its text
lands on the same rows as top's output. Owner screenshot 2026-08-30.
acceptance_criteria: An answer given while the screen is frozen is readable in full and does not overlap the frozen capture; a test asserts the two do not share rows.
close_reason: Fixed in 31fae852, merged to main in PR #157 (ac06a437): the frozen screen is a photograph and the ask ends in one act — the answer is seated beside the capture rather than painted over it.

title: The parse reports the resources a command touches and what it could not determine, not an effect class
description:
`internal/assistant/cmdeffect.go` answers exactly one question: which effect
class is this command. `df` is observe, `rm` is destructive. That is all it
produces, and it is why a territory cannot be matched against anything — the
grant carries paths, and the parse never mentions one.

It must produce, per command:
- WHICH PATHS, and per path whether the command reads it or writes it. This is
  per-program knowledge, not a general rule: `cp`'s last argument is a write,
  `tee`'s arguments are writes, `sort -o` is a write, `grep`'s are reads.
- REDIRECTIONS AS WRITES. `cat f > /etc/x` writes /etc/x. Today `>` merely
  disqualifies the whole parse, which is not the same as saying where the
  write lands.
- WHAT IT COULD NOT DETERMINE, named. Not "disqualified" but "could not
  resolve $BUILD", "contains $(...) whose value cannot be known without running
  it", so the question put to the person can say why.
- Network reach where it is evident from the program (`curl`, `ssh`,
  `kubectl`), so the effects a territory cannot hold are visible rather than
  silently absent.

The existing disqualifier list (sudo, env, xargs, sh -c, find -exec, command
substitution, redirections, backgrounding) is not deleted — it becomes the
reason attached to an unresolved entry rather than a verdict on the whole
command.

Keep the asymmetry that is already recorded: this parse may only LOWER from the
declared worst case, and anything unresolved keeps the worst case. Adding
resources does not change that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The parse returns a structured account — resources with a per-resource verb,
  plus a list of unresolved parts each carrying its reason — and the effect
  class is derived from that account rather than being the account.
- `cat f > /etc/x` reports a write to /etc/x. `cp a b` reports a read of a and
  a write of b. `rm -rf $BUILD` reports a delete of an unresolved path naming
  $BUILD. Asserted, all three.
- Every unresolved entry carries a reason a person can read.
- The existing lowering tests still pass unchanged: this task adds an account,
  it does not re-decide any classification.
notes:
РЕВЬЮ codex по коду, 2026-08-30, первая реализация (61a18642). Четыре находки; первые две — ослабление политики, а не косметика.

Общая причина первых двух: commandEffect перестал смотреть на inv.Disqualified и смотрит только на отчёт ресурсов. Значит между splitCommand, которая ставит Disqualified на уровне ВСЕЙ строки, и shellFeatureReason, которая порождает Unresolved на уровне ОДНОЙ подкоманды, появилась щель. Всё, что попадает в щель, ПОНИЖАЕТСЯ до observe там, где раньше сохраняло declared.

1. cmdeffect.go:368 — подстановка внутри ДВОЙНЫХ кавычек. Вход: ls "--color=$(touch /tmp/pwn)" /tmp. Отчёт: только read /tmp, Unresolved пуст, эффект понижен, а touch исполняется.
2. cmdeffect.go:262 — оператор <> разбирается как две редирекции, первая съедает > как путь. Вход: cat /tmp/source 1<>/tmp/state. Шелл открывает /tmp/state на ЗАПИСЬ, отчёт видит только read.
3. cmdeffect.go:154 — mv a b теряет удаление источника: сообщается read a, write b, хотя mv удаляет имя a. И install стоит в одной ветке с cp и mv, хотя семантика источника у трёх разная.
4. cmdeffect.go:301 — позиционный разбор не знает опций, съедающих следующее слово. Вход: cp -t /dest source — обе роли перевёрнуты: /dest назван read, source назван write.

Отдельно: коммит ушёл через --no-verify (pre-commit умер на отсутствующем frontend/node_modules, см. nocx-y6d9j). Статика, прогнанная координатором вручную, нашла ещё два: несоответствие gofumpt в cmdeffect_test.go и мёртвую функцию commandWords, оставшуюся после замены на commandWordFacts. Оба исправлены до ревью.
ПРИНЯТО координатором 2026-08-30, коммит 5591285f (ветка nocx-4h0m7-2-parse, от 7808b79d).

Три круга. Первый — реализация. Второй — четыре находки codex, все закрыты регрессиями с ТЕМИ САМЫМИ входами (ls "--color=$(touch /tmp/pwn)" /tmp; cat /tmp/source 1<>/tmp/state; mv a b; cp -t /dest source), плюс отдельно покрыт install -m 755 и install -C. Третий — структурный, и он важнее первых двух.

ЧТО БЫЛО НЕ ТАК ПОСЛЕ ВТОРОГО КРУГА: залатаны четыре ИЗВЕСТНЫХ проявления щели, а не сама щель. commandEffect перестал смотреть на inv.Disqualified, значит любая НЕНАЗВАННАЯ форма дисквалификации снова понизила бы destructive до observe молча.

ЧЕМ ЗАКРЫТО: инвариантом, а не ещё одной заплаткой.

  Disqualified ОБЯЗАН влечь хотя бы одну запись в Unresolved.

finalizeInvocation ставит общую честную причину («the command uses a shell feature whose effect cannot be determined»), если дисквалификация случилась, а причины никто не назвал. Это сохраняет замысел бида — дисквалификатор стал ПРИЧИНОЙ у записи, а не вердиктом обо всей команде — и при этом делает щель невозможной.

И тест утверждает САМ инвариант, а не его частные случаи: TestCommandEffect_DisqualifiedAlwaysHasUnresolvedCause прогоняет 13 форм дисквалификации (подстановка в двойных и одинарных кавычках, обратные кавычки, > и >>, <(...), фон через &, sudo, env, xargs, sh -c, find -exec, tee) и на каждой утверждает три вещи: Disqualified взведён, Unresolved непуст, и commandEffect вернул объявленный худший случай. Добавление нового дисквалификатора без причины уронит его.

Гейт на ветке: gofumpt молчит, golangci-lint --build-tags gtk3 по обоим пакетам молчит, go test ./internal/assistant/ ./internal/content/ -count=1 зелёный. Диф от точки ветвления: 5 файлов, +732/-34.
close_reason: Парс отдаёт структурный отчёт: пути с глаголом, перенаправления как записи, сеть, и неразрешённые части с человекочитаемой причиной. Класс эффекта выводится из отчёта. Асимметрия защищена инвариантом Disqualified => непустой Unresolved с тестом на 13 формах. cbfdb628 (PR #154).

title: The floor: nocx's own state and the obviously fatal are unreachable at any setting
description:
`refuse` lives inside the same matrix row as permit and has no precedence of
its own, so there is no way to say "never, whatever else is configured". Every
protection is therefore only as strong as the widest thing the person ever
clicked.

Two consequences, both live:
- nocx-esh2j — the assistant can edit `~/.config/nocx/agent-policy.json`, the
  document that decides what it may do, and the window calls it an ordinary
  file change.
- The owner's own words: "удалить мой home или отформатировать мой диск я
  никогда не попрошу". There is nothing that can express that.

Both references have this and place it deliberately. hermes checks its hardline
list BEFORE the yolo bypass — "a deny rule is the user saying 'never, even
under yolo'". termic emits its one floor rule as the FINAL filesystem and
network rules of both enforcing profiles, because SBPL is last-match-wins and a
deny placed early would be silently inert; and it proves it with a test that
runs a real sandbox-exec against a hostile profile where the user allow-listed
their entire `~`.

Take the position from termic, including the reason: default-denied is NOT
guaranteed-denied, because the allow surface is extensible and one broad
ancestor entry silently swallows the thing you meant to protect.

What is on the floor, at minimum:
- nocx's own config and data directories (the policy document, the vault, the
  ledger, the shell-integration manifest);
- the operations a person will not ask for: erasing a home directory,
  formatting or partitioning a device, `:(){ :|:& };:`-class self-harm.

The second list is a judgement call and must be SHORT and defended in the code
— a long floor is a second policy nobody authored.

Also decide, and record: the config that gates the floor must not be reachable
BY the floor's subject. termic keeps `.termic.yaml` outside every cage for
exactly this reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision on the floor is evaluated before any permit, any standing rule and
  any session overlay, and cannot be answered around by a person or widened by
  a setting.
- A test sets the most permissive policy expressible — every row permit, the
  widest scopes — and asserts a call inside the floor is still refused. It
  fails today.
- The refusal names what it is, in the person's words, and says it is not
  answerable, so nobody hunts for the setting that would allow it.
- The floor's membership is stated in one place with a sentence per entry
  saying why it is there.
notes:
РЕВЬЮ первой реализации (e2b9baed), координатор читал код, 2026-08-30.

ШОВ ВЫБРАН ВЕРНО, и это стоит сохранить: пол штампуется на грант в engine.go (grant.Policy = grant.Policy.WithFloor(c.floor)), поэтому переживает любой грант, намонеченный транспортом; ResolvePolicy сохраняет его при подмене политики воркспейсом; проверка стоит до DecisionForInvocation И до ветки «человек уже сказал нет»; поле floor неэкспортируемое и без JSON-тега, так что документ политики его не переопределит.

Семь находок.

1. КРИТИЧНО. isHomeTarget матчит по префиксу /home/ и /Users/, значит rm -rf /home/dev/project/build отказывается НА ПОЛУ, то есть НЕОТВЕТИМО. Пол — единственный слой, на который человек ответить не может, поэтому ложное срабатывание здесь означает «работа невозможна и настройки не помогут». И это прямо отменяет success criteria эпика: территория человека почти всегда лежит под его домом. На полу должна лежать САМА домашняя директория, а не всё под ней.
2. writesDevice ловит of=/dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/stdout, /dev/tty как «перезапись устройства». Неответимый отказ на безобидном.
3. removesHome взводит recursive на любом флаге, содержащем букву r: --preserve-root, --interactive, --verbose. То есть флаг, ЗАПРЕЩАЮЩИЙ рекурсию в корень, включает признак рекурсии.
4. ДВЕ реализации форк-бомбы: Floor.RawCommandRefusal по сырой строке и отдельная проверка в forbiddenInvocation по склеенным словам. AGENTS.md запрещает это прямо. Верна первая: вторая работает после токенизации, которая нужные байты уже потеряла.
5. Пол отказывает и в ЧТЕНИИ собственного состояния nocx — Floor.Refusal не различает глагол. Может быть верно, но решение принято МОЛЧА, побочным эффектом. nocx-esh2j говорит про правку, не про чтение.
6. NewClient молча подставляет content.NewFloor("", "") — пустой пол, который не отказывает ни в чём и о котором никто не узнает. Продакшн-вызывающих у NewClient не осталось (app.go перешёл на NewClientWithFloor), но ВСЕ тесты internal/transport зовут NewClient(nil, nil), поэтому ни один транспортный тест не способен поймать регрессию пола. В репозитории уже есть ответ на эту форму — ДЕКЛАРАЦИЯ (D10, nocx-o4hg): app.New отказывает тестовому бинарю, не заявившему позицию по OS-keystore. Пол должен стать обязательным аргументом, а работа без пола — заявлением по имени.
7. Полный прогон пакетов КРАСНЫЙ, и воркер его не делал: TestMiddleware_RunCommandClassifiesTheCallEffect/destructive_command — rm -rf / ждёт запроса одобрения, а пол отказывает раньше. Скорее всего прав пол: спрашивать человека про rm -rf / значит предлагать ему нажать «да». Но это изменение заявленного поведения, и тест переписывается ДЕЛИБЕРАТИВНО, с объяснением в теле коммита.
ПРИНЯТО координатором 2026-08-30, коммит 55911f20 (ветка nocx-4h0m7-1-floor, от 7808b79d). Три круга ревью.

ГЕЙТ НА ВЕТКЕ: gofumpt молчит; golangci-lint --build-tags gtk3 по content/assistant/transport молчит; go test ./internal/content/ ./internal/assistant/ ./internal/transport/ -count=1 — все три ok (32.1s / 1.4s / 139.7s). Диф: 33 файла, +669/-109, из них 12 файлов internal/transport — механические правки вызовов assistant.NewClient, санкционированные координатором (см. ниже).

ЧТО ПОЛУЧИЛОСЬ, и почему шов верный:
- Пол штампуется на грант в engine.go (grant.Policy = grant.Policy.WithFloor(c.floor)), поэтому переживает любой грант, намонеченный транспортом, и ResolvePolicy сохраняет его при подмене политики воркспейсом.
- Проверка стоит ДО DecisionForInvocation и ДО ветки «человек уже сказал нет».
- Поле floor неэкспортируемое и без JSON-тега — документ политики его не переопределит.
- Сырая проверка форк-бомбы отдельным путём, потому что токенизация нужные байты теряет; вторая, дублирующая реализация удалена.

ДВА РЕШЕНИЯ, ПРИНЯТЫЕ ЯВНО И ЗАЩИЩЁННЫЕ В КОДЕ:
1. Пол закрывает и ЧТЕНИЕ собственного состояния nocx: политика, vault, леджер и манифест shell-интеграции — это control material, которое агент не касается ни в какую сторону. Формулировки причин переписаны так, чтобы быть верными и для чтения, и для записи («can never inspect or modify»), иначе отказ в чтении сообщал бы человеку про изменение, которого не было.
2. NoFloor() отключает пол ЦЕЛИКОМ через поле enabled, а не только территориальную половину. До этого forbiddenInvocation работал безусловно, и имя NoFloor обещало больше, чем функция делала — ровно болезнь эпика, только в API. NewFloor ставит enabled: true БЕЗУСЛОВНО, поэтому в проде фатальный список действует даже при пустых корнях.

ИДИОМА D10: пол стал ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНЫМ аргументом assistant.NewClient, работа без пола — заявление по имени (content.NoFloor()). Это то же самое, чем app.New отказывает тестовому бинарю, не заявившему позицию по OS-keystore (nocx-o4hg). Дублирующий NewClientWithFloor удалён. Цена — правка вызовов в 12 тестовых файлах internal/transport; фенс координатор снял сознательно, потому что без этого пол оставался бы отключаемым молча.

ЛОЖНЫЕ СРАБАТЫВАНИЯ, УСТРАНЁННЫЕ ДО ПРИЁМКИ (все три были НЕОТВЕТИМЫМИ отказами, что хуже лишнего вопроса): пол по префиксу /home/ и /Users/ ловил rm -rf ~/project/build и тем отменял success criteria эпика; dd of=/dev/null считался перезаписью устройства; любой флаг с буквой r (включая --preserve-root) взводил признак рекурсии.
close_reason: Пол считается до матрицы, стоячих правил и оверлея сессии; штампуется на грант в engine.go; не выражается в JSON. Обязательный аргумент NewClient по идиоме D10, NoFloor отключает пол целиком. Смержено в main как cbfdb628 (PR #154).

title: You draw where the assistant may work, and it stops asking about everything inside it
description:
The owner's own framing, 2026-08-30, after reading pi-permission-system,
hermes-agent, termic and our own dropped carrier experiment:

  «Я хочу разрешить агенту читать все файлы в определённой папке рекурсивно
   (но не секреты). Могу разрешить изменять любые файлы в папке и выполнять
   скрипты. То есть я хочу ограничить его в cwd… Если я девопс, могу
   разрешить команды диагностики машины, кластера. Могу разрешить удалить
   файлы чтобы почистить диск. Но, например, удалить мой home или
   отформатировать мой диск я никогда не попрошу.»

None of that is expressible today, and the reason is that the permission
surface answers the wrong question. It asks, per call, "may the assistant make
a reversible change" — a class, not a place. A person thinks in territory and
verbs: read here, edit here except the secrets, run what I have seen, never
touch that.

WHAT IS WRONG, MEASURED (2026-08-30):
- The territory exists in the data model and is void in practice. runGrantFor
  mints `{path: "/"}` and WithRunScopes appends run scopes to EVERY row, so an
  operator narrowing a row to /repo gets /repo + / (nocx-cmj11).
- The parse answers "which effect class", never "which resources", so a
  territory has nothing to match against (internal/assistant/cmdeffect.go).
- Read, edit, EXECUTE and delete collapse into two classes. Executing a file
  is neither reading nor mutating it — it is delegating your authority to code
  you did not write, and `cat deploy.sh` and `./deploy.sh` are not the same
  risk. The matrix has four rows with no tool behind them; `delegate` is where
  execute belongs.
- There is no floor: `refuse` lives inside the same row as permit and has no
  precedence, so "never, whatever else is configured" cannot be said. The
  assistant can therefore edit the document that decides what it may do
  (nocx-esh2j).
- A pointer command (`./test.sh`, `npm run build`, `make x`) is presented as
  its own text, while what runs lives elsewhere.

WHAT THIS EPIC IS NOT, deliberately:
- NOT the kernel sandbox. That is the colleague's PR #91 (Landlock/Seatbelt),
  and it is the ENFORCEMENT. This epic is the DECISION, and the two are
  complementary: the cage stops what the parse cannot see, the parse asks the
  question the cage cannot phrase. Where PR #91 lands, this epic's answers are
  backed by a kernel; where it does not — old kernels, and every remote host
  over ssh — they are a policy about what we are willing to send, and the
  product must SAY so rather than imply a guarantee we do not have.
- NOT a quarantine/overlay filesystem. Considered and rejected by the owner on
  2026-08-30: duplicated work, and unreachable for ssh, which is where much of
  a terminal's work happens.
- NOT a carrier or a program the model writes. Measured and dropped
  (ADR-0045).
- NOT substitution. We INSPECT, never rewrite: the verbatim command string is
  what runs, per nocx-y47mi SETTLED 1. Expansion is for the question only.

THE HONEST CEILING, to be written into whatever ADR comes out of this: a parse
is a decision procedure, not a fence. An alias in the person's rc files lies;
a compiled binary calls unlink() with no command name; a model that is refused
can reach for Python. This epic makes the question truthful and the common
case quiet. It does not make the answer enforceable. Only the cage does that,
and only where there is a kernel to hold it.

## Success Criteria

A person opens Settings, names a folder as the assistant's territory with
per-verb rules — read all of it, edit all of it EXCEPT the paths they exclude,
execute only what has been seen, delete to the trash — asks the assistant for a
multi-step job inside that folder, and is asked NOTHING for anything the
territory already covers. The one step that falls outside is refused or asked
with the reason named in the person's words ("writes to /etc, which is outside
your project"; "uses $BUILD, whose value we cannot see"), never as "may make a
reversible change".

One automated end-to-end check watches exactly that, through the shipped
backend, with no test-supplied policy on the path.

And: with the territory set to a folder, a call naming a path outside it does
not pass — asserted, because today it does.

Deliberately out: the kernel sandbox (PR #91), enforcement on remote hosts,
the quarantine filesystem, any rewriting of the command string.
notes:
2026-08-31: .5 и .7 числятся в bd ready, но ФАЙЛОВО заняты. Не запускать туда воркера.

Измерено: git diff --stat origin/main...fix/assistant-panel-wave2 -- internal/assistant/cmdeffect.go
даёт +86/-15. Волна 2 соседней сессии переписывает именно этот файл и сейчас идёт
через гейты (PR ещё не открыт).

Почему это касается обоих бидов:
  .7 в описании прямо говорит 'Run the parse (nocx-4h0m7.2) over the file's contents',
     то есть зовёт разбор в cmdeffect.go;
  .5 инспектирует команду на безопасные раскрытия, и точка вызова там же.

Дробить нельзя: новый пакет без точки вызова — это форма nocx-z7s6, её не пропускает
deadcode-ратчет в том же коммите.

bd ready их предлагает, потому что рёбер на чужую волну нет и быть не может — она не
бид. Это ровно тот случай, про который AGENTS.md пишет, что владение файлами живёт
между волнами, а не только внутри одной. Брать после того, как волна 2 сядет в main.

title: The assistant can edit the document that decides what it is allowed to do, and the window calls it an ordinary file edit
description:
The run grant's path scope is `/` (internal/transport/ws_readscreen.go:250) and
the agent policy lives in an ordinary file on that filesystem:
`storage.NewDocumentStore(paths.ConfigDir())` + `agent-policy.json`
(internal/app/app.go:688, :1047), i.e. `~/.config/nocx/agent-policy.json` on
Linux via resolveConfigDir (internal/storage/paths.go:139).

So `files.edit`, `files.create` and `session.run` all reach it. The matrix
classifies that as `mutate-reversible`, exactly like editing any other file, so
the approval window says "change a file". A person answering that question is
not told they are being asked to widen the assistant's own authority — and if
they have ever answered "Allow always" for reversible changes, they are not
asked at all.

The same reach covers everything else nocx owns under that directory: the
vault, the ledger, the settings document, the shell-integration manifest.

THIS IS THE FOURTH EFFECT CLASS THE OWNER NAMED (2026-08-30): "commands that
control nocx itself". Three of the four already exist as effect classes —
observe, mutate-reversible, mutate-destructive. This one does not, and the
matrix has four rows behind which NO tool stands (privilege-change, disclose,
cross-boundary, delegate), so there is a row to grow into rather than a new
axis to invent.

Two halves, and they are separable:

1. THE CLASS. A call whose resolved resource is inside nocx's own state is not
   a reversible file edit; it is a change to the authority that governs the
   call. It belongs in its own row so the window says so and a standing answer
   for ordinary edits does not cover it.

2. THE FENCE. Classification alone is not enough here for the same reason it is
   not enough anywhere: `session.run` has no filesystem capability at all
   (narrowRun in internal/agenttools/narrow.go carries session scopes only, and
   Runner only answers Allows(sessionID)), so a shell command reaches the file
   whatever the row says. The directory has to be excluded from the run fence
   itself, not only decided about.

Related: nocx-cmj11 (the blanket `/` scope defeats an operator's narrower path
scope) is the same fence, seen from the other side.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant to edit `~/.config/nocx/agent-policy.json` (or to run a
   shell command that writes it).
2. The approval window describes an ordinary file change.
3. With `mutate-reversible` on "Allowed" — reachable in one click today from
   any reversible call — no question is asked at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A call resolving inside nocx's own config/data directory is classified in its
  own effect row, and the approval window names what it is.
- A standing answer for ordinary reversible edits does not permit it.
- The run fence excludes nocx's own state, so a shell command cannot reach it
  either; asserted by a test that tries.
- The four empty rows are reviewed at the same time: either this becomes one of
  them or the set is stated to be wrong (AGENTS.md: a row nothing stands behind
  is a decision nobody can make).
notes:
2026-08-31: ребро на nocx-tyhel добавлено по ПЕРЕСЕЧЕНИЮ ФАЙЛОВ, не по важности.

Половина 1 этого бага («КЛАСС») растит новую строку матрицы эффектов и требует, чтобы
инструмент объявил класс privilege-change, когда разрешённый ресурс лежит внутри
собственного состояния nocx. Это ровно механизм nocx-tyhel (ADR-0053: инструмент
объявляет МНОЖЕСТВО классов, до которых может дотянуться), и живёт он в
internal/agenttools/registry.go — файле, который сейчас держат nocx-cmj11 и
nocx-klqjo.

Без этого ребра bd ready предлагал esh2j как свободный, и следующий агент зашёл бы в
registry.go поверх чужой работы. Половина 2 («ЗАБОР», narrow.go + ws_readscreen.go)
пересечения не имеет, но дробить баг пополам не надо — классификация без забора не
чинит его, это записано в самом биде.
2026-09-02, measured while investigating nocx-cd6vp: the floor's path half is not merely weak for a command, it is DEAD. kernel.floorRefusal (internal/assistant/kernel.go:580-586) builds the scope list from the declaration's resolved ResourceRefs, and session.run resolves only a session resource (resourceSession, internal/agenttools/registry.go:397). Floor.Refusal (internal/content/floor.go:61-79) iterates that list and skips every scope whose Kind is not ResourcePath — so for a shell command the loop never has a single path to test, and only forbiddenInvocation's program table (rm/mkfs/dd/fdisk/diskutil) runs. TestFloor_RefusesUnderMostPermissivePolicy proves the config directory is protected for files.read; its session.run cases are only rm -rf $HOME, mkfs and the fork bomb, so nothing asserts the command path. 'cat <configDir>/agent-policy.json' therefore walks past the floor entirely, which makes nocx-4h0m7.1's criterion false for commands. This is the same fact as this bead's half 2, sharpened: it is not that the fence fails to exclude the directory, it is that the floor never looks.

title: A restored turn draws the provider REQUEST body as its answer, and copying an answer puts it on the clipboard
description:
Two surfaces pick a turn's body by media type alone, on an entry that since
ADR-0040 owns no body at all.

`restore-client.ts:253` — `entry.artifacts.find(a => a.mediaType === 'text/plain')`,
then `:257` `chosen = kind === 'ask' ? (text ?? vt) : ...`.
`restore-client.ts:137` (`answerTextForEntry`, the copy path) — the same lookup.

Since ADR-0040 an `ask` entry carries NO artifact of its own: its prose is a
`text` child opened by `OpenProse` (ledger_agent_sqlite.go:860). The comment at
restore-client.ts:258 says exactly that, three lines below the line that
contradicts it.

The only `text/plain` artifacts hanging on an ask entry are the provider
wiretap captures — `internal/app/assistant_wire_capture.go:39-46` writes the raw
OpenAI request and response bodies with `MediaType: content.MediaText`,
`CaptureMethod: content.CaptureRawOutput` and no ExecutionID, so they are the
turn entry's OWN artifacts. `ledger_sqlite.go:352` returns them ordered by
artifact UUID, so which of request/response wins is arbitrary.

The discriminator already crosses the wire and is already typed:
`captureMethod === 'raw-output'` (frontend/src/generated/ledger.get.ts:209).
`ws_agent_dump.go:136` — the intended consumer of these artifacts — filters
correctly on `payload.wire`; restore was never taught the same.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant anything in a pane; let it answer.
2. Reload the app so the pane RESTORES (blocks read back through
   `ledger.get`/`ledger.artifact`).
3. The whole chat-completions REQUEST body — system prompt, every tool schema,
   `"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}` — is drawn as the turn's answer,
   immediately above the real prose, which arrives separately as `text` children
   inside `.cmd-children`. It never appears live: the live path builds prose
   from `agent.delta` and reads no artifacts.
4. Separately, live OR restored: use the answer block's copy action
   (`blocks.ts:976`, called with the ask entry's id). The clipboard receives the
   raw provider request — system prompt and tool declarations included.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A restored turn draws its prose children and nothing else: a turn whose entry
  owns only wiretap artifacts restores with no answer body.
- Copying an answer yields the answer text, never a wiretap capture.
- A unit test drives the artifact selection with a `raw-output` artifact present
  and asserts it is not chosen — the assertion fails on today's code.
notes:
CORRECTION found while implementing, 2026-08-30.

The clipboard leak is LIVE-ONLY, not "live or restored" as the bead first said.
A RESTORED answer block never had an answer reader at all: restored-block.ts:159
calls createCommandBlock(... facts.author, undefined, menuActions, ...) and that
`undefined` sits in the answerText slot (blocks.ts:1318). So on a restored turn
"Copy output" has always refused with "The stored answer is not available".

Three symptoms, one family:
  1. restore draws the wiretap request as the turn's body   — FIXED
  2. LIVE copy puts the raw provider request on the clipboard — FIXED at the reader
  3. RESTORED copy always refuses, because no reader is passed — OPEN, needs the
     source threaded through restoredTurn -> restoredBlock -> createCommandBlock

Done so far on branch worktree/rapid-river-fb46:
  - restore-client.ts: an ask entry is never asked for a body; new
    answerTextForTurn assembles the answer from the turn's `text` children.
  - terminal-content.ts: the copy path is handed answerTextForTurn.
  - restore-client.test.ts: 30 green, red before the change.
  - e2e/agent-restore.spec.ts: asserts a restored turn has no body of its own.
  - terminal-content.test.ts: "copying a restored answer yields the answer,
    never the provider request (nocx-3dteo)" — RED, and it is the acceptance
    for symptom 3.
close_reason: Merged as cb929599 + b05a6202. All three symptoms: a restored turn is no longer asked for a body it does not own (ADR-0040), so the provider wiretap stopped being drawn as the answer; the copy path assembles the answer from the turn's text children, so the raw request stopped reaching the clipboard; and a restored block is now given an answer reader at all, so copying it no longer refuses while the answer is on screen. restore-client.test.ts 30 green (red before), the terminal-content acceptance test drives the real overflow menu through the real wiring, and e2e/agent-restore.spec.ts now asserts the absence it had no line for.

title: A reconnected ssh pane gets a session but never a prompt: the editor stays hidden
description:
## Description

Measured end to end against a real sshd: after a silent transport death, the
reconnect BINDS a new session and then the pane never becomes usable. The
editor root stays display:none indefinitely — 20 seconds sampled once a second,
plus a further 60s wait, all `none`.

This is nocx-rtzo4s FIRST promise ("a user whose ssh session is lost can get a
working shell back"). The parts around it work; the shell does not arrive.

## What the measurement shows

Sampling `.pane.active` once a second after clicking Reconnect:

  t=0s  {editorDisplay:"none", offer:true,  indicator:"lost", rows:1}
  t=1s  {editorDisplay:"none", offer:false, indicator:null,   rows:1}
  ...unchanged through t=19s

So between t=0 and t=1 the pane acquired a session: the offer card is gone and
the connection indicator is gone, which only happens once the pane has a live
session again. `rows:1` throughout — the dead sessions scrollback survived,
which is the other half of the promise and it works. The editor root exists
(class `nocx-editor`) and is never shown.

The backend agrees the reconnect succeeded (stand log, one run):
  09:11:57.020 lifecycle remote transport lost   transport=tpt-e7818c... cause=closed
  09:11:57.300 SSH open via profile              profileId=ssh:custom:e2e-reconnect-...
  09:11:57.392 lifecycle remote channel established  epoch=3 port=44793
  09:11:57.532 shellintegration: publish skipped reason=already-installed
So a second ssh session opened 280ms after the click and its lifecycle channel
came up. What never follows is whatever makes the editor available.

The same pane reached a prompt fine on the FIRST connect in the same test, so
the machinery works on mount and not on rebind.

## What is NOT claimed

The cause is not isolated. _bindSession does re-subscribe the lifecycle
(terminal-content.ts:3350) and reconnect() calls lifecycle.reset() before it
(:3271), so the suspicion is the establishment handshake — prompt_ready and its
establishAck — not completing for the new generation. That is a suspicion, not
a finding.

## Steps to Reproduce

e2e/ssh-reconnect.spec.ts, first case. Open ssh through e2e/fault-proxy.ts with
keepaliveInterval=1000/keepaliveCountMax=2, run a command, proxy.blackhole(),
wait for the offer, proxy.pass(), click Reconnect. The editor never becomes
visible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a reconnect the pane reaches a prompt and a command typed into the
  editor runs on the new shell and produces a block.
- The dead sessions scrollback is still above the divider (already true).
- e2e/ssh-reconnect.spec.ts first case goes green without being weakened.
close_reason: Fixed in 892d2f16: reset() releases the adopted lane. The kernel is pane-scoped and the lane is session-scoped; keeping it across a reset made every fact of the reconnected session fail the lane guard silently. Safe because the feeding subscription is per-session and the previous one is unsubscribed before reset. Pinned by two tests in state.test.ts (reset releases it; a second lane is still rejected while one session is live).

title: The content store can never be rebuilt once an entry is nested
description:
Symptom: the dev stand (and any build) shows the toast "Tabs are not being
remembered — the layout store is unavailable" on every start, and no tab,
workspace or pane is persisted.

Chain: entries.parent_id is a SELF reference with ON DELETE SET NULL. Under
foreign_keys=ON, `DROP TABLE entries` runs an implicit DELETE of every row,
which fires that action and nulls each child's parent_id — and the same
table's `CHECK (parent_id IS NOT NULL OR pos IS NULL)` then refuses the child
that still holds a seat. resetIfSchemaChanged aborts, content.Open fails,
app.go falls back to content.NewStub, layoutStub.Snapshot returns
ErrNotImplemented, layout.read errors, and panes.ts readLayout() raises the
toast. rebuildDropOrder's children-first rule cannot reach this: a
self-referencing table is its own child, so no ordering drops it after its
children. Permanent — every subsequent start hits the same wall.

Fix: suspend foreign keys for the demolition (SQLite's documented procedure for
a schema change), set outside the transaction because the pragma is a no-op
inside one, restored on every path. The membership gate above already refuses a
file holding any table this build does not own, so nothing is left for the
engine to protect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a content.db written by any earlier schema that holds a nested entry
   (a child block with parent_id and pos — every scrollback with one text run).
2. Start the backend (`make dev-web`, `wails dev`, or cmd/nocx-server).
3. The log carries: `durable command history unavailable; starting without it`
   reason=`content: rebuild for schema 15: sqlite3: constraint failed: CHECK
   constraint failed: parent_id IS NOT NULL OR pos IS NULL`
4. The UI raises "Tabs are not being remembered — the layout store is
   unavailable" and nothing is persisted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A file at an older user_version holding a parent entry and a child with
  (parent_id, pos) is REBUILT: Open succeeds and user_version is stamped to
  the current schemaVersion.
  (TestRebuildDiscardsAFileHoldingANestedEntry)
- The rebuild stays all-or-nothing: a file whose foreign keys cross the drop
  order is discarded whole, never half of each schema.
  (TestRebuildDiscardsAFileWhoseForeignKeysCrossTheDropOrder)
- The backend starts with NO content stub call in its log and no
  history-unavailable warning.

Verified on the owner's real content.db: user_version 14 -> 15, 660 rows
discarded, store open, zero stub calls.
close_reason: Fixed in 784d3451, PR #145: the rebuild suspends foreign keys for the demolition. Verified on the owner's real content.db — user_version 14 -> 15, 660 rows discarded, store open, zero stub calls.

title: SSH keepalive never ran, so a silently dead transport was never noticed
description:
The keepalive prober is the only thing in nocx that can notice a transport that
died without saying so — a suspended laptop, a NAT that dropped the flow. Three
defects stacked, and the product had no working detector at all.

1. `internal/session.sshOptionsFromConfig` translated twenty fields of the
   resolved ConnectConfig and dropped four: KeepaliveInterval,
   KeepaliveCountMax, ReadyTimeout, AgentForward. With a zero interval
   `startKeepalive` returns before starting anything, so THERE WAS NO PROBER IN
   THE SHIPPED PRODUCT. The LivenessObserver wired 200 lines above it could not
   fire and liveness `unknown` was unreachable. Third time a field has been
   carried to that function and dropped by it (DesiredMode nocx-mlm7, Shell
   nocx-pu4.1).

2. The success predicate was `err == nil && ok`. A server answers
   keepalive@openssh.com with REQUEST_FAILURE because it does not implement
   that request type — what x/crypto DiscardRequests does and what OpenSSH does
   — so `ok` is false on a healthy link. Wiring keepalive without fixing this
   would have killed every SSH connection after countMax intervals.

3. The probe had no deadline. x/crypto SendRequest takes no context and blocks
   on a bare channel receive holding globalSentMu, so one silent probe stalled
   the prober forever; even stop() could not be observed. Detection fell back to
   the kernel TCP keepalive, at a latency nobody configured.

Also: the prober closed the raw *gossh.Client, bypassing pooledSSHConn.Close —
skipping the ticker cancel, the jump handle release and any mark the pool could
act on. ConnPool.acquire handed out a closed connection until the last session
unwound.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an ssh tab. Suspend the machine, or black-hole the flow (sockets open,
   bytes discarded).
2. Wake. The transport is dead and nothing notices: no exit notification, no tab
   mark, no way to reconnect. The pane sits on a dead pipe in silence.
3. `internal/ssh/ssh_transport_faults_test.go` stages all five network
   conditions deterministically through a switchable relay.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A transport that stops answering is reported unresponsive and then ends the
  session, inside the configured budget.
- A healthy link is never reported unresponsive.
- A slow host keeps its session and reports its round trip.
- The resolver's keepalive, connect-deadline and agent-forward options reach the
  dial.
- A closed pooled connection is never handed to a new caller.
close_reason: Prober started (four dropped options carried), predicate fixed (any reply is proof of life), probe deadline added (terminal on silence, waits for the parked call), pool marks and evicts a closed connection, round trip measured and graded. internal/ssh/netfault_test.go stages all five network conditions.

title: lifecyclePTY forwarded half the signal seam, reopening nothing-running
description:
The merged gate caught this: e2e/ask-about-full-screen-program.spec.ts:717, the acceptance journey for nocx-7l4ex, failed in BOTH browsers with the incident's own four facts — lifecycle running, attempt att-… open, one running block, and session.signal answering outcome 'nothing-running' where 'delivered' was expected, over 'set +m; sh …fullscreen-key-job.sh'.

lifecyclePTY embeds the pty.Pty INTERFACE, so a concrete type's methods are not promoted and each optional method must be forwarded by hand. It forwarded SignalForeground and ForegroundProcessGroup. nocx-uvac6.11 then split a stop into ForegroundJob (name the addressee once) and SignalProcessGroup (signal that exact group), on a branch where this wrapper did not exist — so those two did not travel with it. Reconciling the two branches made stopForeground ASK ForegroundJob before signalling anything; on an ENHANCED local session the optional-method assertion in realSession.ForegroundJob found nothing, returned pty.ErrNoForeground, the policy classified that as reachGone, and Stop said nothing-running about a running full-screen program.

THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE DEFECT: nocx-o3amz, then nocx-7l4ex.13, now this. Every time a method of this seam was added without its forward; every time it compiled; every time the wrong answer was plausible; every time only an end-to-end run caught it. The file's own comment carried the warning — 'Anything else optional a pty grows needs the same forward, for the same reason' — and it was written before .11 grew two more.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an ENHANCED local session (Enhanced: true) through the production wiring.
2. Start a foreground program that holds the terminal.
3. Call ForegroundJob() on the session.
4. Observed (before the fix): pty.ErrNoForeground, so no addressee can be named and Stop reports nothing-running.
5. Expected: a real pgid, and SignalProcessGroup(pgid, 0) succeeds against it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- lifecyclePTY forwards ForegroundJob and SignalProcessGroup alongside SignalForeground and ForegroundProcessGroup.
- A unit test asks for the SEAM rather than for a method, so a method added later and not forwarded fails a test rather than a person's Stop. Proved by removing the forwards and watching that one test go red.
- e2e/ask-about-full-screen-program.spec.ts:717 passes on both browsers.
close_reason: Fixed and merged: lifecyclePTY now forwards ForegroundJob and SignalProcessGroup alongside SignalForeground and ForegroundProcessGroup, and TestLocalEnhancedSession_TheWholeSignalSeamIsForwarded asks for the SEAM rather than a method — proved by deleting the forwards and watching that one test go red. In main via #127 (4a6ebcf0); e2e/ask-about-full-screen-program.spec.ts:717 passes on both browsers. nocx-d8rv9 remains open and is the real close of this family: it names the seam as an interface so a fifth method breaks the build instead of a person's Stop.

title: TestCommitTransportLossIsIndeterminate оставляет вечно крутящийся pre-commit хук: 62 штуки = 2364 форка/с
description:
## Summary

`TestCommitTransportLossIsIndeterminate` оставляет за собой процесс, который
**крутится на CPU вечно**, по одному за прогон. На 2026-08-29 их накопилось 62,
самому старому 5,3 суток.

Измерено до уборки: **2364 форка в секунду**, load average 35-74 на шести ядрах,
379,7 часов процессорного времени сожжено впустую. После pkill — 17 форков в
секунду и load 10,9. Это была основная фоновая нагрузка машины.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `pgrep -cf 'sh \.git/hooks/pre-commit'` — запомнить число.
2. `go test ./internal/git/helper/ -run TestCommitTransportLossIsIndeterminate`
3. Повторить п.1 — обычно на единицу больше, и он не уходит никогда.
4. `readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd` даёт
   `/tmp/TestCommitTransportLossIsIndeterminate<N>/002 (deleted)`

## Механика: гонка окном 20 мс, не блокировка

Хук, который ставит `slowCommitHook` (`indeterminate_test.go:58`):

```sh
#!/bin/sh
touch '<started>'
while [ ! -f '<release>' ]; do sleep 0.02; done
```

Активный опрос 50 раз в секунду, с форком `sleep` на каждой итерации.

`started` и `release` лежат в ДВУХ разных `t.TempDir()` (строки 116-117), и Go
удаляет оба по завершении теста. Тест пишет `release` (строка 141), забирает
результат и возвращается — дальше срабатывает уборка `t.TempDir()`. Если хук не
успел заметить файл в своём 20-миллисекундном окне, файл исчезает, условие
`[ ! -f release ]` остаётся истинным навсегда, и цикл крутится до конца жизни
машины.

Утечка не в том, что процесс чего-то ждёт, а в том, что он активно ждёт условия,
которое уже никогда не наступит.

## Почему это дороже, чем кажется по %CPU

Каждый экземпляр показывает скромные 0,7% CPU, 62 штуки дают около 31% — треть
ядра. Но нагрузку создаёт не счёт, а порождение процессов: 62 x 50 = порядка 3000
форков в секунду. Load average считает runnable-процессы, поэтому машина стояла на
35-74 при почти свободном CPU, и все гейты на ней замедлились.

## Вопрос, который решает, баг это только в тесте или ещё и в продукте

`internal/git/local/local.go:158-200` выглядит корректно: `proc.InOwnGroup`,
отмена контекста -> `stop()` -> `proc.KillGroup`. Но тест зовёт
`repo.Commit(context.Background(), ...)` — контекст, который никто не отменяет, —
и после `conn.kill()` helper-сторону ничто не останавливает.

Нужно установить, чем на helper-стороне управляется контекст порождённой работы:
если он привязан к соединению — продакшн чист и чинить надо только тест; если и
там фоновый, то каждый потерянный на коммите транспорт оставляет висеть git.

Ответ на этот вопрос — первый шаг, до всякой правки.

## Побочный эффект, уже наблюдавшийся

В соседнем worktree крутились сторожевые циклы `until ! pgrep -f "git commit -F"`,
ожидавшие исчезновения процессов, которые сами не исчезали. И диагностика
медленного гейта дважды уходила по ложному следу: `ps` показывал десятки
`git commit`, и это читалось как «агенты застряли на коммитах».

## Acceptance Criteria

- Хук не может ждать вечно: либо ждёт по дескриптору, а не опросом файла, либо
  имеет предел (условие «файл исчез» = выход), либо обе стороны живут за
  пределами `t.TempDir()`. Опрос с `sleep 0.02` без потолка не остаётся.
- После `go test ./internal/git/helper/...` в системе не остаётся ни одного
  процесса `sh .git/hooks/pre-commit` — проверяется в самом тесте, а не глазами.
- Установлено и записано, привязан ли контекст порождаемой на helper-стороне
  работы к соединению; если нет — заведён отдельный бид на утечку в продукте.
- Тест по-прежнему проверяет то, ради чего написан: потеря транспорта на коммите
  даёт `CommitIndeterminate` без ошибки и без head.
close_reason: Смержено в main: PR #136, мерж-коммит bcb0f8cb. Хук больше не может ждать невозможного — выходит, как только исчезает каталог release-файла, плюс потолок. Страж TestSlowCommitHookCannotOutliveItsTest делает гонку детерминированной (сам убирает каталог, как это делает уборка t.TempDir) и наблюдался красным 30 секунд против старого хука, зелёным за 0,029 с против нового; пять прогонов подряд оставляют ноль сирот. CI 8/8 на слитом дереве (прогон 33269084145). Слияние принесло 131fd813 от другого агента, закрывающий ту же гонку с другого конца — dialKillable ждёт выхода peer-а до уборки; это причина, моя правка предохранитель, вместе осмысленнее. Продуктовая половина вопроса установлена и вынесена в nocx-e3sie: nocx-helper служит с неотменяемым контекстом, Serve не отменяет розданный, у commit нет deadline, ребёнок в своей группе процессов — оборванный SSH-канал оставляет git на удалённой машине навсегда; чинить рефлекторной отменой нельзя, это переписывает D12.

title: a signal to an integrated local session never reaches the pty: the wrapper does not forward SignalForeground
description:
The incident nocx-92gfl.4 was filed as — "команду top теперь никак нельзя
закрыть … stop на блоке говорит Nothing is running in this pane any more" —
and it was diagnosed as a program sharing the launcher shell's process group.
It is not. The shell's group was never consulted, because nothing ever asked
the pty.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an INTEGRATED local session (`Enhanced: true`, which every ordinary
   local tab is).
2. Run any foreground command.
3. Call `session.signal`, or press Stop on the running block.

Observed: `nothing-running`, always, for every signal and every command.

`lifecyclePTY` (`internal/app/app.go`) embeds the `pty.Pty` INTERFACE, so a
concrete type's method is not promoted through it. `*pty.LocalPty.SignalForeground`
— the only thing that can reach the foreground process group — was therefore
invisible to the optional-method assertion `realSession.SignalForeground`
makes (`internal/session/session.go`), which falls back to
`pty.ErrNoForeground`.
