comments.text: CURRENT-MAIN CHECK (f79d324, 2026-08-11): the accepted ADR-0025 fallback is still absent from git. internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash:466-470 accepts -i/-o/-F/-J as modeled value options, but domain_request at 498-502 carries only host/user/port; internal/app/childdomain.go:303-318 therefore composes a different command with those options dropped. No commit reachable from current origin/main mentions nocx-c6z0. The bead is closed, so this is recorded here rather than duplicated; the closed acceptance criterion is not true on current main.

title: [bug] bash 3.2 never completes the channel handshake, so every macOS bash session is a conventional terminal
description:
The authenticated lifecycle channel never activates under GNU bash 3.2, so every
bash session on macOS is a conventional terminal: no blocks, no command ledger,
no editor-owned prompt. macOS's /bin/bash IS 3.2 (Apple froze it in 2007), and
this is a macOS-first product, so this is the primary platform's default shell.

Root cause, one line: `read -N` is bash 4.1+, and nocx.bash uses it as its
readable-probe.

    internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash:132  (__nocx_lc_wait_readable)
    internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash:193  (__nocx_lc_ans_refresh)
    internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash:378  (__nocx_lc_read_grant)

Measured on a real 3.2:

    $ /bin/bash -c 'read -t 0 -N 0 </dev/null; echo rc=$?'
    /bin/bash: read: -N: invalid option
    rc=2

The chain: nocx.bash:285 sends hello, :286 calls __nocx_lc_read_frame, which
calls __nocx_lc_wait_readable, whose probe can never succeed on 3.2. The bounded
wait expires, __nocx_lc_init returns 1, __nocx_lc_active stays 0 — so no
prompt_ready, no start, no complete, ever. The kernel sees hello and silence,
which is exactly what CI reports:

    handshake never completed; accepted=[{1 hello ...}]

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE. nocx-cn86 made the script PARSE under 3.2 and stopped
there. `read -N` is an OPTION, not syntax, so `bash -n` accepts it —
TestBashScript_ParsesUnderBash32 is green while the handshake hangs. The
execution coverage was delegated to "scripts_exec_test.go on the macOS runner",
and the macOS runner had not compiled the package since unix.SOCK_CLOEXEC landed
(nocx-1w69), so it never ran them.

WHY IT IS NOT A REGRESSION OF THIS BRANCH. The probe arrived in dac0950
(nocx-u7uh.11). CI run 31418267046's macOS job is the first time that job
reached `go test` at all; on main (run 31414181750) it dies at Lint with
`undefined: unix.SOCK_CLOEXEC`. The branch made a long-standing defect visible.

THE DESIGN FORK, unresolved. bash 3.2 has no non-consuming readable probe at
all. The three call sites want different things and ADR-0024 (line 271) binds
"handshake time is bounded", which rules out simply blocking:

  - :286 handshake and :378 nested grant want a BOUNDED BLOCKING read. A
    watchdog (background `sleep N && kill`) is the only mechanism 3.2 has.
  - :193 __nocx_lc_ans_refresh runs at EVERY PROMPT and must never block. On
    3.2 the honest option is a documented degrade: desync recovery does not
    run, the domain stays visible-prompt rather than silently wrong.

Measured, so the fork is not theoretical: a scratch patch that makes the probe
return "readable" unconditionally turns 9 of the 12 red tests green and BREAKS
TestBashChannel_HelloNeverArrivesKeepsVisiblePrompt and
TestBashChannel_AcceptNeverComesKeepsVisiblePrompt — the two that guard the
bound. Any fix must keep those green.

Also fix the duplication while here: the same `read -r -t 0 -N 0` is inlined at
all three sites. One owner — `__nocx_lc_probe_readable` — and the version
dispatch resolved ONCE in __nocx_lc_init, not per call: the shell's version is a
constant for the life of the process and ans_refresh is the prompt's hot path.

## Steps to Reproduce

On macOS, or on Linux once the matrix from the sibling bead is in:

    go test -count=1 -run TestBashChannel_ ./internal/shellintegration/

## Acceptance Criteria

- TestBashChannel_* all pass on the bash3.2 variant AND on the bash5.x variant.
- TestBashChannel_HelloNeverArrivesKeepsVisiblePrompt and
  TestBashChannel_AcceptNeverComesKeepsVisiblePrompt stay green on both — the
  handshake is still bounded on 3.2 (ADR-0024 line 271).
- `read -r -t 0 -N 0` appears exactly once in nocx.bash, inside one probe
  function; the three call sites call it.
- The bash-version dispatch is evaluated once at init, not per probe call.
- Whatever 3.2 cannot do is named in the script AND visible in the product, not
  only in a comment — a silent degrade the UI contradicts is the failure mode
  AGENTS.md names.
- The macOS `backend` CI job reaches a green internal/shellintegration.
close_reason: Fixed on main by 37fd666 (the readable-probe has one owner and an answer for bash 3.2), before this bead was re-read; the description above states the pre-fix world. Verified rather than assumed: the whole internal/shellintegration suite is green against the real /bin/bash 3.2.57 on macOS and against both bash variants in the Linux container, and the guard was proven to guard by reverting the version dispatch to an unconditional builtin arm — six TestBashChannel_ tests went red on the 3.2 leg at the 10s handshake bound while the two 'hello never arrives' tests stayed green, exactly the split this bead predicted. Reverted after measuring. read -r -t 0 -N 0 now appears once, in the arm guarded by the 4.1 test. An audit for other bash-4-isms (coproc, declare -A/-n/-g, mapfile, mapfile, wait -n, EPOCHREALTIME, exec {var}<>, [[ -v ]] and others) found six hits, all already correctly guarded; remaining coverage work is tracked as nocx-x9c4. Carried forward, because it bites every Mac: on a stock Mac the bash 5.x leg never runs, since bash on PATH IS /bin/bash 3.2 and forEachBash then yields a single variant — the Linux container is the only place that matrix is real. The symptom that reopened this question on 2026-08-12 (shipped v0.1.0 greets with a bare bash-3.2 prompt and no blocks) is NOT this defect: measured on the running app, the shell nocx started is exec'd away by the user's ~/.bashrc before nocx's install line is reached, which is nocx-yww2.

comments.author: shady
comments.text:
STILL LIVE on shipped v0.1.0, and an earlier note in this session wrongly said otherwise. The mistake is worth recording because the log line invites it.

'lifecycle channel established' (internal/lifecyclechannel/adapter.go:149) is emitted when the BACKEND allocates the socketpair and domain — before the pty exists and before bash is started (internal/app/app.go:961). It says nothing about whether the shell read the accept. I twice read it as proof the handshake worked; it is not. Codex caught it.

Measured on the shipped app with NOCX_LOG_LEVEL=debug, launched via open --env: the run logs 'lifecycle channel established' and then NOTHING — no prompt_ready, no establishment acknowledged. The shell never activates its side, so the renderer never switches to enhanced presentation and the user sees the native bash-3.2$ prompt with Apple's zsh notice and no blocks. That is this bead's symptom exactly.

What it is NOT: the 37fd666 fix IS in the shipped binary. `strings` on /Applications/nocx.app/Contents/MacOS/nocx finds __nocx_lc_resolve_probe and probe_mode=helper (twice each — it is a universal binary, so every string appears per architecture), and /usr/bin/perl exists on the machine. So the helper arm is present and should be selectable. A proposed diagnosis that the shipped executable predates the fix is refuted by that.

Leading suspect now, and it is nocx-2hrb: nocx's rcfile sources the user's ~/.bashrc, whose Kiro CLI block re-execs the session under ~/.local/bin/'bash (kiro-cli-term)', which spawns its own plain bash. A shell reached by that exec was never started with nocx's --rcfile, so nocx.bash is never sourced, no hello is ever sent, and no amount of probe fixing helps. Measured process tree: app -> 'bash (kiro-cli-term)' -> bash.

Next measurement, not yet done: run the same binary with the Kiro blocks temporarily out of ~/.bashrc and see whether prompt_ready appears. That separates this bead from nocx-2hrb cleanly.

comments.author: shady
comments.text:
VERIFIED COMPLETE at 2f6df21. Every acceptance criterion of this bead is met and
measured; no code change was needed, because 37fd666 already landed the fix. This
comment records the measurements so the next reader does not re-derive them.

1. TestBashChannel_* on BOTH variants. Green.
   - macOS host (`bash` on PATH IS /bin/bash 3.2.57, so only the 3.2 leg exists
     here): `go test -count=1 ./internal/shellintegration/` — ok, 83.5s, whole
     package, not just the channel tests.
   - Linux container, the real matrix: `scripts/ci-linux.sh --no-keyring --
     ./internal/shellintegration/...` — ok, 138.8s. Verbose re-run confirms every
     TestBashChannel_ body ran under BOTH `bash5.2` and `bash3.2` subtests.
     Note for anyone checking this on a Mac: a stock macOS dev machine has only
     ONE bash, so `forEachBash` yields a single 3.2 leg and the 5.x side is NOT
     exercised locally. The Linux container is where the matrix is real.

2. The two bound-guards stay green — and the guard actually guards. I reverted
   the version dispatch to an unconditional `builtin` arm (i.e. put `read -N`
   back on 3.2) and re-ran: 6 TestBashChannel_ tests go RED on the bash3.2 leg
   (Handshake, AnswersRefresh, CapabilityNeverInEnvironment,
   ChildProcessCannotRead, ChildFrameWithoutCapability, LocalDescriptorTransport,
   each hitting the 10s handshake bound) while HelloNeverArrivesKeepsVisiblePrompt
   and AcceptNeverComesKeepsVisiblePrompt stay GREEN. That is exactly the split
   this bead predicted, from the opposite direction: the suite now fails for the
   original defect and still holds the ADR-0024 bound. Reverted after measuring;
   tree clean.

3. `read -r -t 0 -N 0` appears exactly ONCE — nocx.bash:171, inside
   __nocx_lc_probe_readable's `builtin` arm. The three call sites
   (__nocx_lc_wait_readable, __nocx_lc_ans_refresh, __nocx_lc_read_grant) all
   call the one probe.

4. The dispatch is resolved once: __nocx_lc_resolve_probe is called from
   __nocx_lc_init before the first read, and caches __nocx_lc_probe_mode /
   __nocx_lc_probe_helper. The prompt hot path reads the latch, never re-tests.

5. The design fork this bead left open was resolved BETTER than it framed it. The
   bead expected a watchdog for the handshake plus a documented degrade losing
   desync recovery on 3.2. perl's select() is non-blocking, so ans_refresh keeps
   working on 3.2 and no degrade was spent — 37fd666's body records the
   measurement that chose it. The remaining floor (probe_mode=none: bash <4.1 AND
   no perl) degrades to a conventional terminal with a VISIBLE native prompt.

BASH-4-ISM AUDIT, since the premise was that 3.2 had been unverifiable. Scanned
nocx.bash for coproc, declare -A/-n/-g, mapfile/readarray, ${x^^}/${x,,}, &>>,
|&, wait -n, globstar, lastpipe, ${x@Q}, EPOCHREALTIME/EPOCHSECONDS, SRANDOM,
BASH_ARGV0, read -N, printf %()T, exec {var}<>, [[ -v ]], compopt. Six hits, all
ALREADY correctly guarded: `coproc` (752) and `exec {var}>&-` (768) inside `eval`
behind the 4.1 test; EPOCHREALTIME (1098) behind a presence check with an
explicit 3.2 branch; `read -N` (171) only in the builtin arm; BASH_REMATCH is
3.0+. Nothing new to file. The remaining coverage work is already nocx-x9c4
(extend the matrix to the other 24 real-bash call sites).

CORRECTION to the 2026-08-12 10:37 comment: the leading suspect is cited there as
"nocx-2hrb", which does not exist in the database. The bead meant is nocx-yww2,
"nocx's rcfile sources the user's bashrc, and a second shell integration in it
takes the session over" (P0, open, depends on nocx-viil).

And that suspect is now confirmed on this machine, which is the "next measurement,
not yet done" the comment asked for. ~/.bashrc line 1 is Kiro CLI's pre block; it
evals `kiro-cli init bash pre --rcfile bashrc`, whose output installs
bash-preexec, whose own header states it "will most likely break" if
PROMPT_COMMAND or `trap DEBUG` are set after it — which is precisely what nocx's
markers do. So the shipped-v0.1.0 symptom ("hello and then nothing") belongs to
nocx-yww2, not to this bead: the probe is fixed and proven on a real 3.2, and the
shell that never activates is a different shell than the one nocx started.

The product-visibility half of criterion 5 ("visible in the product, not only in a
comment") is owned by nocx-viil, "A session that fell back to a conventional
terminal never says so", already open and in progress.

Criterion 6 said "the macOS backend CI job reaches a green internal/shellintegration".
That job moved deliberately: ci.yml now runs internal/shellintegration on the
LINUX job, because scripts/install-bash32.sh puts a real 3.2 there and the
dimension that matters is a bash version, not an operating system. The ci.yml
header records the reasoning. Green there, verified above.

Left open rather than closed: the acceptance criteria are objectively met, but the
owner reopened the question today on a symptom that is really nocx-yww2's, so the
close call is theirs.

title: Every bash shell on macOS starts with no integration: a bash-4 construct is a bash-3.2 syntax error
description:
macOS ships GNU bash 3.2.57 as /bin/bash — Apple froze it at the last GPLv2
release in 2007 — and nocx.bash staged the nested child's rcfile with
`coproc __nocx_boot { ... }`, which is bash 4.0+ SYNTAX. The script guarded it
at runtime with `if (( BASH_VERSINFO[0] >= 4 ))`, but a version test cannot
guard syntax: bash parses a function body whole before executing any of it.

So on the platform this product ships to FIRST, every bash shell died while
sourcing the integration ("syntax error near unexpected token `}'") and came
up as a conventional shell with no markers, no blocks and no channel. The same
applies to `exec {var}>&-` (bash 4.1+) a few lines below.

Found only by the macOS CI job — the one place in the repo with a real 3.2.
The pre-commit container is golang:1.26-bookworm, which has bash 5.2, so the
whole Linux side of the gate was green. See nocx-cn86 for the gate half.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS (or: docker run --rm -v .../scripts:/s:ro bash:3.2 bash -n /s/nocx.bash)
2. The file is rejected at the `coproc` token; nothing in it ever runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The shipped bash script parses under GNU bash 3.2 — asserted by a test, not
  by reading it.
- A bash-4+ construct that reaches the file again fails that test on Linux,
  not only on the macOS runner.
- internal/shellintegration and internal/app are green on macos-latest.
close_reason: Shipped. internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash:939 now uses eval with coproc and a bash-3.2 fallback branch at :963. The gate exists: TestBashScript_ParsesUnderBash32 in scripts_bash32_test.go:28 runs bash32 -n, and bash 3.2 is installed both in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:250) and in .githooks/images/ci-linux/Dockerfile. Commit 72951b5b. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: The lifecycle channel does not compile on macOS: SOCK_CLOEXEC is Linux-only
description:
internal/lifecyclechannel/adapter.go:113 calls unix.Socketpair with
unix.SOCK_CLOEXEC. That constant exists on Linux and not on Darwin, and the
file carries no build tag, so the package does not compile on macOS. It is
imported by internal/app/app.go, so this is the PRODUCT failing to build,
not a test-only problem — the macOS half of the release cannot be produced.

Found by the v0.1.0 release run (31411588854), ci/backend. Invisible to every
local gate because all of them run on Linux: the host, the container the
pre-commit hook uses, and the e2e container AGENTS.md prescribes.

Fix shape: a per-OS pair, the convention this repo already uses
(secretservice_linux.go / secretservice_other.go). Linux keeps the atomic
SOCK_CLOEXEC; the other half takes syscall.ForkLock.RLock around
unix.Socketpair plus unix.CloseOnExec on both descriptors, which is what the
standard library does where the atomic flag is unavailable. The deadcode
baseline documents that a per-OS pair needs BOTH halves listed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. GOOS=darwin go build ./internal/lifecyclechannel/
2. It fails: undefined: unix.SOCK_CLOEXEC at adapter.go:113.

## Acceptance Criteria

- go build ./... and go vet ./... succeed on darwin.
- The child descriptor is still inherited by the shell through ExtraFiles,
  and no descriptor leaks across an exec on either platform.
- ci/backend (macOS) is green.
close_reason: Shipped. internal/lifecyclechannel/socketpair_linux.go uses unix.SOCK_CLOEXEC while socketpair_other.go carries the !linux build tag with a ForkLock plus CloseOnExec path; adapter.go:163 calls socketpairCloexec() and no SOCK_CLOEXEC remains in untagged code. Commit 07b8266c. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: Hand-typed ssh with password auth cannot log in: the nested-child wrapper pre-fills the ssh clients stdin
description:
Owner, 2026-08-10, three symptoms from one cause: a hand-typed `ssh` in a
local tab takes 5+ seconds before anything happens, prints doubled echo and
odd indentation, and password login fails outright.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a local (integrated) tab type `ssh root@192.168.0.57` and press Enter.
2. Nothing happens for ~5 s.
3. The prompt is reprinted, the command line echoes a second time, then
   ssh finally runs and asks for the password.
4. Entering the correct password gives "Permission denied, please try again."

## What actually happens

Captured against a real backend with the frames logged (the probe had to send
lifecycle.establishAck itself — without it the shell stays conventional and
the whole path is invisible, which is why a naive capture shows nothing):

    3.00s  >>> ssh root@192.168.0.57
    3.00s  ingest start          (attempt opens, origin=shell)
    3.00s  ingest domain_request env=ssh host=192.168.0.57 user=root
    3.00s  grant composed: an ssh child line of 44132 bytes
    3.00s  ingest domain_suspended
    7.57s  lifecycle.changed: native      <- the child never established

So the nested-domain machinery (nocx-u7uh.11/.28/.29, ADR-0022) DOES fire on a
hand-typed ssh. The parent suspends and runs the composed line instead of the
users command:

    __nocx_ssh_saved=$(stty -g); { printf wrapper; printf capability;
      printf payload; printf terminator; stty raw -echo; cat; }
      | ssh -tt -R 127.0.0.1:CPORT:127.0.0.1:LPORT dst; ...

## Why password auth breaks

The ssh clients stdin is that pipe, and the pipe ALREADY contains the in-band
bootstrap (wrapper, capability, payload, terminator) before ssh has
authenticated. With password auth the client has nothing to type into yet, and
the staged bytes are consumed as the password attempt — hence the immediate
"Permission denied" and the second prompt. The whole in-band contract assumes
the far side reaches a shell prompt, i.e. that authentication is
non-interactive (a key). Every proof of the ssh child (live_sshd_test.go,
nocx-u7uh.29) authenticates with a key, so the interactive-password case was
never exercised.

The delay and the doubled echo are the same mechanism: ~4.5 s waiting for a
child that cannot establish, then the fall back to native, the prompt
reprinted with several 133;B markers, and the command re-echoed.

The password dialog the owner expected is a different path entirely — it
belongs to a PROFILE ssh open, where the backend owns the transport. A
hand-typed ssh is the system ssh client asking in the pty; nothing raises a
nocx prompt there.

## Direction (not yet decided)

The child must not be attempted when it would break the login. Options, in
rough order of appeal:
  1. Detect that authentication will be interactive and run the command
     conventionally (no wrapper) — the parent already falls back cleanly.
  2. Stage the in-band payload only AFTER the far side reaches a prompt,
     rather than pre-filling the pipe.
  3. Keep the users command untouched for hand-typed ssh and offer
     integration afterwards (relates to nocx-pu4.4).

Whatever is chosen, the fallback must be fast: five seconds of nothing, with
no diagnostic, is what makes this read as a hang.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Password-authenticated `ssh` typed by hand logs in exactly as it does in a
  plain terminal, with no doubled echo.
- A test drives an interactive password login through the nested path (a real
  sshd with PasswordAuthentication and a known password).
- When the child cannot be established the parent runs the command without a
  perceptible delay.
close_reason: Fixed in ddbbb995: the client keeps the terminal (argv delivery per ADR-0022) and max_frame is 256 KiB so the grant is actually delivered.

title: Shell integration over ssh works on the first connection to a host and never again
description:
Found while verifying nocx-tr2n against the ows host, 2026-08-10.

With nocx-tr2n fixed an ssh session finally establishes its lifecycle channel,
and blocks still did not appear. The far shell had NOCX_SHELL_INTEGRATION=1,
NOCX_PROMPT_MODE=marker-only and NOCX_LIFECYCLE_PORT set, bash 5.2, the bundle
present and hash-correct at /root/.nocx/integration/v25/nocx.bash — and
NOCX_GENERATION empty, no __nocx_* function defined, extdebug off.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Connect to any host for the first time. The bundle publishes; blocks work.
2. Disconnect and connect again — the bundle is already installed.
3. The session comes up conventional. No markers, no blocks, no diagnostic
   anywhere: not in the backend log, not in shellIntegrationReason, not on
   screen.

## Root cause

launcher_publish.go, the sh publish prelude. `__nocx_gen` is assigned in ONE
place — the final statement of the successful publish path — and
`export NOCX_GENERATION="${__nocx_gen-}"` runs unconditionally at the end.
`__nocx_skip=1` is set when the installed version is >= the one we carry, so
on every connection after the first the prelude skips, `__nocx_gen` stays
empty, and the exported generation is "".

The rcfile the full launcher installs does not embed the scripts: it sources
`${HOME}/.nocx/integration/${NOCX_GENERATION}/nocx.bash 2>/dev/null`
(launch.go launchSourceLine). With an empty generation the path names a
directory that does not exist, the source fails, and stderr is suppressed by
design (ADR-0024 decision 4 wants a clean native prompt, not an error line).
So the shell starts with the integration ENVIRONMENT and none of the
integration, and nothing anywhere says so.

Effect: shell integration over ssh worked on the FIRST connection to a host
and never again. The owner never saw blocks because the bundle had been
installed long ago.

## Why every test passed

Every proof of the full launcher — TestBashFullLauncher_..., the zsh and
posix twins, the sh-publish conformance tests — starts from a fresh
t.TempDir() $HOME, where the publish always happens and __nocx_gen is always
assigned. The second connection to one $HOME was never exercised, and that is
the state every real host is in.

## Fix

The prelude adopts the installed generation when it skips BECAUSE one is
already installed: it re-proves the activation the way the launch carrier
does (design §3.3) — the manifest names a safe generation, every file it
lists exists, is not a symlink, and matches its recorded sha256 — and only
then exports it. A hash mismatch, a missing file or an unknown protocol still
export nothing, so an unprovable generation is never sourced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A second connection to a $HOME that already carries the bundle comes up
  integrated (A/B markers on a real pty).
- A corrupt or hash-mismatched installed generation exports no generation.
- An unknown protocol exports no generation.
- The no-downgrade contract is unchanged: a newer installed generation is
  adopted, never overwritten.
close_reason: Fixed in 528fecb6: the sh publish prelude adopts an already-installed generation after re-proving it, so NOCX_GENERATION is never empty on a host that carries the bundle.

title: An ssh tab never asks for integration — enhanced is renderer-supplied and ssh omits it
description:
Reported by the owner 2026-08-10 with a screenshot: an ssh tab opened from the
connection manager shows plain output — no blocks, no header, no timer.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a saved ssh connection from the connection manager (owner: root@192.168.0.57).
2. Land at the remote prompt; run `ls`, then `pwd`.
3. The output is flat text. No block forms, the pane stays unstructured. The
   same shell integration bundle is installed and current on the far host.

## Root cause

The renderer decides whether a session may become integrated, and for ssh it
never says yes.

  frontend/src/ipc.ts:395 openSSHSession()       — no `enhanced` in the params
  frontend/src/ipc.ts:410 openSSHSessionByHost() — no `enhanced` in the params
  frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:543           — the LOCAL path sends true

internal/transport/ws.go:1229 is the single assignment `Enhanced: params.Enhanced`
(the ssh branch never revisits it), so every ssh session is Enhanced=false. Then
internal/session/session.go:217 skips ssh.WithEnhanced(), and the gate at
internal/ssh/ssh_real.go:174

    if acq.cfg.Enhanced && acq.cfg.RemoteLifecycle != nil && acq.cfg.RemoteLauncher != nil

never runs — no lifecycle channel is ever established for an ssh session. The
launcher then omits NOCX_PROMPT_MODE, NOCX_SESSION_ID and every NOCX_LIFECYCLE_*
(internal/shellintegration/launcher.go:104), the far shell runs baseline
integration (native prompt + OSC 133), and after ADR-0024 markers open no blocks
(frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:1033) — the pane falls to setUnstructured().

Evidence from the owner run (nocx-dev/nocx.log, host 192.168.0.57):

    10:05:04 lifecycle channel established transport=tpt-6311... epoch=1   (local)
    10:06:51 lifecycle channel established transport=tpt-a4d9... epoch=2   (local)
    10:08:09 shellintegration: remote bundle published root=/root/.nocx version=25
    10:08:09 session opened id=d3aa... kind=ssh                            (no channel)

No "lifecycle channel refused" warning either: the gate never reached Establish.

## Why the suite was green

Every test that proves the remote channel supplies the flag by hand —
internal/app/live_sshd_test.go:504, internal/ssh/ssh_lifecycle_test.go (x5),
internal/ssh/ssh_launcher_test.go (x3) all pass WithEnhanced(). The only
production caller is behind an `if` that is false for ssh. nocx-u7uh.4 and
nocx-u7uh.17 closed on a channel that is unreachable in the product.

## Decision (owner, 2026-08-10)

"Always try to open with blocks; if it does not work, fall back to a terminal."
So `enhanced` stops being a renderer-supplied wire parameter: the backend always
requests integration and every layer below already fails open to a visible
native prompt. This also removes the second owner of a question `desiredMode`
(raw|script|relay) already answers per connection — AD-8.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opening an ssh session (profile AND direct-host) establishes the lifecycle
  channel: a test at the transport seam asserts the Config reaching the registry
  has Enhanced set, for kind=ssh, without the renderer sending anything.
- `enhanced` is gone from the open params and from ipc.ts; no caller can forget it.
- A raw/relay destination does not allocate a lifecycle channel it will close
  unused (modeAllowsIntegration is part of the gate).
- The live-sshd proof exercises the production flag, not one the test supplies.
- Blocks appear in an ssh tab against a real sshd.
close_reason: Fixed in eab77cbb: enhanced removed from the wire, handleOpen requests integration for every session, and the mode joins the ssh lifecycle gate.

title: Blocks never appear: setUnstructured runs on every lifecycle change
description:
Reported by the owner: with nocx-u7uh.23 fixed, a command now runs and its output is visible and the editor returns — but there are NO BLOCKS. The output is a flat unstructured stream; the block model never takes over even though the session has a live authenticated domain.

## Cause (coordinator, read from the source — NOT yet confirmed in the UI)

frontend/src/terminal-content.ts, the kernel subscription:

    this._lifecycleChangeUnsub = this.lifecycle.onChange(() => {
      this._syncLifecycleOwnership()
      this._updateCapability()
      this.scrollback?.setUnstructured()      // <-- unconditional
    })

`setUnstructured()` sets ScrollbackController._mode = 'unstructured' and repaints the live container. It is called on EVERY lifecycle change, so every fact — prompt_ready, running, completed, prompt_ready — tears the block model back down. The block projection's openBlock (lifecycle/projections.ts) sets the running/idle modes, and this call fights it on the very next fact.

Two nearby calls are CORRECT and must not be changed:
 - the initial call after `this._projections.attach()`: the kernel starts Native, so a conventional presentation is right until a domain establishes;
 - the one in `renderer.onBufferChange` when leaving the alternate buffer.

The intended rule is the one written in the onBufferChange comment: "A conventional terminal stays unstructured: the scrollback-block model never takes over (ADR-0024 §4)". Conventional means no live authenticated domain — LifecycleState kinds 'native' and 'lost'. With a live domain (prompt_ready / running / desynchronized) the block model owns the pane.

Confirm that reading against ADR-0024 §4 and the block projection before changing it; if the truth is subtler than "native or lost", say so rather than encoding my guess.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a local enhanced session (the fix for nocx-u7uh.23 must be present — commit 3fb6980a).
2. Run `ls`.
3. Observed: the output appears as a flat stream with no block framing; no block is opened, none is frozen.
4. Expected: the command opens a block, the block freezes at the render fence where the output actually ended, and the exit status is shown on it.
acceptance_criteria: In a local enhanced session a command opens a block, the block freezes at the fence where the output ended, and the exit status is on it; the conventional (no-domain) session still shows one continuous unstructured grid with no blocks. Proven in the real UI, not only by a unit test.
close_reason: setUnstructured on every lifecycle change put the pane back into the conventional full-pane grid and hid the block for the whole command; DOM sampling in the real UI showed the block existing-but-hidden both during and after the run. Now gated on shellStateFromLifecycle() !== 'integrated', reusing the existing owner of that question rather than a second derivation; desynchronized falls out conventional per decision 9. Discriminating unit test (fails on old code) plus a lost/desync conventional-fallback test. Committed 858114ca.

title: After any command the editor disappears and never returns
description:
Reported by the owner against the dev app, after nocx-u7uh.22 fixed the readonly error: run any command in a local enhanced session and the editor disappears and never comes back. The terminal is left blank with a bare cursor and no input surface — marker-only prompt means there is no visible native prompt either, so the user has nothing.

## What has already been ruled out (coordinator, measured, not reasoned)

1. THE BACKEND IS CORRECT. A probe against the real composition root (App.New + real WebSocket + real local enhanced session, the same harness as TestLocalEnhancedSessionEstablishesThroughProductionWiring) writes `echo hi\n` as a properly framed data frame and observes exactly the right published sequence:

       {"lane":"...","lifecycle":"prompt_ready","domain":"dom-...","epoch":1}
       {"lifecycle":"running", attempt:{state:"open",   command:"echo hi", origin:"shell", id:"s-dom-...-0"}}
       {"lifecycle":"running", attempt:{state:"completed", exitCode:0, fence:"e5c7..."}}
       {"lane":"...","lifecycle":"prompt_ready","domain":"dom-...","epoch":1}

   The final prompt_ready is emitted, and `attempt` is correctly OMITTED (not null) on the prompt_ready facts, so applyFact's `fact.attempt !== undefined` guard does not reject it.

2. THE FRONTEND KERNEL IS CORRECT. Replaying those four facts verbatim through LifecycleKernel.applyFact gives prompt_ready -> running -> running -> prompt_ready, and shouldShowEditor(state) is true at the end.

So the defect is in the renderer/tab wiring between "the kernel says prompt_ready" and "the editor is on screen".

## Where to look, in order

`_syncLifecycleOwnership` (frontend/src/terminal-content.ts) computes:

    const show = shouldShowEditor(this.lifecycle.state) && this.lifecycle.buffer === 'normal' && !this.nativeMode

shouldShowEditor is proven true, so the suspects are the other two, plus everything downstream of `editor.show()`:

- `this.lifecycle.buffer` stuck somewhere other than 'normal'.
- `this.nativeMode` latched true (enterNativeMode is meant to be user-driven only).
- `_syncLifecycleOwnership` not running on the final transition, or `this.editor` null by then.
- The block/live-region path: EVERY command now emits a render fence (nocx-u7uh.8 carve-out), and the shell writes ESC]1337;NOCX_FENCE;<hex> after the output. The renderer reports the sighting at `line: buf.baseY + buf.cursorY`. If the block manager freezes or truncates the live region at that line, the live region can collapse to zero height — which is the ORIGINAL omp symptom this whole epic exists to fix, arriving this time from our own fence. Check this one seriously.

Reproduce in the real UI, not in a unit test: the unit layers are both already proven green while the product is broken, which is exactly the trap AGENTS.md testing rule 1 describes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the dev stack and open a local session (the owner sees it at 127.0.0.1:5180).
2. The editor is present at the bottom, as expected, at the first prompt.
3. Type any command and press Enter.
4. Observed: the editor disappears permanently; the terminal is blank with a cursor; no visible prompt and no input surface.
5. Expected: the command runs, its output stays visible, the block freezes, and the editor returns at the next prompt.
acceptance_criteria: In a local enhanced session, running a command leaves ALL of its output visible, freezes the completed block, and returns the editor at the next prompt. Proven end to end through the real UI (Playwright against the dev stack), not by a unit test on a layer that is already green. There is no window in which the prompt is suppressed and no editor is available.
close_reason: Root cause found by instrumenting the frontend and reading the browser console, per the owner. The editor hides itself at submit, so by the time the running fact landed editor.isVisible was already false and the 'else if (!show && editor.isVisible)' arm could never run — setReadOnly(false) never fired, the grid stayed read-only for the session, and xterm drops paste() and keystrokes while disableStdin is set. Writability now follows ownership (editor shown iff grid read-only), submit makes the grid writable synchronously, and paste() lifts disableStdin for its delivery. Committed 3fb6980a.

title: readonly __nocx_snapshot_wait_ms breaks every local enhanced session
description:
Reported by the owner against the dev app: the first thing a local enhanced session prints is

    bash: __nocx_snapshot_wait_ms: readonly variable

## Cause

The launcher rcfile deliberately re-sources nocx.bash. It sources the user's ~/.bashrc first (user startup wins), then unsets __nocx_loaded and the rest of the captured state so THIS session's authenticated copy installs over any installer-era one the user's rc already sourced (launcher_bash.go, the rewind block).

That re-source is by design. But nocx.bash declares `readonly __nocx_snapshot_wait_ms`, and a readonly variable can be neither unset nor re-declared, so the second pass errors on that line and prints into the user's terminal.

Locally it fires on EVERY session, because the app installs the gate line into ~/.bashrc itself (App.Start -> EnsureInstalled), so the user's rc has always already sourced an installed copy. The remote tier rarely showed it because a far host's rc usually carries no gate. nocx-u7uh.21 routed local enhanced sessions through the rcfile launcher for the first time, which is what exposed it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have the nocx gate line in ~/.bashrc (the app writes it on start).
2. Open a local enhanced session in the dev app.
3. Observed: `bash: __nocx_snapshot_wait_ms: readonly variable` is the first line in the terminal.
4. Expected: no output from the integration at all.

Minimal reproduction without the app:

    NOCX_SHELL_INTEGRATION=1 bash -c 'source "$HOME/.nocx/shell-integration.bash"; unset __nocx_loaded; source "$HOME/.nocx/shell-integration.bash"'

## Fix

Declare it once per shell rather than once per source: guard the readonly on the variable being unset. The value is identical on both passes, so keeping the first is not a compromise, and readonly still holds for the rest of the session.
acceptance_criteria: A local enhanced session whose ~/.bashrc already sources an installed nocx.bash prints nothing from the integration. Asserted by executing the rendered rcfile against a fixture HOME carrying the installer gate — not by reading the script.
close_reason: Declared once per shell rather than once per source; the rcfile's deliberate re-source over an installer-era install no longer errors. Regression test executes the rendered rcfile against a fixture HOME carrying the installer gate. Committed fca27773. Owner confirmed the error is gone.

title: TEMPORARY: the ci gate is off build-linux/build-macos for packaging iteration
description:
TEMPORARY, on branch fix/empty-prompt-and-linux-release only. build-linux
depends on the full ci.yml gate, so every attempt to fix the packaging step
costs ~15 minutes of backend/frontend/e2e before the build even starts, and the
Linux packaging path has needed several attempts in a row (nocx-xy9z, nocx-zvd7)
because no one had ever run it to completion.

The gate is dropped from build-linux and build-macos while that iteration
happens. It MUST be restored before this branch merges: ci.yml as a called
workflow is the entire reason a tag cannot produce a release from a red commit,
and a release workflow that merges without it looks identical to one that has
it.

Deliberately NOT done as a copy of the job in a throwaway workflow file: that
would mean iterating against a duplicate and proving nothing about the file
that actually builds the release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `needs: [ci, validate]` is back on both build jobs before merge.
- A full dry run of release.yml — gate included — is green on the merged commit
  BEFORE any tag is pushed. The fast runs prove the packaging step, never the
  release.
close_reason: Not done. Proposed dropping the ci gate from the build jobs to iterate faster on Linux packaging; the owner reconsidered within the minute and asked for it back. Nothing shipped: release.yml is byte-identical to the commit before the edit, both build jobs carry needs: [ci, validate], and no TEMPORARY marker survives. Recording it because the reasoning is the durable part — a release workflow that merges without its gate is indistinguishable from one that has it, so the cost of forgetting is unbounded while the saving is 15 minutes per attempt.

title: Enter on an empty prompt throws and hides the command editor for the rest of the session
description:
A user at an ordinary empty prompt presses Enter — the thing everyone does
to get a blank line — and the command editor disappears. It never comes back
for the rest of the session: there is no input-state transition to show it
again, so the pane is left with no prompt at all.

Root cause, from the CI trace of run 31219714125 (e2e/nocxify-journey.spec.ts):

  Error: command must not be empty
      at CommandLedger.open (command-ledger.ts:122)
      at Object.submit (terminal-content.ts)
      at CommandEditor.commit (editor.ts)
      at CommandEditor.submit (editor.ts)
      at CommandEditor.onKeydown (editor.ts)

CommandEditor.submit read the document with no empty guard. commit() is the
atomic handoff (ADR-0004 section 2) and clears + hides BEFORE calling
actions.submit, so by the time CommandLedger.open refused the empty string the
editor was already hidden. The throw escaped onKeydown as an unhandled page
error and nothing showed the editor again.

CommandLedger.open already owned the rule ("command must not be empty") but it
sits downstream of the hide, which is the half that cannot be undone.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a tab and let a command finish so the editor is visible and empty.
2. Press Enter without typing anything.

Observed: the prompt vanishes; the pane accepts no further input through the
editor for the rest of the session. An unhandled "command must not be empty"
is on the console.
Expected: nothing happens, and the prompt is still there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Enter on an empty draft performs no submit and leaves the editor visible and
  usable — asserted at BOTH ends, not just "no submit".
- Whitespace alone is treated the same: it would otherwise open a block for a
  command nobody typed. A LEADING space (` ls`) is still a real command and is
  sent byte-for-byte — only the decision trims, never the payload.
- e2e/nocxify-journey.spec.ts is green on CI.
close_reason: Fixed on main (9d4a7f4). CommandEditor.submit refuses an empty or whitespace-only draft before commit() can clear and hide. Two tests assert both ends — no submit AND the prompt survives and still works; the first reproduced the defect exactly (submit called with "") before the fix. Verified: 2498/2498 frontend, 138/138 e2e in the container, and the CI e2e job green on the merged commit ec3e2a7. The e2e half (nocxify-journey's four raw keyboard sites now route through submitInEditor) landed in the same commit.

title: The Git panel pays a shell-environment timeout on every open
description:
The owner reports the Git panel takes ~6 seconds to refresh, and that answering
"this directory is not a repository" — an elementary check — is slow too.

git is not the cost. Measured on the owner's own repository, the one with 761
untracked files under graphify-out:

    git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 -z --untracked-files=all
        real 0m0.011s
    git rev-parse --show-toplevel --absolute-git-dir
        real 0m0.002s

The cost is `Factory.Open` (internal/git/local/factory.go:77), which resolves
the shell environment FIRST — before probing git and before rev-parse:

    env, envState, envReason = f.env.resolve(ctx)   // up to envTimeout
    ...
    gitPath, version, err := f.probe.probe(ctx, env)
    toplevel, gitDir, err := revParse(ctx, gitPath, env, cwd)

`resolve` runs `shell -i -c "export -p"` with a 5 s default timeout
(internal/git/local/shellenv.go). On the owner's machine it TIMES OUT — the
panel shows "Hooks will run in a degraded environment: context deadline
exceeded", which is that deadline. And `envCache.resolve` deliberately does not
cache a failure ("a transient failure degrades one open and the next retries
instead of poisoning the panel forever"), so the full timeout is paid on EVERY
open rather than once.

So both symptoms are one defect: a probe that only the commit path needs is on
the critical path of every open, and its failure is never remembered.

The environment exists for D6 — git's subprocesses, notably the pre-commit
hook, must not run with a GUI app's bare launchd PATH. status, diff and log do
not need it; they need a PATH that finds git, which the probe already
establishes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a shell whose interactive startup takes longer than 5 s, or otherwise
   makes `$SHELL -i -c 'export -p'` not finish (the owner's does).
2. Open the Git panel on any directory, repository or not.

Observed: several seconds before the panel says anything, every time, including
for a directory that is not a repository at all.
Expected: the repository answer arrives in the tens of milliseconds git takes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test that fails without the fix: with an environment probe that never
  returns, `Open` still answers `OpenNotARepository` for a non-repository, and
  `OpenOK` for a repository, within a bound far below the probe's timeout.
- A test that a FAILED environment resolution is not re-attempted on every
  open — N opens against a failing probe cost about one timeout, not N.
- The D6 degraded-environment warning is still visible in the product before a
  commit; a soft degrade that only shows in a log is the failure D6 exists to
  prevent.
- The commit path still runs with the resolved environment when one is
  obtainable.
close_reason: Fixed in 47bbf45: env resolution off Open's critical path (background prewarm from construction, cancellable at shutdown), remembered failures with a 30s cooldown, commit joins the shared attempt. Tests: Open answers fast vs a never-returning probe, N opens cost one attempt, commit runs with the resolved env. Full gate green (container go test + vitest).

title: nothing gates main: hooks uninstalled, CI only on pull_request, merges skip pre-commit
description:
Two red CI classes reached main today. The defects are tracked separately (nocx-koki,
nocx-d4lh); this bead is the reason nothing caught them.

DECISION (owner, 2026-08-06): CI triggers stay as they are — pull requests and releases
only. No `push: [main]` trigger. That makes the local gate, and the discipline of opening
a PR, the things that have to work.

1. The repo hook is not installed in this clone. `git config core.hooksPath` is unset
   (exit 1), so .githooks/pre-commit — the whole local gate — has never run here.
   .git/hooks/ holds only beads' hooks. Makefile:81 does the wiring; `make hooks` was
   never run. AGENTS.md already names this risk: "`make hooks` is a per-clone step a
   fresh checkout may skip".

2. frontend/node_modules does not exist in this clone, so the frontend half of the gate
   could not have run even with the hook installed: .githooks/pre-commit:33 warns and
   carries on, and Makefile:104 fails the target outright. Both red frontend findings
   were therefore unreachable locally.

3. A clean automatic `git merge` runs pre-merge-commit, not pre-commit, and .githooks/
   has no pre-merge-commit. (A conflicted merge finished with `git commit` does run
   pre-commit, so the gap is narrower than it first looks — but it is real, and it is
   exactly where two independently-green branches produce a red result.) main was
   advanced by five such merges today: 871c3ec, b39a71d, 2889906, 3ef25b3, e994278.

Related, larger, filed separately: the local gate runs Go tests in a Linux container
while the product is macOS-first, which is structurally blind to everything nocx-koki
is made of.

## Steps to Reproduce

    git config core.hooksPath          # empty, exit 1
    ls frontend/node_modules           # absent
    ls .githooks/                      # no pre-merge-commit

## Acceptance Criteria

- .githooks/pre-merge-commit exists and runs the same gate as pre-commit.
- core.hooksPath is set in this clone (`make hooks`).
- frontend/node_modules is installed, so the frontend gate can run at all.
- A merge of two branches that are individually green, but red together, is stopped
  locally rather than discovered by a hand-dispatched CI run.
close_reason: Closed

title: zsh has no command-existence snapshot, so completion never learns any command on macOS
description:
## Summary

internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.zsh implements OSC 133 markers, OSC 7 cwd and the OSC 636;P readiness passport. It does NOT implement the command-existence snapshot: grep for 636;S, 636;H or the word snapshot in that file returns zero. nocx.bash has all of it (the hello at line 456, the snapshot at 436).

The snapshot is the only source the frontend has for which commands exist — command-snapshot.ts is explicit that the frontend cannot know a shell's aliases, functions, builtins and PATH, so it asks the shell. Without a hello there is never a nonce, so every snapshot would be discarded even if one arrived, and the dropdown reports the honest thing forever: 'Command names are still loading — press Tab again in a moment' (suggest/controller.ts:780).

macOS's default login shell is zsh, and macOS is the target platform of this MVP. So on the shipping platform, tab completion never learns a single command name.

Distinct from nocx-0ije, which is about the bash script's first-prompt timing on CI runners. This is not timing: the code does not exist.

## Steps to Reproduce

Verified both directions today.

Red, macOS + zsh (my machine, SHELL=/bin/zsh):
  PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/headless-run.sh e2e/completion.spec.ts
  -> 4 failed. completion.spec.ts:139 fails with Received string: 'still-loading' after the spec's own 20s poll; the spec is written to retry precisely because the snapshot is expected to arrive late, and it never arrives at all.

Green, Linux + bash (container):
  PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/completion.spec.ts
  -> 8 passed.

Same in CI on macos-latest: run 31116081576 fails completion.spec.ts:139 and :217 on both chromium and webkit.

That split is also why nobody saw it: the sanctioned local loop is the container, which is bash.

## Acceptance Criteria

- nocx.zsh emits the session hello and the command snapshot, under the same nonce rules nocx.bash uses and the same forgery defence (the hello before the first prompt).
- completion.spec.ts passes on a macOS host whose login shell is zsh, not only in the bash container.
- The paired assertion AGENTS.md asks for: a test that the snapshot IS obtainable on an ordinary zsh machine, not only tests for the ways it can fail.
- Whatever is done here does not repeat nocx-0ije: that bead records a change to these scripts that passed everywhere available locally and broke the macOS runner, and had to be reverted.
notes:
2026-08-12, implemented on branch worktree-agent-a67ea18675eeb5540 (commit 2a1a66e, not pushed).

nocx.zsh now emits the OSC 636 hello at source time and the snapshot from the
first prompt, under the bash tier's protocol unchanged — same nonce rules, same
once-per-shell latch on $$, same hex escaping, same 8192/65536 caps. Script
version bumped to 37, without which no installed ~/.nocx copy is ever rewritten.

Criterion 1 (hello + snapshot under the same nonce rules and forgery defence):
done, eleven exec/pty tests against a real zsh in scripts_exec_test.go, including
the paired 'and on an ordinary machine it succeeds' — a real interactive zsh on
a pty emitting H then S before the first prompt is usable.

Criterion 3 (the paired assertion AGENTS.md asks for): done, same test.

Criterion 2 (completion.spec.ts on a macOS host whose login shell is zsh) is NOT
checkable today and is carried forward to nocx-wwz0 rather than dropped. Every
enhanced local session runs bash: app.go's localPTYFactory pins
cfg.Command = 'bash' with the transient --rcfile, and the lifecycle kernel is
always wired, so the fallback that would resolve $SHELL is unreachable. The
macOS e2e red this bead recorded was therefore the BASH tier's nocx-cbtc
double-hello (fixed by script v33, whose own comment names it 'the bash twin of
nocx-qduc'). The zsh tier reaches a user through remote zsh hosts today, and
through the local session once nocx-wwz0 lands — which is the bead this one was
blocking, and which now owns the e2e check.

Filed while here: nocx-m02z, nocx-g15o, nocx-y2dl, nocx-yqg0.
close_reason: nocx.zsh emits the hello and the command snapshot under the bash tier's protocol; eleven tests drive a real zsh, script version bumped to 37. The e2e criterion is carried forward to nocx-wwz0 in the notes.

title: devharness specs drive the wrong backend: wails/ipc.js overwrites the injected window.go
description:
## Summary

CORRECTION: filed first as 'WebKit only'. It is not. Shard 3 happened to hold the webkit copies; run 31116081576 shard 2 shows the SAME seven specs failing on chromium. The browser is irrelevant.

Seven specs start their own backend via cmd/devharness and repoint the page at it by stubbing window.go through addInitScript (vault.spec.ts bindEndpoint, tabby-import.spec.ts injectWailsBindings, and the same block copied into connection-password, prompt-vault, vault-settings, history-persistence, recall-search).

Under `wails dev` that stub never survives. The HTML wails serves carries, in this order:

  <script src="/wails/ipc.js">        <- classic
  <script src="/wails/runtime.js">    <- classic
  <script type="module" src="/@vite/client">
  <script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx">

Playwright's init script runs first, then the two CLASSIC wails scripts run — before any deferred module — and install the real window.go. wailsjs/go/main/WailsApp.js reads window['go'] at CALL time, so by the time main.tsx:82 calls GetWSPort() the stub is gone and the app connects to the wails dev backend on 34115.

Evidence, run 31115207733 shard 3:
- devharness-19876.log (vault spec's backend) records startup and NOTHING else. No client ever connected.
- The failure snapshot shows the terminal tab cwd as '.e2e/home' — the wails backend's isolated home — not the spec's mkdtemp under nocx-vault-9fuv0I/home.
- The trace's console has no 'nocx: no Wails runtime' warning, so GetWSPort resolved; it resolved to the wrong backend.

So these specs assert vault setup, imports and password prompts against a backend that already has state and is shared with every other spec — the dialogs they wait for never appear.

Why nobody saw it locally: the headless path (cmd/devharness + vite, NOCX_WS_PORT set) serves index.html with no wails scripts at all, so there is nothing to overwrite the stub and the injection works. That is the path e2e/run-in-container.sh takes and the one AGENTS.md tells everyone to use. These specs could only ever pass there and could never pass under `wails dev` — and until nocx-azxe.2 made CI build devharness, CI never ran them, so the contradiction had nowhere to surface.

## Steps to Reproduce

Any CI e2e job on release/v0.1.0, e.g. run 31116081576: shard 2 fails connection-password, prompt-vault, tabby-import, vault-settings x2, vault x2 on [chromium]; shard 3 fails the same seven on [webkit].

## Acceptance Criteria

- A devharness spec provably drives its own backend under `wails dev`: assert it, do not assume — e.g. the spec fails loudly if the WS port in use is not the one it started.
- The seven specs pass in CI on both browsers.
- One owner for the injection. There are six near-identical copies of the stub across e2e/; whatever the fix is, it lives in harness.ts and the specs call it (AGENTS.md: 'look for the existing answer before you write a second one').
design:
Fix direction, after the owner asked why anything is being substituted at all.

There are two paths and the substitution is correct in exactly one:

- HEADLESS (cmd/devharness + vite, NOCX_WS_PORT set): there is no wails runtime, so window.go does not exist. The stub is the only way the app learns its port and token. Legitimate, and it is what e2e/base-url.ts calls the headless path.
- wails dev: the real bindings are present and wails installs them itself. Per wails discussion #4205 this is the sanctioned e2e arrangement — point Playwright at :34115 and drive the real bindings. Overriding them here is wrong by construction, not merely fragile.

harness.ts already encodes that rule: injectWailsShim returns early when NOCX_WS_PORT is unset, and its comment says so — 'under wails dev the real binding is present, so this is a no-op'. The six copies inside the specs dropped the guard and fire unconditionally. Two answers to one question; the guarded one is right (AGENTS.md, 'look for the existing answer before you write a second one').

Why these specs substitute at all: they need a backend they can STOP AND RESTART mid-test with a fresh token — vault persistence across restart is the whole point of several of them. wails dev gives exactly one backend whose lifecycle Playwright does not own. So the real requirement was never 'override the bindings'; it was 'run on the headless path'.

Hence the fix is a run-arrangement change, not a race to be won. CI today builds devharness and then runs the entire suite through wails dev with NOCX_WS_PORT unset, so those specs start a backend nobody ever talks to. Run them as their own Playwright project or job with NOCX_WS_PORT set, and make them REFUSE to run when it is not — a spec that silently drives a different backend than the one it started is the failure this bug is.
acceptance_criteria:
- The nine devharness specs run on the headless path (NOCX_WS_PORT set), not under wails dev.
- Each one fails loudly rather than silently driving the shared backend when that precondition is absent — assert the WS port in use is the one the spec started.
- One owner for the shim: harness.ts. The six copied blocks in vault, tabby-import, connection-password, prompt-vault, vault-settings, history-persistence and recall-search go.
- Under wails dev the suite uses the real wails bindings and overrides nothing.
- All nine pass in CI on both browsers.
close_reason: Closed

title: frontend lint/typecheck need @types/node, which npm ci never installed
description:
## Summary

tsconfig.test.json declares `"types": ["node"]` and the vitest files import node:fs/node:path/node:url, so the test program now REQUIRES @types/node to be present. Nothing declared it. frontend/package-lock.json had no top-level entry — @types/node is only an OPTIONAL peer of vite and vitest, which npm ci does not install.

Local checkouts had it anyway (a leftover in frontend/node_modules from an earlier npm install, plus the repo root's own @types/node one directory up), so eslint resolved the types and lint was green. CI runs npm ci, which wipes node_modules and installs the lockfile exactly, and its frontend job installs the root only AFTER lint — so in CI the types resolved nowhere, every node: import became an error type, and typescript-eslint's no-unsafe-* rules produced 112 errors.

Run 31115207733, frontend job: environment-passport.test.ts, ports-layout.test.tsx, ssh-transition.test.ts and others.

## Steps to Reproduce

git archive HEAD | tar -x -C /tmp/x && cd /tmp/x/frontend && npm ci && npm run lint
-> 112 errors, and ls node_modules/@types/node is absent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- frontend/package.json declares @types/node as a devDependency and package-lock.json carries the top-level entry.
- In a pristine checkout with no root node_modules, cd frontend && npm ci && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build all pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Terminal cwd and Files root are two sources of truth; the panel must follow the terminal
description: The terminal and the Files panel disagree about the current directory. `cd /`in a tab leaves the panel rooted where it was when the tab was first shown.The owner: the current directory must have ONE source, and the terminal ownsit (OSC 7).This reverses Rule 1 at the top of frontend/src/files/files-store.ts ("ROOTCOMES FROM files.open AND DOES NOT MOVE"), deliberately, at the owner"sdirection. The rule is now: a verified OSC 7 cwd change on the active sessionre-roots the panel.## Steps to Reproduce1. Open an ssh tab; the panel roots at the session"s cwd.2. `cd /` in the terminal. The tab title follows; the panel does not.Three layers are involved: TerminalContent.activeOrigin() already reads thelive _cwd, main.tsx only re-reads it on tab change, and rescope() ignores acwd change on the same session by design. The viewer tab"s activeOrigin() is aFROZEN snapshot (file-viewer-content.tsx), which a cwd-sensitive rescope wouldfight.## Acceptance Criteria- `cd` to another directory in the active tab re-roots the panel, with no  click and no tab switch.- Switching to a file-viewer tab does NOT move the panel"s root.- A session with no OSC 7 (no shell integration) does not thrash, and the  header says the root is not following the terminal.- An unverified cwd never silently re-roots (AD-5).- One e2e: cd in the terminal, the tree shows the new directory"s entries.
notes:
CORRECTION (owner, same session). The AD-5 note below is WRONG and is
withdrawn. AD-5 (architecture.md:138) binds CWD — "cwd falls back to \$HOME,
surfaced not applied silently". It reached the Files panel only because the
OLD design DERIVED the root from cwd, so an unverifiable cwd caused a $HOME
substitution. With the root a constant /, nothing is derived and nothing is
substituted, so the rule has nothing to bite on.

Consequence: NO "not following cwd" indicator is required, and none should be
built. If the cwd is unknown the panel shows / and highlights nothing — that
is the whole behaviour, not a degrade to announce.

The only real residue: until the root becomes /, files.open still passes the
verified cwd as rootPath and the provider still falls back to \$HOME, and
since bd4e84c removed the (inferred) label that fallback is momentarily
silent. It disappears with the root change; no separate work.
close_reason: Root pinned to /, cd reveals via revealPath; onActiveOriginChange seam; spec amended; e2e acceptance green. Landed b47a1f7

title: Generate the release signing keypair, compile the public half in, and prove CI signs with its mate
description: Depends on nocx-nfu5.1 landing a compiled-in keyring. The keypair is generated once with cmd/manifest-sign -keygen: the seed becomes the RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY repository secret and a backup outside GitHub (the design is explicit that losing it with no successor in a shipped keyring strands every install), the public key goes into the compiled keyring. The failure this must foreclose is the one nobody notices until a user cannot update: CI signing with a seed whose public half is not in the artefact's keyring. A signature that is only ever verified by the key that made it proves nothing, so the release workflow verifies the freshly signed manifest against the compiled-in keyring before it publishes.
acceptance_criteria: gh secret list shows RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY; the release workflow verifies manifest.json.sig against the keyring compiled into the build it is publishing, and fails the publish if it does not validate.
close_reason: Acceptance met and now actually demonstrated. gh secret list shows RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY (2026-08-06); the keyring is compiled in (internal/update/keyring.go, wired at main.go:123). The second half of the criterion — the workflow verifies the signature against the keyring the build ships — could not run until nocx-94kl moved it out of the tag-gated job. It ran in dry run 31246707047 and passed. The pair is confirmed, not presumed.

title: Go acceptance tests isolate only through XDG, so on macOS they write the runner's real profile
description: internal/app/history_acceptance_test.go:36 and internal/app/capture_acceptance_test.go:25 isolate the app directories by setting XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME. internal/storage/paths.go:91 resolves darwin from os.UserHomeDir(), so on macOS all three variables are inert and the app under test reads and writes ~/Library/Application Support/nocx-dev. CI run 31083388224 shows it: the backend logs to /Users/runner/Library/Application Support/nocx-dev/nocx.log, the salt is never minted where the test looks, and the second test to run finds 'database exists but its key is gone'. The three tests pass on Linux, which is why this survived. Same class as nocx-ti8w, one layer down: that one isolated the e2e backend, this one leaves the Go suite unisolated. Fix in one place - the knowledge of which variables govern the app dirs on each OS belongs with the code that reads them, not copied into each test.
acceptance_criteria: A helper owned by internal/storage isolates the app directories on both linux and darwin; its own test asserts the resolved config, data and cache dirs all fall inside the temp root. The three internal/app acceptance tests use it, and the backend job on macOS is green.
close_reason: Fix is on main and the gate that would catch a regression is green on ec3e2a7 (run 31246707047: backend, backend-linux x2, frontend, e2e all pass). Fixed by 4c72b82 — a test cannot reach a real profile by forgetting to isolate.

title: Ship v0.1.0: the first published release, built by CI for macOS and Linux
description:
The pipeline already exists and is committed on main (.github/workflows/release.yml): tag v* -> ci.yml gate -> macOS universal (.dmg + .zip) -> Linux AppImage -> signed manifest + gh release create. Nothing needs designing; three things block it from ever completing.

1. CI is red on main, and release.yml calls ci.yml as a hard gate, so no tag can build. Run 31083388224 (workflow_dispatch on main) failed backend-linux in both matrix variants, and the e2e job is cancelled at its 20-minute cap - that one is nocx-qth1, whose cause is playwright.config.ts:85 defaulting to a single worker for 109 tests.
2. The repository has no RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY secret (gh secret list is empty), so the publish job would fail at the signing step.
3. nocx-nfu5.1: main.go:118 passes Keyring:nil with a comment claiming the release pipeline fills it via ldflags. Nothing does, and VerifyManifest rejects an empty keyring, so a shipped build can publish a release it can never verify an update from. The keypair must therefore be generated once, before the artefact is built, so the public half is compiled in and the private half is the CI secret.

Blocked in practice by nocx-qth1 and nocx-nfu5.1; bd refuses a task->epic blocks edge, so they are named here rather than as edges.
acceptance_criteria: A person can open the GitHub Releases page for nocx, download a .dmg (macOS) or .AppImage (Linux) built by CI from tag v0.1.0, install it, and launch it — and the published manifest.json verifies against the keyring compiled into that same artefact. Deliberately out: notarization, a Developer ID, Windows, and any package-manager channel.

title: Opening a saved connection with no credential dies instead of asking for the password
description:
Saving a host from an ssh block (nocx-pu4.7) creates a profile with a host and a user and nothing to authenticate with. Opening it fails with 'ssh connect: nothing to authenticate pi@192.168.0.93 with: no key, no password and no reachable agent' — an accurate error and a dead end: nocx never asks, and never offers to remember.

The mechanism already exists and must be extended rather than duplicated: transport.UnlockRequester lets backend code ask a renderer for the vault passphrase and blocks for the answer, behind an interface wired at the composition root, rendered by frontend/src/prompt-vault.ts. A connection password is a DIFFERENT secret from the vault passphrase, so the surface is reused and the meaning is not — nocx-s8jn already requires every password prompt to name which password it wants.

## Acceptance Criteria
When a connection has no usable credential, or the server asks for a password or keyboard-interactive and nothing is stored, the connect path raises the same prompt surface the vault uses, naming this connection and that it is the host's password — never the vault's. The entered secret authenticates that connection. The prompt offers to remember it, and on accept it becomes a vault secret the profile references (ADR-0017), so the next open does not ask. Declining uses it once and stores nothing. Cancelling fails the connection with the reason the user chose, not with ErrNoAuthMethod. No client connected, a sealed vault and a cancelled prompt are three distinct outcomes with three distinct messages. Assert it end to end against cmd/e2e-sshd with a password-only host: first open prompts and connects, and after 'remember' the second open does not prompt.
close_reason: Landed as 99762f6: prompt rung in the auth ladder (tabby's shape), vault-surface prompt naming the connection and account, remember stores a referenced secret; e2e found and fixed a dropped requester and a read-loop deadlock

title: The nocxify path logs nothing: a real session leaves no evidence of what it decided
description:
A real ssh session on 2026-08-05 wrote an installed fact for pi@192.168.0.93:22 at 19:17:23 — so the planner chose a mode, the oracle answered, the launcher published generation v11 and a passport was accepted — while the backend log for that window contains exactly three lines: application initialized, ws server started, session opened. Nothing about shell.launcherCommand, the oracle verdict, the chosen mode, the minted environment id, the publish, the observation or the fact write.

Diagnosing the P0 (nocx-rojg) came down to reading a JSON file's mtime because there was nothing else. AGENTS.md requires structured logging through the logging interface; this path has none.

Two halves, and the second is why nobody noticed the first: app.go:150 builds the slog handler over os.Stderr only, so where the log lands is whatever the launcher redirected — on this machine a temp dir nobody would think to look in.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run a hand-typed ssh against a real host, then read the backend log: nothing describes what happened.

## Acceptance Criteria
Every decision on the delivery path logs once, at INFO, with the fields that make it diagnosable: the launcherCommand call with destination identity and minted environment id, the oracle verdict including a refusal reason, the chosen mode (raw/bootstrap/installed) and why, the publish result with generation, the observation with its status (accepted/unexpected/ignored/none) and the fact write or invalidation. A refusal logs the reason as a value, never as prose. No secrets, no full payloads, no user command text beyond the destination. Plus: the log has a stable file location the product can name, and a running session can say where it is.
close_reason: Landed as b38ca29: every delivery decision logs once at INFO with typed refusal reasons; the log also lands in the app data dir (dev/release split respected) and the session can say where it is

title: After a successful ssh entry there is no input surface at all: no editor, and the remote prompt is invisible
description:
input-state.ts treats the remote shell's first A as a resync because it interrupts RUNNING_RAW: 'trusted: m.state !== RUNNING_RAW'. After submit the machine IS in RUNNING_RAW, so the first remote A is untrusted, the following B grants no DOM ownership, and the editor never appears. The remote shell is in marker-only mode and prints no prompt of its own, so the user is left with nothing to type into — the invisible prompt ADR-0006 and ADR-0004 s1 exist to prevent.

Evidence from a real session (2026-08-05 19:17): the installed fact for pi@192.168.0.93:22 was written with generation v11, which only happens from an ACCEPTED passport — so the launcher ran, published and was believed; the model entered the environment and the input machine did not follow.

Codex predicted this exact failure during the design review ('the first remote A arrives while the input machine is in RUNNING_RAW; such an A is deliberately untrusted and the following B does not grant DOM ownership - a confirmed environment transition must start a new clean A->B cycle') and the coordinator did not carry it into the P9 brief.

## Steps to Reproduce
Type ssh user@host by hand in an integrated local tab, authenticate successfully, and try to run a command on the remote host: there is no editor and no visible prompt.

## Acceptance Criteria
A confirmed environment transition (expected passport accepted) starts a clean cycle in the input machine, so the remote's following A is trusted and its B grants ownership; the editor is usable on the remote host immediately after entry. Fail-open is asserted too: when no passport arrives, input stays native and a VISIBLE prompt is proven — never zero input surfaces. The test drives it the way a user does, from submit through entry to typing a command that reaches the remote pty.
close_reason: Landed as bb6b508: an accepted passport is now an input event that starts a clean cycle, so the remote's tagged A is trusted and its B grants ownership; the RUNNING_RAW protection against nested/orphan prompts is untouched; both directions proven at user level

title: Typing ssh and pressing Tab inserts a saved host instead of offering the history
description:
The ssh-context test in editor.ts is /\\bssh\\s+/ — it requires whitespace AFTER ssh, so with the caret right after 'ssh' the alias hint list still opens and its single saved host is inserted whole ('ssh root@192.168.0.57'), even though history holds ten 'ssh pi@192.168.0.93' entries. The same derivation is used by acceptHint. Regression from 2d0e0e4, which suppressed the hint list under ssh but only once a space had been typed — and Tab is what a user presses instead of the space.

## Steps to Reproduce
With at least one saved connection and several ssh lines in history, type 'ssh' (no trailing space) and press Tab: the prompt becomes 'ssh root@192.168.0.57' with no chance to choose, and the history rows never appear.

## Acceptance Criteria
A document whose command word is ssh counts as an ssh context whether or not a space has been typed yet, so the alias hint list does not open there. Tab in that state opens the completion dropdown; nothing is inserted by the keypress itself; the history rows starting with 'ssh' are among the candidates. Tests drive Tab from that exact document state and assert both the absence of an insertion and the presence of history rows.
close_reason: Landed as 817d6de: the alias hint surface is deleted rather than re-gated; one derivation of 'am I in an ssh context' remains (commandWord); regression test drives Tab from the document 'ssh' and asserts the dropdown opens, nothing is inserted, and history rows are present

title: Spike: can a hand-typed ssh carry a second channel, so the payload never rides argv
description: If this holds, the visible line is short from the FIRST connection with no remote footprint, which removes most of the reason for a persistent install. See .internal/briefs/nocx-mlm7-spike-multiplex.md
acceptance_criteria: A measured answer, not an argument: whether -o ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPath=... on a hand-typed ssh yields a master a second local process can use for SFTP with no re-authentication; how long from submit until that master is usable; how long a 35 KB push takes; and what the remote bootstrap must wait for and how often it would time out. Written up with the numbers and the commands that produced them, plus a recommendation. Throwaway harness only — no production code.
close_reason: Measured and decided: ADR-0022 keeps argv as the carrier. Multiplexing works (20/20, zero extra auth, <12ms wait) but shortens the line only 190->158 bytes, so it buys three preconditions and a race for thirty bytes. Report at .internal/reports/nocx-mlm7-spike-multiplex.md; kept for the relay

title: nocxify for a hand-typed ssh rides the ssh command, not a shell we type into afterwards
description:
The owner, 2026-08-04, after four rounds on this: 'может сделать как в warp?' — with the decisive screenshots.

Warp's transcript shows the `ssh` command as one block ending at 45.4s, then a NEW block labelled `pi@raspberrypi:~ (0.441s)` whose body is the Debian MOTD. sshd prints the MOTD before the login shell starts, so markers were already flowing when it printed. Typing a bootstrap after the remote prompt cannot produce that, because there was no prompt yet. The integration rode the ssh invocation.

That also settles a safety problem we could not otherwise solve. In-band delivery after submit lands in whatever is reading stdin, and between `ssh host` and the remote prompt that is `password:`, a 2FA challenge or a host-key confirmation — the wrapper would be sent as the secret, to the remote and into its auth log. There is no marker that says the far shell is ready, because the far shell is precisely the one that emits none. So there is no safe moment, and the whole 'offer then type' family is a dead end for this case (nocx-atyf.3, withdrawn).

## The mechanism, which is already in the repo

internal/shellintegration.RemoteLauncher.StartCommand returns the remote start command, and launcher_auto.go's dispatcher is a single line that picks bash, zsh or POSIX on the far side without us knowing which is there. That is what the MANAGED ssh path already sends. For a hand-typed line we own the text before it goes out, so we can send the same thing:

    ssh <flags> <dest>            ->   ssh -t <flags> <dest> '<launcher>'

`-t` is required: a remote command otherwise gets no pty.

The record/send split also already exists — submit distinguishes plan.recordLine from what reaches sendDoc — so the user's own line stays in the history and the block header while the wire carries the expanded one.

## What must not be assumed

ADR-0015 and nocx-difd: `ssh -G` reports a RemoteCommand the host's own config sets, and our rewrite would be refused there. Ask the oracle, do not guess, and fall back to the original line. Fail-open is the invariant: anything uncertain about the rewrite means send exactly what the user typed.
acceptance_criteria: Typing `ssh user@host` in an integrated local tab and pressing Enter yields command blocks on the REMOTE host from its first prompt, with no dialog, no chip and no second action. The history entry and the block header show the line the USER typed, never the rewritten one. Nothing is ever typed into the session after submit — proven by a test that asserts no write to the pty between submit and the remote's first marker. With a host whose ssh config would refuse a remote command (ssh -G RemoteCommand, ADR-0015/nocx-difd), the original line is sent unchanged and the session is an ordinary terminal. Policy off sends the original line. One end-to-end check against a real bash on a real PTY watches the whole arc.
close_reason:
The payload no longer crosses the tty. The backend stages the 35243-byte auto
dispatcher in a 0600 file under ~/.nocx/run and shell.launcherCommand returns
its PATH; the renderer types

  if [ -s 'P' ]; then ssh -t <flags> <dest> "$(cat 'P')"; else <what the user typed>; fi

so the LOCAL shell reads the file and hands the bytes to ssh through argv
(ARG_MAX), not through the line discipline (MAX_CANON). 273 bytes cross the
terminal instead of 35291, and buildRewrite refuses above 4095 outright.

Acceptance, item by item: markers on the remote from its first prompt with no
dialog and no second action — proven end to end by a real interactive bash on a
real pty with only ssh stubbed, behaving as sshd does (last argument is the
remote command, exec'd as the login shell with argv[0] set). The launcher
arrives byte-identical and OSC 133 A and B follow. Fed the old inline line, that
test fails. History and block header still show the user's line (recordLine
unchanged). Nothing typed after submit — the safety-property test still asserts
exactly one paste. RemoteCommand hosts, policy off, -T, an RPC failure and a
stage failure all send the original unchanged; stage-failed is a new refusal the
inline version had no need for.

Two findings that were not in the brief:

1. The reopening's second defect does not exist. $0 is not expanded by the local
shell and never was — shellQuote already wrapped the whole launcher. Measured on
the real 35243-byte payload under bash 5.3 and /bin/sh; argv came back identical
with the literal "$0" intact. Recorded in a comment on this bead.
