Prompt fixed so a budget-cut bundle no longer returns suspect for a budget reason, without opening a route to a false clear. 135 tests, contracts:check clean.

title: Task 3: a table for checks
description:
skill_checks in content.db, SkillCheckRepository on ContentDB, the stub arm, and the 16 to 17 schema rung.

Full task text: .internal/plans/2026-09-05-the-skill-viewer.md, Task 3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A check written and read back is equal field for field, with empty lists as [] not nil.
- Get for an unknown name returns found=false and a nil error.
- A second Put replaces the first; Delete on an absent name is not an error.
- The stub returns ErrNotImplemented from Put and found=false with no error from Get.
- The schema parity test passes with the new rung's digest.
close_reason: Completed: commit 5c6043b8 (four review rounds). skill_checks table in content.db, SkillCheckRepository on ContentDB via a skillCheckSqlite wrapper (APIRunRepository already owns Get(ctx,int64)/Delete(ctx,int64) on the shared receiver and Go has no overloading), stub arm, rung 16->17. Review verified independently rather than on report: the rung digest is a genuine sha256(schemaV1), the two DDL copies are byte-identical, nil<->[] normalisation is symmetric, no new file-creating DB path. One Critical was caught and fixed — the bump left schema 16 unpinned in schemaShapeDigests, so content.Open refused every database the previous build wrote and app.go:811 fell back to the stub; 16's shape was pinned from a database built by 882f34b5's schemaV1 and verified byte-for-byte by the reviewer rebuilding it. Then closed as a CLASS: validateLadderForSchema now refuses any ladder step dethroning an unpinned version, on every Open including a fresh install, proven by deleting the gate and watching only its own negative test fail while the two adjusted tests stayed green. testdata/schema_v16.sql frozen. Full ./internal/content green.

title: Task 5: skills.check
description:
A new wire method that reads the stored check and says whether it still fits, spending nothing.

Full task text: .internal/plans/2026-09-05-the-skill-viewer.md, Task 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No stored check answers checked=false — a result, not an error.
- A stored one answers checked=true with the whole check and current=true when the digest matches.
- After an edit, current=false and the check is still returned unchanged.
- A builtin answers checked=false; a stub store answers checked=false with no error.
- The over-the-wire payload validates against the contract.
close_reason: Completed: commit 1ed6d457 (one review round). skills.check returns the stored check and whether it still fits, spending nothing — reviewer verified in code that no path reaches a model, that all three no-check paths return a result rather than an error, and that both generators are consistent (gen-contracts and gen-openrpc --check both exit 0). A stale check comes back WHOLE with only current false, now asserted by reflect.DeepEqual rather than one field, and the checked/current:false shape is validated off the real socket. Dead-exports ratchet closed HERE rather than deferred: SkillsClient.check landed with it and the baseline SHRANK, verified independently — the skills.check entry is gone and the file went 762->757 lines. The plan's claim that registration belongs in app.go was wrong; it belongs in ws_config_handlers.go beside skills.audit, and the implementer was right to put it there.

title: Task 4: the audit stores what it concluded
description:
Persist the check after the model answers, re-verifying identity first; carry stored/storedError on the wire; refuse a builtin.

Full task text: .internal/plans/2026-09-05-the-skill-viewer.md, Task 4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A successful audit writes a SkillCheck whose digest is material.Digest.
- No lock is held across the model call.
- If the recomputed digest differs, nothing is written and stored=no names the change.
- A store failure still returns the report with stored=no and a reason.
- A builtin is refused before any model is resolved.
- A toggle taken during a check survives it; two checks of different skills both survive.
close_reason: Completed: commit 53d34dd0 (two review rounds). skills.audit now persists the check to content.db keyed by material.Digest, re-verifying the digest after the model answers so a check finishing after an edit, delete or reinstall is discarded rather than filed against bytes nobody has; stored/storedError carry a failed write so the report still reaches the person; builtin refused in the backend before the role is resolved. No lock is held across the model call and the guard for it is now falsifiable — the prior version wrote a skill's default value and could not fail; it now flips an installed skill ON inside beforeReturn and reads it back over a real skills.list, so a whole-document rewrite would clobber it and the test would fire. Verified by the reviewer tracing the hypothetical defect through, plus a fresh -race run. deadcode's helper-rooted chain corrected in the report to the real cmd/nocx-server wiring.

title: A skill opens in its own tab, and what a model concluded about it is remembered
description:
Replaces the Skills card modal. Plan: .internal/plans/2026-09-05-the-skill-viewer.md
Spec: .internal/specs/2026-09-05-the-skill-viewer-design.md (revision 2)
Discovered from the brainstorm nocx-4l3km.

## Success Criteria

A person opens a skill in its own tab, reads any file of its bundle beside the
file list, checks it once, and finds the verdict still there when they come
back — with no second model call. One e2e on cmd/nocx-server watches exactly
that, measuring the absent second call on the fake provider's completion
counter rather than on the screen, and watches a stored verdict say it is
about an earlier version once a file on disk changes. A builtin offers no
check at all.

Deliberately out: checking on install or on a schedule; any behaviour that
depends on the verdict; ageing and archiving (nocx-dzy7l); a skills.changed
notification; encrypting skills.json.

title: Assistant permissions: one list, and each question's answer is a select
description:
The owner, looking at the page: «Ну зачем так сделали? Что это за странная механика? Ну сделать просто dropdown с выбором».

Three strangenesses, one cause. nocx-6szvl removed the third answer because 'Ask every time' offered as a BUTTON changes nothing and reads as Cancel. That is true of a button and false of a select: a button is an act, a select is a state, and showing where you are is exactly what a select is for. Removing the state from the control pushed it into a badge, split the page into 'What you have answered' / 'Not answered yet' so a row JUMPS between lists on every click, and gave taking-an-answer-back a second name (Forget) beside the row's own two buttons.

So: one list of the questions, always all of them, each with one Select — Allowed / Ask every time / Never. The badge and the repeated 'Nobody has answered this…' line go; one sentence above the list says it once. Returning a row to 'Ask every time' IS Forget, with the same preview of what it releases and the same live-runs question; the page stays controlled by the store, so a write the store turns down leaves the select where it was. Why and the places move behind one 'More' on the row. RULES keep their own list below and keep Forget under its own name — a rule has identity and is deleted, not switched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The page renders one list; no row moves between sections when it is answered.
- Each question row has a select whose value is its current answer, including 'Ask every time'.
- Choosing 'Ask every time' on an answered row asks the same confirmation Forget asked, including the live-runs count, and writes nothing if declined.
- A select the store refuses to widen shows 'Allowed' disabled with the reason, never omits it.
- e2e/agent-policy.spec.ts drives the select and still watches a person answer, change and take back.
close_reason: One list of questions, each with a Select holding all three answers (frontend/src/assistant-permissions-section.tsx, commit cc719d57). Releasing an answer is choosing 'Ask every time' and keeps the preview and the live-runs question. Rules keep their own list; Why+Change fold into Details. Kit: SelectOption.disabled (frontend/src/ui/select.tsx). 46 section tests + 9 Select tests green; e2e/agent-policy.spec.ts and e2e/assistant-permissions.spec.ts pass in the container.

title: Снять недельную выборку дрейфа и решить судьбу nocx-ec18
description:
Инструмент готов (nocx-4n6sj). Осталось единственное, ради чего он писался:
получить число и принять по нему решение.

## Как

В консоли работающего приложения:

  nocxCellDrift.enable()     # один раз, живёт в localStorage
  # работать неделю как обычно
  nocxCellDrift.report()     # объект: строки, доли, бакеты, виновники
  nocxCellDrift.reset()      # обнулить выборку
  nocxCellDrift.disable()

Мерить НА MAC. На Linux в этом репозитории fc-list знает одно семейство
DejaVu Sans, и весь стек ui-monospace/SF Mono/Menlo съезжает в
пропорциональный шрифт — там дрейф будет всюду и он не про omp.

## Что решает выборка

- drifted / lines мал (единицы процентов) и wideByAColumn около нуля:
  владелец прав, nocx-ec18 закрывается wontfix С ЧИСЛОМ В ТЕЛЕ, инструмент
  удаляется.
- wideByAColumn заметен: планировать раскладку по колонкам. И пересчитать
  объём заново — цена в теле nocx-ec18 написана под ПОЛНУЮ посимвольную
  сетку, а таблица offenders показывает, сколько ячеек на самом деле
  нуждаются в коробке (на замеренной строке omp это 4 из 152, и при таком
  соотношении виртуализация может не понадобиться вовсе).

## Acceptance Criteria

- В теле nocx-ec18 записан отчёт: сколько блоков и строк измерено, доля
  дрейфа, сколько строк разъехалось на целую колонку и более, таблица
  виновников.
- nocx-ec18 либо закрыт с этим числом, либо получил план, объём которого
  посчитан по таблице виновников, а не по оценке из июля.
- Инструмент удалён вместе с решением: cell-drift.ts, его тесты,
  frozen-line-drift.spec.ts, врезка в blocks.ts, вызов в main.tsx и
  out-параметр serializeRange, если колонки не понадобятся раскладке.
close_reason:
Выборка снята, решение принято, исправление в проде.

Число: один блок omp, 25 логических строк, ячейка 8px. Дрейф на ОДНОЙ строке, 1.105 колонки, wideByAColumn=1. Виновники — 🗑 13.572, ⟳ и ⟲ по 9.087, ⬢ 8.903; сумма промахов 8.649px = 1.081 колонки, что совпало с ручным замером владельца до второго знака. Остальные 24 строки чистые: глобальная коррекция для обычного текста работает.

Решение по этому числу: «4% строк» занижает ущерб, потому что одна строка ломает целую рамку и добавляет прокрутку всему блоку — правильная единица не доля строк, а доля блоков, которые выглядят сломанными. Чинить. Сделано в nocx-ec18.

Инструмент (frontend/src/scrollback/cell-drift.ts, консольная ручка nocxCellDrift) НЕ удалён, вопреки исходному критерию этого бида, и это осознанно: он остаётся средством приёмки для работы по ADR-0009, где та же корневая причина закрывается общим правилом. Удаляется вместе с закрытием эпика по ADR-0009 — там это записано как обязательный пункт.

title: Инструмент: измерить дрейф ширины замороженной строки против сетки
description:
Прежде чем платить за покоординатную раскладку (nocx-ec18), нужно ЧИСЛО:
насколько часто и на сколько замороженная строка шире своих колонок в
реальной работе, а не на одном захвате omp.

Владелец 2026-09-05: «большое желание ничего не делать, это срабатывает
только на omp и только внизу». Возможно он прав — но сейчас это
впечатление, а не замер. Инструмент отвечает на вопрос, не строя решение.

## Что измеряется

При заморозке для каждой .term-line сравнить фактическую ширину
(getBoundingClientRect) с Σ getWidth() × --term-cell-width.

ВАЖНО: scrollWidth > clientWidth НЕДОСТАТОЧНО как признак. serializeRange
намеренно склеивает soft-wrap ("JOIN (owner directive)"), поэтому часть
длинных строк широкие законно. Сравнивать надо с посчитанной суммой
колонок.

Колонки серилизатор уже считает — collectRunsOf ведёт шаг цикла по
getWidth() — но выбрасывает. Инструмент требует их сохранить: data-cols
на term-line. Это же и первый кирпич будущей раскладки.

## Что собирается (локально, без текста команд)

- гистограмма ошибки в колонках
- число строк с дрейфом и число строк, где дрейф >= 1 колонки (то есть
  перенос/прокрутка)
- таблица виновников: для каждого не-ASCII графемного кластера его
  натуральный шаг в DOM против cell-width и 2 × cell-width; «не совпал ни
  с тем, ни с другим» и есть виновник
- сколько строк пропущено потолком выборки

## Границы

- Выключен по умолчанию. Включается один раз, состояние в localStorage.
- Никакого текста команд в хранилище, только кодпоинты и счётчики.
- Восстановленные после перезапуска блоки не меряются: у них нет
  достоверных колонок (restore-client.ts:332 выбрасывает terminalCols).
- Это временный инструмент. Удаляется вместе с закрытием nocx-ec18.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Серилизатор публикует колонки логической строки на term-line, и это
  проверено тестом на строке с двухколоночной ячейкой и с обрезанными
  хвостовыми пробелами.
- Агрегатор — чистая функция над замерами: бакеты, счётчики, таблица
  виновников, ограниченный размер хранилища. Проверен в jsdom.
- Браузерный тест (Playwright, где раскладка настоящая) показывает
  НЕНУЛЕВОЙ дрейф на строке с ⬢ ⟳ 🗑 и НУЛЕВОЙ на строке той же длины из
  пробелов. Без него инструмент не проверяем: 6211 jsdom-тестов были
  зелёными, пока продукт был сломан, потому что jsdom не считает раскладку.
- Отчёт достаётся из работающего приложения одной командой.
close_reason: Инструмент собран и проверен: frontend/src/scrollback/cell-drift.ts + cell-drift.test.ts (23 теста), колонки логической строки выданы serializeRange (out-параметр, serializer.test.ts «serializeRange column accounting»), врезан в _freezeVisual (blocks.ts) до декорации ссылок, консольная ручка nocxCellDrift в main.tsx. Браузерный тест e2e/frozen-line-drift.spec.ts зелёный в контейнере на chromium: строка из 60 W даёт drifted=0, строка 57W+⬢⟳🗑 даёт drifted>0 и непустую таблицу виновников. Он же поймал реальный дефект при написании: .term-line — display:block, и чтение getBoundingClientRect вернуло бы ширину контейнера для каждой строки. Коммит b2431ca1. Выборку снимает nocx-mmn56.

title: [bug] A prompt taller than the window paints its answers past the bottom edge and nothing scrolls, so a person can refuse but cannot decide
description:
frontend/src/styles/components/prompt.css: .ui-prompt-overlay is `position: fixed; inset: 0` with NO
overflow, and .ui-prompt has NO max-height. A question taller than the window paints its answers past
the bottom edge with nothing to scroll — scrollIntoViewIfNeeded moves nothing, because there is no
scroll container to move.

Measured 2026-09-05 while writing nocx-ojfuc.5's e2e, which went red on it:

  the install question is 1063px tall in a 900px window and the prompt does not scroll, so these
  answers cannot be reached: Allow once, Allow in this session, Allow always, Deny once,
  Deny in this session, Deny always

The same spec is green at 1280x1600. On the host, 977px against a 900px window leaves the three Deny
answers unreachable. Playwright sat retrying the click for four minutes before failing, which is what
a person would experience as a window that will not answer.

WHAT A PERSON LOSES: not the ability to dismiss — Escape still refuses — but the ability to DECIDE.
Every answer that distinguishes once from this-session from always is below the fold, so the only
reachable outcome is the refusal, and a person who wanted to allow something has no way to say so.

An install question is the tallest thing nocx asks: it carries the resolved address, the name, the
description, the digest, a manifest and the whole bytes of every file that will land (nocx-ojfuc.2).
The bundle that measured 1063px is TWO SMALL FILES. The skill this epic started from, AgentMail,
names seven. But the defect is the kit's and not the install question's — any prompt tall enough
loses its answers the same way, and the vault unlock and the connection-password ask use the same
overlay.

## Steps to Reproduce

Open any prompt taller than the viewport — an install approval for a two-file bundle at 1280x900 does
it. The answer buttons are painted below the window and cannot be clicked or scrolled to.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A prompt taller than the window keeps every answer reachable, and the answers are what stays
  reachable — a person deciding should not have to scroll past the evidence to find the buttons.
- Nothing becomes compulsory: no forced scroll to enable an answer, and no scroll-to-the-bottom gate.
  nocx-872jc decided that once; this must not reintroduce it by the back door.
- The fix lives in the kit, not in the approval surface, because every prompt shares the overlay.
- A test that fails without the fix: a prompt whose content exceeds the viewport, with every answer
  asserted reachable — which takes a real engine, since jsdom performs no layout.
close_reason: DUPLICATE of nocx-ck02x, which is closed and whose fix is 42b6e4cc — merged into feat/agent-ploicy and NOT on main. I filed this without searching the closed area listing first, which is the check AGENTS.md puts before filing; nocx-ck02x says the same thing in almost the same words and was P0. One behaviour, one bead: nocx-ck02x is the survivor. What this bead did add is a second measurement of the same defect four days later, on a branch cut from main and therefore lacking the fix: the install approval measured 1063px in a 900px window with all six answers unreachable, and Playwright retried the click for four minutes. Resolved on this branch by cherry-picking 42b6e4cc as fcb55793, with the kit README's Prompt row merged to keep both this branch's data-prompt clause (nocx-6wgcw) and the fix's scroll clause.

title: Живая область не дорастает до доступного места: сетка выше бокса, а потолок не выбран
description:
После nocx-hg0dg (d41dbb7e) строка ввода видна, но верх рисунка программы
срезан, и в панели остаётся неиспользованное место.

## Измерено в живой панели владельца, omp запущен

    areaH            721      высота скроллера
    runningBlockH     56.5    высота бегущего блока (шапка)
    capWouldBe       664.5    721 - 56.5, потолок живой области
    viewportH        532      что показано
    viewportScrollH  532      равно viewportH => внутри бокса НЕ прокручивается
    boxH             540      532 + отступы
    screenH          646      полная высота сетки xterm

Два факта из этих чисел:

1. Бокс НЕ упёрся в потолок: 532 против 664.5, свободно 132px.
2. Сетка выше бокса: 646 против 532, около 114px рисунка вне окна, и это
   именно ВЕРХ — на скриншоте у omp срезана верхняя граница рамки
   `╭── omp v17.1.2 ──`.

`viewportScrollH == viewportH` означает, что содержимое не переполняет бокс
внутренней прокруткой: сетка сдвинута трансформом (`_applyEchoShift`), и то,
что выше окна, просто не видно.

## Подозрение (не проверено)

`setLiveHeight` считает `content = min(px - echoShiftPx, cap - pad)`. Если
`echoShiftPx` больше, чем одна строка эха, бокс получается ниже сетки ровно на
эту разницу, а свободные 132px остаются невыбранными. Проверять надо величину
сдвига против числа строк, которые он обязан скрыть.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Открыть локальную панель, запустить omp.
2. Смотреть на верхнюю границу его рамки и на пустое место снизу панели.

Наблюдается: верх рамки срезан, снизу панели место не занято.
Ожидается: программа видна целиком, пока помещается в потолок.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Пока команда идёт и её сетка помещается в потолок живой области, показана
  вся сетка: высота бокса равна высоте сетки, а не меньше.
- Сдвиг эха скрывает ровно те строки, ради которых он существует, и ни одной
  сверх того. Утверждается числом строк, а не пикселями.
- Когда сетка ВЫШЕ потолка, бокс равен потолку — это уже поведение nocx-zn4d,
  и оно не должно сломаться.
close_reason: Тот же дефект, что nocx-hg0dg, с другого конца — закрыт b7000e9e. Клип на сдвигаемом .xterm-inner резал нижнюю строку в собственной коробке до трансляции, поэтому бокс и не дорастал до доступного места. Владелец подтвердил в живой панели: строка ввода видна И лишняя прокрутка исчезла одним изменением. Гипотеза из тела бида про шестикратный сдвиг эха опровергнута замером: сдвиг ровно одна строка (echoShift 19 при ячейке 19, transform matrix(1,0,0,1,0,-19)).

title: [bug] A finished command can render its exit code and be recorded nowhere: rec === null freezes the block and persists nothing
description:
Observed twice on e2e/notification-centre-choice.spec.ts, once in CI and once
in the container, and diagnosed to a named line on 2026-09-04 while working
nocx-dl1o0. NOT the same defect as nocx-dl1o0, which was fixed separately and
was present in only one of the two occurrences.

## The signature

`commandFinished` PASSES — the block header shows `exit 1`, so the command
really ended and the renderer really saw it — and the notification centre's
`block.finished` row never arrives. The count sits at its old value for the
full 30s timeout. The backend's debug log is SILENT: no history.record, no
raise, no error, no stall. Nothing was refused; nothing was asked.

## The mechanism, which is not a guess

frontend/src/lifecycle/projections.ts:184-189:

    const rec = this.ledger.complete(attempt)
    if (attempt.state === 'completed') {
      if (rec !== null) void this.persist(rec, attempt)
      this.blocks.freezeBlock(attempt)     // <- OUTSIDE the guard
    }

The freeze is unconditional; the persist is not. So `rec === null` produces
exactly the observed pair: a block rendered with its exit status, and no
history.record on the wire at all — hence no ledger row and no
block.finished notification, because ws_history_record.go's raise is
downstream of a call that was never made.

That is already asserted at unit level. projections.test.ts:132, 'a
shell-originated attempt opens a block but no ledger record and persists
nothing', ends with blocks.events == ['open:att-9:ssh pi@host',
'freeze:att-9:1'] and persist not called. The mechanism exists and is
covered; what is not covered is how a command the TEST submitted through the
app reaches it.

Two routes reach `rec === null`, and this bead does not yet distinguish them:

1. The attempt is `origin: 'shell'` — the typed line reached the pty rather
   than the app's submit, so no record was opened. `page.keyboard.type` goes
   wherever DOM focus is, and `promptReady` can resolve while input ownership
   is still settling. This is the "two surfaces may never own the same input"
   shape AGENTS.md names: the loser goes on advertising what it can no longer
   deliver.
2. The record was opened at submit but never bound to the published attempt,
   so `complete` finds nothing to close (command-ledger.ts, bindAttempt and
   the submit-id correlation).

Both are load-sensitive and neither leaves a trace.

## Why it is a product bug and not only a test bug

If a person's command can be attributed as shell-originated when they
submitted it through nocx, then for that command the ledger has no row, the
history has no entry, and the Settings toggle "A command finished" governs
nothing — silently, on the path the user actually used. A soft degrade must
be visible in the product, not only in a log (AGENTS.md), and here it is not
even in a log.

Deliberately NOT in scope: that a genuinely shell-originated line records
nothing. That is the command-text decision (a native prompt line may carry a
literal password) and it stays.

## What was measured

- 38 single-worker container runs of the spec with nocx-dl1o0's fix applied:
  37 green, 1 red. The red was the first, on a cold stand.
- 12 of those with NOCX_E2E_CPUS=1: all green. Starving CPU did not reproduce it.
- 2 workers on the shared stand: 7 of 30 red, but with OVERSHOOTING counts
  (33 vs 23, badge 4 vs 2) — cross-worker contamination of one shared feed,
  a different failure. playwright.config.ts pins workers: 1, so that is not
  CI's condition and not this bug.
- No "connection outbound stalled" in any surviving log, so nocx-mrtvy is not
  the cause either.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not reproducible on demand: 1 in 38 under container load, and it did not
reproduce at all under a 1-CPU cap. By reading, the path is exact — see the
lines above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A completed command submitted through the app is recorded, or the reason it
  was not is observable — the failure currently leaves NO evidence anywhere,
  which is why two occurrences cost a full session to diagnose and still did
  not settle which of the two routes it took.
- A test drives the route that produced `rec === null` for an app submit and
  asserts the record lands; and the block projection may not report an
  outcome the ledger did not record, or it may and that is written down where
  the next reader will find it.
- The e2e spec stops being able to fail this way silently: whatever it asserts
  about a finished-command row names which half is missing.
notes:
2026-09-04, commit 8a1a450b: instrumented, and the one provable route repaired.
The bead stays OPEN — the loss itself is not yet proven fixed, and one half of
its acceptance is deliberately untouched.

WHAT LANDED

- LifecycleProjections takes an UnattributedPort and reports a command whose
  authenticated fact found no ledger record: `bind` (the running fact did),
  `complete` (the completion did — the one that costs a finished command its
  history row and its notification), and `abandon` (a submitted record
  consumed by its domain ending). The third is what makes the set useful: the
  completion that follows THAT door carries no app authority, since the
  shell's own start has no token, so the first two would stay silent on it.
  An ordinary shell-originated command is not reported — it opens no record by
  design, and reporting every one would bury the signal.
  Wired at terminal-content's composition root to log.warn with the pane id.

- The fail-open on lifecycle.submitAttempt stopped being silent. `.then(write,
  write)` sent a refusal down the same path as a success; it now logs and
  marks the record CommandLedger.orphan(id). bindAttempt may bind the next
  unattributed attempt to an orphaned record — not the guess nocx-td6d4.10
  removed, but a fact the caller supplied. Only the refusal path marks; the
  no-live-domain path does not, and the code says why.

- Acceptance at the seam a person reaches (type, Enter, refusal): the bytes
  still go out, ONE block carries the command, and the completion is recorded
  with the app-owned text. Red without the mark, with the exact message
  "expected [ {id:1}, {id:2} ] to have a length of 1 but got 2" — a refused
  submit used to draw a duplicate block for one command. That defect is
  closed on its own merits.

WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY THIS IS STILL OPEN

- Which route the two observed occurrences took is still unknown. The
  instrument exists to answer it on the next one; nothing here proves the
  loss cannot happen.
- The second acceptance criterion is untouched: a block that reports an
  outcome nothing recorded is still a soft degrade the UI contradicts, and a
  log is exactly what AGENTS.md says is not enough. How that should READ is a
  product decision, not one to take inside a diagnosis.

Verified: 6265 frontend tests green (317 files), tsc both configs, eslint and
the ratchets clean. A concurrent full-suite run went red on two unrelated
vi.waitFor timeouts under 3x machine load — filed as nocx-tg7rm, not this.
close_reason:
All three criteria met, across 8a1a450b, 77788c48 and af7879da.

1. 'Recorded, or the reason it was not is observable.' LifecycleProjections
emits an UnattributedCommand for a command whose authenticated fact found no
ledger record — , ,  — with the attempt's origin,
whether the backend echoed a submit token, the exit code and how many records
are still running. The three kinds are what tells the routes apart: 
exists because the completion that follows THAT door carries no app authority,
so without it the loss through it reported nothing at all. The ordinary
shell-originated command stays silent, by design.

2. 'A test drives the route that produced rec === null for an app submit and
asserts the record lands; and the block projection may not report an outcome
the ledger did not record, or it may and that is written down where the next
reader will find it.' Both halves. The refused-submit route is driven at the
seam a person reaches — type, Enter, refusal — and the record now lands:
CommandLedger.orphan states that no attempt will echo the token, so the next
unattributed attempt binds to it. Red without the mark, with two blocks for
one command, which was itself a user-visible defect. And the block may still
report an outcome nothing recorded — that stays, because an authenticated
completion is the truth about the command — but it now SAYS so: a muted  chip in the header's own vocabulary, driven by the 
report so the condition has one owner. Absence could not carry it: a native
prompt line is unrecorded by design and renders identically.

3. 'The e2e spec stops being able to fail this way silently.' The third
moment of notification-centre-choice now polls the same conjunction the first
two do, so a timeout names whether the outcome never reached the feed or the
visibility choice stopped being applied.

Gates: 6269 frontend tests, 317 files; tsc both configs plus the e2e config;
eslint and every ratchet clean; two full both-browser container e2e runs on
this tree, the second 559 passed / 9 skipped / 0 failed.

NOT claimed: that the two original occurrences are explained. Which route they
took is still unknown — that is what the instrument exists to answer on the
next one, and it now leaves a trace in the renderer's log AND on the block the
person is looking at. Filed alongside: nocx-mrtvy (closed), nocx-tg7rm,
nocx-o1u23.

title: Полноэкранная программа в ОБЫЧНОМ буфере обрезается: живая область растёт до панели только по ?1049h
description:
omp v17.1.2 в панели nocx рисуется частично, и во время набора не видно строки
ввода. В herdr та же программа рисуется правильно — владелец проверил и на
старой сборке nocx, поведение не новое.

## Что измерено

Снял поток omp ВНЕ nocx (`script -qec omp`, 172 817 байт), чтобы отделить
программу от терминала:

- `ESC[?1049h` — НИ ОДНОГО. omp никогда не уходит на альтернативный экран.
- Вместо этого перерисовка на месте, в обычном буфере: 78 CUU, 469 EL,
  80 пар `ESC[?7l`/`ESC[?7h`, 79/82 скрытий/показов курсора.
- `ESC]133;` — ни одного (то есть это НЕ nocx-mu8s).
- `ESC]7;` — ни одного; `ESC]0;` ставит заголовок `π > tmp` (то есть и вкладка,
  и `/tmp` — сообщения самой omp, не nocx).

## Причина

`terminal-content.ts:2664` — живая область переходит в fullscreen ТОЛЬКО по
`onBufferChange('alternate')`. Программа, которая перерисовывается в обычном
буфере, этого перехода не получает никогда и остаётся внутри модели блоков,
где у живого бокса своя высота.

Та же форма обрезки уже описана в `scrollback/controller.ts` (комментарий к
`_fillPane`) для alt-screen случая: «the rows past the box were clipped by its
overflow — `top` drawing 34 of the 40 rows it had been given». Здесь то же
самое, но перехода в fullscreen нет вовсе, поэтому чинить нужно не размер
бокса, а признак, по которому решается, что программа забрала панель.

Строка ввода omp — самая нижняя из тех, что она рисует, поэтому обрезается
первой. Это объясняет и «не всё отрисовывается», и «не видно строки ввода».

Почему только в nocx: в herdr нет модели блоков и нет зарезервированного
бокса — сетка И ЕСТЬ панель.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Открыть локальную панель в nocx.
2. Запустить omp (или любую программу, перерисовывающую себя в обычном буфере
   без `?1049h`).
3. Набирать текст.

Наблюдается: нижние строки не отрисованы, строка ввода не видна.
Ожидается: то же, что показывает обычный терминал.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Программа, которая перерисовывается в обычном буфере поверх уже
  напечатанных строк, показывает ВСЕ строки, которые нарисовала, включая
  нижнюю. Проверяется на потоке, а не на скриншоте: подать в рендерер
  последовательность, паркующую курсор выше последней напечатанной строки, и
  утверждать, что видимы все строки диапазона.
- Признак «программа забрала панель» перестаёт быть равен «альтернативный
  буфер». Что им становится — решение этого бида; оно должно быть записано,
  потому что переопределяет то, что terminal-content.ts:2664 решает сейчас.
- Не сломано обратное: обычная команда, оставляющая курсор где угодно, панель
  себе не забирает.

## Не входит

Почему omp выбирает `/tmp` и почему у него падает MCP-сервер repowise
(«Transport closed») — и то и другое воспроизводится вне nocx, в чистом PTY,
и к nocx отношения не имеет.

## ЭТО ПЛАВАЮЩИЙ ДЕФЕКТ, и повтор его не воспроизвёл (2026-09-04)

Через несколько минут в той же панели omp отрисовался ПРАВИЛЬНО. Зелёный
повтор — не доказательство, что дефекта нет, только что он не выстрелил
(AGENTS.md, «A rerun is legitimate exactly once»). Ниже — то, что различает
проходы, потому что это сужает причину.

Четыре наблюдения, и различаются они не терминалом, а строкой о MCP:

  сломано,  nocx: "MCP finished with failures. Failed: repowise: Transport closed"
  верно,    nocx: "Connected to MCP servers: codex, repowise."
  верно,    Warp: "Connected to MCP servers: codex, repowise."
  сломано,  чистый PTY (script): та же строка про Transport closed

ПОЭТОМУ «ТОЛЬКО В NOCX» НЕ УСТАНОВЛЕНО. Ни Warp, ни herdr в отказавшем
состоянии не наблюдались — у них MCP подключался. Сравнивались не два
терминала, а два разных сценария запуска omp.

## Кандидат в причину (не проверен)

Когда repowise не поднимается, omp около 30 с висит на `Still connecting:
repowise…` (в его логе watchdog на 31790 мс) и всё это время перерисовывает
одну строку НА МЕСТЕ.

`controller.ts setLiveHeight` меняет высоту бокса только когда изменился
измеренный контент, и это защита, поставленная намеренно: «a program that
repaints in place changes nothing about the layout: `top` redrawing the same
33 rows every three seconds was moving the scroll each time for no reason».
То есть длинная фаза перерисовки на месте — ровно тот режим, где бокс не
пересчитывается. Затем omp разом печатает рамку и промпт, строк становится
больше, и если пересчёт не происходит или считает по устаревшему
`runningLiveCap`, низ обрезается. Нижняя строка — строка ввода.

Это совпадение четырёх наблюдений, а не измерение.

## Как проверять, не полагаясь на удачу

Не ждать, когда повезёт. Воспроизводить детерминированно: подать в рендерер
поток, который сначала долго перерисовывает НА МЕСТЕ одну строку, а затем
разом печатает больше строк, чем помещалось, и утверждать, что видима
последняя. Задержку MCP при живой проверке имитировать
неподнимающимся stdio-сервером, а не ожиданием.

Питомец (pets overlay) присутствует на обоих скриншотах, сломанном и верном,
поэтому он ни при чём.
close_reason: Не дефект сам по себе — измерения опровергли его тело. Захват из самой панели (152x33) показал: сетка xterm целая, замороженный текст совпадает с ней посимвольно, и tmux из того же захвата даёт ту же сетку. Содержимое верно на всём пути; ломается ПОКАЗ замороженного блока, что уже описано в nocx-ec18 (152 против 140, метрики шрифта блока против сетки). Доказательства перенесены туда, приоритет поднят до P1. Заодно в b36643e2 закрыт настоящий, но ДРУГОЙ дефект, найденный по дороге: сетку переразмеривали на каждом куске вывода от роста шапки блока — SIGWINCH посреди перерисовки; тест доказанно красный без исправления.

title: [bug] outbound.stalled has no subscriber: the overflow policy's resync is a renderer behaviour that does not exist
description:
Found on 2026-09-04 while fixing nocx-dl1o0 (the feed store's own dropped-hint
window), by asking what recovers a hint the TRANSPORT dropped rather than the
store.

## What is actually wrong

internal/transport/outbound/outbound.go:328 `overflow` is the terminal policy
for a full refreshable queue. It marks the connection stalled, drops the busy
frame, and pushes `outbound.stalled` through the reserved overload slot. The
constant's own doc says why that is sound:

  "StallNoticeMethod is the control-plane notification the reserved slot
   carries when the refreshable queue overflows. The renderer treats it as
   a cue to reconnect: a connection whose outbound data plane is saturated
   cannot deliver everything it owes, and the reconnect surface (with the
   session replay ring) is how the product makes that visible."

**The renderer does not treat it as anything.** grep for `outbound.stalled`
over frontend/, e2e/ and contracts/ returns zero hits. Dispatcher routes a
notification by looking its method up in `subscribers` and does nothing when
the set is absent (frontend/src/dispatcher.ts:576) — so the notice arrives,
finds no handler, and is discarded in silence.

So every refreshable frame dropped in a stall episode is lost permanently:
nothing reconnects, nothing resyncs, and no surface says the connection is
behind. `control.saturated` — the INBOUND lane refusing work — is handled and
raises a toast (dispatcher.ts:171); its outbound twin is not.

The backend half is equally quiet: the only observer of the stall is
`OnStall` in ws.go:2046, which is a slog.Warn and nothing else. Nothing puts
a stall on the wire as state, and StallCount() has no reader outside its own
package. AGENTS.md: a soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only
in a log.

## Why it matters beyond the transport

It is the second door to nocx-sb3f's silence, and it is the one that is
currently unguarded from BOTH sides. nocx-dl1o0's fix makes the feed store
chase a hint it coalesced itself; a hint this policy discards never reaches
the store at all. The notification feed is only the example that surfaced it
— every refreshable notification on the connection has the same exposure.

Same SHAPE as nocx-gbhwh (a dispatcher seam built and never consumed), but a
different seam and a different loss: gbhwh is the socket dropping being
invisible, this is the socket staying up while frames are discarded.

## Steps to Reproduce

By reading: outbound.go:79-95 (the notice and its promise), outbound.go:328
(the overflow policy), ws.go:2046 (the only observer), dispatcher.ts:576 (an
unsubscribed notification is dropped), and a grep for the method name over
frontend/ that returns nothing.

Under load it is a real loss rather than a reading: a dropped notify.feed.
changed on a quiet feed leaves the notification centre a revision behind with
nothing to recover it. That is the shape observed twice on
e2e/notification-centre-choice.spec.ts (once in CI at moment C, once in the
container at moment A) as a block.finished row that never arrived — NOT yet
proven to be this cause, because no stall was logged in the runs whose logs
survived.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `outbound.stalled` has exactly one owner in the renderer, and what it does
  is what the backend's doc already decided — reconnect and resync — or the
  backend's doc is changed to say what it really does.
- A stall is visible in the product, not only in a log: a person can tell
  that the connection fell behind, by the same route control.saturated takes.
- A test drives a saturated refreshable queue and asserts the renderer acts
  on the notice; and a test asserts the feed reaches the current revision
  after a hint was dropped by the queue rather than by the store.
- Deliberately out: which delivery class a notification rides. That is
  nocx-sb3f and it stays there.
close_reason:
Fixed in 77788c48 (frontend/src/dispatcher.ts). outbound.stalled has exactly one owner in the renderer now, and it does what the backend's doc had already decided: it closes the socket, taking the same path the heartbeat's dead socket takes — pending calls rejected, waiting published, retry scheduled, onDisconnect fired. The reconnect is the resync: every store re-reads on onConnect, which is the only thing that recovers a frame the queue dropped.

The remedy is deliberately the OPPOSITE of control.saturated's, and the code says why rather than leaving the asymmetry to be discovered: a refused request has an answer, so a toast makes it visible; a stalled queue has already dropped frames, so there is nothing to retry and nothing to tell the caller. Visibility is the reconnect surface itself, which is what internal/transport/outbound names ('the reconnect surface, with the session replay ring, is how the product makes that visible').

Test: dispatcher.test.ts 'an outbound stall drops the socket, because the connection cannot deliver what it owes' — delivers the notice on a live socket and asserts the close, one onDisconnect, reconnectPending, and that an in-flight call rejects. Red before the handler existed. The Go half was already covered (outbound_test.go TestQueueFullMarksStalledAndDropsFrame and the reserved-slot test beside it).

Not claimed: that this was the cause of the notification-centre-choice red. It was not — no stall appears in any surviving log of those runs, and that is recorded on nocx-2vb9y. This was found by asking what recovers a hint the transport dropped, and it was a real hole regardless.

title: The epic's happy path: a page in the conversation becomes an installed skill
description:
The epic's happy path, and the check that closes it.

From the epic's acceptance criterion: a person pastes into the CONVERSATION the page they actually
have — an HTML docs page, not a raw file — says install the skill from it, and gets it, without ever
constructing a raw URL.

One e2e on the shipped backend against a local fixture server: the assistant resolves the page to a
repository and a file, proposes the install, the approval names the RESOLVED source and every file
that will land, approving writes the bundle under the installed root, and the row afterwards records
what resolved. The skill arrives INERT — nocx-0bsa4 — so the check ends with a skill on the page and
switched off, not with one in play.

Deliberately out: registries and their slugs, /.well-known/ discovery, arbitrary ZIP URLs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One spec watches the whole path in one browser context, against a fixture server it stands up
  itself, with no duration waits and no pixel constants.
- The model is scripted, and the spec says plainly in its header that a scripted model proves the
  WIRING and not the model's judgement.
- A negative control is run and reported: break one link in the chain, watch the spec go red naming
  what is missing, put it back.
- The spec asserts the skill is off afterwards, and that turning it on is a separate act by the
  person.
close_reason: 7e7acb2d, green in the container (12 passed alongside the cherry-picked prompt-height suite). e2e/skill-install-by-asking.spec.ts: one test, one context, its own fixture serving an HTML docs page, the SKILL.md it names and the reference file that document links; the person's message names only the page. The scripted model is a function of the request body — it takes the document address out of the page text carried in the fetch result — so the address the install used provably came from the page's bytes and was never typed; the question is asserted to contain the page address and NOT the document's. What that does not prove is judgement, and the header says so. Asserted: the window names the resolved address, name, description, digest, manifest and both files' exact bytes; approving puts the bundle on disk; the row sentence and the card digest are read OFF THE APPROVAL WINDOW rather than off a constant; the skill is off afterwards and turning it on is a separate act. Negative control run and reverted: dropping the install block on its way to the notification reddens it on the sentence about a resolved address. Product fact recorded in the header: fetch.url extracts text nodes only, so href targets never reach the model — a docs page whose document is reachable only through a link is unresolvable, and the fixture states the address in visible text as docs pages do.

title: Settings loses acquisition and keeps management
description:
Design §5: "Settings keeps management and loses acquisition. The list, the enable switch, deletion
and change detection have no conversational substitute and stay. The paste box, the parse and the
candidate picker go."

This is the half that makes the epic a deletion rather than an addition. Two surfaces owning one
input is the failure AGENTS.md names most often, and here it would be worse than usual: the paste
box asks a person to hunt for a raw address, which is exactly the labour the assistant removes.

What goes: the paste field, classifyPastedSource, the install dialog and the preview flow behind it.
What stays and must be proved still to work: the list, the enable switch, deletion, change
detection, the card, the file viewer and the audit.

The e2e that owns the paste box today is e2e/skill-install-url.spec.ts. It does not merely lose an
assertion — its subject stops existing. Decide deliberately whether it is deleted or becomes the
management spec, and say which in the commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Settings page offers no way to type or paste a source address, and nothing in it calls
  skills.preview.
- Every management capability still works, watched by a test: list, enable, disable, delete, the
  changed-bytes status, the card, the file viewer, the audit.
- The dead-exports and deadcode ratchets are clean afterwards. Removing a surface removes its
  helpers too; a ratchet baseline is not the place to park them.
- Whatever happens to skills.preview as a JSON-RPC method is deliberate and stated: still needed by
  the tool's own path, or gone. Not left reachable by nobody.
close_reason: 47cb6b0b plus 4af8739b. Deleted: skills-install-dialog.tsx entire, every acquisition signal and handler in skills-section.tsx, the Install-from-a-URL heading action, SkillsClient/SkillsStore preview+install, their generated types, and the skills.preview/skills.install JSON-RPC methods with their four contracts and their openrpc entries — established by reading that the assistant's path is Go end to end (executor -> SkillLibrary -> Store) and the kernel's resolve half calls Store.Preview directly, so neither crosses JSON-RPC and both methods had no caller left. The tool's own params contract, contracts/tools/skills.install.schema.json, is a different file and stays. The dialog's wording was checked against the approval window BEFORE deleting: everything it said lives there since f70f52ba; the two sentences that were only the paste box's went with it. Kept: list, row grammar, provenance badge, both evidence lines, the switch on row and card, changed-bytes status, Re-approve, Delete, card, manifest, file viewer with marks, audit. One helper served both sides — the surface's one rule for showing the backend's own words — and stayed with its comment rewritten. e2e/skill-install-url.spec.ts became e2e/skills-management.spec.ts rather than being deleted: half of what it proved was about the row AFTER an install and it was the only e2e watching an installed row; its fixture now carries a deliberately wrong digest so the status it asserts is earned by the product's own hash. The absence assertions are written so a box under a different id or component still fails them (every input is a checkbox; no button label matches url|address|paste|install|import|fetch) and the dispatched method set is asserted WHOLE. Ratchets unchanged at 149/82 and honestly so: no skills symbol was ever parked in either, and the two orphan wire types were removed at source. Follow-up: 4af8739b retired five schema descriptions still citing skills.preview as a shape's home. NOT PROVED: the management e2e ran chromium in the container only; the audit assertion proves the reading arrived and what it owes, not the report's content, which a fake wrote; and the epic still has NO end-to-end proof of acquisition — that is nocx-ojfuc.5.

title: The approval names what RESOLVED, not what was asked for
description:
Design §5: "the approval names the RESOLVED source, the name, the description, the digest and the
files that will land", and "the description is prominent, because it is the one part of a skill that
lives in the system prompt afterwards".

The model asked to install from a page; what it resolved that page to is the thing the person is
actually deciding about, and the address the model typed is not it. A question naming the ASK rather
than the ANSWER would let a person approve a page they read and receive a repository they never saw.

Settings' install dialog already draws exactly these facts from a PreviewResult and has the wording
for them (frontend/src/skills-install-dialog.tsx). This is where that wording goes to live, because
nocx-ojfuc.4 takes the dialog away. Move the vocabulary, do not write a second one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The approval question for skills.install carries the resolved source address, the skill's name,
  its description, the digest and every file that will land — the same manifest skills.preview
  names, not a shorter one.
- The description is drawn as the prominent part, and the surface says WHY: it is what the assistant
  is offered on every ask afterwards.
- A person can read any file that will land, before approving, through the viewer nocx-872jc built.
  Not a second viewer.
- The wire change is declared in contracts/ with additionalProperties false, generated, asserted
  over the socket, and the generated type lands with its consumer.
- Approving installs exactly the bytes that were shown: a test moves the bytes between the question
  and the approval and asserts the install refuses rather than writing what was not shown.
close_reason: f70f52ba. agent.approvalRequested carries one optional install block (additionalProperties false, every field required): the resolved address, name, description, digest, and every file that will land with its bytes and the findings that matched in that file. Drawn through FileReadout — the same viewer nocx-872jc built, findings as marks on the line they matched — with the MarkerList manifest and its reasoning moved out of the Settings dialog that nocx-ojfuc.4 deletes. The description is a StatusCard title with the why beside it; the digest is drawn as what it buys and what it is not. The block is keyed on the PRESENCE of the facts, not on a tool name, so there is no literal to go stale. skill.PreviewResult gained Bundle and Digest as json:"-" so skills.preview's contract is untouched; bundle.go now has ONE owner of 'SKILL.md first, then support files' and the manifest, digest and bytes are three projections of it. An install proposal leaves the one-finding row empty — it is one finding wide and the files carry all of them marked in place. Bytes travel in the question rather than being fetched per file: a second request would re-read the store's one mutable preview slot, so 'approving installs exactly what was shown' would become a claim instead of a property, and it would add a second reader to nocx-aesm2's slot; rejected options recorded in skillinstall.go and the schema. Also fixed: the contract generator and prettier disagreed about the same file, so no schema could declare an array with minItems whose items are objects — both are CI gates. NOT PROVED: nobody has watched a person do this (renderer tests are jsdom, wire tests are Go, joined only by the product — nocx-ojfuc.5 is the happy path); 'prominent' is a design claim a DOM assertion cannot settle; no bundle near the 32-file/576 KiB ceiling is measured at the wire or in the DOM, and 32 expanded readouts in one modal is untried; the bytes-move test moves them at the origin between question and resume, not within one pair of fetches, which is what the digest bounds rather than prevents.

title: skills.install is a tool the assistant can call, and it is a door
description:
The assistant can already search, read a page, follow it to a repository and list a directory. What
it cannot do is the last step: write the skill. Today acquisition lives only in Settings, behind a
box the person pastes a raw URL into — which is the surface design §5 removes.

This child adds skills.install to internal/agenttools' declaration table and wires its executor. It
is a DOOR in ADR-0053's sense: what it can cause depends on bytes that do not exist yet, so it
declares a SET of effect classes and the decision is made at execution against what actually
resolved. Read ADR-0053 before writing the declaration, and name in the code which of its clauses
the declaration is satisfying.

The machinery it needs mostly exists. internal/skill's Store.Preview fetches a document, parses its
frontmatter, scans it, fetches the bundle and remembers the digest; Store.Install re-fetches,
compares against the remembered digest and writes under the installed root. The two-step is already
built for exactly this shape: preview, decide, write. Do not build a second acquisition path beside
it.

What is new is that the fetch happens inside a tool call rather than behind a person's button, so
the question the gate asks has to be asked at the right moment: after resolution, so it can name
what resolved, and before any byte is written.

## Acceptance Criteria

- skills.install is in the declaration table with a params schema, a description written for the
  MODEL in the register the neighbours use, an effect SET rather than a singleton, an explicit
  OutputTrust, a bounded result, and scope family "skill".
- The executor reuses Store.Preview and Store.Install. There is no second fetch path, no second
  digest and no second manifest.
- Nothing is written before the person answers, and a refusal writes nothing at all — asserted by a
  test that refuses and then checks the installed root is empty.
- A skill installed this way is INERT on arrival, exactly as one installed from Settings is
  (nocx-0bsa4): the tool cannot enable what it wrote.
- Every failure of the fetch has a test: the document is not there, it is not a skill, the bundle
  references a file that 404s, the origin changes across a redirect.
- deadcode -whylive names the executor as reachable from main.
close_reason: 39b4f18c. skills.install is row 23 of the declaration table with contracts/tools/skills.install.schema.json: params are a url and nothing else, effect SET {mutate-reversible, cross-boundary}, OutputTrustUntrusted, 8 KiB drop-tail, 120s, ScopeFamily skill, InGo. The result is bounded by construction — enabled is const:false in the contract, so inert-on-arrival is checked by the kernel's result checker rather than claimed by a comment. Resources resolve to the destination and the skill FAMILY, never a name, because at argument-resolution time no name exists. executeSkillsInstall calls Store.Install and nothing else; SkillLibrary gained Preview/Install, which *skill.Store already implemented, so app needed no wiring change; three Go fakes gained the pair, each refusing by default. Ordering: preview inside the call, after the policy decision and before the question, write on approval — ask-first-fetch-after rejected in code with its reason. The resume skips the preview, or the re-remembered digest would retire the bytes-moved refusal permanently; a test fails if it is not skipped. NOT PROVED: nothing about the approval surface (no frontend consumer of the name yet, no e2e); the classifier arm is correct by construction only; the pre-gate deadline is applied but untested; standing-no-prevents-the-fetch holds by code placement only; deadcode -whylive proves the symbol live through an RTA dynamic edge identical in shape to executeSkillsCreate's, so it proves not-dead and not reachable-by-a-user — the Ask-level happy path is what does that. Two findings filed rather than folded in: nocx-ykjai (ForGrant's alternation vs this row's conjunction, closed at enforcement, open at offer time) and nocx-aesm2 (one preview slot, two callers).

title: A dev or local build embeds no helper artifacts, so it refuses every pane
description:
Since ADR-0057 a local pane IS a session on this machine's helper daemon, and
the daemon binary comes from the artifacts embedded by internal/helper/deploy.
Those artifacts are gitignored and produced only by `make helpers`.

`make helpers` was a prerequisite of `build-release` AND OF NOTHING ELSE, on
reasoning the Makefile stated outright: the artifacts served the REMOTE panel,
so a build without them cost a developer one button they were not using.

That reasoning died with ADR-0057 and nothing updated with it. The result is a
binary that logs "helper: the local generation is not installed" at Start and
then refuses EVERY local pane — correctly, per ADR-0057, and unusably: there is
no terminal at all and nothing tells the developer why.

The e2e suite is not affected: e2e/stand.ts calls `make helpers` on its way up,
which is where this was noticed by contrast.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From a fresh checkout (or after `rm -f internal/helper/deploy/artifacts/bin/*.gz`),
   run `make dev-web`, `make dev` or `make build`.
2. Open the app and try to open a terminal pane.

Observed: the backend log carries "helper: the local generation is not
installed" and every local pane is refused. Expected: a pane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `make dev`, `make build` and `scripts/dev-web.sh` build the artifacts before
  the binary that embeds them, from the one owner of the build matrix
  (`make helpers`), never a second copy of it.
- `go build ./...` still compiles with no artifacts present — the package
  embeds its own .gitignore, and a bare checkout, `go vet` and every unit test
  must keep building. Compiling is not what broke.
- The Makefile comment that states the old rule is corrected rather than left
  standing, because it is now false and it is the first thing a reader trusts.
close_reason: Fixed in 208ddb8a: helpers is a prerequisite of build-server and dev, scripts/dev-web.sh calls the same target, and the Makefile comment stating the old release-only rule is rewritten. Verified: go build ./... still compiles with the artifacts removed, and the e2e stand (which already called make helpers) opens a local pane through the daemon — .e2e/home/.nocx/run/2-58ff6c33a3c66ec9.sock.

title: [bug] The approval window branches on 'run' while the tool has been 'session.run' since August: the command block and the variable expansion are dark
description:
frontend/src/agent-approval-prompt.tsx:493 reads `if (ask().tool !== 'run') return null`. The tool
has been named `session.run` since d71263ab (2026-08-30, nocx-9inie, "the shell tool joins the
family it belongs to") — internal/agenttools/registry.go:378 is the registration and
internal/assistant/execute.go:954 compares against the same string. That commit's own message says
"the renderer never branched on it"; this line is the one place it did, and it was missed.

So for EVERY real command proposal the gate is false and four things are dark in production:

- the lead sentence "The assistant wants to run this command";
- the command's own labelled CodeBlock (aria-label "The command this question is about"), which is
  nocx-njn8s's whole deliverable;
- the variable expansion beside it, because <Show when={expandedCommand()}> is nested inside that
  same branch — that is nocx-4h0m7.5's whole deliverable;
- and statedInTheWindow() therefore stops claiming `command`, so a single-line command (no newline,
  so not isMachineText) falls through to partitionedArguments() and is stated as a FACT ROW rather
  than as bytes in a block.

Two beads' worth of shipped work are invisible in the product while both suites are green.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: all ten command-proposal fixtures in agent-approval-prompt.test.tsx pass
`tool: 'run'`. The tests were written from the component, so they encode the component's belief
about the tool's name, and the component and its tests are wrong together — AGENTS.md testing rule
4, exactly. There is no contract check on the value either: agent.approvalRequested declares `tool`
as a plain string, so no schema disagrees with 'run'.

Found by the e2e for nocx-872jc (a219d68f), which addresses the command by its bytes rather than
through that block and so passes either way. This bead is filed separately because it is not the
skills epic's deliverable.

## Steps to Reproduce

Ask the assistant anything that makes it propose a shell command, with the policy gate set to ask.
The approval window opens with no lead sentence, no command block and no variable expansion; a
single-line command appears as a fact row.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The renderer compares against the name the backend actually sends, and it does so in ONE place
  that cannot drift from the registry silently — the fix is not merely changing the literal.
- Every command-proposal fixture in agent-approval-prompt.test.tsx carries the tool name production
  sends, and at least one test fails if the renderer's name and the registry's disagree.
- The lead sentence, the labelled command block and the variable expansion are all drawn again for
  a proposal of the shipped tool, asserted through a test that would have caught this.
close_reason: bcba9918. The name is no longer a bare string on either side: contracts/agent.approvalRequested.schema.json enumerates tool from internal/agenttools' declaration table, which makes the generated renderer type a union; the two by-name branches are declared once each with 'satisfies AgentApprovalRequested[tool]', so a dead name is a compile error at the declaration (TS1360) and again at the comparison (TS2367); and TestApprovalRequestedToolEnumMatchesTheTable asserts the enum and the table are one set, naming both directions. Demonstrated: renaming session.run to shell.run in registry.go alone reddens the Go test; bringing the contract into line to satisfy it then reddens both tsc projects, every fixture, and a vitest case that needs no type checking. Reverted, registry.go verified clean. The enum also found three dead frontend names (readScreen, files.write, someone.elses.tool) and four Go 'run' fixtures, two of them over-the-wire contract tests asserting a name the socket no longer carries. NOT PROVED: no end-to-end check watches the four repaired things in the shipped product — the new assertions are component-level and e2e/read-every-byte.spec.ts passes either way by design; and nothing tests the claim that only declaration names can reach this notification (read from einoadapter.go's WrapInvokableToolCall). The same trap un-fired elsewhere is nocx-scoy0.

title: The two bootstrap facts died with the local fork, and the diagnosis they carried died with them
description:
nocx-ie23r.3 deleted internal/bootstrapprogress whole, together with the
transport sink, LaunchOptions.BootstrapFD, its applyIntegrationLoss arm and 530
lines of tests. The reason given was correct as far as it went -- the descriptor
had to be inherited by a child the COORDINATOR forked, and after .3 the
coordinator forks nothing -- and the deadcode ratchet made leaving it a new
violation.

WHAT WENT WITH IT is not a mechanism but a DIAGNOSIS, and its package comment is
the argument for filing this:

  "It exists because 'the shell never proved itself' had exactly one detector --
   the handshake bound expiring -- and that one signal cannot tell three very
   different situations apart... The only thing left was ten seconds of silence,
   identical to a shell that never started and to a rc that hung."

  neither fact         our rcfile never began executing
  the first only       the user's startup did not return control
  both, and no hello   our own bootstrap broke after the user's rc

That was measured on the shipped app against a real foreign terminal wrapper,
which holds our end of the socketpair open so no EOF ever arrives either.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW, NOT LESS. ADR-0057 removed the local fallback: when a
local pane does not come up there is no Tier A behind it, and nocx-ie23r.4
requires a refusal naming what failed, why, and what to do. "Ten seconds of
silence" is exactly the input that cannot produce that sentence. The epic that
raised the bar on the diagnosis is the one that deleted the instrument.

AND THE FORK DID NOT DISAPPEAR, IT MOVED. internal/helper/session.LocalSpawner
forks the shell now, so the descriptor can be inherited from the DAEMON; what is
missing is the way back -- the two facts have to reach the coordinator over the
helper protocol instead of over a coordinator-held pipe. That is the work.

The package's own boundary must survive the move verbatim: this channel carries
no authority and must never acquire any (ADR-0024 decisions 2, 4 and 7). The
descriptor is inherited, anything descended from the shell can write to it,
nothing is verified, and a forged fact may spoil a diagnosis and do nothing
else. It may never open an editor, mint a domain, complete an attempt, or change
what the product does -- only what it says went wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The two facts reach the coordinator for a helper-hosted pane, local and
  remote, and the three-way distinction above is asserted case by case: a shell
  that never started; a user rc that does not return; a bootstrap that broke
  after the rc returned. Three tests, three different sentences.
- The facts ride the helper protocol as data with no authority. A test asserts
  that a forged fact changes no product behaviour -- no domain, no attempt, no
  editor, no integration verdict -- only the text of a diagnosis.
- nocx-ie23r.4's refusal uses the distinction: a pane that failed to bootstrap
  says WHICH of the three happened, and a test reads that off the real wire.
- The deleted tests come back in substance, retargeted at the new carrier. The
  530 lines are recoverable from 6e2a97ac^; do not rewrite from memory what can
  be read.

title: A peer that answers and hangs up mid-handshake reports one of three errors, chosen by a race
description:
Found while building nocx-ie23r.1 and deliberately NOT fixed there: fixing it
means re-deciding SocketConn's semantics, which the remote path shares.

Over the local socket, a peer that answers and then hangs up mid-handshake
produces THREE different errors depending on which goroutine wins:

  - ErrNotOurHelper  -- the read pump saw what the peer said
  - ErrLost          -- SocketConn calls a peer close transport loss (pinned by
                        its own test)
  - a bare EPIPE from the hello write, with no sentinel at all

client.Dial selects over the first two, and Go resolves a select at random. It
surfaced the honest way: a test written to pin ErrNotOurHelper failed two
DIFFERENT ways in two runs.

WHY IT IS P1 RATHER THAN A CURIOSITY. ADR-0057 and nocx-ie23r.4 require a
refusal to name what failed, why, and what to do, with the reason drawn from a
CLOSED SET. This failure is in no set: the same physical event answers with three
names, one of which (ErrLost) says transport loss about a peer that spoke. A
refusal built on it either names the wrong cause or names a different one each
run, and a person cannot act on either.

AGENTS.md's own rule applies: a flake is a defect, not weather. The run that gave
a stable answer is the one that got lucky.

nocx-ie23r.1 worked around it rather than papering over it: its fixture is an
impostor that STAYS CONNECTED, which is deterministic (ErrSentinelTimeout) and
isolates "answered wrong" from "went away". The workaround is honest and the
underlying ambiguity is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A peer that answers and hangs up mid-handshake yields ONE named error, the same
  one every run, and a test runs the case enough times to prove the select is no
  longer deciding it.
- The three current outcomes are each reachable only by the event they actually
  describe: a peer that spoke wrongly is never reported as transport loss, and a
  write that failed before any answer is never reported as a wrong answer.
- The remote path keeps the same guarantee, since SocketConn is shared. Whatever
  is decided is decided once, for both carriers.
- The error is in the closed set ADR-0057's refusal draws from, or the set gains
  it deliberately.

title: The daemon never exits: D2's lifecycle is designed and not implemented
description:
D2 of the generation-daemon lifecycle design says the daemon keeps running through
bridge EOF and through the last detach, EXITS when its last session exits, and
gives a daemon that has never owned a session one bounded startup grace -- with
the admission-versus-shutdown transition atomic, the listener entering a
non-admitting draining state BEFORE it concludes the session count is zero, so no
spawn is ever acknowledged by a daemon that then exits.

None of it is in the tree. endpoint.Serve runs until its context is cancelled or
its listener closes; cmd/nocx-helper supplies a context cancelled only by SIGINT
and SIGTERM; session.Service has no empty-session callback, no grace and no
draining state; a process exiting removes its session and nothing else. grep over
internal/helper and cmd/nocx-helper for a grace or a last-session shutdown
returns nothing.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is why this is P1 rather than a note:

1. A generation never retires itself, so it holds its lifetime lock forever.
   nocx-wrugm's retirement -- "an old generation lingers exactly as long as it
   still holds a session" -- rests on a premise that is currently false, which
   makes this a prerequisite of that epic rather than a detail inside it.
2. Any reasoning that starts from "the daemon dies with its last session" is
   reasoning about a design and not about this tree. That sentence has already
   been used as a load-bearing argument once (nocx-dkawo.15, where the record's
   lifetime was said to coincide with its participants' by construction). The
   conclusion there survives -- a record in memory dies with its process either
   way -- but the argument as stated was about D2 and D2 is not built.

Found while writing the local-helper design (adversarial review by codex,
verified against the tree by grep).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A daemon whose last session exits shuts down: its lock is released, its
  endpoint is unlinked, and a probe afterwards reports it gone.
- A daemon that has never owned a session exits after a bounded startup grace
  whose length is derived from measured launch-to-first-spawn p99, not chosen.
- The transition is ATOMIC: at the deadline either a first-session admission wins
  and the daemon stays, or shutdown wins and every subsequent spawn is REFUSED.
  A caller either gets a session or a clean refusal, never a promise nobody
  keeps. There is a test that races a spawn against the deadline.
- Bridge EOF and last detach are NOT shutdown, and each has a test: the pid is
  unchanged, the lock still held, the session's process still running.

title: A finding says which file it was found in, and support files are scanned too
description:
Named as a deliberate gap when the bundle landed (b32ba7f4, nocx-0bsa4.1).

skill.Scan reads the BODY of a SKILL.md and nothing else. Now that a skill can carry references/ and scripts/, a bundled setup.sh gets no findings anywhere: not in the install dialog, and not on the card where the person reviews it before turning the skill on. The one file whose contents most warrant a look is the one nothing looks at.

This belongs to this epic and not to the bundle's, because spec §8 puts findings "marked in place" in the viewer: one capability in three places. A second finding surface built beside it is exactly what this epic exists to prevent.

What it needs, and why it was not folded into the bundle work: Finding carries patternId, line and lineNumber, and says nothing about WHICH file it was found in. Adding a path is a contract change to agent.approvalRequested and skills.preview both, plus their generated types and their consumers — and the shape those consumers want depends on what the card draws, which is why it waits for the card.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A finding names the file it was found in, and one vocabulary says it: the same Finding shape reaches the approval question, the install dialog and the card.
- Every text file of a bundle is scanned, not only SKILL.md, and a test drives a finding in a support file.
- The card marks a finding on the line it matched, in the file where it sits — not summarised beside the list.
- The wire change is declared in contracts/ with additionalProperties false, generated, and asserted over the socket; the generated types land with their consumers in the same commit or the dead-exports ratchet refuses them.
- Scanning stays advisory: a finding never refuses an install and never disables a skill.
close_reason: 74c4540a. Path is a field of skill.Finding and a parameter of Scan, so a finding cannot be produced without naming a file; AuditFinding deleted as the second vocabulary. scanBundleFiles scans every fetched bundle file in Preview. skills.file carries findings scanned over exactly the bytes it returns, and FileReadout marks the matched line in the file itself — marks live only on the text outcome, so a refused file has none by construction. Contracts moved with additionalProperties false and asserted over the socket; generated types landed with their consumers. Tests: TestPreview_AFindingInABundledScriptNamesTheScript, TestFindingsAlwaysNameAFile, TestInstall_AFindingInASupportFileRefusesNothing, TestSkillsFile_AMatchedLineInASupportFileArrivesWithTheBytes (no engine wired), and TestSkillsAudit_ReadingACardSpendsNoModelCall extended to open scripts/fetch.sh at call count 0. NOT proved: nothing visual is verified (the CSS test asserts declarations, not that a mark is legible; no theme-sweep contrast test), and no e2e watched it.

title: Answer this now opens a dialog whose three answers include the state you are already in
description:
Reported by the owner on first sight of the shipped page, with a screenshot: five unanswered questions, each with Answer this now. Open one, choose Ask every time, and the page looks exactly as it did — as though nothing was answered.

Three defects, one shape.

1. ASK EVERY TIME IS NOT A THIRD ANSWER FOR AN UNANSWERED ROW. It IS the unanswered state. So the panel offers three options of which one is a no-op indistinguishable from Cancel, and a person who picks it concludes the page did not take their answer. Not answered yet is where the row already was and where it stays.

2. FOR AN ANSWERED ROW, ASK EVERY TIME AND FORGET ARE THE SAME ACT under two names. Taking an answer back and setting the row to ask are one thing, and a surface with two names for one concept is the duplication AD-8 exists to prevent. Forget also previews what it releases; the panel's third button does not, so the two names are not even equally safe.

3. THE DIALOG IS NOT EARNING ITSELF ON THE UNANSWERED PATH. Answer this now and Change open the same change panel. That panel carries two things a row cannot: the place picker and the sentence explaining why Allowed is missing. For an unanswered row it carries neither — there are no places yet (its own fallback says nocx has not learned any places yet), and Allowed is always offered for a row. So the click buys a person nothing and costs them the sense that answering worked.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings, Assistant permissions, on a fresh profile.
2. Not answered yet lists five questions. Press Answer this now on any of them.
3. Choose Ask every time.
4. The panel closes and the page is unchanged. Nothing says the answer was taken, because there was nothing to take.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An unanswered question offers its real answers where it is asked, without a dialog. A test drives them from the row.
- Ask every time is not offered as an answer to a question nobody has answered. If it is shown at all it is shown as the state the row is in, never as a button that changes nothing.
- On an answered row, taking the answer back has ONE name and one behaviour, and it previews what it releases the way Forget does today.
- The panel survives only where it carries what a row cannot: the places, and the reason Allowed is missing. A test asserts a row with nothing extra to say does not open one.
- No new vocabulary: the words already on the page are the words.
close_reason: Merged as 5f823a96 (worker 68a63e4f). ANSWER_ORDER is two answers, not three, and that one line settles all three defects: Ask every time is the STATE of an unanswered question, not an answer to it. Red first, and the second red named the defect exactly: 'a control wrote the row the state it was already in: expected {decision: ask, scopes: []} to not deeply equal {decision: ask, scopes: []}' — that is Answer this now then Ask every time, a write that leaves the row precisely where it was. The row now carries its answers; the panel carries the places, and only the places (panelCarriesMore is places().length > 0 for a row) — because canBeAllowed never withholds anything from a row, which has no selector, so the places were the only thing the dialog owned. Where places exist the panel survives and draws the answers beside them: what may happen and where are one decision. Row and panel build the same control from one answerButton and write through one answerWith, so they cannot drift. The unanswered row STATES 'Ask every time' in its kind badge — said, never offered. Taking an answer back has one name: Forget, with its preview. Frontend suite 6240 tests green; both epic e2e specs green in the container after the harness change.

title: Quit nocx, open it again, and the build is still running
description:
The epic happy path, end to end, through cmd/nocx-server - the SHIPPED coordinator, not a harness beside it.

This is the sentence the epic exists for: a local pane program survives the nocx
that started it, which the helper has always given a remote session and a local
one has never had.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Start a long-running program in a LOCAL pane through cmd/nocx-server; stop the
  backend; start it again. The process pid is unchanged, the pane reattaches to
  it, and its output continues.
- The check watches the sequence end to end and reads the pid from the operating
  system, not from a record nocx wrote about itself.
- Two coordinators reaching for the same generation produce one serving daemon and
  no error surface.

title: A local pane is opened through the helper, and the second PTY owner is gone
description:
Design L1 and L6 of .internal/specs/2026-09-04-the-local-helper-design.md
(revision 2). The carrier, the local install and the idempotency key landed in
nocx-ie23r.1 (fc453786); this is what makes a pane use them.

A local pane is opened today by localPTYFactory calling pty.NewLocal in the
backend, so it dies with the backend. After this the destination resolves to the
local generation and a carrier, exactly as a remote one resolves to its
generation and the bridge.

internal/pty does NOT disappear and must not: the helper's session.LocalSpawner
already spawns through pty.NewLocal (spawn_local.go:85). What moves is the
CALLER.

TWO THINGS REVISION 2 CORRECTED, and both change the size of this bead:

1. localPTYFactory is NOT just a PTY constructor. The type spans
   internal/app/app.go:2296-2673 and is constructed at :694. Besides NewPTY it
   owns the shell-replacement watcher (:2634), integration status reporting
   (:2660) and bootstrap-progress plumbing (:2673). Each needs a destination --
   the daemon, the open path, or deletion -- NAMED before the work starts.
2. Every helper route is gated on the destination being remote, by construction:
