   helperRegistry.OpenHosted returns "not mine" unless cfg.Kind ==
   session.KindRemote and then probes over ssh (internal/app/helper_git.go:
   455-470); sessionOpener calls it only on the remote branch; cold-start
   readoption refuses any binding without Host, ProfileID and HelperCommand and
   adopts as KindRemote (internal/app/session_readopt.go:129-190, :348-363). A
   local hosted-open and a local durable binding are new code, not a new case in
   an existing switch.

WHERE THE HISTORY SAYS TO BE CAREFUL (repowise, verified against git log):
app.go is a bug magnet -- 30 fixes in 6 months, last 2 days ago, hotspot 98%,
and `New` is a brain method carrying 14 of those fixes. session_readopt.go's
`Readopt` is already the file's most complex conditional. A local branch
appended to either is how they become unreadable; the branch goes behind a seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opening a local pane goes through the local endpoint. The shell process is a
  child of the DAEMON, not of the backend, and the test asserts the parentage
  rather than the code path.
- localPTYFactory is DELETED, not bypassed, and its four responsibilities each
  have a named destination in the commit message.
- A source-walking test over the packages on the local open path fails if
  pty.NewLocal is constructed anywhere but internal/helper/session -- the shape
  of internal/helper/endpoint's no_tcp_listener_test.go. A grep at review cannot
  hold this: D11 exists so a local special case is impossible to reintroduce by
  accident.
- UNIQUENESS IS NOT REACHABILITY. That test passes on a tree where local open is
  broken everywhere, so it is paired with a real open through cmd/nocx-server
  proving the one constructor is reached through the socket.
- Everything a local pane had keeps working through the new owner: the shell
  integration activation environment, resize, signals, and the exit status. Each
  is a test, not a claim.
- The pane's durable claim is written BEFORE the spawn, using the idempotency key
  nocx-ie23r.1 added (L7), so a backend that dies between the two comes back to
  the session rather than to a live PTY nothing claims.

## Deliberately out

- The unreconciled path and the eighth cause (nocx-ie23r.2).
- The refusal's wording and its closed sets (nocx-ie23r.4).
- Any change to the remote path's behaviour.
close_reason:
A local pane is opened on this machine's helper daemon, and the backend owns no
PTYs. Commit 6e2a97ac, 47 files, +2130/-4425.

VERIFIED BY THE COORDINATOR, not taken from the report: go build -tags gtk3 ./...
green; TestOnlyTheHelperConstructsALocalPTY green; and the three that carry the
claim -- TestALocalPaneIsTheDaemonsChild,
TestALocalPaneIsRefusedWhenThisMachineHasNoHelper,
TestALocalOpenClaimsThePaneBeforeItSpawns -- run green here in 11s.
deadcode -whylive reaches localHelperOpener.OpenHosted from
transport.sessionOpener.Open, and the worker printed the CONTRAST beside it
(sqliteContent.AddEdge, "reachable only through reflection") so the run is
evidence rather than a formality.

SHAPE. internal/app/helper_local.go is the local route; helper_hosted.go is the
spawn-attach-adopt half EXTRACTED ONCE and shared with the remote route rather
than copied; hostedOpeners is a four-line dispatcher, so neither OpenHosted nor
sessionOpener.Open nor Readopt grew an arm -- which is what the brief asked for,
because all three were already the most complex conditionals in their files.
internal/transport drops `cfg.Kind == KindRemote &&` from its helper branch: the
seam is asked for every destination and each opener answers for what it owns.
session.Reg keeps its PTYFactory seam and the shipped root supplies NONE, so a
local session with no helper is refused in the words Reg.Open already used for a
missing ssh factory -- ADR-0057 enforced by construction rather than by a check.

THE TWO TESTS THAT WERE THE POINT, both delivered:
- The source walk over internal/app fails if pty.NewLocal is constructed outside
  internal/helper/session, and it was PROVED TO FIRE: a temporary construction in
  internal/app made it red with file and position named.
- And a real open, because uniqueness is not reachability: the shell is asked its
  own pid (echo $$), ps names its parent and what that parent runs, and the
  assertion is that the parent is NOT os.Getpid() and IS nocx-helper. Read off
  the operating system, not off a code path or a record nocx wrote.

Everything a local pane had, each as a test rather than a claim: the activation
environment, the capability never exported, resize, foreground signalling, exit
status. Plus L7: the claim is written before the spawn, and a refused open leaves
no claim.

THE FOUR DESTINATIONS for localPTYFactory's responsibilities, named as the brief
required: NewPTY -> the daemon (LocalSpawner already forks through internal/pty);
integration status reporting -> the open path, off the helper's launch record;
the shell-replacement watcher -> kept in the open path, since it is a kernel
question about a pid on this machine, now ending on sess.Done() rather than a pty
wrapper's Close; bootstrap-progress plumbing -> DELETED, see below.

FOUND ON THE WAY AND FIXED, all inside the path being built, all with tests:
(1) the in-memory zsh/POSIX launch never substituted the capability, so a
helper-hosted zsh got a lane, a domain, an epoch and an fd and nothing to
authenticate with -- invisible while no helper-hosted session ran zsh, and it
would have been EVERY local zsh pane; (2) WSServer.OpenSession never started the
hosted lifecycle bridge, so every backend-opened pane -- wave participants
included -- would have integrated never. That one is a defect in nocx-dkawo.6's
own work, found by the epic that started using it; (3) CreateSession could not
write a session in the default workspace on a fresh profile, no workspaces row
existing, so the first pane of a new install failed on a FOREIGN KEY. Latent
until local panes became hosted sessions; the fix inserts only
DefaultWorkspaceID and explicitly refuses to mint a workspace for a caller's
typo (AD-8); (4) a helper-hosted session could not be signalled at all --
AttachedSession answered none of the run-lease ladder's three questions. The seam
was added along with proto.SpawnParams.Pgid and its contract entry: addressing,
never authority.

TWO CONSEQUENCES FILED RATHER THAN ABSORBED, because each is a loss the commit
does not repay:
- nocx-ubo1i (P1): internal/bootstrapprogress was deleted whole with 530 lines of
  tests. The mechanism was genuinely unreachable after the coordinator stopped
  forking, but what died with it is a DIAGNOSIS -- the only thing that could tell
  "our rcfile never began", "the user's rc did not return" and "our bootstrap
  broke after it" apart from ten seconds of silence. ADR-0057 removed the local
  fallback and nocx-ie23r.4 demands a refusal that names a cause, so the epic
  that raised the bar deleted the instrument. The fork moved rather than
  vanished: LocalSpawner can inherit the descriptor and the facts can ride the
  helper protocol.
- nocx-8ahfr (P2): a local zsh pane changed tiers -- from the coordinator's
  on-disk transient-ZDOTDIR tier to the in-memory one, the person's own login zsh
  through fd 3 with no shadowing -- and about 800 lines of launcher_local_zsh_test
  went with the caller that was deleted. Probably better and arguably what N4
  always wanted, but nobody chose it as a change and the coverage was not
  retargeted except for the one test carrying the product assertion.

NOT VERIFIED HERE: procwatch is darwin-only (Linux returns ErrUnsupported), so
the shell-replacement watch on a NON-CHILD pid cannot be exercised on this host.
The kqueue registration is unchanged and only the pid's provenance moved, but
CI's backend job is where that gets its first real run -- worth reading its
result rather than assuming.

Also expected and environmental: 12 internal/shellintegration tests fail on this
Linux host for a missing GNU bash 3.2 fixture. Pre-existing, unrelated.

Nothing pushed; no PR.

title: A local session can be asked about, and its unreconciled state reaches the notice that already exists
description:
Design L5 of .internal/specs/2026-09-04-the-local-helper-design.md (revision 2).

REVISION 2 CORRECTS THIS BEAD. It was filed claiming this epic owns the rule
"ask before you delete, and unknown is not absent". It does not: that rule is
already built. dropDeadSessions and closeOpenEntries no longer exist -- they
survive only in comments. internal/content/reconcile_sqlite.go carries the three
verdicts including VerdictUnknown, and internal/app/session_reconcile.go states
the discipline in its header ("A FAILURE IS NEVER A VERDICT", with a causeFor
whose type cannot return one). It landed with nocx-k6p18.5.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is what makes that rule reach a local session:

1. An inventory for the LOCAL generation that can be asked. Every helper route
   today is gated on the destination being remote: helperRegistry.OpenHosted
   returns "not mine" unless cfg.Kind == session.KindRemote and then probes over
   ssh (internal/app/helper_git.go:455-470); cold-start readoption refuses any
   binding without Host, ProfileID and HelperCommand (session_readopt.go:129-190).
2. A durable binding that says which pane a local session belongs to, carrying a
   generation instead of a host and a profile.
3. The eighth cause. The unreconciled state ALREADY has a surface and a closed
   vocabulary, and a local one extends them rather than inventing a parallel
   pair: frontend/src/unreconciled-notice.tsx defines UnreconciledCause as seven
   values (notYetAsked, ambiguousInventory, noInventory, connectionRefused,
   timedOut, hostUnreachable, vaultSealed), unreconciledAccount(rows) builds the
   card, terminal-content.ts:4946 mounts it once per pane, and it travels the
   wire as restore-client.ts:42's `unreconciled: UnreconciledCause | null`. So a
   local endpoint that could not be asked is a NEW CAUSE plus a contract change,
   not a new component. The card's own rule binds it: it never claims the session
   ended and never claims it is running.

OBSERVED 2026-09-04, AND IT CORRECTS THE LINE ABOVE. A local session IS enrolled
as pending and DOES reach the notice today — it just reaches it with the wrong
answer. A dev stand on a pre-.3 tree, restarted, showed a local tab carrying:

  "5 commands in this tab: neither running nor finished
   Their session may still be running: nothing on this host can be asked
   whether that session is still there."

That is `noInventory` (session_reconcile.go:161/192 — no binding, so no
inventory owns the id) and verdict `unknown`. The card's rule is that it never
claims the session ended and never claims it is running; here the second half is
not merely cautious, it is FALSE. Those five commands were on a PTY the BACKEND
forked, so they died with the backend and are certainly gone. The truthful
verdict for a pre-.3 local session is `absent`.

So this bead is not only adding a cause for a case nobody reaches. It is
replacing a sentence the product says today that is untrue. After nocx-ie23r.3 a
local session survives the coordinator, which makes "may still be running"
finally a real possibility; what is owed here is the inventory that turns it back
into `live` or `absent`, and the eighth cause for when the local endpoint itself
cannot be asked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With the local endpoint unreachable at start, the local inventory WAS
  attempted, the session is unknown, its ledger rows survive, nothing is deleted,
  no replacement shell is spawned, and the pane shows the unreconciled notice
  with a cause naming the local endpoint. Asserted by making the endpoint
  unreachable, never by calling the reconciler directly. A safe default that
  never asks fails this.
- A reachable local generation that does not report the session yields absent and
  the rows are closed. The same input over an unreachable endpoint yields a
  different outcome, and one test holds both.
- The new cause is added to UnreconciledCause, to the contract, and to the
  generated renderer type in the same commit -- the schema is the declaration and
  the frontend type is generated from it.
- No second unreconciled surface is added.

title: The local carrier: one install, one handshake, a socket instead of an ssh lane
description:
Design L1, L2 and L7 of .internal/specs/2026-09-04-the-local-helper-design.md
(revision 2), plus the open questions 4-6 it names.

The helper binary ships embedded (helper/deploy/artifacts) and the daemon already
serves locally (cmd/nocx-helper serve, endpoint.Listen). What does not exist is
the backend reaching it: nothing constructs a HelperConn over endpoint.Dial, and
nothing installs the artifact onto the local filesystem.

One installer, two transports: locally the content-addressed directory is written
directly instead of over sftp, and the generation is the same content hash of the
same bytes. The handshake is NOT skipped locally - it is what proves the binary
answering is the generation we installed (D21), and a stale binary under ~/.nocx
is likelier on the machine where builds land than on a server.

L7 IS THIS BEAD TOO, because the carrier and the protocol are one change. The
helper mints the authoritative session id, so a backend that dies between the
spawn and the durable pane binding leaves a live PTY that no pane claims - and
with D2 unimplemented (nocx-2b0mq) it holds it forever. SpawnParams carries no
idempotency key today. The rule is the wave record's own, bought by the same
shape: the claim exists BEFORE the first irreversible effect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A local carrier wraps endpoint.Dial as a HelperConn and client.Dial completes
  the hello / sentinel / hello-ok handshake over it, against a daemon the test
  started.
- The install writes the same content-addressed layout the remote installer
  writes, from the embedded artifact, and a second install of the same generation
  is a no-op.
- A responder on the expected generation's socket answering with a WRONG content
  hash is rejected, and the refusal names the mismatch. (A mismatched binary at
  the install path hashes to a different generation and proves nothing about the
  handshake - do not use it as the fixture.)
- SpawnParams carries a caller-minted idempotency key, and a spawn repeated with
  the same key returns the same session rather than a second one.
- Every failure boundary has a test, and the INVARIANT IS STATED AS AN INTERVAL
  WITH BOTH ENDS, not as a moment. deploy.Ensure has a dozen: artifact selection,
  Lstat, removing an incomplete tree, Mkdir, temp create, write, sync, close,
  rename, directory sync, marker, verification read. Which of them leave a tree
  the next attempt may reuse, and which leave one it must remove first? Write the
  answer down in the package, not only in tests.
- Install succeeds but the process fails to start: the install remains reusable
  and no socket or lock claims a daemon exists.
- The detached child starts while the caller is cancelled: endpoint.Ensure
  currently returns on context cancellation WITHOUT terminating the process it
  started. Say what that daemon is, and how the retry tells it from a stale
  socket.
- Bind succeeds and then startup fails: the listener is established before the
  instance id is minted (cmd/nocx-helper/main.go:105-141), so an exit there
  leaves a socket with nothing behind it. Name which side repairs it and how a
  prober tells it from a daemon that is merely slow.
- A socket that accepts but answers a wrong hello stays UNKNOWN. Nobody unlinks a
  live endpoint because its protocol answer was unexpected.
- Lands wired: deadcode -whylive names a path from main() to the local carrier.

## Deliberately out

- The machine namespace and the socket-name width (nocx-1lj00). This bead
  inherits the layout as it is.
- D2's daemon lifecycle (nocx-2b0mq).
close_reason:
The local carrier, the local install and the idempotency key. Commit fc453786.

EVIDENCE a stranger can check, and the coordinator ran these rather than
believing them:
- deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive '.../internal/helper/local.Install' ./... prints
  cmd/nocx-server.main -> run -> App.Start -> App.installLocalHelper ->
  local.Install. The same for local.Open through cmd/nocx-helper's
  alreadyServing. Both land wired and neither chain is a stub.
- go build -tags gtk3 ./... green; the two wiring tests run green here in 2.6s;
  the worker's full run: internal/app 179s, every internal/helper package ok,
  under -race.

CRITERIA:
- Local carrier over endpoint.Dial performing the SAME hello/sentinel/hello-ok
  handshake as the ssh lane: internal/helper/local. cmd/nocx-helper's
  alreadyServing had hand-rolled that dial and handshake and now calls the one
  owner - a second implementation deleted rather than left beside the first.
- One installer, two transports; a second install of the same generation is a
  no-op, asserted by mtime.
- The handshake fixture is an impostor on the RIGHT generation's socket
  answering a wrong content hash. A mismatched binary at the install path was
  refused as the fixture, correctly: it hashes to a different generation and
  proves nothing about the handshake.
- SpawnParams.idempotencyKey (contracts/helper/session.spawn.params.schema.json,
  maxLength 128, ErrBadKey -> ErrCodeBadParams), and a repeated spawn answers
  with the first session. SessionEntry deliberately does not echo it: an
  idempotent spawn IS the lookup, so the pre-spawn claim finds its session by
  retrying rather than by a second field.
- THE INSTALL INTERVAL, both ends, written in the package and not only in tests:
  "usable from the moment its marker exists over a binary that hashes to the
  directory's key until something removes it; outside that interval it is a tree
  the next attempt must remove first, and there is no third state." Twelve
  boundaries in three groups, and the directory sync is the one that shows the
  boundary was actually found - the binary is fully in place there and still
  unusable. TestEveryInstallBoundaryLeavesATreeTheNextAttemptCanFinish fails
  each of eleven in turn.
- The three design holes answered rather than restated: an install claims bytes
  and never a process, so a start that dies leaves no socket and no lock; a
  cancelled caller's detached child is a legitimate helper of our own generation
  and killing it would be the wrong repair, and the retry never needs to tell it
  from a stale socket because net.Listen leaves no state where the file exists
  unbound; and the bind-then-fail window was SHRUNK rather than documented - the
  instance id is now minted before the bind, so no fallible step remains between
  binding and serving.
- Open question 2 closed by measurement: cold install 34ms, warm 3ms. The
  falsifier in section 8 does not fire; the install stays at Start.

SENT BACK ONCE, and this is the part worth reading. The first round satisfied
-whylive and left the seam unexecuted: withoutLocalHelperInstall() was applied to
every app test and nothing opted in, so Start -> installLocalHelper -> Install
was reachable and run by no test. That is the shape AGENTS.md names as the one
the ratchet cannot catch. internal/app/local_helper_install_test.go now opts in
on a HOME it owns: Start installs a generation that satisfies the completeness
predicate, a second start reuses it by mtime, and a refusing artifact source
leaves the backend SERVING - proven over the real socket with history.query,
not by Start returning nil - with the failure logged exactly once. Both tests
were shown to FAIL when the call site is stubbed out.

FOUND AND NOT FIXED HERE, filed as nocx-mkzp3 (P1): a peer that answers and
hangs up mid-handshake reports one of three errors chosen by a select race, one
of which claims transport loss about a peer that spoke. It breaks ADR-0057's
closed-set requirement for a refusal's reason. Not fixed inside this bead
because the fix re-decides SocketConn's semantics, which the remote path shares.
The bead's fixture works around it deterministically rather than papering over
it.

KNOWN AND DELIBERATE: nothing prunes a local generation, so each `make helpers`
rebuild leaves another ~4 MB under ~/.nocx/helper until retirement lands
(nocx-wrugm, whose prerequisite is nocx-2b0mq).

Nothing pushed; no PR.

title: Every local pane is the helper's, and its program survives nocx
description:
D11 of the level-1 design was decided on 2026-08-31 -- "The helper runs on every
machine, including yours. Locally the coordinator connects to its endpoint
directly... no 'local special case', and no code path that exists only for one
of them" -- and the local half was never built. The endpoint package says the
same thing in its own doc comment. What the tree actually does: the helper is
wired for git (helperGitFactory, app.go:820) and for remote sessions, while a
local pane is opened by pty.NewLocal in localPTYFactory (app.go:2472-2586), with
no branch that would choose the helper for a local destination.

The owner settled two things on 2026-09-04:

1. THE LOCAL PATH NO LONGER EXISTS WITHOUT THE HELPER. Not a preference for
   uniformity: a second PTY owner is a rarely-exercised path that diverges
   silently from the one everybody uses.
2. THERE IS NO FALLBACK. If the local helper cannot start, nocx does not open a
   terminal through some other route -- it SHOWS THE PERSON THE ERROR, ITS
   CAUSE AND WHAT TO DO. The distinction that makes this right: a remote host is
   an environment we do not control and a helper failure there must degrade; the
   local machine is an INSTALLATION, the binary ships with the app, and a daemon
   that will not start is a broken nocx rather than a reason to quietly run a
   different terminal.

Decided here rather than asked: THERE IS NO LOCAL CONSENT. The consent axis
(delivery-modes N3, ADR-0034) exists for a persistent footprint on SOMEBODY
ELSE'S machine. Locally there is nothing to deploy, the binary arrives with the
app, and D12 already froze the trust boundary at the Unix account.

WHAT THIS BUYS BESIDES UNIFORMITY, and it is the reason it is worth an epic:
a local pane gets what the helper already gives a remote one -- the program
survives the nocx that started it. Close the window, reopen it, and the build is
still running.

## Success Criteria

- Opening a local pane goes through the local helper endpoint. No caller in the
  session path constructs pty.NewLocal, and a test walks the local open path and
  asserts so -- the same shape as the endpoint package's existing no-TCP test.
- A program started in a local pane is still running, and its pane reattaches to
  it with its scrollback, after nocx is closed and reopened. One automated check
  watches exactly that, end to end, through cmd/nocx-server.
- When the local helper cannot start, the person is told in the product: what
  failed, why, and what to do about it. A refusal is never a blank pane and never
  a silently different terminal, and there is a test for the refusal path.
- No local consent surface is added, and none is asked for.

## Deliberately out

- Level 2 -- durable TABS with their ledger rows, and reaching them from another
  machine. That is a server, and it is nocx-6ojko onward.
- Any change to the remote path's behaviour.
- The orchestration dispatcher's move into the helper, which rides on this and is
  the wave epic's business.
