title: Subagent rows: the grid already draws them and we throw them away
description:
Measured across the three tools the owner named, 2026-09-03:

  termic  — does not model subagents at all. Its one subagent-aware line SKIPS sidechain turns
            (src-tauri/src/cli_server.rs:1682-1687) so the parent's last message can be found.
  herdr   — REFUSED deliberately, twice, after shipping the opposite and regressing. Its claude hook
            drops subagent events by name, because Claude's SubagentStop can arrive after the main
            turn already stopped and "never let it revive an idle pane"
            (assets/claude/herdr-agent-state.sh:52-59). Its opencode plugin tracks child sessions
            ONLY so they cannot speak for the pane.
  orca    — DOES model them, and its UI is the target: AgentSubagentSnapshot{id, agentType, model,
            description, state, startedAt}, synthetic rows grafted into the parent's lineage tree,
            chevron expanded by default because "spawned child agents are actionable work", "+N"
            when collapsed, no PTY of their own, click activates the parent.

But orca's carrier is the vendor hook and there is NO fallback: with no SubagentStart there are no
rows, no count, no chevron — and worse, the parent flips to done while children run. That is exactly
what D6 of the 2026-08-24 mechanism design forbids as a carrier, and herdr's two regressions are the
same failure observed independently.

WHAT WE HAVE THAT NONE OF THEM DO: a live VT grid. internal/agentdriver/testdata/captures/
claude-subagent.jsonl already draws, from 25s, a task panel with a row per child carrying name, task,
elapsed and token flow — "◯ Explore  List files in directory   11s · ↓ 11.6k tokens" — and the
elapsed ticks and the arrow flips direction. Everything orca gets from hooks, on screen, with no
vendor cooperation.

herdr cannot do this because its manifest engine is boolean and cannot extract a value. Ours is
boolean too, today; that is the blocker and it is filed separately.

THE RULE TO CARRY OVER, bought by herdr twice: a child fact may never decide the parent's state.
Same shape as the 2026-09-03 design's rule that a declared checkpoint may not decide wave state.

## Acceptance Criteria

A person watching a pane whose agent spawned children sees a row per child with its name and what it
is doing, and the count when collapsed. Watched end to end against claude-subagent.jsonl, which
already contains the frames.

A child row appearing or vanishing does not change the parent's screen state, asserted.

Hooks are not the carrier. Falsified if the rows disappear when no vendor hook is installed.
notes:
DELIBERATELY OUT: reading the agent's own transcript on disk. Owner decided 2026-09-03; recorded so it is not re-proposed.

The candidate was real and both other tools use it. termic reads ~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/<session>.jsonl
and skips turns marked isSidechain:true to find the parent's last message (cli_server.rs:1682-1687);
orca's AI Vault reads ~/.claude/projects/<enc>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl with a meta.json sidecar
(session-scanner-subagent-transcripts.ts:6-30).

MEASURED against claude-subagent.jsonl, which is why this is a finding and not a preference: the task
panel is drawn EXACTLY while children are alive — rows present at 25s through 38s, gone by 43s because
the child finished and the main turn resumed, and the child's result is on screen in the parent's own
transcript by 50s ('- frames/'). The screen covers the whole live window rather than part of it.

So the transcript adds two things and both are weak: the child's final result, which the parent prints
to screen anyway; and a window of roughly three seconds around 40s where the mode line says subagents
exist while the panel has already collapsed.

The stronger reason is that it is a FOURTH SOURCE CLASS with no rule. AD-6 governs the byte stream,
ADR-0024 the authenticated channel, D9 of the 2026-08-24 mechanism design names process exit and the
participant's own declaration. A file a vendor writes is none of those, so adopting it needs its own
decision — for a marginal gain, and Claude-only, so it could never be the general answer regardless.

If it is ever reconsidered, the trigger to look for is a case where children are LIVE and the screen
cannot name them for longer than the collapse window above.

title: The driver answers a scalar, and three things now need it to answer an observation
description:
Driver.Classify(panegrid.Frame) State returns one value (internal/agentdriver/agentdriver.go:104).
Three separate requirements have now each hit that wall, which is the signal it is the wall and not
three coincidences:

1. SUBAGENT ROWS. The claude-subagent capture draws a task panel carrying, per child, a name, a task
   description, an elapsed time and a token flow ("◯ Explore  List files in directory  11s · ↓ 11.6k
   tokens"). Today the whole panel reduces to the single word "working".
2. PROGRESS (nocx-tnx44, and nocx-i2pwl which names this same contradiction from the other side).
3. DECLARED CHECKPOINTS, from the 2026-09-03 mesh-and-progress design: the declared row and the
   measured row must be shown side by side and never merged, which needs two values where there is
   one.

Shape to decide: Classify returns an Observation — the screen state, plus OPTIONAL structured extras
the rule was able to extract. Optional matters: a rule that captured nothing yields the scalar it
yields today, so no agent regresses and no value is invented.

The grammar needs the matching half: VALUE EXTRACTION. Every predicate in internal/agentdriver/
predicate.go is boolean today, and so is herdr's manifest engine (src/detect/manifest.rs:154-181 has
contains/regex/all/any/not and no capture-group read) — which is precisely why herdr cannot report a
child count from a screen and had to take children from hooks or not at all. Extraction is the
capability that makes the screen a viable carrier.

Keep the two properties that already hold: evaluation reads only the frame it was handed, and the
predicate bounds stay engine-owned. An extractor is a region plus a pattern, and the region's cap is
still the engine's.

## Acceptance Criteria

Driver answers an observation whose scalar state is byte-for-byte what it answers today for every
frame in testdata/captures. A rule that extracts nothing produces an observation with no extras. At
least one extractor exists with a test that it captures and a test that it refuses its near-miss,
and the region cap still bounds it.

Falsified if the extras can decide the scalar state, or if an extractor can read outside a capped
region.
close_reason: Driver answers Observation{State, Extras}. agentdriver.go: Observation/Extra/Observer + Registry.Observe (Registry.Classify is now its projection). document.go: RegionSpec shared by Pred and the new Extractor; documentDriver.Observe decides the branch walk first and extracts after, so extras cannot reach a branch; validate refuses an uncapped extractor, one over maxExtractorRows=16, an unbound anchor, an uncompilable pattern and one naming no capture group. predicate.go: one region walk (eachRow) behind anyRow and the new capture. claude.rule.json declares the 'subagents' extractor, proven on testdata/captures/claude-subagent.jsonl (rows 23s-39s, glyph/name/task/elapsed/flow/tokens; absent fields absent, not empty). Corpus unchanged: 2529 frames x 9 captures sampled every 250ms are byte-for-byte identical to HEAD (same md5); adversarially breaking the task-panel branch and the spinner suffix turns tests red. Tests: internal/agentdriver/observation_test.go, extract_test.go. Commits 2ea9c640 and 7c8792b4 (the second wires rowOpensWith, which no document could name and the deadcode ratchet had been reporting since the rule became a document).

title: The lifecycle capability travels outbound on the very descriptor it exists to defend against
description:
ADR-0024 states the property twice, and it is the stated reason the per-epoch capability is
mandatory rather than belt-and-braces:

  "The transport stops everything that can only write to the terminal; the capability stops a
   DESCENDANT THAT INHERITED THE TRANSPORT."
  "a descendant that inherited the descriptor still cannot produce the capability, which is
   exactly the measurement that made the capability mandatory"
  (docs/decisions/0024-…md, decision 2's measurement and the decision-10 re-read at :741-745)

internal/lifecycle/kernel.go:1284 asserts the same in a production comment.

READ FROM THE CODE, not measured at runtime: the capability is written in cleartext on the
OUTBOUND half of that same descriptor.

  • internal/lifecyclecodec/codec.go:449 — Encode sets Cap: hex.EncodeToString(env.Capability[:])
    on every outbound frame. Encode's own comment names it the outbound half.
  • Four outbound constructors populate it: internal/lifecycle/kernel.go:864, :875, :1039, :1050
    (agentOutbound, grantOutbound, the accept path, refreshOutbound).
  • The carrier is one socketpair whose child end is handed over via exec.Cmd.ExtraFiles, which
    clears FD_CLOEXEC, and nocx.bash cannot close it — it needs it for the shell's life.
  • Its NUMBER is exported: internal/shellintegration/launcher.go:129 writes NOCX_LIFECYCLE_FD into
    the env block and :149 names it in the export line (:132/:152 for NOCX_LIFECYCLE_PORT).

So the secret that exists to distinguish the shell from its descendants is placed on the channel
every descendant inherits, addressed by a variable every descendant can read. The inbound
protection (a non-exported shell variable, export -n at two sites) is real and is not the issue;
the outbound direction undoes what it buys.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and must be before this is called exploitable: a descendant reading a
frame races the shell's own reader, and no such race has been run. That is a difference of
degree, not of kind — but it is the difference between "the property does not hold by
construction" (established, from the code) and "here is a working extraction" (NOT established,
and deliberately not attempted).

AND THE TEST THAT GUARDS IT CANNOT SEE THIS. internal/lifecycle/adopt_test.go:72-78 comments "a
descendant … cannot know the capability" and then forges with Capability{} — the ZERO value,
which an explicit zero check refuses. It proves a descendant that guesses NOTHING fails. It never
exercises a descendant that READ the value. Testing rule 1: it asserts what the code does, not
what an actor can do.

Found 2026-09-03 while researching the wave authority model (nocx-z3nkr), which cannot be written
on top of this: the whole model rests on "only the enrolled tree may speak for the participant".

## Steps to Reproduce

Read the four sites above together. No runtime step is claimed.

## Acceptance Criteria

Either the outbound frame stops carrying the capability and a test asserts an outbound frame
contains no bearer material; or ADR-0024's decision-2 measurement is amended to say plainly that
a descendant CAN obtain it and what then justifies the capability, with kernel.go:1284 and
adopt_test.go corrected in the same commit. Not left with the code and the comment disagreeing.

A test that exercises a descendant holding a capability it READ, rather than one it zeroed.
close_reason: Fixed as 182191e0. The exposure was REAL, not a misreading: the bearer rode the outbound half of the very descriptor it exists to defend, handed over with ExtraFiles which clears FD_CLOEXEC, its number exported. The fix is a deletion because the field never did the work it appeared to: its one production reader was the shell's accept check, which could not authenticate the peer because the shell's own hello hands that peer the capability a frame earlier — dom plus epoch answer 'is this accept mine' out of non-secret values. Nothing else validates it (remote adapter routes only to an already-accepted claimant; adoption takes the bearer from the helper's control channel; the JSON-RPC contract forbids it reaching the renderer). New codec test drives a real kernel through all five outbound kinds, watched red on every one. adopt_test now refuses four guesses including the value HARVESTED from the channel, replacing the zero-guess that could never fail. Five stale documents corrected, ADR-0024 amended. Deliberately not closed: nocx-zo2ng, a nested grant still carries the CHILD's capability on the parent's descriptor.

title: Brainstorming: mesh from day one, and progress a participant declares
description:
Two amendments the owner raised against .internal/specs/2026-08-24-orchestration-mechanism-design.md:

1. D10 decided STAR now with addressable nodes, mesh deferred. Owner: do mesh from the start,
   every participant may address every other.
2. New: ask agents to DECLARE progress, so a percentage (or equivalent) can be displayed.

Prior art already settled and shipped, which this must extend rather than duplicate:
nocx-9le.5.7/.9 (progress is live and lossy, completion retained and flushed on attach; state
comes from the result, never from a progress sample; a progress frame does not mint and a late
one does not resurrect), nocx-szb40 (observation with provenance, reduced, bound to epoch +
lifecycle domain + attempt + output offset), nocx-tnx44 (progress as a moving|stalled facet from
transcript growth, not frame equality).

Feeds nocx-z3nkr (the authority model), which cannot be written until the topology is decided.

## Acceptance Criteria

Both amendments are answered in a design doc under .internal/specs/, the owner has approved it,
and the mechanism design references the answers rather than restating them. The doc states what
mesh does to the authority model, to the per-fact deadline and to the wait-for graph, and what a
declared progress value may and may not decide.
notes:
OWNER DECISIONS, 2026-09-03.

MESH. Amends D10. 'Everyone talks to everyone' conflates two axes, and separating them is the
same distinction nocx-z3nkr says is missing (membership is not delegation):
  axis 1, may A TALK to B  -> MESH from day one.
  axis 2, may A ACT on B (reassign scope, interrupt, spawn, close) -> STAR, coordinator only.
The wire is general, the authority graph stays a tree, delegate-further is deferred and not
denied. Rationale the owner accepted: axis 2 costs transitive revocation and a rule for what a
human takeover of B does to A's rights over B, in the very authority model we are about to write;
axis 1 costs nothing extra because D10 already made nodes addressable.
Consequences to write up: the per-fact deadline of D2 belongs to the RECIPIENT's supervision and
still escalates coordinator -> human, so the coordinator learns 'B has an undispatched fact from
A' WITHOUT its content (preserves the content/commitment split named in D10's rejected column);
D12's wait-for cycles become multi-hop and load-bearing in v1 rather than theoretical; the
busy-pane delivery weakness now applies to every pair, not just coordinator->worker.

DECLARED PROGRESS. New. Owner: workers have no reliably pre-known scope, may have one task, so
step k-of-n is wrong; wants CHECKPOINTS, and accepts the number is approximate and may freeze
('Может ли воркер застыть на 90%? Конечно может.').
  Shape: a named checkpoint declared when reached, APPENDED not overwritten - the szb40
  observation model, so no new machinery. No denominator. Optional approximate estimate on the
  checkpoint. Optional artifact reference (commit/file/test run) which the coordinator MAY
  corroborate from what we already own; a gradient, not a requirement.
  Carrier: the existing 'Report, structurally' call of §7.2. No new carrier, no vendor hooks.
  Class: persuasion per §5 - raises probability, carries no invariant.
  Rules inherited verbatim from the SHIPPED transfer decision nocx-9le.5.9/.7: state comes from
  the result, never from a progress sample; a progress declaration does not MINT a participant;
  a late one does not RESURRECT a finished one; progress is live and lossy while the report is
  retained and flushed on attach. Bound to epoch + lifecycle domain + attempt + output offset so
  a claim from a previous incarnation cannot attach to a new one.
  WHY THE FREEZE IS NOT A DEFECT: the declared row is ALLOWED to lie because the measured row
  beside it catches the lie. nocx-tnx44's moving|stalled comes from transcript growth, so a stuck
  worker reads '90% · stalled'. The two rows never merge. A lone percentage rendered as measured
  would be the defect; a percentage beside an independently measured 'stalled' is true and more
  useful than either half.
  WAKE: a checkpoint does NOT wake the coordinator and does NOT enter D2's undispatched-fact set
  or start a deadline - it is information, not a fact needing judgement, and is read at the
  coordinator's next call. It reaches the human's SCREEN immediately regardless, because the
  backend watches always. Costs zero tokens.
close_reason: Spec written, approved and committed as e301aef5. Amends D10 (mesh on talk, star on act) and adds declared checkpoints plus the advisor as a third source to the mechanism design.

title: The ssh-child harness sends suspend and activate back to back, so the wait passes on the pre-suspend state
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. internal/app, TestLiveSshd_SSHChildAssembly_LateCandidateAfterParentActivation.
2. Тест шлёт `h.suspendParent(); h.activateParent()` подряд, затем ждёт
   `parent == DomainEstablished && lane.Domain == parent`.

## Что происходит

Оба кадра пишутся в слушатель и применяются его насосом, так что «послал» — не
то же, что «применилось». Пока не применён ни один, предикат ожидания УЖЕ
истинен: родитель Established и владеет полосой с самого establishParent. То
есть ожидание проходит на состоянии, МИМО которого оно должно ждать. Дальше
насос применяет suspend, следующее утверждение читает родителя и видит
Suspended, и только потом применяется activate.

На CI (run 33732628468, ci-mac, коммит 05be3675):

    ssh_child_assembly_test.go:1058: parent state after late hello = 3, want Established

3 — это DomainSuspended. На Linux не воспроизводится ни при -count=120 -race:
насос там успевает между двумя send.

Воспроизведено детерминированно: если придержать оба кадра до конца ожидания,
затем применить suspend и применить activate заметно позже, отказ повторяется
СЛОВО В СЛОВО. То есть это дефект теста, а не ядра — поздний кандидат
отвергается корректно, и ребёнок остаётся Pending.

Четыре из пяти вызовов `suspendParent()` уже несли это ожидание рядом с собой,
одно из них с комментарием «the suspend frame is processed by the listener's
pump; wait for it». Пятый — тот, где два кадра идут подряд и между ними нет
ничего, — его не нёс.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Ожидание живёт в самом `suspendParent()`, а не у вызывающих, чтобы шестой
  вызывающий не мог его забыть.
* Четыре копии рядом с вызовами убраны.
* Красный-затем-зелёный на одном дереве под принудительным окном.
close_reason: Ожидание перенесено в suspendParent, четыре копии убраны. Красный-затем-зелёный под принудительным окном воспроизводит текст CI слово в слово. Коммит 23056b66.

title: The remote-commit spec latches on the hook's first line, not on the commit
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. e2e/git-remote.spec.ts:248, «a commit from the panel, on a remote host,
   through its own pre-commit hook».
2. Хук фикстуры (cmd/e2e-sshd/main.go:1071-1078) первым делом делает
   `touch $marker`, а ПОТОМ печатает ~88 KiB — 500 строк в stdout и 500 в
   stderr, ради чего фикстура и существует.
3. Спек ждёт появления маркера и сразу читает HEAD.

## Что происходит

Git двигает ветку только после того, как pre-commit хук ЗАВЕРШИЛСЯ. Между
появлением маркера и перемещением HEAD лежит целый хук с его выводом, и в этом
интервале репозиторий всё ещё на `initial`. Опрос возвращается внутри этого
интервала, следующая строка читает HEAD внутри него же — и падает.

Наблюдалось: CI run 33729238718, ci-e2e (webkit), 263 passed / 1 failed;
chromium той же ноги зелёный. В снятом DOM видно мёртвое соединение и «Connection
lost» — это НЕ причина: `finally` спека шлёт фикстуре SIGKILL
(git-remote.spec.ts:394) до того, как пишется трасса, так что снимок показывает
уборку, а не отказ.

Спек — член зонтичного nocx-6wgcw, и это первый его случай, разобранный до
причины.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Опрос ждёт события, о котором утверждение: HEAD несёт сообщение.
* Маркер остаётся утверждением — но как факт о том, КАК коммит случился
  (хук отработал на удалённой машине), а не как защёлка «готово».
* Красный-затем-зелёный: с расширенным интервалом в хуке старая защёлка
  падает стабильно, новая проходит.
close_reason: Защёлка перенесена на HEAD; красный-затем-зелёный в webkit-контейнере, красный воспроизводит текст CI побайтово. Интервал в хуке фикстуры расширен, чтобы старая защёлка падала каждый раз. Коммит 05be3675.

title: The import ask spends its source read on an empty destination and throws the export away
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Открыть API testing → Import collection, пока `api.collections.list` ещё
   в полёте (загруженная машина, или человек, который щёлкает насквозь).
2. Вставить Postman-экспорт в поле вставки.
3. Нажать карандаш «Change where this goes» — этот клик снимает фокус с поля
   вставки и есть обычный порядок действий.

## Что происходит

`onCommitPaste` зовёт `previewSource(readable, postmanDest().trim(), …,
firstRead=true)`. `previewPostman` отвечает сразу на два вопроса — что
внутри архива и примет ли его назначение, — поэтому бэкенд отказывает целиком:
«Invalid params: dest is required» (ws_api_handlers.go validateAPIFolderPath).

Смертельным это делает собственное правило `previewSource`, применённое не к
тому отказу: чтение ИСТОЧНИКА при отказе забывает источник, потому что
отказали именно источнику. Здесь архив в порядке, а МЕСТА не было — и диалог
выбрасывает только что вставленный экспорт, показывает человеку фразу про
параметр, и дальше не предлагает ничего: Import выключен, предложения положить
секрет в хранилище нет, вернуться можно только вставив заново.

Наблюдалось на CI run 33725508605, ci-e2e (webkit),
e2e/api-secret-in-path.spec.ts:106 — по артефактам видно и тост, и потерянный
источник. Тот же спек и тот же класс, что в nocx-s47is, но это ВТОРОЙ путь
того же интервала: тот бид закрыл случай «корень приехал после источника, и
папку никто не предложил», а этот — «человек закончил с источником раньше, чем
появилась папка».

## Acceptance Criteria

* Чтение источника не уходит на проволоку, пока назначения нет, и происходит
  само, как только папка появилась — любым путём: корень приехал или человек
  напечатал её.
* Отказ про МЕСТО не выбрасывает источник.
* Красный-затем-зелёный модульный тест на этот интервал.
close_reason: Чтение источника в диалоге импорта ждёт назначения вместо того, чтобы уйти впустую и выбросить экспорт. Красный-затем-зелёный модульный тест. Влито в main в PR #177.

title: make ci-full can never be green on a non-FHS Linux host: fixtures name /bin/bash and /bin/echo, and the host leg runs a package only the containers can serve
description:
AGENTS.md makes `make ci-full` on the merged tree the integrator's mandatory gate. On this
NixOS development machine that command could never come back green: `test-ci` failed with
18 failures across two packages, identical on a clean `origin/main` worktree, so it is the
machine and not the branch. A mandatory gate that always fails is a gate nobody runs.

The 18 are two different things.

FIVE are a real defect: test fixtures naming an absolute FHS path the PRODUCT never
assumes. internal/app's factory fixtures used `fixedShell{path: "/bin/bash"}` and asserted
against the same literal, while internal/loginshell — which owns that question in the
product — resolves the account's shell and carries `/run/current-system/sw/bin/bash` as a
named NixOS case in its own table. internal/shellintegration's zprofile-exec test wrote
`exec /bin/echo`. And the live-sshd zsh tier proof failed with `exec: zsh: not found`
because zsh here lives in the developer's per-user nix profile under `$HOME/.nix-profile/bin`
while the fixture (correctly) MOVES `$HOME`, and this host recomputes the session PATH from
the new HOME; sshd_config `SetEnv PATH` does not survive that, measured.

THIRTEEN are deliberate and stay that way. internal/shellintegration fails rather than
skips without a GNU bash 3.2 (requireBash32, nocx-cn86), because a skip is how a real 3.2
regression reports green on every Linux machine in the project. macOS has that bash; Linux
has it only after `scripts/install-bash32.sh`, and the container images bake it in. The
defect there is in the GATE, not the test: `make ci-full` claimed to be the whole gate
while its host leg ran, unconditionally and natively, a package whose fixture only the
containerized leg has.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a non-FHS Linux host (NixOS, Guix) with no `bash32` installed, in any nocx worktree:
2. `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/app/ ./internal/shellintegration/`
3. 18 failures: 5 in internal/app (4 x `fork/exec /bin/bash: no such file or directory`,
   1 x `exec: zsh: not found` after a 15s timeout), 13 in internal/shellintegration
   (12 x `no GNU bash 3.2 found`, 1 x `no such file or directory: /bin/echo`).
4. `make ci-full` therefore stops at `test-ci` and cannot proceed to any other job.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No test fixture in internal/app or internal/shellintegration names an absolute
      shell or coreutils path that the product does not itself name.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/app/ ./internal/shellintegration/` on a non-FHS Linux host
      fails only on the bash-3.2 fixture, and on nothing else.
- [ ] The tests that were fixed still FAIL when the product reports the wrong shell —
      proved by mutation, not by inspection.
- [ ] `internal/shellintegration` still FAILS rather than skips without a bash 3.2.
- [ ] `make test-ci` states which package this host is not the place for and where that
      package IS run, decided from evidence (a bash answering `--version`) rather than
      from a variable somebody sets.
- [ ] Nothing is dropped from `make ci-full`: whatever the host leg defers is inside the
      ci-backend/ci-linux partition of `./...`, which `make ci-os-split` keeps honest.
notes:
Fixed on feat/relay-pty-owner: ef801fb9 (fixtures + test-ci) and 0d41ebb2 (the ci summary line).

Group A, the defect: internal/app now resolves bash through one requireShellBinary helper
beside fixedShell (three near-copies of the resolve-or-fail idiom in that package became
one), and the assertions compare the product's report against the INJECTED path, so they
still fail for a basename, a name, the account's own shell or nothing. Mutations:
filepath.Base(shell) in localPTYFactory.report -> TestLocalEnhancedSessionReportsWhatItStarted
red; a literal in procs.Started -> TestLocalEnhancedSessionIsWatchedForReplacement red;
`&& false` on the zprofile replay -> TestLocalZshSession_AZprofileThatExecsStillRuns red;
nocx.zsh dialling port+1 -> TestLiveSshd_ZshAdapterReachesAcceptedDomain red.

The live-sshd zsh case was NOT the same shape and is worth remembering: sshd_config SetEnv
PATH does not survive on this host (measured -- the host's own bashrc rebuilds PATH from
the moved HOME after sshd has set it), so the shell directory is appended through the
.bashrc the fixture already plants, and only when the sshd default path does not cover it.

Group B stands as it was: internal/shellintegration still FAILS rather than skips without a
GNU bash 3.2. What changed is the gate. `make test-ci` asks scripts/have-bash32.sh -- this
machine, for a bash answering --version as 3.2, the same three candidates requireBash32
asks, kept in step by TestBash32Probe_AgreesWithTheSuite -- and defers the package with a
notice naming ci-backend when the answer is no. ci-backend and ci-linux partition ./...
exactly, so nothing leaves ci-full.

Still open, and why this is not closed: the containerized tail of `make ci-full`
(ci-backend, ci-linux, ci-frontend, ci-e2e) was NOT run from here -- a coordinator was
holding the Docker daemon for those same three scripts. Host-side legs measured green:
ci-os-split, test-ci (90 packages), build-ci, ci-mac. lint-ci dies on EACCES while an e2e
container run is in flight in the same worktree (root-owned .e2e/home); that is transient
and belongs to the concurrent run, not to this bug.
close_reason: Already shipped and on origin/main: ef801fb9 (fixtures + test-ci) and 0d41ebb2 (the host gate's summary), both ancestors of origin/main; the bead's own notes named them and it stayed open. Verified first-hand on this NixOS host today, not from the notes: 'go test -count=1 ./internal/app/' is ok (was 5 failures), a full 'make ci' host leg came back green across every Go package, and test-ci now prints 'NOT RUN HERE: ./internal/shellintegration/... this host has no GNU bash 3.2' naming make ci-backend as where it IS run — decided by scripts/have-bash32.sh asking a bash for its version, not by a variable. shellintegration still fails rather than skips without one (nocx-cn86 intact), and ci-os-split (Makefile:382) keeps the partition honest.

title: The backlog is a dump: stale in_progress, 60% unlabelled, and duplicates nobody can find
description:
Measured 2026-09-01: 3145 beads, 791 open, 126 in_progress of which 91 untouched >7d (oldest 41 days); 479 of 791 open beads (60%) carry no label at all; 66 distinct labels including 'epic' (165) and 'bug' (3) which restate issue_type, and 'assistant-sweep-0830' (42) which is a date; 505 open beads have no parent.

Cost, measured in one session: nocx-viil was in_progress since 2026-08-12 with its work SHIPPED (the refusal vocabulary is in contracts/ and frontend/src/integration/status.ts, and the generated contract doc cites the bead by name); a worker re-derived that surface from scratch before noticing. nocx-fz4qa / nocx-22k1c.4 / nocx-k6p18.29 are the same defect filed three times in different vocabulary.

Mechanism: when in_progress lies, nobody trusts status; when nobody trusts status, filing a new bead is cheaper than searching; every new bead makes the next search worse. Stale status is the first-order problem, labels the second.
acceptance_criteria: Every in_progress bead untouched >7d is either closed with code/commit evidence in its reason, or back to open. Every open bead carries exactly one area label from a closed list. 'epic', 'bug' and date/sweep tags are gone. The duplicate clusters found are closed against a named survivor. AGENTS.md states the rules with the failures that bought them.
notes:
BACKLOG WORK IS DONE AND PUSHED; THE AGENTS.md COMMIT IS NOT, and is blocked by something outside this task. All bd writes are in Dolt and pushed: 72 beads closed, 14 returned to open, 731 given an area label, 210 label rows removed (epic, bug, assistant-sweep-0830), 3 dependency edges added, 2 beads created.

The AGENTS.md change is written, complete and prettier-clean in the working tree of /home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/feat-relay-pty-owner, but it is UNCOMMITTED. .githooks/pre-commit runs golangci-lint over the whole tree rather than over staged paths, and another session is working live in this same worktree; its uncommitted edit to internal/shellintegration/launcher_local_zsh_test.go introduces 'declaration of err shadows declaration at line 1073' at :1080, which fails the hook for everyone committing here. Verified that this is NOT in HEAD: the offending lines are + lines in that session's working diff, and HEAD itself committed clean at ab3d2895.

Not worked around deliberately: --no-verify is forbidden by AGENTS.md, editing another session's file is out of scope, and git stash is shared across worktrees and would have yanked live work out from under them. Ten retries over five minutes did not clear it because that session kept editing (Makefile, scripts_bash32_test.go and scripts/have-bash32.sh appeared during the wait).

To finish, once that session's tree is lint-clean, from the worktree:
  git commit -F /tmp/nocx-AGENTS-md-commit-message.txt -- AGENTS.md
The prepared message is at that path and already carries this bead's id.

title: A pane presented as a plain terminal hides the restored blocks the ledger holds for it
description:
Found while fixing nocx-k6p18.31, and it is separable from it.

A pane whose lane has no live authenticated domain is presented as a conventional
terminal: terminal-content.ts calls scrollback.setUnstructured(), the controller sets
_setFilledPane(true), and style.css hides everything that is not the live container —

  .scrollback-inner.inner-fullscreen-mode > *:not(.xterm-live-container) { display: none }

For a session that was never integrated that is correct: there are no blocks. But a
pane RESTORED from the ledger (nocx-k6p18.22) can hold blocks from a previous run and
then be presented conventionally now — measured on the k6p18.30 acceptance run, where
every restored block was built, carried data-restored=true, and was display:none.

nocx-k6p18.31 removes the common cause by re-establishing the lifecycle channel, so an
ordinary re-adoption is integrated again and the blocks show. What remains is the
DEGRADED arm: an older helper generation that cannot hand the lifecycle identity back
leaves the pane conventional with reason channel-unavailable, and its restored history
is still hidden with no way for a person to read it. The same shape reaches any pane
that restores a past and is conventional now.

The question to settle is whether a restored, already-frozen block is part of the
conventional-terminal presentation at all. It carries no live region and claims no
input ownership, so showing it re-derives authority from nowhere; hiding it loses
history the ledger definitely holds. ADR-0024 decision 4 forbids render-derived
block-like grouping for a LIVE session, which is a different thing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a helper-hosted session on a remote host and run a command, so the ledger
   holds a block for it.
2. Stop nocx-server and start it again against a helper generation that does not
   answer session.adopt-lifecycle (or, before nocx-k6p18.31, any generation).
3. The pane comes back with live output and the integration card says the tab is a
   plain terminal — and every restored block is in the DOM and display:none.

## Acceptance Criteria

A pane taken back for a session whose lifecycle channel could not be re-established
still shows the blocks the ledger holds for it, or states in the product where its
history went. Checked through the seam a person reaches, not by asserting a class.
