documents into one answer, which is what re-fetching buys.

Separate absolute ceiling on the snapshot. Windowing must not turn today's bounded
fetch into an unbounded allocation — a caller asking for windows of a 900 MB
response is the case to refuse.

THE INTERVAL, both ends: the snapshot exists from the first fetch until the RUN
becomes terminal — completed, failed or cancelled — and is discarded there. It must
SURVIVE approval/egress suspension, because that is a continuation of the same run,
not its end; engine.go:450 already distinguishes the two and is the seam to hang it on.

Revision gone: refuse explicitly and say what to do — 'snapshot expired; restart with
start 0 and no revision'. Never transparently re-fetch an offset continuation.
close_reason: runSnapshots in internal/assistant/fetch_snapshots.go: process-lifetime, keyed by run id and an opaque 16-byte revision, mutex-guarded, nothing persisted — the same shape and reasoning as runCheckpoints beside it. apifetch.FetchText now returns a whole TextDocument and no longer windows anything; the assistant owns the window. Continuation is served from the snapshot with no second HTTP request, proven by a counting fetcher that asserts calls==1 and that the two windows concatenate to the document. Absolute snapshot ceiling 8 MiB, separate from the 64 KiB result window. Interval closed on c.Discard(runID), which is called on every terminal outcome and NOT on approval/egress suspension — so a snapshot survives the person answering a prompt. Expired revision refuses by name and never re-fetches. The result's url stays the original authorized identity because URLScope.Allows is byte-exact and a redirect target would be refused. Landed in 8d7d8f9a.

title: fetch.url joins the window vocabulary session.read and files.read already speak
description:
fetch.url is the only read tool in the product that refuses rather than windows. Its contract pins the three fields that would say otherwise:

    "truncated": { "type": "boolean", "const": false },
    "omitted":   { "type": "integer", "const": 0 },
    "lossy":     { "type": "boolean", "const": false }

The vocabulary to adopt is not invented here — it is on main. session.read takes start/count and answers total, window, returned, truncated, dropped, remaining. files.read answers window, seen, returned, truncated, dropped, remaining. Spell fetch.url the same way; do NOT introduce offset/limit, and do NOT put a selector grammar inside the URL string (omp does that, we have typed params).

Cut windows on line boundaries, never mid-line — the first byte of window two must not be half a word.

The result must let the model do the next call without arithmetic (hermes' _truncate_with_footer computes the offset for the model rather than making it guess). Whether that is a note field or a projection of the typed fields, it says: showing lines X-Y of N, M remaining, continue with start=Y+1.

Contract work per AGENTS.md rule 5: schema updated, renderer types regenerated and committed (npm run contracts:check), the Go DTO conformance test and the over-the-wire test both updated.
acceptance_criteria: contracts/tools/fetch.url.schema.json takes start/count and answers with the same field names session.read uses; no const-pinned field remains. A response larger than the bound returns a first window with truncated=true and a stated remaining, and the over-the-wire test validates the real payload off the real socket.
notes:
DESIGN DECIDED 2026-09-01 after a codex review; this overrides the start/count wording in the description above.

Copy files.read (BYTES), not session.read (lines). Reason, and it is decisive: web
text is arbitrary UTF-8 — minified HTML is routinely one line larger than the whole
64 KiB bound, so a line-addressed window cannot express 'the next piece' at all.
Byte addressing always can. This also adds a second user of files.read's meaning of
'window' rather than inventing a third.

Params:  url, optional start (decoded-UTF-8 byte offset, default 0), optional revision.
Result:  url, contentType, total, revision, window{start,end}, returned, text,
         truncated, dropped, remaining, lossy.
Next call: same url, same revision, start = window.end.

- NO count. The declaration's 64 KiB ResultBound already fixes the maximum window.
- DELETE omitted. dropped/remaining is the existing vocabulary and omitted is a
  third word for the same idea.
- Do NOT copy files.read's 'seen'. It exists to bind files.edit and has no meaning here.
- window.end must land on a UTF-8 boundary. Prefer a line boundary too when the
  content has lines, as files.read does — but bytes are the address, lines are a
  courtesy.

GRANT HAZARD, from the same review: URLScope.Allows (agenttools/registry.go:43) is
byte-for-byte string equality. A continuation repeating the identical original URL
is inside the grant. A REDIRECTED final URL is not, and naming it would be refused.
So the result's 'url' stays the original authorized request identity; the redirect
target is metadata, never the continuation key.
close_reason: fetch.url now takes url + start (decoded-UTF-8 byte offset) + revision and answers total/revision/window{start,end}/returned/text/truncated/dropped/remaining/lossy. Byte addressing, copying files.read, because minified HTML is routinely one line longer than the whole bound and a line address cannot name the next piece of it. omitted deleted, count never added, seen not copied. window.end always lands on a UTF-8 boundary and prefers a line boundary when the content has lines. dropped==remaining follows the house convention already in execute.go:577 and :857, not a new idea. Landed in 8d7d8f9a with nocx-sizd4.4; pre-commit gate passed on that commit.

title: A page in a legacy encoding is transcoded, not refused for not being UTF-8 on the wire
description:
FetchText demands utf8.Valid(body) and otherwise raises ErrNotText, ignoring the charset parameter sitting in the Content-Type header it just parsed. Any windows-1251 page — most of the older Russian web — is unreadable for that reason alone.

Honour the declared charset and transcode to UTF-8. golang.org/x/net is already a direct dependency (go.mod:84), so golang.org/x/net/html/charset adds nothing to the module graph; it also sniffs a meta charset out of an HTML prologue when the header says nothing, which is the common case.

Bounds, both ends: the ceiling applies to the bytes read off the wire, and transcoding can grow them — decide and state which side of the bound is authoritative rather than letting a windows-1251 page silently exceed it after conversion. Set lossy=true when the decoder substituted replacement characters, and stop pinning that field dead in the schema (it is const false today).

Failure paths: an unknown charset name; a declared charset the body does not actually obey; a body that is valid UTF-8 with a wrong charset declared.
acceptance_criteria: A windows-1251 page is returned as correct UTF-8 text with lossy=false. A body that does not obey its declared charset comes back with lossy=true rather than an error. An unknown charset name is refused by name.
close_reason: charset.NewReader decodes the declared charset and sniffs an HTML meta prologue; an unsupported charset name is refused by name; lossy is now a live field (schema const removed) and is set when the decoder substituted replacement characters. Ceiling decision, commented in code: maxBytes governs wire bytes AND decoded text is refused if transcoding pushed it past the ceiling — interim, superseded by the windowing in nocx-sizd4.3. GAP FOUND AND FILED as nocx-sizd4.8: html/charset does not read an XML declaration, so a legacy feed declaring its encoding only in <?xml ...?> decodes as mojibake silently. Landed in e675b8ee.

title: The bytes decide whether a response is text, not a six-entry MIME whitelist
description:
textContentType (internal/apifetch/fetch.go:225) admits exactly text/plain, text/html, text/markdown, application/json, application/xml, application/xhtml+xml. text/xml is not in it, so habr's RSS is refused before a byte is read; nor are application/rss+xml, application/atom+xml, text/csv, application/javascript, application/yaml.

Replace the gate with the decision the same file already makes for the import path: look at the bytes. Fetch() decides JSON by first byte with a comment saying why ('a server that mislabels JSON is common'). Do the same here — omp's sampleLooksBinary (fetch.ts:772) is the shape: a NUL byte, or three or more U+FFFD in a 4096-byte sample at over 1% density, means binary and is refused; anything else is text. Content-Type is retained in the result as a hint for the shape dispatch, never as a gate.

Failure paths to test (AGENTS.md rule 3): a real binary (PNG header) is still refused; an unlabelled response (no Content-Type) is text; a text response with one stray NUL is refused; text/xml, application/rss+xml and text/csv all pass.
acceptance_criteria: fetch.url on https://habr.com/ru/rss/news/t/1077012/?fl=ru returns text instead of ErrNotText. A PNG is still refused. A response with no Content-Type at all is accepted as text.
close_reason: Content-Type is a hint, not a gate: the body decides. NUL in the first 4096 bytes or >1% U+FFFD with >=3 occurrences means binary and is refused; everything else is text. textContentType deleted, no second owner left. Verified: text/xml, application/rss+xml, text/csv and an unknown type all pass; PNG still refused; no Content-Type header accepted; empty and one-byte bodies do not trip the ratio test. Landed in e675b8ee with nocx-sizd4.2.

title: A page that is a feed, a legacy encoding, or too big is read — not refused
description:
## What a user can do that they could not before

Paste a URL that is a feed, a page in a legacy encoding, or a document larger
than the tool's bound, ask a question about it, and get an answer. Today all
three come back as `fetch.url did not finish` and the ask is over.

The screenshot that opened this (2026-09-01): `https://habr.com/ru/rss/news/t/1077012/?fl=ru`
twice in a row, both times

    apifetch: the response is not UTF-8 text: content type "text/xml; charset=utf-8"

## Success Criteria

The end-to-end check, and it is the one that closes this epic: a person pastes
that habr RSS URL, asks what the news items are, and the answer names an item
from the feed. Then the same for a page bigger than the bound: the question is
about something that appears only in the tail, and the answer names it, having
read a second window rather than being handed a short copy.

Stops being false exactly once: today `FetchText` refuses `text/xml` before
reading a byte, and the wire contract pins `truncated` to `const false`, so
neither answer can exist.

## Why this shape

**`fetch.url` is the only read tool in the product that refuses instead of
windowing, and the vocabulary it is missing is already on main.**
`contracts/tools/session.read.schema.json` takes `start`/`count` and answers
with `total`, `window`, `returned`, `truncated`, `dropped`, `remaining`.
`contracts/tools/files.read.schema.json` answers with `window`, `seen`,
`returned`, `truncated`, `dropped`, `remaining`, plus an opaque `revision` that
binds a later call to the exact bytes this one saw. `fetch.url` has
`truncated`/`omitted`/`lossy` and all three are pinned dead:

    "truncated": { "type": "boolean", "const": false },
    "omitted":   { "type": "integer", "const": 0 },
    "lossy":     { "type": "boolean", "const": false }

So this epic does not invent paging for fetch. It makes fetch join the house
vocabulary — AGENTS.md "look for the existing answer before you write a second
one", applied to a wire contract rather than a predicate. Any child that
proposes a `offset`/`limit` spelling, or a selector grammar inside the URL
string, is wrong: `session.read` already decided how a window is asked for.

**Content type stops being a gate and becomes a hint.** `textContentType`
(internal/apifetch/fetch.go:225) is a six-entry whitelist. `text/xml` is not in
it, and neither are `application/rss+xml`, `application/atom+xml`, `text/csv`,
`application/javascript`, `application/yaml`. A whitelist of MIME types is a
list that is always one server away from being wrong, because the server writes
it and we do not. The bytes are the witness we already believe elsewhere:
`Fetch` (the Postman import path in the same file) says so in a comment and
decides JSON by first byte, deliberately, "a server that mislabels JSON is
common". The text path should decide the same way.

## What was read, and what was taken from where

Both reference implementations were read in full on 2026-09-01.

**oh-my-pi — `~/repos/oh-my-pi/packages/coding-agent/src/tools/fetch.ts` (1911 lines).**
MIME is normalized (charset stripped, :250) and used as a hint. Binary is decided
from the bytes: `sampleLooksBinary` (:772) — a NUL, or three or more U+FFFD in a
4096-char sample at over 1% density. Then a dispatch by shape (:1288-1350): json
pretty-prints; `isFeed || (isXml && body contains "<rss"/"<feed")` goes to
`parseFeedToMarkdown` (:519); text passes through; html goes to a reader chain.
Truncation is `truncateHead` on line boundaries at 50 KB / 300 lines
(`session/streaming-output.ts:292`), the full text is persisted to an artifact
ONLY when it actually truncated (`executeReadUrl` :1712), and the notice the
model reads is built from typed metadata by `formatTruncationMetaNotice`
(`tools/output-meta.ts`):

    Showing lines 1-300 of 4210 (50.0 KB limit). Use :301 to continue.
    Read artifact://<id> for full output

TAKEN: bytes-decide-binary, dispatch by shape, feed to markdown, line-boundary
cuts, the truncation notice as a projection of typed fields rather than a string
built at the call site, and lazy persistence — nothing on disk when it fit.
NOT TAKEN: the five-backend reader chain (native/trafilatura/lynx/parallel/jina),
markit binary conversion, sqlite/archive/notebook rendering, image inlining, and
the `:50-100` selector grammar embedded in the URL string.

**hermes-agent — `~/repos/hermes-agent/tools/web_tools.py` (1698 lines).**
A different philosophy: parses nothing locally, delegates to reader APIs
(Firecrawl/Exa/Parallel/Keenable) with a keyless free ring as a one-shot rescue.
Not a model for us — we have no reader backend and should not acquire one. What
IS worth taking is its truncation footer, `_truncate_with_footer` (:716): a
head+tail window (75/25, snapped to markdown line boundaries), the full text
written to `cache/web/<slug>-<digest>.md`, and a footer that hands the model the
exact next call with the offset already computed —
`read_file path="…" offset=312 limit=200` where 312 is `head.count("\n") + 2`,
so the model does not guess where the gap starts.

TAKEN: tell the model the arithmetic, do not make it do the arithmetic.

## The one thing neither of them has to solve, and we do

A file and a terminal ledger do not change between two reads. A web page does.
`files.read` already answers this with `revision`, an opaque token binding a
later `files.edit` to the exact bytes observed. Fetch needs the same idea for a
different reason: window 2 of habr must come from the same document as window 1,
not from a re-fetch of a feed that has since moved. Body cached for the run,
keyed by final URL after redirects, continuation served from the cache.

`URLScope.Allows` (internal/agenttools/registry.go:47) matches the URL string
exactly, so a continuation naming the same URL is already inside the grant. No
grant work is needed for this and none should be invented.

## Deliberately out

- Remote reader backends of any kind. Local only, and `golang.org/x/net` is
  already a direct dependency (go.mod:84), so feed parsing, HTML parsing and
  `html/charset` transcoding add nothing to the module graph.
- Binary payloads: PDF/DOCX conversion, sqlite, archives, notebooks, inline
  images. `fetch.url` returns text or says it cannot.
- A selector grammar inside the URL string. Params are typed by schema here.
- POST, headers, cookies, auth. A fetch stays a bare GET on the direct route,
  and `route.InsecureTLS` stays ignored (fetch.go package comment).
acceptance_criteria: A person pastes https://habr.com/ru/rss/news/t/1077012/?fl=ru, asks what the news items are, and the answer names an item from the feed. And on a page larger than the tool's bound, a question about something appearing only in the tail is answered — the model read a second window, using the same start/count vocabulary session.read already uses, served from the same document as the first.
close_reason: Merged to main as cce042e1 (PR #171). All eight CI jobs green including ci-e2e (webkit); the two webkit failures seen locally were container artefacts. DONE WHEN proved by TestAgentAsk_FetchURLDecodesLegacyRSSEndToEnd and TestAgentAsk_FetchURLReadsTailFromOneSnapshot in internal/transport, which drive the real apifetch client over the real socket.

title: A marked line is not read as the subject of the question
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `df -h`.
2. Select one line of its output and accept the mark (the chip counts 1).
3. Ask "what does this mean?".

Observed: the assistant explains what `df -h` is. Its call was
`session.read … id=att-581fff725edf7adf start=6` — no count, so it read from
the marked line to the end of the block and answered about all of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The prompt says a person's mark is the SUBJECT of the question, not merely
  something readable, and that reading it comes before answering.
- A row mark names both bounds as required, and says what goes wrong without
  the count.
- The whole-block form still says to omit both.
close_reason: Fixed and covered on fix/assistant-bugs

title: Escape does not stop the assistant outside a summon
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant something in an ordinary pane (no summon over a running
   program).
2. While it is writing the answer, press Escape.

Observed: nothing happens. The only way to stop the turn is the answer's ⋮
menu.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Escape stops the answer that is being written, whether or not the editor
  has focus, and whether or not it was summoned.
- It reaches the SAME Stop action the ⋮ menu carries — one stop, two ways to
  reach it, and repeating Escape is a no-op.
- With no turn live, Escape still belongs to the draft and to the overlays
  that already claim it.
close_reason: Fixed and covered on fix/assistant-bugs

title: Typing costs the backend a request per character, and cancelling only discards the answer
description:
Typing one line into the prompt editor issues control-plane requests
proportional to its LENGTH, and the backend does every one of them.

Found while fixing two flaky e2e specs (nocx-k1691). The trace of CI run
33510673551 showed hundreds of per-character control-plane requests while
nocxify-journey typed its long option-bearing ssh line, then the renderer's
"Cannot reach the nocx backend" overlay, and no lifecycle.submitAttempt after
Enter. The command never started. The spec was blamed first; the code says
otherwise.

## The mechanism, read in the source rather than inferred

frontend/src/suggest/controller.ts:19 states the design plainly: "A keystroke
aborts: every user document change starts a fresh query, and a provider may not
deliver after abort (batches are dropped by generation, never trusted)."
runQuery() calls this.abort?.abort() and starts a new query on every document
change. There is NO debounce anywhere on that path — LATENCY_BUDGET gates only
whether the dropdown opens, never whether a request is sent.

And the abort is client-side only. Every provider has this shape
(frontend/src/suggest/providers.ts:351):

    const result = await opts.complete(q, ctx.cwd)
    if (signal.aborted) return { candidates: [] }

The RPC is ISSUED, awaited, and only then discarded. Aborting throws away the
answer; it does not stop the work. So an N-character line costs up to N rounds
of fs.complete / shell.complete / history.query, every one of them served.

On a remote session shell.complete runs the remote shell's own completion
machinery over SSH, so the cost is not local.

## Why this belongs to the same family as nocx-8hdia

That epic removed background load nobody asked for — a poll that enumerated
every watched directory twice a second, panels that kept working while hidden.
This is the same shape from the other side: load proportional to a person's
typing, which is worst exactly when they are typing fastest. The epic's parting
sentence was that nothing owns what we cost a host (nocx-5ry87). This is a
second, larger contributor to that same unowned total, and it should be measured
with it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a pane with shell integration live.
2. Type a long command with a path argument — the ssh line from
   e2e/nocxify-journey.spec.ts is 120+ characters and reproduces it.
3. Watch the control plane: a request per keystroke, none coalesced.
4. Under load (the e2e container, a remote session) the backend becomes
   unreachable and the submit never lands.

## What NOT to do

Do not "fix" this by having tests paste instead of type. That was the first
attempt on nocx-k1691 and it was reverted: e2e/nocxify-journey.spec.ts exists to
prove a HAND-TYPED ssh line reaches the plan with its options, so replacing
pressSequentially with fill removes the coverage and hides this defect. A spec
must not be edited to match the defect it caught.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Typing a line of N characters costs a number of control-plane requests that
  does not grow with N — asserted by counting requests over a typed line, not by
  inspection.
- A keystroke that supersedes an in-flight query does not leave the backend
  doing work whose answer will be discarded: either the request is not sent, or
  the cancellation reaches the backend.
- The completion surface stays as responsive as it is now for a person typing at
  human speed. State the responsiveness target and where the number came from,
  in internal/discovery/schedule.go's form.
- e2e/nocxify-journey.spec.ts passes while still TYPING its line.
- Not in scope: the recall overlay's own query (opened deliberately, not per
  keystroke), and any change to what the completion offers.
notes:
WORK IN FLIGHT WAS ORPHANED AND IS PARKED AS A PATCH, NOT LOST.

An omp worker had implemented both halves of this bead — fewer requests while
typing, and a cancellation that reaches the backend — and its pane was gone by
the time the work was reviewed, leaving the changes uncommitted in the
coordinator's worktree. They were parked rather than committed because
golangci-lint is red on them:

  internal/completion/local.go:79  func `completeLocalPath` is unused
  internal/transport/ws_complete.go:90,103  shadow: `err` shadows line 64

Parked at (durable, outside the session scratchpad):

  /home/dev/.herdr/parked/wip-7jujk.patch          (git diff HEAD, 1215 lines)
  /home/dev/.herdr/parked/wip-7jujk-untracked.tgz  (contracts/rpc.cancel.params.schema.json,
                                                    internal/transport/ws_rpc_cancel.go)

Taken against a59fb9cf. origin/main has since been merged in (d520de72) and it
touched frontend/src/terminal-content.ts, which the patch also touches — expect
that hunk to need resolving on reapply.

WHAT IT CONTAINS, from the diffstat: a `rpc.cancel` method (schema + Go handler
+ registration + openrpc), dispatcher/ipc/history-client carrying the cancel
through, and the suggest controller/providers reworked so an aborted query
stops the request rather than only discarding its answer.

WHAT IT STILL NEEDS: the two lint failures fixed, a review against the brief's
two halves, and the responsiveness number written down with where it came from
(internal/discovery/schedule.go's form) rather than guessed. The acceptance
check is that nocxify-journey passes while still TYPING its line — do NOT
convert the spec to paste, which was tried on nocx-k1691 and reverted.

SEPARATELY: nocx-k1691's ssh-reconnect half is now FIXED and is unrelated to
this bead after all. The hypothesis that renderer starvation explained both
failures was wrong for that one — see nocx-k1691's notes: the cause was quick
connect's ad-hoc fallback firing while the saved profile list was still
loading. nocxify-journey:341 is still open and may or may not share this bead's
cause; nothing has established that it does.
close_reason:
Landed as 7e9ad0c7. All four criteria met.

- Requests do not grow with N: controller.test.ts counts provider calls over a
  25-character typed line and gets ONE. A 150 ms trailing debounce coalesces
  the burst.
- The cancellation reaches the backend: a new rpc.cancel notification carries
  the JSON-RPC id; the connection owns a cancellation interval per in-flight
  request; fs.complete / history.query / shell.complete run under a context
  that ends when it arrives. Three tests in ws_rpc_cancel_test.go drive it over
  the REAL socket, and the first was shown falsifiable — removing shell.complete
  from the cancellable set turns it red on "rpc.cancel did not reach the
  completer".
- The responsiveness number is named and sourced: 150 ms matches files-store.ts
  FILTER_ACTIVATION_DEBOUNCE and sits under the 250 ms first-result budget.
- nocxify-journey.spec.ts:341 passes while still TYPING its line (19.0s,
  chromium, container). The spec was NOT converted to paste.

Deliberate amendment to the parked patch: the dropdown does NOT close during
the debounce. Hiding it on each keystroke made the panel blink out under a
fast typist; it now keeps its rows until the replacement query answers, as it
did before. The ghost is safe through that window because ghostAcceptable
refuses a box whose document has moved, on both the draw and the accept path.
Pinned by a test, also shown falsifiable.

The parked patch was reviewed rather than trusted, and carried two regressions
it had not reported. queryHistory had lost the line that puts the search term
on the wire — six tests in history-client.test.ts were red on the patch, so
the frontend suite had never been run against it. And a withdrawal after a
vault-sealed retry named the id the server had already answered, so a retried
request could not be cancelled; fixed test-first.

NOT established: that nocxify-journey:341 shared this bead's cause. One green
run does not establish it and repeat runs would not either — see the note on
nocx-k1691. What IS established is that the per-character load is gone, which
is asserted by counting, not by timing.

title: Asking about a running full-screen program answers blind: the screen never reaches the model
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `top` in a pane and let it paint.
2. Press Ctrl/Cmd+Enter. The screen freezes and the badge says "Screen frozen while you ask".
3. Ask anything about it — the owner asked "Привет! А что это?".

Observed: the chip reads "marked for the question · 0", the ask carries no
attachedContent, and the assistant answers from nothing at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Summoning over a running command attaches that command's screen, in EITHER
  buffer: procps `top` owns the whole viewport without taking the alternate
  screen, and the attachment must not turn on the buffer kind.
- The system prompt the backend builds names the automatic attachment with the
  id session.read accepts, and does not elsewhere forbid reading it.
- An approved session.read over that attachment comes back with the screen
  rather than timing out.
- Watched end to end by e2e/ask-attaches-the-frozen-screen.spec.ts, with the
  fake model scripted to make no tool call for the "is it told" half and to
  read by id for the "does it come back" half.
close_reason: Fixed and covered on fix/assistant-bugs

title: Two e2e specs fail on CI for want of an assertion, not for want of time
description:
Two e2e specs failed on CI in two consecutive runs of PR #166, one per run, in
different browsers, out of 250+ that passed. Neither is a regression from that
branch — it touches no ssh code, no command blocks and no pane editor. Both are
recorded as evidence on nocx-6wgcw; this bead is the fix for the two specs
themselves, because at least the first of them is a spec defect and not harness
noise.

## 1. ssh-reconnect.spec.ts:289 — waits on NOTHING, and that is the whole bug

    Locator:  locator('.pane.active .nocx-editor-input')
    Expected: visible
    Received: hidden
    63 x locator resolved to <div ... class="cm-content ... nocx-editor-input">
    at openConnection (e2e/ssh-reconnect.spec.ts:122)

The element EXISTS for the full thirty seconds and never has a box. That is not
a slow connection; it is the pane not being in front.

Immediately before, the test runs setReconnectPolicy (line 101), which opens
Settings with Meta+comma, waits for the sections rail, changes the setting, and
then closes Settings with:

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape')

and asserts nothing afterwards. The next thing the test does is open a
connection, whose pane is then behind a Settings page that may not have closed
yet. AGENTS.md's rule — "wait on an observable state change, never on a
duration" — is violated here in its worst form: this waits on neither.

The fix is to assert the closed state before returning. Note also that this
spec hand-rolls the Settings open that e2e/harness.ts already provides as
settingsReady(); a second implementation of one concept is the defect AGENTS.md
names, so prefer extending the harness with the closing half over adding a
third spelling.

## 2. nocxify-journey.spec.ts:341 — different symptom, cause not yet known

    Locator: .pane.active .cmd-block.cmd-block-running filtered by "ssh -i"
    Error: element(s) not found     (NOT "hidden" — nothing matched at all)
    at e2e/nocxify-journey.spec.ts:405

The state before it is clean: the warmup block is asserted visible and the
running count is asserted to be 0, both with their own waits. So the failure is
in what happens after submitInEditor(primaryLine).

"Not found" rather than "hidden" narrows it: either no block was created, or a
block was created and had already FROZEN before the first poll — a frozen block
loses .cmd-block-running, so a connection that failed instantly would produce
exactly this. Do not guess between those. CI attaches the trace and
error-context.md for the failing test; download them and read the DOM at the
moment of failure before proposing anything.

    gh run download 33510673551 --name <artifact>    # run 1, chromium

## Steps to Reproduce

Both are intermittent on CI and neither reproduces on demand; the evidence is
the two runs below rather than a local repeat.

1. Push a branch and let ci.yml run both e2e jobs.
2. Run 33510673551 — ci-e2e (chromium) failed nocxify-journey.spec.ts:341;
   webkit green. 251 passed, 1 failed.
3. Run 33516570069, the same branch plus a merge of origin/main —
   ci-e2e (webkit) failed ssh-reconnect.spec.ts:289; chromium green.
   259 passed, 1 failed.

For the ssh-reconnect one the mechanism does not need a repeat, because it is
visible in the source: setReconnectPolicy presses Escape and asserts nothing
after it, so whether the next step sees a closed Settings page is decided by
scheduling. Reading e2e/ssh-reconnect.spec.ts:101-123 is the reproduction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ssh-reconnect's Settings close waits on an observable state, and the open/close
  pair goes through one helper rather than a second hand-rolled copy.
- nocxify-journey's cause is IDENTIFIED FROM THE TRACE, stated in writing, and
  fixed — or, if the trace shows a product defect rather than a spec defect,
  that becomes its own bead with the evidence and this one says so.
- Neither fix is "add a longer timeout" or "add a wait". A spec that needs more
  time is broken on a fast machine too; it has only not been caught yet.
- Both specs pass in the container run for their own browser.
notes:
ATTEMPT 1 FAILED AND WAS REVERTED (4e742ace, reverted by 70cef310). The
measurements are the useful part; do not repeat them.

WHAT WAS TRIED. setReconnectPolicy closed Settings with a bare Escape and
asserted nothing, so the first fix replaced it with a harness helper that
closed Settings and waited for an observable state. Two mechanisms were tried
for the close and BOTH are wrong:

  Meta+W    — does not close Settings at all. Container run: `.ui-settings`
              still present after 15s, and it took ssh-reconnect:199 down with
              it. Two failures where there had been one.
  first tab — clicks .nocx-tab-title first, the pattern agent-policy.spec.ts
              spells as backToTerminal. The TARGET test went green (5.9s), and
              ssh-reconnect:199 went red at line 277, sixty seconds of a hidden
              editor after a reconnect.

Escape itself is a no-op here, which is worth knowing: settings.tsx's
handleKeydown is the whole keyboard surface and it uses Escape only to clear
the search box. So the original line never closed anything, and the spec passed
because of whatever else happened to be true.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT. At the merge commit d54fc7bb, PW_PROJECTS=webkit
over e2e/ssh-reconnect.spec.ts in the container: BOTH tests pass, 23.1s. So the
container baseline is green and the failure being chased exists only on CI. The
first fix therefore traded a rare CI red for a reliable local red, which is
worse, and that is why it was reverted rather than iterated on.

WHY THE TAB SWITCH BREAKS :199, as far as it is understood: leaving Settings by
activating the first tab changes which pane is in front when openConnection then
runs, and therefore which pane is active after the reconnect that :199 performs.
The Escape version left Settings in front. So the two are not the same test with
a better wait — they are different topologies, and :199 depends on the old one.

WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT NEEDS. Not another mechanism guessed from the source. The
CI failure is a race that the container does not reproduce, so it has to be read
from the CI artifact for the failing run (trace.zip plus error-context.md), and
the question to answer from it is narrow: at the moment the editor was hidden,
WHAT was in front of the pane, and how did it get there. Only then is it
possible to say whether the spec, the harness or the product is at fault.

Also note nocx-7jujk, which now blocks this bead: the OTHER spec in it
(nocxify-journey:341) fails for a product defect — typing costs a control-plane
request per character and cancelling only discards the answer — and its fix is
in flight. It is possible, though not established, that the same backend
saturation explains this one too: both failures are an element that exists and
never gets a box while the renderer is starved.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ATTEMPT 2 — CAUSE FOUND IN THE CI ARTIFACT, AND IT IS THE PRODUCT (a59fb9cf)

The artifact answered the narrow question above, and the answer retires every
hypothesis in the notes before it. NOTHING was in front of the pane. The
accessibility snapshot in error-context.md for run 33516570069 shows the SSH
tab selected and its tabpanel in front, containing:

  "Terminal failed to start: ssh connect: nothing to authenticate
   root@e2e-reconnect-1788271823781 with: no key, no password and no
   reachable agent"

So the editor is hidden because no shell ever started; the pane's z-order,
Settings, and the Escape key are all irrelevant. And read the host: it is the
PROFILE'S NAME used as a hostname, under root, with none of the profile's
credentials. The app did not open the saved profile at all.

WHY. quick-connect.tsx loads its providers asynchronously when the dialog
opens, and filteredItems falls through to getQueryItems() — the ad-hoc
"Connect to <host>" row — "only when every real match missed". During the
load, every real match misses because no real match EXISTS yet. So a query
naming a saved profile yields exactly one row, "Connect to <that name>",
selected by default, and Enter dials it. The fallback's own comment promises
this cannot happen ("a mistyped alias cannot silently become an ad-hoc
connection to a host that merely shares its name"); the promise simply had no
force during the window where the answer was unknown.

Rare on CI and never here because it is a footrace between one profiles.list
RPC and Playwright's fill+Enter, and the container is faster than the runner.

THE FIX. The fallback is gated on the load having finished, and the empty
state reads "Loading…". Enter on an empty list is then a no-op, so the five
specs that pressed Enter straight after fill now wait for the saved row first
— the wait git-panel.spec.ts and git-remote.spec.ts already used. A unit test
in quick-connect.test.tsx holds the promise across the load window; it fails
with the guard removed.

Note that e2e/quick-connect.spec.ts:120 had ALREADY written this race down in
a comment ("the listbox is rendered before its providers have answered, and
Enter on an empty list is correctly a no-op"). What it missed is that on the
hosts variant Enter was not a no-op: the ad-hoc row made it a connection to
the wrong machine.

STILL OPEN under this bead: nocxify-journey:341, which is a different failure
and stays blocked on nocx-7jujk.

2026-09-02 — nocx-7jujk IS CLOSED (7e9ad0c7, PR #170), so this bead is no
longer blocked. Under that commit nocxify-journey:341 passes while still
TYPING its line (19.0s, chromium, container).

Do NOT read that as the cause being found. Nothing has established that :341
shared 7jujk's cause, and a green run cannot establish it — repeat runs would
not either, which is why none were taken. What 7jujk established, by COUNTING
rather than by timing, is that the per-character control-plane load is gone;
whether that load was what :341 tripped over remains unknown.

So the honest options for whoever takes this: either find an assertion that
distinguishes the two, or close this half deliberately on the grounds that the
named mechanism is gone and say so — the same amendment AGENTS.md rule 2
permits when a criterion cannot be met as written.

title: Three dead functions the epic left behind: two skill store constructors and an assistant constructor with no caller
description:
`node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs --platform=linux/amd64` on the merged branch:

```
DEADCODE RATCHET: 85 unreachable functions on linux/amd64 (89 baselined, 3 NEW):
  NEW: internal/assistant/assistant.go: newClientWithoutSkillRoots
  NEW: internal/assistant/assistant.go: NewClientWithoutSkillRoots
  NEW: internal/skill/write.go: NewStore
```

CI runs this and pre-commit does not, so the branch is green locally and red on the
runner. Both are the same defect in two places — a second constructor for one
thing, where the first stopped being used:

- Task 8 added `skill.NewStoreWithDocumentStore` and pointed `internal/app/app.go:698`
  at it. `skill.NewStore` kept its name and lost its only production caller.
- `NewClientWithoutSkillRoots` came out of Task 5's review: the fence roots had a
  nil default that silently disabled the fence, so the constructor was renamed for
  what it lacks. That was right, but nothing in production calls it — only tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `internal/skill` exposes ONE constructor for the store. The document store is
  not optional in production; a test that has none says so at the call, rather
  than reaching a second constructor that exists for its benefit.
- The assistant's no-skill-roots constructor is deleted, or, if a test genuinely
  needs it, it moves to a test seam and the reason is written down. Prefer
  deletion: AGENTS.md's clean-only rule names dead code alongside compatibility
  shims, and this repo is greenfield.
- `node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs --platform=linux/amd64` reports 0 NEW.
- No baseline entry is added. Baselining these would record the defect rather
  than fix it.
close_reason: 195cc50e, merged. skill.NewStore and skill.NewStoreWithDocumentStore collapsed into one constructor — the document store is not optional in production, so a test that has none says so at its own call site. The assistant's NewClientWithoutSkillRoots and its unexported twin are deleted rather than baselined. check-deadcode.mjs --platform=linux/amd64 now reports 0 NEW with no baseline entry added; net -13 lines. Found only because the deadcode ratchet is a CI job and NOT part of pre-commit, so the branch was green on this machine and would have been red on the runner.

title: A skill whose bytes changed since the person approved them is not read as approved
description:
The spec names an open path and this closes it: `session.run` can compute a skill
directory's path and write `SKILL.md` there, bypassing `skills.create/update` and
therefore bypassing the classifier, the scan-on-write and the person's approval
(`.internal/specs/2026-08-31-assistant-skills-design.md` §7, "Deliberate cuts").
Today the read side only scans; nothing knows the bytes are not the bytes anybody
agreed to.

The shape is taken from /home/dev/repos/lifemodel, which solved it for the same
file format: `policy.json` beside `SKILL.md` carries a `contentHash` over the
skill's files, and a mismatch moves the skill to `needs_reapproval` at LOAD time
rather than at write time. The hash covers every file in the skill directory —
`scripts/`, `references/`, not only SKILL.md — because a helper script is
instruction too; the sidecar itself is excluded, being ours rather than the
author's.

Our version is smaller: we already have `skills.json` as the enablement document
and `skill.Scan` on read, so this is a hash per skill and a third state, not a new
file per skill.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Approving a skill write records a digest over every file in the skill directory,
  computed deterministically from sorted paths and contents.
- Discovery compares the digest at load; a mismatch marks the skill changed rather
  than dropping it, and `skills.read` still returns the bytes — framed untrusted,
  naming the skill and saying the person approved different bytes.
- A changed skill is absent from the prompt index until the person approves it
  again: the model is not told to follow a procedure nobody agreed to.
- The Skills page shows the changed state with the path, and offers re-approval.
- Asserted end to end: write a skill through `skills.create`, approve it, modify
  its `SKILL.md` on disk directly, and observe it leave the index and come back
  after re-approval.
- Builtin skills are exempt, as they are from the scan — they are our bytes.
close_reason: 88ed4bca on feat/ai-skills-hash (merge pending, Task 9 is mid-flight in the main worktree). A length-prefixed sha256 over every file in the skill directory, symlinks hashed by target, recorded on approval in skills.json; discovery compares it at load and derives a Status. A changed skill leaves the prompt index and skills.read still returns its bytes, prefixed with a sentence naming the skill and wrapped in FrameUntrusted — visible, never silent. Only MANAGED skills carry a digest: an authored skill is the person's own file, edited by hand on purpose, and was never approved through our seam. My brief was wrong on one point and the worker was right: it said to put the filter in discoverDetailed as the one owner, but the criterion needs the index and the read to DIFFER. Discovery owns the status; the two consumers apply their own rule to it.

title: The run fence is nailed to / and content, and nothing can narrow it
description:
`runGrantFor` (internal/transport/ws_readscreen.go) supplies the run fence itself,
as three literals: this session, `/`, and the content root. A policy row's selector
is intersected with the fence (`AsGrant`/`narrowRow`), so the narrowest policy
anybody can express is bounded by what the fence names — and the fence names
everything.

Two symptoms already recorded as separate defects came from this one place:
nocx-m3tfx (a row set to permit governs writing to ANY file, because the path fence
is `/`) and the skills global toggle in nocx-si0dh, which could not be expressed
until `note`/`snippet`/`skill` family roots were added to the content hierarchy.
The content half is now fixable because that vocabulary exists; the path half is
not, because there is no way to say "the fence is this directory".

This is not the same as narrowing a policy row. The fence is the outer bound that
holds even when the matrix is set wide; a person who wants "this assistant never
leaves ~/projects, whatever else I set" has nothing to write it in.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set "Make changes that can be undone" to permit with no scope.
2. Ask the assistant to edit a file outside any project — `~/.ssh/config`.
3. It is permitted. There is no setting anywhere that would have prevented it
   without also forbidding every other edit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The fence is an input to `runGrantFor`, not three literals inside it, and its
  owner is named — the workspace when nocx-mp2vd lands, the profile until then.
- A person can state the fence and it holds regardless of the matrix: one test
  sets every row to permit, sets the fence to one directory, and asserts a write
  outside it is refused rather than asked.
- The fence is recorded with the grant, so the ledger answers "what could this run
  reach" from the record (`grant_scopes`, internal/content/ledger_sqlite.go).
- An unset fence keeps today's behaviour exactly, and says on the surface that it
  is unset rather than looking like a narrow one.

title: A person says what a command is and how widely their answer applies, instead of permitting one exact line
description:
Today the only reusable answer a person can give an approval is "allow always",
and it is saved as the exact token list they were shown
(`content.LiteralInvocationRule`, refusing any `*`). Two consequences, both from
`InvocationRule.Matches`, which requires the same number of subcommands AND the
same number of tokens in each:

- "any `df`, whatever the flags" is not expressible at all, even by an operator.
  `["df","*"]` matches `df` with exactly one token.
- "`df` of this folder" is a separate rule from `df -h /home`, and from
  `df -h /home/dev`. Rules accumulate one per exact command line.

And for a program the parser does not understand, the person is not asked what it
is — the ceiling answers for them. `session.run` declares `mutate-destructive`,
`ResourceReport.Effect` returns the ceiling whenever `Unresolved` is non-empty, so
`fd`, `jq` and `htop` are all asked about as irreversible changes forever. The
allowlist in `cmdeffect.go` cannot be completed and MUST NOT be delegated to the
person: its entries carry flag-level disqualifiers (`sort -o` writes, `uniq -w`
writes) that nobody approving a dialog can be expected to know.

The move is to change WHAT the person's answer is. Not "permit this line" — an
authority decision that bypasses the matrix — but "this is a read", a checkable
fact about the command, after which the matrix decides as it already does.

Widening is offered as a MENU GENERATED FROM THE PARSE, never as free text: free
text in a dialog under time pressure is exactly the over-matching
`LiteralInvocationRule` was written to prevent. Authoring a pattern by hand belongs
on the policy page, where the person can see the whole rule set at once.

What makes "any arguments" safe without knowing anything about the program: a rule
carries the CLASS it was approved at, and matches only while derivation still
produces that class. `df` approved as observe stops matching the moment an
invocation derives a write.

Related and separate: nocx-vb5w2 (the report is incomplete), nocx-c2aik (network
has no row of its own), nocx-takqr.3 (the answers are invisible).

## Success Criteria

- Approving `df -h /home/dev` with "any path" makes `df -h /tmp` run without a
  question, while `df -h > /etc/hosts` still asks — one automated check watches
  all three.
- For a program the parser does not understand, the dialog says so, offers the
  person a class, and saving that class alone does NOT permit the command: the
  next call still asks, as the class the person named.
- The dialog never accepts a typed pattern. Every widening is chosen from options
  derived from the parse, each labelled with what it covers.
- A domain widening offers only suffixes of the actual host, cut at the public
  suffix, so `*.com` cannot be produced.
- Every saved answer is visible and revocable inside its effect row on the Agent
  policy page (nocx-takqr.3), with the class it was approved at.

title: Network access is decided by the row labelled 'changes that cannot be undone', and cross-boundary is unreachable
description:
The effect set has a `cross-boundary` row and `curl` does produce a
`ResourceNetwork` verb (internal/assistant/cmdeffect.go, the `case "curl"` arm),
which maps to `EffectCrossBoundary` in internal/content/resources.go. But
`ResourceReport.Effect` only ever LOWERS, and only along relations named in
`effectBelowCeiling`:

```go
case EffectMutateDestructive:
    return derived == EffectMutateReversible || derived == EffectMutateDestructive
```

`cross-boundary` is not among them, so a network command falls back to
`session.run`'s declared ceiling — `mutate-destructive`. Nothing can land on the
cross-boundary row, `LiveEffects()` (internal/agenttools/registry.go) reports it
dead because no DECLARATION carries it, and the Settings page hides it.

So "may the assistant reach the network" is answered by the row a person reads as
"Make changes that cannot be undone". Someone who permits destructive changes has
permitted egress in the same click, and nothing says so. This is nocx-m3tfx's
shape again: a row answering a question that is not written on it.

The vocabulary is already there for the fix. `Resource.Path` carries the URL
("Path also carries non-filesystem targets such as a URL or SSH destination"), and
`ResourceDestination` is in the ledger's closed kind set (internal/content/ledger.go:249).
What is missing is the mapping, a containment predicate, and reachability.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set "Make changes that cannot be undone" to permit.
2. Ask the assistant to run `curl https://example.com`.
3. It goes to the network with no question. Nothing in the setting mentioned the network.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A network command resolves to the `cross-boundary` row, and `LiveEffects()`
  reports that row live — liveness accounts for effects reachable through command
  derivation, not only effects named in the declaration table.
- A network resource becomes a `GrantScope{Kind: ResourceDestination, ID: <host>}`.
- `GrantScope.Contains` answers host containment by label from the right, so
  `github.com` contains `api.github.com`; the public suffix is a floor, so
  `*.com` and `*.co.uk` are not expressible.
- Permitting destructive changes does not permit egress: one test sets that row to
  permit and asserts `curl https://example.com` still asks.
- The approval dialog for a network call names the host it is going to.
close_reason: Fixed upstream, verified on the merged tree (13a37222). The effectBelowCeiling ladder this bug was filed against no longer exists: ResourceReport.Effect now derives the class from the resource verbs and returns it whenever the declaration set CONTAINS it (internal/content/resources.go), so ResourceNetwork -> EffectCrossBoundary is reachable because session.run declares cross-boundary among its effect set (internal/agenttools/registry.go:372). The row is also live rather than dead: fetch.url declares cross-boundary alone (:325), so LiveEffects reports it and the Settings control governs something, with 'reach another host' as its label (frontend/src/effect-labels.ts). ResourceDestination is in use as a grant scope in the run fence. Not verified by me end to end: that a curl in session.run renders on the cross-boundary row in the product — the unit mapping is asserted (internal/content/resources_test.go:19) and the declaration carries the class, but I did not watch a person permit egress separately from destructive changes.

title: The value of a flag never becomes a resource: curl -o writes a file the approval never names
description:
`resourceOperands` (internal/assistant/cmdeffect.go) skips the value of any flag
listed in `optionTakesNextValue`, and nothing else picks it up:

```go
if !optionsEnded && strings.HasPrefix(arg.value, "-") {
    if optionTakesNextValue(program, arg.value) && i+1 < len(args) { i++ }
    continue
}
```

`-o` is in curl's list, so the ResourceReport names the URL with verb `network`
and says NOTHING about the file being created. The same holds wherever a flag's
value is a path: `ssh -i`, `bash --rcfile`, `curl -F`.

The effect class comes out safe today, but by accident: one `network` verb derives
`cross-boundary`, `effectBelowCeiling` refuses that sideways step from
`mutate-destructive`, so it falls back to the ceiling and asks. The defect is not
the class — it is that the person is asked while being shown half of what the
command does. `UnresolvedResource.Reason` exists precisely so an approval surface
can explain what the parser could not determine, and here the parser does not even
record that it skipped something.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant to run `curl -o ~/notes/dump.json https://api.github.com/repos/x/y`.
2. Read the approval dialog: it names `api.github.com` and no file at all.
3. Approve. The file is created; nothing in the question said it would be.

## Acceptance Criteria

- For every program in `optionTakesNextValue` whose flag value is a filesystem
  path or a destination, that value appears in the ResourceReport with the right
  verb — one case per program, `curl -o` and `ssh -i` among them.
- A flag value the parser cannot classify is recorded as `Unresolved` with its
  reason rather than dropped silently, so the command falls to the ceiling for a
  stated reason.
- The approval surface renders every resource in the report; a test drives
  `curl -o <path> <url>` and asserts the person is shown both the destination and
  the file write.

title: The epic's end-to-end check does not exist: two halves are asserted, the join between them is not
description:
The nocx-8hdia epic's last success criterion is not met, and it is the criterion
AGENTS.md rule 2 exists to protect: "An automated check watches a person do it:
open the panel on a directory, collapse the sidebar, and observe that listings
stop; re-open, and observe exactly one immediate listing."

What exists after the epic is TWO ADJACENT HALVES, neither of which is that check:

- The frontend half. files-view.test.tsx asserts the panel sends files.visible
  false when the sidebar collapses, when another view takes the front (via
  onCleanup, because the panel UNMOUNTS), and when the window is hidden.
- The backend half. ws_files_test.go's TestFilesPoll_HiddenPanelIssuesNoListing
  and TestFilesPoll_BecomingVisiblePollsImmediately drive files.visible over a
  real socket and count real provider listings.

Both are real checks over real seams. Neither watches the chain. A defect that
broke the join — the panel computing visibility correctly and never sending it,
the transport accepting it and never reaching the watcher — passes both suites.
That is the exact shape of the 2026-07-29 connection-manager failure: every unit
correct, the user's task impossible.

## Why this is its own bead rather than a line in another one

The obvious construction does not work, and whoever takes this should know that
before starting. The e2e suite drives the real UI against a real
cmd/nocx-server, so it can collapse the sidebar — but the thing to be asserted
is an ABSENCE of filesystem listings, which the UI cannot see. There is no
product surface that says "the backend issued no listing", and inventing one for
a test would be the tail wagging the dog.

Two candidate approaches, neither yet evaluated:

1. The backend already logs through log/slog behind the logging interface. If a
   listing is (or can be) logged at debug, an e2e spec can read the server's log
   as the observable. Check what cmd/nocx-server already emits before adding
   anything, and do not add a log line whose only consumer is a test without
   saying so.
2. A transport-level test that drives the REAL store rather than the panel —
   closer to a unit test, and it would still not cross the socket the way the
   product does.

Prefer whichever actually crosses both seams. If after evaluating both the
honest answer is that one check cannot span it, say so IN THE EPIC and amend the
criterion deliberately — that is a legitimate outcome, and it is much better than
a check that looks end-to-end and is not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One automated check exercises the whole chain: a real panel collapses, and a
  real backend issues no filesystem listing on its behalf; re-opening produces
  exactly one.
- It fails if the join is broken in either direction — the signal not sent, or
  the signal sent and not acted on. Demonstrate that by breaking each side once
  and showing the check goes red.
- No product surface is invented solely to make the test observable; if a log
  line is added for it, that is stated where the line is added.
- Not in scope: any change to the visibility behaviour itself, which is done.
notes:
Work was STARTED and PARKED on 2026-09-01, unfinished and uncommitted. The
work-in-progress diff (390 lines across cmd/nocx-server/main.go, internal/app/app.go,
internal/transport/ws.go, internal/transport/ws_files.go, e2e/stand.ts and
e2e/files.spec.ts) was saved to the coordinator's scratchpad as
wip-8hdia.8.patch and then reverted, so nothing of it is on the branch.

The approach it had chosen was candidate 1 from the description: make the
backend's listings observable to an e2e spec, by threading a files.* list trace
through cmd/nocx-server and the app wiring and reading it from the stand.
Whoever picks this up should re-evaluate that choice rather than inherit it —
it was parked before it produced a passing check, so it is a direction, not a
result. In particular the description's warning still stands: do not add a
product surface, or a log line whose only consumer is a test, without saying so
where it is added.

Parked because the epic's other seven beads were finished, verified and ready
to go out as a pull request, and this one is a test-only bead that can land on
its own. The epic stays OPEN until it does: its last success criterion is this
check, and closing the epic without it would be exactly the "green suite over a
broken product" that AGENTS.md rule 2 exists to prevent.

title: A replayed OSC 133 completion has no restored block to land on
description:
Found by nocx-k6p18.6's third round, 2026-09-01, when the worker was asked to either write
the acceptance test or name what the test would need. It named this, and the coordinator
verified the three load-bearing claims by reading the code rather than taking them on
report.

nocx-k6p18.6 asks for one sentence: a command running when the coordinator is replaced has
its real exit status shown on its block after the reattach, derived frontend-side from the
replayed bytes. Every piece of that exists EXCEPT the identity mapping, so the bytes arrive
and have nothing to land on.

## What is already there

- `WSClient.reclaimSession` / `SessionHandle.recovered` deliver the replay bytes;
  `ipc.ts` queues them into `pendingData`. `SessionRecovery` reports byte/gap/size
  metadata only.
- `TerminalContent` receives those bytes through `session.onData`, and `XtermRenderer`
  parses OSC 133 and surfaces each marker with its `exitCode` — which is correct and is
  where parsing belongs (AD-6, ADR-0001: the backend never sniffs the stream).

## What is missing, and each was checked

1. `CommandMarkerEvent` (`frontend/src/renderers/types.ts:43`) carries kind, exitCode,
   line, col and buffer. **No durable entry identity and no attempt identity.**
2. `TerminalContent`'s marker callback (`frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:2450`) logs
   every marker and acts only on `B` (`:2457` — `if (marker.kind === 'B') this._settle()`).
   **C and D are ignored**, so a replayed completion is observed and dropped.
3. `BlockManager.restorePast` (`frontend/src/scrollback/blocks.ts:1864`) ADOPTS the
   restored elements into the DOM and draws the "Previous session" boundary. It registers
   **no live `BlockRecord`**, so `freezeFromAttempt` — which freezes a live block bound to
   an authenticated lifecycle attempt — has nothing to freeze. Restored blocks do carry
   durable `data-entry-id` values; nothing reads them back.

## What is owed

Associate a replayed OSC 133 boundary — D and its exit code above all — with the restored
block's DURABLE ENTRY IDENTITY, and freeze that restored block. Likely points: the marker
callback in `terminal-content.ts`, restored-block registration in `restorePast`, and a
narrow restored-block completion operation in `scrollback/controller.ts` or `blocks.ts`.

## Forbidden, and each is already decided elsewhere

- Not through `recoverAck`, not through a fact on the fresh domain, and not through
  `syncLifecycleLedger` — that is publisher-side and sees only the current coordinator's
  authenticated facts, so it cannot be a replay bridge.
- `docs/lifecycle-protocol.md` :438 and :460: a Lost domain is never revived, and reattach
  establishes a FRESH domain. The bytes supply the outcome; the domain does not.
- The backend never parses the stream. All of this is renderer-side.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a command on a remote host through the helper.
2. Replace the coordinator while it runs.
3. Reattach. The window replays, the renderer parses the same OSC 133 D it would have
   parsed live, and the marker callback drops it because no restored block claims it.
4. The block stays open or shows unknown while its outcome is in the scrollback.

## Acceptance Criteria

A replayed OSC 133 D marker reaches the restored block that owns its entry id, and that
block shows the real exit status rather than `unknown` and rather than staying open. A test
drives replayed C/output/D bytes against a restored ledger block fixture and asserts the
status. Nothing revives a Lost domain and nothing carries an outcome on a lifecycle fact.
close_reason: Implemented the missing renderer-side replay bridge in commit 2df9a82b: recovered OSC 133 C/D markers are buffered during the recovered write, then ledger-order D completions settle restored blocks by durable entry id. Added acceptance coverage for restored status, failure exit text, and nested causal-turn lookup; no lifecycle domain is revived.

title: Async lifecycle acks from an old bind could settle on the new shell
description:
Found while working nocx-k6p18.6, 2026-09-01, and confirmed by the coordinator against the
diff: it is a real defect and it is NOT what that bead asked for, so it gets its own record
rather than being folded into an acceptance it does not satisfy.

TerminalContent's lifecycle acknowledgements are async. `establishAck` and `recoverAck`
both await a round trip, and nothing identified WHICH BIND issued them. So an
acknowledgement minted against the old shell could settle after a reconnect and mutate the
new shell's episode: `_recoveryAcking` left standing across a rebind, `_recovery` cleared
by an ack for a fence that is no longer current, an establishment generation retired
against a lane that no longer exists.

## Fix, as landed in 994c335a

A monotonic `_bindGeneration` incremented on every bind, plus a recovery ack CLAIM keyed by
(bindGeneration, sessionId, fence, generation). Every async continuation re-checks the
claim before mutating anything, and stale claims are reset on session loss, rebind, a
native transition and a recovery replacement. A refusal now releases the claim while
keeping the episode pending, so a later fence replay is a legitimate retry rather than a
lost episode.

## What this is NOT

It does not deliver nocx-k6p18.6's acceptance (an exit status arriving on a block after
reattach, derived from replayed bytes) and it does not touch nocx-k6p18.18 at all. Those
stay open.

## Owed

The commit landed with an EMPTY BODY, against the commit rule. Whoever picks this up
should restate the reasoning in a follow-up or amend, because the why is exactly what a
one-line subject loses.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A pane is bound to a session and a recovery episode is pending; `_ackRecovery` awaits
   `recoverAck`.
2. The socket drops and the pane rebinds to a fresh shell before that await resolves.
3. The old acknowledgement settles and clears `_recovery` / retires an establishment
   generation belonging to the shell that no longer exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

An acknowledgement minted against one bind never mutates a later bind's episode; a refusal
releases the claim while leaving the episode pending for a legitimate retry. Tests drive a
delayed acknowledgement across a rebind and assert the new shell's episode is untouched.
close_reason:
Acknowledgements now know which bind minted them.

establishAck and recoverAck both await a round trip and carried no bind identity, so an acknowledgement issued against the old shell could settle after a rebind and mutate the new shell's episode: _recoveryAcking left standing across a rebind, _recovery cleared by an ack for a fence no longer current, an establishment generation retired against a lane that no longer exists.

The fix is a monotonic _bindGeneration incremented on every bind, plus a recovery ack CLAIM keyed by (bindGeneration, sessionId, fence, generation). Every async continuation re-checks the claim before mutating anything, and stale claims are reset on session loss, rebind, a native transition and a recovery replacement. A refusal releases the claim while keeping the episode PENDING, so a later fence replay is a legitimate retry rather than a lost episode — which is the half that makes this a fix rather than a lock.

A third defect surfaced from the same reading and landed with it (8fe62302): a fresh session abandoned its pending command because an OLD domain had ended, the ended counter having survived the reset. Closed-domain ids stay — they are what rejects a stale fact — and only the counter resets.

Pre-fix reds, after being asked to name the property rather than a count:
  `a late acknowledgement from the old bind must not mint a duplicate acknowledgement for the current bind`
  `a fresh session must not abandon its pending command because an old domain ended`

The first round's version of these read `expected [ … ] to have a length of 2 but got 1`, which is behavioural and says nothing a year from now.

FILED, NOT FOUND BY THE BEAD: this work arrived inside nocx-k6p18.6 and satisfies none of that bead's acceptance. It got its own record rather than being folded into an acceptance it does not meet — which is the only reason it is visible as a separate defect at all. The commit that carried it (994c335a) landed with an EMPTY BODY; 971164ff carries the reasoning after the fact.

title: Wire the summarizing draft into the ask: kernel resolves the role, calls DraftSkill, proposes skills.create
description:
Task 4 (nocx-zuf28, 23cceab9 on feat/ai-skills-task4) landed `profile.RoleSummarizing`,
`assistant.ComposeDraftInput` and `assistant.DraftSkill` with **no production caller**.
The plan required the role and its first consumer in one commit precisely so this could
not happen (`internal/profile/role.go:14-18`; RoleClassifier is the counter-example —
assignable for months with nothing asking for it; and nocx-rtg0, where an encrypted store
shipped with no caller for its write path).

The worker was right that it could not finish: the plan names
`internal/assistant/kernel.go` as the consumer, and what the kernel is supposed to hand
the person is a proposed `skills.create` call — a tool that does not exist until Task 6
(nocx-tbxwq). Task 4's own sequencing put the consumer before the thing consumed.

So the wiring moves to Task 6, and this bead is the edge that makes that a fact rather
than a memory. AGENTS.md: "A reported blocker becomes a bead with a dependency edge in
the same minute, or it evaporates between rounds."

## Acceptance Criteria

- `internal/assistant/kernel.go` resolves `profile.RoleSummarizing` through
  `profile.ResolveRole` — the one resolver — and builds its model client the way
  `internal/assistant/classifier.go` builds the classifier's, not by a second path.
- The draft's `name`, `description` and `body` become the proposed `skills.create`
  arguments the person sees in the approval; the flow from "remember this" to that
  proposed call is exercised in one test.
- A failed or unassigned summarizing call does not block the ask: the assistant answers,
  says it could not draft the skill and why, and nothing is written.
- An unassigned `summarizing` spends the answering role's endpoint, as the roles surface
  already tells the person (nocx-0s2gh.3).
- `deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive '.../internal/assistant.DraftSkill' ./...` prints a live
  path from main, not "reachable only through reflection".
close_reason: 4318fbb3. The kernel resolves RoleSummarizing through profile.ResolveRole and builds its client the way the classifier does; on a skills.create proposal it REPLACES the model's own fields with the arguments DraftSkill generated from the whitelisted input (Question + Prose only), memoized across approval resume so the person approves the same bytes that get written. A draft failure is a bounded tool result: the ask still answers, no approval opens, nothing is written. Production path confirmed by grep rather than by the -whylive probe, which again ran through reflect and proves nothing (RTA blind spot): ws_agent.go:1016/1300 -> AskParams.SkillDraft -> engine.go:415 -> toolSeams -> kernel.go:1402.

title: The automatic frozen attachment over-attaches every finished command; the alternate-buffer rule is not the fix
description:
The automatic frozen attachment fires for EVERY finished command that printed
something, so a person who marks block A is silently also handed block B, under
a sentence that calls it "the current screen of the full-screen program".

Measured: e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts:614 `expect(beforeSystem).not.toContain(markerB)`
fails in both browsers on the merged epic tree.

The obvious fix — give `toggleInputTarget` (frontend/src/terminal-content.ts
~:5326) the alternate-buffer rule `summonEditor` (~:4989) already has — is
WRONG, and two measurements say so:

1. `_syncLifecycleOwnership` (terminal-content.ts:5643) reads
   `(summoned || this.lifecycle.buffer === 'normal')`, so an UN-SUMMONED
   visible editor and the alternate buffer are mutually exclusive. Measured in
   a probe: lifecycle held at prompt_ready, editor visible, `_fireBufferChange
   ('alternate')` -> `ed.isVisible === false`, kind still prompt_ready.
   `toggleInputTarget` is reached only when `editor.isVisible` is true
   (terminal-content.ts:3177), and `captureAutomaticFrozenFrame` re-checks
   `editor.isVisible` after its await. So the buffer rule does not narrow that
   call site, it DELETES it — `captureAutomaticFrozenFrame` becomes dead code.

2. It would break this epic's own happy-path e2e.
   e2e/agent-reads-the-screen.spec.ts:397 presses Ctrl+Enter on a VISIBLE
   editor at a ready prompt and requires the automatic attachment. Its fixture
   (line 116) is explicitly "a normal-buffer TUI" — a background child
   repainting one row, never the alternate buffer.

The real discriminator is elsewhere. `automaticAttachmentOwner(true)` admits
`_lastFrozenBlock` whenever `_screenWriteGeneration > _lastFrozenWriteGeneration`
(terminal-content.ts:4884), and the SHELL'S OWN PROMPT REDRAW after a command
finishes satisfies that, which is why every finished `echo` qualifies.

Three candidate rules, none of them chosen here:
  a) "newer bytes" must mean bytes after the prompt was redrawn, not after the
     block froze. Risk: the prompt_ready fact arrives on the lifecycle channel
     asynchronously against renderer parsing, so the ordering may not be
     reliable.
  b) An explicit person mark supersedes the automatic attachment (the sentence
     already says "not a person mark", and dbc23587 is "keep automatic and
     marked items separate"). In the failing spec the flip happens BEFORE
     `pointAt(blockA)`, so the automatic capture is never cleared.
  c) The prompt sentence in internal/assistant/systemprompt.go is what is
     false, and the attachment is legitimate. Rejected by the e2e, which
     asserts markerB is absent from the payload, not merely mis-described.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run two finished commands that print, e.g. `echo alpha` then `echo beta`.
2. Ctrl+Enter on the visible editor at the prompt (switch to Ask).
3. Mark the FIRST block and ask a question about it.
4. The system prompt carries an "attached automatically" item for the SECOND
   block, described as the current screen of a full-screen program.

Reproduced as e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts:487, both browsers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts:487 passes in both browsers: no automatic attachment
  for a finished normal-buffer command whose only following bytes are the
  shell's prompt redraw.
- e2e/agent-reads-the-screen.spec.ts still passes: the normal-buffer
  background child that keeps repainting IS attached automatically on the
  Ctrl+Enter flip.
- frontend/src/terminal-content.test.ts:8698 and :8722 both stay
  non-vacuous — each refusal is bought by its own named reason.
- `captureAutomaticFrozenFrame` is either reachable or deleted; not kept as
  a call site no state can reach.
close_reason: Fixed in b8449b69, merged to the epic branch at 1f1297cf. The 'newer bytes' baseline now closes on the screen handback — the OSC 133 B marker nocx.bash appends to PS1 as its final action — rather than on the block's freeze, so a finished command whose prompt redrew no longer qualifies. Judges green in both browsers on CI 33503446220: agent-ask.spec.ts:488 refuses the attachment, agent-reads-the-screen.spec.ts:338 keeps it. The intermediate one-frame fence (b32bdf59) was measured and discarded: parse cadence in the container is ~100ms against a ~16ms frame, so the window saw a write about one time in six, and no wider frame count would be anything but a disguised duration. Non-vacuity verified by mutation both ways. No-shell-integration gap filed as nocx-7l4ex.22.

title: A tapped socket that waits silently for more than 30s is closed by the server, and every wait helper reports the corpse instead of the cause
description:
## The trap

readLoop (internal/transport/ws.go:2620, :2628) sets
SetReadDeadline(now + s.heartbeatReadWindow) around every inbound frame, and
heartbeatReadWindow is DefaultHeartbeatReadWindow = 30s
(internal/transport/heartbeat.go:14). That window is refreshed ONLY by frames the
client sends; server pushes do not touch it, and the server sends no WebSocket
pings, so there are no pongs either. A client that goes quiet for 30 seconds has
its socket closed — correct production behaviour, and exactly what
TestHeartbeat_ReadDeadlineClosesSilentPeer asserts.

socketTap (ws_run_lease_test.go:64) is not that client. It only READS. After the
last RPC a test sends, nothing goes up the socket at all, so every tap-based test
is silently on a 30-second budget it never declared. Nine test files build taps:
ws_run_lease_test.go, ws_run_lease_effect_test.go, ws_agent_gap_test.go,
ws_agent_errorwords_test.go, ws_signal_test.go, ws_agent_cancel_test.go,
ws_active_client_test.go, ws_ack_ownership_test.go, ws_reclaim_test.go.

And waitForRunState's own deadline is ALSO 30 seconds, so the two race and the
server always wins by a hair. The test can never reach its own timeout, which
means it can never print its own error.

## What it costs

tapNotify, tapCall and tapDataFor all report the closure as "socket closed before
X arrived". That sentence names the messenger. The cause — the run was never
bounded, or never started, or the server never pushed — is not in it, and the
reader has no reason to suspect a read deadline they did not know existed.

Measured: this misdirected an investigation for hours on PR #164 across three CI
rounds, including a wrong turn into nocx-2h08 (the CLOSED outbound-pump
starvation bug), whose signature it imitates. The real defect was nocx-qmtr2, and
it took two minutes to find once the deadline was known.

## Steps to Reproduce

Any tap-based test that waits more than 30s without writing. Concretely, on this
tree before nocx-qmtr2 was fixed: insert `time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)` before the
ledger.bind call in submitLeaseCommand and run

  go test -race -run TestRunLease_OutputBudgetBoundsAndTheBlockNamesIt -count=1 ./internal/transport/

  --- FAIL: TestRunLease_OutputBudgetBoundsAndTheBlockNamesIt (31.25s)
      ws_run_lease_test.go:1003: socket closed before agent.runState arrived

Nothing in that output points at heartbeat.go.

## Two fixes, and they are not alternatives

1. CHEAP, and it removes the misdirection: the three "socket closed" sentences
   say why a socket closes — the server releases a client that sends nothing for
   DefaultHeartbeatReadWindow, so a wait longer than that is the first thing to
   check.

2. RIGHT, and it removes the trap: socketTap behaves like the renderer and sends
   transport.ping inside the window while it waits. heartbeat.go's own comment
   says that is the contract ("A renderer sends its application heartbeat inside
   this window"). This needs a write mutex on the tap — gorilla allows one
   concurrent writer — and the ten WriteMessage call sites in those nine files
   routed through it. Deliberately NOT done inside PR #164, which is a frontend
   branch: perturbing ten write sites across nine transport test files is not a
   change to slip into a connection-overlay PR.

Raising the window for tests is explicitly NOT the fix: it would leave a test
that passes only on a fast enough machine, which AGENTS.md forbids in as many
words.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A tap-based test that waits longer than the read window either keeps its socket
  alive the way the renderer does, or fails with a sentence that names the read
  window. Not neither.
- TestHeartbeat_ReadDeadlineClosesSilentPeer still passes: the window is not
  weakened, disabled, or made configurable-away for the suite at large.
- The nine tap-based files still pass, and no test's frame accounting is changed
  by the heartbeat traffic.
notes:
A better acceptance criterion, from a review by a colleague on feat/relay-pty-owner: state it as a property of the SUITE, not as a feature to add, because 'add a ping' is not falsifiable and this is.

  No transport test waits SILENTLY for longer than heartbeatReadWindow.
  Either the tap behaves like a live client, or the wait is shorter than the
  window and the code says so.

That is checkable by grep over the nine tap-based files, and it stays checkable
as tests are added. Their framing of why: a silent wait longer than the window
can never produce an honest message — it will report a closed socket whatever
the wait was actually about, so the window turns such a test into a detector of
itself rather than of the thing under test.

title: Task 3: The static scan, at both boundaries
description:
Plan: `.internal/plans/2026-09-01-assistant-skills.md` — Task 3. Read that task in full before starting; it carries the code for every step.



**Files:**

- Create: `internal/skill/scan.go` — `Scan(b []byte) []Finding`, the pattern table.
- Create: `internal/skill/scan_test.go`
- Modify: `internal/assistant/execute.go` — `executeSkillsRead` frames a finding untrusted.
- Test: `internal/assistant/skills_read_test.go`

## Acceptance Criteria
