Search stays global and is asserted: a non-empty filter queries everywhere whatever rung the panel is on, and the explicit recall shortcut opens on everywhere. Contract, generated type, Go validation and the SQLite predicate moved together; 338 frontend tests and two Go packages green.

title: The model is made to repeat a sessionId the backend already knows, and the system prompt exists to prop that up
description:
`run`, `session.list` and `session.read` declare `"required": ["sessionId"]`.
The resolver takes it from the model's arguments — registry.go:47,
`resourceArgument`, whose signature receives `RunContext` and discards it:

    return func(args map[string]any, _ RunContext) ([]ResourceRef, error) {
        id, ok := args[arg].(string)

The parameter has exactly ONE legal value and the backend already holds it.
`runGrantFor` (ws_readscreen.go:250) mints the grant with a single session
scope — the pane's own session — and the scope check is an exact identity
match made BEFORE the ask branch. The model is not choosing anything; it is
being asked to reproduce a string.

What that cost, in the code's own words — internal/assistant/systemprompt.go:13:

  "It exists because of a refusal the person saw: `run` and `readScreen` take a
   sessionId, the run's grant is scoped to exactly one session, and the scope
   check is an exact identity match made BEFORE the ask branch. A model that
   was never told the id must invent one, and an invented one is refused
   terminally rather than put to the person."

The fix chosen then was to TELL the model the id (systemprompt.go:100-103): a
"Where you are / Session id: <uuid>" section plus a paragraph instructing it to
echo the string into every call. So a whole section of every request, a UUID in
every call, and a live failure mode — one wrong character is a terminal refusal
the person is never shown. The symptom was treated; the parameter was not.

The machinery to supply it is already declared and dead. registry.go:34:

    // RunContext carries only immutable identities of the run. It is passed to
    // resource resolvers for resources whose parent scope comes from the run,
    // never for mutable UI state.
    type RunContext struct { RunID, Workspace, Session string }

The only production construction is kernel.go:356,
`agenttools.RunContext{RunID: runID}` — `Session` is never filled. The field is
documented for exactly this case and has no writer.

`session.read`'s `id` (which item) stays a model parameter: that IS a choice.
Only the session is not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant anything; read what the request carries
   (the turn's raw dump, or internal/assistant against the fake OpenAI server).
2. The system prompt contains "Session id: <uuid>" and an instruction to pass
   that exact string as `sessionId` on every tool that takes one.
3. Every session tool call in the transcript repeats that uuid.
4. The assistant's own answer to "what can you do" reports the session id back
   to the person as if it were a fact about its situation, because it is
   carrying it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `sessionId` is gone from the params schemas of the session tools; a call that
  sends one fails `additionalProperties: false`.
- The session resource resolves from `RunContext.Session`, which is filled at
  the one place the kernel is built.
- The system prompt no longer states a session id or instructs the model to
  echo one; the attached-items paragraphs (systemprompt.go:129, :175) lose the
  "with the exact sessionId above" clause.
- A test drives a session tool with no sessionId argument and asserts the call
  reaches the pane's session — failing today.
close_reason: Merged as a1421546. sessionId is gone from the three session tools' params schemas; the session resource resolves from RunContext.Session, which the transport fills beside runID rather than recovering it from grant.Scopes — recovering it would have let an operator-authored session scope on a policy row win the union and silently redirect every session tool in every pane. The system prompt no longer states a session id or instructs the model to echo one. The end-to-end check that watches the assistant look at its own pane now runs under a policy naming a different session. go test on agenttools/assistant/transport green.

title: The backup spec's chosen file disappears before the preview is asked for (chromium, CI)
description:
CI run 33302820068, job ci-e2e (chromium), on PR #145 — a branch whose only
change is inside internal/content's schema rebuild, which the e2e suite cannot
reach (a disposable $HOME gives every run a FRESH content.db, so
resetIfSchemaChanged returns at `len(tables) == 0` long before the changed
lines). webkit was green on the same commit; the spec passes in the container
locally in 1.6s.

WHAT THE ARTEFACTS SHOW (playwright-traces-chromium, run 33302820068)

- `.ui-file-input__name` = "backup.json" PASSED (spec line 58), so the file was
  taken. The failure is one line later, waiting for the preview heading.
- The final snapshot and the last trace frame both show "No file selected" —
  the input went back to empty AFTER the assertion that it was not.
- stand/backend.log is SILENT from 08:58:52.511 to 08:59:04.958. The whole
  10-second wait falls inside that gap: `backup.preview` was never called.
- The saved backup.json in the artefact is valid and 236 bytes, so
  readBackupText's size guard cannot have fired and the JSON is not at fault.
- No console error at the time; the only console error in the whole trace is
  the unrelated CSP frame-ancestors notice.

SO: the renderer never set `state.contents`, and the FileInput's `fileName`
signal went back to null. Two ways that happens in
frontend/src/backup-restore-section.tsx, and the evidence does not yet separate
them:

  (a) `readBackupText(file)` rejected — the catch bumps `fileInputResetKey`
      (line 147) and raises a danger toast. But no toast is visible in the last
      frame, which argues against it.
  (b) BackupRestoreSection REMOUNTED — a fresh FileInput starts with fileName
      null and a fresh store starts with contents null, with no toast and no
      RPC. This fits every observation. The likely trigger is the
      `tab.placement` write two steps earlier: its settings.changed broadcast
      can land after the navigation and after setInputFiles. That is the same
      family nocx-rv53x cleared out ("the suite stops racing the settings
      load").

Distinguishing them is the first task: capture page.on('console') and the toast
region in the spec, or assert on the toast, and re-run chromium until it
reproduces.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE SPEC: if (b), a person who picks a backup file while
any settings write is in flight silently loses their selection — the surface
goes back to "No file selected" with nothing said. That is a soft degrade the
UI contradicts, which AGENTS.md names as the thing not to ship.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the e2e suite on CI, chromium project: e2e/backup-restore.spec.ts:9.
2. Intermittent. Not reproduced locally in the container (1 passed, 1.6s) nor
   on webkit in the same CI run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The cause is named: either readBackupText rejecting (a) or the section
  remounting (b), with the evidence that separates them.
- If (b): choosing a file survives a settings.changed arriving mid-selection,
  and a selection that IS dropped says so instead of silently emptying.
- The spec asserts the app's own refusal (the toast) rather than only the
  absence of the preview heading, so the next failure names the broken step —
  the same lesson nocx-hphhh already applied one line earlier.
- e2e/backup-restore.spec.ts passes on both projects across 5 consecutive CI
  runs.
notes:
2026-08-30, after PR #145 merged: main carries 4ca731a9 'fix(frontend): a settings refresh must not rebuild the page you are in (nocx-2x2vu)', which is hypothesis (b) in the body — a settings.changed remounting the page you are on. That commit was NOT in the tree that produced the red run (33302820068 was cut before it). Likely already fixed there; confirm before closing rather than assuming, and keep the spec-side criterion (assert the app's own refusal, not only the missing heading) either way.
Backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh: checked against nocx-hphhh (closed the same day as shipped) and found DISTINCT — do not close it against that bead. hphhh's fix is present in e2e/backup-restore.spec.ts (it waits for the Restore backup heading before setInputFiles, then asserts .ui-file-input__name is backup.json), and this bead's own trace says that assertion PASSED and the failure is one line later, waiting for the preview heading. This bead was filed 2026-08-30 against CI run 33302820068 on PR 145, after PR 111 merged hphhh's fix. Its evidence is that the file name settled and the input then reverted to 'No file selected' while the backend was never asked for a preview — a defect downstream of hphhh, as the bead itself says. Its acceptance is also still unmet: there is no toast or refusal assertion anywhere in backup-restore.spec.ts. Worth checking whether commit 4ca731a9 fixed the product half; the spec-side criterion is outstanding regardless.

title: The notes and snippets tools are never offered to the model, and their operations are never wired
description:
`nocx-0go2j` ("The assistant keeps your notes and snippets") is closed, and the
nine `notes.*` / `snippets.*` tools cannot be reached in the product. Two
independent gaps, either one alone sufficient.

1. NO CONTENT SCOPE ON THE RUN GRANT. `runGrantFor`
   (internal/transport/ws_readscreen.go:250) mints base scopes
   `{session, path:/}` only. `Registry.ForGrant`
   (internal/agenttools/registry.go:582) drops any tool whose declared
   `ResourceKinds` are not all covered by a grant scope; every notes/snippets
   row declares `content.ResourceContent` (registry.go:349-461), which nothing
   covers. They are filtered out before the model is offered anything.

2. THE OPERATIONS ARE NEVER PASSED. `AskParams.NoteOperation` /
   `SnippetOperation` (internal/assistant/assistant.go:236-237) are read at
   engine.go:410-411, and `grep -rn "NoteOperation:" internal` is empty outside
   internal/assistant/notes_snippets_test.go. ws_agent.go builds AskParams at
   :1172 and sets neither. Even with the scope, the capability would be nil.

Also here, smaller and possibly deliberate: `git.status` (registry.go:330) is
declared with `Narrow: nil`, and ForGrant skips every row with no capability
constructor, so it can never be offered either.

Why the gate did not catch it: the epic's end-to-end check is
internal/assistant/notes_snippets_test.go, which supplies its own
NoteOperation/SnippetOperation and its own grant — it exercises the tools past
the composition root, so neither the mint nor the AskParams wiring is on its
path. AGENTS.md rule 2, in the shape the deadcode ratchet cannot see (a dead
method behind a live interface).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the app with an agent policy set (any matrix that permits observe), open
   a pane and ask the assistant to list its tools.
2. It names files.read/edit/create, session.list/read and run — never
   notes.search, notes.create, snippets.list or any other content tool.
3. Confirmed off the seam rather than off the model: build the grant exactly as
   runGrantFor does, with a permit-everything matrix, and print
   `Registry.ForGrant`. Output is those six names and
   `grant scopes: [{session s1} {path /}]`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test at the composition root's seam asserts the offered tool set for a
  default run grant CONTAINS notes.search and snippets.list — failing today.
- An end-to-end check watches the assistant create a note through the shipped
  backend and the person see it in the Notes panel, with no test-supplied
  NoteOperation on the path.
- Whether git.status is meant to be reachable is decided explicitly: either it
  gets a Narrow, or its row says in the code why it is declared and unreachable.
notes:
The first of the two gaps here is the same mint as nocx-cmj11 and
nocx-4h0m7.4: runGrantFor carries no content scope, which is why ForGrant drops
every notes.*/snippets.* row. Take it as the SECOND STEP of the worker that
does .4 + cmj11 (see the FORM note on nocx-4h0m7.4), not as a separate task —
three workers editing WithRunScopes at once is the alternative. The second gap
(NoteOperation/SnippetOperation never passed in ws_agent.go) is independent of
the mint and still has to be done.
close_reason: Landed on main in e548b3b8 (PR #157, wave 1). Both gaps closed: the run grant now carries a content scope, so notes.*/snippets.* rows survive ForGrant, and NoteOperation/SnippetOperation are passed through agentSpecs into the handler (ws_agent.go:551-552, :1224-1225, :2377) rather than being declared and unreachable.

title: A slow ssh host never reaches the UI: no session.liveness arrives, so the indicator the epic shipped never draws
description:
## Description

Measured end to end against a real sshd behind a controllable network
(e2e/fault-proxy.ts): with the link adding 800ms of round trip, the pane never
draws the `slow` indicator. Over 25 seconds — 25 keepalive probes at a 1s
interval — `document.querySelector(".ui-connection-indicator")` is null, while
2 `.nocx-connection-mark` hosts are mounted. The mark host exists and the
component renders nothing, which is its behaviour when the condition is
`reachable`: so `_liveness` is null or its grade is false, and no
session.liveness carrying slow=true ever reached the renderer.

This is the axis nocx-rtzo4 shipped ("a pane says when its host is slow"). It
is proven at unit level and, so far as this measurement goes, does not happen
in a real run.

## Evidence, and what is NOT claimed

The fault injector was verified independently before blaming the product: an
echo server behind the same relay measures 2ms in pass and 801ms under
slow(400). So the backend really is being handed ~800ms, comfortably past the
500ms `slowRoundTripEnter` in internal/session/liveness.go.

Every link in the chain was read and is present:
- internal/session/session.go:805 passes KeepaliveInterval (the nocx-c4e96 fix
  is alive on main), so the prober starts;
- session.go:538 adds WithLivenessObserver(r.hostLivenessObserver(cfg.Host));
- internal/ssh/ssh_dial.go:233 and :445 both call startKeepalive with
  cfg.Liveness;
- session.go:568 sets `host: cfg.Host`, the same string observeHost matches on;
- terminal-content.ts:3664 subscribes onLiveness INSIDE _bindSession, so it
  survives both mount and rebind.

The cause is NOT isolated. internal/transport/ws_liveness.go PublishLiveness
has five silent early returns (session gone, wrong incarnation, terminal, no
rx, no subscriber) and any of them would produce exactly this. Every one is a
soft degrade visible only in the absence of a mark, which is the shape
AGENTS.md condemns — whichever it turns out to be, it should stop being silent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an ssh session against cmd/e2e-sshd through e2e/fault-proxy.ts, with
   profile options keepaliveInterval=1000, keepaliveCountMax=2.
2. Call proxy.slow(400) — 800ms round trip, past the 500ms enter threshold and
   well inside the 2s a silent probe is allowed.
3. Watch the DOM for 25s. No .ui-connection-indicator ever appears; the tab
   carries no warning; the session stays healthy the whole time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A session whose host answers past the slow threshold draws the `slow`
  indicator, and clears it when the host answers promptly again.
- Whichever early return in PublishLiveness was swallowing it no longer fails
  silently: a liveness fact that cannot be delivered says so.
- e2e/ssh-reconnect.spec.ts second case ("a host that is merely answering late
  is marked slow and offered nothing") goes green without being weakened.
close_reason: Fixed in ac522b05: ipc.ts rebuilt the liveness fact field by field and omitted roundTripMs and slow — the only two fields with no local counterpart to copy from. Backend was measured publishing slow=true at 801ms correctly; the loss was entirely renderer-side. Absent stays absent, per the contract. Pinned by two tests in ipc.test.ts.

title: typed ssh: take the -R port from the master instead of guessing it, and carry it in frame 2
description:
Wiring task. Depends on nocx-kqkvu.1 (the mux method) and nocx-kqkvu.2 (the
listener expectation).

Today internal/app/childdomain.go:randomPort() guesses 40000+rand(20000) —
entirely inside Linux's default ephemeral range (32768-60999) — and bakes it
into the -R of the user's own ssh line. A collision makes the forward fail, the
far shell's dial is refused, the domain never enters, and nothing says so.

The port cannot be known when the command is built: the mux master does not
exist until the user has authenticated. So it moves off the carrier's argv and
into frame 2, which is delivered after ownership is proven.

CROSSES A BOUNDARY, read before writing: ADR-0022 (the ssh command line is the
carrier), ADR-0024 (the bootstrap frame protocol and its ordering), ADR-0049
(the adapter is mux-only, no fallback), AD-5, AD-6 (the backend never sniffs the
byte stream — parsing ssh's "remote port forwarding failed" warning is OUT), and
docs/lifecycle-protocol.md. Frame 1 keeps its digest commitment; frame 2 gains a
field and stage-1 must validate it as strictly as it validates the addressing it
already checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- randomPort() is gone from internal/app/childdomain.go, with no replacement guess anywhere.
- typedDelivery.doRun opens the remote forward through the proven `master` returned by awaitOwnership (typed_line.go step 1), with listen 127.0.0.1:0 and connect 127.0.0.1:<local listener port>, BEFORE any frame is delivered.
- A refused forward reports ssh.ReasonChannelUnavailable through the existing reportOutcome path — the same reason a never-proven control socket already reports — and nothing is minted or written remotely beyond the abort frame that path already writes.
- The allocated port travels in frame 2 (SecretFrame), not in the carrier's argv. carrierArgCount and stage-1's positional reads are updated together; frame 1's bytes and its digest commitment are unchanged in shape.
- Stage-1 validates the port from frame 2 (digits only, 1-65535) and refuses the frame otherwise, using the same refusal vocabulary it already has; it exports NOCX_LIFECYCLE_PORT only from a validated value.
- The listener created in buildSSHChildBootstrap has an owner for its whole lifetime: today it is closed only on construction failure and the success path at childdomain.go:367-372 transfers no ownership. typedDelivery closes it on every terminal outcome.
- The listener expectation from nocx-kqkvu.2 is registered when the domain is requested and cancelled on the first hello, so a forward that came up but produced no shell is reported too.
- Go unit tests cover: forward refused, forward allocated then hello arrives, forward allocated and no hello, and frame 2 carrying an invalid port.
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` are green; the packages touched pass their own `go test`.
close_reason: Landed as 41eacee2 on fix/typed-ssh-forward-port. randomPort gone; the proven mux master binds 127.0.0.1:0 and the far kernel names the port; it travels in frame 2's body; carrier down to six args. Listener now owned for its whole life and registers an expectation. Reviewed twice: round 1 deleted the late-hello property test rather than its obsolete plumbing, and changed SecretFrame's contract without checking the profile-path caller. Both fixed; the capability-implies-port invariant is now enforced in Prepare. backend-linux and frontend CI jobs green on the merged tree.

title: lifecyclechannel: a domain that never gets a hello must report loss, not sit at starting
description:
internal/lifecyclechannel.Listener applies its handshake bound INSIDE the
accepted-connection path: listener.go:231 sets SetReadDeadline(HelloTimeout) on
a candidate `c` that already connected. If nothing ever connects — which is
exactly what a failed -R produces — no timer runs, no loss is reported, and the
integration axis that typedRunner.arm opened as `starting` stays there forever.

That is the silent half of nocx-kqkvu. AGENTS.md: "A soft degrade must be
visible in the product, not only in a log."

The descriptor sibling already has the contract to copy: internal/lifecyclechannel/adapter.go
reports LossHelloTimeout. This task gives the listener the same one for a domain
that was registered and never showed up.

Scope is this package only. The route from the reported loss to the UI is a
separate task; this one must not touch internal/app.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Listener takes an EXPECTATION for a domain (registered by the caller when the domain is requested) and arms a timer for lifecycle.HelloTimeout at that moment, not at accept.
- The first accepted, capability-proven hello for that domain cancels its timer.
- A timer that fires reports loss through the same seam and with the same reason vocabulary the descriptor adapter uses for LossHelloTimeout — one owner for "the shell never answered", not a second spelling of it.
- Closing the listener cancels every outstanding expectation; no goroutine and no timer outlives Close.
- A domain that is expected twice, or cancelled twice, is idempotent — no double report and no panic.
- Tests: hello arrives before the deadline (no loss), hello never arrives (exactly one loss with the right reason), hello arrives after the timer fired, Close with an expectation outstanding, and `-race` clean.
- `go vet ./internal/lifecyclechannel/` and `go test -race ./internal/lifecyclechannel/` are green.
close_reason: Expectation timer landed on fix/lifecycle-hello-timer (02971d7f). Reuses LossReporter/LossHelloTimeout. Reviewed twice: first round derived the lane from the kernel and fell back to an empty one (a loss addressed to nobody); second round still had no test pinning the lane. Both fixed; 8 tests, -race green.

title: mux: open a remote forward on the proven master and learn the allocated port
description:
internal/ssh/mux speaks OpenSSH PROTOCOL.mux v4 but implements only hello,
alive-check, new-session and terminate. MUX_C_OPEN_FWD / MUX_S_REMOTE_PORT are
missing — note that 0x80000007 is the gap in the named constants at mux.go:58-69,
between sSessionOpened and sTTYAllocFail.

They are what lets nocx stop GUESSING the child domain's -R port. Asking the
master for listen port 0 makes the far kernel choose a free one and report it
back, which is the same rule internal/lifecycleremote already follows for the
profile path (adapter.go:75 bindAddr = "127.0.0.1:0") and the same rule
internal/tunnel/tunnel.go:117 states outright: bind first, never pre-check,
report the port the OS assigned.

Scope is this package only. Nothing calls the new method yet; the wiring is a
separate task.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `(*Master).OpenRemoteForward(listenHost string, listenPort int, connectHost string, connectPort int) (int, error)` exists, dials its OWN fresh control connection with helloExchange exactly as Alive and Exit do, and returns the port the master reports.
- listenPort 0 returns the allocated port from MUX_S_REMOTE_PORT; a non-zero listenPort accepts MUX_S_OK and returns that port back.
- MUX_S_PERMISSION_DENIED and MUX_S_FAILURE come back as distinct named errors carrying the master's own reason string, never as a generic failure.
- A reply type the client does not name is an error, never a silent skip — the rule the package states at mux.go:56.
- Tests extend the existing fake master in mux_test.go and cover: allocated-port success, fixed-port success, permission denied, failure, an unnamed reply type, and a short/truncated packet.
- `go vet ./internal/ssh/mux/` and `go test ./internal/ssh/mux/` are green.
close_reason: OpenRemoteForward landed on fix/mux-remote-forward (84bb6cbf): MUX_C_OPEN_FWD/MUX_S_REMOTE_PORT, four named errors, nine tests. Reviewed: first round returned port 0 for a dynamic request answered MUX_S_OK; fixed symmetrically both ways.

title: The reconnect has no end-to-end check: a lost ssh pane getting a shell back is proven on fakes only
description:
nocx-rtzo4's FIRST success criterion is 'a user whose ssh session is lost can get a working shell back to the same endpoint without losing the scrollback of the one that died, AND ONE END-TO-END CHECK WATCHES THEM DO IT'. That check does not exist. The reconnect landed in PR #139 proven by unit tests over fakes: reconnect-setting.test.ts covers the ask/auto/never policy, terminal-content.test.ts covers _bindSession rebinding against a fake session, and internal/ssh's netfault table stages the transport faults backend-side. Nothing watches a PERSON lose a real ssh connection and come back to a working shell.

This is exactly the shape AGENTS.md rule 2 was bought by (nocx-rtg0): every unit correct, the user's journey unproven, and 'deadcode is empty' read as 'the feature works'. The epic must NOT be closed on PR #139's merge.

What the check has to watch, through the seams a person reaches:
 • an ssh pane is live against a real sshd (the e2e stand already raises one — see the ssh specs and e2e/stand.ts)
 • the transport dies SILENTLY, not loudly: the black-hole condition, not a kill. A killed connection is the loud loss the product already handled; the whole defect this epic fixed was the silent one.
 • the pane says lost and the offer appears on the tab, the tab is NOT closed
 • activating the offer yields a working shell at the same endpoint — a command runs and its output appears
 • the dead session's scrollback is still readable above the divider, and the divider says this is a NEW shell
 • the offer is REFUSED for a merely unreachable host (that session may still be alive; this is the negative half and it is the one a happy-path-only check will miss)

Note the ask/auto/never policy means the check must set the policy through Settings rather than assume a default.
acceptance_criteria: One e2e spec, running in e2e/run-in-container.sh against a real sshd, watches a person lose an ssh session to a SILENT transport death and get a working shell back at the same endpoint with the dead session's scrollback still above the divider; plus one case asserting no offer is made for a merely unreachable host. Green in both chromium and webkit in CI.
close_reason: Delivered in b9182a24: e2e/ssh-reconnect.spec.ts plus e2e/fault-proxy.ts. Green on chromium AND webkit in the container. It found nocx-7z3sr and nocx-y3i0s, both of which made the epic's first criterion false. Negative half asserted through 'slow' rather than 'unreachable' — a durable unreachable is unreachable through the prober, reasoning in the spec header.

title: A settings refresh rebuilds the page you are working in
description:
Every settings write broadcasts `settings.changed`; SettingsObserver answers it by
refetching describe+snapshot. `refresh()` calls `setDeclarations` with a fresh
array — every wire answer is parsed from its own JSON — which recomputes
`sections()` and `settingsPages()`, minting new page objects. `activePage()` is
rendered through a `keyed` Show, so the new object identity destroys and rebuilds
the active component page, throwing away whatever the person was doing in it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Settings, change any setting (the write broadcasts `settings.changed`).
2. Go to Backup & Restore and choose a backup file before the refresh lands.
3. When the refresh completes, the page rebuilds: the file goes back to "No file
   selected", the strategy radios and the preview vanish, and nothing on screen
   says why.

Observed on CI webkit in `e2e/backup-restore.spec.ts` (run 33280326039): the
preview rendered at +85ms and the page reset at +3.7s, so the assertion on the
preview heading timed out. Flaky only because it depends on whether the refresh
lands before or after the file is chosen.

The guard test that already existed — settings.test.ts, "a settings refresh does
not take back the file you chose" — waited on the `getSnapshot` CALL COUNT, which
rises at the TOP of `refresh()`, so it asserted in the gap between the request and
the rebuild it triggers, and passed whatever the rebuild did.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A settings refresh that carries a declaration the previous one did not leaves the
  active component page mounted: the file chosen before the refresh is still
  chosen after the new section is on the rail.
- Switching between component pages still replaces the body (the `keyed` Show
  keeps doing what it was added for).
close_reason: Fixed in 4ca731a9: activePage() compares by id, so a keyed Show no longer rebuilds the active component page on a settings refresh. Guard test made deterministic (it waited on the getSnapshot call count, which rises before the rebuild).

title: make dev-web: the coordinator handshake never ran — an ESM file with a CommonJS entry guard
description:
`make dev-web` never reaches vite. The stand has been broken since the cutover
wired `node e2e/coordinator.ts` into scripts/dev-web.sh (57400e85, nocx-gpyxp)
— the backend comes up and names its discovery socket, and the handshake that
reads the port and token off it is what dies.

Two halves of one contradiction, and either alone is fatal:

1. Root package.json declares `"type": "commonjs"`, so Node takes a bare `.ts`
   as CommonJS and refuses its `import net from 'node:net'` outright:
   "Cannot use import statement outside a module". Syntax detection does not
   rescue it — an explicit type field is what turns detection off. The field
   cannot simply be flipped to "module" either: fifteen specs plus stand.ts and
   sshd-fixture.ts read `__dirname`, which Playwright supplies only under its
   CommonJS transform.

2. The file's own CLI entry test was `require.main === module` — a CommonJS
   idiom in a file written in ESM syntax. Whichever format Node picked, one of
   the two had to lose. Load it as ESM and the guard is silently false, which
   prints an empty hello rather than an error.

## Steps to Reproduce

    make dev-web

On a tree with `frontend/node_modules` present, it stops at:

    the coordinator's hello carried no port or no token:

On a fresh worktree it stops earlier, with the SyntaxError from `node
e2e/coordinator.ts` quoted above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `make dev-web` prints "Backend up", the ssh forward line with a real backend
  port in it, and reaches "VITE ... ready" on http://127.0.0.1:5180/.
- `node e2e/coordinator.mts <socket>` prints `WSPORT=` and `WSTOKEN=` when run
  straight from a shell.
- The suite's other two callers are unaffected: `npx playwright test --list`
  still collects 474 tests in 89 files, and one spec that starts the shared
  stand passes in the container.
- `npm run typecheck`, prettier and eslint stay clean.

## Fix

Rename to `e2e/coordinator.mts`, so the extension rather than the package.json
fixes the format for Node and Playwright alike, and replace the guard with the
ESM test `resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`.
stand.ts and harness.ts import `./coordinator.mjs`; the rest of the suite keeps
its CommonJS transform and its `__dirname`.
close_reason: Merged in PR #143 (8711ebf6). coordinator.ts -> .mts, entry guard on argv[1]; make dev-web reaches vite.

title: An ssh pane comes back empty after a suspend, and nothing found so far explains it
description:
The owner's report had two halves and only one is explained. The backend defect
(nocx-c4e96) explains the SILENCE — nothing noticed a dead ssh transport, so no
exit was ever reported. It does not explain the other half: after a suspend, in
the SAME process, ssh panes came back with no content at all — no scrollback and
no editor — while local panes revived.

Nothing found in the renderer erases a pane's content in place. A contrast
experiment (an ssh server killed under a live app) produced the designed
behaviour: the tab kept its mark, its scrollback and its editor. So whatever
empties the pane is specific to the WAKE, and the wake is the one moment nobody
could observe. Three plausible mechanisms were identified and none could be
chosen between by reading:

- the AD-9 reset path (`renderer.reset()` clears the buffer, `lifecycle.reset()`
  hides the editor) — but reset needs `offset < ring.base`, and a silently dead
  session produces no bytes to advance the base, so this looks excluded;
- a WebGL context lost to a sleeping GPU — explains an empty canvas, does not
  explain a missing CodeMirror editor;
- a pane measured at zero — WebKit measures a hidden pane at ~0 (AD-6's UI-layer
  corollary records the hazard from the other side), and `refreshAtlas()` runs
  only on `setVisible(true)`, with no wake handler anywhere.

`frontend/src/wake-report.ts` is on this branch and measures exactly what the
three disagree about, one line per wake: buffer rows, whether the accelerated
renderer is still attached, the pane's measured box, whether the editor is
present and whether it is visible, and the pane's connection condition. It writes
to the log the backend already keeps.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open several tabs including ssh, close the laptop lid, open it.
2. Local tabs revive; the ssh pane is empty — no content, no editor — with the
   tab still on the strip. Same process, not a restart.
3. Read `~/Library/Application Support/nocx/nocx.log` for the `panes at wake`
   line and compare the ssh pane's row against a healthy local one in the same
   instant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The mechanism that empties the pane is named from the wake report rather than
  guessed, and the fix is against that mechanism.
- A pane that survives a suspend comes back with its scrollback.
- `wake-report.ts` is DELETED with this bead. A diagnostic that outlives its
  question becomes noise nobody dares remove.

title: A lost ssh pane offers a way back, and can say a host is merely slow
description:
A pane can say a host is gone. It cannot say a host is STRUGGLING, and that is
the state a person actually meets — a loaded server, a long link. The prober now
measures every round trip (nocx-c4e96); this is the surface that draws it, plus
the offer that has to exist when the session is finally lost.

WHAT IS BUILT (this branch): the measurement reaches the renderer
(`session.liveness` carries `roundTripMs` and the backend's `slow` grade — the
grade has hysteresis, so a renderer thresholding the number itself would be a
second derivation); `ui/connection-indicator.tsx` draws the pane's corner mark
and nothing at all in the healthy state; the pane owns one derivation
(`connection-condition.ts`) that the mark and the tab both read; the tab's
warning mark has one arbiter instead of two writers; the agent dot stops
asserting what it last observed once the bytes behind that observation stop
arriving.

WHAT IS NOT: the reconnect offer itself. A lost session is terminal and there is
no path from `lost` back to `live` — `_sessionLost` is set once and never
cleared, and the only owner of "this pane must have a session" is `mount()`,
which runs once per pane by construction (`panes.ts` Pane.start is mount-once).
Rebinding a fresh session onto a live TerminalContent means resetting the
lifecycle kernel, the integration subscription, the drop target, the markers,
the exit and reset callbacks and the offset bookkeeping, in the most delicate
file in the repository. That is this task, and it is why it is not a follow-up
comment on the branch that measured the round trip.

DECIDED WITH THE OWNER, so the implementer does not re-open it:
- Policy ask / auto / never. `auto` retries with backoff; when the attempts are
  spent, the tab carries an explicit offer. The tab is NEVER closed.
- The offer is a StatusCard in the flow, on the editor's line — not an overlay.
  The editor is hidden for a lost session anyway, so the place is free, and the
  scrollback stays readable in full.
- An unreachable host gets NO offer: the session may still be alive on the far
  side and a Reconnect button there invites killing live work.
- A redial is a NEW SHELL, not a resurrected one, and the surface must not
  pretend otherwise. The old process may still be running on the host.
- Open question left to implementation: same pane below a visible divider
  (recommended — keeps the promise "the tab is not closed" literally) versus a
  new tab beside a frozen forensic pane.

## Success Criteria

- A user whose ssh session is lost can get a working shell back to the same
  endpoint without losing the scrollback of the one that died, and one
  end-to-end check watches them do it.
- The ask / auto / never setting governs whether it happens by itself.
- A reconnect that succeeds reports the endpoint it actually reached, so a
  consumer can tell whether it is the same filesystem.
- Deliberately out: reviving the old remote process. There is no mechanism for
  it and the surface must not imply one.

title: The archive preview never runs in the shipped app, and the ask re-sends the whole archive on every keystroke
description:
Three findings on one gesture, all in the import ask's archive path.

## The preview does not exist where the product ships

A native pick and a native drop both answer with a PATH, and chooseExport
(api-pane.tsx) writes it into the source and stops — it never calls
previewPostman. Only the browser route (chooseDocument, bytes) previews. So in
the Wails window — the one the owner uses — "Archive contains 16 collections
and 1 environment" never appears, the per-document list never appears, and
anything the preview is meant to gate (the type: secret offer in nocx-zn386)
would never be offered.

The backend half is already there and already tested: api.import.postman
accepts `preview` for a path ending .zip and answers through
PreviewPostmanArchive. Nothing is missing but the call.

e2e/api-import-zip.spec.ts drives the BYTES route, which is why the gap is
invisible: the acceptance proof exercises the one entrance the shipped app does
not use.

## Every keystroke in the destination re-sends the archive

onDest re-runs previewPostman on each input event, and the archive travels
again as base64 every time — it is the destination that changed, not the
bytes. At the owner's 43 KB that is 58 KB per character; at the 16 MiB limit it
is 21 MB per character.

## The wait is invisible

`busy` only disables the Import button. The kit has Spinner and ProgressBar and
this ask uses neither, so the one wait a person actually sits through — file
read, base64, round trip — says nothing at all.

Reading is not the cost, measured: 12 ms for 16 documents, 132 ms for 200,
621 ms for 800 (~10 KB each, 40 requests). The cost is the transfer and the
round trip, which is why the answer is to stop re-sending rather than to draw a
better wait.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In the Wails window, open Import collection… and choose a Postman .zip with
   the system picker (or drop it on the ask).
2. No summary line, no document list — the ask looks exactly as it does for a
   single JSON document.
3. In `make dev-web`, drop the same file: the summary appears. Type in the
   destination field and watch a preview call leave per character.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A .zip chosen by the native picker or arriving as a native drop is previewed,
  and the summary and document list appear. Asserted through the path
  entrance, not only the bytes one.
- The archive is sent once per source, not once per keystroke: changing the
  destination re-validates the destination without carrying the bytes again.
- The first read draws the kit's Spinner in the source region; the destination
  re-validation draws nothing, because re-asking about an archive already read
  is not a wait a person is sitting through.
- Import stays disabled while a preview is in flight, as it is today.
close_reason: A .zip chosen with the system picker or arriving as a native drop is previewed through the path route, so the summary exists in the shipped app; the archive is sent once per settled destination (TextField onCommit) rather than once per keystroke; the first read draws the kit Spinner. Measured: read+convert is 12/132/621 ms for 16/200/800 documents, so the cost was the transfer, not the parse.

title: The importer destroys the credentials it imports, and only that door still enforces a rule the product dropped
description:
Importing a real Postman workspace produced 93 notes reading "imported
credential material is not carried; supply the value after import" — one per
bearer token, basic password, apikey value and credential-shaped header in the
archive. The values are not moved anywhere. They are dropped, and the person
retypes them by hand.

## Two rules got welded into one, and only one of them was decided

The owner's decision (design 2026-08-25 §10, the line carrying the [owner]
mark) is "A Postman document never yields a secret REFERENCE": a foreign file
must not address a record in this machine's vault. That is the attack ADR-0042
concedes it reintroduces the spelling for, and dropSecretReferences is what
answers it. It stands and is not in question here.

What actually destroys the values is the older §8 rule, "a collection file may
never spell a token", kept alive in curl.go's `credentials` enum:
credentialsStayOnRequest for the form, credentialsToImport for the file writer.
Its own comment states the limit it was written under: "The credential was not
protected by that, only lost; the only thing §8 protects is a FILE".

That rule is no longer the product's. nocx-14exx decided a credential the
person pasted stays where they put it; nocx-flidy then rewrote the panel's
promise to say so out loud, and its criteria end with "Nothing here rewrites,
refuses or sanitises a header." A credential SAVED from the form lands in the
request file in full. The Postman importer refuses to write the very thing the
save path writes, so "may a credential be in a request file" has two answers
decided by which door it came through.

The destination §6.3 promised — "The value goes to the vault, and the
identifier that points at it goes into the app's binding document" — was
removed by nocx-jjnch (T4) along with apibind, secretOffer and the BindWriter
seam. Half the rule went with it: taken out of the file, and nowhere to put.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Import a Postman export carrying an Authorization header or a bearer auth.
2. Open the imported request: the header is gone and the note says to supply
   the value after import.
3. Import the same credential as a curl line, save it into a collection: the
   header is in the request file, in full.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A credential literal in a Postman document is carried into the imported
  request exactly as the same credential is carried when a curl-imported
  request is saved. Asserted on the written file's bytes, both doors in one
  test so the two answers cannot drift again.
- `{{secret:secrow:…}}` arriving inside an imported document is still dropped
  and still reported. The [owner] rule is untouched, and a test says so.
- A Postman variable of `type: secret` is the ONE case that asks: the import
  offers to store its value in the vault, and does not decide for the person
  (ADR-0047). Everything else is carried with no question asked — measured on
  a real export, `type: secret` is rare (0 of 6 variables in the owner's), so
  the ask must not appear for an ordinary import at all.
- Where the offer is accepted, the value is minted through the SAME door the
  environment editor and the Auth tab already use (proposeSecret + the
  existing create ask) — no second minting path, and the value does not reach
  the renderer.
- `internal/apiimport` still has no path of its own reaching a vault write:
  what T4 deleted comes back as a seam the capability layer holds, not as
  apiimport importing a vault.
- The design documents stop describing the removed rule: §6.3 still says the
  value goes to the vault through a binding document that no longer exists,
  and §10's three bullets no longer read as one owner decision.
- An ADR records the reversal, because this undoes part of nocx-jjnch
  deliberately rather than by drift.
close_reason: Landed in 91c63f87+9fdbfd31 (PR #144). A credential an import finds is carried, both doors asserted in one test; type:secret is offered to the vault, unticked by default, minted by the capability with rollback; apiimport still reaches no vault write; {{secret:…}} still dropped and reported. ADR-0051 + the two design docs corrected. e2e/api-secret-in-path.spec.ts is the offer's end-to-end proof.

title: A probe's permit outlives its own response, so the next probe is refused
description:
The agent-probe semaphore has capacity 1 and lives per server. The JSON-RPC response is
written INSIDE m.handle (internal/transport/ws.go:2505-2507), while the permit is released
in a defer that runs after the task Run returns. So between "the answer is on the wire" and
"the token is back" there is a window, and a sequential client that reads its response and
immediately issues the next probe falls into it — and is refused -32004 control-saturated
with scope agent-probe and retryAfterMs 0, which is the server admitting the refusal is
meaningless.

Same shape as nocx-f9har (a settled exchange whose cancel token still resolves): the
RESOURCE IS RELEASED LATER THAN THE RESPONSE SAYS IT IS. One is a semaphore, one is a
registry entry. AGENTS.md rule 3 names it — an invariant stated as an interval needs both
ends, and both of these have only a start.

Severity: a red CI job on a green product, and a real refusal a real sequential client can
meet under load.
Confidence: high on the mechanism (the code path is quoted above and the rejection names the
scope); the flake itself was NOT reproduced.
Evidence: ci-backend (no-secret-service) job 99097747277; ws_assistant_test.go:698;
internal/transport/ws.go:2505; control.NewSemaphore("agent-probe", 1) at ws.go:1326.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. CI, ci-backend (no-secret-service), job 99097747277: the SECOND endpoints.probe in
   TestAgentStatus_AProbeOfAnotherModelIsNotReportedForThisOne is refused with
   {"code":-32004,"data":{"reason":"control-saturated","scope":"agent-probe",
   "retryable":true,"retryAfterMs":0}} while the first succeeded.
2. NOT reproducible on demand: 30 runs at default parallelism and 60 more under
   `taskset -c 0 ... -cpu 1` are all green. The window is narrow and opens only under load,
   which is why both this and nocx-f9har surfaced on a loaded runner.
3. It did not recur on the next CI run at ede8f899 (8/8 green).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A client that has received the response to a probe is never refused the next one for
  agent-probe capacity.
- The resource is released no later than the response that reports the work done — stated as
  an interval with both ends, in the code that owns it.
close_reason: agent-probe moved to the waiting class, the same answer the native picker already got: a probe is a serialisation point, not a scarce worker. The permit's interval is now stated with both ends in the handler that owns it. Wait bound sized against assistant.ProbeTimeout, which is exported so the two cannot drift.

title: api.request.cancel is accepted after the exchange has settled
description:
TestAPIRequestCancel_ASecondCancelAfterItSettledChangesNothing failed on CI (run 33267018136, ci-backend no-secret-service) in 0.00s — a race, not a timeout:

    ws_api_cancel_test.go:161: cancelling a settled exchange was accepted; the token stops resolving when it settles

The contract the test states is the far end of an interval: once api.request.send has answered, the token must stop resolving, so a later api.request.cancel is REFUSED with -32602 rather than silently accepted. It was accepted, so the token outlives the settling it is supposed to be scoped to — the registry entry is not removed in the same critical section that publishes the outcome.

Consequence for a person: Stop on an exchange that already came back reports success and stops nothing. The next run under a reused token is then reachable by a cancel meant for the previous one.

NOT caused by the change it surfaced under. internal/transport is byte-identical between 0c867d45 (where this job was green an hour earlier) and afd0b486 (where it failed) — verified with git diff over internal/pty, internal/transport, internal/app and internal/session. It came in with the API work and had not been caught until a loaded runner widened the window.

This is AGENTS.md's interval rule: 'write invariants with both ends'. The registry has a start (the token resolves from send) and no enforced close.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. go test -race ./internal/transport -run TestAPIRequestCancel_ASecondCancelAfterItSettledChangesNothing -count=50 on a loaded machine.
2. api.request.send returns outcome answered.
3. api.request.cancel with the same token is sometimes accepted instead of refused.
4. Expected: -32602 every time, because a settled exchange has no token to resolve.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The token is removed from the registry in the same critical section that publishes the settled outcome, so no cancel can observe a settled exchange as live.
- The test passes under -count=100 -race.
- A test names the interval explicitly: the token resolves from send until the outcome is published, and not one instant longer.
close_reason: Fixed in #138 (merged 2026-08-29): handleSend drops the cancel token before enqueueing the result, so the token's interval ends when the outcome is published rather than when the function returns. CI 8/8 on the merged tree.

title: The gnome-keyring case inverts: the machine that was set up silently now gets the sheet
description:
The end-to-end check the epic is closed by, and it is an INVERSION of a spec
that exists: `e2e/vault.spec.ts`, "silent vault setup with gnome-keyring".

That case runs the `-tags nocx_login_session` build against a real Secret
Service — the one machine state where silent setup used to fire — and today
asserts that the setup sheet does NOT appear:

    await expect(
      page.locator('.ui-prompt-overlay').filter({ has: page.locator('#vault-setup-passphrase') }),
    ).not.toBeVisible()

After `nocx-hqklb` that is exactly backwards. The case keeps its build, its
gnome-keyring skip guard and its disposable XDG root — all of which are the
expensive part and all of which stay correct — and asserts the opposite: the
sheet appears, the person answers it, and a recovery code comes back.

Renamed with it: "silent vault setup with gnome-keyring" names a mode that no
longer exists, and a spec whose title lies is worse than no spec.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The case reaches the same point in the flow (a password field wanting a
  secret, an uninitialized vault) and `#vault-setup-passphrase` IS visible.
- Answering the sheet completes the save: the profile row appears, as it
  does today.
- The recovery code is shown to the person after setup — the assertion that
  makes this the epic's happy path rather than a refusal test.
- `PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/vault.spec.ts` is green,
  and the case is not silently skipping: the run reports it as passed, not
  as skipped, on a host where gnome-keyring is reachable. If the container
  has no Secret Service the skip is honest — say so in the handoff rather
  than reporting the epic proven.
close_reason:
Landed as b56749f2.

e2e/vault.spec.ts case 3 inverted: it kept its -tags nocx_login_session build, its gnome-keyring reachability guard and its disposable XDG root, and now asserts that the setup sheet APPEARS on a machine with a working Secret Service, that answering it completes the save, and that a recovery code comes back. Renamed to match. The recovery code is the assertion that makes it the epic's happy path rather than a refusal test — it is the thing the silent mode never minted.

AND IT RUNS RATHER THAN SKIPPING, which the bead allowed but did not want. gnome-keyring, dbus and dbus-x11 go into e2e/Dockerfile, and e2e/container-entry.sh runs the tests inside a dbus-run-session with the keyring started in it. Best effort by construction: a keyring that will not start leaves the spec's own guard to skip the case exactly as before, so this cannot take other specs down.

Measured, chromium, in the container, after the change: 3 passed, 0 skipped. Before the change the same command reported 2 passed, 1 skipped.

Note for CI: the e2e job uses this same image, so that case will now run there too — which is the point, since a permanently skipped case is how an epic's happy path stops being watched.

title: A test, not an accident, keeps verification material out of the keystore
description:
ADR-0050 step 2: the keychain keeps no verification material. Not a hash of
the passphrase — it opens nothing, so it buys no convenience and adds an
offline verification oracle. Not the argon2id output either: that IS the
key-encryption key, so storing it recreates silent setup with a layer on top.
And not the recovery code or its envelope: the recovery code exists to
survive the loss of the machine, and a copy on that machine defeats the only
case it is for.

This is true the moment `nocx-hqklb`'s first child lands — with the root key
gone, the only thing the vault writes to the system provider is a secret a
person created. It is true by accident, and the next person adding a
convenience ("remember that the passphrase was right") will not know it was
decided. This child makes it true by a test.

The guard belongs at the seam, not in a comment: a fake system provider that
records every `Put`, driven through the whole lifecycle a vault has —
`Setup`, `Seal`, `Unseal` by passphrase, `Unseal` by recovery code,
`ChangePassphrase`, `RegenerateRecovery` — and asserting that the only ids
written are the ones a `Create` call asked for.

`internal/contentkey` is explicitly not in scope (ADR-0050 step 5): it is not
a vault secret, its threat model is the detached copy rather than a live
attacker, and its read deliberately passes no seal gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test drives `Setup` → `ChangePassphrase` → `RegenerateRecovery` →
  `Seal` → `Unseal(passphrase)` → `Unseal(recovery)` against a recording
  system provider and asserts the set of ids `Put` was called with is
  EMPTY.
- The same test with one `CreateNamed` in the middle, against a vault whose
  default provider is the system one, asserts the set is exactly that one
  secret's id — so the assertion above is not passing because the recorder
  is broken.
- The test names in its own comment why each of the three candidate items
  (passphrase hash, argon2id output, recovery envelope) is refused, so the
  next person reads the reasoning rather than the rule.
close_reason:
Landed in ab2795a9, in internal/vault/vault_passphrase_required_test.go.

Two tests, and the second is what makes the first mean anything:
- TestKeystoreHoldsNoVerificationMaterial drives Setup -> ChangePassphrase -> RegenerateRecovery -> Seal -> Unseal(passphrase) -> Seal -> Unseal(recovery) against a recording system provider and asserts the set of ids Put was called with is EMPTY.
- TestKeystoreHoldsExactlyTheSecretsAPersonCreated runs the same lifecycle with one Create against a vault whose default provider is the system one, and asserts the set is exactly that secret's id. Without it the first passes just as well against a provider that silently drops every Put.

The test carries the three refusals in its own comment rather than deferring to the ADR — a passphrase hash opens nothing and adds an offline oracle; the argon2id output IS the key-encryption key, so storing it recreates silent setup; the recovery code exists to survive the loss of the machine and a copy on that machine defeats the only case it is for.

internal/contentkey is explicitly out of scope (ADR-0050 step 5).

title: Setup refuses an empty passphrase, and the OS-held root key stops existing
description:
ADR-0050 step 1, taken through every layer in one change because the contract
check binds them: the JSON Schema in `contracts/`, the generated renderer type
and the Go DTO cannot disagree across two commits.

WHAT GOES:

- `internal/vault/vault.go` — the `silent` branch of `Setup` and the
  readiness probe that exists only to feed it; `unsealWithOSKey`;
  `UnsealRequest.UseOSKey`; `osKeyID` (the ROOT-key one — `contentkey.go`
  has its own and keeps it); the `HasOSKey`/`OSKeyCapable` fields of the
  status snapshot.
- `internal/vault/document.go` — `HasOSKey`. Greenfield, so it is deleted
  rather than deprecated; no migration and nothing reads an old document.
- `internal/transport/ws_vault.go` — `means: "os"`, `OSKeyAvailable`,
  `OSKeyCapable`.
- `contracts/vault.setup.params.schema.json` — `passphrase` becomes
  required, non-empty (`minLength: 1`), and its description stops promising
  an OS-held-key path.
- `contracts/vault.unseal.params.schema.json` — `os` leaves the `means`
  enum.
- `contracts/vault.status.schema.json` — `osKeyAvailable` and `osKeyCapable`
  leave `required` and `properties`.
- `frontend/src/generated/vault.status.ts` — regenerated, never hand-edited.
- `frontend/src/prompt-vault.ts` `setupVault()` and
  `frontend/src/terminal-content.ts` `ensureVaultForSave()` — the
  `status.osKeyCapable` branch that calls `vault.setup({})` goes; both fall
  through to the setup dialog the vault layer owns, which is what they
  already do on a machine with no keystore.

`Setup` with an empty passphrase returns an error naming what is required.
It does not fall back and it does not warn: a soft degrade the UI contradicts
is how a mode that does not exist survives a release.

## Acceptance Criteria

As assertions, written before the implementation:

- `Setup(ctx, SetupRequest{})` returns a non-nil error, and the vault is
  still `StateUninitialized` afterwards — it minted nothing.
- `Setup` with a passphrase returns a `SetupResult` whose `RecoveryCode` is
  non-empty, and the document holds BOTH a passphrase envelope and a
  recovery envelope. (The paired "and on a normal machine it succeeds" for
  the refusal above.)
- No `Setup` path calls `Put` on the system provider. A fake provider that
  records every `Put` sees none during setup, with and without a keystore
  that reports itself ready.
- `vault.setup` over the real socket with `{}` is refused with -32602, and
  with `{"passphrase": ""}` likewise.
- `vault.unseal` with `{"means": "os"}` is refused with -32602 — the enum no
  longer carries it.
- `vault.status` over the real socket validates against the amended schema,
  which forbids `osKeyAvailable` and `osKeyCapable` by
  `additionalProperties: false`.
- `npm run contracts:check` passes with the generated type committed.
close_reason:
Landed as ab2795a9.

Setup refuses an empty passphrase and refuses a cancelled context, both before minting anything. The OS-held root key is removed as a concept rather than left unreachable: the silent branch, doc.HasOSKey, osKeyID for the root key, unsealWithOSKey, UnsealRequest.UseOSKey, reportOrphanedOSKey, the wire's means 'os', and the osKeyAvailable/osKeyCapable status fields — plus doc.PreferredUnseal, read by nothing and carrying 'os-key' as its only non-empty test value. All in one commit because the contract check binds schema, generated renderer type and Go DTO to each other.

Every acceptance assertion measured:
- Setup(SetupRequest{}) errors and leaves StateUninitialized with no document — TestSetup_EmptyPassphraseRefusedWithReadySystemProvider.
- Setup with a passphrase returns a recovery code and both envelopes — TestSetup_WithPassphraseMintsBothEnvelopesAndTouchesNoKeystore.
- No Setup path Puts to the system provider, ready keystore or not — same two tests.
- vault.setup with {} and with {"passphrase":""} refused -32602, and the refusal does not reach the vault — TestVaultRPC_Setup_EmptyParamsRefused, _ExplicitEmptyPassphraseRefused.
- vault.unseal means 'os' refused -32602 — TestVaultRPC_Unseal_OSMeansRefused.
- vault.status over the real socket validates against the amended schema (additionalProperties:false now forbids both fields).
- npm run contracts:check passes with the generated type committed.

New behaviour worth knowing: Setup now checks ctx.Err() explicitly. It used to discover cancellation through the system provider's Put — the only provider call before its commit point — so without the check, 'a cancelled Setup changes nothing' would have gone silently with the key.

Gates: internal/vault, internal/transport, whole frontend suite (5551 tests) green; scripts/ci-linux.sh green in both keyring variants except the pre-existing nocx-6niab flake in internal/session, a package this branch does not touch; deadcode ratchet 85 unreachable, all baselined, none new.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
FOLLOW-UP DEFECT, found and fixed inside this bead: de63b764.

Removing the silent path removed an accidental deferral with it. requestSetup used to await vault.status() to choose between the silent path and the sheet; that round trip was what put openSetup() on a later turn. Without it, the sheet was raised while the activating click was still being handled, and the connection editor's native <dialog> went down with it — taking the sheet, which is re-homed inside that dialog, with it. The person activated a row and was returned to Settings holding nothing.

Caught by e2e/secret-panel-position.spec.ts in BOTH engines, and confirmed a regression rather than container flake by running the same spec on pre-change main (4a6ebcf0) in a throwaway worktree: 6 passed there, 2 failed here.

A microtask is not enough, measured not assumed: await Promise.resolve() still lost the dialog in chromium and webkit. The browser's light-dismiss handling for <dialog> belongs to the click's task, so the boundary has to be the end of that task — setTimeout(0), written out with its reason so the next faster call does not silently remove it again.

title: Every vault has a passphrase and a recovery code — the silent OS-key setup is gone
description:
ADR-0050 steps 1 and 2, which are the half of it that needs no macOS and no
release identity. Steps 3 and 4 — a darwin provider that calls
Security.framework under our own signature, and an item that requires user
presence — are a separate epic, blocked on two measurements nobody has made
and on a release signing identity that exists only as a measurement.

WHAT IS WRONG TODAY. `Setup` with an empty passphrase mints a root key and
puts it in the OS keystore, minting NEITHER a passphrase envelope NOR a
recovery code (`internal/vault/vault.go`, the `silent` branch). Two product
paths take it without asking anybody: `prompt-vault.ts` `setupVault()` and
`terminal-content.ts` `ensureVaultForSave()` both call `vault.setup({})` the
moment `status.osKeyCapable` is true. So on a machine with a working keyring
a person's vault is created with no second way in, and — measured on the
owner's Mac, 2026-08-29 — the key that opens it is readable by any process
under the same login with one `security find-generic-password -w`, because
the trusted application in the item's ACL is `/usr/bin/security` itself.

The keychain half of that is a documented non-goal (the vault design's T4,
explicitly out of scope) and this epic does not try to defend it. What it
removes is the mode whose ONLY protection was T4 being out of scope, and
whose failure mode is not a threat model position at all: lose the keychain
item and the vault is gone, because nothing else opens it.

WHAT SHIPS.

1. `Setup` refuses an empty passphrase. Every vault gets a passphrase
   envelope and a recovery code; there is no mode in which the root key is
   obtainable without one of them.
2. The OS-held root key ceases to exist as a concept, rather than being left
   in place unreachable: the `silent` branch, `doc.HasOSKey`, `osKeyID` for
   the root key, `unsealWithOSKey`, `UnsealRequest.UseOSKey`, the wire's
   `means: "os"` and the `osKeyAvailable`/`osKeyCapable` status fields go
   together, in one change, because the contract check binds the schema, the
   generated renderer type and the Go DTO to each other.
3. Nothing the vault writes to the keystore is verification material — not a
   passphrase hash, not the argon2id output, not the recovery code or its
   envelope. True today by accident; this makes it true by a test.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY OUT.

- The system provider as a store for INDIVIDUAL secrets stays. ADR-0050
  considered removing it and refused: it costs a wire contract and a renderer
  type to buy a property a narrower change buys as well.
- `internal/contentkey` keeps its own arrangement under its own, narrower
  threat model (ADR-0050 step 5, ADR-0018 §3). Its keystore path is not
  touched here.
- `release.yml` is not touched. It already builds `cmd/nocx-server` without
  `nocx_login_session`, so the shipped coordinator takes the file provider —
  which is the stronger of the two and the reason `nocx-e7bhr` had its sign
  backwards.
- Steps 3 and 4 of the ADR. Separate epic.

## Success Criteria

A person setting up a vault on a machine with a working OS keystore is asked
for a passphrase and is given a recovery code — the case that today is set up
silently with neither. Watched end to end by `e2e/vault.spec.ts`'s
gnome-keyring case, which asserts the inverse today and is inverted by this
epic: the setup sheet appears where it currently must not.

Stops being false exactly once: `vault.setup` with an empty passphrase is
refused on every path, and `grep -rn 'HasOSKey\|UseOSKey\|osKeyAvailable\|
osKeyCapable' --include=*.go --include=*.ts --include=*.json .` outside
node_modules returns nothing.
close_reason:
ADR-0050 steps 1 and 2 shipped. Three commits on worktree/calm-stone-1931: ab2795a9 (the removal + the step-2 guard), b56749f2 (the e2e inversion + gnome-keyring in the image), de63b764 (a follow-up light-dismiss regression the e2e caught).

SUCCESS CRITERION, watched end to end: e2e/vault.spec.ts case 3 runs the -tags nocx_login_session build against a REAL gnome-keyring and asserts the person is asked for a passphrase and given a recovery code — the case that until now was set up silently with neither. It PASSES rather than skipping, in both engines: the image now carries gnome-keyring and dbus and the tests run inside a dbus-run-session.

STOPS-BEING-FALSE CRITERION met: grep for HasOSKey|UseOSKey|osKeyAvailable|osKeyCapable across *.go, *.ts, *.tsx and *.json outside node_modules returns nothing, and vault.setup with an empty passphrase is refused on every path — validator, handler and vault.

Gates run on this branch:
- go test ./internal/... — green except the /bin/bash-dependent packages, which cannot run on this NixOS host (memory on-this-nixos-dev-host-make-ci-and).
- scripts/ci-linux.sh, both keyring variants — green except TestBootstrapWindow_QuarantinesTheUsersInputAndNotItsOwn, which is the already-open nocx-6niab in a package this branch does not touch; today's reproduction is recorded as a comment there.
- deadcode ratchet, linux/amd64 — 85 unreachable, all baselined, none new; 4 baselined entries are now gone because this change deleted them.
- frontend vitest — 5551 passed.
- e2e/run-in-container.sh, whole suite, both engines — 462 passed, 8 skipped, 0 failed. The 8 are the pre-existing clipboard and settings-scroll skips.

NOT run: make ci (host-side macOS job) — this host cannot; CI is the source of truth for it.

Left behind deliberately: ADR-0050 steps 3 and 4 as nocx-rybbm, blocked on two macOS measurements and a release signing identity. nocx-xsd03 stays open by hand until that closes too — bd cannot express task-blocked-by-epic. One unrelated defect found on the way and filed rather than fixed here: nocx-tyrvl, two projections of vault.status that disagree.

title: A real Postman .zip still cannot be imported: its members are nested under the export directory
description:
nocx-r1uk0 measured the real export and wrote the layout down:

  <export-uuid>/archive.json
  <export-uuid>/environment/<uuid>.json
  <export-uuid>/collection/<uuid>.json

ReadPostmanArchive (internal/apiimport/archive.go) looks the manifest up as
members["archive.json"] — at the ROOT — and mints every document path as
"<kind>/<id>.json", also at the root. So the owner's export fails at
"Postman archive has no archive.json manifest", which is the same symptom the
bug this epic was discovered from reported: the zip cannot be imported.

Every test and the e2e spec build their archive with no prefix, so the shape
that was measured is the one shape nothing exercises.

Second defect on the same read: validateArchiveMember refuses any member whose
path is not path.Clean of itself, and a ZIP directory entry ends in "/" — so an
archive carrying explicit directory entries (a real one usually does) is
refused before the prefix is even reached, while the IsDir() checks downstream
imply they were meant to be skipped.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Export a workspace from Postman — the file is a .zip.
2. API workbench, collections menu, "Import collection…", choose that .zip.
3. The ask refuses: "Postman archive has no archive.json manifest".

## Acceptance Criteria

- An archive whose members all sit under ONE top-level directory imports
  exactly as a root-level one does, asserted on the reader.
- Directory entries are skipped, not refused.
- Two top-level directories, or a member outside the manifest's directory, is
  refused out loud.
- The e2e archive is built in the shape a Postman export actually has.
close_reason: Archive members are read relative to the export directory the manifest lies in, and ZIP directory entries are skipped. Unit tests cover nested, flat, two manifests, a member outside the export directory, and a manifest two levels down; e2e/api-import-zip.spec.ts now builds the nested shape with its directory entry and passes in the container.

title: The pty signal seam is defined four times structurally and nowhere by name
description:
Follow-up to nocx-8vh0w, which fixed the third instance and added a seam test. That test shortens the feedback loop from a 16-minute browser run to ~10 seconds, which is real. It does not close the hole, for two reasons, and both have a cheap structural answer.

## 1. The guard is an enumeration, guarding an enumeration

The test's check is an anonymous interface literal listing three methods by hand. So a FOURTH optional method joining this seam must now be remembered in four places, not three:

  internal/app/app.go:2209                     lifecyclePTY's forward (anonymous literal)
  internal/session/session.go:1159             realSession's assertion (anonymous literal)
  internal/transport/run_lease.go:115          runLeaseSession (anonymous literal)
  internal/app/signal_foreground_local_test.go:148  the new test (anonymous literal)

Four sites define one seam by structural typing and none by name. The trigger for all four is human memory — exactly what failed three times (nocx-o3amz, nocx-7l4ex.13, nocx-8vh0w).

## 2. A missed forward still answers with a lie

The new forwards keep the shape that produced every instance:

  if !ok { return 0, pty.ErrNoForeground }

There are 7 such degrades across internal/app and internal/session. A wiring defect is reported as a fact about processes, indistinguishable from the truthful "nothing is running" — so classifyForeground reads reachGone and Stop says nothing-running. AGENTS.md: "A soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log." This one is not visible even in a log.

## Proposed fix

A. NAME THE SEAM, ASSERT IT AT COMPILE TIME. Declare it once in internal/pty and assert every implementation and wrapper:

    type ForegroundControl interface {
        SignalForeground(syscall.Signal) error
        ForegroundProcessGroup() (int, error)
        ForegroundJob() (int, error)
        SignalProcessGroup(int, syscall.Signal) error
    }
    var _ ForegroundControl = (*LocalPty)(nil)      // stubs exist on windows already
    var _ ForegroundControl = (*lifecyclePTY)(nil)

Adding a method to the interface then breaks the build of every wrapper until it is forwarded. The compiler names the place; nobody has to remember it. Feasible today: signal_foreground_windows.go already stubs all four, so LocalPty satisfies it on every platform.

B. A MISSED FORWARD MUST NOT BE ABLE TO SAY "nothing is running". Where the type assertion fails, return an error distinct from ErrNoForeground so classifyForeground maps it to reachFailed, not reachGone — the person is then told nocx could not tell whether the command stopped, which is true, instead of a refusal they act on. This is defence in depth that survives a forgotten forward, where A prevents one.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add a fifth method to the pty signal seam (any signature) and use it from the stop policy.
2. Forward it in realSession but NOT in lifecyclePTY.
3. Observed: compiles; TestLocalEnhancedSession_TheWholeSignalSeamIsForwarded passes, because its interface literal does not list the new method; an enhanced local session answers ErrNoForeground; Stop reports nothing-running over a running command. Fourth instance, found only by e2e.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Adding a method to the named seam interface without forwarding it in lifecyclePTY FAILS TO COMPILE. Demonstrated by doing it.
- With a forward deliberately removed, no path reports foregroundNothingRunning; the outcome is unreconciled. Demonstrated by removing one.
- The four anonymous interface literals above are replaced by the one named type.

title: The merged stop ladder lost main's unreconciled tail
description:
Reconciling nocx-uvac6.11 with nocx-7l4ex.10-.12 replaced main's stopForeground body with .11's stopProcessGroup. That was the right choice — .11's body is the one that keeps the addressee — but a rule main's body carried did not exist in .11's and went out with it.

The tail reached when every rung failed and none delivered:

    main:      return foregroundUnreconciled   // something is there and nocx cannot prove it stopped
    159e9fc8:  return foregroundNothingRunning

nothing-running is a refusal a person acts on. Shown beside a block that is still running it is verbatim the contradiction nocx-7l4ex.12 was filed as, and stopForeground twenty lines above already refuses to say it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take 159e9fc8 (the reconciliation of #127 onto main).
2. Drive stopProcessGroup so all three rungs fail with an error that is not ErrNoForeground. SignalProcessGroup folds only ESRCH and pgid <= 0 into ErrNoForeground, so an EPERM from kill(-pgid) does this — the shape a sudo inside the execution produces, where the group is no longer the backend's to signal.
3. Observed: all three rungs take the continue, delivered stays false, and the tail answers foregroundNothingRunning about a command that is running.
4. Expected: foregroundUnreconciled.

Not caught by: three greps over the merge (they searched for NAMES and this rule has none), any test on either side (neither exercises an EPERM path), or the mutation pass (it targeted the two known halves). Found by reading the merge line by line against main.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The tail of stopProcessGroup returns foregroundUnreconciled, with a comment naming why nothing-running is refused there and how the tail is reached.
- The existing signal-path tests still pass unchanged.
- The neighbouring EPERM-on-poll defect is NOT fixed here: it is nocx-iuzak, and it predates this merge on both sides.
close_reason: Fixed in the commit that names it: the tail of stopProcessGroup returns foregroundUnreconciled again, with a comment naming both why nothing-running is refused there and how the tail is reached (EPERM from kill(-pgid), which SignalProcessGroup does not fold into ErrNoForeground). Signal-path tests unchanged and green. nocx-iuzak left open deliberately — the EPERM-on-poll defect predates this merge on both sides.

title: Neither half of the stop-ladder fix is independently guarded
description:
Found sweeping the #121+#128 merge (worktree-lucky-harbor mutation-tested the merged tree).

The stop ladder's correctness has TWO halves, both from nocx-uvac6.11:
  A. the addressee — the foreground job's group is named ONCE, before the first signal (foregroundJob -> stopProcessGroup(pgid));
  B. the poller — the existence check addresses THAT group (groupGone(pgid)), not "is anything in front" (the deleted cooperatedForeground).

Mutation testing of the merged tree found the suite catches only the CONJUNCTION. So TestStopForeground_SignalsOnlyTheGroupItStartedAgainst guards the pre-fix STATE, not either invariant. A future change that reintroduces one half ships green. The two halves mask each other, which reads as defence in depth and is actually the absence of a guard on each.

This is AGENTS.md rule 3: the invariant is stated as a conjunction and tested only where both ends fail together.

## Steps to Reproduce

On the merged tree, apply each mutation separately and run `go test ./internal/transport`:

1. Revert ONLY the poller: `groupGone(sess, pgid, grace)` -> `cooperatedForeground(sess, grace)` (poll `SignalForeground(0)` instead of `SignalProcessGroup(pgid, 0)`).
   Observed: suite GREEN. The ladder still signals `SignalProcessGroup(pgid, ...)`, so it cannot reach a successor group.
2. Revert ONLY the addressee: make `stopProcessGroup` re-read the foreground group at every rung instead of using the captured pgid.
   Observed: suite GREEN. A correct `groupGone(pgid)` sees the named group is dead, so no escalation follows.
3. Revert BOTH.
   Observed: RED — "a command the person started afterwards was signalled: [terminated killed]".

## Proposed fix, cheap and needs no new scenario

The merged protected test already asserts "the addressee is named exactly ONCE" by counting reads on the fake. Apply the same counter to the independent-group ladder:

  A. assert the ladder reads "what is in front" EXACTLY ONCE across INT/TERM/KILL — a count, not an outcome.
  B. assert the existence poll is issued against the CAPTURED pgid — i.e. `SignalProcessGroup(pgid, 0)`, never `SignalForeground(0)`.

Both use the fake already in internal/transport/foreground_signal_test.go, which distinguishes "which group is in front" from "which groups still exist".

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reverting ONLY the addressee turns at least one test red, and that test is named for the addressee.
- Reverting ONLY the poller turns at least one test red, and that test is named for the poll.
- Reverting both: both red.
- Demonstrated by actually applying each mutation and pasting the output, not by reasoning.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Duplicate consolidated: nocx-uk3r4 described the same gap and is closed in favour of this one. Two things from it are worth keeping and are NOT in the description above.

Two concrete scenarios, one per half, so each revert reddens exactly one named test:
- ADDRESSEE alone: the job IGNORES SIGINT and stays alive while a successor group takes the foreground. A correct poller then does not short-circuit, so the ladder escalates, and every rung must address the ORIGINAL pgid with the successor receiving nothing. Reverting the addressee sends TERM/KILL to the successor.
- POLLER alone: the job takes SIGINT and exits, and a successor takes the foreground. A correct poller answers 'gone' and the ladder stops at INT. Reverting the poller escalates against the dead group.

And one change the second scenario needs in the handoffSession double: record the ATTEMPT before the h.live[pgid] check, so a signal aimed at a dead group is visible as an attempt instead of vanishing.
