Without it the only discriminator left is the returned outcome word, which is weaker evidence than the addressee list signalsTo() gives.

Cause of the duplicate was mine as coordinator: I told each of two sessions that its bead was the only one, having asked them the same question separately.

title: Оборванный SSH-канал во время коммита оставляет git на удалённой машине навсегда
description:
## Summary

Установлено при работе над nocx-hgtt0, который просил ответить на этот вопрос до
всякой правки. Ответ: утечка не только в тесте.

Если транспорт к `nocx-helper` умирает во время коммита, порождённый `git`
остаётся жить на удалённой машине неограниченно долго. Никто его не убивает и
ничто не ограничивает его по времени.

## Steps to Reproduce

Наблюдалось косвенно: тот же класс сирот накапливался локально из теста
(nocx-hgtt0, 62 процесса за 5 суток, 2364 форка в секунду). Прямое
воспроизведение: запустить `nocx-helper` на удалённом хосте, начать коммит с
медленным pre-commit хуком, оборвать SSH-канал. `git` на удалённой машине
продолжает работать; хелпер к этому моменту уже вышел.

## Цепочка, каждое звено проверено чтением кода

1. `cmd/nocx-helper/main.go:45` — `h.Serve(context.Background())`. Контекст,
   который никогда не отменяется.
2. `internal/helper/host/host.go:118` — `Serve` раздаёт этот контекст запросам
   (`h.frame(ctx, ...)` затем `go h.request(ctx, req)`) и возвращается по EOF,
   НЕ отменяя его.
3. `host.go:204` — `reqCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)`; `stop()` стоит в
   `defer` и потому не выполнится, пока обработчик висит в `repo.Commit`.
4. `internal/git/local/commit.go:53` — `spec{}` коммита не имеет поля
   `deadline`, в отличие от `status`, где стоит `r.ceilings.statusWall`. У
   коммита нет потолка по времени вовсе.
5. `internal/git/local/local.go:158-200` убивает группу процессов ТОЛЬКО по
   отмене контекста, которая по пунктам 1-3 не наступает.
6. `internal/git/local/factory.go:95` — `Stop()` гасит лишь прогрев окружения,
   порождённые процессы не отслеживает.
7. `internal/proc/group.go:36` — `Setpgid: true`, поэтому `git` переживает
   смерть хелпера и переезжает к init.

## Почему нельзя чинить рефлекторно

Очевидная правка — `Serve` отменяет контекст при возврате — меняет поведение,
выбранное намеренно. Именно то, что коммит на той стороне ДОВОДИТСЯ до конца,
делает исход `CommitIndeterminate`, а не `Failed`: клиент не может знать,
случился коммит или нет, и потому не имеет права повторять. Отмена превратила бы
это в «убит на середине» и породила бы свой класс частичных состояний.

Отсутствие потолка у коммита тоже, вероятно, намеренно: пользовательский
pre-commit хук может законно работать минуты — гонять тесты, линтеры.

Поэтому это решение, а не патч. Варианты, между которыми надо выбрать:

- Щедрый потолок по времени у коммита (минуты) с исходом `CommitIndeterminate`:
  не убивает законный медленный хук, но и не оставляет процесс навсегда.
- Отмена контекста при закрытии соединения, с явным пересмотром D12.
- Сборщик на стороне хелпера: пережившие соединение процессы дожимаются при
  выходе `main`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Выбранный вариант зафиксирован как ADR, если он меняет D12.
- Есть тест, где транспорт умирает во время коммита и порождённый `git` НЕ
  переживает выход хелпера — проверяется наблюдением за процессом, не глазами.
- Исход при потере транспорта на коммите по-прежнему `CommitIndeterminate` без
  ошибки и без head, либо изменение явно обосновано в ADR.
- Законный медленный pre-commit хук (минуты) по-прежнему доводится до конца.

title: Three e2e specs still assert the wire slug the centre stopped showing
description:
Found by the containerized e2e suite while integrating nocx-9wsb5, 2026-08-29.

Six failures, three specs across two browsers, all asserting a wire slug as rendered
text: e2e/notification-block-finished.spec.ts, e2e/notification-centre-grouping.spec.ts
and e2e/notification-centre.spec.ts.

They are not regressions. nocx-a9gf4 removed the slug from in front of a person and its
acceptance criterion already says any test asserting the slug moves with it. What went
wrong is planning: the brief that changed the catalogue labels named only
e2e/notification-channels.spec.ts as a consumer, and a grep for the six wire kinds finds
four spec files, not one. The unit suites did not catch it because their fixtures carry
their own labels; only the e2e specs read the real ones.

Worth keeping as a shape rather than an incident: when a value crosses from Go into what
a person reads, its consumers are not only the code that imports it. e2e specs read the
PRODUCT, so they consume every such value without importing anything, and a search for
importers will not find them.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Change a RoutableKind Label in internal/notify/catalogue.go.
2. Run the unit suites: green, because their fixtures are synthetic.
3. Run e2e/run-in-container.sh: the specs asserting the old wording fail.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The three specs assert the catalogue noun phrase, and their prose agrees with their code.
- e2e/run-in-container.sh is green on those three files in both browsers.
- Carried out under brief .internal/briefs/nc-w7-slugs.md.
close_reason: Merged at f674098d; three expected strings, 6/6 green in both browsers

title: Убрать .beads/issues.jsonl из git и машинерию merge driver-а
description:

Коммит 43029809. Замечание: критерий 'bd config get export.git-add = false' был неверен — bd резолвит корень по базе, которой в worktree нет, и читает конфиг главного клона; заменён на проверку содержимого файла.

title: pre-push публикует снапшот бэклога в refs/beads/snapshot
description:
## Summary

План, Task 1. Новая функция `publish_beads_snapshot` в `.githooks/beads-hook.sh`,
вызывается из `.githooks/pre-push` ПЕРЕД `push_beads_state`. Тест-харнесс
`scripts/test-beads-snapshot-hook.sh`, 19 проверок.

Три load-bearing решения, каждое куплено находкой ревью: `--no-verify` на
внутреннем push (иначе рекурсия без дна), вызов перед `push_beads_state` (иначе
под `set -e` не выполняется в единственном нужном сценарии), remote жёстко
`origin`, а не `$1`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `sh scripts/test-beads-snapshot-hook.sh` печатает `19 passed, 0 failed`.
- Регрессия на рекурсию: настоящий `git push` с установленным `core.hooksPath` запускает `pre-push` ровно один раз.
- Регрессия на порядок: при падении `bd dolt push` хук возвращает ненулевой код И снапшот на remote опубликован.
- Снапшот побайтово равен `bd export` (сравнение `cmp`, не `$(...)`).
- Каждый внешний вызов имеет тест, где он падает: `bd export`, `git hash-object`, `git mktree`, `git commit-tree`, `git push`.

close_reason: pre-push публикует снапшот в refs/beads/snapshot. 19/19 тестов, оба регрессионных проверены мутацией: без --no-verify хук отрабатывает 25 раз вместо одного, при обратном порядке вызовов снапшот не публикуется. На живом remote реф опубликован и побайтово равен bd export (2720 строк, 6656690 байт), в списке веток не значится. Сквозное восстановление: 2720/2720, id сохранены. Коммит 63bc085f.

title: A feed hint that arrives during an in-flight read is dropped, and a quiet feed stays behind
description:
Found while integrating nocx-9wsb5, 2026-08-29, and deliberately not carried by it.

A worker rewrote FeedStore.refetch (frontend/src/notify/feed-store.ts) to add a pending
revision, a connection epoch and a retry loop, on the argument that a notify.feed.changed
hint arriving DURING an in-flight read is dropped and the mutation it announced can be
lost until some later mutation raises another hint.

That is a correct reading of the code. It was reverted because it re-decided a documented
decision inside an unrelated task: the comment it replaced calls the window "deliberate and
bounded" and cites nocx-sb3f, whose whole argument is that a droppable hint costs one
refetch rather than a lost row. Whether the window is still the right trade is a question
for whoever owns that decision, with the reasoning in front of them.

The concrete case: a hint for revision N+1 arrives while the read for N is in flight;
refetch returns the in-flight promise, the hint is discarded, and the feed sits at N until
another mutation happens. On a quiet feed that is the last notification you were told about
not appearing until the next one does.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Hold a notify.feed.read response open.
2. Raise an event so notify.feed.changed fires for the next revision.
3. Let the read complete. The store applies the older snapshot and never refetches.
4. Raise nothing further: the panel and the bell stay one revision behind indefinitely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision, written down, on whether the window stays: it is nocx-sb3f decided one way
  and this bug reports the cost, so the answer belongs beside that reasoning rather than in
  a diff.
- If it closes: a test that holds a read open, fires a hint under it, and asserts the store
  reaches the newer revision with no further mutation.
- Whatever is decided, the comment says which it is, so the next reader does not have to
  re-derive it from behaviour.
notes:
2026-09-04, coordinator on feat/agent-ploicy: this is no longer only a reading of the code. It was OBSERVED, and the observation contradicts the premise the decision rests on.

Full two-browser container run on the merged tree, 43.6 minutes: 558 passed, 9 skipped, 1 failed. e2e/notification-centre-choice.spec.ts:125, WEBKIT ONLY — chromium passed the same commit in the same run in 12.0s. The same spec alone in webkit passes in 7.6s. Under the full run it took 37.9s and failed.

WHERE it failed is the point. commandFinished PASSED — the block header showed 'exit 1', so the command really finished. The next assertion, line 273, waited 30 seconds for the third COMMAND_FINISHED row and never got it. The mutation happened and the row did not arrive. That is this bead's shape exactly: a hint for revision N+1 arriving while the read for N is in flight, discarded, the feed sitting at N.

Load widens the window, which is why it takes a 43-minute two-browser run to see it and why webkit sees it first.

THE EVIDENCE BEARS ON nocx-sb3f DIRECTLY. That decision calls the window 'deliberate and bounded' on the argument that a droppable hint costs ONE REFETCH rather than a lost row. On a quiet feed it cost a lost row for at least 30 seconds — until some later mutation would have raised another hint. The cost the trade was made on is not the cost being paid.

NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: the fix re-decides a documented decision, and re-deciding a settled question inside somebody else's bugfix is how it stops being settled. Whoever owns nocx-sb3f should look at it with this in front of them. Raised to P1 for that reason, not because the e2e flake is urgent.

My branch touched neither the spec nor frontend/src/notify — 'git diff origin/main...HEAD' over both is empty. Nothing was weakened, no timeout widened, no retry added.

Repro cost: the whole suite, both browsers, ~45 minutes. It does not reproduce in a three-file window.
close_reason:
Fixed in 7e14c46d (frontend/src/notify/feed-store.ts). The window does NOT stay, and the decision is written where the reasoning it answers lives — the header comment now points at the chase, and the block above `hinted` says why coalescing is kept while the loss is not: the old bound was a mutation, not a duration, so on a quiet feed the announced row never appeared. The backend already promised the hint has a successor (ws_notify_feed.go, BroadcastFeedChanged); the renderer was the half not keeping it.

Criterion 2, verbatim: feed-store.test.ts 'chases a hint that arrived under an in-flight read, with no further mutation' holds read #2 open, fires hint 3 under it, resolves that read with the OLDER revision 2, emits nothing further, and asserts the store reaches revision 3 — plus that it stops there (3 reads, stable across a tick), so the flood argument still holds.

Two more tests came with it. 'forgets a pending hint across a reconnect' guards a real trap, not a hypothetical: the pending number belongs to the old backend's revision numbering, which a restart resets, so without the reset every later snapshot is below it and the chase never terminates — removing that one line makes the vitest worker abort. And the existing 'drops a snapshot older than the one it already holds' was strengthened: discarding a reordered snapshot must not also discard the hint it failed to satisfy.

Scope kept: a hint the refreshable outbound queue discards never reaches this store and is still lost. That door is nocx-sb3f, untouched, and the code now names which door is which. While establishing that, nocx-mrtvy was filed — outbound.stalled, the notice that policy depends on, has no subscriber in the renderer at all.

NOT claimed: that this closes the e2e red on notification-centre-choice.spec.ts. That failure reproduced once WITH this fix applied and did not reproduce in 25 further single-worker runs; no stall was logged in any run whose log survived. It is tracked separately.

title: ci-e2e (webkit) fails on a different spec almost every run
description:
The webkit e2e job fails on a different spec almost every run, and the same
commit both passes and fails. Three distinct failures across two runs of ONE
commit, plus a green run of the same commit earlier:

## Steps to Reproduce

Run `ci-e2e (webkit)` repeatedly on one commit (4e9d087d observed):

- run 33248486551 — green.
- run 33250569484, first attempt — `ask-about-full-screen-program.spec.ts:461`
  ("freezes, answers twice with one composer, thaws, and quits normally"):
  `atBottom: false, tailVisible: false`, with
  `Timeout 5000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate`.
- run 33250569484, rerun of the same job — that act PASSED, and instead
  `backup-restore.spec.ts:9` and `secret-panel-position.spec.ts:291` failed.

The three specs share nothing but the runner. Chromium is green on all of the
same runs, so it is webkit-specific or webkit-slower rather than a product
defect the browsers disagree about.

The one failure whose text we have is a 5-second budget on a scroll settling
(`expect.poll(...).toMatchObject({seated, atBottom, tailVisible})`). AGENTS.md:
"a test may not depend on timing. Wait on an observable state change — a frame,
a record, a DOM state — never on a duration. A spec that needs a slow machine
to pass is broken on a fast one too; it has only not been caught yet."

## Expected

The webkit job's result is a fact about the product, not about the runner's
load that afternoon. Today a red webkit job carries no information, which is
worse than no job at all: it trains everyone to re-run rather than read.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The three specs above wait on observable state rather than on a duration, or
  the budget is justified in the spec with what it is waiting for and why no
  observable exists.
- `ci-e2e (webkit)` passes ten consecutive runs on an unchanged commit.
notes:
2026-08-29, четвёртый спек в списке, и он даёт новую улику.

Прогон 33277630612, ci-e2e (webkit), PR #129 после обновления из main (main уже
содержал #141 и #138). Chromium и остальные шесть джобов зелёные, красный один:

  ✘ backup-restore.spec.ts:9 — строка 62,
    expect(getByRole('button', {name: 'Merge backup', exact: true})).toBeEnabled()
    Error: element(s) not found, таймаут 5000 ms.

Диф #129 — frontend/src/frame/*, read-screen, xterm; #138 — одна строка в
internal/transport (путь api.request.send). Ни один не касается backup.preview.
Пересечения по файлам нет.

НОВОЕ: отказ СДВИНУЛСЯ ВНИЗ по спеку. nocx-hphhh чинил ровно этот спек и ровно
эту пару шагов — отсутствие ожидания готовности секции и утверждение на два шага
ниже места поломки. Та правка работает: `.ui-file-input__name` теперь прошло,
заголовок «Preview — merge» тоже прошёл, то есть файл был прочитан И превью
пришло. Упало на кнопке, которая живёт ВНУТРИ того же `<Show when={preview()}>`,
что и заголовок (backup-restore-section.tsx:311 открывает Show, 314 — заголовок,
~405 — кнопка).

Отсюда следует то, что стоит проверить первым: раз заголовок был виден, а кнопки
не было все пять секунд, `preview()` должен был стать ложным ПОСЛЕ прохождения
заголовка и остаться таким. Это не «не успело» — это состояние, которое ушло.
Кандидаты: повторный вызов превью, обнуляющий preview на время запроса, или
ошибка, которая гасит блок молча. Проверять по трассе: был ли второй
backup.preview и что вернул.

Пятисекундный бюджет здесь — дефолт Playwright, а не осознанный выбор; но
поднимать его нельзя ровно по причине из описания бида: это закрепит симптом.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-6wgcw, which supersedes it in its own words and carries the discriminator this bead's framing lacked. This bead read the instability as webkit being flaky or slower; 6wgcw disproved that — the configuration, not the browser, predicts the failures — and has since root-caused the mechanism with evidence from CI run 33621032607: an earlier spec sets a vault up on the shared stand, internal/vault/presence.go auto-seals it ten seconds after the last client page goes away, and every later spec that assumes no vault exists meets a sealed one, whose native dialog makes the rest of the document inert. That also explains why the failing set never repeats. The discovered-from edge between the two already exists. This bead's two unique specs are carried into 6wgcw rather than lost. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: A helper test deletes its fixture repo while the peer is still committing into it
description:
The helper peer is still committing into the fixture repo when the test body ends, so
t.TempDir cleanup races git: `TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat .../002/.git: directory
not empty`. Every assertion passes and the test still fails.

The host serves frames synchronously inside Serve read loop, so the commit runs on the
peer goroutine. The test waits only for the CLIENT (<-done), which returns the moment the
transport dies — while the git it spawned is mid-write.

Severity: a red CI job on a green product.
Confidence: certain.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Add at the end of TestCommitTransportLossIsIndeterminate a select on conn.exited with a
   default branch that logs.
2. `go test ./internal/git/helper -run TestCommitTransportLossIsIndeterminate -count=5 -v`.
3. The default branch is taken on 5 of 5 runs: the peer is always still running when the
   body ends. CI is simply slow enough for RemoveAll to lose the race.

## Acceptance Criteria
- dialKillable waits for the peer to exit before any t.TempDir cleanup runs.
- The wait is on an observable (conn.exited), never a duration; a deadline bounds only the
  failure case.
close_reason: dialKillable waits on conn.exited before any t.TempDir cleanup; probe proved the peer runs past the test body 5/5. go test -count=5 green. 131fd813

title: Decide whether nocx offers an OS-keychain mode at all, now that its protection is measured
description:
Split out of nocx-e7bhr, which was filed as "the shipped vault can never reach
the login keychain" (P0) and whose measurement showed the sign was backwards.
That bead's comment carries the numbers; this one is the decision they leave.

WHAT IS MEASURED, on the owner's Mac, 2026-08-29. A secret under the system
provider is stored in the macOS login keychain in PLAINTEXT
(internal/vault/system/system.go:242) and is readable by any process running
as the user with one command — `security find-generic-password -s nocx -a <id>
-w` — silently, because /usr/bin/security is the trusted application in the
item's ACL and that is the same tool nocx itself goes through. A Swift binary
asking under its OWN signature was prompted for the user's password, which is
what makes the mechanism clear: the gate is real, and the thing it trusts is a
general-purpose CLI. The vault's root key, passphrase, recovery code and seal
state all sit outside that path. A secret under the file provider is under a
data key under the root key, wrapped argon2id into the passphrase and
separately into the recovery code.

THE DECISION, and it is not "add a build tag":

1. Do we offer the passphraseless setup at all? It is the only mode where the
   ROOT KEY ITSELF goes to the keychain (vault.go:295-304), so the whole vault
   inherits the protection measured above — and the process holding it now
   outlives the window by design.
2. Do we want INDIVIDUAL secrets in the keychain — the DefaultProvider choice
   at vault.go:394-398 — when the keychain adds no protection our own store
   lacks and subtracts the root key from the path?
3. If either answer is yes, what makes it honest? A caller reaching the
   keychain under its OWN signature IS gated by a consent prompt; shelling out
   to /usr/bin/security is what removes that. Whether nocx can reach the
   keychain as itself — SecItem APIs rather than go-keyring, and what that
   costs across re-signing and updates — is not established and would have to
   be, before the mode is worth having.
4. Linux is a separate answer, deliberately: the Secret Service under a
   desktop AppImage and a headless VPS are not the same case, and one build
   tag cannot be right for both by accident.

WHAT IS OUT. Changing release.yml is out until this is decided. The current
release build takes the file provider, which is the stronger of the two, so
there is no urgency and nothing to repair.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not a defect. The measurement that prompted it is reproducible from
nocx-e7bhr's comment: write an item the way go-keyring does, then read it from
an unrelated process via /usr/bin/security and again from a binary using
SecItemCopyMatching under its own signature.

## Acceptance Criteria

An ADR in docs/decisions/ answers all four questions above and says which
modes ship. Whatever it decides, the code and the release build agree with it
by construction rather than by accident: if a keychain mode ships, a release
build asserts its keystore stance on the BUILT BINARY rather than by reading
the workflow; if it does not, the silent-setup path and the system provider go
or are gated so that no release build can select them. nocx-e7bhr is closed by
that ADR, as decided rather than as fixed.
notes:
ADR half DONE: ADR-0050 landed as a4665deb, on main. It answers all four questions this bead posed and says which modes ship.

The second half of this bead's acceptance — 'the code and the release build agree with it by construction rather than by accident' — is NOT done and is now two epics, because steps 1-2 and steps 3-4 have different prerequisites:

  nocx-hqklb  ADR-0050 steps 1-2. Silent setup removed, passphrase + recovery
              code mandatory, keystore holds no verification material. Needs
              no macOS and no signing identity. IN PROGRESS.
  nocx-rybbm  ADR-0050 steps 3-4. Security.framework under our own code
              identity, item requires user presence. Blocked on two
              measurements nobody has made and on a release signing identity
              that exists only as a measurement. Both need a Mac.

bd cannot express task->epic blocking ('tasks can only block other tasks'), so this bead stays open by hand until both are closed. Close it then, not before.

nocx-e7bhr is closed as DECIDED by the ADR (closed with --force: it depends on this bead, and this bead outlives it).

title: The merge slot says who holds it, not just that it is held
description:
bd merge-slot check answers "held by shady2k" for every agent on this
machine, because bd resolves the holder as --holder, then \$BEADS_ACTOR, then
git user.name, then \$USER — and neither of the first two is set anywhere in
this repo. git user.name is the same string for every worktree and every
agent, so the slot proves that someone is merging and nothing else.

Measured cost, 2026-08-29, twice in one session: a coordinator could not tell
its own stale hold from another agent live hold, spent the investigation on
worktree mtimes and beads timestamps to guess, and ended up asking the owner.
Later the same session the slot changed hands mid-CI and the same question
had to be asked again.

The holder string should carry what a person decides on: which worktree and
which branch. Both are available with no infrastructure:

  bd merge-slot acquire --holder "$(basename "$PWD"):$(git branch --show-current)"
  # Holder: feat-agent-tools:feat/agent-tools

Two parts, because a rule nobody can follow cheaply is not a rule:

1. scripts/merge-slot.sh wraps acquire/release/check and computes the holder,
   so the correct call is SHORTER than the bare one.
2. AGENTS.md merge-slot paragraph uses the script and says in one line why the
   bare command is not enough.

Deliberately out: a lock with a lease or a timeout. A claim is not a lock
(AGENTS.md says so about beads generally) and this changes only what the slot
REPORTS, never what it enforces.
acceptance_criteria:
bd merge-slot check names the worktree and branch of the holder, not a
username shared by every agent on the machine. The AGENTS.md merge-slot
paragraph shows the command that produces it. Acquiring through the wrapper
from two different worktrees produces two distinguishable holder strings.
close_reason: Done. scripts/merge-slot.sh computes --holder as worktree:branch; AGENTS.md's merge-slot paragraph routes through it and says why the bare command is not enough. Verified: acquire from this tree reports 'Holder: feat-agent-tools:feat/agent-tools' where it previously reported 'shady2k', the string every agent on the machine shared.

title: A macOS temp directory named after the test overruns sun_path, so bind refuses its own socket
description:
Found by CI on PR #132 (run 33243823170), ci-mac:

  --- FAIL: TestBindPublishesTheSocketOnAnOrdinaryDirectory
      bind_internal_test.go:84: bind: coordinator: socket path exceeds the
      platform's unix-socket limit: 126 bytes at /var/folders/df/
      djsxfhc17x95674wsm_g8s980000gn/T/TestBindPublishesTheSocketOnAn
      OrdinaryDirectory4091818170/001/.srv.sock.39887

t.TempDir() embeds the TEST'S OWN NAME, and macOS roots it under
/var/folders/<two random components>/T/. sun_path is 104 bytes there against
108 on Linux, and /tmp is short, so the same test passes on ci-linux and
fails on ci-mac — the length of the test's name is what decides it.

The external test package already avoided this with shortDir(); the internal
one (bind_internal_test.go) had not.

## Steps to Reproduce

go test -tags gtk3 -run TestBindPublishesTheSocketOnAnOrdinaryDirectory
./internal/coordinator/ on macOS.

## Acceptance Criteria

The internal bind tests build their directory with os.MkdirTemp under a short
prefix rather than t.TempDir, so no test's name can push the socket path past
sun_path. Green on ci-mac.
close_reason: Fixed in 22fb8743, merged in fad33a64. bind_internal_test.go builds its directory with shortTempDir (os.MkdirTemp under a short prefix) instead of t.TempDir, so no test name can push the socket path past sun_path. ci-mac green on 8ad6e36d.

title: The notification panel names sessions and kinds in words
description:
Design §4 rendering half, §7, §10 filter clearing. AXES moves inside the component so labels can read props. Kind badge, its tooltip and the Kind filter all read notify.catalogue; unknown kinds fall back to the wire value with dots AND camel-case split, capitalised (pane.workFinished -> `Pane work finished`), from first render until the first successful read. sessionNameOf comes from the composition root as a prop beside canActivate. Sessions with no name collapse into ONE option, `Unavailable sessions` -- not `Closed`, since the name is also missing after a renderer reload and for every non-local backend.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No id and no dotted slug is rendered in any kind badge or filter option, in any state.
- Hiding a kind CLEARS a filter pick that named it. activeOn treats a vanished option as ALL without clearing the stored pick (notifications-panel.tsx:190), so otherwise hiding silently drops the filter and un-hiding silently restores one the user forgot.
- The panel distinguishes `nothing to catch up on` from `could not read`.
- PaneManager is NOT modified. sessionDisplayName keeps its signature and its consumers (panes.ts:1109, 1193, 2170; blocks.ts:1617).
close_reason: Merged into worktree/brave-field-ac50 at 2e66743f; returned three times — the refetch rework, a second derivation of the kind id, and runtime monkey-patching of the pane graph

title: Settings can say which kinds the notification centre shows
description:
Design §5. Six settings keyed notifications.centre.<kindId>, registered in app.go by a loop over the same DefaultCatalogue the routing toggles use. All default ON. Namespace is `centre` and not `route`: visibility delivers nothing, is not a channel, and exists for a kind with no offered routing pair.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The set of registered notifications.centre.* keys equals the presented kind ids exactly.
- Same Section as the routing settings (sectionBlocks is per-section); label is exactly `<kind label> -> Notification centre`; NO second RegisterSectionGroup (app.go:568 already does it, a second call panics, settings.go:195); registered AFTER the routing toggles so the column lands third.
- The centre cell description says the event is recorded either way and this governs showing and counting.
- The delivery cell's closing sentence becomes `With every delivery channel off, this kind reaches no channel -- it is still recorded in the notification centre.` (catalogue.go:131) -- beside a third column that may be on, the old wording is a lie the user can see.
close_reason: Merged into worktree/brave-field-ac50 at 10444350; returned twice in review — for the four missing registration assertions, then for the unused-var warning that init() answers honestly

title: The settings matrix parser serves both notification namespaces
description:
Design §5. parseRouteSettingKey/RouteCell and their comments in settings-domain.ts become notification-MATRIX vocabulary and accept both notifications.route.<kind>.<channel> and notifications.centre.<kind>, the latter mapping to cell (<kind>, centre). Leaving routing names on a parser that no longer only parses routes satisfies `look for the existing answer` in the letter and makes the API meaning false.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Both namespaces fold into ONE matrix; a malformed key in either is still refused and renders as an ordinary setting row.
- Column order is first-seen, so banner/toast/centre follows registration order -- asserted.
- Fixture labels in settings-domain.test.ts and settings.test.ts move to the noun-phrase wording so they do not drift from the catalogue.
close_reason: Merged into worktree/brave-field-ac50 at 1a4da787; diff reviewed against the brief's assertions

title: The kit says which rows are activatable, and paints a legible count badge
description:
Design §8, three kit repairs.

1. CollectionRow sets data-activatable=true when given onActivate; collection-view.css gives THAT row cursor:pointer. The rows were always clickable (notification-activation.test.tsx:139 proves it) -- nothing said so.
2. RecordRow.kind gains a typed `description` passed to the Badge's title (record-row.tsx:88 takes {label,tone} only, though Badge already accepts a title).
3. Badge gains typed variance for a SOLID fill -- opaque background, contrasting text, and a ring whose colour comes from a named CSS custom property with a token default, because Badge cannot know what it sits on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The HOVER background does NOT move onto the new variance. Connections (connections.tsx:2119) and Operations (operation-row.tsx:184) have action-bearing rows with no onActivate and would LOSE hover. Hover means `the pointer is over this row`; the cursor means `clicking does something`. Two facts, two rules -- asserted both ways.
- An activatable CollectionRow carries data-activatable and a non-activatable one does not; both still take hover.
- RecordRow passes its kind description to the badge title.
- Contrast asserted at browser level (jsdom does not resolve custom properties to colours) against a named threshold.
close_reason: Merged into worktree/brave-field-ac50 at 1a4da787; diff reviewed against the brief's assertions

title: notify.catalogue: one owner for the kind vocabulary, served over the wire
description:
Design §4. Catalogue must RETAIN its kind declarations (it drops them today, catalogue.go:138) and expose PresentedKinds; reconstructing from Pairs() is forbidden -- a kind with no offered pair would vanish while still raisable. The copy becomes DEEP (Trusts/DefaultChannels are nested slices, catalogue.go:69; the existing Pairs() copy is shallow, catalogue.go:256, and catalogue_test.go:251 misses it because it mutates only scalars). Labels become noun phrases. New JSON-RPC read notify.catalogue with contract, generated type, Go validation and an over-the-wire conformance test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- PresentedKinds returns every declared kind including one with NO offered pair -- unit test on a purpose-built catalogue (heuristic kind + network-only channel), since the shipped catalogue's two channels are both local (catalogue.go:372) and cannot produce that case.
- A real-socket test asserts notify.catalogue conforms to contracts/notify.catalogue.schema.json and returns the shipped presented set exactly.
- Mutating a nested Trusts slice through a returned Pair AND through PresentedKinds leaves the catalogue unchanged.
- Labels are noun phrases: Terminal bell, Command finished, Session ended, File transfer finished, Program notification request, Work seems to have finished.
- e2e/notification-channels.spec.ts:113 moves with the labels.
close_reason: Merged into worktree/brave-field-ac50 at 10444350; returned twice in review — for the four missing registration assertions, then for the unused-var warning that init() answers honestly

title: The bell counts what you asked to see
description:
Design §6 and §10. FeedStore.unreadCount() becomes a memo over occurrences() and the hidden set -- count visible rows whose read is false -- NOT wireUnread minus hiddenUnread, which would span two independent signals (feed-store.ts:39, :51) and have an intermediate state. The hidden set is ONE reactive projection owned by the composition root, fed by the EXISTING settings reconciliation (main.tsx:935); a second SettingsObserver handler would give one push two refetches. main.tsx:937 hard-codes observer.setRevision(0) and the first snapshot's revision is dropped with its block-local variable -- it must be carried. Also: a display-revision signal bumped by onDisplayChange (panes.ts:202) so a tab renamed while the panel is open relabels its filter option; main.tsx:546 states this rule for activeOrigin already.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The memo equals the wire count when nothing is hidden, excludes hidden kinds otherwise, and is UNMOVED by the panel's own filter.
- A batch of settings changes applies as ONE replacement: no render observes three kinds hidden and three not.
- The store distinguishes `not yet known` from zero; a never-successful first read must not show a confident zero forever (feed-store.ts:38, :96, :67).
- The hidden set is seeded before the sidebar mounts (main.tsx:385 awaits the snapshot, store is built at :1047, sidebar mounts at :1131) so there is no flash.
- dropped stays GLOBAL and its wording says so -- it carries no kind and cannot be restricted.
close_reason: Merged into worktree/brave-field-ac50 at 2e66743f; returned three times — the refetch rework, a second derivation of the kind id, and runtime monkey-patching of the pane graph

title: The notification centre speaks to a person, and you choose what it shows you
description:
The notification centre shows wire identifiers, its rows look inert, its unread badge is
illegible, and Settings cannot say which kinds it shows. Five defects reported by the owner
with screenshots, 2026-08-29.

Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-29-notification-centre-refinements-design.md
It amends centre design §6 and the unreadCount description in contracts/. §5 (unfiltered
ingest) is untouched: the backend pipeline is not modified at all.

## Success Criteria

A bell and a finished command are raised in a named tab while the window is elsewhere.
The rail badge shows a legible count. Every row names its kind in words ("Terminal bell"),
and the session filter offers the tab title -- no kind badge and no filter option contains
a dotted slug or a session id. Clicking a row focuses its tab. Turning
"Terminal bell -> Notification centre" off removes those rows and lowers the count; turning
it on restores every such row the feed still holds, including ones raised while it was off,
each with the read state it had.

Deliberately out: marking a row read by clicking it; what a dead row click does;
per-kind dropped; findBySession resolving non-local backends.
close_reason: Merged as PR #137 (1a047629). All five refinements shipped; e2e watched the happy path end to end (460 passed).

title: Queued TUI interrupt is scoped to the lifecycle attempt it was requested for
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Hold the session write loop behind an earlier blocked write.
2. Request session.signal while authenticated lifecycle attempt A is open and foreground group guard returns nothing-running.
3. Let A finish and command B start before the queued 0x03 drains.
4. Release the write loop.

## Observed
The unscoped 0x03 can reach B because attempt identity is checked only before EnqueueWrite.

## Expected
The queued interrupt is dropped unless exact attempt A is still open immediately before the channel write. No PTY sniffing and no protected shell-group signal.
acceptance_criteria: A queued fallback interrupt carries an exact lifecycle-attempt guard evaluated immediately before the channel write. If A is no longer open, the byte is dropped and session.signal returns unreconciled rather than delivered. A deterministic test holds the write queue, ends A, opens B, releases the queue, and proves B receives no 0x03. Existing shared-group q/Stop E2E and Linux/macOS CI pass.

title: no test reaches the protected-group path the Stop fallback was written for
description:
Review of PR #128 (nocx-92gfl.4). The fallback shipped with two green tests and
neither of them reaches it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Delete `reconcileSharedShellForeground` and its call site.
2. Run `go test -tags gtk3 ./internal/transport -run TestSessionSignal_` and the
   `ask-about-full-screen-program` e2e act.
3. `TestSessionSignal_SharedShellGroupUsesAuthenticatedLifecycle` fails for the wrong
   reason and the e2e stays green.

Why: the unit test runs on `newLifecycleTestEnv`, which hardwires `newRegWithStub`
(`ws_lifecycle_test.go:85`). A stub has no foreground group at all, so what the test
actually covers is "any ErrNoForeground plus an app attempt that was never started
enqueues 0x03" — which is finding 2 of nocx-7l4ex.10, asserted as if it were correct.
It also contradicts this test file's own header, which says a stub cannot prove
foreground-group behaviour.

The e2e act runs `sh 'script.sh'` typed at an interactive shell. Job control gives it
its own process group, so the ordinary TIOCGPGRP ladder handles it and the
`delivered` assertion holds with or without the fallback.

Measured on a real pty running `bash -i`, which is what `pty_local.go:143` launches:
default job control puts the child in its own group; `set +m` then a command puts the
child in the SHELL's group with the shell still alive; `exec cmd` also shares the group
but destroys the shell. ADR-0024:122 already names this topology — "`set +m` puts shell
and command in one group".

## Expected

An automated check watches a person stop a program that shares its launcher shell's
process group, and the outcome set the renderer branches on is enumerated where the
repository enumerates it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A real-PTY test disables job control with `set +m`, waits for the prompt, starts a
  helper that installs its behaviour before printing a marker absent from the submitted
  command line, and asserts `ForegroundProcessGroup() == LocalPty.Pid()` while the
  helper is alive.
- That test attaches an authenticated `start`, not merely `submitAttempt`.
- It asserts the helper's own receipt or exit AND that the launcher shell resumes;
  cleanup restores `set -m`.
- `TestSessionSignal_DTOConformsToContract` (`ws_contract_test.go:6447`) enumerates
  `unreconciled`, which its own comment already requires of it.
- An over-the-wire test produces fallback `delivered` and `unreconciled` off the real
  socket.
- Tests for the failure paths: the write queue refusing the byte, and a Stop whose
  context is cancelled while it waits.
close_reason: Fixed in 2a62f02f. TestSessionSignal_StopsAProgramInsideTheLauncherShellsGroup puts tail -f in the launcher shell's own group with set +m over a real pty and the real socket, with an authenticated start; deleting the mechanism turns its answer back into the incident's exact words. Policy table covers all four kernel answers including the failed kill and the refused queue; TestSessionSignal_DTOConformsToContract enumerates unreconciled; TestSessionSignal_UnreconciledOverTheWire proves it off the socket. The e2e act now types set +m so the journey crosses the protected group.

title: session.signal's protected-group fallback trusts an unstarted attempt, an ambiguous lane, and a failed kill
description:
Review of PR #128 (nocx-92gfl.4). The 0x03 fallback is selected from a collapsed
answer and from evidence that does not yet mean what it is read to mean.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. **A failed kill becomes a terminal write.** `internal/pty/signal_foreground.go:49`
   returns `ErrNoForeground` for BOTH "the foreground group is the protected launcher
   shell's" and "ESRCH, no such group". `foreground_signal.go:68` then collapses every
   OTHER kill failure (EPERM, an ioctl error) into `foregroundNothingRunning` as well,
   with a comment saying so. `reconcileSharedShellForeground` reads every
   `nothing-running` as "the guard fired", so a permission failure silently becomes a
   terminal write.

2. **An attempt that has not started is read as a running program.** Submit a command
   and stall the input queue or the renderer's write. `docs/lifecycle-protocol.md:186`:
   an app attempt is open from SUBMIT, before the bytes that could cause the shell's
   own `start` are written to the pty. Lifecycle says `Running` while the shell is
   still at its prompt, and Stop writes `0x03` into that prompt.
   `ExecutionAttempt.Started` (`internal/lifecycle/attempt.go:41`) flips only on an
   authenticated `start` and is exactly the discriminator this needs;
   `runningLifecycleAttempt` ignores it.

3. **The lane is chosen by map iteration order.** `runningLifecycleAttempt` breaks on
   the first lane whose owner is the session, over a Go map, and drops
   `lifecycleMu` before reading that lane's state. `lane -> session` is many-to-one by
   construction: `replayLifecycleFacts` collects all of a session's lanes,
   `unregisterLifecycleLanes` deletes all of them, and `RegisterLifecycleLane` replaces
   only the named lane. No live path mints two lanes for one session today — client
   reconnect is `attach` and does not recreate the channel — so this is latent rather
   than a live defect. It is still the wrong shape, and it is a two-line fix.

## Expected

The mechanism is selected from the kernel's own answer about foreground topology and
from an attempt the shell has authenticated, never from a collapsed error and never
from an arbitrary lane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `internal/pty` exposes a distinct error for the protected-shell-group branch;
  `ErrNoForeground` keeps its ESRCH/no-process meaning; every other kill error stays a
  failure and never selects the fallback.
- The fallback requires an attempt with `Started == true`.
- The lane resolver scans every lane bound to the session, refuses an ambiguous answer,
  and holds `lifecycleMu` across the state read.
- One test each: a kill that fails with something other than the guard, a
  submitted-but-not-started attempt, and a session with two lanes of which one is
  running.
close_reason: Fixed in 866b377b (pty: ErrProtectedForeground wrapping ErrNoForeground) and 2a62f02f (transport: one policy, two mechanisms chosen by classifyForeground; resolver requires Started, scans all lanes of the session, refuses ambiguity, holds lifecycleMu across the state read; a failed kill(2) is unreconciled and never selects the fallback).

title: Exec reports a connection loss for a lease its caller closed
description:
`discoveryConn.Exec` could report `ErrExecLost` for a lease its own caller had
just closed. Surfaced as a red `ci-backend (no-secret-service)` job on PR #128,
whose diff does not touch `internal/ssh`.

Closing a lease releases its pooled reference, and releasing the last reference
is what shuts the transport — so `closed` and `done` are BOTH shut a moment
apart on the ORDINARY path, and the loss is a consequence of the close, not a
fact about the host. `Exec`'s own header says so: "closed is checked before
done — sequentially, not in one select: when the lease was explicitly closed
AND the connection died, a select would pick between two ready cases at
random."

Two later paths broke that rule.

1. The in-flight select lists `<-c.done` and `<-c.closed` as two cases of ONE
   select — exactly the random pick the header forbids.
2. `classifyExecError` checked `done` BEFORE `closed` — the inverse ordering,
   and the path that actually fired: the exec goroutine woke on `errCh` (the
   session Close made `Run` return), fell through to classification, and by
   then `done` was shut too.

A caller distinguishing "I closed it" from "the host went away" therefore got
the wrong answer intermittently, and discovery would record a dead host where a
tab merely died.

## Steps to Reproduce

    go test -race -run TestDiscoveryConn_Close_MidExec_StopsRemoteExec -count=300 ./internal/ssh/

About 2 failures in 300 on a 4-core Linux box:
`Exec error after Close = ssh: exec connection lost, want ErrExecClosed`.
GOMAXPROCS=1 hides it; the window is the exec goroutine not yet parked in the
select when Close runs, so all three channels are ready when it arrives.

## Fix

One owner for the precedence: `discoveryConn.leaseErr()` derives the
lease-level error, closed before done, and every path reads it — the pre-flight
check, the in-flight select's wake, and `classifyExecError`. Waking on either
channel is fine; deciding the answer from which one woke you is not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A lease that is closed AND then lost answers `ErrExecClosed` from every exec
  path, asserted deterministically — no `-count` loop needed to see it.
- A lease that is only lost still answers `ErrExecLost`; a live lease answers
  no lease error (the paired positives).
- `classifyExecError` on a closed-then-lost lease answers `ErrExecClosed`.
- Inverting the precedence turns the new test RED at the closed-and-lost case.
- `go test -race -run TestDiscoveryConn_Close_MidExec_StopsRemoteExec -count=400`
  is green.
close_reason: leaseErr() is the one owner of lease-state precedence (closed before done); pre-flight, the in-flight select's wake and classifyExecError all read it. TestLeaseErr_ClosePrecedesLoss asserts closed-and-lost deterministically — inverting the order is red in one run. -race -count=400 green. PR #130.

title: An edit that would delete a line the assistant did not name is refused, not applied
description:
An edit that would remove a line the assistant did not intend to remove is
refused, instead of being applied.

Today hashline.Apply verifies WHERE it writes -- the revision token pins the
file's bytes and the window the read displayed -- but nothing verifies WHAT
the range ends on. `PUT 6.=11:` with an end line one too large deletes the
following statement, and both the patch and the resulting file are valid.

Add a verified end anchor to the patch grammar: the operation names the first
line it must NOT touch, together with that line's exact text.

  PUT FROM 7 UNTIL 10:"\treturn 0"

Apply resolves the replacement to 7..9 and refuses unless line 10 of the
pinned revision is byte-for-byte "\treturn 0". EOF is an explicit successor.
A mismatch is a hard error in the same family as ErrStaleRevision, never a
best-effort application.

THIS IS NOT A CONVENIENCE. It does not make the assistant's job easier --
hashline.Read already bakes line numbers into the text, so an assistant that
can see line 10 can equally write `PUT 6.=9:`. What it buys is that a
miscounted boundary becomes a refusal rather than a silent deletion, which is
the same promise nocx-q4so4 already makes about stale reads. Do not describe
it as block operations; nocx-qh5pz closed those, and its notes say why.

The successor line is a better witness than the construct's own last line: a
closing delimiter is almost always "}" and carries no identity, whereas the
first untouched sibling is usually distinctive.

DELIBERATELY OUT: inferring the end line, fuzzy or normalized matching of the
successor text, and any degradation of a failed verification to an unverified
apply.
acceptance_criteria: Apply refuses with a distinct error when the named successor line does not match the pinned revision byte-for-byte, and ZERO bytes are written in that case. Apply succeeds and replaces exactly up to the line before the successor when it does match. Verified over the real socket, not only in a unit test: the refusal reaches the assistant as a hard error and the file on disk is unchanged. A patch with no successor clause keeps working exactly as today.

title: Capture fence is a write barrier, not the next parse boundary
description:
Review of PR #129 (nocx-2ryxf.3). The starvation diagnosis was right and the
instrumented evidence stands, but the fence it shipped — "resolve at the first
completed onWriteParsed pass" — trades one defect for another.

xterm 5.5.0 `WriteBuffer._innerWrite` hands each queued chunk to the parser
WHOLE, fires that chunk's callback, and only THEN checks its 12 ms budget. So a
parse pass stops BETWEEN chunks and never inside one, and a completed pass can
end with bytes that were already queued when the capture was asked for still
unparsed. A bulk write (`cat` of a large file, a reattach ring replay) is then
answered with a screen from several passes ago — the same class of lie the fence
exists to prevent, in the other direction.

Two further consequences of the same reading:

- The 1000 ms local bound sits ON TOP of the browser's background-tab timer
  clamp. xterm continues parsing from setTimeout(0), and a hidden document
  (window minimised or occluded) has those clamped to ~1 s, so a capture on a
  backgrounded window would fail on a renderer that was about to answer.
- `frame/types.ts`, `renderers/types.ts` and the nocx-3j9b report still carried
  the repudiated model at the SEAM definitions ("a snapshot mid-queue can hold
  row 1 from before a write and row 20 from after it"), so the fence had two
  written owners disagreeing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a program that repaints continuously (`top`) or emits a large burst
   (`cat` of a big file) in a pane.
2. Ask the assistant a question that reaches `session.read` on that pane.
3. Before this fix: under `top` the fence never opened and the broker timed out
   at 30 s. With PR #129 as it stands: the capture answers at the next parse
   boundary, so under a burst the frame can be several passes behind the bytes
   the renderer had already been given when the request arrived.

## Fix

The fence is a write barrier: an empty `write('', cb)` on xterm's FIFO queue
settles once everything queued BEFORE it has been parsed, and writes arriving
afterwards go behind it and cannot postpone it. Complete under a bulk write,
unstarvable under a repainting TUI, and it needs no reasoning about passes.
`hasUnsettledWrite()` keeps one job: with nothing queued, skip the barrier —
issuing one on a motionless screen costs a parse pass, and a parse pass advances
the generation, which would report an unmoved screen as "moved" (ADR-0029).

Test debt paid in the same pass: mint.test.ts's "no frame mixes rows from before
and after one write" was green while asserting nothing — it awaited the fence
only after running both passes synchronously. The fake also modelled a sub-chunk
split xterm does not do, while claiming to be verified against its source.
acceptance_criteria:
- The fence opens with writes still queued (not global emptiness) — asserted on FakeSource and on the real XtermRenderer under a writer that repaints every parse pass.
- The fence does NOT open before every write queued before the request has parsed — a pass that gets through only the first chunk leaves it closed.
- A write arriving after the request cannot postpone the fence.
- A capture on a screen nothing wrote to leaves the generation unchanged (compareIdentity: same).
- A barrier that never settles rejects on the local bound, above the ~1s background-timer clamp and far below the broker's 30s, and read-screen answers outcome=failed.
- Both rejected fence models are RED against the suite: degrade the barrier to 'next parse boundary' and to 'queue emptiness' in turn, and each fails at least one assertion.
- No seam doc still describes the retired model.
close_reason: Fence rewritten as a write barrier (write('', cb) on xterm's FIFO queue) in d67644b6 on fix/live-screen-capture-bounded. Both rejected models — 'next parse boundary' and 'queue emptiness' — are now red against the suite on FakeSource and on the real XtermRenderer. Seam docs in frame/types.ts, renderers/types.ts and the nocx-3j9b report brought with it; the spec's fence section rewritten. Full frontend suite 5482/5482 green. Containerized jobs and e2e left to whoever integrates, per AGENTS.md.
