title: Grant presentation reconciles from the target, and its E2E stops branching on the start state
description:
Follow-ups from the review of PR #127 (nocx-a7mw7.5), all in the grant
presentation path. Independent of nocx-a7mw7.6.

1. AN OPEN BLOCK MENU SURVIVES A TARGET CHANGE. Overflow-menu items are built
   at open time from grantsAvailable(), and #127 closes menus only when the
   pane hides (terminal-content.ts:3607). setActive is also called
   programmatically — :4358 (ask entry) and :4597 (restore) — so a menu opened
   in Ask stays open advertising Mark after an automatic flip to Run. That is
   the exact defect nocx-a7mw7.5 exists to remove.
   → reconcileGrantPresentation() closes the pane's overflow menus too.

2. RECONCILE REUSES A FUNCTION THAT TAKES FOCUS. reconcileGrantPresentation()
   calls onSelectionChange(), which contains the nocx-45vkz ownership transfer
   (active.blur() at terminal-content.ts:672-690). The target-switch chord can
   therefore pull focus out of the composer. Reconcile wants the PROJECTION
   half of that function, not the ownership-transfer half.
   → split onSelectionChange into "claim the selection" and "project the
     offer"; reconcile calls only the projection.

3. IN RUN THE BLUR IS DEAD WEIGHT. The transfer runs before the availability
   check, so a Run selection still blurs the composer and then shows nothing —
   focus lost to protect an affordance that is no longer offered. The
   availability test belongs ahead of the claim.

4. THE E2E'S RUN ASSERTIONS ARE CONDITIONAL. e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts pointAt()
   computes `startedInRun` from the live indicator and puts every Run
   assertion behind it. At the later call sites it is already false by
   construction, and if the default start target ever became Ask the whole Run
   half stops testing anything while staying green — rule 1/2 in AGENTS.md.
   → assert the precondition or drive the target explicitly; never branch on it.

5. Minor: the setVisible() at terminal-content.ts:3304 is superseded by
   reconcileGrantPresentation() on :3311; editor.ts:561's "Null hides both
   chips" is stale now that the grant chip has a different owner;
   toggleInputTarget's comment (:4615) still names two entry points; the spec
   insert is missing the blank line before "Two rules fall out".

## Acceptance Criteria

- A programmatic setActive() to the shell target while a block menu is open
  closes that menu; a test watches it.
- Switching Run -> Ask with the composer focused and a stale scrollback
  selection present leaves the composer focused.
- A selection made in Run does not blur the composer; a test asserts
  document.activeElement is still the composer afterwards.
- pointAt() runs its Run assertions unconditionally, or fails loudly when the
  pane does not start in Run.
close_reason:
Run selections no longer claim the focus (the availability check moved ahead of the nocx-45vkz ownership transfer); the draft swap now holds and re-asserts the scrollback Range it would otherwise discard, on the same Range object; reconcileGrantPresentation closes the pane's block menus, covering the programmatic setActive that pane-hide could not. E2E pointAt no longer branches on the live indicator — pointAtFromRun asserts the pane is in Run and owns the Run coverage, and the specs that need Ask as setup flip through the real chord. Minors: duplicate setVisible at mount removed, setModelChip and toggleInputTarget comments corrected, spec paragraph break fixed.

CORRECTION to item 2 of this bead's description: splitting onSelectionChange into claim/projection is NOT wanted. After a flip to Ask the scrollback genuinely owns the selection, so reconcile must run the full claim, exactly as a fresh drag in Ask would. What was actually wrong was the ORDER — the claim ran before the availability test. Commit 4bad3cc5.

title: The target chord has one owner: fold the editor and summon claimants into one capture-phase arbiter
description:
Review of PR #127 (nocx-a7mw7.5) found the fix added a THIRD claimant on
Command/Ctrl+Enter — a document-level bubble handler in TerminalContent —
beside the two that already existed:

- CommandEditor.onKeydown, capture on editor.root (editor.ts:498, branch :901)
  → toggleInputTarget(), reached only when focus is inside the composer.
- the summon listener, capture on the xterm host (terminal-content.ts:3274)
  → summonEditor(canSummonEditor()); capture is mandatory there because
  xterm's textarea would otherwise turn the chord into a CR into the running
  command's stdin.

Those two are not two owners of one behaviour; they are two behaviours under
one key, split by `editor.isVisible`. The split is encoded as DOM position +
phase rather than read from the state — and the state test already exists:
canSummonEditor()'s first check is `if (editor.isVisible) return silent
'editor-visible'`. The DOM placement is a second, weaker copy of it.

The third claimant exists only because onSelectionChange's nocx-45vkz focus
transfer calls active.blur(), which parks focus on <body> — neither the
editor nor the grid — so neither existing claimant sees the chord. Its guard
chain (rootContains / isTextEntry / closest(button) / hasOpenOverlays /
document.querySelector('.cmd-overflow-menu')) has no unit coverage at all.

## What to build

ONE owner: a capture-phase keydown on document, per pane, gated on
`this._active && target.isConnected` — the position `_globalKeydown`
(terminal-content.ts:2673) already occupies, in capture rather than bubble.
Capture at the root runs before CM6's keymap, before xterm's textarea and
before the editor's own root-capture, so one place arbitrates all three
situations:

    if (!isTargetChord(e)) return
    if (!this._active || !target.isConnected) return
    if (hasOpenOverlays()) return
    if (isTextEntry(active) && !paneRoot.contains(active)) return
    e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation()
    if (this.editor?.isVisible) this.toggleInputTarget()
    else void this.summonEditor(...)

Deleted with it: the Ctrl+Enter branch in editor.ts and its onToggleTarget
action, the summon capture listener on the xterm host, and PR #127's document
bubble branch together with the completion?.dismiss() patch it forced.
canSummonEditor() keeps its refusal vocabulary and sheds only 'editor-visible'.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Exactly one keydown listener in the renderer tests `Enter` with a
  Command/Ctrl modifier as a target chord; grep proves the other two are gone.
- With focus in the composer, the chord flips the target and inserts NO blank
  line (CM6 defaultKeymap binds Mod-Enter to insertBlankLine; the single owner
  must swallow it in capture, never return early).
- With focus on <body> after a scrollback selection, the chord flips the target.
- With focus in the live grid while a command runs and the editor is hidden,
  the chord summons the editor and never reaches the pty as a CR.
- With an overlay open, or focus in a text control outside this pane, the
  chord is not consumed by this pane.
- Only the active pane acts on the chord with several panes mounted.
close_reason: One capture-phase listener at the document root now recognises the target chord, per pane. The editor-root and xterm-host claimants and PR #127's document bubble branch are gone; editor.ts no longer has an onToggleTarget action. editor.isVisible chooses flip vs summon. The arbiter chain moved from a closure to arbitrateEditorKey() so the chord can give the editor's surfaces first refusal through the same decision the editor uses. Two dead states fixed with tests that failed first: the summon was unreachable unless focus was in the grid, and an open block menu swallowed the chord in silence. 8 new specs; frontend suite 5484/5484; all pre-commit static gates green. Commit c27e0a88.

title: A session-ended notification says 'Not delivered' and arrives twice
description:
Found by the coordinator in the same container e2e run, and proven ours by the same baseline (the spec passes at 64244ad4).

  expect(received).toBe(expected)
  Expected: "Local session ended"
  Received: "Not delivered: Local session ended ×2"
  e2e/notification-centre.spec.ts:162

Two defects in one string. The notification is reported NOT DELIVERED, and it arrives TWICE. Both point at nocx-uo1k6, which moved notifications from a direct Wails injection to client-host requests routed to an attached client: a delivery that now fails reports honestly (which is the right behaviour for no UI host) but there IS a UI host here, and something is also raising it twice.

ADR-0026 already binds which client serves an ask and how a disconnect cancels one. Read it before changing the routing — the answer to 'who delivers' exists.

## Steps to Reproduce

PW_PROJECTS=chromium ./e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/notification-centre.spec.ts on feat/nocx-server at 4ec7963e. It passes on a worktree at 64244ad4.
acceptance_criteria: The notification arrives once and is not marked undelivered when a UI host is attached. A test asserts BOTH: the count and the absence of the 'Not delivered' prefix — the duplicate and the false failure are separate defects and one fix must not be assumed to cover the other. e2e/notification-centre.spec.ts and notification-centre-grouping.spec.ts pass in the container.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/nocx-server as 9fe58ad6.

MY BRIEF WAS WRONG AND THE WORKER CORRECTED IT: I insisted 'Not delivered:' and the '×2' were two separate defects and that one fix must not be assumed to cover the other. They are ONE. The renderer's client-host answered 'failed' whenever it found no Wails bindings — and a browser client has none, so in e2e every delivery 'failed' and the fallback path raised the notification a second time. Both halves of the string came from the same wrong equation: no native bindings == cannot deliver. A browser client can show a notification perfectly well; it just cannot show a NATIVE one.

Proved by the reverse operation: fix removed, the exact string came back and notification-centre.spec.ts went from 4.0s to a 30s timeout; fix restored, 2 passed at 32.1s and the spec is back to its baseline timing.

Also run: transport, clienthost, notify, deadcode 85 all baselined with 0 new, contracts:check, tsc on both projects, the full vitest suite at 5428 passed, and the two specs in the container.

Outside the names in the brief but not on the do-not-touch list, and justified: frontend/src/panes.ts gained the onPanesChanged subscription because PaneManager owns 'which pane holds this session' and the layout chain is the backend's projection, absent when the layout store cannot be read; plus main.tsx wiring, and contracts/host.resolved.schema.json with its generated TS, which the outcome change requires.

title: LocalPty.Resize touches the pty file with no lock and no closed check, so a resize during teardown races the fd
description:
Found by the nocx-44349 worker while proving its own fix, in a package its diff never touched, and reported rather than filed (its brief allowed no bd).

internal/pty's pty_local.go: Resize reaches lp.file and calls pty.Setsize -> os.File.Fd() with NO lp.mu hold and NO closed check, while Close closes that same file UNDER lp.mu. So any resize concurrent with teardown races internal/poll destroying the descriptor. The race detector reports it through LocalPty.Resize -> pty.Setsize -> os.File.Fd() against readPump.

It is pre-existing and structural — it does not matter who calls Resize or from which goroutine, so nocx-44349 neither introduced it nor could fix it by changing its own call site. It surfaces as TestWSServer_DisconnectSurvivesSession and TestWSServer_CreditCloseUnblocksWriter failing under -race in scripts/ci-linux.sh, intermittently.

Note this got easier to hit, not more dangerous, once resizes began arriving on a lane goroutine (nocx-eidfb.2): the race was always there, the traffic is new.

## Steps to Reproduce

./scripts/ci-linux.sh, or go test -race on internal/transport, repeatedly: TestWSServer_DisconnectSurvivesSession or TestWSServer_CreditCloseUnblocksWriter fails with a data race naming LocalPty.Resize and os.File.Fd().
acceptance_criteria: A resize concurrent with Close is safe by construction: Resize takes the same lock Close does and refuses a closed pty, rather than the caller being asked to sequence them. Asserted by a -race test that forces the overlap, repeated enough that the old code fails it. The two transport tests named above stop being intermittent.

title: Notes and snippets reach the assistant through their existing operations, with no bridge written
description:
The first projection wave, and the test of whether the machinery composes. Files: internal/agenttools, internal/capability/note.go and snippet.go, contracts/tools/.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One automated end-to-end check watches the assistant create a note, find it by its text, edit it and delete it, and do the same for a snippet, through the SAME capability operations the Notes and Snippets panels use.
- No second implementation of note or snippet behaviour anywhere. If a bridge turns out to be necessary, STOP and report it rather than writing one — that would mean the design is wrong, and learning it on notes is the point of choosing notes.
- A grant scoped to one note permits that note and refuses its sibling, asserted end to end rather than at the capability layer alone.
- The new tool rows carry every required declaration field, and their params schemas live in contracts/tools/.
- Tool output is declared untrusted: a note body is text somebody else wrote.
- go test ./internal/agenttools/... ./internal/assistant/... ./internal/capability/... -count=1 and targeted golangci-lint pass.
close_reason: Seven tools over the same capability.NoteOperation and SnippetOperation the panels use, no bridge written; create and update split so an omitted id cannot silently create; end-to-end through the real Ask pipeline plus a sibling-refusal test. Landed as 61fac13b.

title: Vault.Snapshot probes the system keystore on every call, so every vault.status is a keychain write
description:
Found by the nocx-qhg3q worker while implementing D10's declared keystore stance — outside its brief, and reported rather than quietly changed.

internal/vault/vault.go:1797 Vault.Snapshot lists the providers and calls p.Status(ctx) on each. internal/vault/system/system.go:134 Status is 'return p.Probe(ctx)', and Probe's FIRST operation is a WRITE — a fresh random entry, system.go:138. So on a build where the system provider is in play, every vault.status RPC performs a keychain write, not merely the one at startup.

On macOS a keychain write is the operation that raises a modal, which is why this matters beyond cost: it is a second and larger source of the nocx-o4hg dialog storm than the startup probe everyone was looking at. D10's declared stance (nocx-qhg3q) now gates whether the system provider is in play at all, so a headless or excluded build issues zero keyring calls — but on a tagged desktop build this remains per-call.

Arrived from nowhere during other work, so no parent.

## Steps to Reproduce

On a build with the system vault provider in play, call vault.status N times and count the operations reaching the keyring seam (internal/vault/system's Keyring interface). The count grows with N: one write, one read and one delete per call. On macOS each write against a keychain that cannot be resolved is a modal dialog.
acceptance_criteria: A status query does not write to the OS keystore. Asserted by counting keyring operations across N vault.status calls on an in-play provider: the count does not grow with N. Readiness may be cached, re-probed on a stated event, or answered without a write — the criterion is the count, not the mechanism.

title: Lazy tool presentation: essential union loaded, and tools.search over the eligible catalogue
description:
See the briefed design. Files: internal/agenttools, internal/assistant, contracts/tools.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Declared tool set is essential union loaded, rebuilt from Registry.ForGrant on EVERY model call, never by mutating the previous slice.
- tools.search returns only tools eligible under the current grant and currently available; it searches eligible, never Registry.All().
- loaded is presentation state: intersected with the current eligible set each call, storing names rather than copied schemas.
- A hidden tool called by name still executes through declaration, narrowing, policy and executor — hiding is presentation, never a second authorization.
- tools.search does not become unreachable when a grant refuses Observe: either it is effect-free presentation infrastructure, or lazy presentation switches off for that run.
- No execution bridge of any kind (ADR-0045).
- A test proves a grant shrinking mid-run removes a previously loaded tool from the next call.
- Lazy presentation off below a measured schema-token threshold, both projections tested.
close_reason: essential union loaded, rebuilt from ForGrant each call; tools.search over the eligible catalogue and reachable when Observe is refused; hidden tools execute through the full pipeline, proven by the tool's output reaching the next model request; loaded state private and -race clean. Landed as e6b17c14.

title: A policy row that governed nothing now governs writing to any file, and the person who set it to permit was answering a different question
description:
Until files.edit and files.create landed, EffectMutateReversible had NO tool behind it: LiveEffects() was [observe, mutate-destructive], and the Settings policy page offered a control over an effect class nothing could carry. Choosing permit on that row was a decision about nothing.

It is now the row that decides whether the assistant may write to a file, and the run grant's path scope is "/" (internal/transport, runGrantFor). So a person who set that row to permit — reasonably, because it did nothing — now has an assistant that edits files anywhere without being asked, and nothing told them the question changed.

An untouched row is safe: an invalid or unset decision resolves to ask (EffectPolicy.DecisionFor), so a fresh install offers the tools and asks before each write. The defect is confined to a row explicitly set to permit while it was inert, which includes any profile carried forward from a shipped build.

This is the shape AGENTS.md warns about in a different guise: a control that governed nothing is indistinguishable from one that governs something, and only the declaration table knows which is which. LiveEffects exists for exactly that reason and is now telling the truth — the settings surface just has no way to say that the truth changed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a profile where the assistant policy has MutateReversible set to permit (a setting made while the row was inert).
2. Ask the assistant to change a file.
3. The edit applies with no approval, over a grant whose path scope is the whole filesystem.

## Acceptance Criteria

A person whose stored policy permits an effect class that has newly gained tools is told before the first such call is permitted silently — the effect gains meaning, and the surface says so once rather than acting on an answer to a different question. Deliberately out: changing what an untouched row decides, which is already ask and already correct.
close_reason: Won't do: greenfield, the owner is the only user (2026-08-29). An untouched policy row already resolves to ask, so a fresh profile is correct; the defect only existed for a row explicitly set to permit while it was inert, and there is no population that did that. Reopen if the setting ships to anyone else while an effect class can still gain its first tool after the fact.

title: Every capability operation declares its agent disposition, and a missing one fails the build
description:
Implement what docs/assistant-ui-action-capability-map.md classified. Files: internal/capability/, internal/agenttools/.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every operation in internal/capability carries a disposition: Direct(metadata) | Adapted(agentOperation, reason) | Excluded(reason).
- A user-facing operation with no disposition DOES NOT ASSEMBLE — the same enforcement registration.go applies to a missing params validator. Not a permissive default: nil must be a build failure, because optional is fail-closed for security and fail-SILENT for the completeness requirement.
- The classification matches the committed map; where implementation shows the map wrong, change the map in the same commit and say so.
- A test proves no operation's domain gate lives in its transport binding: an operation constructed without transport holds the same gates.
- go test ./internal/capability/... ./internal/agenttools/... -count=1 and targeted golangci-lint pass. No repo-wide gates.
close_reason: Disposition on all 23 operations; a missing one refuses construction. Map verified correct against the wiring for all 23 and annotated as no longer authoritative. Gate ownership proven at the operation; the transport half is nocx-o9era.3. Landed as 9d325ce7, with two transport test doubles fixed by the coordinator as a merge defect.

title: A push is cheap again: pre-push stops running the containerized suites
description:
`pre-push` ran the two containerized suites — the whole Go module under -race,
the whole vitest suite — before a push could leave the machine. Measured on the
owner's box (12 cores, 16 GiB, OrbStack VM capped at 7.8 GiB) on 2026-08-28,
pushing a branch whose entire diff was frontend/ and .beads/issues.jsonl:

  go test -race (container)   273 %CPU  1.99 GiB
  vitest        (container)   455 %CPU  1.72 GiB
  another worktree's vitest   369 %CPU  2.10 GiB
  load average                4.3 -> 21.6 over four minutes, still running

Two of those three were this hook, and the Go half had no business running:
there is no .go file in that diff. The scoping could not see it. git hands a
pre-push hook the REMOTE's sha per ref, and for a branch the remote has never
seen that sha is forty zeros — no range to diff — so the hook took its
conservative branch and ran everything. Every task here gets its own worktree
and its own branch, so the first push of a branch IS the push: "scoped to what
the push actually changes" described a path that almost never executed.
Observed again an hour later, unprompted, from two other worktrees at once.

The scoping was fixable (`git rev-list <tip> --not --remotes=<remote>` answers
it whether or not the remote knows the branch). Not taken: it would make a
heavy gate fire half as often rather than make the push cheap, and a gate a
person waits four minutes for is one they learn to pass with --no-verify.

What catches a break instead, unchanged: pre-commit (static, seconds), CI as
the source of truth, and `make ci-full` on the merged tree by whoever
integrates. The runners in containerized-tests.sh stay — three test failure
messages already tell a developer to invoke them by hand.

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] `sh -n .githooks/pre-push` passes and the file is executable
[ ] A push runs no container: `docker ps` during one shows none from this
    worktree
[ ] The hook still calls push_beads_state, so refs/dolt/data still moves —
    beads-hook.sh is untouched
[ ] .githooks/containerized-tests.sh still defines go_test_containerized and
    vitest_containerized, and the three test messages naming it stay true
[ ] AGENTS.md "How we work" item 4 no longer claims pre-push runs the two
    containerized suites

title: The live region keeps the height it had when the pane was smaller
description:
The live region's height was an inline pixel value captured ONCE at mode entry:
`controller.ts` `setUnstructured` (:324) and `enterFullscreen` (:531) both read
`scrollbackArea.clientHeight` and wrote it to the box. `setLiveHeight`, the
re-measure path, returned at its first line unless the mode was `running`, so
nothing re-applied it when the scroller changed size afterwards.

The scroller does change size: the integration card is in the pane's flex flow
(`notice.tsx` `mountIntegrationNotice`), so raising and dismissing it takes its
own height off the top and gives it back. A markerless session enters
`unstructured` while the card is up; dismissing the card refits the xterm GRID
to the fresh `clientHeight` (`terminal-content.ts` `usableViewport`) and left the
BOX at the old height.

Because `.scrollback-inner` has `margin-top: auto` the stack hangs from the
bottom of the scroller, so the leftover space showed up as a blank strip at the
TOP and the rows past the box were clipped by `overflow: hidden`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an SSH session that fails to integrate, so the "Not integrated" card is
   raised and the terminal fills the pane underneath it.
2. Dismiss the card. A blank strip the height of the card stays above the
   prompt.
3. Run `top` (procps: it does NOT use the alternate screen, so nothing
   re-enters fullscreen either). It draws 34 of the 40 rows it was given; the
   rest are below the box.

Also, with no card involved: resize the window while an alt-screen program is
running.

## Acceptance Criteria

- "The live region fills the pane" has one owner that every re-measure reaches,
  rather than two copies run at mode entry.
- A test changes the scroller's height in `unstructured` and in `fullscreen` and
  asserts the box follows; an idle pane is left alone.
- Delivering a new viewport (the pane resize seam) re-measures the box, not only
  the grid.

title: Every bootstrap deadline is reported as a connection that ended
description:
`shellintegration`'s bootstrap writer tests `errors.Is(err,
shellintegration.ErrBootstrapDeadline)` (`bootstrap.go:348` and `:399`), but no
stream in production returned that sentinel: `internal/ssh` returned its own
(`ssh_bootstrap.go:25`) and `internal/session` a third
(`bootstrap_window.go:60`). The comparison was false for every session ever
opened.

Two consequences, both live:

- `ReasonBootstrapTimeout` was unreachable in production. Every bootstrap
  deadline reached the user as `bootstrap-interrupted`, i.e. "the connection
  ended", which is not what happened.
- The deadline branch is also the one that writes `abortHeader` to unblock a far
  side sitting on a header read. It never ran.

Green because each package's fake returned that package's own sentinel: the
implementer wrote the code and the test, and they agreed with each other.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an SSH session whose far side goes quiet during setup (or drive
   `DeliverBootstrap` with a stream returning `ssh.ErrBootstrapDeadline`).
2. The card says "The connection ended while nocx was still setting this session
   up" and no abort frame reaches the far side.

Seen in nocx.log 2026-08-28T17:35:15.095: `bootstrap.go:403` — the NON-deadline
branch — carrying error="ssh: bootstrap deadline".

## Acceptance Criteria

- One sentinel is shared by the writer and every stream that feeds it, in the
  interface's leaf package rather than three copies.
- A deadline reported by the production readers produces `bootstrap-timeout`,
  and the abort frame reaches the far side.
- The test that proves it lives where the real driver and the real vocabulary
  meet, not in a package whose fake can return the answer the writer wants.

title: A1.4 — the cutover: production runs on the coordinator, e2e follows it, devharness is deleted
description:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-28-the-nocx-server-design.md D11, section 7, section 8. The last step, and where the epic's acceptance test lives.

Production Wails starts using the coordinator instead of an in-process backend. cmd/devharness (51 lines of app.New + Start) is deleted: it is a second, similar thing to what nocx-server now is, and the suite should exercise the shipped server. e2e moves onto nocx-server, carrying NOCX_E2E_HOME_DIR and e2e/preflight.ts with it.

That move is what closes nocx-o4hg and nocx-nhhr: the keystore stance becomes a property of how the server is started rather than a flag missing on one path. Note the cause recorded on nocx-o4hg is wrong and corrected in the same commit, along with AGENTS.md, which repeats it — see the comment on that bead for the four security(1) commands that establish the real cause.
acceptance_criteria: The epic's end-to-end check, watched by one automated e2e run: start a long command, close the browser context ENTIRELY, wait until the command has produced more than 256 KiB and left markers for several seconds, open a FRESH client, reclaim the same pane by its server-issued identity, and see both the output produced while detached and the markers proving the process ran throughout. cmd/devharness no longer exists and nothing references it. nocx-o4hg and nocx-nhhr are closed, and neither AGENTS.md nor that bead still carries the re-signing explanation.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/nocx-server as 62d38687. The epic's acceptance test exists and it asserts rather than documents: e2e/coordinator-reclaim.spec.ts opens a page, starts a marker-per-second command, CLOSES THE BROWSER CONTEXT ENTIRELY, and a FRESH page reclaims the same pane — sessionId, sessionEpoch, instanceId and paneId all compared — with markers monotonic and markerAtReturn - markerAtDetach >= MARKERS_WHILE_DETACHED. That subtraction is the whole point: it proves the process RAN while nobody watched, rather than that a pane rendered. More than 256 KiB is produced while detached, so the ring genuinely filled and the recorder was genuinely exercised.

Pane adoption landed first, as briefed: TerminalContent can now be constructed with an existing SessionHandle, which is what nocx-oevq4 could not reach from its own ownership and honestly said so.

cmd/devharness is deleted. AGENTS.md's keychain section is rewritten with the MEASURED cause and explicitly says the old explanation was wrong and why — our binary never enters a keychain ACL because go-keyring shells out to /usr/bin/security, so re-signing cannot produce a prompt; the dialog was a disposable $HOME with no keychain in it, once per backend start, because a read fails silently and a WRITE raises.

Verification run by the coordinator on the merged tree is in progress separately (make ci-full). The worker's scoped run: build, vet, coordinator and cmd/nocx-server tests, deadcode, gofumpt, contracts:check, tsc in both projects, prettier, eslint, and 5419 vitest tests — all green; one pre-existing environmental failure in internal/app (no /bin/bash on this host).

FOUND AND NOT FIXED, correctly, now nocx-e7bhr at P0: release.yml builds cmd/nocx-server with -tags release only, never nocx_login_session, so the shipped coordinator is a headless build by tag and the installed app's vault can never reach the login keychain. Neither nocx-qhg3q nor nocx-ln6ht was wrong alone; the composition is.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
INHERITED FROM nocx-oevq4, and it is a reachability gap, not a nicety. The backend can list live sessions and hand one back, and the renderer can call it — but no pane ADOPTS a reclaimed session, so reclaimSession is reachable from tests and not from the product. TerminalContent.openRequestedSession always opens its own session; taking an existing one over needs a TerminalContent that can be constructed with an existing SessionHandle, in frontend/src/terminal-content.ts.

Until that exists, A1.4's acceptance test cannot pass by construction — it asks a fresh client to reclaim the same live pane, which is exactly the step missing. Treat it as the first thing A1.4 builds, not as a detail discovered at the end.

This is the nocx-rtg0 shape (a complete path with no production caller) and the A1.1 worker named it that way itself rather than letting it pass as done.

title: A1.3 — an update cannot certify a mixed pair, and the Linux server is versioned
description:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-28-the-nocx-server-design.md D4 second half, section 4, section 2's ADR-0003 row.

The defect this prevents: transaction.go:175 swaps the bundle and keeps the rollback journal pending; a surviving old coordinator answers the new window; the new renderer reports healthy; transaction.go:376 verifies only the on-disk bundle identity, not the running backend's version; :386 begins finalisation and :403 deletes the journal. A mixed pair certifies the update and disarms rollback. Health must be tied to the expected UI/server pair.

Linux: an AppImage unmounts its FUSE directory when the process exits, so a daemon spawned from inside it loses its own executable at exactly the moment it must survive. The binary is copied on first run to a VERSIONED path ~/.local/share/nocx/bin/nocx-server-<version>-<hash>, promoted atomically, and always spawned from there. A stable mutable name is forbidden — it eventually runs stale code forever. Content-hash verification and pruning already exist in internal/helper/deploy.

macOS: nocx-server is a second executable in the bundle. Under ADR-0003 it carries the same ad-hoc signing as the app, or it is the one file Gatekeeper meets unblessed.
acceptance_criteria: An update whose new coordinator has not started cannot be reported healthy: a test drives the exact sequence — swap the bundle, leave the old coordinator running, let the new UI connect — and the rollback journal SURVIVES. On Linux, updating the app updates the spawned server: after an update the running daemon is the new version, asserted on its reported build version, not on a file path. A stale versioned copy is pruned. The macOS bundle's second executable is signed with the app.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/nocx-server after nocx-c4wek landed, so the two halves arrive together. certifyPair refuses finalisation on three distinguishable grounds — the reporting build is not the installed one, no coordinator probe is wired (ErrPairUnverifiable), or the answering coordinator's build differs (ErrPairMismatch) — and leaves the rollback journal intact in every case. Fail-closed by construction, which is the only correct default for a check whose failure mode is disarming rollback. Commit travels through the seam and is deliberately not compared: the release manifest names no commit, so a check against a fact nobody recorded would be theatre.

Verified BY READING ONLY, and this is the part CI has to prove: the macOS bundle assembly, lipo, codesign, the AppImage packaging and its extraction check. None can be exercised on a Linux box.

serverbin and the probe are still unreachable until the launcher calls them — that is nocx-o5t6c, filed rather than hidden, and deadcode stays red until it lands.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Complete and reviewed; HELD UNMERGED until nocx-c4wek (A1.0b) lands the wiring, because merging alone would put 22 unreachable functions on the epic branch and turn ci-mac/ci-linux red. Branch w-a13-update, commit c57acb6c.

Verified by the coordinator against the code: internal/update/pair.go makes health a claim about a PAIR, and certifyPair refuses finalisation on three distinct grounds — the reporting build is not the installed version, no probe is wired (ErrPairUnverifiable), or the answering coordinator's build differs (ErrPairMismatch) — each with its own message and the rollback journal left intact every time. Fail-closed by construction, which is the correct default for a check that disarms rollback. Commit is carried through the seam and deliberately not compared, because the release manifest names no commit and a check against a fact nobody recorded is theatre.

Scope held exactly: internal/update, Makefile, .github/workflows/release.yml, scripts/appimage. No main.go, no internal/coordinator, no transport, no frontend.

Honest limits the worker stated and I am recording rather than losing: the macOS bundle assembly, lipo, codesign, the AppImage packaging and its extraction check were verified BY READING ONLY — none can be exercised on this Linux box. That is the part CI has to prove.

Also from that worker: the disk hit ENOSPC mid-edit and truncated internal/update/updater.go to zero, which it restored from git. It then trimmed ~/.cache/go-build of entries unused for >2 days, 73G to 51G.

comments.text: Correction: the wiring follow-up is nocx-hz415, not nocx-o5t6c as the close reason says.

title: A1.2b — the vault seals when the last client leaves, and the keystore stance is declared not discovered
description:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-28-the-nocx-server-design.md D9, D10.

D9: today main.go:639 -> app.go:2478 -> internal/vault/vault.go:754 seals the vault on app shutdown. With a daemon, quitting the window stops doing that, and the root key would sit in a live heap for days — an exposure that did not exist before. So the vault seals when the last client detaches. The cost is named and must be visible: an SSH session needing a secret while you are away does not reconnect by itself; it suspends, states that it is waiting for unlock (unlock_requester.go:205-227 already returns ErrNoClientConnected) and continues when you return. ADR-0032 keeps the dialog renderer-owned — do NOT invent a daemon-native dialog.

D10: verified on macOS this session — $HOME DOES move the login keychain, a read under a $HOME with no keychain fails silently, and a WRITE raises a modal nobody can dismiss on a headless host. internal/vault/system/system.go:138's Probe opens with exactly that write, on every backend start. So 'probe then fall back' cannot be the mechanism: the probe IS the failure. The stance is declared — by the launcher on a desktop start, by a build property on a headless one — and the write-probe runs only once the stance says the system keystore is in play. Note that NOCX_NO_SYSTEM_KEYSTORE is today an environment variable; for a process living for days that must become a build property, not something any process of the user can supply.
acceptance_criteria: The last client detaching seals the vault, asserted on the vault's own state and not on a log line. A session that needs a secret while sealed suspends with a reason a person can read, and resumes after unlock — no hang, no silent failure. On a host with no login keychain the coordinator starts, chooses the file provider, and raises ZERO modal dialogs — asserted by a test that runs with a $HOME containing no keychain.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/nocx-server as 5e45840d. deadcode on the merged branch: 85 unreachable, all baselined, exit 0 — nothing new. Tests run by the coordinator in the worker's own tree: vault, vault/file, vault/system, coordinator and transport (131s) all ok.

Both halves landed. Sealing is driven by client presence (internal/transport/client_presence.go, internal/vault/presence.go), not by process exit or a timer, and the interval is asserted with both ends named. The keystore stance is declared rather than discovered — and the worker asserted the property the macOS modal actually depends on rather than claiming to have tested the modal: TestNotInPlay_ProbeAndStatusMakeNoKeyringCall counts keyring operations and requires zero from an excluded provider, since the modal IS the operation. ADR-0032 held: no daemon-native prompt was invented.

Two small fixes made by the coordinator to complete the merge, both mechanical: three govet 'shadow' findings in the worker's new tests (renamed to getErr/unsealErr/putErr), and prettier on frontend/src/vault.tsx. Worth noting the worker reported the full static gate green on its own commit and the merged tree disagreed — the pre-commit gate does not see what a merge produces.

Discovered and filed rather than fixed: nocx-1lyqp, Vault.Snapshot probes the keychain on every call.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text: Correction: the bug discovered during this task is nocx-pq26e. The close reason names nocx-1lyqp, which was written before the bead existed and is not a real id.

title: A1.1s — output keeps flowing while nobody is attached, and the reclaim says what was missed
description:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-28-the-nocx-server-design.md D6, D7, D7a. BLOCKED on the D6 decision — the two answers build different things.

Why it exists: the ring is 256 KiB (ring.go:14) and blocks its writer when full (ring.go:74, implemented at :83), and the acks come from a client. With nobody attached nothing acks, so a detached session freezes after 256 KiB — the daemon stalls the very work it exists to protect.

D7a, whichever answer wins: the spill cursor is NOT an acknowledgement. AD-9 (architecture.md:181) and ring.go:186 both mean by ack that the FRONTEND received the bytes. A cursor saying the coordinator persisted them frees the memory ring but is a different fact with a different invariant. Two cursors, two names.

D7: the reclaim outcome must be visible and the renderer does not do this yet — a reset returns 'resumed' (ipc.ts:419) and the {resumed,lost} aggregate (:444) counts sessions the backend no longer holds, not replay gaps. The hook exists (state.resetCallback, :417); the notice does not use it. And 'clear + resync' owes a definition: reset today clears the decoder and renderer (terminal-content.ts:3018) while the backend returns no state when the offset is gone (ring.go:157). Replay must not begin inside a UTF-8 sequence or a VT escape.

AD-6 stays intact: bytes are spilled verbatim as transport buffering, never parsed, never a second scrollback.
acceptance_criteria: A session with no client attached keeps producing output past 256 KiB — asserted by the process still running, not by the pane rendering. On reclaim the client is resynchronised to a stated position, and replay never begins mid-rune or mid-escape. Reaching the bound produces the behaviour the D6 decision chose, and the product SAYS what happened — a degrade that reaches only the log fails this criterion.
close_reason: Superseded by nocx-22k1c before any work started. That epic already owns 'the backend keeps the output while no client is attached', and it already decided the answer this task got wrong: build ON the shipped capture path (nocx-2f0f, closed 2026-08-19 — ws_ledger_capture.go, capture-client.ts, artifacts/artifact_chunks, byte budget and eviction in nocx-2f0f.5), same store, same provenance, same retention knobs, never a second one beside it. This task proposed a bounded per-session spill FILE, which is exactly the forbidden second store. Its premise came from a wrong reading of ws_history_record.go:187, which governs a different path. D7a's distinction survives and moves to nocx-22k1c: a cursor saying the coordinator persisted bytes is not a frontend acknowledgement.

title: A1.1 — a fresh client reclaims a live pane, and one client owns it
description:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-28-the-nocx-server-design.md D5, D8, section 5. Today contracts/panes.create.schema.json:5 deliberately carries no live session id and says the session dies with the backend; that stops being true. The coordinator owns a durable paneId -> (instanceId, sessionId) association, and a claim is refused when instanceId differs — which is how AD-7 keeps holding across a coordinator restart (session.go:424 mints it, :516 stamps it, ws_session_handlers.go:561 carries it).

The gap this closes is precise: frontend/src/ipc.ts:355 is a Map in renderer memory and the reconnect pass at :403 reattaches only what is in it, so a fresh window today reattaches nothing and the live PTYs are orphaned.

Ownership (D8): ws.go:64 is a single subscriber slot and :75 replaces it silently. Make that explicit — a second attach takes the session and the displaced client is TOLD it lost it.

The ui-state ADR owns persisted pane facts; state the split rather than duplicating it — the pane is the renderer's durable identity, the live-session binding is the coordinator's, neither owns the other's half. New results get JSON Schemas in contracts/ with additionalProperties:false and explicit required, generated renderer types, and a test that validates the real payload off the real socket.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh client with an empty renderer session map lists the live sessions with their pane bindings and reclaims one. A claim carrying a stale instanceId is refused. Invariant asserted as an INTERVAL, not a moment: the association exists from before the session is announced to a client until either the session ends or the coordinator's instanceId changes. A second client attaching to an owned session takes it AND the displaced client observes that it lost it.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/nocx-server. Verified by the coordinator, not from the report: all three new result shapes carry a schema with additionalProperties:false AND an explicit required (sessions.live, attach, session.displaced), and each has BOTH a DTO conformance test and a …_OverTheWireConformsToContract test off the real socket — testing rule 5 satisfied in the form that actually proves the server sends it. 21 tests in ws_reclaim_test.go. The interval invariant is asserted as an interval, by name: TestReclaim_ThePaneAssociationHoldsFromBeforeTheAnnouncementUntilTheSessionEnds. Displacement is a real session.displaced notification, so the loser is told rather than silently replaced — ws.go:81 says why.

Run by the coordinator: go test ./internal/transport/... ./internal/session/... — 5 packages ok (transport 93s); and from frontend/, contracts:check and tsc --noEmit both clean.

My brief was wrong about two commands and the worker said so: contracts:check and tsc live under frontend/, not at the repo root. Corrected for later briefs.

Outside the stated ownership but not on the do-not-touch list, all justified: internal/capability/capability_test.go (fake registry needs the new interface method), frontend/src/test-support/panes-fixtures.ts (fake client gains onSessionDisplaced), .githooks/control-goroutines-baseline.json (two relays re-keyed for a changed signature), ws_session_ops_test.go (a test whose two-connection premise D8 makes impossible was rewritten rather than deleted).

DELIBERATELY INCOMPLETE, and reported rather than hidden: no pane adopts a reclaimed session yet — reclaimSession is reachable from tests and not from the product, because TerminalContent.openRequestedSession always opens its own session and taking one over needs frontend/src/terminal-content.ts, which this worker did not own. That is the nocx-rtg0 shape and the worker named it as such. Recorded on nocx-gpyxp (A1.4), where the epic's end-to-end acceptance lives.

title: A1.0b — the launcher: find the coordinator, spawn it detached, refuse an incompatible one
description:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-28-the-nocx-server-design.md section 4, D4. The Wails app stops starting the backend in-process and instead connects to the socket; if absent or dead it takes an exclusive lock beside the socket (two windows starting together must not raise two daemons), spawns nocx-server detached — setsid, stdio to /dev/null — and polls for readiness with a timeout. herdr's pattern, /home/dev/repos/herdr/src/server/autodetect.rs:181-218. The spawn environment is cleaned: an inherited NOCX_WS_ADDR or profile override makes the daemon resolve something other than what the launcher expects.

On a version mismatch A1.0b refuses to use the coordinator, stops it, starts the right one, and SAYS live sessions died. Graceful handover is A2.
acceptance_criteria: Cold start with no daemon raises exactly one. Two launchers started together raise exactly one. A spawn that fails is reported in the UI and does not hang. A deliberately older coordinator is refused, replaced, and the loss of its sessions is stated in the product, not only in the log. NOCX_WS_ADDR set in the launcher's environment does not reach the daemon.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/nocx-server. Verified by the coordinator against the code: GetWSPort and GetWSToken keep their names and signatures at main.go:384 and :406, so the renderer and the seven e2e specs that call them are untouched and no frontend file changed. The spawn is genuinely detached — syscall.SysProcAttr{Setsid: true} with nil stdio, which os/exec gives /dev/null — and takes no arguments at all, so the token cannot travel by argv even by accident. SpawnEnvironment strips the inherited overrides rather than passing them through. A version mismatch produces a typed NoticeSessionsLost rather than a log line, which is what makes the loss a thing the product says instead of a thing the log knows. go test ./internal/coordinator/... run by the coordinator: ok.

main.go lost 516 lines: the Wails root stops being the backend and becomes a window plus a launcher, which is the whole point of A1.

Not done here, correctly: the versioned copy under ~/.local/share/nocx/bin/ — serverBinaryPath resolves beside the executable, right for the macOS bundle and a plain build, and the code names the gap. That is nocx-ln6ht's serverbin, and wiring the two together is nocx-o5t6c.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
WIRING HANDOFF from nocx-ln6ht (A1.3), which is complete and held unmerged until this lands. Three edits in main.go, which A1.0b owns:

1. Inject a CoordinatorProbe into the updater. internal/update/pair.go defines the seam and internal/update/transaction.go now refuses to finalise without it — fail-closed, rollback journal kept. One line at the update.NewUpdater call (main.go:226): Coordinator: <the launcher's probe>, or update.NewInProcessCoordinatorProbe(version.Version, version.Commit) while the backend is still in-process. This is exactly the fact the launcher holds from the discovery Hello.
2. Call serverbin.Ensure/Prune and spawn from the path it returns. internal/update/serverbin is the versioned Linux install (~/.local/share/nocx/bin/nocx-server-<version>-<hash>, atomic promotion, content-hash verification, pruning). Without this the launcher spawns from inside the AppImage and the daemon loses its own executable when the window exits.
3. cmd/nocx-server has no --version flag, so the release smoke checks cannot assert the coordinator's version independently. Today both binaries link from one $LDFLAGS in one step so they cannot differ, and the workflow says so. Low priority, but note that A1.0a deliberately gave that binary NO flag parsing at all so a token could not arrive by argv — a --version flag is fine, a flag that accepts a value is the thing to think twice about.

Why this is a handoff and not a bug: deadcode currently reports 22 new unreachable functions (20 in serverbin, 2 in the in-process probe). The A1.3 worker refused to baseline them, correctly — that is the nocx-rtg0 shape, where a store shipped with a complete write path nothing called. The ratchet is not in pre-commit, so a commit passes, but ci-mac and ci-linux go red until this wiring exists. The task split is mine and it is the AGENTS.md nocx-z7s6 failure: a task that adds a Go package must land with the wiring that makes it reachable.

comments.text: Correction: the wiring follow-up is nocx-hz415. The close reason above names nocx-o5t6c, which was written before the bead existed and is not a real id.

title: A1.0a — cmd/nocx-server serves a discovery socket that says who it is
description: Design .internal/specs/2026-08-28-the-nocx-server-design.md section 4. The new build target plus the socket it serves, landing together so the commit is reachable (AGENTS.md: a task that adds a Go package lands with the wiring that makes it reachable). Parent dir 0700, socket 0600, peer-UID checked on every connection (SO_PEERCRED / getpeereid), symlink and foreign owner refused, bind atomic (temp name + rename) so two racing launchers cannot leave a live daemon without a socket. The hello states build version, protocol version and the loopback TCP address, and hands back the per-launch token minted at ws_auth.go:199. Paths derive from storage.AppDirName, so nocx vs nocx-dev isolation and Isolate for tests come free.
acceptance_criteria: A test client connects to the socket and reads back the daemon's build version, protocol version, TCP address and token. The token is NOT in argv, NOT in the process environment, NOT on disk and NOT in any log line — asserted, not assumed. A connection from a foreign UID is refused. A socket path that is a symlink is refused. Two concurrent binds leave exactly one live socket and one live daemon.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/nocx-server as f8a6767d. cmd/nocx-server plus internal/coordinator land together, so the package is reachable from a main and the deadcode ratchet is satisfied.

Verified by the coordinator against the code, not the report: SO_PEERCRED on Linux and getpeereid on darwin behind one interface with a test double (peer_linux.go / peer_darwin.go / peer_other.go); os.Lstat so a final symlink is never followed, and a symlink socket path refused with a named sentinel (ErrSymlinkPath); MkdirAll+Chmod 0o700 on the runtime directory; Chmod 0o600 on a temp name then os.Rename into place, so the bind is atomic; syscall.Flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB with the lock file deliberately not unlinked, because unlinking breaks flock's semantics.

The token: zero log calls reference it, and cmd/nocx-server/main.go contains no flag parsing, no os.Getenv and no os.Args read at all — so it cannot arrive or leave by argv or environment by construction, rather than by discipline. WSServer gained an additive Addr() beside Port(), because a discovery reply that named a port and let the client guess the host would be guessing on the client's behalf.

go test ./cmd/nocx-server/... ./internal/coordinator/... run by the coordinator: both ok. 823 lines of package test plus a bind-internal test; a failure test for every external call, each paired with a success.

internal/coordinator joined OS_PKG_DIRS in the Makefile, which is where the darwin peer-credential path first executes on ci-mac. Packaging is untouched — nocx-server is not yet in the release workflow or the macOS bundle, which is A1.3's 'where the binary lives'.

title: The coordinator outlives its window: quit nocx, reopen it, find the pane still running
description:
The Go backend stops being part of the Wails process and becomes cmd/nocx-server, a detached per-user daemon the desktop app finds, spawns and attaches to. Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-28-the-nocx-server-design.md (sections 3-8; this epic is A1). Wails becomes a window plus a launcher; the coordinator owns sessions, the ledger, the vault and the assistant.

Two build targets, not one artifact with a role flag (D1): internal/helper/deploy/build.go:82 is //go:embed all:artifacts and Makefile:104 builds three helpers into the shipped binary, so an artifact serving both roles would embed itself. AD-2 already prescribes multiple targets.

Crosses AD-2, AD-3, AD-7, AD-9, AD-10, ADR-0002 (whose own 'Revisit when' names this design), ADR-0003, ADR-0026, ADR-0032, the ui-state ADR, ADR-0036/0037 and ADR-0043 — section 2 of the design says what each already decided.

DELIBERATELY OUT: an autonomous agent with no client attached. ws_agent.go:756 terminalizes a run on disconnect and that stays true. The honest promise is 'the command the agent started keeps running; the agent's next step waits for a client'.
acceptance_criteria: Watched end to end by one automated e2e check, under three conditions without which it proves nothing: (1) start a long command, quit the client entirely (close the browser context), reopen a FRESH client and reclaim the same pane by its server-issued identity; (2) the command must have produced MORE THAN 256 KiB while detached, or the ring never filled and the spill was never exercised (ring.go:14/74); (3) the command leaves a marker per second and the markers spanning the detached window are counted after the return — that is what proves the process RAN rather than that a pane rendered. Plus: on a version mismatch the launcher refuses the old coordinator, replaces it, and SAYS live sessions died; and a mixed UI/coordinator pair can never report the update healthy (transaction.go:376/403).

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Scope corrected before any work started (2026-08-28). Two open epics already own halves of what this one first claimed, found by AGENTS.md's 'already filed?' check at filing time:

- nocx-22k1c owns recording output while no client is attached, and had already recorded that capture shipped with nocx-2f0f and that a recording must build ON that path, never beside it. This epic's A1.1s proposed a second store and is closed unstarted.
- nocx-eidfb owns the geometry of a session with no client — AD-1 has open carry {cols,rows} and the channel is created at that size, so a detached session has no size at all. This epic had not noticed it.

Both are dependencies of A1.4 (the cutover, where the acceptance test lives), not of the epic: the foundation, the launcher, the client host and the updater work do not touch either. Design corrected in commit 29e8ea4b.

title: The hooks leak lock-holding bd processes, and three concurrent pushes put six containers on an 8 GiB VM
description:
Two independent defects in the git hooks, both invisible to whoever pays for
them, and both measured on 2026-08-28.

**The hooks leak processes that hold the backlog's exclusive lock.**
`pull_beads_state` and `push_beads_state` wrap `bd` in `timeout` with no
`--kill-after`. `timeout` sends SIGTERM, and `bd dolt pull` ignores it — a
wedged run survived `kill` and needed `kill -9`. So the timeout reports 124,
the hook prints "backlog may be stale" and returns 0 as designed, and the `bd`
process keeps running, still holding `.dolt/noms/LOCK`. Every worktree on the
machine shares one embedded store, so each abandoned run freezes `bd ready`,
`bd create` and `bd export` everywhere until somebody finds the pid by hand.
`post-merge` and `post-rewrite` call the pull side, so an ordinary `git pull`
is enough to leak one. Observed: four sessions queued behind a single orphan,
the longest waiting 85 minutes.

**Three workers pushing at once put six containers on an 8 GiB VM.**
`CPU_SHARES=512` is documented at length, but the reasoning weighs the hook
against the *desktop* and was measured on one hook run. It cannot weigh a hook
against another hook: concurrent pushes all carry 512, so they are equal to each
other and together still take every core — a weight bounds a share, never an
aggregate. CPU is not the binding resource anyway. Each push runs two containers
(`go test -race`, `npm ci` + vitest), both memory-hungry, and this Docker VM has
12 CPUs but only 8 GiB. AGENTS.md already recorded the symptom without naming
the cause: "the containerized jobs serialize on one Docker daemon and one CPU,
so parallel workers each running four jobs finish later than the same work run
in sequence."

## Steps to Reproduce

Leaked lock holder:
1. With `bd dolt pull` unable to complete (nocx-v48vl), run `git pull`.
2. Wait past `BEADS_PULL_TIMEOUT` (60s). The hook prints the stale-backlog warning.
3. `pgrep -f 'bd dolt pull'` still returns a pid; `lsof .beads/embeddeddolt/nocx/.dolt/noms/LOCK` shows it holding the lock.
4. From any other worktree, `bd ready` blocks until that pid is killed with -9.

Container pile-up:
1. Have three worktrees each push a change touching `*.go` and `frontend/`.
2. `docker ps` shows up to six containers; the desktop becomes unusable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hook that times out leaves no `bd` process behind, and no lock held.
- Only one containerized gate runs at a time on a machine, however many
  worktrees push together.
- A push is never blocked forever by the serialization: a dead holder is
  reclaimed, and a slow one eventually yields with a warning.
- A push that runs neither suite (beads-only, docs-only) does not queue at all.
- The behaviour is covered by a test that needs no Docker.
close_reason:
Both defects fixed, but only half of it the way this bead proposed, and that is worth recording.

The leaked lock holders are fixed as filed: timeout -k 5 in .githooks/beads-hook.sh, so an interrupted bd dolt pull or push is actually killed instead of surviving with the embedded store's exclusive lock. Verified on a real git merge afterwards: zero orphans where the old hook left one every time.

The container pile-up was NOT fixed by the machine-wide lock this bead is mostly about. That lock was the wrong altitude: it changes WHO WAITS, not what a push costs, so the first pusher still paid four minutes and the second paid four more waiting. nocx-fwsw2 found the real cause -- the pre-push scoping never fired at all, because git hands the hook the REMOTE's sha, which for a branch the remote has not seen is forty zeros, so there was no range to diff and every push ran both suites regardless of what it touched. With every task on its own worktree branch, that was every push. The suites came out of pre-push entirely and a push went from ~4 minutes to 8 seconds.

The lock survives where it still guards something -- scripts/ci-linux.sh, scripts/ci-frontend.sh, e2e/run-in-container.sh -- and scripts/test-gate-lock.sh passes 11/11 against the current tree. What no longer takes it is a push, because a push no longer starts a container. The default CPU caps added here (ci-linux and the e2e runner were uncapped) also stand.

Criteria met: no process left holding the lock after a timeout; one containerized run at a time on the paths that start containers; a beads-only or docs-only push queues for nothing; covered by a test that needs no Docker. The criterion about three simultaneous pushes is met by removal rather than by serialization.

title: The UI-action inventory: every user-facing action mapped to its operation and its agent entry
description:
Analysis and a tracked document, no production code. Method count cannot prove UI coverage: some methods are callbacks, some UI actions compose several methods, some renderer-local actions call none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A tracked file maps every user-facing UI action to the internal/capability operation(s) behind it, the intended agent entry point, and the headless acceptance test that would prove it.
- Each operation in internal/capability is classified Direct / Adapted / Excluded against the seven-part pre-projection test in the parent epic, with the reason written for every Adapted and Excluded one.
- A UI action reachable by no operation is named as such rather than omitted.
- Counts, not adjectives: how many operations, how many in each class.
- No production code changes. This task produces the map the projection waves are cut from.
close_reason: 95 UI action families mapped, 23 capability operations classified 14 Direct / 7 Adapted / 2 Excluded with reasons, 21 action families with no operation named individually. Three Direct classifications re-verified against criterion 1 with file:line evidence after review. Landed as 2952405e.

title: internal/hashline, files.read revisions, and a strict one-file files.edit
description:
Build the edit path end to end in one task, because a Go package that lands without its caller cannot pass the deadcode ratchet (AGENTS.md, and nocx-z7s6 is the bead where a plan made that unavoidable).

Read the parent epic nocx-q4so4 in full, including the 2026-08-28 notes — they carry three findings verified against oh-my-pi that change what to build.

Files: internal/hashline (new), internal/filesystem, internal/assistant/execute.go, internal/agenttools/*, contracts/tools/.

## Acceptance Criteria

- files.read returns a strong opaque revision plus line-window addressing and numbered output, and records which lines were displayed. Its contract stops describing byte offsets as 'lines'.
- files.edit takes { path, revision, patch } with exactly four operations: PUT N.=M: / PUT <N: / PUT >N: / CUT N.=M.
- AN EDIT AGAINST A STALE READ IS REFUSED, with no recovery, no proximity search and no head/tail exception. Asserted by a test that reads, mutates the file behind the assistant's back, then applies: the apply fails, says so, and the file is untouched.
- Any byte changed invalidates the revision — no normalisation of trailing whitespace, BOM or line endings when TESTING staleness.
- Only lines displayed under that revision may be addressed.
- The refusal is a tool result the model can act on, not a run failure.
- files.create (create-if-absent) also lands; files.move and files.delete deliberately do not.
- The approval names the FILE and shows what will change.
- Blocks (PUT N*), registers, MV and REM are deliberately out — nocx-qh5pz owns them.
close_reason: internal/hashline with four operations, files.read revisions + displayed-line window, strict one-file files.edit and files.create. Stale edit refused as a tool result through the real Ask pipeline; ledger asserted to record files.edit rather than a shell command; every capability narrowed to the call's resources with a negative assertion each. Landed as 171194d9.

title: Params contracts exist as a mechanism, proven on notes.* and snippets.*
description:
Establish the params-contract mechanism and prove it on the notes.* and snippets.* methods only — NOT on all 175.

Files: contracts/, contracts/README.md, internal/transport tests, frontend generated types. internal/agenttools, internal/assistant and internal/content are owned by other workers this wave — do not edit them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A params contract exists for every notes.* and snippets.* control method, in the same style as the existing result contracts: additionalProperties false plus an explicit required list.
- Naming keeps params and results distinguishable and the README says which is which.
- A Go test proves the REGISTERED paramsValidator and the schema agree for each of those methods: params the schema rejects, the validator must reject too. This is the point of the task — a schema nothing enforces is theatre.
- contracts/README.md's 'Params, for now' out-of-scope entry is updated to describe what now exists and what is still unswept.
- The remaining unswept methods are listed somewhere durable so the sweep can finish later.
- Do NOT adopt OpenRPC in this task; it is the parent epic's second half and needs the full method set first. Say in the notes what you learned that bears on it.
- go build ./... and the transport package's own tests pass. Do not run repo-wide gates or the e2e suite.
