title: The resource kinds the first projection wave needs, and ADR-0020 amended to say why
description:
Apply the parent epic's four-part test to the nouns the notes+snippets projection wave needs, implement what passes it, amend ADR-0020.

Files: internal/content/ledger.go, internal/content/effectpolicy.go, docs/decisions/0020-*.md and their tests. internal/agenttools and internal/assistant are owned by another worker this wave — do not edit them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each candidate noun (note, snippet, workspace, tab, pane, tunnel, endpoint) is judged against the four-part test in writing, and the judgement is in the ADR amendment — including the ones REJECTED and why.
- The kinds that pass exist in content.ResourceKind with canonical-id and containment rules.
- A grant scoped to one note's sub-scope permits that note and refuses its sibling. Asserted by a test.
- effectpolicy's validation accepts the new kinds and still refuses a malformed scope.
- ADR-0020 is amended, not rewritten: the original decision text stays and the amendment is dated and additive.
- go build ./... and go test ./internal/content/... pass. Do not run repo-wide gates.
close_reason: Two kinds added (content, workspace) with sub-scope containment; ADR-0020 amended with the four-part judgement for all seven candidate nouns including the five rejections. Landed as aea3e505.

title: A call's resources come from its arguments, and the capability is the intersection with the grant
description:
Replace the singular ResourceArg/Resources[0] derivation (internal/assistant/kernel.go, namedResource) and the grant-only Narrow (internal/agenttools/registry.go).

Files: internal/agenttools/registry.go, narrow.go, internal/assistant/kernel.go and their tests. internal/content is owned by another worker this wave — do not edit it; define ResourceRef in internal/agenttools.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A declaration resolves its resources from validated arguments plus the run context, returning zero or more ResourceRef (kind + canonical id), not one.
- The scope check tests EVERY resolved resource against the grant; a call whose first resource is in scope and whose second is not is refused. Asserted by a test.
- The approval shows every resolved resource, not the first.
- Narrow receives the call's resolved resources and the capability it builds carries the intersection of those with the grant, never the whole grant. Asserted by a test.
- The five existing rows keep working unchanged: files.read, session.list, session.read, run, git.status.
- go build ./... and go test ./internal/agenttools/... ./internal/assistant/... pass. Do not run repo-wide gates.
close_reason: ResolveResources + Narrow(grant, resources, runCtx); every resolved resource scope-checked; capability is the intersection. Path containment unified onto content.GrantScope.Contains. Landed as 282c7d71.

title: Tool output is framed as untrusted only when the tool reads, so run's output is not framed at all
description:
internal/agenttools/registry.go:94, FrameToolResult: `if d.Effect != content.EffectObserve { return result }`. The frame marking tool output as untrusted data is gated on the tool's declared EFFECT. `run` is EffectMutateDestructive, so the output of an arbitrary program — a log file, a curl response, an ssh host's MOTD, a commit message someone else wrote — reaches the model unframed, while files.read's output is framed.

Output trust and call effect are ORTHOGONAL. Everything a program hands back is attacker-influenceable regardless of what the call does to the world, and a mutating call returns text just as readable as an observing one. The framing predicate needs its own metadata rather than borrowing the lattice.

Projection makes it worse: API responses, git text, filenames, note bodies and remote errors all arrive through operations whose effect is not Observe.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Grant the assistant a session and permit mutation.
2. Have it call `run` with a command whose output contains instructions addressed to a model (`cat` a file containing "ignore previous instructions and …").
3. Inspect what reaches the model: internal/assistant/kernel.go:1519 FrameForModel -> Declaration.FrameToolResult returns the result unchanged because the effect is not Observe.
4. Compare with files.read on the same file, which IS wrapped in the untrusted-data frame.

## Acceptance Criteria

Whether a tool's output is framed is decided by metadata of its own, not by its effect class; `run`'s output is framed; a test asserts the frame for at least one Observe tool and one mutating tool, and asserts that adding a row without stating its output trust does not assemble. Verified 2026-08-28: FrameToolResult is reached only from FrameForModel and nothing else frames anything.
close_reason: OutputTrust is its own required declaration field; run is untrusted; the framing test proves an observing and a mutating tool frame identically. Landed as e7483014.

title: The assistant keeps your notes and snippets: writes one, finds one, fixes one
description:
First projection wave, chosen to be the cheapest honest test of the whole mechanism rather than the most valuable domain. notes.create/delete/update/get/list/search and snippets.create/delete/list/reorder/update already exist as control methods over capability.NoteOperation and capability.SnippetOperation; they are self-contained, bounded, headless, and have no connection-owned identity — which is what makes them Direct.

What this wave is really proving: that a disposition plus multi-resource narrowing plus lazy presentation compose into a working tool without a bridge being written for the feature. If it needs one, the design is wrong and better to learn it on notes than on files.
acceptance_criteria: One automated end-to-end check watches the assistant create a note, find it by its text, edit it and delete it, and do the same for a snippet, through the same operations the Notes and Snippets panels use — no second implementation of any of it. A grant scoped to one note refuses the sibling. Deliberately out: every other domain; this wave is notes and snippets because both are Direct under the pre-projection test and neither touches session ownership or renderer lifetime.
close_reason: The assistant creates a note, finds it by its text, edits it and deletes it, and the same for snippets, through the operations the panels use.

title: The assistant finds the tool it needs instead of being shown every tool there is
description:
PROJECTION MAKES THIS MANDATORY, not an optimisation. Once the assistant reaches the UI surface, the eligible catalogue is far past what can be declared eagerly.

State model:

    eligible = Registry.ForGrant(grant)
    visible  = essential ∪ loaded
    model tools = eligible ∩ visible
    search catalog = eligible − visible

loaded is PRESENTATION state, never authority — it is intersected with the current eligible set every call, because a grant change or a resumed attempt can remove a tool. Store loaded NAMES, never copied schemas; resolve description and schema from the registry on each projection.

WHY NOT xd:// (oh-my-pi's mechanism, packages/coding-agent/src/tools/xdev.ts). It mounts tools as virtual devices over read/write: 'write xd://<tool>' with content = JSON args. In a codebase with an effect lattice that is unsound — the declared outer effect is a mutation even when the inner tool is Observe, the resource is supposedly a path though xd://… is not one, the approval and the ledger name 'write' rather than the operation the person authorised, and the write capability cannot confer the inner tool's authority. oh-my-pi repairs this by re-resolving the inner tool, re-validating its args and recomputing its approval tier (xdev.ts:427), which is itself the proof that the inner tool is the semantic unit and 'write' is only presentation. Against ADR-0045.

THE BOOTSTRAP EDGE. tools.search must NOT be an ordinary grant-gated Observe tool: if a grant refuses Observe but permits mutation, the model loses its only route to discovering the mutators it IS allowed. It is effect-free presentation infrastructure — logged and routed, holding no domain capability — or lazy presentation switches off for that run and every eligible tool is shown. No silent policy exception for catalogue convenience.

THE ROUTING PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTS, inverted: einoadapter.go's unknown-tool anchor is kept in the ToolsNode precisely so ADK can route a call the model cannot see. Lazy loading needs that for every eligible-but-unloaded tool. But BeforeModelRewriteState currently filters state.ToolInfos destructively (einoadapter.go:123) and engine.go:389 derives executors and ToolInfos together at construction — both have to change.

Activation is measured on schema tokens, selection accuracy, turns and task completion, not on raw tool count. The essential set is measured too.
acceptance_criteria: With lazy presentation on, the model's declared tool set is essential ∪ loaded, rebuilt from Registry.ForGrant on EVERY model call rather than filtered from the previous slice; tools.search reveals only tools eligible under the current grant and currently available; a name the model guesses without loading still reaches the real declaration, narrowing, policy and executor. A test proves a grant that shrinks mid-run removes a previously loaded tool from the next call's set. Deliberately out: any execution bridge — no tool_call, no write-to-URL, no xd:// (ADR-0045: declared calls are the only carrier).
close_reason: The assistant is shown essential tools and finds the rest by search, with execution always a declared call by the tool's own name (ADR-0045).

title: Every operation says whether the assistant may reach it, and forgetting to say fails the build
description:
internal/capability ALREADY IS the neutral operation catalogue — agent, api, api_scope, backup, capture_tabby, config, content, endpoint, files, git, layout, ledger, note, open, secret, session, snippet, uistate, vault. Each is New<Domain>Operation(domainGate, lane, service): transport-independent, holding its own gates and service, with the methodSpec handler a thin wrapper. So this epic classifies what exists; it does not build a catalogue.

WHY DISPOSITION CANNOT BE AN OPTIONAL FIELD. Optional is fail-closed for security and fail-SILENT for the completeness requirement the owner set (2026-08-28: 'по хорошему любая функция UI должна быть доступна агенту'). Somebody leaves notes.search's field nil and every assembly test stays green. Requiring one of three values turns 'somebody forgot' into 'the server does not build'.

THE PRE-PROJECTION TEST. An operation is Direct only if all seven hold:
1. It runs headless — no wsConn, connState, current selection, or reverse renderer request.
2. Every affected resource resolves from explicit arguments plus the immutable run context, BEFORE the side effect.
3. It returns exactly one bounded, self-contained result or error.
4. Its ownership and cancellation lifetime make sense for an agent run, session or workspace.
5. Retry and idempotency behaviour are defined.
6. The result is enough to choose the next action without consulting undocumented UI state.
7. Its agent params schema exposes no transport handle or presentation mechanic.
If the test needs a fake websocket, it failed.

Expect fewer than half to be Direct. Direct: notes, snippets, history/ledger queries, much config CRUD. Adapted: files/git bindings, layout creation, tunnel lifecycle, api send/cancel, backup. Excluded: acks, resolved callbacks, notification ingress, dialogs, capture bookkeeping, renderer-lifetime watches, agent-control methods.

METHOD COUNT DOES NOT PROVE UI COVERAGE — some methods are callbacks, some UI actions compose several methods, some renderer-local actions call none. Hence the mapping table rather than a schema count.
acceptance_criteria: Every operation in internal/capability carries a disposition — Direct(metadata) | Adapted(agentOperation, reason) | Excluded(reason) — and an operation without one does not assemble, the same enforcement registration.go already applies to paramsValidator. A checked table maps each user-facing UI action to its operation(s), its agent entry point and a headless acceptance test, and a UI action with no row fails that check. A test proves no operation's domain gate lives in its transport binding: an operation constructed without transport holds the same gates. Deliberately out: writing the adapters themselves — each projection wave does its own.
notes: 2026-08-28, coordinator: the blocks edge to nocx-f22br was removed. It encoded 'not yet', not a file collision — o9era lives in internal/capability, f22br in contracts/ and internal/transport, and they do not touch the same files. What o9era actually needs from f22br is the params-contract MECHANISM, which landed in 2a8e69f4; the remaining 155-method sweep is not a precondition, because each projection wave brings the params contracts for the methods it projects. AGENTS.md warns about exactly this edge, and 13 of 20 epic edges were once removed for being it.
close_reason: Every capability operation declares Direct/Adapted/Excluded and one that does not refuses to construct; the UI-action map records what each is and names the 21 action families no operation reaches; gate ownership proven at the operation and at the binding.

title: Every control method describes its parameters, and one manifest describes the whole surface
description:
contracts/ holds 175 schemas and every one of them describes a RESULT. contracts/README.md, 'Deliberately out of scope': 'Params, for now. Results are where the renderer's assumptions live; params are checked by the handler.' The same section defers OpenRPC with an explicit trigger: 'worth adopting when method-level metadata starts being duplicated — not to fix one response shape.'

Projecting agent tools from the operation catalogue is exactly that moment. The agent needs a params schema per operation; the renderer needs a result schema; both need error shapes; the agent additionally needs its disposition. Without a manifest each of those grows its own copy of the method list, which is the duplication the README named.

Note that contracts/tools/*.schema.json are params schemas (with $defs/result lifted out) while contracts/*.schema.json are result schemas — they are documents of different kinds, and contracts/tools/ cannot dissolve into contracts/ until params contracts exist and are proven equivalent to the registered validators.

Relates to nocx-bt3w (the result-contract sweep) and nocx-98rn (no dispatch without validation); this epic is the params half neither of them owns.
acceptance_criteria: Every registered control method has a params contract in contracts/ alongside its result contract, generated types on the renderer side and a Go conformance test, and the registered paramsValidator is proven equivalent to the schema for each — a method whose validator accepts what its schema rejects fails the build. One manifest (OpenRPC or equivalent) references params, results, errors and the agent extension without redefining any shape. Deliberately out: the binary data plane (AD-1).
close_reason: Every registered control method has a params contract alongside its result contract, the registered validator is held to it in both directions by a registration-driven test, and one OpenRPC manifest references params, results and errors without redefining any shape.

title: A grant can name notes and workspaces, so the assistant is given one without being given everything
description:
The ledger's closed set is six: environment, session, path, credential, destination, tool (internal/content/ledger.go:245). Notes, snippets, workspaces, tabs, panes, tunnels and endpoints have no kind at all, so Registry.ForGrant cannot filter them and Narrow cannot scope them. The set is deliberate, durable policy vocabulary under ADR-0020, so growing it is an architectural decision and needs the ADR amended rather than a constant appended.

The test for a NEW kind — all four must hold:
1. A person might reasonably grant access to it while denying access to sibling resources.
2. It has a stable canonical identity.
3. It has meaningful equality and containment rules.
4. A capability can actually enforce that scope.

If authority over a parent necessarily includes the child, the child is a hierarchical SUB-SCOPE, not another kind.

Expected outcome, to be confirmed rather than assumed: two new kinds — `content` (sub-scopes note/<id>, snippet/<id>) and `workspace` (tabs and panes beneath it). Secrets stay `credential`; remote targets stay `destination`; a tunnel is session + destination and earns a kind only if independent grant/stop authority becomes a real requirement. Turning the policy matrix into an entity model is the failure mode.
acceptance_criteria: content.ResourceKind carries the kinds the first projection wave actually needs, each justified in ADR-0020's amendment against the four-part test below; a grant scoped to one note's sub-scope permits reading that note and refuses its sibling, proven by a test. Deliberately out: a kind per noun — tab, pane, tunnel, endpoint, snippet as separate kinds are explicitly rejected here, with the reasoning recorded.
close_reason: A grant can name one note and refuse its sibling, proven by TestScopedNoteGrantPermitsOnlyThatNote and the containment table. ADR-0020 amended additively.

title: A call accounts for every resource it touches, and the permission is narrowed to exactly those
description:
Today the registry cannot say what a call touches. `ResourceArg` is singular and its kind is taken as `Resources[0]` (internal/assistant/kernel.go, namedResource), so a source-plus-destination call cannot be expressed at all. And `Narrow func(grant content.Grant)` never sees the call's arguments (internal/agenttools/registry.go), so it narrows to the WHOLE grant rather than to the resource this invocation named — weaker than the architectural phrase 'narrowed per call' in ADR-0028.

Shape to replace them with:

    ResourceKinds []content.ResourceKind          // presentation-time upper bound
    ResolveResources(args, runCtx) ([]ResourceRef, error)
    Narrow(grant, args, runCtx) (Capability, error)

ResourceRef is kind plus canonical id. Creation needs parent-scope semantics: creating /repo/new.go is authority under the PARENT path, creating a tab is authority within a workspace.

This is a precondition for every other epic on this spine: until it lands, no tool touching two resources can be declared honestly, and every capability is wider than the call that holds it.

Found by an adversarial review (codex, 2026-08-28) and verified against the code in the same session.
acceptance_criteria: A tool call naming two resources (e.g. a source and a destination) is scope-checked against BOTH and its approval shows BOTH; the capability built for that call carries only the intersection of the call's resources with the grant. Proven by a test where the first resource is inside the grant and the second is outside, and the call is refused. Deliberately out: which tools have two resources — that arrives with the projection epics.
close_reason: A call naming two resources is checked against both and refused when either is outside the grant; the capability carries only the call's resources intersected with the grant. Proven by TestMiddleware_RefusesWhenAnyResolvedResourceIsOutsideScope and three Narrow tests.

title: The composer's card grows a pixel the moment a completion ghost appears
description: Reported by the owner (2026-08-28, macOS app, dev build with the inspector): the composer card changes size slightly the moment a completion ghost appears. Measured in the running app: `.nocx-editor` 76 → 77px, the line box 16 → 17px, with `ghost: false` → `true` the only difference. ## Steps to Reproduce In the macOS app (WKWebView; a dev build shows it in the inspector), click into the composer and type a prefix that has a completion candidate — `unam` on a machine with `uname` on PATH. The card and the line box each gain a pixel the moment the ghost tail renders, and lose it again when the draft empties. The scrollback above the card moves with it. It does NOT reproduce in a browser on the dev stand (`make dev-web`) or in Playwright's WebKit and Chromium at the shipped font stack: whether the buffer box overflows depends on the metrics of whatever `ui-monospace` resolves to, and WKWebView resolves it to a font no browser here does. Forcing `Monaco` on `.cm-scroller` reproduces it in both engines. ## Cause CM6 draws an `` beside every inline widget — its own workaround for caret bugs next to uneditable content — and styles it `height: 1em; vertical-align: text-top`. `text-top` anchors that box to the top of the line's CONTENT AREA, so whether it fits is a question about the font's ascent and descent rather than about the line height: with a font whose content area is shorter than 1em the box hangs below and the line box grows to cover it. The completion ghost is the only inline widget the composer draws, so the growth arrives exactly when a suggestion does. Measured across seven mono stacks at 11–18px, in WebKit and Chromium: every stack is 0.000 except one, and the one is whatever `ui-monospace` resolves to inside WKWebView (the owner's canvas probe: the stack and `ui-monospace` measure 86.543 for ten `m`s where `Menlo` is 84.287 and `Monaco` 84.014, so it is none of the named fallbacks). Monaco is the reproducible stand-in and gives +0.344 in WebKit, +1.000 in Chromium. That is why it showed in the shipped macOS app and in no browser the dev stand runs — the same shape as the scrollbar-gutter defect (nocx-6c546). ## Fix `vertical-align: top` on the buffer, scoped to the composer: the box is then anchored to the top of the LINE BOX and its own height is that line's line-height, so it can never be the taller of the two. A fact about the box model rather than about the font, which is what makes it font-independent. The buffer stays in the DOM — deleting it would take CM6's caret workaround with it. ## Checks - `e2e/command-editor.spec.ts` "the composer keeps its height when the first character is typed" already described this defect, with per-engine numbers, and allowed 2px of slack for it. It now polls for the card not moving at all (0.01px). Negative control in the container, chromium: with the fix 6 passed; with CM6's `text-top` restored, that case fails and the other five pass. - `cmd-output-wrap.test.ts` asserted that NO rule targets `cm-widgetBuffer`, which forbade the fix along with the old target-token widget it was written against. It now asserts what may not come back: a width, an indent, a padding or a margin on the buffer. ## Acceptance Criteria - Typing a character that raises a completion ghost does not change the height of `.nocx-editor` — no tolerance, on either engine the e2e suite runs. - The check fails if the fix is reverted: demonstrated, not assumed. - The rule is font-independent: it may not depend on which font `ui-monospace` resolves to on the machine running it.
close_reason: Fixed in 42f8b521: the widget buffer is aligned to the top of the line box, which is font-independent. Verified by the owner in the macOS app, and by e2e in the container on chromium with a negative control — the case fails with CM6's text-top restored.

title: a ~/.zshenv or ~/.zprofile that execs leaves the transient ZDOTDIR, and the capability in it, on disk
description:
The zsh tier's transient ZDOTDIR holds a .zshrc carrying the session's per-epoch
capability and recovery fence. Two things are supposed to remove it: the .zshrc
phase erases the directory before any user code runs, and the EXIT trap armed in
the .zshenv phase covers a startup that dies before reaching it.

`exec` runs neither. It replaces the process image without running EXIT traps,
and the .zshrc phase never arrives. So a user whose ~/.zshenv or ~/.zprofile ends
in an exec leaves a 0700 directory in TMPDIR containing the capability — once per
session, for the life of the machine.

Both tiers. The local one has LocalLaunch.Cleanup, but the caller runs it only
when the SPAWN fails, which this is not.

Found while closing nocx-2ka0, which is what made the .zshenv and .zprofile
phases run on the local tier at all.

## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-28 with a real zsh:

1. mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/nocx-zsh.XXXXXX", write the tier's .zshenv (trap
   plus the ~/.zshenv replay), .zprofile and .zshrc into it.
2. Put `exec /bin/echo EXECED` in the fixture $HOME/.zprofile.
3. ZDOTDIR=<dir> zsh -l -i
4. EXECED is printed and <dir> still exists afterwards, with the .zshrc in it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a session whose ~/.zprofile execs, no nocx-zsh.?????? directory remains,
  proven with a real zsh on a real pty.
- The same for a ~/.zshenv that execs.
- The session still runs the exec'd program: fail-open is unchanged, and this
  must not become a reason to refuse a startup file.

title: the backend log grows without bound, and terminal-output debug lines are what fill it
description:
Measured 2026-08-28 on the owner's Mac: ~/Library/Application Support/nocx/nocx.log
is 608 MB. It has no upper bound and nothing ever truncates it.

Two independent causes, and the file only behaves once BOTH are fixed:

1. internal/app/app.go:651 opens the file O_APPEND with no rotation, no size cap
   and no retention. It grows for the life of the install.

2. The level knob cannot filter the line that fills it. frontend/src/log.ts has
   no level filter at all — log.debug() calls the Log binding unconditionally —
   and internal/app/app.go:330 logs every frontend line at Info. So a frontend
   debug line is promoted to Info BEFORE the backend handler's level is applied,
   and NOCX_LOG_LEVEL cannot suppress it. frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:2899
   calls log.debug('nocx: session data received', {length}) for every chunk of
   PTY output: that one line is 29749 of the last 30000 records in the file.

No content is disclosed — the fields are {length} only — so this is size and
I/O, not a leak.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the shipped app normally for a few weeks, opening tabs and running
   commands.
2. ls -la "~/Library/Application Support/nocx/nocx.log" — it is hundreds of MB.
3. tail -c 5000000 nocx.log | grep -o 'msg="[^"]*"' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
   — "frontend: nocx: session data received" is ~99% of the records.
4. Setting NOCX_LOG_LEVEL=warn does not stop it: the line reaches the handler
   already labelled Info by internal/app/app.go:330.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The log file has a bounded size on disk however long the install lives,
  proven by a test that writes past the bound and asserts what remains.
- A frontend log.debug line does not reach the file at the default level,
  proven end to end: the renderer calls debug, the file gains no record.
- A frontend log.error line still does, at every level that should carry it.

## Out of scope

Deleting the terminal-content.ts debug line is not the fix. The level plumbing
is: with it unfixed, the next debug line anybody adds reintroduces this.

title: pages.yml's release trigger is inert: GITHUB_TOKEN-created releases start no workflow, so the live page keeps advertising the previous version
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Tag a release and let release.yml publish it (the only way this repository ships).
2. Watch for a `pages` run afterwards.

Measured on v0.3.0, 2026-08-28:

  gh release view v0.3.0 -q .publishedAt        -> 2026-08-28T12:45:04Z
  gh run list --workflow=pages.yml --limit 2    -> newest is 11:03:04Z, event=push

No pages run followed the release. The live page went on serving

  data-version>Download v0.2.0
  data-released>2026-08-20

while the repository held v0.3.0 and the Releases page carried the v0.3.0 artefacts.

## What is wrong

pages.yml carries the trigger written for exactly this, with a comment saying why:

  # A release alone must be able to refresh the page ... without this trigger
  # the site keeps advertising the previous release until somebody happens to
  # touch site/.
  release:
    types: [published]

It never fires for our own releases. release.yml:494/511 creates them with
`gh release create` under `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`, and GitHub does not start a
workflow run from an event a GITHUB_TOKEN produced - the documented anti-recursion rule.
So the trigger is inert for the only path that actually publishes, and the comment above
it describes behaviour the repository does not have. A trigger that cannot fire is worse
than a missing one: it is a promise the next author will read and believe.

The gap is not cosmetic. The download button on the page names a version, and
pages.yml's stamp is what keeps it honest - the whole reason check-site.sh only refuses
the page falling BEHIND the newest tag (spec 11b) is that this step publishes the tag
that exists. If the step never runs, the page advertises the previous release
indefinitely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- pages.yml triggers on `workflow_run: {workflows: [Release], types: [completed]}`,
  which is about a workflow finishing rather than a release being published and so is
  not reached by the anti-recursion rule.
- The deploy job is guarded so a FAILED release does not redeploy:
  `github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`.
  workflow_run fires on completion, not on success.
- The `release: published` trigger is KEPT, for a release published by hand through the
  UI where the actor is a person and the event does fire, with a comment saying it is
  the fallback and not the primary.
- The comment above the triggers records why the obvious one is the dead one, so this is
  not rediscovered.
- Proven on the next release: the tag is pushed, and a `pages` run with
  `event=workflow_run` follows it without anyone dispatching anything.

title: The landing and the README carry v0.3.0's surfaces, not v0.2.0's
notes: Landed as PR #117 on docs/release-v0.3.0-refresh. Notes rewritten (grant, approval width, fullscreen summon, dump+instructions, secrets in any field, folder variables, archive import, pane observation, Experimental carrier, new fixes); README status+pitch to v0.3.0; site/index.html and site/ru/index.html rewritten section 04, new section 05 (API), Operations in the matrix, hero transcript recaptured, notes links to v0.3.0.md. Version badges deliberately left at v0.2.0 — check-site compares data-version to the newest tag and pages.yml stamps from it; they move in the tagging commit.

title: The approval action buttons sit outside their own group's box in WebKit at 420px
description:
Found 2026-08-28 by the first full containerized e2e run of the merged feat/ai-assistant tree: 436 passed, 3 failed, and this is one of them.

e2e/agent-policy.spec.ts, WEBKIT only, at the 420px narrow viewport:

    expect(box.y).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(groupBox.y)
    Expected: >= 410
    Received:    388.90625

A button's top edge is 21px ABOVE the top edge of the .ui-action-group it belongs to. Chromium passes. The geometry assertion was written yesterday under nocx-takqr.6 and verified in chromium; nocx-takqr.7 touched the same helper today and also verified chromium only. Nobody had run it in WebKit until now.

## Which of three it is has to be established, because they need opposite fixes

1. A real layout defect — the group does not bound its buttons. It may wrap at 420px so the measured group box is one row while a button sits in another, or the group may not establish the containing box the assertion assumes. Then the kit component's layout is what changes.
2. The assertion is wrong about what a group's box means. If .ui-action-group legitimately does not bound its children (display: contents, a transform, a differently-measured wrapping flex), then it is asking for something that was never true and merely holds in Chromium. Then the assertion changes and the commit says what the box actually means.
3. The container. AGENTS.md says layout-sensitive specs fail in this container and pass in CI — Linux WebKit at a container-default viewport, a different architecture from the runner. 21px is large for a font-metric difference, so this is the least likely, but it must be ruled out with a measurement rather than an adjective.

## Steps to Reproduce

PW_PROJECTS=webkit e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/agent-policy.spec.ts

## Acceptance Criteria

- Which of the three it is, established and stated, before anything is edited.
- e2e/agent-policy.spec.ts green in the container in BOTH chromium and webkit.
- If the assertion changes rather than the product, the commit says what an action group's box actually bounds and why the old assertion held in one engine only.
- If the kit changes, the surface still only places the component and does not repaint it.
close_reason: Merged as dce86fd0. Established as the first of the three possibilities, not the container and not a stale assertion: the kit's action group carried align-items: center, so at 420px its wrapped rows were centred within the group and the group's own box did not contain the buttons in it — measured at 21px above its top edge in WebKit, while Chromium happened to agree with the assertion. align-items: stretch, one line in styles/components/action-group.css. It is a change to a SHARED kit component: every ActionGroup now stretches its rows, which for a row of equal-height buttons is identical to what it did before. Assertion unchanged. e2e/agent-policy.spec.ts green in both engines.

title: The dump's composition change left five dead constructors, and the ratchet is red
description:
Measured on feat/ai-assistant after merging main: 'node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs' reports 90 unreachable functions, 89 baselined, 5 NEW — assistant.newClient, assistant.NewClient, assistant.newClientWithRegistry, httpguard.newGuardedHTTPClient, httpguard.newGuardedHTTPClientWithResolver. CI runs this ratchet in both the backend and backend-linux jobs, so it is a guaranteed red pull request.

Commit 500f66c8 moved the composition root from assistant.NewClient(logger) to assistant.NewClientWithWireRecorder(logger, recorder) and left the old constructors behind for the tests. assistant.NewClient(nil) now has 19 call sites in 12 files, every one of them a test, and nothing in production reaches it.

That is a backward-compatibility shim kept so call sites would not have to change, which AGENTS.md forbids in as many words, and it is a second answer to 'how is an assistant client built' — the AD-8 failure this codebase keeps paying for.

Two things the collapse must not disturb, because each was bought: NewClient still fails when the tool registry assembles EMPTY (nocx-jtz3q — the shipped bundle has no contracts/ tree and a cwd-relative path assembled a quiet empty set), and the wire tap stays OUTSIDE the guard in httpguard.go so it records what actually left rather than what we hoped to send.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs
2. The summary line reports 5 NEW.

## Acceptance Criteria

- node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs reports 0 NEW.
- One exported constructor builds an assistant client; NewClientWithWireRecorder is gone and no second construction path remains.
- The empty-registry failure still happens and is still asserted.
- Any of the five deliberately kept is added to the baseline with the reason named in the commit body — never silently.
close_reason: Merged as a8c1123f plus a one-line wording restore. NewClient(logger, recorder) is the single exported constructor; NewClientWithWireRecorder and the ...WithResolverAndRecorder chain are gone, and newGuardedHTTPClientWithResolver with them. 19 test call sites updated. Ratchet before: 90 unreachable, 89 baselined, 5 NEW. After: 85 unreachable, all baselined, 0 NEW. The empty-registry refusal (nocx-jtz3q) and the tap's position outside the guard are both untouched and still asserted.

title: T1 A request's chosen environment survives a restart
description:
Where the choice lives is the decision this task makes, and it must be written down.

Today `chosenEnvironments` (`api-store.ts:656`) is an in-memory map keyed by COLLECTION handle, empty at start and never persisted. Two gaps: it does not survive a restart, and it cannot hold two requests in one collection under different environments.

`environmentFor` (`api-store.ts:856`) is the single owner — the picker and the send both read it, so the control cannot say one thing while the wire carries another. Whatever is added keeps that property.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A person picks an environment for a request, restarts, and the request is still under it; a sibling request in the same collection is under its own.
- The default when nothing was ever chosen is unchanged and asserted: exactly one environment means that one, otherwise none. The comment above it explains why a panel must not pick alphabetically when a candidate is usually production.
- The picker and the send still read ONE function.
- Where the choice is stored is deliberate and stated in the code — a request file, a collection-level document, or workspace state — with the reason. If the answer is not obvious, an ADR in `docs/decisions/`.
- The stored choice is read back off disk by a test, not from a signal.
- Deliberately out: the folder level (T2).
close_reason: The choice was an in-memory signal keyed by collection: it did not survive a restart, and two requests in one collection could not differ. It lives in the request file now as a tri-state — absent means never chose (the default governs), empty means 'no environment' on purpose. The default is untouched and asserted; picker and send still read one function; writes are queued against races with open/send/delete. ADR-0043 records that a request file is committed, so this is a SHARED choice, with the cost named: one person's production choice is inherited by the next and review is expected to catch it. Old files without the field stay valid, held by a test. 94 to 96 frontend tests.

title: PR 113 CI: the deadcode ratchet rejects internal/testwait, and shell-mode's editor wait is preceded by a vacuous one
description:
Three of eight CI jobs on PR #113 (run 33099131940) are red on two independent
causes.

`ci-mac` and `ci-linux (no-secret-service)` fail the deadcode ratchet with six
NEW violations, all of them `internal/testwait`. The package is test-support —
78 `_test.go` files import it and nothing else does — but the ratchet's
exclusion matches a package DIRECTORY named `…test` (`storagetest`,
`vaulttest`, the `httptest` convention), and `testwait` puts the word on the
wrong end. So a genuine test-support package is read as production code with
six dead functions.

`ci-e2e (webkit)` fails `e2e/shell-mode.spec.ts:225` — the editor is `hidden`
after a 10s wait, while the same spec passes under chromium in the same run.
The wait before it is the cause: `.nocx-editor-recovery` is `display:none` from
construction (editor.ts:351) AND sits inside the root that `hide()` blanks
(editor.ts:385, 1119), so `expect(recovery).not.toBeVisible({timeout: 20_000})`
closes instantly and is satisfied by the exact state the next line rejects. Of
the 30s the two waits nominally share, the editor gets 10. Same shape as
nocx-sx4sg.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `gh run view --job 98611828819 --log -R shady2k/nocx` — six `NEW:
   internal/testwait/wait.go` lines, exit 1.
2. `node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs --platform=linux/amd64` on the branch.
3. `gh run view --job 98611828805 --log -R shady2k/nocx` — the webkit timeout
   at shell-mode.spec.ts:225.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs --platform=linux/amd64` reports every
  unreachable function baselined, with no NEW entries.
- `gofumpt -l .` is empty and `golangci-lint run --build-tags gtk3 ./...` exits
  0 after the rename.
- `./scripts/ci-linux.sh` is green in both keyring variants.
- In `e2e/shell-mode.spec.ts` the editor's visibility is waited for BEFORE the
  recovery chip is asserted absent, so the recovery assertion can no longer
  pass on a hidden editor.
- `ci-mac`, `ci-linux` and `ci-e2e (webkit)` all pass on PR #113.
close_reason: Fixed in 331ab510, 32a81c37, 8d3b992b. All eight CI jobs green on run 33110254898.

title: A standing answer is offered only for shell invocations, so a tool that is not a command can only ever be allowed once
description:
Found on 2026-08-27 by finally running e2e/agent-policy.spec.ts, which had been written but not run. The spec is from PR #102 (d3078f14) and is ON MAIN, where it was green. It is red on feat/ai-assistant.

## What happens

The approval prompt for a `session.read` call offers TWO buttons — "Allow once" and "Deny once". The four standing answers are absent, so "Allow always" cannot be clicked and the observe row can never carry a standing decision. The e2e fails at the action-fit assertion with "locator resolved to 2 elements"; it would have failed at the click one step later.

## Why, read from the diff against main

The whole standing offer is NEW on this branch — `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- internal/transport/ws_agent.go` shows `agentApprovalStanding`, `standingOffer`, and `n.Standing = standingOffer(ap.Invocation)` as additions. The renderer gates the four standing buttons on it: `agent-approval-prompt.tsx:371` filters SCOPES to `once` unless `ask().standing.available`.

`standingOffer` takes a `content.Invocation` and asks `content.StandingRule` (internal/content/rules.go:60), which is entirely shell-shaped: not parsed, no commands, more than one command, disqualified, or `LiteralInvocationRule`'s error. A tool call that is not a shell command — `session.read`, `session.list` — has no invocation to parse, so it falls out on "the command has no complete invocation to show" and standing is never available for it.

But a standing answer is written against the EFFECT ROW (observe), not against a command. Step 5 of the same spec asserts exactly that: the Agent policy page shows the decision on the observe row. An effect row needs no canonical invocation label.

## Why no unit test caught it

Every backend case in internal/transport/ws_agent_approval_scope_test.go drives the `run` tool — `TestAgentApprovalRequested_StandingOfferOmitsUnshowableInvocations` feeds Invocations directly, and the "always" matrix row asserts `n.Tool == "run"`. There is no case for a tool that is not a shell command. Every unit correct, the user's task impossible.

## What this bead is NOT

Do not weaken the rule for `run`. The canonical-invocation requirement exists so a person's yes covers only what they were shown, and for a shell command that is the invocation label. The question here is what a standing answer is over when the proposal is not a command at all.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/agent-policy.spec.ts`
2. The first test fails: the approval prompt for `session.read` renders only "Allow once" and "Deny once".

## Acceptance Criteria

- A standing answer is offered for a tool call that is not a shell command, and what it is over is stated in words the person can read before answering.
- The `run` tool's behaviour is unchanged: an invocation that cannot be shown canonically still offers no standing answer, with the same reason sentence. Asserted.
- A backend test drives a NON-`run` tool through the same path — the gap that let this ship.
- e2e/agent-policy.spec.ts passes unmodified in e2e/run-in-container.sh, including the click on "Allow always" and the observe row's state line afterwards.
close_reason: Merged as 003435be + e0273ad9. A non-command proposal now offers a standing answer over its classified effect row; a command still requires the canonical invocation and an unshowable one still offers nothing, with the same reason sentence, asserted. The person reads what the answer covers before answering. The effect vocabulary has one owner again (frontend/src/effect-labels.ts); the backend carries no words. Contract description and generated type updated. e2e/agent-policy.spec.ts passes unmodified at 1280px and 420px in the container, with the geometry check waiting on getAnimations().finished instead of the product dropping its animation.

title: Linux desktop: Download в удалённом Files ничего не сохраняет
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the packaged/Wails desktop application on Linux.
2. Open an SSH tab and the Files view for that remote host.
3. Open a regular remote file's menu and press `Download`.
4. Observe that no save dialog/file appears; the button has no useful outcome.

## Duplicate and task-gap check

The parent epic `nocx-9le.8` is still in progress. Its backend/wire child is `nocx-9le.8.1`; the browser UI child `nocx-9le.8.3` is closed. No earlier bug covered the Linux desktop failure. Source comments in both `frontend/src/files/download-save.ts` and `files-view.tsx` explicitly promised a desktop native-save child `nocx-9le.8.4`, but it had never been filed; this bead is that missing half rather than a duplicate of `.8.3`.

## Proven current gap

`createDownloadSurface` unconditionally injects `createBrowserDownloadSaver()`, including in the native Wails build. That saver creates a detached `<a download>` and calls `click()`. This works only if the host webview implements browser download handling; the reported Linux WebKitGTK surface does not.

The abstraction already anticipates another `DownloadSaver`, but its current `save(url)` shape is insufficient for a native dialog: `files.download` also returns the authoritative `name`, `transferId`, and `size`, while the flow passes only the URL. Cancellation or native-start failure also needs to retire the already-open transfer instead of leaving it until ticket expiry.

## Existing reusable capability and constraints

`internal/backup.SaveToFile` already proves the platform adapter pattern: Linux uses `zenity --file-selection --save --confirm-overwrite`, macOS uses osascript, and cancellation is distinct from failure. Reuse/extract the dialog capability, not `backup.SaveToFile` itself: that method accepts the entire document in memory, while downloaded files must remain bounded streaming transfers.

ADR-0040 (`docs/decisions/0037-an-http-download-route-beside-the-websocket.md`) requires bulk bytes to stay off the WebSocket and forbids `fetch -> Blob` because memory would grow with file size. AD-3 keeps Wails thin; AD-8 requires an injected capability rather than platform switches in the flow. The native path must preserve binding/session authorization, single-use ticket semantics, progress/done notifications, cancellation, and cleanup of partial destination files.

## Documentation gap

ADR-0040 currently reasons primarily about a browser saving the HTTP response. A desktop native destination path changes that consequence and must be clarified in the ADR/design before implementation; do not silently create a second transfer engine.
design:
1. Use BMAD/design first to amend ADR-0040 with the desktop path. The intended direction already recorded in source is a backend/native saver implementation of `DownloadSaver`, not a Blob fallback and not opening the bearer-ticket URL in an external browser.
2. Extend the saver input with the authoritative `files.download` result fields needed by a native dialog (`name`, `transferId`, resolved URL/route, `size`) and make dialog cancellation/start failure explicit. Browser saver remains the anchor/Content-Disposition implementation.
3. Add a transport/native capability that selects a local destination and streams the existing transfer into it with bounded memory. Reuse the existing transfer/ticket source of truth; do not copy the SFTP read loop. The RPC must authorize the transfer by connection/session ownership and must not accept an arbitrary source path or arbitrary external URL.
4. Write to a same-directory temporary file, fsync/close, then atomically promote. Cancel, short body, remote read failure, local write failure, connection loss, and process shutdown remove the partial temp and leave an existing destination untouched.
5. Keep long dialog/transfer work off the WebSocket read loop and use the existing serialized dialog/capability boundary. Keep progress and terminal outcome authoritative in `files.downloadProgress`/`files.downloadDone`.
6. Select native saver only in the Wails runtime; browser builds keep the current HTTP attachment path. Update contracts/generated types, DTO and real-wire conformance for every touched method.
acceptance_criteria:
- On Linux Wails, `Files -> remote regular file -> Download` opens a native save dialog; choosing a path writes byte-for-byte the remote file there, including a file larger than the transfer chunk/buffer.
- Cancelling the dialog creates no destination and retires the pending transfer without waiting for ticket TTL. An existing destination is unchanged on cancel or any pre-promotion failure.
- Remote read failure, short transfer, local permission/write failure, SSH loss, explicit cancel, and shutdown produce one visible failed/cancelled terminal outcome and leave no partial temp file.
- The browser build still starts a streamed HTTP attachment and never buffers the body into a Blob. Local-desktop eligibility remains unchanged (`Download` absent where `Show in Finder` is the action).
- A real-backend acceptance test against `cmd/e2e-sshd` downloads a remote fixture through the native saver seam into a temp directory and compares bytes. Separate tests cover dialog cancel and cleanup intervals.
- Contracts remain exact (`additionalProperties: false`, explicit `required`), generated frontend types match, and DTO plus over-the-wire conformance pass.
- ADR-0040 and the download design describe both browser and desktop destinations and preserve AD-1, AD-3, AD-6, and AD-8.
notes:
2026-08-28 implementation evidence:
- Root cause confirmed: Wails/WebKitGTK used the browser-only detached anchor path, so Linux had no download manager to accept the streamed HTTP response.
- Added transferId-only files.downloadSave RPC, strict generated contract, immediate authorized one-shot claim, native SaveFile adapter, bounded io.Pipe bridge into the existing atomic local transfer.Sink, path-redacted wire errors, and clean native/browser frontend composition.
- Browser GET attachment path remains unchanged; native work reuses Source/Sink and keeps file bytes and local paths off the WebSocket.
- Added Go/TypeScript coverage for authorization, ownership/direction/expiry/races, dialog admission/cancel/failure, interruptible remote reads, queue rejection, bounded backpressure, durable atomic promotion/cleanup, path privacy, exact contracts, real socket conformance, native/browser saver selection, and no-Blob browser behavior.
- Current focused evidence after rebase to 8422d6f8: go test -race ./internal/transport -run 'Download|download' -count=1 passed; transfer/local/native focused race tests passed; 5 frontend download files passed (87 tests); contracts, typecheck, lint, format, GTK compile, and golangci-lint passed.
- Current Linux Wails + cmd/e2e-sshd manual proof: selected remote 840000-byte remote-large.bin (>256 KiB chunk), native SaveFile opened with authoritative filename, saved download-final.bin, and both source/destination SHA-256 were f7b1ab0e689a5b080ef01dd058e3a2fbc57437263ff21c4ad800b3459b3b8c0b. A second dialog cancel created no second file. Smoke artifacts and processes were removed.
- Review-driven hardening: local path never reaches RPC/done frames; preclaim prevents TTL stranding on dialog-queue rejection; early local failures and explicit cancel interrupt a blocked remote Read; post-claim disconnect does only nonblocking cancellation in the read-loop handler; Wails' non-dismissible-dialog limitation is documented and prevents promotion while retaining the single dialog gate.
close_reason: Closed

title: После resize или переноса окна между мониторами терминал входит в вертикальную осцилляцию
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a terminal tab with enough output to make vertical movement obvious; also try a continuously repainting TUI.
2. Resize the application window, or drag it between displays (especially displays with different scale/DPR).
3. Repeat because the failure is intermittent.
4. Observe that terminal content can enter a persistent state where it moves vertically up and down at very high speed, continuing after the geometry gesture ends.

## Duplicate and history check

No open bead describes this symptom. `nocx-3gh` is the nearest closed bug: it added adjacent-size dedupe plus an 80 ms trailing debounce before `session.sendResize`, because forwarding every intermediate grid size produced a SIGWINCH storm. That fix has no behavioral regression test in `terminal-content*.test.*` or e2e. `nocx-dau` fixed a distinct one-frame stretch by removing an extra rAF around ResizeObserver delivery.

## Current geometry path

The binding design in `.internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md` §B.5 is:
`Tab ResizeObserver -> TerminalContent.viewportChanged -> renderer.fitViewport -> renderer.onResize -> debounced PTY resize`.

Current code also has a second, output-driven pass:
`onWriteParsed -> scheduleLiveResize -> ScrollbackController.setLiveHeight -> TerminalContent.refitIfResized`.
`setLiveHeight` may change the scroll stack and scroll-to-bottom; `usableViewport` reads `scrollbackArea.clientWidth/clientHeight` and `runningLiveCap`; `_applyEchoShift` moves the live xterm grid by a row-derived `translateY`. On DPR changes, `XtermRenderer` invalidates cell metrics and republishes them.

## Working diagnosis — must be measured, not assumed

The persistent two-direction motion is more consistent with a geometry feedback loop than with the already-fixed one-way SIGWINCH storm: two layouts/grid sizes, live caps, scroll positions, or echo shifts may alternate. Adjacent-value dedupe does not stop an A/B oscillation. Moving between displays adds a DPR/cell-metric transition and makes this path especially suspect. This is a hypothesis, not a proven root cause.

## Required investigation

Capture one frame-aligned trace through the existing seams: pane rectangle, usable viewport, scrollback client/scroll dimensions, runningLiveCap, cell width/height, DPR, cols/rows, viewportTopLine, echo-shift transform, scrollTop, and outgoing resize timestamps. Compare ordinary prompt, long scrollback, running normal-buffer TUI, and alternate-screen TUI. Identify the first value that alternates; fix its owner rather than rate-limiting or hiding the resulting motion.

Before editing, compare the affected frontend paths with `origin/main`; the current feature branch has no changes in them. Preserve AD-1/AD-6 and §B.5: no PTY bytes in JSON, no backend stream sniffing, and no second geometry observer inside content/renderer.
design:
1. Write a deterministic failing regression at the geometry owner before changing production code. The test must drive the real presentation -> content -> renderer seam far enough to expose the alternating state, not assert a helper copied from the implementation.
2. Instrument only behind the existing decision-tracing/log seam; no permanent per-frame production logging.
3. Fix the first oscillating owner. Candidate boundaries to disprove or confirm: pane ResizeObserver delivery, output-driven live-height/refit feedback, scrollbar-induced width changes, DPR cell-metric invalidation/refit, and echo-shift toggling.
4. Keep local fitting immediate. Keep the settled PTY resize policy separate; do not reintroduce an rAF delay or a second ResizeObserver.
5. Update the geometry design/architecture notes only if ownership or ordering changes; otherwise record the regression and invariant in the existing test.
acceptance_criteria:
- On the reported desktop surface, repeatedly resize the window and move it between displays with different scale/DPR while (a) at a prompt with scrollback, (b) a continuously repainting normal-buffer program, and (c) an alternate-screen TUI. After each gesture the content reaches one stable vertical position and remains stable for at least 5 seconds; no rapid up/down motion occurs.
- A deterministic regression test fails on the pre-fix A/B geometry/scroll oscillation and passes after the fix. It asserts a user-observable invariant (stable grid/vertical position), not source text or a private debounce constant.
- One settled gesture produces at most one final PTY resize for the final cols/rows; unchanged sizes produce none. Existing immediate local fit behavior remains intact.
- The fix introduces no second ResizeObserver and does not move terminal/scroll ownership across AD-6 boundaries.
- The reproducer trace and proven root cause are appended to this bead before closure.
notes:
Implementation evidence, 2026-08-27:

- Proven structural root: `TerminalContent.viewportChanged` and the output-driven `refitIfResized` independently called `fitViewport`; only the latter carried a height-only guard. A pane fit was invisible to the output path, which could immediately fit the same rectangle again after resize-echo output. The guard now covers width+height and is shared by both paths.
- Display moves had a second convergence gap required by geometry design §B.5: the xterm DPR listener invalidated cell metrics but never re-fit the last authoritative viewport. `XtermRenderer` now caches that viewport, refits inside it on every DPR change, and re-arms the resolution media query after each move so 1→2→1.5 is observable.
- `TerminalContent.dispose` now cancels a pending trailing resize.
- Added behavioral coverage: identical cross-path frames fit once; three grid changes inside 80 ms send only the final grid; disposal sends none; repeated DPR changes converge without alternating rows. Existing live DPR test fixtures were corrected to fire a snapshot of listeners, matching browser event dispatch while the handler re-arms.
- Focused evidence: terminal-content.test.ts 199/199; renderers/xterm.test.ts 93/93; panes.test.ts 79/79. Frontend typecheck and lint passed.
- Real Linux Wails v3/WebKitGTK 2.52.5 smoke used an isolated HOME. A normal-buffer 20 Hz clear/redraw loop and alternate-screen `top -d 0.1` were resized repeatedly and moved across both attached displays. Two screenshots five seconds apart after each gesture held the same vertical geometry; both programs stayed live and usable.
- No AD ownership/order changed; no architecture/design amendment is needed.
close_reason: Closed

title: What this agent is emitting, live, and what the rule sees on it
description:
D12 is explicit that this is not optional: "a rule the user must write blind is a dead rule." Today a person editing a rule has no way to see the screen it runs against.

The view shows the enrolled pane's current frame as the RULE sees it - the grid, where the cursor is, which rows are full-width rules, which regions the anchors resolved to - and beside it the value the rule currently answers and WHICH BRANCH produced it. A rule that answers unknown says which branches were tried and where each stopped.

This is the surface calibration is built on, so it lands before calibration rather than after.
acceptance_criteria:
From Settings, for an enrolled pane, a person sees the live frame with the rule's own reading overlaid, and the current value with the branch that produced it. An unknown says where the evaluation stopped.

Falsified if the view shows raw text without the rule's reading - that is a terminal, and they already have one.
close_reason:
Shipped on feat/agent-orchestration in 67e0baf7 (backend) and bc2eb3ac (frontend), pending the coordinator's merged gate.

The reading: internal/agentdriver/explain.go — Explanation/AnchorReading/BranchReading/PredicateReading/BelowReading/ExtractorReading, produced by threading an optional recorder through the SAME decide() the product acts on (nil on every production path), so the branch a person is shown is the branch that decided the pane's state. Registry.Explain fails OPEN (HasRule false, frame still readable) because refusing to say anything about an agent with no rule leaves the person who has to write one looking at nothing.

The wire: agent.emitting (contracts/agent.emitting{,.params}.schema.json, additionalProperties:false + explicit required), internal/transport/ws_agent_emitting.go, wired at internal/app/app.go through the same agentdriver.Registry the watcher classifies with. paneobserve.Watcher.Watching() lists enrolled panes from the ENROLMENT act, so a settled screen is listable before any sweep.

The view: frontend/src/agent-emitting-section.tsx + emitting-client.ts, Settings -> Agent screens (assistant group), reached from settings.tsx via settings-content.ts and main.tsx.

Evidence a stranger can check:
- TestExplainAgreesWithClassifyOverTheCorpus + a one-off dense sweep: 3249 frames across all 9 captures at 250ms granularity, Explain and Classify agreeing on state AND on which branch produced it.
- TestAgentEmitting_OverTheWireConformsToContract: real result off the real socket, validated against the schema, carrying both halves.
- TestAgentEmittingCreatesNoEnrolment: asking about an unenrolled pane leaves panegrid.Count() unchanged — the method adds no third power to the AD-6 amendment.
- agent-emitting-section.test.tsx 'polls while it is open, and stops when it is gone': the interval's second end.
- testdata/captures unchanged (git diff empty); claude.rule.json and claude.go untouched.
- deadcode -whylive reaches agentdriver.documentDriver.Explain from main; ratchet clean.

AD-6: no amendment written. The amendment's list is exhaustive over what the grid may DECIDE; a read-out handed to the pane's own operator decides nothing, creates no enrolment, moves no wave/lifecycle/execution state, reaches no network destination, and is neither shown as the person's terminal nor persisted as their history.

Known gap filed separately: the design's §5 guided calibration and §6 on-disk user rules are nocx-etejh and beyond; this view is read-only.

title: The rule is a document, and claude.go is the first one written in it
description:
Today the classifier is Go code and the only way to change it is to change nocx. Split it: a closed set of NAMED PREDICATES implemented in Go, and a per-agent DOCUMENT that composes them into an ordered list of branches per screen value.

The predicate set is closed on purpose. A user composes predicates; a user cannot invent one and cannot lift a bound a predicate enforces. From the measured claude driver the set is: cursor_on(glyph); row_opens_with(glyph); full_width_rule(); between_rules(); region(anchor, direction, max_rows, col0_only); matches/contains inside a region geometry already narrowed; nearest_nonblank_above(anchor) contains(text); below_mode_line_opens_only_with(glyphs).

Two of these carry the safety, and neither is a string: cursor_on is the predicate an agent CANNOT FORGE, because printed text cannot take the cursor - the TUI parks it after every repaint. region's max_rows is a cap THE ENGINE OWNS: it is what stops an agent whose printed lines abut the chrome from extending the region a forged marker would be looked for in. Branch ORDER is part of the document and is a safety property too - the dialog branches evaluate before the free-text branch, so a dialog can never be masked by an input box drawn beneath it.

claude.go is re-expressed as the first document in this grammar. That rewrite is the grammar's proof: a grammar that cannot express the one driver we know is correct is not ready to be offered to anybody else. If the claude rule cannot be written without a new predicate, the predicate is missing - add it deliberately rather than widening an existing one.
acceptance_criteria:
internal/agentdriver evaluates a document against a panegrid.Frame and returns the same closed set it returns today. The claude rule is a document, not Go branches, and testdata/captures tests pass UNCHANGED - not adjusted, not re-recorded.

For every predicate: a test that it matches, and a test that it refuses the near-miss it exists to refuse. Specifically cursor_on refuses the same glyph printed into the transcript, and region refuses an anchor an agent tried to push out of range by printing.

Falsified if a document can express a region without a cap, if branch order is not part of the document, or if the claude tests needed editing to pass.
close_reason: Committed as HEAD of feat/agent-orchestration. internal/agentdriver now evaluates claude.rule.json against a panegrid.Frame and returns the same closed set; testdata/captures passes UNCHANGED, verified adversarially by deleting the spinner branch and watching TestATurnInFlightIsWorking fail. Predicate set is closed, each with a match test and a near-miss refusal test. deadcode -whylive traces documentDriver.Classify from main. The design's eight predicates needed seven additions, of which cellAtCol-vs-rowOpensWith, region.stopAtBlank and the three-valued below-the-mode-line verdict are safety rather than convenience; requireBound was the one the plan did not foresee.

title: Calibration: the person reproduces each state, and the frames are labelled
description:
Verifying a rule against a recording it happened to be pointed at proves nothing: a rule that never matches looks exactly like a rule that works. The fix is to make the human produce the evidence. nocx asks the person to drive their agent into a named state - "now let it ask you for permission", "now let it work", "now leave it waiting for input" - and captures the frame WITH ITS LABEL.

cmd/agent-capture (nocx-szb40.7) already records a real PTY to JSONL and replays to any moment, so the recorder exists; what is missing is the labelling and the guided flow around it.

Required labels are the three a person can produce on demand: idle, working, asks-you. exited is read from the process and is not a screen label at all. menu-open, error and waiting-on-child are optional - uncalibrated they fall to unknown, which is busy, which is a refusal rather than a wrong answer.

The labelled set is the artifact: it is what the proposal is derived from and what verification replays against.
acceptance_criteria:
A person walks the calibration for an agent and ends with a labelled capture set on disk. Skipping an optional label is allowed and leaves that state uncalibrated; skipping a required one does not complete the calibration.

A test that a labelled set round-trips through cmd/agent-capture's replay and yields the same frames.

Falsified if a label can be attached to a frame the person did not produce for it, or if a completed calibration can lack one of the three required labels.
close_reason: Landed on feat/agent-orchestration as ef4c42e3 (calibration) and c20fdfb2 (the capture format extracted so there is one owner). internal/agentcalib holds the walk: an ordered step list, one pending step, and capture/skip/redo/abandon as the only verbs. No signature in the package takes a Label or a Frame — the label comes from the pending step, the frame from the pane's live grid at the instant the person answers, and the wire (contracts/agent.calibration.answer.params.schema.json, additionalProperties:false) carries no label field at all; TestAgentCalibrationCarriesNoLabelOnTheWire and calibration-client.test.ts hold that from both ends. Skipping a required label is refused (TestARequiredStepCannotBeSkipped) and Set.Complete is derived rather than stored (TestCompletenessIsDerivedNotStored). The bead's own test is TestLabelledSetRoundTripsThroughReplay, plus TestTheCaptureIsTheOneTheCommandReplays; a real set was also replayed by hand with 'agent-capture replay -at 0,2,5'. Surface: Settings -> Calibrate an agent (frontend/src/agent-calibration-section.tsx). testdata/captures unchanged — old and new binaries print byte-identical screens for all nine captures over four mark sets.

title: A rule earns the right to be typed against, by classifying every label it was given
description:
nocx-szb40.3 states the failure this exists to prevent: a mistimed keystroke does not fail to arrive, it answers whatever modal is on screen, and can approve a tool call the person never saw. An earlier design proposed sending Escape first so a mistimed keystroke would be recoverable; it is not.

So typing authority is EARNED, and the currency is the labelled set: the rule is replayed against every labelled frame and each must classify to its label. A rule that has not done that may light the indicator - a wrong dot costs nothing - and may not gate typing.

The verdict is shown with its consequence stated in the product, not in a log: "verified against 3 of 3 labelled states - may type" / "not verified - indicator only". A soft degrade the UI contradicts is how a feature that does not exist survives a release.

This is a property of the RULE, not of who wrote it: a shipped rule whose labels no longer classify loses typing authority too, which is precisely what should happen when an agent's update breaks it.
acceptance_criteria:
A rule that classifies every labelled frame correctly may gate typing; changing one label so it no longer does revokes that, and both states are visible in Settings with their consequence named.

The wave (nocx-dkawo.1) reads this verdict and refuses to type into a pane whose rule is unverified.

Falsified if an unverified rule can gate typing, if the verdict lives only in a log, or if a shipped rule is exempt from its own verification.
close_reason: Committed as f0f30e50. Typing authority is earned: Verify replays the rule against every labelled frame and each must classify to its label. The gate is STRUCTURAL — Verdict.mayType is unexported and written in exactly one statement (verify.go:209), so the zero value, a struct literal, a forgotten field and a missed lookup all deny typing without anyone remembering to check, and an outside caller writing it does not compile (proved: vet refuses agentcalib.Verdict{mayType: true}). The label-to-state mapping already existed in Step.Expect and was not duplicated; a test asserts totality over the label set and that no label maps to unknown or exited. A shipped rule is not exempt because no exemption was written: Verify looks the rule up in the same Registry the watcher classifies through. verify_corpus_test.go watches the shipped claude rule earn authority against all six labels and lose it when one label stops classifying, which is the shape an agent's update takes. Paint/replay fidelity asserted so 'verified' cannot mean verified against a screen the product never produces. Verdict shown with its CONSEQUENCE in Settings, not the outcome.

title: The state model grows what it was missing: a TUI error is not busy, and unknown stays
description:
The driver answers five values. Two facts the owner named have nowhere to go, and one existing value is being asked to cover a case where it is actively wrong.

A TUI's OWN error - api unavailable, overloaded, no connection, quota exhausted - is chrome the agent draws, so it is readable. Today it falls to unknown, and unknown is treated as busy, and busy tells the person "it is running, leave it alone" when the truth is "come here, this will not resolve itself". It is not asks-you either: there is nothing to answer. It needs its own value.

An agent WAITING ON A CHILD - a subagent, an MCP call, a shell - is distinguishable for an agent whose chrome says so (claude draws a task panel and no spinner) and indistinguishable for one that does not. So it is an optional REFINEMENT of working, present when a rule captured it, never a required value.

And the boundary that must not move: an error the agent PRINTED and then went back to waiting is idle, deliberately. On the screen it is indistinguishable from idle because it IS idle - the agent finished, badly, and is waiting for you. Telling those apart needs meaning, and no driver reads meaning.

unknown is not a state of the agent, it is a state of our knowledge, and every consumer treats it as busy so the failure direction is a refusal. It may never be dropped or defaulted away.
acceptance_criteria:
The screen facet is idle | working (optional refinement waiting-on-child) | asks-you | menu-open | error | unknown, and the frontend distinguishes error from both busy and asks-you at a glance.

A test that an agent drawing an error banner classifies as error and NOT as unknown; a test that a transcript-printed error with a live input box classifies as idle; a test that an uncaptured refinement resolves to working rather than to a guess.

Falsified if error is folded into unknown or into asks-you, or if any consumer stops treating unknown as busy.
close_reason: Committed as b4add409. StateError added to the closed set, to contracts/session.observationChanged.schema.json, to the generated TS and to the frontend projection as its own PaneActivity with --color-danger, solid rather than spinning. Measured, not assumed: a new capture (claude-error.jsonl, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at a dead port) shows the error is drawn in the SAME slot as the spinner, and that BEFORE this branch the frame classified as free_text, not unknown as the bead predicted — nocx reported a pane that cannot reach its API as ready for input. Tests: error at three moments; the finished-turn summary in the same slot is still not an error; an error printed into the TRANSCRIPT with a live box stays free_text; the frontend keeps error distinct from working and waiting. waiting-on-child deliberately NOT added — optional by design, no rule produces it, and a value with no producer is vocabulary that cannot be reached; the subagent capture already asserts that case resolves to working. Only the RETRYING error class is captured; quota and overload draw their own chrome and are not claimed.

title: A rule is stored, edited, and switched off, per agent
description:
D12: rules are local, user-editable settings with SHIPPED DEFAULTS, switchable off per agent. Today there are no settings at all - the registry is compile-time.

Shipped rules are embedded in the binary and are NOT written to disk. That is the property that makes an upgrade useful: it improves an agent the person never touched, and never silently rewrites one they did. A user rule for an agent REPLACES the shipped one for that agent entirely - not a merge, because a half-overridden rule is two owners of one decision (AD-8).

Switching detection OFF is not the same as deleting the rule: off means the pane reports unknown, i.e. busy, i.e. nocx will not type into it. Deleting a user rule returns the shipped one.

Storage goes under internal/storage/appdir.go, so a dev stand keeps its own and an e2e run cannot touch the developer's.
acceptance_criteria:
One document per agent under the app directory, readable and editable by hand and from Settings. A user rule replaces the shipped one for that agent; deleting it restores the shipped one; disabling reports unknown.

An upgrade that ships a better claude rule improves an untouched install and leaves an edited one alone - asserted, not assumed.

Falsified if a shipped default is written to disk on first run, if a user rule merges field-by-field with a shipped one, or if disable and delete do the same thing.

title: An agent nocx has never seen is described by the person who runs it, and a driver that broke is repaired without an update
description:
Today a driver lives only in Go: internal/agentdriver is a compile-time registry
with one implementation, claude.go. When Claude Code changes the text of a
button, the person running it has no move except to wait for a nocx release —
and an agent nocx ships no driver for is `unknown` forever, which every consumer
treats as busy, so it can never join a wave.

Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-27-agent-driver-configuration-design.md

## What this crosses, and what those documents already decided

The 2026-08-15 orchestration spec's D12 decided that detection rules are LOCAL,
user-editable settings with shipped defaults, switchable off per agent, and
accompanied by a live "what is this agent emitting" view — against herdr's
network manifest catalogue, which is a network dependency for correct behaviour
and so against vision.md's "no cloud, ever". D12 adds that the view is NOT
optional: "a rule the user must write blind is a dead rule". nocx-szb40 cited
D12 but carried only its network half into "deliberately out"; the local half
was neither included nor excluded, and so was never built. This epic is that
half.

The AD-6 amendment (docs/architecture.md:151) permits a live VT grid for an
ENROLLED pane and grants it two powers, both POSITIONAL. ADR-0041 pins
charmbracelet/x/vt for exactly that reason — it reproduces xterm.js's column
geometry, and "a chrome anchor is a thing at a position". A user-authored rule
reads the same panegrid.Frame under the same interval and gains no power the
shipped driver does not have.

AD-8 and "look for the existing answer before you write a second one" decide the
shape: not a Go classifier plus a separate user-rule engine, but ONE grammar
with two authors. claude.go becomes the first document written in it, against
its existing corpus tests unchanged — a grammar that cannot express the one
driver we know is correct is not ready to be offered to anybody else.

## Why not termic's shape

termic keeps an editable agent registry (transferable, and its own epic) but
detects state with `signals: {busy, idle, attention}` — regexes over the OSC 0/2
TITLE. In this repository's provenance table that is `declared-anonymous`, the
row marked "may wake your phone: no by default", because a file containing
ESC]0;Action Required BEL would push a notification from a cat. nocx already has
that source and already draws it weaker. Porting it would be a step backwards.

## The step forwards nobody else has

cmd/agent-capture (nocx-szb40.7) records a real PTY and replays it to any
moment. That makes the emitting view a GUIDED CALIBRATION: nocx asks the person
to drive their agent into each named state, captures the frame WITH ITS LABEL,
proposes a draft rule from the differences between labelled frames, and then
REPLAYS the rule against every label as the gate. A rule that has not
classified every labelled state correctly may light the indicator and may not
gate typing — which is the concrete answer to the failure nocx-szb40.3 names: a
mistimed keystroke does not fail to arrive, it answers whatever modal is on
screen, and can approve a tool call the person never saw.

## Deliberately out

Launch configuration (its own epic). The acknowledgement facet, nocx-s6hj2. Any
network fetch of rules. Reading meaning out of the transcript — every predicate
is about chrome and geometry. The attention queue, phone notifications and
delegation.

## Success Criteria

A person runs an agent nocx ships no driver for, walks the calibration
reproducing idle, working and asks-you, accepts or edits the rule nocx proposes,
and afterwards that pane's tab distinguishes all three states and the pane is
eligible to be typed into. No nocx release, no code change, no network. And a
person whose shipped driver broke on an agent update repairs it by editing one
literal in the same surface. One automated check watches the first sentence end
to end against a real backend.

Falsified if a user rule can lift a bound the engine owns (a region cap, the
cursor requirement, branch order), if an uncalibrated state resolves to anything
other than unknown, or if a rule that fails verification can gate typing.
