The other two are the same SSH-fixture-dependent shape, timing out around 33s.

## Baselined, so this is not the main merge

All three fail identically at 0cb012cc — the branch head BEFORE main was merged in — measured in a separate worktree with the same image and the same command on 2026-08-26. The merge (0de9cff0) changes nothing about them.

NOT the fixture: cmd/e2e-sshd's own tests all pass, including both the pty-less exec channel and the direct-tcpip channels main added.

This is branch functionality — origin/main has no git-consent-required at all — so it cannot be seen from main, and will not be seen by anyone who does not run e2e on this branch.

## Deliberately out of scope

Three further webkit-only failures in the same run (git-panel.spec.ts:960, sidebar-resize.spec.ts:184, vault-sealed-probe.spec.ts:190). AGENTS.md names that class: the container runs Linux WebKit at a container-default viewport, and layout-sensitive specs fail there and pass in CI.
acceptance_criteria: The three named specs pass in the container on this branch, or each is shown to be a container-only divergence with a CI run at the same commit saying so.
close_reason: All three green. Three distinct causes, none of them consent: (1) e89316f0 — the helper artifacts were built only by 'make ci-e2e', never by the script CI actually runs, so git.open answered unsupportedPlatform and the consent card could not render; the stand builds them now. (2) beff10c6 — the bash JSON decoder wrote octal escapes without printf %b's leading zero, so the carrier loader's 'exec 2>&1' reached the far side as 'exec 2>1'. (3) 831caeb6 — cmd/e2e-sshd held a command's exit until the client closed a stdin the mux client never closes, costing 48.2s and the control socket with it. Verified: full container suite, both browsers, from a wiped .e2e — 427 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed.

title: [bug] A sealed vault runs your command and then throws the result away, saying only 'the details are in nocx's log'
description:
Measured on the owner's machine, run 128, from nocx's own log:

  level=WARN msg="agent ask: the run failed" run=128 reason=failed
    sentence="the model failed to answer. The details are in nocx's log."
    error="[NodeRunError] failed to stream tool call 836099376: agent tool
           \"run\": egress screening failed — the result was withheld:
           vault is sealed
           node path: [node_1, ToolNode]"

What the person saw: their question, the model's thinking, the command running
green with `ok` in 275ms and its output on screen — and then the turn failing
with a sentence naming a log a desktop user cannot open.

TWO DEFECTS, and the second is the serious one.

1. THE CAUSE HAS NO ARM BECAUSE IT HAS NO TYPE. policy.go:528 returns a plain
   fmt.Errorf("agent tool %q: egress screening failed — the result was
   withheld: %w"). classifyAskFailure matches by TYPE, deliberately and by its
   own doc comment, so an untyped error cannot be reached by any arm and lands
   on UnexplainedFailureSentence. Compare run 86 in the same log, which DID
   get a proper sentence because it came back as a typed *ToolFailedError.

   This is exactly the shape nocx-0645a fixed for HTTP responses: a nameable,
   actionable cause reported as "look in a log". And the action here is one
   click — unlock the vault.

2. THE COMMAND ALREADY RAN. The gate screens the RESULT, so by the time it
   fails closed the effect has happened. `df` is harmless; the same path
   governs every tool the policy permits. So a person can be in a state where
   a command executed, its result was discarded, the model never learned the
   outcome, and the only account of it is a log line. The gate failing closed
   is CORRECT — nothing may leave when the gate cannot see (design §7.1) — but
   a fail-closed gate placed AFTER the effect is a design fact that must be
   visible in the product, not discovered from a log.

   A sealed vault is not an exotic state: it is the state after every restart
   and after any timed re-seal. So the readiness ladder (nocx-rikz5: one
   sentence per unready state, one repair page) should refuse or warn BEFORE
   the run, exactly as it does for an unassigned answering role — rather than
   letting a person spend a command to find out.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Leave the vault sealed (the state after a restart).
2. Ask the assistant something that makes it call a tool — "how much disk
   space do I have?".
3. The command runs and shows `ok` with its output.
4. The turn then fails: "the model failed to answer. The details are in nocx's
   log."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The egress gate's failure is a TYPED error with an arm in
  classifyAskFailure, reached by type and never by matching text.
- The sentence names the repair in the product's words — the vault is sealed
  and unlocking it is what fixes this — and does not mention a log.
- One owner for the sentence, shared with the other endpoint/tool sentences
  (internal/assistant/endpoint_error.go is the precedent), not a third place
  where an unusable outcome is described.
- A person is told BEFORE spending a command: with the vault sealed, asking a
  question that would call a tool states the problem and offers the unlock,
  through the existing readiness ladder rather than a second mechanism. If the
  ladder cannot express it, say so and file that rather than inventing one.
- Paired tests: sealed vault produces the named sentence and no unexplained
  fallback; an unlocked vault still screens and still succeeds.

## Deliberately out

- Letting a tool result bypass the gate when the vault is sealed. The gate
  fails closed on purpose and that does not change.
notes:
MECHANISM, read from the code, and it makes the fix cheaper than the bead implies.

WHY THE VAULT IS INVOLVED AT ALL. policy.go screenResult (~line 886) is the
egress gate, and it runs on EVERY return path of a permitted tool — the
success and the error alike, because an error string carries paths, hostnames
and names too. It performs two checks:

  masking.Detect(result)      — heuristic: does this LOOK like a credential
  m.known.FindKnown(ctx, res) — does this text contain a value the vault HOLDS

The second is the one that needs the vault open, and it is the whole point: it
is what stops a tool result carrying one of the person's stored secrets off
the machine to the model provider. It has nothing to do with producing the
answer. It matters more here rather than less, because the model was on
another host on the LAN — the bytes really do leave.

Sealed, FindKnown cannot answer, so the gate cannot see, so nothing leaves.
That is the design's fail-closed contract and it is correct.

THE FIX IS SMALLER THAN FEARED: vault.ErrVaultSealed is already a typed
sentinel (internal/vault/errors.go:12), so classifyAskFailure can reach this
with errors.Is without anybody inventing a new error type. What is missing is
only the wrapping being preserved to that point and an arm that names it.

WHY NO UNLOCK PROMPT — the owner's question, and the answer is the second
defect stated plainly: nothing consults the vault before the run. The
readiness ladder resolves the answering role, the endpoint and the model; the
vault is not one of its rungs. And the gate is deliberately placed AFTER
execution because it screens a RESULT. So the earliest moment anyone can learn
the vault is sealed is after the command has already run.
WHY NO UNLOCK PROMPT — found, and it explains why this has been 'fixed' several
times without covering this case. The owner: «Мы уже раз 5 чинили это.»

The machinery all exists:
  - frontend/src/agent-status-line.ts:33 has the rung — case 'sealed' ->
    'The vault is locked — unlock it to use the assistant'.
  - frontend/src/submit.ts raises the unlock prompt through the dispatcher
    seam, discriminating on code -32001 / data.reason 'vault-sealed'.

It did not fire because the rung that feeds it asks a DIFFERENT QUESTION.
internal/transport/ws_assistant.go:237:

    func (h assistantStatusHandlers) credentialStateFor(ctx, ep) string {
        if !ep.NeedsCredential() {
            return credNotRequired        // returns before the vault is touched
        }
        ...
    }

The owner's endpoint is configured 'This endpoint does not require an API key',
so NeedsCredential() is false, the function returns on its first line, the
vault is never consulted, and readiness reports everything fine.

THE RUNG IS NAMED FOR WHAT IT MODELS: 'can I obtain this endpoint's
credential'. The egress gate needs the vault for an unrelated reason — to
compare a tool RESULT against stored secrets — and that need exists whether or
not the endpoint has a key. Every previous fix was on the credential path. This
is a second, unmodelled need for the same resource, which is why none of them
reached it. It is a missing owner, not a forgotten prompt.

CONSTRAINT THE FIX MUST NOT BREAK, stated in that function's own comment: the
status read DELIBERATELY swallows the sealed condition 'so agent.status never
raises the unlock prompt while somebody is looking at a settings page'
(asserted by assertNoPendingAsk). So the new rung must answer 'the vault is
needed and sealed' on the QUESTION path, not by making the status read start
prompting. Extend the ladder with the second question; do not repoint the
first one.

Also note the run only needs the vault if a tool may actually be called — a
grant with no permitted tools screens nothing. Whatever asks the question
should ask it for the run that is about to happen, not globally.
close_reason: Both halves done: nocx-1mf3v.1 gives the withheld result a typed error and a sentence naming the cause (ab1cc64c); nocx-1mf3v.2 puts the egress gate on the stanced unlock seam so the vault is raised before a command is spent (d36cb646).

title: grid-width.spec.ts waits on a condition its own second assertion rejects
description:
`e2e/grid-width.spec.ts` polls for the first half of the invariant and then
measures the second half once, unpolled — and the polled predicate is
satisfied by exactly the state the unpolled assertion fails on.

The poll waits for `screen.width - area.clientWidth <= 0`. A grid that has not
been fitted yet is much NARROWER than the box, so the difference is a large
negative number and the predicate passes on the first evaluation. The next
statement then reads that same un-fitted layout and computes
`fill = screen.width / area.clientWidth`, which is nowhere near 1.

Observed: `Expected: > 0.98, Received: 0.5761316872427984` — CI run
32898435382, job 97966349087, `ci-e2e (webkit)`, at 3.1s. The identical spec
passed on webkit in run 32894251201 an hour earlier at the same tree plus one
test-only commit, so nothing about the product changed between green and red.

This is the same shape as nocx-2qo02: a wait whose closing event is not the
event the assertion depends on. Here it is worse in one way — the predicate is
not merely satisfied early by accident, it is satisfied BY the failure state.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `ci-e2e (webkit)` under enough load that the authoritative fit lands after
   the first poll evaluation.
2. The first assertion passes; `expect(fill).toBeGreaterThan(0.98)` fails with
   a ratio around 0.58.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The wait ends only when BOTH halves hold: the grid is not wider than the
  scroller AND it fills it. Neither half is measured outside the settled
  state.
- On timeout the failure names which half is unsatisfied and with what
  numbers; a bare boolean is not enough to debug a layout defect from CI logs.
- No sleep and no duration.
- Green on both engines in CI.
close_reason: Both halves of the invariant are one polled predicate now, so the wait closes on the settled layout instead of on a condition the un-fitted layout satisfies. The polled value carries overhang and fill so a CI timeout names which half failed and by how much; both are restated with one matcher each afterwards. Typecheck and eslint clean; CI is the verification that counts for a layout spec, since the container runs Linux WebKit at a different viewport.

title: A local model that speaks tool calls as text is understood, and its calls run like any other
description:
## What a user can do that they could not before

Point nocx at a local model whose serving stack has no tool-call parser for it
— the common case for community quants in LM Studio — ask a question that
needs a tool, and watch the tool actually run. Today the model's own markup is
printed as the answer and the turn is reported completed.

## Success Criteria

The end-to-end check that closes this epic: a person configures
tiel-coder-35b-a3b-mlx-oq4e (or any model that answers in text-format tool
calls), asks "how much disk space do I have?", and a real `run` block appears
in the scrollback with df output in it — through the same grant, the same
approval and the same ledger entry as a native tool call.

Stops being false exactly once: today that question yields a block reading
`<tool_call><function=run>...` and settling as completed.

## Why, and what was measured

The owner: «Ну надо сделать, чтобы и такие модели работали нормально. Я вот
проверил omp и он прекрасно работает с этим же эндпоинтом.»

Measured 2026-08-25 by curl against the owner's LM Studio, same tools array,
same prompt, stream:false, nocx not in the path:

  tiel-coder-35b-a3b-mlx-oq4e  -> tool_calls: []     finish_reason: stop
                                  content: <tool_call><function=run>...
  qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b         -> tool_calls: [run]  finish_reason: tool_calls
  zai-org/glm-4.7-flash        -> tool_calls: [run]  finish_reason: tool_calls

So the server parses tool calls; it has no parser for THAT model's template.
Agents that work with it (omp among them) parse the calls out of the text
themselves. eino does not and will not do this for us: there is no hermes,
qwen or xml tool-call parser anywhere in eino v0.9.13 or eino-ext — checked
the module cache directly.

## The seam, decided before the work is briefed

`adk.ChatModelAgentMiddleware.WrapModel(ctx, m model.BaseModel[M], mc) (model
.BaseModel[M], error)` — eino's own hook for wrapping the model call, in the
SAME middleware pipeline nocx already uses for newOrderedAnswerMiddleware and
the policy middleware (engine.go builds cfg.Handlers today).

Why this seam and not another, since the alternatives are what make it right:

- Wrapping at the model boundary means a synthesized tool call is
  indistinguishable from a native one by the time anything else sees it. It
  flows through ToolsNode, the policy middleware, the grant, the approval
  gate, the attempt ledger and the block — unchanged. **Nothing may parse tool
  calls downstream of the policy, or the parser becomes a way around ADR-0020.**
  chatmodel.go:331 fixes the order (WrapModel is applied before the event
  sender), which is what makes this true rather than hoped for.
- Parsing in the transport, or in the renderer, or in classifyAskFailure would
  each put a second door into tool execution beside the one the whole
  authority design hangs on. That is the reason to reject them, and it is not
  a matter of taste.

## Deliberately out

- Guessing formats. Which dialects are supported is an explicit, listed set
  with a test per dialect; an unrecognised envelope stays a failed turn with
  the sentence nocx-mro7e gives it, never a silent best-effort parse.
- Making this the default for endpoints that DO return native tool calls. A
  model that answers natively must not be re-parsed.
notes:
CODEX DESIGN REVIEW 2026-08-25. It confirms the seam and OVERTURNS three of the
guards this epic was written with. Source citations are into eino v0.9.13 in
the module cache.

CONFIRMED — WrapModel is the right seam. handler.go:231 names 'processing or
transforming the response stream' as its use case, and react.go:492 branches on
len(chunk.ToolCalls) > 0, which is exactly where a synthesized call must exist.
The alternatives were checked and are worse: BeforeModelRewriteState only
changes model INPUT; AfterModelRewriteState and AfterChatChatModel run after
the event sender has already observed the raw stream, so the UI would show the
XML and events would disagree with state; decorating cfg.Model loses
request-local visibility of the effective tool set.

CORRECTION 1 — WithTools was a non-problem, and I had it backwards. WrapModel
receives model.BaseModel[M] and tool binding does NOT flow through user
wrappers; ADK passes the effective tool list per call via request options
(wrappers.go:1210), and TypedModelContext.Tools hands the wrapper that list.
So the wrapper implements Generate and Stream ONLY. Do not design it around
WithTools.

CORRECTION 2 — 'buffer from the opening marker' is unsafe and is withdrawn.
Streamed output cannot be retracted, so a parser that starts buffering
mid-prose either retracts what the person already read or executes a quoted
example. Recognise instead ONE grammar, whole-response:

    optional whitespace, one or more COMPLETE envelopes, optional whitespace, EOF

No prose before, between or after. Interleaved prose+call is OUT OF SCOPE by
decision, not by omission. Reasoning content is separate, is forwarded
immediately, and NEVER participates in recognition.

CORRECTION 3 — 'an unmatched tool name is prose' is wrong. An otherwise valid
envelope naming a tool that was not declared is a model/config mismatch, and
rendering it as prose hides it. It must be a VISIBLE unsupported-tool failure
with no partial execution.

CORRECTION 4 — finish_reason cannot be the trigger. LM Studio says 'stop' here,
but other servers omit it or send it only on the last delta. The configured
dialect and the grammar decide. (This also corrects the 'detection signal'
note on nocx-mro7e.)

THE BIGGEST ONE — this must be OFF BY DEFAULT, enabled per endpoint/model
profile, never auto-detected from one response. Codex's reason is the one that
settles it: scanning arbitrary model prose for envelopes 'makes data and
instructions syntactically indistinguishable inside the component authorized to
run shell commands'. One dialect initially. Not a general multi-dialect parser.

MECHANICS worth keeping verbatim:
- Handler order is a SECURITY property. The parser is INNERMOST (registered
  last, since first-registered is outermost) so the answer-ordering wrapper
  never drains raw XML. Prove it with a test over the real Handlers slice, not
  with a comment.
- Emit all synthesized calls ATOMICALLY in one final chunk with unique Index
  values. That is what avoids eino's streaming concat bug (schema/message.go
  :1284) — the same bug as eino#927.
- Any native ToolCall seen ANYWHERE in the stream means return native output
  unchanged. Never merge the two representations: that risks double execution.
  The guard can only be decided at EOF, not per chunk.
- Call ids: sha256 over a versioned prefix + the FRAMEWORK-ASSIGNED message id
  + ordinal + dialect + tool name + canonical arguments JSON. The message id is
  what stops two identical calls in different turns sharing an id and
  misassociating tool results and ledger rows. ADK injects it before user
  wrappers, on the first chunk for streams (wrappers.go:1098).
- Resume is guaranteed by PERSISTENCE, not determinism; determinism is defence
  in depth. Test: stream synthesizes id X, policy suspends, checkpoint saves,
  resume makes ZERO model calls, tool/policy sees exactly X and the original
  argument bytes.
- No regex and no XML library. A tiny dialect scanner with a documented
  escaping contract: parameter values can contain </parameter> and <tool_call>.
  Reject entities, CDATA, comments, namespaces, processing instructions,
  nesting, and duplicate parameter names (last-wins can hide a benign first
  'command' followed by a hostile second).
- Atomic all-or-none across multiple calls. Never run call 1 when call 2 is
  malformed.
- Bound candidate bytes, call count, parameter count, name and argument sizes.
  On any bound: fail closed as a tool call, flush the original prose, synthesize
  nothing. Bound tightly — flushing a huge candidate at once also hurts the UI.
- A parse rejection is a COMPLETED unsupported response, never a transient
  model error. Otherwise model retry logic re-rolls the same deterministic
  template failure.
- The allowlist must come from the EFFECTIVE tool list, since BeforeAgent and
  BeforeModelRewriteState can alter it. mc.Tools is backward-compatible but
  deprecated; isolate that behind a small adapter and pin it with a version
  test.
- The UI must say the endpoint is running a compatibility parser.

VERDICT: build it as ONE explicit off-by-default shim for the measured
Qwen3-Coder parameter dialect. Reject 'scan all model prose for any known
envelope'. Document the LM Studio chat template as the PREFERRED fix and this
as an adapter for a known-broken serving configuration.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND UPSTREAM 2026-08-26, and it makes the serving-side fix
concrete rather than aspirational.

LM Studio's own model API says it plainly. Every chat model on the owner's
server advertises tool_use EXCEPT this one:

  tiel-coder-35b-a3b-mlx-oq4e     arch=qwen3_5_moe   mlx   capabilities: NONE
  qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b            arch=qwen3_5_moe   mlx   capabilities: [tool_use]
  qwen/qwen3.8-27b                arch=qwen3_5       mlx   capabilities: [tool_use]
  zai-org/glm-4.7-flash           arch=glm4_moe_lite mlx   capabilities: [tool_use]
  huihui-glm-4.7-flash-abliterated arch=glm4_moe_lite mlx  capabilities: [tool_use]

Same architecture as a working model, same runtime, and another community
abliterated repack works too. So it is not MLX, not the architecture, and not
community quants as a class.

WHY: Tiel-Coder is a Qwen3.5-35B-A3B derivative in the Ornith-1.0-35B line,
whose chat_template.jinja carries two hard assertions —
raise_exception('System message must be at the beginning.') and
raise_exception('No user query found in messages.'). llama.cpp, LM Studio and
Ollama all AUTO-GENERATE a tool-call parser by PROBING the template with
synthetic message sequences that do not put the system message first. The
probe hits the assertion, the probe fails, and the runtime concludes the model
has no tool_use capability — which is exactly the empty capabilities field
above. Upstream discussion: huggingface.co/deepreinforce-ai/Ornith-1.0-35B
discussions/10, whose fix is to delete both raise_exception calls. It also
confirms the dialect we measured: <function=name><parameter=k>value.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS EPIC:
- The 'preferred fix belongs in the serving stack' line is now actionable, not
  a shrug: override the Prompt Template in LM Studio (My Models > model
  settings > Prompt Template) with the template minus the two assertions.
- It STRENGTHENS the case for off-by-default. The failing population is not
  'models with an exotic dialect' but 'models whose template fails a runtime's
  capability probe' — a packaging bug, upstream-fixable, and one the model
  author may fix next week. A shim that is on by default would silently keep
  parsing text for models that have since started answering natively.
- The capability probe gives nocx a HONEST pre-flight signal it does not use
  today: LM Studio's /api/v0/models reports capabilities per model. That is a
  better answer to nocx-mro7e's 'a person can find out BEFORE asking' criterion
  than exercising a tool in the probe, at least for LM Studio. It is
  vendor-specific, so it informs rather than replaces the generic check.
OWNER PUSHBACK 2026-08-26, and it is the strongest argument this epic has.

Asked whether hand-editing the model's chat_template.jinja is really the
method, the owner: «А это точно правильный метод? Что каждый человек так
правит саму модель?»

No, and the coordinator was wrong to lead with it. Editing files inside a model
directory is a workaround, not a method. The repair ladder is, in order: the
PACKAGER fixes the template (lmstudio-community builds already carry the fix,
which is why every working model on the owner's server comes from them or from
huihui-ai, and the broken one is a personal repack); the USER overrides it
non-destructively in LM Studio's Advanced Configuration > Prompt Template; and
only then, never routinely, does anyone touch the model's own files.

The consequence for nocx is the point. If our honest answer to 'my local model
does not work' is 'edit a Jinja file inside the model directory', we are moving
work onto the person that the product should absorb — and omp already absorbs
it, which is why it works with this model and we do not. So this epic is
justified by the owner's own question, not merely by convenience.

IT ALSO REPAIRS THE WEAK SPOT IN 'OFF BY DEFAULT'. Codex's off-by-default is
right on the security argument and wrong if it means a person must GUESS that
a toggle exists. LM Studio publishes capabilities per model on /api/v0/models
(measured: the broken model reports none, every working one reports tool_use).
nocx can read that and say what is wrong in one sentence, then offer the
compatibility mode right there.

That is the ladder nocx-rikz5 already built for model readiness — one sentence
per unready state and one repair page — so this is extending an existing
answer rather than inventing a second one. Default off, discovery automatic:
the person chooses, but never has to know the toggle exists beforehand.

This supersedes nothing in the codex review; it fills the gap the review left
between 'off by default' and 'a person can find out before asking'
(nocx-mro7e's criterion).
SERVING-SIDE FIX ATTEMPTED AND FAILED, 2026-08-26. Measured end to end on the
owner's LM Studio. This settles whether the epic is needed.

STEP 1 — the template's tool format IS fixable from the UI, and it worked.
The model's chat_template.jinja (template_version qwen3.8-froggeric-v22.3.2)
carries BOTH dialects behind one switch on line 2:

  {%- set _tool_format = tool_call_format if tool_call_format is defined else 'xml' %}

with a json branch and an xml branch at lines 200-203. Changing that single
word in LM Studio's Advanced Configuration > Prompt Template changed the
model's output from

  <tool_call><function=run><parameter=command>df -h</parameter>...</tool_call>
to
  <tool_call>{"name": "run", "arguments": {"command": "df -h", ...}}</tool_call>

— the standard Hermes/Qwen JSON form. So the override DOES reach the server,
and this also explains why an earlier attempt to force the JSON form with a
system prompt failed: the template injects its own <IMPORTANT> instruction,
which outranks anything the caller says.

STEP 2 — and it changed nothing that matters. tool_calls stayed [], finish
'stop'. LM Studio does not parse even its own standard format for this model.
Removing the raise_exception('No messages provided.') guard as well did not
help either.

WHY, and this is the durable finding: capabilities is a STATIC, INDEX-TIME
property of the packaged model, not a runtime one. Measured — three models
report tool_use while state=not-loaded, and the broken one reports none while
state=loaded:

  tiel-coder-35b-a3b-mlx-oq4e   state=loaded      caps= NONE
  qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b          state=not-loaded  caps=[tool_use]

A prompt-template override lives in the preset. It CANNOT change an index-time
capability, so no amount of UI configuration fixes this. The earlier
raise_exception-probe theory is therefore moot: whatever probing happens reads
the model's own files, not the override.

CONSEQUENCE — 'push it back onto the serving stack' is refuted on a live case.
The owner did the correct, supported, non-destructive thing through the
official UI and it did not work. What remains is repackaging the model or
abandoning it, and neither is an answer a product can give a person. Codex's
recommendation to document the chat template as the PREFERRED fix stands as
advice, but it can no longer be the ONLY answer, and this epic is not optional.

CONSEQUENCE FOR DETECTION — sharper than what is written above. The question
is not 'does this endpoint support tools' but 'will this endpoint parse tool
calls for THIS model'. LM Studio answers it directly on /api/v0/models: an
empty capabilities array while nocx is sending a non-empty tools array means
the calls will never be parsed whatever the model emits. That is the honest
pre-flight signal for nocx-mro7e's 'a person can find out BEFORE asking'
criterion, and it is per endpoint+model, not per endpoint.

ALSO OBSERVED, and it must not be softened by the parser: the model returned
sessionId 5c3b52a2cf894afd36d24704476a0def for an input of
5c3b52a2cf894afd36d24f04476a0def — one character lost. A synthesized tool call
carries arguments a model wrote and may corrupt. It gets EXACTLY the same
validation as a native one — scope check, grant, approval — and no leniency
anywhere for being locally parsed.
DESIGN REPLACED 2026-08-26 with omp's, after the owner asked for it and after
reading its source in ~/repos/oh-my-pi. What follows supersedes the WrapModel-
parses-emptiness design above. Two corrections to earlier notes first, both
measured:

- CAPABILITIES IS NOT THE GATE. The model now returns native tool_calls with
  finish_reason 'tool_calls' while /api/v0/models still reports no
  capabilities. The earlier 'capabilities is an index-time gate' conclusion was
  wrong. What fixed it was the FORMAT: one word in the Jinja template,
  else 'xml' -> else 'json'. The first measurement that showed JSON output with
  empty tool_calls was taken before the model reloaded.
- MANUAL MODE ALSO WORKS. The owner switched Prompt Template to Manual/ChatML
  and tool calls still arrive natively, so in Manual mode LM Studio owns tool
  rendering and parsing itself rather than delegating to a Jinja template. The
  coordinator predicted this would break tools; it did not.

THE OMP ARCHITECTURE, which is what we build.

1. THE TRIGGER IS PROVIDER METADATA, NOT OUTPUT SNIFFING.
   packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts resolveDialect(format, model):
     format 'native'  -> no dialect, use native tool calling
     format 'auto'    -> model.supportsTools !== false ? native
                                                       : preferredDialect(model.id)
     otherwise        -> that dialect, forced
   supportsTools comes from the provider's own capability report
   (packages/catalog/src/provider-models/openai-compat.ts). Default is 'auto'.
   THIS is why omp needs no user configuration: the switch is the server's own
   answer, not a heuristic over the model's prose and not a setting.

2. THE DIALECT IS IMPOSED, NOT GUESSED. In in-band mode omp renders the tool
   catalog INTO THE SYSTEM PROMPT in a chosen dialect
   (dialect/catalog.ts renderInbandToolPrompt) and scans the output for THAT
   dialect. preferredDialect(modelId) switches on a model-family token with a
   fallback. It never tries to detect which dialect a model 'naturally' speaks.

   This dissolves the security objection codex raised — 'scanning arbitrary
   prose makes data and instructions syntactically indistinguishable inside the
   component authorized to run shell commands'. There is no scanning of
   arbitrary prose: we asked for that format, in that turn, and we only look
   for it when we asked.

   It also removes the need for 'off by default'. Nothing is guessed, so there
   is nothing for a person to have to opt into.

3. CHANNEL ARBITRATION BEATS OUR 'ONLY WHEN NATIVE IS EMPTY' GUARD.
   dialect/owned-stream.ts, on #toolChannel: 'records which channel produced
   the turn's FIRST REAL CALL so the other is dropped - no double-dispatch, and
   NO GUESSING FROM EMPTINESS. Nameless ghost parts never lock a channel.'
   Codex had already noticed our guard could only be decided at EOF. First-call-
   wins is decidable live, mid-stream, and cannot double-dispatch.

4. THE SCANNER IS A STREAMING EVENT SOURCE, not a whole-response matcher.
   dialect/types.ts: InbandScanner { feed(text): events[]; flush(): events[] }
   emitting text / thinkingStart / thinkingDelta / thinkingEnd / toolStart /
   toolArgDelta / toolEnd. Because the dialect was imposed, it can stream
   argument deltas instead of buffering a candidate — which is what makes
   codex's 'buffering the whole candidate is unavoidable' not apply to us
   either. That conclusion followed from sniffing, and we are not sniffing.
   Options carry stringArgs (verbatim string params) and the tool schemas.

WHAT STAYS FROM THE CODEX REVIEW: the seam analysis (WrapModel is where the
stream is transformed, and handler order is a security property, parser
innermost); synthesized calls get EXACTLY the native validation path — scope,
grant, approval, ledger — with no leniency; deterministic ids derived from the
framework message id; atomic all-or-none; strict bounds; a parse rejection is a
completed unsupported response, never a transient model error.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE BRIEF, do not let a worker decide it alone: in in-band
mode the native tools array must NOT be sent to the model, but ToolsNode must
still hold the tools so it can EXECUTE them. ADK applies tools per invocation
via request options (adk/wrappers.go:1210), so the wrapper has to suppress that
option while cfg.ToolsConfig keeps the tools registered. Confirm that is
reachable before briefing the wiring task.
PRIORITY LOWERED 2026-08-26 by measurement, not by opinion.

With the poisoned history removed, this model answers with NATIVE tool calls
5 times out of 5 through nocx's exact request shape (see nocx-mro7e for the
runs). So the case that justified this epic — 'a local model that cannot speak
native tool calls' — is not the case the owner actually hit. He hit
nocx-mro7e's history poisoning, on a model that CAN speak native tool calls
once LM Studio is configured for it.

This epic stays open and its design stands: models that genuinely lack native
tool calling exist, and omp's architecture is the right answer for them. But it
is no longer the fix for the reported symptom, and nocx-mro7e is. Do not take
this epic before that bug is closed and the owner has re-measured.

title: [bug] A model that emits its tool call as text is reported 'completed', and the raw markup is shown as the answer
description:
Asked "Сколько у меня места на диске?" against a local endpoint, the model
answered in 3.8s, the block settled as **completed**, and what the person read
was this, verbatim, as the answer:

    <tool_call>
    <function=run>
    <parameter=command>
    df -hT -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '^Filesystem' ; echo '---'; df -h / 2>/dev/null
    </parameter>
    <parameter=sessionId>
    5c3b52a2cf894afd36d24f04476a0def
    </parameter>
    </function>
    </tool_call>

The model did everything right. It chose `run`, it built a sensible command,
it named the session. What it did not do is emit a NATIVE OpenAI `tool_calls`
payload — it emitted its own chat template's tool-call markup as ordinary
assistant text, which is what many open-weight models do unless the serving
stack has a parser for that model's format.

Three separate defects, and only the first is arguably somebody else's.

1. NOTHING PARSED IT, so no tool ran. That may be correct: nocx speaks the
   OpenAI tool protocol and this was not it.

2. **The run is reported `completed`.** A turn whose entire content is an
   unexecuted tool call is not a completed answer, and calling it one is the
   silent degrade AGENTS.md refuses: "A soft degrade must be visible in the
   product, not only in a log." There is already an arm for the neighbouring
   case — `ErrMalformedModelOutput` says "the model asked for a tool call nocx
   could not act on... a different model may handle tools better" — and it is
   never reached here, because the model produced no tool call at all, only
   prose that looks like one.

3. **The probe cannot warn anyone.** `Probe.Run` (internal/assistant/probe.go)
   passes `nil` for tools and `nil` for handlers, and its comment says the
   probe asks only "does this model answer". So Test endpoint goes green on an
   endpoint that cannot call a tool, and nothing in the product ever states
   that this endpoint/model pairing does not support tool calling. There is no
   ProbeKind for it: assistant.go declares ProbeModel and nothing else.

The person is left with a product that says the thing worked while showing
them markup, and a Test button that agreed with it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an endpoint against a local server (LM Studio) whose model emits
   tool calls in its own template format rather than native OpenAI tool_calls.
2. Press Test endpoint: green.
3. Ask a question that needs a tool ("how much disk space do I have?").
4. The block settles `completed` in a few seconds and shows the raw
   `<tool_call>...` markup as the answer. No command ran, no attempt was
   recorded, the ledger has no call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A turn whose answer contains an unexecuted tool-call payload does NOT settle
  as `completed`. It says, in the product's words, that the model asked for a
  tool in a format nocx does not speak, and that a different model or a server
  that parses this one's format is the repair.
- The detection is by SHAPE, not by a list of vendor markup strings that will
  be out of date next month. Decide and write down what the signal is — an
  answer that parses as a tool-call envelope, a turn that produced no tool
  call and no prose a person can use, or something better — and say in the
  code why the alternatives were rejected.
- Whatever detects it has ONE owner shared with the endpoint-error sentences
  (nocx-0645a), rather than a second place where an unusable answer is judged.
- A person can find out BEFORE asking that an endpoint cannot call tools:
  either the probe exercises a tool and reports it, or the product states
  plainly that it does not know. A green Test button must not imply a
  capability that was never tested.
- Paired tests: a model that emits template markup is caught; a model that
  emits a real tool call still runs it; an ordinary prose answer is still
  `completed`.

## Deliberately out

- Parsing foreign tool-call formats and executing them. nocx speaks the OpenAI
  tool protocol; teaching it a second dialect is a decision, not a bugfix, and
  it needs its own bead and an ADR if it is ever wanted.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-25 after the owner asked whether the defect is ours.
Checked against the eino ToolsNode guide and cloudwego/eino issues 440 and 927.

FINDING: nocx does send the tools array, and the evidence is in the owner's
own screenshot. The model named the tool 'run' with parameters 'command' and
'sessionId' — that is nocx's registry schema verbatim. It cannot have come
from the system prompt: systemprompt.go line ~131 says 'Deliberately no list
of tools. What each tool does is written on the tool itself', and the prompt
names only sessionId, never 'run' or 'command'. So the schema reached the
model through the OpenAI tools array, which means engine.go built and sent it.

The wiring is also correct on inspection. Ask() builds declaredTools() from
the grant, streamModelAnswer() puts them in
adk.ChatModelAgentConfig.ToolsConfig.ToolsNodeConfig.Tools, and a non-empty
tool set is what takes ADK off buildNoToolsRunFunc — the no-tools path that
sends no tools array at all.

So the model was offered native tool calling and answered with its chat
template's markup as assistant TEXT anyway. That is the serving stack: LM
Studio needs a tool-call parser for that model's format to turn it into
tool_calls. Not nocx's send path.

The three defects this bead lists are unaffected — they are all about what
nocx does with that answer, not about how it asked.

NEITHER issue explains this symptom, but 927 IS a latent bug for us:
- eino#440 is about ReAct Generate() returning only the final message. Not our
  path; we stream through adk.Runner.
- eino#927 is 'cannot concat ToolCalls with different tool id' when a model
  emits SEVERAL native tool calls in one streamed response. We would hit that
  the moment a model does it, and the error is neither an APIError nor a
  RequestError, so it lands on UnexplainedFailureSentence — 'the details are
  in nocx's log' — which is the same dead end nocx-0645a just removed for HTTP
  errors. Worth its own arm, or its own bead, once someone reproduces it.
PROVEN AGAINST THE REAL ENDPOINT 2026-08-25. Three requests, same server, same
tools array, same prompt, stream:false. Sent by curl, so nocx is not in the
path at all:

  tiel-coder-35b-a3b-mlx-oq4e  -> tool_calls: []       finish_reason: stop
                                  content: the raw <tool_call>...</tool_call>
  qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b         -> tool_calls: [run]    finish_reason: tool_calls
  zai-org/glm-4.7-flash        -> tool_calls: [run]    finish_reason: tool_calls

So LM Studio parses tool calls correctly on that machine. It does not parse
THIS model's format — a community MLX quant whose template LM Studio has no
tool-call parser for. nocx receives exactly the bytes curl received, and the
send path is not implicated: this closes the question the owner raised.

The owner's observation that other agents work with this model is consistent
and is the real point: those agents parse tool calls OUT OF THE TEXT
themselves rather than relying on native tool_calls. That is why they work
where nocx does not, and it is the argument for reopening the 'Deliberately
out' below.

DETECTION SIGNAL, now concrete and cheap: the response carried
finish_reason 'stop' WITH an empty tool_calls array and content that is a
tool-call envelope. That is a shape, not a vendor string — it is the third
acceptance criterion above, answered.

IMMEDIATE WORKAROUND for the owner, needing no nocx change: use
qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b or zai-org/glm-4.7-flash, both already loaded on that
server, both returning native tool calls.
The 'Deliberately out' above — teaching nocx a second tool-call dialect — is
WITHDRAWN. The owner asked for it directly on 2026-08-25 after confirming omp
works against the same endpoint, and it is now epic nocx-1ny0r, which carries
the measurement and the seam.

This bead keeps what it was always about: what nocx does with an answer it
cannot use. That work does not go away when the parser lands — it is what
happens for the dialects the parser does NOT recognise, and the detection
signal is the same one (finish_reason 'stop' with an empty tool_calls array
and content that is a tool-call envelope).
ROOT CAUSE MEASURED 2026-08-26, and it is ours. This bead is no longer about
cosmetics; it is the fix.

Ten curl runs against the owner's LM Studio, nocx's EXACT request replayed from
its own Developer log — same three tools with their $schema/$id/title, same
stream_options, same system prompt:

  A, history containing a prior assistant turn whose content is the raw
     <tool_call> markup:   NATIVE, XML-TEXT, NATIVE, NATIVE, XML-TEXT  (2/5 fail)
  B, identical but WITHOUT that turn:  NATIVE x5  (0/5 fail)

So the request shape is not implicated — bisecting $schema/$id/title out and
stream_options out changed nothing. What fails the turn is that NOCX REPLAYS A
FAILED TURN'S RAW MARKUP INTO THE CONVERSATION AS AN assistant MESSAGE. The
model reads its own previous 'answer' as the house style and reproduces it.

It is a RATCHET, not a coin flip. Every failure adds another poisoned turn, so
the probability of the next one rises. And it degrades past format: on one run
the model, seeing a tool call in history with no result after it, FABRICATED
one —

  [TOOL_RESULT]
  <result>
  Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
  udev            3.9G     0   3.9G   0% /dev

— invented df output, presented as an answer. That is a data-integrity defect:
the assistant can show a person terminal output that no command produced. It
promotes this bead above nocx-1ny0r.

THE FIX FOLLOWS DIRECTLY from criterion 1 already written above: a turn whose
content is an unexecuted tool-call envelope does not settle as 'completed'. It
must also NOT ENTER THE HISTORY as an ordinary assistant answer. Whatever the
UI shows the person, the messages replayed to the model must not contain a
fabricated-looking assistant turn that models the wrong behaviour.

Add as a criterion: after a turn fails this way, the NEXT question sends a
message list that does not contain the failed turn's markup, and a test asserts
that on the outgoing payload.
close_reason: The judgement has one owner in internal/assistant beside the endpoint-error sentences, by SHAPE not by vendor strings: the whole trimmed prose must be a sequence of complete, non-nested envelopes, each valid in the XML-parameter or JSON-in-tags dialect. A sequence rather than one block because the model's own template instructs a separate closed block per function — the first cut missed that and I sent it back. finish_reason is deliberately not consulted. The engine returns a typed failure when tools were offered, no call crossed the policy seam, and the answer is only an envelope (which needed the tool-call callback routed through the tallying sink). In priorAnswerMessage the predicate leads and the recorded state follows, so replay safety does not depend on a second thing being right — also a send-back. Tests assert on the OUTGOING payload of the next question. go vet clean, targeted tests green in internal/assistant and internal/transport, verified by the coordinator. Merged as 7183117d. NOT closed by this: executing such a call, which is nocx-1ny0r.

title: The chip and its popover name what the mark MEANS: the person's interest, not a grant
description:
The whole vocabulary of this surface says permission — grant, GrantController,
GrantBlock, data-granted, "Dismiss all" — and permission is not what the mark
does. The owner, asked directly on 2026-08-25:

  «Выделение нужно не для того, чтобы ограничить скоуп, а сказать модели что
  именно интересует пользователя.»

Marking is ATTENTION. It tells the model what the question is about. It has
never been a fence: narrowSession (agenttools/narrow.go) builds its
SessionReader from ResourceSession scopes alone, so session.read reaches every
item in the session whatever was marked — see nocx-hnh7r, whose premise this
decision corrects.

"marked for the question - 0" is therefore not merely an awkward placeholder
standing in for a stronger claim, which is how nocx-wcswn and nocx-hnh7r read
it. It is a phrase built around the wrong concept. So is the count: a person
asking about two blocks does not want to be told the number 2, they want to
see which two.

This bead is the naming pass, and it is deliberately not the styling one
(nocx-5u3oz.12) nor the visibility one (nocx-5u3oz.14).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The chip, its tooltip, its aria-label and every row and control in its
  popover read as "this is what the question is about". No word in the user-
  visible surface claims a permission, a grant or a scope.
- The empty state says what the mark is FOR, or the chip is absent - it does
  not report a count of nothing (see nocx-5u3oz.14 for when it is on screen).
- The identifiers follow the concept. If the renderer's word stays `grant` the
  code disagrees with the product in the way nocx-wszzh was filed for; if it
  changes, it changes in one pass across grant.ts, ask-entry.ts, the
  data-attribute and the tests, with no second vocabulary left behind.
- The system prompt and the ask payload say the same thing to the model that
  the chip says to the person. If the prompt currently frames marked blocks as
  a permission, it is part of this change; if it says nothing about them at
  all, that is a finding to report, not to fix silently.
- No user-visible Cyrillic (nocx-wszzh).

## Deliberately out

- Per-item narrowing of session.read. That is nocx-hnh7r and, after this
  decision, needs its own justification.

title: api-testing.spec.ts reads the binding document once, before the import has written it
description:
`e2e/api-testing.spec.ts:239` polls until the collection directory exists and
then reads `api-bindings.json` synchronously, on the stated reasoning that the
directory arriving is the import's closing event. It is not.

`ImportInto` (internal/apiimport/write.go) renames the staging tree into place
at line 157 and offers the secret values to the BindWriter at line 184 — step
5 of its own documented contract, "only then are the secret values offered".
Each offer is `JSONStore.Bind`, which does a vault `CreateNamed` (key
derivation and an encrypt against the passphrase vault this spec sets up in
its first step) before `api-bindings.json` is rewritten. So dest exists and
the binding document does not, for as long as that vault write takes.

The window closes on its own, or the import fails and `undo` removes dest
again — which is why waiting is safe and reading once is not.

The invariant in write.go's header names both ends correctly for FAILURE
("no state in which dest exists and this import is unfinished" is upheld by
undo) but the spec read it as a promise to an outside observer, which it is
not. Worth a second look at whether the comment should say so.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `ci-e2e (webkit)` on a loaded runner. Observed on run 32889355601 at
   commit d3078f14 — one failure, 206 passed:
   `Error: the import bound no secret at all — there is no binding document`.
2. The same commit was green on webkit in PR #102's run 32883305438 an hour
   earlier, so nothing about the code changed between green and red.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The spec waits on the binding document rather than reading it once, and
  still refuses to pass on a document holding no bindings.
- No sleep and no duration is introduced: the wait is on observable state, per
  the AGENTS.md rule that a test may not depend on timing.
- `PW_PROJECTS=webkit e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/api-testing.spec.ts` green.
close_reason: Shipped, and then made moot. The fix landed as commit e406e149, 'test(e2e): the binding document is waited for, not read once (nocx-2qo02)', an ancestor of HEAD. The spec was subsequently deleted outright by 1fb02459, 'refactor(api): delete legacy binding store (nocx-0jw8l)' — e2e/api-testing.spec.ts no longer exists and grep for api-bindings.json across e2e/ returns nothing. Verified during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh. Duplicate sibling nocx-3skn6 closed alongside.

title: [bug] An endpoint that answers with an HTTP error has no arm, so a misconfigured local model says 'the details are in nocx's log'
description:
A person points nocx at a local endpoint, asks a question, and 31ms later the
block says "the model failed to answer. The details are in nocx's log." That
is the DEFAULT arm of classifyAskFailure (ws_agent.go:1824) - the arm reached
when nothing else matched - and it names a log a person using the app cannot
open. The one thing they needed to know was that the endpoint replied 404
because the base URL carries the wrong path, or that it does not serve the
model id they typed.

The mapping in classifyAskFailure is careful about the causes it knows:
StreamError, RunLeaseError, ToolFailedError, malformed tool output, cancelled,
deadline, and *url.Error for a dial that failed. What has no arm is the most
common failure of all - the endpoint was REACHED, and answered with an HTTP
error. *url.Error does not cover it: the transport succeeded. So a 404 on the
path, a 401 on the key, and a model id the endpoint does not serve all land on
the sentence that says nothing.

The probe has the opposite defect for the same class. Probe.Run puts
`streamErr.Error()` raw into ProbeResult.Error (probe.go:80), so the Test
button shows the framework's own text - `[NodeRunError]`, `node path`,
`ToolNode` - which is exactly what nocx-avogl.3 removed from the ask path.
One class of error, two surfaces, two opposite policies, neither of them a
sentence a person can act on.

There is no owner for "the endpoint answered with an error". That is the bug;
the two symptoms are what it looks like from each side.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings - Endpoints: add an endpoint with base URL
   http://<host>:1234/api/v1 (LM Studio's native REST path, not its
   OpenAI-compatible /v1) and a model id, no API key.
2. Ask the assistant anything.
3. The block fails in ~30ms with "the model failed to answer. The details are
   in nocx's log."
4. Press Test endpoint on the same endpoint and read the framework's raw
   error text instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An endpoint that answers with an HTTP status has its own arm, and the
  sentence names what a person can change: the address, the key, or the model
  id. Reached by a TYPE, never by matching the framework's text.
- The status-to-sentence mapping has ONE owner, and both the ask path and the
  probe read it. The probe stops putting a raw framework error on screen.
- A test drives each of 401, 404 and a model-not-found body through that owner
  and asserts the sentence, plus the paired case that an ordinary answer still
  succeeds.
- No framework internals reach the wire from either surface.
close_reason: assistant.EndpointErrorSentence is the one owner of endpoint-error -> sentence; classifyAskFailure and Probe.Run both read it. Arms for 401/403 (credential), 404 (address, naming the /v1 path), model_not_found (quoting the model id) and any other status, all reached by TYPE — *einoopenai.APIError / *openai.RequestError carry HTTPStatusCode, which is why go.mod promotes go-openai to direct; the file says why. The probe stops putting raw framework text on the wire, and the last-resort sentence is a shared constant. New arm ordered after cancelled/deadline, before *url.Error. go vet clean; targeted tests green in internal/assistant and internal/transport, verified independently by the coordinator. Merged as 21bb5dc2.

title: The pre-commit gofumpt step walks nested agent worktrees under .claude
description:
The pre-commit hook runs `gofumpt -l .`, a filesystem walk from the repository
root. Claude Code's `isolation: worktree` puts agent worktrees at
`.claude/worktrees/<id>/`, inside that root, so the walk descends into other
branches' checkouts. Those carry whatever formatting their commit had, cannot
be fixed from main, and block every commit in the repository until the
worktree is removed.

Go tooling does not have this problem: `./...` skips directories whose name
begins with `.`, so `go build`, `go test` and golangci-lint never see them.
gofumpt walks the filesystem instead, so only it trips.

The same lesson was already learned for prettier — `.prettierignore` lists
`.claude/`, with a comment about exactly this class of failure on
`test-results/`. gofumpt never got the equivalent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have any agent worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` whose HEAD predates a
   formatting fix on main (e.g. `agent-a0f7478c4e7b46ca7` at 8883a908).
2. `git commit` anything at all, including a docs-only change.
3. The hook fails with `FAIL: gofumpt` naming files under
   `.claude/worktrees/.../internal/content/`.

`gofumpt -l internal/content/` on main is empty at the same moment, so the
report is about code that is not being committed and is not on this branch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gofumpt step reports nothing for a file under `.claude/`, with a stale
  agent worktree present.
- The gofumpt step still fails on an unformatted `.go` file inside the
  repository proper, tracked or newly created and not yet added.
- `make hooks` / the installed hook needs no per-machine configuration for
  either.

title: [bug] A granted block wears the composer's identity rail, and draws it twice
description:
The mark that says "this block is granted" is a 3px accent bar down the left
edge — which is exactly what `.nocx-editor` already uses as its own identity
(style.css:166, `border-left: 3px solid var(--color-accent)`). So the same
rail means "this is the composer" in one place and "this block is marked" in
another, and a person reading the pane sees one vocabulary for two concepts.
That is the duplicate-owner shape AGENTS.md refuses, in CSS rather than in Go.

Second, the mark draws its rail twice over itself: `.cmd-block[data-granted]`
(style.css:1059) sets `box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0` at 65% accent AND a
`::before` of `width: 3px` at full accent in the same place. The ::before
covers the box-shadow completely, so one of the two has no effect at all.

Third, the tint that was supposed to carry the mark is
`color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-accent), transparent 94%)` — 6% accent over
canvas, which is not visible on the tokyo-night background. nocx-wcswn asked
for "a left rail plus a faint tint from existing tokens"; the tint arrived
faint enough to be absent, leaving the rail as the whole signal, and the rail
is the composer's.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a pane, run a command, and mark its block for a question.
2. Look at the pane: the marked block's left rail and the composer's left
   rail are the same 3px accent bar.
3. Inspect `.cmd-block[data-granted]` — the box-shadow inset rail is fully
   covered by the ::before rail.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A granted block is distinguishable from the composer at a glance, and the
  two do not share one visual signal.
- The mark is drawn once — no rule whose only effect is to be covered by
  another.
- The tint is visible on the default theme, or it is removed and the mark
  carries its meaning some other way. It still must not look like a selection
  (nocx-wcswn's constraint).
notes:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-25 — this supersedes nocx-wcswn's whole-block-only rule
and changes what this bead is about.

Asked whether to keep the whole-block mark and merely make it visible, the
owner answered: «Если выделили блок, то подсвечиваем блок (не рельсы), если
выделена строка - подсвечиваем строку.»

So the mark's GRANULARITY FOLLOWS THE GESTURE, and the rail goes away:

- A whole block marked  -> the whole block is highlighted, as a fill. Not a
  left rail.
- Rows selected and marked -> those rows are highlighted, and the block is not
  filled behind them.

That reverses nocx-wcswn's 'A marked block is marked WHOLE - a left rail plus
a faint tint, not per term-line'. It reinstates the per-row marking that
nocx-a7mw7 originally promised, without reinstating the surfaces nocx-wcswn
deleted (the floating Attach, referenceChipLabel, the fingerprint dedupe).

Removing the rail also settles this bead's original finding for free: the rail
was the composer's own identity (.nocx-editor border-left) worn by a block,
and it was drawn twice over itself. With no rail there is no collision and no
double draw.

STILL OPEN, and it is not a styling question: a row-level mark has to reach
the model as a fact, and today session.read reads a BLOCK. Either the prompt
says which rows of the block the person pointed at, or the row mark is a lie
the renderer tells itself. Decide that before implementing, and read
ADR-0020 and the tools spec before touching the boundary.
RESOLVED, the open question above: a row-level mark CAN reach the model, and
needs no new tool.

contracts/tools/session.read.schema.json already declares 'start' (first
output line) and 'count' (how many, max 2000) beside 'sessionId' and 'id'. So
the window a row mark describes is exactly the window session.read already
takes. 'the person is pointing at item X, lines 12-14' is expressible today.

What is missing is only the carry: the renderer's mark is a block id
(GrantBlock.itemId in frontend/src/ask-entry.ts) with no line range on it, and
the ask payload's attachedContent (frontend/src/agent-ask.ts) is
{itemId, command, state} — block-level. A row mark therefore needs a line
range on the mark and on the payload, and the prompt has to say which lines
the person pointed at. It does not need a protocol change to session.read.

So the row highlight is not a lie the renderer tells itself, provided the
range travels. If a wave implements the row highlight WITHOUT the range
reaching the model, that is the defect this note exists to prevent.
close_reason: The mark follows the gesture: a whole-block mark fills the block, a row selection fills only its rows, and no mark wears the composer's accent rail — which also removes the double-drawn rail and raises the fill from an invisible 6% to 14% accent. The row range travels to the model: on GrantBlock, in the ask payload, and in the prompt, which tells the model to pass start and count to session.read for a row mark and omit both for a block. count is capped at the contract's 2000; start deliberately has no ceiling, since refusing a mark past line 2000 would defeat the epic it serves. tsc clean, 395 frontend tests green in 5 files, go vet clean, Go scoped tests green — all verified by the coordinator.

title: [bug] A marked block with no command renders a blank row in the grant popover
description:
The grant popover lists a marked block by its command text, and an answer
block has none — so the row renders with a dismiss button and nothing to
read. The chip counts 1, the popover says nothing.

grantBlockFromElement (frontend/src/ask-entry.ts:31-37) derives `command`
from `data-recorded-command` ?? `.cmd-header-text` ?? '', and GrantController
.renderPanel (frontend/src/grant.ts:87) puts that straight into
`displayText`. nocx-wcswn specified "listing each marked block by its
command"; the ask kind was never a command, so nobody chose what its row
says. The empty string is not a decision, it is the absence of one.

The row is also the only thing identifying the block a person is about to
dismiss, so a blank row makes dismiss-the-right-one impossible without
opening each in turn via reveal.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant something and let it answer.
2. Mark the answer block for a question (block menu, or select and Attach).
3. Open the grant chip: the row is blank apart from the × dismiss.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every block kind that can be marked has a row label chosen for that kind,
  not an empty string reached by fallthrough.
- A block whose label would be empty still identifies itself in the popover.
- A unit test marks an ask block and asserts the row is not empty.
close_reason: Cause confirmed: ?? does not fall through on '', so a present-but-empty data-recorded-command stopped the chain before .cmd-header-text, which held the ask block's question all along. The label is now a rule in BLOCK_KIND_RULES — the table that already owns every per-kind fact and says no call site checks the kind — with an explicit non-empty fallback per kind, so no row can be blank. tsc clean both projects, 179 tests green across grant/ask-entry/blocks. Merged as 79d228d1.

title: [bug] 8 of 10 assistant e2e proofs are red on feat/ai-assistant while main's pass in the same container
description:
Every epic on feat/ai-assistant that is not the readiness slice fails its own
end-to-end proof. This is the check AGENTS.md rule 2 makes the ONLY evidence
that a feature is wired, so while it is red those epics cannot be closed and
the branch cannot honestly go to main.

## It is not the container, and that is the load-bearing measurement

`e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts` exists on main too. On a pristine `git archive
origin/main` tree, in the SAME image and the same command, it passes 6/6 in
26.5s. On feat/ai-assistant the same file fails at its first case and the rest
of the file is skipped by the serial cascade. So the usual "the container's
failure set is not CI's" reading does not apply here — the container is
demonstrably capable of running these specs.

## It is not the merge with main either

`e2e/agent-answer-stream.spec.ts` fails IDENTICALLY on 21ac673e (the branch head
before origin/main was merged in) and on the merged tree — same assertion, same
"failed" chip. The merge is not the cause; this predates it.

## The measurement

    PW_PROJECTS=chromium ./e2e/run-in-container.sh <the nine assistant specs>
    → 8 failed, 2 passed, 6 skipped by cascade (3.9m)

    FAIL agent-answer-stream.spec.ts:156   the turn's chip reads "failed"
    FAIL agent-ask.spec.ts:284             .nocx-editor-reference-chip never appears
    FAIL agent-policy.spec.ts:242          (30.5s timeout)
    FAIL agent-reads-the-screen.spec.ts:320 (37.5s timeout)
    FAIL agent-restore.spec.ts:270         (16.0s)
    FAIL agent-tool-approval.spec.ts:153   the approval prompt never becomes visible (3.7s)
    FAIL agent-turn.spec.ts:329            the turn's chip reads "failed"
    FAIL ask-about-a-running-command.spec.ts:296 (34.6s)
    PASS assistant-readiness.spec.ts (both cases)

Two symptoms, not eight. FOUR specs fail because the turn terminalizes as
`failed` rather than `completed` — the chip is read 56 to 63 times over 30
seconds and never changes. TWO fail because a surface that should appear does
not: the editor's reference chip, and the approval prompt.

## What the backend says, which is the puzzle

Nothing. `test-results/devharness/devharness-auto.log` for the agent-turn run
shows the vault initialising, the secret created and retrieved three times, two
sessions opening cleanly — and not one ERROR or WARN. The run fails without the
backend logging a reason, which is itself worth fixing: AGENTS.md says a soft
degrade must be visible in the product, and a turn that dies silently is the
same defect one level down.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `PW_PROJECTS=chromium ./e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/agent-turn.spec.ts`
2. Observe the answer block's `.cmd-header-exit` chip reading `failed`.
3. For the contrast that proves it is not the environment:
   `git archive origin/main | tar -x -C /tmp/mainbase` then
   `cd /tmp/mainbase && PW_PROJECTS=chromium ./e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts`
   → 6 passed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All nine assistant specs pass in the container, on the merged tree.
- The turn-terminalizes-as-failed cause is NAMED, not worked around by relaxing
  the assertion to accept `failed`.
- Whatever makes a run fail also LOGS why, so the next occurrence does not have
  to be diagnosed from a chip in a screenshot.
- The two missing-surface failures (reference chip, approval prompt) are each
  either the same cause or filed separately with their own evidence.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND for at least two of the eight, and CI named it independently.

`readScreen` IS NOT A REGISTERED TOOL. internal/agenttools/registry.go holds
five rows — files.read, session.list, session.read, run, git.status — and none
of them is readScreen. So:

  - agenttools.NewScreenReader has NO production caller (only
    internal/assistant/readscreen_test.go).
  - There is no narrowReadScreen beside narrowSession and narrowRun, so nothing
    ever mints a *ScreenReader.
  - policyMiddleware.executeInRenderer type-switches on *agenttools.ScreenReader
    for readScreen — a branch nothing can reach — and its default arm returns
    `capability is %T, not a renderer-executable capability`.

That is the ContentDB.Add shape AGENTS.md rule 2 records, with the same tell: a
full implementation, its own tests, and a COMMITTED CONTRACT
(contracts/agent.readScreenRequest.schema.json, agent.readScreenResolved) for a
path no user can reach. It plainly accounts for
agent-reads-the-screen.spec.ts:320 and agent-tool-approval.spec.ts:153 (which
scripts a readScreen proposal); whether it accounts for the four
turn-terminalizes-as-failed specs is NOT yet established and should be measured,
not assumed.

HOW IT GOT THIS FAR, which is the more useful half:

CI run 32872132780 failed ci-linux (no-secret-service) AND ci-mac with one line:

    DEADCODE RATCHET: 86 unreachable functions on linux/amd64 (89 baselined, 1 NEW):
      NEW: internal/agenttools/screen_reader.go: NewScreenReader

So the ratchet DOES catch this, and has been catching it — but nothing local
runs it. `node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs` is a step in ci.yml's backend and
ci-linux jobs and is NOT in scripts/ci-linux.sh, so `make ci-full` never runs
it despite AGENTS.md calling those scripts byte-for-byte their CI counterparts.
The only local runner is the pre-commit hook. Filed separately.

WHAT NOT TO DO: baselining NewScreenReader would turn the one gate that found
this into a gate that never will again. AGENTS.md's own words for this case —
"a silent degrade the UI contradicts is how a feature that does not exist
survives a release".

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

CORRECTION AND THE REAL CAUSE, 2026-08-25. The note above says readScreen was
never wired. That reading was wrong, and the owner supplied the missing fact:
readScreen was DELIBERATELY REMOVED and replaced by session.read
(nocx-2ryxf.1). It was not an unfinished feature; it was a finished
replacement that left three things behind.

1. DEAD CODE — fixed in bbe9a27f. agenttools.ScreenReader, its constructor,
   executeReadScreen and the arm of executeInRenderer that consumed one.
   Nothing could reach them once no registry row named readScreen. The
   deadcode ratchet now reports 85 unreachable, all baselined, none new.

2. SIX E2E SPECS STILL SCRIPT THE DELETED TOOL, and this is what makes eight
   proofs red. `grep -l "name: 'readScreen'" e2e/*.spec.ts` →
   agent-answer-stream, agent-policy (6 occurrences), agent-reads-the-screen,
   agent-tool-approval, agent-turn, ask-about-a-running-command. The fake model
   proposes a tool the registry does not have, the call fails, and the turn
   terminalizes as `failed` — which is exactly the symptom recorded above, and
   it accounts for six of the eight.

   MEASURED, not inferred: changing the scripted name to `session.read` in
   agent-answer-stream.spec.ts and re-running it in the container moves the
   failure from the 30s `failed`-chip timeout to a later assertion at 11.1s.
   The turn COMPLETES. That probe was reverted — it is one of six and the
   migration belongs with the fix — but it is the evidence for this diagnosis.

3. AND UNDERNEATH IT, A THIRD LAYER the rename does NOT fix. With the tool
   name corrected, agent-answer-stream then fails on
   `expect(.ui-tool-call).toHaveCount(1)` → received 0. There is no
   `.ui-tool-call` anywhere in frontend/src, and the spec's own comment cites
   `frontend/src/ui/tool-call-line.ts`, which does not exist either. What the
   renderer actually does for a call that opens no block is
   `createCommandBlock('tool', …)` (scrollback/blocks.ts:2441) — ADR-0040's
   "THE BLOCK IS THE ACCOUNT OF THIS CALL". So the spec asserts a DOM shape
   the design superseded.

WHAT THE FIX IS, THEREFORE: not a rename. Each of the six specs has to be
re-read against ADR-0040 and against session.read's actual arguments
(`sessionId` plus `start`/`count`, not `region:{start,end}`), and re-asserted
on the tool-kind command block. That is nocx-shxv0's and nocx-2ryxf.1's
territory, not a mechanical sweep.

CI AGREES, INDEPENDENTLY. Run 32872132780 — the first CI run this branch has
ever had, every earlier one reports `skipped` because the PR was a draft —
failed ci-e2e on BOTH chromium and webkit. So this is not the container-only
class AGENTS.md warns about; the runner sees it too.

The two remaining failures are NOT explained by any of the above and still
need their own diagnosis: agent-ask.spec.ts:284 (.nocx-editor-reference-chip
never appears) and agent-restore.spec.ts:270.

CI'S FAILING SET IS EXACTLY THESE EIGHT, 2026-08-25. Run 32874289674,
ci-e2e (chromium), feat/ai-assistant at bbe9a27f:

  agent-answer-stream  agent-ask  agent-policy  agent-reads-the-screen
  agent-restore  agent-tool-approval  agent-turn  ask-about-a-running-command

and NO OTHER SPEC IN THE SUITE FAILS. Two things follow. The set matches the
container run case for case, so the container was telling the truth. And since
the tree under test is origin/main merged into this branch, a merge that had
broken something would have shown up somewhere outside the assistant — nothing
did, so the merge is clear and this bead is the whole of what is red.
close_reason: Every assistant proof is green on the runner (CI 32883305438, ci-e2e chromium and webkit both pass) and in the container (409 passed; the 8 local reds are the documented known-red set plus two webkit container-viewport layout specs, none of them assistant). Two causes, both named rather than worked around: six specs scripted readScreen, a tool nocx-2ryxf.1 deleted — a name the registry does not hold is refused as malformed model output, which is why the turn terminalized as failed — and the .ui-tool-call assertions named a class that never existed, superseded by ADR-0040's tool child. agent-restore's missing badge was a PRODUCT defect, not a spec one: lifecycle.submitAttempt stamped every ledger row source=user and history.record's close never rewrites the column, so the assistant's own command was stored as the person's; the submit now carries the author, required with no default. agent-ask's chip was nocx-wcswn's grant replacing the reference chip. Commits ecc1345d, f3c1c353.

title: An agent launched in a nocx pane is enrolled, and the interval has both ends
description:
An agent launched in a nocx pane must be ENROLLED before anything can say what it is
doing, and today nothing enrols anything: `panegrid.Store.Enrol` has no caller outside
its own tests. The grid landed in nocx-szb40.2 as a write path, and this is the act that
opens the interval.

## What this crosses, and what those documents already decided

The AD-6 amendment (docs/architecture.md, nocx-szb40.2) permits the backend to keep a
grid under two constraints, and the first is THE INTERVAL: a grid exists only between an
explicit Enrol and the matching Withdraw, and enrolment is an ACT — a control-plane call
naming a pane — "never an inference that a pane's title looked like an agent, because an
inferred set has no upper bound and no audit". So `detectAgentStatus` may not enrol, and
neither may anything else that reads the title.

The orchestration design's §7.1 (D5) decides the act: nocx defines an alias in the panel
session it already composes — NO rc file is edited — the wrapper resolves the per-agent
adapter, requests enrolment, has it PINNED TO ITS OWN PID, and `exec`s the real agent,
because `exec` preserves the pid so the pin survives and the wrapper does not. If
enrolment cannot be established it REFUSES VISIBLY (D4: failure is closed, no enrolment,
no orchestration, "and the pane says so"). A bare `claude` typed outside a nocx panel
session stays an ordinary agent and is marked as not orchestrated.

THE CHANNEL ALREADY EXISTS AND MUST NOT BE REBUILT. §7.1 says "the private local socket",
which reads as a new transport and is not one: ADR-0024 decision 2 and
docs/lifecycle-protocol.md already ship an authenticated channel that is not the tty —
local through a descriptor handed over at spawn (`NOCX_LIFECYCLE_FD`), remote through a
loopback port on the pooled SSH connection. Enrolment is an event on that channel. The
consequence is not cosmetic: the per-epoch capability is "substituted into the
integration script text, never passed as an environment variable", so the wrapper has to
be a function INSIDE the bundle that already holds it, not a separate binary reading an
env var. A second socket would also be a second authenticator, which is the second-owner
defect AGENTS.md names.

Config staging (tool surface, hooks) is §7.1 step 4 and is NOT here — it is what the
dispatcher needs, and the dispatcher is nocx-dkawo. This task is enrolment only.

## Why this exists as its own bead

nocx-szb40.3 was written to carry both the classifier and the act that makes it
reachable. It cannot: the classification has exactly ONE consumer, the indicator of
nocx-szb40.4, and a driver landed without it is a package called only by its own tests —
`deadcode`'s RTA cannot report a dead method behind a live interface, so the gate would
say green about a feature that does not exist, which is nocx-rtg0's failure exactly.
Enrolment, by contrast, is whole on its own and visible on its own.
acceptance_criteria:
Launching the agent through the nocx pane wrapper enrols that pane: the backend holds a grid for it, and holds none for a pane where the same agent was started by hand outside a nocx panel session.
Ending the agent closes the interval: the grid is gone after the process exits, and gone after the session ends, with no path that leaves one open.
Enrolment that cannot be established refuses visibly rather than degrading in silence: the pane says it is not orchestrated.
The enrolment event travels on the ADR-0024 channel and introduces no second transport and no second authenticator.
close_reason:
The enrolment act ships: agent_enrol/agent_withdraw on the ADR-0024 channel, an agent wrapper in both shell tiers, and the composition root's paneEnroller opening the grid. Commits 52b3719a and f4a6bed2.

Three of four acceptance criteria are asserted end to end; the fourth is structural and documented. What is NOT asserted is the wrapper's no-channel branch, filed as its own bead rather than left as prose.

The bead's second criterion turned out to be false when it was written: the interval had no second end at all, because szb40.2 hung the withdrawal off sess.StartOutput believing it blocks. It does not. Writing the test for the END rather than the start found it.

title: Watch it work: a running block is marked, named in the prompt, and read by its id
description:
Parent: nocx-a240p. Its three children are closed and its success criterion is not yet proven, so the epic stays open until this lands.

The criterion: a person runs a command, marks its block while it is STILL RUNNING, asks a question, and the model reads that block through session.read using the id it was given in the prompt - no guessing, no session.list search, no id invented by either side.

What is already asserted elsewhere, and must not be rebuilt here: the renderer puts the attempt id on the block and a grant names it (frontend tests, nocx-1025c); the ask carries the grant list and the prompt names each item (nocx-p4f7r).

What is NOT asserted anywhere is the thing this epic exists for: that a RUNNING block is addressable and readable at all. Before this epic no ledger row existed for a running command, so there was nothing to name. That is the seam to prove, and it is a backend check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One test, over the real transport: a command is submitted and is still running; an ask arrives naming that blocks id in attachedContent; the model calls session.read with that id; the read returns that blocks content and reports it as running.
- The id in the prompt and the id the tool accepts are the SAME string, asserted by reading both rather than by construction.
- The command then completes, and a second read of the SAME id returns the finished output with its exit code. One id across the whole life of the block is the epic thesis; assert both ends of that interval.
- A read of an id the person never marked is not silently served differently - state what happens today and assert it, so nocx-hnh7r has a baseline to change.
- The test is falsifiable: break the id chain deliberately once, confirm it goes red, put it back, and report what you changed.
close_reason: merged; running read and completed read on the same id taken from the prompt, unmarked-id baseline recorded, falsifiability shown
