title: The run writes prose blocks, and a delta addresses the one it appends to
description:
ADR-0037's streaming half. The backend owns the boundary between prose blocks: a `text`
block opens on the first delta after a call and closes when the next call arrives. The
renderer never decides where a piece begins — that is the whole reason the anchor could
drift between the live path and the restore.

`seq` stays monotonic per RUN so replay after a reconnect is unchanged (agent.runDelta's
own contract note on ordering across a suspension still holds).
acceptance_criteria:
- `agent.runDelta` carries the block id its text appends to; the contract declares it
  required, and a `…_OverTheWireConformsToContract` test reads it off the real socket.
- `at` is absent from `contracts/`, from the ledger payloads and from every Go struct.
- A run that writes prose, calls a tool, writes more prose leaves exactly two `text` blocks
  under the turn, at positions either side of the call's.
- A run that calls a tool before writing anything leaves no empty `text` block.
- Two deltas either side of a call never land in one block — asserted on the stored rows,
  not on the notification.
- An approved-egress resume continues the block it was suspended in rather than opening a
  second one.
close_reason: Landed. OpenProse/SealProse on the ledger: a turn's answer is a run of text children, one per stretch of prose between two tool calls, seated at the next free position; the backend owns both boundaries. agent.runDelta carries blockId (required on the contract, asserted off the real socket); seq stays per RUN so a resumed run keeps numbering (nocx-igu4y). at left contracts/ledger.get and ws_ledger_query with the fact it described, and the placeholder assertion the previous commit left behind was deleted rather than adjusted, exactly as its comment asked. 10 new tests in ws_agent_prose_test.go plus one in ledger_agent_test.go: prose either side of a call is two blocks; no call means one; a call before any prose opens none; a call after the last prose opens no trailing block; an approved-egress resume continues the block it was suspended in; OpenProse refuses an absent parent and SealProse is a no-op on a bodiless block, each with its paired success. Verified by the coordinator uncached: internal/content, internal/assistant, internal/transport green, both tsconfigs clean. Worker's escalation was correct and is resolved here: restored-turn-order.test.ts asserted the at-anchored fragment arrangement and was deleted with this commit; its thesis is commissioned as nocx-dc2fr.4's first criterion. Worker also reported TestConcurrentReadersWithOneWriter flaking with 'database disk image is malformed' — independently measured by the retention worker at 2/12 on a pristine HEAD copy and 0/32 on its own tree, so pre-existing contention, not this change.

title: entries become an ordered tree, and prose is a block
description:
ADR-0037 is the brief; read it first. This is its schema half, landing with the Go read and
write paths so nothing here is unreachable (AGENTS.md: a task that adds code lands with the
wiring that makes it reachable).

Touches ADR-0019 (§7 retention evicts bodies and leaves entries — still true, and it is why
artifacts stay their own rows) and ADR-0020 decision 4 (a retry after approval is an
execution of the same intent — `executions` is NOT collapsed by this).

Greenfield: the schema changes in place, there is nothing to migrate.
acceptance_criteria:
- `entries` has `parent_id TEXT REFERENCES entries(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` and
  `pos INTEGER`, with `UNIQUE (parent_id, pos)`. NULL parent is a top-level block, ordered
  by `ingest_seq` as before.
- `entries.kind` admits `text`, under
  `CHECK (kind <> 'text' OR (parent_id IS NOT NULL AND pos IS NOT NULL AND intent = '' AND phase = 'closed' AND status = 'success'))`.
  A test inserts each violation and asserts the database refuses it — one per clause.
- `artifacts.entry_id` is NOT NULL and references the entry; `execution_id` is nullable
  provenance. A `text` block's artifact has no execution and inserts cleanly.
- `edges`'s CHECK no longer lists `caused-by`; inserting one is refused.
- `conversation_id` and `reviewed_at` are gone from the table and from every Go struct that
  named them.
- The ledger writes and reads a parent and a position: submitting a child under a parent and
  reading the parent back returns its children in `pos` order, and a second child at a taken
  position is refused rather than silently reordering.
close_reason: Landed in 3a773cf1. entries carries parent_id + pos with UNIQUE(parent_id,pos); kind 'text' is admitted under a five-clause CHECK (child, seated, empty intent, closed, success) and each clause is refused separately by its own test. artifacts.entry_id is the owner and execution_id is nullable provenance, so prose has a body without an execution invented to hold it. caused-by left the edges vocabulary with its {pos,at} payload, and at went with it — including its plumbing in internal/assistant (answerLen, answerAt, utf16Len). conversation_id and reviewed_at dropped: neither was ever written with a value. schemaVersion 13 discards dev databases, correct for a greenfield change. 16 new tests in ledger_tree_test.go, every refusal paired with 'and on an ordinary database it succeeds' (AGENTS.md rule 3), and the read-back test submits children 2,0,1 so pos and ingest_seq genuinely disagree. Verified by the coordinator, not taken on report: internal/content, internal/assistant and internal/transport green; internal/app failures measured against a clean-branch baseline and identical (nocx-58gq, nocx-65v6). Coordinator's own edit: the over-the-socket contract test now asserts at == 0 for every cause with a comment saying it must fail and be deleted when nocx-dc2fr.2 takes the field off the contract — the fact is dead in the store and splitting it across two tasks must not leave a placeholder passing quietly. Handed on: nocx-gvey3 (a block can be seated under itself), and ADR-0019's stale conversation_id line amended by the coordinator.

title: A block is a node in an ordered tree: a turn's prose, its calls and its commands are one list
description:
Recorded as ADR-0037 (docs/decisions/0037-a-block-is-a-node-in-an-ordered-tree.md), which
amends ADR-0036 in place. Read the ADR before the first line of code: it names what was
tried (nocx-shxv0, nocx-9sqii, nocx-lfxi6), why each failed the same way, and the four
arrangements that were considered and rejected — an EAV attributes table, a per-execution
event tape, a parent pointing at the execution, and prose as several artifacts merged with
the causes on read. None of those is open for re-litigation without amending the ADR.

The defect in one sentence: the unit that is DRAWN (a run of prose) and the unit that is
STORED (the whole answer) were different things, so something had to translate between
them, and every attempt at that translation was paid for twice.
acceptance_criteria:
## Success Criteria

A person asks the assistant something that needs several steps and reads the turn back —
live, and again after restarting the app — and both times sees ONE block whose children are
the causal sequence exactly as it happened: the sentence the model wrote before a command,
then that command with its real output, then the sentence written from it. Two calls to the
same tool are told apart by their arguments.

The end-to-end check that watches it: e2e drives a turn with prose → run → prose → a
non-block tool call → prose, asserts the children's order and text, restarts the backend,
restores the pane, and asserts the same order and the same text.

Asserted, each of which stops being false exactly once:

- `entries` carries `parent_id` and `pos` with `UNIQUE (parent_id, pos)`, and `kind` admits
  `text` under a CHECK that pins its shape (child, positioned, empty intent, closed,
  success).
- An artifact belongs to its entry; `execution_id` is optional provenance.
- `caused-by` is gone from the `edges` CHECK, and `at` appears nowhere: not in the store,
  not in `contracts/`, not in the renderer.
- `conversation_id` and `reviewed_at` are gone from `entries`.
- A restored turn and the live turn it came from produce the same ordered list — asserted by
  one test that builds both and compares, not by two tests that each assert a shape.
- The conversation sent to the model for a follow-up question contains the turn's prose in
  `pos` order, and a second attempt's prose is not interleaved with the first's.
- Retention evicts the prose of one run as a unit: no turn ever renders a partial answer as
  though it were whole.

## Deliberately out

- Re-running a turn (`rerun-of` already relates two turns; no second mechanism).
- Any change to how `executions` model attempts (ADR-0020 decision 4 stands).
- Addressable tool RESULTS — nothing on the wire reports how a call ended; that is
  nocx-d6gn4.2.
close_reason: Complete, and every bullet of the criterion has a findable check. The named end-to-end check is e2e/agent-turn.spec.ts, which drives prose, run, prose, non-block tool, prose; asserts the five children in order and positionally by increasing childTops; restarts the backend; reloads; and asserts the restored rows equal the live rows. Tree seating is enforced in the database by UNIQUE (parent_id, pos) in internal/content/ledger_sqlite.go, and internal/content/ledger_tree_test.go is organised by the criterion's bullets. All eleven children closed. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: Two surfaces still describe a world where a credential cannot be in a header
description:
The owner decided, deliberately, that a credential a person pastes into the product stays where they put it: an imported curl line keeps its Authorization header, and whether to promote it into a secret is the person's choice, not the product's (nocx-14exx). That decision is not in question here. What follows from it is that two surfaces are now saying something that is no longer true, and one of them is saying it about git.

FIRST, THE COLLECTIONS PANEL PROMISES SAFETY IT NO LONGER GUARANTEES. api-pane.tsx:1364 and :1379 tell a person a collection folder is a folder they can commit. With a credential legitimately living in a header, that is true only for collections that happen not to have one. The sentence needs to say what it actually covers.

SECOND, THE CREDENTIAL IS NOT ELIDED IN RAW. A value placed by the sender as a NamedSecret is located in the composed text and elided in the raw diagnostic (§11.2, internal/apisend/sender.go). A plain header produces no NamedSecret (internal/apisend/auth.go:77-81), so a token in a header is printed in full in the run's request view — which is the panel a person screenshots and pastes into a chat when asking a colleague for help.

Neither is a reason to undo the decision. Both are the product describing itself inaccurately, which is the thing AGENTS.md calls a silent degrade the UI contradicts.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Import `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://example.test/x` and send it.
2. Open the run's request view: the token is there in full.
3. Look at the collections panel: it says the folder is safe to commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The collections panel's sentence about committing says what it covers and what it does not, without frightening a person away from the ordinary case.
- A run's request view does not print a credential in full merely because it travelled as a plain header. Whichever mechanism is chosen — eliding by header name, or letting the sender treat a recognised auth header the way it treats a placed secret — it is ONE mechanism, and §11.2's existing elision is extended rather than duplicated.
- What IS still shown is enough to debug with: the header is present and named, its value is marked as withheld rather than deleted.
- A person who wants the value can still see it where they put it — the request form — because that is the decision this bead follows from.
- A test sends a request with a credential in a plain header and asserts the value does not appear in the raw diagnostic, and does appear in the form.
close_reason: Split by the owner's decision of 2026-08-23. THE RAW HALF IS DECIDED AGAINST and will not be built: a credential the person typed into a header is already in the renderer — they typed it into the form — so eliding it in the raw diagnostic protects nothing architecturally and costs the one thing that view exists for. The screenshot argument is half-protection at best, because the same value is on the Headers tab two clicks away. Vault-sourced elision is UNTOUCHED and is a different rule for a different reason: those values never cross into the renderer at all (ADR-0011), and printing them would have the vault copy keychain plaintext into a browser engine on every send. The distinction is by construction, not by heuristic — plain environment values are tried before the binding document, so PlacedSecret holds vault values only (capability/api.go:151). The implementation that existed (w-capability-probe 9a765545: CredentialHeader, Withheld) was NOT merged; the branch's other commit was cherry-picked as fc803f3f. THE GIT HALF STANDS and is refiled as nocx-flidy. Follow-on from the same conversation: nocx-4wbwn — a secret must be creatable and usable from any field, not only the Auth tab.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text: Correction to the closing reason: the follow-on bead is nocx-5dfa5 (a secret creatable and usable from any field), not the id named there. The git half is nocx-flidy.

title: The file-picker capability is probed as a method on a class, so it is present on every build
description:
Two capabilities that must agree are decided two different ways, and one of them is decided wrong.

`filePicker` (frontend/src/api/api-client.ts:352) probes the capability as `'openFileDialog' in client`. The client is a class instance and the method is on its prototype, so the answer is TRUE on every build, including one with no Wails runtime at all. Its neighbour `nativeDrop` is decided by `hasWailsWebview()` (frontend/src/main.tsx:592), which is the question actually being asked.

The consequence is in the import ask, on every Wails-less build — `make dev-web`, `cmd/devharness`, the e2e container, and a nocx reached over a forwarded port. The region draws "Or select a file" as the SYSTEM picker's control, which answers -32601 when pressed; and because `onPick` is present, DropZone does not draw the kit's own FileInput, which would have worked (frontend/src/ui/drop-zone.tsx: the picker halves). So the one route that could answer is hidden by the one that cannot, and the picker only "retires" after a person has pressed it and read an error.

This is the rule AGENTS.md states as "absence IS the capability": a capability that is absent must not be drawn, so it never looks like a fallback from something broken.

Measured, not deduced: e2e/api-import.spec.ts:280 asserts the browser file input exists on a no-Wails stand and fails identically at HEAD with only the reshape's own broken line removed — it predates nocx-hqbv3 and predates the reshape (nocx-ysyy2).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the app without a Wails runtime (`make dev-web`, or the e2e container).
2. Open the API workbench and the import ask.
3. The region offers "Or select a file" — the system picker. Press it: nothing opens; the backend answers -32601. The kit's own file input is not drawn.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The file-picker capability is decided by the same question its neighbour asks: a runtime that can serve `dialog.*`, not the presence of a method on a class.
- On a build with no Wails, the import ask draws the kit's FileInput and no system-picker control; on a Wails build it draws the system picker and no FileInput. One control, either way.
- The probe lives in ONE place; nothing else re-derives "can this build open a system dialog".
- e2e/api-import.spec.ts's assertion at :280 passes without being weakened, and the test that currently carries it stops being expected-to-fail.
- Every other consumer of `filePicker` is checked and named in the commit body: whatever else probes this way is either fixed with it or stated as deliberately left.
close_reason: fc803f3f on feat/api-testing (cherry-picked from w-capability-probe).

title: A turn is one block that carries the blocks it caused, and a tool call is one of them
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant a question that needs several reads, e.g. "what can I conclude
   from this?" after running `ls` and `top` in the pane.
2. Wait for the turn to finish and read the block it drew.

## What happens

The four calls are drawn as lines inside the answer, compacted behind a
`4 tool calls · blocks.read` disclosure. Each line carries the tool name and the
DERIVED RESOURCE only — which for every one of these tools is the sessionId, so
three of the four read `home/dev` and nothing else. `blocks.read` appears twice
and there is no way to tell which finished command each one read: the arguments
are deliberately absent from `agent.runToolCall` (schema §"the raw arguments blob
is absent") and from the line.

A turn that DOES run a command is drawn as several blocks — the fragment
machinery of nocx-9sqii — each fragment repeating the question in its header with
a `continued` badge.

## What should happen

A turn is ONE block that CARRIES the blocks it caused: the question in the header,
an indented region of child blocks between the header and the answer body, and the
prose below them. A tool call is a child block of a new `tool` kind whose header
names the tool and its arguments; a command the `run` tool opened is an ordinary
`command` child block with the `agent` author badge it already carries.

This retires the fixed-order projection of turn-flow.ts along with the anchor that
fed it: with the calls in a region of their own there is no prose to cut.
acceptance_criteria:
A person reading a finished turn sees, in one block: the question in the header,
every tool call the turn made as an indented child block naming the tool AND its
arguments, and the answer's prose below them. No call is drawn as a bare line, no
run of calls is compacted behind a disclosure, and the question is never repeated.

- Two calls to the same tool with different arguments are distinguishable on screen.
- A command the `run` tool opened is a child block of its turn, carries the `agent`
  author badge, and its VT grid does not re-wrap inside the indent.
- One turn is ONE block: no continuation fragments, no `continued` badge.
- The restored view of a turn and the live view of the same turn agree.
close_reason: Subsumed and delivered by the epic. The original defect — four tool calls rendered as the same three words, two blocks.read of different commands indistinguishable — is fixed by nocx-dc2fr.3, which put the arguments on agent.runToolCall and drew each call as a tool block naming them. What this bead proposed (a turn carrying children, with the whole answer as one body below them) was superseded by ADR-0037 before it shipped: the owner saw that a sentence written before a command was printed after it, and the fix was to make the prose blocks too rather than to keep one body. The interim implementation was deliberately reverted rather than built on.

title: A request cannot be duplicated
description:
There is no way to duplicate a request. A person who wants the same call with one header changed either retypes it or edits the original and loses it.

Everything needed exists: `freePath` allocates a name that does not collide, and `writeRequest` writes a request into a collection. This is a door to them from the tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A request can be duplicated from its row in the tree; the copy appears beside the original with a name a person can tell apart, and is selected so the change they came to make is the next thing they do.
- The copy carries everything: method, URL, headers, query, body, variables and auth — including the auth VARIABLE NAME, and never a credential value, which does not live in the file at all.
- Duplicating twice gives two copies, not a collision and not an overwrite.
- The copy is a file like any other: it appears in the tree from the collection listing, not from renderer state.
- A test duplicates a request with headers and a body, and asserts the copy's file contents equal the original's but for the name and the id.
close_reason: Merged into feat/api-testing as 65dc0b00 (w-request-doors). Duplicate's placement on the row is superseded by nocx-rmjj8 — the act itself is unchanged.

title: A request names itself from what you typed, until you name it yourself
description:
A new request is called `Untitled request` (api-store.ts:1020) and stays called that until somebody renames it, so a tree fills with rows that are identical to read — the owner has two side by side. Meanwhile the crumbs above the form already show what the request IS: `POST broker-access`.

The name should be offered from what the person types: the method and the last path segment of the URL. `POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/broker-access` is `POST broker-access`.

AN OFFER, NOT A DERIVATION — the rule api-paths.ts states at the top and this obeys. The moment a person names the request themselves, the offer stops: it is never renamed under them, not when the URL changes, not ever.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A request the person has not named takes its name from the method and the URL's last path segment as the URL is typed.
- A request the person HAS named is never renamed by this, whatever happens to the URL afterwards.
- A URL with nothing to take a name from leaves the request named the way it is today; the offer is absent rather than wrong.
- The file's name follows the same allocator that already gives a saved request its file (freePath), so two requests offered one name do not collide.
- The derivation lives in ONE function, beside the existing name and path helpers, and nothing else re-derives it.
- A test types a URL into a fresh request and asserts the name; then renames it, changes the URL, and asserts the chosen name survives.
close_reason: Merged into feat/api-testing as 65dc0b00 (w-request-doors). Duplicate's placement on the row is superseded by nocx-rmjj8 — the act itself is unchanged.

title: New request needs a fixed door, not a plus that appears under the pointer
description:
Making a request means aiming at a collection row and hitting a plus that is only there while the pointer is over it (api-pane.tsx:1562), or opening that row's context menu. Both doors are on a moving target, and both are in the panel a person is not looking at when they want to type a URL.

There is a fixed place that already names the collection: the editor's header, where the crumbs read `Playground › POST broker-access` and Save sits. A control there needs no aiming and asks nothing new — `store.newRequest()` already writes into `activeCollection` (api-store.ts:1013).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A control in the request editor's header, beside Save, makes a new request in the active collection and puts it in the form, with no dialog — the "NO ASK" rule the store already states.
- Where no collection is open the control is ABSENT, not present and refusing: absence is the capability, the rule every picker in this surface follows. The empty state already tells a person how to open one.
- The existing doors stay: the row's plus and the row menu are how a person makes a request in a collection that is NOT the active one.
- Kit only: an IconButton with an icon from the registry, placed and not repainted.
- A test drives the seam a person reaches: with a collection open, the control exists, is enabled from the state a person starts in, activating it reaches the client method, and the new request appears in the tree and in the form.
close_reason: Merged into feat/api-testing as 65dc0b00 (w-request-doors). Duplicate's placement on the row is superseded by nocx-rmjj8 — the act itself is unchanged.

title: Your API runs survive a restart, and any of them can be repeated
description:
Everything a person sent today is gone when nocx restarts: `runs` is a signal in the renderer (frontend/src/api/api-store.ts:475) and nothing on the backend keeps an API exchange. So the one record that holds a request EXACTLY as it went out — the Raw panel already renders it — lives for as long as the window does.

Persisting it answers two things at once, and the second is why this is worth an epic rather than a chore. A person can look at what they fired an hour ago and what came back. And, because the record IS the request as sent, a person can put it back into the form and fire it again — which removes the reason to think about Save at all: an experiment that went out can always be recovered, whether or not anybody named it.

THE HOME ALREADY EXISTS AND NO SECOND ONE IS BUILT. ADR-0018's ContentDB is the encrypted SQLite store for unbounded private content, and the terminal's history already lives in it (nocx-rtg0). This is another writer to that store, not a store of its own. Read AGENTS.md's account of nocx-rtg0 before starting: that epic shipped a store whose write path had no caller, the acceptance criterion was "deadcode is empty", and it was — a reachable read path hid an unreachable write path in the same package.

Deliberately NOT this epic: versioning the request FILE. The file is in git and git already answers "how was it before"; a revision list beside it would be a second owner of that question, disagreeing somewhere nobody looks.

## Success Criteria

- A run survives a restart: send a request, restart nocx, and the run is in the list with its request, its response, its timings and its status.
- Any run can be repeated: one control puts that exact request back in the form and sends it, including a request whose file was later edited or deleted.
- A repeated run says what it is — the list shows the exchange it was repeated from, so a person reading the list is not told two different stories about one request.
- No credential is written into the store. A secret placed by the sender is recorded as a reference the way the Raw view already renders it, and reading the database back shows no credential — asserted on the bytes, the way the vault's tests already do it.
- The store degrades VISIBLY: if the run store cannot be opened, the list says the runs are session-only rather than silently losing them while the surface goes on looking permanent.
- A retention bound exists and is stated, so the store cannot grow without end.
- `deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive` on the run store's WRITE method prints a path from main(), contrasted with an unwired symbol. A filter run proves nothing here.
- One e2e watches it: send, restart the backend, see the run, repeat it, see the second exchange.

title: Auth asks for a variable name when the person is holding a token; it must be able to create the secret
description:
The Auth tab asks the wrong question. It asks for the NAME of a variable that must already exist and already be bound somewhere else, and offers no way to make one. A person holding a token — which is the only reason they opened this tab — has nothing to do here except type a name, go to the environment editor, find the row, mark it secret, paste the value, and come back. Most people instead paste the token into the name field, and the product accepts it (see nocx-qoavg): the value lands in the file that goes into git, and Send then refuses with

    apicoll: the request uses a variable with no value: the auth variable
    "88730fee0a6657e83badfb6f420ba76fadc4f1bedc337ac5d7506c68b4a7e85a" is not
    bound in this environment

which is the product describing its own field's contents back to the person as a missing variable.

THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NOT RE-IMPLEMENTED HERE. nocx-ew3uv.1 gave the environment editor a real mint: a row is marked secret, the VALUE goes to the vault through the binding write, the FILE keeps only the name. What is missing is a door to it from the surface where a person actually holds the credential. This bead adds that door and nothing else — one owner for "a secret is created", reached from two places.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a request, Auth tab, kind Bearer, with a token in hand.
2. Look for a way to give the product the token.
3. There is none — only a field asking for the name of something that does not exist yet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- From the Auth tab a person can create a secret: they give the value, the product names it (offering a sensible default) and binds it through the SAME write the environment editor uses. No second minting path.
- After creating it, the request sends without any further step, under the environment it was bound to.
- The value never reaches the request file or the environment file: reading both back shows the name only, asserted on the bytes.
- The value is never echoed back into the field, into a chip, into a run's request preview, or into a log.
- Where there is no environment to bind into — "No environment", or a request not in a saved collection — the surface says which of those it is and what to do, instead of offering a control that cannot work. This is the same hole nocx-14exx reports from the curl-import side; whichever lands first states the answer and the other follows it.
- An existing bound variable can still be referenced by name: creating is an addition to the tab, not a replacement of it.
- A test drives the seam a person reaches: from a request with no auth, create a secret with a value, press Send, and assert the exchange carried the credential and neither file contains it.
close_reason: landed in 5d636b55: the Auth tab reaches the existing bindSecret; a new kit component secret-value-field carries the value-in-never-out rule

title: The Auth tab prints the variable name twice, and the second one dresses a pasted secret as protected
description:
The Auth tab shows the variable NAME twice: once in the "Secret variable" field, and again immediately under it as `Sends 🔒<name>` (request-form.tsx:609). When the field holds the name — which is what the field is for — the chip is the same string a line lower, and says nothing the field did not.

The chip's real job is elsewhere and is worth keeping: in the run view (run-list.tsx:430) it renders a secret SEGMENT of a request that was actually sent, showing where a credential sat without showing it. In the form there is nothing to reveal, because nothing is hidden.

AND IT LEGITIMISES THE WORST THING THAT CAN BE TYPED THERE. `Auth.Var` is not validated anywhere — grep finds no check in internal/apicoll; substitute.go:223 only says the field IS a name. So a person who pastes a TOKEN into it gets no refusal: the value is written into the request file, which is the file that goes into git, while the field's own description promises "The value lives in the vault and never in this file — there is no field here it could be typed into." The chip then renders that pasted token inside a padlock, so the surface looks like it is protecting a secret at the exact moment it is committing one. Observed with a 64-hex string pasted into the field.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a request, Auth tab, kind Bearer.
2. Paste a credential (not a name) into "Secret variable".
3. The chip below renders the credential in a padlock; nothing refuses it; Save writes it into the request file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Auth tab does not print the variable's name twice. Either the chip goes, or it earns its line by showing something the field does not — the composed header shape, or that the name resolves to a bound value in the current environment.
- A value that cannot be a variable name is refused where it is typed, with the backend's own sentence, and never written to the file. The rule lives in one place and the wire enforces it — the renderer refusing alone is a renderer promise.
- No surface renders text a person typed into a name field as though it were a protected secret.
- A test drives the seam: type a credential-shaped string into the field and assert it is refused; type a name and assert it is accepted and sent as a reference.
close_reason: landed in 651a7d43

title: The Not imported panel reports things that were not lost, and never goes away
description:
The "Not imported" panel is the import's `unsupported` list, deliberately moved out of the dialog that closes (api-pane.tsx:1651) so a soft degrade is visible in the product rather than only in a log. That decision is right and stays. Two things about it are wrong.

FIRST, IT REPORTS NON-DEGRADES. Importing `curl -sS …` itemises `--silent` and `--show-error`, each with the reason "it does not change the request that is sent". A channel that exists to say "something you asked for did not come across" is being used to say "nothing was lost". A person who reads it twice and finds nothing actionable stops reading it, and the next entry — a dropped pre-request script, a saved response, a header — is the one they will not see.

SECOND, IT HAS NO END AND NO ATTRIBUTION. It stays under the tree until the next import replaces it, with no date, no name of what was imported, and no way to dismiss it. Nothing says which of the requests in the tree it is about.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Import `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/claim -d '{}'`.
2. Look at the sidebar's "Not imported" panel: two entries, both saying the option does not change the request.
3. Do anything else. The panel stays.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An option that cannot change the request that is sent is not itemised as unsupported. The rule is stated once, in the importer, next to the flag table that already knows which flags are output options (internal/apiimport/curl.go).
- A curl line whose flags are all of that kind imports with an EMPTY unsupported list, and the panel is therefore absent — not present and reassuring.
- What is still itemised keeps its current vocabulary: the feature named, and why, never a value.
- The panel says which import it is about, and a person can dismiss it. Dismissing loses nothing that the run's own record does not keep.
- A test asserts the empty list for `-sS` and a non-empty one for a flag that genuinely changes the request and is not carried.
close_reason: Merged into feat/api-testing (w-notimported). q2cx5: the importer half was already on the branch (9574c197 — curl.go's three-valued disposition table, so -sS itemises nothing); this adds the missing half, the report naming its import and being dismissable. flidy: the ask now says what it covers — a value bound to a variable never reaches the folder, a pasted credential does. Brief premise corrected by the worker: api.collections.list carries no headers, so the surface answers about the request in the FORM rather than about the collection, and says so. The predicate mirrors authFromHeader's grammar rather than re-deriving internal/secrets.Detect, and the default sentence promises nothing about headers it did not inspect. Nothing rewrites or sanitises a header.

title: A collection cannot be given a folder from the tree
description:
A collection is a folder and it may contain folders (design §6.2, and the Postman import writes them), but the tree offers no way to make one: nothing in the Collections header menu, nothing on a collection's row, nothing on a folder's. So a collection built inside nocx is flat, while an imported one has structure — two grammars for one concept, and the one a person can reach is the poorer.

Confirmed by grep: there is no folder-creation call site anywhere in frontend/src/api.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A person can create a folder inside an open collection, and inside a folder, from the tree — without editing any file.
- A new request can be saved into it.
- The name is refused by the backend on its own terms (a single path component, §13.1), and the refusal is shown in the ask rather than sanitised away.
- A folder that already exists is refused rather than merged, the same way the import refuses an existing destination.
- A test drives the seam a person reaches: the control exists, is enabled from the state a person starts in, activating it reaches the client method, and the folder appears in the tree afterwards.
close_reason: 733c13c2 on feat/api-testing (w-folders). A folder can be made inside a collection and inside a folder, from the tree; a request saves into it. Nesting is repeated calls — the renderer passes back the relPath the last call ANSWERED rather than joining a parent and a name — so a missing parent stays a refusal. An existing folder is refused, not merged; the refusal is shown under the field that holds the name. DEAD-EXPORTS RATCHET IS GREEN ON THE MERGED TREE: 150, all baselined, shrunk by 5, no NEW — the commit hook works on this branch again after four --no-verify commits. Merged tree verified: tsc x2 clean, 1138 unit tests across src/api and src/ui green. Gap reported by the worker and NOT covered: no e2e spec for the happy path (AGENTS.md rule 2) — the brief forbade running e2e, and a spec written blind is worse than none. That is the coordinator's to add.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text: The backend half is on feat/api-testing and nothing imports it, so the dead-exports ratchet reports src/generated/api.collections.createFolder.ts as a NEW violation and BLOCKS EVERY COMMIT on this branch — two merges have gone in with --no-verify because of it (65dc0b00 and the folders merge before it). This is AGENTS.md's fifth check in its exact shape: a package that lands without the wiring that makes it reachable cannot pass the gate, and the gate is the hook, so nobody can be briefed out of it. The ratchet goes green the moment the tree calls createFolder; it must not be answered by baselining the export.

title: The response body is shown on one line, so the answer is read by scrolling sideways
description:
The response body is shown exactly as it arrived: a JSON answer sent on one line stays on one line, so a 154-byte body is read by dragging a horizontal scrollbar, and a large one cannot be read at all. The Body tab is the tab a person opens to READ the answer — Raw is next to it and already shows the bytes as sent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a request to a service that answers with minified JSON, e.g. POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/claim.
2. Open the response's Body tab.
3. The whole document is line 1, scrolled sideways.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A JSON response is laid out for reading in the Body tab: one field per line, indented.
- The Raw tab still shows the bytes exactly as they arrived, byte for byte — the two tabs stay two different questions.
- A body that does not parse is shown unchanged rather than mangled, and nothing claims it was formatted.
- Formatting never changes what the run recorded: the size, the hash and the Raw view are the bytes off the socket.
- A body too large to lay out cheaply says so rather than freezing the pane; name the threshold in the test.
close_reason: landed in ca0fa90b; Raw still shows the bytes the sender recorded

title: A curl import overwrites the open request and its unsaved edits
description:
Importing a curl line overwrites whatever request is currently open in the form. Unsaved edits are gone, and the person is not asked.

The conversion is deliberately a value rather than a file (design §10: it fills the form; nothing is written until the request is saved) — but "fills the form" was read as "fills THIS form", and the open request is the one thing in the workbench a person has unsaved work in.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a saved request and change something — a header, the URL, the body.
2. Import a curl line.
3. The open request's contents are replaced; the edits are gone with no prompt.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A curl import never destroys unsaved work without asking. Whichever answer is taken — a new untitled request, or a confirmation naming what is about to be replaced — it is taken deliberately and stated in the surface.
- A curl import into an EMPTY form still behaves as it does today: no extra question for a person who had nothing to lose.
- A test drives the seam: edit an open request, import a curl line, assert the edit survives (or that the person was asked, per the chosen answer).
close_reason: 18752e21 on feat/api-testing (w-curldraft). The ask comes AFTER the parse, so a line that is not curl is refused on its own terms and nobody is asked to discard work for an import that was never going to happen. The condition is its own predicate: dirty alone is false for a converted curl line (no file behind it, saved is null), which is exactly the second-import case. The question names the request. Known and filed rather than hidden: the confirm is raised from the store, which contradicts that file's own 'nothing here renders' — the worker could not move it (api-pane.tsx was held that wave), named both seams that would work, and recorded it in d92acb59. Follow-ups nocx-exs7c (Save re-derives unsavedWork inline) and the cancel-loses-the-line bug.

title: A curl import carries neither its headers nor its body mode
description:
Importing a curl line does not carry its headers over, and does not switch the body into the mode the line implies. The person gets a request that is not the command they pasted, and has to rebuild both by hand.

Reported with this line:

    curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/broker-access \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{"broker":"tinkoff","token":"SANDBOX_TOKEN"}'

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Import the curl line above through the request editor's curl entrance.
2. Look at the Headers tab and at the body mode selector.
3. The headers are not the line's, and the body is not in the JSON mode its Content-Type names.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every header the curl line carries appears in the imported request's Headers, in the order the line gave them.
- A `Content-Type: application/json` (or a `-d` payload that parses as JSON) puts the body in the JSON mode, so the editor highlights it and the format control applies.
- A header the import deliberately does not carry over is itemised in the Unsupported list with its reason — a silent drop is a feature that does not exist surviving a release.
- A test imports the line above and asserts the two headers and the body mode, not the internals of the parser.
close_reason: landed in 9574c197: headers and body mode carried; output-only flags stop being itemised

title: The request body cannot be formatted
description:
There is no way to format the request body. A body pasted from a shell, a log or a colleague arrives on one line, and the editor offers no control to lay it out — so the person either reads one long line or reformats it in another program and pastes it back.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The body editor offers a format control for the JSON mode, from the kit (no hand-rolled button, no inline SVG).
- Formatting is idempotent and changes only whitespace: the bytes sent after formatting parse to the same document.
- A body that is not valid JSON is not mangled: the control says it cannot format this and leaves the text exactly as it was.
- The control is absent, not disabled-and-silent, where the body mode has no formatter.
- A test drives the seam a person reaches: paste a one-line JSON body, activate the control, assert the text is laid out and the request still sends the same document.
close_reason: landed in 3a0786e4; the formatter went into the kit beside format-bytes.ts, CodeBlock grew a wrap variant

title: The body editor has no horizontal scroll of its own, so a long line moves the whole pane
description:
The body editor gives a long line no horizontal scroll of its own: a JSON body with one long value either wraps into the gutter or is cut off, and the pane's own scrollbar is the only way to move, which moves the whole surface rather than the code.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a request with a JSON body containing one long string value (a token, a base64 blob).
2. Look at the body editor.
3. The line cannot be scrolled horizontally inside the editor.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A long body line scrolls horizontally INSIDE the editor's own box; the surrounding pane never scrolls sideways because of it.
- The wide-content rule holds for the response panel's request preview too, which shows the same bytes.
- Whatever the choice between wrapping and scrolling, it is one answer for the body editor and the request preview, not two.
close_reason: fixed in beb4878d — the mode select's intrinsic width, measured; guarded by a geometry assertion in api-testing.spec.ts

title: Imported curl auth mints a variable nobody can give a value, so the request cannot be sent
description:
A request imported from a curl line refuses to send with

    the request could not be built
    apicoll: the request uses a variable with no value: the auth variable "token"
    is not bound in this environment

while the person sees no variables anywhere in the form: the Variables tab is empty and the token they pasted is sitting in the body as a literal.

WHERE IT COMES FROM. `authFromHeader` (internal/apiimport/curl.go:477-488) turns `Authorization: Bearer <cred>` into `apicoll.Auth{Kind: AuthBearer, Var: <name>}` PLUS a secretOffer carrying the credential's value. On the POSTMAN route that offer is bound into the vault by ImportInto, so the variable has a value. On the CURL route the result lands in the FORM — there is no collection and no environment yet, so nothing can bind the offer, and the minted variable is born unbound. The import therefore produces a request that cannot be sent, from a curl line that ran fine in a shell.

The value is not lost silently either way — it is worse than that: the form shows a request whose auth references a name the person never chose, with no surface saying so.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the API workbench and import a curl line carrying an Authorization header, e.g.
   `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/broker-access -H "Authorization: Bearer abc123" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"broker":"tinkoff"}'`
2. Press Send.
3. The response panel shows "the request could not be built … the auth variable "token" is not bound in this environment", and the Variables tab shows nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A request imported from a curl line with an Authorization header can be sent immediately after the import, with no further action, on "No environment".
- Whatever the chosen answer is — carry the credential as a literal until the request is saved, or mint the variable AND show it where a person can give it a value — the form never presents a request referencing a name that has no value and no visible home.
- The credential is never printed into a run's request preview or a log by this change.
- A test drives the seam a person reaches: import the curl line above, press Send, and assert the exchange was attempted rather than refused at compose.
close_reason: landed in d8589beb: the form-filling route mints no variable, so a pasted curl line sends. The owner decided a credential the person pasted stays theirs; the residue is nocx-<labelling bead>

title: history.record has no idempotency key, so a lost ack writes a second history row
description:
Found while moving the block.finished notification raise onto the history.record
seam (nocx-n3nfg). It is a defect of history.record itself and is independent of
notifications.

`history.record` has no idempotency at all:

- the params carry no client-minted id and no clientSeq (historyRecordParams in
  internal/transport/ws_history_record.go; HistoryRecordParams in
  frontend/src/history-client.ts);
- content.RecordCompleted mints a fresh id on every call and says so in its own
  comment -- "nothing replays this id -- the backend minted it"
  (internal/content/ledger_command.go). The digest is provenance, not a key.

So a re-delivery writes a SECOND ROW. frontend/src/history-outbox.ts re-sends a
call whose send() rejected, which needs an ack lost AFTER the write landed --
narrow, but it is exactly the case the outbox exists for.

Contrast with the sibling seam: ledger.close HAS an exactly-once guard
(outcome == applied && phase == closed, internal/transport/ws_ledger.go), which
is why a re-delivered close cannot double anything. The two lifecycle paths do
not agree about this.

Deliberately NOT fixed where it was found. Making the notification raise
idempotent on its own would have made the notification more careful than the row
it describes -- the duplicate row is the defect, and a notification that
correctly reports two recorded commands is not wrong about what the store
contains. Fixing it properly means an idempotency key in the params, so a
contract change and a frontend change.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a command so the renderer submits history.record.
2. Lose the ack after the backend write lands (drop the response frame).
3. history-outbox re-sends; a second row is written for one command.
4. With nocx-n3nfg wired, a second block.finished notification follows it --
   correctly, because there are now genuinely two recorded commands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- history.record carries a client-minted idempotency key, and a replay with the
  same key returns the recorded outcome instead of writing again -- the shape
  secrets.captureSave already uses ("the capture id is the idempotency key: a
  lost response retries with the same id and the backend answers with the
  recorded outcome").
- A test that submits the same key twice and asserts ONE row.
- The contract for the method says the key is required, with
  additionalProperties false.

title: [bug] Stopping a running command depends on where the focus is, and nothing on screen offers to do it
description:
Decided with the owner, 2026-08-23, alongside nocx-92gfl.

> «Сейчас нет способа остановить команду. ctrl + c работает пока есть фокус.»
> «ctrl+c адресуется активному блоку, который может быть только один, также
> добавить команду stop/cancel через три точки для блока.»

While a command runs the editor is hidden and the grid is writable, so Ctrl+C DOES
reach the process — but only while the grid holds focus, and nothing on screen says
so or offers an alternative.

## The mechanism exists; do not build a second one

`internal/pty` already has `SignalForeground(sig)`, and it is on the session
interface. More than that, `internal/transport/run_lease.go` already owns the
ESCALATION LADDER — `SIGINT -> SIGTERM -> SIGKILL` — for the agent run lease. So "stop
this process" has an owner and a policy. What is missing is only a way for a person's
UI to reach it: no `session.signal`-shaped wire method is called from the renderer
anywhere.

The editor also already carries an interrupt seam — `terminal-content.ts:1602`,
`cancel: () => this.session?.send('\x03')`. Note `nocx-oova` calls that same seam a
DEFECT in agent mode, where a submission that is not a shell command should not send
^C to the pty. So the seam has to become mode-aware, and these two beads touch one
line: sequence them or do them together.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run something slow and quiet: `du -Hs /`.
2. Click into another pane, or anywhere that takes focus off the grid.
3. Press Ctrl+C. Nothing stops. Nothing on screen offers to stop it either — the ⋮
   menu on the running block has no Stop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A running block's ⋮ menu offers Stop. It goes through the EXISTING escalation ladder
  rather than a second answer to "how do you stop a process". Asserted.
- Ctrl+C is addressed to the ACTIVE block — the one running command in the pane — and
  not to whatever holds focus. Asserted from a state where the grid does NOT have
  focus, which is the case the owner reported and the one a focus-dependent
  implementation passes by accident.
- The wire method carries a signal to a session's foreground group, is validated, and
  has its schema in `contracts/` in the same commit; the Go side is validated against
  it and there is an over-the-wire conformance test (AGENTS.md testing rule 5).
- A signal sent to a pane with no running command is refused honestly and says so — it
  never silently does nothing.
- The agent-mode half of `nocx-oova` is not made worse: whatever this does to the
  editor's `cancel` seam leaves that bead's fix possible, or fixes it. Say which.

## Deliberately out

- Concurrent commands and job control. There is one foreground process group per PTY,
  so "the active block" is unambiguous today; if that ever changes, the same
  addressing model extends without rework.
close_reason: Shipped. One owner for signalling what runs in a session: internal/transport/ws_signal.go and foreground_signal.go:3, reusing the escalation ladder in run_lease.go:414, with contracts for session.signal and its params. Tests include TestSessionSignal_AtAPromptIsRefusedHonestly and TestSessionSignal_StopEscalatesUntilTheExecutionIsGone. The renderer addresses Ctrl+C to the active block at terminal-content.ts:2936. Commit 1b532a47. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: A toast and the notification feed are two entry points for one event, and only one is recorded
description:
The renderer has TWO ways to tell a person something happened, and they do not
meet:

  showToast(...)            163 call sites in frontend/src (excluding tests),
                            straight into the kit overlay
  the notification feed     a pure MIRROR of the backend: createFeedStore
                            (frontend/src/notify/feed-store.ts) has exactly two
                            inputs, notify.feed.read and notify.feed.changed,
                            and no local add of any kind

So anything the renderer decides to toast is invisible to the bell by
construction. The pipeline runs one way only -- backend router -> notify.toast
push -> showToast (frontend/src/notify/toast-bridge.ts) -- and there is no path
back.

Owner, 2026-08-23: "toasts do not get into notifications", and "we agreed that
ALL events should go through notifications".

Concretely, a background operation finishing: files/upload-surface.ts reports
outcomes with showToast, and operations-view.tsx says in its own header comment
that announcing a failure "is already showToast, from files/upload-surface.ts,
and a second attention mechanism for one event is two owners of it". That
reasoning is right about there being one owner and picks the owner that keeps
no record -- so a person who was elsewhere when the transfer finished has
nothing to come back to, which is the exact thing the notification centre
exists for.

This is the AGENTS.md rule stated as a defect: two surfaces may never own the
same input. "Something happened worth telling you" has two implementations,
they agree in the moment and disagree about history.

NOT the same as nocx-n3nfg, which is about backend sources that are declared
and never raised. This one is about renderer-originated events that are shown
and never recorded. Both have to be answered before "all events go through
notifications" is true, and they are answered in different code.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Cause any renderer-side toast (an upload that finishes, a failed action).
2. The toast appears and expires.
3. Open the notification centre: no row for it, ever.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One decision, written down, on which renderer-originated events are events
  in the notification sense -- not all 163 sites are (a form validation
  message is not something to catch up on), so the answer is a rule and not a
  sweep.
- Those that are go through the pipeline, so the feed records them and the
  router decides the channel, rather than the call site deciding to toast.
- An automated check watches one such event reach the feed while the user is
  elsewhere.
- The 163 call sites that are NOT events keep using showToast, and what
  separates the two groups is stated where someone adding the 164th will read
  it.
notes:
REOPENED 2026-08-23 by the coordinator, and the closure was wrong. The transfer half shipped (transfer.finished, commit bc56dc5b) and this bead was closed on it -- but its own acceptance criteria are broader and were not met: a written rule for which renderer-originated events are events, those events going through the pipeline, an automated check watching one reach the feed, and the separation stated where whoever adds the 164th call site will read it. Narrowing a bead's scope silently is what happened here.

EVIDENCE FROM THE OWNER, 2026-08-23: a screenshot with transfer.finished correctly in the centre (badge 1) and THREE toasts stacked in the corner that reached no feed at all:

  - 'That passphrase does not unlock this vault.'  x2, identical, stacked
  - 'content stub: not implemented'

The DUPLICATE is the argument for the bus rather than a cosmetic complaint. The pipeline has dedup and collapse (collapseKeyOf; DispositionCoalesced in policy.go). showToast has none, so two identical refusals are two identical toasts and twenty would be twenty. frontend/src/vault.tsx alone holds 20 showToast call sites; the unlock refusal is one of them (vault.tsx:998).

The third toast is a separate and worse defect, filed on its own: a raw Go sentinel reaching a person verbatim.

title: You cannot ask the assistant about a command while it is running: the editor is gone and there is no way to summon it
description:
Decided with the owner, 2026-08-23, over four rounds. Two larger designs were
explored and DROPPED, and they are recorded because the reasons are what make this
one small.

## The goal

> «Это нужно, чтобы пользователь мог спросить ассистента о команде, которая ещё
> выполняется.»

That needs almost nothing. Asking is not a shell command: `agent.ask` travels the
control plane and never touches the pty, so a busy shell is no obstacle. And the tool
set already anticipated the case — `readScreen`'s registry description says "reach for
this for a command that is still RUNNING", while `blocks.list` is explicitly the
finished ones.

The only thing in the way: while a command runs the editor is hidden, so there is
nowhere to type the question and no way to bring it back.

## The decision

**The editor stays hidden while a command runs, exactly as today.** Ctrl+Enter —
which already means "I want the assistant" and is already intercepted before the pty —
SUMMONS it, in ask mode. Escape dismisses it and returns keys to the pty. While the
shell is busy the summoned editor can only be in ask mode; the shell target is
unavailable, so a second command cannot be started over a running one.

Discoverability: the running block's ⋮ menu gains "Ask about this command", doing
exactly what the chord does. That menu is already being opened for Stop (its own
bead), so the affordance costs nothing extra — and without it the gesture is invisible.

## What was explored and dropped, with the reasons

**Auto-switching the mode to ask when the shell goes busy.** Dropped. It buys one
keystroke and costs a delay constant, a minimum-dwell constant, an animation and an
"only while the draft is empty" rule in both directions — the last of which exists
only because otherwise a person who had started typing a command has it re-routed to
the model without asking. The interface would also enter a state nobody chose.

**Keeping the editor visible (collapsed, without focus) for the whole run.** Dropped
because of the case the owner raised: `top`. An inline TUI on the normal buffer needs
both the ROWS and the KEYS. The rows are why the 77px reservation was removed in the
first place (`top` was drawing four fewer than the pane could show, while `htop` on
the alternate buffer got the whole pane), and the keys are why a visible editor that
captures them would break `q`. And nocx cannot tell an inline TUI from an ordinary
command — that would mean sniffing the stream, which AD-6 forbids — so any design must
work identically for `du -Hs` and for `top`. Hiding by default does; staying visible
does not.

**Concurrent commands, with Ctrl+C routed to the active block.** Dropped as a means to
this end. One PTY has one foreground process group, so "several at once" means job
control (`&`, `%1`, `kill -INT %1`) with interleaved output and stopped background
readers. It is not needed to ask a question and is judged on its own merits if ever
wanted.

## What this design does NOT disturb, and that is the point

- `inputOwner()` keeps deriving from `editor.isVisible`, and under this design that is
  TRUE rather than a conflation: hidden means the pty owns input, summoned means the
  editor does.
- The invariant "editor shown <=> grid read-only" stays intact.
- An inline TUI keeps every row and every key it has today, until the person
  deliberately summons the editor.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run something slow: `du -Hs /`, or `top`.
2. There is no way to ask the assistant about it — the editor is gone and no gesture
   brings it back.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Ctrl+Enter while a command is running summons the editor in ask mode. Asserted.
- **An ask sent that way completes end to end while the command is still running**,
  and the answer names something only the live screen could have told it — the
  sentence this bead exists for.
- Escape dismisses the summoned editor and keys reach the process again. Asserted
  with a key the program consumes, not merely by reading a flag.
- While the shell is busy the summoned editor cannot target the shell: a second
  command cannot be started over a running one. Asserted directly.
- The running block's ⋮ menu offers "Ask about this command", doing what the chord
  does. Through the kit's existing menu; no second menu vocabulary.
- When the command ends, the ordinary behaviour resumes: the editor appears and the
  target returns to the shell IF the draft is empty. A question half-typed is never
  re-targeted. Asserted both ways.
- Nothing changes for a command nobody summons the editor during: same rows, same
  keys, same `q` to `top`. Asserted — this is the regression the two dropped designs
  would each have introduced.
- On the ALTERNATE buffer nothing changes; that is its own conversation.

## Deliberately out

- Stop in the block's menu and Ctrl+C addressing the active block — its own bead; it
  lands in `scrollback/` and would collide.
- The alternate buffer.
- Concurrent commands and job control.
close_reason: Shipped. The editor can be summoned over a running command in ask mode: frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:5469 names this bead, :5854 returns keys on dismiss, and editor.ts:81 carries the mode. Tests: terminal-content.test.ts:8499 describes asking about and stopping a running command, and e2e/ask-about-a-running-command.spec.ts:311 watches it end to end. Commits 1b532a47, 3508d953, 18eaf3f9. All four children are closed. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: [bug] The turn's header chips are a second variant: built in another place, with a different class list and one chip fewer
description:
Raised by the owner, 2026-08-23, from two screenshots of one pane: a `df` command
block above an assistant turn below it.

    command block:   [ 📁 home/dev ]              [ 27ms ] [ ok ]        ⋮
    assistant turn:  [ 📁 home/dev ]                      [ completed ]  ⋮

«Почему вот эти чипы, их количество, расположение отличается от блока команды? Всё
должно быть одинаково, агент не должен создавать второй вариант.»

He is right, and the cause is two separate divergences.

## 1. The terminal chip is constructed twice, with different class lists

`frontend/src/scrollback/blocks.ts:422` — the command's exit chip:

    'nocx-chip nocx-chip-ok cmd-header-exit cmd-header-exit-ok'
    'nocx-chip nocx-chip-fail cmd-header-exit cmd-header-exit-fail'

`frontend/src/scrollback/blocks.ts:2038`, inside the answer flow's close — the turn's:

    'nocx-chip nocx-chip-ok cmd-header-exit'
    'nocx-chip nocx-chip-fail cmd-header-exit'

The `-ok` / `-fail` modifier is missing on the turn's. **This is not visible today** —
`style.css` carries only `.cmd-header-exit { min-width: 44px }` and paints nothing on
the modifiers — and it is still the defect AGENTS.md names under "two surfaces may
never own the same input": two constructions of one chip that agree everywhere anyone
has looked, and will disagree the day someone styles `.cmd-header-exit-ok`.

## 2. A turn carries no duration, so the group holds one chip instead of two

`addAnswerBlock`'s `buildFragment` calls `createCommandBlock` with `durationMs = null`
and `exitCode = null`, and the duration chip is emitted only `if (durationMs !== null)`.
So the right group has one chip where a command's has two, and the placement follows
from the count.

A turn HAS a duration — the model took time to answer, and how long is exactly as
worth knowing as `df` taking 27ms. Nobody decided it should be absent: the code
comment explains the CONTINUATION case ("drawn as a settled block with no duration and
no exit code") and says nothing about the first fragment, which is the one that closes.

## The fix is one owner, not one more chip

Adding a duration where a duration is missing would leave two constructions in place
and a third variant one bead away. The header's right group needs a single owner that
decides, per block kind, what it contains and in what order — the way
`blockKindRules` already owns the wrapping, the highlight and the status vocabulary
(nocx-ex636).

## NOT in scope, and deliberately

The status VOCABULARY difference — `ok` for a command, `completed` for a turn — is a
decision `nocx-ex636` took on purpose: an answer is not a command's output and does
not borrow its words. This bead does not reverse it. If the owner wants one word for
both, that is a separate decision against ex636 and he takes it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a command in a pane; note `[27ms] [ok]` in its header.
2. Ask the assistant something in the same pane; note `[completed]` alone.
3. Compare the right-hand groups: different count, different left edge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ONE construction of the header's terminal chip, for every block kind. Asserted:
  the class list a command's chip carries and the one a turn's carries come from the
  same place, and a test would fail if a second construction appeared.
- The right group's contents and order are decided per kind in ONE place, beside the
  existing per-kind rules — not at two call sites hundreds of lines apart.
- A finished turn shows how long it took, in the same chip, with the same formatting
  and in the same position as a command's. Asserted. If the answer turns out to be
  that a turn must NOT show a duration, say so in the code and assert the ABSENCE —
  what may not stand is the accident.
- The two headers agree on geometry: same right edge, same gap to the ⋮ menu, same
  chip order. Asserted against the DOM, not against a screenshot.
- A continuation fragment keeps its deliberate emptiness (no duration, no terminal
  chip until the turn closes on it) and the assertion for it stays.
close_reason: Shipped in ac511f0d + 9f28d09d, merged as 9fdcf75f. The header's right-hand group has one owner deciding per block kind what it contains and in what order, beside the existing per-kind rules — the terminal chip is no longer constructed at two call sites hundreds of lines apart, and the turn's missing -ok/-fail modifier goes with it. A finished turn now shows how long it took, in the same chip and position as a command's. REVIEW CAUGHT A SECOND DEFECT the worker had flagged as unverified and I confirmed as certain: closeAttempt never set DurationMs, FinishExecution's COALESCE therefore left the column NULL, the wire carried null, and restore-client's '?? 0' would have drawn a restored turn as 0ms — a lie the change itself would have made visible, invisible to unit tests because a LIVE turn's duration is the renderer's own clock. Fixed both halves: the backend records the turn's duration (the schema comment forbidding the difference of two clocks was reasoned about and amended in place, not ignored — both ends here are one process's clock), and a null now draws NO chip while 0 draws 0ms, so absence reads as unknown rather than as a dropped chip. Three tests, all red first, including one reproducing the exact 0ms. Full gate green on the merged tree: ci-linux both variants, ci-frontend 3807 tests, e2e 377 passed.

title: [bug] The approval prompt still hands a person JSON, and never says where the call lands on disk
description:
Raised by the owner, 2026-08-23, against the live surface after nocx-njn8s. What a
person is shown when the assistant proposes `readScreen`:

    The assistant is asking to call readScreen with these arguments:
    ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ {"sessionId": "d70a2dd1d748f2af8c68183020189d68"}   │
    └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    This call reaches the tab home/dev on this machine.
    This call can read and inspect.

Three things are wrong and one is missing.

**The session id is printed back.** nocx-vnzek took the 32-hex handle off the
tool-call line because it says nothing to a person; nocx-njn8s took it out of the run
sentence for the same reason; and it survives in the blob — which for `readScreen` is
its ONLY argument, so the blob adds nothing at all to the sentence directly beneath
it. The one surface where the id is still shown is the one asking a person to decide.

**The arguments are JSON.** njn8s gave `run` a sentence and left every other tool the
verbatim blob, on a rule that is right and is not what is being changed here: a
paraphrase is honest only while it is EXHAUSTIVE. The mistake was concluding that
exhaustive means per-tool. A generic renderer that lists EVERY parsed argument as a
named row is exhaustive by construction, and it is honest for tools nobody has
written a sentence for yet.

**Nothing says where the call lands on disk.** `home/dev` is the pane's display
title, not a statement about a working directory, and a person deciding on a
destructive call needs the directory as much as the machine.

**And the wording of the effect and the two policy paragraphs outweigh the facts.**
Five paragraphs, of which two are about what approval covers and how long an answer
lasts. Those are correct and should stay; they should not be the bulk of the window.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant something that makes it call `readScreen` with the policy row
   unset, so the run suspends and the prompt appears.
2. The window prints the raw arguments JSON with the session id inside it, and names
   no working directory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Every parsed argument is shown as a named row, for every tool.** Asserted that
  nothing is dropped: a tool with an argument the surface has no words for still
  shows that argument. Unparseable arguments, or arguments that are not an object,
  keep the verbatim blob — that fallback stays and stays honest.
- **A value that names a resource the prompt has already named renders as the
  product's name for it, not as its handle.** A `sessionId` shows the tab and the
  machine; it never shows the 32-hex id, on any surface of this window. Asserted.
- **The working directory is named, and its VERIFICATION STATUS is not lost.**
  nocx already distinguishes a cwd verified by OSC 7 from a guess
  (`TerminalContent._cwdVerified`, AD-5 — only a verified cwd may be handed to
  `files.open` as rootPath). An unverified cwd must not be stated as fact; decide the
  wording deliberately and assert both cases. ONE derivation, through
  `PaneManager.sessionWhere`, which already carries the tab and the machine — never a
  second callback that could disagree.
- **`run` keeps what njn8s gave it:** the command verbatim in a code block, the
  machine and the tab in the lead. The rows are added beside it, not instead of it.
- **The facts a decision needs come before the policy prose.** What runs, with which
  arguments, in which directory, on which machine — then what approving covers and
  how long an answer lasts. Those two paragraphs keep their wording.
- **Through the kit.** A read-only named-fact list does not exist in
  `frontend/src/ui/` today (Field wraps a control; RecordRow describes a record in a
  row). Either extend one at a 90% fit with typed variance, or add one component to
  `ui/` with its CSS, a stable identity class, a test and a README row. Never a
  hand-rolled row family inside the surface.

## Deliberately out

- The cwd shown is the pane's as of the moment the question is asked, and a shell can
  `cd` between the question and the answer. Binding an effect to preconditions is
  nocx-d6gn4.1 and is not in this bead — but do not word the sentence so that it
  promises more than it knows.
close_reason: Shipped in 33c893d5, merged as 9d4e7c1c. Every parsed argument is a named row now, for every tool, through a new kit component FactList (ui/fact-list.tsx + styles/components/fact-list.css + test + README row + index export) — njn8s's exhaustiveness rule stands; what this reverses is the conclusion that exhaustive meant per-tool. A value naming a resource the window already named renders as the product's words, so the 32-hex session id is on no surface of the window. The working directory is named and cwdVerified travels WITH cwd through PaneManager.sessionWhere and is not optional, so an unverified path is never stated as fact (AD-5). run keeps njn8s's command-verbatim lead. Facts precede the two policy paragraphs, whose wording is unchanged. Two existing tests changed deliberately, each carrying a CHANGED DELIBERATELY comment. e2e/agent-tool-approval.spec.ts reads only the dialog title and the tool name; neither moved. Not verified by the worker and therefore mine: the e2e suite and any visual rendering — fact-list.css is asserted through identity classes, not computed geometry.

title: Opening a collection that is already open puts it in the tree twice
description:
Measured 2026-08-23. e2e/api-secret-in-path.spec.ts PASSES on fffbdeeb and FAILS
on the epic head with: strict mode violation, .api-tree__row filtered by
"send message" resolved to 2 elements — same data-rel-path, two different
collection handles (0fa8f65b... and f1a98b41...).

Cause: api.collections.open on a path that is already open mints a SECOND handle
instead of answering with the one that exists, so the same folder appears twice
in the tree with two identities.

This was hard to reach until nocx-vkp9d made the import open its own destination.
Now the ordinary sequence does it: import (which opens), then reach for
"Open a collection folder..." out of habit, and the collection is there twice.
Postman does not show one collection twice.

The fix belongs to whoever mints the handle, not to the tree: a second reader of
"is this path already open" in the renderer would be a second owner of collection
identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opening a path that is already open answers with the handle that exists and
  adds no second row to the tree.
- The answer says which it did, so a surface can tell "opened" from "already
  open" and need not guess from the tree.
- Two DIFFERENT paths that resolve to the same folder (a symlink, a trailing
  slash, . segments) count as the same collection, or the refusal says why not.
- e2e/api-secret-in-path.spec.ts passes UNCHANGED — it is the check that found
  this, and needing to edit it would mean the product still does the wrong thing.
close_reason: c3ad0930 on feat/api-testing (w-openonce). The fix is on the MINTER: identity is the DIRECTORY (os.SameFile on device+inode), not the path, so a trailing slash, a dot segment, a symlink and a second mount are one collection. Open answers a struct carrying AlreadyOpen, so a surface is told which happened instead of guessing from the tree. Close moved onto the minter in the same change — the table used to answer for folders somebody had closed, so the next open came back 'already open' naming a handle no list held; both ends of the handle interval are now named. Dead handles are excluded by the same check() resolve() uses. e2e/api-secret-in-path.spec.ts is byte-identical, which was the criterion. Merged tree verified: go build -tags gtk3 clean; apicoll, apiimport, capability, transport, pathname all ok; contracts:check clean; tsc clean. e2e run is the coordinator's, at the epic gate.

title: The import takes the document, because the backend is not always your machine
description:
api.import.postman accepts a DOCUMENT as well as a path.

The path names a file on the BACKENDS machine. In the desktop app that is also
the persons machine, so the field reads naturally; over a forwarded port
(make dev-web is documented as "forward both ports over SSH") it names a file on
the server, which is almost never meant. The document is the general case: the
renderer has bytes from a browser drop or a file input, and bytes reach any
backend.

apiimport.ImportInto already takes a READER; capability.ImportPostman only opens
the file first. maxAPICurlLineRunes (1 MiB) is the precedent for bounding a text
parameter on the control plane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- api.import.postman accepts EITHER path OR document, and refuses both-or-neither
  by name with a sentence saying which.
- A document over the bound is refused with a sentence naming the bound and
  pointing at the path parameter; the bound is stated once, beside the curl one.
- A document import writes the same collection a path import of the same bytes
  writes - asserted by importing the same export both ways and comparing.
- The refusals a path import already has are unchanged.
- Contract updated, regenerated and committed; the over-the-wire conformance test
  covers the document route.
