title: One effect kernel: both carriers become the same canonical invocation before policy
description:
Two ways for the assistant to reach an effect is defensible. Two owners of what an
effect IS is the AD-8 fuse, and it is the single thing that decides whether this
epic is an experiment or a permanent fork.

    direct tool call ──┐
                       ├─ canonical invocation → policy → narrowed capability → action entry
    program binding  ──┘

The interpreter binding must be a generated or mechanical adapter over the same
canonical tool descriptor the wire tools are projected from. It independently
defines none of: schema, effect, resource extraction, authorization, result
serialization, error classification, ledger behaviour, egress behaviour.

## The consequence nobody names, and it is a real cost

Collapsing the model-facing surface to one `execute` makes every proposal look like
the same innocuous tool from outside. Providers, framework middleware, generic
telemetry, UI previews, evaluation datasets, rate limits and failure classification
all lose the ability to tell a proposed `files.read` from a proposed destructive
`run`. The interpreter becomes both the security kernel AND the observability choke
point, so every effect must emerge as a first-class internal action before it can
execute. If any binding does host work directly, the architecture has failed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One registry, one enforcement path. Asserted: the same effect proposed through
  either carrier produces the same policy decision, the same narrowed capability and
  the same ledger shape.
- A binding cannot perform host work without producing a canonical invocation first.
  Asserted by a test that would fail if a binding reached a host function directly.
- Effects stay individually visible to telemetry and to the surfaces that classify
  them, even when the outer tool name is `execute`. Asserted.
close_reason: Absorbed by nocx-d6gn4.12 (closed): one effect kernel behind an interface, reached by the carrier rather than by eino, every invocation canonical before policy. Its own wording — 'BOTH carriers become the same canonical invocation' — lost its referent when nocx-d6gn4.14 removed both composing carriers; one carrier remains and it goes through that kernel. The kernel's tests are internal/assistant/kernel_test.go, and it survived the deletion, which is the check that it was a seam and not a switch.

title: A tool result is one artifact doing four jobs, and they are pulling apart
description:
One artifact currently serves as: the model's window onto a result, the human's
rendering of it, the audit representation, and — if anything is ever replayed — the
authoritative value the program observed. Those four have incompatible requirements
and the collision is already visible: the model's window is capped at 64 KiB
(MAX_RUN_OUTPUT_WINDOW_CHARS), retention evicts heavy bodies while their entries stay
(ADR-0019 §7), and terminal-derived text is openly an imperfect representation of
what was on screen.

A branch decision cannot be reproduced from a truncated window, a rendered grid, or
a body that has since aged out. So either the roles separate, or replay is unsound
and "the ledger is the journal" stays false.

This has value on its own, ahead of any program carrier: addressed results let the
model say "the thing I read a moment ago" instead of carrying it in context.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A tool result is an addressed artifact with a durable typed handle and provenance,
  and a later call can take the handle rather than the bytes.
- The four roles are distinct and each says which it is: authoritative replay
  payload, audit representation, model-facing window, human-facing rendering.
- Retention policy is stated per role. The replay payload's retention is not the
  audit body's, and an evicted replay payload makes its execution non-resumable
  rather than silently resumable from a different value.
- Asserted: a result whose model window was truncated still reproduces exactly for
  the role that requires exactness.
notes:
=== THIRD ADVERSARIAL ROUND, 2026-08-26 ===

A HANDLE IS NOT A BEARER CAPABILITY, and this is the security line of the bead. Today
authority is narrowed from the RUN's grant. A handle carried into a later run must
still be authorized against its underlying resource and its egress class - it confers
nothing by being held. Design it so that possessing a handle and being permitted to
dereference it are separate facts.

"One result becomes addressed artifacts" is not enough either. A durable handle needs:
type, content identity, provenance, sensitivity/egress classification, retention
state, authorization semantics, and EXPLICIT behaviour when its bytes have expired.
ADR-0019 already requires provenance and honest gaps for artifacts - extend that, do
not invent a parallel notion.

AND THE FINDING THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS: this bead probably captures a large fraction of
the whole epic's context benefit on its own. files.read returns up to 64 KiB straight
into the tool result (internal/assistant/execute.go), while the UI already exposes a
ledger entry handle rather than duplicating result bytes (internal/assistant/
assistant.go). Typed handles plus bounded slice / parse / summarize / compare /
pass-by-reference remove repeated byte transport with NO language runtime at all.
If that makes ordinary tool sequences cheap enough, it WEAKENS the carrier's economic
case - and it strengthens only the executor substrate, never the claim that models
should be authoring programs. Whoever takes this bead should expect that outcome and
report it rather than defend the epic.

title: Every effect revalidates the world it assumed, immediately before it runs
description:
True today, without any of the rest of this epic. Between the moment a call is
proposed and the moment it executes, a person can answer an approval, a shell can
change cwd, a branch can move, a file can be edited, an ssh session can reconnect to
a DIFFERENT machine and credentials can rotate. Exact resource identity does not
cover any of that: the identity is still the same while what it names has changed.

Under replay it gets worse rather than better, which is why it is here: replay
faithfully reuses the recorded observation and reconstructs the old request
perfectly. Internally deterministic, externally stale — and more legitimate-looking
than before.

## READ FIRST, and do not re-decide it

`nocx-x8s2.1` already rejected two of the obvious shapes, with reasons: a predicate
the MODEL authors at proposal time (it must be written blind to what will later
change, and it needs a language and an evaluator we would have to invent), and
asking the model again at delivery (the confirmation is itself a 1-4s round trip, so
the race is moved rather than closed). This bead generalises that decision to every
effect; it does not get to overturn it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A mutation declares preconditions and the host revalidates them immediately before
  execution. Failed validation invalidates the approval and terminates the attempt —
  it never silently re-observes and continues.
- The binding is per effect class and is stored, not inferred: a file mutation binds
  to the file's digest or its absence; a git operation to repository identity and
  HEAD; a keystroke to frame identity; a remote action to host fingerprint and
  connection identity; a session action to the session's authoritative instance and
  never to a recycled display name.
- An observation carries freshness metadata, so "how old is what this decision was
  made from" is answerable from the record.
- Asserted for at least two classes end to end, including the case that matters:
  approval given, world changed, effect refused.
notes:
=== THIRD ADVERSARIAL ROUND, 2026-08-26: this bead was NOT well defined ===

"Revalidate immediately before execution" creates ANOTHER time-of-check/time-of-use
interval. A check followed by an effect is still a race, only a shorter one, and a
bead that ships bespoke per-tool checks buys reassurance without closing anything.

What the bead must define FIRST, before any check is written:
  - typed preconditions - what CLASS of assumption is being asserted;
  - stable identity tokens - and which assumptions can be closed ATOMICALLY by
    executing through a capability bound to an open file descriptor, a git object id,
    a connection epoch, or a session incarnation, versus which cannot be closed at all;
  - who observes them, and whether the executor can bind the token to the effect
    atomically rather than checking and then hoping.
A session id today expresses SCOPE. It does not assert that an ssh reconnect still
names the same remote machine. That gap is the example to design against.

SCOPE CORRECTION. The replay half of this question moves OUT of this bead and into
nocx-d6gn4.4: under replay, revalidation must distinguish a RECORDED precondition
outcome (reconstructing the interrupted attempt) from a FRESH check (a new physical
attempt). Conflating them either makes replay nondeterministic or lets a stale fact
authorize a new effect. That distinction needs .4's command and attempt identity, so
it cannot be settled here. What stays here is a defect that exists TODAY, with no
carrier and no replay, and it stays on the front for that reason.

acceptance_criteria:
A person drags a Postman export from their file manager onto the import ask and presses Import: the export's path and a destination under nocx's own collections folder are already filled in, and the terminal pane underneath does not also react to the drop.

## Success Criteria

- The ask opens with the backend's defaultRoot in the destination and Import disabled until it grows a last segment.
- A files.dropped naming target "api-import" fills both fields; one naming "terminal" leaves them alone and reaches the prompt instead.
- A drop whose target names nothing is refused by the backend and emitted to nobody.

- make ci-full green on the merged tree.

title: the grouping spec's row filter matches the other browser project's rows, so it counts 2
description:
e2e/notification-centre-grouping.spec.ts raises three OSC 777 notifications from
one session and asserts they collapsed into ONE row, located by
page.locator(ROW).filter({ hasText: "build three x3" }).

Both browser projects run this file against ONE devharness and one $HOME
(playwright.config.ts declares chromium and webkit; workers is 1, so they run in
sequence), and the panel offers no way to empty the feed -- quietBell marks rows
READ, which zeroes the bell badge but leaves the rows. So webkit starts with
chromium row already in the feed, raises an identical one, and the filter
matches both: expected 1, received 2, stably (64 x "locator resolved to 2
elements", not a race that settles).

The spec already knew the feed is shared -- the totals later in it are READ
rather than assumed, with a comment saying rows from earlier spec files are
legitimately there. But a hasText filter cannot be read, it has to MATCH, and
the titles were not unique to the run that raised them. Same for REMOTE.

CI hid it and is not red: ci-e2e runs one job per browser IN PARALLEL, so each
browser gets its own backend and the collision cannot happen. The container runs
both in sequence against one, which is why it is what saw this. Neither
environment is lying: the spec had a precondition -- a feed holding only its own
rows -- that it never established.

The product is correct and is not changed: collapse is keyed {sessionId, kind},
these are two different sessions, so two rows is the right answer.

The bell assertions are unaffected and stay as they are: quietBell marks
everything read first, so the badge counts only what this test raised.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/notification-centre-grouping.spec.ts
   (both projects -- do NOT set PW_PROJECTS)
2. chromium passes; webkit fails at :321 with toHaveCount(1) receiving 2.
3. PW_PROJECTS=webkit alone passes, which is what makes it look like a load
   flake in a full run and is not one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The spec passes with BOTH projects in one container run, which is the
  configuration that reproduced it every time.
- The fix makes this test rows identifiable as its own rather than clearing the
  feed -- no product change, and no "clear all" invented for a test.
- Feed-global counts stay READ rather than assumed.
close_reason: Fixed in 24c791a6. Titles carry the project name; both projects green in one container run — the configuration that reproduced it every time.

title: lint-ci omits the platform build tags, so make ci-full cannot run on a Linux host
description:
Makefile:429 runs `golangci-lint run ./...` with no build tags. Every other Go
target in the Makefile carries $(WAILS_PLATFORM_TAGS) -- build (62), build
release (70), run (79), test (98), test-ci (433), build-ci (444) -- which
resolves to `gtk3` on a Linux host with webkit2gtk-4.1 present (Makefile:19).

Without it, golangci-lint cannot load a wails v3 internal package and dies:

  buildir: failed to load package webview: could not load export data for
  "github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/internal/assetserver/webview"
  make: *** [Makefile:429: lint-ci] Error 3

So `make ci`, and therefore `make ci-full`, fails at its second step on Linux
and never reaches the other three jobs. AGENTS.md names `make ci-full` as THE
gate an integrating agent must run, and agents on this project run on Linux,
so the documented gate is unrunnable for them.

CI is NOT affected and is not red: the `golangci-lint run ./...` step lives in
the `ci-mac` job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:131, runs-on macos-latest), where no
gtk tag is needed. That is why this survived -- the target mirrors the macOS
backend job, and only a Linux HOST running it hits the gap.

Proved by contrast rather than argued: `golangci-lint run ./...` fails with the
webview load error, and `golangci-lint run --build-tags gtk3 ./...` exits 0 with
no findings, on the same tree in the same shell.

Discovered while running `make ci-full` on feat/notifications. Not caused by it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a Linux host with webkit2gtk-4.1 present, from a clean tree: `make lint-ci`
2. gofumpt passes; golangci-lint fails with "buildir: failed to load package
   webview: could not load export data" and make exits 3.
3. `golangci-lint run --build-tags gtk3 ./...` on the same tree exits 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- lint-ci passes the platform tags the same way test-ci and build-ci do, via
  $(if $(WAILS_PLATFORM_TAGS),...) so macOS (where the value is empty) is
  unchanged and keeps running exactly `golangci-lint run ./...`.
- `make lint-ci` exits 0 on a Linux host with webkit2gtk-4.1 present.
- `make ci-full` gets past lint-ci on Linux and runs all four jobs.
close_reason: Shipped. Makefile:20 defines GOLANGCI_BUILD_TAGS from WAILS_PLATFORM_TAGS and Makefile:497 passes it to golangci-lint run, empty on macOS so that runner keeps running exactly run ./... . Commit 4d2f2f3d. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: proof-matrix's last-settings-row locator matches hidden sections, so it measures a null box
description:
e2e/proof-matrix.spec.ts asserts, in two places, that the settings content area
scrolls its last row into view. Both located the subject as
page.locator(".ui-settings-row").last().

Settings renders EVERY section and hides the unselected ones with
.st-vis-hidden { display: none } (frontend/src/settings.tsx:1274,
frontend/src/styles/surfaces/settings.css:314). So the unscoped locator matches
the rows of every section on the page, and .last() returns whichever section
happens to declare a row last -- a display:none element, which has no box.
boundingBox() then returns null and the assertion fails as expect(rowBox)
.not.toBeNull().

Latent since the hiding was introduced. It cost nothing only while Interface
was the last section to declare a row; the Notifications section (nocx-z73vk)
registered after it and took both assertions straight to null.

The subject was always meant to be the OPEN section last row. Fix is the
locator that says so: .ui-settings-row:visible. Also asserts the row is visible
BEFORE measuring it, so a section that stops rendering rows fails as "there is
no visible row" rather than as a mystery null.

Distinct from nocx-vuhkm, which is a real narrow-layout defect in
e2e/settings-scroll.spec.ts (a stacked rail taller than the pane evicts the
content scroller). This one is a test-locator defect and fixing it neither
masks nor touches that.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/proof-matrix.spec.ts
2. "the content area actually scrolls the last setting row into view" and
   "content remains scrollable at narrow breakpoint" both fail with
   expect(received).not.toBeNull() / Received: null.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Both specs pass on chromium AND webkit in the container.
- Reverting only the locator change reproduces both failures -- the fix is
  shown to be load-bearing by contrast, not asserted.
close_reason: Fixed in 93cbf147. Locator scoped to :visible; both specs green on chromium and webkit in the container, and both reproduce as Received: null with only the locator reverted.

title: Narrow settings layout: a stacked rail taller than the pane evicts the content scroller
description:
At the narrow (stacked, <640px) breakpoint the page rail sits above the content and is laid out flex: 0 0 auto in a column with no overflow, so a rail taller than the pane pushes .ui-page__scroll out of the pane entirely and the content becomes unreachable. Design §6.2 says in as many words: 'At the narrow breakpoint the rail stacks above the content and does not scroll independently.' It does not say what happens when the stacked rail is taller than the pane, and this is that case.

Measured in the container on webkit, causation proved by experiment rather than argument -- hiding the ONE rail row the new Notifications section added and changing nothing else:

  with:    railH 513, paneH 482, scrollerTop 551, paneBottom 520, reachable false  (11 items, 33px each)
  without: railH 480, paneH 482, scrollerTop 518, paneBottom 520, reachable TRUE

The narrow layout had 2px of slack and one 33px nav row consumed it. e2e/settings-scroll.spec.ts:83 was green before and is red now for that reason alone -- and it was green on a technicality: the scroller measures 40px there, which is its own padding around a zero-height content box.

Discovered by nocx-z73vk (the notification routing matrix), which added the eleventh rail row. Not caused by it.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. PW_PROJECTS=webkit e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/settings-scroll.spec.ts
2. 'scrolls the last section in narrow (stacked, <640px) layout' fails: the last section is unreachable.

## Why a worker must not patch this
Every in-place fix collides with a numbered invariant that has its own test:
- rail scrolls at narrow -> contradicts §6.2 clause 4, frontend/src/ui/scroll-ownership.test.tsx:23, and e2e/proof-matrix.spec.ts:876 which asserts the rail is NOT scrollable at 600x250;
- rail shrinks with overflow-y: visible -> rail content paints over the content below;
- .ui-page__body becomes the scroll owner -> adds a third owner, which §6.2 forbids by name;
- trimming rail chrome to buy ~30px -> green today, re-arms the identical trap at section twelve.

## Acceptance Criteria
- §6.2 gains a clause saying what a stacked rail does when its content exceeds the pane, decided deliberately and recorded (an ADR if it changes the invariant).
- At the narrow breakpoint the last section is reachable with eleven rail entries and with twenty.
- Whatever is chosen, the scroll-ownership test still passes or is amended in the same commit with the reason.
- The test no longer passes on a zero-height content box: it asserts the scroller has content, not merely padding.

title: The turn draws its conclusion above the evidence it was distilled from
acceptance_criteria:
A turn reads in the order it happened: the question, what the assistant did,
the evidence it got back, and only then the conclusion drawn from it.

## What the owner saw, 2026-08-23

He asked "Как мне проверить сколько места на диске?". On screen, in this order:
the question; a `▶ Thinking` note; a bare `▸ run home/dev` line carrying neither
arguments nor result; the finished answer "41G свободно, занято 79%"; and THEN,
below the whole turn, the `df -h` block with its twelve lines of raw output —
the evidence the answer was distilled from, standing after the conclusion.

«Когда агент вызывает команду, то она появляется под вопросом.»

## The shape

One causal sequence is projected as a different one:

    causal:  question -> tool call -> evidence -> answer
    drawn:   question -> call marker -> answer -> evidence

The `▸ run` line is empty for the same reason the block is in the wrong place:
its content went to the tail. One command occupies two positions and the useful
half is in the position nobody reads first.

## Which decisions this overturns, and what they said

**nocx-shxv0 (closed 2026-08-22) decided the opposite, deliberately.** Its last
criterion was "Decide deliberately whether the agent's shell run stays a
top-level block as well ... or becomes part of the answer flow", and it chose
"stays", stating the ownership in `submitAgentCommand`'s comment: the BLOCK owns
the command, the answer's LINE owns WHEN. That ownership rule is KEPT here and
is not what was wrong. What was wrong is that the two owners were drawn in
different neighbourhoods, so the reader met the conclusion before the evidence.

**ADR-0036 says "a turn is a block, so it appears where blocks appear".** This
bead makes a turn appear as SEVERAL fragments around the blocks it caused, so
that sentence needs amending — deliberately, in the ADR, not routed around.

**nocx-nm9md** ("a tool call cannot be opened") is left standing but narrows:
for `run` the block IS what the line would have opened, so nm9md keeps only the
tools that open no block (readScreen, blocks.list, blocks.read).

## The arrangement chosen, and the two rejected

Chosen — flat causal interleaving. The turn renders in fragments; the agent's
command stays an ORDINARY top-level block, drawn between them at the point the
call happened.

Rejected — nesting the block inside the turn's body: it puts a fixed VT grid
(which must not re-wrap) inside reflowing prose, and the nested block then has
to be argued back into being a first-class block for selection, copy, re-run and
block navigation. Rejected — hoisting the command above the question: in a
terminal vertical position is a claim about time, and that claim would be that
the command preceded the intent that caused it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant a question it answers by running a shell command
   ("Как мне проверить сколько места на диске?").
2. Read the turn top to bottom. The answer written from the command's output
   stands above the block that produced it, and the `run` line inside the turn
   names neither the command nor its result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A turn that ran a command draws, in document order: question, tool activity,
  the command's own block, the answer text written from it. Asserted off the DOM
  order, on a turn driven end to end — not eyeballed and not on a fixture.
- The `run` tool's line is GONE from the answer flow: the block occupies that
  position. Asserted that no surface restates the command text, its output, its
  exit status or its duration.
- The agent's command is still an ordinary top-level block: every assertion that
  holds for a human's block — selection, copy, re-run, block navigation, "what
  did I run" — holds for it, asserted by the same tests over both authors.
- A tool that opens no block keeps its line: nothing else owns its occurrence.
  Asserted for readScreen.
- A turn drawn in fragments is identifiable as ONE turn, from a stored identity
  rather than from a colour. Asserted: a person (and a test) can tell a
  continuation fragment from a second answer.
- Answer text emitted BEFORE a call stays above the block; text emitted while
  the command is still running lands below it. The tail stays the live write
  location — nothing is repainted into a position it already left. Asserted.
- A turn with five tool calls stays readable: completed no-block calls compact
  into one expandable line rather than five. Asserted at five.
- A turn with no tool calls renders exactly as it does today. Asserted.
- The live view and the restored view of one turn agree (nocx-h1l4o).
notes:
--- Handed over from nocx-h1l4o, 2026-08-23 ---

The relation now exists: a command an assistant turn ran, and every action entry,
carries a stored caused-by to its turn WITH a causal position, and restore reads it
(d1ab78aa). Your last criterion — "the live view and the restored view of one turn
agree" — has its mechanism.

ONE THING IS DEFERRED INTO THIS BEAD, deliberately. The causal position orders the
calls; it does not say WHERE IN THE PROSE each one sat. So a restored turn currently
puts its calls at the head of its flow, while live a call sits between the prose
before it and the prose written from its result. Anchoring a call mid-prose needs the
answer to be a TIMELINE rather than one artifact — and that is precisely what this
bead's "flat causal interleaving" makes it. So the fix is yours, not a follow-up:
when the turn becomes fragments, the anchor becomes a stored fact for free.

Two tests will tell you when you have it. frontend/src/scrollback/restored-turn-order.test.ts
asserts the restored order against the LIVE path rather than a fixture — including
"puts the command the turn ran where the live path put it: after the turn", which is
the very arrangement you are changing. It is meant to go red when you move the live
one, and following it is the work.
close_reason: Shipped in 738d9069 + b340693d, merged as 64f8fac5 and 4946b0f8. A turn is drawn as fragments around the blocks it caused: scrollback/turn-flow.ts is the single owner of the projection (answer + causes -> ordered pieces) and BOTH the live path and the restore read it, so they cannot disagree. Backend supplies the two facts the renderer could not derive: Declaration.OpensBlock (true for run alone) and the anchor 'at', the call's offset into the answer counted in UTF-16 units off the engine's existing builder; both are on the contracts as required. ui/tool-call-group.ts is a new kit component (README row, CSS, native <details>) compacting 4+ consecutive no-block calls. ADR-0036 amended IN THE FILE: the sentence 'a turn is a block' is marked in place and a closing amendment says what is dropped (turn/single-block identity), what survives (one entry, blocks.list, shxv0's ownership rule, reasoning not persisted) and re-records both rejected arrangements. The merged e2e gate caught a real defect the unit tests could not: submitAgentCommand answered agent.runResolved with the renderer's per-tab block counter instead of the store-minted entry id, so the command's caused-by edge named no row and the FK refused it — h1l4o's own backend test was green because it built the resolution itself, which is AGENTS.md testing rule 4 exactly. Fixed in b340693d with the failing unit test kept, plus a pair holding apart the two adjacent cases (a command at the very start of the answer opens the continuation its prose goes in; the same turn with no prose after the command opens none). Full gate green on the merged tree: ci-linux both keyring variants, ci-frontend 3780 tests, e2e 377 passed. make ci remains red on the pre-existing lint-ci build-tags defect (nocx-bkrub), baselined at 9c730ed3.

title: caused-by, with an order, joins a command to the turn that caused it
acceptance_criteria:
A restored turn is arranged the way the live one was, from a stored relation
rather than a guess.

## Which decisions this touches, and what they already say

ADR-0036 ("an assistant turn is one entry") ends by naming this as the next
step: "A tool call stays its own entry and stays out of the restore... It is
currently anchored to nothing at all, which means a restored turn comes back
without the calls it made; `caused-by`, freed by this decision, is the relation
that will join an action to its turn." AD-8 (one owner per behaviour) says the
relation has ONE owner: the ledger, not a second copy in the renderer.

ADR-0019 is the one ledger with disposable projections — so the arrangement on
screen is a projection OF the relation, never a fact the renderer stores.

## Why it is needed now

The chronological turn (see the sibling bead) draws the agent's command block
between the turn's fragments. Live, the renderer knows the order because it
watched it happen. After a restart it knows nothing: the turn is one entry and
the command is a separate ordinary shell entry with author='agent', and
`ingest_seq` is commit order, not causal position within a turn. Without the
relation the restored tab draws the command as an unrelated block somewhere in
the flow, and the same session looks like two different things depending on
whether the backend was restarted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A command an assistant turn ran carries a stored `caused-by` to that turn AND
  a position within it. Asserted in the store, not inferred from ordering.
- An action entry (a non-`run` tool call) joins its turn by the SAME relation,
  so a restored turn comes back with the calls it made. Asserted.
- Restore reproduces the live arrangement from the relation: the same document
  order and the same fragments, asserted against a live turn's DOM order rather
  than against a fixture the test wrote.
- A missing, unreadable or dangling relation degrades to plain ledger order,
  with the command drawn as an independent agent block. It NEVER guesses a
  parent. Asserted for each of the three cases.
- The relation survives a turn whose command outlived it (the run finished after
  the answer closed) and a turn that failed mid-call — both asserted, both ends
  of the interval named.
- The renderer sends no arrangement of its own: the paneId precedent in
  `ledger.open` applies — a second copy on the wire is the one nobody checks.
close_reason: Shipped in d1ab78aa, merged into feat/ai-assistant. AddCause/Caused sit on the repository seam rather than going through AddEdge, because the position may not come from the caller: an in-memory counter restarts on every approval resume, which re-runs the pipeline over a turn that already has causes. Position lives in the edge payload, not a new column — it is a fact of one relation out of six and payload is the declared sparse extension ledger.get already carries. The policy middleware is the single writer (action entries, proposal entries, and the run tool's decode of the renderer-minted shell entry) and learns its turn from the transport's rc.entryID; the renderer sends no arrangement. All six criteria asserted: store-level position, action entries by the same relation, live-vs-restored DOM order compared against the live path, all three degradations (no relation / unreadable / dangling) plus a circular one, and both interval ends (TestTheRelationOutlivesTheTurnThatClosedFirst, TestATurnThatFailedMidCallKeepsTheCallsItMade). DEFERRED to nocx-9sqii and recorded there: the interleaving POINT of a call within the prose is not reproduced — a restored turn puts its calls at the head of its flow, because anchoring a call mid-prose needs the answer to be a timeline rather than one artifact, which is exactly what 9sqii's fragments make it.

title: Three e2e specs name the panel filter by where it used to sit, and the shell has moved it
description:
`nocx-708q.2/.3` moved every panel's filter out of the panel and into the shell's
pinned slot (`.ui-sidebar-view__filter`), which is a SIBLING of
`.ui-sidebar-view__body` where the panel root lives. Three e2e specs still name
the field by where it used to be, and CI's `ci-e2e` job failed in both browsers
on the same three — deterministically, not as a flake.

The product is not broken. The notes filter is still there, still labelled
"Search notes", and Settings' field is still auto-focused; only the selectors
are stale:

- `notes.spec.ts:75,100` — `.notes-panel input[type="search"]` matches nothing
  now, so `fill` waits out the 30 s timeout.
- `proof-matrix.spec.ts:102` — `.ui-search-field input[type="search"]`
  `.first()` used to be Settings' field and is now the Files panel's filter
  ("Filter files by name"), which is not focused when Settings opens. `.first()`
  over a global class was always position-dependent; the panel work is what made
  it wrong.

The fix is the rule these specs were already meant to follow: reach the control
the way a person does, by its accessible name, so it survives the shell deciding
where to put it.

This is CI red, not container red — the container's own failure set is different
and neither of these is layout-sensitive.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/notes.spec.ts e2e/proof-matrix.spec.ts`, or CI
   run 32600294644 (`ci-e2e (chromium)` and `ci-e2e (webkit)`).
2. Both browsers: 3 failed, 181 passed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The three specs locate the field by role and accessible name
  ("Search notes", "Search settings"), not by ancestry or `.first()`.
- Both e2e projects are green on CI.
- No production change: this is a stale test, and the check is that the fix
  touches only `e2e/`.
close_reason: The three specs ask by role and accessible name ('Search notes', 'Search settings') instead of by ancestry or .first(). Container chromium: notes 4 passed, proof-matrix 34 passed. Only e2e/ touched. Commit 49395996.

title: The table is built from settings and swapped into the live router
description:
Epic 3 task 2. One Bool per (kind, channel) from the catalogue; the router accepts a validated table atomically; the registry's notifier rebuilds it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One Bool per (kind, channel) registered from the catalogue, in a Notifications section, with today's single row (program.notify at programRequest to the banner) as the only default that is on.
- The router accepts a validated table atomically: a raise resolves against exactly one table, and a swap takes effect only for raises that begin after it. Tested under -race with raises in flight during a swap.
- Every rebuild re-runs the trust-capability validation. A failing table is refused WHOLE, the previous stays live, and the failure is visible to the user rather than only in a log.
- Turning every toggle of a kind off makes that kind reach nothing.
- A settings change reaches the router without a restart.
- contracts/settings.set.schema.json exists with additionalProperties:false and explicit required, the renderer type is generated from it, and both conformance cases exist including the one off the real socket.
close_reason: Closed

title: The approval prompt shows a JSON blob, not what the assistant wants to do
acceptance_criteria:
A person asked to approve a call reads a SENTENCE naming the three facts they
are deciding on: what command, on which machine, in which tab.

## What happens

Owner, 2026-08-23, on the shipped policy prompt:

  The assistant wants to make changes that cannot be undone.
  The assistant is asking to call run with these arguments:
    {"command": "df -h", "sessionId": "ab607acafd6d89e698a8913b7623cf95"}
  This call reaches home/dev.

Three defects in four lines. The command is buried in a JSON blob a person has
to parse by eye. The session id is printed back verbatim inside it — the exact
handle nocx-vnzek took off the tool-call line, still on the surface that bead
explicitly said should get the same treatment. And the machine is never named
at all, which is the one fact that decides whether `rm -rf` lands here or on a
production host.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a tab and ask the assistant to run a command that escalates, e.g.
   "how much disk is free?" — the run tool is mutate-destructive.
2. The approval prompt names the effect, prints the raw arguments JSON with
   the 32-hex session id inside it, and names no machine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `run` proposal reads as a sentence: the command verbatim in a code block,
  the machine and the tab named in the lead. Asserted.
- The machine is `user@host` for a session whose ACTIVE domain is remote, and
  "this machine" for a local shell — the ssh binding AND a hand-typed ssh,
  which is the case that matters. ONE derivation: TerminalContent.hostLabel,
  the same one the block header and the close prompt read.
- The tab is the pane's own name, through PaneManager's existing derivation —
  no second answer to "what is this session called".
- Nothing is hidden: the friendly rendering is used only when the parsed
  arguments are exactly the two the run schema declares. A third argument
  falls back to the verbatim blob. Asserted.
- Every other tool keeps the verbatim arguments blob, and its location
  sentence names the machine too.
- No pane holds the session: the prompt says nothing about where, and never
  prints the id back. Asserted.
close_reason: Shipped in c324cce9. A run proposal reads as a sentence — machine and tab in the lead, command verbatim in a code block — with where() derived once through PaneManager.sessionWhere (sessionDisplayName + TerminalContent.hostLabel, now public for that caller). The friendly rendering is gated on the PARSED KEYS, so a third argument on run puts the verbatim blob back; every other tool keeps the blob and gains the machine on its location sentence. The session id is never printed back. Nine assertions in agent-approval-prompt.test.tsx plus one in panes.test.ts cover every AC, including the egress tense case.

title: Three transfer options are test seams living in production files, so the deadcode ratchet reports them
description:
`transfer.WithChunkSize`, `transport.WithTransferStallTimeout` and
`transport.WithTransferTicketTTL` have no caller outside their own tests:
production always takes the defaults. They are test seams — the doc comment on
`WithTransferTicketTTL` says so in as many words ("the tests use it to reach the
expiry path through the SAME code production takes") — but they sit in
`sink.go` and `ws_upload.go`, which deadcode compiles like any other production
file.

`.githooks/check-deadcode.mjs` states where a test helper belongs: "a `_test.go`
file, which deadcode never compiles without -test and so never reports, or a
test-support PACKAGE". These are in neither.

Baselining them is the wrong answer: the baseline is for violations that exist,
and these are not violations of reachability at all — they are correctly
unreachable from main() because nothing in production configures a chunk size or
a stall timeout, and YAGNI says nothing should until somebody asks.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs` on this branch (or CI's `ci-mac` /
   `ci-linux` jobs, run 32599442936).
2. "DEADCODE RATCHET: 89 unreachable functions (89 baselined, 3 NEW)" — the
   three above. Two jobs red, one cause.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The three options move to `export_test.go` in their own packages, unchanged in
  name and signature, so every existing test compiles untouched.
- `node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs` reports 0 NEW, and the baseline does not
  grow — `update-deadcode-baseline.mjs` is not run.
- `go test ./internal/transfer/... ./internal/transport/...` stays green.
- Nothing in production gains a knob nobody asked for.
close_reason: The two transport timeouts moved to internal/transport/export_test.go; the chunk bound became a parameter (NewSink/NewSource take it, DefaultChunk exported, the one-option Option/config framework deleted). check-deadcode.mjs: 87 unreachable, all baselined, 0 new. Commit 6c0ac86a.

title: The feed retains a bounded tail of each run
description:
Epic 2 task 1. RunMember{ID,At,Title,ReadAt}, Occurrence.Run, Occurrence.RunDropped, FeedLimits.MaxRunRetained. Plan: .internal/plans/2026-08-22-notification-centre-epic-2.md

## Acceptance Criteria
- A fresh occurrence has Run of length 1 (itself), and Count == len(Run) + RunDropped holds for every occurrence at all times.
- A join appends a member with its own id, instant and title.
- Past MaxRunRetained the OLDEST member is dropped and RunDropped rises by one.
- MarkAllRead marks the row and every retained member; a later join clears only the row's mark.
- Member Title bytes count against MaxRetainedBytes, and evicting a row releases every byte its members held (assert f.bytes returns to its prior value after an add-then-evict cycle).
- NewFeed rejects MaxRunRetained < 1.
- The epic-1 flood test still holds with members present.
close_reason: Closed

title: The panel expands a run and narrows the feed
description:
Epic 2 task 4. Expansion and narrowing in the notifications panel.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A row whose count > 1 is expandable; a row of one is a leaf. Expanding lists retained members newest first, each with its own timestamp and unread mark.
- A row with runDropped > 0 states it inside the expansion ("20 of 4310 shown").
- Narrowing by host, session and kind, built from the kit; place, never repaint.
- Narrowing hides other hosts' rows and the panel states "N of M shown"; the BELL's badge does not change when a filter is applied.
- Clearing the filter restores every row, and a row expanded before the filter is still expanded after.
- No CSS rule sets a painting property on a ui-* class.
close_reason: Closed

title: The run reaches the renderer
description:
Epic 2 task 2. Schema, DTO and generated types gain run[] and runDropped.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each occurrence gains run (array of {id, at, title, read}) and runDropped (integer, minimum 0); both required; additionalProperties:false on the member object.
- run is built with make, never nil.
- A member carries no trust, no level and no body.
- npm run contracts:check passes; the DTO case covers an empty tail, a full one and one with runDropped > 0; the over-the-wire case takes the real result off the real socket.
close_reason: Closed

title: RecordRow learns a disclosure
description:
Epic 2 task 3. An optional controlled disclosure on the kit's RecordRow, in TreeRow's and Section's vocabulary.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Optional controlled disclosure: expandable, expanded, onToggle; a native button part with aria-expanded, Enter/Space operable, same chevron gesture and same data-disclosure vocabulary (expanded|collapsed|leaf) TreeRow and Section use.
- A row given no disclosure props renders as today, data-disclosure=leaf, and reserves the disclosure's width.
- Activating the disclosure does NOT activate the row.
- The disclosed children are the caller's, passed as a slot.

title: The grouping acceptance check
description:
Epic 2 task 5. e2e/notification-centre-grouping.spec.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Drives the UI, never the store; waits on observable state, never on a duration.
- One session raises a run; the feed shows one row with a count; the spec expands it and reads the individual occurrences, each with its own time.
- Two hosts have raised; narrowing to one hides the other's rows, the panel states the narrowed count, and the bell's badge is unchanged.

title: The happy path, watched end to end
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A devharness test serves a fixture OpenAPI 3.1 document over loopback, imports it BY URL, and asserts: the folder tree matches the spec tags; a chosen request has the expected method, URL and query rows; the environment carries the servers URL.
- The same test then opens that request, presses Send, and reads the response.
- It waits on observable state, never on a duration.
- It runs with the disposable `$HOME` the suite requires.

title: The import dialog takes a file, a paste or a URL
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A person can reach the OpenAPI import from the collections tree without editing any file.
- The dialog offers all three sources; choosing URL reveals the connection picker beside the URL field, listing global connections plus a direct option.
- The destination folder field has a Browse button using the same `dialog.*` method the Postman import already uses.
- Only kit components: the guard against raw controls and direct Kobalte imports stays green, and the surface adds no `background`, `border`, `color`, `font-*`, `padding` or `box-shadow` to a kit component.
- After an import, the `Unsupported` list is shown, as it already is for Postman.
- The test drives the seam a person reaches: the control exists, is enabled from the state a user starts in, and activating it reaches the client method.

title: api.import.openapi, with its contract
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- One new JSON-RPC method `api.import.openapi` taking the source (file | text | url), the optional connection id, and the destination; returning the `Unsupported` list in the shape `api.import.postman` already uses.
- `contracts/api.import.openapi.json` lands in the SAME commit, with `additionalProperties: false` and an explicit `required`.
- `npm run contracts:check` passes with the generated renderer type committed.
- `…_DTOConformsToContract` and `…_OverTheWireConformsToContract` both exist; the second validates the real result off the real socket, not a payload the test built.
- No `Unsupported` entry on the wire carries a value out of the document.

title: The spec is fetched by a send, through a connection the person chose
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `capability.ImportOpenAPI` takes a source of file | text | url and, for url, sends a GET through `internal/apisend` with `RouteID` = the chosen connection. There is NO second HTTP client: assert `internal/capability` gains no `net/http.Client` construction for this path.
- The fetch completes BEFORE `ImportInto` is called: on a fetch that 404s, times out, exceeds the byte ceiling, or returns a non-spec, `dest` does not exist afterwards. One test per failure.
- The fetch sends no credential. A 401 surfaces as an error naming the status and telling the person to download the document and import it as a file — visible in the product, not only in a log.
- `internal/apiimport` still cannot reach `net/http`: `TestPackageNeverExecs` unchanged and green.
- The `http://` rule is not re-derived: the path goes through `httppolicy` via `apisend`.

title: ImportInto recognises a third document shape and writes the tree
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `ImportInto` dispatches to the OpenAPI converter on the top-level `openapi` key, and to the Postman converter on `item`/`info.schema`. A document with neither is refused by name. Assert both JSON shapes route correctly — they share a first byte.
- The whole tree lands as ONE atomic arrival: `dest` does not exist until every file is written, synced and renamed.
- An FS failure injected on the Nth file leaves `dest` absent — no partial collection.
- An existing `dest` is refused, never replaced.
- The converter is reachable from `main`: `deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive <converter symbol> ./...` prints a path from `main`, not "reachable only through reflection".

title: servers becomes one environment, and the servers we did not take are said out loud
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Exactly one environment file is written. For a URL import it is built from the server whose origin matches the fetched URL; for file/text it is `servers[0]`.
- It carries `baseUrl` and the route the person chose (`RouteConnection` + profile id, or `RouteDirect`).
- A server URL with variables (`https://{region}.api.com`) is filled from each variable's `default`.
- Every other `servers` entry produces an `Unsupported` line naming that server. No environment is created for it — asserted by counting environment files, so a future "helpful" addition fails this test.
- Variable names from `securitySchemes` appear in the environment's `SecretVars`; no values do.

title: An operation becomes a request
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- One operation produces one `apicoll.Request`; folder = first `tag` minted by `slug()`; untagged lands in the root.
- Name = `summary`, else `operationId`, else `METHOD /path`. A name of `../../etc` yields a folder segment `etc` and no traversal — assert against the minted PATH, not the display name.
- URL is `{{baseUrl}}` + path, and `/users/{id}` becomes `/users/{{id}}`.
- Path parameters land in `Request.Variables` (the request's own, not the environment), empty and enabled.
- Query parameters land in `Query`: `required: true` → `Enabled: true`, otherwise present with `Enabled: false`.
- Header parameters land in `Headers`.
- A `requestBody` with an `example` carries it VERBATIM plus the media type as `Content-Type`; without one the body is empty. No body is ever generated from a schema.
- Auth: `http`+`bearer` → `Auth{Kind: bearer, Var: "{{<scheme key>}}"}`; `http`+`basic` → basic; `apiKey` → apikey carrying its name and `in`; `oauth2`/`openIdConnect` → `AuthNone` + an `Unsupported` line. Operation-level `security` wins over the document's.
- No file written anywhere under the collection root names a secret (design §8); `BindWriter` receives ZERO calls on this path.

title: The OpenAPI document parses, and a version we cannot do is refused by name
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A 3.0 and a 3.1 fixture both parse into the document model; JSON and YAML spellings of the same fixture produce an identical model (yaml.v3 is already a direct dependency — no new one).
- A document with `swagger: "2.0"` is refused with an error naming Swagger 2.0 and naming 3.0/3.1 as what is supported. It is NOT parsed as far as it will go.
- Every bound is a number and each has a test that crosses it: document bytes, operation count (reuse `names.go` `maxItems`), internal `$ref` depth.
- An internal `$ref` resolves; a cyclic one stops at the depth bound and does not recurse.
- An external `$ref` (one naming another URL) is NEVER fetched: the package still cannot reach `net/http` (`TestPackageNeverExecs` stays green) and the ref becomes an `Unsupported` entry naming the operation.
- No `Unsupported.What` ever carries a value out of the document.

title: [epic] A collection is made from the service's own OpenAPI document, fetched from wherever it lives
acceptance_criteria:
DONE WHEN a person gives the import dialog the OpenAPI URL of a service reachable only through an SSH connection, picks that connection, and receives a collection whose folders are the spec tags, whose requests are its operations, and whose one environment already carries the servers URL and that same connection — then opens a request and presses Send having edited nothing but a value. Watched end to end by a devharness test that serves a fixture OpenAPI 3.1 document over loopback.

Deliberately out: bodies generated from schemas, Swagger 2.0, external $ref fetching, OAuth2 flows, re-import/sync of a changed spec, authenticating the spec fetch.

title: A feed row stops being clickable the moment its session ends
description:
`PaneManager.findBySession` (frontend/src/panes.ts:1979) resolves through `content.activeOrigin()`, which returns null once the terminal content has seen its session exit (frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:713). So a `session.ended` row -- the epic's own first source -- is unactivatable by construction, even when its tab is still on the strip marked as lost. The epic promises "clicking the row focuses the tab".

Second half of the same gap: `notify.raise` leaves `Attribution.Backend` empty (internal/transport/ws_notify.go:150-158) while `findBySession` requires 'local', so a program notification from a live tab is unactivatable too.

Found by the epic's e2e check (2026-08-22), which fails on this assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A pane is resolvable by the session id it holds for as long as the pane exists, whether or not that session has ended -- the lookup does not go through the live content origin.
- `notify.raise` stamps `Attribution.Backend` with the local route, so a program notification's row resolves too.
- `canActivate` then means what the panel's meta line claims: the row is inert exactly when the tab is gone, not when the shell exited.
- A test drives it through the UI: a row from a tab that is still open focuses that tab; a row whose tab has been closed is inert.
close_reason: Closed

title: A local shell that exits cleanly is reported as a lost connection
description:
`lifecyclePTY` (internal/app/app.go:1511) embeds the `pty.Pty` INTERFACE, and `WaitErr() (error, bool)` is declared only on the concrete `*LocalPty` (internal/pty/pty_local.go:277). A method on a concrete type is not promoted through an embedded interface, so the type assertion in internal/session/session.go:905 fails for every enhanced local session, `ExitOutcome` has no shell report to read, and it correctly refuses to invent one -- returning ExitInterrupted.

User-visible: a local shell you exit normally leaves its tab marked "Connection lost" instead of closing, and the exit status is gone. Predates the notification centre; found by that epic's e2e check (2026-08-22), which needs the exited/interrupted distinction to map notification levels.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `*lifecyclePTY` satisfies `interface{ WaitErr() (error, bool) }` by forwarding to the embedded pty when that pty provides it, and reports `false` when it does not.
- A test asserts an enhanced local session whose shell exits 0 classifies as ExitExited with status 0, and one that exits non-zero carries that status -- not ExitInterrupted.
- The paired failure test: a session whose pty genuinely provides no report still classifies as ExitInterrupted and does not panic.
close_reason: Closed

title: Every activity-bar panel invents its own arrangement inside a shell that is already shared
description:
Owner: bring every activity-bar panel to one shape. The shell is shared and applied centrally (sidebar.tsx constructs SidebarView once for every view), but each panel invented its own arrangement inside it, and the differences only surface when somebody looks at two panels in one session.

Known so far, from fixing Files: the filter slot existed with ZERO callers so every panel rendered its search field in the scrolling body and every filter scrolled away; .files-filter carried horizontal margin on top of the body's own inset, leaving the field 48px narrower than its panel; and .ui-sidebar-view__header > h2 set only flex, so the heading kept the UA's 1.5em and 0.83em margins and the header measured 72px for one word. Files is fixed and is the reference; Ports, Git and Notes are not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every panel's filter is declared through SidebarViewDescriptor.filter and pinned by the shell; none renders a search field inside the scrolling body.
- No panel adds horizontal inset on top of the body's own; content across panels lines up.
- Panels that do not go through SidebarView are found and either moved onto it or the reason recorded.
- Differences between panels are enumerated in the report — what each was doing and why it is now one thing — rather than silently normalised.
- Kit-level where the kit can own it; a panel says only what the kit cannot know for itself.
close_reason: Merged as c955ddb3..ddcf7c82 plus the coordinator's two follow-ups. Three panels moved onto the shell's pinned filter slot (Ports, Git, Notes); Files was already there. THE DELIVERABLE IS THE TEST, not the diff: panels-one-shape.test.ts reads the SHIPPED stylesheets, because jsdom computes no cascade, and binds three rules for panels nobody has written yet — header, filter and body share one inset; no panel root adds its own; .ui-sidebar-view__body is the one scroll owner. The worker named the two divergences it could not touch (they were in another worker's branch) instead of working around them, and recorded ops-list as an exception ON THE RECORD rather than excluding it silently. Both closed once that branch landed: the Files filter's own margin is gone now the kit row supplies it, the operations headings no longer inset 16px on top of the body's 8px, and its two lists no longer each declare a scroller inside the scrolling body. The exception list is back to empty, which is the correct lifetime for it.

title: Decide how much of a collapsed run the feed keeps
description:
Epic 1 collapses a consecutive run into one row: Count rises, the newest Event replaces the held one, and the constituent occurrences are gone. Epic 2's success criterion is that a collapsed row EXPANDS to the individual occurrences, each keeping its own timestamp and unread mark -- which the epic-1 shape cannot serve.

Retaining all constituents is not the answer either: the flood test admits 10000 occurrences from one session, and keeping them restores exactly the unbounded growth collapse exists to prevent. So the question is what bounded remainder an expansion is allowed to show, and how the row states honestly what it is no longer showing.

Found by review of the epic-1 backend (codex, 2026-08-22), not by a user.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A decision is recorded (ADR or a spec section) naming: what a collapsed row retains per constituent, the bound on that retention, what an expansion shows when the bound was hit, and where the retained data lives (the Occurrence, or beside it).
- The bound is stated in both currencies the feed already uses -- a count and bytes -- or the decision says explicitly why one suffices.
- The decision names what happens to a constituent's unread mark when the run collapses, given that epic 1 clears the row's ReadAt on every join.
close_reason: Decided in .internal/plans/2026-08-22-notification-centre-epic-2.md D2: a row retains its newest MaxRunRetained (20) constituents as RunMember{ID,At,Title,ReadAt}, counts the rest in RunDropped, member bytes count against MaxRetainedBytes, and MarkAllRead marks the row and every retained member while a later join clears only the row's mark.

title: A queued file exists only in a loop variable, so a multi-file drop shows one file and hides the rest
description:
Owner dropped two files: one uploads and the second is nowhere. Not a display bug — the queue does not exist as data.

upload-flow.ts sends strictly one at a time (for … await sendOne(…)), and the store only learns of a transfer when files.upload has returned its transferId. So a file waiting its turn lives in a loop variable and nowhere else: it cannot be shown, counted or cancelled. Drop five and you see one, with no way to know how many are coming or to stop them.

The sequential send itself is deliberate (design section 4, one at a time per binding) and stays. What is missing is that the batch is not represented.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Drop two files on a tab. The first shows in Operations with progress; the second appears only when the first finishes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The whole batch is registered before the first send, so every file is visible from the moment it is dropped.
- A waiting file says it is waiting rather than showing a progress bar at zero, which would claim bytes are moving.
- Cancelling a waiting file removes it from the batch and sends NOTHING on the wire — there is no transfer to cancel yet.
- Cancelling a waiting file does not cancel the batch, and cancelling the running one does not silently drop the rest — say which it does and test it.
- The badge counts what a person would call outstanding, and the grouping in the list still reads correctly with waiting rows in it.
- A refusal that stops the batch (an unusable destination) accounts for the files never attempted rather than leaving them waiting forever.
close_reason: Merged as 07f52646 + caa7d13a. 3879 tests. THE QUEUE: the whole batch is registered before the first send, so every dropped file is visible, counted and stoppable from the moment it lands; a waiting row says it is waiting and draws no bar at zero, which would have claimed bytes were moving. Cancelling a waiting file sends nothing on the wire — there is no transfer yet — asserted on the service double rather than by eye. THE FOLDER: refused in the drop handler before anything is registered, via webkitGetAsEntry().isDirectory off dataTransfer.items, with tests asserting it is NOT decided by size or MIME type; a mixed drop sends the files, names the folder and says how many are on their way. THE MANGLED NAME WAS NOT OURS, and the worker proved it rather than assuming: File.name is passed verbatim in the browser and filepath.Base in Go, nothing anywhere composes a name; the Wails half already refused directories via !info.Mode().IsRegular(), which is how it established the owner was on the browser path, and 192 B is an APFS directory entry. It could not reproduce 15498198pril and says so — then left a test that feeds exactly that string in as a File.name and requires the same characters out, so a composer introduced later fails rather than being argued about.

title: The operations row is hard to read: no hierarchy, wrapping numbers, a hairline progress bar and a button eating the width
description:
Owner, looking at a running upload in the panel: everything is too small and hard to take in. Named concretely rather than as a feeling.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a large upload and open the Operations view at the panel's default width.
2. The progress bar is a hairline between the title and the numbers; '99.1 MB of 328.3 MB' and '7.1 MB/s' wrap onto two lines; the path shows as /home/... ; Cancel takes about a third of the width.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Progress is the visual anchor of a running row, not a hairline between two text blocks.
- A percentage is shown, so nobody does arithmetic to learn that 99.1 of 328.3 is a third.
- Nothing wraps, and the row's height does not change as the numbers do.
- Cancel stops competing with the content for width, while staying keyboard reachable and discoverable without hover-only knowledge.
- A path ellipsises so the LEAF survives — the tail is the informative end.
- A finished row and a running row are distinguishable at a glance rather than by reading.
- Checked at the panel's MINIMUM width and at a wide one; the kit is used and never repainted.
close_reason: Shipped. frontend/src/ui/operation-row.tsx:168 gives the row a percent figure and hierarchy, and progress-bar.tsx:26 gained the md track size for it. Tests: ui/operation-row.test.tsx:172 and :238, operations/operations-view.test.tsx:70, files/download-operations.test.tsx:94. Commits 910a70d1, 1fd326b1, 352fff3b via merge 6847d257. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: An open is answered before it is finished, and nothing can wait for the difference
description:
Named by the worker that fixed nocx-bmpif, which closed the reads rather than the window. An open is not over when its RESPONSE arrives — the subscriber install and other tail work continue after it — and no test helper can wait for that tail. Every wait built on 'the response came back, therefore the server is ready' is racy by construction, and the two defects fixed today were both symptoms of it.

The worker names two candidate shapes: a signal the helper can wait on, or the integrationPTYFactory pattern generalised. It did not choose between them and neither do I.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A caller, test or otherwise, can wait for an open to be COMPLETE rather than merely answered.
- The waits fixed in nocx-bmpif and 1ab22b28 are re-expressed on it, so the workaround does not outlive its cause.
- The fix is argued against the alternative rather than picked.

title: The bell, the panel, and click-to-tab
description:
Plan task 8. BellIcon in the kit, notifications-panel.tsx, sidebar badgeCount, registration in main.tsx.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The bell is a view in the top zone of the activity bar, not an action.
- With zero unread the bell carries NO badge element at all.
- Rows are kit RecordRow inside a role=list; kind badge toned from level; count > 1 renders as xN.
- The panel header action is an IconButton "Mark all read", disabled at zero unread.
- An empty feed renders the kit EmptyState.
- dropped.count > 0 renders one non-activatable row at the bottom naming the count and the span.
- Activating a row resolves (backendId, sessionId) to a tab in the RENDERER and focuses it; a row whose session is gone is not activatable and says so.
- No CSS in notifications-panel.css sets background, border, color, font-*, padding or box-shadow on a ui-* class.
- A test asserts the unread count is unchanged after focusing the tab a notification came from, and changes only on Mark all read.
close_reason: Closed

title: The wire: three methods, three schemas, both conformance tests
description:
Plan task 5. contracts/notify.feed.{read,markRead,changed}.schema.json, generated renderer types, internal/transport/ws_notify_feed.go, BroadcastFeedChanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- notify.feed.read returns {revision, unreadCount, occurrences[], dropped} and nothing else; additionalProperties:false on every object.
- Each occurrence carries id, at, title, body, kind, level, count, read, backendId, sessionId, host and NO trust.
- notify.feed.markRead returns {revision}; notify.feed.changed carries {revision} and nothing else.
- With no feed wired all three answer -32601.
- npm run contracts:check passes; a _DTOConformsToContract and an _OverTheWireConformsToContract case exist for each method.
- BroadcastFeedChanged reaches every client and survives a full queue on one of them.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ingress: stamping moves, once
description:
Plan task 3. Create internal/notify/ingress.go; Router.Raise stops stamping At; Attribution gains Backend.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Admit stamps ev.At from the injected clock when zero and leaves a non-zero At alone.
- Router.Raise no longer stamps At and its comment says why.
- Admit records into the feed BEFORE submitting for delivery.
- An event whose policy disposition is DispositionSuppressed is still in the feed.
- Attribution.Backend is carried through unchanged and reaches the feed.
- Failure-path tests: sink refuses, feed full (both Admits still deliver), MarkAllRead racing Admit under -race, occurrence interval has both ends.
close_reason: Closed

title: session.ended, the feed's first honest source
description:
Plan task 4. Raise a session.ended event from monitorExit in internal/transport/ws.go; add the route in internal/app/app.go.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exactly one session.ended event per session end, with Trust: TrustAttested.
- Level maps from cause: ExitExited status 0 -> success; non-zero -> warning; ExitInterrupted -> warning.
- Title names host and cause; body carries the exit status when there is one; neither is built from any byte of the stream (AD-6).
- Attribution carries Backend "local", the session id and the host.
- A server with no ingress wired still emits the exit notification and does not panic.

title: The occurrence record and the bounded feed
description:
Plan task 1. Create internal/notify/feed.go + feed_test.go: Occurrence, FeedLimits, NewFeed, Add, Snapshot, MarkAllRead, OnChange, DroppedRecord.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Add returns a distinct id per call; Snapshot lists occurrences newest first.
- Exceeding MaxOccurrences evicts the oldest READ occurrence first; an unread one only when no read one exists.
- Exceeding MaxRetainedBytes (UTF-8 Title+Body of every held occurrence) evicts by the same rule until inside budget.
- Every eviction increments Dropped.Count and widens [Oldest, Newest]; the dropped record is outside the occurrence budget and never itself evicted.
