title: The exchange can be stopped by the person who started it
description:
The renderer mints a token and passes it in `api.request.send`. The transport
registers a cancel function under that token for exactly as long as the
exchange runs, and drops it when the exchange settles. `api.request.cancel`
fires it.

The token is the renderer's own rather than the JSON-RPC request id: the id
belongs to the dispatcher and is not exposed to callers, and opening it up for
one button would be a second addressing scheme.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The registration interval is stated in the code with both ends: the token
  resolves from before the exchange starts until the exchange settles, and
  never afterwards.
- Cancelling a token that is not registered is refused by name, not silently
  accepted.
- A cancelled exchange comes back as `outcome: "stopped"`, never as a failure.
- A second cancel of the same token after it settled changes nothing.
- Two exchanges in flight at once cancel independently.
close_reason: landed on feat/api-testing in 38261a5e

title: A failed send returns the attempt, not a bare error
description:
`apisend.Client.Send` currently returns `Response{}, err` on any network
failure and drops what it already holds: the composed request text, the
placements of the secret spans, the tracer's timings and the remote address.
It returns the exchange with `Failure` set instead.

`error` is reserved for a violation of this package's calling contract
(`ErrFileBody`, `ErrAuthUnresolved`) and never for a network outcome.

The phase is classified from the error — `net.DNSError`, a TLS verification
failure, `ErrNoConnection` / `ErrSSHDialTimeout`, `context.Canceled`, a
deadline — together with what the tracer saw (a remote address means the dial
landed; a TLS time means the handshake started).

## Acceptance Criteria

- For every failure the package can produce there is a test asserting the
  PHASE, and the composed request text is present on the returned exchange.
- A send to a name that does not resolve returns phase `resolve` and a request
  block; nothing is returned as a bare error.
- The paired "and on a normal machine it succeeds" test still passes: an
  answered exchange carries `failure` unset.
- The redaction rule is unchanged — no credential reaches a failure reason, and
  the existing redact() coverage still holds.
close_reason: landed on feat/api-testing in 38261a5e

title: api.request.send answers an exchange, not a response
description:
The result of `api.request.send` stops being "the response" and becomes the
exchange. It gains `outcome` (`answered` | `failed` | `stopped`); a `request`
block present whatever the outcome — the composed raw text with its secret
spans, which the sender already has before it dials; `route`, `environment`,
`remoteAddr`, `timings` and `certificates` as far as the attempt got; a
`response` that is null unless answered; and `failure { phase, reason }`
otherwise. Phases: `compose`, `resolve`, `dial`, `connection`, `tls`,
`exchange`, `timeout`, `stopped`.

`api.request.send` params gain a client-minted `token`, and
`api.request.cancel { token }` is declared beside it.

Schema first, then the generated renderer type, then the Go DTO — in that
order, because the schema is the contract and the other two are satisfying it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `contracts/api.request.send.schema.json` declares the shape with
  `additionalProperties: false` and an explicit `required` at every level.
- A failed exchange validates against the schema with `response: null` and a
  `failure` naming one of the eight phases; an answered one validates with
  `failure: null`.
- `contracts/api.request.cancel.schema.json` exists and the method is declared.
- `npm run contracts:check` passes with the generated renderer type committed.
- The Go DTO conformance test and the over-the-wire test both cover a FAILED
  exchange, not only an answered one.
close_reason: landed on feat/api-testing in 38261a5e

title: Watch a request go out, stop it, and read why it failed
description:
Today a run IS its answer: the row in the Response column is built from the
result of `api.request.send`, so it cannot exist before the answer does. Three
things follow, and they are one defect wearing three faces.

Nothing to show while a request is in flight — there is no object yet, so the
only signal is a disabled Send button. Nothing to stop — no party names the
exchange while it runs, so there is no handle to cancel. And a failure is not a
run at all: it comes back as a JSON-RPC error, one sentence with no request, no
route, no timing beside it, while `apisend` HAS all of that at the moment it
fails (`Send` returns `Response{}, err` and drops the composed request text, the
tracer's phases and the remote address on the floor).

The model this epic installs: a run is an EXCHANGE, and it exists from the
moment Send is pressed. It ends in one of three ways — answered, failed,
stopped — and the row is the same row throughout, filled in as facts arrive
rather than replaced when they do.

What stays a JSON-RPC error is what is NOT an exchange: an unknown handle, a
request file that will not read, a domain gate that refused. Everything that
happened to an attempt to send is a run.

## Success Criteria

- Pressing Send puts a row in the Response column immediately, carrying the
  method, the address, the environment and a running elapsed time, before any
  answer exists.
- That row can be stopped, and a stopped run says it was stopped rather than
  reporting a failure.
- A send that never landed — a name that does not resolve, a refused dial, a
  handshake that failed — is a run with the request text we composed, the route
  it went out under, how far it got and the phase it died in.
- One automated check watches a person do all three end to end.

Deliberately out: retry of a failed run, a request history that outlives the
window, and any per-request timeout setting.

title: T9.1 The renderer calls a transfer failed on results that mean running or unknown
description:
Codex final review, finding 4.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Lose the network mid-body, or have a POST answered 409: upload-flow.ts:102 routes both through store.failLocally (:114), and upload-store.ts:258 makes the phase terminally failed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A 409 means another claimant's body is running; the UI does not announce failure and does not remove the cancel surface.
- A network failure during the body leaves the transfer unsettled; only files.uploadDone settles it.
- A test for each that fails against the current code.
close_reason: Merged as 277ff282. A 409 and a network failure no longer produce a terminal failed phase — the transfer is unsettled until files.uploadDone settles it, and cancel stays offered where cancelling still means something. Genuinely local terminal errors stay terminal.

Deliberately out: renaming a request's FILE, binding a secret variable from the panel, and a global (non-per-environment) TLS switch.

title: T12.1 AD-1 records the HTTP upload route as its own amendment
description:
ADR-0036 records that file bytes travel on a streamed POST beside the WebSocket rather than on either of its planes. AD-1's own text still says it binds all frontend<->backend communication, with no exception recorded. The house convention is for AD-1 to record its amendments inline — it has been widened that way twice already (docs/architecture.md:109, :110) and ADR-0024 declares Amends: AD-1 in its header. Raised by the worker that wrote ADR-0036; the coordinator decided AD-1 does need the line.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AD-1 in docs/architecture.md records the exception inline, in the same voice and shape as its two existing amendments, and points at ADR-0036.
- The amendment says what is carried there and what is NOT: PTY bytes never leave the data plane, and control messages never leave the JSON-RPC plane.
- ADR-0036 gains an Amends header if that is what the convention requires; check ADR-0024 and match it.
- No behaviour changes and no code is touched.
close_reason: Merged as 13d8e22e. AD-1 carries the amendment inline in the exact shape of the two before it, with both halves — what the route carries and, explicitly, that PTY bytes never leave the data plane, control messages never leave the JSON-RPC plane, no msg-type is allocated for an upload, and nothing further may be added to the route without its own ADR. title: T10.1 The collision question is a kit component that knows nothing about the wire
description:
Carved out of T10 so it can be built while the transport surface is still being written: the dialog knows nothing about JSON-RPC, bindings or tickets.

title: T2.1 The sink's cleanup and retry paths tell the truth about why they failed
description:
Five defects codex found in the landed sink (3aeac879). Filed by the coordinator from an adversarial review, not from a user report.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Point the sink at an SFTP server without posix-rename@openssh.com and make Remove fail — the outcome names the stranded path and swallows the reason.
2. Make Close fail after a complete write — the temp is removed, contradicting spec section 6.
3. KeepBoth against a read-only directory — 32 round trips, then an error saying no free name.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A failed cleanup reports WHY, not only WHICH path was stranded.
- A failed Close after a complete write strands the temp, per spec section 6, instead of removing it.
- A permission or transport failure is never reported as name exhaustion and never costs 32 round trips.
- The Sink contract names who unblocks a stalled source reader on cancellation.
- Each of the above has a test that fails against the current code.
close_reason: Merged as e6b95e6e. All five codex findings closed: tryRemove now returns (paths, error) and every caller errors.Join's the cleanup reason onto the primary; a failed Close after a complete write strands the temp and removes only the reservation, per spec section 6; notCollision stops the KeepBoth search on any refusal the adapter classified, with a stated admission rule — a refusal belongs there when the next suffix cannot change the answer; the copy loop and Sink.Put document that the CALLER unblocks a stalled reader, since an io.Reader has no context. CARRY FORWARD to the transport tasks: whoever supplies the streamed POST body must close it on request cancellation, or a stalled upload never unwinds.

title: Watch a person ask the assistant to look at their session, end to end
description:
The epic nocx-avogl has four closed children and NO end-to-end check. Its own success criterion is a sentence about a person, and nobody has watched it happen:

  "A person asks the assistant to look at their session; it calls readScreen with the RIGHT session id and answers. Watched end to end, against the real backend."

AGENTS.md rule 2 is what makes this a bead rather than a nicety: every epic that is not a chore proves its happy path, and deadcode and coverage are floors that can never report a feature that is missing. Four green units are exactly the state nocx-rtg0 was in when history had no writer at all.

cmd/devharness runs the real backend headless, so there is no excuse about the harness.

What makes this checkable NOW and was not true before the epic: the model is told the session id verbatim (nocx-avogl.1), so a readScreen call carrying it passes the exact-identity scope check that used to refuse an invented one terminally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An automated check drives a real ask against the real backend, with a grant that permits readScreen, and asserts the tool was called with the session id of the pane the question was asked in — not any id, that one.
- The answer reaches the block. A run that refuses or fails does not pass this test.
- It fails if the system prompt stops carrying the session id: the assertion is on the id that travelled, not on the prompt text.

title: T4 The remote provider's sink reaches the binding, so internal/transfer is live
description:
Task 4 of .internal/plans/2026-08-21-upload-to-the-active-tab.md (commit 4e2995ed). The plan is the brief; read that task's section in full.

It translates two things: the SHAPE (ssh.FSFile vs transfer.RemoteFile — Go matches result types by identity, so a method not an assertion) and the VOCABULARY (the posix-rename sentinel), and asserts the untranslated fs.ErrNotExist contract holds in both directions. MY ACCEPTANCE CRITERION WAS UNSATISFIABLE and the worker said so rather than fudging it: -whylive on transfer.sink.Put and filesystem.handle.Upload both answer 'reachable only through reflection', because RTA cannot see a method behind a live interface — the exact blind spot AGENTS.md documents. title: Accepting a remote path completion duplicates the typed directory prefix: cd repos/t -> cd repos/repos/tabby/
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an SSH session (cwd `~`, holding `repos/tabby` and `repos/termic`).
2. Type `cd repos/t`.
3. The dropdown offers `repos/termic/` and `repos/tabby/` — already wrong: the
   display rule intends the last segment only (`termic/`, `tabby/`).
4. Accept either row.
5. The line reads `cd repos/repos/tabby/`.

## Root cause

`internal/completion/scripts/nocx_complete.bash` prints compgen's whole
replacement word in the TSV `name` column (`repos/tabby`). Both the Go contract
(`internal/completion/completer.go`, `Candidate.Name`) and the wire contract
(`contracts/shell.complete.schema.json`, `shellEntry.name`) declare `name` to be
"the last path segment for a file". `LocalCompleter` honours that; the SSH
completer does not.

The renderer's shell adapter (`frontend/src/suggest/providers.ts`,
`shellCompleteProvider`) relies on the contract: it builds
`insertText = tokenPrefix + display`, where `tokenPrefix` is the token up to the
last slash. With `name` carrying that prefix already, the prefix is doubled.

Evidence: running the script against a fixture tree emits
`path<TAB>repos/termic<TAB>/tmp/x/repos/termic<TAB>1`.

Affects every nested path completion on a remote session, including the very
common `cd dir/` step-into.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test runs the real script against a fixture tree with a nested token and
  asserts the `name` column is the last segment while `path` stays absolute.
- Accepting `repos/t` -> `repos/tabby/` yields `cd repos/tabby/`, asserted
  through the renderer's shell adapter.
- The dropdown row for a nested token displays `tabby/`, not `repos/tabby/`.
- A bare token (`re`) and a trailing-slash token (`repos/`) still complete
  correctly.
close_reason: Fixed: the remote completion script now prints the last path segment in the name column, restoring the Candidate.Name / shell.complete contract the renderer's insert path depends on. Covered by a Go test that runs the real script against a fixture tree and five renderer tests asserting the line a pick produces.

title: Choosing a folder works only where Wails does, which is neither dev-web nor a networked backend
description:
Choosing a folder must not depend on a native dialog. dialog.openFile and the new
dialog.openDirectory both go through Wails, and the dev-web harness has no Wails at all —
nor would a backend served over the network. So in two of the three configurations nocx
runs in, there is no way to choose a folder.

Orca answers this the same way and the owner pointed at it: a native dialog for the desktop
case, and its own routed tree (useFileExplorerTree over a runtime file client) everywhere
else. We already have the routed half in files.list, bound to a provider by a bindingId.

NOT IN SCOPE, deliberately: browsing a REMOTE host for a collection. internal/apicoll reads
with os.ReadFile/os.Lstat/os.Mkdir, so a collection lives on the backend machine. A picker
that offered a remote folder would advertise what the reader cannot deliver.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. make dev-web, open the API pane, create a collection.
2. There is no way to browse for a folder, because the only picker is native.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A kit component that browses directories through a caller-supplied list callback and
  returns an absolute path or null.
- It knows nothing about JSON-RPC, bindings, or which machine it reads — tested with a stub
  and no backend at all.
- Only directories are selectable; typing a path stays possible; a failed listing shows its
  reason in place and the dialog stays usable.
- The native picker remains, as an accelerator that fills the same field, not a second
  decision-maker.
notes:
Owner settled the split, and the reason is his rather than mine: a collection lives on the BACKEND's filesystem not because apicoll happens to use os.ReadFile, but because of AVAILABILITY — a collection on a remote host stops opening the moment that host is unreachable, and a collection must open always. A chosen property, not a limitation to lift later.
The PICKER itself supports every filesystem nocx can reach; it is a general dialog and the caller decides which machine. For collections the caller passes the backend-local lister.
close_reason: Done and integrated in 5e731bd3 / 654910a2. Verified on the merged tree: typecheck, lint (dead-exports all baselined, shrunk by 4), 3612 frontend tests green.

title: Opening the API pane for the first time asks you to make a collection instead of giving you one
description:

should not present a form asking you to make a collection. Postman removed its Scratch Pad
and that absence is part of the complaint this feature answers, so we ship the opposite: a
collection is already there, ready to take a request.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. make dev-web with no collections ever opened.
2. Open the API pane. It says "No collections open" and offers a form.

## Acceptance Criteria

- First open of the pane, with nothing open and no prior seed, creates a collection in the
  default location and opens it. No dialog appears.
- It is an ORDINARY collection: renameable, committable, deletable. NOTHING may branch on
  "is this the built-in one" — that condition existing at all is the defect.
- Seeded lazily on first open of the pane, never at install or app start.
- Seeded once: deleting it does not make it grow back.
- Same default location the create dialog pre-fills — one answer to where collections live.

title: A collection's location cannot be chosen with a picker: there is no directory dialog
description:

DialogService (internal/transport/ws_dialog.go:28) declares OpenFile alone. The fix is to extend that interface rather than add a second service, and to keep its cancellation contract, which is written out above the interface and is not obvious.

AND THE DEGRADE MATTERS MORE THAN THE PICKER: the dev-web harness has no Wails at all, which is the configuration this was found in, so the method is -32601 there. Typing the path by hand must stay a first-class path, not a fallback that looks broken.

title: Triage: ledger.search and ms7v.2 may be one FTS index under two beads
description:
Raised by the 2026-08-21 assistant-search design (section Risks): nocx-rtg0.21 (ledger.search: full-text over intent and derived output, with honest coverage) and nocx-ms7v.2 (Search over output: FTS across intent and derived text) both want an FTS index over the same corpus, filed under two different epics by two different routes. Neither names the other.

Two owners of one index is the defect the design section 1 exists to prevent, and it is cheapest to settle before either starts — after, it is a migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One of the two is the owner of the index, or the split between them is stated in both beads in a sentence naming what each owns.
- The decision is recorded where the next reader will hit it: in nocx-rtg0.21 and nocx-ms7v.2, not only here.
- nocx-ms7v.7 (indexing unit, substring promise) is named as upstream of whichever wins, since it is unanswered and both depend on it.

title: Brainstorming: a search tool over sessions for the assistant
description:

Two prior arts collide with it and must be dispositioned before any brief: the ms7v search epic (the person's own search over the ledger, MVP, blocked) and the one-session grant scope (policy.go:502-520, exact identity match) that a cross-session tool cannot satisfy today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The idea is disambiguated with the owner (agent tool vs the ms7v surface vs live scrollback grep).
- Every prior-art hit is dispositioned: folded in, or ruled out with the reason.
- A design section exists and the owner approved it, or the idea is deliberately dropped with the reason recorded.

title: The conversation survives, and nobody is asked to manage a window
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-21-what-the-model-is-told-design.md, sections 2, 3 and 3a. Hermes's shape (docs/micro-compaction.md), adapted to our durable ledger.

Nothing carries over between questions today: every ask assembles its own message list, so a follow-up cannot mean what it says.

## Success Criteria
- A person asks a question, then a follow-up with nothing attached, and the answer is about the same thing. They work for an hour; the conversation stays inside the model's window with no action from them. clear ends it, and the next question starts from nothing. Watched end to end.
- Head/tail/middle: the prompt and the newest turns are verbatim, and every question the person typed is verbatim wherever it sits.
- The rolling summary is a durable ledger entry with an edge to what it absorbed, so restore needs no special case.
- Tool traces ride as facts with a handle, never as their text.
- The window is fetched per (endpoint, model) where the provider reports it, and the percentage in use is shown as an estimate until provider usage is captured.

## Deliberately out

title: Attaching is a choice: the selection stops attaching itself
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-21-attaching-context-to-a-question-design.md (approved 2026-08-21). Continues nocx-4wtlh, which said of itself 'build it so it can be changed'.

Today a selection anywhere in a finished block's output raises a reference chip on selectionchange, so copying attaches; one drag across three rows stacks three chips (1-1, 1-2, 1-3 are three fingerprints); and the chip is labelled with term-line coordinates rather than what it carries.

## Success Criteria
- A person selects a word and copies it, types a command, presses Enter: it runs in the shell and nothing was attached. They drag three rows, press Attach, see those rows marked in the block and one chip naming their text; the ask carries exactly one reference. Watched end to end.
- Attaching never moves the input target.
- The floating Attach, the block menu's Attach output and the chord all raise the chip through ONE function.

## Deliberately out
- Files and images as attachment sources (their own bead, after this).
- Naming references in the prompt and a tool that reads more of a frame (their own bead).

title: A refused or failed run says what happened in our words, not eino's
description:
The owner's screenshot shows this on the answer block:
  the model failed to answer: [NodeRunError] failed to stream tool call call_7947...: agent policy: tool call refused
  node path: [node_1, ToolNode]

node_1, ToolNode and NodeRunError are the framework's internals. The product must say what was proposed, what happened to it and what the person can do; the trace belongs in the log.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A policy refusal renders a product sentence naming the tool and the reason, with no framework identifiers in it, asserted over the real error the middleware returns.
- The framework's text is logged once, at the boundary that catches it.
- A malformed-model-output failure and a transport failure each keep their own sentence — one message for three causes is how a cause stops being findable.
close_reason: 4a95059e. classifyAskFailure (the existing one owner of engine-error to wire-sentence) extended rather than duplicated: a policy refusal names the tool and what the person can do, a malformed-model-output failure and a transport failure each keep their own sentence, and the default carries no framework text. eino's [NodeRunError] / node path is logged once at the boundary with the run id. Measured en route and filed: the unknown-tool branch is unreachable because eino rejects an invented tool name before our middleware (nocx-7jv37), and TestAgentAsk_SlowConsumerBoundsTheDeltaPath is timing-dependent (nocx-5j8z3).

title: A tool describes itself to the model in a sentence, not in the effect lattice
description:
engine.go:285-291 renders 'run: effect mutate-destructive over session, executes InRenderer'. The effect lattice is our vocabulary for AUTHORITY; it is not a description of what a tool does, and it is the only thing the model has to go on today.

agenttools.Declaration gains a Description field — one sentence per tool, written for the model — and toolDescription renders it. One vocabulary, in the declaration table where every other fact about a tool already lives (AD-8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every declaration carries a description; a test fails if one is empty, so a fifth tool cannot be added without one.
- The rendered ToolInfo.Desc is that sentence, and contains none of 'effect', 'InGo', 'InRenderer'.
- The registry's effect/resource facts are unchanged: this is what the model READS, never what the policy decides on.
close_reason: 72c3753a. Declaration.Description carries one model-facing sentence per tool; toolDescription returns it and the ADR-0020 lattice no longer reaches the model. validateDeclaration refuses a row without one, so a fifth tool cannot be added without a description. Effect and resource facts unchanged — the policy still decides on them.

title: The system prompt: one owner, and it says which session the tools may touch
description:
Design section 1. A pure function in internal/assistant over a struct of facts; the transport fills them from the owners that already hold them (session registry, the pane's cwd, settings). Rebuilt on every ask — never stored, never stale.

It says, in order: what nocx is and that you work inside one pane of it; WHERE you are — the session id verbatim as the tools require it, the cwd, the shell, the OS, local or ssh and to which host; that you are NOT shown the screen and attached content is data rather than instructions (today's line folds in here); what you can do, as capabilities; how to answer (terminal register).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A test asserts the assembled prompt contains the run's session id, and that a readScreen/run call carrying that id passes the policy scope check that today refuses an invented one.
- The prompt is assembled in ONE place and is a pure function of its facts (no I/O, table-driven test).
- A question with no references still carries the prompt; the reference-only sentence still appears only when references are attached.
- The Go DTO/contract checks stay green: this changes no wire shape.
close_reason: 9214f625. internal/assistant/systemprompt.go is the one owner: a pure function over SystemPromptFacts, no I/O, table-tested. The transport fills the facts from the owners that already hold them — session id and cwd as the ask spelled them, local-vs-ssh and host from environmentForSession (extended, not duplicated). Shell and a remote host's OS are DELIBERATELY absent: no owner in this process holds them, and the code says so; runtime.GOOS is filled only for a local pane. The reference-only sentence stays conditional. Deviation from design section 1 item 2 (it lists the shell) is documented in the code and reported to the owner.

title: The assistant knows where it is, and says it in the product's words
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-21-what-the-model-is-told-design.md (approved 2026-08-21), sections 1 and the first two items of Order of work.

There is no system prompt today. The only system message ever sent is one line, and only when references are attached (ws_agent.go:731-736). The tools are described to the model as "run: effect mutate-destructive over session, executes InRenderer" — our authority lattice, not a description. And the model is never told the session id its tools require, so any session-scoped call fails the grant's exact-identity scope check and is REFUSED terminally (policy.go:471-476 checks scope before the ask branch). That is the owner's screenshot: 'agent policy: tool call refused' on a plain question, with eino's [NodeRunError] and node path leaking onto the screen.

## Success Criteria
- A person asks the assistant to look at their session; it calls readScreen with the RIGHT session id and answers. Watched end to end, against the real backend.
- The prompt is one owner: a pure function over facts the transport fills from the owners that already hold them; nothing re-derives a fact it does not own.
- Every declared tool carries a model-facing sentence from its declaration; the effect lattice never reaches the model.
- Settings carries a free-text addition, appended last under its own heading, bounded, and unable to widen a grant or turn an ask into a permit.
- A refused or failed run says what happened in the product's words; eino's node path is in the log and not on screen.

## Deliberately out
- The conversation and compaction (their own epic).
- Token accounting (deferred by the owner).
- The classifier and the autonomous run (their own epics).

title: The endpoint editor never asks the vault, so its secret pickers show secrow: handles and offer nothing
description:
Reported by the owner from a running dev stand: the Edit Endpoint dialog showed
`secrow:dd39558499fe31b5ddce0f88a5d31320` where the secret's name belongs, and the
picker offered no rows. Nothing was lost — vault.json holds that secret under the
name "openrouter API key", kind=password, and sha256(id)[:16] is exactly the handle
shown. The vault was simply SEALED (the backend had restarted; hasOSKey=false).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set up the vault with a passphrase and save an AI endpoint with an API key.
2. Restart the backend (or press Lock now) so the vault is sealed.
3. Settings -> Endpoints -> Edit the endpoint.
4. No unlock dialog appears; the API key picker shows the raw `secrow:...` handle
   as its label and its dropdown is empty.

## Cause
endpoints-section.tsx loadInventory() reads the vault status ITSELF and returns
early when it is sealed or uninitialized, so vault.inventory is never called and
the dispatcher's sealed seam (ADR-0032) never fires. passwordRows() is then empty
and secretOptions() (key-material-input.tsx:64) labels the bound-but-unlisted row
with the row handle itself.

The skip came from 96c947b5 ("the door must not ask", nocx-lyyk). It is the outlier:
connections.tsx loadSecretRows() — the SAME editor-opens-a-secret-picker shape —
calls inventory() and lets the seam raise the unlock, and says so in its comment.
ADR-0032 is explicit: needing the vault is a property of the CALL, not of the call
site; the vault raises its own unlock. An editor that must render secret NAMES is
asking the vault for data, and a caller that inspects the vault state to decide not
to ask is exactly the per-call-site logic the ADR deletes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Opening the endpoint editor (new or edit) on a sealed vault calls vault.inventory
  and the unlock dialog appears; after unlocking, the picker lists the secrets by
  NAME and the bound row is selected by name.
- Dismissing the unlock leaves the editor usable with an empty picker, and does not
  report a store failure ('unavailable') on the rows.
- An UNINITIALIZED vault is still not probed: there is nothing to unlock.
- The endpoints LIST (page load) still never raises the unlock — only an editor and
  the vault-backed operations do.
- e2e vault-sealed-probe.spec.ts covers the door raising the unlock.
close_reason: fixed on feat/ai-assistant: a93154c7, 829b4626

title: T7 raw: placements on the request, a bounded search on the response
description:
The response has no placements; saying it used the same mechanism was wrong.

Plan: `.internal/plans/2026-08-21-api-testing.md` Task 7
Spec: `.internal/specs/2026-08-21-api-testing-design.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Exact byte match renders a badge naming the secret.
- Our span with different bytes renders a damage badge naming the SHAPE, and the surviving bytes appear NOWHERE in the payload.
- Not our span renders plain text.
- No Span ever carries a secret value in any state, over the wire.
- The response search runs on the DECODED body only; it does NOT find transformed spellings and a test pins that so coverage is never overstated; overlapping matches collapse to the longest.
- A server echoing the token into an error message shows it as a badge.
- No reveal state persists across a remount.
notes:
DONE in 2261feef. Raw rides on the SEND RESULT, not a method of its own — the coordinator overruled the plan here: raw belongs to a particular run, so a second round trip could only fetch the raw of a different send, and two racing sends would swap them.
Three span states implemented; the backend ELIDES the bytes and writes a placeholder, so a renderer that ignores spans shows no credential at all.
Coordinator verified with a probe against the MARSHALLED JSON (not the struct): neither the whole secret nor its surviving 24-byte prefix crosses in the damaged case; the exact-match case carries the NAME and not the value, nor its base64 wrapping. Damage reported as 'truncated, 24 of 54 bytes'.
Worker caught a case not in the brief: an empty value would match at every offset and turn the whole body into badges. And wrote the paired negative test — 'does not find a base64-wrapped spelling' — so 'finds an echoed token' is never read as more than it is.
Frontend follow-up was needed: run-list rendered text and never read spans, so the badges did not exist. Found by the dead-exports ratchet on the MERGED tree, not visible from either branch. Fixed; the kit grew a 'damaged' variant rather than the surface growing its own span.
close_reason: Done, 2261feef. Raw rides on the send result (coordinator overruled the plan's separate method: raw belongs to one run). Three span states; coordinator probe against the MARSHALLED JSON confirms neither the secret nor its surviving prefix crosses in any state. Frontend renders the spans as kit chips including a damaged variant.

title: Amend ADR-0020: a grant's subject may be a pane, not only an execution
description:
`authority_grants.execution_id` is `NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES executions(id)`, so today a grant belongs to an agent run. A sandboxed pane needs the same object with a different subject.

Decide between generalising the subject (`pane_id` beside `execution_id` with a CHECK that exactly one is set) and a parallel relation, and amend ADR-0020 §5/§7 deliberately — not inside a feature branch, which is why #91 went back to draft.

title: A sandboxed pane holds a grant, and the workspace minted it
description:
PR #91 models the sandbox as `panes.ephemeral` — a boolean naming the consequence ("do not restore") and dropping the cause: this pane's authority was granted once, interactively, and cannot be re-granted without asking.

ADR-0020 §5 already decided the shape: the workspace mints a default grant from its policy and is NOT the enforcement object, because "dragging a tab must never silently confer or revoke the right to write to production". `authority_grants` and `grant_scopes` exist; `resource_kind` already includes 'path'. The gap is the subject — `authority_grants.execution_id` is NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES executions(id), so a grant belongs to an agent run.

Ruled out during the #91 review, recorded so nobody re-derives them: PaneKind (orthogonal, and SSH sandboxing is coming); EnvironmentKind (a sandbox is a constraint on a place, not a place); no pane row at all (leaves entries.pane_id null and the tab ungrouped); `closed_at` (window membership, enforced live by renderFromLayout); a single-column pane_sandbox table (a flag with extra steps).

`workspaces.payload` is already a declared sparse extension, so the workspace half needs no schema change.
acceptance_criteria: A user opens a tab whose filesystem authority came from its workspace's policy, narrowed once at launch, and one automated check watches them do it: the workspace carries a policy, the pane carries the grant minted from it, and after a restart that pane does not come back as an ordinary shell — with no boolean in `panes` saying so. Explicitly out: agent-lane grants changing behaviour, SSH sandboxing, and any re-minting of a grant without asking.

title: Two blinking carets in the command editor after repeated Backspace
description:
Reported by the owner (2026-08-21, macOS build): after pressing Backspace
repeatedly in the command editor, TWO blinking carets appear at once — one at
the start of the input line, one further right. Both blink.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not yet reliable. Observed once: type in the composer, press Backspace
repeatedly/rapidly. The screenshot shows the composer card (location + cwd
chips, the `Run` gutter token) with the right-hand caret sitting well past
where an empty document would place it, plus a second caret at the line
start. Whether Backspace is causal or coincidental is unknown; so is whether
a split or a tab switch preceded it.

## What the code says so far (investigation, not a fix)

- The composer uses the NATIVE caret: editor.ts installs no `drawSelection`,
  so `.cm-cursor` is never rendered (the theme rule at editor.ts:236 is
  vestigial). A native caret only paints in the FOCUSED element, so two
  blinking carets cannot both belong to one CM6 view.
- Only two `new EditorView` sites exist (editor.ts:338, cm-host.ts:139) and
  cm-host is never mounted on the terminal surface. One CommandEditor per
  pane (terminal-content.ts:1318).
- xterm cursor is unlikely: `cursorInactiveStyle: none` (renderers/xterm.ts:303,
  the fix for the earlier "second cursor" defect, item 9), `cursorBlink`
  defaults to false, and at an idle prompt `.xterm-live-container.live-idle`
  is `height: 0; overflow: hidden` — nothing of the grid can paint there.
- Prior art for two composers painted at once: editor.ts `show()` documents an
  inline `visibility: visible` that repainted an inactive pane editor on top
  of the active one at the same coordinates.
- No custom blinking element: the only `@keyframes` near the composer are
  pulses and spinners, none caret-shaped.

## Next evidence needed

A DOM dump taken WHILE both carets are on screen: `document.activeElement`,
every `.nocx-editor` rect + computed display/visibility + `.cm-content` text +
whether it carries `.cm-focused`, the `.xterm.focus` count, live-container
heights, visible input/textarea count. Asked of the owner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The root cause is named, not guessed: one mechanism that explains a SECOND
  BLINKING caret given that the composer paints only the native one.
- An automated check reproduces the two-caret state before the fix and fails
  after it — a spec that asserts the observable (one caret-owning surface
  focused / one composer painted), never a duration.
- Repeated Backspace in the composer leaves exactly one caret, at the
  document position the text says it should be.
close_reason:
Fixed in 9d6af2f9. Root cause named: not a second caret but a stale painting of the one native caret — it did not blink, sat where the caret stood before the erase, and cleared only on a forced repaint, with a clean DOM at the time. WKWebView does not always invalidate the rectangle it painted the caret in when the inline widget beside it (the completion ghost) is removed; CM6 leaves the DOM selection alone because isEquivalentPosition walks across the line's trailing
and calls offset 0 and offset 1 the same place. drawSelection makes the caret a DOM element and turns the native one transparent, so no browser-painted rectangle exists to be left behind. Verified by the owner in the macOS app.

title: The sandbox cannot start on a non-FHS Linux: runtime read-only roots blow the 256 cap
description:
`runtimeReadOnlyRoots` adds one read-only root per PATH binary directory and per ELF RUNPATH/DT_NEEDED library directory. Under FHS those collapse into a handful; under Nix every store path is its own directory. Measured on the dev host: 339 roots against `maxRoots = 256`, so every sandboxed launch fails `-32007 "policy exceeds 256 roots"`. The same shape threatens a Homebrew-heavy macOS, where each formula owns its own Cellar prefix.

It fails closed, which is the right direction, but the feature is dead on a whole distribution and the message names an internal bound rather than anything a user can act on.

## Steps to Reproduce
On NixOS, `go test -run 'TestNewLocal_SandboxedEndToEnd' ./internal/sandbox/` — "policy: sandbox: policy exceeds 256 roots". A probe calling `runtimeReadOnlyRoots(os.Getenv("SHELL"), os.Environ())` returns 339 roots with a nil error.
acceptance_criteria: A sandboxed shell launches on a Nix-style host, or sandbox.status reports a typed, actionable reason before the action is offered.
close_reason: Fixed on PR 91 (feat/sandbox-current) in the review-fix pass.

title: Measure: does a shell request survive a refused exec on the same channel
description:
Design section 6.4 names this row as the one that must be PROVEN, not assumed. P4 cannot state its outcome and the superseding ADR cannot be written until a fixture answers it. Measurement only: no product code, no carrier change.

## Acceptance Criteria

A fixture test against a real sshd opens a session channel, obtains a pty-req, has an exec request REFUSED, and then issues a shell request on that SAME channel; the test records whether the shell request succeeds and whether a usable prompt follows. The same sequence is run against the in-process gossh fixture and any divergence between the two is recorded. The answer is written back into design section 6.4 as a stated outcome rather than a promise, and is available for P7 to carry into the superseding ADR.
close_reason: Measured. exec-refused on a channel that already holds a pty leaves the channel and the pty usable: shell on that same channel reaches a working prompt on the same connection with no second authentication — conditional on the refusal arriving as (false, nil) rather than (false, io.EOF), which is the discriminator an implementer branches on. Found in the process: a stock OpenSSH server cannot be made to refuse exec at all (five restriction mechanisms all accept and substitute), which produces an outcome section 6.4 has no row for and which is strictly worse than a refusal — the channel is consumed and no native prompt exists on any channel of that connection. Proposed as a sixth row via P7.

title: P10 The installed fact is read, or it is deleted
description: Discovered while writing the design. InstalledFactStore.Get has no non-test caller - deadcode answers 'reachable only through reflection' - while the comment above it promises that the delivery planner reads it. The fact is written and never read. This is the repo's named failure shape: a live write path whose read is dead.
acceptance_criteria: deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive on the reader either shows a path from main, or the reader and its unused half are gone. No comment in the tree promises a consumer that does not exist.
close_reason: Landed in ba13cd97 on worktree/quiet-cloud-3a8d; full pre-commit gate green including the containerized go test -race run.

title: P9 An integrated session starts like a login the user recognises
description: Design section 9. Because we pass a command rather than asking for a shell, sshd does a quiet login: no banner, and hushlogin never consulted. Verified: no tier and no Go file mentions motd or hushlogin. The bash tier additionally runs interactive NON-login, so /etc/profile and ~/.bash_profile are never read - on a managed fleet that is the deviation that bites.
acceptance_criteria: Against a fixture with /etc/motd an integrated session of each tier prints it exactly once, and nothing when ~/.hushlogin exists. For each tier a variable exported only by /etc/profile is observable in the integrated shell, OR that tier and that reason appear in a declared-deviation allowlist checked by the same test. Every declared deviation is readable through the real wire result the product consumes.
close_reason: Landed in 1585e053 on worktree/quiet-cloud-3a8d; full pre-commit gate green including the containerized go test -race and vitest runs.

title: P8 End to end: a typed ssh and a saved connection both reach an integrated prompt, and the command carries nothing
description: Design section 0. This is the check that reports a missing feature - the unit tests cannot. Written against the seam a person actually reaches.
acceptance_criteria: The epic's acceptance check, automated: over a fixture sshd both paths reach an integrated prompt; the recorded exec request for each is under 1 KiB with no generation data and no secret; with MaxSessions 1 both reach a working prompt, un-integrated, named, with one authentication.

title: P7 The superseding ADR, and the two binding texts this changes
description: Design section 10. ADR-0022 was right on its own terms - the only prize was the visible line's length. What changed: integration at first contact is no longer mandatory, and the command line acquired costs it did not weigh. We want multiplexing for a different reason than it was measured against.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0022 is superseded by an ADR that names its two dead premises, the new reason multiplexing is wanted, and the spike's implementation traps. ADR-0024 is amended with what the capability defends and against whom. The delivery-modes design loses first contact as an argv event. The observable consequence of a control socket and a master process outliving the typed command is declared.
close_reason: Landed in 1585e053 on worktree/quiet-cloud-3a8d; full pre-commit gate green including the containerized go test -race and vitest runs.

title: P6 Command discovery is bounded and shared instead of re-run on every session
description: Design section 8. NOT disabled - the owner rejected default-off, and there is no measurement that the scan has harmed a host. Cache is backend-owned and in memory only: it dies with the application. Invalidation is by event, not clock: the mtime of each PATH directory, at most 32 stats per session, with a 1h backstop. Today the 250ms budget stops only WAITING, and exit cleanup group-kills only when the job is a group leader.
acceptance_criteria: The scan's deadline terminates the whole process group including a member that ignores TERM and requires KILL, and every member is reaped. A timeout publishes no partial snapshot; a cache hit starts no second scan; a cache older than its bound is not served as current. Each of running, ready, stale, timed-out, failed maps to a distinct asserted user-visible string.
close_reason: Landed in d86ab983 on worktree/quiet-cloud-3a8d; full pre-commit gate green including the containerized go test -race and vitest runs.

title: P5 Ordering, loss and refusal: nothing is minted before it can be used, and every refusal is named
description: Design section 6. The ordering exists to close a mutation race, NOT to let the publish decide validity - after a failed publish the far side may still accept a generation installed earlier. Terminal states are integrated, conventional(reason) and session-failed(reason); the third is not a variant of the second. Also carries the recovery fence's own backend-copy events: its expected value lives until recovery acknowledgement or teardown, not necessarily until the capability's events.
acceptance_criteria: Nothing is minted before the lifecycle receiver is ready and the publish attempt has reached a terminal outcome: with the lifecycle channel refused, no capability and no fence are ever generated. Each row of the refusal matrix produces its named reason. Each loss interval produces its outcome and the three loss events are distinguished. A session moves out of starting to a terminal state within the integration deadline on every path.
close_reason: Landed in 1585e053 on worktree/quiet-cloud-3a8d; full pre-commit gate green including the containerized go test -race and vitest runs.

title: P4 A typed ssh is wrapped, its own connection becomes the master, and there is never a second authentication
description: Design section 4.3-4.4. Mux-only, no fallback: the spike measured that sftp -o ControlMaster=auto silently opens its own connection and re-authenticates under MaxSessions 1. Reuse of a master the user owns is REJECTED, not deferred - liveness is not identity. DECISION GATE: this bead also settles by fixture whether a shell request survives a refused exec on the same channel, and does not close until that answer is written back into the design section 6.4 and the ADR.
acceptance_criteria: On the typed path no publish, no minting and no remote mutation occurs before the mux handshake proves ownership of that specific socket. With the socket refused, exactly one authentication is recorded and no second TCP connection appears. Against a fixture with MaxSessions 1 the session reaches a working prompt with a named refusal and one authentication. Every option the user gave is preserved with its semantics and the exit status exactly. The master's ownership interval closes: after the last owned session ends the master exits and the socket is removed within 5s of injected time.
close_reason: Landed in 1585e053 on worktree/quiet-cloud-3a8d; full pre-commit gate green including the containerized go test -race and vitest runs.

title: P3 The publisher works to numbers, and the residue of a failed attempt is bounded in aggregate
description: Design section 7. DECISION GATE: N is not implemented against until it is measured, brought back, written into the design and approved. This bead does not close while N is still a letter. Today the publisher polls a lock every 25ms for 5s, breaks it, and polls another 5s - roughly 400 metadata operations per waiter.
acceptance_criteria: Fault injection at every FS-seam boundary including a failing cleanup: the manifest is byte-identical to before the attempt and owned residue is at most one staging slot. A second attempt against un-clearable residue creates no second slot. 100 concurrent local calls for one destination produce one remote publish; across processes at most one commit per content digest. Lock probes number at most K and total at most 1.55s of injected time; a singleflight waiter performs none. The measured maximum FS-seam calls and bytes on each path is at or below the ceiling recorded in the design, and the source constant equals that measured maximum.
close_reason: Landed in ba13cd97 on worktree/quiet-cloud-3a8d; full pre-commit gate green including the containerized go test -race run.

title: P2 The loader and stage-1: a bounded frame carries the code, an unlinked descriptor carries the secret
description: Design section 4.1 and 5.2. The loader is the SOLE owner of the original termios and installs traps before the first stty; stage-1 never re-saves it. LOADER_READY and STAGE_READY are distinct. Includes the failure paths the mechanism creates: absent or unreadable /dev/fd/N, a failed source, closing the stage descriptor, and a signal between a successful digest check and the start of sourcing. A regular file, not a pipe - launcher_bash.go:190 records why.
acceptance_criteria: Stage-1 is delivered as a frame of at most 32 KiB; over-cap and digest mismatch are each refused. Paired hasher cases: sha256sum present succeeds, only shasum present succeeds, neither yields stage-digest-unavailable with no stage-1 executed. No filesystem directory entry naming secret-bearing storage ever exists: unlink precedes the first write, and a failed unlink results in no write at all. On every catchable exit path the restored termios byte-equals the saved termios and cleanup run twice behaves as cleanup run once.
close_reason: Landed in ba13cd97 on worktree/quiet-cloud-3a8d; full pre-commit gate green including the containerized go test -race run.

title: P1 The managed path emits one short carrier, and the full argv launcher is retired from it
description: Design section 4.1-4.2. Today shellStartCommand (internal/ssh/ssh_real.go:763) runs EnsureInstalledRemote, discards its result, and returns the full self-installing launcher regardless. Grammar, not just length: an encoded payload must not be able to satisfy the assertion.
acceptance_criteria: shellStartCommand emits the same carrier whether the preceding publish succeeded, failed or was not attempted. For every ShellKind the command matches an explicit allowlist grammar and is under 1 KiB. A fixture recorder storing the exec request as one field, limited to 1 KiB, accepts every command we emit and refuses today's.
close_reason: Landed in ba13cd97 on worktree/quiet-cloud-3a8d; full pre-commit gate green including the containerized go test -race run.

title: A far shell is integrated without the bundle or a session secret ever entering the SSH command
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-20-integration-delivery-carrier-design.md — read it first;
it is committed alongside this epic and was reviewed to approval before decomposition.

WHAT A USER CAN DO THAT THEY COULD NOT BEFORE: a host reached by typing `ssh` by hand
comes up integrated, through a connection nocx owns.

The managed path today delivers the bundle twice — over SFTP, and then again inline in an
~89 KiB SSH exec command (measured: auto 91,198 B, against our own 120 KiB cap). That
command also carries the per-epoch capability and the recovery fence verbatim, so both
reach the far host's process arguments where a same-user descendant reads them while they
are still valid.

This epic moves the bundle and the secrets onto channels and leaves a short, honest command
that still says what was run. It also stops treating a typed `ssh` as a separate delivery
mode: the axis is whether we own a channel, not how the user expressed the intent.

DELIBERATELY OUT: the relay tier; a compiled remote helper; compression or minification of
any payload; hiding the exec request from a recorder; reuse of a multiplex master the user
owns.

SHIPPING SHAPE (owner's decision): the epic lands as ONE change. No partial release, and
the PR is opened only after every child is implemented — in particular there must be no
interval in which the command is already short while a secret is still inside it.

TWO ANSWERS COME FROM MEASUREMENT, NOT FROM THIS BRIEF, and their packages do not close
without them: whether a `shell` request survives a refused `exec` on the same channel
(P4's fixture, written back into the design and the ADR), and the real ceiling on remote
FS operations (P3 measures, the number is approved into the design, only then is code
written against it).
acceptance_criteria: Over a fixture sshd, a typed `ssh` and a saved connection both reach an integrated prompt, and the exec request recorded for each is under 1 KiB and contains neither generation data nor a session secret. With the fixture's MaxSessions at 1, both still reach a working prompt, un-integrated, with a named reason and exactly one authentication. A taint canary placed in the capability and the recovery fence appears in none of: the emitted command, the far host's argv, the environment, any directory entry under any remote root written to, product logs, or shell history.
close_reason: All eleven packages landed on feat/nocx-m8jwn-channel-carrier (PR #103, https://github.com/shady2k/nocx/pull/103). All eight CI jobs green: ci-mac, ci-backend and ci-linux in both keyring variants, ci-frontend, and both ci-e2e browsers. The section 0 check is asserted end to end -- a typed ssh and a saved connection both reach an integrated prompt over a fixture sshd, the exec request each records is 952 bytes against a 1 KiB bound and carries neither generation data nor a bearer, and with MaxSessions at 1 both reach a working prompt un-integrated with a named reason and exactly one authentication. The taint canary is checked per surface and found on none: the emitted command, the far host's argv read from inside the process that holds it, the environment, the remote home and the session's temporary directory by name and by content, product logs, shell history, and the terminal. Merge is the owner's; this bead tracks the work, not the merge.

title: [bug] Window geometry is never saved: the sampler is gated on a probe of a window Wails v3 has not created yet
description:
Every launch opens at 1024x768 whatever the user last set — nocx-mqie.1 regressed
by the Wails v3 move (nocx-mgbjx), and the evidence is on disk: uistate.json has
sidebar and activeTab written correctly while `window` is all zeros.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch the app, resize the window, quit.
2. Launch again.

Observed: the default 1024x768. `~/.config/nocx*/uistate.json` shows
`"window": {"width":0,"height":0,...}` while `sidebar` and `activeTab` next to it
are current.

## Root cause

`WailsApp.restoreWindow` (main.go) probes the window ONCE and returns early when
the probe cannot answer:

    _, displays, ok := probe.Geometry()
    if !ok { ...warn...; return }   // <- the Watch goroutine below never starts

In v3 `WebviewWindow.Size()` returns (0,0) while `w.impl == nil`, and `impl` is
created in `WebviewWindow.Run()`. `application.App.Run` starts services FIRST
(application.go:677 startupService -> our ServiceStartup -> restoreWindow) and
only afterwards launches the pending window runnables, in goroutines
(application.go:~748). `window.Show()` in main() is a no-op before Run because
`globalApplication.impl == nil`.

So at ServiceStartup the window does not exist, Geometry reports ok=false, and
the early return skips `go store.Watch(...)` for the WHOLE session. Nothing ever
samples the window, SetWindow is never called, and the document keeps its zeros.
Restore then reads zeros and yields the default on every launch.

This is a one-shot probe at the one moment it cannot succeed. v2 gave a context
at OnStartup when the window already existed, which is why the ported code
worked there and not here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Window size and position restore across a restart (the nocx-mqie.1 contract
  again), on a build using the v3 shell.
- The sampler starts even when the first probe cannot answer — a window that is
  not realised yet is an ordinary state, not a reason to abandon persistence for
  the session.
- Restore is applied once the window can actually report a geometry, not once
  before it exists.
- A test asserts the sampler still runs and records after a probe that answered
  `ok=false` first.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed against the Wails v3 source and the on-disk document):
application.Run starts services first (application.go:677 startupService) and
only afterwards launches the pending window runnables, in goroutines (~L748).
WebviewWindow.Size returns (0,0) while w.impl == nil, and impl is created in
WebviewWindow.Run. window.Show() before shell.Run() is a no-op
(globalApplication.impl == nil). So restoreWindow's single probe in
ServiceStartup always answered ok=false, and its early return skipped
`go store.Watch(...)` for the whole session.

Evidence: ~/.config/nocx-dev/uistate.json carried a current sidebar and
activeTab beside "window": all zeros.

FIX: uistate.Store.RestoreAndWatch — one loop, readiness waited for rather than
required; first successful probe places, every later one samples. Store.Watch
removed (no callers left). main.go keeps two adapters (wailsWindowProbe,
wailsWindowPlacer) and no policy.

Tests were run against the reinstated old shape to confirm they detect it.
Reachability confirmed: deadcode -whylive traces main -> App.Run ->
startupService -> ServiceStartup -> restoreWindow -> RestoreAndWatch.

NOT VERIFIED BY ME: the on-screen result on macOS. This box is Linux and has no
display; the mechanism is asserted by unit tests, not by watching a window
reopen.
close_reason: Window geometry restores again. restoreWindow probed the v3 window during ServiceStartup, before the platform window exists (Size() answers 0,0 while impl is nil), read ok=false as failure and returned before starting the sampler — so nothing was ever recorded and uistate.json kept the zeros every launch restored. uistate.Store.RestoreAndWatch is now one loop that waits for readiness rather than requiring it; Store.Watch removed (no callers). Tests verified against the reinstated old shape. Commit b9cfbe65. NOT verified on macOS by me: this box is Linux and headless.

title: The vertical tab row reserves width for a close button that is not there
description:
The vertical strip's rows truncate their title (and subtitle) about 36px early.
The owner's screenshot at the default 240px strip:

  1  vm-agents: worktree-g…
     herdr --remote dev@192.16…

with visibly empty row to the right of the ellipsis.

CAUSE. `.tabstrip-vertical .nocx-tab-label` (frontend/src/styles/components/tab.css)
carries `margin: 0 26px 0 calc(22px + 10px)`. The 26px on the right is room for the
close button — but that button is `position: absolute; right: 4px; opacity: 0`
(`.nocx-tab > .ui-icon-button`), so it is out of flow and invisible until the row is
hovered. 26px of margin plus the row's own 10px padding is 36px taken from every
label in the strip, permanently, for something that is never in the flow.

This is the same defect the horizontal strip already fixed and wrote down, in the
rule immediately above: "The right one does NOT reserve room for the close button —
that button is `opacity: 0` until the tab is hovered and it sits absolutely on top,
with the hover gradient behind it... Reserving 24px for something invisible was 24px
taken from every label in the strip, permanently, and it is what turned a narrow tab
into `ho…`." The vertical rule was written later (a7908ca6) and did not inherit it.

Second, smaller thing in the same two rules: `.tabstrip-vertical .nocx-tab-label` is
declared TWICE (tab.css:187 and :418) at equal specificity. The first sets
`margin-left: 24px` and the second's `margin` shorthand overrides it whole, so the
earlier rule is dead — and its comment ("no index digit to clear") is no longer true.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Settings > Interface > tab placement: vertical.
2. Open a tab whose title is longer than the row (a path, or a remote command).
3. Pointer away from the strip.
4. The title ellipses with ~36px of empty row to its right.

## Acceptance Criteria
- With the pointer away from the strip, the vertical row's label right edge is
  within the row's own 10px padding of the row's right edge, measured in a real
  browser (Playwright) — jsdom computes no layout and cannot see this (nocx-4wbx).
- The close button still reveals on hover and still closes the tab.
- Exactly one rule sets `.tabstrip-vertical .nocx-tab-label`'s margins.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #98: the vertical label's 26px right margin (room for an out-of-flow, opacity:0 close button) is gone, leaving the row's own 10px padding as the gap; the dead duplicate margin-left rule went with it. Measured in a real browser via e2e/tabs.spec.ts — right gap 36px before, 10px after, chromium and webkit.

title: Context menu rows show no icon in the packaged macOS app
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the packaged macOS app (WKWebView).
2. Open the tab strip's "More" menu, or right-click a tab, or right-click a
   row in the file tree.

Every row's label sits indented past an icon column that is reserved and
empty — no glyph anywhere. The same menus in the dev stand (Chromium) show
the marks. Owner reported it with two screenshots; the sidebar and tab-strip
icons render correctly in the same frames, so it is the menus specifically.

## Root cause

The kit's icons are inline `<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">` components carrying no
`width`/`height` attribute — that is what lets one component serve a 12px row
and a 24px button — so the SLOT has to state the size. Every icon slot in the
stylesheet does: `.ui-search-field__icon svg`, `.ui-toast__icon svg`,
`.ui-tree-row__type-icon svg`, and nine more. `.ui-context-menu__icon` is the
only one that does not.

With no rule, the svg falls back to its intrinsic size as a flex item.
Measured under both engines against a real mount of the kit's ContextMenu:
Chromium resolves it to the slot's 14×14; WebKit resolves it to 0×0. The slot
itself is 14×14 in both, which is why the labels are still indented.

Not catchable in jsdom: the element is in the document either way and only its
box is empty.
acceptance_criteria: A Playwright spec opens the strip menu and a tab's own menu on the real app and asserts each row's icon svg has a non-zero rendered box. It fails on the webkit project before the fix and passes on both projects after.
close_reason: Fixed in 312338b9: .ui-context-menu__icon svg { width: 100%; height: 100% } — the same rule the other eleven icon slots already carry. Regression spec e2e/context-menu.spec.ts covers the strip menu and a tab's own menu; verified red on webkit (icon svg width 0) and green on both projects after. nocx-oak7b carries the lint ratchet.

title: The Linux install path is the read-only AppImage mount, so self-update can never apply and every start warns
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the released AppImage on any host.
2. Every start logs:

   WARN update reconcile at startup failed error="reconcile: lock error:
   open lock file /tmp/.mount_nocx-0LDJJDO/usr/bin/.nocx-update.lock:
   read-only file system"

## Diagnosis

main.go:194 derives the install path from os.Executable(). Inside an AppImage
that is the squashfs mount (/tmp/.mount_nocx-XXXXXXX/usr/bin/nocx), not the
.AppImage file the user launched. upgradeInstallPath() walks up looking for a
.app and otherwise returns the executable verbatim -- its comment says "the
executable itself (the AppImage)", which is true of a bare binary and false of
every distributed AppImage.

The consequence is not only the warning. internal/update/updater.go:130 puts
the flock beside the install path, which is read-only, so reconcile fails on
every start; platform_linux.go:60 Preflight checks that same read-only
directory is writable; and Exchange (platform_linux.go:153) renameat2's the
install path, so even past those it would swap a file inside the mount rather
than the user's AppImage. The Linux half of ADR-0007's self-update has
therefore never been able to apply an update in a shipped artefact -- while
Settings goes on offering the control (AGENTS.md: a soft degrade must be
visible in the product, not only in a log).

The AppImage runtime exports APPIMAGE (the absolute path of the .AppImage file)
and OWD; platform_linux.go already reads APPIMAGE for its Preflight refusal, so
the fact is available at the composition root and is simply not used there.
acceptance_criteria:
Assertions:

1. With APPIMAGE set, the updater's install path equals $APPIMAGE, not
   os.Executable(); with APPIMAGE unset the behaviour is unchanged.
2. Starting the shipped AppImage produces no "reconcile at startup failed"
   warning, and the lock file appears beside the .AppImage file.
3. Preflight's writability check is applied to the directory holding the
   .AppImage; Exchange targets the .AppImage file.
4. A failure path: when the directory holding the .AppImage is genuinely not
   writable (e.g. /opt owned by root), the user sees the refusal in the UI, not
   only in the log.

title: The composer does not change height when you type the first character
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a fresh tab on macOS (the packaged app, WKWebView).
2. Look at the composer card at the bottom with an empty draft.
3. Type one character.

The whole card — chip row, Run token, the prompt line — jumps down by 10px,
and the scrollback that hangs from its top edge moves with it. Owner
reported it with two screenshots five seconds apart; measured off those
screenshots, the card is 86.8px empty and 76.8px with one character.

## Root cause

Measured, not inferred. base.css styles `::-webkit-scrollbar` at 10px, so
scrollbars in this app are CLASSIC, not overlay — they take layout space.
CM6's `.cm-scroller` carries `overflow-x: auto`, and WebKit reserves a 10px
horizontal-scrollbar gutter for the empty document and never re-evaluates it
until the document changes. Chromium does not.

Proven by bisection in a real browser (Playwright, both engines) against an
isolated mount of the real CommandEditor: setting the scrollbar to 20px
makes the gap 20px; `overflow-x: hidden` on the scroller removes it in
WebKit and changes nothing in Chromium.

The composer runs `EditorView.lineWrapping` with `word-break: break-word`,
so it can never scroll sideways — the horizontal scrollbar it reserves room
for cannot ever appear.
acceptance_criteria: A Playwright spec on the real app asserts the composer card's height is identical with an empty draft and after one character is typed. It fails on the webkit project before the fix and passes on both projects after.
close_reason: Fixed in 35b5f128: .nocx-editor .cm-scroller gets overflow-x: hidden. The composer wraps, so the horizontal scrollbar WebKit was reserving 10px for can never appear. Regression spec in e2e/command-editor.spec.ts — verified red on webkit (86.796875 vs 76.796875, exactly the 10px of ::-webkit-scrollbar) and green on both projects after.

title: Integrate PR 91 sandbox with current main
description: Port the final PR 91 sandbox behavior onto the current workspace/pane architecture without restoring deleted TabManager ownership. Reconcile ADR numbering, preserve backend-authored fail-closed policy and session identity, and make sandbox panes explicitly non-restorable while retaining durable pane/workspace/history identity.
acceptance_criteria: PR 91 is mergeable onto current main; sandbox panes use PaneManager and carry paneId/workspaceId; restart cannot reopen a sandbox pane unsandboxed; ADR IDs are unique and references current; generated contracts and tracker export are regenerated through their owners; focused tests, native sandbox smokes, browser verification, make ci-full, gosec, and npm audit complete with no task-introduced blocker.

Local task-specific e2e passed 112/112 after fresh-main merge; real Landlock source smoke passed enforcement + PTY end-to-end. Inherited scans remain tracked by nocx-0lita and nocx-l3pk; local serial WebKit flake investigation recorded as nocx-6wayi, while hosted WebKit is green.
