title: The local-zsh launcher test asserts a snapshot that the shell is allowed to defer
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Push anything that runs ci.yml.
2. `ci-backend` fails, sometimes in one matrix variant and sometimes in both:

   ```
   --- FAIL: TestLocalZshSession_IsIntegratedOnTheUsersOwnShell (1.46s)
       launcher_local_zsh_test.go:444: no OSC 636 hello/snapshot —
       completion would never learn a command name: "…"
   ```

   The dumped output CONTAINS `\e]636;H;` and does not contain `\e]636;S;`.
   The hello is there; the snapshot is not.

Observed three times on 2026-08-20 across two commits — both variants of one
run, then with-secret-service of another. Passes locally in 0.10 s, and 10
consecutive local runs are green.

## Actual

The snapshot is BEST EFFORT AT A PROMPT and the test treats it as synchronous.
`__nocx_snapshot_pump` (internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.zsh) runs at
every prompt boundary: if the source-time background job has finished, it
emits; if not, the FIRST prompt waits `__nocx_snapshot_wait_ms` and then, in
the script's own words, "on timeout the payload is left for a later prompt
rather than delaying this one".

`__nocx_snapshot_wait_ms` defaults to 250 ms, and the comment above it says
what that number is for:

    250 ms is a budget for a HUMAN's prompt, so a test that asserts the
    mechanism would otherwise be asserting that a loaded runner finished
    inside a UX deadline.

That is exactly what this test does. It runs one command and asserts on
`636;S`, so it passes only when the background build — which enumerates
commands, builtins, functions, reswords and aliases and sorts them — finishes
inside a UX deadline on a shared CI runner.

`NOCX_SNAPSHOT_WAIT_MS` exists for precisely this and ten tests in
scripts_exec_test.go already set it to 15000. The launcher tier never
inherited it.

## Not proven, stated rather than glossed

The failure could not be reproduced locally, including with
`NOCX_SNAPSHOT_WAIT_MS=1`: this machine finishes the background build before
the first prompt looks, so the budget never binds here. The case rests on the
script's documented degrade path matching the observed output exactly (`H`
present, `S` absent), not on a local reproduction. CI is the only place that
can confirm it.

## Residual

Raising the budget widens the margin rather than removing the last race: a
build that outlives 15 s would still leave the payload for a later prompt. A
fully deterministic version would drive prompts until `636;S` appears. That is
deliberately not done here — the env override is the mechanism this package
already has for this question, and adding a second one beside it is what
AGENTS.md's "look for the existing answer" section is about.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given the CI backend job, when it runs on three consecutive pushes, then
TestLocalZshSession_IsIntegratedOnTheUsersOwnShell passes in both matrix
variants each time.

title: The workspaces e2e asserts a design that was withdrawn before it ran
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run e2e/workspaces.spec.ts on feat/workspaces.
2. It fails on its first assertion: `.nocx-workspace-chip .ui-button` is
   expected visible on a fresh stand, and no such element exists.

## Actual

The spec is written against workspaces-ux §4.3, which was WITHDRAWN before it
ever ran. §4.3 gave the horizontal strip ONE chip: the default wore it too with
an empty label, and every other workspace was reachable only through that
chip's dropdown. The spec asserts exactly that — a visible chip with
`toHaveText('')`, and a switcher menu it drives every later step through.

The shipped design is the rework: every workspace is a pill IN the row, one
click switches, a workspace's own actions live on its pill's context menu, and
THE DEFAULT DRAWS NO PILL AT ALL (§4.2 — it draws no chrome). The unit test over
the same seam, frontend/src/panes-workspaces.test.ts, asserts the opposite of
this spec ("gives the default workspace no pill at all, whatever else exists")
and is green.

So the epic's headline e2e check and the unit tests beneath it were
contradicting each other, with the unit tests right.

## Why it went unnoticed

nocx-isoph was closed on 2026-08-18. The first CI run in feat/workspaces'
history was 2026-08-19 — every prior run skipped, because the PR was a draft and
every job in ci.yml is guarded on `!draft`. So the epic's "one automated check
has watched a user do it end to end" (AGENTS.md, testing rule 2) was never
actually watched: 143 commits went unchecked by e2e.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a fresh stand, when the spec runs, then it creates a workspace from the
strip menu, switches to it by clicking its pill, closes it from that pill's
context menu, and asserts throughout that the default workspace draws no pill —
and it passes in the containerized chromium run.
close_reason: Fixed in 09fa9911. workspaces.spec.ts rewritten against the shipped rework: every workspace is a pill in the row, one click switches, actions come from the pill's context menu, the default draws no pill, and a folded workspace's tabs stay in the row hidden — so the spec counts what is SHOWN. Passes in the container.

title: The e2e suite's sidebar state crosses spec boundaries, and its panel helpers toggle
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. On feat/workspaces, run the containerized chromium suite.
2. e2e/git-panel.spec.ts alternates down the file: :71 passes, :117 fails,
   :157 passes, :196 fails, :247 passes, :293 fails — nine failures in all.
3. Every failure is the same: `[data-testid="git-branch"]` resolves to the
   right element with the right text, and is `hidden`.

## Actual

`resetStand` (then `resetLayout`) reset the workspace/tab/pane chain between
specs and nothing else. Since nocx-mqie.1 the sidebar's collapse and its
ACTIVE VIEW are a second persisted document (uistate, ADR-0033), so a spec that
opened Git left Git open for the next one — and every activity-bar button is a
TOGGLE, so the next spec's `click()` closed the panel instead of opening it.
Pass and fail then alternate, because each run flips the state the next one
inherits.

Same cause, second shape, INSIDE one spec: e2e/notes.spec.ts:105 opens the
panel, reloads the page, and opens it again. The reload brings the panel back
by itself, so the second "open" closes it. A between-tests reset cannot help
there; the helper has to be idempotent.

Also reached: sidebar.spec.ts:47 (`#sidebar` is `collapsed` when the test
expects it open), ports-row-width.spec.ts.

## Expected

A spec starts from the state a fresh profile is in, whatever the previous spec
did; and a helper called "open the panel" opens it rather than toggling it.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given the containerized chromium suite, when it runs twice at the same commit,
then git-panel.spec.ts has no failures and the failing set is identical between
the two runs. Given a spec that reloads the page with a sidebar view open, when
it asks for that view again, then the panel is open — not closed.
close_reason: Fixed in 05cc398f. resetStand resets the UI-state document alongside the pane chain, so the sidebar's active view no longer crosses a spec boundary; showSidebarView is idempotent for the single-test case (notes reloads mid-test and the panel comes back by itself). git-panel went from nine alternating failures to none, twice.

title: A context menu takes the keyboard and never gives it back
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open nocx. The prompt editor has focus.
2. Click the tab strip's "More" (the chevron beside +).
3. Pick "Quick connect…".
4. Press Escape to dismiss the picker.
5. `document.activeElement` is `<body>` — the caret is gone from the prompt.

Measured in the e2e container, one probe per step:
editor -> `BUTTON.ui-context-menu__item` -> `INPUT.ui-search-field__input` -> `BODY`.

## Actual

The kit's ContextMenu focuses its first row on open — it has to, the rows are
keyboard-walkable — and never restores focus to whoever held it.

This was invisible while every row's action did its work and vanished: focus
fell to `<body>` and `terminal-content.ts`'s document-level key rescue caught
the next keystroke. It became visible when the tab-strip rework (nocx-isoph.5)
made "Quick connect…" a menu row. The picker that row opens records
`document.activeElement` as the element to restore when it closes — that was
the MENU ITEM, unmounted by the time the picker closed, and `focus()` on a
detached node is a silent no-op.

## Expected

Escaping an overlay opened from a menu row puts the keyboard back where it was
before the menu took it — the prompt the person had been typing in.

## Note on the fix

Restoring BEFORE the row's `onSelect` runs is the load-bearing half: `onSelect`
is what opens the next overlay, and that overlay reads `document.activeElement`
to decide where to return focus later. An outside pointerdown is excluded — it
is on its way to a new owner, and pulling focus back over the top of it would
make a click somewhere else land somewhere else again.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given the prompt has focus, when a person opens the strip menu, picks a row
that raises an overlay, and dismisses that overlay, then focus is on the prompt
— asserted at the ContextMenu seam (three unit tests: item activation, Escape,
and the outside-click exclusion) and end to end by
e2e/quick-connect.spec.ts "Escape closes the picker and restores focus to the
prompt".
close_reason: Fixed in 808a034b. ContextMenu now restores focus to its opener, and does so BEFORE the row's onSelect runs — onSelect is what opens the next overlay, and that overlay reads document.activeElement to decide where to return focus later. An outside pointerdown is excluded: that pointer is on its way to a new owner. Three unit tests at the seam (item activation, Escape, the outside-click exclusion) and e2e/quick-connect.spec.ts end to end.

title: README and make init still tell you to run `wails dev`, which v3 removed
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Clone the repo on macOS, run `make init`. It closes with "Ready. Run 'wails dev' to start the app".
2. README's Getting started says the same: `wails dev`, and `NOCX_DEVTOOLS=1 wails dev`.
3. Run it. v3's binary is `wails3`, and it answers `open ./build/config.yml: no such file or directory`.

## Cause
The Wails v3 migration dropped the CLI dev loop — the Makefile says so itself at :46, 'v3 has no dev CLI without a Taskfile, and replicating the watcher is not worth inventing one for'. There is no Taskfile in the repository and no build/config.yml; .gitignore:26 ignores /build/* wholesale, so no clone can ever have one. The run instructions were not migrated with the build.

## Fix
README and the make init message name `make dev` (and `make dev-web` for frontend iteration), which is what actually runs the app: the frontend build the embed requires, then `go run`.

## Also found, deliberately left to its own bead
AGENTS.md:45 tells an agent that on the default e2e path 'playwright.config.ts applies it to the wails dev backend'. playwright.config.ts:18 says wails is not started there at all — it starts cmd/devharness. That paragraph is about the $HOME isolation guarantee, so correcting it needs the isolation re-verified rather than the words swapped.
acceptance_criteria: Given a fresh clone, when make init finishes, then the command it names starts the application. Given README's Getting started, when a reader follows it verbatim, then the app runs and the devtools variant opens the inspector. No instruction in README names a wails CLI command that this build does not have.
close_reason: README's Getting started and make init's closing line now name make dev (and make dev-web for frontend iteration), with a note saying plainly that there is no wails dev, why, and what make dev does instead. The stale AGENTS.md claim about playwright.config.ts applying $HOME to a wails dev backend is left to its own bead: it is about an isolation guarantee and needs the guarantee re-verified.

title: A closed tab or pane is marked closed, never deleted
description:
## Why
Two things are wrong today and they are the same thing. A clean start (restore.onStartup off) leaves the stored rows alone, so the next launch with restore back ON reopens the tabs of the session BEFORE the clean one, and every clean-start session piles its leftovers on top of that. And an ordinary Cmd-W already DELETEs the row, which nulls entries.pane_id (ON DELETE SET NULL) — so today every close permanently loses that pane's blocks anchor. The session-search surface we want next would be built on a store that forgets.

The owner's decision: panes and tabs are NEVER deleted, only marked closed. Workspaces ARE deleted when their last open tab leaves (whether an empty workspace should survive as furniture is a separate, open question).

## The schema conflict this creates, and its answer
tabs.workspace_id is NOT NULL REFERENCES workspaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. If workspaces are still deleted, the cascade takes the closed tabs with them and the panes after that — exactly what the marking exists to preserve. So the column becomes nullable with ON DELETE SET NULL, and the invariant is stated as a CHECK: an OPEN tab is always in a workspace, a CLOSED tab may have outlived its workspace. Same shape and same reason as tabs.parent_id, which is already ON DELETE SET NULL for provenance.

## Scope
- closed_at INTEGER (NULL = in the window) on tabs and panes. Not on workspaces.
- Every close path marks instead of deleting: DeleteTab, DeletePane, dissolveTabIfEmpty (layout_sqlite.go:382, :643, :743).
- dissolveWorkspaceIfEmpty keeps DELETing the workspace once its last OPEN tab has gone; the default workspace keeps its exemption.
- Every read that feeds the window filters closed_at IS NULL — that read IS the window set.
- The clean start (panes.ts readLayoutWithoutAdopting) marks the leftovers closed instead of only hiding them behind notShown, so what the chain holds is always the last session.
- Bump schemaVersion (internal/content/sqlite.go, currently 10) in the same commit — that is the whole migration protocol here, and the file is rebuilt rather than migrated.
- entries.pane_id survives a close, a clean start and a workspace deletion.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tab with panes, when it is closed, then its rows still exist with closed_at set and entries.pane_id still resolves to the pane. Given a closed tab, when the chain is read, then it is not in the window set and the strip does not draw it. Given restore.onStartup off, when the application starts, then the leftovers are marked closed, and when it is turned back ON and the application restarts, then only the tabs of the clean session reopen. Given a workspace whose last open tab closes, then the workspace row is deleted and its closed tabs survive with workspace_id NULL, their panes intact and their blocks still anchored. Given an OPEN tab, then it always has a workspace.
close_reason: closed_at on tabs and panes; every close marks, every window read filters; workspaces still deleted with tabs.workspace_id nullable + CHECK; ClearWindow wired from the composition root for the clean start; schemaVersion 10 -> 11. Commit 36582bdc on worktree-agent-a7497ee47d7cad97c.

title: A sealed vault is reported as "no password is stored", and the loop never ends
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Save an ssh connection's password (Remember), so the profile references a vault secret.
2. Restart the application. The vault starts sealed.
3. A restored ssh pane asks for the password, saying "no password is stored for this connection".
4. Answer it with Remember on: the save needs the vault to WRITE, so the sealed error surfaces there, the unlock dialog appears, the open is re-sent — and asks for the password again.

## Cause
addPasswordMethods swallowed the secret lookup's error (a log.Debug and nothing else), so a sealed vault produced no savedPassword rung and the ladder fell through to the prompt. The prompt's reason is derived from the absence of that rung, so it stated the one thing that was not true.

## Fix
The lookup's ErrVaultSealed / ErrVaultUninitialized is propagated out of buildAuthChain, before the dial. The transport already maps it to reason=vault-sealed; the renderer raises the unlock it owns and the dispatcher re-sends the open, which then finds the stored password. Every other lookup failure is still a skipped rung.
acceptance_criteria: Given a profile with a stored password and a sealed vault, when a session opens, then the open fails with reason=vault-sealed and no ssh password prompt is raised. Given the vault is then unlocked, when the open is re-sent, then it authenticates from the stored secret and asks nothing. Given a profile whose bound secret no longer exists, when a session opens, then the prompt is still raised and still says no password is stored.
close_reason: ErrVaultSealed/ErrVaultUninitialized from the stored-secret lookup now propagate out of buildAuthChain before the dial, so the existing vault-sealed seam raises the unlock and the dispatcher re-sends the open. Every other lookup failure is still a skipped rung. internal/ssh suite green; pre-commit gate green.

title: A slow ssh dial holds the session gate, so every other pane's open is refused
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Restore a workspace with several ssh panes, or open a second pane while one ssh handshake is waiting on its password prompt.
2. Observe the renderer's "The terminal is busy — that action was refused. Try again in a moment." toast, and panes that die with "Terminal failed to start: Control plane busy".

## Cause
capability.NewOpenOperation composed [config, session] gates with the lane and held all three for the WHOLE open, dial included (the conservative grain open.go's own comment offered to refine). The gates are capacity one and wait DefaultDomainConflictWaitTimeout (1s); an ssh handshake takes seconds, and one waiting on a human takes as long as the human does. Every other open — and every config, vault, git and files request — is refused after that second.

## Fix
The open is two-phase: Prepare resolves the profile under [config, session] (store and vault reads), Dial opens the session under the execution lane alone. Canonical acquisition order survives the split.
acceptance_criteria: Given an ssh open whose dial is in flight, when a second pane opens, then it is not refused with control-saturated. Given the same, when a config or files request arrives, then it is not refused. The canonical gate order is unchanged: no phase holds the lane while waiting on a domain gate.
close_reason: Two-phase open: Prepare resolves under [config, session], Dial holds only the lane. Regression test at the production wait bound (an in-flight dial refuses neither a config mutation nor a second open) proven red without the fix; the two acceptance tests that used a blocked dial as a gate-holder now hold the gate with a blocked resolve. Full internal/transport, internal/capability and internal/ssh suites green; pre-commit gate incl. containerized go test -race green.

title: Closing the overview leaves the keyboard on the button that opened it
description:
`OverviewController.close()` called `restoreFocus(entry)`, handing the keyboard
back to whatever was focused when the overview opened. That is the ordinary
dialog contract and it is wrong for this surface, in both directions:

- OPENED FROM THE TOOLBAR BUTTON: the keyboard returns to the button, which
  keeps a visible focus ring and swallows every keystroke. Typing a command
  does nothing at all, with no indication why. This is what the owner reported.
- OPENED, THEN USED: `overview-panel.tsx:173` calls `port.activate(paneId)` and
  `props.onClose()` back to back, so `restoreFocus` takes the keyboard AWAY
  from the pane the person just chose from a card. Same cause, worse effect,
  and nobody had reported it.

The overview covers the whole workspace. There is nothing behind it to return
to except a pane, and WHICH pane is a question only the application can answer
after the fact — frequently not the one it was opened from. So the surface
must not restore an invoker; it must hand input to the pane in front.

This is AGENTS.md's "two surfaces may never own the same input" with the loser
still advertising: the button goes on holding focus it can do nothing with.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Click the overview button in the activity bar.
2. Press Escape.
3. Type. Nothing is entered; the button still carries the focus ring.

And the second path:

1. Open the overview, click a card for another pane.
2. The pane activates, then loses focus to whatever opened the overview.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Closing the overview leaves the keyboard in the ACTIVE pane, whichever way it
  was closed — Escape, the close control, the backdrop, or choosing a card.
- Choosing a card leaves the keyboard in the pane that card selected.
- Opening by the keyboard chord and closing with Escape still lands typing in
  the pane, as it already did.
- The intent is expressed through `OverviewPort`, not by reaching into
  PaneManager from the controller, and the fake carries it so it is testable.
close_reason: Fixed at 5c35548a on feat/workspaces. close() asks the port for focusActive() instead of restoreFocus(entry): the overview hands the keyboard to the pane in front, which is the pane a card selected when a card was used. New intent on OverviewPort, implemented in PaneManager, counted by the fake. cameFrom is still recorded for a nested overlay to restore to. Verified by unit test through the fake; the three interactive paths (button+Esc, button+card, chord+Esc) were confirmed by the owner in the running app. NOT covered by an e2e spec.

title: The composer's reserved box costs an inline TUI four rows of pane
description:
The composer (`.nocx-editor`) is a `flex:none` sibling of the scroller inside
`.pane`, so whatever height it holds, the terminal does not get. Measured live:
pane 721px = scroll area 644px + composer 76.8px.

At submit the composer must give up KEYBOARD ownership — the running program
needs stdin, and ADR-0004 forbids sniffing the byte stream to find out whether
it wants it, so the handoff is unconditional. `nocx-i4h04` made it give up the
keyboard WITHOUT giving up the box: `suspend()` sets `visibility:hidden` +
`inert` and stays a flex item. The reason was real — the scrollback hangs from
the scroller's bottom edge (`.scrollback-inner` has `margin-top:auto`), so
releasing 76.8px moves the whole history in one frame, and that jump is what
`nocx-i4h04` was filed against.

WHAT IT COSTS, and why the trade is now wrong. An inline TUI on the NORMAL
buffer pays the box permanently. `top` (procps) does not use the alternate
screen; `htop` does. So `htop` enters `enterFullscreen()`, which releases the
box AND hides the block chrome, and gets the whole pane. `top` does the same
job and gets neither: 644 - 56.5 header - 28.5 padding = 559px, about four rows
fewer than the pane can show. That is the same asymmetry `nocx-6w4z` declared
closed — "two programs doing the same thing looked like two different
products" — closed only on the alternate-buffer side.

THE TRADE HAS AN EXPIRY AND NOBODY NOTICED IT PASS. `b97d30b3` reserved the
box; `a8aebec4`, the very next commit, added the settle glide, which answers
the same question better — the displacement is played back as a 140ms
transform instead of being designed away. Two answers to one problem, and the
static one is simply older. The owner has now reported the reserved box a THIRD
time; `editor.ts` records the previous two in `suspend()`'s own comment.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX JITTERS. Removing the reservation alone brings the jump
back, because the glide does not cover it: at Enter, `commit()` hides the
editor and then `actions.submit()` synchronously reaches
`ScrollbackController.beginBlock`, which opens a `_glide` of its own. Two
glides for one transition, and the second calls `_cancelGlides()` — killing the
first mid-flight. Neither ever sees the whole displacement.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `top` in a pane and count its rows; compare with `htop` in the same pane.
   `top` is short by about four, and a strip of dead canvas sits under it.
2. Remove the reservation (`suspend()` -> `hide()`) and press Enter on `ls`:
   the scrollback jumps rather than settles.
3. With the box released, let a command finish: the composer returns, takes
   77px back, and the last rows the command printed stay hidden behind it,
   because `overflow-anchor: none` is set on the scroller deliberately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `top` on the normal buffer gets the same pane height `htop` gets on the
  alternate buffer, less only the running block's header.
- Pressing Enter settles rather than jumps: emptying the draft, releasing the
  composer's box and opening the running block are ONE glided displacement.
- A command finishing leaves its last printed rows visible — the composer's
  return does not hide them — and does not drag a person who had scrolled up.
- The keyboard handoff is unchanged: `hide()` still runs before `submit()`, so
  the grid is writable before a byte can flow (nocx-u7uh.23).
- `suspend()` and its `data-suspended` attribute are gone, with the tests and
  comments that prescribed them.
close_reason: Fixed at 397b6284 on feat/workspaces. The composer leaves the layout at submit (hide(), box and all), and commit() settles around the whole transition — clearing the draft, releasing the box, opening the block — so one displacement gets one glide. beginBlock split into the glided public call and a raw beginBlockNow, because nesting _glide leaves two animations on one element. The composer's return holds the bottom via scrollToBottomIfFollowing, called inside the mutation. suspend() and data-suspended removed with the four tests and two comments that prescribed them. Verified: 349 targeted unit tests, full frontend vitest via the pre-commit hook, and e2e/command-editor.spec.ts 5/5 in the container (chromium). NOT verified in CI.

title: The restore e2e's happy path does not pass yet: no restored block appears after a restart
description:
e2e/restore.spec.ts is written and its OFF half passes: with the setting off,
a restart gives one fresh tab, nothing restored, no boundary. The ON half is
test.fixme and this bead is why.

## Steps to Reproduce

Remove the test.fixme in e2e/restore.spec.ts and run:
PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/restore.spec.ts

Observed: after the backend restart and reload the tabs come back, and
'.pane.active [data-restored="true"]' is never found.

## What is known

The spec has already earned its place — it found two real defects that 3431
unit tests did not, both now fixed and covered:

1. The one-shot restore was spent on the FIRST setVisible(true), which
   arrives before the pane has a scrollback to draw into. No unit test could
   see it: a test shows a pane that is already mounted.
2. A restore that raced the reconnect after the restart recorded 'could not
   ask' as 'there was nothing', and the pane then had no past for the rest
   of the session. blocksForPane now throws rather than swallowing, and the
   pane retries on the reconnect report.

After both, the page still shows no restored block. The page's own log
during the run carries no capture failure and no restore failure, which
means the read answered with an empty page rather than erroring.

## The next step, so nobody repeats the guessing

Establish which end is empty, and do it with evidence rather than by
reasoning: either the first session never captured (no entries with that
pane_id) or the second session asks with a pane id that does not match. The
cheapest instrument is a diagnostic that prints the block's frozen class
before the restart (a running block never records) and, after it, the
paneId the read used against the ids the layout snapshot returned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test.fixme is removed and the spec passes in the container.
- Whatever is found is fixed in the product, not by weakening the spec: the
  assertions are the epic's own promise.
close_reason: Verified this session: PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/restore.spec.ts — 3 passed (45.7s), including the ON half that carried the test.fixme. The fixme is gone from the spec and the assertions were not weakened. What was found is written where it was fixed: neither end was empty — both blocks were written and ledger.query answered for exactly those pane ids — the read was never issued, because a restored pane is activated BETWEEN Pane.start() and the renderer being built, so its one show found no scrollback and 'not yet' had no 'later' (a page load is not a reconnect). mount() is the later.

title: A critical environment must produce a row and no artifact, and capture does not check it
description:
The epic's own acceptance says it: 'An environment marked critical produces a
row and no artifact' (design §7.4). CaptureOutput honours history.outputEnabled
and entries.sensitivity, and does not yet read the criticality of the
observation its execution pinned.

It is the same shape as the other two refusals and lands in the same place —
decided inside the transaction, answered as (false, nil) so the ack says the
body was not kept and the renderer stops sending chunks rather than treating a
privacy rule as a failure.

Filed rather than folded into nocx-y0pmn because it is a behaviour, not a
test: the round-trip check would have asserted a rule that was not there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A command whose execution pinned an observation with criticality='critical'
  stores its entry and no artifact; CaptureOutput answers stored=false and no
  error.
- routine and sensitive observations are unaffected.
- The refusal is read from the execution's OWN pinned observation, not from
  the environment's latest: what mattered is what was true when it ran.
close_reason: CaptureOutput reads the criticality of the observation the execution PINNED (joined from environment_obs_id, not the environment's latest) and stores no body when it is critical, answering (false, nil) like the other two refusals. The entry is untouched. Committed 58ede6fa.

title: A layout reorder test still expects the numbering nocx-h2xbu changed, so internal/transport is red on a clean tree
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

go test ./internal/transport/ -race -run TestLayoutReorderRefusesANonPermutation

Observed: FAIL — 'reordered = [{...0002 Position:1} {...0001 Position:2}], want
ws-2 first'. Red on a clean tree, with nothing staged.

## What is wrong

The ORDER is right and the POSITION is what the test still expects from before
nocx-h2xbu. That bead made the default workspace keep position 0 and the
user's workspaces be written after it — 'THE DEFAULT IS NOT A MEMBER OF THE
ARRANGEMENT', in ReorderWorkspaces' own words — so the first user workspace is
at position 1 now, and the assertion still reads Position != 0.

The test was not updated with the commit that changed the numbering (dd979129
on feat/workspaces). It has been failing since, which also means the
pre-commit hook's go test -race stops any Go change in this package until it
is fixed. Found while implementing nocx-2noew, whose diff does not touch
layout at all — verified by stashing and watching it fail on the clean tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test asserts the numbering h2xbu decided: the first user workspace comes
  back at position 1, not 0, and the default is not a member of the
  arrangement.
- The refusal half of the test is untouched: a partial permutation is still
  -32602 and still moves nothing.
- go test ./internal/transport/ -race is green.
close_reason: The reorder test now expects position 1, the numbering h2xbu decided. internal/transport green. Committed 2c6ac9e2.

title: Enter and Right took the same completion row through one call, so Enter could not stop
description:
Two keys took the selected completion row through one call, and the footer
named them differently: '↵ to insert' and '→ to accept'.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Type 'cd ' so the dropdown opens with directories.
2. Select one and press Enter.

Observed: the directory is inserted and the list REOPENS one level down —
Enter walked. Expected: Enter takes the row and stops. The only way out of
the walk is Escape, which dismisses the surface that is helping you.

## What is wrong

Both keys ran apply(), which re-queried whenever the row was a directory. One
behaviour advertised as two is the shape AGENTS.md names: the loser goes on
advertising what it cannot deliver.

THE SPLIT: apply() takes a walk flag. Enter and a click STOP — they take the
row and close, and the next Enter, on a command now sitting in the line where
it can be read, runs it. Tab, Right and End WALK — a directory taken with
them re-queries, so a path is walked with one key. The footer says '→ to
accept and continue'.

The same shape the recall overlay has after nocx-w7h.4's reversal: the first
Enter takes, the second runs. One rule across both surfaces over the input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Enter on a directory row inserts it and closes the dropdown; no re-query
  follows and the list does not reopen.
- Right or End on the same row inserts it and the list shows what is inside.
- Tab with exactly one match walks it, for the same reason.
- A click behaves as Enter does.
- The footer names the two keys apart.
close_reason: apply() takes a walk flag: Enter and a click stop, Tab/Right/End walk a directory, and the footer names the two keys apart. Committed 6a8ef29a.

title: A frozen block's body is captured in one transaction
description:
Plan: .internal/plans/2026-08-19-output-capture.md Task 2. CaptureOutput resolves the entry's execution and writes the artifact and its chunk together; the caller cannot do it because the two must land in one transaction and it does not have the execution id. AppendChunk gains a seq rather than reading MAX(seq)+1, which makes the agent's delta path idempotent too — its handler already has the number, and a second append method would be two owners of one table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fresh artifact id writes one artifacts row against the entry's execution and one chunk; byte_len equals the body length.
- The same call again writes nothing and returns nil: one chunk, byte_len unchanged.
- The same artifact id with a different media type is ErrIDConflict and nothing changes.
- An unknown entry id is ErrNoSuchEntry and nothing is written.
- With history.outputEnabled off the call succeeds and no artifact appears.
- Chunks arriving out of order both land and Artifact returns them in seq order.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fresh artifact id writes one artifacts row against the entry's execution and one chunk; byte_len equals the body length.
- The same call again writes nothing and returns nil: one chunk, byte_len unchanged.
- The same artifact id with a different media type is ErrIDConflict and nothing changes.
- An unknown entry id is ErrNoSuchEntry and nothing is written.
- With history.outputEnabled off the call succeeds and no artifact appears.
- An entry whose sensitivity is 'sensitive' stores no body, by the same shape. Nothing sets that column today, so the check is correct and currently unreachable; it is written now because the alternative is remembering it on the day sensitivity becomes settable.
- Chunks arriving out of order both land and Artifact returns them in seq order.
close_reason: CaptureOutput lands the artifact and its chunk in one transaction against the entry's own execution; idempotent on (artifact,seq) via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with byte_len moved only on a real insert; AppendChunk takes its seq, which makes the agent delta path idempotent too; output-off and sensitive both return nil and store nothing. Seven tests in ledger_capture_test.go. Committed 8593c05c.

title: The per-command output cap is the user's, and the ceiling is the backend's
description:
Plan: .internal/plans/2026-08-19-output-capture.md Task 5. history.enabled, history.retentionDays and history.outputEnabled already exist and already reach content.Policy through policyFromSettings and app.go's notifier; only the cap is new. The total-size and age knobs belong to nocx-rtg0.30 and are not touched here — two epics writing the same four knobs is the one-owner defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- history.outputCapKB exists in the History section, default 256, bounds 16 to 4096, and reaches content.Policy without a restart.
- The renderer caps at the configured value: with the setting at 16 KiB a 100 KiB body arrives capped and sealed truncated='cap'.
- The backend refuses an artifact past 1 MiB whatever the setting says.
close_reason: history.outputCapKB declared (256 KB default, 16-4096 bounds), wired through policyFromSettings and app.go's live notifier into content.Policy, and read by the renderer through output-cap.ts — the renderer applies it because cutting text on a character boundary is its job (AD-6). A test asserts the settings default and content.DefaultOutputCapBytes are ONE number. The size and age knobs stay nocx-rtg0.30's. Committed f19be7bb.

title: The block's rows are emitted three ways from one walk
description:
Plan: .internal/plans/2026-08-19-output-capture.md Task 1. serializeRange does four things beyond emitting spans — joins wrapped rows, trims the trailing empties, trims the leading band readline erased, skips empty runs — and a second implementation of those four would drift from the first, showing up as a restored block that does not match the block a person saw. So the walk moves into one internal function and three emitters differ in nothing else. SGR needs the RAW cell colour (mode plus value), not CellAttrs, whose fg/bg are already resolved against a theme snapshot: resolving here is what would bake the old palette into a restored block.

## Acceptance Criteria

- serializeRangeText over a range returns the characters with no markup and no escape sequences.
- serializeRangeSGR emits the 16-colour short form, the 256-palette form and the 24-bit form, and its SGR-stripped output equals serializeRangeText's.
- One test drives the same lines through all three modes and asserts the same row count: the join and both trims cannot disagree.
- Every pre-existing serializeRange test still passes — the HTML path is byte-identical after the extraction.
close_reason: One walk, three emissions: collectRunsOf over any attribute type and walkRange over any row emitter; serializeRangeSGR and serializeRangeText added, the HTML path byte-identical (3383 frontend tests green). Committed b3fa7685.

title: A frozen block sends what it printed
description:
Plan: .internal/plans/2026-08-19-output-capture.md Task 4. The bodies are parked on the BlockRecord rather than sent at freeze, because the artifact hangs on an entry and the entry id arrives with the history.record ack — a different event that may land before or after the visual freeze. attachRecordedAck already solves that ordering with afterVisualFreeze, and this rides it instead of inventing a second mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Freezing a block sets rec.captured with the SGR body, the plain body and the dimensions the serializer saw.
- An ack carrying entryId sends application/vt first and then text/plain with derivedFrom naming the first artifact.
- A body over the cap keeps the head and the tail, drops the middle, and both calls carry truncated:'cap'.
- A body over 64 KiB is sent as several calls with increasing seq whose bodies concatenate to the whole.
- A failing call is logged and lost: nothing about the block changes and no error reaches the person.
- An ack with no entryId sends nothing.
close_reason: The visual freeze parks the SGR and text bodies on the record with the grid the serializer saw; attachRecordedAck sends them against the ack's entryId through the afterVisualFreeze parking nocx-ggha already built, clearing the field so a block cannot be captured twice. capture-client owns the cap (head+tail on a character boundary), the chunking at the wire ceiling, and the stop on stored=false. 12 unit tests plus one that drives the whole path the way a person does. Committed 38c044d8.

title: ledger.capture takes a frozen block's body
description:
Plan: .internal/plans/2026-08-19-output-capture.md Task 3. The method follows ws_ledger_query.go's shape: no params schema, the handler is the check. Ceilings are input validation and not a preference — 64 KiB per chunk, 1 MiB per artifact — because a renderer is untrusted whatever the user's setting says.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A capture for a known entry answers stored:true; the same call again answers stored:true and the store holds one chunk.
- A body over 64 KiB is -32602 and the message names the ceiling; an artifact that would exceed 1 MiB is -32602.
- A mediaType outside {application/vt, text/plain} is -32602; an id that is not a UUIDv7 is -32602.
- With the content store unwired the method answers -32601, like every other ledger.* method.
- TestLedgerCapture_OverTheWireConformsToContract validates the real result off the real socket against contracts/ledger.capture.schema.json.
close_reason: ledger.capture registered beside the other ledger reads: params validated (UUIDv7 artifact id, the two media types, seq from 1, per-message ceiling), capture method owned by the method rather than the caller, per-artifact ceiling checked inside the transaction, and the ack carries stored so retention-off is an answer rather than a failure. Six wire tests including the contract validated off the real socket.

title: The epic's happy path: the output of a past command is still readable
description:
Plan: .internal/plans/2026-08-19-output-capture.md Task 6. deadcode cannot report that a feature is wired — on an interface-first tree RTA counts every method a live interface value can hold as reachable — so this is the check that watches the feature happen. It is the shape nocx-rtg0 shipped wrong once: a store with no writer, under a green ratchet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Through the real socket: record a command, capture its body, close and reopen the content store, read the body back, and the bytes match what was sent.
- Entry A's artifact holds A's body and none of B's, asserted by capturing two blocks back to back.
- With history.outputEnabled off the entry is stored, no artifact appears, and the ack says stored:false.
- deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive on sqliteContent.CaptureOutput prints a path from main(), pasted into the bead beside a contrast run on a method that is not wired.
acceptance_criteria:
- Through the real socket: record a command, capture its body, close and reopen the content store, read the body back, and the bytes match what was sent.
- Entry A's artifact holds A's body and none of B's, asserted by capturing two blocks back to back.
- With history.outputEnabled off the entry is stored, no artifact appears, and the ack says stored:false.

Renderer half asserts the freeze parks both bodies and that a command printing nothing parks an EMPTY body rather than none — no classifier anywhere in the capture path. Committed 5ede798d.

title: A fast command's freeze snaps instead of gliding: the settle turns following off
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a command that finishes FAST — on a local shell, inside the ~140ms the
   settle takes. The owner's machine: 27ms from Enter to the frozen block.
2. Watch the block header.

Owner's capture, 2026-08-19, after nocx-i4h04.2 landed:

```
E+  0ms  top=644  blockH=57  live=8  suspended
E+ 11ms  top=641
E+ 19ms  top=629          <- the settle for the block opening, gliding
E+ 27ms  top=561  blockH=84  live=0  shown   <- 68px in one frame
```

The opening glides. The freeze does not: it snaps 68px.

## Cause

The pane decides "am I following the output" with an `IntersectionObserver`,
and it watched the live region. `IntersectionObserver` reports the TRANSFORMED
box, and the live region is INSIDE `.scrollback-inner` — the element the settle
displaces. So while the first glide was unwinding, the observed element was
outside the scroller and the pane concluded the person had scrolled away.

`_following` false has two effects, and the invisible one is worse than the
visible one: every later glide is skipped (movement the person did not cause is
not theirs to watch), and `setLiveHeight` stops scrolling to the bottom as
output arrives. A long command would have stopped following its own output.

It reproduced only where a command finishes inside the settle it started. In
the e2e container the backend round trip is ~900ms, so the glide had always
finished and the observer had always recovered before the freeze — six
commands, two runs, all clean, and the defect sitting underneath them.

## The fix

A one-pixel sentinel, a SIBLING of the stack rather than a descendant, with a
matching negative margin so it costs the layout nothing. The observer watches
it. Where the output ends is a fact about layout; it must not be answered by an
element whose paint the settle is deliberately moving.
acceptance_criteria: The element the follow observer watches never leaves the scroller while a settle is unwinding — asserted structurally in controller.test.ts (the sentinel is a sibling of the stack, not a descendant) and measured in the container (max distance below the scroller's bottom edge stays negative across two commands).
close_reason: The follow observer watches a one-pixel sentinel that is a sibling of the stack, not a descendant, so a settle can no longer make the pane read as scrolled-away. Container: the sentinel stays inside the scroller for every frame of every settle where the live region reached +59. Commit b168e662.

title: The block flicks back a row when a command finishes, and every change to the pane is a jump
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. At a prompt, run any command — `ls`, `seq 1 10`, `printf 'A\nB\nC\n'; read x`.
2. Watch the block's header.

Expected: it takes its place and moves as one motion.
Actual (owner's own frame capture, 2026-08-19, `580 → 542 → 561`): it rises as
output arrives and drops back one grid row the instant the command finishes —
9ms apart, which the eye reads as a flick rather than as two movements.

## Cause

Two things, and they compose.

**The live region reserved a row the block would not keep.** The frozen body
ends at the render fence; the shell has by then moved the cursor one row past
it, onto the row the NEXT prompt will occupy, and `liveContentHeight` counted
the cursor deliberately. So the running region was exactly one row taller than
the block it becomes.

**And every change to the pane's height was instant.** The stack of blocks
hangs from the bottom edge of the scroller, so a block opening, output
arriving and a block freezing each displace the whole history at once.

## The fix

The cursor row is no longer counted — `liveContentHeight` measures written
rows, and null now means "cannot measure" where 0 means "nothing written yet",
which were one value and had to stop being one.

And the pane MOVES rather than jumping: FLIP on the two elements of the stack,
140ms, `prefers-reduced-motion` and not-following both skip it. What animates
is a transform, which takes no part in layout — the `transition: height` that
was tried and removed re-laid the box on every frame of output and never
finished.

Three things had to be right for the glide not to invert:
- the origin is the last PAINTED position, not the current layout: within one
  task the live region can take a row and the freeze give it back, and neither
  state is ever drawn;
- the in-flight transform is cancelled BEFORE the mutation, so a
  `scrollIntoView` inside it reads layout rather than the offset the glide is
  hiding;
- the freeze only scrolls for a block taller than the viewport, which is the
  case that call was written for; for one that fits it was a second owner of
  the scroll position.

## Measured

Container, chromium, 605px scroller, 20px cell, six commands, two runs: every
path monotone. `true`, `ls`, `seq 1 10`, a three-line printf, a five-line
dripped loop and a shell-side hold — the header never moves back down, and the
hold and dripped cases now freeze with no movement at all.

## What is deliberately given up

A program waiting for input on a row it has written nothing to shows no cursor
until the first keystroke — `read x` with no prompt is the case; `read -p` is
not. The owner took that trade against the frame capture, 2026-08-19.
acceptance_criteria: Submitting a command moves the block header monotonically — it may rise as output arrives and must not fall back at all (one pixel of rounding), asserted in command-editor.spec.ts after the settle has finished; and the movement is a 140ms transform glide, skipped under prefers-reduced-motion and when the pane is not following.
close_reason: Cursor row no longer counted (liveContentHeight measures written rows; null vs 0 split), and the pane glides to its new geometry with FLIP — painted origin, transform cancelled before the mutation, scroll only for a block taller than the viewport. Container, six commands, two runs: every path monotone; hold and dripped freeze with zero movement. Commit a8aebec4.

description: Project strict host-HOME descendants from the backend-authorized sandbox workspace and explicit RO/RW grants into the isolated runtime HOME as disposable symlink aliases. Preserve native target rules as the sole access-class authority; do not scan, copy, mount, or special-case applications. Linked implementation for PR 91.
acceptance_criteria: Sandboxed shells resolve eligible explicit host-HOME grants through their usual ~/ paths on Linux and macOS while native RO/RW enforcement remains authoritative; required homeProjections metadata is exposed end to end; source and packaged native smokes prove RO, RW, nested, and retarget-denial behavior; documentation and contracts are updated.

title: The block does not settle when a command is submitted: the running region and the frozen block are not the same box
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a pane and let it reach a prompt.
2. Type `seq 1 10` and press Enter.
3. Watch the block's header.

Expected: the header takes its place and output fills in below it — moving up
as a terminal scrolls, never back down.
Actual: it sits still while the command runs, then leaps ~150px up the pane at
the moment the command has already finished; other commands end with a visible
drop back down.

## Cause

Four separate owners of the pane's height were moving at once. Measured frame
by frame in the e2e container (chromium, 605px scroller, 20px cell):

1. **The composer left the layout.** `hide()` set `display:none` at submit, so
   the scroller grew 77px and the scrollback — which hangs from its bottom edge
   (`.scrollback-inner` has `margin-top:auto`) — moved by that much. Fixed by
   suspending the composer instead: same flex slot, `visibility:hidden`,
   `inert`. This REVERSES a deliberate decision; the history and why the trade
   flipped are written on `suspend()` in editor.ts.

2. **The live region was measured before the grid had the rows.** xterm parses
   asynchronously; the measure was scheduled from `session.onData` one line
   after `renderer.write()`, so its animation frame read the grid without the
   output. A command printing everything in one chunk has no next chunk to
   correct it: `seq 1 10` measured three rows live, froze eleven lines, and the
   header leapt 153px up. Fixed by measuring on `renderer.onWriteParsed`.

3. **The frozen row pitch was not the grid's.** `.term-line` was
   `min-height: 1.2em` = 16.8px against a 20px cell, so every frozen line was
   3.2px shorter than the live row it replaced — six lines dropped the block
   19px at freeze, thirty would drop it 96. This is the vertical twin of
   nocx-yy9g and is fixed the same way: the renderer's measured `cellHeight` is
   published as `--term-cell-height` and the line lays out on it. It was also a
   fidelity defect standing still — frozen text denser than the live text it is
   a photograph of.

4. **The body padding was on one side only.** `.cmd-output` has 2px/6px; the
   live region had none, so the box changed by 8px at every freeze. Both now
   read `--cmd-output-pad-*`, and the controller reads the value off the
   element rather than repeating the number in TypeScript.

## What is left

A command that holds the shell (`read x`) still falls back by exactly ONE grid
row at the freeze. That row is real: the frozen body ends at the render fence,
and the grid's cursor sits one row below it — the row the next prompt would
occupy. The live region cannot drop it without hiding the cursor of a program
waiting for input, and the block cannot keep it without swallowing the row the
next command's echo lands on (nocx-4yhi). Bounded and asserted at one row; a
better answer needs the fence and the cursor to stop disagreeing.
acceptance_criteria: Submitting a command moves the block header monotonically: it may rise as output arrives, and at the freeze it must not fall back by more than one grid row. An e2e assertion in command-editor.spec.ts measures the header against the scroller before Enter, while running and after the freeze, and reads the tolerance from --term-cell-height rather than a literal.
close_reason: Four owners of the pane height fixed: composer suspended instead of removed from layout; live region measured on onWriteParsed instead of on write; frozen row pitch published from the renderer as --term-cell-height (vertical twin of nocx-yy9g); body padding shared through --cmd-output-pad-*; and .nocx-chip reset so a <button> chip is the same box as a <span> one. Measured in the e2e container: 'true' freezes with no movement at all, 'seq 1 10' and a three-line printf move up once and never back. Residual one-row drop on a shell-side hold is nocx-i4h04.1. Commit b97d30b3.

title: workspaces.reorder can never succeed: two rules forbid the same id
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have at least two workspaces.
2. Open a workspace heading's menu and pick Move up or Move down.

Observed: a toast, 'Could not reorder the workspaces: Invalid params: ids must be a UUIDv7'. Every reorder failed, whichever way it was sent.

## What is wrong

Two requirements contradicted each other. The transport refuses any id that is not a UUIDv7 (§7: layout ids are durable and client-minted), while content.ReorderWorkspaces demanded a permutation of EVERY stored workspace — one of which is the reserved 'workspace:default'. A renderer that included it was refused by the transport; one that omitted it was refused by the store. The error named the half that was not the problem.

## The rule

The default workspace is not a member of the arrangement a user made: it renders no chrome at all (§4.2), no surface offers to move it, and it keeps position 0. The order is the user-made workspaces, written at 1..n. The answer still carries every row, because the renderer replaces its cache with it and a list without the default would drop the workspace every ungrouped tab belongs to.
acceptance_criteria: Move up / Move down on a workspace heading reorders it and raises no toast; a reorder naming the default workspace is refused with ErrNotAPermutation; the default stays at position 0 whatever order arrives; the answer contains every workspace including the default; a store test states each of those.
close_reason: Landed on feat/workspaces

title: Filter sandbox access inbox by application and keywords
description:
## Context
The Sandbox access Settings page lists denied filesystem attempts but cannot be narrowed when many applications and paths are present.

## Expected Behavior
Add an application filter and a keyword filter to Settings > Developer > Sandbox access. Filtering is client-side and must not mutate, dismiss, resolve, or hide backend events permanently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- User can restrict visible access events to one observed application.
- User can search visible events by keyword using documented, deterministic matching semantics.
- Filters compose and can be cleared without re-fetching or changing event state.
- Loading, empty-inbox, no-match, error, resolve, and live-refresh behavior remain correct.
- Focused frontend tests cover both filters and their composition.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix sandbox access paths truncated to root
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a sandboxed shell.
2. Access a denied file or directory outside the allowed roots.
3. Open Settings > Developer > Sandbox access.
4. Observe an event whose path is only / rather than the attempted target.

## Expected Behavior
The event records the complete attempted file or directory path.

## Actual Behavior
The access inbox can display only /, losing the target file or directory and making the proposed rule unusable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A denied event records the complete attempted file or directory path, not only /.
- Relative openat/openat2 paths resolve against the tracee cwd or dirfd.
- Absolute paths remain complete after canonicalization.
- Focused regression tests cover the reported root-only failure.
notes: Diagnosis 2026-08-18: the observed `/` is not string truncation. A local strace of OpenCode 1.18.18 shows Bun component walking with `openat(AT_FDCWD, "/", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY)`, then `/home/`, `/home/<user>/`, and relative `package.json`. Under Landlock the first root directory open is denied, so later target syscalls never occur and the backend cannot honestly report a target it never observed. The inbox also intentionally observes only denied openat/openat2; metadata probes use newfstatat/statx/access and are not Landlock denial events. Blocked on product/security choice: explain strict root ancestor denials, or design a larger virtual/mount-root compatibility layer. Granting `/` read access is unsafe.
close_reason: Not a path truncation: '/' is OpenCode/Bun's exact first ancestor-directory open, and Landlock denies it before later target syscalls exist. Verified the generic RO chain and native enforcement; no OpenCode-specific change requested.

title: Add sandbox denied-access inbox
description:
## Context
Sandboxed commands currently fail without exposing which descendant attempted the denied filesystem access or allowing a deliberate future-session grant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Linux and macOS observers record bounded, per-session denied read/write attempts without parsing PTY output or weakening native enforcement.
- Settings has a separate Sandbox access page showing attribution, path, access, count, health, and explicit Dismiss/Add global RO/Add global RW actions.
- Resolution uses backend-minted event IDs, revalidates the exact existing directory, atomically updates current global settings, and affects future sandbox sessions only.
- Events are memory-only PrivateMetadata; unsolicited notifications and ordinary logs carry no paths.

title: Sandbox denied-access inbox and global grants
description: Extend the opt-in per-tab filesystem sandbox with a Settings surface for denied filesystem attempts. The backend must attribute each observable denial to the sandbox session and executable, classify the requested access, retain a bounded private-metadata event list, and never weaken native enforcement. The user can promote the denied directory into the existing global read-only or read-write baseline, or dismiss it; running policies remain immutable, so grants apply only to future sandbox tabs. Research and document deployable macOS Seatbelt and Linux Landlock observation paths before implementation; do not claim support where the OS cannot deliver events without extra privilege.

Each event offers Add read-only, Add read-write, and Dismiss; add actions atomically update the existing global sandbox path settings through backend authority, deduplicate entries, reject conflicts, and state that the grant applies to future tabs only. Unsupported platform/kernel/permission states are explicit and never fabricate or infer denials. Contracts, architecture/ADR, focused backend/frontend tests, native smokes, and security review cover the shipped behavior.
