title: Sandbox action launches opencode instead of the specified interactive shell
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable sandbox.enabled.
2. Invoke the sandbox action and select a workspace.
3. Complete the permission dialog.
4. Observe that authenticated bootstrap replaces the shell with opencode.

## Expected
The original nocx-y46q contract holds: Quick Connect exposes `Sandboxed shell…` with stable id `__sandboxed_local__`; after authenticated nocxify bootstrap the selected workspace contains an interactive sandboxed shell.

## Actual
nocx-y46q.17 reversed the parent contract and commit 11498f1e renamed the action to `Sandboxed opencode…`, added a fixed backend OpenCode intent, and executes `opencode` after bootstrap. Each ephemeral HOME also repeats OpenCode first-run behavior.

## Root Cause
A real bootstrap-artifact accessibility bug was conflated with an unrequested product change. The runtime-tree artifact fix is required; the fixed OpenCode launch contradicts the parent epic, its original spec, and nocx-y46q.5.
acceptance_criteria: The sandbox action is `Sandboxed shell…` with stable id `__sandboxed_local__`; its open request remains command-free; the backend does not resolve, authorize, or execute opencode; the enhanced bash/zsh bootstrap artifact remains inside the sandbox runtime tree and authenticates nocxify; after authentication the interactive shell remains foreground in the canonical workspace; ordinary local/SSH behavior is unchanged; OpenCode-specific status/transport/UI code and tests are removed; affected docs explicitly supersede the mistaken fixed-OpenCode decision; Linux sandbox PTY smoke and targeted frontend/backend tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: The renderer never tells open which pane it is opening, so every block's anchor is null in the product
description:
FOUND while closing nocx-rtg0.28, which put entries.pane_id in and derived it
from the session. The backend half is complete: open takes paneId, validates
its shape, resolves pane -> tab -> workspace, records it on the session, and
every ledger entry that session writes carries it. Verified over the socket.

THE PRODUCT NEVER SENDS IT. frontend/src/ipc.ts has three openers -
openSession, openSSHSession, openSSHSessionByHost - and not one puts paneId in
the params, though the renderer has held the id all along: PaneManager.mintPane
returns the UUIDv7 and hands it to TerminalContent as `paneId`, which already
carries it on history.record and secrets.paneClosed. So params.PaneID is empty
on every open in the shipped product, the session is the pipe of no pane, and
every block's anchor is null - the durable edge exists in the schema and no
user ever gets one.

THE SAME SEAM'S OTHER HALF IS ALSO UNWIRED. `grep -rn workspaceId frontend/src`
finds no reader for the open ack's derived workspaceId either. nocx-isoph.2
resolves it correctly and answers nobody; the workspace feature works through
the layout methods instead, so nothing went visibly wrong.

AND IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE ADDED, which is why this is its own bead rather than a
line in rtg0.28. mintPane calls this.layout.openTab(...) and returns
opened.paneId WITHOUT awaiting opened.created, so the pane row is written
concurrently with the session open. open refuses a paneId naming no pane -
deliberately, "the pane you named does not exist and you named no pane are
different facts" - so sending it today makes opening a tab a race whose loss is
a tab that never appears. The ordering is a decision, not an oversight to
patch.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. grep -n "'open'" frontend/src/ipc.ts - three call sites, no paneId.
2. Open a tab in the product, run a command, read entries.pane_id: NULL.
3. grep -rn workspaceId frontend/src - nothing reads the ack's field.
acceptance_criteria:
- Opening a tab sends the pane's UUIDv7 as open's paneId, and a test watches a
  command recorded in that tab come back anchored on that pane through the
  REAL wire — not through a store-level Submit.
- The open ack's workspaceId has a reader. It is derived (nocx-isoph.2) and
  today nothing in frontend/src reads it, so the derivation answers nobody.
- The RACE is closed, and named in a comment: mintPane fires layout.openTab
  and returns the id without awaiting `created`, while open refuses a paneId
  that names no pane. Either the open waits for the row or the backend admits
  a pane it has not seen yet — decided deliberately, not by whichever promise
  wins.
- With no layout store the id is still minted and open still succeeds: that
  path must not become a refusal.
close_reason:
Commit aab52603. Five of six criteria met outright; the sixth is met as far as
the spec permits and is recorded honestly below.

The renderer now names its pane on all three openers, and the race is closed
the way it was decided: mintPane returns PaneIdentity{paneId, registered} and
the session waits for its pane's row, so `open` keeps refusing a pane it cannot
resolve (nocx-isoph.2's decision, which stands). The readiness comes off the
SAME two-armed handler that already knew the answer, so the single-handler
structure and the unhandled-rejection comment it carries survive intact. Every
call site is covered, including the restore path (Promise.resolve(true) for a
row that already exists) and workspace creation, which needed a paneRef to
order the chrome against its own readiness.

Two things the worker did better than the brief. The identity REPLACED the bare
string in TerminalContent's constructor instead of arriving as an optional
extra — an optional type-checks when forgotten, and the compiler named all six
construction sites. And criterion 5 could not be met as written: a refused
create disposes the chrome BEFORE the session is requested, so there is no
second open to count. The first draft failed on toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2) and
was rewritten to assert the invariant over every call — no open names a pane
the chain does not hold — which is the rule rather than the dispose race.

+14 tests, 0 regressions (3225 → 3239 full frontend), tsc clean on both configs.
Coordinator verified the one thing the worker could not: the new await adds no
hang class, because a dead socket rejects pending calls (Dispatcher.
rejectAllPending), so `registered` resolves false and the open goes out
unanchored.

CRITERION 6, precisely: the ack's workspaceId is decoded onto SessionHandle and
read into the session-opened log. That is a decode-and-observe reader, not a
behavioural one, and there is no honest behavioural consumer available — the
contract says the field carries no behaviour and design §5.5 forbids any
surface before the fence epic from acting on membership. Inventing a consumer
would have violated the spec the field came from. What will consume it is named
on nocx-isoph.

title: Sandbox-enabled tab strip offers shield launch
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable sandbox.enabled in Settings.
2. Return to the terminal tab strip.
3. Observe that the only direct new-session action is the ordinary + button; sandbox launch remains hidden in Quick Connect.

## Expected

A shield action appears immediately beside + and opens the existing Sandboxed opencode flow.

## Actual

No sandbox launch action is present beside +.
acceptance_criteria: The shield button appears next to + only while sandbox.enabled is true, updates live after settings changes and strip orientation replacement, and invokes the same picker/permissions/newSandboxedTab path as Quick Connect. Focused tests and browser smoke cover visibility and activation.
notes: Implemented in frontend/src/tab-strip.tsx and frontend/src/main.tsx: shield action is live-gated by sandbox.enabled in both strip orientations, preserves wiring across orientation replacement, and delegates to the shared openSandboxedTab flow used by Quick Connect. Added focused horizontal/vertical visibility, adjacency, live-toggle, and activation tests; browser smoke verified horizontal/vertical placement, live hide/restore, and activation reaches the native directory-dialog RPC. Wails production build and launch smoke passed. Full frontend gate passed. Host make ci reaches Go race tests but is blocked by the repository's Bash 3.2/hostile-prompt shellintegration fixture requirements; the previously established container/GitHub backend gates are green.
close_reason: Shield action implemented and verified in both tab-strip orientations

title: A block has no durable anchor: entries hangs on the session, which dies with the backend
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-16-tabs-panes-and-blocks-design.md §6.1.

    block.pane_id      the anchor. Durable, and what makes restore possible
    block.session_id   provenance. Which pipe it ran in; null after it is gone

THE FIRST OF THOSE TWO DOES NOT EXIST. `pane_id` appears nowhere in
internal/content/sqlite.go. `entries` anchors on

    session_id TEXT REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

and nothing else — which is verbatim the line §6.1 quotes as the defect: "anchoring
only on the session loses every block the moment the backend restarts".

A session dies with the backend (D5). A pane does not. So after a restart the
session id is nulled and the block hangs on nothing, while the pane whose blocks
they were is sitting right there with a durable row.

HOW IT WAS MISSED, because the shape recurs. Every ledger bead this session —
the write path, the read path, the redaction receipt, the environment read — was
scoped to the ledger's OWN shape, and the pane tables landed afterwards in a
different epic. The join between them had no owner in either. Nobody skipped it;
it fell between two correct scopes.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY, and this is why it is filed now rather than inside restore:
nocx-isoph.4 made the strip survive an application restart. Tabs and panes come
back; their blocks cannot, and not because restore is unbuilt but because the
column that would make it possible is absent. Every day the ledger records
commands against this schema is a day of blocks that can never be re-attached.

BOTH EDGES ARE NEEDED AND NEITHER DOES THE OTHER'S WORK (§6.1). Keeping only the
session loses the blocks on restart; keeping only the pane loses the answer to
"where did this run", which matters the moment a pane has been through an inline
ssh — and §8's inline-ssh restore case works ONLY because that edge exists.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. grep pane_id internal/content/sqlite.go — nothing.
2. Read the entries table: session_id is the only anchor, ON DELETE SET NULL.
3. Restart the backend. The session row goes; the entry's session_id is nulled;
   nothing names the pane the command ran in.

## Acceptance Criteria

- entries carries pane_id, and a block written in a pane is still found BY THAT
  PANE after a full backend restart — asserted across a restart, not by reading
  the column back in the same process.
- session_id keeps its meaning as provenance and keeps being nulled when the
  pipe goes. A test asserts both at once: after a restart the block still names
  its pane AND no longer names a session.
- A block that ran on the far side of an inline ssh still says so after the
  restart. That is §8's inline-ssh case and it is the one that proves the two
  edges are not redundant.
- The frontend mints the pane id, so it is untrusted input on this path too:
  the shape is validated, and an entry naming a pane that does not exist is
  refused rather than stored dangling.
notes:
FOLLOW-UP OWED, noticed 2026-08-18 after the close and recorded so it is not
lost: dropDeadSessions has no FAILURE-path test. AGENTS.md rule 3 says every
external call gets a test where that call fails, and its DELETE is one — a
failure there aborts Open, so the store does not start and the product runs on
the stub. Nothing asserts that today.

Not fixed in place because internal/content was handed to a parallel worker
(nocx-rtg0.12, retention watermark) the same afternoon and two writers in one
directory is how a merge stops being a merge. The coordinator adds it on the
merged tree.
close_reason:
All four criteria met at the store and the wire, commit 5c27da2f.

entries.pane_id exists, is indexed for the restore read, and a block written in
a pane is found BY THAT PANE after the store is closed and reopened — asserted
across the restart, never by reading the column back in the writing process.
The same test asserts the other edge in the same breath: after the restart the
block still names its pane and no longer names a session, which took making the
nulling real (dropDeadSessions at Open — DeleteSession had no production caller
at all). A command on the far side of an inline ssh keeps its local pane and
its remote environment across the restart, which is what proves the two edges
are not redundant. And a pane id naming no pane is refused before the insert,
through the chain lookup the layout code already uses, with the SHAPE checked
separately at open so a malformed id and an absent one are different answers.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS, and filed as nocx-rtg0.29 with a blocks edge: the renderer
sends no paneId on open, so in the product every anchor is still null. The
schema and the backend are ready for it; the wiring is a decision about
ordering that belongs in its own bead.

title: The renderer asks instead of owning: order, activation and decoration come from the backend
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-16-tabs-panes-and-blocks-design.md §4.1, §4.5.

The big frontend one. Today PaneManager owns the ordered model, the activation
rules and the MRU stack, and state/pane-model.ts is a framework-neutral copy of
that model. After this bead the backend owns all of it and the renderer renders
what it is told.

WHY THIS IS NOT 'MOVE THE STATE': the renderer keeps a cache, and a cache is
fine. What it may no longer do is DECIDE. Ordering, activation and membership
come from the backend; the renderer asks and re-renders. The test that this
worked is that a reload of the renderer alone — without restarting the backend —
brings back the colours, names, order and pinning, because they were never in
the renderer to begin with.

THE LABEL AND THE INDICATORS ARE COMPUTED, NEVER STORED (§4.5). A tab created by
a DRAG was never named by anybody, so demanding a name asks for something the
user did not give: its identity is its panes, so their titles are its label —
`nocx · srv-01 · claude`, elided to the available width. A name the user DOES
type is stored and wins. The activity and attention indicators are likewise
derived from the panes, because attention arrives at a pane.

AND A PANE'S OWN TITLE HAS THREE SOURCES, IN THIS ORDER (nocx-n8n82, already
shipped): the title the program declared (OSC 0/2), then the command running in
the foreground, then the pane's cwd. The label flows pane -> tab, and a tab can
only be named by its panes if a pane is named by what is in it.

READ frontend/src/ui/README.md AND LIST frontend/src/ui/ BEFORE BUILDING ANY
CONTROL. The kit owns how controls look. A surface may PLACE a kit component and
may never REPAINT it; wanting to repaint means the component is missing a
variant, and the variant goes in the kit. Two epics have already spent
themselves unwinding hand-rolled controls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user colours a tab, pins it, renames it and reorders it; the renderer is
  reloaded WITHOUT restarting the backend, and all four survive. Watched by one
  automated check driving the real UI against the real backend — this is the
  epic's headline assertion and it belongs here.
- An unnamed tab holding two panes is labelled from both their titles; a tab the
  user names shows that name instead. Both asserted.
- A pane running a program that declares a title shows the declared title; one
  running a foreground command with no declared title shows the command; one
  idle shows the cwd. Three assertions, because the middle rung is the one that
  was missing.
- The renderer decides nothing: a test asserts that with the backend refusing a
  reorder, the strip does NOT reorder optimistically and then snap back.
- No new control is hand-rolled: the CSS integrity gate stays at zero and every
  control used is named in frontend/src/ui/README.md.
notes:
THREE THINGS nocx-isoph.2 HANDED FORWARD. All three are load-bearing and one will bite on the first line of code.

1. THE RENDERER MINTS v4 AND THE WIRE REQUIRES v7. Every layout id is validated strictly — version nibble 7 plus the RFC 4122 variant — because §7's table says UUIDv7 and a schema that says v7 while accepting v4 advertises what it does not deliver. crypto.randomUUID() produces v4. So this bead needs a v7 minter in the renderer before it can create anything, and the timestamp prefix is not decoration: it is what makes the id sortable and what §7 leans on. Note the older pane.close notification still accepts any bounded string; converging it is noted in layout.go and is not automatic.

2. THERE IS NO READ METHOD, and nocx-isoph.2 names it the single biggest gap it left. The renderer cannot read the layout back at all, and a close cannot even tell it whether the replacement tab was minted. 'Order, activation and decoration come from the backend' is this bead's own sentence, and it cannot be true until a read exists — so designing that read is the first thing here, not an afterthought. It is also where the epic's headline assertion lives: reload the renderer without restarting the backend and find the colours, names, order and pinning intact.

3. DeletePane HAS NO WIRE CALLER, and the reason is a name collision rather than an omission: the renderer's word for it, pane.close, is already taken by the capture-scoping notification — a different act under the same word. Decide the two names here. This is adjacent to nocx-wyp3p, where the backend calls a WebSocket connection a tab; do not merge the two, but read it before choosing.

THE E2E SUITE CAUGHT TWO PRODUCT DEFECTS, not test artefacts, and both were invisible to every unit test. Recorded because this is the clearest example this repo has of why rule 2 exists.

1. AFTER ONE RELOAD WITH AN SSH PANE, A USER COULD NEVER REORDER AGAIN. tabs.reorder refuses anything that is not a permutation of the workspace's members, and the request was built from the panes the RENDERER DRAWS — correct exactly while it draws every row the chain holds. A restored ssh pane is in the chain and deliberately not reopened, so it was missing from the ask and every reorder was refused. The order now comes from the cache, so a row the renderer cannot draw keeps its place instead of vanishing from the request.

2. A VIEW PANE WAS SWEPT TO THE END. Opening Settings and then a connection put the new tab BEFORE Settings. Ten of the twenty-one failures were this, while the specs that caught it are named 'persists across restart' and say nothing about ordering.

3. And four connections meant four 'not reopened' warnings on every reload; now one, naming the count.

THE HARNESS RESET HAD TWO WAYS OF QUIETLY DOING NOTHING: it clicked the close control on every tab and swallowed failures — and a click cannot reach a row the renderer does not draw, which is precisely how the ssh rows accumulated all run and caused defect 1. It now opens the control plane the way the renderer does, reads the chain, closes every pane in it, and THROWS, because it is the precondition of every test rather than a courtesy. It also runs BEFORE each test: a teardown answers for the test that has just died and is skipped exactly when it mattered.

ON THE SHORTENED EXPECT BUDGET (eb532957): two specs did fail for want of time, and in both the spec was waiting on nothing — a keyboard chord pressed immediately after page.goto, before the shortcut was wired. The fix was to wait for the app, not to raise the number back. connections-settings went 22.7s to 3.6s; three snippets cases went from 60s timeouts to about 3s each.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/workspaces at 6d6e7a5b (ac8f34d8). The backend owns the ordered model, the activation rules and the decoration; the renderer keeps a cache and no longer decides. state/pane-model.ts and the store's paneModel slice are deleted — the framework-neutral copy of rules the backend now owns.

layout.read is the read that makes it true, and its shape is argued rather than assumed: ONE call returning the whole chain FLAT, on the content domain's single operation lane, so the renderer draws one consistent picture rather than three a mutation can interleave with, and the first draw is one round trip rather than 1+N+N*M. Flat because the edges are already on the rows and a tree would be a second encoding of them. defaultWorkspaceId is on the wire because the default never renders and never acquires a name, so the renderer cannot recognise it by sight and a copy of workspace.Default in the frontend would be a second owner of the one id whose whole purpose is having exactly one.

The name collision is resolved in both directions: panes.close is DeletePane's wire caller, and the capture notification became secrets.paneClosed — the domain that already owns a pending capture, past tense because it reports rather than asks. Leaving them one letter apart was the defect.

Two prohibitions kept by refusing convenience. The close does NOT carry the replacement back; the renderer re-reads, because reconstructing a transaction it did not run would be the renderer deciding again. And the capture notification's id shape is deliberately NOT converged to the layout's UUIDv7 check: the layout validates because it STORES the id, the capture domain stores nothing, and restating the rule there would give it a second owner in a package with no id of its own.

MRU and the active tab stay in the renderer, and the reason is §10: a window is a viewport, so two windows on one workspace have two answers, and §4.5's stored list has no active column.

One defect existed only in the merge with nocx-isoph.6 and is described in the merge commit.

Flagged and now under the coordinator's gate: e2e cross-spec contamination, because tabs survive a reload and the suite runs one stand for the whole run. The worker added a teardown through the product's own control and could not run the suite.

title: A container exists only while it holds a member, and creation always brings content
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-16-tabs-panes-and-blocks-design.md §4.1, §4.4,
and §4.2 of the 2026-08-15 workspaces UX design.

A workspace exists only while it holds at least one tab; a tab only while it
holds at least one pane. Neither needs lifecycle code: the container's row goes
in the SAME TRANSACTION that removes its last member.

CREATION IS ALWAYS CREATION-WITH-CONTENT. 'New workspace' mints it together with
its first tab. There is never a moment when an empty container exists, which is
what makes the rule above cheap rather than a sweep.

AND THE TAB IS MINTED AND DESTROYED AUTOMATICALLY (§4.4): dragging a pane out of
a tab mints a tab for it; dragging it into another changes its tab_id and the
tab left with no panes is removed. The pane's identity, its blocks, its history
and its live pipe are untouched in both directions, because only a reference
moved. That round trip being lossless is the whole reason the words were swapped
in nocx-ehkvy.

THE REPLACEMENT TAB BELONGS TO THE DEFAULT WORKSPACE. When the last tab in the
application closes, a fresh one appears; it goes to the DEFAULT workspace, never
to the one being closed, or closing a workspace resurrects it.

ATOMICITY IS INHERITED AND STILL UNDESIGNED (§12 q. 5 / workspaces-ux §4.4):
whether a pane can be dragged between workspaces while a subtree move is in
flight is open, and a partial move MUST FAIL CLOSED. This bead does not have to
solve it, but it must not leave a pane in two places or in none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Removing the last pane from a tab removes the tab, in one transaction — a
  test kills the transaction partway and finds either both gone or both present,
  never a tab with no panes.
- Removing the last tab from a workspace removes the workspace, same property.
- An empty workspace cannot be created: the create-workspace call without a
  first tab is refused, and a test asserts the refusal.
- Closing the last tab in the application yields a new tab in the DEFAULT
  workspace, asserted by reading its workspace_id, not by looking at the strip.
- A pane moved between tabs keeps its id, its cwd and its live session — the
  test asserts the SAME session is still attached afterwards, because 'a new
  pane with the same contents' is the failure this design exists to prevent.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/workspaces at 1d93862d (0bcc4b00). Creation is creation-with-content in the signature itself — CreateWorkspace takes its first tab and first pane, CreateTab takes its first pane — so an empty container is unrepresentable rather than swept away. Deletion unwinds pane to tab to workspace in one transaction.

The atomicity test is the best thing in it and the method is worth keeping: 'kill the transaction partway' is a SQLite RAISE(ABORT) trigger on the second statement, not a SIGKILL. Deterministic, no sleep, no signal whose landing point is luck — AGENTS.md forbids timing-dependent tests, and this is what the alternative looks like. Three variants, and a two-transaction implementation fails the first one.

And the move's identity is asserted on the ROWID, because every field of a re-inserted pane equals the original's — only the row identity distinguishes 'the pane moved' from 'a new pane with the same contents', which is the failure this whole design exists to prevent.

Three refusals decided rather than guessed: the DEFAULT workspace is exempt from dissolution and cannot be deleted (sessions.workspace_id cascades, so deleting it would destroy restore keys); a close that would empty the application without a caller-minted Replacement is refused whole, because §7 says durable ids come from the frontend; and a cross-workspace pane move is refused pending §12 q5's atomicity model, with the pane asserted to stay in exactly one place.

Honest limit stated rather than faked: there is no pane-to-session link in the tree, so the live-session assertion is that the same INCARNATION is still alive and still passing bytes through its pipe after the move, with its durable row intact. Nothing pretends a link exists.

The signature change was flagged as an integration hazard for nocx-isoph.2 and relayed to that worker mid-flight.

title: The frontend asks the backend for a workspace, a tab and a pane, and cannot mint one behind its back
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-16-tabs-panes-and-blocks-design.md §4.1, §4.4, §7.

The frontend ASKS the backend to create, move and destroy a workspace, a tab and
a pane, and renders what it is told. This is §4.1 arriving: an invariant whose
two ends live in two processes has no owner, and the fix is moving the objects
rather than writing a protocol.

WHAT LANDS: create / rename / recolour / pin / reorder / close for a workspace
and a tab; move a pane between tabs; and the ack shapes, each with a schema in
contracts/ carrying all three checks. workspaceId MOVES FROM THE SESSION TO THE
TAB here (§4.5, nocx-fraus): the invariant is unchanged — never null, one owner
of the default, which internal/workspace.Default already holds — and on the
session it becomes derived, because the backend now owns the whole chain and
resolves pane -> tab -> workspace itself.

A FRONTEND-MINTED ID IS UNTRUSTED INPUT (§7), and the word is already in the
schema. Three consequences, none optional:

  1. The shape is validated, never believed.
  2. An insert on an existing id FAILS; it never overwrites. A repeat of the
     SAME request returns the SAME object — that is what entries.client and
     entries.digest are for, and the pattern already exists in this repo.
  3. KNOWING AN ID CONFERS NO RIGHT TO USE IT. UUIDv7 embeds a timestamp and is
     guessable by construction, so nothing here may treat possession of an id as
     evidence of anything.

The retry case is not hypothetical: AD-9 exists because the socket drops. A
create whose answer was lost is retried, and without the idempotency key that
retry produces a second tab.

THE BACKEND GAINS A TAB ROW; IT GAINS NO TAB ADDRESS (§4.4). Every
backend->renderer address stays a sessionId the renderer resolves. A tab holds
several panes, so 'the tab that spoke' is still not well defined, and the
renderer still knows where a session is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Sending the same create twice with the same client-minted UUIDv7 returns the
  SAME object and creates no second row — asserted OVER THE REAL SOCKET, by
  counting rows, not by absence of an error.
- A create carrying an id that already belongs to a DIFFERENT object fails and
  changes nothing.
- A malformed id is refused with -32602 before anything is written.
- Every method's result validates against its schema off the real socket. Every
  object carries additionalProperties:false plus an explicit required.
- workspaceId is gone from the session's stored state and is derived; a test
  resolves a pane's workspace through the chain and gets the same answer the
  session used to give.
- No backend->renderer notification anywhere gains a tab id. A test asserts the
  addresses are still session ids.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/workspaces at bd59c5a9 (fe714fd2). Twelve methods on the control plane with twelve contracts, each with the three checks plus a negative case proving the schema can fail. The worker merged the sibling lifecycle branch itself and reconciled the signature change rather than leaving it for the coordinator.

The idempotency argument is the best judgment in it. entries binds its key to client plus digest; these rows bind to the digest alone, and the reasoning is that the retry the key exists for arrives ON A NEW CONNECTION — that is what 'the socket dropped' means — so a connection-scoped client would turn exactly the AD-9 case into a conflict. Proved by a test that replays the create across a reconnect and counts rows.

workspaceId is now genuinely derived: the field is gone from session.Config and Session, open takes a paneId, and the ack resolves pane to tab to workspace before anything is spawned. nocx-fraus's field was the intermediate step and this is the destination.

The 'no tab address' prohibition is held by two tests with positive controls: a scan of every contract for a tabId property, and a real exit notification off the socket asserted to be addressed by sessionId. A prohibition asserted only in prose is a comment.

deadcode -whylive now shows a real chain from main to CreateWorkspace, MovePane, ReorderTabs and WorkspaceForPane. Every one of them answered 'reachable only through reflection' before this bead — which is exactly what nocx-isoph.1's by-hand note predicted and why that note existed.

Three consequences handed to nocx-isoph.4 and recorded there: the renderer mints v4 while the wire requires v7; there is no read method at all; and DeletePane has no wire caller because pane.close is taken by the capture-scoping notification.

title: Workspace, tab and pane are rows the backend owns
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-16-tabs-panes-and-blocks-design.md §3, §4.5, §5, §7.

The first of this epic's children, and the only one with no user-visible effect:
the three objects become rows the backend owns. Everything else in the epic is
built on this seam, so a field invented here is a field the whole chain inherits.

WHAT LANDS

    workspace   flat, never nested. id (client-minted UUIDv7), name, position
    tab         workspace_id, colour, name, position, pinned, layout direction,
                seen-mark, and the lineage parent edge (§4.2)
    pane        tab_id, cwd, kind (local|ssh), endpoint, size share

WHAT IS STORED AND WHAT IS ONLY COMPUTED (§4.5), because getting this wrong
gives one fact two owners. Stored on the tab: colour, name, position, pinned,
layout direction, workspace_id, the seen-mark. NOT stored: the activity
indicator, the attention indicator, the label. Attention ARRIVES AT A PANE, so
storing it on the tab too means the two diverge the first time a pane is dragged
elsewhere. What is genuinely the tab's own is 'I have seen this', which
duplicates nothing.

TWO EDGES ON A TAB AND THEY MUST NEVER BE ONE (§4.2). `parent` is lineage — who
spawned whom, immutable, never set by hand — and the display grouping is a
separate, symmetric relation set by dragging. Carrying both on one column is the
failure AGENTS.md names. The lineage half already has an owner: session.Ref and
validateParent, from nocx-9hu9d. Extend it; do not write a second.

THE DISPLAY GROUP HAS NO ROW (§4.3). A, B and C shown together is a value shared
by the members, not a row of its own, so nothing can outlive its membership.
Pull any of them out and the rest do not notice.

SIZE IS A PROPERTY OF THE MEMBER, DIRECTION A PROPERTY OF THE SET (§5): each
pane stores its own share, the tab stores the direction.

THE SCHEMA COST, stated because it is not obvious. Adding tables is a change to
schemaV1, and internal/content/sqlite.go:354 makes a schemaVersion bump DROP
EVERY TABLE and log 'history discarded' — including the user's real command
history. nocx-rtg0.19 also bumps, for deleting command_history. Land these two
under ONE bump if the timing allows; if it does not, say in the commit that this
is a second discard and why it was accepted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The three tables exist with the columns above and a repository seam over them,
  and a test writes and reads back every stored field.
- A test asserts the tab has NO column for activity, attention or label. The
  point of this bead is the absence as much as the presence.
- Panes do not nest: the schema makes a pane whose parent is a pane
  unrepresentable, not merely unused.
- A workspace cannot be nested in a workspace, likewise structurally.
- Every foreign key's delete behaviour is stated and tested: what happens to a
  tab when its workspace goes, and to a pane when its tab goes.
- deadcode -whylive on the new repository methods, and the output is in the
  commit. -filter cannot fail on this package (AGENTS.md).
close_reason:
Merged into feat/workspaces at bc5fe5a3 (52baf76f). workspaces, tabs and panes are rows with a LayoutRepository over them, schemaVersion 4 to 5, rows discarded per the owner's decision the same day.

The absence criterion was mutation-checked, which is what makes it evidence: adding an 'attention' column to tabs makes TestTabStoresNoActivityNoAttentionAndNoLabel fail with the column named. Storing attention on the tab would have given one fact two owners the first time a pane is dragged.

Best judgment call: 'extend the lineage owner' could not mean internal/content importing internal/session, which would drag pty, ssh and storage into the store's dependency tree. So the three shape rules — self, cycle, depth — moved into a new dependency-free internal/lineage, with internal/session calling it and its error values re-exported under the old names so every errors.Is site keeps working. One implementation, two callers, no copy.

Two more worth keeping. There is deliberately NO method that changes a tab's parent, and that absence is what makes a cycle unreachable through the seam rather than merely refused. And CreateWorkspace moved off LedgerRepository, because workspaces was already owned there and adding tabs without moving it would have left one table with two repository owners.

Reported gap, now recorded on nocx-8m2x6: panes have no stored order, which is invisible until drag makes reordering a user-visible operation.

deadcode -whylive answers 'reachable only through reflection' for all eleven new methods — the known RTA answer for this package, and honest here since nocx-isoph.2 is what puts them on the wire. The by-hand reachability note in layout.go says so.

title: ledger.query cannot express the recall search box: no text filter
description:
Found by nocx-rtg0.20's five-field checklist, and it is the one the checklist
could not have caught by looking at the RESULT alone: all five result fields are
answerable from the ledger, but the REQUEST is not.

history.query accepts `text` — a case-insensitive substring over the command,
within the rung (nocx-ms7v) — and sqliteContent.Query implements it as
`instr(lower(command), lower(?))`, deliberately not LIKE, so a search for
"100%_done" matches that literal and nothing else.

ledger.query has no text filter at all. Full-text belongs to ledger.search
(nocx-rtg0.21), which nocx-rtg0.20's brief put deliberately out of scope.

SO THE RECALL OVERLAY'S SEARCH BOX CANNOT BE REPOINTED. nocx-rtg0.19 makes
history.query answer from the ledger; with no text predicate it would either
drop the filter silently — returning a superset that looks like it works, the
exact failure mode the filter tests exist to catch — or answer nothing.

TWO WAYS OUT, and they are not equal:

  1. Give ledger.query the same substring predicate over `intent`. Cheap: the
     WHERE builder is one append away, and it reuses the owner's existing rule
     rather than inventing a second matching semantics.
  2. Land nocx-rtg0.21 (ledger.search, full-text with coverage) first and repoint
     the search box at that instead.

(1) is what history.query promises today and is a like-for-like cutover. (2) is a
better product and a bigger bead — it needs FTS, which does not exist. Choosing
(2) as the answer to a cutover blocker is how a cutover acquires a feature.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read contracts/history.query.schema.json and sqliteContent.Query: `text` is
   part of the request and is implemented.
2. Read contracts/ledger.query.schema.json and content.ledgerWhere: there is no
   text predicate.
3. There is no way to express the overlay's search box as a ledger.query.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ledger.query answers a substring search over the intent, within the rung,
  with the SAME semantics history.query has today — case-insensitive, no
  wildcard grammar. A test searches for a literal containing % and _ and gets
  that command and nothing else.
- The filter is proved to EXCLUDE, not merely to return rows.
- Coverage still means the store-wide horizon and is unaffected by the text
  filter, exactly as it is unaffected by the rung.
- If the answer chosen is nocx-rtg0.21 instead, say so here and move the edge —
  do not leave both open with neither owning the cutover.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/workspaces at b6675c96 (3e6cddaf). ledger.query gains the SAME predicate history.query already runs — instr(lower(e.intent), lower(?)) — moved to the ledger's column rather than reinvented, so there is one matching semantics and not two.

The %/_ literal case is proved by EXCLUSION rather than by the survivor: the fixture carries a decoy row '1000-and-done' which a LIKE pattern of '100%_done' matches and instr() does not. A test where only the intended row survives cannot tell a correct predicate from a lucky one.

Every case names the WHOLE expected page, so a silently-ignored filter fails — and the red run showed exactly that superset before the fix, which is the property the bead asked for. Coverage was extended in place rather than duplicated: the store-wide horizon is now asserted under a text filter that excludes the oldest row, and again under a needle matching nothing.

No contract change and none needed: contracts/ declares results and params are explicitly out of its scope, so the three checks are unchanged rather than skipped.

This was the last blocker on nocx-rtg0.19 that was about capability. What remains there are the four mapping decisions already recorded on it.

title: Sandbox permissions list stacks vertically
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable sandbox and start the Sandboxed opencode action.
2. Add or load multiple folders in either permission class.
3. Observe that entries flow horizontally beside each other.

## Expected
Each directory entry occupies its own row; the list reads top-to-bottom.

## Actual
Directory entries render next to each other in the permissions menu.
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox permission entries render one per row from top to bottom in both access sections. Existing add/remove/check behavior is unchanged. Focused UI test and actual browser surface verify the layout.
notes: Implemented in frontend/src/styles/surfaces/sandbox-permissions.css with a flex column and bounded kit spacing. Regression coverage reads the shipped stylesheet in sandbox-permissions-dialog.test.tsx. Chromium dev surface measured both visible lists as display:flex/flex-direction:column with strictly increasing Y coordinates (RO 337→364; RW 659→686→713), and visual inspection confirmed one full-width row per path. `make frontend-ci` passed, focused test 9/9 passed, Wails v2.13.0 production build and application-initialized smoke passed. Security delta is CSS/test/docs only: no secret, transport, policy, dependency, or input boundary changed. Repository scans still report pre-existing findings tracked by nocx-0lita and nocx-l3pk. Host `make ci` reached Go race tests and failed only in shell-integration host-environment tests (missing required Bash 3.2 plus hostile-prompt/snapshot fixtures); the authoritative frontend gate passed.
close_reason: Sandbox permission baselines now render as vertical one-row-per-directory lists; regression test, browser geometry check, Wails build/smoke, and full frontend gate pass.

title: An entry knows its environment id and nothing can read the host back
description:
Found by nocx-rtg0.23's twelve-column checklist. Smaller than its sibling
nocx-rtg0.24 but on the same critical path.

contracts/history.query.schema.json declares `host` on every entry, and
command_history holds it as a plain column. The ledger stores instead
`entries.environment_id`, derived by environmentForSession from session.Host()
— which is the RIGHT shape (one owner for "where is this session", AD-8, and
the same string command_history's column holds, "" for local).

What is missing is the read back. LedgerRepository exposes no environment read
at all, so given an entry there is no seam that answers "which host was this".
Hashing forward works — EnvironmentIDFor turns a host into an id, so FILTERING
by host is answerable — but RENDERING a row's host is not.

So the asymmetry is: the ledger can find rows for a host and cannot say, of a
row it found, which host it was.

WHY IT BLOCKS nocx-rtg0.19: history.query answers `host` today and must keep
answering it from the ledger. It is deliberately a separate bead from
nocx-rtg0.24 because the work is unrelated — this one is a read method and a
join, that one is storage plus a key-type decision — and one bead carrying both
is how a bead stops being handed over whole.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read contracts/history.query.schema.json: `host` is required on historyEntry.
2. Read internal/content/ledger.go's LedgerRepository: there is no method
   returning an Environment, by id or otherwise.
3. Read an entry back through Entry(ctx, id): it carries environment_id and
   nothing that resolves it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an entry, its host is answerable through the repository seam, and a test
  asserts the value for both a local entry ("" or whatever local is spelled as)
  and an ssh entry.
- The derivation stays in one place: environmentForSession remains the only
  thing that decides where a session is. Reading an environment back must not
  become a second derivation — if the read has to reconstruct anything, that is
  the defect, not the fix.
- ListEntries or its successor returns the host without N+1 reads. State in the
  commit how, because a join added later is a rewrite of the query this bead
  ships.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/workspaces (f4ba62ea). An entry resolves its environment through a LEFT JOIN inside the entry query itself, shared as a const between Entry and ListEntries so nocx-rtg0.20's ledger.query inherits it rather than bolting one on later — which was the reason this bead went first.

Verified rather than accepted: the join is one shared const, and TestListEntriesResolvesEveryHostInOneStatement pins the pool to one connection, installs a SQLITE_TRACE_STMT callback and requires exactly 1 statement for 5 entries across 5 distinct environments. An N+1 would be 6 and a broken trace would be 0, so the assertion cannot pass vacuously. Ran the three new content tests myself: green.

The shape decision is resolve rather than denormalise, and the argument is the one the brief demanded: environments.endpoint already holds what environmentForSession wrote, so a host column on entries would be a second owner of one fact, and any schemaV1 change discards the user's history on next open. A missing environment answers nil and never empty string, because empty string is a real answer meaning the local machine — LEFT rather than INNER, since dropping the entry is the one answer worse than 'unknown'.

The worker mutation-checked its own assertions: forcing Host() to return empty makes all three host tests fail on the SSH row while the local row stays green, which is precisely why the criterion demanded both.

deadcode -whylive on Environment.Host says 'reachable only through reflection' — the known RTA answer for every method in this package, and honest here: its caller is history.query answering from the ledger, which is nocx-rtg0.19/.20. The join itself is live; -whylive on environmentScan.value prints a real chain ending at sqliteContent.Entry.

title: The ledger loses the redaction receipt, and the vault rewrite is keyed on the table being deleted
description:
Found by nocx-rtg0.23's twelve-column checklist and filed the same hour. The
checklist was written into that bead precisely so this would be a finding rather
than a surprise discovered halfway through deleting a table.

WHAT command_history HOLDS AND THE LEDGER DOES NOT. history.query promises four
fields on the wire — contracts/history.query.schema.json declares maskedCount,
maskedKinds and redactions on every entry, plus host. Three of them have no
counterpart in the ledger at all:

  masked_count   ws_ledger.go does `masked, _, _, err := maskCommandSafe(...)`
  masked_kinds   and discards the findings. Nothing stores them.
  redactions     No column, no payload arm, nothing.

The masking itself is NOT the gap — ledger.open masks the intent through the
same maskCommandSafe owner, so no raw secret reaches the database. What is lost
is the RECEIPT: the "3 secrets masked" line, the overlay's unresolved chips, and
the spans a user can act on.

AND THE REWRITE PATH IS COUPLED TO THE OLD TABLE'S KEY TYPE, which is the
sharper half:

    RewriteRedaction(ctx context.Context, id int64, span content.Redaction,
                     reference string) error

`id int64` is command_history's autoincrement rowid. The ledger's key is
entries.id TEXT — a client-minted UUIDv7. So the vault-capture flow that turns a
masked span into a vault reference (ws_capture.go:224 → capture_tabby.go:78 →
CommandHistory().RewriteRedaction) cannot address a ledger row at all. This is
not a column to add; it is a seam whose signature assumes the table being
deleted.

WHY IT BLOCKS nocx-rtg0.19. That bead makes history.query answer from the
ledger. Answering it while silently returning maskedCount 0 and redactions []
would be a soft degrade the UI contradicts — the overlay would offer chips for
secrets it can no longer find, and AGENTS.md names that shape by itself: a
feature that does not exist surviving a release because the degrade was visible
only in a log.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read contracts/history.query.schema.json: maskedCount, maskedKinds and
   redactions are declared on every historyEntry.
2. Read internal/transport/ws_ledger.go: maskCommandSafe's second and third
   return values are discarded.
3. Read internal/content/ledger.go and the schemaV1 entries table: no column and
   no payload arm holds any of them.
4. Read internal/capability/capture_tabby.go:30 — RewriteRedaction takes an
   int64 row id, which the ledger does not have.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ledger stores what history.query promises: the masked count, the masked
  kinds and the redaction spans, for an entry created through ledger.open.
- A span can be rewritten to a vault reference on a LEDGER row. Decide and state
  whether RewriteRedaction takes the entry's UUIDv7 or gains a second seam, and
  say why in the commit — the id type is the whole defect, so the choice must be
  argued rather than implied.
- The full vault-capture flow works end to end against the ledger: a masked
  span, offered, saved, and the row afterwards holding a reference rather than
  the secret. Watched by one automated check, because the parts have each been
  green while the user's task was impossible before in this repo.
- A test asserts the receipt is NOT empty — maskedCount reflects what was
  actually masked. A field that silently answers zero is the soft degrade this
  bead exists to prevent.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/workspaces at eff57167 (c7a8278e). The ledger stores the masking receipt in entries.payload under one nested 'masking' key — no schemaVersion bump, so nobody's real history is discarded twice — and LedgerRepository gained its own RewriteRedaction taking the entry's UUIDv7.

The id-type decision came out better than the brief asked for. The compiler forced it: sqliteContent implements both repositories on one struct, so a second RewriteRedaction with a different signature does not compile — which is the type system saying what AD-8 says. Ledger() now returns a ledgerRepo receiver so the boundary is real. And the thing that must not fork turned out not to be the addressing but the DECISION: span validation that refuses rather than corrupts, plus idempotency by membership in the row's current redactions, is now applyRedactionRewrite with both paths as callers. doRewrite's hard-won care was shared, not retyped.

One finding the brief did not anticipate and that is the sharpest thing in this commit: FinishExecution had to start merging the payload with json_patch rather than assigning it, because two writers now own different keys of one column. Assigning would erase the receipt; having the close resend it would RESURRECT a span a capture save had already consumed, and the retried save would then replace text at stale offsets — precisely the corruption the idempotency rule exists to stop. TestLedgerClose_DoesNotResurrectARewrittenReceipt is that assertion.

Verified rather than accepted: ran the 17 new content tests and the capability router test myself, all green. The no-raw-secret property is asserted three ways including a byte scan of the closed database file.

Also deleted capability.ContentService.RewriteRedaction — a second seam for one behaviour with no caller at all.

title: internal/content: a concurrent-reader test says the database disk image is malformed
description:
Reported by the nocx-rtg0.3 worker on 2026-08-17 and recorded rather than
dismissed, because the failure mode is corruption rather than a timeout.

    sqlite3: database disk image is malformed

WHAT EACH OF US MEASURED, and the two disagree:

  • The worker: 2 failures in 5 runs, on a clean feat/workspaces worktree, while
    several agents and containers were active. It verified its own change to
    internal/content was comments only, by diff.
  • Me, immediately afterwards, same host, idle machine, isolated:
    `go test -count=1 -race ./internal/content/ -run TestConcurrentReadersWithOneWriter`
    six consecutive runs, six passes.

So it is load-dependent, like the class nocx-j41jx and nocx-2h08 belong to. What
makes it worth its own bead rather than a line on one of those: those two are
tests waiting on the wrong thing. THIS ONE SAYS THE DATABASE FILE IS CORRUPT,
and the store it corrupts is the one the next four beads are about to make the
live path for every command a user runs.

TWO OUTCOMES, and they need different work, so find out which before fixing:

  1. The TEST is wrong — sharing a file across processes or connections in a way
     the product never does, or tearing down while a writer is mid-transaction.
     Then the fix is the test and the store is fine.
  2. The STORE is wrong — a concurrency discipline that does not hold under load.
     Then it is release-blocking, and it must be found before nocx-rtg0.19 makes
     the ledger the only place a command is recorded.

Do not assume (1) because it is the cheaper answer. ADR-0019 makes this file the
one authoritative ledger; "the test was sloppy" is the conclusion, never the
hypothesis.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load the machine — several containers or agents running.
2. `go test -count=1 -race ./internal/content/ -run TestConcurrentReadersWithOneWriter`
3. It fails perhaps two runs in five with `database disk image is malformed`.
4. On an idle machine, six consecutive runs pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The failure is REPRODUCED before it is fixed, under artificial contention, so
  the fix is verified against a failure rather than against silence.
- Which of the two outcomes above it is, stated in the commit with the evidence.
- If it is the store: a test that fails before and passes after, and it does not
  depend on timing — it waits on an observable state, never on a duration.
- If it is the test: say precisely what it did that the product never does, or
  the same fix will be argued about again the next time this appears.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-lc15n, which was filed 2026-08-16 about the same test and the same 'database disk image is malformed' error, with a stronger sighting: the CI macOS runner rather than a local container. I filed this without running AGENTS.md's first check — bd query for an existing bead — which is the exact failure that section exists to prevent. Both observations from today are merged onto nocx-lc15n.

title: A close cannot record the exit code or the duration of a row that already exists
description:
Found while implementing nocx-rtg0.3, and filed the same hour rather than left in
a report — the shape that made nocx-rtg0.19 necessary is the shape this bead is
avoiding.

THE LEDGER RECORDS STRICTLY LESS THAN command_history DOES, so the cutover
cannot happen until this is fixed. That is not a nice-to-have: nocx-rtg0.19
deletes command_history and makes history.query answer from the ledger, and a
history.query that has lost the exit code is a product regression a user sees.

WHAT IS MISSING, precisely. For an entry whose row ALREADY EXISTS, a close has
nowhere to put:

  • the shell payload — exitCode, trusted, markers
  • durationMs

FinishExecution takes only { EndedAt, TerminationReason, Status }.
SubmitEntry.Payload and SubmitEntry.DurationMs are write-once at creation, and
writing facts through Submit on a LATER event would change the idempotency
digest and turn every replay into ErrIDConflict — so the obvious workaround is
worse than the gap.

The asymmetry this produces today: a close that CREATES its own row (the
out-of-order case, §6.3) records duration, and a close on a row that was already
opened cannot. One method, two behaviours, decided by whether an earlier packet
arrived.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN nocx-rtg0.3: that bead's brief said the repository is
finished and needs no changes, and closing this needs a LedgerRepository change.
The worker refused the un-persistable fields AT THE WIRE rather than accepting
and silently dropping them, which is the right call — a field accepted and
dropped is a lie the schema endorses.

No product regression exists today, because command_history is untouched and
still the live path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- FinishExecution can persist the shell payload and the duration for an entry
  whose row already exists, WITHOUT going through Submit and without disturbing
  the idempotency digest.
- A close on an already-open row and a close that creates its own row record the
  SAME facts. A test asserts both paths against the same expected row, because
  the defect this fixes is precisely that they differed.
- Re-delivery of the close is still a no-op — assert by counting rows and
  executions, not by absence of error.
- Whatever history.query answers from command_history today, it can answer from
  the ledger afterwards. Enumerate those fields from the four read paths in
  sqlite.go and check them off one by one; a field that cannot be answered is a
  finding to report before nocx-rtg0.19 starts, not a gap to discover during it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a ledger entry over the wire (ledger.open), so the row exists.
2. Send ledger.close for that same id carrying an exit code and a durationMs.
3. Read the row: neither is there. FinishExecution takes only EndedAt,
   TerminationReason and Status, and SubmitEntry.Payload/DurationMs are
   write-once at creation.
4. Now repeat with a close for an id that was NEVER opened. That path creates
   the row from the envelope and DOES record the duration. Same method, two
   behaviours, decided by whether an earlier packet arrived.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/workspaces at e900c9ee (d23fbd3d). FinishExecution now writes started_at, ended_at, duration_ms and payload in the same transaction as the run's end, so the two close paths agree by construction rather than by two code paths that happen to match — cmd.entry.DurationMs was REMOVED to make FinishExecution the single writer of those columns. No schema change and no migration: entries already had every column; the UPDATE was simply missing.

The twelve-column checklist did the job it was written for. Four of command_history's columns are not answerable from the ledger, and finding that here rather than mid-cutover is the whole value: trusted is deliberately absent (ADR-0024 deleted it as a field crossing the wire, and the column has been written 0 ever since), host is stored as environment_id with no read seam (nocx-rtg0.25), and masked_count/masked_kinds/redactions have no counterpart at all (nocx-rtg0.24) — that last one also carries RewriteRedaction, whose signature takes command_history's int64 rowid while the ledger's key is a UUIDv7. Both now block nocx-rtg0.19.

Verified on the wire rather than from the report: contracts/history.query.schema.json declares host, maskedCount, maskedKinds and redactions on every entry and does not declare trusted, which confirms both halves of that account.

One narrow reading flagged by the worker and accepted: the schemaV1 comment was corrected without bumping schemaVersion, because the bump exists for shape drift and the shape is byte-identical — bumping would discard every existing store's rows for a comment.

title: ledger.query and ledger.get: the read path, and the only ordering implementation
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §6.2, §6.6.
Split out of nocx-rtg0.3 on 2026-08-17, and the reason is a measurement rather
than a preference.

nocx-rtg0.3 was written as "three events and the queries". The three events map
onto repository methods that EXIST — Submit, StartExecution, FinishExecution. The
queries do not: LedgerRepository offers ListEntries(ctx, limit) and nothing else.
Every filter §6.2 names for ledger.query — environmentId, cwd, kind, status,
since, before, scope — has no read behind it. So the read path is a store change
plus a wire method, and the write path is a wire method over a finished store.
Two different jobs that were sharing one bead.

WHAT LANDS

• A filtered read on LedgerRepository. Ordered by seq DESC — seq is the total
  order (§6.3), assigned by the backend writer. Wall-clock milliseconds are NOT
  a key: two windows submit in the same millisecond, and UUIDv7 is identity
  rather than authority.
• ledger.query { environmentId?, cwd?, kind?, status?, since?, before?, limit,
  scope } -> { entries: Entry[] }.
• ledger.get { id } -> { entry, edges, artifacts: ArtifactMeta[] }. This one
  maps onto Entry, Edges and Artifact, which all exist.
• Schemas in contracts/ with the three checks contracts/README.md requires.

ledger.query IS THE ONLY ORDERING IMPLEMENTATION (§6.2). The frontend cache
renders what it holds and never answers a recall query with its own ordering, or
the same keystroke returns different results depending on which pane it came
from.

DELIBERATELY OUT: ledger.search (full-text over intent and derived output —
needs FTS that does not exist; nocx-rtg0.21) and ledger.attention (the
unreviewed queue; nocx-rtg0.22). Both are filed so neither evaporates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ledger.query with no matches returns {"entries": []} and never null — asserted
  OVER THE REAL SOCKET against the schema, not against a fixture the test built.
  That exact defect has shipped here before: vault.status marshalled providers as
  null and both suites were green.
- Every filter §6.2 names is exercised by a test that proves it EXCLUDES
  something, not merely that it returns rows. A filter that is silently ignored
  returns a superset and looks like it works.
- Ordering is by seq DESC and a test proves it with two entries written inside
  the same millisecond.
- ledger.get returns an entry with its edges and artifact metadata, and an
  unknown id is an error rather than an empty success.
- Both schemas carry additionalProperties:false plus an explicit required, or the
  check is theatre.
close_reason:
Merged into feat/workspaces at a5c65004 (de64cd8e). ledger.query and ledger.get are on the wire, ordered by ingest_seq DESC, inheriting nocx-rtg0.25's environment join rather than adding a second one — a new test measures 1 row against 5 rows in 5 environments and fails if the statement count follows the rows.

All five result fields are answerable: entries always [] and never null, exhausted by fetching limit+1, hasRows read with SELECT EXISTS in the SAME transaction as the page, scope echoed and never silently widened, coverage as MIN(ended_at) store-wide and independent of every filter — asserted by a rung that excludes the oldest row still reporting that row's horizon.

The checklist earned its place again, and this time by catching something a result-shaped checklist could not: the REQUEST is not answerable even though every result field is. history.query takes a text filter and ledger.query has none, so the recall overlay's search box cannot be repointed — nocx-rtg0.26, which now blocks nocx-rtg0.19.

Four mapping decisions the cutover must make are recorded on nocx-rtg0.19 rather than left to be discovered while the table is being deleted: the status enums differ by 'pending', host is nullable here and not there, the paging cursor changes from row id to seq, and the host rung assumes an environment kind that stops holding when containers ship. Plus nocx-rtg0.27, a store trap where an empty payload makes an entry permanently uncloseable.

title: DocumentStore rename can outpace durable bytes and in-memory state
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Inspect internal/storage/document.go writeAtomic: the temp file is written and closed without tmp.Sync before Rename.
2. Inject syncDirectory failure after Rename through a filesystem seam.
3. Observe writeAtomic returns an error after the destination changed; Registry.commitLocked keeps old values/revision although disk contains the new document.
4. A power loss between Rename and durable temp contents can also lose an acknowledged write.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Temp-file contents are synced before Rename.
- The write commit point is explicit.
- A post-Rename directory-sync failure cannot leave Registry memory/revision contradicting the destination document.
- Fault-injection tests cover pre-commit and post-commit failures.
- Existing atomic-write permissions and cleanup remain intact.

Found by security review during nocx-83oba; inherited and not caused by the sandbox diff.

title: In the granted path the tool audit row carries no run id, so the thread does not join
description:
Found by nocx-dw3.3's readback, and asserted there as TestRun_GrantedPathToolAuditCarriesNoRunIdLink.

In the AUTHORISED path (the policy asks a person, they approve) recordProposal writes an approval block carrying runId, so a reader can join the tool attempt to the run. In the GRANTED path - the policy permits the call and nobody is asked, which is the common case at higher autonomy - openAttempt writes the audit row with tool, effect, args and optionally the classifier verdict, and no run id at all. The row exists, carries its grant and its span, and is joined to nothing.

So the epic's criterion "the proposal, the decision, the attempt and the result are one readable thread" holds where a person was asked and does not hold where the agent acted alone. That is the wrong way round: the autonomous case is the one where the ledger is the ONLY account of what happened.

The middleware already holds m.runID (internal/assistant/policy.go:141, wired at newPolicyMiddleware). The change is that the granted attempt's payload names it too. Check before writing: whether any contract schema or renderer surface reads this action payload, since the shape is durable.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run TestRun_GrantedPathToolAuditCarriesNoRunIdLink in internal/transport/ws_run_thread_test.go: an autonomous-preset exchange proposes a tool call, the policy permits it, the call runs and the run completes. The kind=action audit row is present with its grant, its commit order and its span inside the run, and its payload has no approval block and no runId - nothing joins it to the run it belongs to.

## Acceptance Criteria

A granted (unasked) tool call's audit row carries the run id, and a readback joins question, run, attempt and answer into one thread in the granted path exactly as it already does in the authorised one.
TestRun_GrantedPathToolAuditCarriesNoRunIdLink is inverted rather than deleted - it becomes the assertion that the link is there, so the gap cannot come back unnoticed.
The authorised path is unchanged: its approval block still carries runId, attempt, tool, callId and argHash, asserted.
If a contract or renderer reads this payload, it is updated in the same commit; if none does, the report says so.
close_reason: openAttempt now writes the middleware's run id into the granted attempt's payload, so a thread joins where the agent acted alone exactly as it did where a person was asked - the autonomous case being the one where the ledger is the only account of what happened. Written conditionally on the run id being set, so an unbound caller records no link rather than a misleading empty one; the transport's ask always binds it. recordProposal untouched. The test that recorded the gap is inverted and renamed rather than deleted, and the authorised test now pins all five fields of the approval binding. Nothing on the wire or in a contract reads this payload - checked before writing. Merged 9b950f36.

design: Binding design: docs/decisions/0036-sandbox-two-class-directory-grants.md and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-17-sandbox-two-class-permissions-design.md. BMAD proposal: _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/2026-08-17-sandbox-two-class-permissions-change-proposal.md. Plan: .internal/plans/2026-08-17-sandbox-two-class-permissions-v1.md.
