title: Brainstorming: nocx multi-host worker orchestration + tab groups
acceptance_criteria: A design spec exists in .internal/specs/ and the user has approved it
notes:
SUPERSEDED BY THE SPEC. The running summary that was here is now
.internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-lineage-and-orchestration-design.md (second draft),
which is the record. This note keeps only what the spec cannot: what the review changed and why.

Adversarial review by codex, 2026-08-15, then four rounds of argument. It found four defects,
two of them authorial errors in the first draft:

1. AUTHORIAL. The draft said "the attention queue that already exists". It does not:
   frontend/src/tabs.ts:52 is ONE boolean per tab, cleared by activating the tab (:170) and not
   set while the tab is active (:265). nocx-ms7v.4 is a filed bead. Three workers - finished,
   asking, failed - collapse to one dot that activation erases. This is exactly AGENTS.md's
   "a file on main is not a feature", one rung worse: a bead is less than a file.
2. AUTHORIAL. The draft cited ADR-0029 as the notification core; 0029 is about keystrokes.
   nocx-hz94 carries the same wrong number. Filed as nocx-nqm5 (also records that
   docs/decisions/ already holds two 0006 files, so the collision is structural).
3. DESIGN. The draft put an immutable grant on the SESSION. internal/content/ledger.go:319
   already says "Grant is the authority recorded on a run", and :151 says the workspace mints.
   Failure: a session created in staging, dragged to production, shows inside the production
   story while still authorised only for staging.
   The reviewer's first fix - mint per run from the CURRENT workspace - was rejected in
   argument because it restores ADR-0020's original hole with a delay: dragging then confers
   production authority at the next run start, announced by a dialog the user clicks through.
   Landed: AuthorityBinding, approved once by a human, pinned to a policy revision; the
   workspace OFFERS, the human APPROVES, the run REALIZES; moving changes presentation only.
4. DESIGN. The draft's capability token in the environment is not ADR-0028 narrowing - every
   descendant inherits it, so `npm test` hands it to a postinstall script. An inherited FD does
   not fix it either (the agent cannot pass it to a shim without passing it to every child;
   CLOEXEC stops the shim too). Landed: enrolment of a process TREE, pinned by a non-reusable
   handle, approved once by a human. The reviewer's "only nocx-launched agents may enrol" was
   rejected in argument - it breaks the owner's stated case, `claude` typed into a tab by hand.
   Enrolment is therefore an act available to an already-running foreground process.

Also changed: lineage carries provenance ONLY, with a separate revocable Delegation for
continuing authority (takeover suspends send-input, preserves observe - ADR-0020 §3's
"demoted, not evicted"; the discriminator is "did the authenticated authority context change",
not "did a human touch the PTY"). Liveness gains `unknown` and an epoch. D11 drops
"precedence is time order" - there is no shared clock, and evidence is instead bound to
session epoch + lifecycle domain + attempt + output offset, which is the one thing nocx knows
that no orchestrator does. D4 revised TODAY though epic E is deferred, because its first form
("a version mismatch refuses") strands a live session with no rescue.

REJECTED FROM THE REVIEW: deriving ephemeral focus sets instead of user-created workspaces.
Settled owner input, not an open question.

CARRIED TO THE OWNER, NOT ADOPTED: a narrow exception to AGENTS.md's "no backward-compatibility
shims" for a deployed generation holding irrecoverable live external state. Spec §9.4.

NOT YET COMMITTED: the pre-commit hook refuses a docs-only commit in a worktree without
frontend/node_modules, though the commit's classification would run zero gates. Filed nocx-02vx.
Awaiting the owner's choice between `npm ci` and --no-verify.

title: The settings rail is a flat list of nine, so related pages sit apart and the next AI page lands anywhere
description:
Owner, 2026-08-15, on being shown the AI Endpoints page: 'а все настройки AI куда запихивать будем? отдельной страницей? если да, то кажется нужна группировка или табы в настройках'. And immediately after: 'secrets и vault из той же оперы'.

## What is wrong

frontend/src/settings.tsx:919 renders one flat <ul>: the sections generated from backend declarations (Interface, History, Clipboard, Test) followed by the component pages (Backup & Restore, Connections, Secrets, Vault, AI Endpoints). Nine peers, no structure. Vault and Secrets are one subject and sit apart from each other; Test is a fixture section shown to users; and the assistant is about to add at least a second page (the grant/permissions and the masking policy are named in the design and in nocx-a21v), which today would land wherever the registry array happens to put it.

## This was already decided, and deferred on purpose

.internal/specs/2026-07-26-tab-and-settings-foundation-design.md, Bucket 2: 'nested categories' are listed as OUT OF SCOPE until a real declaration needs one, and the same paragraph binds HOW they arrive — 'as declaration schema in Go, never as frontend exceptions'. The condition has now arrived. So this is executing that decision, not making a new one, and a frontend-side lookup table of ids to group names is the one shape it may not take.

## Groups vs tabs — decided

Groups in the rail, not tabs inside a page. Three reasons, and the first is the binding one: page identity is already an address (SettingsComponentHandle.scrollToKey, newSecret and newConnection all open a page by id, from the palette and from the prompt), and a tab level makes that address two-part and gives two surfaces a claim on 'which page am I on' — the thing AGENTS.md forbids. Second, tabs would fix the assistant only, while the rail's problem is also Vault/Secrets. Third, Bucket 2 wants a schema field, which a rail group is and a tab strip is not.

## The structure the owner approved

- Assistant — Endpoints (renamed: the group carries the 'AI'), later the grant/permissions page and the masking policy
- Vault — the vault page and Secrets
- Connections — TOP LEVEL, no group. The owner's call: it is a working surface, not a setting.
- Application — Interface, Clipboard, History, Backup & Restore
- Developer — Test

A page with no group renders at top level, so grouped and ungrouped entries coexist in one rail. That is a requirement, not an accident of the data.

## Where the group lives

The group belongs to the SECTION, not to the individual setting. A Group field on each Declaration would let two declarations in one section name different groups — a contradiction the type would permit. So Go declares the group catalogue (id, title, order) and which group each section belongs to, and it ships in the settings snapshot beside the declarations. A component page is not a declaration and cannot come from Go, so its registry entry in settings.tsx names a group ID from that catalogue. One catalogue with one owner; two kinds of member.

## The rail is kit work

frontend/src/ui/README.md first. The rail is currently hand-rolled inside settings.tsx as <nav><ul class='ui-settings-section-nav'> with ghost Buttons, while the kit owns PageRail (page-rail.tsx) — a surface is building its own navigation control. Grouping goes into the kit with its identity classes, its CSS in styles/components/, its test and its README row; settings.tsx places it and does not repaint it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The rail renders group headings, and every page appears under exactly its declared group; a page with no group renders at top level alongside the groups, asserted with Connections.
- A generated section's group comes from the Go snapshot: adding a section to a group is a Go-side change with no frontend edit, asserted by a test that adds one through the settings registry and reads the rail.
- Two declarations in the same section can never disagree about the group — the type does not permit stating it twice, asserted by construction (there is no per-declaration group field).
- A group id a page names but the catalogue does not declare is a build or test failure, not a page silently rendered at top level.
- Deep links still resolve to a page id alone: scrollToKey, newSecret and newConnection open their page with the group expanded/visible, and no second address component is introduced, asserted.
- Search results still name their section, and searching is not scoped to a group.
- Test is under Developer and no user-facing group.
- The grouped rail is a kit component with an identity class family, a CSS file in styles/components/, a test suite and a README row; settings.tsx contains no bespoke nav markup afterwards.

## Deliberately out

The Assistant group has exactly one page today. The later ones (grant/permissions, masking) are not built here; this bead is the rail and the schema only. Renaming the vault page itself is a separate question.
notes:
Owner, 2026-08-15, approved: the vault page inside the Vault group is renamed **Protection** (provider, passphrase, sealing, reset), so the group reads Vault → Protection + Secrets rather than Vault → Vault. This supersedes the 'Deliberately out' line that called the rename a separate question.

Added criterion: the page's registry id stays 'vault' — only the display title changes. Deep links (activeComponentPage('vault')) and any test selecting by id must be unaffected, asserted; a rename that moved the id would break the palette's entry points, which is the whole reason page identity is an address.
close_reason: Shipped. The rail is grouped from a backend catalogue: internal/settings/settings.go:941 registers the assistant, vault, application and developer groups, the kit gained frontend/src/ui/grouped-rail.tsx with its CSS, test and README row, and settings.tsx consumes the snapshot via setGroups(desc.groups) rather than a lookup table. Tests: settings_test.go:918 and frontend/src/settings.test.ts:733. Commits 97f40d3f, 5681ea82, ca94606f, 77f62a84, 8f81d338. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: EditableRowList rebuilds every row on a keystroke, and the model field's suggestions are browser chrome
description:
Two defects in one surface, found while the endpoint form was being used for real.

1. EditableRowList keyed its rows with <For> over values, and both callers replace the row object on every edit. A value-keyed list disposes the row's DOM and rebuilds it per keystroke — taking focus, IME composition, selection and any open popup with it. Keying by position (<Index>) with an accessor row is the fix; the accessor becomes the component's identity contract and callers must read row().field inside a binding.

2. The model field offered its suggestions through a native <datalist>: type, spacing, colours and lifecycle owned by the browser, not the kit. The kit had no combobox at all — a missing primitive, not a near-fit.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings -> AI Endpoints -> add an endpoint.
2. Type into the model row's name field. Each keystroke rebuilds the row: focus is lost and any open suggestion list closes on the very write that carried the keystroke.
3. Observe the suggestion list: it is the browser's datalist, in the platform's type and colours, not the kit's.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Typing into a row of EditableRowList keeps the same DOM node: focus, selection and an open suggestion list survive the keystroke, asserted.
- Both callers (connections forwards, endpoint models) read the accessor and update in place, asserted.
- Model suggestions render through a kit component with our type and colours, keyboard-operable (Up/Down/Enter/Escape) and carrying combobox ARIA, asserted.
- A value the suggestion list does not contain is still typeable and submitted — the list narrows what is offered and never refuses a value, asserted.
- The new component has its identity class family, its own CSS file, a test suite and a README row.
close_reason: EditableRowList keys by position with an accessor row, so a keystroke no longer disposes the row's DOM; the native datalist is replaced by SuggestionField, the combobox the kit did not have. Merged as c0e3770a.

title: The endpoint form invents its own key input instead of reusing secret selection
description:
Owner, 2026-08-15: "мы должны переиспользовать выбор секрета, а не внедрять
новую механику."

The connections editor already answers "where does this secret come from": a
segmented control — Choose file / Path / Paste key / Secret — and, when Secret
is chosen, a picker of the vault's existing secrets ("Key for root@192.168.0.57").
The endpoints editor answers the same question with a bare password field and
the sentence "Leave blank to keep the saved key. A new key replaces it."

Two vocabularies for one concept, and the newer one is strictly poorer:

- An endpoint can only MINT a key. It cannot reference a secret the vault
  already holds, so a person with one API key used in two places stores it
  twice, and rotating it is two edits and a silent divergence.
- "Leave blank to keep" is a mode the person has to infer from a caption.
  The connections control makes the mode explicit and selectable, which is
  why it does not need the caption.
- The endpoint's key cannot be seen, named, or reused from the Secrets page
  the way a connection's can.

This is the same shape as ADR-0030's own reasoning: an endpoint REFERENCES a
secret it owns. Owning one is a case of referencing one; the form only
implements owning.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings -> Connections -> edit a profile -> Authentication -> Public Key.
   Note the source segmented control and the saved-secret picker.
2. Settings -> AI Endpoints -> edit an endpoint. The key is a bare field with
   a caption describing an implicit mode.

## Expected behavior

The endpoint's key uses the SAME control the connections editor uses: choose an
existing vault secret, or provide new material. One vocabulary, one component.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The endpoint editor's key uses the connections editor's secret-selection
  component; there is no second control and no second "leave blank" convention.
  Extend that component if it needs a variant; do not fork it.
- An endpoint can reference an EXISTING vault secret without minting a copy,
  asserted end to end, with the Secrets page showing one secret used by both
  holders.
- Replacing an endpoint's key still works, and the implicit "leave blank to
  keep" mode is gone — the mode is whatever the control says it is.
- nocx-4egm (a key typed into the form is stored without one) is re-checked
  against the reused control; the two may share a cause.
close_reason: An endpoint carries custom HTTP headers, sent on the completion and on the connection check; a header value is a literal or a vault reference chosen with the same source control the key uses, which is the control the connections editor already had, now shared. Refused names and control characters are rejected before any request; headers drop across an origin change like the credential. ADR-0030's open question — may an endpoint reference a secret it does not own — is answered there: owning is a case of referencing. Merged as a7d38e9c and 96141079.

title: An AI endpoint can carry custom HTTP headers
description:
Owner, 2026-08-15: "нужно в форму добавить возможность использовать
собственные заголовки http, если пользователю необходимо".

Real need, not a nicety. OpenRouter wants HTTP-Referer and X-Title for
attribution and rate limits; Azure OpenAI authenticates with api-key rather
than Authorization; corporate gateways want a tenant or a routing header.
Without this those endpoints are simply unusable, whatever else works.

## What this is

Zero or more name/value pairs on the endpoint record, sent on every request
that endpoint makes — the streaming completion AND the connection check, so a
Test that passes means the real calls will too. The editor already has
EditableRowList for the model rows; header rows are the same shape.

## The decisions this must make deliberately

- WHERE THE VALUE LIVES. A header value can be a credential (Azure's api-key
  IS the key). If any header value may hold a secret, it belongs in the vault
  like the API key does (ADR-0030), not in the record. Decide, and write down
  why — a record that holds one secret in the vault and another in plain text
  is worse than either choice made consistently.
- WHAT MAY BE SET. Header injection is the obvious hazard: names and values
  must be validated (no control characters, no CR/LF) — see hasControlChars
  and validateProbeParams in ws_assistant.go. And some headers must NOT be
  settable: Authorization would silently fight the credential resolution, and
  Host, Content-Length and the hop-by-hop set would break the request. Name
  the refused set and say why each is on it.
- REDIRECTS. httpguard.go drops the credential across an origin change. Custom
  headers must follow the SAME rule or the guard has a hole beside it: a
  header carrying a token would survive a redirect the Authorization header
  would not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An endpoint with custom headers sends them on the completion and on the
  connection check, asserted against the e2e fake, which already records every
  request's headers.
- A header name or value carrying CR/LF or a control character is refused
  before any request is made, asserted.
- The refused-name set is enforced and its message names which header and why.
- Headers are dropped across an origin change exactly as the credential is,
  asserted with a redirect.
- The form edits them through the kit's EditableRowList; no bespoke control.
close_reason: An endpoint carries custom HTTP headers, sent on the completion and on the connection check; a header value is a literal or a vault reference chosen with the same source control the key uses, which is the control the connections editor already had, now shared. Refused names and control characters are rejected before any request; headers drop across an origin change like the credential. ADR-0030's open question — may an endpoint reference a secret it does not own — is answered there: owning is a case of referencing. Merged as a7d38e9c and 96141079.

title: Reaching for a locked vault must raise the unlock dialog, not report a dead end
description:
Owner, 2026-08-15: "Даже если vault заблокирован у нас архитектурно сделано
так, чтобы при обращении к vault появлялся диалог разблокировки."

The architecture already does this and the assistant path does not use it.
`saveSecretWithVault` raises the setup/unlock sheet and retries the operation;
`RequestUnlock` exists on the transport and `vault.unlockResolved` is in the
closed ingress-critical set precisely so a resolution cannot queue behind the
lane. That is the established answer to "the vault is sealed and I need a
secret".

The assistant path answers it differently, and wrongly, in two places I wrote
today:

1. `refusedProbeResult` (ws_assistant.go) returns a probe RESULT reading "the
   endpoint's credential is unavailable — unlock the vault". It tells the
   person to do the thing the product is supposed to offer to do. A Test
   button that names the obstacle instead of clearing it is a dead end with
   good manners.
2. `agentStatusLine` maps `credentialResolvable: false` to "Credential
   unavailable — the vault may be locked". But
   `assistantStatusHandlers.credentialResolvableFor` returns false for THREE
   different facts — no reference at all, the secret was deleted, the vault is
   sealed — and the sentence asserts the third. An endpoint that simply has no
   key is told to unlock a vault, which is not its problem.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an endpoint whose key is in the vault; seal the vault.
2. Press Test. The result names the locked vault instead of offering to unlock
   it.
3. Separately: configure an endpoint with NO key. The readiness line says "the
   vault may be locked".

## Expected behavior

Reaching for a credential the vault holds raises the unlock dialog and resumes
the operation, as the connections and secrets paths already do. And a status
sentence names the fact that is actually true.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Test on an endpoint whose credential needs a sealed vault raises the unlock
  sheet and completes the probe after unsealing, asserted end to end.
- Cancelling the unlock leaves no fabricated verdict and no toast claiming a
  failure the user chose.
- The three cases behind `credentialResolvable: false` are distinguished on
  the wire and each gets its own sentence; an endpoint with no key never
  mentions the vault.
notes:
2026-08-15, coordinator, answering the owner's 'Любое обращение к vault уже должно триггерить разблокировку. Это не так?':

NO — and that is the actual defect, larger than the assistant path.

RequestUnlock is threaded into exactly ONE call site: app.go's connection.NewResolver(..., connection.WithUnlockRequester(tp.RequestUnlock), ...). The SSH connection path raises the unlock dialog because somebody wired it there by hand. The secret store itself does not: secrets.Get(ctx, id) from anywhere else returns an error and leaves the caller to describe it.

So 'reaching for the vault raises unlock' is the right architecture and a wrong description of the code. It is true for connections and nowhere else.

CONSEQUENCE: fixing the assistant path by threading RequestUnlock into it too would make a THIRD owner of one behaviour, and the fourth caller would arrive without it exactly as this one did. The owner is the secret-access layer, not each caller. Every path — endpoints, the ask, whatever comes next — should get the unlock because it asked the vault for a secret, not because somebody remembered.

Same shape as the params-validator defect fixed in 3b47ae3 today: a behaviour that lived as a convention each caller had to remember, made structural instead. Scope this bead accordingly: the fix is one owner, not one more caller.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-y7fg, which was filed 2026-07-31 at P0 and is still open. I filed this without running AGENTS.md's first check ('Already filed?'), which would have found it in seconds. Findings worth keeping have been moved onto y7fg.

title: e2e/git-panel.spec.ts asserts the old SSH refusal, which the remote helper made false
description:
Found by the coordinator running the containerized e2e job on the merged tree
for epic nocx-457v: 290 passed, 2 failed, and the two are the same spec in
chromium and webkit.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On the merged epic branch, run `make ci-e2e`.
2. `e2e/git-panel.spec.ts:699` — "on an SSH tab the mutation controls are absent
   from the DOM, not merely disabled" — fails after ~22s in both browsers.

The spec is not wrong about the old product; it encodes the refusal the epic
existed to remove. Its own name is the claim that is now false. This is a stale
test, not a regression: nothing in the merged branch broke the panel, the panel
simply does something different now and this spec still asserts the old thing.

What the truth is now, and why the fix is not just an inversion: on an SSH tab
the answer depends on consent. With no consent recorded for that machine,
git.open answers consentRequired and the panel offers consent — the mutation
controls are still absent, but the reason and the surface are different, and the
spec must assert the offer rather than bare absence. With a consented, installed
helper the controls are PRESENT, which is git D14: what the panel cannot do it
does not draw, and now it can. That positive path is already covered by
e2e/git-remote.spec.ts (nocx-9rz0), so this spec should own the no-consent path.

Not caught earlier because a worker on this plan does not run the e2e suite —
that is the coordinator's job at the merge gate, and it worked as intended. The
coordinator's own review of nocx-1xxa checked the two greps the plan named
(OpenRemoteUnsupported, "wait on the relay") but did not search for other specs
asserting the old behaviour, which is the gap worth remembering.

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] e2e/git-panel.spec.ts asserts what the panel does now on an SSH tab with no
    consent: the consent offer is present and the mutation controls are not.
[ ] `make ci-e2e` is green in both chromium and webkit.
[ ] No other e2e spec still asserts the pre-helper SSH refusal — grep for it
    rather than assuming this was the only one.
close_reason: The spec now owns the no-consent path: e2e/git-panel.spec.ts:701 asserts the consent offer is present and the mutation controls absent. Green in both browsers in the container, alongside git-remote.spec.ts:248 (the epic's acceptance test). Fix committed as dfc3cb43 on feat/git-manager.

title: Test endpoint conflates two checks, so it is dead exactly when it is needed
description:
Owner, 2026-08-14, looking at a New Endpoint dialog with name, base URL and key
filled and no models yet: "зачем тебе модель, чтобы проверить соединение?"

Nothing. The button conflates two different checks:

1. CAN I REACH THIS API WITH THIS KEY — address, TLS, key, entitlement. Needs
   no model at all; `GET {baseUrl}/models` answers it in one request.
2. DOES THIS MODEL ANSWER — needs a model id, and streaming a real completion
   is the right way to ask.

`endpoints.probe` does only (2), and `testDisabled()` therefore requires a first
model. So in the one state where a person most wants to know whether the URL and
key are right — a brand-new endpoint, no models typed yet — the control is grey
and says nothing about why. The `No models — add the model id the API
understands.` line sits below it and is not connected to it.

The form's order compounds it: the Test button renders ABOVE the model list, so
it appears before the thing it requires.

And the response to (1) carries the endpoint's model ids, which is what the
person is otherwise typing by hand. Nothing in the repo touches `/models` today
(grepped: no hits in internal/ or frontend/src).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings -> AI Endpoints -> "+ New endpoint".
2. Fill Name, Base URL and API key. Add no model.
3. "Test endpoint" is disabled, with no statement of why.

## Expected behavior

Test checks the connection as soon as there is a base URL, needs no model, and
reports what it found. A per-model check remains available where a model exists.
No control is disabled without saying why.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a base URL and a key and NO model, Test runs and reports whether the
  endpoint is reachable and the key accepted — asserted end to end against a
  real backend.
- A successful connection test makes the endpoint's models selectable, and
  typing a model id by hand STILL WORKS: `/models` is not universally
  implemented, and a picker that gates configuration would make a working
  endpoint unconfigurable. Asserted both ways, including an endpoint that
  answers 404 to `/models`.
- The per-model streaming check still exists where a model is present.
- No disabled control in this dialog without a rendered reason.
- The request rides the guarded HTTP client, so the dial-time address rule and
  the drop-credential-on-origin-change rule apply unchanged.
- Credential resolution is nocx-reu5's rule, unchanged: a typed key wins, else
  the named endpoint's stored credential, else none.
close_reason: Test needs no model: an absent model routes to a connection check (GET /models over the guarded client) and the result names which check ran. A 404 to /models is a successful connection check. Discovered models are suggestions, never a gate, and are fetched silently on focus too. Plus the params prohibition and the 102-method sweep. Merged as c73f2381.

title: Test button on a saved endpoint always probes with an empty key
description:
The Test button probes the form's DRAFT values, and `openEdit` deliberately
leaves the key blank — ADR-0030 section 3, the material never crosses back, and
an empty key on update means "keep the existing material". `runProbe` then
sends `key: d.key`, so testing a SAVED endpoint sends an unauthenticated
request.

Against any endpoint that requires a key that is a 401, and the button reports
a failure for an endpoint that works perfectly. The control lies in exactly the
case it exists for: you press Test on the endpoint you already configured, to
find out whether it still works.

Why it was not caught: the only path anyone exercised is a NEW endpoint with a
key typed into the form, where `d.key` is the real key. And the local-model
case (Ollama and friends) legitimately has no key, so an empty key succeeds
there too. Both green, the middle case broken.

The shape is deeper than the missing value. `endpoints.probe` takes a raw key
string, so it has no way to say "use the credential this endpoint owns" — which
is the whole of ADR-0030. The probe needs to accept the endpoint id and let the
BACKEND resolve the secret, exactly as the ask path does; a typed key still
wins when present, because testing a new key before saving it is the other
thing this button is for.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an AI endpoint with a real base URL and a real API key. Save it.
2. Open it for editing. The key field is blank, as designed.
3. Press Test.
4. The probe fails on authentication, although the saved endpoint is fine.

## Expected behavior

Testing a saved endpoint tests what will actually be used — its stored
credential. Typing a new key into the form tests that key instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Test on a saved endpoint whose key is in the vault succeeds, asserted
  end to end against a real backend, with the request carrying the stored
  credential as its Bearer.
- Test with a key typed into the form uses the typed key, not the stored one.
- Test on an endpoint with no credential (a local model) still probes without
  one.
- The key is never sent back to the renderer at any point.
- A sealed or unavailable vault gives a probe RESULT naming that, not a Go
  error and not a silent failure.
notes:
2026-08-14, owner: 'вот кнопка в форме, как ты думаешь чего я ждал? Конечно
она должна работать. Либо убрать ее отсюда вовсе. Мы кажется такую же проблему
решали в тесте ssh соединения.'

THE EXISTING ANSWER, and it is exactly where the owner pointed:
connections.test takes ONE parameter — profileId (internal/transport/ws_probe.go,
connectionsTestParams). The renderer names the record; the BACKEND resolves the
profile and its secret and dials. The material never crosses the wire in either
direction, and the test tests what will actually be used.

endpoints.probe took name/baseUrl/key/model instead — the draft, with the key as
a raw string. That is why testing a saved endpoint sends no key at all: openEdit
deliberately leaves the field blank (ADR-0030 section 3).

So this is not a missing default. endpoints.probe must be able to name the
endpoint and let the backend resolve the credential it owns, the way
connections.test already does. Extending that existing shape is the fix; a
default or a re-fetch on the renderer side would be a second answer to a
question the repo has already answered.

WHAT SURVIVES BEYOND THE PRECEDENT: a draft that has not been saved yet must
still be testable, and a key typed into the form must win over the stored one —
that is the other half of what this button is for, and connections.test has no
equivalent because a connection is always saved before it is tested.
close_reason: endpoints.probe now names the endpoint and the backend resolves the credential it owns — the connections.test shape. A typed key still wins. A credential that cannot be resolved is a probe RESULT naming that, never a no-key dial. Proven at the wire in e2e: stored key, typed key and no-credential all assert the actual Authorization header, and the key field is asserted empty throughout. Merged as 0b3c54d4.

title: The notification policy is never constructed: suppression, debounce and coalescing do not run
description:
notify.NewPolicy has no production caller. deadcode reports Policy.Submit,
Policy.flush, Policy.suppressed and WithResultHandler unreachable. The pipeline
wired in a5d3d67e is notify.raise -> Router -> banner: the policy is bypassed, so
suppression, the debounce window and coalescing are written, tested, and never
run.

Two things block wiring it, and they are different sizes.

1. Focus. Policy needs a notify.Focus with WindowFocused() and FocusedSession().
   The backend knows neither -- the renderer owns which tab is active, and no
   channel reports it. This is the mirror of nocx-jiwq.1: that one is
   backend->renderer (focus this tab), this one is renderer->backend (I am
   looking at this tab). Both are the same missing seam.

   A default that reports "nothing focused" is honest and unblocks most of the
   value: debounce and coalescing need no focus at all, and suppression then
   never suppresses, which is the safe direction -- the user is notified rather
   than silently not. Mirror notify.HostHolder, which does exactly this for the
   attention surface.

2. The wire contract. NotifyRaiser is Raise(ctx, ev) Outcome and the handler maps
   out.Err to -32603. Policy.Submit(ev) returns a Disposition and delivers later,
   when the window closes, so there is no synchronous outcome to report. That is
   arguably the correct semantics -- a program asking for a notification should
   not block until a debounce window closes -- but it changes what notify.raise
   answers and how a delivery failure becomes visible. Decide it deliberately;
   ADR-0029 requires a refused delivery to be visible somewhere the product can
   show, and today the only path is the result handler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- notify.NewPolicy is constructed in the composition root and deadcode reports
  nothing unreachable in internal/notify.
- Two raises for the same session and kind inside the window produce ONE banner
  naming the count, observed end to end rather than in a unit test.
- A raise for the session the user is looking at is suppressed once focus is
  reported; with no focus reporting it is delivered, not dropped.
- notify.raise's answer, and how a delivery failure reaches the user, are stated
  in the ADR or the spec before this closes.
close_reason: Already done on feat/notificcations before this wave: notify.NewPolicy is constructed at internal/app/app.go:829 with notify.FocusHolder{} as the honest 'nothing focused' default the bead asked for, and deadcode -filter 'nocx/internal/notify' reports nothing unreachable but test helpers. Verified by the coordinator against the tree, not taken on report. The bead's second blocker — what notify.raise answers when delivery is deferred — was decided rather than dropped: the RPC keeps its immediate {} acceptance, and the visibility of a post-acceptance failure is nocx-r6pxp, which depends on nocx-sb3f. The WithResultHandler wired at app.go:831 today only calls logger.Warn, which is exactly the invisibility r6pxp tracks.

title: Backend cannot ask the renderer to focus a tab, so notification click has nowhere to land
description:
internal/notify/wailsadapter's Host takes Lookup (sessionID -> tab) and Focus
(tabID -> error) and cannot be given either, because no such capability exists.
PublishLifecycle is the only backend->renderer push in internal/transport and it
carries lifecycle facts only; the renderer has tab.focus() in frontend/src/tabs.ts
but nothing reaches it from the backend.

Discovered while wiring nocx-hg2a into the composition root. The adapter already
handles the absence honestly -- it logs "notification click cannot be honored: no
tab resolver is wired" and refuses to focus anything -- so banners deliver today
and clicks do nothing. That is acceptable only while no UI offers click-to-focus.

The shape this needs: a control-plane notification from the backend naming a
session, and a renderer handler that activates the owning tab. AD-1 governs it
(control plane, not data plane) and AD-7 matters -- session id is
server-authoritative, so the backend names the session and the renderer resolves
which tab holds it, rather than the backend guessing a tab.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A backend-initiated control-plane message names a session and the renderer
  activates the tab that owns it.
- wailsadapter.Host is constructed with real Lookup and Focus, and the "no tab
  resolver is wired" error path is unreachable in production.
- An automated check watches a notification click bring the owning tab forward.
- Clicking a notification for a session whose tab has closed does nothing visible
  and does not error to the user.
notes:
ANSWER TO THE OPEN QUESTION (coordinator, 2026-08-15): ADDRESS BY SESSION.

The worker's refined position is right, and the reason is stronger than 'the
backend has no tab id today'. It is that the backend must never acquire one:

  - AD-7 makes the SESSION the identity the backend legitimately owns and is
    server-authoritative over. A tab is a renderer concept.
  - A tab can hold several sessions — ws_history_record.go's own sessionIDsOf
    comment says so — so 'the tab that spoke' is not even well defined from the
    backend's side. The session that spoke is.
  - The renderer already knows which tab a session is in, so session -> tab is a
    lookup it can do and nobody else can.

So notify addresses sessionId; the renderer resolves it and focuses. No new
backend concept, and nothing here waits on nocx-ebl4 — that epic adds session
IDENTITY (epoch, parent edge, workspaceId, liveness), not tab identity, so
jiwq.1 is NOT blocked by it and can proceed now.

This also settles nocx-wyp3p, filed the same day for the other half of the same
confusion: tabID(wconn) returns the WebSocket connection id while being named
for a tab. Its resolution is to be renamed to the connection it actually scopes,
or re-keyed on the session — never given a third, invented identity.

Recorded in .internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-ux-design.md §5.2, which also
records that the first draft of that section argued the opposite and was wrong.
SEAM CHANGED UNDER YOU, 2026-08-16, during the Wails v3 migration (nocx-mgbjx). Your acceptance says the adapter is 'constructed with real Lookup and Focus'. That pair is gone, and it should be read as Focus(sessionID) now.

WHY IT WENT. Deps.Lookup(sessionID) -> tab plus Deps.Focus(tab) required the BACKEND to resolve a session id to a tab, which is an addressing identity the backend deliberately does not have — a tab can hold several sessions, and every backend-to-renderer address in this product is a sessionId the renderer resolves. That is why no composition root could ever supply the pair, and why every valid click was discarded: the seam asked for something that does not exist on this side of the wire.

WHAT EXISTS NOW. Deps.Focus is func(sessionID string) error and main.go supplies it: it raises the window and returns an error naming the session it could not route, so an unrouted click is logged by session rather than dropped silently.

WHAT IS STILL YOURS, and it is the whole of this bead: actually activating the tab. That needs a backend-to-renderer control-plane notification over the WebSocket (AD-1), a renderer handler, and a contract schema — internal/transport, contracts/, frontend/. Wails v3's EmitEvent was deliberately NOT used as a shortcut: it would be a second control plane beside the one AD-1 declares, and the v3 runtime here is wired for bindings only.

Also relevant: a test that enshrined the old shape was rewritten. TestClickUnknownSession used to assert the backend resolves a session id and finds none — it asserted the invented identity. It now asserts the click reaches Focus and that a Focus failure is logged naming the session.
close_reason: Closed

title: Files panel self-saturates on remote startup
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open an SSH session whose filesystem provider takes longer than the filesystem domain wait to list the root.
2. Open the Files panel.
3. Observe that the renderer submits files.list and files.watch for the new binding without waiting for the initial listing.
4. One request acquires the capacity-one filesystem conflict gate; the other is refused with -32004 control-saturated and the product shows the sticky "The terminal is busy" toast.

## Expected
The Files panel establishes its root listing first, then installs the matching watch set. The product must not create two conflicting filesystem operations during startup or first expansion. Directories that cannot be listed are not polled.

## Actual
openScope issues issueList and pushWatchSet back-to-back. Dispatcher work is concurrent, so either request can win the filesystem gate. Reveal/expand paths can likewise publish a watch for a directory before its first listing settles.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new files binding whose initial files.list is still pending, when the panel opens, then files.watch has not been submitted. Given that initial list succeeds, when its result is applied, then files.watch is submitted for the root. Given a newly expanded directory whose first files.list is pending, then it is not added to the watch set until the list succeeds; tooLarge, timedOut, and error directories are not watched. Existing reconnect and explicit refresh retry behavior remains available.
close_reason: Files panel startup, first expansion, reveal and refresh now sequence list/watch work instead of contending for the capacity-one filesystem gate. Pending or failed directories never enter the watch set; reveal baselines once after the full walk. Red ordering tests, 39 store tests, full frontend gate (146 files / 2682 tests), containerized Files E2E (8/8), Wails debug build, and native smoke all pass.

title: The remote-helper plan's task split cannot pass the deadcode ratchet: task 4 adds a package nothing calls until task 5
description:
Found while supervising task 4 of the remote-helper plan
(.internal/plans/2026-08-13-remote-helper.md). Same shape as nocx-z7s6, which
filed it against the snippets plan: this is the second plan with the defect, so
it is a planning failure mode rather than one bad plan.

Task 4 creates `internal/helper/proto` — a frame codec — and nothing imports it
until Task 5 creates `cmd/nocx-helper`. On its own it is unreachable from every
main() in the module, so `.githooks/check-deadcode.mjs` fails the commit, and
`update-deadcode-baseline.mjs` refuses to write a baseline that grows. There is
no sanctioned way to commit Task 4 alone.

The gate is right and must not be worked around. A codec package with no caller
is exactly the shape AGENTS.md records shipping twice (nocx-rtg0's
ContentDB.Add, nocx-ak2d's InstalledFactStore.Record — written, covered, wired,
and called by nobody). The plan is what is wrong.

The same question is open, unmeasured, for Tasks 6, 9 and 10:
`internal/helper/client`, the deploy package and the consent path are all
reachable only once Task 11 wires them into app.go. Tasks 7 and 8 are probably
fine — a git service registers into the host and so is reached from
cmd/nocx-helper — but that is a prediction, and predicting is what caused this
bead. Measure each one.

Note what it cost the first time: per nocx-z7s6, a worker read "run only your
unit tests" as excluding the pre-commit hook and committed through
`git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`. A correctly-briefed worker is simply stuck
instead, which is what happened here — the worker stopped and reported rather
than bypassing, and wrote no code at all.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Implement plan Task 4 (`internal/helper/proto`) exactly as written.
2. `git commit` it on its own.
3. The pre-commit hook fails the deadcode ratchet: every function in the new
   package is unreachable from main(), and the committed baseline may only
   shrink.

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] The plan states explicitly which tasks land as one commit, and every landing
    group passes `node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs` on its own.
[ ] The grouping is derived from a measured violation list, not predicted.
[ ] Worker briefs for this plan name the pre-commit hook as a gate the worker
    must pass, so "run only your unit tests" cannot be read as licence to bypass
    it.
close_reason: Every landing group in the plan has now been measured against node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs on a real tree, and the plan records them: tasks 4+5+the helper half of 7 as one commit, 6+the client half of 7 with its composition-root wiring, 9 with its Ensure wiring, 10, and 11. The two acceptance criteria are met — the plan states which tasks share a commit, and every grouping was derived from a measured violation list rather than predicted. The third is met too: every worker brief on this plan named the pre-commit hook as a gate that must pass, after nocx-z7s6 recorded a worker reading 'run only your unit tests' as licence to commit through core.hooksPath=/dev/null. The pattern recurred five times in total and the answer was never a hand-edited baseline, never a bypass, and never a production knob invented to make a test seam reachable: twice the seam was deleted because it should not have existed, twice the code was deferred to land with its caller, and once dependency injection removed the need for the seam entirely. One durable lesson is in bd remember: an instruction to REMOVE code must carry an instruction to park it at a git tag first, because consent.Store.Grant was removed from a working tree before its only commit and became genuinely unrecoverable.

title: The ledger has no owner for 'which workspace does this session belong to'
description:
nocx-f4s5 needed to record a ledger `sessions` row for the tab a frame was
captured from, and found that the schema demands a workspace owner per session
while the product has no workspace concept at all: no registry, no minting, no
grant policy, no reader. ADR-0020 section 5's workspace is schema-complete and
unused, and the ledger write path has no production caller, so there was no
existing authoritative seam to extend.

What f4s5 did, deliberately and reversibly: a session that is NOT already
recorded is ensured under `content.DefaultWorkspaceID` ("workspace:default")
and its `sessions.payload` is stamped with `captureEnsuredSessionMarker`. A
session recorded by anyone else keeps its own workspace and never gets the
marker (ensure is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), and
TestCaptureFrame_PreservesAnExistingSessionsWorkspace asserts both ends.

What is NOT decided, and is why this is a bug rather than a note: the
authoritative mapping from a session to its real workspace. Whoever invents
workspaces owns it. The marker exists so that decision stays executable — the
migration MUST re-parent the marked rows to their real workspaces BEFORE
dropping the default row, because sessions.workspace_id is ON DELETE CASCADE
and dropping first deletes every synthetic session.

Two writers for one table is the shape AD-8 forbids; this closes when there is
one.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Capture a frame from any live tab (`agent.captureFrame`).
2. Read the ledger: `SELECT workspace_id, payload FROM sessions`.
3. The row sits under `workspace:default` with the ensure marker in its
   payload — a workspace nobody chose, because nothing in the product can
   choose one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single owner decides a session's workspace, and `CaptureFrame` reads it
  rather than minting a fallback.
- `DefaultWorkspaceID` and `captureEnsuredSessionMarker` are deleted, and the
  migration that re-parents the marked rows has run before the default row is
  dropped.
- A test proves a session captured before the cutover still resolves to its
  real workspace afterwards.
acceptance_criteria:
• A single owner decides a session's workspace, and CaptureFrame reads it rather than minting a fallback. Two writers for one table is the AD-8 shape this bug is about; it closes when there is one.
• captureEnsuredSessionMarker is deleted. It means "nobody chose this workspace", and once an owner exists nothing is unchosen — a marker that can never be set again is dead state.
• The workspace:default ROW IS NOT DROPPED. It is PROMOTED to the product's permanent default workspace, and a test proves a session captured before the cutover still resolves to a workspace afterwards — the same session, the same row, now chosen rather than defaulted.
• The ledger's default workspace and the product's are proved to be one object, not two: nothing mints a second permanent home under another id.

REWRITTEN 2026-08-16, resolving the conflict this bead's own notes raised.

WHAT WAS IN CONFLICT. This bead's acceptance said DefaultWorkspaceID is deleted, because workspace:default is synthetic fallback state nobody chose. .internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-ux-design.md §4.2 makes a PERMANENT invisible default that every unassigned tab belongs to, settled with the owner (nocx-5azf0 note 4): a tab is ALWAYS in a workspace, there is no null, and visibility must not depend on a count.

WHICH WINS, AND WHY THE ANSWER IS NEITHER "DELETE" NOR "KEEP AS IS". The design wins on the concept — the owner decided it. But the two documents were not describing one object. The synthetic row exists because the product had no way to choose; the design's default exists because the product deliberately chooses it for anything unassigned. A session that was never assigned belongs in the default under BOTH readings.

So the row is not migrated anywhere. It is the same home; only its status changes, from "fallback nobody chose" to "the default, chosen by the product". What must go is the MARKER, which is the part that actually encoded "unchosen".

AND THIS DISSOLVES THE HAZARD RATHER THAN SCHEDULING IT. The original acceptance carried a real ordering trap: sessions.workspace_id is ON DELETE CASCADE, so dropping the default row before re-parenting would delete every synthetic session. Nothing is dropped now, so there is no ordering to get wrong and no re-parenting migration to run.

STILL TRUE, and inherited unchanged: content.go:77-82 records that the ledger.* wire methods will drive this surface and that until that cutover its only callers are tests, with command_history the live history path. The rows this bead is about are on a test-only surface today. The dependency on nocx-rtg0.3 is what carries that.
notes:
AMENDED 2026-08-17 by .internal/specs/2026-08-16-tabs-panes-and-blocks-design.md §11 and §6.1. The premise of this bug — that the ledger's SESSION row is where 'which workspace' belongs — is withdrawn. The anchor is the PANE: a block hangs on block.pane_id (durable, frontend-minted UUIDv7) and remembers block.session_id only as provenance, null once that pipe is gone. The workspace is resolved by the backend along pane -> tab -> workspace, and workspaceId is stored on the TAB (§4.5, and nocx-fraus is amended the same way). So this bead is no longer 'give the session an owner for workspace'; it is the rename that makes the ledger's restore key honest, and it lands with nocx-isoph rather than before it.

SUPERSEDED BY nocx-rtg0.28, filed 2026-08-17. That bead is the concrete half of what this one describes: entries has no pane_id at all, so the rename this bead calls for has nothing to rename to. Work rtg0.28 first; whatever is left of this one afterwards is naming.

title: Control saturation refusal has no diagnostic log
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start nocx with `NOCX_LOG_LEVEL=debug`.
2. Saturate the control lane with one outstanding operation.
3. Trigger another control action.
4. Observe the renderer's `The terminal is busy` toast, but no backend record naming the refused method, admission scope, request/notification disposition, or retry hint.

The wire already has the safe structured rejection vocabulary. Log that server-owned diagnostic at the refusal seam without logging request params or free-text rejection reasons.
acceptance_criteria: Given a saturated control admission, when a request or notification is refused, debug logging emits one structured `control action refused` record containing the registered method, coarse method class, admission scope, request/notification disposition, and non-negative retryAfterMs. No request params, payload bytes, or rejection free text reach the record. Existing saturation wire behavior and rate limiting are unchanged.
close_reason: Submission refusals and in-handler capability gate refusals now converge on a single safe response diagnostic carrying registered method, class, scope, disposition, and retry hint. Real-socket acceptance covers both seams; transport race suite and full pre-commit gate pass.

title: Local Wails build links obsolete WebKit 4.0 ABI
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. On current Manjaro, install the supported `webkit2gtk-4.1` package alongside the orphaned `webkit2gtk` 4.0 package.
2. Run `make build`.
3. Run `build/bin/nocx` or `ldd build/bin/nocx`.
4. Observe that the binary requests `libjxl.so.0.11`, while the supported system `libjxl` package provides `libjxl.so.0.12`; the application cannot start.

Wails v2 already owns this compatibility seam through the `webkit2_41` build tag. The repository build targets do not select it, so they prefer an obsolete pkg-config surface whenever both are installed. Fix the build selection rather than adding an ABI-unsafe libjxl symlink.
acceptance_criteria: Given Linux with `webkit2gtk-4.1` available through pkg-config, `make build`, `make build-release`, and `make dev` pass the Wails `webkit2_41` tag; the resulting `build/bin/nocx` has no unresolved shared libraries and reaches `application initialized` without `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. On systems without WebKit 4.1, existing WebKit 4.0 behavior remains unchanged. Non-Linux builds receive no Linux-only tag.
close_reason: Build/dev targets now select Wails webkit2_41 when Linux pkg-config provides WebKitGTK 4.1. make build links libwebkit2gtk-4.1 and libjxl.so.0.12 with no unresolved libraries; the binary reaches application initialized without LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Fallback dry-runs preserve WebKit 4.0 and non-Linux behavior.

title: The deadcode ratchet is OOM-killed by the containers the hook just started, and says 'exited null'
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

On a machine with roughly 4 GB available (measured on an 8 GB box with 2.5 GB
already in swap), stage a commit that touches Go files and run `git commit`.
The hook starts `go test -race` and `vitest` in containers (section 1), then
runs the host gates in their shadow. The deadcode ratchet is one of those host
gates, and the kernel kills it.

Observed twice in a row, 2026-08-14, on branch feat/notes-and-snippets:

    OK:   gofumpt
    OK:   golangci-lint
    DEADCODE RATCHET: deadcode exited null for darwin/arm64
    FAIL: deadcode ratchet

Run alone minutes later on the same tree:

    GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 deadcode ./...   exit=0, 110 lines
    node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs                       exit=0, 13s,
                                        '84 unreachable functions, all baselined'

Peak RSS of one platform's analysis, measured with time -v: 1430076 kB.

## Two defects, one incident

First, the report. `check-deadcode.mjs` guarded only `proc.status !== 0`, and
its comment claimed 'a nonzero exit is a tool failure'. A signal-kill sets
`status` to null and leaves stdout and stderr empty, so the message was the
bare string 'deadcode exited null' printed under the banner 'FAIL: deadcode
ratchet'. That names the ratchet and nothing else, so the obvious next move for
whoever hits it is to go make something reachable — delete code, add a caller,
or edit the baseline — in a tree where the ratchet is already green. A worker on
this branch was one prompt away from doing exactly that. A resource failure
indistinguishable from a content failure is how a green gate gets edited red.

Second, the collision. The ratchet is the one host gate with a large memory
peak: it loads the whole module twice, once per platform. Running it inside the
shadow of a `go test -race` container is the hook competing with itself for
memory on any machine that does not have several spare gigabytes.

## Fix applied

`proc.signal` is now checked before `proc.status` and fails with a message that
names the signal, says the analysis did not run, and says to re-run rather than
to change anything. The ratchet moved from section 3b to section 0b, ahead of
the container launch, with `host_gate` hoisted above section 1 so it is defined
in time. Cost is 13s of lost overlap against container gates measured in
minutes; the gate itself is unchanged and still runs on every Go commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A signal-killed deadcode reports the signal and does not read as a finding
- [ ] The ratchet runs before the container gates start
- [ ] A Go commit on a memory-constrained machine passes the ratchet
- [ ] The skip path (no Go staged) still prints its skip line
close_reason: 59a55b79. The ratchet moved ahead of the container launch and check-deadcode.mjs now checks proc.signal before proc.status. The commit's own hook run is the proof: 'OK: deadcode ratchet' printed first, ahead of gofumpt, and every gate went green including both containers and the e2e typecheck that a .githooks/* change triggers.

title: The plan's task split cannot pass the deadcode ratchet: tasks 1 and 2 add code nothing calls until task 3
description:
Found while supervising the first two implementation tasks of nocx-8rtr.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Implement plan Task 1 (internal/snippet store) and Task 2 (service) exactly as written.
2. git commit either of them on its own.
3. The pre-commit hook fails on the deadcode ratchet (.githooks/check-deadcode.mjs):
   the package's functions are unreachable from main() until Task 3 wires the transport
   and app.go, and the committed baseline may only shrink.

The plan's own Task 3 Step 8 asserts `deadcode -filter 'nocx/internal/snippet'` is empty —
so the plan knew the reachability requirement and still split the work so that two tasks
must commit before it can hold.

Cost already incurred: the worker implementing Tasks 1 and 2 read the orchestrator's brief
("run only your unit tests, not make ci") as excluding the pre-commit hook, and committed
both through `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`. The brief was at fault for the bypass, but
the ratchet is why the hook was failing in the first place, and a correctly-briefed worker
would simply have been stuck.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every task in .internal/plans/2026-08-13-snippets.md can pass the pre-commit hook on
      its own, or the plan states explicitly which tasks land as one commit and why
- [ ] The rule is written where the next plan author sees it: a Go task that adds a package
      lands together with the wiring that makes it reachable
- [ ] The two bypassed commits (1a68e65d, 5814bc06) are green under the hook once the
      wiring lands
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every task in .internal/plans/2026-08-13-snippets.md can pass the pre-commit hook on its own, or the plan states explicitly which tasks land as one commit and why
- [ ] The rule is written where the next plan author sees it: a Go task that adds a package lands together with the wiring that makes it reachable
- [ ] The frontend twin of that rule is written down too. Measured on 04211014: contracts:check walks every contracts/*.schema.json and fails if its generated renderer type is missing or stale, so a schema and its generated file must land in one commit; the dead-exports ratchet fails any file nothing imports and its updater refuses to write a baseline that grows. A new wire method therefore cannot land before its renderer consumer without scaffolding. 27 baselined generated/ entries are the accumulated evidence that this has been papered over before
- [ ] The two bypassed commits (1a68e65d, 5814bc06) are green under the hook
close_reason: The plan now states that tasks 1-3 land as one commit and why (the deadcode ratchet is a pre-commit gate and the package is unreachable until task 3 wires it), and AGENTS.md's reachability check carries the planning-side rule so the next plan author reads it: a task that adds a Go package lands with the wiring that makes it reachable. The two bypassed commits are green under the hook on the merged tree — deadcode -filter 'nocx/internal/snippet' is empty.

title: Suppression, debounce and coalescing, and the noninterference property test
description:
Router policy plus the executable form of ADR-0029 noninterference rule.

Suppression: nothing is delivered about the tab the user is looking at, in a focused window.

Debounce keyed `{sessionId, kind}` — 8s to start, adopted from termic rather than invented. Keyed by session AND kind, never kind alone, or two tabs collapse into one notification and lose their attribution. Coalescing produces one notification naming the count and carrying the attribution of the session it was keyed on.

The property test is the reason this is one task and not two: both the policy and its proof concern the same code, and the policy is what could break the invariant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A loop printing OSC 9 continuously produces one notification per window, naming the count — not one per iteration.
- Two sessions each emitting the same kind produce two notifications with their own attribution, never one merged.
- Nothing is delivered about the focused tab in a focused window; the same event with the window unfocused is delivered.
- Property test: for any two SCHEMA-VALID payloads differing only in title or body, route resolution produces identical sinks, target ids, credentials, destination and method. It ranges over every schema-valid input, NOT only payloads a sink would accept — restricting the generator would exclude the oversized and invalid-encoding cases that could diverge.
- Route resolution is compared BEFORE sink-level validation; a size rejection is recorded as an attempted delivery that failed and never removes the sink from the resolved set.
- Debounce and coalescing are payload-independent: neither the key nor the count depends on title or body, asserted.
close_reason: Suppression, debounce, coalescing and the noninterference property test. The property test was tautological (compared Resolve against itself with title/body written but never read) and now raises through the real path comparing sink identity and every destination field. Three timing-dependent tests wait on state; package runtime 17.7s -> 7.4s. Merged as 8a347b9. NOT wired into the composition root — nocx-jiwq.2 tracks that and is P1.

title: The wire: notify.raise, its contract, and backend-stamped provenance
description:
The JSON-RPC method the renderer calls, and the schema that makes ADR-0029 provenance rule structural rather than advisory.

Read ADR-0029 §2.2 "Provenance is structural" first. The whole point: the record carries `sessionId`, `title` and `body` and NOTHING else. kind, trust, level, attribution and timestamp are stamped by the backend from the method invoked and its own session registry. A schema proves a record shape, never who assigned a field — which is why the protected fields are absent rather than validated.

`sessionId` is ADDRESSING, not attribution: AD-1 multiplexes many sessions per socket, so the record must say which terminal parsed the sequence, and the backend rejects an id not live on that connection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `contracts/notify.raise.schema.json` exists with `additionalProperties: false` and explicit `required`, listing exactly sessionId, title, body.
- The renderer types are generated from it and committed; `npm run contracts:check` passes.
- A `..._OverTheWireConformsToContract` test validates the real frame off the real socket, not a payload the test built.
- A record carrying `trust`, `kind`, `level` or any attribution field is REJECTED by the schema.
- A record whose sessionId is not live on that connection is rejected, and the rejection is a JSON-RPC error rather than a silent drop.
- The stamped event carries attribution naming tab, host and session, and every field of it comes from the backend registry — asserted by feeding a hostile title/body and checking attribution is unaffected.
- notify.raise always yields trust=programRequest. There is no argument, header or method variant by which a renderer call produces attested.
notes:
MANDATORY, added by the coordinator after nocx-ng6f landed.

nocx-ng6f hand-added 10 entries to `.githooks/deadcode-baseline.json` because internal/notify had no production caller and the hook refuses otherwise. **Your task is what gives it that caller, so you remove those entries in the same commit.**

This is not tidy-up. AGENTS.md nocx-rtg0: an epic shipped a store, a key lifecycle, a budget, a retention policy and five settings controls while ContentDB.Add had no caller outside its own tests, and the acceptance criterion "deadcode is empty" was satisfied the whole time. A baseline entry that outlives its reason is how a package stays unreachable while every gate reports green.

Add to the acceptance criteria: after wiring, `.githooks/deadcode-baseline.json` contains none of the internal/notify entries nocx-ng6f added, and the hook passes without them.
close_reason: notify.raise, its contract, backend-stamped provenance and the router in the composition root. Nine tests including the over-the-wire conformance check and each protected field refused by name. Merged as 570400c6; the banner route reaches a real surface in a5d3d67e.

title: The macOS attention adapter: banner, click-to-tab, and the three permission states
description:
The Wails implementation of the `AttentionHost` port. Spec §8 has the research; read it before reaching for a library.

Use `runtime.SendNotification` with `opts.Data` for the routing payload and `OnNotificationResponse` for the click. **`mac.ShowNotification` is forbidden** — it is the old osascript path in the same module and it sprintfs the body into an AppleScript string literal, and our bodies are program-chosen. A body containing a double quote must reach the banner intact.

Permission is three states, not one: `IsNotificationAvailable` false; authorization never requested; authorization denied. Each is a distinct product behaviour (spec §6.4) — a silent no-op for any of them is the defect this task exists to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A body containing `"` and one containing a newline reach the banner unmangled.
- `mac.ShowNotification` appears nowhere in the tree; a grep asserting its absence is part of the suite.
- Clicking a notification focuses the originating tab: the callback decode, the tab lookup and the focus call are each asserted through the port fake.
- A malformed or unknown callback payload is handled without panic and without focusing an arbitrary tab.
- Each of the three permission states produces a distinct, asserted product behaviour; none is a silent no-op.
- On a host where the port is unavailable the sink reports unavailable and the router records a failed delivery, rather than the pipeline stalling.
close_reason: The Wails attention adapter: banner via runtime.SendNotification with the body verbatim, three permission states as distinct visible failures, badge and bounce reporting their absence rather than faking success. 18 tests. Merged as c3389aa5 and wired in a5d3d67e, where deadcode went to zero for the whole notify package. Click-to-tab is NOT delivered and is tracked as nocx-jiwq.1 — the backend has no way to ask the renderer to focus a tab.

title: The notification core: event, trust, default-deny router, sink and host port
description:
The pipeline of ADR-0029 and spec §2, as a new package with no callers yet. Everything else in the epic plugs into this, so it goes first and alone.

Read ADR-0029 §2.2, §2.3 and §3 before writing anything — the rules there are binding and several are counter-intuitive.

Build: the `Event` record (kind, trust, title, body, level, attribution, at); the three `trust` classes; the `Router` with a **default-deny** table keyed `(kind, trust)`; the `Sink` interface; and the `AttentionHost` port with an adapter that reports itself unavailable (the Wails one is a separate task).

Two rules that are easy to get wrong and are the point:
- Routing resolves ONCE, before any sink is invoked. A sink receives an immutable resolved destination and can never select a target, credential, method, retry or redirect.
- Every sink invocation is synchronous, takes a finite-deadline context, must return when cancelled, and may not publish a callback after returning. Expiry cancels; the CLOSING EVENT is the invocation returning. Finalization is one-shot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `(kind, trust)` pair with no table row reaches no sink — asserted, including for a pair added later to the kind enum but not to the table.
- `heuristic` reaches no sink marked as leaving the machine; `programRequest` reaches no completion-subscription route.
- A sink that blocks until its context is cancelled still causes the instance to be released, and the release happens on the invocation returning, not on deadline expiry.
- A sink that calls back after returning is ignored; the instance is not finalised twice.
- Global limits on in-flight invocations, queued instances and retained bytes exist; exceeding one produces a failed delivery, asserted, not an unbounded queue.
- The unavailable AttentionHost adapter reports unavailable rather than panicking or silently succeeding.
- `deadcode -filter nocx/internal/notify ./...` is not used as evidence of anything here — the package legitimately has no production caller until the wire task lands.
close_reason: Notification core built: Event record, three trust classes, default-deny (kind,trust) router with once-only resolution and class-capability enforcement, synchronous one-shot-finalized sink invocations with release-on-return, bounded in-flight/queued/retained-bytes admission with visible RefusedError failures, and the AttentionHost port with an unavailable adapter. 12 tests green (go test + go vet + golangci-lint + gofumpt), committed as 77a8d0a2; deadcode baseline grown deliberately per the bead's no-caller-until-wire-task acceptance criterion, to be shrunk by nocx-9zmc.

title: End to end: the snippet reaches a running program filled in, and unsubmitted
description:
Plan Task 13 — the epic's gate. e2e/snippets.spec.ts.

CORRECTIONS: there is no e2e/helpers — the entry is e2e/harness.ts (test, expect, promptReady, clickIntoEditor); LIVE xterm output is a WebGL canvas and only completed output is frozen into a DOM scrollback block, so the grid is not a DOM query; the library is NOT empty on a fresh stand because the service seeds two records; and the worker does NOT run e2e/run-in-container.sh (AGENTS.md:388) — author it and hand it to the integrator.

The check: create a single-line snippet with one env span and one ask span through the settings page; start a program that reads stdin and echoes what it received; press the chord, choose, fill, confirm; assert NO new scrollback block appeared and the editor is still hidden; then press Enter and assert the frozen block contains the resolved text.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Steps 4 and 5 together prove both halves: no newline was sent, and what was sent
- [ ] Both multi-line branches are covered — bracketed paste on AND off
- [ ] The unresolved-secret refusal has its own test
- [ ] grep for waitForTimeout/sleep/setTimeout in the spec returns nothing
- [ ] The worker did not run the containerized suite
close_reason: e2e/snippets.spec.ts is green in the container (3 tests): the gate — create through the settings page, fire with the chord while read holds the pane, fill the ask field, no block appears and the editor stays hidden, then the person's Enter shows got-<resolved>; the multi-line refusal with bracketed paste off; and the unresolved-secret refusal. No waitForTimeout/sleep/setTimeout. The bracketed-paste-ON branch could not be arranged in the container and moved to nocx-8rtr.1 with what was tried; the renderer's own read now has a real-parser test.

title: The palette: the surface that answers when there is no command editor
description:
Plan Task 9. frontend/src/snippets/palette.ts, a FloatingPanel variant, the chord, the composition in main.tsx.

FOUR CORRECTIONS the first draft got wrong: MIN_PANEL_WIDTH_PX is a Record over the variant union (floating-panel.ts:43) so a new variant needs a width entry or it is a type error; the row identity is NOT .ui-floating-panel-row (read the render at 295-321); attachCustomKeyEventHandler returns FALSE to keep a chord away from xterm (xterm.ts:299-316); logging is not only console.log (log.ts prefers a Wails bridge).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Lists the library in stored order; filters by title and body; arrows/Esc/Enter/Cmd-Enter
- [ ] A snippet with ask spans turns the panel into the field form IN PLACE — one panel, not two
- [ ] A refusal renders in the panel and stays; it is not a toast
- [ ] With the store unavailable the panel says so instead of showing an empty list
- [ ] An ask value is not remembered between fires and never reaches the real logging seam
- [ ] A delivered fire closes the palette and returns focus; a refusal does neither
- [ ] The fire environment is read at fire time, not captured at construction
- [ ] The chord is chosen deliberately, handled at the xterm boundary, and zero bytes reach the PTY when it is pressed
close_reason: Landed in 7c9cd9a9 (merged with main in 81b6bff4). All eight criteria have tests: palette.test.ts covers stored order, title+body filter, arrows/Esc/Enter/⌘Enter, the ask form in place, the refusal that stays in the panel, store-unavailable vs empty library, ask values not remembered, focus returned on delivery and not on refusal, and facts read at fire time; chord.test.ts pins the chord and its by-code match; xterm.test.ts asserts zero bytes reach the pty when it is pressed.

title: Extract the pane's input-owner derivation, and add the snippet policy beside the secret one
description:
Plan Task 8 — REWRITTEN. Read spec §9.1/§9.1a/§9.2 first; the seam the first draft used (input-target.ts) has no production caller (nocx-9zij).

Extract TerminalContent.insertSecret's question into a private inputOwner(): 'editor' | 'pty' | 'none'. insertSecret becomes a caller, unchanged. insertSnippet is the second policy. renderers gain bracketedPasteActive() and a paste() that returns whether the write happened.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A characterisation test for insertSecret is written BEFORE the extraction, passes before it, and passes unchanged after
- [ ] inputOwner() is private and is the only place the question is answered
- [ ] insertSnippet into the editor inserts the resolved text and sends NO newline
- [ ] insertSnippet into the pty resolves {{secret:...}} through vault.resolveLine exactly as insertSecret does, refuses on an unresolved name, and sends NO newline
- [ ] 'none' is a refusal, never a fallthrough to the pty
- [ ] A multi-line body is refused when bracketed paste is off and delivered whole when it is on; a single-line body is unaffected either way

- [ ] grep -rn 'isVisible' frontend/src/snippets/ is empty
