A characterisation test written before the extraction passes unchanged after it. 'none' refuses rather than falling through to the pty; a multi-line body is refused unless bracketed paste (mode 2004) is on; paste() returning false is a refusal, not a reported delivery. grep -rn isVisible frontend/src/snippets/ is empty.

title: A notification catches you on your phone
description:
## What a user can do that they could not before

Route a notification to a service you already carry — Bark, ntfy, a Telegram bot — so that a build failing while you are away from the machine reaches you. Without nocx building an app, a relay or a push protocol.

**Governed by ADR-0029** §2.2 (destination, secret-bearing URLs, retention) and specified in `.internal/specs/2026-08-13-notification-system-design.md` §4.1, §4.1.1, §4.2, §6.3, §6.4, §7. The destination rule is absolute and the secret rules are not negotiable — read the ADR first.

Scope: the NotificationTarget entity with its own store and CRUD surface, the vault-backed secret (ADR-0017), four typed presets, the HTTP sink with per-context encoders and deadlines, and the visible delivery failure.

## Success Criteria

- A user creates a custom target through the UI, its secret goes to the vault, the app restarts, a command fails, and a local test HTTP server receives a POST carrying the event and its backend-stamped attribution. Driving the UI is the point; poking the store proves the sink, not the feature.
- No stream-derived field appears in any URL position for any preset — asserted per preset, including Bark on its JSON /push endpoint.
- A sentinel secret in a Telegram-shaped target appears in no log, no returned or wrapped error, no trace, no panic output and no fixture failure output — the `*url.Error` path specifically, since its Error() prints the URL and Go does not redact a path segment.
- Redirects are refused.
- A push returning non-2xx, timing out, or hitting its deadline raises a danger toast naming the target by name and never its URL.
- CR, LF and NUL are rejected in every payload position; an oversized payload fails visibly and is never truncated into concatenation.
- An adapter that blocks until cancellation still closes its interval; a callback arriving after cancellation is ignored rather than double-finalising.
- Saturation by many sessions produces visible failed deliveries, not an unbounded queue.
- A heuristic event never reaches a target.
- Either redaction is extended to the push body, or the target UI states that unredacted terminal content leaves the machine. nocx-2x8x covers scrollback, ledger and clipboard for vault-injected secrets and does not cover this.

## Deliberately out

An inbound webhook endpoint; a durable retry queue (ADR-0029 §2.2 makes adding one a deliberate amendment); a provider whose only endpoint puts message content in the URL.
notes:
Hard prerequisite that the backlog cannot express as an edge: **nocx-sb3f**. bd refuses `blocks` from an epic to a bug, so it is a `related` edge plus this note.

The visible-delivery-failure toast is a backend→renderer notification with no successor. Today TryNotify enqueues on the REFRESHABLE queue, whose overflow policy drops the frame — so under saturation the one surface that reports a failed push vanishes silently, which is the exact failure this epic is required to make impossible. Fix nocx-sb3f first, or the acceptance criterion about the danger toast is untestable under load.

title: A program in a pane can reach you when you are not looking
description:
## What a user can do that they could not before

Run something in a pane — a build, an agent, a program on a host reached over ssh — look away, and be told when it wants you. The program prints OSC 9 or OSC 777; nocx raises a banner; clicking it lands on the tab that spoke.

Today nocx registers OSC 7, 52, 133, 636 and 1337 and neither 9 nor 777, so a program asking for attention is ignored. BEL lighting a tab dot is the whole of what exists.

**Decided by ADR-0029** (a program may ask; it never chooses) and specified in `.internal/specs/2026-08-13-notification-system-design.md` §2, §3, §4.2, §4.3, §6, §9. Read the ADR before touching the router or the wire.

Scope: the pipeline (event, router with its default-deny table, sink interfaces, the AttentionHost port), the OSC 9/777 receiver, sources `program.notify` and `bell`, the toast / OS banner / sound sinks, backend-stamped attribution, suppression, debounce and coalescing. Plus taking our own bundle identifier before anything depends on it.

## Success Criteria

- A program on a real pty through cmd/devharness prints OSC 9; `notify.raise` crosses the real socket, conforms to its contract in contracts/, and carries `sessionId`, `title` and `body` and nothing else.
- The backend rejects a `notify.raise` whose `sessionId` is not live on that connection.
- The router resolves the expected sinks, and the AttentionHost fake is invoked with the exact title, body and backend-stamped attribution naming tab, host and session.
- A property test over schema-valid payloads differing only in title/body asserts identical route resolution, compared before sink validation.
- OSC 9;4 (ConEmu progress) produces no event.
- A second OSC 1337 handler is not registered; if RequestAttention is added it discriminates inside the existing fence handler.
- Nothing is delivered about the focused tab in a focused window.
- Debounce keyed {sessionId, kind} coalesces a flood into one notification naming the count; a loop printing OSC 9 does not produce one notification per iteration.
- `mac.ShowNotification` appears nowhere in the tree; a body containing a double quote reaches the banner intact.
- The bundle identifier is ours, not `com.wails.*`, in both Info.plist and Info.dev.plist.
- Packaged-build experiment recorded: on a clean macOS profile the banner appears, clicking it focuses the originating tab, authorization survives an update under the same bundle id, and the effect of a `wails dev` re-sign is written down. Manual actions limited to granting permission, seeing the banner and clicking it; the rest asserted by the harness.

## Deliberately out

Push (epic B), the dock badge (A2), completion subscriptions (A3), agent events (a child of nocx-dw3), OSC 1337 RequestAttention.

title: The frame's identity can miss a buffer switch, and a queued capture can hang forever
description:
Found by an adversarial review of 2fab1f76 (codex, read-only, 2026-08-13). Two defects in
one module's lifecycle, plus the test gap that let both through.

1. PRE-MOUNT SUBSCRIPTIONS ARE SILENTLY DROPPED, and the frame's identity now depends on
   them. XtermRenderer.onResize (xterm.ts:554) and onBufferChange (xterm.ts:562) are written
   as `this.term?.onX(...)`, so before mount() they register nothing and say nothing.
   onWriteParsed does NOT behave this way -- it keeps pre-mount subscribers and attaches them
   in mount() via _ensureWriteParsed(). The asymmetry predates this commit; what is new is
   that CaptureIdentityTracker's correctness rests on those two events.
   CONSEQUENCE: construct the tracker before mount and the identity never learns about a
   buffer switch or a resize. A frame saved on the normal buffer then compares as `same`
   after entering the alternate screen if no parsed write intervenes, and a resize reads as
   `moved` or `same` rather than `notComparable`. That is ADR-0029's guarantee defeated in
   the wiring rather than in the logic -- the logic is correct and never receives the event.

2. A CAPTURE CAN HANG FOREVER ACROSS DISPOSAL. capture-identity.ts:87 registers a waiter
   when hasUnsettledWrite() is true and resolves it only from _onWriteParsed. Dispose the
   renderer -- tab close, renderer replacement -- while a write is queued and the xterm
   subscription goes away with the subscriber list; the waiter is neither resolved nor
   rejected, and awaitSettled() never returns. This is an interval with no closing event,
   which AGENTS.md rule 3 names directly.

3. THE TESTS CANNOT SEE EITHER. Every buffer-switch and resize test uses FakeSource, whose
   subscriptions exist immediately; the real-renderer tests construct the tracker only AFTER
   mount. No test performs the lifecycle the renderer's own comments claim to support --
   subscribe first, mount later, then switch buffers or resize.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Construct a CaptureIdentityTracker over an XtermRenderer that has not been mounted yet.
2. Mount the renderer.
3. Mint a frame on the normal buffer and save its identity.
4. Enter the alternate screen with no intervening parsed write, and compare.

Observed: comparability reports `same`. Expected: `notComparable` -- it is a different
buffer instance.

For (2): mint a frame while a write is queued, dispose the renderer before the parse
settles, and await the capture. Observed: the promise never settles.

## Acceptance Criteria

- onResize and onBufferChange keep pre-mount subscribers and attach them at mount, the way
  onWriteParsed already does -- asserted by subscribing before mount, mounting, then firing
  each event.
- A tracker built before mount reports `notComparable` across a buffer switch and across a
  resize, asserted through the REAL renderer rather than FakeSource.
- awaitSettled() has a closing event on every path: disposal (or renderer replacement) makes
  a pending capture settle -- reject, or resolve as not-capturable, deliberately chosen and
  written down -- and a test disposes mid-capture and asserts the promise settles.
- The paired positive stays asserted: the ordinary capture still resolves after the parse
  settles.
close_reason: onResize and onBufferChange keep pre-mount subscribers and attach at mount, like onWriteParsed — so a tracker built before mount now sees the discontinuity and reports notComparable, asserted through the real renderer. awaitSettled() has a closing event on disposal, asserted by a test that would hang before the fix. test-source.ts can now express one write across several parse passes, so the multi-chunk test asserts the interleaving xterm actually has. The other on* methods with the same shape are audited and deliberately left: none carry an identity and their callers subscribe after mount. 6c45a727.

title: Terminal output disappears silently when xterm's write watermark is hit
description:
Introduced by 2fab1f76 (the capture-fence work), found by an adversarial review the same day.

BEFORE: XtermRenderer.write() was `this.term?.write(data)`. When xterm refused a write --
it throws before queueing once its pending-data watermark is exceeded -- the exception
reached the caller.

NOW: the write is wrapped in try/catch so the unsettled-write counter cannot stick. The
catch repairs the counter and RETURNS SUCCESS. So under flow control the bytes are dropped
with no exception, no log, no backpressure signal and no mark on screen. The user sees a
terminal that quietly lost output.

The counter repair is correct and must stay -- a stuck counter would wedge the capture
fence forever. What is wrong is swallowing the condition along with it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Drive a session that produces output faster than xterm parses it -- e.g. `yes` piped
   through something dense, or a large `cat` of a binary-ish file -- until xterm's
   WriteBuffer watermark is exceeded.
2. Watch the rendered output.

Observed: bytes vanish. Nothing in the UI or the log says a write was refused.
Expected: either the write is retried/queued by us, or the refusal is surfaced -- and in
every case it is logged, because silent loss of terminal output is indistinguishable from
a program that printed nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A write refused by xterm's watermark is observable: asserted on a renderer whose
  underlying write throws, that the condition reaches a caller or a logged signal rather
  than being discarded.
- The unsettled-write counter is still exact after a refused write -- the fence must not
  wedge. Assert both: the counter returns to its prior value AND the refusal is reported.
- A test drives the throwing path and a paired test drives the ordinary path, so "it
  succeeds normally" is asserted alongside "it reports the failure".
close_reason: write() surfaces xterm's watermark refusal again instead of swallowing it; the unsettled-write counter is still repaired first so the capture fence cannot wedge. Deliberately not logged in the renderer — a log would let the caller keep believing it delivered bytes that are gone. The call site still does not catch it: nocx-x8s2.5, and that gap predates both changes. 6c45a727.

title: the live region's echo shift moves the grid by the char box, not the row pitch, so half the echoed command stays on screen
description:
In the macOS app a RUNNING block shows a sliver of the shell's echo of the command
between the header and the first output line, cut across the middle (the bottom of
the glyphs is what stays visible). Frozen blocks are clean. Reported fine in the web
build.

Mechanism (confirmed by an independent second read): the live region is the grid
itself, and `_echoShiftPx()` (frontend/src/scrollback/controller.ts:327) hides the
echo row by translating `.xterm-inner` up by `rows * renderer.cellHeight`, with
`.xterm-live-container` clipping the top. `XtermRenderer.cellHeight`
(frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts:740) measures `.xterm-char-measure-element`, which
xterm styles `line-height: normal` — the CHAR box, not the row pitch. xterm's real
pitch is `floor(ceil(charH*dpr) * lineHeight)/dpr` (lineHeight 1.2), exposed via
`_renderService.dimensions.css.cell` and already read by `_getCellDims()` in the
same file for `fit()`, `cellWidth` and `liveContentHeight()`. Shift < pitch, so the
residual stays on screen.

Two derivations of one quantity — AD-8 as a working habit. Both tests that touch
`cellHeight` stub it with a literal (gutter.test.ts:134,
scrollback/controller.test.ts:404), so no test can see the divergence.

Open sub-case, to be settled by measurement on the Mac: whether `cellHeight` reads a
real span or falls through to the constant `Math.ceil(FONT_SIZE*LINE_HEIGHT)` = 17px.
xterm 5.5 prefers an OffscreenCanvas measure strategy and only creates the DOM span
when that throws, so which engine picks what decides whether the span exists at all
— the likeliest explanation for macOS-broken/web-fine.

Two further defects on the same value, found while reading:
- `_getCellDims()`'s own fallback returns char height too (xterm.ts:441), so it lies
  the same way whenever the render service is unavailable.
- `_cachedCellHeight` is invalidated only on `term.onResize` (xterm.ts:335); the DPR
  watcher (xterm.ts:371) only publishes a notification, so moving the window between
  displays leaves a stale value when rows/cols do not change.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. macOS app (`wails dev` or a build), a tab with shell integration.
2. Submit a command from the app editor that runs for several seconds and prints
   output (the report used `herdr plugin install …`, which waits at a prompt).
3. While the block is still RUNNING, look between the header's command text and the
   first line of output: a horizontal slice of the echoed command line is visible,
   cut across the middle. It disappears when the block freezes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cellHeight` and `_getCellDims().height` are the same quantity — the row pitch the
  grid is fitted to — with no path returning a char box.
- A test fails before the fix and passes after it, driving both off one fake render
  service instead of stubbing `cellHeight` with a literal.
- On a Retina Mac and in the web build, a running block shows NO fragment of the
  echoed command between the header and the first output row.
- The stale-cache path is covered: a DPR change with no grid resize re-reads the
  pitch.
close_reason: Fixed in 2e7a5279 and confirmed visually in the macOS app: a running block now shows nothing between the header's command and the first output row. cellHeight reads the render service's row pitch, the char-measure fallback is gone from _getCellDims, the pre-measurement guess is no longer cached, and the DPR watcher clears the cache. Four tests in xterm.test.ts, red before the fix.

title: Мусорные глифы копятся в долгой сессии: обе точки вызова refreshAtlas() потеряны рефакторингами, фиксы nocx-e27 и nocx-q18 стали мёртвым кодом
description:
## Summary

Симптом (скриншот владельца, реальное macOS WKWebView-приложение): во время долгой
работы в herdr часть символов на экране превращается в мусорные глифы — пятнами,
внутри слов, преимущественно на приглушённых (dim/цветных) участках. Кириллица
рядом рендерится корректно, то есть байты в буфере целы: это дефект отрисовки, а
не декодирования (ср. nocx-6de/nocx-ao7, где виноват был TextDecoder в ipc.ts).
Выход из herdr и повторный вход лечит — экран перерисовывается целиком.

Это тот же класс, что nocx-e27 (P0) и nocx-q18 (P1): глифы рисуются по устаревшим
координатам текстурного атласа WebGL. Оба были закрыты одним и тем же лекарством —
перерисовкой всего вьюпорта через refreshAtlas() (term.refresh(0, rows-1)).

## Root cause

Обеих точек вызова больше нет, метод остался.

1. `2cc1e10b` поставил `tab.refreshAtlas()` в путь активации вкладки — это и был
   фикс nocx-e27. `21fd7f6a` (refactor(tabs): TabContent seam, помечен PARTIAL)
   перенёс метод в TerminalContent и потерял вызов в TabManager.
2. `e0d0a490` (refactor(tabs): B.5 geometry authority) убрал ResizeObserver
   внутри рендерера вместе с его `refreshAtlas()` после safeFit — это был фикс
   nocx-q18. Новый путь Tab -> viewportChanged -> fitViewport зовёт только
   `t.resize(cols, rows)` и никакой перерисовки за собой не тянет.

Сегодня grep по frontend/src даёт у `refreshAtlas()` ровно ноль вызывающих вне его
собственного определения (terminal-content.ts:1986, renderers/xterm.ts:615) и мока
в test-support/tabs-fixtures.ts:132. Мок и есть причина, почему это прошло молча:
интерфейс TerminalRenderer его объявляет, фикстура его подделывает, тесты зелены,
а deadcode у нас только для Go.

Почему проявляется именно со временем: живая область меняет высоту по
`liveContentHeight()` -> `scrollback.setLiveHeight` (terminal-content.ts:1860), так
что herdr, дописывая вывод, гоняет fitViewport -> t.resize десятки раз за сессию,
и каждый ресайз пересобирает атлас. Компенсирующей перерисовки больше нет, а
42-мс насос принудительного refresh включён только на Linux/WebKitGTK
(FORCED_REFRESH_MS, isLinuxWebKit) — на macOS его нет. Испорченные ячейки
поэтому не заживают сами, пока программа не перепишет весь экран.

## Steps to Reproduce

Воспроизводится только в реальном приложении на macOS WKWebView — по заметкам
nocx-q18 ни Chromium, ни WebKit в Playwright этот класс не дают.

1. Собрать приложение и открыть вкладку.
2. Работать в herdr (или любой TUI, переписывающей нижнюю живую область) достаточно
   долго, чтобы высота живой области сменилась много раз.
3. Смотреть на текст, который программа больше не переписывает: символы пятнами
   становятся мусорными глифами.
4. Выйти из herdr и войти снова — экран чистый.

Различающий эксперимент перед фиксом (10 секунд): когда мусор на экране, потянуть
за угол окна так, чтобы поменялось число строк/колонок. Вылечилось — локус
подтверждён, лекарство верное (перерисовка). Не вылечилось — испорчены сами записи
кэша глифов, и лечением будет clearTextureAtlas в паре с перерисовкой, а не одна
перерисовка.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Активация вкладки и изменение геометрии вьюпорта снова тянут за собой
  перерисовку всего вьюпорта, и это видно из кода одним grep-ом.
- У пути активации и у пути ресайза есть юнит-тест на то, что перерисовка
  запрошена, чтобы следующий рефакторинг не унёс её третий раз молча.
- Владелец подтверждает на реальном приложении: длинная сессия в herdr больше не
  набирает мусорные глифы. Проверка визуальная, как у nocx-e27 и nocx-q18;
  автоматической не будет.
notes: Смержено в main: PR #83, мерж-коммит a15fd7b9 (2026-08-13). Все семь джоб CI зелёные на слитом дереве. Бид остаётся открытым до визуальной проверки владельцем на реальном macOS-приложении — автоматической проверки для этого класса нет (nocx-q18).
close_reason: Shipped. Both lost refreshAtlas call sites are restored: frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:4314 repaints inside setVisible, and frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts:648 ends setGrid with _repaintViewport. Tests name the bead: terminal-content.test.ts:6399 and renderers/xterm.test.ts:1444. Commit 23bf2597 via PR 83. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: Ask about a frozen block from the ordinary flow, and watch the answer arrive
description:
Owner, 2026-08-13: "the first thing I want is to be able to talk to the AI and ask
it a question about a block."

WHY THIS BEAD DID NOT EXIST. The design's own value sentence is "a command in a
block, OR a full-screen program that owns the viewport". The nine children
sequenced only the second one: nocx-ckth is the panel geometry for a live program
(shrink its font, return the editor below), and nocx-7ul8 is pointing at a region
without the program noticing. Neither is needed to ask about a frozen block --
selection there is ordinary DOM, and there is no live region to shrink. So the
cheapest end-to-end path through the whole epic had no bead, and the expensive one
was the front.

WHAT THIS IS. The surface, and only the surface: a gesture on a frozen block puts
a chip naming it in front of the editor, the editor accepts a question through
AgentInputTarget (nocx-4ff.7, ADR-0004 section 3 -- the registry stays the only
thing routing a submit), and the answer renders in the flow as an entry, streaming
in and closing. No panel, no alt-screen, no keycaps.

The frame source is the FROZEN one: a block after its freeze has no xterm cells
left and its text has already been through frontend/src/scrollback/serializer.ts,
so provenance records source=frozen plus the serializer version. Do NOT extract a
second text derivation here -- that is nocx-2f0f.3's artifact, and AD-8 says the
owner is whoever already has it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With an endpoint configured, a user points at a finished block, types a question
  and gets an answer that names something actually printed in that block --
  asserted end to end against a real backend (cmd/devharness), not a mock.
- A chip names the block before the question is sent, and the payload to the model
  contains that block's output and no other block's.
- The answer streams in and terminalizes; a second ask while the first streams
  lands its deltas on the right entry.
- The submit is routed by InputTargetRegistry.active(), asserted -- not by a panel
  boolean or a second editor.
- Provenance on the captured frame records source=frozen and the serializer
  version; no second text derivation exists in the codebase.
- With no endpoint configured, the surface says so (agent.status), asserted on the
  surface rather than on a log line.
notes:
2026-08-14, coordinator: THE ASK IS ACTIVATED FROM THE BLOCK, AND THAT IS IN SCOPE HERE.

The worker found that terminal-content.ts's setAgentMode has no caller — the
agent target can be registered and routed and still be unreachable to a person.
Verified: setAgentMode exists at terminal-content.ts:2406 and nothing calls it.

Decided rather than deferred. It is not nocx-7ul8, which owns pointing at a
REGION of a live program without the program noticing; a frozen block is
ordinary DOM and already selectable. It is not nocx-4ff.7, which owns the
per-mode draft, the per-mode history and the explicit mode indicator, and which
was re-sequenced behind this bead today so it extends the target rather than
owning a second one.

Selection must NOT be the activation. Selection already means copying, and AD-8
forbids two surfaces owning one input: a user who selects a block to copy it and
then types a command would have it silently routed to the model. Activation is a
deliberate non-modal affordance attached to the frozen block, with one primary
action, which raises the chip and calls setAgentMode(true); dismissing the chip
returns the target to shell. The chip's presence IS the mode for now, which is
the minimum nocx-4ff.7 later refines.

The kit almost certainly already has the shape: BlockReceipt is vanilla-emitted,
attached to the frozen block, non-modal with focus staying in the editor, one
primary action naming its scope, waits on its block until answered, and several
blocks can carry one at once. Extend it, or record in the code why it did not
fit.
2026-08-14, worker: the ask is reachable — activation from the frozen block, wired end to end.

The surface now exists: every frozen command block carries an Ask control (ui-button ghost sm, header-right, before the ⋮); clicking it raises the ask chip (BlockReceipt.forAsk — badge Ask + the block's command as value, primary Ask focuses the editor, Done dismisses), selects the block non-toggle (visual anchor; selection never activates), calls setAgentMode(true), and puts agent.status on the chip (the ONE sentence derivation, agentStatusLine, extracted from the endpoints section so the two surfaces cannot drift). Dismissal (or a `clear` that takes the block — controller onClear) returns the target to shell.

THREE decisions recorded in code, each with its why:

1. THE SUBMIT SEAM WAS BROKEN, and the red test caught it: the editor's shared submit handler ran the SHELL orchestration for any submission — takeKeyboardToGrid, holdRawUntilSubmitted, ledger record, running block, lifecycle.submitAttempt — before routing via sendDoc. An agent question would have hidden the editor, handed the grid the keys, and opened a phantom running block + ledger record + attempt for prose. Fixed at the composition root: the registry's active target is consulted FIRST (ADR-0004 §3 — the registry is the single routing authority, never a mode boolean); a target declares `routesToShell` (InputTarget capability — shell true, agent false), and the shell orchestration runs only for shell submissions. The editor itself stayed passive; no if(mode) branch inside it.

2. The ask's scope is the CHIP's block, resolved through the renamed seam `askBlock` — never re-derived from DOM selection. Selecting another block to COPY while the chip is up must not silently retarget the question (that is the AD-8 two-derivations defect the coordinator warned about). The chip names its block and the payload follows the chip, by construction.

3. ONE ask chip at a time (recorded in forAsk's doc comment): the capture receipt is a stack of independent offers; the ask chip IS a mode, and a mode names one scope. Activating a second block moves the chip; mode stays agent.

Coverage: the ask activation seam is asserted in terminal-content.test.ts through the REAL chain (real TerminalContent/controller/BlockManager freeze, real editor submit): activation raises the chip naming the block; the question crosses agent.captureFrame + agent.ask with THAT block's rows (source=frozen) and no other block's; NOTHING shell ran (no pty bytes, no lifecycle.submitAttempt, no running block); dismissal returns the shell flow; a second activation moves the chip and the payload follows; no endpoint -> the chip says 'No endpoint configured yet' from agent.status on the surface. Kit/block/status-line units also pinned. Full suite: 154 files / 2778 tests green; tsc, eslint, prettier, git diff --check clean; dead-exports baseline shrank by 5. Go untouched by this round; make ci-full/e2e intentionally NOT run (coordinator integrates).
2026-08-14, coordinator: I closed this and reopened it within the minute. The
code is merged (d7943fe0) and every component and integration assertion is
green, but the FIRST acceptance criterion is 'asserted end to end against a real
backend (cmd/devharness), not a mock' — and that run has never passed. It stops
at endpoint creation on nocx-qtim, so no feature-dependent assertion in
e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts has executed yet.

Closing on green unit suites while the end-to-end check has never run is the
exact reading that let nocx-rtg0 ship an unreachable write path: 'deadcode is
empty' was read as 'history works'. This closes when the spec runs and passes,
not before.
close_reason: PROVEN, not assumed: e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts runs against a real backend (cmd/devharness) with a scriptable OpenAI-compatible SSE fake on loopback, and passes 3/3 unchanged. Written from the acceptance criteria by a worker that never saw the implementation; it found nocx-qtim, nocx-8rwj and nocx-wmy4 before it could pass. Merged as 3f337b84.

title: Staleness cannot be generation equality: a self-refreshing TUI would be permanently undrivable
description:
Found by the owner, 2026-08-13, against the epic's own acceptance criterion.
Refined with the owner the same day; the refinement is recorded below because
the first proposal was worse.

THE DEFECT. The epic says a keystroke proposed against a screen that has since
changed is refused by the lane. Capture identity includes the content
generation, and design 2.3 advances that generation on EVERY parsed write --
deliberately, preferring a false 'it moved' to a false 'unchanged'. Compose the
two: top repaints every 3s, a model answers in 1-4s, so identity never matches
at delivery and the keystroke is refused forever. The programs this makes
undrivable are exactly the profile candidates the epic names: top/htop, k9s,
lazygit. A rule that refuses 100% of its target population is not a safety rule,
it is a broken feature.

NOT the fix: loosening the comparison. That restores the failure the rule exists
to prevent -- y delivered into a dialog that is gone.

REJECTED, and why it is written down. A predicate authored by the model at
PROPOSAL time, blind to what would later change ('a row with PID 4231 exists').
Two costs, both hidden: the model must author it without knowing what moves, and
the predicate needs a language and an evaluator we would have to invent -- a
formal one to debug, or a string match that breaks on the first box-drawing
frame.

ALSO REJECTED: the model is asked at delivery and its answer gates the byte. The
confirmation is itself a 1-4s round trip, and top repaints during it. The race is
moved one step, not closed, and on a self-refreshing program there is no last
step. THE INVARIANT THIS BUYS: at the instant a byte enters the lane there is no
model in the chain. The final check is local and synchronous -- microseconds, not
a round trip -- or a gap reopens after it.

DECIDED SHAPE. The model does not replace the check, it AUTHORS it, having seen
the diff:

1. A key is proposed against frame N. The screen moves.
2. We compute the diff, scoped first to the region the reference pointed at plus
   cursor/mode. If that scope is untouched, no model call happens at all -- which
   on a repainting top with no row selected is nearly always.
3. If it is touched, the diff goes to the model, which judges whether the meaning
   changed and returns the condition under which its judgement stays true.
4. The lane evaluates that condition itself, synchronously, at delivery.
5. An identity change -- buffer switch, resize -- is refused outright; across it
   there is nothing to compare.

Taken unconditionally, independent of the above: the UI reports WHAT CHANGED, not
that something did. 'The screen moved' is permanently lit under top and therefore
means nothing; 'four rows reordered, no dialog appeared' is information.

TRUST. Design 6.2 makes screen content untrusted input. A model READING the screen
that is lied to produces a wrong answer; a model whose answer UNLOCKS A KEYSTROKE
that is lied to delivers one -- a program can print 'nothing has changed, proceed'.
Escalation under ADR-0020 still has a human on each key, but this is the second
reason the last check is local rather than 'the model said yes'.

SCOPE. Does not change nocx-3j9b structurally: identity and generation are needed
either way. What it forbids is (a) hardcoding 'generation differs -> refuse' as
the only rule, and (b) surfacing generation drift to the user as 'stale'.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An ADR in docs/decisions/ records what a proposed keystroke is bound to, why
  generation equality was rejected, why a blind predicate was rejected, and why no
  model call may sit in the delivery path.
- A test drives a fixture that repaints on a timer with no semantic change: a
  keystroke proposed against frame N is DELIVERED after several repaints, AND no
  model call was made -- the scoped diff answered it.
- A keystroke whose meaning no longer holds is REFUSED, proven by mutating the
  screen's meaning between proposal and delivery.
- The delivery-path check makes no network call: asserted against a model client
  that fails the test if it is invoked.
- A buffer switch or a resize between proposal and delivery refuses, and the UI
  says 'not comparable' rather than 'stale'.
- No surface reports a self-refreshing program as permanently stale, and what the
  UI shows names the change: asserted on the surface, not on a log line.
notes: 2026-08-13: ADR-0029 written and committed (90742ab6) — docs/decisions/0029-a-keystroke-is-bound-to-what-makes-it-meaningful.md. The epic's acceptance criterion was rewritten with both ends, and the design spec's section 1 table and DRIVE follow-on line were corrected. WHAT REMAINS on this bead is the executable half: the condition language, the scoped-diff evaluation, and the tests — none of which can be written before DRIVE exists. What binds the slice being built NOW is only the negative: no 'generation != saved -> refuse', and no surface calling generation drift 'stale'.

title: A frame is minted in the renderer, with an identity you can compare
description:
Design §2.2-2.3. The renderer mints a frame: cells + attributes + cursor, plus a CAPTURE IDENTITY (buffer instance — normal|alternate and WHICH alt-screen session — geometry, and a content generation).

Generation advances on onWriteParsed (present in the xterm typings, NOT yet exposed by our adapter) plus the explicit state-changing operations: buffer switch, resize, clear, reset. NOT on onRender: ADR-0005 has us force periodic repaints on Linux WebKitGTK, so a paint-driven generation would stale a motionless screen continuously on one platform. onWriteParsed is also the CAPTURE FENCE — write() queues parsing, so a snapshot taken mid-queue can hold row 1 from before a write and row 20 from after it.

TWO SOURCES, recorded, not pretended to be one:
- live (alt screen, running block): cells of the active xterm buffer; provenance records buffer instance, geometry, generation, and that rows may be evicted by the 10k scrollback cap;
- frozen (a block after its freeze): there are NO xterm cells left, and the serializer has already joined wrapped lines and dropped leading/trailing blanks. This source is the derived-text artifact of nocx-2f0f.3 — do not build a second one.

Deliberately conservative: a write repainting identical cells still advances the generation. We prefer a false 'it moved' to a false 'unchanged'.
notes: 2026-08-13, from the implementation (worker B, worktree frame-capture-identity): the design's claim that onWriteParsed IS the capture fence was wrong, and the spec has been corrected. onWriteParsed fires at the end of EVERY parse pass, and a pass can land between the chunks of one large write — so waiting for one fire settles nothing. The exact settle signal is xterm's per-write callback write(data, cb), which fires when THAT write's bytes are parsed; the renderer keeps an unsettled-write count from it and the fence waits for zero, re-checking after every onWriteParsed fire. onWriteParsed keeps advancing the generation and waking the waiter. Comparability landed as a distinct union — same | moved | notComparable — not a flag on staleness, per ADR-0029. The frozen source is a seam satisfied from blockOutputText plus a new SERIALIZER_VERSION constant in scrollback/serializer.ts; no second VT-to-text derivation exists.
close_reason: Frame minted in the renderer with a capture identity (buffer instance incl. alt session, geometry, generation). Generation advances on parsed writes and explicit mutations, never on repaint (ADR-0005). Comparability is a distinct union — same|moved|notComparable — and nothing wires drift to a refusal or calls it 'stale' (ADR-0029). Two sources recorded: live cells, and frozen via the existing serializer with SERIALIZER_VERSION; no second text derivation. Found and corrected the design's claim that onWriteParsed is the capture fence. 2fab1f76.

title: Point at a region without the program noticing
description:
Design §3.4. The picker EXTENDS xterm's existing forced-selection escape hatch — Option on macOS, Shift elsewhere, which already means 'the user wants to select, not to click at the program' inside mouse-tracking applications. It does NOT add a parallel pointer listener: that would be a second claimant on one mouse event, and two surfaces owning one input is the defect whichever wins by evaluation order.

In the flow: modifier + drag across part of a block's output produces a chip in the editor. On the alternate screen: mouse-down MINTS THE FRAME at that instant (you cannot circle something that is moving), the drag happens on the frozen frame, release produces the same chip.

Open check, not an assumption: that the modifier is free on macOS AND on Linux WebKit in the TUIs we care about.

title: Masking learns to read output, in the one place that already owns it
description:
Design §6.1. Today history.record is the single writer of durable rows and masks the SUBMITTED COMMAND (maskCommandSafe). It does not look at output, cells or frames — so a token a pager printed would leave the machine in the clear.

The detector is EXTENDED into the artifact-ingest path, and that path becomes the single owner of durable-and-egress masking. Renderer-supplied redaction ranges are HINTS ONLY: the renderer is not the authority, or we have two detectors that disagree. Note the seam: the reusable owner is the masking service, not ws_history_record.go itself — an artifact repository must not depend on a WebSocket handler.

What leaves the machine is the referenced regions with masked spans removed; what is stored is masked by the same owner in the same place.
close_reason: Masking extracted into internal/masking as the service both callers use — the seam this bead named — so durable rows and egress screening share one recognizer with two policies. ws_history_record.go now delegates.

title: The panel: the live program shrinks by font, the editor comes back
description:
Design §3.1-3.3. A hotkey opens a panel: the live program is re-rendered at a SMALLER FONT in the upper region and the ordinary flow and editor return below it. The PTY is NEVER RESIZED — no SIGWINCH, no reflow, no misbehaving program; terminal output is text, so it stays crisp. Below a floor where a dense program (k9s, htop) becomes unreadable, OUR PANEL shrinks, not the program. The frame block is rendered at the same reduced font as the live region: two pictures of one screen must be comparable by eye.

There is NO SECOND INPUT SURFACE. Input ownership EXTENDS the existing machine — lifecycle state, buffer state, editor visibility, renderer read-only state, takeKeyboardToGrid(), and InputTargetRegistry.active() — expressed as states of it, never as a panel boolean layered on top, which would disagree with it exactly when the program exits while the panel is open. Everything else (editor visibility, disableStdin, focus, the focus ring, what a click on the live region does) derives from that one state.

Needs AgentInputTarget (nocx-4ff.7, ADR-0004 §3) — the registry stays the only thing that routes a submit.

title: eino wired in, with zero tools declared and the answer streaming out
description:
Design §4.1-4.4, ADR-0028. Wire cloudwego/eino behind the composition root with the OpenAI-compatible adapter. We write NO tool-calling loop, NO SSE client and NO provider adapter — that is most of what adopting the framework buys.

RUN MODES: explain declares zero tools and terminates after the first completed response; agent declares ours and runs until the model finishes or policy/lease/cancel stops it. Context assembly differs: explain is question + referenced frames, agent adds tool calls and their results.

Stream out over the control plane as per-entry notifications (nocx-dw3.1). The ledger is authoritative; eino's checkpoints, message history and retries are implementation detail of a run and nothing in the product reads them to answer 'what happened'.

MEASURE AND REPORT, do not assume: eino/compose + flow/agent/react with no provider adapter is already 78 modules and 126 packages, including logrus — a second logging vocabulary against our one-slog-interface rule. Report go list -deps and stripped binary size before and after the adapter; logrus is explicitly undecided (contain, tolerate, or veto).
notes: 2026-08-14, inherited from nocx-kn9q: this bead now also owns the http:// address rule and the Test button. Not scope creep — both need the HTTP client to the model, which arrives here and exists nowhere else in the tree. What is inherited, from design 4.5: http:// permitted ONLY for loopback and private addresses, ENFORCED ON EVERY CONNECTION rather than in the form, because a hostname can resolve public at validation and private at dial time, a redirect can walk https-public to http-private, IPv6 loopback / link-local / IPv4-mapped / cloud metadata addresses are all reachable by name, and proxy env vars can reroute a request the user believes is local. Redirects are re-checked as new endpoints; the credential is never forwarded across an origin change. And Test probes what will actually be used (streaming now, tool calling before the agent rung claims support), not one cheap completion. The endpoint record ships without any of this and deliberately implies none of it.
close_reason: internal/assistant behind one Client interface: adk.ChatModelAgent + eino-ext openai adapter, zero tools, streaming. Dial-time http:// rule with per-redirect recheck and credential dropped on origin change. logrus contained at the composition root with a receipt test. Test button + agent.status with contracts. Measured: 127→189 modules, 326→470 packages, 18.6→34.6 MB stripped. Merged as 18783434.

title: agent.captureFrame and the ask transaction: identities exist before the model is called
description:
Design §5, §7. The renderer ingests the frame FIRST — agent.captureFrame, returning a BACKEND-MINTED frame id — and agent.ask references it. An earlier draft contradicted itself by carrying a frame id into agent.ask while claiming the same transaction created the frame.

ONE BACKEND-OWNED ASK TRANSACTION records the frame reference, the question and a PENDING RUN before the model is called. Streaming content follows; the identities and the recovery state exist first. Otherwise a frame lands with no question, a question with no run, or a retry duplicates both.

RECOVERY IS TWO LINES, NOT A MACHINE: on start, every non-terminal run becomes INTERRUPTED — the block says so and the user asks again. Nothing is retried automatically. The one ordering rule that makes it honest: an attempt is written down BEFORE the tool is invoked, never after, so an interrupted run can say 'this may already have happened'.

Run state is on the wire because the renderer draws it: prepared, streaming, awaiting_approval, and the terminal set completed|cancelled|failed|interrupted. A reconnecting renderer READS the state; it does not infer liveness from notifications having stopped.

Depends on the ledger subset (nocx-rtg0.2).
close_reason: agent.captureFrame + agent.ask: backend-minted ids, one ledger transaction before the model, run state on the wire, interrupted-on-start sweep. Merged as d7943fe0 with its consumer.

title: Endpoints and models: a base URL you choose, a key the vault holds
description:
Design §4.5. Modelled on Warp's custom-endpoint dialog. An endpoint has a display name, a base URL, a credential and one or more models, each with an optional alias for the picker. Endpoints are a list.

THREE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCES FROM WARP:
- The API key is NOT stored in the endpoint record. The field is an input; the record holds an OPAQUE SECRET REFERENCE into the vault (ADR-0016, ADR-0017). Warp stores the key with the endpoint; we already decided otherwise and a second answer is not allowed.
- The wire schema is a FIELD on the record (it cannot be inferred from the URL) but there is NO select while there is one implementation. A select with one option is UI for a feature that does not exist.
- http:// is permitted ONLY for loopback and private addresses, and that is enforced ON EVERY CONNECTION, not in the form: a hostname can resolve public at validation and private at dial time, a redirect can walk https-public to http-private, and IPv6 loopback, link-local, IPv4-mapped and cloud metadata addresses are all reachable by name. The credential is never forwarded across an origin change.

Plus a Test button that probes what will actually be used (streaming now; tool calling before the agent rung claims support), not one cheap completion. Built from the kit per frontend/src/ui/README.md; this form meets the open bead nocx-74cn (the kit has no validation).
notes:
2026-08-14, coordinator scoping before dispatch. Two findings and one split.

FINDING 1 — AN ENDPOINT IS SHAPED LIKE A PROFILE, NOT LIKE A SETTING. Endpoints are a LIST
of records each holding a vault secret reference. internal/settings is scalar declarations;
internal/profile is exactly this shape and already owns secretrefs.go. Extend that answer
rather than inventing a second one.

FINDING 2 — AND THAT MEANS VAULT RESET MUST SEE THEM. internal/vaultreset takes ONE
SecretReferenceStore, described in its own comment as "the profile store seen from here",
and its Impact struct literally has a ProfileCount field. A second kind of record holding
secret references is INVISIBLE to it: the reset preview under-reports what the user is about
to lose, and ClearAllSecretReferences leaves endpoint records pointing at secrets that no
longer exist. This is the defect shape this repo keeps paying for — one behaviour, two
owners, agreeing everywhere except where it matters. Whatever is built here participates in
that bookkeeping, or the bead is not done.

THE SPLIT. The Test button and the connect-time http:// restriction MOVE TO nocx-edio, and
this is deliberate rather than dropped. The bead requires Test to probe "what will actually
be used (streaming now)" and requires http:// to be refused for anything but loopback and
private addresses ON EVERY CONNECTION rather than in the form -- because a hostname can
resolve public at validation and private at dial time, and a redirect can walk https-public
to http-private. There is no HTTP client to the model anywhere in the tree yet; it arrives
with eino in nocx-edio. A Test button without one is a control that lies, and a form-level
address check would advertise an enforcement that does not exist.

So this bead is: the record, its storage, the opaque vault reference (ADR-0016/0017), the
wire shape and its contract, the form built from the kit, and the vault-reset bookkeeping.
The form MAY reject an obviously malformed URL as a courtesy; it MUST NOT present that as
the address restriction, and the code says so where a reader will look.
close_reason: Landed in 8158f2fb: the record in internal/profile, four endpoints.* methods with contracts, the AI Endpoints Settings surface, vault reset counting endpoints (ADR-0030, ADR-0031). The key is an input only — an endpoint that has one opens with the field empty.

title: The policy and the narrowed capability: our two functions in eino's middleware
description:
Design §4.1-4.3, ADR-0028. eino has no policy and no grant and cannot have one: 'is this destructive', 'is this lane in scope', 'is this path inside the grant' are asked in terms of OUR environments, lanes, connections, vault and ledger. So we write two things over our own types and wire them at the framework's seams.

1. A function answering PERMIT / ASK / REFUSE.
2. A constructor for the NARROWED CAPABILITY a tool holds.

THREE SEAMS, strongest first (adk.TypedChatModelAgentMiddleware):
- BeforeAgent — rewrites the run's tool configuration, so a tool the grant forbids is NEVER DECLARED to the model. The strongest refusal is the one never proposed.
- BeforeModelRewriteState — rewrites ToolInfos before each model call, so a scope that narrows mid-run narrows what is on offer.
- WrapInvokableToolCall — 'at request time when the tool is about to be executed', where the arguments are visible: refuse by not calling next; escalate with compose.StatefulInterrupt BEFORE next so nothing has touched the domain; permit by calling next with the scoped capability.

TWO RULES, both bought by defects found in review:
- The grant is over RESOURCES AND EFFECTS, never tool names. One 'run a command' tool is a universal escape hatch. This was the --no-tools mistake made a second time.
- The dispatcher NARROWS rather than checks. A check is advisory while the tool still holds a full session.Manager, the vault and the filesystem. Go package privacy is NOT the boundary — it does not stop code in the same package and it rots at the first refactor.

A refusal TERMINALIZES the run: suppressing one call and continuing lets the model ask for the same effect another way.
close_reason: Policy pipeline at eino's WrapInvokableToolCall: refusal terminalizes via ErrPolicyRefused, batch latch, StatefulInterrupt before next with approval bound to the canonical argument hash, narrowed ScopedReader capability asserted by trying to escape it. Merged 5d233b9b.

title: Make the two-owners defect fail the build, not the review
description:
Three defects in one session had one shape: a derived answer computed at more than one
call site, where the two agreed everywhere except in the state nobody tried.

- `nocx-a88r` — the Port input painted `fvNum('port') || 22` while the validator read
  `formProfile()?.options.port`. The user saw 22, the validator saw empty, and every
  connection adopted from an alias became uneditable.
- `nocx-vczn` — the password action read the secrets inventory while the binding it was
  describing lived on the draft.
- `nocx-heum` — Detected and Forwarded each owned a port's state, so the row carrying
  the Forward action never showed that the action had worked.

AGENTS.md already forbids this in prose ("Two surfaces may never own the same input",
"Does something already decide this?"). Prose did not stop three instances in one day.
This bead makes the mechanically-detectable subset fail the build, using the machinery
the repo already has: `frontend/lint-fixtures/` carries four custom checks
(`check-css-colors`, `check-css-integrity`, `check-dead-exports`, `check-kit-identities`)
with `update-*-baseline.mjs` ratchets, all wired into `npm run lint`.

Deliberately NOT in scope: the two stronger levers. Making the raw draft unreachable
behind a resolver, and generating both the input and the validator from one field
declaration, are real fixes for the same class and are a larger change; the owner chose
the linter first. Do not start either here.

Also out of scope by nature, and worth stating so nobody believes the check is complete:
a lint rule cannot catch a genuinely NEW second surface — the second suggestion dropdown
AGENTS.md describes, with its own list, keys and accept path. That stays a review
question.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not a runtime defect. The reproduction is historical: check out the pre-fix shape of
`frontend/src/connections.tsx` (before the nocx-a88r commit) and run `npm run lint` — it
passes, while the file contains a field whose painted value and validated value come
from different sources.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new check under `frontend/lint-fixtures/`, wired into `npm run lint` beside the
  existing four, that **fails on the pre-fix `connections.tsx`** — the real historical
  defect, not a synthetic sample. This is the criterion that matters: a checker that has
  never been shown to catch the bug it was written for is decoration.
- It passes on the current tree, or ships with a baseline in the established
  `update-*-baseline.mjs` shape so existing accepted cases ratchet down rather than
  blocking the build. Any baselined entry is listed with one line saying why it is
  acceptable.
- False positives are named and bounded: the check reports what it cannot decide rather
  than guessing, and the message tells the reader what to do — not just what is wrong.
- Running it is fast enough for the pre-commit hook, which already runs the other four.
- A test for the checker itself: fixtures that must trip it and fixtures that must not.
  A linter with no tests is the same trap as a feature with no tests.
close_reason: Shipped in #80: check-two-owners.mjs, proven against the real pre-fix connections.tsx; its baseline shrank on its own when the port fix landed.

title: A minted password binds only the draft, so the vault gains a secret no connection uses
description:
Minting a password from the connection editor stores the secret in the vault immediately
and shows the row as "Password: <name>" — which reads as done — while the profile's
reference to it lives only in the draft. Settings → Secrets then honestly reports the
secret as used by **0 connections**, and the connection still has no password.

Owner, 2026-08-13: "OK, I created a password for pi, why does it say 0 connections?"

**Confirmed from the store, not inferred.** `~/.config/nocx-dev/profiles.json` at the
time of the report:

    { name: "192.168.0.93", host: "192.168.0.93", port: null,
      auth: "password", passwordSecret: null }

So a save DID happen — `auth` went from null to `password` and persisted — and
`options.passwordSecret` did not. The backend's count is correct:
`profile.ComputeSecretUsage` does include `passwordSecret`
(`internal/profile/usage.go:79`), so "0 connections" is the truth about the stored
profile, not a display bug.

Two mechanisms are possible and BOTH must be ruled in or out with evidence:

1. **The binding is never saved because the user has no reason to save again.** After
   nocx-vczn the action row names the minted secret the moment it is minted, so the
   editor looks finished. The binding is persisted only by "Save Connection", and
   nothing on screen says so.
2. **A race.** `saveProfile` builds its patch from `dirtyFields()` and the draft as they
   stand when Save is pressed (`decideSaveRoute(profile, dirty)`), while the mint's
   `bind` runs asynchronously behind a vault prompt. A Save that lands before `bind`
   carries `auth` and not `passwordSecret` — exactly the stored shape above.

The deeper problem is that "mint-and-bind at the action moment" (ADR-0017) is currently
mint-and-*draft*: the secret becomes real immediately and irreversibly, while the
reference that makes it useful does not. That split is what produces a vault row nobody
uses, and it is the same split nocx-rieq records from the other side — a cancelled edit
stranding a secret.

Recommended direction, to be confirmed: **persist the binding at the moment of the
mint**, so the two halves of "mint-and-bind" happen together and the editor's "done"
appearance is true. That also closes nocx-rieq, because there is no window in which a
secret exists bound to nothing. The cost is that OK on the password dialog becomes a
write to the profile, which a subsequent Cancel would not undo — state that in the UI
rather than leaving it implicit.

Also worth fixing regardless of mechanism: two profiles named 192.168.0.93 exist in the
store, one with `auth: null` and one with `auth: "password"`, both with `port: null`.
Whether adoption or the editor can create duplicates is a separate question — file it
if so.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings → Connections → edit a connection → Authentication → Method = Password.
2. "Set Password", type one, OK. The row reads "Password: <name>".
3. Settings → Secrets.

Observed: the secret is listed against **0 connections**, and `profiles.json` carries no
`passwordSecret`.

Expected: the secret is used by 1 connection, and connecting uses it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After minting a password from the editor, the profile stored on disk carries
  `options.passwordSecret`, and Secrets reports 1 connection. Asserted end to end
  through the editor a user drives, with the persisted patch inspected — not the draft.
- The race is closed, not narrowed: a Save pressed while the mint is still in flight
  must not produce a profile with the method changed and the binding missing. Write the
  test that fails against today's code by ordering those two events.
- Whatever the chosen model, the UI never shows a binding as done while it is only in
  the draft. If a further action is required, the surface says so.
- The failure paths stay visible (nocx-vczn): a refused or cancelled vault operation
  still says what did not happen.
- Paired ordinary case: on a normal connection, setting a password and connecting with
  it works.
close_reason: Shipped in #80: OK writes the binding to the stored profile, and a save arriving mid-mint waits for it — race closed, not narrowed.

title: Hidden row actions reserve the width the forwarded destination needs
description:
Removing `.ports-row__dest`'s `max-width: 40%` (nocx-na05) made the destination longer
and still truncated. The owner's row at the default rail width:

    127.0.0.1:8000
    → 192.168.0.93:...
    [Forwarded]

The address line above it — one character shorter — fits. So the cap was not the whole
cause, and the remaining one is measurable rather than a matter of taste.

**Hidden action buttons still reserve their width.** `frontend/src/styles/surfaces/ports.css`:

    .ports-row__main > .ui-icon-button { opacity: 0; }
    .ports-row:hover > .ports-row__main > .ui-icon-button { opacity: 1; }

`opacity` does not remove a flex item from layout. The buttons occupy the row whether or
not they are visible, and a FORWARDED row carries three of them — Copy, Open, Stop —
where a plain detected row carries one.

The arithmetic, at `SIDEBAR_WIDTH_DEFAULT = 240` (`frontend/src/sidebar-width.ts:43`),
`.ui-icon-button[data-size='xs']` = 18px (`styles/components/icon-button.css:48`), and
`.ports-row__main { gap: var(--space-2) }` = 8px (`tokens.css:43`):

- plain detected row: 1 button + 1 gap = 26px taken from the text column
- forwarded row: 3 buttons + 3 gaps = 78px

A forwarded row's text column is therefore ~52px narrower than a plain one — around
seven characters — which is exactly the gap between `127.0.0.1:8000` fitting and
`→ 192.168.0.93:8000` not. The rows with the most to say are given the least room to say
it, and only while the pointer is elsewhere.

**Why this survived two rounds of tests: jsdom computes no layout.** Every existing
assertion is DOM text and stylesheet contract, and both are satisfied by a row that
visibly truncates. Whatever the fix, it needs an assertion in a real browser — the
Playwright suite can measure `scrollWidth` against `clientWidth`; vitest cannot, and no
amount of care in vitest will catch the next one.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a saved SSH connection whose host has listeners.
2. Ports view at the default sidebar width (240px), pointer away from the row.
3. Forward a detected port whose remote address is a full IPv4 (`192.168.0.93:8000`).

Observed: `→ 192.168.0.93:...`.

Expected: the destination is readable without pointing at the row.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At the default rail width, with the pointer NOT over the row, a forwarded row shows a
  full `192.168.0.93:8000` destination — asserted in a real browser by comparing the
  element's `scrollWidth` to its `clientWidth`, not by reading its text content.
- The same assertion covers a plain detected row, so the fix cannot be bought by making
  ordinary rows worse.
- Copy, Open and Stop stay reachable by pointer AND by keyboard — `:focus-within` is why
  the current rule exists, and a fix that reclaims the width by making the actions
  keyboard-unreachable is not a fix.
- Whatever reclaims the space is stated as a decision: hidden controls not reserving
  layout, fewer controls on the row, or a different place for them. The kit rules still
  apply — a surface may place a kit component and never repaint it.
- The ellipsis remains for a genuinely over-long destination, so the row can never
  overflow its column.
close_reason: Shipped in #80: hidden actions moved out of flow; verified in a real browser (scrollWidth 144>139 before, 217=217 after) and guarded by e2e/ports-row-width.spec.ts.

title: The port field paints a default the validator cannot see, so an adopted connection cannot be edited
description:
Setting a password on a saved connection fails with the toast "Port is required" while
the General tab plainly shows Port = 22.

Owner, 2026-08-13, on 192.168.0.93: "I'm trying to set a password for an
already-created connection, it complains there is no port. But there is one."

The port has two owners in `frontend/src/connections.tsx`, and they disagree exactly
where it matters.

**What the field shows** (~:2143): `value={fvNum('port') || 22}` — the input paints 22
whenever the resolved value is falsy, so a draft carrying no port at all looks correct
to the user.

**What the validator reads** (~:1482):

    port: () => combine(required('Port'), portRule())(String(formProfile()?.options.port ?? ''))

`formProfile()` is `editing()`, the raw draft. A profile with no explicit
`options.port` gives `String(undefined ?? '')` === `''`, and `required('Port')` rejects
it. The user sees a valid port and the validator sees an empty one.

This is the shape AGENTS.md names as the defect itself: two derivations of one
question — "what is this connection's port" — that agree everywhere except in the one
state nobody tried. Here that state is common rather than exotic: `adoptAliasProfile`
(`frontend/src/profiles.ts`) deliberately omits the port unless one was supplied,
precisely so "absent" stays distinguishable from "explicitly 22". Every connection
created that way, and every import that leaves the port to the default, is born unable
to be edited.

Note also that `|| 22` swallows a genuine 0 as well as absence, so the field cannot
show an invalid stored port back to the user — worth deciding deliberately rather than
inheriting.

The fix must give the port ONE owner. The effective-value machinery (`fvNum`, the
effective/inheritance resolution the rest of the form uses) is the existing answer; the
`|| 22` in the field is the second one that grew beside it. Both the field and the
validator must read the same resolved value, and whichever way it goes, "absent means
inherit the default" and "explicitly set" must remain distinguishable in what gets
SAVED — collapsing them would silently pin 22 onto every profile and change what the
ssh config resolution does.

Check the same pattern on the neighbouring fields before concluding: `host`, `name`,
the keepalive numbers, and anything else where the input paints a fallback the
validator does not know about.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings → Connections → edit a connection that has no explicitly stored port (one
   adopted from an alias, or imported with the port left at the default). 192.168.0.93
   is one.
2. General shows Port = 22.
3. Authentication → Method = Password → "Set Password" → type one → OK.

Observed: toast "Port is required"; the password is not minted; the row still reads
"No password set".

Expected: the password is minted and bound. The port shown is the port validated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A profile with no explicit `options.port` passes validation, and its password can be
  minted and bound. Asserted through the editor a user actually drives, not by calling
  the validator directly.
- The field and the validator read the SAME resolved value — asserted by a test that
  would fail if a second fallback were reintroduced in either place.
- An explicitly stored port still validates, and an invalid one (0, negative,
  non-numeric, above 65535) is still rejected with its message — the fix must not turn
  the rule off to make the symptom go away.
- Saving a profile that never had an explicit port does not silently gain one, unless
  that is chosen deliberately and stated.
- The paired ordinary case per AGENTS.md rule 2: on a normal machine, with a normal
  connection, setting a password succeeds end to end.
close_reason: Shipped in #80: fieldValue owns the resolved value; input and validator read it, and the save carries no synthesized port.

title: A forwarded row cuts its destination to two characters on a line nothing else uses
description:
A forwarded row shows the local bind on one line and the destination beneath it as
`→ 19…` — the destination, which is the whole point of the row, is cut to two
characters while the line it sits on is almost entirely empty.

Owner, 2026-08-13, with a screenshot: `127.0.0.1:9993` / `→ 19…` / `Forwarded`.

The cause is a constraint left over from the layout that was just replaced.
`frontend/src/styles/surfaces/ports.css` `.ports-row__dest` carries:

    flex: 0 1 auto;
    max-width: 40%;

with the comment "Secondary text (the forward's destination) yields before the address
does: a capped share that shrinks to nothing when the row is tight." That was correct
when the destination sat BESIDE the address on one line and the two competed for the
rail's width. nocx-heum moved the destination onto its own line inside the stacked
`.ports-row__text` column, so the 40% now caps it against a line nothing else is using.

`.ports-row__addr` on the line above already shows the right pattern for a stacked
line: `min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`
and no percentage cap, with the comment "it now owns its own line, so the ellipsis is
a floor that should never be reached at the rail's default width". The destination now
owns its line too.

Worth checking in the same pass, since it is the same restructure: whether the
`Forwarded` badge and the `→` arrow still earn their vertical space now that the row
is three lines tall in a narrow rail, and whether the local bind or the destination
should be the row's primary line. The user is looking for "where do I reach this", and
that is the local bind — but they identify the row by the remote port they forwarded.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a saved SSH connection whose host has listeners.
2. Ports view → Forward a detected port, e.g. `:::9993`.
3. Look at the row at the sidebar's default width.

Observed: `→ 19…` — the remote destination is unreadable.

Expected: the destination is readable at the default rail width; the ellipsis is a
floor for genuinely long values, not the normal case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At the sidebar's default width, a forwarded row shows a full `host:port` destination
  for an ordinary IPv4 address and port (e.g. `192.168.0.93:9993`) with no ellipsis.
- The ellipsis still appears for a destination genuinely too long for the rail, so the
  row can never overflow its column.
- The address line above it is unaffected — it keeps its own truncation behaviour.
- A layout test asserts the rendered destination text is the full string, not a
  prefix. Asserting the CSS rule is not the same thing and does not count.
close_reason: Shipped in #80 together with nocx-4wbx — the 40% cap was only half the cause.

title: Nested sudo launcher assumes --preserve-fds support
description:
In an integrated bash session, typing `sudo -i` is intercepted by internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash. The integration skips the user's original command and unconditionally runs `sudo --preserve-fds=3,N -i env -u BASH_ENV bash --rcfile /dev/fd/N -i`. Sudo implementations or versions without the long `--preserve-fds` option reject this launcher and print usage, so the requested root shell never starts. The repository's own fake-sudo test explicitly says the host sudo lacks this option, but production has no capability check or conventional fallback. This is distinct from nocx-aupk: that bug is the macOS shared nested-domain path; this defect is a deterministic unsupported-sudo-option failure on any host with such sudo.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start an enhanced remote bash session on a host whose `sudo --help` does not advertise `--preserve-fds`.
2. Run `sudo -i`.
3. Observe `sudo: unrecognized option '--preserve-fds=3,N'`; no root shell starts.

The original command is lost because the DEBUG trap returns non-zero under extdebug after the generated launcher returns.
acceptance_criteria: On a host whose sudo lacks `--preserve-fds`, entering `sudo -i` runs the user's command conventionally and reaches the sudo shell without exposing nocx's internal launcher arguments. On a preserve-fds-capable host, the integrated child-domain path still establishes. Capability detection is deterministic and tested for both outcomes; a generated launcher failure never silently consumes the user's original command.
close_reason: Capability-gated sudo fallback and BASHOPTS isolation implemented and proven

comments.author: avlokhturo
comments.text: Observed alongside the refusal: `bash: warning: cannot start debugger; debugging mode disabled`. This is a separate Bash startup symptom, not sudo's parser error. nocx enables `shopt -s extdebug` in nocx.bash:930. A deterministic local reproduction is `bash --noprofile --norc -c 'shopt -s extdebug; export BASHOPTS; env -u BASH_ENV bash --noprofile --norc -c "shopt extdebug"'`, which makes the child try the configured debugger startup file and emit the same warning when it is absent. Confirm whether the affected remote shell has exported BASHOPTS (`declare -p BASHOPTS` shows `-x`) before deciding whether this belongs in this bead or a separate one; do not conflate it with the unsupported sudo option.

comments.author: avlokhturo
comments.text: Fixed at the shell ownership seam. Both bash and zsh now probe sudo --help for --preserve-fds before emitting start/domain_request; unsupported sudo runs the untouched user command conventionally. sudo/su and their child Bash commands scrub exported BASHOPTS so nocx's internal extdebug cannot trigger bashdb. Added real-PTY acceptance for bash/zsh unsupported sudo, exported-BASHOPTS sudo and su, and retained happy/stillborn lifecycle paths. Validation: targeted nested suite and version digest pass; targeted race pass; golangci-lint passes; containerized full Go suite passes; build/root/frontend gates pass (145 files, 2614 tests). Host make ci remains environment-red only because bash 3.2 and dash are absent plus two known zsh host failures; the prescribed containerized run is green.

title: A password set from the connection editor never binds, and a cancelled vault op says nothing
description:
Editing a saved connection, choosing Method = Password and pressing "Set Password"
leaves the row reading "No password set", and the Secrets page lists no row for that
login. The password never becomes a usable credential for the connection.

Observed on 192.168.0.93 (pi@192.168.0.93:22). The Secrets page at the same moment
lists only `Passphrase for root@192.168.0.57` and `Key for root@192.168.0.57` — so
the vault itself works and other secrets bind; it is this path that does not.

Two candidate mechanisms, BOTH of which must be ruled in or out by evidence before
anything is edited — do not fix on the first plausible one:

1. The label reads the INVENTORY, not the binding. connections.tsx:2038
   `boundPasswordName` is `secretRows().find(e => e.id === fvStr('passwordSecret'))?.name`.
   A freshly minted row that has not landed in `secretRows()` yet makes the memo
   undefined, so the action goes on saying "No password set" and offering "Set
   Password" even when `options.passwordSecret` IS bound on the draft. That would
   make this a display defect over a correct binding — and the Secrets page would
   then be stale for the same reason.

2. The mint never happened and nothing said so. connections.tsx:2571 the failure
   path is `if (err instanceof VaultOperationCancelledError) return` — a silent
   return, no toast, no log, no state change. A cancelled or refused vault
   operation is therefore INVISIBLE: the dialog closes, the row still says "No
   password set", and the user is given no reason at all. AGENTS.md forbids exactly
   this shape — "a soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log",
   and here it is not even in a log.

Whichever is the root cause, the silent-cancel path at :2571 is a defect in its own
right and is in scope.

Related surface, same flow: `savePassword` mints with a generated name from
`secretNameFor('password', loginLabel(user, host))` and binds `row.row` into
`options.passwordSecret`, marking the field dirty — the binding is only persisted
when the profile is then saved. Check whether "Save Connection" actually writes it,
and whether cancelling the profile edit strands a minted secret with no owner.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings → Connections → edit 192.168.0.93 → Authentication.
2. Method = Password. Password source = "Type a new one".
3. Press "Set Password", type a password, confirm.
4. Press "Save Connection".

Observed: the Password row still reads "No password set" with a "Set Password"
button. Settings → Secrets lists no row for pi@192.168.0.93. Connecting still has no
stored password.

Expected: the row names the bound secret ("Password: <name>") and the Secrets page
lists it against 1 connection — or, if anything failed, the product SAYS SO.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After minting a password from the connection editor, the Password action names the
  bound secret rather than "No password set" — asserted without waiting on an
  inventory refresh, since the binding is known at that moment.
- The new secret appears in the Secrets page for that login, reporting 1 connection.
- Saving the connection persists `options.passwordSecret`; reopening the editor shows
  the bound secret still bound.
- Every failure path of the mint is VISIBLE in the product: a cancelled or refused
  vault operation leaves a message on screen naming what did not happen. Asserted as
  a test per failure path — including the cancel path, which currently returns
  silently.
- Paired with each "returns an error when…", a test that on an ordinary machine the
  mint SUCCEEDS (AGENTS.md testing rule 2).
close_reason: Shipped in #80: the minted name is trusted at bind, the inventory reloads, and a cancelled vault prompt now says so in the product.

title: The ports panel shows this machine's listeners under a tab that walked to a remote host by hand
description:
The ports panel scopes to what the session was OPENED with, never to where the pane
has since walked. A local tab in which the user typed `ssh pi@192.168.0.93` by hand
reports the reserved "local" target, so the panel lists THIS MACHINE's listeners under
a tab sitting on the Pi, and the row action is structurally Copy instead of Forward
(ports.tsx:511 swaps on isLocal(), plus the hard guard at ports.tsx:235).

This is nocx-695k.3 regressed. That fix returned null from portsTargetId inside a
hand-entered environment and named the host through portsUnavailableReason. Commit
6cba76fd (nocx-u7uh.1/.3, "the shell speaks over a channel") deleted both together
with the environment stack when it moved to ADR-0024, and never re-wired them to the
replacement fact — the ACTIVE DOMAIN's host/user, which terminal-content.ts still
tracks (_host/_user, line 334) and which already draws `pi@192.168.0.93` on the block
header and the location line.

Three things the severance left behind, all in frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:

1. portsTargetId (:458) returns LOCAL_TARGET_ID regardless of the active domain.
2. portsUnavailableReason (:466) returns "" unconditionally — so the panel's
   "Cannot see the ports on <host>" empty state (ports.tsx:384) is UNREACHABLE dead
   code, and the degrade is invisible in the product.
3. onPortsTargetChange (:194) is declared and wired in tabs.ts (:470, :519) but has
   NO CALLER — so even a corrected target would not re-scope the panel until the
   user switched tabs.

Out of scope, deliberately: forwarding directly over a hand-typed ssh. tunnel.open
(ws_tunnel.go:148) resolves a SAVED PROFILE into host+ClientConfig and dials nocx's
own connection; a hand-typed ssh is a child process of the local shell and there is
no connection nocx owns. The path to forwarding is therefore to open the host as a
connection, which is what the empty state must offer.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a local shell tab.
2. Type `ssh pi@192.168.0.93` and log in. Shell integration comes up on the remote —
   the block header shows `pi@192.168.0.93` and `home/pi`, so nocx knows where the
   pane is.
3. Open the Ports view in the sidebar.

Observed: "Detected / This machine" listing the LOCAL mac's listeners (ControlCe,
Raycast, node…), each row offering Copy. There is no Forward action anywhere.

Expected: the panel names the host the pane is actually on and says it cannot
enumerate it, and offers the action that would make forwarding possible.

Contrast: on a saved-connection tab (ct-alertmanager, ct-pihole) Forward is present
and works — confirmed by the owner, so the managed path is sound and only the
hand-typed path is broken.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A local tab whose ACTIVE DOMAIN names a remote host reports portsTargetId === null,
  and portsUnavailableReason === that host. Asserted both directions: a local tab with
  no remote domain still reports LOCAL_TARGET_ID and "".
- A saved-profile ssh tab keeps reporting its profile id while it sits on its own
  host, and reports null once the pane walks onward to a DIFFERENT host by hand.
- Walking into and back out of a hand-typed ssh fires onPortsTargetChange, so the
  panel re-scopes with NO tab switch.
- The panel renders "Cannot see the ports on 192.168.0.93" for that tab — never this
  machine's listeners — and that state offers an action that opens the host as a
  connection.
- One automated check watches a user reach a remote host by hand-typed ssh, see the
  honest empty state, take the offered action, and end up on a tab where the Forward
  control exists.
close_reason: Shipped in #80: the ports scope follows the pane via the kernel's domain stack, and the honest empty state offers to open the host as a connection.

title: a shellintegration test fixture leaks both socketpair ends into the shell it starts
description:
TestBootstrapProgress_AClosedDescriptorCostsNoTerminal (nocx-yww2) fails on main, and it is the fixture rather than the product.

Every fixture in internal/shellintegration mints its lifecycle channel with syscall.Socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0), which leaves BOTH descriptors inheritable. exec then hands the shell the intended end as fd 3 through ExtraFiles AND leaks both raw ends at whatever numbers the test process had free — which varies with what ran earlier in the same process and on the same machine.

The closed-descriptor test announces NOCX_BOOTSTRAP_FD=4 and deliberately hands over fd 3 only, on the premise that fd 4 does not exist in the shell. Measured here, the socketpair got fds [4 5], so fd 4 in the shell WAS the kernel end of its own lifecycle socket: the rcfile's 'startup-entered' went into the kernel end, came straight back out of the shell's fd 3, and the handshake read the header '73746172' ('star') instead of an accept frame, refused the session and left it conventional. Ten seconds later the test reported 'handshake never completed', naming neither the descriptor nor the loopback.
