developed and exercised on Linux, which is the same shape as the defect that
work was fixing.

This is the third instance in one session of the same class — a gate that
encodes the host it was written on. The other two are nocx-0odm (the deadcode
baseline was a snapshot of one machine) and nocx-sw4p (the script assumed the
bash version its author had). Worth a look as a pattern rather than three
bugs: the local gate should be able to state which host assumptions it makes.

## Steps to Reproduce

On an arm64 Mac:

    docker build .githooks/images/go-tests     # dies on the cp
    git commit                                 # hook fails at "go test -race (container)"

## Acceptance Criteria

- Both images build on arm64 and amd64 hosts.
- `bash32 --version` reports 3.2 inside each image, asserted in the build
  itself so a broken stage cannot ship silently (go-tests already does this).
- scripts/install-bash32.sh installs a working bash32 on both architectures.
- No file under .githooks/images or scripts names an architecture except where
  it is deliberate, and where it is, a comment says why.

title: [bug] the deadcode ratchet cannot pass on macOS, so the pre-commit hook blocks every commit from a Mac
description:
The pre-commit deadcode ratchet cannot pass on macOS, so no commit can be made
from a Mac without --no-verify — which skips gofumpt, lint and the
containerized test run along with it.

    DEADCODE RATCHET: 94 unreachable functions (95 baselined, shrunk by 1, 1 NEW):
      NEW: internal/vault/system/secretservice_other.go: SecretServiceAvailable
    FAIL: deadcode ratchet

The baseline was generated on Linux. `deadcode` sees one GOOS at a time, so on
a Mac the build-tag-gated `_other` halves compile and their Linux siblings do
not. The baseline's own header anticipates HALF of this:

    "build-tag-gated files (e.g. secretservice_linux.go) only appear on the OS
     they build for, so an entry that vanishes on another platform is a free
     shrink, not a violation."

A vanishing entry is handled. An APPEARING one is not, and it is the same fact
seen from the other platform. Regenerating on macOS does not fix it, it mirrors
it: the Linux entries would then vanish (free shrink, fine) and reappear as NEW
violations the next time a Linux machine runs the hook.

So the baseline cannot be a snapshot of one machine. It has to be the UNION
across the platforms the product builds for, and
.githooks/update-deadcode-baseline.mjs has to merge rather than replace.

Note this is a HOST gate, not a containerized one — host_gate in
.githooks/pre-commit runs it on whatever the developer is running. And CI never
runs deadcode at all (no step in .github/workflows/ci.yml), so the hook is the
only place this check exists: it is simultaneously the only enforcement and
unpassable on the primary target platform.

`SecretServiceAvailable` itself is not the defect and should not be "fixed" —
it is a deliberate cross-platform stub whose only callers are tests, and its
Linux sibling is already baselined at lines 331 and 335.

The comment in internal/lifecyclechannel/socketpair_linux.go (this branch)
already states the required behaviour — "Both halves must stay listed in the
deadcode baseline: the update script sees one OS at a time and reads the half
it did not compile as a free shrink" — so the rule is known and only the tool
does not implement it.

## Steps to Reproduce

On macOS, with any Go change staged:

    git commit          # dies on the ratchet, in a file you did not touch

## Acceptance Criteria

- The pre-commit hook passes on macOS AND on Linux from the same committed
  baseline, with no per-machine regeneration.
- update-deadcode-baseline.mjs merges platforms rather than replacing, and says
  in the file which platforms the union covers.
- A genuinely new unreachable function still fails the ratchet on both
  platforms — proven by adding one and watching it fail, not by inspection.

title: [bug] the child-environment probe fails on a macOS workstation but passes on the runner, so the secret-leak check cannot report
description:
TestLocalEnhancedChildEnv_SecretNeverReachesIt fails on a macOS workstation and
passes on the macOS CI runner, which makes the test — not the product — the
thing to look at first.

    app_test.go:382: the child's actual environment must carry the activation
                    gate (proving this is the right process)

It fails at the step that FINDS the child and reads its environment, before any
assertion about the secret. So the test cannot currently report what it exists
to report: on this machine it would pass or fail for reasons unrelated to
whether the secret leaked.

Reading another process's environment on Darwin goes through KERN_PROCARGS2,
which is restricted in ways that differ between a workstation and a fresh CI
runner (SIP, hardened runtime, whether the reader is the same uid and
session). That is the first hypothesis, not a conclusion.

Arrived with the childenviron_darwin_test.go added in 07b8266 on this branch.
Confirmed pre-existing relative to nocx-sw4p: it fails identically with that
fix stashed.

TestLocalEnhancedSessionEstablishesThroughProductionWiring fails right after it
with `panic: repeated read on failed websocket connection` (app_test.go:485) —
likely the same root cause cascading, but it is a PANIC rather than a failure,
so it takes the whole package's run down with it and should be made to fail
cleanly regardless.

## Steps to Reproduce

    go test -count=1 -run 'TestLocalEnhancedChildEnv_SecretNeverReachesIt' ./internal/app/

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test either passes on a macOS workstation, or states in one sentence the
  environmental precondition it requires and fails with THAT message.
- A test that cannot observe the child's environment does not report "the
  secret did not leak" — it must be impossible for this check to pass
  vacuously.
- TestLocalEnhancedSessionEstablishesThroughProductionWiring fails rather than
  panics when its websocket dies.

title: [bug] a nested sudo/su/ssh never establishes its child domain on macOS, in both bash and zsh
description:
A nested environment (sudo/su/ssh entered from inside a session) never
establishes its child domain on macOS. The parent requests the domain, the
grant path times out, and the parent runs the user's command conventionally —
so the nested shell is a plain terminal with no blocks.

Red on the macOS CI job (run 31418267046) and reproducible on a macOS
workstation:

    TestBashNestedChildDomain            (10s timeout)
    TestZshNestedChildDomain             (35s timeout)
    TestBashNestedChildDomainSu          (10s)
    TestZshNestedChildDomainSu           (35s)
    TestBashNestedChildDomainSuFallback  (10s)

NOT the bash 3.2 readable-probe (nocx-sw4p). Measured both ways: they fail
identically with nocx-sw4p's fix applied and with it stashed, and the ZSH
variants fail too — zsh never used `read -N`, it uses zselect, which is present
and working on macOS (verified: `zmodload zsh/zselect` succeeds on zsh 5.9).
Two shells with two different probes failing the same way puts the defect in
the nested-launch path they share, not in either probe.

One observation worth keeping for whoever takes this: with nocx-sw4p's fix in,
TestBashNestedChildDomain's timeout went from 10s to 20s. The failure did not
change, but the path got further before giving up — so the probe fix is a
precondition for diagnosing this, not a fix for it. Take this bead AFTER
nocx-sw4p lands, or the two defects mask each other.

Not reproducible on Linux: these tests are green on both backend-linux matrix
legs. So it is macOS-specific, and the bash-version matrix from nocx-x9c4 will
NOT catch it — this one needs the macOS job or a Mac.

## Steps to Reproduce

    go test -race -count=1 -run 'NestedChildDomain' ./internal/shellintegration/

## Acceptance Criteria

- All five nested-domain tests pass on the macOS `backend` CI job.
- The root cause is stated as one sentence naming the shared step that fails,
  and it accounts for BOTH the bash and the zsh variant.
- If the cause turns out to be two causes wearing one symptom, this bead splits
  rather than growing.

title: Extend the bash-version matrix to the other 24 real-bash call sites
description:
The channel suite now runs every bash on the machine (forEachBash / bashVariants
in scripts_bash32_test.go), which is what makes the bash 3.2 defect reproducible
on Linux without a Mac. 24 further call sites still resolve `requireShell(t,
"bash")` — the PATH bash only, which on every developer machine and both Linux
CI jobs is a 5.x:

    internal/shellintegration/scripts_exec_test.go   16 sites
    internal/shellintegration/launcher_test.go        6 sites
    internal/shellintegration/nested_domain_test.go   3 sites
    internal/shellintegration/nested_detect_test.go   1 site

scripts_exec_test.go is the one that matters most, because it is the file
TestBashScript_ParsesUnderBash32's own comment points at as the place where
"what 3.2 DOES" is covered — and it is exactly the coverage that was not
happening. nested_domain_test.go matters second: TestBashNestedChildDomain,
TestBashNestedChildDomainSu and TestBashNestedChildDomainSuFallback were all red
on the macOS runner in CI run 31418267046.

NOT DONE IN ONE PASS, deliberately, and the reason is cost rather than taste:
these tests drive real shells on real ptys and the package already takes 249s on
the macOS job and 106s on Linux. The nested-domain tests are 10-35s EACH.
Doubling all 24 without measuring is how a suite becomes something people skip.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four files is either converted to forEachBash or carries a
  one-line comment saying why its bash is version-independent.
- The package's wall-clock on the Linux CI job is stated before and after; if
  the increase is over 60s, the slow tests carry the matrix and the fast ones do
  too, or the split is justified in the commit body.
- No test drops its existing PATH-bash coverage to gain 3.2 coverage — the
  matrix ADDS a variant, it does not swap one.

title: macOS test portability: /proc and a 104-byte sun_path
description:
Two Linux assumptions in test code that only fail on the ship platform, both
found in the same red macOS CI job as nocx-nag7:

1. TestLocalEnhancedChildEnv_SecretNeverReachesIt and
   TestBashChannel_CapabilityNeverInAnyEnvironment read /proc/<pid>/environ.
   macOS has no /proc, so the assertion that the per-epoch capability never
   reaches a child's environment — the strongest security property in
   ADR-0024 decision 2 — was proven on exactly the platform that does not
   ship, and unprovable on the one that does.

2. TestLiveSshd_SSHChildAssembly_* bind an ssh-agent socket under t.TempDir().
   t.TempDir() spells the test's full name into the path; darwin's sun_path is
   104 bytes and its temp base is already ~49, so bind failed with "invalid
   argument". Linux has 108 bytes and a short /tmp, which hid it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `go test ./internal/app/... ./internal/shellintegration/...` on macOS.
2. "open /proc/<pid>/environ: no such file or directory", and
   "listen unix .../agent.sock: bind: invalid argument".

## Acceptance Criteria

- The capability-leak assertion runs and passes on darwin, reading the
  kernel's own view of the environment there too.
- No test binds a unix socket at a path whose length depends on the test's
  name.
- internal/app is green on macos-latest.
close_reason: Shipped. The /proc reads are gone, replaced by the portable readShellEnviron in internal/app/shellenviron_test.go:38 (base64 env -0 over the pty) and by the child reporting its own env in internal/shellintegration/channel_exec_test.go:889. The 104-byte sun_path bound is asserted in internal/app/ssh_child_assembly_test.go:259. Commits 9c0f6950 and 72951b5b. Note: the comment at ssh_child_assembly_test.go:259 mis-attributes the fix to nocx-cn86; the code is correct, only the comment is mislabelled. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: The pre-commit go container is not the CI environment, and nothing says so
description:
The pre-commit hook runs go tests in a container that does NOT match CI, so
"green locally" has never predicted "green in CI" — and nothing says so.

  local (.githooks/images/go-tests)   CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
  golang:1.26-bookworm (Debian)       ubuntu-latest
  Go baked into the image             setup-go@v7
  Debian zsh                          Ubuntu zsh via apt
  compaudit perms NOT fixed           compaudit perms fixed (chmod go-w)
  no Secret Service at all            with-keyring=true runs gnome-keyring
                                        under dbus-run-session
  all host cores                      2 cores

The keyring variant has no local equivalent whatsoever, and it is one of the
two variants CI gates on.

AGENTS.md warns that the E2E container failure set is not CI s. It says
nothing of the kind about this one, so it reads as a faithful pre-flight and
is not.

Observed cost, 2026-08-10: a release attempt and a follow-up PR both came
back red from CI after the local container was green; two pre-commit runs
failed on container tests that passed in isolation and were dismissed as
load. Main itself is red on both Linux variants with a DIFFERENT set of
tests than the PR — the suite is unstable on a 2-core runner and no local
gate can currently see it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the hook container: it passes.
2. Push: CI fails on tests the container never exercised the same way.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One command reproduces the CI backend-linux job locally, both matrix
  variants, on the same base image and package set, with the runner s core
  count.
- Either the hook uses that image, or the hook prints in one line what it
  does NOT cover, the way AGENTS.md does for the e2e container.
- The offline/warm-run property the current image was built for is stated
  and either kept or deliberately traded.
close_reason: Shipped. scripts/ci-linux.sh runs both keyring variants and .githooks/images/ci-linux/Dockerfile pins --platform=linux/amd64 to be the runner; the gap is now stated out loud in .githooks/pre-commit:284 and Makefile:230, which names backend-linux, e2e and frontend as NOT covered. Commits 0258425b and 72951b5b. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: TestOneLaneSeveralDomainsNoCurrentDomain fails under low parallelism, so it fails on CI runners
description:
TestOneLaneSeveralDomainsNoCurrentDomain fails in CI (ci/backend-linux,
with-keyring=false) with "adapter_test.go:639: read accept: EOF". It passes
on a many-core developer host and reproduces on demand under low
parallelism, so it is a scheduling-dependent defect and not a flake in the
usual sense — a CI runner simply has fewer cores than the machine the test
was written on.

Found by the v0.1.0 release run (31411588854).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. GOMAXPROCS=1 go test -race -count=10 \
     -run TestOneLaneSeveralDomainsNoCurrentDomain ./internal/lifecycleremote/
2. It fails; the log shows "lifecycle remote transport lost ... error=<nil>",
   i.e. the transport closed before the accept was read.

Note the plain many-core run passes 20x under -race, which is why it reached
main.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test passes 50 consecutive runs under GOMAXPROCS=1 with -race.
- Whatever the cause, it is stated as an interval with both ends: what the
  transport guarantees from establishment until the accept is delivered.
close_reason: Shipped. internal/lifecycleremote/adapter_test.go:661 replaced the parallelism-sensitive race with a state wait, waittest.WaitFor(t, root suspended, ...) on d.State == lifecycle.DomainSuspended, and the comment names this bead. Commit 07b8266c. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: cleanEnv is Linux-tagged but used by untagged tests, so shellintegration does not build on macOS
description:
cleanEnv is defined in internal/shellintegration/inband_pty_test.go, which
is //go:build linux. Two test files that call it carry no build tag:
channel_exec_test.go (lines 312, 851, 853, 971, 1156) and
nested_domain_test.go (385, 598). On macOS the helper is not compiled and
the package tests do not build.

The Linux-only tag on the definition is deliberate and documented (termios
bit semantics differ on darwin); the tag is missing on the USERS, or the
helper belongs in a file without one.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. GOOS=darwin go vet ./internal/shellintegration/
2. It fails: undefined: cleanEnv.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The shellintegration package and its tests build on darwin.
- Whichever way it is resolved, the Linux-depth suite keeps its documented
  Linux-only tag and its reason.
close_reason: Shipped. cleanEnv moved out of the Linux-tagged file into untagged internal/shellintegration/env_test.go:22, whose header names this bead; inband_pty_test.go keeps its //go:build linux tag. Commit 07b8266c. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: Explore project context and query the KB
close_reason: Context and KB explored: found N3 (2026-08-05 delivery-modes design) superseding D1/D2 consent, the footprint as its compensating control, and in-band as a no-persistent-trace path

title: Brainstorming: consent before remote nocxify install, fallback to conventional terminal
description:
Brainstorming session: the user proposes that nocx OFFER to install the
shell-integration bundle on a remote host rather than installing it silently,
and fall back to a conventional terminal when the offer is declined.

Raised while resolving blocker A on PR 69 (nocx-292k): the installed-fact
writer was severed on the branch, so remote installs are invisible and the
footprint surface reports "Nothing installed" after a real install.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A design document exists at .internal/specs/ and is approved by the owner.
- The design says what happens on decline, on re-connect, and where the
  answer is remembered.
- Its relationship to PR 69 is explicit: fixed in the merge, or its own epic
  with a dependency edge.

title: Land the shell-channel branch on top of the control-plane rewrite
description:
shady2k/fix-omp-hide is 41 commits ahead and 21 behind main, and the two sides rewrote the same transport. main's PR #68 (nocx-sfv6) replaced the method switch in internal/transport/ws.go with a registration table — every method a capability-scoped handler struct under a domain gate, plus internal/capability and internal/transport/control. This branch edited the same ws.go (+157) and ws_shell.go, and 6cba76fd deleted internal/transport/ws_shell_launcher.go, which main had just adapted to the new dispatch.

git merge origin/main conflicts in ws.go (5 hunks), ws_shell.go (4), ws_shell_launcher.go (delete/modify) and .beads/issues.jsonl (regenerable).

The method sets were compared: only three methods on this branch are absent from main — lifecycle.submitAttempt, lifecycle.recoverAck, lifecycle.establishAck. Everything else exists there in the new form, so the job is to carry this branch's delta onto main's architecture, not to merge line by line.

Three decisions belong to the owner and gate the work:

1. Which gate and submission the three lifecycle.* methods register under. They are ack-shaped and session-scoped; the ingress-critical set is closed and validated at construction, so claiming immediate for them would fail the server build — deliberately.
2. Whether shell.launcherCommand and shell.environmentObserved stay dead. 6cba76fd killed them as the P7 stream-and-passport surface gated on the marker latch ADR-0024 (this branch's) forbids; main rewrote them into launcherHandlers. If they stay dead, main's registrations go with them.
3. Which of the two ADR-0024 documents renumbers. This branch carries 0024-authenticated-shell-integration-channel.md, main brought 0024-control-plane-runs-off-the-read-loop.md, git merged them silently because there is no textual conflict, and 'ADR-0024' is referenced in 97 files — one string now naming two documents.

Tracked on PR #69 (draft): https://github.com/shady2k/nocx/pull/69

## Acceptance Criteria

- origin/main is merged into the branch with no conflict markers, and the three lifecycle.* methods are registered in main's control-plane registration set rather than in a restored switch.
- The full gate passes on the merged tree: gofumpt, golangci-lint, go test -race ./..., and the frontend's prettier/eslint/typecheck/vitest.
- Exactly one ADR carries the number 0024, and no reference to ADR-0024 in code or docs is ambiguous.
- The merge slot is taken before integrating and released afterwards, including on the failure path.
close_reason: Merged as 05181a9c. origin/main fully merged (0 behind), no conflict markers; the three lifecycle.* methods register on a dedicated control.NewOrderedSubmission in main's registration table, not a restored switch — proven by the goroutine ratchet passing with an untouched baseline. Full gate green incl. containerized go test -race and vitest. Exactly one ADR-0024 (lifecycle); main's control-plane ADR renumbered to 0026 across its 9 referrers. Merge slot acquired and released.

title: One automated check watches a real shell receive an inserted secret
description:
Split out of nocx-fk32 when the owner closed it, 2026-08-10. The feature is delivered and the owner verified the chain by hand; what is missing is a test, and a test bead inside a closed feature evaporates between sessions.

Three seams carry an inserted secret and only two are held by unit tests against fakes: the input-ownership decision (terminal-content.test.ts asserts exactly 'hunter2\\n' goes to the pty, and that an unresolved reference never does), the backend's vault.resolveLine, and the composition root's wiring from the tab-strip icon to the pane. The last one is the stick that breaks in a refactor without dropping a single unit test.

e2e/prompt-vault.spec.ts already drives the adjacent scenario through cmd/devharness, so this is one spec against that harness, not new infrastructure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Against a real shell at a password prompt, opening the tab-strip picker and choosing a secret makes the far side receive the secret's value, and the test asserts what arrived at stdin rather than what the renderer called.
- The check fails if the composition root stops routing the icon to the pane.

title: Quick vault says 'No matches' when the vault is not set up, or when unlocking was cancelled
description:
The quick vault renders vault.inventory and nothing else. A failed call is skipped silently by the dialog's provider loop, so two different facts arrive as one empty list:

- Protection has never been set up: vault.inventory fails with reason vault-uninitialized, nothing intercepts it (only saveSecretWithVault handles that reason), and the picker says 'No matches' — which reads as 'you have no secrets' when the truth is 'there is no vault yet'.
- The unlock prompt was cancelled: the dispatcher's global vault-sealed seam raised the dialog and rejects the call, and the picker again says 'No matches' while the vault sits locked.

A soft degrade the UI contradicts is how a feature that does not exist survives a release (AGENTS.md). quick-connect already has the shape for this: an unavailable ssh -G renders as a row naming the condition, never as an empty list. The prompt's '@' picker already has the same two offers, and the same two seams exist in the composition root (vaultController.openSetup, vaultController.openUnlock).

Sealed on its own is NOT part of this: the dispatcher raises the unlock dialog and retries the call, so an unlock that succeeds fills the list already.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a profile with no vault set up, open the tab-strip key icon. It says 'No matches'.
2. With a sealed vault, open it and dismiss the unlock dialog. It says 'No matches'.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With no vault set up, the picker shows one row offering to set protection up, and activating it opens the vault's setup dialog.
- When the inventory could not be read, the picker shows one row naming the condition and offering to unlock, and activating it opens the unlock dialog.
- Neither state offers 'Add a secret…' — there is nowhere to put it yet.
- Both rows carry the same words as the '@' picker's offers, so the two surfaces cannot drift into saying different things about one vault.
close_reason: Landed in 67f9d08c. Uninitialized renders the setup offer, a failed inventory renders the unlock offer, and neither state offers 'Add a secret…'. Sealed alone stays with the dispatcher's unlock-and-retry seam, and a test pins that a sealed vault whose inventory resolves shows the list rather than an offer row. The three sentences are exported from ui/secret-picker.ts so both surfaces read the same words.

title: Quick vault offers to create the secret it could not find
description:
Owner, 2026-08-10: the quick vault lists what the vault holds and stops there — a name that is not in the list has no answer, and the create dialog lives in Settings, which the user has to know about.

The '@' picker (frontend/src/ui/secret-picker.ts) already answers this: a synthetic last row 'Add a secret…' carrying the typed filter as the name, routed through requestCreate -> tm.onCreateSecret -> openSettingsTab().startNewSecret(name). The seam is reused here; only the row is new.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the tab-strip key icon (quick vault).
2. Type a name the vault does not hold.
3. The panel says 'No matches' and offers nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The quick vault always renders a last row 'Add a secret…', and 'Add <typed> to the vault…' when the filter is non-empty — including when nothing matched and when the vault is empty.
- Activating it closes the picker and opens the vault create dialog with the typed name prefilled, through the same seam the '@' picker uses.
- The row never appears in the server list or in the palette.

Still outstanding after this (recorded on nocx-fk32): the two surfaces are two implementations of one concept, and a sealed or uninitialized vault still reads as 'No matches' in the quick vault.
close_reason: Landed in 90554c7: getTrailingItems on the provider interface, the create row on SecretsQuickConnectProvider, and the composition root routing it to openSettingsTab().startNewSecret — the same seam the '@' picker creates through. Three checks in quick-connect.test.tsx cover the last-row position, the no-match case carrying the typed name, the empty vault, and the row's absence from the palette and the server list.

title: Insert a saved secret into the pane in front, from a picker beside quick connect
description:
Owner, 2026-08-10: 'давай сделаем возможность вставить пароль из vault', and after weighing the two candidate surfaces: 'делаем иконку рядом с quick connect'.

Replaces the askpass direction for the local ssh case. nocx-jee1 is deferred with the reasoning; the owner's ruling is that nocx cannot know what is on screen, so the surface must be always available rather than offered at a moment we would have to infer.

## Why this shape and not the other two

Both candidate surfaces were already settled in this repo and the record decided it.

- A full Vault in the activity bar collides with .internal/specs/2026-07-27-ui-shell-kit-and-theming-design.md 2.4: 'Connections leaves the activity bar entirely. It was never a view of the workspace; it is an action, and putting an action in the view list is what produced nocx-rp2j.' The activity bar holds views that re-scope to the tab in front (Files, Ports, Git all take activeProfileId/activeOrigin). The vault re-scopes to nothing.
- An offer attached to the running ssh block was considered and rejected by the owner: we do not know what will be on screen, and inferring 'a password is being asked' from the stream is what ADR-0004 and AD-6 forbid.
- The same spec already chose this shape for this class of problem: 'Launching is a modal quick-connect picker, opened from a caret beside the + in the tab strip and from a keyboard shortcut. Type to filter, Enter to open a tab.' An action needing a filterable list is a modal picker from the tab strip. It needs no new primitive.

## What to build

A third icon in the tab strip actions, beside New tab and the quick-connect caret, in BOTH orientations. It opens the SAME QuickConnectController under a new PaletteVariant ('secrets'), listing names from vault.inventory — names only, never material.

The target is chosen by who owns input, and this is the point of the design:

- The TERMINAL owns input (a raw password prompt, a nested ssh handshake, sudo, mysql -p): the chosen secret is resolved through vault.resolveLine('{{secret:NAME}}') and written to the pty. That method exists for exactly this — 'the resolved value goes to the caller for the PTY write and nowhere else'. No newline is appended; the user presses Enter. Because the password is not echoed, the insert must be confirmed visibly (a toast), or the user will press the key twice.
- The EDITOR owns the prompt: the REFERENCE {{secret:NAME}} is inserted into the draft, not the value. This is ADR-0021's whole argument — a command carrying a reference moves to another machine and resolves that machine's secret; a command carrying a pasted key is both dead and dangerous — and the reference already renders as the SecretChip.

## Deliberately out

- No inference about what is on screen, ever. Nothing reads the stream to decide whether to offer, to order, or to preselect (AD-6, ADR-0004).
- No destination-aware ordering in this bead. During an ssh handshake the lane has no active domain, and deriving the destination from the typed line is the defect AGENTS.md records for 2026-08-05. Order by recency.
- No askpass helper, local or remote (nocx-jee1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- From a terminal at a raw password prompt, the user opens the picker from the tab-strip icon, types to filter, presses Enter, and the far side receives the secret without the user typing it; the pane shows a confirmation that something was inserted, because the prompt echoes nothing.
- With the editor owning the prompt, the same picker inserts {{secret:NAME}} into the draft and it renders as the secret chip; nothing resolves until submit.
- The picker lists names only. No secret value reaches any log, any history row, any draft in the terminal case, or any surface other than the pty write.
- A sealed vault raises the existing unlock dialog rather than failing silently.
- The dialog is the existing QuickConnectController under a new variant — no second picker component, no new primitive.
- One automated check drives the terminal case end to end against a real shell: pick a secret, and the value arrives at the far side's stdin.
close_reason:
Owner's call, 2026-08-10: 'Закрывай эпик.' The picker ships — the tab-strip icon, the secrets variant, the provider, the insert seam that routes by who owns input, the create offer and the vault's states as offers (nocx-fk32.1-.3), verified by hand end to end.

The one acceptance criterion not met is the automated check against a real shell; it left as nocx-nylp rather than as a sentence in a closed bead, with a discovered-from edge back here. The recorded correction (this picker and the prompt's '@' picker are two implementations of one concept) and the unbuilt keyboard shortcut also remain — neither has a bead yet.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Landed in 2b115e32: the icon, the picker variant, the provider and the insert seam, with unit coverage on the target decision (frontend/src/terminal-content.test.ts, 'inserting a saved secret into the pane in front') and on the picker's kind separation (quick-connect.test.tsx).

NOT done, and the bead stays open for it: the last acceptance criterion — one automated check driving the terminal case end to end against a real shell, so that the chain icon → picker → resolve → pty write is watched rather than assumed. The unit tests prove each half against fakes; nothing has yet watched a real shell receive the value. Per AGENTS.md rule 2 that is exactly the check that reports a missing feature, so it is the remaining work here, not a nicety.

Also unbuilt and deliberately so: the keyboard shortcut. The shell design pairs the tab-strip caret with a chord, and this picker should have one too; it was left out to keep this commit to the surface the owner asked for.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Owner review, 2026-08-10, and one of the three is a design correction on what I built.

1. 'почему из ключика нельзя создать новый секрет' — because I built a second picker instead of finding the first. frontend/src/ui/secret-picker.ts ALREADY has everything asked for: a synthetic 'Add a secret…' last row seeded with what was typed (its own comment: 'asking them to type it again is how a feature goes unused'), an offer to unseal a sealed vault from inside the panel, an offer to set up an uninitialized one, and the honest empty state. PromptVaultController hosts it on the editor's '@' trigger, and requestCreate routes to tm.onCreateSecret → openSettingsTab().startNewSecret(name), which is the create dialog.

So the quick-connect 'secrets' variant plus SecretsQuickConnectProvider are a second vocabulary for one concept — exactly what AGENTS.md forbids, and I quoted the rule in the commit while breaking it. THE CORRECTION: the tab-strip key icon should open the existing SecretPicker, whose onInsert(name) routes to TerminalContent.insertSecret(name) — the one genuinely new thing here, because the picker has only ever had one target (the editor's draft) and the terminal case needs the pty. Then delete the variant, the provider, PaletteVariant 'secrets', the 'secret' item kind and their tests. The remaining question is anchoring: SecretPicker is a FloatingPanel positioned at the caret, and opened from the tab strip it needs an anchor — the icon itself.

2. 'enter нужно вставлять сразу' — done in fc189136; the reasoning is recorded there.

3. 'даже после exit обе команды активны' — a different bug, and the screenshot proves yesterday's fix works: the exit blocks froze at 141ms/142ms while the parent ssh blocks kept climbing. That is nocx-z5k9, now reproduced and fixed in fc189136: freezeEntered had no caller anywhere.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Owner verified by hand, 2026-08-10: the tab-strip picker creates, inserts and reports correctly after nocx-fk32.1-.3 (90554c7, 399574d4, 67f9d08c).

What that does NOT close: the last acceptance criterion is still open, because a hand check and an automated one answer different questions — nothing yet watches a real shell receive the value, so nothing will notice when it stops. Also still open: the recorded correction (the tab-strip picker and the prompt's '@' picker remain two implementations of one concept) and the unbuilt keyboard shortcut.

title: The parent's ssh block stays running after the child exits, in a case the trace does not reproduce
description:
Split out of nocx-mlyu on 2026-08-10. The owner observed the parent's 'ssh pi@…' block showing the running dot and a climbing timer (2m0s) with no exit code after the far session exited.

A trace against a real sshd did NOT reproduce it: the parent recovers, its attempt completes with the real status at its next prompt boundary, and the lane returns to the parent (nocx-mlyu comment, 2026-08-10). The two presentation defects that trace DID find are fixed under nocx-mlyu; this bead is the remaining, unreproduced half.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an integrated local tab, type 'ssh pi@192.168.0.93' and log in over a real network, not localhost.
2. Run a few commands on the far host — blocks appear, so the child domain is live.
3. Type exit.
4. Observed by the owner: the parent's ssh block keeps the running dot and a climbing timer with no exit code. Traced against a local sshd: the parent recovers and completes with exitCode 0. The difference between the two environments is what this bead has to find.

## What to check first

Why the parent's channel would be inactive at its return boundary in the owner's environment and not in the traced one. Candidates, in order: the ssh client's -R teardown closing the transport the parent shares; a refresh_request buffered during the suspension that the parent answers into a dead channel; __nocx_lc_recover firing while the parent was blocked inside the launch (internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash:722, 253, 1107).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The failure is reproduced in an automated check BEFORE any fix is written — a red test naming the condition under which the parent's channel is inactive at its return boundary.
- After the far session exits, the parent's ssh block freezes with the real exit status in that condition too.
- If it cannot be reproduced after a bounded attempt, this bead records what was ruled out and what would be needed to catch it in the wild, rather than a speculative fix.

title: After a nested ssh exits, the parent's block never closes and the tab falls to unstructured
description:
Owner, 2026-08-10, after nocx-beib landed and blocks finally work inside a
hand-typed ssh. Three symptoms, and the shape suggests one cause.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an integrated local tab type `ssh pi@192.168.0.93` and log in.
2. Run a few commands on the far host — they get proper blocks with
   durations and ok, so the child domain is live.
3. Type `exit`.
4. The parent`s `ssh` block still shows the running dot and a climbing timer
   (observed at 2m0s), with no exit code. The `exit` block does the same
   (1m1s).
5. Type `ssh pi@192.168.0.93` again: the pane is now unstructured and shows
   the previous attempt`s output — `exit`, `Connection to … closed`, the
   earlier password prompt — as one continuous terminal.

## What is probably happening

Everything the parent must do when the child closes is behind ONE gate in
__nocx_prompt_command (internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash:744):

    if [[ "${__nocx_lc_active:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        if [[ "${__nocx_nested_active:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
            __nocx_lc_send domain_activated
        ...
        complete / prompt_ready

If the parent`s channel is not active at that boundary — __nocx_lc_active is
cleared by __nocx_lc_recover (line 722) and at 253/1107 — then no
domain_activated is sent, so the kernel keeps the parent Suspended; no
complete is sent, so the attempt stays open and the block never freezes (the
dot and the missing exit code); and the lane has no active domain, so the
renderer falls to the unstructured presentation, which is exactly what
symptom 3 looks like — a plain terminal still holding the previous output.

Unverified: WHY the parent`s channel is inactive on return. Candidates worth
checking in order: the ssh client`s -R teardown closing the transport the
parent shares; a refresh_request buffered during the suspension that the
parent answers into a dead channel; the recovery path firing while the
parent was blocked inside the launch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After the far session exits, the parent`s `ssh` block freezes with the real
  exit status.
- The tab returns to the structured presentation, and a second `ssh` starts
  from a clean block rather than showing the previous attempt.
- A test drives the whole cycle against a real sshd: parent integrated →
  child established → child exits → parent completes its attempt and owns
  the lane again. The existing assembly proof stops at the activation frame;
  this one has to watch the BLOCK close.
close_reason:
Fixed in 631a6e49. Three symptoms, two causes, both in the renderer — the parent's channel was never the problem.

1. The projections read only the lane's CURRENT attempt, so a nested domain's attempt (which the backend kernel and the renderer's reducer both correctly moved to unknown) never reached abandonBlock. reconcileBound now runs on every pump and subsumes the lost-lane sweep that used to be the only one.

2. Driving the cycle against a real sshd found the harder half: the far shell's start frame for 'exit' usually never gets out, because the command destroys the shell that would have sent it. So the block has NO attempt at all — it was opened at the app-owned submit and nothing could ever finish it. The kernel now counts domains that ENDED (the one thing a suspension does not do) and an unbound pending record is abandoned when one does.

3. 'native' meant three things and shellStateFromLifecycle answered all three with 'unsupported', so the structured presentation was torn down twice per nested session. Native over a non-empty domain stack is now a handover and keeps its structure; only an empty stack is a genuinely conventional terminal. No wire-contract change: a suspended domain is still on the stack.

Criterion 3 is TestLiveSshd_SSHChildAssembly_ExitFreezesTheChildBlockAndCompletesTheParent (internal/app/ssh_child_assembly_test.go): the whole cycle against the real sshd, watching the blocks, not stopping at the activation frame. It states its invariant over the DOMAIN — nothing of a closed domain is left open — because whether 'exit' becomes an attempt is a race the product cannot win; the renderer's two answers to the two outcomes are pinned in frontend/src/lifecycle/projections.test.ts.

Still open: nocx-z5k9, the owner's parent-block symptom in an environment the trace does not reproduce.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Traced against a real sshd (ssh localhost from an integrated tab, then exit). The lane's own sequence, from the published facts:

  prompt_ready                      parent
  running  open      'ssh localhost'   parent attempt opens
  native                              <- lane has NO domain
  prompt_ready                      child
  running  open      'exit'            child attempt opens
  native                              <- lane has NO domain again
  running  open      'ssh localhost'   parent back
  running  completed 'ssh localhost'   exitCode 0
  prompt_ready

Three separate things, and only the first is what the bead assumed:

1. The parent DOES recover here — its attempt completes with the real status
   at its next prompt boundary. So the owner's forever-running 'ssh' block is
   not a dead parent; it is a parent that has not reached a prompt boundary
   yet, or one whose channel died for a reason this path does not reproduce.
   Reproducing THAT is the remaining work.

2. The 'exit' block can never close. The shell that would send the completion
   is the one the command destroys, so the attempt stays open by
   construction. Every nested session ends on one, which is why it is the
   most visible instance. This needs a decision, not a fix: either the
   backend completes an attempt whose domain closed, or a block whose domain
   is gone is frozen with a stated 'unknown' rather than left running.

3. The lane passes through 'native' twice per nested session — once when the
   parent suspends, once when the child closes. The renderer answers native
   with the unstructured presentation, which shows the whole terminal buffer,
   and that is what the owner reported as 'I see output from previous
   attempts'. The buffer is not stale state; it is the pane correctly showing
   a conventional terminal, at a moment that is really a handover between two
   domains.

So the bead is at least two beads: the parent's own recovery (1, still
unreproduced), and the presentation of the handover interval plus the
terminal attempt (2 and 3), which are design questions about what a block and
a pane should claim while no domain owns the lane.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Split on 2026-08-10 after reading the code the trace pointed at. This bead now owns the two defects that ARE reproducible and share one cause; the unreproduced parent-recovery half moved to nocx-z5k9.

Cause, one sentence: the renderer's projections only ever process the lane's CURRENT attempt, and 'native' means three different things.

1. projections.ts pump() opens with 'if (state.kind !== "running") return; const attempt = state.attempt'. When the child domain closes, the lane already belongs to the parent, so the child's 'exit' attempt — which the kernel and the renderer's own state.ts:405-414 both correctly moved to 'unknown' — never reaches abandonBlock(). The running dot never stops. The only sweep over non-current attempts is abandonBound(), called on 'lost' alone.

2. shellStateFromLifecycle maps 'native' to 'unsupported', i.e. 'a conventional terminal'. state.ts:236-241 says outright that the renderer cannot tell suspend from close on that fact. So during a handover — parent suspended, or child closed and the parent's fact not yet in — the UI declares the shell unintegrated and drops to the unstructured presentation showing the whole buffer. That is symptom 3.

Owner's decision (2026-08-10): distinguish the handover interval from a conventional terminal. It needs no contract change — 'native' with a non-empty domain stack IS the handover; an empty stack is the genuine conventional terminal.

title: mc is unreadable because the palette is rendered literally — no minimum contrast
description:
Owner, 2026-08-10, comparing mc over ssh in nocx and in Warp on the same host:
in nocx the panels are unreadable, in Warp they are fine.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open any host and run `mc` (its default skin paints panels as
   `_default_ = lightgray;blue` — an ANSI colour used as a BACKGROUND).
2. Under the default theme (tokyo-night) the panel text is grey on light blue.

## Root cause

xterm.js renders the palette literally. Warp does not: it raises the
foreground against the actual cell background, which is why the same mc shows
DARK text on light blue there and light grey here.

Measured for tokyo-night (--terminal-ansi-7 #a9b1d6 on --terminal-ansi-4 #7aa2f7):

  mc _default_  lightgray on blue :  1.19 : 1   (4.5 is the readability floor)
  mc marked     yellow on blue    :  1.26 : 1
  mc selected   black on cyan     :  9.96 : 1   (the one readable row on screen)
  classic mc    white on #0000aa  : 13.29 : 1

No built-in theme clears the floor for that pair. Best are light (3.49),
solarized-dark/light (3.00), dracula (2.26), nord (2.21); worst are one-dark
(1.11), catppuccin-mocha and tokyo-night (1.19).

xterm.js has the mechanism as a first-class option and we never set it, so it
sits at its documented default of 1 = "do nothing"
(frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts, the new Terminal({...}) block).

## Fix

Set minimumContrastRatio: 4.5 (WCAG AA, the floor the numbers above are
measured against). Only pairs that would be unreadable are adjusted; anything
already above the floor renders exactly as the theme declares, so the palette
stays honest.

Deliberately out: a Settings toggle. If the fixed value turns out to be wrong
for someone, that is a separate bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts the option reaches the live Terminal instance, at the value
  the product ships — not that a constant exists.
- mc over ssh is readable under the default theme.
close_reason: Fixed in 0119164a: minimumContrastRatio 4.5 on the Terminal the renderer mounts; confirmed by the owner on mc over ssh.

title: A session that fell back to a conventional terminal never says so
description:
The owner had to ask why an ssh tab had no blocks, and the answer was only findable by reading the backend log. AGENTS.md states the rule this breaks in as many words: a soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log.

The concrete case that exposed it is nocx-340t (the remote bundle publish fails on an SFTP rename, so no lifecycle channel is ever established), but the defect is general: every path that lands a session in a conventional terminal — forwarding refused, an unsupported remote shell, a publish failure, a handshake that timed out, an establishment the renderer never acknowledged — degrades correctly and silently. From the user's side an integrated session and a degraded one differ only by the absence of things they might not have been expecting anyway.

The epic that built this (nocx-u7uh) made 'conventional' an honest, deliberate state; what it did not do is give the user a way to know they are in it, or why. That is the missing half.

Design questions the fix has to answer rather than assume: where the fact belongs (the tab, the pane, a one-shot toast — the kit has Section/Badge/showToast, and frontend/src/ui/README.md is required reading before anything new is drawn); how much of the reason is safe to show, given the reason often names a host, a path, or a policy; and whether a user can act on it (retry, install manually, ignore for this host) or is merely informed. A banner nobody can act on is noise, and noise is what makes people stop reading banners.

Do NOT surface the raw backend error text. The publish failure above is an SFTP status code and a path — meaningful here, meaningless in a pane.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an ssh session to a host where the integration cannot install (nocx-340t reproduces one such host reliably).
2. Observed: a plain terminal with a native prompt. Nothing in the product says integration was attempted and failed, or why, or what to do.

## Acceptance Criteria

A session that is conventional because integration was attempted and failed says so in the product, in a place the user is already looking, with a reason at the granularity a user can act on — and a session that is conventional by design (no integration requested) does not nag. Proven by a test per path that fails today. The wording is decided with the owner, not invented in code review.
close_reason: Shipped and never closed. The refusal vocabulary is in the tree: contracts/session.integrationChanged.schema.json declares the notification and its reason enum (ssh.RefusalReason), frontend/src/generated/session.integrationChanged.ts is generated from it, frontend/src/integration/status.ts maps every reason and frontend/src/integration/notice.tsx renders it, with tests in status.test.ts and notice.test.tsx. Both the schema and status.ts cite this bead by name. Children nocx-viil.1 and nocx-viil.2 stay open as refinements. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: Remote shell integration can never be republished: SFTP v3 rename refuses an existing manifest
description:
Diagnosed from the owner's dev log, 2026-08-09, after they asked why an ssh tab had no blocks.

At 23:52:42, exactly when the tab opened:
  remote bundle publish refused  root=/root/.nocx
    error="publisher: rename /root/.nocx/manifest.json: sftp: Failure (SSH_FX_FAILURE)"
  ssh: shell integration publish failed  host=192.168.0.57

So the integration bundle never lands, there is no lifecycle channel, and the session is a conventional terminal — which is the correct fallback for a failure but not a failure that should be happening.

Cause: internal/shellintegration/install_remote.go:68 implements the publisher's atomic activation with client.Rename, which is SFTP v3 SSH_FXP_RENAME. OpenSSH refuses it when the destination exists, and the destination is manifest.json — which exists on every host that was ever set up successfully. So the FIRST publish to a host works and every publish after it fails forever. The same host shows the same error on 2026-08-08 and twice on 2026-08-09, always on the same path.

pkg/sftp v1.13.11 (already the vendored version) exposes PosixRename, the posix-rename@openssh.com extension, which replaces atomically. The publisher's whole design rests on rename being an atomic activation pointer (publisher.go:26 and :202-203 say so), so the adapter is the layer that broke that promise, not the design.

Servers that do not advertise the extension need an answer too — remove-then-rename reopens a window the publisher deliberately closed, so if that is the fallback, name the window and what a reader who hits it should expect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Connect to a remote host with shell integration and let it install (first publish succeeds).
2. Connect again, or connect after any change that republishes.
3. Observed: the log carries "remote bundle publish refused ... rename ... SSH_FX_FAILURE" and the session has no blocks, no editor, no lifecycle channel.

## Acceptance Criteria

Publishing the bundle to a host that already has one succeeds, and the session gets its lifecycle channel. Proven against a real sshd (internal/app/live_sshd_test.go already drives one) by publishing twice in a row — the second publish is the test, and it fails today. What happens on a server without posix-rename is decided, implemented and stated.
close_reason: SFTP carrier now uses advertised posix-rename for atomic manifest replacement; servers without it retain the prior activation, and real OpenSSH production-connect acceptance plus containerized go test -race ./... pass.

title: A frozen block is wider than the live grid: DOM advance is not xterm's snapped cell width
description:
Reported by the owner with paired screenshots, 2026-08-09, after nocx-juau stopped the re-wrapping. The layout no longer folds, but it no longer MATCHES either: the same omp panel that ends around x=1633 while the program runs ends around x=1692 once frozen — roughly 3-4% wider — and a horizontal scrollbar now appears for content that fitted the pane perfectly a moment earlier.

Cause: the two surfaces agree on the font and disagree on the metric. frontend/src/renderers/font.ts says xterm rasterises into a GPU atlas snapped to whole device pixels, so its cell advance is a ROUNDED value; the DOM lays the same characters out at the font's natural fractional advance. The families are identical (both the FONT_FAMILY constant and --font-family-mono resolve to the same chain), so this is not a font-substitution problem — it is a per-cell rounding difference that accumulates over a line. Over ~100 columns a fraction of a pixel per cell is several columns of drift.

This is the same defect nocx-juau's wrapping was a symptom of, one level down: the frozen block reproduces the characters and not the geometry. Removing the wrap made it visible rather than causing it.

The measurement already exists: XtermRenderer._getCellDims() returns xterm's real CSS cell width from the render service — the same source FitAddon uses.

Note the wide-glyph gap nocx-juau named is a separate, narrower case of the same family (a fallback font's advance for an emoji or nerd-font symbol is its own metric, not the mono cell). Fixing the general metric may or may not fix it; say which after measuring rather than assuming.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an integrated session run omp (or any TUI drawing a full-width box) in a pane it fits exactly.
2. While it runs: the box fits, no horizontal scrollbar.
3. Exit it. Observed: the frozen block is visibly wider and a horizontal scrollbar appears.

## Acceptance Criteria

N columns of frozen output occupy exactly N times the terminal's cell width, so a block that fitted the pane while live still fits it once frozen and grows no scrollbar. Proven by a test that fails today. The wide-glyph case is answered by measurement either way — fixed, or recorded as what remains.
close_reason: The renderer's real cell width (_getCellDims, the fit path's source) is published as a custom property; the difference against the DOM's own advance — measured by a probe inside the scrollback so it inherits the block's font — is applied as per-character letter-spacing, so N frozen columns advance exactly N x cellWidth. Refreshed on mount, resize and device-pixel-ratio change; every block, old or new, adopts the current geometry, deliberately. Wide glyphs measured: the general metric does not land a fallback glyph on exactly two cells, but the live terminal overhangs them identically, so no new drift — exact per-glyph geometry stays a named gap. jsdom pins the plumbing only; real-browser pixel alignment is unverified.

title: A frozen block wraps terminal lines, so full-width TUI layout falls apart
description:
Reported by the owner with paired screenshots, 2026-08-09, after the colour fix landed: omp's status bar and its composer box render correctly while the program runs and come apart in the frozen block — the bar spills onto extra lines and the box-drawing borders no longer meet.

Cause, frontend/src/style.css:631: .cmd-output sets white-space: pre-wrap together with overflow-wrap: break-word, and also overflow-x: auto. The first two make a long line WRAP; the third never engages, because a wrapped line never overflows. So any output as wide as the terminal — a status bar, a full-width rule, a boxed panel — is folded onto a second line in the frozen block, and every box-drawing character after the fold lands in the wrong column.

The rule contradicts the reason the font is monospace at all. base.css:84 says it in as many words: the places that opt into monospace are the ones whose column alignment matters, and .cmd-output is named there first.

There may be a second, narrower contributor once wrapping is gone: a wide glyph (emoji, nerd-font symbol) occupies two terminal columns, and its advance width in the DOM font is not guaranteed to equal two monospace cells. The serializer already skips xterm's spacer cells correctly, so this would be a font-metric mismatch rather than a serialization bug. MEASURE whether it is real before changing anything for it; do not fix it speculatively.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an integrated session run a TUI that draws a full-width status bar or box (omp).
2. While it runs: the bar and the box are intact.
3. Exit it. Observed: in the frozen block the bar wraps and the box-drawing no longer lines up.

## Acceptance Criteria

A frozen block preserves the column alignment of the live output: a line as wide as the terminal is not folded, and horizontal room is reached by scrolling rather than by wrapping. Proven by a test that fails today. Whether a wide glyph still shifts the columns after that is answered with a measurement, and either fixed or recorded as a named remaining gap.

## ВЕРНУЛОСЬ. Переоткрыто 2026-09-05, тем же владельцем и на той же программе

Симптом слово в слово тот, что описан выше: у omp статусная строка и рамка
композера целы, пока программа идёт, и разваливаются в замороженном блоке.

Причина не та, что была: базовое правило, которым этот бид закрыли, на месте и
верно — `.cmd-output { white-space: pre; overflow-x: auto }`. Но ca7ebe46
(2026-08-15, nocx-ex636) добавил ПОВЕРХ него правило по настройке:

    :root[data-output-wrap='on'] .cmd-block[data-block-kind='command']:not([data-wrap]) .cmd-output {
      white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: break-word; overflow-x: visible;
    }

а `terminal.wrapOutput` объявлен `Default: true` (internal/settings/settings.go)
и в output-wrap.ts. То есть действующее поведение обычного командного блока по
умолчанию снова `pre-wrap` — ровно то, что этот бид запрещал.

## Тест не мог этого увидеть, и это отдельный дефект

frontend/src/scrollback/cmd-output-wrap.test.ts сторожит именно этот регресс, и
он зелёный. Его `shippedValue` отбирает правила фильтром
`/^\.[\w-]+$/.test(s)` — то есть ТОЛЬКО голые селекторы по классу. Составной
селектор с `:root[data-output-wrap='on']` не рассматривается вовсе. Тест
утверждает про `.cmd-output` то, что в каскаде перебивается, и проходит, пока
поставляемое поведение противоположно.

Это ровно та форма, ради которой написано правило AGENTS.md про зелёный набор
над сломанным продуктом: тест проверяет написанное, а не то, что видит человек.

## Что измерено сегодня, прежде чем это нашлось

Захват снят ИЗ САМОЙ панели (`stty size` → 33 152; `script -qec omp`,
151 690 байт) и проигран при 152x33:

- сетка xterm — рамка целая, верхняя граница ровно 152 ячейки, кончается `╮`;
- `serializeRangeText` того же диапазона совпадает с сеткой посимвольно;
- tmux при 152x33 из того же захвата даёт ту же сетку.

Содержимое верно на всём пути: PTY → парсер → сериализация. Ломается показ.
(Осторожно: строка `╰─ …пробелы… ─╯` — НОРМАЛЬНАЯ пустая строка ввода omp,
tmux рисует так же; я принял её за поломку и ошибся.)

## Чинить не возвратом дефолта

Дефолт `true` поставлен осознанно (ex636), и просто перевернуть его — значит
переоткрыть то, что чинил ex636. Направление, которое сохраняет оба: переносить
по ШИРИНЕ СЕТКИ, а не по текущей ширине блока. `rec.captured.cols` уже
записывается при заморозке, а `--term-cell-width` уже публикуется
(scrollback/cell-metric.ts). Тогда длинная обычная строка по-прежнему
переносится — ровно там, где её переносил терминал, — а рамка TUI остаётся
целой, потому что она в сетку помещалась.

И тест обязан читать каскад целиком, включая составные селекторы, иначе он
снова не заметит.

## Решающая проверка (одно действие, без Mac)

Выключить «Wrap long output lines» (Настройки → Interface) или у сломанного
блока ⋮ → перенос выключить. Если рамка становится целой — причина эта.
close_reason:
Закрыто той же работой, что и nocx-ec18, и по его же приёмке: «строка шириной в терминал не складывается, а горизонтальная ширина достигается прокруткой, а не переносом».

Доказано браузерным тестом e2e/frozen-line-grid.spec.ts «a full-width row does not fold while output wrapping is on»: строка ровно во всю ширину терминала со значками на конце даёт ОДИН визуальный фрагмент при явно выставленном data-output-wrap='on' — то есть при боевом значении настройки, а не при выключенной. Счёт идёт по уникальным top из Range.getClientRects() с допуском в полстроки: округление высоты пропустило бы рост меньше половины строки.

Причина, по которой этот бид возвращался дважды, устранена в корне, а не заглушена: складывалась строка не потому, что перенос включён, а потому что в DOM она была ШИРЕ своих 152 ячеек. Верно разложенной строке сворачиваться нечего — замечание владельца из тела бида, оказавшееся точным. Дефолт terminal.wrapOutput не тронут, правило :root[data-output-wrap='on'] на месте, ex636 не переоткрыт.

Второй дефект, названный в теле — что cmd-output-wrap.test.ts не видел составных селекторов и потому молчал, — тоже исправлен: shippedValue расширен до модели элемента с классами И атрибутами, иначе новые правила .term-cell[data-cols='2'] он бы снова не проверил.

Замер про широкий глиф, который тело бида требовало сделать прежде правок («MEASURE whether it is real before changing anything»), сделан: инструмент nocx-4n6sj, четыре виновника с числами, 8.649px на строке. Спекулятивно ничего не чинилось.

title: A frozen block loses the colours the live output had
description:
Reported by the owner with paired screenshots, 2026-08-09 (codex and omp, before and after exit).

While the program runs its output is coloured — codex's update box and its links, omp's gradient logo, its blue section headings. The moment the block freezes, the same content renders monochrome: the links lose their blue, the box borders and headings go plain, omp's gradient logo becomes one flat pale colour.

Ordinary palette colour appears to survive: an "ls" block still shows its blue directory names. So this is not "the serializer drops all colour" — it is narrower, and the difference is worth establishing before touching anything. Both programs that lose it use 24-bit RGB (mode 2) and attributes like dim/italic; "ls" uses the 16-colour palette.

Start at frontend/src/scrollback/serializer.ts — its header comment claims it maps "256-color + RGB + attributes", and the relevant code is paletteToRGB plus the mode-1/mode-2 branches around lines 114-143 and the cell read at ~201. Establish by measurement which colour modes actually reach the emitted span and which do not; a fixture cell per mode is cheaper than reading the code twice.

Consequence: the block ledger is supposed to be the durable record of what a command printed. A record that silently drops the colouring is a worse record than the terminal it replaced, and it is the part of the product a user reads afterwards.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an integrated session run a program that uses 24-bit colour (codex or omp).
2. While it runs: output is coloured.
3. Exit it. Observed: the frozen block renders the same text without its colours.

## Acceptance Criteria

A frozen block preserves the colours the live output had, for the palette, 256-colour and 24-bit RGB modes alike, plus the attributes the serializer claims to carry. Proven by a test per colour mode that fails today for the modes that are broken, and a paired assertion that the modes which already worked still do.
close_reason: Measured against a real xterm 5.5.0 buffer: getFgColorMode() returns raw attribute bits (0x01000000/0x02000000/0x03000000), which the serializer compared against 1 and 2 — matching nothing, so EVERY coloured cell froze as default, not just RGB. RGB was additionally unpacked with R and B swapped. Modes normalised in one place, dim carried, fixture test per mode pinning what a real buffer returns. The 'palette survives' reading taken from a screenshot was wrong and is recorded as such.

title: The echoed command line is still shown while the command runs — the outputStart fix applies only at freeze
description:
Follow-up to nocx-4yhi, reported by the owner with screenshots 2026-08-09 after that fix landed.

The frozen block is now correct: 'codex' appears once, in the header, and the body starts with the program's own output. But WHILE the command runs the body still begins with the echoed 'codex' line, so the duplication the user complains about is exactly as visible as before — it just goes away when the command ends.

Cause: nocx-4yhi gave BlockRecord an outputStart and serializeRange honours it, and serialization happens only at freeze. The live region is not serialized — it is the xterm grid itself, and the grid still holds the echoed line at the block's creation row. So the running block shows one row more than the frozen one will.

This is the same shape as nocx-m87n's remaining half: what the live region SHOWS and what the block will CONTAIN are decided in two different places, and they now disagree by exactly one row.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an integrated session submit 'codex' (or any command) from nocx's editor.
2. While it runs, look at the running block: header says 'codex', first body line says 'codex'.
3. Let it exit: the frozen block shows the command once, correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

The running block shows the same rows the frozen block will contain — the echoed command line is not displayed inside the live region. Asserted by a test that fails today. The block must still be created before the bytes are written (ADR-0024 §5, §7 attachment), and nocx-m87n's clearViewport guards and nocx-zn4d's cap agreement stay asserted.
close_reason: The live region now shifts the grid by outputStart - viewportTopLine, so the echoed command line leaves the running block the same way it leaves the frozen one. The block is still created before the bytes; the m87n clear guards and the zn4d cap agreement stay asserted.

title: The echoed command line is inside the block body as well as in its header
description:
Reported by the owner with a screenshot, 2026-08-09, on shady2k/fix-omp-hide: running 'ls' produces a block whose header reads 'ls' and whose body reads 'ls' followed by the output. Same for 'pwd'. The command appears twice.

Cause: terminal-content.ts:775 opens the block at the app-owned submit with startLine = renderer.cursorLine(), and that call happens BEFORE write() sends the bytes to the pty. So startLine is the prompt line, and the shell's echo of the command the user typed falls inside the block's serialized range (blocks.ts serializeRange from rec.startLine).

Before ADR-0024 the block started at the shell's OSC 133 C, which the shell emits AFTER echoing the command line, so the echo was naturally excluded. The epic stopped consuming C (it is render-only now, decision 1) and the start line moved to the renderer's own cursor position at submit time — one row too early.

The ordering at that call site is deliberate and must be preserved: the comment explains the block opens before any bytes so the published running fact always finds a block to bind to (ADR-0024 §5, §7). So the fix is not 'open the block later' — it is that the block's OUTPUT range must begin after the echoed line, whatever the block's own creation time.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an integrated session type 'ls' in nocx's editor and submit.
2. Observed: the frozen block's header says 'ls' and the first line of its body is also 'ls'.
3. Expected: the command appears once, in the header; the body is the command's output.

## Acceptance Criteria

A submitted command's frozen block contains its output and not its own echoed command line, asserted by a test that fails today, with the block still opening before the bytes are written so the running fact binds to it (that ordering has its own existing coverage — do not break it). Behaviour for a shell-originated attempt (typed at the shell while keys are raw) is decided and covered too.
close_reason: The block's creation line and its output range are now two different things: startLine is what the running fact binds to, outputStart is where serialization begins. The app-owned submit passes startLine+1 because it opens the block before the bytes and the shell's echo lands on the creation line; a shell-originated block opens after its own echo and keeps the default. The pre-ADR-0024 code got this free from OSC 133 C, which the epic stopped consuming.

title: Provide a real dash for shellintegration full suite
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `PATH=/tmp/nocx-dash-harness:$PATH LC_ALL=C go test ./...` on this workstation.
2. Observe shellintegration failures in dash scenarios because `/tmp/nocx-dash-harness/dash` is bash, not dash.

The full Go suite cannot pass here because no genuine dash executable is installed. Shellintegration tests enumerate dash and fail when a bash symlink is used as a substitute; the implementation is not the cause. CI/container must provide dash or the suite must be run in an image that includes it.
acceptance_criteria: PATH contains a genuine dash implementation and go test ./... passes without a shell shim.

title: Finish structured backup restore port
description: Complete the structured Backup & Restore port from PR #61 on current main. Preserve current transport and profile APIs, remove obsolete export paths, and finish verification blockers without changing unrelated product behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The current worktree builds; backup.create, backup.preview, backup.restore and backup.saveToFile use the current registry and real WebSocket; contracts and generated types pass; backup e2e passes; remaining full-gate blockers are fixed or recorded as separate beads; the change is committed with this bead ID.
close_reason: Port committed as d196ebe; backup real-socket acceptance, contracts, generated types, frontend suite, and backup e2e all pass. Full go test remains blocked only by missing genuine dash, tracked in nocx-wxgf.

title: A tall inline TUI cannot be scrolled to its bottom — the live region clips what the grid still holds
description:
Reported by the owner with a screenshot, 2026-08-09: 'omp' running in an integrated session, block header live at 17s. The pane shows omp's banner and the start of the conversation, and the bottom of the program — including its composer, the part a user must reach to type — cannot be scrolled to.

Where to start: ScrollbackController.setLiveHeight (frontend/src/scrollback/controller.ts:229). It caps the live region at 'scrollbackArea.clientHeight minus the running block's header' and sets that as an INLINE height on the live container. When the program's grid is taller than that cap, the rows past it are still in the terminal's viewport but outside the box that displays it, and nothing scrolls the box — so those rows are unreachable rather than merely off-screen. The auto-scroll that exists (_scrollToBottom) runs only when the region CHANGED SIZE and only while _following is true, so a program that repaints in place at its capped height never triggers it.

Related history worth reading before changing anything: nocx-6w4z made the live region grow to the scroller precisely so that programs which repaint a whole screen WITHOUT the alternate buffer (top, claude, any TUI that keeps your scrollback on purpose) stopped being drawn into 140 pixels. This is the same family of defect one step along, so the fix must not reintroduce that one — the comments in setLiveHeight and enterFullscreen state what each rule buys.

Consequence: an inline TUI taller than the pane is unusable in an integrated session, because the place you type is the place you cannot see. alt-screen programs are unaffected (enterFullscreen owns that path).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an integrated session run 'omp' (an inline TUI that repaints without the alternate buffer) in a pane shorter than its output.
2. Observed: the bottom of the program, including its input composer, cannot be brought into view by scrolling.
3. Expected: everything the program draws is reachable — either the region grows, or the pane scrolls to it.

## Acceptance Criteria

A program whose inline output is taller than the pane can be scrolled to its last drawn row while it is still running, and the case is covered by a test that fails today. The nocx-6w4z behaviour it must not regress — a whole-screen repaint without the alternate buffer is not squeezed into a fixed height, and 'top' repainting in place does not move the scroll — stays asserted.
close_reason: Two surfaces owned one number: setLiveHeight clamps the live box to the scroller less the running block's header, while the grid was fitted to the bare scroller — 276 against 300 on the reported pane, so the last rows were drawn outside the clipping container and nothing scrolled them. Both now fit to a single named runningLiveCap; the nocx-6w4z growth and no-yank behaviours stay asserted. Red-first test, vitest 2497 green.

title: The live region shows the whole viewport, so a running block replays commands already frozen above it
description:
Reported by the owner with screenshots, 2026-08-09, on shady2k/fix-omp-hide. First diagnosis (block model merges two attempts) was WRONG and is recorded here so nobody repeats it: a worker wrote the exact acceptance test for it — two shell-originated attempts, no teardown, every fence ordering — and it passes against today's code. The attempt model is correct.

ROOT CAUSE, found from a second set of screenshots (two ordinary commands, then codex): the live region shows the WHOLE terminal viewport, not the rows of the running command. renderers/xterm.ts:579 liveContentHeight() measures from viewport row 0 to the last non-empty row, and ScrollbackController.setLiveHeight sizes the live box to that. Nothing offsets the region to the running block's startLine. So every row still in the viewport — including commands already frozen into blocks above — is displayed a second time inside the running block.

It only looks like 'two runs merged' because that is what a fresh session shows: with a few short commands the grid has not scrolled, so everything is still in the viewport. Run enough output and the earlier rows scroll out and the symptom disappears, which is why it never showed up in any test.

Evidence: with 'ls', then 'pwd', then 'codex' running, the live block's body contains ls + its output, pwd + its output, codex, and then codex's banner — while the two frozen blocks above already hold the same ls and pwd rows.

Sibling defect, same screenshots, filed separately: the echoed command line is inside the block body as well as in its header.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a fresh integrated session.
2. Run 'ls', then 'pwd' (short output; the grid must not scroll).
3. Run any longer-lived command, e.g. 'codex'.
4. Observed: the running block's body replays ls, pwd and their output above the new command's own output.

## Acceptance Criteria

The live region displays only the rows belonging to the running command — the rows above its start line are shown once, in their frozen blocks, and never a second time in the live region. Asserted by a test that puts two completed commands and one running command in a viewport that has NOT scrolled, and that fails today. The nocx-6w4z growth behaviour and the nocx-zn4d cap agreement stay asserted.
close_reason: clearViewport existed for exactly this and commit 6cba76fd (the severance, nocx-u7uh.1/.3) deleted all three of its call sites along with the marker paths they lived in. Restored through one guarded helper on all four freeze paths: never while a newer command owns the running slot (its unserialized window sits below), never in fullscreen. The first diagnosis — the block model merging attempts — was disproven by a test that still stands as regression protection.

title: zsh has no nested-domain machinery — sudo/su/ssh from a zsh session stay conventional
description:
nocx-u7uh.11 built the nested child-domain flow on the bash tier only. The zsh script has the lifecycle channel but not the nested flow: zsh has no DEBUG-trap command suppression, so the parent cannot intercept the entering command the way bash does with 'shopt -s extdebug' plus a DEBUG trap returning 1. It needs the accept-line widget instead, plus its own fd/CLOEXEC staging port for the grant and the preserved descriptor.

Consequence: a user whose shell is zsh — the macOS default — gets NO child domain for sudo, su or ssh. The session keeps reporting the parent's identity for a shell that is no longer the parent, which is the exact defect nocx-u7uh.11 existed to remove, narrowed to one tier. The mechanism does not preclude the port; it was simply not built.

nocx.posix is out of scope by design: it has no lifecycle channel at all and is conventional.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run nocx with zsh as the session shell, integrated.
2. Type 'sudo -i' and enter the child shell.
3. Observed: no child domain is established; the lane still names the parent domain, and cwd/host/title keep the parent's values.
4. Expected: the same authenticated child domain the bash tier gets.

## Acceptance Criteria

A zsh parent entering sudo, su or ssh establishes an authenticated child domain, suspends before the child hello, and re-activates only through an authenticated activation — proven on a real pty the way TestBashNestedChildDomain proves the bash tier. The stillborn-child interval is covered too: a failed launch still activates the parent at its next prompt boundary and a late frame from the child that never established is rejected.
close_reason: The zsh tier gets the nested-domain flow on the accept-line widget (zsh's DEBUG trap cannot suppress a command). Two zsh-specific defects found by measurement: zle gives a widget-launched command /dev/null stdin, and zle skips precmd for a line a widget consumed. TestZshNestedChildDomain and TestZshNestedChildStillborn pass on a real pty; script version 25.

title: The recovery fence is parsed by nothing — decision 8's ACK cannot fire
description:
Found by the coordinator while reviewing nocx-u7uh.23. The composite ACK of ADR-0024 decision 8 — the whole point of nocx-u7uh.15's AC3 — cannot fire in production.

frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts registers exactly one OSC 1337 handler, in `_ensureFenceOsc`:

    this.fenceOscDisposable = this.term.parser.registerOscHandler(1337, (data: string) => {
      const parsed = parseRenderFence(data)
      if (parsed && this.term) { ...fan out to this.fenceSubs... }
      return false
    })

`parseRecoveryFence` (same file) is never called from it, and `recoverySubs` — which `onRecoveryFence` pushes into — is never invoked from anywhere.
