New git.log operation on the Repo seam with its own contract and an over-the-socket conformance test. e2e 'a commit made from the panel appears at the top of the Commits list' is green.

Deliberately out and still out: the branch graph, commit selection, opening a commit's diff.

title: Every changed row says how much it changed (+N −N)
description:
Reported by the owner against orca, which puts a green +N and a red -N on every row. nocx shows only a status letter, so 'M' is the same word for a one-character typo and a rewritten file.

Not listed as out of scope in the design's section 4 — it was never considered. That is a gap, not a refusal.

The shape to respect: git status does not carry line counts, so this is git diff --numstat and --cached --numstat, and the counts must arrive as part of the SAME status answer the panel already scopes by epoch (design D17) rather than as a second source the panel joins. One owner per behaviour.
acceptance_criteria:
An e2e watches a user open the Git panel on a repository with a tracked file that gained 3 lines and lost 1, and read '+3 −1' on that file's row without leaving the panel.

Deliberately out: untracked files carry no counts (a numstat per untracked file is one git process per file, and 761 of them is the exact case the D9 cap exists for) — the row shows nothing rather than a wrong or expensive number.
close_reason:
Delivered and merged. Every tracked row carries +N −N from git diff --numstat, riding the SAME status result the panel already scopes by epoch rather than a second source joined in the renderer. Untracked files carry no counts by design — one git process per file, which is what the D9 cap exists for — and absent renders nothing, never +0 −0. e2e '+3 −1 on a changed row, nothing on untracked' is green in the container.

Placement corrected on acceptance: the counts arrived between the status letter and the path, where their fixed width came out of the file name — the part the row exists to show. They sit at the trailing edge now, as in both reference products.

title: Git panel rows wrap: the status row has no flex container
description:
Reported by the owner with a screenshot: every row in the Git panel renders the
status letter and the file icon on one line and the path on the next, and long
paths overflow the panel instead of ellipsising.

Cause: FileStatusRow's three parts (status, type icon, path) carry flex-item
declarations (`flex: 0 0 auto`, `flex: 1 1 auto`) but their parent is
`.ui-collection-row__info`, which is a plain BLOCK — and it must stay one,
because connections.tsx, secrets.tsx and footprint-section.tsx stack a name
over a meta line inside it. So the parts lay out as inline content and wrap.

Introduced by my own acceptance fix on nocx-qo07: the worker wrapped the whole
CollectionRow in a div, which orphaned role=listitem from its role=list, and I
removed the wrapper INSTEAD OF moving it inside the info slot. That inner
wrapper was the flex container.

No gate could see it: jsdom computes no layout, so all ten unit tests stayed
green, and the e2e asserted only that rows are visible and clickable — both
true of a wrapped row.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Git view on a tab standing in a repository with changes.
2. Look at any row in Staged or Unstaged.

Observed: the status letter and the file glyph sit on one line and the path on
the line below it; a long path runs past the panel's right edge.
Expected: one line — letter, glyph, path — with the path ellipsised at the tail.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Playwright assertion, red before the fix and green after, that the status
  letter and the path of a row share a line (their vertical centres agree
  within a line) and that the row does not overflow its list horizontally with
  a deeply nested path.
- `.ui-collection-row__info` is unchanged, so the three surfaces that stack
  blocks inside it are unaffected.
close_reason:
Fixed in 7b6698d. The three parts of a status row had flex-item declarations and no flex parent — the wrapper that made them a row had been removed during acceptance of nocx-qo07 instead of being moved inside the info slot, where it belongs.

The regression test is geometric and lives in the e2e (jsdom computes no layout, so no component test can see this): it reads bounding boxes and was red before the fix because the path's centre sat a full line below the letter's.

Fixing the wrap exposed the ordering defect underneath it — a path ellipsised as one string loses the file name, so files under one deep directory rendered as identical rows. Name first, directory after and dimmed, with the shrink priority absolute rather than weighted.

title: e2e typecheck is red: connection-password.spec.ts uses Page without importing it
description:
## Summary

The frontend CI job's last step, "Typecheck the e2e suite" (`npm run typecheck` at the repo root), fails on main. Playwright transpiles without typechecking, so the suite still runs; only the dedicated typecheck step sees it, and that step is what is red.

`setupVault()` at e2e/connection-password.spec.ts:154 is annotated `page: Page`, but line 25 imports only `{ test as base, expect }` from `@playwright/test`. The sibling spec with the identical shape, e2e/vault.spec.ts:15, imports `type Page` alongside.

## Steps to Reproduce

    npm run typecheck    # repo root, not frontend/

Also reproduced on CI run 31164732414, job `frontend`, step "Typecheck the e2e suite", exit code 2.

- The `frontend` job on CI is green through its final step.

title: Tab-scoped tunnel teardown is racy: closing one tab kills another tab's forward on the same profile
description:
Found while landing the git panel epic (nocx-flff). The git work is NOT the
cause — it is the load that exposes it.

## Steps to Reproduce

In the repo's own test container (the image built by .githooks/containerized-tests.sh),
on a branch where internal/git exists:

    go test -race -count=1 ./internal/git/... ./internal/transport/

Fails 2 runs out of 2:

    --- FAIL: TestTunnelTabTeardown_DoesNotStopOtherTabsForward
        ws_tunnel_test.go:320: dial forwarded address 127.0.0.1:PORT:
            connect: connection refused

Line 320 is the FINAL roundTrip(t, addrB): tab B's forward worked, tab A's
connection was then closed, and afterwards B's listener was gone. That is
exactly the invariant the test exists to defend.

## What was measured, so nobody re-derives it

- baseline (no internal/git), full `go test -race ./...` in the container: GREEN
- with internal/git, full ./... in the container: RED, twice, on this test
- with internal/git, ./internal/transport/ alone: green, 5+ runs
- with internal/git, transport + git/spawn only: green
- with internal/git, transport + git/local only: green
- with internal/git, transport + all THREE git packages: RED, twice
- baseline, transport + shellintegration (another heavy process-spawning
  package): green
- the tunnel test alone under artificial CPU load on baseline: green, 3 runs

So it is neither CPU load nor one particular package: it is the degree of
concurrent package execution. The git work adds three packages to the parallel
set and widens a window that already existed.

## Where to look

unregisterConn -> stopOwnerTunnels (internal/transport/ws.go:3009). The design
is tab-scoped and the comment at ws.go:3007 says each forward holds its OWN
pooled reference, so stopping one tab's forwards never touches another tab's on
the same shared connection. Under concurrency B's forward is stopped anyway.
Both tunnels in the test use profileId ssh:p1:1 — they share one connection,
which is precisely the case the invariant is about.

## Why it matters beyond the gate

If teardown can reach another tab's forward, a user closing one tab drops a
port forward another tab is actively using. The test is right; the product is
racing.
acceptance_criteria: go test -race ./internal/git/... ./internal/transport/ in the repo's test container passes repeatedly, and TestTunnelTabTeardown_DoesNotStopOtherTabsForward holds under concurrent package load rather than only when transport runs alone.
close_reason: Not a product bug: the tab-scoped teardown invariant holds. The test's connB became garbage mid-test, Go's netFD finalizer closed its socket, and the server correctly tore down B's forward as a disconnected tab — which is why only the memory-churning git packages reproduced it. Test-only fix: three tunnel tests hold their connections via defer-close. Container repro 5/5 green; 300x host stress green where pre-fix was 68/300 red.

title: A known_hosts file that does not parse silently disables host-key verification
description:
hostKeyCallbackFor (internal/ssh/ssh_real.go:260) calls knownhosts.New once and captures its error in a closure. When the file does not parse, every subsequent connection takes the 'unknown host key' path instead — the mild first-contact prompt — rather than reporting that the store is unreadable. The error is never logged and never reaches the UI.

So one malformed line turns every host into a first-contact prompt. The user accepts it, believing they are trusting a new host, and connects with no verification at all against a file that still contains the real keys. AGENTS.md: a soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log — this one is not even in a log.

Found while fixing nocx-9224, whose trust write now refuses such a file explicitly (9030eb7). That makes the asymmetry worse, not better: the write says 'this file does not parse, fix line N' while the read says nothing and quietly stops verifying.

## Steps to Reproduce

Put a malformed line in known_hosts, e.g. 'db.example.com ssh-ed25519 not-base64!!'. Connect to any host that IS correctly recorded in the same file. Instead of verifying against its recorded key, nocx presents the unknown-host-key dialog. Nothing in the log or the UI says the file failed to parse.

## Acceptance Criteria

A known_hosts file that knownhosts cannot parse produces a distinct, product-visible outcome that names the file and the offending line — not the unknown-host-key prompt. A test asserts that a host with a valid recorded key does NOT reach the first-contact path when an unrelated line in the file is malformed.

title: main is red: a dead export from the jump-route work fails the pre-commit ratchet
description:
1786a52 (nocx-shat) landed HostKeyDecisionEvidence as an exported interface in frontend/src/host-key-dialog.tsx. Nothing outside the file consumes it, and HostKeyDialogProps — the only thing that uses it — is not itself exported, so the export was never wanted.

The dead-exports ratchet in the pre-commit hook counts it as NEW against its baseline, so EVERY commit fails the gate until it is resolved.

## Steps to Reproduce

On a clean checkout of main, with no changes staged, run 'cd frontend && node lint-fixtures/check-dead-exports.mjs'. It reports 'DEAD-EXPORTS RATCHET: 135 violations (137 baselined, shrunk by 2, 1 NEW)' and names src/host-key-dialog.tsx: HostKeyDecisionEvidence. Any 'git commit' fails the same way.

Found while committing nocx-mx27, which the gate blocked.

## Acceptance Criteria

The pre-commit hook passes on a clean checkout of main. The symbol is either consumed or not exported — the baseline is not widened to accept it.
close_reason: Dropped the export keyword; ratchet back to 134, all baselined. 7d7e8b5

title: e2e: 29 failures on CI need triage by first error, not by final timeout
description:
CI run 31127401140: e2e shards 1/2/3 fail 10/11/6 (64/54/62 passed) and e2e-headless
fails 2 of 20. 29 failures is not 29 defects — several are setup failures whose whole
spec then cascades.

Observed shapes, unclassified until traces are read:

- `browserContext.grantPermissions: Unknown permission: clipboard-write` — a setup
  failure on an engine that does not support the permission (WebKit). Everything after
  it in that file is cascade, not evidence.
- `locator.click` timeouts on `.ui-tree-row__name` / `bigdir` (e2e file tree). Not
  automatically environmental — the node may be absent, covered, outside the scroll
  owner, or the tree may not have loaded. Arrived with the same b07652e that nocx-koki
  covers, so a real regression is plausible.
- `expect(page.locator('.cm-form')).toBeAttached()` — element not found.
- `expect(sameNode).toBe(true)` — DOM identity/remount. The most defect-shaped of the
  set if the invariant is user-visible (focus/selection survival).

AGENTS.md is binding on the method here: the container's failure set is not CI's, and
CI is the source of truth. Do not "fix" a spec that is only red on Linux WebKit.

## Steps to Reproduce

    gh run view 31127401140 --log-failed

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every one of the 29 failures is attributed to either (a) a product regression with a
  bead, (b) a test/infrastructure defect with a bead, or (c) a known environment
  divergence recorded with the reason it is not a product defect.
- The count of independent root causes is stated, not the count of red tests.
- No spec is changed on container evidence alone.
notes:
2026-08-11 triage. The 14 container failures are NOT 14 defects and the count
has not moved, but the composition has and one cause is now closed.

CLOSED — the sshd fixture denied remote forwarding. cmd/e2e-sshd handed every
global request to gossh.DiscardRequests, so `tcpip-forward` was refused and
every SSH session came up conventional ("lifecycle channel refused; session
stays conventional"). Fixed in 968fd52; e2e/shell-mode.spec.ts's SSH journey
goes from a 10s timeout on a hidden editor to 1.6s green, verified isolated and
in the full suite. That is 2 of the 14 (both browsers).

NEW in the same run, unattributed — do not assume these are mine, and do not
assume they are not:
  [chromium] git-panel.spec.ts:699   panel says "No repository to show / Focus a
                                     terminal tab", i.e. no focused terminal tab
                                     at all, where it expected the remote notice
  [chromium] enhanced-input.spec.ts:10
Both chromium-only, where the surviving cluster fails on both engines — which is
the shape of a flake, but that is a reading and not a measurement.

STILL RED, both engines, cause unknown (this is the real remaining work):
  completion.spec.ts:139        enhanced-input.spec.ts:34
  focus-after-tab-switch.spec.ts:29   history-persistence.spec.ts:119
  multi-tab-input.spec.ts:12    nocxify-journey.spec.ts:338
None of these is an SSH spec except nocxify-journey, so the fixture was not
their cause. They share a shape worth starting from: each needs the enhanced
input editor to own the keyboard, which needs the shell to reach prompt_ready.

Method note that paid for itself: the backend log at
.e2e/home/.local/share/nocx-dev/nocx.log named the fixture defect in one line
after the Playwright output had spent 13 minutes describing a hidden editor.
Read it first next time.
2026-08-11, second triage. The count is answered and the causes are named.
The container reproduces CI EXACTLY once it is given the runner's capacity —
which is the finding under all the others.

MEASUREMENT. Local container at NOCX_E2E_CPUS=4: 13 failed / 261 passed.
CI run 31478263946 (same tree): 12 failed / 262 passed. The deterministic
core is IDENTICAL — five specs, both engines:
  completion.spec.ts:139   enhanced-input.spec.ts:34
  focus-after-tab-switch.spec.ts:29   multi-tab-input.spec.ts:12
  nocxify-journey.spec.ts:338
They differ only on the flaky tail (history-persistence:119 chromium,
enhanced-input:10, tabby-import:119). So 'the container's failure set is not
CI's' was never about the container — it was about CORE COUNT. An uncapped
run on a many-core Mac is a different machine from ubuntu-latest's 4 vCPU,
and NOCX_E2E_CPUS was opt-in, so nobody was reproducing CI unless they knew
to reach for it. It is now the default (0 opts out); scripts/ci-linux.sh
already defaulted its own cap to 4.

ONE ROOT CAUSE, four specs. Every one of them asserts a snapshot of state
that the product changes ON ITS OWN, in a window whose width is machine
speed:

  multi-tab-input:12, focus-after-tab-switch:29 — capture tab 2's title
  right after promptReady, assert 2s later that it is unchanged. A fresh
  tab's title starts '~' and becomes its cwd when the shell's OSC 7 lands,
  which is AFTER promptReady. Fast machine: OSC 7 beats the capture, strings
  match. 4 vCPU: it does not. Fixed by asserting 'never shows the marker'
  instead, ordered after tab 1's title HAS become the marker so the check is
  not vacuous. Verified green on both engines.

  completion:37, :73, :139 — all three need the OSC 636 command snapshot.
  nocx.bash can only EMIT it from a prompt (a shell idle in readline runs no
  traps — nocx-z9s9.16), the first prompt grants 250ms, and the
  __nocx_snapshot_waiting latch is set ONCE, so every later delivery needs a
  LATER PROMPT. :139 polled Tab for 45s waiting for it — Tab produces no
  prompt, so it waited for an event its own polling excluded. Fixed with a
  commandSnapshotReady() helper that produces prompts (a no-op 'true') until
  printf is actually offered, then asserts the real property.

  enhanced-input:34 — waited for a blur event as proof the PTY handled
  Ctrl-C. cancel() sends \x03 and clears the draft locally; nothing promises
  a hide/blur cycle around the new prompt. Replaced with the contract: the
  line is empty, a command typed afterwards runs, and the abandoned draft
  never ran (the last is new — the blur trick never asserted it).

STILL OPEN: nocxify-journey:338, history-persistence:119.

METHOD NOTE. 250ms and 'the title will not change in 2s' are both claims
about how fast the machine is, written on a machine where they were true.
That is the same class as nocx-0odm/nocx-dw5o/nocx-sw4p — a gate encoding
the host it was written on — and it is now four more instances.
Final state of this triage. Full container suite at NOCX_E2E_CPUS=4:
BEFORE 13 failed / 261 passed (14.3m) → AFTER 4 failed / 270 passed (11.3m).
Four failures, two specs, both engines.

FIXED, verified in the full suite:
  multi-tab-input:12, focus-after-tab-switch:29  — tab-title snapshot race
  completion:37, :73, :139                       — the OSC 636 nonce defect
  enhanced-input:10, history-persistence:119, tabby-import:119 — were flaky,
                                                   green with the above

THE PRODUCT DEFECT, and the one worth carrying forward. completion could
never work in a local bash session, and the cause was not timing. The
launcher rcfile rewinds and re-sources the script on purpose — nocx.bash's
own comment calls it EVERY local enhanced session — and the second pass
minted a fresh nonce and announced a SECOND OSC 636 hello.
command-snapshot.ts keeps the FIRST by design (a re-hello is the
re-anchoring its forgery defence exists to prevent), so the snapshot,
emitted later under the second nonce, failed the match and was discarded and
the store stayed 'unavailable' for the life of the session. Both frames were
well-formed; they merely disagreed, which is why every check that read one
frame at a time stayed green. Script v33 mints the nonce, the staging file
and the hello once per shell — the same treatment __nocx_snapshot_wait_ms
already got in v20 for the same re-source, applied to the rest of the block.
Guarded by TestBashSnapshotSurvivesTheSecondSource, which reproduces the
rcfile's rewind and fails without the fix with the production symptom.

Found by instrumentation, not by reading: the renderer logged the refusal as
{code:-32603} for five distinct backend rules and the backend logged nothing
at all. Both now name the rule. That is what turned 'cause unknown' into a
cause, and it is the reusable part.

STILL RED, split out as nocx-xplc: enhanced-input:34 and
nocxify-journey:338. Ctrl-C at an enhanced prompt stops the shell answering
— not a race (a 20s retry lands nothing) and NOT a regression of this branch
(verified against origin/main's v28 script in the container).

This bead's own acceptance is met: every failure is attributed, and the
count of independent causes is three, not twenty-nine.

title: internal/filesystem tests fail on macOS: three OS-semantics assumptions
description:
CI run 31127401140 (backend, macos-latest) fails 13 tests in internal/filesystem/local
and .../sftp while backend-linux is green. Three independent macOS-only causes, all
invisible to the Linux container the pre-commit gate runs Go tests in.

1. Symlinked TMPDIR. /var is a symlink to /private/var, so Canonical (local.go:189,
   :368, :445 — the filesystem.go:111-118 contract) returns /private/var/... while the
   tests build `want` lexically from t.TempDir(). 11 failures. The contract is right,
   the tests are wrong: dropping EvalSymlinks would give one file two identities.

2. Case-insensitive APFS. TestListOrdinaryDirectory (sftp_test.go:140-144) creates
   both b.txt and B.txt; on APFS the second overwrites the first, so four files exist,
   not five. The test asserts case-sensitive byte-order sorting, which real files
   cannot express on a case-insensitive filesystem.

3. The SFTP fake violates the contract it models. fsfake_test.go:95-101 returns the raw
   root for RealPath(".") but EvalSymlinks for every other path, so its two halves
   disagree on macOS. Root() canonicalises the override (sftp.go:187) while newRoot
   reads home from RealPath(".") (sftp.go:214); HasPrefix in displayOf (sftp.go:227)
   misses and Display loses ~/project. Production code is correct.

## Steps to Reproduce

On macOS (not in the Linux container):

    go test -count=1 ./internal/filesystem/...

13 failures, identical to CI run 31127401140. Green in the container and on CI's
backend-linux job, which is why the local gate never reported it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `go test -count=1 ./internal/filesystem/...` passes on macOS and on Linux.
- Canonical expectations are derived with filepath.EvalSymlinks, not by string-patching
  /private, and Entry.Path assertions still assert the lexical parent (local_test.go:180).
- The sorting assertion no longer depends on two filenames differing only in case.
- fakeFS.RealPath(".") and fakeFS.RealPath(abs) agree on canonicalisation.
- CI job `backend` (macos-latest) is green on the commit that closes this.
close_reason: Closed
