- groups.create refused every call the renderer could make. JSONStore.CreateGroup requires a non-empty id and the handler minted none, so it answered "group ID is required". profiles.create had minted ids since nocx-uxs5.10; groups.create had simply never been called by a UI. All nine backend tests for it pass an explicit id, which is why nothing caught it.
- The renderer was naming the SSH config file in its own UI text ("~/.ssh/config"). The real path is composed in the composition root from $HOME. sshConfig.path reports it, deliberately cheap — no stat, no `ssh -G` — so a dialog may ask merely to draw itself.

Also here: currentUser() read $USER/$LOGNAME rather than the passwd database, and fell back to the literal string "root" when both were empty. OpenSSH takes the login name from getpwuid(getuid()), and ssh_config(5) documents the User default as "the name of the user running ssh". An app launched from Finder can have no $USER at all, so the fallback was reachable — and root is the worst available guess: the most privileged account, the one an intrusion-detection rule watches first.

## Acceptance Criteria

groups.create mints an id when the renderer sends none, with a test that passes an empty id. sshConfig.path returns the path the resolver actually reads. currentUser() resolves through os/user and never returns root by default.

title: Kit: dialogs get a body, a definite size and a section rail
description:
The dialog work behind the connection-manager pass, all of it in the kit so the next surface inherits it.

- Dialog had no body: children were dropped straight into a gapless flex panel, so a dialog whose body was several Fields had its label sitting on the control above it. Every caller that looked right did so by remembering to wrap its content in a Section. Now `.nocx-dialog__body` owns the rhythm and the scroll — content taller than the panel used to be clipped by `overflow: hidden` and unreachable.
- Dialog had a max-width on a `<dialog>`, which is `width: fit-content`, so the panel shrank to whatever the body needed and changed width when the body changed. `size` now names a definite width.
- Tabs (new): a vertical section rail with the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, rows drawn as ghost Buttons so "the current choice in a list" has one look. Every section renders into one grid cell, so the box is the size of the largest and switching cannot resize it — measured rather than guessed.
- SegmentedControl (new): the same radiogroup ARIA as Radio in one row, for few and short options. Five auth radios were five rows.
- Toast was invisible whenever a modal dialog was open: showModal() puts the dialog in the browser's top layer, above every z-index in the normal layer. The host now renders inside the topmost overlay.
- Dialog had no initial-focus policy despite its own doc claiming one. A scrolling body is focusable, so opening a form put the focus ring around the whole body.
- Dialog takes an opt-in `onSubmit`, so Enter in a single-line field confirms.
- Nine icons added (Lucide, ISC).

## Acceptance Criteria

The kit README records the size rule and the dialog-body type rule. Every record editor uses one dialog size. A toast raised from an open dialog is visible. Opening a dialog focuses a control, not a scroll container.

title: Connection manager: groups can be created, imported and acted on
description:
The connection manager shipped without a way to create a group, and several defects sat behind that one.

Found by the user clicking through the surface on 2026-07-29, none of it by any gate.

- No "New group" button anywhere. The group EDITOR existed in full — impact preview, danger confirmation, delete — reachable only from a group header that only appeared once a group already existed.
- An empty group rendered as nothing at all, so a created group looked like a failed button and could not be reached to be renamed or deleted.
- The toolbar had a 320px filter and one button with the rest of the bar empty.
- Import lived only on the Export / Backup / Import page; the user wants connection import on this surface.
- Row actions were words where a glyph is conventional; the surface was already inconsistent with itself (plug icon for Connect, words for Test and Edit).
- The group name was required but the failure was reported by a Toast, which is invisible while a modal dialog is open.
- The delete confirmation never named the group it was about to destroy, and focused its own destructive button.

## Acceptance Criteria

A group can be created from the surface and appears in the list while empty. The import dialog covers ~/.ssh/config, Tabby and a configuration export. Row actions use icons where a glyph is conventional. Required-field failures appear under the field. The delete confirmation names the group and does not focus the destructive action.

title: Every action has a keyboard path, and a gate keeps it that way
description:
## Success Criteria

See acceptance.

## Why this is not the hotkeys bead

nocx-8yg.7 ("Keybindings / hotkeys", description: "Configurable.") and nocx-8yg.10 (command palette) are about SPEED and DISCOVERY for someone who already can reach an action. This epic is about whether the action can be reached at all. The three are independent: a product can have configurable hotkeys and still contain a button no keyboard can press.

It is also not a feature that is done once. Keyboard reachability breaks every time somebody writes a div with an onClick, which is why the deliverable is a gate plus a sweep, not a screen.

Both of those beads live under nocx-8yg, which is blocked on nocx-2gf because app hotkeys and the editor keymap contend for the same chords. This epic has no such contention: it adds no chord.

## What is already known

The repo has already met this defect and documented it in place rather than fixing it generally. connections.tsx carries a comment on the connection row explaining that the row is deliberately NOT clickable, because "a div with an onClick and no role, tabindex or key handler is unreachable by keyboard and invisible to a screen reader, and both custom lint rules miss it: no-raw-controls only sees real control tags, and no-role-impersonation only fires on a role that is present."

That is the gap, stated by a past session and left open: the existing rules see elements that ARE controls, and cannot see elements that merely BEHAVE as controls.

Two concrete findings from 2026-07-29 that belong to this epic's sweep:

- The group delete confirmation focused its destructive button, because showModal() focuses the first focusable descendant and the body was text. Fixed by autofocus on Cancel, but nothing prevents the next confirmation from doing it again.
- The dialog body became a scroll container and therefore focusable, so opening a form put the focus ring around the whole body instead of the first field. Fixed by an initial-focus policy in Dialog. Both were found by a user with macOS full keyboard access on, not by any gate.
acceptance_criteria: A lint rule fails the build on an element that behaves as a control without being one: an onClick handler on a non-interactive tag with no role, no tabindex and no key handler. A sweep brings existing surfaces up to it. Dialog has a stated initial-focus policy and a test for it, including that a destructive confirmation does not focus its destructive action. DONE WHEN: the rule is in the gate, green, and the sweep is closed. OUT OF SCOPE: configurable key bindings (nocx-8yg.7) and the command palette (nocx-8yg.10) — those are speed and discovery, this is reachability.

title: NOCX_WS_ADDR is accepted and ignored, so the dev stand moves ports every run
description:
app.New accepts WithWSAddr (app.go:49), stores it in optionSet.wsAddr, and never passes it anywhere. The transport already has WithListenAddr (ws_auth.go:182) and defaults to 127.0.0.1:0 (ws.go:256), so the option was accepted and discarded and the listener always took an ephemeral port.

scripts/dev-web.sh pins WS_PORT=9880 on purpose, checks the port is free, refuses to start if it is not, and then hands the backend NOCX_WS_ADDR. The backend ignored it, so the script read the real port back off stdout and carried on - which is why nobody noticed. The stand worked; the port merely moved on every run.

The cost lands on the SSH forward the stand exists for: the printed "ssh -L <port>:127.0.0.1:<port>" changed each restart, and an already-open tab kept talking to a port that no longer existed. The symptom is "the backend stopped responding", which points nowhere near the cause.

## Steps to Reproduce

NOCX_WS_ADDR=127.0.0.1:9880 ./cmd/devharness, then ss -ltnp: the listener is on a random high port, not 9880.

## Acceptance Criteria

app.New forwards wsAddr to transport.WithListenAddr, with a test that New with WithWSAddr listens on exactly that address. Fixed by the same commit; the bead exists so the commit can name it and so the missing test is on record.

title: Group defaults reject the auth field the merge actually applies
description:
profile.go:266-277 lists the allowed keys for a group's Defaults, and "auth" is not among them - yet SparseSSHOptions.Auth is a real inheritable field with json tag "auth" (profile.go:244), and the merge applies it (profile.go:588-591). UnmarshalJSON records it as unknown (profile.go:282-300), so Defaults.Validate() (profile.go:338-346) rejects it.

Every write path that calls Validate is affected: CreateGroup (store.go:263), UpdateGroup (store.go:295), ApplyGroups (store.go:405), SaveGroup (service.go:108), AtomicImport (service.go:241).

## Steps to Reproduce

Open a group's editor, set the Auth mode default, save. The write fails with "unknown keys in defaults: auth".

## Acceptance Criteria

"auth" is in allowedFields, with a test that a group carrying an auth default round-trips through create, update and apply. While there, a test that asserts the allow-list and the struct's json tags agree, so the next added field cannot drift the same way.
close_reason: Closed

title: Unvalidated host becomes an ssh -G positional argument
description:
open with kind ssh passes params.Host straight to ResolveConfig (ws.go:759), which builds argv as exec.CommandContext(ctx, sshPath, "-F", configPath, "-G", host) (ssh_resolver.go:232,241). The host is a positional argument with no "--" terminator and no check for a leading dash, and later flags win over earlier ones.

No shell is involved and -G does not connect, so this is argument injection into a fixed binary rather than command execution. It is still an unintended read/write primitive against the ssh client.

## Steps to Reproduce

Call open with host set to a string beginning with a dash that ssh reads as an option - for example one that re-points the config file, overriding the -F the app itself passed.

## Acceptance Criteria

The argv carries "--" before the host, or the host is rejected when it begins with a dash, with a test. Profile Host on profiles.create gets the same treatment: it is equally unchecked and reaches the dialer.
close_reason: Review fix: stored-profile resolution now rejects option-like hosts even without an ssh-config resolver, before any oracle or dial; added domain sink regression.

title: rollout.run has no upper bound on concurrency or target count
description:
ws_rollout.go:55-62 checks only that credentialId, versionId and targetIds are non-empty. runner.go:127-132 gives batchSize, globalConcurrency and bastionConcurrency a lower bound only - "if <= 0 { default }" - and nothing bounds them above or bounds len(targetIds). The handler runs on context.Background() (ws_rollout.go:69) with no deadline.

## Steps to Reproduce

Call rollout.run with ten thousand target ids and globalConcurrency 100000. The runner opens outbound SSH handshakes as fast as the OS allows, against the whole fleet, with no deadline and no way to stop it.

## Acceptance Criteria

Upper bounds on batchSize, globalConcurrency and bastionConcurrency, and a cap on len(targetIds), each with a test at the boundary. The run takes a context with a deadline. Note the security framing already recorded for this epic: a burst of authentication attempts across many hosts is indistinguishable from spraying, so the bound is not merely a resource limit.
close_reason: Not a current defect: accepted ADR-0017 section 2 deleted rollout.run, the rollout runner, credential versions, and RolloutPanel. The production tree contains no rollout.run or rollout implementation to bound.

title: No read limit on the WebSocket: one frame allocates whatever it claims
description:
internal/transport/ws.go:562 calls conn.ReadMessage() on a gorilla Conn whose SetReadLimit is never called - grep finds zero occurrences in the repo, so the limit is unlimited. handleControlFrame (ws.go:576-607) then json.Unmarshals the whole buffer, and DecodeFrame (frame.go:107-121) allocates len(data)-18 with no cap of its own, so a binary frame costs a second copy.

profiles.importTabby (ws.go:1875-1881) is the widest mouth: an arbitrary YAML string parsed whole.

## Steps to Reproduce

Send one text frame of a few hundred megabytes on the control plane. The process buffers all of it before any handler runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

SetReadLimit is called once on the connection with a documented value, and a test asserts a frame above it closes the connection rather than allocating. One limit covers every method, which is why this belongs with the dispatch work rather than with any single handler.
close_reason: Already fixed: wsReadLimit is 16 MiB, newWSConn applies it through outbound.NewWebSocket which calls SetReadLimit, and TestControlFrame_AboveReadLimit_ClosesCleanly asserts close code 1009 while a fresh connection remains usable.

title: NeedsReview is documented as a resolver gate but nothing reads it
description:
profile.go:53-54 says "The resolver refuses profiles with this flag set". It does not: grep across internal/ (tests excluded) finds NeedsReview only in profile.go and service.go, and ErrProfileNeedsReview (service.go:18-24) is returned by nothing. connection/resolver.go never reads the field.

That flag is what AtomicImport sets (service.go:229) for exactly the credential-hijack case in the sibling bug, so the safety net for that import is inert.

## Steps to Reproduce

Import a configuration that trips the AtomicImport review path, so the stored profile carries needsReview. Connect it. The resolver builds a config and dials as though nothing were flagged.

Separately: profiles.update (ws.go:1209-1223) accepts the flag from the renderer, so even once the resolver honours it the renderer can switch it off.

## Acceptance Criteria

The resolver returns ErrProfileNeedsReview for a flagged profile, with a test. The flag is backend-owned on the write path the way credentials.create owns secretId, with a test that a renderer-supplied value is ignored.
close_reason: Review fix: removed obsolete NeedsReview from profile and backup wire/persistence, deleted dead errors/service/tests, and added strict-backup regression coverage.

title: Promotion, retirement and revocation are three transitions
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

Spec section 6 states these apart deliberately: "Conflating them would drain transports that
are legitimately still running a pinned previous version."

- **promote candidate** — the candidate becomes current. The previous version stays usable for
  profiles explicitly pinned to it, and NOTHING is drained.
- **retire previous** — the version may no longer be selected for new connections; the user
  chooses whether existing transports on it drain (sections 3.7, 3.8).
- **emergency revoke** — a separate destructive action that closes everything using the
  version now.
- Promotion happens on a declared threshold, not on a feeling. State it.
- A straggler pin is keyed by PROFILE PROVENANCE, not by endpoint. Two profiles can share an
  endpoint; pinning one must not pin the other.
- Each transition is testable in isolation, and the test asserts what does NOT happen —
  promotion draining nothing is the property that breaks silently.
close_reason: Three transitions with threshold below the transport, profile-keyed pins, negative tests for promotion draining nothing. Revision pass required for tests and threshold placement.

title: A rollout is a bounded run, not a loop over hosts
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

Spec section 6. Every constraint below is load-bearing; none is optional.

- A canary selection is probed first. The canary is an EPHEMERAL selection, not a persisted
  set — "if it survived across rollouts it would be a fleet under another name, and section 3.3
  chose one tree."
- Rollout proceeds in bounded batches, with per-endpoint status recorded.
- Concurrency is bounded GLOBALLY and PER BASTION, not per target. One dead bastion must be
  reported once, not as forty independent password failures.
- Every probe forces a fresh transport, bypasses the pool, authenticates and closes without
  launching a shell or running a command.
- A probe sends ONLY the intended candidate method — never the full auth chain. MaxAuthTries
  is finite and burning it is how a rollout locks the fleet out.
- NEVER try several passwords against one host. That triggers lockouts and is
  indistinguishable from password spraying.
- Verify the host key BEFORE probing.
- keyboard-interactive and MFA cannot be bulk-probed. Detect and exclude them with a stated
  reason rather than attempting and failing — they need their own interaction model, which is
  not this bead.
- A rollout can be stopped, and stopping leaves a coherent state that says what was reached.

## Note for whoever takes this

The safety constraints above are the reason this epic was held for a session with the owner
present. Build and unit-test it freely; do NOT run it against real hosts without saying so
first.
close_reason: Rollout runner in internal/rollout, wired at app.go, 13 unit + 7 transport tests. Evidence now feeds the promotion threshold (coordinator closed that seam).

title: A probe result knows what it was a result OF, and expires when that changes
description:
## Why this is its own bead

Spec section 6 is exact about it, and a rollout that trusts a stale probe reports a fleet
healthy that is not:

"a probe result is keyed by endpoint, host-key identity, credential version, effective
username and auth policy, plus a timestamp, and is invalidated by any change to the endpoint,
group chain, ~/.ssh/config, host key or credential."

## What exists

connections.test (nocx-uxs5.3, internal/transport/ws_probe.go) probes one target and returns a
typed outcome — accepted, rejected, unreachable, host-key problem, needs-interactive. It has
no notion of a result that persists or expires.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A probe result record carrying the full key above. Not "host + ok"; every component, because
  each one changing makes the answer wrong in a different way.
- Invalidation on any change to those inputs. A group-chain edit that changes the effective
  username invalidates every result computed under the old one — reuse the effective-profile
  engine to notice, do not re-derive.
- Results are operational evidence, not profile configuration (spec section 6). Specify
  retention, manual clearing, and what import/export does with them — the spec asks for this
  explicitly and it is the kind of thing that gets decided by accident.
- Distinguish a network failure from a rejected password. Report "locked" ONLY when the server
  actually says so: generic SSH errors do not carry that, and guessing it is how a UI tells
  someone their account is locked when it is not.
close_reason:
A probe result carries the full section 6 key — endpoint, host-key fingerprint, credential version, effective username, auth policy and timestamp — with invalidation guards and a documented retention/clearing/export policy. connections.test records every classified outcome through it, the store is constructed and injected at the composition root (app.go:98, :114, :190), and TestConnectionsTest_StoresResult fails if that wiring is removed.

The first pass built all of it and wired none of it: nothing constructed the store and nothing called ProbeConfigWithResult. That was reported honestly, which is why it was a revision rather than a rewrite, but it would have been the fourth instance this session of code unreachable from main() — and the first one this session would have INTRODUCED rather than inherited. The blocker named (host-key fingerprint unavailable through Prober) was solved by widening the narrow transport-declared interface, the pattern app.go already uses twice.

title: A credential can stage a candidate version without disturbing the current one
description:
## What exists

Wave 1 shipped the model: Credential.Versions, CurrentVersionID, CandidateVersionID
(internal/profile/credential.go). CandidateVersionID is documented there as "Unused until wave
8 — carried here so the model exists, not built on". This is wave 8.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A candidate version can be created with its own secret material, without touching the
  current one. Creating it changes nothing about how ordinary connections authenticate.
- The secret goes through the same backend-owned path as any other; the renderer never sees or
  transmits a secret reference (ADR-0011).
- Staging is reversible: a candidate can be discarded before any rollout begins.
- Only one candidate at a time, or state deliberately what several would mean.
- An ordinary connection uses CURRENT. Never candidate, never a fallback between them. Spec
  section 6: "Forbidden: a candidate rejection followed by an invisible retry with the current
  version during an ordinary connection — it hides rollout state and spends extra
  authentication attempts." Test that an ordinary connect with a candidate staged still
  authenticates with current, and that a failure does not silently try the other one.

## Deliberately out

Rollout orchestration, probing, promotion. Those are siblings. This bead is the staging
ground they stand on.
close_reason:
credentials.stagePassword creates a candidate with its own secret and leaves CurrentVersionID untouched; credentials.discardCandidate removes it and its secret, idempotently; one candidate at a time is enforced at the store layer. Secrets go through the existing backend-owned path — the renderer never sees a reference.

The no-silent-fallback invariant holds, and by construction rather than by guard: the resolver publishes exactly one secret reference, from cred.Current() (resolver.go:159-165), and internal/ssh has no knowledge of Versions or Candidate at all, so the dial path cannot reach a second version. TestResolve_UsesCurrentVersionSecret pins it with a credential carrying TWO versions, asserts only current's secret crosses, and asserts the SecretID CHANGES on promotion — because an unchanged one would let the pool reuse the old transport (spec 3.7).

Coordinator note: the brief demanded a separate test that a failed connect does not retry with the other version. That was a wrong instruction — no such mechanism exists to assert the absence of, so the test would have passed trivially and kept passing if the mechanism were later added elsewhere. nocx-383c.3 is where internal/ssh first gains version knowledge, deliberately, and its brief must carry the constraint.

title: Changed lines must be covered, or the gate says so
description:
## Why this ranks above mutation testing

Measured against the 2026-07-29 session, where thirteen defects were found by reading diffs
rather than by any gate:

- Nine were tests that did NOT EXIST. Two of those were large: a 653-line rewrite of the
  connection list with zero tests, and the group editor with zero tests. Both were caught only
  because the coordinator counted `it(` blocks before and after, and both reports quoted a
  passing suite total another wave had produced — true, and misleading.
- One would have been caught by mutation testing (a nil slice where the wire contract required
  an empty array; the assertion `len() == 0` could not tell them apart).
- Three were reachability, which neither tool looks at (nocx-nc4i).

A changed-line coverage gate catches the nine directly and cheaply. Mutation testing (nocx-u4b,
nocx-ckoy.5) is the refinement that comes AFTER coverage exists — it measures whether existing
assertions are strong, which is a question you can only ask once there are assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gate reports coverage for the lines a commit or PR changes, for both Go and TypeScript,
  and fails on new uncovered lines rather than on a whole-repo percentage. A repo-wide number
  moves too slowly to notice a single untested feature landing.
- It runs where it does not cost the commit: the pre-commit hook was brought from 67s to 3-29s
  deliberately (nocx-ro3h) and must not regress. CI on a PR is the natural home; note that CI
  currently runs only on PRs to main and release branches.
- Existing uncovered code is baselined per item, the way ADR-0014 baselines raw-control
  violations: stale entries harmless, growth an error. A global percentage threshold is not
  acceptable — it is the form that gets gamed.
- The failure names the file and lines, so the fix is obvious rather than a hunt.

## The trap to write into the config

Coverage measures execution, not assertion. A test that calls a function and asserts nothing
raises the number. This gate exists to catch ABSENCE, not to certify quality — say so where
the threshold is configured, so the next person does not mistake a green gate for a tested
feature.

title: ssh -G replaces the library as the ssh_config resolver
description:
## What changes

internal/ssh/ssh_config.go resolves aliases through github.com/kevinburke/ssh_config. That
library does not support Match, and a Match block anywhere in the file makes Decode fail, at
which point ResolveHostName silently returns the original host — every alias in the file stops
resolving and nobody is told (nocx-n7yv).

Replace it: ask `ssh -G <host>` and parse its answer. The reference implementation is the
oracle.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A resolver behind an interface, injected at the composition root — not a package-level
  function reaching for os/exec wherever it is called.
- Results are cached. The motivating case is forty hosts; forty subprocesses on one list
  render is not the design. State the invalidation rule deliberately: mtime of the config
  files, a TTL, or explicit refresh — and say why in a comment.
- **Honest degradation, stated in one place**: no ssh binary, ssh -G failing, or ssh -G being
  slow are three different conditions and must not all collapse into "no config". The user is
  told, once, not on every connect.
- The existing callers — ResolveHostName and resolveAuthzEndpoint — go through it. Note that
  resolveAuthzEndpoint is on the AUTHORIZATION path: both sides of that comparison must
  resolve through the same resolver, or the check compares unlike things. Read
  checkAuthorization before touching it.
- Timeouts. An ssh -G that hangs must not hang a connect.
- Tests do not shell out to the real ssh. Put the oracle behind the interface and fake it;
  add one build-tagged or skipped-by-default test that runs against a real ssh for
  conformance.
- nocx-n7yv is closed by this: a config with Match resolves correctly.
close_reason: kevinburke/ssh_config is gone from go.mod. A ConfigResolver interface asks ssh -G, is injected at the composition root, caches by config mtime with generation purging, times out, and returns typed errors — binary-not-found, timeout, parse-failure — each warned once rather than collapsing into 'no config'. The authorization invariant holds: resolveConfig and resolveAuthzEndpoint both go through the same injected resolver, so checkAuthorization still compares like with like. The ordinary suite never shells out to ssh; the real-ssh conformance test is env-gated, and the coordinator gave it a make target because NOCX_TEST_SSH_G appeared nowhere outside the test file — a conformance test nobody can discover is one that never runs. Verified by running it: 6 subtests pass against the real binary, including match_directive_does_not_break_resolution.

title: ADR: ssh -G is the resolution oracle for ~/.ssh/config
description:
## The decision to record

nocx will not parse ~/.ssh/config itself. It will ask OpenSSH what configuration it would
apply, via `ssh -G <host>`, and treat that answer as authoritative.

## Why this needs an ADR

It is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and a genuine trade-off — the three tests
AGENTS.md sets for recording a decision.

**What forced it.** github.com/kevinburke/ssh_config v1.2.0 does not support the Match
directive. Verified empirically: Decode returns an error for a Match block anywhere in the
file, and ResolveHostName treats any decode error as "no config" and returns the original
host. So one Match block silently disables alias resolution for the entire file
(nocx-n7yv). Wave 7 is about to promise that a users ssh aliases appear in nocx; for anyone
with a Match block that promise would be silently false.

**What it buys.** Correctness by construction: the reference implementation is the oracle, so
there is no subset to declare and no conformance gap to chase. Spec section 9 item 3 asked for
"the declared supported subset and the ssh -G conformance fixture set" — that task largely
dissolves, because the supported subset becomes "whatever the users ssh supports".

**What it costs, and this is the part the ADR must be honest about.** An external process on
the resolution path. A subprocess per host, so caching and invalidation become our problem. A
hard dependency on an ssh binary being present — always true on macOS and Linux, a separate
question on Windows. And ssh -G output is a stable-ish text format, not an API.

## Alternatives considered, to be recorded with their reasons

- Keep the library and declare Match unsupported, failing loudly instead of silently. Cheap
  and honest, but the feature simply does not exist for a real class of users.
- Write our own parser. First-obtained-wins ordering, Include, Match with exec conditions and
  canonicalization make this a long tail of subtle divergence from the reference, discovered
  by users rather than by tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An ADR in docs/decisions/ following the house style, including the amendment convention
  ADR-0001 uses.
- The degradation path is stated: what nocx does when no ssh binary exists, when ssh -G fails,
  and when it is slow.
- The relationship to nocx-n7yv is named — this ADR is what closes that bug class.
close_reason: ADR-0015 records the decision to ask ssh -G rather than parse ~/.ssh/config, with what forced it (the library's Match failure and the silent fallthrough in ResolveHostName), what it buys, and what it costs — an external process on the resolution path, a subprocess per host, an unversioned text format, and no path to a no-ssh build. Both rejected alternatives carry their reasons. Windows is recorded as an open question with two concrete resolutions rather than asserted settled; the worker corrected that itself after its first report.

title: A single Match directive silently disables all ssh_config resolution
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Put any Match block in ~/.ssh/config, e.g.:
   ```
   Host prod
     HostName 10.0.0.1

   Match user deploy
     ForwardAgent yes
   ```
2. Connect to the alias `prod` from nocx.
3. nocx dials the literal host `prod` instead of `10.0.0.1`.

## Cause

github.com/kevinburke/ssh_config v1.2.0 does not support Match. Verified empirically: Decode
returns `ssh_config: Match directive parsing is unsupported` for a Match block anywhere in the
file — before, after, or inside a Host block. ResolveHostName (internal/ssh/ssh_config.go)
treats any decode error as "no config" and returns the original host, so the failure is
total and silent: every alias in the file stops resolving.

The library also carries `panic("cant handle Match directives")` inside Config.Get
(config.go:355), which nocx calls. That path is unreachable today only because Decode fails
first; it is one refactor away from being a crash in the connect path.

## Why it matters more now

Wave 7 (nocx-c2ym) makes ~/.ssh/config a live, read-only source surfaced in the palette and a
terminal hint. A source that silently returns nothing for a large class of real configs cannot
carry that promise, and the spec requires the supported subset to be declared and
conformance-tested against `ssh -G` (spec section 9 item 3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A config nocx cannot fully parse does not fail silently. The user is told which file and
  which construct, once, without a dialog on every connect.
- The behaviour with an unparseable config is stated deliberately: today every alias silently
  stops resolving, which is the worst of the options because it looks like the config is
  empty rather than unreadable.
- Whatever parser strategy wave 7 lands on, the Match case is covered by a test.
close_reason: Closed by nocx-c2ym.2 and ADR-0015. nocx no longer parses ~/.ssh/config, so the library's Match failure cannot silently disable alias resolution. Proven against the real ssh binary by the conformance subtest match_directive_does_not_break_resolution, reachable via make conformance.

title: The backend answers what moving a profile between groups would do
description:
## The gap

Spec section 3.3 requires that "moving or reparenting shows the effective-field diff before it
is applied". groups.impact (nocx-uxs5.11) answers that for changes to a GROUP — its defaults,
its parent, its deletion. It has no answer for the other direction: moving one PROFILE from
one group to another.

Found by the group-UI worker, which correctly refused to approximate it in the renderer. A
profile is affected by inheritance without naming the group, so a renderer-side guess is the
class of error this epic has repeatedly sent back.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An RPC takes a proposed profile group change — profile id, target group id (or none, for
  promotion to root) — and returns the effective-field diff for that profile.
- Same shape as groups.impact so the renderer has one way to display a diff, not two: per
  field old value, new value, and whether the change is dangerous.
- Computed by resolving the profile twice through ResolveEffectiveProfile — current group
  chain versus proposed. Do NOT write a second resolver; groups.impact already does exactly
  this and is the model to follow.
- Accepts several profiles at once. Dragging a multi-selection is one question, not N.
- Nothing is written. This is a preview.

## Note

The existing profiles.update path applies the move. This bead adds only the preview that must
precede it.
close_reason: profiles.moveImpact returns the effective-field diff for a proposed profile group change, reusing the fieldDiff/profileImpact/groupImpactResponse types from groups.impact so the renderer has one diff shape rather than two. Computed by resolving each profile twice through ResolveEffectiveProfile — current group versus proposed — with no second resolver. Accepts several profiles, writes nothing. Found by the group-UI worker, which correctly refused to approximate it in the renderer.

title: The backend computes a group change's blast radius, and guards the tree
description:
## Why this is backend work

Spec section 3.3 is binding: "editing group defaults shows the blast radius (changes the
credential for 37 connections)" and the count is computed on the backend, never counted in
the renderer. The renderer cannot count it correctly anyway — inheritance means a profile can
be affected without naming the group, which is the same trap credentials.usage was built to
avoid.

Section 3.3 also states the guards outright: "the backend validates group cycles, missing
parents and maximum depth, and a groups ParentGroupID or defaults cannot be changed through
generic CRUD that bypasses the impact workflow."

## Acceptance Criteria

- An RPC answers, for a proposed group change, which profiles it would affect and HOW: the
  effective-field diff per profile, not a bare count. Section 3.3 wants the diff shown before
  a move or reparent is applied.
- The dangerous fields are distinguished from cosmetic ones. A change to credential,
  username, endpoint or jump route is not the same event as renaming a folder, and the
  response must let the UI say so.
- Group deletion states what happens to children — reparent, promote to root, or refuse —
  and the answer is the backend s, not a renderer convention.
- Bulk group changes are atomic.
- ParentGroupID and defaults cannot be changed through generic groups.update. Close that
  door: today groups.update takes a whole group.
- Cycles, missing parents and maximum depth are validated and rejected with typed errors.
- The computation reuses the effective-profile engine (nocx-uxs5.1). Do not write a second
  resolver.

## Deliberately out

All UI. That is nocx-uxs5.9, which this unblocks.
close_reason: groups.impact returns the effective-field diff per profile, computed by resolving each profile twice through the SAME ResolveEffectiveProfile — current tree versus proposed — so there is no second resolver to drift. Dangerous fields (credentialId, user, auth, jumpHost, port) are distinguished from cosmetic ones. groups.update now refuses ParentGroupID and Defaults changes and directs to impact+apply, closing the generic-CRUD door section 3.3 names. Apply was a load-validate-write across three separate lock acquisitions and was sent back: the tree could move between the blast radius the user confirmed and the state the change landed in, and two individually valid applies could interleave into a cycle. ApplyGroups now validates and writes under one lock and takes a bulk slice.

title: The pre-commit gate spends 29 seconds defeating a cache that was correct
description:
## Measured

The hook costs ~67s. Where it goes: go test -race in a container 30s, vitest in a container
18s, eslint 8s, the Solid fixture gate 4s, prettier 3s, tsc 3s, gofumpt 1s, golangci-lint 0s.

`go test -race -count=1 ./...` (.githooks/containerized-tests.sh) deliberately defeats Gos
test cache. Measured on the same tree: without -count=1 a warm run is **1 second** with 18
packages cached; with it, 30 seconds every time. The cache is keyed on the test binary and
its inputs, so a package whose code changed still re-runs — the flag buys nothing and costs
29 seconds per commit.

It was not a decision. Neither d7f2ef5 (which introduced the gate) nor 6a170a2 (which moved
tests into containers) mentions -count=1 or the cache at all. It arrived incidentally.

The two containers also run in sequence although they share nothing, and both run on every
commit regardless of whether the commit touches that language.

## Why not just move tests to pre-push

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs only on pull requests to main and on release/** branches,
so a feature-branch push is checked by nothing but this hook. AGENTS.md also values
bisectable history, and a broken intermediate commit is precisely what the hook prevents.

## Acceptance Criteria

- -count=1 is gone, with a comment saying why the cache is trusted so it does not come back.
- The two test containers run concurrently, and a failure in either still fails the commit
  with its own output attributable to the right runner.
- A commit that touches no Go files skips the Go container; one that touches no frontend
  files skips the frontend container, eslint, tsc and the fixture gate.
- The scoping is conservative: if the changed set cannot be determined, everything runs.
- gofumpt, golangci-lint and repo-wide prettier stay unconditional — together they are 4
  seconds and they cover files the scoping would otherwise miss.
- The beads export stays last, so a failing gate never leaves .beads/issues.jsonl rewritten
  for a commit that never happens.
close_reason: Measured 67s to 29s worst case (everything runs) and 3s for a commit touching neither language. -count=1 removed with a comment recording why the cache is trusted; the two containers now start together and run under the host linters; per-language gates scoped to the staged set, with anything unclassifiable running everything. Failure attribution verified against a simulated failing runner before landing. Commit a166a43.

title: Group editing shows its blast radius before it applies
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

Spec section 3.3 is binding here: provenance explains state, it does not make mutations quiet.

- Groups get an interface, including what a group hands down.
- Editing group defaults shows the blast radius before applying — "changes the credential for
  37 connections" — computed on the backend, never counted in the renderer.
- Moving or reparenting a profile shows the effective-field DIFF before it is applied.
- A change to credential, username, endpoint or jump route requires explicit confirmation,
  visually distinct from a cosmetic folder move.
- Group deletion states what happens to children: reparent, promote to root, or refuse.
- Bulk group changes are atomic.
- ParentGroupID and defaults cannot be changed through generic CRUD that bypasses this
  workflow.
close_reason: Groups get an editor: defaults editing with the blast radius from groups.impact shown before applying, delete stating what happens to children, and an auth-affecting change gated behind an explicit confirmation that disables the apply control until given. Danger comes from the backend's flag rather than being re-derived. The profile-move preview is wired to profiles.moveImpact, the endpoint whose absence the first worker correctly escalated instead of approximating. The first pass shipped the whole editor with zero tests while reporting a suite total another wave had produced — the second occurrence of that pattern in this epic; there are now 7, including the mirror case that a cosmetic change does NOT demand confirmation, without which the suite would pass on a UI that always asks and that users learn to click through.

title: The editor shows every field provenance, with a revert control
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Every field in the connection editor shows where its effective value came from —
  "2222 - from group Prod", "deploy - from credential prod-ops" — rendered from the closed
  source enum of nocx-uxs5.1. The renderer switches on kind and never parses ids or labels.
- Editing a field flips it to "overridden here" and offers a revert control.
- Revert calls profiles.patch unset (nocx-uxs5.2). It never writes the inherited value into
  the profile — that would make "inherited 2222" and "overridden to 2222" indistinguishable
  forever after.
- Provenance links are reachable by keyboard. Spec section 5 makes accessibility acceptance
  criteria, not polish.
close_reason: Every editable field shows its provenance from the closed source enum; editing flips it to 'overridden here' with a revert that calls profiles.patch unset and consumes the returned effective entry. Revert control is a kit IconButton with an ariaLabel. Coordinator fixed a materialisation path the revision left: revert wrote the inherited value back into the draft, and a later name edit routes through profiles.update, which writes the whole profile — so the reverted field would have been pinned to the value it used to inherit. The draft now drops the key; pinned by a test asserting the key is absent from the wire JSON.

title: The connection list is full-width, filtered, grouped and live
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Connections is a full-width list, not a two-column split. Editing happens in the kit Dialog;
  the screen job is finding and connecting, which happens daily, and editing does not deserve
  half the width permanently (spec section 5).
- A filter narrows the list, and groups render as a tree.
- A row reports STATE, not just an address: live connected/disconnected, the credential in
  force AND where it came from, last used. All of it comes from the backend
  (nocx-uxs5.1, nocx-uxs5.4) — the renderer displays, it does not resolve.
- The credential shown on a row LINKS to its record in the Credentials section.
- Test is a row action distinct from Connect (nocx-uxs5.3).
- One primary action in the toolbar. The Tabby import moves into the existing
  Export / Backup / Import section.
close_reason: Connections is a full-width list with a filter, a group tree, live connected/disconnected state and last-used from sessions.status, the credential in force with its provenance and a link to its record, and Test as a row action distinct from Connect reporting the typed probe outcome in words. Editing is in the kit Dialog; Tabby import moved into Export / Backup / Import. Accessibility was right first time: the row is role=listitem with no click handler of its own and every action is a real kit Button. The first pass shipped 653 changed lines and zero tests — sent back; there are now 13 behaviour tests, including a non-accepted probe outcome and an assertion that Test does not open a session. Suite 949 to 962.

title: A session knows which profile it came from, and when it was last used
description:
## What is missing

Spec section 5 wants a row that reports live connected/disconnected state and last-used, and
spec section 9 item 13 names the gap: session.Config retains host and config, not a profile
id. Nothing in internal/session carries a ProfileID, so the list cannot say which of its rows
is the connection currently open in a tab.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A session records the profile id it was opened from, server-side. AD-7 keeps session id
  server-authoritative, so this association is minted where the session is, not claimed by
  the renderer.
- Last-used is persisted per profile and survives a restart.
- An RPC reports, for a set of profiles, which are live right now and when each was last
  used, so the list can render state without polling every session individually.
- Closing or losing a session updates the state the list sees.
- The handler lives in its own file. Only the dispatch case line goes in ws.go.

## Note

A profile deleted while a session is open must not strand the session. State what happens
and test it rather than discovering it.
close_reason: Session records its profile server-side, last-used persisted, sessions.status answers for the whole list in one call. Coordinator moved the ProfileID assignment inside the ssh branch after Resolve: it was set before the branch, so a local PTY could carry an unvalidated profile id and the list would draw a row connected with nothing behind it. Commit 0a52ecd.

title: Test is a wire, not a plan
description:
## What is missing

Wave 4 built the forced-fresh probe primitive — RealClient.Probe (internal/ssh/ssh_real.go:167)
— and nothing exposes it. Spec section 5 makes Test a first-class row action separate from
Connect, and section 6 needs the same primitive for rotation, so this is the wire both depend on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A connections.test RPC probes one saved profile and reports a typed outcome, resolved
  through the effective-profile engine so it tests what Connect would actually do.
- The outcome distinguishes at least: accepted, rejected, unreachable, host-key problem,
  needs-interactive. "It failed" is what this replaces.
- The probe is forced-fresh and pool-bypassing — testing a pooled connection tests nothing.
- The host key is verified before probing.
- It never tries a second credential against the same host. That is indistinguishable from
  password spraying and triggers lockouts; MaxAuthTries is finite.
- The handler lives in its own file, NOT inside the existing ws.go handler bodies. Only the
  dispatch case line goes in ws.go.

## Deliberately out

Rotation orchestration (wave 8, nocx-383c). This bead ships the single-target primitive it
will stand on.
close_reason: connections.test probes one saved profile and reports a typed outcome — accepted, rejected, unreachable, host-key problem, needs-interactive. Resolved through the effective-profile engine, forced-fresh, host key verified first, exactly one auth method on the wire. The first attempt re-derived the auth precedence in a parallel function that had already drifted from buildAuthChain — cfg.AuthMethods ignored, keyboardInteractive collapsed into password — and was rejected; the probe now takes its single method FROM buildAuthChain. Wired through a narrow Prober interface adapted at the composition root.

title: A stored profile can say "not set", and an override can be reverted
description:
## What is wrong

Spec section 3.3 calls presence-aware stored values "a prerequisite, not a refinement".
Wave 2 made the inheritance LAYERS sparse and left the stored profile dense
(internal/profile/profile.go:108); the conversion still treats zero and false as absent
(profile.go:379, profile.go:498). So a profile cannot override an inherited true with
false, and "inherit the port", "use 22 explicitly" and "unset" remain one state.

profiles.update unmarshals a whole SSHProfile (internal/transport/ws.go:1052) and has no
patch semantics at all, so "revert this field to what it inherits" cannot be expressed.
Reverting means DELETING the field from the stored sparse profile — spec section 3.3 forbids
ever materialising an inherited value — and a whole-object update cannot say that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Stored profile options are presence-aware, so an explicit false or zero survives a
  round-trip and is distinguishable from unset.
- A profiles.patch RPC takes explicit set and unset:
  { id, set: { "options.port": 2200 }, unset: ["options.user"] }
- Paths come from a closed allowlist, never arbitrary reflection or JSON paths. set and
  unset must be disjoint; overlapping is an error, not a precedence puzzle.
- Apply, validate and persist atomically.
- unset removes presence. It never copies the inherited value in.
- The call returns the new effective entry, so the UI receives the inherited value and its
  provenance without a second round trip.
- No magic sentinel and no overloading of JSON null: null already means "not supplied" for
  pointer patches and would become ambiguous for genuinely nullable values later.

## Test

Set options.port, then unset it. Reload from storage and assert the stored port is ABSENT
rather than the inherited 2222, while the returned effective port is 2222 sourced from the
group.
close_reason: StoredSSHProfileOptions is the only options type on SSHProfile; the parallel dense-stored representation, its second update path and a lying ToPartial are deleted. profiles.patch takes set/unset over one allowlist living beside its mutators. Verified independently by the coordinator: an explicit false marshals present, reads back, and resolves to false sourced 'profile' against a group default of true. The first attempt added the presence-aware type BESIDE the dense one and was rejected. Commit 0a52ecd.

title: The resolver composes the credential layer, and provenance crosses the wire
description:
## What is missing

ResolveEffectiveProfile (internal/profile/profile.go:391-426) overlays hardcoded defaults,
global defaults, the group chain and the profile. There is no credential layer, so the
composition spec section 3.4 promises does not exist: a credential supplies username and
auth mode, and nothing resolves them. And no RPC returns an effective profile at all —
internal/transport/ws.go carries CRUD only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The resolver composes the credential layer, so effective username and auth mode carry
  credential provenance.
- The provenance edges are distinct and must not collapse: if a GROUP supplies
  credentialId, then credentialId source is that group while user and auth source is the
  CREDENTIAL. Getting this wrong is the predicted failure.
- A batched profiles.effective RPC returns the full field set for a list of profile ids,
  preserving request order, with a typed per-profile error entry when one cannot resolve.
- Source is a closed wire enum: profile | group | credential | sshConfig | global | default.
  The renderer switches on kind and links by id; it never parses id or label. The internal
  "group:<id>" prefix string (profile.go:239) stops crossing the wire — usage.go:85 already
  has to parse it and that is the smell this removes.
- Every field appears with its effective value even when zero, false or empty. Omission
  would make "effectively false" indistinguishable from unresolved.
- The response is built by an explicit renderer-safe DTO whose TYPE has no secret-reference
  fields — not by blanking fields after marshalling a domain struct.

## Test that must exist

Store a profile with no local port, user or auth; give its group port 2222 and credential
prod-ops; make that credential supply user deploy, auth publicKey and fake secret-reference
canaries. Assert port provenance is the group, credentialId provenance is the group, user
and auth provenance is the CREDENTIAL, and that the raw JSON contains none of the canaries.
close_reason: Resolver composes the credential layer; profiles.effective is batched and field-oriented with a closed source enum and a DTO whose type carries no secret references. Provenance edges stay distinct — credentialId from the group, user/auth from the credential — asserted apart in the transport test with secret canaries. Commit 0a52ecd.

title: Reachability is a manual recipe, not a gate
description:
## What is wrong

AGENTS.md check 5 — "Is the code you found actually reachable?" — is a manual recipe and
nothing else. `deadcode` appears in no gate: `.githooks/pre-commit` runs gofumpt,
golangci-lint, `go test -race`, eslint, the Solid fixture check and vitest. Nothing in
either language asks whether the code under test is reachable from the product.

The frontend has no equivalent tool at all. `frontend/package.json` carries no `knip` and
no `ts-prune`, so a public method of an exported class that nobody calls is invisible: it
has exactly the shape of a legitimate public API.

This is the defect class AGENTS.md itself documents — 26 unreachable vault functions with
green tests, three closed beads hardening a subsystem the product never executes. It has
now produced a second instance: `ProfileClient.updateCredential`
(`frontend/src/profiles.ts:234`) has no caller in the app, and the credential editor
therefore creates duplicates instead of updating (`nocx-0w2f.6`). Wave 1 built the update
path; nothing noticed the renderer never took it.

Reading found both. A gate would have found them the day they landed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reachability check runs in `.githooks/pre-commit` for both languages and fails the
  commit on growth.
- Go: `deadcode ./...` over `nocx/internal/...`, with a declared, reviewed exemption list —
  not a bare allowance for anything already unreachable.
- TypeScript: `knip` (or an equivalent) configured with class members included, so an
  uncalled public method is reported. Verify against the known case before declaring it
  done: the check must report `ProfileClient.updateCredential` on the commit before
  `nocx-0w2f.6` is fixed.
- Existing unreachable code is baselined the way ADR-0014's raw-control guard baselines
  violations — per item, so stale entries are harmless and only growth is an error. A
  single global suppression is not acceptable; it would hide the next vault.
- The baseline is generated by a deliberate script, never as a side effect of running the
  gate.

## Why this is not just "add a linter"

The two tools disagree about what "used" means, and both are right in their own language.
A test calling a function makes it used for `unused` and unreachable for `deadcode`; that
difference is precisely what hid the vault. State in the configuration which definition
each gate uses and why, or the next person will turn the noisy one off.

title: The backend can say which connections use a credential
description:
## What is missing

The Credentials section has to answer "who uses this identity" — the question neither
Tabby nor Orca answers, and the one that makes deleting a credential a decision rather
than a guess. The data exists after wave 2, but nothing exposes it: `ws.go` carries only
CRUD for `profiles.*`, `groups.*` and `credentials.*`, and no method returns an effective
profile.

Counting on the frontend is wrong and would look right. A group hands `credentialId` down
through the sparse layer (`internal/profile/profile.go:114`, merged with provenance at
`:444-446`), so a scan of `options.credentialId` misses every profile that inherits its
credential and reports 0 for a credential four hosts actually use.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A JSON-RPC method `credentials.usage` returns, for every credential, the profiles that
  resolve to it — both the ones naming it directly and the ones inheriting it from a group.
- Resolution goes through the wave-2 effective-profile engine, not a field scan. A profile
  naming its own credential does NOT also count against its group's.
- Each entry says where the reference came from, so the UI can distinguish "this connection
  points at the credential" from "this connection inherits it from group Prod".
- The result is derived on every call, never stored (spec section 3.1 — the reverse view is
  computed).
- Go tests: a profile naming a credential; a profile inheriting one from its group; a
  profile whose own credential overrides its group's; a credential nobody uses.

## Contract

Fixed by the coordinator so the frontend can be built against it in parallel. Do not
change it without saying so — another worker is compiling against this shape.

```
credentials.usage   (no params)  ->  { "usage": [ CredentialUsage ] }

CredentialUsage {
  credentialId: string
  profiles:     ProfileRef[]
}

ProfileRef {
  profileId:   string
  profileName: string
  source:      "profile" | "group"
  groupId?:    string      // set when source == "group"
  groupName?:  string      // set when source == "group"
}
```

A credential nobody uses appears with an empty `profiles` array. It is not omitted — the
frontend must be able to say "not used by anything" without inferring it from a missing key.
close_reason: credentials.usage computes the reverse view through the wave-2 effective-profile engine. Coordinator fixed two contract defects after review: the unused-credential case marshalled as "profiles": null rather than [], and the source field leaked raw engine values; the closed set is now profile|group|global.

title: Import collision policy for credentials, profiles and groups
description: Discovered while landing wave 1a (61b5aa8). export/import.go used SaveCredential, which replaced the whole stored record and therefore blanked SecretID whenever the imported payload lacked one — the same orphaning defect nocx-ec2u fixed for the RPC path. Wave 1a swapped it to CreateCredential, so a duplicate import now FAILS instead of silently orphaning a secret. That is deliberate and safer, but it is not a designed policy: re-importing a config the user exported themselves now errors. Spec section 9 item 8 also requires that an imported profile naming an EXISTING LOCAL credential need review before it is connectable, since otherwise an import can authorize a local secret for endpoints named in the imported file.
acceptance_criteria: A declared, tested policy for importing a record whose ID already exists locally — for credentials, profiles and groups — covering both the Tabby and configuration-export paths, applied inside one transaction so a failure halfway leaves nothing partially written.
close_reason: Delivered by 116cce5: the collision policy is declared and tested — profiles and groups overwrite, credentials refuse (an import payload carries no secret references, so overwriting would orphan the stored password), and an imported profile naming an existing local credential is marked needs-review and will not resolve until cleared.

title: The resolver selects the current version
description: Plan task 7. DO NOT tidy away the BoundHost/BoundPort assignments — checkBinding refuses an empty BoundHost and removing them breaks every stored password until wave 2 lands. That was the flaw writing the plan found in the spec's first wave boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Resolve publishes the selected version's PasswordSecretID and PassphraseSecretID on the config; a test asserts the resolved SecretID differs across two versions, which is the property poolKeyFor depends on; cfg.BoundHost and cfg.BoundPort keep being set from cred.Host and cred.Port.
close_reason: Landed in 1b6ce8a, full gate green. Coordinator-verified rather than taken on report: BoundHost/BoundPort still set from cred.Host/cred.Port (resolver.go:85-86), Credential.Host still present, the promotion test asserts the resolved SecretID actually changes sec:7 -> sec:8, and the branch had not moved under the worker's files.

title: A credential carries secret versions
description: Plan task 6. Spec section 9 item 2 lists the auth-specific version schema as a plan input — this task is where it is DECIDED. Write the chosen shape into spec section 3.9 before writing the test, so the document and the code agree.
acceptance_criteria: CredentialVersion is typed per auth method — password carries PasswordSecretID, public key carries KeyFingerprint plus an optional PassphraseSecretID, agent carries neither; a legacy record with a bare SecretID and no list reads as one current version with no migration step; savePassword appends a NEW version and moves current to it rather than overwriting.
close_reason: Landed in 1b6ce8a, full gate green. Coordinator-verified rather than taken on report: BoundHost/BoundPort still set from cred.Host/cred.Port (resolver.go:85-86), Credential.Host still present, the promotion test asserts the resolved SecretID actually changes sec:7 -> sec:8, and the branch had not moved under the worker's files.

title: Profiles and groups get the same create/update distinction
description: Plan task 5. Profiles keep a whole-record update on purpose: they have no backend-owned field the renderer cannot see. That changes in wave 2 when provenance arrives. Do NOT pre-build a profile patch here. The tabby and export importers are pointed at Create-then-Update as an explicit way station; wave 3 routes them properly.
acceptance_criteria: profiles.create with an existing ID returns -32602 and changes nothing; profiles.update with a missing ID returns -32602 and creates nothing; same for groups; profiles.create mints its own ID when none is sent. nocx-u5ai is fully satisfied.
close_reason: Landed in 1b6ce8a, full gate green. Coordinator-verified rather than taken on report: BoundHost/BoundPort still set from cred.Host/cred.Port (resolver.go:85-86), Credential.Host still present, the promotion test asserts the resolved SecretID actually changes sec:7 -> sec:8, and the branch had not moved under the worker's files.

title: The store tells create from update
description: Plan task 3. The read-merge-write must hold the mutex: doing it in the caller lets a concurrent savePassword land between the read and the write and be silently discarded.
acceptance_criteria: CreateCredential refuses an empty ID and refuses to overwrite an existing one; UpdateCredential refuses a missing ID and merges the patch UNDER THE STORE MUTEX; SetSecretRefs is the only path that writes backend-owned references; SaveCredential is deleted.
close_reason: Landed in 61b5aa8, full gate green. Verified by the coordinator against the acceptance criteria rather than the worker's report: Host/Port/ErrCredentialHostRequired carried over unchanged, UpdateCredential merges under the store mutex, create ignores the renderer's id and mints via NewCredentialID, update refuses a missing id with -32602, both still reject secretId/passphraseSecretId, neither response carries a secret reference.

title: The handler applies a patch and mints the ID
description: Plan task 4. The renderer's ID is minted from the FIRST keystroke of the name and never revised (spec 2.4), so typing p first permanently yields cred:p:... — that is why it is ignored rather than honoured.
acceptance_criteria: credentials.create ignores any renderer-supplied id and mints its own with NewCredentialID; credentials.update requires an id and returns -32602 without one; secretId/passphraseSecretId are still rejected; no response carries a secret reference; the task-1 regression passes.
close_reason: Landed in 61b5aa8, full gate green. Verified by the coordinator against the acceptance criteria rather than the worker's report: Host/Port/ErrCredentialHostRequired carried over unchanged, UpdateCredential merges under the store mutex, create ignores the renderer's id and mints via NewCredentialID, update refuses a missing id with -32602, both still reject secretId/passphraseSecretId, neither response carries a secret reference.

title: The connection list answers questions
description: Wave 6. Spec section 5. Needs profile-to-session association and last-used persistence, which do not exist today — session.Config retains host and config, not a profile ID (spec section 9 item 13). The + create-a-credential affordance belongs here, not to wave 5, because it lives in the form this wave rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: Connections is a full-width list with a filter, a group tree and live connected/disconnected state; a row shows the credential in force and where it came from, and links to it; Test is a row action distinct from Connect; creation starts from one field accepting deploy@host:port, a bare alias or ssh://; every field in the editor shows its provenance with a revert control; group editing shows its blast radius before applying; failures speak from a typed error taxonomy instead of Internal error (nocx-3isn); TextField composes Field so required markers appear everywhere at once.
close_reason: Wave 6 landed in eight commits (0a52ecd, d01ca47, 23842eb, eddd0ab, ec59a55, 4588ea8, 850ea91, 4c4cc99, bad6c56). The connection list is full-width, filtered, grouped and live; every field shows its provenance with a revert that unsets rather than materialising; Test is a wire with typed outcomes; sessions know their profile; groups state their blast radius before applying; creation starts from one field and a credential can be made without leaving the form; failures say what failed. Four beads were added mid-wave from defects found while reviewing worker output: nocx-uxs5.10 (editing a connection created a duplicate — the wave-5 credential bug, never generalised to profiles), nocx-uxs5.11 and .12 (the backend halves of group and move impact), and the reachability gap filed as nocx-nc4i.

title: SSH does what the profile says
description: Wave 4. Spec sections 2.7, 2.9, 3.7. NOTE: spec rev.3 WITHDREW the claim that the pool is not invalidated on password rotation — poolKeyFor already keys on cfg.SecretID. What remains is narrow. The probe primitive here is what wave 8's rollout is built on.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-hop jump routes survive resolution; keepalive, readyTimeout and agentForward are applied (nocx-49x); public-key pool identity is a key fingerprint rather than a path; the agent-auth pooling choice is made explicitly; the jump route is a structured recursive identity; pool.go's stale doc comment is corrected to say SecretID; a forced-fresh pool-bypassing probe primitive exists; transport drain and revocation exist.
close_reason: Landed in 4cb82ee (four options applied), 65f9ea5 (resolver wiring) and this commit (multi-hop routes, public-key fingerprint identity, explicit agent-pooling decision, forced-fresh single-method probe, pool drain). Coordinator-verified: the probe takes one auth method, verifies the host key before authenticating, bypasses the pool and closes without a shell — the constraints that stop a fleet rollout locking out the fleet.

title: A connection knows what it inherited, and says so
description: Wave 2. Spec sections 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5. Blocked-by design note: mergeInto treats zero as unset and copies booleans only when true, and Defaults is map[string]any, so provenance is currently UNREPRESENTABLE — typed sparse values are a prerequisite, not a refinement (spec section 9 item 1).
acceptance_criteria: ProfileGroup.Defaults is real backend-side inheritance with typed sparse presence-aware values; every effective field carries provenance and an inherited value is never materialized into the stored profile; one resolution yields DialEndpoint, HostKeyIdentity, AuthorizationPair and DisplayTarget; the precedence table is closed; group cycles and depth are validated; the TypeScript inheritance copy is deleted and deadcode reports nothing unreachable in internal/profile; Credential.Host and checkBinding are replaced by computed authorization in this same wave.
close_reason: Landed in 43f8f4b (typed sparse inheritance, provenance, unknown-key tolerance) and this commit (computed authorization, resolver wiring, Credential.Host deleted). Coordinator-verified: empty authorization refused, comparison against the resolved endpoint not the alias, authorized endpoint and dial target are separate inputs so the check is not self-authorizing, aliases connect, drift refused. deadcode 17 -> 7.

title: Every writer goes through one door
description: Wave 3. Spec sections 2.8, 3.3, 3.4. Today importer/tabby.go and export/import.go call SaveProfile directly and import credentials in a second pass, so a failure halfway leaves a partially imported store on disk.
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary CRUD, the group impact workflow, Tabby import, configuration import and ssh_config adoption all route through the effective-profile service; imports are transactional with a declared collision policy; an imported profile naming an existing local credential requires review before it is connectable.
close_reason: Landed in 116cce5. Coordinator-verified: the partial-failure test asserts the store file is unchanged byte-for-byte after a failed import (service_test.go:385,418); all writers route through the profile service; the credential collision refusal is covered rather than incidental.

title: Brainstorming: connection manager refactor — groups + shared credentials
acceptance_criteria: A design spec for the connection-manager refactor exists in .internal/specs/ and the user has approved it
close_reason: Design approved and committed (.internal/specs/2026-07-29-connection-manager-design.md rev.3, three review rounds), wave-1 plan written (.internal/plans/2026-07-29-wave-1-credential-correctness.md), eight epics created under the connmgr label with the wave-1 task chain, PR #59 closed with the rationale. Terminal state reached.

title: Connections form validates a null draft, so a saved profile reports every filled field as required and Connect does nothing
description:
The rules in `profileValidation` read `editing()`. The form panel renders
`editing()` OR, when that is null, the profile named by `selectedID`. Those are
not the same object, and the second case is reached constantly: `handleProfileClick`
sets `selectedID` and clears `editing` on purpose, and `saveProfile` ends in
`setEditing(null)`.

Whenever the form is showing a stored profile rather than a draft, every rule
reads `undefined` and reports its field as required. `gate()` then refuses
Create and Connect, reveals all errors and raises a warning toast — so a form
full of correct values shows "Name is required" under a filled Name box, and
Connect silently does nothing. Right after a save it reads as "the save failed",
which is the one thing that did work.

Fixed by giving the rules and the panel one memo, `formProfile()`, so the object
being validated is by construction the object on screen.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings -> Connections -> + New connection, fill Name/Host/User, press Create.
2. The profile is saved and the form redisplays it.
3. Press Connect. Nothing happens; Name, Host and Port are marked required
   while visibly containing values. Same on clicking any saved connection in the
   list and pressing Connect without editing a field first.

## Acceptance Criteria

A saved profile selected in the list validates against its own stored values:
Connect opens a tab, and no filled field reports itself required. Covered by
e2e/connections-settings.
close_reason: Rules and panel read one formProfile() memo; e2e/connections-settings green

title: Session ID generation ignores entropy failure and registry collisions
description:
session.NewID discards crypto/rand errors and Reg.Open inserts the result without collision detection. Entropy failure produces an all-zero ID; a repeated ID overwrites a live registry entry and leaks its channel, violating server-authoritative identity and the fail-closed token policy.

## Steps to Reproduce

Inject an entropy reader that returns an error or the same 16 bytes twice, then open sessions. The registry accepts an all-zero or duplicate ID and replaces the existing map entry.
acceptance_criteria: Session ID creation returns an error on entropy failure, Reg.Open closes the newly opened channel and fails cleanly on generation failure, and collisions are retried or rejected without replacing a live session. Deterministic tests cover both cases.

title: Profile and group create operations are indistinguishable from update
description:
profiles.create and profiles.update both call the same SaveProfile upsert, and groups do the same. Empty IDs are accepted and create with an existing ID silently overwrites data. The backend comment that it may generate its own ID is not implemented.

## Steps to Reproduce

Create a profile or group, then call the corresponding create method again with the same ID and different data, or create with an empty ID. The request succeeds and overwrites or stores invalid identity.
acceptance_criteria: Create requires or generates a valid unique ID and conflicts on an existing ID; update requires an existing ID and fails when it is absent. Profiles, groups and import paths share one validation rule with tests for empty, duplicate and missing IDs.
close_reason: Fixed in 61b5aa8 (credentials) and 1b6ce8a (profiles and groups). Create refuses an empty or duplicate ID and mints its own when none is sent; update refuses a missing ID. One validation rule per entity in the store, with Err*IDRequired/Err*Exists/Err*NotFound sentinels, and the import paths route through Create with an explicit Update fallback rather than an implicit upsert.

title: Unknown session kind silently opens a local shell
description:
handleOpen defaults to KindLocal and switches only when kind equals ssh. Any typo or unsupported kind therefore opens a local PTY instead of returning invalid params, which is surprising and can execute in the wrong trust context.

## Steps to Reproduce

Send open with valid dimensions and kind set to a misspelling such as shh. The server opens a local session instead of returning invalid params.
acceptance_criteria: Open accepts only the documented local representation and ssh; every other non-empty kind returns JSON-RPC invalid params and creates no session.

title: State-changing JSON-RPC notifications mutate state without correlation
description:
The control dispatcher accepts open, close, resize, attach and CRUD methods when req.ID is absent. An open notification can create a PTY and ring but has no response carrying the authoritative session ID, leaving an unmanageable live session. Only true notification methods such as ack should permit a missing ID.

## Steps to Reproduce

Send a valid JSON-RPC open frame without an id. The server creates a session even though no authoritative session ID can be correlated to the caller.
acceptance_criteria: All request-only methods reject a missing JSON-RPC ID before mutation; notification-only methods are explicitly enumerated. Tests prove an open notification creates no session and emits the protocol-correct response behavior.

title: A live session can have two active reconnect subscribers
description:
handleAttach replaces sessionRx.subscriber but does not cancel the previous ringToConn or revoke the old connState. If a second connection attaches while the first is alive, both can receive output and the old connection can still send data, resize and close; shared ACKs can trim replay bytes against the wrong subscriber.

## Steps to Reproduce

Open a session on connection A, keep A alive, then attach connection B to the same session ID. Produce output and send control operations from both connections.
acceptance_criteria: Each session has exactly one active subscriber lease. Reattach atomically revokes and stops the prior subscriber before output or control moves to the new one; stale ACK, data, resize and close operations are rejected. A two-live-connection integration test covers the handoff.

title: Configuration import is non-transactional and leaves partial state on failure
description:
ImportConfiguration persists profiles, then groups, then credentials one record at a time. If record N fails, records 1 through N-1 remain committed while the RPC returns only an error and no partial result. Retrying can apply more mutations over the half-imported state.

## Steps to Reproduce

Import a payload containing one valid profile followed by a record whose repository save fails. Observe that the valid profile remains persisted although the operation reports failure.
acceptance_criteria: Import validates the full payload before mutation and commits all affected configuration atomically, or rolls back completely on any failure. Tests inject failures at every aggregate boundary and prove the prior state is unchanged.

title: Import drops settings and portable private content that export promises to carry
description:
ConfigExport includes settings and PortablePayload may include conversations and command history, but ImportDeps has no settings or ContentDB capability. Both import paths restore only profiles, groups and credential metadata; portable import decrypts Private and then ignores it. This breaks the round-trip promised by ADR-0011 and the closed nocx-oqof epic.

## Steps to Reproduce

Export non-default settings and, when ContentDB is available, private content. Import the file into a clean data directory. Profiles return, but settings and private content do not.
acceptance_criteria: Configuration export-import restores settings. Portable export-import restores opted-in conversations and command history when ContentDB is available, reports unavailable content honestly, and a full round-trip test proves every declared carried field survives.
close_reason: Landed in 207aaab: settings restored via Registry.ApplyValues, private content via RestorePrivateContent, symmetry pinned by a field-by-field round-trip test. The hdwh edge was a collision guard on internal/export/import.go; the collision was resolved in the same pass, and transactionality remains open on its own.

title: Update state API is a placeholder and cannot report pending restart
description:
GetUpdateState calls Reconcile, suppresses its error and always returns an empty string. The Wails API promises pending state, but the frontend can never learn which transaction or version is waiting for restart.

## Steps to Reproduce

Apply an update so the journal records a pending restart, then call GetUpdateState. It returns an empty string regardless of the journal or reconciliation result.
acceptance_criteria: The updater exposes a typed transaction state derived from its journal, including pending version and actionable errors; GetUpdateState no longer returns a constant placeholder or suppresses reconciliation failures.
