title: Task 8: a rule is written and forgotten one at a time, and the renderer can see them
description:
Plan task 8, absorbs nocx-takqr.3. policy.get already carries rules and policy-client.ts has never read them. A whole-document write from the page races the prompt, which is exactly nocx-39bly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- policy.setRule writes one rule and policy.forgetRule removes one by id; neither rewrites the document, and a rule saved by the prompt a moment earlier survives a page gesture — asserted directly.
- policy.get carries every rule with its provenance and policy-client.ts exposes them.
- Both methods have a schema and an _OverTheWireConformsToContract test.
- A refused write raises the danger toast and the surface re-reads; no local dirty state exists.

title: Task 12: a permission is widened from a command that was read, never from one that was run
description:
Plan task 12. A permit cannot be typed from nothing because nothing would classify it; it is widened from a classified witness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Allow a command takes a typed command, classifies it WITHOUT executing it, shows what the widened rule would and would not match, and only then saves a Program rule carrying that effect.
- policy.classify cannot execute anything: a test that a command with a side effect leaves no trace.
- Write a refusal writes a HasFeature or Exact refusal and never a permit.
- A permit cannot be typed from nothing anywhere on the page.
- policy.classify has a schema and an over-the-wire test.

title: Task 3: a command's network resource is a destination scope, so a row can bound curl
description:
Plan task 3, bead nocx-yso3z. namedResourceScope (internal/content/effectpolicy.go:303-307) yields a scope only for an absolute path, always of kind ResourcePath, so a destination scope bounds fetch.url and not curl.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A row whose destination scope is https://github.com does not permit curl https://example.com.
- One test drives the same policy and the same address through a command and through fetch.url and compares the outcome.
- The ResourceVerb to scope-kind mapping is exhaustive: a verb with no scope kind fails a test rather than returning false silently.

title: Task 5: a rule may narrow loosely and may widen only under the effect it was granted for
description:
Plan task 5, beads nocx-6to7g and nocx-pvr2h. InvocationRule.Matches requires equal token count and matches positionally (rules.go:131-148), so "all df commands" and "curl with -o anywhere" are both unwritable. The asymmetry is the content: a loose matcher is safe for narrowing and unsafe for widening.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Program rule with permit and no GrantedUnder is an unparseable policy.
- A HasFeature rule with permit is an unparseable policy, in any spelling.
- Program{df} granted under observe permits df --output=source and does NOT permit find . -delete when granted for find under observe.
- HasFeature{curl, writes-option-named-path} refusing beats Program{curl} permitting, through EvaluateInvocation and not through the store.
- A disqualified invocation still bypasses rules entirely, refusals included.
- LiteralInvocationRule still produces only Exact and still refuses a pattern character.
- A tool-kind scope and a tool name as a row key are still refused.

title: Task 4: an out-of-scope resource asks or refuses by cause, and one evaluator says which
description:
Plan task 4, bead nocx-okdsm. DecisionForInvocation returns ask (effectpolicy.go:246-248) where the declared path returns RefusedOutOfScope (kernel.go:79,599), and EffectRow's doc (:61) states refusal as the rule for both. An ask a person cannot usefully answer is worse than a refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A permitted invocation naming a resource outside an EDITABLE row scope returns Decision ask, Cause row-scope, and the resource that fell outside.
- The same resource outside the run fence or a capability returns Decision refuse, Cause fence. No expansion is offered.
- The declared path returns the same Verdict for the same policy and resource; one test compares whole verdicts.
- The EffectRow doc comment matches the code beneath it.
- The filesystem capability still refuses, symlink escapes included: a policy ask does not become a filesystem read.
- nocx-j5fdf is closed as superseded with the difference named.

The worker also found TestPolicyNarrowRowRefusesOutsideRunFence passing vacuously — it set Declaration.Effect while the kernel reads Tool.Effect — fixed it, and the trap is filed as nocx-030ut. It corrected the brief's citation: the Contains doc is at resource_scope.go:64-72, not :43-47. Coordinator gated the MERGED tree, which is where this change met nocx-jxq97's kernel.go edit: build -tags gtk3 clean, and -count=1 -race on content 192.1s, transport 245.0s, assistant 9.3s, filesystem 1.4s, agenttools 1.1s — all ok. No conflicts.

title: Task 7: an out-of-scope ask can be answered by widening the row, once and boundedly
description:
Plan task 7. The ask from Task 4's row-scope cause must be answerable, and the answer must not become an approval-fatigue channel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An ask caused by row-scope carries the resource; answering with expandScope widens the row and resumes the call in ONE store write, and a store failure leaves neither applied.
- Identical out-of-scope asks are deduplicated within a run.
- Repeated expansion asks are capped per run, and reaching the cap is stated in the run, never a silent stop.
- A declined expansion refuses that effect and resource for the rest of the run's life: asserted at both ends, refused until the run ends and asked again in the next run.
- Cause fence never offers expandScope.
- agent.approvalRequested and agent.approve get their schemas and over-the-wire tests in the same commit.

title: Task 10: a standing answer says so where it was given
description:
Plan task 10. Today a standing answer disappears into the store with nothing on screen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a standing answer the scrollback carries one line naming what was saved, in the person's words, with Undo and Manage permissions.
- Undo targets the mutation id and fails loudly if the store moved underneath it; it never restores a snapshot.
- An egress answer produces no receipt.

The receipt is a new kit component (frontend/src/ui/block-notice.ts + its CSS + a README row) drawn in the scrollback right after the answer, in the person's own words — answerLabel and approvalScopeCoverage were LIFTED to module scope and reused, so there is still one sentence-builder and not two. It travels as its own notification, agent.standingAnswerSaved, with a schema: a per-run fact routed by run id lands in the turn that asked without main.tsx-to-pane plumbing, exactly as the deltas do. Undo forgets by id through PolicyClient.forgetRule and never restores a snapshot. A once answer and an egress answer draw nothing. main.tsx was DISCARDING applyStandingAnswer's warning entirely and now shows it, so a failed save can no longer be silent while a receipt claims success. Merged tree fully green: build+vet -tags gtk3, content/assistant/transport under -race, contracts:check, tsc --noEmit, and the whole frontend suite — 317 files, 6205 tests.

title: Task 6: a widened rule carries where it came from and the reading it was saved under
description:
Plan task 6. Task 1 changes how commands are read, so a rule saved under the old reading may classify differently under the new one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Program rule whose EvaluatorVersion differs from the current one does not apply and is reported as needing confirmation.
- An Exact rule is unaffected by a version change.
- Confirming a rule rewrites its version and nothing else.
- Every rule has a stable id from creation and two rules never share one.

title: Task 7: an out-of-scope ask can be answered by widening the row, once and boundedly
description:
Plan task 7. The ask from Task 4's row-scope cause must be answerable, and the answer must not become an approval-fatigue channel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An ask caused by row-scope carries the resource; answering with expandScope widens the row and resumes the call in ONE store write, and a store failure leaves neither applied.
- Identical out-of-scope asks are deduplicated within a run.
- Repeated expansion asks are capped per run, and reaching the cap is stated in the run, never a silent stop.
- A declined expansion refuses that effect and resource for the rest of the run's life: asserted at both ends, refused until the run ends and asked again in the next run.
- Cause fence never offers expandScope.
- agent.approvalRequested and agent.approve get their schemas and over-the-wire tests in the same commit.
close_reason: Landed as af078810 + d45ecf5a, merged as ff061349. decideInvocationWithReason now returns the content.Verdict it already had; the ask carries OutOfScopeFact{Cause,Resource}. agent.approvalRequested grows outOfScope{cause,resource,widening{available,reason}}; agent.approve grows scope:'expand'; agent.runState grows notices. Atomicity: Approve (in-memory) then ONE SetPolicy write, and on failure Revoke back to pending plus an RPC error rather than a warning — the opposite trade from applyStandingAnswer, because a widening that did not stick would resume a call against a row that still excludes it (TestAgentApprove_ScopeExpand_AStoreFailureAppliesNeither asserts askCount()==1). assistant.WidenRowScope goes through the policy's JSON wire form and content.ParseEffectPolicy, so effectpolicy.go and rules.go were untouched. Bound: MaxWideningAsksPerRun=3, keyed by (runID,effect,resource), and the run SAYS it stopped (TestAgentRunState_SaysTheRunStoppedAskingToWiden). Both ends of the decline interval asserted. Both schemas plus _OverTheWireConformsToContract in the same commit; npm run contracts:check OK. Verified on the merged tree: transport race suite PASS (1723 tests, 0 FAIL), content+assistant ok.

title: Task 3: a command's network resource is a destination scope, so a row can bound curl
description:
Plan task 3, bead nocx-yso3z. namedResourceScope (internal/content/effectpolicy.go:303-307) yields a scope only for an absolute path, always of kind ResourcePath, so a destination scope bounds fetch.url and not curl.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A row whose destination scope is https://github.com does not permit curl https://example.com.
- One test drives the same policy and the same address through a command and through fetch.url and compares the outcome.
- The ResourceVerb to scope-kind mapping is exhaustive: a verb with no scope kind fails a test rather than returning false silently.
close_reason: Merged as d49edce3 (worker commit 76b2abcb). scopeKindForVerb is an exhaustive ResourceVerb table: network to destination, read/write/delete/execute/source to path with the absolute rule unchanged, unknown explicitly to no kind — it is the verb of an UnresolvedResource only and never reaches namedResourcesWithinRow, and giving it a kind could only ever declare an undetermined operand INSIDE a scope. Four tests: destination bounding across five cases, command-vs-fetch.url agreement through the real resolver out of agenttools.Assemble, per-verb scope form, and an exhaustiveness test that reads the ResourceVerb constants with go/ast rather than a hand-kept list — the worker verified it trips by removing network from the table. Coordinator re-ran go test -tags gtk3 -count=1 ./internal/content/ -race independently: ok, 241.9s. Finding filed: nocx-7z6po.

title: Task 5: a rule may narrow loosely and may widen only under the effect it was granted for
description:
Plan task 5, beads nocx-6to7g and nocx-pvr2h. InvocationRule.Matches requires equal token count and matches positionally (rules.go:131-148), so "all df commands" and "curl with -o anywhere" are both unwritable. The asymmetry is the content: a loose matcher is safe for narrowing and unsafe for widening.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Program rule with permit and no GrantedUnder is an unparseable policy.
- A HasFeature rule with permit is an unparseable policy, in any spelling.
- Program{df} granted under observe permits df --output=source and does NOT permit find . -delete when granted for find under observe.
- HasFeature{curl, writes-option-named-path} refusing beats Program{curl} permitting, through EvaluateInvocation and not through the store.
- A disqualified invocation still bypasses rules entirely, refusals included.
- LiteralInvocationRule still produces only Exact and still refuses a pattern character.
- A tool-kind scope and a tool name as a row key are still refused.
close_reason: Landed as 74d85d47, merged 0f0dd0f4-range into feat/agent-ploicy. InvocationRule.Pattern replaced by a closed InvocationSelector (Exact/Program/HasFeature) plus ID and GrantedUnder (internal/content/rules.go). The asymmetry is enforced in validateInvocationRules, so the unsafe form is an unparseable document: HasFeature+permit refused in every spelling, Program+permit without GrantedUnder refused, !=1 selector field refused, unknown feature refused, grantedUnder outside the lattice refused. The widening guard is one continue in the rule loop of EvaluateInvocation (effectpolicy.go:283-289) — the only layer told what the call classified as — and it was mutation-checked: replacing it with 'if false' makes 'find . -delete' return permit and TestAProgramPermitCoversEveryArgumentUnderOneEffectAndNoOther fail. Match arity differs by direction on purpose: Program requires every subcommand to be that word, HasFeature any. Feature vocabulary moved to content.FeatureWritesOptionNamedPath; assistant/cmdeffect.go aliases it. Verified on the merged tree: go test -tags gtk3 -count=1 -race ./internal/content/ ./internal/assistant/ ok (400.9s / 14.1s), go vet clean.

title: Task 12: a permission is widened from a command that was read, never from one that was run
description:
Plan task 12. A permit cannot be typed from nothing because nothing would classify it; it is widened from a classified witness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Allow a command takes a typed command, classifies it WITHOUT executing it, shows what the widened rule would and would not match, and only then saves a Program rule carrying that effect.
- policy.classify cannot execute anything: a test that a command with a side effect leaves no trace.
- Write a refusal writes a HasFeature or Exact refusal and never a permit.
- A permit cannot be typed from nothing anywhere on the page.
- policy.classify has a schema and an over-the-wire test.
close_reason: Merged as the nocx-fl0o3-classify merge (worker c748fa3a). policy.classify parses and classifies a command WITHOUT running it: assistant.ClassifyInvocation over CanonicalInvocation (the parser a run uses) and the declared effect set the transport already holds as liveEffects — the renderer never supplies it. + Allow a command… shows what the widened rule would and would not allow BEFORE saving, then writes one Program rule carrying the effect the reading found in grantedUnder; + Write a refusal writes HasFeature or Exact and never a permit. Params+result schemas with additionalProperties:false and an over-the-wire test. Nothing added to the kit and no CSS: the panels place TextField (its error slot carries the backend's refusal, so no surface-owned error vocabulary), FactList, ActionGroup, Button, Caption, Stack, Dialog. THE NEVER-RUNS-IT PROOF is TestPolicyClassify_ReadsTheCommandAndNeverRunsIt: three commands whose execution would leave a file — touch, sort -o (an option-named write path) and echo > (a shell redirection), three shapes because three different parts of the parser touch the text — all into one t.TempDir(), then each path asserted absent AND the directory asserted empty. The structural argument is in the handler comment: the only code that sees the string is a pure parse and a pure predicate over it. Worker corrected my brief's motivating example and was right: find cannot be widened at all — it is not in readPrograms, so it goes unresolved and StandingRule refuses it, and find . -delete is separately disqualified. So the preview teaches by naming effects rather than by showing a witness. Merged tree green: transport and assistant under -race, contracts:check, tsc --noEmit, 6220 frontend tests, all ratchets at baseline.

title: Task 8: a rule is written and forgotten one at a time, and the renderer can see them
description:
Plan task 8, absorbs nocx-takqr.3. policy.get already carries rules and policy-client.ts has never read them. A whole-document write from the page races the prompt, which is exactly nocx-39bly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- policy.setRule writes one rule and policy.forgetRule removes one by id; neither rewrites the document, and a rule saved by the prompt a moment earlier survives a page gesture — asserted directly.
- policy.get carries every rule with its provenance and policy-client.ts exposes them.
- Both methods have a schema and an _OverTheWireConformsToContract test.
- A refused write raises the danger toast and the surface re-reads; no local dirty state exists.
close_reason: Merged as 56d40a92 (worker branch nocx-fliln-one-rule, 919015ab). policy.setRule and policy.forgetRule write one object each, read-modify-write under the store's own lock in globalpolicy.go; ids are server-authoritative (a rule with no id is minted one, a rule naming an id that does not exist is refused -32602). policy.set now REFUSES a document carrying 'rules' with -32602 naming policy.setRule, so the matrix write can no longer touch them at all — the nocx-39bly guard 'absent means nothing to say' stops being load-bearing. Both methods have params+result schemas with additionalProperties:false and _OverTheWireConformsToContract tests off the real socket; openrpc.json and the generated TS regenerated in the same commit. Merged tree green: go test -count=1 -race ./internal/transport/... (286s) ./internal/assistant/... ./internal/content/...; frontend contracts:check, tsc --noEmit, npm run lint (dead-export baseline shrunk by 1), 28 vitest tests. Worker corrected the brief on four points, all accepted: mintID is unexported so the store round-trips through ParseEffectPolicy (the WidenRowScope move) to get the mint AND the validation gate in one crossing; WithRule was rejected because it appends-only and silently drops what validation rejects, wrong for a wire path that must refuse; PolicyClient.set could never send rules (PolicyMatrix has no such key) so the renderer was never the live half of the defect; go build needs -tags gtk3 on Linux.

title: Task 11: Assistant permissions answers questions instead of editing a matrix
description:
Plan task 11. Replaces frontend/src/agent-policy-section.tsx.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two sections: answers given (every rule and every row off its default, as a sentence, with Why, Change, Forget) and questions not answered yet (live rows on ask, with Answer this now).
- Why renders the backend trace and nothing computed locally.
- Change offers the three answers and, for a row, a picker of places nocx names itself: no free-form field and no scope-kind select.
- Forget previews what it releases before it is taken, naming the calls whose outcome changes.
- A rule needing confirmation is shown as inert with Review and Forget.
- The words effect class, resource scope and refuse do not appear, and no control names a tool: a test per claim.
- Every control comes from frontend/src/ui/; the surface places kit components and never repaints them.

title: Task 9: the decision explains itself, in the order it was taken
description:
Plan task 9. DecisionForInvocation returns one Decision and short-circuits the refusing row before rules are read, so the trace cannot be reconstructed in the renderer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The trace for a permitted call lists the rule that permitted it, the row consulted and the resource verdict, in that order.
- A shadowed rule appears with the step that short-circuited it, rather than implying it was consulted.
- The trace is not reconstructed in the renderer: a test greps frontend/src for the precedence words and finds none.
- policy.explain has a schema and an over-the-wire test.

title: Task 4: an out-of-scope resource asks or refuses by cause, and one evaluator says which
description:
Plan task 4, bead nocx-okdsm. DecisionForInvocation returns ask (effectpolicy.go:246-248) where the declared path returns RefusedOutOfScope (kernel.go:79,599), and EffectRow's doc (:61) states refusal as the rule for both. An ask a person cannot usefully answer is worse than a refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A permitted invocation naming a resource outside an EDITABLE row scope returns Decision ask, Cause row-scope, and the resource that fell outside.
- The same resource outside the run fence or a capability returns Decision refuse, Cause fence. No expansion is offered.
- The declared path returns the same Verdict for the same policy and resource; one test compares whole verdicts.
- The EffectRow doc comment matches the code beneath it.
- The filesystem capability still refuses, symlink escapes included: a policy ask does not become a filesystem read.
- nocx-j5fdf is closed as superseded with the difference named.

title: A skill someone else wrote is installed by its URL, and nocx keeps knowing where it came from
description:
A skill someone else wrote is installed by its URL, and nocx keeps knowing where it
came from. Spec §14 deferred exactly this — "Installing a skill from a hub or a URL,
and therefore hermes's trust tiers for external sources — we have no external source" —
so the tiers were deferred WITH the source rather than instead of it. This epic
supplies both.

Read before building: the four trust layers in
.internal/specs/2026-08-31-assistant-skills-design.md §6. Layer 1 is the binding one
here — provenance is STRUCTURAL, the root a file was found in, because content cannot
forge which directory it is in. A downloaded skill therefore cannot be `authored` or
`managed`; it needs a root and a provenance of its own, or it inherits trust it did
not earn.

## What the two prior arts settled

hermes (/home/dev/repos/hermes-agent) is the model, and three of its decisions are
load-bearing rather than incidental:

- A URL install NEVER clones a repository. It fetches SKILL.md plus only the support
  files SKILL.md itself links, under an allowlist of directories, same-origin —
  "Bare URLs cannot safely enumerate a repository, so only exact references below
  references/templates/scripts/assets are fetched" (tools/skills_hub.py:1605). SSRF is
  re-checked on every redirect hop, redirects followed manually.
- The pipeline is quarantine → scan → policy → confirm → install, and `--force` cannot
  override a `dangerous` verdict for a non-builtin source (tools/skills_guard.py:1003).
- An update re-runs the whole pipeline pinned to the recorded source, refuses to change
  provenance, and SKIPS a skill the person has edited locally.

omp (/home/dev/repos/oh-my-pi) is the counterexample and worth one line: it has no
skill installer at all, plugins carrying skills install with no confirmation, no hash,
no scan, and no record of the commit fetched.

## What nocx already has that hermes does not — so do not rebuild it

- Read-side integrity: a skill whose bytes changed since approval is not framed
  trusted (nocx-dy1go). hermes has no load-time check against its lock at all.
- The static scan runs at BOTH boundaries, not only on write.
- Every skills mutation asks the person whatever their standing policy says
  (isSkillMutationTool).

## Success Criteria

- A person pastes a URL into the Skills page, sees the name, description, body, the
  scan finding and where it came from, approves, and the skill is in the list and used
  by the next ask in another pane.
- The bytes land in a root of their own with a provenance of its own, distinct from
  authored and managed, visible on the row.
- Only SKILL.md and the support files it links are fetched, from the same origin, under
  an allowlist; a link that escapes is refused rather than skipped silently.
- The installed skill records its source URL and content hash, and the record is what a
  later update is pinned to: an update cannot change the source and cannot silently
  overwrite bytes the person edited.
- A scan finding never downgrades the result silently — it is evidence in the approval,
  and refusal names what was rejected and where.
- One Playwright spec watches a person install from a fake local endpoint end to end,
  with no waitForTimeout.

## Deliberately out

- An agent-callable install tool. hermes has none on purpose, and the reason is ours
  too: the assistant proposing to install a URL it read in terminal output is the
  injection this product's whole trust model exists to stop. A person installs; the
  assistant may not.
- A hub, an index, a search, a marketplace. One source kind: a URL a person pastes.
- git clone, archives, npm — anything that fetches what SKILL.md did not name.
- Signature verification. hermes does not verify NVIDIA's signatures either; a tier
  earned by a hardcoded repo list is not a boundary and should not pretend to be.

title: A command destination is never a destination scope: only absolute paths become scopes, so a row cannot bound curl
description:
namedResourceScope (internal/content/effectpolicy.go:303-307) returns a scope only when the resource path is an absolute path, and always of kind ResourcePath. Every other resource a command names — a URL, an ssh destination, a kubectl cluster, all recorded with verb ResourceNetwork — yields no scope at all, so namedResourcesWithinRow cannot bound it.

Consequence: a destination scope on a row governs fetch.url, which resolves a real ResourceDestination (internal/agenttools/registry.go:96), and does NOT govern curl or ssh, whose destinations are invisible to the row. A person who narrows "reach another host" to one address has narrowed the declared tool and left the command path unbounded.

This is the second instance of the split nocx-okdsm names: command resources go through namedResourcesWithinRow, declared resources through the kernel scope check, and the two disagree about kinds as well as about the out-of-scope outcome. The fix should be one evaluator returning one typed cause, not two predicates kept in step by hand.

Found by an adversarial review of the Agent policy redesign (nocx-0ykkk) on 2026-09-03.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A network resource named by a command produces a destination scope, and a row destination scope bounds curl and ssh the way it bounds fetch.url.
- A test that the same policy and the same address give the same outcome through a command and through the declared tool.
- Resource kinds a command can name are enumerated in one place, and a kind with no scope form is a compile-time or startup failure, not a silent pass.

title: A refusal cannot name an argument: rule matching is fixed-arity and positional, so curl -o is unwritable
description:
InvocationRule.Matches requires an equal token COUNT and compares positionally (internal/content/rules.go:133, 138, 142). So a rule cannot say "curl with -o anywhere in its arguments": [["curl","-o"]] matches only the literal two-token command curl -o, which nobody runs. The real invocation curl -o out.txt https://x is four tokens and never matches.

Asked for by the owner on 2026-09-03 while reviewing the Agent policy page: forbid curl -o while allowing curl.

Deny rules themselves already exist and already win — InvocationRule.Decision is permit|ask|refuse, DecisionForInvocation takes the most restrictive of all matching rules (effectpolicy.go:229-237, restrictiveRank) and a rule stricter than the row beats the row (effectpolicy.go:242). What is missing is only the ability to WRITE the narrow one.

Not nocx-6to7g. That bead is the other axis — a rule covering one command with any arguments, which WIDENS and therefore needs a guard (it must carry the effect class it was granted under, or "any find" permits find . -delete). This bead is narrowing, and narrowing needs no guard at all: a refusal cannot permit anything, so a matcher too loose for a permit is safe for a refusal. The two land in the same pattern language and must be designed together, which is why they are linked and not merged: their safety arguments are opposite and a single bead would lose that.

Still not a rule over a tool name (ADR-0028 decision 4): curl is a command word in a parsed invocation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A rule can refuse a command carrying a given argument anywhere in its argument list, across invocations of differing length.
- A test that such a refusal beats a widened permit for the same command, through DecisionForInvocation rather than through the store.
- The looser matcher is available to refuse and to ask, and REFUSED for permit: a test that a permit rule cannot be written in the loose form.
- A disqualified invocation still bypasses rules entirely, refusals included, and falls to the row.

title: There is no rule between one exact command and a whole effect class, and the naive one widens the effect
description:
InvocationRule fixes the number of subcommands and the number of tokens in each, and * matches within one token, never "and whatever follows" (internal/content/rules.go:20-26). So df, df -h and df -h / are three separate rules, and df --output=source asks again.

The owner asked for "all df commands" on 2026-09-03 while reviewing the Agent policy page. Today the only wider answer available is the effect row, which permits EVERY observing command, not every df.

The naive widening is unsafe and this bead exists to say why before anyone writes it. DecisionForInvocation applies a matching rule over the row (effectpolicy.go:238-245) and the effect comes from the CONCRETE call, so a trailing-wildcard rule for find would permit find . -delete, which classifies as mutate-destructive, under a permission granted while observing. A widened rule must therefore carry the effect class it was created under and match only invocations classified the same way — otherwise widening a rule silently widens the effect it was granted for.

Deliberately NOT a rule over a tool name (ADR-0028 decision 4): df is a command word in a parsed invocation, not a tool id, and nothing here may name a tool.

Blocks the Agent policy page redesign (nocx-0ykkk): the page has to offer a widening gesture on a saved answer, and it cannot offer one the store cannot hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A rule can cover one command with any arguments, and it is bound to the effect class it was created under.
- A test that the same widened rule does NOT permit an invocation of that command which classifies under a stricter effect.
- A test that a disqualified invocation (redirection, background, unresolved input) still bypasses rules entirely.
- A widened rule is distinguishable from an exact one wherever an answer is shown, because they cover different amounts.
- The prompt still saves EXACT rules only: widening is an operator gesture, never something a person does by clicking Allow always.

title: A destination grant is one exact URL or the whole internet: there is no origin between them
description:
A destination scope holds a full URL (internal/agenttools/registry.go:96 stores u.String()) and Contains compares destinations by exact identity, with one escape: id "*" contains everything (internal/content/resource_scope.go:86).

So the only two grants a person can express for the network are "this exact URL" and "any address at all". "Everything on github.com" — the request the owner made on 2026-09-03 while reviewing the Agent policy page — has no form in the store, and a page cannot offer a gesture the store cannot hold.

The narrow fix is origin containment: https://github.com contains https://github.com/owner/repo. Subdomains are a separate decision and should not be smuggled in with it — *.github.com is a wider grant than github.com and must be said out loud.

Blocks the Agent policy page redesign (nocx-0ykkk): the place picker there offers workspace, session and destination, and destination is the one whose only honest options today are one URL or the whole internet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A destination scope can name an origin, and Contains reports a URL at that origin as inside it.
- Whether a subdomain is inside is decided explicitly and asserted either way.
- "*" keeps its meaning and stays distinguishable from an origin grant on the surface.
- A test that an origin scope does NOT contain a URL at a different origin, including a host that merely shares a suffix (github.com.evil.example).
notes:
2026-09-03, owner decision: subdomains ARE included. A destination scope naming github.com contains api.github.com. Matching is LABEL-WISE, never string-suffix: notgithub.com is outside, and github.com.evil.example is outside because it does not end at a label boundary of .github.com. Still open and deliberately not decided here: whether an https origin contains an http URL at the same host (leaning no — a scheme downgrade is not the same place), what a port does to containment, and whether the stored form is an origin string or a structured value.
Enforcement is in two places, not one: URLScope.Allows (internal/agenttools/registry.go:44-54) compares the raw URL by exact equality with a '*' escape, so an origin taught only to GrantScope.Contains would be shown by the page and ignored by the capability that dials. Origin containment lands in both, with a test that the capability refuses an origin-mismatched URL. Related: the command path has no destination scope at all (see the sibling bead).

title: An out-of-scope resource asks on the invocation path and refuses on the declared path, and the model says only refuse
description:
Two paths answer "the call named a resource outside the row scopes" differently, and the model documentation states only one of them.

- internal/content/effectpolicy.go:246-248 — DecisionForInvocation: a PERMITTED invocation whose named resources fall outside the row scopes returns DecisionAsk.
- internal/assistant/kernel.go:79, 599 — the declared-resource path produces RefusedOutOfScope, a refusal.
- internal/content/effectpolicy.go:61 — EffectRow doc: "a call naming a resource outside the row scopes is refused, never silently re-scoped (ADR-0020 decision 6)". True for the kernel path, false for the invocation path it is written above.

Found while designing the Agent policy page (nocx-0ykkk). It blocks that page: a scope control cannot honestly say what a scope does when the answer depends on which path classified the call, and the person setting the scope cannot see which path they are on.

Not nocx-j5fdf. That bead asks for a row to be able to ESCALATE instead of refusing, which is new behaviour. This one is that the two shipped paths already disagree and the comment records one of them as the rule.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set the "make changes that can be undone" row to permit with one path scope, /workspace.
2. Have the assistant propose a shell command naming a path outside it, e.g. touch /tmp/x. The invocation path (DecisionForInvocation) answers ask.
3. Have a declared tool call resolve a resource outside the same row scopes. The kernel answers RefusedOutOfScope.
4. Read internal/content/effectpolicy.go:61: it states refusal as the rule for both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One stated answer for an out-of-scope resource and both paths give it, or the difference is named in the model as deliberate with the condition that selects each.
- The EffectRow comment matches the code it sits above.
- A test pinning the invocation path and the declared path against the same policy and the same out-of-scope resource, asserting the same stated outcome.

title: A workspace-scoped tool assembles with no sub-scope family, while a content one may not
description:
internal/agenttools/registry.go:806 refuses to assemble a declaration naming content.ResourceContent
unless it also names a ScopeFamily. There is no equivalent rule for content.ResourceWorkspace, so a
workspace-scoped tool assembles with no sub-scope family at all.

The ledger documents a workspace hierarchy exactly parallel to content's: workspace/<id>/tab/<id>/
pane/<id> (internal/content/ledger.go:257-260) beside note/<id>, snippet/<id>, skill/<id>. If the
sub-scope family is a requirement for one hierarchy it is not obviously optional for the other.

This matters now rather than in the abstract: A11 of .internal/specs/2026-09-03-the-waves-authority-
model-design.md decides that a wave PARTICIPANT is addressed as a ResourceWorkspace sub-scope,
precisely because the kind set is closed at eight and content's sub-scoping is the established
precedent. So the first tool to exercise this is a wave tool.

Found 2026-09-03 by the worker fixing nocx-intbc, who flagged it rather than deciding it — correctly,
because it is a design question for nocx-dkawo and widening it inside a one-omission fix would have
been the wrong call.

## Acceptance Criteria

Either a workspace declaration must name a scope family and assembly refuses one that does not, with
a test; or the asymmetry is deliberate and registry.go says in as many words why content needs the
family and workspace does not. Not left as an accident of which kind was implemented first.

title: Quota-exhausted and overloaded draw their own error chrome, and neither is captured
description:
nocx-l5lok added StateError against a captured RETRYING banner — the API unreachable, claude drawing
"Connection refused … · Retrying in 4s · attempt 5/10" in the status stack. That is one class of the
TUI's own error. The design names three more: overloaded, quota exhausted, no connection.

Each draws its own chrome and none is in internal/agentdriver/testdata/captures. The retry branch
matches on "· Retrying in", so an error that does not retry is not detected at all and the pane reads
free_text again — the exact failure l5lok existed to fix, for the classes it could not measure.

Reproducing them is the work: connection-refused was induced by pointing ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at a dead
port, and the others need their own inducement (a 429 or 529 from a stub endpoint should do it, which
is the same technique one layer up).

Do NOT write these branches from a guess about the chrome. The corpus README's first paragraph is the
reason, and l5lok's own measurement is the evidence: the bead predicted the uncaptured frame would
classify as unknown and it classified as free_text.

## Acceptance Criteria

A capture per error class in testdata/captures, taken against a stub endpoint returning the status,
with the README table naming what each holds. The claude rule classifies each as error, and each has
a near-miss test. Whatever cannot be reproduced is named in the README as not covered, rather than
guessed at.

title: nocx-tnx44 needs cross-frame state, which the Driver contract forbids
description:
nocx-tnx44 asks for a progress facet moving|stalled whose predicate is "the TRANSCRIPT stopped
growing", explicitly not frame equality, and says it is "a second question asked of the SAME rule".

The rule cannot answer it as the interface stands. internal/agentdriver/agentdriver.go:102-104 binds
the driver: "It reads only the frame it is given: a driver holds no state between frames, because a
rule that remembers is a rule that can be stuck." Classify takes one panegrid.Frame and returns one
State. Growth is a relation between two frames, so no driver can compute it.

And the Frame cannot help. panegrid.go:84-87 is the whole of a Cell — {Text string, Width int}. No
colour, no styling, no cursor visibility, no scrollback, no "changed since last frame". The package
comment says a verdict computed there would be a third power the AD-6 amendment does not grant.

So one of three has to move, deliberately: the driver gains a memory (and the comment's reason for
forbidding it has to be answered — a rule that remembers is a rule that can be stuck); or the
sequence lives OUTSIDE the driver in paneobserve, which already sweeps frames, with the rule
supplying only "which rows are transcript" as a pure per-frame answer; or tnx44 is re-scoped.

The middle one looks right on the evidence — it keeps the driver stateless, puts the clock where a
clock already is, and matches tnx44's own "which region is transcript is something only the rule
knows". But it is a design decision, not an implementation detail, and tnx44 is written as though the
rule answers it directly.

Found 2026-09-03 planning nocx-ayc4v.

## Steps to Reproduce

Read agentdriver.go:97-105 beside nocx-tnx44's acceptance criteria.

## Acceptance Criteria

tnx44's criteria name where the frame sequence and the clock live, and the Driver contract either
stays stateless or its doc comment answers why it no longer needs to be. Whichever is chosen, the
rule's own contribution stays a pure function of one frame.

title: The session reconciliation pass has no partial-failure test
description:
internal/app/session_reconcile_test.go has call counters but no Nth-call failure injection, so the
pass that decides live / absent / unknown for every carried-over session at startup has never been
watched failing midway.

This is the one place in the repo where that matters most, because session_reconcile.go:228-253 is
where "A FAILURE IS NEVER A VERDICT" is enforced — causeFor cannot return a verdict at all, by type.
The rule is stated and the type backs it; what is missing is the test that a failure PART WAY THROUGH
a multi-session pass leaves the un-judged sessions un-judged and completes them on the next pass.

The house pattern exists and is close by: internal/content/reconcile_test.go:287
(TestARefusedAbsentSweepLeavesNothingHalfJudged) does exactly this one layer down, with a RAISE(ABORT)
trigger on a second connection, a reopen, and "the next pass completes exactly what the first one
could not". internal/shellintegration/publisher_fault_test.go:244 is the discovered-table form.

Found 2026-09-03 writing the spawn-and-register interval (nocx-u0apy), which extends this pass and
names the gap rather than inheriting it.

## Acceptance Criteria

A test that fails the inventory call on the Nth session of a multi-session reconciliation pass and
asserts: the sessions judged before the failure keep their verdicts, the rest stay pending with an
unknown cause, no session anywhere reads absent on the strength of a failure, and a second pass with
the fault healed completes exactly the remainder.

Asserted through a freshly constructed reader over the same path, not through the fake's memory.
close_reason: Committed as fee9b635. Production code is CORRECT — no defect — and that verdict is worth something only because the test was watched failing three ways (a failed ask turned into absent, into live, and the pass aborted on first failure), all six positions red each time, each break reverted. Table discovered from a fault-free pass rather than written; faults the re-adoption path because a held inventory is memoized per id space and cannot fail part way through; every durable assertion reads through a freshly opened store. Constraint recorded for later tests here: a live verdict is memory-only and absent is the only one with a durable trace.

title: D13 requires a foreground-pgid check that ADR-0024 rejects as an authority
description:
Two live documents disagree, and the wave's enrolment design sits on the disagreement.

D13 of .internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-lineage-and-orchestration-design.md requires that nocx
"verifies it belongs to that session's current foreground group" as part of authenticating an enrolling
process.

ADR-0024 lines 122-128 rejects exactly that as an authority, by name: "It answers 'who owns tty input
now', never 'who wrote these bytes' … tmux collapses every pane to one outer pgid, ssh has no local pty
to ask, and set +m puts shell and command in one group." internal/procwatch/procwatch.go:18 cites that
rejection as settled.

The mechanism exists in code (internal/pty/signal_foreground.go:30, internal/transport/foreground_signal.go:60,
internal/helper/proto/session_service.go:322-326) and is used for signals, which is what ADR-0024 permits.
Using it to authenticate is what ADR-0024 refuses.

One of the two has to move, deliberately. Found 2026-09-03 writing the wave authority model (nocx-z3nkr),
which declined to resolve it inside itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

Either D13 drops the foreground-group requirement and names what replaces it, or ADR-0024 is amended to
permit the check under a stated interval with both ends. The losing document says so in its own text, so
a reader of either learns the outcome.

title: Scope expansion refuses where D9 says it should escalate, and the ask has no carrier
description:
D9 of .internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-lineage-and-orchestration-design.md says spawning into an
environment outside the fence is "scope expansion and escalates". Today effectKernel.inScope returning
false produces RefusedOutOfScope (internal/assistant/kernel.go:568-570) — a REFUSAL, not an ASK.

A refusal is the safer default and it is what ships. But the difference matters for the product D9
describes: a coordinator that meets a wall it could have asked a human to move is a coordinator that
stops, and the human never learns there was a question.

The fix must NOT be a special case for one tool. Escalation is a property of how a row treats an
out-of-fence resource, and inventing that inside the wave design would be re-deciding a general
question inside a specific one. Design it where the policy matrix lives.

Named in .internal/specs/2026-09-03-the-waves-authority-model-design.md section 6 and deliberately
left out of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

A row can declare that an out-of-fence resource escalates rather than refuses, expressed once in the
policy matrix and not per tool. A test that an out-of-fence spawn produces an ask carrying the
environment it wants, and that an out-of-fence read still refuses.

Falsified if escalation is implemented as a branch naming a specific tool.
notes:
EVIDENCE NOT FOUND FROM THIS MACHINE, 2026-09-03, recorded rather than reopened.

The close reason names .internal/specs/2026-09-03-assistant-permissions-design.md section 5.3 and a
content.Verdict, 'implemented and merged today'. A worker was dispatched here before that close was
visible (this session had pushed the shared backlog all day and never pulled it — that is the process
miss, and it is mine). On finding the close, the worker was stopped and the following was checked:

  - origin/main: this branch is 0 commits BEHIND it, so whatever main has, this tree has.
  - the spec: absent from this tree, from every remote branch (checked with git ls-tree over each),
    and from all 13 local worktrees plus /home/dev/repos/nocx (checked with find).
  - content.Verdict: does not exist. internal/content has SessionVerdict, which is the
    reconciliation vocabulary and a different thing.

So the work may well exist on a machine this session cannot see — the owner works from a Mac against
this host — in which case nothing is wrong except that the evidence is unverifiable from here. But
AGENTS.md asks a close to name a file, symbol, test or commit a STRANGER can check, and none of the
three named here resolves.

NOT REOPENED: another session closed this deliberately and may hold the work unpushed. Whoever did
should either push it, or point at where it lives, or reopen. If it turns out never to have landed,
the bead's own requirement still stands and the design constraint in it is still the right one:
escalation belongs in the policy matrix, expressed once, never as a branch naming a tool.
close_reason: Superseded by nocx-t6h2u and .internal/specs/2026-09-03-assistant-permissions-design.md §5.3, implemented and merged today. That bead asked for a row to ESCALATE instead of refusing while keeping an out-of-fence read refusing. The accepted design splits on the CAUSE instead: a resource outside an EDITABLE row scope asks and the ask names what fell outside, a resource outside an IMMUTABLE fence refuses because approval cannot make it executable. So an out-of-fence read still refuses, as this bead required, and the escalation it wanted exists — but it is a property of the cause, expressed once in content.Verdict, and not a branch naming a tool, which this bead's own falsification clause forbade.

title: Grant.ExpiresAt is written as zero and never compared to a clock, so "expiring" is nominal
description:
ADR-0020 section 5 defines the authority grant as "a versioned, EXPIRING capability issued to one agent
turn or one execution". The field exists (internal/content/ledger.go:599-605), is persisted
(internal/content/ledger_sqlite.go:842) and is read back (:1530).

But EffectPolicy.AsGrant (internal/content/effectpolicy.go:403-405) returns Grant{Version: 1, Policy:
effective} and never sets it, and runGrantFor (internal/transport/ws_readscreen.go:277-305) is the only
production mint. So every grant in the store has expires_at = 0, and grep finds nothing anywhere that
compares ExpiresAt to a clock. Only tests assign it (ledger_test.go:1085).

This is AGENTS.md's own shape: a field that exists, is written, is read, and governs nothing — the
history-store defect one rung down. Either the ADR's "expiring" is real and something must enforce it,
or the field is dead and should go, with a decision that says why.

Found 2026-09-03 researching the wave authority model (nocx-z3nkr).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run any assistant tool call so a grant is minted and recorded.
2. sqlite: SELECT execution_id, expires_at FROM authority_grants;

Observed: expires_at is 0 for every row. Expected: either a real deadline, or no column.

## Acceptance Criteria

Either a mint sets a deadline and a consumer refuses a grant past it, with a test that watches an
expired grant be refused; or the field is removed and ADR-0020 is amended to drop "expiring", with the
reason recorded. Not left as it is.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED (tightening branch, not removal) — working tree only, uncommitted.

WHERE THE DEADLINE COMES FROM: content.GrantLifetime = 1h, a constant in the house style of DefaultUnreconciledRetention, stamped by EffectPolicy.AsGrant (the one production mint). It bounds ONE TURN, not one command: both ends of a turn re-mint (ws_readscreen.go runGrantFor at the question, ws_agent.go resumeRun at an approval resume), so a long approval never resumes on stale authority. Sizing rationale and the known interaction with settings.AgentRunWallClockMinutes (ceiling 240 min) are written at the constant; the follow-up is nocx-ddqi4.

WHO ENFORCES: the capability CONSTRUCTOR, not a predicate before dispatch. agenttools.withinGrantLifetime wraps every declaration Narrow once, in assemble(), so an expired grant yields no capability at all (content.ErrGrantExpired). This is ADR-0028 decision 4 in its own terms — expiry is the one bound narrowing cannot express as a smaller object, so the constructor declines to construct. The kernel additionally decides RefusedExpired before the attempt is opened, so the model gets a refusal AS AN ANSWER instead of a terminal "construct capability" error; that is the same defence-in-depth shape RefusedByDecision already documents.

A RUN ALREADY STREAMING: a capability handed out while the grant was live keeps working to the end of that call. The deadline refuses the NEXT construction only.

FILES: internal/content/ledger.go (ExpiresAt doc, GrantLifetime, ErrGrantExpired, Grant.Expired), internal/content/effectpolicy.go (AsGrant stamps), internal/agenttools/registry.go (withinGrantLifetime + wrap in assemble), internal/assistant/kernel.go (RefusedExpired + decide + sentence).

TESTS (each paired): internal/content/grant_expiry_test.go, internal/agenttools/narrow_expiry_test.go (incl. every executable declaration), internal/assistant/grant_expiry_test.go, plus TestRunGrantFor_StatesTheDeadline in internal/transport/ws_readscreen_test.go.

ALSO FIXED (mine, outside the brief-stated file allowance, flagged for review): internal/transport/ws_agent_systemprompt_test.go compared two runs grants byte-for-byte; a per-run deadline legitimately differs between runs, so the comparison now normalises ExpiresAt out and asserts the mint stated one.

NO SCHEMA OR CONTRACT CHANGE: authority_grants.expires_at already exists NOT NULL and was already written and read back; no contracts/ schema carries the grant shape.

GATES: gofumpt clean, go vet clean, content + agenttools + assistant + transport green (transport red only on TestOpenRPCManifestMatchesRegisteredMethods / TestParamsContractsAgreeWithRegisteredValidators, which is another worker landing agent.calibration in the same worktree, 205 manifest vs 207 registered).
close_reason: Committed as 3155a3a8. Made the expiry REAL rather than removing it: the deadline is reachable because nothing bounds a single streaming turn in wall-clock terms, and a grant is immutable once execution starts so a mid-run policy edit cannot reach it. GrantLifetime is a constant in the DefaultUnreconciledRetention house style, stamped at the one production mint; it bounds a TURN, not a command, because both ends of a turn already re-mint. Enforcement is the capability CONSTRUCTOR, wrapping every declaration once inside assemble — expiry is the one bound narrowing cannot express as a smaller object since no capability means 'none', so the equivalent is declining to construct. The kernel additionally refuses as an ANSWER before an attempt is opened. A run already streaming is untouched. Paired tests throughout. Filed nocx-ddqi4.

title: A tool declaring ResourceWorkspace fails assembly: the kind set in agenttools is missing one
description:
internal/agenttools/resourcekind.go:16-37 lists allResourceKinds / supportedResourceKind with SEVEN
kinds and omits content.ResourceWorkspace, while the ledger's set (internal/content/ledger.go:244-262)
has EIGHT and the SQL CHECK (internal/content/sqlite.go:826-827) accepts all eight. The comment in
resourcekind.go still says "the same six", so it has been behind twice.

Consequence: validateDeclaration (internal/agenttools/registry.go:801-805) REFUSES ASSEMBLY of any
tool row naming ResourceWorkspace. Nothing declares it today, so nothing is red — this is a trap laid
for the next workspace- or wave-scoped tool, which is exactly what nocx-dkawo needs.

Found 2026-09-03 researching the wave authority model (nocx-z3nkr).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add ResourceKinds: []content.ResourceKind{content.ResourceWorkspace} to any row in the
   declarations table in internal/agenttools/registry.go.
2. Run the agenttools assembly tests.

Observed: assembly fails. Expected: it assembles, because the ledger and the store both accept the kind.

## Acceptance Criteria

allResourceKinds and supportedResourceKind cover every member of the ledger's ResourceKind set, and a
test fails if the two sets ever diverge again rather than a comment claiming they agree.
close_reason: Fixed as b29b1990. ResourceWorkspace added to allResourceKinds and supportedResourceKind, stale 'the same six' comment removed. The guard is the point: resourcekind_test.go parses internal/content/*.go with go/ast and measures agenttools against the ledger's own constants rather than restating them — a third copy would rot as the second did — following internal/notify/catalogue_test.go including its no-constants-found guard. Both divergence directions watched failing before the fix. Discovered nocx-zjyh1 on the way: ResourceContent requires a ScopeFamily at assembly and ResourceWorkspace requires nothing, though the hierarchies are parallel.

title: Step 7: transition to writing-plans
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

writing-plans invoked, or the amendments folded into nocx-z3nkr's brief.
close_reason: Transition is not writing-plans: the spec feeds nocx-z3nkr, which the owner directed as the next work. UI design (nocx-5azf0, jv3q, edhcu.1, ms7v.4 and the parity checklist in nocx-dg51h) deferred by the owner until a first wave runs.

title: A relay-mode connection that falls back to a plain shell says nothing: the session path has no helper refusal
description:
Found while fixing nocx-bzac4.

helperRegistry.OpenHosted decides whether the helper hosts the PTY. When the platform
probe fails for ANY reason it returns `(HostedSessionOpen{}, false, nil)` — not
selected, no error, nothing said — and the transport falls through to the ordinary
open. The user gets a plain SSH shell.

For a connection whose Delivery mode is `relay`, that is an explicit choice the product
silently did not honour. The Git panel path is honest about the same failure: it
returns a GitOpenRefusal carrying `unsupportedPlatform` or `execForbidden` with a
message naming the recovery (helperProbeRefusal). The session path has no equivalent —
there is no refusal channel on the open ack for it, and no fact is published.

nocx-bzac4 widened the set of destinations that reach this arm: the probe now dials with
the connection-password prompt suppressed (a probe may not stop a person), so a
password-only destination with nothing remembered yet fails the probe and takes this
path on its FIRST open. It succeeds on the second, once the password is stored — which
is a defensible degrade, and is exactly the kind that must be visible rather than
inferred.

AGENTS.md: "A soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log." Today it
is not even in a log.

## Steps to Reproduce

Set a saved SSH connection's Delivery mode to Relay, on a host whose platform the
matrix does not ship (or block exec on it). Open a tab: it opens as a plain shell with
no indication the helper was refused.

## Acceptance Criteria

A relay-mode connection whose helper selection was refused says so in the product —
the same vocabulary the Git panel already uses (unsupportedPlatform / execForbidden /
deployFailed) — and an automated check watches a user see it.

title: Every remote open dials the destination twice: the helper platform probe's connection is closed before the session's own
description:
Found while fixing nocx-bzac4.

internal/app.probeHelperPlatformAt takes a DiscoveryConn lease to decide whether the
helper may host the PTY. On the OPEN path (helperRegistry.OpenHosted) that lease is the
ONLY reference on the pooled connection, so ConnPool.Release closes it as soon as the
decision is made (internal/ssh/pool.go, "pool connection closed (last ref)"). The
session's own Connect then dials, authenticates and handshakes a second time.

Every remote tab therefore costs two TCP connections, two key exchanges and two
authentications against the far sshd. The git path does not pay this: it probes on a
session that already holds a pool reference, so the probe shares it (AD-4 — the
DiscoveryConn doc comment says exactly this).

nocx-bzac4 fixed the user-visible half — the second dial was raising a second
connection-password prompt in front of a user who had already answered — by suppressing
the prompt rung on the probe. The second dial itself is still there.

The fix is to share one connection across the decision and the open: hold the probe's
lease until the session has taken its own reference. Only the transport's open handler
knows when the fall-through open finished, so the releaser has to travel back through
the HelperSessionOpener seam — which crosses into internal/transport and was
deliberately out of scope for the bugfix.

## Steps to Reproduce

Open any SSH profile against a server that logs authentications (cmd/e2e-sshd, or a
real sshd with LogLevel VERBOSE). One tab produces two successful authentications.

## Acceptance Criteria

A Go test at the open seam counts the destination's accepted authentications across one
open and asserts exactly one.

title: TestLifecycleChanged_DeadSessionGetsNoRecoveryClaim fails reproducibly under -count=2 and passes under -count=1
description:
Split out of nocx-e8w5 during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh, before its sibling nocx-klsl was closed into it. Both of those are 'transport notification tests time out under container load' beads, and this observation was buried inside one of them where it would have been read as another load flake and never looked at.

It is not a load flake. e8w5 recorded it as: the test additionally fails REPRODUCIBLY under -count=2 while passing under -count=1. That is in-process, deterministic, and involves no clock and no container — a test that is not idempotent within one binary, which means state survives between the two runs that should not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. go test -tags gtk3 -count=1 -run TestLifecycleChanged_DeadSessionGetsNoRecoveryClaim ./internal/transport/  — passes.
2. go test -tags gtk3 -count=2 -run TestLifecycleChanged_DeadSessionGetsNoRecoveryClaim ./internal/transport/  — the second iteration fails.
3. Observed: reproducible, on one machine, with no container and no parallel load. Not yet re-measured since the nocx-td6d4 wave (commits 13ac6a3f, 9a736ee8, 39c52646) rewrote this package's waits, so confirm it still reproduces before investigating.
acceptance_criteria: go test -count=2 -run TestLifecycleChanged_DeadSessionGetsNoRecoveryClaim ./internal/transport/ passes, and the reason it did not is named — which state was carried between the two runs, and who owns resetting it. Not fixed by widening a timeout. If it no longer reproduces, close with the run that shows it.

title: TestRunLease_WallClockTerminalizesAndTheLedgerNamesIt arms a 1500ms clock and then does its setup
description:
`TestRunLease_WallClockTerminalizesAndTheLedgerNamesIt` arms a 1500 ms
wall-clock lease and only then does its setup: submit the command into a real
session, read the child's pid file, and wait for the child to be alive
(`internal/transport/ws_run_lease_test.go:705-726`). Every one of those steps is
work, and none of it stops the clock. When the machine is loaded the lease fires
during the setup, the run terminalizes before the test has established there is
anything to cancel, and the assertions that follow are about a run that ended
for the right reason at the wrong time.

Reproduced on 2026-09-02: one failure in four runs of
`go test -count=5 -race ./internal/transport/ -run 'TestParkedRun|TestRunLease'`.
The other three passed, and `-count=1 -race` over the whole package passes. On
`origin/main` the same repeated run passes — but that proves nothing about the
test, only that the neighbouring load differs: `main` has fewer tests matching
that `-run` pattern, so the machine is quieter when this one runs.

This is the class AGENTS.md forbids by name — "a test may not depend on timing.
Wait on an observable state change — a frame, a record, a DOM state — never on a
duration. A spec that needs a slow machine to pass is broken on a fast one too;
it has only not been caught yet." It is the same family as `nocx-ubd2q`
(`TestLocalPty_SignalForegroundReachesTheExecution`), which cost a red PR on an
unrelated diff twice in five days.

The fix is not a bigger number. 1500 ms buys nothing if the setup can take
1500 ms; it just moves the threshold. The bound must not start counting until
the thing it is supposed to bound is actually running — arm the lease after the
child is confirmed alive, or hold the clock until the observable precondition
the test already waits for (`waitChildAlive`) is true.

Not caused by nocx-6dzxq, checked: that branch's diff against `origin/main` in
this file changes one comment on a DIFFERENT test's `WallClock` line and touches
neither this test's timings nor its body. What the branch did was add tests that
run beside it, which is load, not causation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `go test -count=5 -race ./internal/transport/ -run 'TestParkedRun|TestRunLease'`
2. Repeat. Roughly one run in four fails with
   `--- FAIL: TestRunLease_WallClockTerminalizesAndTheLedgerNamesIt`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The lease's wall clock is not armed until the execution it bounds is observably
  running; the test states which observable event that is.
- 200 consecutive runs under `-race` on a machine also running the rest of the
  package are green — asserted by actually doing it once, and the count recorded
  in the close reason.
- No assertion in the test depends on a duration elapsing; every wait is on a
  state change.
- The sibling tests in this file that arm a short bound before doing setup are
  audited in the same pass and listed, fixed or explicitly cleared.

title: Two helper-hosted tabs on one host make every reconciliation on that host ambiguous
description:
Found by reading while building nocx-k6p18.30.

helperRegistry.hosts is keyed by session id and holds ONE hostHelper per session
— that is the design (D4, and the comment says so: two sessions to the same host
each get their own helper). inventories() then returns one helperSessionInventory
per entry, each carrying that helper's generation, host and account.

Two helper-hosted sessions on the SAME host therefore produce TWO inventories with
the SAME {generation, host, account}. reconcileSessions' ownership scan matches
both, counts matches == 2, and answers unknown/ambiguousInventory with "multiple
inventories claim this session id space" — for every carried-over session on that
host, for ever.

That branch was written for a broken ownership map ("a condition that can only
arise from a bug is the one that must be loud", nocx-k6p18.15). Two tabs to one
host is not a bug; it is the ordinary case. So the loud condition fires on a
correct state, and the recordings of every session on a two-tab host are held to
the retention age instead of being judged.

nocx-k6p18.30 does not hit it on the startup pass — helperRegistry.hosts is empty
at that point and re-adoption's inventories are consulted one session at a time,
never appended to the shared set — so this is about LATER passes and about any
pass run once tabs are open.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open two helper-hosted tabs to the same host, same account, same generation.
2. Run reconcileSessions with helperReg.inventories() (a later pass, or any pass
   after the tabs exist) over a carried-over session on that host.
3. Verdict is unknown/ambiguousInventory rather than live or absent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two sessions on one host produce ONE inventory for that {generation, host,
  account}, or the ownership scan treats agreeing inventories as one owner.
- ambiguousInventory still fires for inventories that genuinely disagree — the
  loud condition must not be quietly widened into silence.
- A test opens two hosted sessions on one host and reconciles a third carried-over
  one, asserting a real verdict.

title: A helper-hosted session's factory carries no host-key fingerprint, so an uninstall never closes its channel
description:
Found by reading while building nocx-k6p18.30, and it predates it.

helperRegistry.OpenHosted builds its sessionFactory WITHOUT `fp` — the machine's
host-key fingerprint, which is the consent key and the key D25's uninstall closes
channels by (internal/app/helper_git.go, the literal at the OpenHosted spawn).
The git-panel path (helperGitFactory's selection) DOES set it, from
sess.HostKeyFingerprint().

Two consequences, both silent:

- CloseHelpersFor(fp) matches on h.f.fp, so an uninstall of that machine does not
  close a helper-hosted TAB's channel before deleting the directory the helper
  runs from. D25's own sentence is "no helper may be running out of a directory
  being deleted".
- isClosing(f.fp) is asked with "", which is never in the closing set, so a
  helper-hosted session's git open is not frozen during an uninstall either.

nocx-k6p18.30's re-adoption leaves it empty too, deliberately and for consistency:
it now has the fingerprint durably (sessions.payload carries it) and setting it on
only one of the two paths would be two behaviours for one concept. Fixing this
means setting it on BOTH.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a helper-hosted tab on a machine (not the git panel — the tab itself).
2. Uninstall the helper for that machine from the footprint surface.
3. The tab's helper channel is not closed first, and the install directory is
   removed under a running process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- OpenHosted's sessionFactory carries the probed fingerprint, and so does
  re-adoption's (it has it on the binding).
- A test watches CloseHelpersFor close a helper-hosted SESSION's channel, not
  only a git binding's — the existing TestHelperCloseHelpersForClosesOnlyTheMachine
  proves the git half and would not have caught this.

title: A live tab is not told about a hole the execution host's window left; only the recording is
description:
Found while doing nocx-k6p18.25.

The helper's bounded output window can be reclaimed past this coordinator, and
the bytes in between reach nobody. The coordinator now records that as a Gap
with its own bounds and reason (content.GapReasonHostWindow), so a client that
READS THE RECORDING back -- a reclaim, session.output -- is told exactly what is
missing and who took it.

A LIVE tab is not. internal/transport's ringToConn steps over the hole and goes
on sending (ws.go, 'session output pump stepped over a hole'), so the renderer
splices two non-adjacent stretches of output and nothing on screen says so. It is
the same soft degrade AGENTS.md names, one surface further along.

The reason it was not fixed with the rest: this carrier has NO mid-stream reset
shape at all. The renderer's only reset is answered at attach (contracts,
ipc.ts), so telling a live tab means a new wire shape across contracts, transport
and the renderer -- a deliberate design, not a line in a bugfix.

Deliberately NOT the fix: writing nocx's own text into the byte stream. That was
tried in nocx-k6p18.25 and rejected: session.output's contract says the backend
hands back what the session printed and never interprets it (AD-6), and injected
bytes are replayed out of a recording for ever as though the shell had printed
them.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a tab on a helper-hosted host and watch it live.
2. Make the coordinator fall behind the helper's window (a large burst plus a
   slow renderer), so the helper reclaims past it and sends EventSessionReset.
3. Watch the tab: output before the hole and output after it are drawn as one
   continuous screen, with no statement that anything is missing.
4. Reclaim the same session in a new window: the recovery notice DOES report the
   hole, from session.output's gaps. The two surfaces disagree about the same
   session.

## Acceptance Criteria

A live subscriber crossing a hole is told, in the product and not only in a log,
that output is missing and how much -- through a control-plane shape, never by
bytes injected into the stream. The renderer resets its decoder across the hole
for the same reason the recording's reader does. An automated check watches a
live tab meet a reset and report it.

title: The zsh bootstrap-write failure path leaks the lifecycle socketpair's child fd
description:
Found 2026-09-02 by an adversarial second reading of feat/relay-pty-owner.

internal/helper/session/spawn_local.go:135-146. Every other failure arm closes
BOTH ends of the lifecycle socketpair (:99-107, :122-134). This one closes
lifecycleParent and returns without closing lifecycleChild. launch.Cleanup --
which the code deliberately composed at :110-116 to close exactly this fd -- is
not called here either.

## Steps to Reproduce

A zsh login shell (the only kind with a non-empty launch.Bootstrap,
internal/shellintegration/launcher_local.go:319), with req.Lifecycle != nil, where
lp.Write(". /dev/fd/3\n") fails -- a PTY master that closed under us because the
shell exec'd and died immediately: a bad Cwd, a missing binary.

Observed: one socketpair descriptor leaks per occurrence, in a daemon that lives
as long as the host session does. Expected: the arm closes both ends like its
three siblings.
acceptance_criteria:
A spawner test with a Process whose Write errors asserts the open-fd count is
unchanged across the failed spawn. Removing the close again turns that named test
red.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-09-02, verified by the coordinator. Commit aebd6874.

Four failure arms had four hand-written unwinds and one of them had drifted --
which is the actual defect, the missing close being its symptom. All four now call
one `release()` closure defined before the first thing that can fail.

The instrument is `launch.Abort()` plus explicit closes of both socketpair ends,
NOT `launch.Cleanup`, and the distinction is real: Cleanup is composed for the
SUCCESS path, where an exec has already duplicated the child end into the shell,
so it closes only the script pipe's reader and leaves the writer goroutine to
drain. Abort closes the writer, waits for that goroutine, then the reader -- the
correct half when there is no shell to deliver a script to. My brief pointed at
Cleanup; the worker read both and used the other one, and it is right.

THE SEAM IT HAD TO OPEN, and the hazard it found on the way. The bootstrap write
cannot be made to fail with a real terminal -- a PTY master refuses a write only
once its slave has no openers, which is a race against the shell's exec and would
have been a timing-dependent test, which AGENTS.md forbids outright. So the pty
constructor became an unexported field returning a new `localPTY` interface. That
interface is DELIBERATELY wider than session.Process, because service.go reaches
SignalProcessGroup, Cwd and ProcessGroup by TYPE ASSERTION: an interface omitting
Dir/SignalProcessGroup would still compile and would silently stop the helper
signalling a job on the host. TestLocalProcess_KeepsTheAssertedSeams pins all
four. The constructor also returns through a named nil, because a
(*pty.LocalPty)(nil) handed back as an interface is not nil.

The invariant is stated as the span -- no descriptor this function opened outlives
a failed spawn, on ANY arm -- not as "both ends are closed on this arm". The table
drives two arms; the other two are not provokable in-process (they fail only when
the kernel refuses a socketpair or a pipe) and now run the same unwind. One
warm-up spawn precedes the measurement so lazy runtime opens do not pollute the
delta.

MY OWN MUTATION, a different end from the worker's two: deleting the
lifecyclePARENT close from release(). Both subtests go red --
  the_PTY_never_starts: leaked 1 descriptor(s): 8 open before, 9 after
  the_bootstrap_write_fails: leaked 1 descriptor(s): 10 open before, 11 after
so the sibling arm is load-bearing rather than passing along. Reverted; tree
byte-identical; ./internal/helper/... green.

NOT VERIFIED: the deadcode ratchet and macOS, both CI-only jobs.

title: A domain widening offers only suffixes of the actual host, cut at the public suffix
description:
A command naming a host is the one widening where the obvious generalization is
catastrophic: `*.com`. The epic's bound is that a domain widening offers only
SUFFIXES OF THE ACTUAL HOST, cut at the public suffix — so `api.github.com` offers
`api.github.com` and `*.github.com` and stops there.

Needs a public suffix list. `golang.org/x/net/publicsuffix` is the ordinary answer
and is already in the module graph's neighbourhood (x/crypto is a direct
dependency); confirm before adding, and if it is a new direct dependency say so in
the commit body rather than letting it arrive silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- For a resource whose path is a URL or SSH destination, the menu from .4 contains
  the host itself and each suffix above it down to — and not including — the
  public suffix; asserted on `api.github.com`, `a.b.co.uk` and a bare `localhost`.
- No option is ever produced at or above the public suffix: one test enumerates
  the menu for `x.com`, `x.co.uk` and `x.github.io` and asserts the public-suffix
  option is absent from all three.
- An IP-literal destination offers only itself.

title: The animal stands half outside the pane at the ends of its ground
description:
Seen by the owner on 2026-09-02 (screenshot: the cat in the bottom-left corner, clipped by the window and smeared) and confirmed by a rAF probe, which recorded the world transform at x = -29.

`pet.x` is the animal's centre; a ledge's `x0`/`x1` are the ends of the BLOCK. The walk is clamped to `[x0, x1]`, so at either end half the body hangs past its ground.

## The criterion this bead was first written with was WRONG, and the correction is the point

It said "a ledge too narrow to hold the whole animal is not offered as terrain at all". Measured on a live stand at 1400px with six commands, standard pet (petWidth 94): inserting half a body at each end raises the width a candidate needs from 72px to 166px, and EVERY chip drops out of the landscape — 84, 77, 64, 53, 52, 44px wide. `.pane.active .nocx-chip` is in DEFAULT_LEDGES deliberately, so that rule deletes a part of the world on purpose built. At the maximum pet size the threshold becomes 252px and nothing but full-width command blocks survives; the animal would live on the floor, which is the state this whole epic exists to cure.

Two overhangs, and only one of them is a defect:

- Over the PANE's own edge the body is cut off by the window. Half the animal is simply not there. That is what the owner photographed.
- Over a BLOCK's or a chip's edge the body is fully visible, hanging over nothing. That is what a real cat on a small object looks like, and it is not a defect.

So the body-width inset belongs to the FLOOR — the pane's own edges — and nowhere else. Block and chip ledges keep the geometry they had: the element's span less the existing 8px inset, with `minWidth` unchanged at 56. There is then no double count, because the body is subtracted exactly where hanging over means disappearing.

## Success Criteria

- The whole drawn animal is inside the pane in every frame, at the standard and the maximum pet size.
- The number of usable candidates on a real pane is unchanged by this bead: chips are still ground.
- Overhanging the end of a block or a chip stays legal, and no test forbids it.
- Stepping off an edge still leaves AT the edge, so the drop still lands on the blocks below rather than always on the floor.
close_reason: Landed as fb2a9901. Measured on the live stand: teleport gone (was dy=3117 to y=-3589 on an output burst, now no jump on scroll, 41px on a burst, 66px on a 700px window resize); the sprite never leaves the pane (was 31px outside, now 0); cornered by a fast cursor, zero land phases and zero distinct positions over four seconds.

title: A finished command can freeze its block and record nothing: the attempt binds to no app-owned record
description:
Seen red on PR #174 (run 33631538213, ci-e2e webkit) at
e2e/notification-centre-choice.spec.ts:178 — badge "1", expected "2", 61 polls
over 30 s. The change under review was a renderer repaint and cannot reach
this path. CI runs e2e with `workers: 1` (playwright.config.ts:102), so no
other spec was touching the shared stand.

## The evidence chain, from the trace artefact

Reconstructed from the trace's DOM snapshots and console log (t = Playwright
clock, ms):

1. Baseline after mark-all-read: bells=1, finished=47, unread=0.
2. t=411441..411513 pane A's command ends. Session data arrives in chunks
   1, 83, 18, 39, 16 (the 1 byte is the BEL).
3. t=411509 A's Terminal bell row appears; t=411580, 71 ms later, A's
   Command finished row appears. unread=2. The gateA site passes.
4. t=411976 mark-all-read. unread=0.
5. t=412160 the click on tab C; gateB is written right after.
6. t=412307..412354 pane B's command ends. The same chunk shape:
   1, 83, 10, 8, 39, 16.
7. B's Terminal bell row appears. Its Command finished row NEVER does: at
