   t=442229 the list holds "primary webkit" (pane A's command) once and
   "secondary webkit" (pane B's) zero times, finished is still 48.

So the command ran, ended, and the shell printed its next prompt.

## Where the loss is NOT

- Not a lost lifecycle completion. Every command block in the final DOM is
  accounted for: two frozen with `exit 1` (panes A and B) and exactly one
  still running, in pane 3 — pane C, whose gate was never written. Pane B's
  block FROZE, so its authenticated completion arrived and the kernel
  derived it.
- Not a refused establishment. Our three sessions (18958389…, aafb508d…,
  5ad0018c…) each logged a clean "lifecycle channel established" and drew no
  refusal. The `e-publisher` refusals in the log (14 across 191 sessions)
  belong to earlier tests.
- Not cross-spec interference on the shared feed: single worker, and in the
  30 s window the feed received exactly one event.
- Not machine slowness in general: A's two paths were 71 ms apart.

## Where the loss is

`LifecycleProjections.pump` (frontend/src/lifecycle/projections.ts:183-190):

    const rec = this.ledger.complete(attempt)
    if (attempt.state === 'completed') {
      if (rec !== null) void this.persist(rec, attempt)   // history.record
      this.blocks.freezeBlock(attempt)                    // the exit chip
    }

The block freezes on the attempt alone; the record is persisted only when the
attempt bound to an app-owned ledger record. `rec === null` therefore produces
EXACTLY the observed combination: a block frozen with a real exit status, no
history row, and no block.finished notification — the backend raises it only
on a landed history.record (internal/transport/ws_history_record.go:471).

The binding is first-fit (frontend/src/command-ledger.ts:140):

    const pending = this._records.find(
      (r) => r.status === 'running' && !this._boundRecordIds().has(r.id))
    if (pending === undefined) return null

Two ways to get null for a command a person actually submitted: the published
attempt arrives before the submit's record exists, or the record was already
claimed by an earlier attempt. Either classes an app-owned submit as
shell-originated, which is the one case designed to persist nothing (its line
may carry a literal password).

DEDUCED, NOT YET MEASURED: that this is the branch taken in the recorded
failure. It is the only code path that yields a frozen block with no row, but
no instrumentation in the artefact names it.

Second consequence, worse than the missing notification and not yet
confirmed: a record left `running` and unbound stays first-fit for the NEXT
attempt, which would persist it under the following command's outcome.

## Reproduction

- Not reproducible on demand. A full webkit suite in the CI container passed
  it (8.1 s); the spec alone passes 5/5.
- `--repeat-each --workers=2` produces a DIFFERENT failure (badge too high,
  copies of the spec inflating a shared feed). Not this defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- A unit test at the projections seam demonstrates the state: an attempt that
  completes with no bound record freezes its block and persists nothing.
- The decision is taken and recorded: either an app-owned submit's record can
  never fail to bind (close the race), or the failure to bind is VISIBLE
  rather than silent. A finished block the history and the notification centre
  never learn about is the soft degrade AGENTS.md forbids.
- Whichever is chosen, the stranded `running` record cannot be claimed by a
  later attempt.
- e2e/notification-centre-choice.spec.ts gains the observable its neighbour
  already uses (notification-block-finished.spec.ts waits for the finished
  BLOCK before asserting the row, and reads unread off the row rather than a
  global badge number), so the next occurrence says which half failed.
notes:
2026-09-02. The fix is decided and it is not a design question: bind the app-owned ledger record to the published attempt BY ID, the way the assistant lane already does, instead of re-deriving the pairing by first-fit.

Two facts settle it. First, the correlation already half-exists: lifecycle.submitAttempt takes a client-minted requestId (contracts/lifecycle.submitAttempt.params.schema.json) and ws_lifecycle.go:523 uses it to bind a run to an attempt by equality -- but only when source is assistant. The human's Enter passes nothing, so the same question has two answers in one codebase: by id for the agent, by guess for the person. The guess is what breaks.

Second, keeping the id from the submitAttempt RESPONSE is not enough: Publisher.SubmitAttempt calls publishLane BEFORE the handler writes r.TryResult, and the handler does masking, EnsureEnvironment and ledger.Submit in between -- so the published attempt reaches the renderer before the response that names it. The token must travel INTO the call and come back ON the attempt.

Shape of the fix: the renderer mints a submit token at submit and keeps it on the ledger record; lifecycle.submitAttempt carries it; the kernel stores it on the ExecutionAttempt; the publisher echoes it on the published fact and in the result; the renderer binds by equality and never searches. attempt.origin === 'app' with no matching token is then a contradiction, and must be visible rather than silently taking the shell-originated branch that persists nothing.

Attempt IDENTITY stays server-minted (ADR-0024 decision 5); the token is correlation only, like the agent path's requestId. ADR-0024 constraint b is about the SHELL-minted id and is untouched. Fail-open is preserved: a refused submitAttempt leaves no token, no attempt, a conventional session, and the bytes still go out.

Also fixed by the same change: a stranded record left 'running' can no longer be claimed by a later attempt, because nothing matches by position any more.

Owner decided against an ADR: this is a bug, not a decision.

2026-09-02, implemented. Branch fix/attempt-record-binding, PR #176, two commits:
a468a550 the binding fix across contracts, Go and the renderer; 3631fedc the
spec's diagnostic wait.

Red first, and the red is worse than the report it came from: with the
projection binding by position, a record left behind by a REFUSED
lifecycle.submitAttempt (fail-open, the bytes still go out) is claimed by the
next command's attempt, so one command's exit status is stored under another
command's text. Deterministic, no race.

Verified: frontend typecheck, eslint, ratchets, prettier, 5891 tests;
contracts:check; Go gofmt, vet and the tests for internal/transport (DTO and
over-the-wire contracts), internal/lifecycle, internal/lifecyclepub,
internal/lifecycleremote. Dropping the echo from the publisher projection
turns the publisher test red, checked by hand. The amended e2e spec passes in
the CI container under webkit and chromium.

NOT run, by AGENTS.md (the integrator's, on the merged tree): make ci-full,
the containerized jobs, the full e2e suite. Not merged.
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #176 (commits a468a550 + 3631fedc, merge e0409582). A submit now carries its own correlation token: minted into the ledger record, sent on lifecycle.submitAttempt, kept on the kernel attempt, echoed on the published fact and the result. Binding is an equality, never a first-fit search, so a record left behind by a refused fail-open submit can no longer be claimed by the next command's attempt — which was storing one command's exit status under another's text. The e2e spec now waits for the block the ledger closed before asking the bell, so the next occurrence of anything like this names which half failed.

title: Two panes, one pet: the animal watches whichever command spoke last
description:
The window has one pet and every pane talks to it directly. The pet's state
carries only an Author -- no pane, no attempt, no command identity -- so with
two commands in flight the rule is "last event wins", and that rule is
nowhere in the design.

Found by review on 2026-09-02. Splits are Phase 2 in docs/architecture.md, so
this is reachable today only through tabs; it becomes visible the moment two
panes are on screen at once.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long command in pane A.
2. In pane B, run a short one and let it finish.
3. Watch the pet: `data-watching` on `.pet-layer` goes to `nothing` while the
   command in A is still running.

`react` clears `attending`; the controller in B then looks only at its OWN
running block (controller.ts, `_settleFrozen`), finds none, and does not put
the animal back to watching A.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A command finishing in one pane does not end the pet's attention to a
  command still running in another.
- Attention names WHAT is being watched, not merely whose lane it is in, so
  "is this still running" cannot be asked of the wrong pane.
- Two commands finishing out of order each get their own answer, and neither
  is swallowed.
- A test drives two panes with overlapping commands; today there is none.

title: The animal does not repeat itself
description:
The menu is drawn afresh every time with the same weights, so the same occupation can come up three times running. Uniformity reads as noise, not as character.

Remember the last two activities and damp their weight to between zero and a quarter. Sitting, lying, sleeping and watching are exempt -- a cat sitting twice is a cat.

Also give the conspicuous choices a budget: jumping, running and turning together should not exceed about two a minute of unattended behaviour. In a terminal the animal is permanently in peripheral vision, and one noticeable action a minute feels far more frequent than the number suggests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Over hundreds of seeded minutes, no non-exempt activity ever occurs twice in a row.
- Conspicuous events stay under the budget at the 95th percentile.
- The distribution is still recognisably the mood's: damping must not flatten a worried cat into a calm one.
close_reason: Last two occupations damped to 0 and 0.25, sit/lie/sleep exempt, watching menu untouched. Conspicuous budget ~2 per rolling minute held as ages advanced by dt. An exhausted budget never forces something more visible: an edge turn is unavoidable so it is uncharged rather than forbidden, and walking is damped instead. Idle pause is a 0.4-2.0s range drawn per cycle. Committed 1da218cd.

title: Three frames of air instead of eight of running
description:
A falling animal plays the run cycle, because no falling was drawn. Eight frames of running in mid-air is worse than one still frame.

Name three frames in the pack -- rising, apex, falling -- chosen from the sheets that exist, and hold them by vertical speed instead of cycling. Tilt the body 3-5 degrees with the sign of vy. An ordinary step down should not use the jump's anticipation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No walk or run cycle advances while the animal is off the ground.
- The frame follows the sign and magnitude of vy.
- A pack that names no air frames still works, holding one frame rather than cycling.
close_reason: Pack names rise/apex/fall frames; airborne pose chosen by sign and size of vy, clip clock frozen off the ground, body tilts up to 4 deg on the expressive layer. A pack naming none holds one frame. Indices reasoned, not seen — comment says so. Committed 1da218cd.

title: The pointer is not a binary threat
description:
Any cursor inside the radius means flight. A cursor that arrives slowly, or sits still nearby, is not the same event as one that lunges, and treating them alike is why the animal never seems to notice you -- only to escape you.

Keep a little history of the pointer: speed, approach speed, dwell. Fast entry or movement straight at it -> flee. Slow approach -> turn and watch. Still for 0.5-1.0s nearby -> sit. Directly over the body but motionless -> step aside rather than bolt. Repeated calm encounters lower the threat for a while.

All of it from the same passive pointermove; the layer still takes no events.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A slow approach does not produce a run.
- A fast approach still does, within 150ms.
- The layer's pointer-events stays none, and no listener is added to a pane.
close_reason: Pointer history (speed, closing speed, dwell) derived in the pure step from position and dt; the overlay still only reports a position. One alarm decision, remembered on the state. Lunge -> flee, slow approach -> turn and watch, still nearby -> sit, motionless on the body -> step aside. Calm encounters raise the threshold. Cornered-at-the-edge now asks whether the pointer is alarming, not merely near. Committed b4ef2ce1.

title: Walking at the speed the drawing walks
description:
The position advances at 60fps and the sprite changes at 10fps, so unless walkSpeed happens to match the pace the artist drew, the feet slide. Nothing today ties them together, and the numbers were chosen by eye.

Measure how far the animal travels in one cycle of the source walk and run, make that the base speed, and drive the clip's rate from the actual speed rather than the intent. Add acceleration over 100-250ms so it does not start and stop instantly, and slow the clip with it -- easing the position alone makes the sliding worse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At the gait's contact frames the world position of the foot moves less than one source pixel per frame.
- Starting and stopping take at least 100ms.
- Changing pets.size does not reintroduce sliding.
close_reason: Stride declared in body lengths per cycle (walk 1, run 3), body length taken from the loader's trim; speed = stride/cycle duration x display scale, so pets.size cannot reintroduce sliding. 180ms gait ramp through a signed vx, clip rate tied to actual speed via the shared gaitSpeed. Committed a07896cd.

Measure how far the animal travels in one cycle of the source walk and run, make that the base speed, and drive the clip's rate from the actual speed rather than the intent. Add acceleration over 100-250ms so it does not start and stop instantly, and slow the clip with it -- easing the position alone makes the sliding worse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At the gait's contact frames the world position of the foot moves less than one source pixel per frame.
- Starting and stopping take at least 100ms.
- Changing pets.size does not reintroduce sliding.

title: Two webkit e2e specs fail intermittently: a refusal toast and a remote pre-commit hook
description:
e2e/snippets.spec.ts:355 ('a snippet whose secret cannot be resolved refuses, and
writes nothing') and e2e/git-remote.spec.ts:248 ('a commit from the panel, on a
remote host, through its own pre-commit hook') fail intermittently under webkit.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take any commit whose diff touches no frontend runtime code and no e2e code.
2. Run ci-e2e (webkit) on it — in CI, or `PW_PROJECTS=webkit e2e/run-in-container.sh`.
3. Observed: the two specs above fail, snippets.spec.ts:355 the more often.
4. Rerun the same job on the same commit, changing nothing.
5. Observed: it passes.

Expected: two runs of one commit agree.

## The evidence that it is a flake, not a regression

2026-09-02, PR #172 (nocx-364y7) — a five-file change touching only
internal/assistant, internal/transport and a generated prompt artifact:

- ci-e2e (webkit) FAILED on both specs. Run 33614386740.
- The same commit, rerun with nothing changed: PASSED.

snippets.spec.ts:355 also failed in the local container on two unrelated
branches (nocx-sizd4 on 2026-09-01, and this one) while ci-e2e (webkit) was
green on both of those PRs. It is the more frequent of the two.

## What it is not

Ruled out by reading diffs, not by assumption:

- Not that branch: it changes no line under frontend/ runtime or e2e/.
- Not PR #169, merged into main immediately before: `git diff cce042e1..3cb68c51`
  touches neither frontend/src/ui/toast.ts nor its stylesheet nor any snippet path.

## Where to look

snippets.spec.ts:355 fails at line 371 waiting for `.ui-toast__message` filtered
on 'could not be resolved' — "element(s) not found", 10s timeout. So the refusal
toast either never rendered or had already been dismissed when the assertion ran.
A toast with a lifetime is a duration the spec is racing, which is the shape
AGENTS.md forbids: wait on an observable state change, never on a duration. Check
whether the toast auto-dismisses, and whether the refusal can be observed
somewhere that does not expire.

git-remote.spec.ts:248 failed at 7.6s in the same run and has not been seen
failing locally. It needs its own look and may be a different cause.

## Why a bead rather than a rerun habit

A suite that is retried until green stops being a gate. Two specs that fail on a
change which cannot have caused them will be blamed on the next innocent branch
too — this one cost an investigation already.
acceptance_criteria: Both specs wait on an observable state change rather than on a duration, and ten consecutive ci-e2e (webkit) runs of the same commit are green. Not satisfied by raising a timeout.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-6wgcw, which already names snippets.spec.ts:355 among the twelve specs that fail in the mixed containerised run. Third filing of this phenomenon — nocx-3f1yq was closed the same way on 2026-09-01. The genuinely new data (CI's own webkit job failing, then passing on rerun of the same commit; git-remote.spec.ts:248 as a spec not previously named) is appended to nocx-6wgcw.

title: A pet lives on the command blocks
description:
Owner asked for a live prototype in the real app before the design doc is
written (brainstorming BS5-BS10 are still open, deliberately).

A CC0 cat (luizmelo Pet Cats) walks the ledges the terminal already has --
the top edge of each frozen command block -- and what it does follows the
outcome of commands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Terrain is derived from block rectangles by a pure function: a ledge is
  produced only when it has head clearance above it, and the function is
  tested without a DOM.
- The pet's state machine is pure and tested: locomotion, mood and activity
  are three separate axes, so a mood never multiplies the locomotion states.
- A block that disappears under the pet drops it into `fall`; it never
  teleports to another ledge.
- The overlay reads geometry from a snapshot refreshed by observers, never
  by calling getBoundingClientRect per frame.
- The vendored pack carries its own LICENSE and a provenance note naming
  source URL, date and SHA-256.
- Running `make dev-web`, a command's success visibly changes what the pet
  does.

## Deliberately out

BYOP pack import, the Shimeji importer, a settings surface beyond on/off,
e2e coverage. Those wait for the design doc.

title: The renderer collapses a shell completion function into a path, and names its failure as an SSH config failure
description:
Two renderer-side losses of fidelity on the shell.complete contract, both found
while reviewing nocx-7jujk's parked patch and fixed in the same commit as that
bead because they sit in the lines the cancellation work already touched.

1. contracts/shell.complete.schema.json declares `source: 'path' | 'command' |
   'function'` and says in the schema's own prose that the UI uses it "to
   distinguish an adapter answer from a local guess and to show the appropriate
   evidence column". shellCompleteProvider mapped it
   `e.source === 'command' ? 'command' : 'path'`, so every candidate a remote
   bash COMPLETION FUNCTION produced was badged `path` — a claim about the
   remote filesystem that the backend never made.

2. When the adapter answered with a reason, the provider surfaced it as
   `hosts-unavailable`, whose message vocabulary is the degraded `ssh -G`
   resolver. A remote shell whose completion failed was reported to the user as
   SSH CONFIG trouble, which sends them to look at the wrong thing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an SSH session and type a line whose completion a bash completion
   function serves (`git checkout ma`, with git's completion installed on the
   remote).
2. The dropdown badges every row `path`, though no path was involved.
3. Break the remote adapter (an unreachable host, a shell with no completion
   machinery) and repeat: the empty row reads in the `ssh -G` resolver's
   vocabulary, blaming SSH configuration for a completion failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A candidate whose entry says `source: 'function'` carries that source and is
  badged as its own kind, not as a path.
- A completion failure is named as a completion failure. The `ssh -G` message
  vocabulary is reserved for the host resolver.
- Both are asserted by a test.
close_reason: Landed in the same commit as nocx-7jujk (7e9ad0c7), in the lines that bead already touched. A candidate whose shell.complete entry says source 'function' now carries that source and is badged 'function' in the dropdown, instead of being collapsed to 'path' — a claim about the remote filesystem the backend never made. A completion failure is named as one (kind 'completion-unavailable') instead of borrowing the 'ssh -G' host resolver's vocabulary. Both asserted by tests in providers.test.ts, controller.test.ts and completion-dropdown.test.ts. A withdrawn query stays silent: reason 'cancelled' is not surfaced as a failure.

title: Brainstorming: pets in the terminal
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Design doc written to .internal/specs/ and approved by the owner

title: A feed's own XML declaration names its encoding, and nothing reads it
description:
Measured on the branch for nocx-sizd4.2, with a probe against golang.org/x/net/html/charset:

    ct="text/xml"                            -> <?xml encoding="windows-1251"?>...Ïðèâåò
    ct="text/xml; charset=windows-1251"      -> <?xml encoding="windows-1251"?>...Привет

charset.NewReader sniffs a <meta charset> out of an HTML prologue and does NOT
read an XML declaration. So a feed served as text/xml whose ONLY encoding
statement is <?xml version="1.0" encoding="windows-1251"?> — which is the
ordinary shape of a legacy RSS feed — decodes as latin-1 mojibake and no error
is raised anywhere. Silent corruption, not a refusal.

nocx-sizd4.2 is not wrong: it honours the header charset and the HTML meta, and
that is what its brief named. This is the third place an encoding can be
declared and the only one nothing reads.

## Steps to Reproduce

Serve a body of windows-1251 bytes as Content-Type: text/xml with no charset
parameter, whose first line is an XML declaration naming windows-1251. FetchText
returns text; the Cyrillic in it is wrong.

## Where it belongs

With the feed work (nocx-sizd4.5), which is already parsing the XML prologue —
one owner for 'what does this document say it is', per AGENTS.md. Do not add a
second sniffer beside charset.NewReader: extend the one decode path so the
declaration is consulted when the header is silent, and state the precedence
(header wins over declaration wins over sniff) in a comment.

Precedence matters and must be tested: a header charset that CONTRADICTS the XML
declaration keeps winning, because the transport layer is closer to the truth
than the document's opinion of itself.
acceptance_criteria: A windows-1251 body served as text/xml with no header charset, whose XML declaration names windows-1251, decodes to correct Cyrillic. A body whose header charset contradicts its XML declaration decodes by the header. A feed with no declaration and no header charset is unchanged from today.
close_reason: decodeText now consults the XML declaration when the header is silent, through the ONE existing decode path — no second sniffer beside charset.NewReader. Precedence stated in a comment and tested: header charset beats the XML declaration beats content sniffing; a header contradicting the declaration keeps winning because the transport is closer to the truth than the document's opinion of itself. An unsupported charset named by a declaration is refused by name, as a header one already was. Commits bcfdbb22 and e2fdefae.

title: Two webkit e2e specs pass alone and fail under full-suite load
description:
Both fail only when the whole webkit project runs, and both pass when their file is run on its own in the same container image.

  e2e/secret-panel-position.spec.ts:361 - a field further down the form opens its panel at ITS OWN offset
  e2e/snippets.spec.ts:355 - a snippet whose secret cannot be resolved refuses, and writes nothing

Measured 2026-09-01 on feat/ai-skills at 9f446541, e2e/run-in-container.sh with PW_PROJECTS=webkit: 251 passed, these 2 failed. Re-running snippets.spec.ts (with connections-settings.spec.ts, which failed the same way in an earlier loaded run) alone: 6 passed. Chromium runs the whole suite green - 253/253.

Both failures are the same shape and it is the shape that matters: expect(locator).toBeVisible() reaching its 10s timeout with 'element(s) not found'. Not a wrong value, not a changed selector - something that should have appeared did not appear in time, on a box that was also running another agent's containerized CI job. AGENTS.md is explicit that this is a defect in the test rather than in the machine: 'a test may not depend on timing. Wait on an observable state change - a frame, a record, a DOM state - never on a duration. A spec that needs a slow machine to pass is broken on a fast one too; it has only not been caught yet.'

Neither spec is touched by the skills epic (nocx-si0dh): one is the secret panel's vertical offset, the other is snippet secret resolution refusing to write.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. PW_PROJECTS=webkit ./e2e/run-in-container.sh, ideally with another containerized job running.
2. Watch those two fail.
3. PW_PROJECTS=webkit ./e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/snippets.spec.ts - green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the two specs names the observable state it waits on, and neither waits on a duration or on 'it will have happened by now'.
- PW_PROJECTS=webkit ./e2e/run-in-container.sh is green with a second containerized job running concurrently - the condition under which they were measured failing.
- The same two spec files are still green run alone, so the fix did not trade one environment for the other.
- No timeout is raised to buy the pass; if a wait is genuinely long, what it waits FOR is stated rather than how long.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-6wgcw, which I failed to check for before filing — the five-checks rule in AGENTS.md exists for exactly this and I skipped it. nocx-6wgcw already names secret-panel-position AND snippets among the twelve specs that fail in the mixed containerised run ON ORIGIN/MAIN at ac06a437, while passing in every single-project configuration. That settles what I filed mine to ask: the two webkit failures on feat/ai-skills at 9f446541 are pre-existing and environmental, not the skills epic's. My run adds one data point to that bead's table — webkit-only, 251 passed, 2 failed (secret-panel-position:361, snippets:355), on a box concurrently running another agent's ci-linux.sh — which is consistent with its finding that a different subset fails per run under load. Related: nocx-n26p1, nocx-it6m, nocx-rj81l are the same phenomenon on other specs.

title: Lazy tool presentation and the search tool are unreachable: nothing sets AskParams.Presentation
description:
Found while diagnosing nocx-364y7 (the "Noted." bug): part of the reason the
model has every schema in front of it is that the lazy catalog never turns on.

`AskParams.Presentation` (assistant/assistant.go:266) is the switch. Every
assignment to it in the tree is in `internal/assistant/tools_presentation_test.go`
(:36, :64) — the transport builds AskParams at ws_agent.go:1246 and does not set
it. So in the shipped product `p.Presentation` is always nil, `mw.presentation`
stays the zero value, `Lazy` is false, and `Registry.Project` returns every
eligible tool. The `search` tool goes with it: engine.go:435 offers it only
`if p.Presentation != nil && p.Presentation.Lazy`, so a schema and a registry
entry exist for a tool the model is never given.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -rn "Presentation" --include=*.go internal/ cmd/ | grep -v _test`
2. Every hit is a declaration or a nil check. There is no assignment.
3. Run an ask and count the tool schemas the model receives: all of them.

## Why the gates did not catch it

The AGENTS.md shape exactly: a reachable read path hiding an unreachable branch.
`Project` IS live — the middleware calls it every turn — so deadcode reports
nothing, and it never could: RTA marks methods reached through an interface as
reflection-reachable, and this is a live function whose `if lazy` arm is dead,
which is finer-grained than deadcode sees at all. The four tests in
tools_presentation_test.go pass because each one sets Presentation itself.
Testing rule 2: the epic that shipped this (nocx-0h66x, closed) had no check
that watched a person get an answer with the catalog on.

## What to decide, not just fix

Wiring it is one line, and that is the trap — DefaultSchemaTokenLimit is 4096 and
the default essential set is {files.read, session.read}, so flipping it hides
notes.*, snippets.*, fetch.url, git.status and session.run behind a search the
model must think to call. On a small local model (google/gemma-4-26b-a4b is what
surfaced nocx-364y7) that is likely to make tool use worse, not better. So this
bead is: decide whether lazy presentation ships, measure it against a real ask on
a small model, and then either wire it with an end-to-end check that watches a
person get an answer through the catalog, or delete it and its schema.

Deleting is a legitimate outcome. What is not legitimate is leaving a switch, a
tool, a contract and four tests for a feature the product cannot reach.
acceptance_criteria: Either an ask through cmd/nocx-server is answered with the catalog on — the model receives the essential set, calls search, loads a hidden tool and uses it — or lazy presentation, the search tool, its schema and its tests are deleted. Not a third state.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-7icvn, filed 2026-08-30 and describing the same defect (AskParams.Presentation has no production caller). Its acceptance criterion and the token measurement are carried over to nocx-7icvn; work that bead.

title: JSON and HTML arrive in the shape a reader can use
description:
Two remaining shapes from the same dispatch:

JSON — pretty-printed rather than one line, so a window boundary lands somewhere legible.

HTML — extracted to text. Today the package comment says markup is retained deliberately, 'no lossy HTML extraction is hidden from the model'. That was honest when the bound was a hard refusal and lossy was pinned false; it stops being the right default once lossy is a real field the result can set, because 64 KiB of <script> and <style> is not an honest representation of a page either — it is the page's boilerplate, chosen by position.

Local extraction only. omp's five-backend reader chain (native/trafilatura/lynx/parallel/jina) is explicitly out — we have no reader backend and are not acquiring one. golang.org/x/net/html is already a direct dependency and is enough to drop script/style/nav and keep the text.

Set lossy=true when extraction ran, and update the package comment and the schema description, which both currently promise the opposite.
acceptance_criteria: A JSON response comes back indented. An HTML page comes back as its text with script and style content absent, lossy=true. The package comment and the schema description no longer claim markup is retained.
close_reason: JSON is indented (by content type OR a first non-space { or [, the same by-the-bytes rule apifetch.Fetch already uses); a body claiming JSON that does not parse comes back unchanged. HTML is extracted to text with script/style/noscript/comment content gone and block elements producing line breaks, via golang.org/x/net/html — no new module, no external reader service. Extraction sets lossy. THE lossy DECISION, made deliberately: one field now carries both meanings and the schema description was rewritten to say so, rather than adding a second field. The apifetch package comment and TextDocument doc comment, which both promised markup is retained, were corrected. One end-to-end test goes through the real FetchText. Commit 014d1739; coordinator follow-up c433ca37 renamed feed.go to render.go (it stopped being about feeds) and removed a test-only wrapper the dead-code ratchet would have reported.

title: An RSS or Atom feed reads as a list of items, not as XML markup
description:
A feed returned as raw XML spends the tool's whole byte bound on markup and namespace declarations, and the model has to parse a document format to answer 'what is the news'.

omp's dispatch (fetch.ts:1288-1350) is the shape: a feed is a Content-Type containing rss/atom/feed, OR an XML content type whose body contains <rss or <feed — the second test is what makes habr work, because habr sends text/xml. parseFeedToMarkdown (:519) then renders title, pubDate, description and link per item.

golang.org/x/net/html is already a direct dependency; no new module.

Do not silently drop items to fit a bound — that interacts with the window work (nocx-sizd4.3), and a feed rendered short must say so through the same truncated/remaining fields, not by quietly ending early.
acceptance_criteria: The habr feed comes back as a titled list of items with links and dates, and the raw XML markup is not in the output. A malformed feed falls back to the raw text rather than erroring.
close_reason: internal/assistant/feed.go renders RSS and Atom to markdown — title heading, then per item title/date/description/link, capped at 10 with the cap stated in the output rather than silently applied. Dispatch is oh-my-pi's rule including the second clause that matters: an xml content type whose body contains <rss or <feed, which is what makes habr work since it sends text/xml and nothing else. Shape is decided in ONE place, in the assistant, with a comment saying apifetch owns acquisition and must not grow a second shape rule. Rendering happens at snapshot time, so total and the window offsets describe the rendered document. A document that parses as neither RSS nor Atom, and a malformed one, both fall back to raw text. Commits 53986319 and e2fdefae.

title: The mark offer appears mid-drag, and a second row mark replaces the first
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Drag across some output. The "Mark N lines" button appears while the
   pointer is still down, naming a range that is still growing.
2. Mark one line, then select a different line and mark that. The chip still
   counts 1 — the second mark replaced the first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The offer is made once the gesture ends, not during it; a keyboard
  selection, which has no gesture, still offers immediately.
- Several row marks on the SAME block coexist and the chip counts them all.
- Marking the whole block subsumes its row marks rather than sending the same
  rows twice.
close_reason: Fixed and covered on fix/assistant-bugs

title: Tool calls should expand to show what was sent and what came back
acceptance_criteria: A person can expand a tool call in an answer and see the arguments the model sent and the result the tool returned, without leaving the pane; a long result is bounded on screen the way an answer's other long content is, and nothing that the masking owner hides in a durable record is revealed here.
notes:
WHAT EXISTS TODAY. A tool call that opens no block draws one child row whose header is toolCallTitle(): the tool name plus its arguments as key=value (src/scrollback/tool-call-title.ts, built from AnswerToolCall in scrollback/blocks.ts:404). The arguments ARE shown — that part of the ask is already met, modulo readability (nocx-hp8p2.12).

WHAT IS MISSING, and it is not a rendering choice. AnswerToolCall carries callId, tool, effect, args, resource, opensBlock — and no RESULT. The tool's return value never reaches the renderer at all, so 'what came back' cannot be drawn from anything currently on the wire. This is a contract change: a new field or a companion notification on agent.runToolCall, its schema in contracts/, the generated renderer type, and the Go side validated against it.

TWO THINGS THAT MUST BE DECIDED, not assumed:
- MASKING. internal/content's frameText comment records that the durable record is masked by one owner (nocx-a21v). A tool result shown in the pane must not become a second, unmasked path to the same bytes.
- SIZE. A session.read result is a whole screen; agent-tool bounds already cap what the MODEL receives (toolBound MaxBytes). The renderer needs its own bound, or one answer can carry megabytes of DOM.

DISCLOSURE, once the data is there: the answer already has a disclosure vocabulary — createReasoningNote (the collapsible Thinking note, expanded per setting). A tool call's expansion should reuse it rather than invent a second collapsible.

REPORTED WITH: a screenshot of `session.read session=* Claude Code id=att-cf87c40a4ab68275`, which is also what nocx-hp8p2.12 fixes.
close_reason: The tool result is now the action entry's own body (ADR-0040 had left 'action' the one block kind with no artifact): written through CaptureOutput so retention/sensitivity/criticality gate it, after the egress gate and masked by internal/masking as a belt for the approved-resume case, and skipped for a call that opens a block. The renderer expands a call on demand via ledger.get + ledger.artifact, reusing the answer's disclosure — ReasoningNote generalised to Disclosure with data-kind, the tool-result body height-capped so a long result scrolls rather than being cut. Commit 90280ef2.

title: Ordered list markers split across two lines in an answer
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant something it answers with a NUMBERED list.

Observed: every item renders as two rows — the digit alone on one, then the
period and the item's text on the next. Bulleted lists are fine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A numbered item renders on one row, marker and text together, for one- and
  two-digit numbers alike.
- The hanging indent still lines every item's text up in one column.
- Bulleted lists are unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed and covered on fix/assistant-bugs

title: The prompt offers the frozen screen without saying the question is about it
acceptance_criteria: When a frozen screen is attached, the system prompt states that the person is looking at that screen as they ask, that the question is about it unless they say otherwise, that a bare deictic points at it, and that reading it comes before answering.
close_reason: Fixed and covered on fix/assistant-bugs

title: A program that clears the screen loses its first line to the echo shift
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `top` (any program that clears the screen and repaints from home).
2. Look at the top of its running block.

Observed: the first line of the program's own output is missing — `top`'s
`top - HH:MM:SS up ... load average: ...` header never appears, while every
row below it is there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A full-viewport program that clears the screen shows its FIRST output row
  in the running block.
- An ordinary command still hides the shell's echo of itself: the running
  block and the frozen one start on the same line.
- Neither behaviour depends on a clear event, since a program that merely
  overwrites the echo row emits none.
close_reason: Fixed and covered on fix/assistant-bugs

title: An answer seated over a running command lands above the command's own output
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a full-screen program (`top`) and summon the assistant over it.
2. Ask something and get an answer.
3. Press Escape (or the new close button) while the program is STILL RUNNING.

Observed: the answer is seated between the command's header and the program's
own live output — the reply appears to have been spliced into the middle of
`top`. Quitting `top` restores the expected order, which is what shows the
seating itself is right and only the live region's position is wrong.

Expected: the program's output stays with its command, and the assistant's
replies sit below all of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An answer seated while its command is still running appears BELOW that
  command's live output, not between the command and it.
- A command started after that answer opens below the answer, not above it —
  the ordering must hold for the next command too, which is what makes the
  naive fix (seat after the live container) wrong.
- The order does not change when the command finishes: what a person saw
  during the run is what they keep.
notes:
THE CAUSE IS AN INVARIANT, NOT A LINE.

_seatSummonedAnswers (src/terminal-content.ts) inserts each answer right after the command's element: insertBefore(answer.el, anchor.nextSibling). That is correct for a FINISHED command. For a running one it is not, because the program's output is not in the block — it is in .xterm-live-container, which BlockManager keeps as the last child of .scrollback-inner (blocks.ts _own(el, this._xtermContainer): every new block is inserted BEFORE it). So 'after the command block' is necessarily 'above the live output'.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG. Seating the answer after the live container puts it last and looks right — until the next command opens, which _own also inserts before the live container, i.e. ABOVE the answer that was already seated. The reply then floats above a command that came after it.

WHAT THE ORDERING ACTUALLY REQUIRES. The live region has to belong to the RUNNING BLOCK — sitting immediately after the block whose output it is — rather than being permanently last in the scrollback. Then anything seated later goes below it and stays below it, and a new command opens below that. That is a change to blocks.ts's placement invariant ('the one door into .scrollback-inner'), not to the seating call, so it wants its own pass and its own test.

WHAT THE OWNER SEES TODAY, and it is the evidence the seating itself is fine: quitting top restores the expected order, because the freeze moves the rows into the block and the live container empties.
close_reason: The live region now belongs to the block whose output it is: it sits immediately after that block, and everything the manager opens goes at the tail below it. Seating anchors on the block's tail. Both halves were needed — either alone breaks the other direction. Commit ae4dac66.

title: A selection inside the frozen screen cannot be attached
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Summon the assistant over a running full-screen program (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter).
2. Select a few characters or rows inside the FROZEN SCREEN.

Observed: nothing is offered and nothing is attached — the chip still counts
zero person marks. The same gesture inside a scrollback block does offer to
mark it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A selection inside the frozen screen offers the same mark affordance a
  scrollback selection does, and accepting it attaches those ROWS.
- What travels is the automatic attachment's own id plus `start`/`count`, so
  the model reads exactly the selected band rather than the whole screen —
  no second attachment and no copied text on the wire.
- The selected rows are painted as granted, the way `.term-line` rows are in
  a block.
- Dismissing the row mark leaves the automatic whole-screen attachment intact.
notes:
WHERE IT STOPS, both barriers in the same event.

1. grantBlockFromSelection (src/ask-entry.ts:44) resolves a selection through blockOf, which is `closest('.cmd-block')`. The frozen screen is .nocx-freeze-frame inside the live container, not a block, so the mark is never built.
2. onSelectionChange (src/terminal-content.ts:766) then requires scrollback.scrollbackInner.contains(grant.blockEl) before it shows the affordance. The frame is not in the scrollback either.

WHY IT SURFACED ONLY NOW. The frame was pointer-events:none until nocx-hp8p2.6 made it scrollable — there was no selection to attach. Enabling the wheel enabled the gesture, and the gesture leads nowhere.

THE MECHANISM IS ALREADY THERE, end to end: GrantBlock carries start/count, agent-ask puts them on the wire, and for an AUTOMATIC item the backend turns them into a FrameRegion (internal/assistant/blocks.go executeSessionItemScreen -> executeSessionScreen, region when count > 0), which the renderer answers from the pinned frame. So the row mark needs no new contract — it is the automatic attachment's own id plus a row span.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING
- Row indices from a selection in the frame: .nocx-freeze-frame__row children, start = index of the first, count = how many the range spans.
- The affordance's containment check has to accept the frame, not only scrollbackInner.
- GrantController.repaintBlocks paints .term-line rows; a frame's rows are .nocx-freeze-frame__row, so the granted paint finds nothing to mark.
- The automatic whole-screen attachment must survive a row mark being added and dismissed — they are one item id with and without a span, which grant.ts currently keeps in two separate lists (blocks vs automaticBlock).
close_reason: The frozen screen is a second markable surface: a selection in it narrows the automatic attachment (its own id plus a row span), counted and painted as a person mark, dismissable back to the whole screen. grantRows is the one owner of which rows a mark covers; applyMarkedWindow is the one owner of a mark bounding a read. Commit 37f0473d.

title: readScreen ships cells nobody reads: send the frame as text rows
acceptance_criteria: A readScreen resolution for a full screen is bounded by its TEXT, not by its cell grid: the ~880 KB an 80x200 screen costs today falls to the order of its 9 KB of characters, measured in a test that captures a full-width screen and asserts the resolution size. No consumer loses anything: session.read still returns the same Text, and the ledger still records the same frameText.
notes:
WHAT WAS MEASURED (2026-09-01, the owner's live stand). A session.read over a running `top` produced a resolution of 878,536 bytes. The same screen as text is ~9 KB: a screen is ~200x44 cells and each cell travels as its own object with attributes.

NOBODY READS THE ATTRIBUTES, on either path.
 - pull: internal/assistant/blocks.go:355 joins cell.Char per row into sessionReadResult.Text. No attribute reaches the model.
 - push: internal/content/ledger_agent_sqlite.go:341 frameText does the same, and says so — 'the cells' ATTRIBUTES are not retained ... the renderer keeps the full cells for drawing'.
The renderer needs the cells to DRAW, and it has them locally; the wire carries them for nothing.

WHY IT IS NEARLY WIRED ALREADY. frameRowWire has a {kind:'text', text} variant and BOTH backend consumers already handle it in the first branch of their loop. What refuses it is validateLiveFrameBody (internal/transport/ws_agent.go:2248): for a live frame it requires kind=='cells' and exactly identity.cols of them. That check is the whole of the work on the Go side, plus a shape bound for a text row.

SCOPE. contracts/ schema for agent.readScreenResolved (and agent.captureFrame if it goes too), the generated renderer types, validateLiveFrameBody, liveFrameToWire on the renderer, tests both sides. A contract change — AGENTS.md says change it deliberately.

RUNNING BLOCKS RIDE THIS PATH TOO. A finished block is already read as plain text from the store (ws_blocks.go blockBody). A RUNNING block's session.read goes to executeSessionItemScreen -> readScreen, so it pays the same cost.

DISCOVERED FROM nocx-hp8p2.4, where a frame refused on the ingress ('cursor is out of bounds') killed a run. Size was not that defect's cause, but the same over-large payload is what made the refusal expensive.
close_reason: A live frame row is its text on the wire: 1,497,189 bytes of cell grid for a full screen becomes 9,945 of characters. Contract, generated type, validateLiveFrameBody and liveFrameToWire changed together; the cells vocabulary is gone from the transport rather than left accepted beside the text one. session.read's Text is byte-for-byte unchanged. Commit 3f09ffed.

title: A session without shell integration never emits OSC 133 B, so the automatic attachment has no handback to baseline against
description:
The automatic frozen-frame attachment baselines its "newer bytes" test on the screen
handback, which closes on the OSC 133 B marker that nocx.bash appends to PS1
(nocx-7l4ex.21, b8449b69).

A session with no shell integration never emits B. The baseline therefore stays where
the block froze, and the shell's own prompt bytes read as newer again — so a finished
command that printed anything is attached to the model under the sentence calling it
the current screen of a full-screen program.

This is the pre-fix behaviour for such sessions rather than a new regression, and it
was reported by the worker that shipped the fix rather than discovered later. Filed so
it does not live only in a commit body.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a pane whose shell has no nocx shell integration, so no OSC 133 A/B is emitted.
2. Run a command that prints something, and let it finish.
3. With the editor visible at the prompt, press Ctrl+Enter to flip to Ask.
4. The grant chip reads "frozen screen attached automatically" and the finished
   command reaches the model. Expected: nothing is attached — nothing is painting.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A session with no shell integration does not attach a finished command on the
  visible-editor Ask flip.
- The rule that decides it is named in code with both ends of its interval, the way
  the B-based one is.
- A test covers the no-integration case; it fails without the change and for its own
  reason.

title: The Files panel says when it has stopped keeping up, and stays silent when it is merely pacing itself
description:
Split out of nocx-8hdia.3 after a design consultation (codex, 2026-09-01)
established that the honest carrier for this is a NEW notification, which means
a contracts/ schema, a generated frontend type, a backend emit path and a
frontend surface — a different kind of work from the scheduler itself, and one
that cannot even be written until the scheduler exists to detect the condition.

nocx-8hdia.3 bounds one dispatch to one path with per-path due times. The
consequence it must state honestly is that at 512 watched paths, exact
freshness, bounded load and full enumeration cannot all hold: when the scheduler
falls behind, it prefers stale-but-responsive over continuous load. This bead is
the half that keeps that from being a SILENT degrade — the thing AGENTS.md
forbids ("a soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log").

## What a person gets

A Files panel that says so when it has actually stopped keeping up, and says
nothing at all when it is merely pacing itself — which is almost always.

## The threshold, declared

60 seconds of VISIBLE, refresh-eligible time without a successful observation of
some eligible path. The number is grounded rather than invented: routine idle
polling caps at 10s and the failure ladder caps at 60s, so ordinary round-robin
deferral lights nothing, while work that cannot complete inside the whole
failure envelope does.

HIDDEN TIME MUST NOT COUNT, and a hidden->visible edge gives the catch-up pass a
fresh window. Otherwise a panel hidden for an hour warns before its first
catch-up attempt has even been made.

## The carrier, and why nothing existing works

  files.refreshStateChanged { bindingId, state: "ok" | "delayed" }

A NOTIFICATION, not a callable. Nothing else crosses the wire — no paths, no
queue depths, no ladder positions, no internal errors. Binding-level state,
emitted only on the threshold-crossing and recovery EDGES, and re-emitted on
attach and on a reconnecting files.watch (AD-9: a reconnect must not lose a
state the user can see).

Why not something that exists, each checked:

- files.changed means "this directory is dirty, re-list it", not "we could not
  observe it" (contracts/files.changed.schema.json:5).
- files.watch.degradedReason is provider ESTABLISHMENT mode — local live
  watching fell back to polling — and explicitly excludes designed remote
  polling (contracts/files.watch.schema.json:10).
- A files.watch RESPONSE cannot report a transition that happens minutes after
  the request.
- control.saturated describes a different failure.

## The surface

Reuse the sticky inline message and Retry that already exist for stopped refresh
(frontend/src/files/files-store.ts:263, frontend/src/files/files-view.tsx:664).

NOT the Polling badge: its shared judgment deliberately hides routine and
designed polling (frontend/src/ui/watch-badge.tsx:54), and this bead's whole
point is that routine pacing stays invisible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A binding that misses the declared threshold while visible reports "delayed",
  and one that recovers reports "ok"; both on the EDGE only, never repeatedly.
- Hidden time does not count toward the threshold, and a panel that becomes
  visible after a long hide gets a fresh window before it may warn. Asserted.
- The wire shape is declared once in contracts/ with additionalProperties false
  and an explicit required; the renderer's type is GENERATED from it and the Go
  side validated against it, including a test that validates the REAL
  notification off the REAL socket, not a payload the test built.
- A reconnect re-delivers the current state, so a panel that was showing
  "delayed" still shows it after an AD-9 reconnect.
- Routine round-robin deferral at the ceiling produces NO notification at all.
  This is the criterion that keeps the feature honest and it must be asserted
  with the watch set at its ceiling.
- One automated check watches a person see it: with the scheduler unable to keep
  up, the panel shows the message; when it catches up, the message goes.
- Not in scope: the scheduler itself (nocx-8hdia.3), and any per-path detail on
  the wire.
close_reason:
Landed as 5679f1ff. This closes the epic: the trade-off nocx-8hdia.3 stated in a
comment is now stated in the product.

ONE BIT ON THE WIRE. files.refreshStateChanged { bindingId, state: "ok" |
"delayed" } — no path, no queue depth, no ladder position, no timing, no provider
error text. A NOTIFICATION rather than a callable, because it is a transition
nobody asked about. Edges only, never repeated while a state holds. Re-sent on
attach, so an AD-9 reconnect can neither leave a withdrawn warning on screen nor
drop one the server still means.

WHY NOT AN EXISTING CARRIER, recorded in the schema so it is not re-derived:
files.changed means "this directory is dirty, re-list it", not "I could not
observe it"; files.watch.degradedReason is provider ESTABLISHMENT and explicitly
excludes designed remote polling; a files.watch RESPONSE cannot report a
transition minutes after its request; control.saturated is a different failure.
The next person seeing a fifth files.* wire shape gets the answer in the file.

THE THRESHOLD IS DERIVED, not picked: 60s of VISIBLE, refresh-eligible time,
because routine idle polling tops out at 20x500ms = 10s and the failure ladder at
120x500ms = 60s. Ordinary round-robin deferral therefore lights nothing, while
work that cannot finish inside the whole failure envelope does. Hidden time does
not count and a visibility edge grants a fresh window — without that, a panel
hidden overnight warns before its first catch-up attempt exists.

THE SURFACE IS THE ONE THAT EXISTS: the sticky inline message with Retry, not the
Polling badge, whose shared judgement deliberately hides routine and designed
polling — which is precisely this bead's point. Two facts now share that strip
(the watch could not be established / the loop is not keeping up); they differ in
cause and not in consequence, and the comment says so.

THE THREE CONTRACT CHECKS ARE ALL PRESENT, including the one that matters: the
real notification validated off the real socket, which also exercises the
reconnect replay rather than a payload the test built.

TWO SEND-BACKS, both about reasoning that was not written down — the schema had
no record of the rejected carriers, and a two-condition guard sat under a
one-condition comment. I made the last edit myself rather than sending a third
time: the worker's rewrite had dropped the original argument for a sticky message
("a toast cannot answer 'why is this stale?' ten minutes later" — the argument is
about TIME, and the replacement lost that), and restoring text I had already
quoted needed no worker context. That edit changed the user-facing string, which
broke the test asserting it — the test was RIGHT to assert it; I updated both.

VERIFIED: the focused -race pass the worker's advisor asked for, run by me —
TestFilesRefreshState|TestFilesPoll, EXIT=0, no races. 66 tests green in
files-view.test.tsx after my edit. contracts:check, golangci-lint, gofumpt,
eslint, tsc and prettier all clean, plus the full pre-commit static gate.

NOT RUN, deliberately: make ci-full, the containerized jobs and e2e belong to
whoever integrates, on the merged tree.

title: A change arriving during a dirty flush is erased by the flush that did not deliver it
description:
Found while implementing nocx-8hdia.6; not part of that work and reverted from it.

filesWatcher keeps a `dirty` map (path -> rev known when it went dirty) for
changes that arrive while no subscriber is attached, and flushes it when one
appears (AD-9 reconnect). The flush SNAPSHOTS the map, delivers, and then clears
it unconditionally.

A mutation landing between the snapshot and the clear is therefore erased: the
entry it wrote is removed by a clear that was deciding about the OLDER entry it
replaced. Nothing re-announces it, because the poll loop's baseline for that path
was already advanced when the change was first detected — filesPollPath writes
w.paths[path] = listing.Rev before emitting. So the rev the loop compares against
already matches what is on disk, and the change is invisible to every subsequent
poll.

## What the person sees

A Files panel showing a stale listing after a reconnect, with no files.changed
replay, until something else changes in that directory or they refresh by hand.
The window is small — it needs a mutation inside one flush — but the loss is
PERMANENT, which is the wrong direction: nocx-8hdia.5 established that the safe
direction is a false positive (a redundant re-list), never a false negative.

## Steps to reproduce (needs a wedge)

1. Watch a directory and drop the subscriber, so changes accumulate in `dirty`.
2. Reattach a subscriber to start the flush.
3. Mutate the watched directory between the flush's snapshot and its clear.
4. No files.changed is ever delivered for step 3.

## The shape of the fix, not yet decided

The reverted attempt carried a per-path generation counter (`dirtyGeneration
map[string]uint64`) so a clear only removes the entry it actually delivered.
That is one answer; a swap-and-replace of the whole map under the lock is
another and may be simpler. Decide it with the interval stated at BOTH ends
(AGENTS.md rule 3): the entry exists from the moment the change is detected
until the notification for THAT change has been handed to a subscriber.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A mutation arriving during a dirty flush is delivered, not erased.
- Asserted by a test that wedges the flush between its snapshot and its clear,
  not by inspection.
- The existing reconnect-replay behaviour is unchanged for the ordinary case.

title: Migrate the four assistant specs onto e2e/ask-gesture.ts
description:
nocx-hp8p2.2 extracted the ask/grant gesture into e2e/ask-gesture.ts because it
would otherwise have been the FIFTH copy of the same six helpers: flip the input
target with the real chord, select a block's output, press the offer, read the
grant chip, send the line, read the model's system prompt back off the fake.

The four specs that own the existing copies were NOT migrated in that bead, and
the reason is scope rather than taste: the brief for nocx-hp8p2.2 scopes the
verification budget to one new spec on a shared, contended test lock, and a
mechanical edit to four large green files that nobody is permitted to run is a
worse trade than one tracked follow-up.

  e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts           — switchToAsk, pointAt, selectWholeOutput,
                                    confirmOffer, expectGranted,
                                    grantedCommands, askFromPrompt, runCommand,
                                    systemPrompt, attachedItemID
  e2e/agent-turn.spec.ts          — askFromPrompt
  e2e/agent-refusal-stop.spec.ts  — askFromPrompt, toolResults, chatRequests
  e2e/agent-answer-stream.spec.ts — check which of the above it carries

The copies agree today. A second implementation of one concept is a regression
with a delay fuse (AGENTS.md, "Look for the existing answer before you write a
second one"): they agree everywhere anybody looks and disagree somewhere nobody
did.

agent-ask.spec.ts's pointAtFromRun — the Run-half assertion that the offer does
NOT appear before the chord — is deliberately NOT in the shared module: it is an
assertion about the product, not a gesture, and it belongs to the spec that owns
that claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The four specs above import the gesture helpers from e2e/ask-gesture.ts and
  carry no local copy of any helper the module exports.
- Nothing the module does not export moved into it: assertions about product
  behaviour stay in the spec that owns the claim.
- All four specs pass in the e2e container on both browsers after the move, and
  the report says so with counts.
- The "not migrated, deliberately" paragraph at the top of ask-gesture.ts is
  removed, since it is then no longer true.
