title: DECISION — proto.Version has not been bumped, and the wire has grown a service since
description:
Carried through nocx-k6p18.1 and nocx-k6p18.3, both of which declined to bump and both of
which said so rather than leaving it implicit.

The argument each time: nothing is deployed, so bumping would refuse every dev helper for
no gain. That was true, and it is still true. What has changed is the size of what was
added without a bump — nocx-k6p18.1 added a frame type, nocx-k6p18.3 added a whole
service with three ops and their schemas.

The reason this is a decision rather than a chore: a generation is content-addressed and
immutable, two are resident at once, and one lingers as long as it holds a session —
months. The moment a generation is PUBLISHED, the version number it carries becomes a
fact other binaries reason about, and everything added without a bump becomes
indistinguishable from what was there before.

So this must be settled before the first publish, and the deploy work (nocx-6ojko) is
where that becomes real. It is cheap now and impossible later.
acceptance_criteria: Either proto.Version is bumped with a stated rule for when it must be, or the code says why one version number is correct across these additions. Settled BEFORE any generation is published, because after that it is not a decision any more.
close_reason: proto.Version bumped to 2 in fe418228, with the rule written beside it in version.go rather than left in the bead: from the first published generation, any change to a frame type, a service, an op or a result shape requires a bump. Owner decided the bump directly. Verified the bump is the constant alone — every call site reads proto.Version, no literal comparisons; internal/helper tests, git/hostsvc and transport/control all green. One consequence recorded in the same commit: deploy keys the install directory by this value (D7), so the prune test's stale sibling is now a superseded VERSION as well as a superseded hash, and its comment was corrected to say both.

title: The helper has no observations on macOS, which is the platform we ship
description:
Found by nocx-k6p18.3, 2026-08-31, and reported by its own author.

D3 says the helper may report DERIVED diagnostics — cwd, argv, foreground process, start
time — because those are facts about a process and the OS is their source. On Linux it
does, through procfs. On macOS ProcFS returns nil: there is no /proc, and proc_pidinfo
needs cgo, which the ~2.8 MiB size argument refuses.

macOS is the platform nocx ships on first. So on the shipped platform the inventory falls
back to launch metadata alone.

That is not a correctness failure — launch metadata is the AUTHORITY and OS inspection is
only EVIDENCE, which nocx-k6p18.3 enforced in two fields that can never be one. The
inventory is still right. What is missing is everything that CHANGES after launch: a
session whose shell has cd'd somewhere else reports the directory it started in, and a
tab that shows its working directory shows a stale one, silently.

The Inspector interface is the seam and it is already there, so this is an implementation
behind an existing boundary rather than a design question.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS, spawn a helper session and cd somewhere inside it.
2. Ask the helper for the inventory.
3. cwd is the launch directory, and there is nothing saying the observation is unavailable
   rather than unchanged.

## Fix

A cgo-free darwin Inspector, or an explicit "unavailable on this platform" the product can
say. What must not happen is a stale launch value presented as a current observation —
that is exactly the lie the authority/evidence split exists to prevent, arriving by the
back door.
acceptance_criteria: On macOS the helper answers the same derived diagnostics it answers on Linux — cwd at minimum — through the existing Inspector seam, without cgo. Or, if that is impossible without cgo, the product says the diagnostics are unavailable rather than reporting them as absent, and the size cost of the alternative is measured and stated rather than assumed.
close_reason:
Committed as edd3d4f1 on worktree-agent-a363d8ef4e491cc85. Merged and re-verified: go test ./internal/helper/... all ok, and GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 build rc=0 on the merged tree.

THE ANSWER IS BOTH BRANCHES, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. sysctl answers more than the bead assumed, cgo-free: argv via unix.SysctlRaw('kern.procargs2'), command name and liveness via unix.SysctlKinfoProc('kern.proc.pid'). CWD IS NOT REACHABLE, with evidence rather than assertion: macOS's KERN_PROC subdivides by pid/pgrp/tty/uid/session and none carries a working directory; kern.proc.cwd is FreeBSD's, not Darwin's; and the only route, proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDVNODEPATHINFO), is a libSystem SYMBOL rather than a syscall number — x/sys/unix on darwin has no Syscall, and its syscall_syscall takes a libc function POINTER, so a numeric call jumps to that address and crashes. lsof was rejected too: a fork per inventory row on a host we do not own, plus a diagnostic that depends on a tool being installed.

SO cwd RIDES THE SECOND BRANCH, EXPLICITLY ON THE WIRE. New required field Observation.Unavailable, a closed enum of cwd|argv|foregroundCommand, never omitempty. Three states a reader can tell apart: observed null (nobody could be asked), unavailable [] (asked, everything answered), unavailable ['cwd'] (asked, unknowable — DO NOT read launch.cwd as current). Asserted as BYTES, requiring the two payloads to differ, not as a struct comparison.

And the rule is PER-OBSERVATION, not per-platform: a refused /proc/<pid>/cwd under a uid change or a hardened container is named identically, because the reader's problem is the same and the reason is not its business. That generalisation was not in the brief and is better than what the brief asked for.

IT CORRECTED MY UNDERSTANDING OF THE RATCHET, and this is worth keeping. The first cut wrote a second Inspector beside ProcFS, and the deadcode ratchet REJECTED it: 2 NEW, parseProcArgs2 and sysctlInspector.Observe. RTA does NOT rescue methods of a type nothing instantiates — so AD-8's interface blind spot cuts BOTH ways, and my note that the ratchet is structurally blind to interface-held methods is only half the story. Restructured to internal/contentkey's shape as the brief asked: one osInspector over a per-OS procSource, with only the syscall leaves build-tagged. The derivation is now constructed on every platform, so the reporting rules and the procargs2 parse run in the suite on Linux while the ratchet sees nothing orphaned on either OS. One parser reads both layouts, because /proc/cmdline and procargs2 differ only by a header — two would have agreed everywhere and disagreed on the variable NUL padding.

SIZE, measured against the ~2.8 MiB argument that refused cgo: x/sys/unix was ALREADY in the helper's darwin dependency graph via internal/pty, so zero new dependencies. darwin/arm64 2894386 -> 2912626, +17.8 KiB, 0.63%. darwin/amd64 +13.7 KiB, 0.46%.

HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT COULD NOT VERIFY: the three syscalls themselves, because this is a Linux host and a compiling syscall is not a working one. It arranged for macOS CI to execute them rather than leaving that gap open — TestTheHelperHasAnInspectorOnEveryPlatformItShipsOn observes the running test process through whatever NewInspector resolves to and fails if argv is empty, which on the macOS runner is kern.procargs2 against a real process and pins the golden vectors to the real blob format; and session_service_contract_test.go now uses NewInspector, so the macOS job validates the sysctl inspector's real output against the frozen schema over the real socket. If either goes red on macOS, darwinSource is where to look.

GOOS=darwin go build ./... cannot be run at all — wails v3 needs cgo on darwin — and that was confirmed pre-existing by building the pristine HEAD tree to the identical failure, rather than assumed.

title: The discard surface has no producer left, and the ratchet cannot see it
description:
Created by nocx-lmb6v.1, 2026-08-31, and reported by its own author rather than found later.

The ladder deleted the rebuild, and the rebuild was the only thing that ever discarded
rows. So HistoryStatus.Discarded, the `discarded` field in
contracts/history.status.schema.json and its generated frontend type,
historyDiscardSentence, its tests, and the Settings notice that renders it can now never
fire. Config.OnDiscard is already gone.

THE RATCHET CANNOT CATCH THIS, and that is the reason this is a bead rather than a
cleanup somebody will notice: deadcode's RTA counts a method a live interface can hold as
reachable, which is most of this codebase under AD-8. The orphan is recorded in the doc
comment on Discarded, where it sits, because a comment is the only marker the tooling
leaves room for — and AGENTS.md is explicit that a comment is not a task, which is why
this exists.

This is the vault.status defect inverted. There, the renderer's type declared a field the
server never sent. Here the server declares a field it can never send. Both are a wire
contract that stops describing the wire, and both were invisible to a green suite.

Deliberately out of nocx-lmb6v.1: removing it is a wire-contract change touching Go, the
schema, the generated types and the frontend, which does not belong inside a migration
bead.
acceptance_criteria: Nothing in the product offers a sentence that can never be shown. Either HistoryStatus.Discarded and its whole chain — the contracts/history.status.schema.json field, the generated type, historyDiscardSentence and the Settings notice — are removed together, or a producer exists that can raise it. The wire contract and the generated types are changed in the same commit, never hand-edited.
close_reason:
Committed as 31c1bb3d on worktree-agent-ad790a936ea2ff20a. 6 files, +59/-176.

THE EVIDENCE THAT NO PRODUCER EXISTS, gathered rather than assumed, and the fourth line is empirical: (1) grep for call sites returns exactly one line, the declaration; (2) Discarded appears in NO interface declaration anywhere — it is a method on the concrete *HistoryStatus, and the only caller was the composition-root branch nocx-lmb6v.1 deleted; (3) the ladder cannot raise one on any of its three refusal paths, all of which fmt.Errorf and end 'no rows were discarded', because the refusal's whole promise is byte-non-modification, while a successful rung migrates inside one transaction and a failed one rolls back — nothing in either direction throws a row away; (4) Discarded does not appear in .githooks/deadcode-baseline.json AT ALL, so the gate was blind to it for the entire time it was orphaned, exactly as the bead predicted.

WHAT THE WORKER'S OWN GREP FOUND BEYOND THE BRIEF, and all three would have been left behind: sameStatus and asHistoryStatus in history-status.ts were two more readers past the sentence itself; the detachedOutput description in the SCHEMA explained itself by reference to discarded ('exactly as discarded does'), so leaving it would have left the contract naming a field it no longer declares; and aStatus's doc comment in the test cited discarded as the exemplar of 'HistoryStatus gains fields', now reworded to 'came and went', which is the better example.

THE REFUSAL HAS AN ADEQUATE SURFACE OF ITS OWN and it is a different one, correctly: app.go raises HistoryDegradeOpenFailed with the open error's text, and historyUnavailableSentence renders 'Commands are not being kept' plus the detail, which names the version to update to. schema_migrate.go says so in its own comment, so this was designed rather than accidental.

AND THE WORKER REFUSED TO RE-HOME THE DISCARD'S WORDS ONTO IT, which is the judgement call worth recording: refused means history is NOT RUNNING AND EVERY ROW IS STILL ON DISK; discarded meant it WAS RUNNING AND STARTED FROM NOTHING. Giving the refusal 'earlier history was discarded' would tell someone their rows were thrown away at the one moment they demonstrably were not.

The schema is the source of truth and was changed there; the generated frontend type was REGENERATED via npm run contracts, never hand-edited. Two stale prose references were checked and deliberately left, both already accurate historical records.

go test ./internal/content/... ok 22.7s; ./internal/transport/... ok 100.5s; contracts:check clean with a green baseline before the change, so it is a real signal; tsc clean on all three projects; 80 frontend tests pass; the full pre-commit gate passed including the two-owners, row-grammar and error-vocabulary gates.

title: The e2e stand cannot start from a deep worktree: the coordinator socket path exceeds the 110-byte unix limit
description:
Found 2026-08-31 while trying to look at a UI change in a browser from an agent
worktree. Nothing to do with the change; it blocks the e2e stand for every
worktree whose path is long enough, which is every `.herdr` worktree.

`e2e/stand.ts` starts `cmd/nocx-server` with a disposable `$HOME` under the
repo, so the coordinator's discovery socket is built from the repo path:

  <worktree>/.e2e/home/.local/share/nocx-dev/run/.srv.sock.786432

For `/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-green-cloud-9a0b` that is over
the platform's `sun_path` limit, and the backend exits during startup with

  coordinator: socket path exceeds the platform's unix-socket limit:
  110 bytes at <path>

The error message is good — it names the limit and the path, which is why this
took one read rather than an afternoon. What is missing is a path that stays
short regardless of where the repo is checked out.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a git worktree under a deep path — any `.herdr` worktree qualifies:
   `/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-<name>`.
2. Run the e2e stand from it (`e2e/run-in-container.sh`, a Playwright MCP
   session, or anything reaching `e2e/global-setup.ts`).
3. `startStand` fails in `awaitCoordinator` (`e2e/coordinator.mts:174`) with the
   backend log ending in the socket-path error above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The e2e stand starts from a worktree whose absolute path is long enough to
  break it today, asserted by a test that constructs the runtime directory from
  a deliberately long base and checks the resulting socket path fits.
- Wherever the fix lands, the disposable `$HOME` and the profile isolation the
  suite depends on (AGENTS.md, `e2e/home-isolation.ts`) still hold — a short
  socket path must not be bought by putting the run directory back under the
  developer's real home.
- The error, if it can still happen, keeps naming both the limit and the path.

## Notes

The obvious shapes: put the runtime directory under a short `$TMPDIR`-based
path while the rest of `$HOME` stays in the repo, or hash the profile path into
a short stable name. Which one is right depends on what else reads that
directory — not investigated here.
notes:
NARROWER THAN FILED, corrected 2026-09-01 after actually running the suite.

The container is NOT affected. `e2e/run-in-container.sh` mounts the repository
at /work, so the coordinator's socket path is built from a short root and fits
well inside the 110-byte limit — the whole connection-overlay spec runs from
this worktree that way, ten tests, no trouble.

What fails is the HOST path: a stand started directly on the developer machine
(the Playwright MCP's `generator_setup_page`, or `npx playwright` against
playwright.config.ts) builds the disposable $HOME under the worktree itself,
and `/home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/worktree-<name>/.e2e/home/.local/share/
nocx-dev/run/.srv.sock.<n>` is over the limit.

So the practical impact is smaller than this bead first claimed: agents can and
should verify e2e in the container, which is CI's environment anyway, and the
host path is the one that needs the short runtime directory. A symlinked `.e2e`
does NOT work around it for the container, because the symlink target does not
exist inside it — and it is not needed there.

title: A content.db copied while nocx is running is an almost-empty file
description:
Measured, not theorised, while implementing nocx-7qunp on 2026-08-31:

  snapshot while open: main=4096  wal=2949120  shm=32768

A live content.db is a 4 KB main file and megabytes of hot -wal. Nearly the whole
database is in the WAL, and the main file is close to empty until the handle closes
and checkpoints it.

So anything that takes only `content.db` — a backup, a sync, an rsync to a host, a
support bundle, a deploy that seeds a machine from an existing profile — captures an
almost-empty database and will look like it worked. The failure is silent and total,
and it is the kind that is discovered when the copy is the only remaining copy.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run nocx and produce some history, so content.db has rows.
2. While it is still running, copy ONLY content.db to another path.
3. Open the copy. The rows are not there; the file is ~4 KB.

## Fix

Wherever the product copies this file, either move the -wal and -shm with it or force
a checkpoint before the copy. Which of the two is right depends on the caller — a
backup wants a checkpointed single file, a live migration may want all three.

Orthogonal to nocx-7qunp and it lands squarely on the tier-2 remote-host work, which
is why it carries the remote-host label: deploying a server to a host, and anything
that seeds one machine's profile from another, is exactly this operation.
acceptance_criteria: Any path that copies, backs up, ships or deploys a content.db either takes the -wal with it or checkpoints first, and a test proves the copy holds the rows — not merely that a file arrived.

title: The reported gap is one round-trip stale, and a second reclaim cannot report one at all
description:
Found while giving recovered.gaps its first reader (nocx-fz4qa), 2026-08-31. It was
invisible until something drew it; now that the product states the number to a person,
the number being stale is a defect rather than a curiosity.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Detach a pane whose session keeps producing, so the ring keeps moving.
2. List sessions: reclaimSession derives the hole from entry.replayFrom, taken from the
   sessions.live listing.
3. Attach. state.offset is then overwritten with result.from.
4. If the ring moved between the listing and the attach, result.from is the truth and
   the reported gap is stale — UNDER-reported if the ring freed more than the listing
   showed, over-reported if it did not.

## The second half

A second reclaim of the same pane cannot report a hole at all. TerminalContent's
adoptLiveSession sets _adoptAttempted and never retries, and SessionHandle.recovered is
only ever populated by reclaimSession — so a session rebound by any other path arrives
with recovered === null and is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A FRESH OPEN. That is the shape
AGENTS.md calls a silent degrade the UI contradicts: the pane is missing bytes and says
nothing, which is exactly the state nocx-fz4qa existed to end.

Fine today because there is one reclaim path. It is a trap for whoever adds the second,
and the helper epic (nocx-k6p18) adds reattachment paths by design.

## Fix

Recompute the account after the attach settles, from result.from, and make the recovery
account a property of BINDING a live session rather than of one function that happens to
be the only current caller.
acceptance_criteria: The hole a reclaimed pane reports is derived from what the attach ACTUALLY returned, not from a listing taken before it — asserted with the ring moving between the two. A pane rebound by a path other than reclaimSession either carries its recovery account or is provably unable to have a hole; it is never silently indistinguishable from a fresh open.

title: The sessions-lost warning is proven to be RAISED and never proven to be SEEN
description:
Found while verifying nocx-p2q1q's acceptance, 2026-08-31. Not a blocker for that
epic — it is the last link of a chain whose other links are all tested.

internal/coordinator/launcher_test.go:420 asserts a version mismatch is refused, the
coordinator replaced, and exactly one Notice of kind NoticeSessionsLost raised naming
both versions. That is the launcher's half and it is thorough.

The delivery half has no test at all. showNotices() raises the Wails warning dialog at
main.go:652, wired at main.go:610, called at main.go:301 — and main_test.go covers only
resolveBackend, two tests. So the chain is proven as far as the Announcer INTERFACE and
stops there.

This is the shape AGENTS.md's rule 1 names: every unit correct, and nothing asserting
the user is told. "Your running sessions were killed by an update" is precisely the
message that must not be the one that silently fails to appear.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Arrange a build-version mismatch between the window and a running coordinator, so the
   launcher refuses and replaces it and raises NoticeSessionsLost.
2. Observe that launcher_test.go asserts the notice exists.
3. Grep main_test.go for showNotices, for the dialog, or for any assertion that the
   notice reaches a surface. There is none.

## Fix

Test the seam that main.go:301 crosses, so the notice is proved to reach the surface
rather than the interface. If the Wails dialog itself cannot be driven headlessly, the
seam moves one step down to something that can be — that is the ordinary answer, not a
reason to leave the link untested.
acceptance_criteria: One test drives the chain from a version mismatch to the surface a person actually looks at, so 'the launcher says live sessions died' stops meaning 'the Announcer interface was called'.

title: Connect to a nocx host from another machine and see the tabs that are open there
description:
The second half of tier 2, and the deliverable the whole 2026-08-31 turn was for:
the owner works from a desktop and a laptop against one VM and wants both to see
the same work.

SSH IS A CARRIER HERE, NOT THE PROTOCOL. The ordinary nocx WebSocket rides inside
an ssh channel unchanged, the way internal/apisend/ssh_dialer.go already makes
HTTP ride one — so AD-1's binary data plane is not re-wrapped in JSON-RPC, it is
the same plane on a different socket. The authoritative endpoint on the host is a
private unix socket in a 0700 directory; reaching it needs no port forwarding at
all, because `nocx-helper bridge <generation>` runs over the pty-less exec lane
and copies bytes. direct-streamlocal is an optional carrier improvement, never the
boundary. And because reaching that socket already required becoming the Unix
account, the ssh carrier needs no authentication of its own — only a non-ssh
carrier does.

WHAT IS SHARED AND WHAT IS NOT. Name, order, pinned state, split topology, blocks
and the helper-session binding live on the host. Which of those tabs this window
shows, the active tab, window size and position, scroll and selection are
per-machine — ADR-0048 already decides that UI state is a per-machine document,
and this extends that local projection with the set of remote tabs this window
has open.

MUTATION IS OPTIMISTIC, NOT LAST-WRITE-WINS. One monotonically increasing
workspace revision, incremented transactionally by every shared layout mutation;
a mutation carries the revision it expected and an idempotent mutation id; a
stale revision returns Conflict with the current revision rather than silently
overwriting; the server broadcasts the new revision and a client that missed one
resnapshots instead of applying deltas over a gap. Orca reached the same
coarseness for its remote workspace sessions (baseRevision / stale-revision /
conflict phase) — and its web client, which cannot rename at all and keeps
renames in browser localStorage, is what this epic exists not to be.

THE NAME IS A LADDER, NOT A FIELD, and this is taken from orca deliberately: a
user-set name, a quick-command label, an OSC title, a generated name, the live
title and "Terminal N" are SEPARATE fields resolved at render, first non-empty
wins, and auto-generation refuses to run once a user-set name exists. That is
what lets the helper's derived facts (cwd, argv, foreground process) arrive as
lower rungs without ever colliding with the name a person gave.

THE HELPER HOLDS NO HUMAN NAME. It mints a stable generation-qualified
HostSessionID and reports derived diagnostics; the ledger owns the name and the
binding from pane to that identity. Those are not the same primary key — many
panes on many machines may project one host session.

WIRE COMPATIBILITY IS DECLARED SEPARATELY FROM THE SCHEMA. A peer never opens the
remote database, so the floor must not be encoded in content.db's user_version:
the handshake declares control-plane and data-plane versions with a minimum peer
for each, ranges must intersect or the connection is visibly refused, and an older
client never deploys its server over a newer remote generation.

DELIBERATELY OUT: the browser (nocx-0h9ib); reconciling two clients that both want
to type — the controller lease is named in nocx-eidfb and this epic consumes it,
it does not re-decide it.
acceptance_criteria: With nocx-server running on a host and tabs open there, connect to it from a second machine as a connection of type nocx. Its tabs appear, with the names the user gave them, and their blocks. Rename a tab from the second machine: the first machine sees the new name. Close the lid on the second machine and reopen it: the tabs are still there and still named. An older client whose wire protocol the host no longer accepts is REFUSED with the version it needs, and neither the host's server nor its database is downgraded.
notes: Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-31-level-2-the-server-on-the-host-design.md

title: An update on your machine does not interrupt a program on the server
description:
Replaces nocx-op33k, which was closed as superseded: it proposed handing sessions
OVER between two coordinators and opened blocked on ADR-0043's warning that two
backends against one content.db is unproven. Neither applies now. The helper holds
the PTY, the coordinator is replaced under it, and only one coordinator ever holds
the store.

THE MECHANISM IS COEXISTENCE, NOT HANDOVER. Helper installs are content-addressed
and immutable, so two generations can be resident at once. An old generation
lingers exactly as long as it still holds a session; new sessions go to the new
one; the new one retires the old when its last session ends. Retirement is
rename-to-tombstone, so a generation being removed can never be selected.

WHAT THIS OWES BESIDES THE GENERATIONS (the debt the 2026-08-31 review surfaced,
and the reason "just stop deleting" is not the fix):

  * The startup sweep may no longer judge. dropDeadSessions and closeOpenEntries
    are founded on a theorem that is being repealed — "a session lives inside one
    backend process and cannot outlive it". A replacing coordinator must ask
    before it deletes, and there are three answers, not two: the generation
    reports the session (live), the reachable generation says it does not exist
    (absent), or nobody could be asked (unknown). Unknown may never collapse into
    absent — a refused connection, a timeout, a sealed vault and an unreachable
    host are all unknown.
  * The recording resumes rather than restarts. Deleting it and starting fresh
    loses exactly what the promise exists to keep: a coordinator that recorded
    thirty minutes, updated, and returned after the helper's window had rolled
    would throw those thirty minutes away. So the recording keeps its durable
    cursor and records an explicit hole — Skip(session, resumeAt, reason) — with
    a reason distinct from the per-command cap, and stays appendable afterwards.
  * The command's exit code must still be able to land. Removing the forced
    phase='closed' is necessary and not sufficient: today a lifecycle transport
    loss makes the domain Lost and its open attempts unknown, so nothing would
    deliver the real exit. The helper keeps the lifecycle rendezvous and the
    material to authenticate recovery for the PTY's lifetime; the replacing
    coordinator sends a refresh_request and rebuilds its kernel from the shell's
    authenticated active_attempt / last_completed / next_seq (docs/lifecycle-
    protocol.md). The lifecycle KERNEL does not move into the helper — that would
    import block policy into the execution host — and no durable event journal is
    added, which would be a second ledger with its own retention and migrations.
  * ONE INVARIANT TO FREEZE, because the snapshot is only sufficient under it:
    no new top-level command may begin while no writer is attached. One command
    may finish during the absence and the shell then waits at its prompt, which
    active_attempt plus last_completed fully describes. If autonomous submissions
    are ever allowed with no coordinator present, a single snapshot stops being
    enough and the event journal becomes unavoidable.
  * Three verbs, frozen here so tier 2 need not reinterpret an overloaded one:
    detach (drop this attachment, the process survives), close-session
    (deliberately end the helper-hosted session), uninstall (revoke machine
    consent and, after naming the live work, end everything).

DELIBERATELY OUT: durable tabs on the host, and anything a second machine sees.
Closing a tab here loses the tab, never the process — it is findable in the
helper's inventory and reattachable.
acceptance_criteria: Start a long command on a remote host through the helper. Update nocx. The command runs throughout and the same pane is reclaimed with its output continuous where the coordinator was present, and carrying an explicitly-reasoned gap where it was not. The old helper generation is still resident and still holds that session; new sessions opened afterwards go to the new generation; and once the last session of the old generation ends, the new one removes it. Uninstalling names every running process first and asks.
notes:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-31-level-1-the-helper-owns-the-host-design.md

2026-09-04, and a RETRACTION of a note written earlier the same day. That note
said this epic's reconciliation half had moved to nocx-ie23r. It had not, because
there is nothing to move: THE RULE IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED.

dropDeadSessions and closeOpenEntries no longer exist -- they survive only in
comments. internal/content/reconcile_sqlite.go carries the three verdicts
including VerdictUnknown, and internal/app/session_reconcile.go states the
discipline in its own header ("A FAILURE IS NEVER A VERDICT", with a causeFor
whose type cannot return one). That landed with nocx-k6p18.5, AFTER this epic's
description was written -- which is how a description from 2026-08-31 was read as
a statement of the present. Found by an adversarial review (codex) and verified
against the tree.

So this epic keeps what it always owned and nothing was taken from it: generation
coexistence across an update, retirement by rename-to-tombstone, uninstall naming
live work first. Its description's "the startup sweep may no longer judge" bullet
is DONE and should be read as history, not as remaining work.

One thing it gained rather than lost: D2 of the generation-daemon lifecycle
design is not implemented either (no last-session shutdown, no startup grace, no
non-admitting drain state anywhere under internal/helper or cmd/nocx-helper), and
retirement cannot work without it. Filed separately; this epic depends on it.

title: resetIfSchemaChanged rebuilds a database written by a NEWER schema
description:
internal/content/sqlite.go:491. The gate is `onDisk == schemaVersion` -> return,
and ANY inequality falls through to the rebuild. The unknown-table check that
follows only refuses a file holding a table name this build does not own, so a
newer schema that adds or CHANGES COLUMNS inside familiar tables sails past it
and is destructively rebuilt by the older binary.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a content.db with the current build, so the file is stamped at
   schemaVersion N.
2. Check out a commit whose schemaVersion is N-1 — one that changed columns
   only, adding no table this build does not know.
3. Run it. resetIfSchemaChanged reads user_version N, finds N != N-1, walks the
   table list, recognises every name, and rebuilds — discarding the rows written
   under the newer schema.

Under greenfield this reads as the discard the file already promises, which is
why nobody has minded; the log even says "history discarded". It stops being
tolerable the moment a database is shared between two machines or two versions,
which is what the tier-2 remote server makes true.

## Fix

One direction check: onDisk > schemaVersion refuses without modifying a byte.
The migration path for onDisk < schemaVersion is nocx-lmb6v and this bug does
NOT wait on it — refusing upward is correct with or without migrations.

Found by codex during the 2026-08-31 architecture review; confirmed by reading.
acceptance_criteria: Open a content.db stamped with a schema version HIGHER than the running binary's: the store refuses and modifies nothing. Asserted directly against resetIfSchemaChanged, not through a caller.
close_reason:
Committed as e2948a33 on worktree-agent-ac64e9f7d600a87a5. One direction check ahead of the rebuild: onDisk > schemaVersion returns an error and touches nothing; onDisk < schemaVersion is unchanged and still discards. TDD, and the red run printed the defect verbatim — 'was=16 now=15 rowsDiscarded=200', the 15 binary destroying rows written by 16 while telling the user the file was OLDER. The refusal reaches a person through the surface that already exists: Open's error becomes the detail of HistoryDegradeOpenFailed and Settings prints it under 'Commands are not being kept', naming the version to update TO. No new degrade reason was added, deliberately — the store's existing newer-schema refusal already speaks through openFailed and a second vocabulary for one fact is the duplicate-owner defect.

THE 'not one byte' CLAUSE, investigated rather than assumed. It is asserted literally against resetIfSchemaChanged (sha256 + size + mtime either side, with a throwaway control proving the assertion is not vacuous). It is NOT true of Open, and the reason is more interesting than the pragma order I suspected: content.db is not SQLCipher but ncruces/go-sqlite3 with the adiantum VFS, so the key is installed in the connector's init hook and reordering pragmas inside Open is structurally free. Measured: reading user_version before journal_mode still yields journal_mode=wal. The reorder is safe and POINTLESS, because WAL is a property of the FILE, not of our connection — a live content.db is a 4 KB main file plus a ~2.9 MB hot -wal, and CLOSING the handle checkpoints the whole WAL into the main file and deletes it, on a connection that never issued a journal_mode pragma at all. Only a read-only probe connection could deliver byte-identity, which is surgery and would move the direction decision out of the function the criterion names. So the promise kept is 'no rows were discarded', true on every path. Not corruption: the checkpoint is schema-blind page copying, and the refused file ends up cleanly checkpointed, still stamped 16, still holding every row and the column this build has never heard of.

A fourth test was added on the follow-up round and it closed a real gap — the three committed tests all used rollback-journal fixtures, so none covered the sharing scenario the bead is about. TestOpenRefusesANewerDatabaseArrivingInWalWithoutLosingARow builds main + hot -wal copied while the writer holds it, -shm deliberately absent so recovery is genuine, and asserts wal > main so it cannot silently degrade into the ordinary case. go test ./internal/content/... ok 22.538s.

title: content.db survives a version change, and an older nocx refuses rather than rebuilds
description:
PREREQUISITE of the tier-2 remote server, not a follow-up to it, and the
ordering is the point.

Today content.db is rebuilt on any schema change and the rows are lost by
design (sqlite.go's resetIfSchemaChanged says so in as many words). That is
correct while the database is LOCAL and DISPOSABLE: lose it and you reopen your
tabs. The owner confirmed on 2026-08-31 that this is a phase and migrations
will exist ("Мы сбрасываем схему и не делаем миграцию только потому что он у
нас greenfield. Потом будет миграция конечно").

The premise expires exactly when a remote server owns tabs, names and blocks
that are the ONLY copy and are shared between the user's machines. Restoring
them from the laptop is then impossible, so a schema bump shipped with an
ordinary update would destroy work. Hence this lands before tier 2, not with it.

THE MINIMUM PROTOCOL (codex review, 2026-08-31):
  onDisk == current -> open
  onDisk <  current -> one explicit ordered migration per edge (14->15), in one
                       crash-safe operation, user_version updated only after
                       that edge commits
  onDisk >  current -> REFUSE, without modifying a byte

An older binary's only legal response to a newer schema is a visible refusal.
It never rolls back.

DELIBERATELY OUT: a minMigratableSchema floor. While the chain is complete
there is nothing to declare; it is owed only if old steps are ever retired.
And the SERVER-TO-SERVER wire compatibility floor is NOT this — a peer never
opens the remote database, so it must not be encoded in user_version. That
belongs to the connection epic.
acceptance_criteria: A database written by schema N+1, opened by a binary at N: refused, with not one byte modified, and the product says which version is needed. A database at N-1, opened at N: migrated by an explicit ordered step, and its rows are still there afterwards. A migration killed midway: the old database is intact and the next start completes or refuses, never a half-migrated file. Released old-schema fixtures are in the suite, migrated forward, with a failure injected in the middle.
notes: Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-31-level-2-the-server-on-the-host-design.md
close_reason:
content.db survives a version change, and an older nocx refuses rather than rebuilds. Thirteen children, all closed, merged onto feat/relay-pty-owner through 9aac2bb4.

Each acceptance clause has a named test, and they run against the real Open on real files rather than against a harness beside it:

  N+1 opened at N, refused, not one byte modified
    TestMigrateRefusesADatabaseWrittenByANewerSchemaWithoutTouchingAByte
    TestOpenRefusesADatabaseWrittenByANewerSchemaAndKeepsItsRows
    TestOpenRefusesANewerDatabaseArrivingInWalWithoutLosingARow
  N-1 migrated by an explicit ordered step, rows still there
    TestADatabaseOneVersionBehindIsMigratedAndKeepsEveryRow
    TestAReleasedSchema14DatabaseMigratesForwardWithItsRowsUnaltered
    TestAnUpgradeKeepsTheTabsAndPanesTheUserHadOpen
  migration killed midway, old database intact
    TestAMigrationKilledBetweenTheStampAndTheCommitLeavesTheOldDatabase
    TestAFailureMidEdgeLeavesTheFileByteForByteAsItWas
    TestKillChildStampsAndBlocks
  released old-schema fixtures, migrated forward, failure injected in the middle
    TestReleasedSchema14FixtureIncludesTheAPIRunTablesAndCounter (the fixture is
    now the file a released build actually wrote) plus the two above

The refusal is not only a log: app.go:951 raises HistoryDegradeOpenFailed with the error text, which is the Settings surface, so "which build can open this" reaches a person rather than a slog line. That was the condition nocx-lmb6v.4 existed to protect.

`go test -race -count=1 ./internal/content/...` green on the merged tree, 213s.

WHAT THIS EPIC COST AND WHY, kept because the pattern will recur:

The rebuild was never a bug. It was correct for a store that was local and disposable, and ADR-0021 recorded that correctly. What expired was the PREMISE, when content.db stopped being disposable — and nothing in the code or the documents noticed, because a premise has no compiler. Five of the thirteen children are consequences of that single unnoticed expiry: the ADR still promising a discard surface, the surface with no producer, the fixture that was never the file a build wrote, the second version counter, the digest with no rung.

Twice in this epic a worker fixed "a validator that says yes to the case it cannot judge" (nocx-lmb6v.8) and then wrote a new one with the same shape within the hour (nocx-lmb6v.6, round one). The lesson did not transfer by having been learned. One residual of that shape is recorded in .6's close reason rather than hidden: the !ok branch still ends in return nil for a version in neither the pinned set nor the ladder, unreachable today because the direction check and the ladder floor bracket it.

Twice a worker's pre-fix evidence was a COMPILE error rather than a red test, which proves the symbol did not exist and nothing else. Both times the coordinator ran the mutation instead. That is now the standing check for this repo, not a special measure.

DELIBERATELY OUT and unchanged: minMigratableSchema — retiring old rungs. nocx-lmb6v.13 landed the mechanism that will notice if that work leaves the API-run refusal clause behind, so the retirement inherits it rather than discovering it.

title: A host becomes a nocx host: the server is deployed to it, and that is its own consent
description:
Tier 2 of the two-level split (see the 2026-08-31 rewrite of the execution-host
designs). Tier 1 is the helper: native integration, git, filesystem, completion,
and it holds the PTY. Tier 2 deploys a full nocx-server to the host, which then
owns durable workspace/tab/pane state and its own ledger.

WHY CONSENT IS SEPARATE AND NOT INHERITED. ADR-0034 keys consent to the machine
identity by host-key fingerprint, and it was written about the HELPER's
footprint. A full server is a materially different footprint: it creates an
encrypted database on that host, it may later expose a web endpoint, and it
holds user-authored state that is the only copy. Smuggling that through the
helper grant would let one yes authorise a second, larger thing. So the stored
grant distinguishes helper execution from full host service.

And the reverse edge matters as much: helper uninstall is all-or-nothing FOR
HELPER GENERATIONS. It must never silently define deletion of a tier-2
content.db, because that database holds tabs and blocks the user has not been
warned about.

DELIBERATELY OUT: the manual install path (you may always put nocx-server on a
host by hand); the web endpoint (its own epic); what the connection UI shows
once connected (its own epic).
acceptance_criteria: From the app, deploy nocx-server to a host you already reach, and the grant recorded for it is DISTINCT from the helper's footprint grant: the consent list shows two entries, and granting the helper never implies the server. Removing the helper leaves the server's content.db untouched. Removing the server is its own explicit act which names, before it runs, the durable state it will delete.
notes: Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-31-level-2-the-server-on-the-host-design.md

title: make ci-full is not the whole gate: the dead-code ratchet runs only in CI
description:
AGENTS.md names four commands as the whole gate — `make ci`,
`scripts/ci-linux.sh`, `scripts/ci-frontend.sh`, `e2e/run-in-container.sh` —
and `make ci-full` runs all four. None of them runs the dead-code ratchet.

`.githooks/check-deadcode.mjs` exists and CI runs it as its own step in both
`ci-linux` (`--platform=linux/amd64`, no-secret-service variant only) and
`ci-mac` (`--platform=darwin`). Locally it is run by nothing: pre-commit prints
"the dead-code ratchet — CI's `ci-mac` and `ci-linux` jobs" in its own
NOT-covered list, and the two shell scripts do not call it.

Observed 2026-08-31 on PR #162: all four local commands were run on the merged
tree and reported green; CI came back red on three jobs, all of them the
ratchet, on one new unreachable function (`WithHeartbeatReadWindow`). The
integrator followed AGENTS.md exactly and still shipped a red PR, which means
the instruction is wrong rather than the person.

The cost is not the fix — that took two minutes — it is that "I ran the gate"
stops meaning "CI will pass", and the next integrator learns to distrust the
gate rather than the sentence that describes it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Introduce an exported function nothing in production calls.
2. `make ci-full` — green.
3. `node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs --platform=linux/amd64` — fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ratchet runs from one of the four commands AGENTS.md calls the gate, on
  both platforms CI checks it on, or AGENTS.md stops calling those four the
  whole gate and names the ratchet separately.
- A new unreachable function is caught locally before push, demonstrated once.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-hf346, which is the earlier bead (2026-08-25 against this one's 2026-08-31) and carries the measured CI run id and the greps. Both name one behaviour: make ci-full never invokes .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs, so a newly unreachable function passes every local gate and reddens CI. Two sightings of one defect — hf346 saw NewScreenReader in run 32872132780, this bead saw WithHeartbeatReadWindow in PR 162. NOT FIXED: Makefile:273 ci-full still lists seven targets and none is a ratchet step. This bead's extra criterion, that the check runs with the platform arguments of BOTH platforms CI checks, is the one thing it adds and should be folded into nocx-hf346. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: Полный webkit-набор на main падает на api-run-lifecycle
description:
Полный контейнерный набор webkit на `origin/main` (`ac06a437`) даёт 234
прошедших и одно падение, не связанное ни с какой веткой в работе:

```
[webkit] e2e/api-run-lifecycle.spec.ts:114:7
  › an API run you can watch, stop, and read a failure off
  › Send shows a pending row, Stop settles it as stopped, and a name that
    does not resolve reads as a run with its phase and its request
```

Измерено 2026-08-31 при снятии базы под другую задачу. Спек проходит на том
же дереве в изолированном запуске — как и два падения, которые расследуются
отдельно, это может оказаться взаимодействием внутри набора, а не дефектом
спека.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Дерево на `origin/main`.
2. `PW_PROJECTS=webkit ./e2e/run-in-container.sh` — весь набор, не один файл.
3. Падение воспроизводится в полном прогоне; изолированный запуск спека
   зелёный.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Установлено, дефект это продукта, дефект спека или перенос состояния между
  спеками через общий стенд — с доказательством, а не по правдоподобию.
- Полный webkit-набор на `main` зелёный.
- Если причина — перенос состояния, названо, что именно переносится и кто
  обязан это убирать.
close_reason: Поглощён nocx-6wgcw: то же явление, увиденное шире. Смешанный прогон на main роняет 12 тестов, webkit-only — один (api-run-lifecycle), поодиночке всё зелёное. Меряться и чиниться это должно как одна нестабильность набора, а не как отдельное падение одного спека.

title: path classification conflates missing paths with stat failures
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Click a terminal path link whose target has disappeared or is inaccessible.
2. Observe that files.stat returns an error, pathKind returns unknown, and the opener falls through to the file viewer.
3. Observe the viewer's read error instead of a classification-specific outcome.

## Problem
files.stat currently maps every provider error to unknown, so a missing path and an unclassifiable path (for example permission denied) both fall through to the file viewer. That preserves the prior fallback but can show the viewer's read error for a path the user cannot open. Decide and test distinct user-facing handling for confirmed absence versus inability to classify, without restoring parent-directory enumeration.
acceptance_criteria: A path that is confirmed absent does not open the viewer and receives the intended user-facing refusal. A path whose kind cannot be classified has an explicit, tested policy that does not misrepresent the path as a regular file. The policy is covered through the real link-opening seam.
close_reason: Closed

title: The completion dropdown stays open after Enter accepts a row — red once on the merged tree, green on both parents
description:
## Что наблюдается

e2e/completion.spec.ts:194 «a real command completes: Tab opens the dropdown,
arrows pick, Enter inserts», chromium, CI, прогон 33384016828 (дерево
e52f56d3 — слияние ветки nocx-92kes с main):

    e2e/completion.spec.ts:229
      await expect(dropdown).not.toBeVisible()
        Locator: .ui-floating-panel[data-variant="completion"]
        Expected: not visible   Received: visible
        14 × locator resolved to <div role="listbox" data-open="true" …>
    239 passed, 1 failed

Строка ВЫШЕ прошла: `expect(page.locator(INPUT)).toHaveText(chosen)`. То есть
Enter принял строку и вставил текст — а список остался открыт.

## Почему это не «медленная машина»

Отказ съел все пять секунд, 14 опросов подряд видели `data-open="true"`. По
диагностике из памяти [a-flaky-go-test-in-this-repo-is]: провал, съевший окно
целиком, — потерянное событие, а не поздний приход. Список не «не успел
закрыться», его никто не закрыл.

## ЧТО ИЗМЕРЕНО про происхождение

  дерево                                   ci-e2e (chromium)
  ---------------------------------------- -----------------
  PR #157 (то, что стало main, ac06a437)   зелёный
  c0fe7b69 (ветка nocx-92kes до слияния)   зелёный
  e52f56d3 (СЛИЯНИЕ этих двух)             КРАСНЫЙ
  e52f56d3, перезапуск того же job         зелёный

Локально в контейнере на слитом дереве: `PW_PROJECTS=chromium
e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/completion.spec.ts` → 8 passed.

То есть дефект не воспроизводится по требованию, но и не существовал ни в
одном из родителей: первое же испытание слитого дерева было красным.

## Почему это стоит отдельного бида, а не строки «флак»

Перезапуск зелёный — этого достаточно, чтобы влить (владелец так и решил), и
недостаточно, чтобы называть причину. Открытый вопрос ровно один: закрытие
выпадающего списка после Enter зависит от чего-то, что в слитом дереве стало
другим. Кандидат, НЕ проверенный: ветка nocx-92kes меняет
main.tsx:fireSnippet (askFields → needsForm) — путь, которым из ЭТОГО ЖЕ
списка выстреливает сниппет; а волна #157 трогает фокус, диалоги и
жизненный цикл блоков. Обе стороны трогают то, кто владеет вводом после
Enter.

Смежный, но другой: nocx-6bfy («список рекламирует стрелки, которые забирает
recall») — про клавиши, а не про закрытие.

## Как проверять

`--repeat-each=20` на этом спеке под нагрузкой, chromium, на дереве
e52f56d3. В упавшем прогоне взять trace.zip и посмотреть, приходило ли
событие закрытия вообще, или пришло и было перекрыто повторным открытием.

## Чего не делать

Не увеличивать таймаут: пять секунд съедены целиком.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Названо из трассы, почему список остался открыт: событие закрытия не
  пришло, или пришло и его перекрыло повторное открытие.
- Спек проходит 20 прогонов подряд под нагрузкой без отказа.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Дерево e52f56d3 (или main после 1977e986).
2. `PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/completion.spec.ts`
3. Ожидается 8 passed; в CI однократно наблюдался отказ на строке 229.
   Локально за один прогон не воспроизведён.

title: deploy: a non-numeric proto.Version installs fine and can never be pruned
description:
deploy.Prune matches install directories with installDirName = `^[0-9]+-[^-]+-[^-]+-[0-9a-f]{64}$` (internal/helper/deploy/prune.go:22), so the version component is ASSUMED numeric. Nothing validates it.

internal/helper/deploy/install.go takes its version from proto.Version, a plain string constant (internal/helper/proto/version.go:6, currently "1"). A non-numeric value — "1.1", "2-rc", "v2" — installs and serves perfectly well: Ensure builds the directory name from it and the helper runs out of it.

It just becomes UNPRUNABLE. Prune skips any directory its regex does not match, and the comment says why that skip exists — "a foreign directory that merely resembles ours is left alone" — so our own directory is silently treated as foreign. The footprint then grows without bound on every host, and nothing reports it: Prune returns nil having done nothing.

Found by an adversarial review of the 2026-08-31 execution-host design (nocx-50vmp). Filed standalone because it is true on main today and is not caused by that design — though that design makes it worse, since generations are then meant to accumulate deliberately and the prune path becomes load-bearing.

The fix is a choice, not obvious: validate at the single point where the name is built (fail loudly at install rather than silently at prune); or widen installDirName and give up the foreign-directory guard; or make the version component structurally unable to be non-numeric. Prefer the first — a rule the construction path cannot get past, in the style of host.Register.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set proto.Version to "1.1" (or any non-numeric value) and build.
2. Install the helper on a host, then change the version again and install a second time.
3. deploy.Prune runs with keep = the current directory and returns nil.
4. Both directories remain under ~/.nocx/helper. Neither matched installDirName, so neither was ever a pruning candidate; the footprint grows on every version change and nothing says so.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a non-numeric proto.Version, an install either fails loudly at the install site or produces a directory Prune can match; it can never produce one Prune silently skips.
- A test asserts the coupling directly: for the version the installer uses, the name it builds matches installDirName. The two are held together rather than agreeing by coincidence.

title: The containerized gate scripts do not run the dead-code ratchet
description:
## What happens

AGENTS.md says the three containerized scripts are byte-for-byte their CI counterparts in
software, and a coordinator runs them before pushing to main. All three were green on
fix/assistant-panel-wave1. The PR then came back red on ci-linux (no-secret-service), at a
step none of them runs:

    FAILED STEP: Dead-code ratchet (linux)
    DEADCODE RATCHET: 87 unreachable on linux/amd64 (89 baselined, 5 NEW)

CI has the ratchet as its own workflow step — .github/workflows/ci.yml:373 for linux and
:153 for darwin — invoked as 'node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs --platform=...'.
scripts/ci-linux.sh does not call it at all. Neither does pre-commit, which says so
honestly in its own summary: 'NOT covered here: the dead-code ratchet — CI's ci-mac and
ci-linux jobs'.

So pre-commit is truthful about the gap and the containerized script is not. The script is
the one a coordinator is told to trust before pushing.

## Why it matters

This is the gate that most needs to match, because the ratchet is the one check whose
verdict depends on the WHOLE program rather than on the diff. A branch can add nothing
dead and still turn a function dead by removing its last caller somewhere else — which is
exactly what happened here, twice, in commits that were themselves correct.

It also cost this wave a public red PR after a full local gate reported green, which is
the specific outcome the 'run the gate CI runs, not a subset of it' rule exists to
prevent. The rule was followed and the outcome happened anyway, because the subset was in
the script rather than in the choice of scripts.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a branch, remove the last caller of any exported test-only helper.
2. Run ./scripts/ci-linux.sh — green, both keyring variants.
3. Open a PR — ci-linux (no-secret-service) fails at 'Dead-code ratchet (linux)'.
4. Run 'node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs --platform=linux/amd64' by hand — reproduces
   locally in about two minutes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- scripts/ci-linux.sh runs the ratchet its CI job runs, on the same platform argument, and
  fails when the job would fail. A test or a dry run demonstrates the pairing.
- If the ratchet is deliberately excluded — it is slow, or it belongs to a different
  runner — then AGENTS.md stops claiming those scripts are CI's counterparts without
  qualification, and names what they do not cover. Whichever is chosen, a coordinator can
  read one place and know what a green local gate does and does not promise.
- The darwin side is decided in the same breath: ci-mac runs the ratchet too, and 'make
  ci' cannot run on the NixOS host at all, so the mac ratchet has no local path either.
  Say what covers it.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-hf346, which was filed earlier for the same gap with its own measured cost (CI run 32872132780). Evidence merged into that bead.

title: 2>/dev/null makes an ordinary read command look destructive
description:
## What happens

Asking the assistant to look at disk usage produced 'du -sh /* 2>/dev/null | sort -hr |
head -n 10', and the run suspended for approval with:

    suspensionTool=session.run  suspensionEffect=mutate-destructive

(backend.log, run=121, 2026-08-31). du reads. Nothing in that pipeline writes anything.
The same session's earlier 'df -h' correctly suspended as observe (run=117).

## The cause

cmdeffect.go's withoutRedirections (:344) treats '2>' as a redirection, records its target
/dev/null with content.ResourceWrite, and then ALSO calls appendUnresolvedRedirection —
which adds an Unresolved entry saying the redirection 'remains unresolved even though its
target was recorded'. Per ADR-0053 an unresolved parse takes the WORST member of the
declared set, so the whole invocation escalates to mutate-destructive.

Both halves are individually defensible. A redirection IS a write, and a target that was
recorded but not fully understood SHOULD take the worst case — that is the deny-side
asymmetry working as intended. The result is still wrong, because '2>/dev/null' is the
one write that mutates nothing and it appears in a large share of ordinary commands.

## Why it matters beyond noise

The owner's policy asks about everything, so today this costs one extra approval. The
damage is to the approval's MEANING: if reading disk usage is presented as destructive,
the word stops carrying information and the person starts approving destructive by habit.
A classification that cries wolf is worse than a coarse one.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant anything it answers with a command carrying 2>/dev/null — 'what is
   taking up space', 'find every X', most du/find phrasings.
2. Read the approval prompt: the effect is mutate-destructive.
3. Compare with the same command minus the redirection: observe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A read-only command with 2>/dev/null classifies as observe, and a test states it.
- The general rule behind it is written down rather than special-cased on one path:
  either /dev/null (and the null device generally) is a target whose write mutates
  nothing, or discarding a file descriptor is distinguished from redirecting output to a
  file. Whichever is chosen is stated in code where withoutRedirections can be read.
- A genuine write redirection — '> file', '>> file', '2> log.txt' — still classifies as a
  file mutation, and a test asserts the pair together so the two cannot drift.
- The deny-side asymmetry is preserved: no change here may make an over-match PERMIT
  more. Compare nocx-etugj, which is the same asymmetry read in the other direction.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #159 (0f9250ae). The null device and file-descriptor duplication are classified as stream routing rather than filesystem mutation; every real file target stays a mutation. Verified by probe against the pre-fix baseline, not by the worker's tests: the effect is lowered in exactly six places, all of them that sink, and cat /etc/shadow > /dev/null still records /etc/shadow as a read — which is what makes the lowering safe rather than merely quiet. The same round closed a gap it did not open: a LEADING redirection was invisible to the parse and its write recorded nowhere, held up only by the unknown-program net nocx-etugj had to restore.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: The daemon's log path is unnameable, so the failure that most needs it says nothing
description:
When the coordinator is spawned but never becomes ready, the launcher classifies the
failure as not-ready (nocx-mgrfo) and the overlay shows it to a person. The one thing that
person needs -- where the daemon wrote down why it did not start -- cannot be named.

nocx-server owns its own log file now (main.go:55). The window only talks to it over the
discovery socket, and the handshake carries four facts; the log path is not one of them.
main.go:195 LogFilePath() returns "" for exactly this reason, and its comment says
restoring it needs a control-plane call rather than a guess at a path.

A first attempt at nocx-mgrfo derived the path as <DataDir>/nocx.log. That is a second
owner for a concept whose first owner deliberately refuses to answer, and it is wrong in
the worst case: not-ready means the daemon never came up, so there may be no file at that
path at all. It was removed; the remedy now says nothing about where to look.

The honest fix is to make the path knowable: the daemon states it in the handshake, where
the client already learns the WS address and the token.

Note the ordering problem this does NOT solve, and say so in the design: a daemon that
never becomes ready never sends a handshake either. So the path must come from a source
that exists before readiness -- the spawner knows what it launched and with what
environment -- or the not-ready remedy stays silent about it by design. Decide which,
deliberately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A person whose backend failed to start is told where to look, and the path named is the
  path the daemon actually writes to.
- The path has ONE owner. LogFilePath() either answers or is deleted; it does not coexist
  with a second derivation.
- The not-ready case specifically is covered, including when no handshake ever arrived.
- Paired: on an ordinary machine the named path exists and contains that run's log.

title: Re-add the written-file version capture with the writer path that calls it
description:
The dead-code ratchet went red on main after #154 was merged with a red CI.
This bead records what was removed to make it green, so the epic re-adds each
piece WITH the wiring the gate requires (AGENTS.md, nocx-z7s6).

Removed in worktree/calm-cloud-2509:

1. assistant.CaptureWrittenFileVersion — no caller anywhere, not even a test.
   A convenience wrapper over the ...From form.
2. assistant.CaptureWrittenFileVersionFrom, and its test
   TestFileVersion_WrittenContentProvidesHashWithoutReadingAgain. Test-only.
   It binds bytes a WRITER already holds, and the assistant has no file-write
   capability yet — grep finds only systempromptgen. Built for a caller that
   does not exist.
3. effectKernel.decideInvocation — a two-value wrapper over
   decideInvocationWithReason, called only by matrixpolicy_test.go, which now
   calls the three-value form.
4. content.NoFloor() — test-only, 82 call sites across 25 test files, all
   rewritten to content.Floor{}. The intent it documented moved onto the Floor
   type, where it governs every zero value rather than one spelling of it.

CaptureFileVersion and VerifyFileVersion were NOT touched: they are wired
(kernel.go:652, approvals.go:237) and the enforcement they give is intact.

WHY REMOVAL RATHER THAN BASELINING: the ratchet baseline may only shrink, by
design — check-deadcode.mjs says so, and update-deadcode-baseline.mjs refuses
a baseline that grows. A test-only helper added after the baseline is a new
violation with nowhere to be recorded, which is the gate deliberately forcing
wiring or removal.

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] The assistant has a file-write capability, and the written-file version
capture lands in the SAME commit as the caller that uses it, with its test
[ ] `node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs` stays green across that commit
[ ] Nothing here re-adds a convenience wrapper with no caller

title: A web client cannot get a token: pairing, and the Settings item that governs it
description:
A browser client has no way to obtain the capability token. In a browser GetWSPort throws,
the token falls back to "" and the auth layer refuses the socket (scripts/dev-web.sh's own
header records this). The dev stand works only because dev-web.sh lifts WSTOKEN out of the
coordinator's unix socket and injects it -- a path a real browser does not have.

Owner's direction, 2026-08-30: the token comes from PAIRING, surfaced as a new item in
Settings.

This is an authentication feature with a security surface of its own and it gets its own
design session. It does NOT block the 2026-08-30 reconnect work: that design's endpoint
provider seam (§5) is two implementations of one interface, so the web provider can be
filled in without touching the connection state machine.

AD-1 already binds the shape: "Security invariant for when web ships: auth token +
bind-to-localhost by default."

## Acceptance Criteria

- A person pairs a browser client from Settings and that client reaches a working session
  without any token being copied by hand or read from a log.
- One end-to-end check watches them do it.
- The token never travels through a URL, a log line, argv or the spawned daemon's
  environment -- the constraint GetWSToken already states for the desktop path.
- Unpairing revokes: a paired client that has been removed cannot open a socket.

title: A crash-looping coordinator is raised forever: the daemon counts its own crashes and says why it will not come up
description:
A daemon that crash-loops is respawned without a ceiling: the client's re-discovery
(2026-08-30 design §3) may raise one on every attempt, and nothing counts how often that
has already happened.

The accounting belongs to the daemon, not the client (owner, 2026-08-30). A crashed
process cannot report its own death, so the mechanism is a start record written on start
and a clean-exit record written on shutdown, in the runtime directory the daemon owns; the
NEXT instance reads a start with no matching clean exit and concludes the previous one died.

`srv.lock` cannot supply this: internal/coordinator/lock.go:11 states the kernel releases
the flock "however it dies", so a clean exit and a crash are indistinguishable to it by
construction.

To explain itself the refusing daemon must COME UP, hold the socket and answer Hello with
a reason and a remedy, serving no sessions. A daemon that simply exits explains nothing --
the client gets ErrNoCoordinator and silence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- N abnormal exits inside a window make the next instance come up refusing, and it answers
  Hello with a typed reason and a remedy rather than exiting.
- A clean run resets the count; so does a version change.
- The overlay renders that reason verbatim -- the seam is the 2026-08-30 design's blocked
  state, which already carries a kind, a sentence and a remedy.
- Paired per AGENTS.md testing rule 3: and on an ordinary machine a daemon that starts and
  stops cleanly is never refused.

title: ci-frontend.sh has no npm cache, so every run depends on the network — and it leaks the gate lock
description:
Two defects in one runner, both measured on 2026-08-30 by the session running
the territory-floor gate.

1. NO CACHE, SO THE NETWORK IS A DEPENDENCY OF EVERY RUN. ci-frontend.sh died
three times in a row with two lines of log, immediately after
'=== frontend: npm ci ==='. The cause turned out to be npm error code
ETIMEDOUT: the container could not reach the npm registry, and it also had to
pull node:24-bookworm. The exit status was 146, which is not a signal anyone
can read anything into. Meanwhile the e2e runner passed on the same machine at
the same time — because 449ed02d gave IT an npm cache (nocx-7jt3u), and
ci-frontend.sh still does npm ci live into both of its volumes on every run.

A gate that fails on a slow registry teaches everyone to re-run it, which is
the same disease nocx-3icu1 was about, arriving through the network instead of
through timing.

2. THE GATE LOCK LEAKS. ci-frontend.sh ends in  while
gate_lock_release is installed as a trap on EXIT. exec REPLACES the process
image, so the trap never fires and /tmp/nocx-hook-gate-1000.lock is left
behind; a stuck lock was observed after exactly such a run. Unrelated to the
npm death, same file.

Do not turn this into 'prune docker'. Disk (7.2G free of 197G, 27GB of
reclaimable docker volumes) and memory (swap exhausted) were both measured the
same afternoon and are real, but neither caused this.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run ./scripts/ci-frontend.sh with the npm registry slow or unreachable: it dies
after '=== frontend: npm ci ===' with exit 146 and no explanation, and leaves
/tmp/nocx-hook-gate-1000.lock held.
acceptance_criteria: ci-frontend.sh reuses a cached npm store the way e2e/run-in-container.sh does, so a second run does not reach the registry; a run that still cannot install says WHY in its own output rather than dying with two lines; and the gate lock is released even though the script ends in exec — proven by running it and checking the lock afterwards.
notes:
THE WIDER SHAPE, and the reason this is worth more than a cache flag. A fresh
worktree without node_modules breaks FOUR entry points, and every one of them
reports its own death as a FAILED CHECK rather than as a missing dependency:

  - .githooks/pre-commit — dies on the missing frontend/node_modules and says
    the check failed. Workers answer that with --no-verify, and then no static
    check runs at all: an unformatted test and a dead function got through that
    way (nocx-y6d9j).
  - .githooks/pre-merge-commit — delegates to pre-commit, so a MERGE commit
    dies the same way, and this is the one path where a commit could otherwise
    reach main with no local gate at all.
  - npm run contracts — a worker with no node_modules could not regenerate the
    contract types and hand-edited frontend/src/generated/*.ts instead, which
    is precisely the file the repository says is generated and never edited
    (observed on nocx-stop-is-an-answer, 2026-08-30, caught at review).
  - scripts/ci-frontend.sh — this bead.

Also, the root and frontend/ are two installs. Workers told to run npm ci in
frontend/ still have no eslint or prettier, which live at the root, so
pre-commit fails on the FIRST of the four above even after they think they have
installed. Anything that tells a worker to install should name both.

title: A tab with no agent in it shows the agent-exited dot
description:
The tab strip paints a hollow ring before an ordinary shell tab's title —
'1 ○ repos/nocx' — in a pane where no agent was ever started.

The ring is not decoration and it is not 'no agent'. tab.css:322 gives
data-agent-status='exited' a transparent background with a 2px muted border,
which is exactly the hollow ring in the screenshot; a pane with no agent is
supposed to carry NO data-agent-status at all, and the dot is then 0px wide
(tab.css:287-300). pane-observation.ts says so in its own comment: null means
'there is no agent in this pane', and 'unknown' is reserved for an agent that
is there but unreadable.

So the derivation is handing back a state for a pane that has none. Measure
before editing: is the pane's activity 'exited' or 'unknown', and which source
produced it — the enrolled driver, or the terminal TITLE heuristic
(pane-observation.ts:97-132, where an unreachable host also displaces down to
'unknown')? A shell tab titled with a path is the likeliest input to have been
read as evidence of something.

Whichever it is, the fix is that an ordinary shell pane produces null, and the
tab draws nothing.

## Steps to Reproduce

Open a plain shell tab, start no agent in it, and look at the tab: a hollow
ring sits before the title. Owner screenshot 2026-08-30.
acceptance_criteria: A tab whose pane has never hosted an agent carries no data-agent-status and shows no dot; a pane whose agent has genuinely exited still shows the ring; a test drives both and asserts the attribute, not the pixels.

title: The snippet form offers a choice and a tick, and asks only what applies

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] A select renders with its options and its default preselected; a flag renders un-ticked
[ ] Ticking a flag reveals the fields inside its block seeded with their defaults; un-ticking hides them and keeps what was typed
[ ] The submitted map carries FLAG_ON for a ticked flag and '' for an un-ticked one

title: The snippet preview renders the parse and derives nothing
description:
Plan Task 5 (.internal/plans/2026-08-30-snippet-parameters-and-conditions.md). preview.ts becomes a pure render over parse(): param, flag and problem part kinds join env/secret/unrecognised. preview.test.ts's bare-{{cwd}} assertion reverses.

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] describeBody contains no regular expression and no brace literal outside its header comment
[ ] A bare {{cwd}} reports as a param; {{evn:cwd}} and {{ask:port}} still report as unrecognised

title: Snippets: a body that offers a choice and varies its own text
description:
Spec: .internal/specs/2026-08-30-snippet-parameters-and-conditions-design.md
Plan: .internal/plans/2026-08-30-snippet-parameters-and-conditions.md

A user saves a phrase whose CHOICES and whose PARAGRAPHS both vary, and fires it
filled in. The case that drove it: an orchestrator prompt the owner retypes several
times a day, where the worker it names alternates between three and whole sentences
are kept or dropped by hand before every fire.

The `ask:` namespace is retired. A `{{...}}` with a colon is a namespaced directive;
without one it is a parameter, declared inline with its default and its option list.
Conditions are Jinja-shaped -- `{% if x %}` / `{% if not x %}` / `{% endif %}` --
parsed here, not by an engine: Handlebars and Mustache render `{{secret:NAME}}` to
empty on the vault path, Nunjucks and LiquidJS refuse to parse it, and none of them
can express an inline option list.

One parser feeds preview, form and fire. Supersedes 7.1 and 7.2 of the snippets
design; 8 and 11.1 stay binding.

## Success Criteria

[ ] One e2e watches a person create a snippet with an option list and a condition,
fire it with the palette chord while a program owns the pane and no command editor
exists, pick from the select, leave the flag un-ticked, and see the resolved text
reach the program with the excluded sentence gone, NO blank line where it was, and
no trailing newline
[ ] parse() is the only function in frontend/src/snippets/ that reads the grammar:
preview.ts, resolve.ts, the dialog and snippets-settings.tsx carry no brace literal
and no regular expression over a body, checked by reading the diff
[ ] For a body carrying each diagnostic kind, the settings preview and a fire report
the SAME diagnostic -- one table, both surfaces
[ ] A field inside a switched-off block is never asked, and an {{env:...}} inside one
never refuses the fire
[ ] {{secret:NAME}} survives resolution byte-for-byte, and secret-reference.ts,
secret-chip.ts and submit.ts appear in no commit of this epic
[ ] reference-namespaces.ts no longer lists ask, and the disjointness test is updated
rather than deleted
[ ] The seeds fire in an ordinary local pane, proved by a test

## Deliberately out

- else, nesting, loops, filters
- Branching on a value (worker == codex) -- additive later, breaks no condition
- Escaping | inside a default
- Migration of stored {{ask:...}} bodies: greenfield, they become literal text
close_reason: All 7 success criteria verified: e2e 6265fe9f (watched failing); parse() the only grammar reader; parity table over every DiagnosticKind; switched-off blocks neither ask nor refuse; {{secret:}} byte-for-byte and the three vault files untouched by every commit; ask retired from the registry with its test updated; seeds proved by two Go tests.
