title: The shipped coordinator is built without nocx_login_session, so the installed app's vault can never reach the login keychain
description:
Found by the nocx-gpyxp worker by reading, outside its ownership, and correctly reported rather than fixed.

.github/workflows/release.yml:199-204 builds cmd/nocx-server with '-tags release' and nothing else. The keystore stance introduced by nocx-qhg3q is a BUILD property: internal/app/keystore_build_login.go is '//go:build nocx_login_session' and keystore_build_headless.go is its negation, which 'makes no claim to a login session'. So the shipped coordinator is a headless build by tag, takes the file provider, and the installed desktop app's vault can never use the macOS login keychain.

Neither task that produced this was wrong alone. nocx-qhg3q made the stance declared rather than discovered, which is right and is what stops a modal nobody can dismiss on a headless host. nocx-ln6ht put nocx-server into the bundle, which is right. The COMPOSITION is the defect, and it is invisible from either branch — the same shape as the contract staleness that only appeared when two green branches met.

Note the coordinator, not the window, is now the vault's process, so this is not cosmetic: it decides where a shipped user's secrets live.

## Steps to Reproduce

Build the release bundle and inspect the coordinator's keystore stance: it reports the headless source (internal/app's buildKeystoreSource), never 'build (nocx_login_session)'. On macOS, a fresh install therefore stores secrets in the file provider with its own passphrase rather than in the login keychain.
acceptance_criteria: The shipped macOS coordinator reports the login-session stance, and a release build asserts it rather than assuming it — a smoke check on the built binary, not a reading of the workflow. Decide and record deliberately whether the Linux coordinator claims a login session too; AppImage and a headless VPS are not the same case and the tag cannot be right for both by accident.
close_reason:
Decided, not fixed, by ADR-0050 (docs/decisions/0050-the-keystore-holds-a-key-only-a-person-can-take.md, commit a4665deb).

This bead's sign was backwards and the ADR says so in as many words. It was filed as 'the shipped coordinator cannot reach the login keychain' — a P0 asking for the missing -tags nocx_login_session. Measurement on the owner's Mac (this bead's own comment) showed the release build is the SAFE one: an item written the way go-keyring v0.2.8 writes one carries no trusted-application list, so /usr/bin/security reads it silently from any process under the login. Adding the tag would have turned a configuration that is safe by accident into the vulnerable one.

What ships instead: ADR-0050 steps 1-2 as epic nocx-hqklb (silent setup removed; every vault gets a passphrase envelope and a recovery code; the keystore keeps no verification material), and steps 3-4 as epic nocx-rybbm (Security.framework under our own signature; an item requiring user presence), which is blocked on two macOS measurements and a release signing identity.

release.yml is deliberately untouched: it already builds cmd/nocx-server without the tag, which is the stance the ADR keeps.

Closed with --force because its only open blocker is nocx-xsd03, the decision bead that produced the ADR — that bead outlives this one by design.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
MEASURED ON THE OWNER'S MAC, 2026-08-29, and it inverts this bead's sign.

The system provider stores PLAINTEXT (internal/vault/system/system.go:242 —
keyring.Set with the secret as-is; the package's own DeleteAll comment says
"this provider stores plaintext"). What protects it is the keychain item's
ACL, never the vault's root key: Provider "knows nothing about sealing", so
Seal/Unlock gates nocx's API path and not the bytes at rest.

What the ACL actually is, dumped from an item written exactly as go-keyring
v0.2.8 writes one (`security -i` <- `add-generic-password -U -s .. -a .. -w ..`,
NO -T flag):

  authorizations (6): decrypt derive export_clear export_wrapped mac sign
     -- with NO `applications` list on this entry
  applications (1): / authorizations (1): encrypt

Two probes, because the dump alone is ambiguous and reading it as "an empty
list means anybody" was wrong:

  1. A Swift binary calling SecItemCopyMatching AS ITSELF -> macOS prompts for
     the user's password. So the ACL does gate by application.
  2. `security find-generic-password -s .. -a .. -w` from an UNRELATED Terminal
     window -> printed the secret SILENTLY. Delete likewise.

So the trusted application is /usr/bin/security itself — Apple's general
purpose keychain CLI, which anything can invoke. Any process running as the
user reads a nocx secret with one shell command: no prompt, no passphrase, no
unsealed vault. The Swift probe was asked for consent only because it asked
under its own signature; going through the same tool nocx goes through asks
nobody. This is the concrete consequence of the fact AGENTS.md already
records — go-keyring shells out to /usr/bin/security, so OUR signature never
enters a keychain ACL at all.

THEREFORE the title of this bead has the sign backwards. A shipped coordinator
built WITHOUT nocx_login_session keeps every secret in the file provider,
under a data key under the root key, wrapped by argon2id into the passphrase
and separately into the recovery code — a strictly stronger position than the
login keychain gives, and the one that matches a coordinator which outlives
its window.

There is nothing to fix here as filed. What is left is a product decision,
split out rather than settled inside a bugfix.

title: recovered.gaps has no consumer: a reclaimed pane knows what is missing and never says so
description:
Left by nocx-22k1c.2 and reported rather than hidden. SessionHandle now carries recovered.gaps — the retention bound's gaps, plus an unrecorded gap for the stretch neither the recording nor the ring holds, derived in the renderer from produced and replayFrom so neither owner is copied onto the wire. Nothing reads it.

The worker expected nocx-22k1c.3 (the 'no blocks here, and why' notice) to consume it, but that task had already closed by the time this one finished. So the fact exists, is correct, and is invisible — which is the shape AGENTS.md forbids: a client reclaims a pane, the backend knows exactly what it could not give back, and the product says nothing.

This is a frontend-only task: the seam and its content already exist.
acceptance_criteria: A pane reclaimed across a gap says what is missing, in the product, and names whether the gap is the retention bound or the unrecorded stretch. A pane reclaimed with no gap says nothing — assert the negative, or the notice appears always and means nothing.
notes: Backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh examined this bead against nocx-22k1c.4 and nocx-k6p18.29 on the hypothesis that all three are one duplicate cluster. They are NOT, and the beads say so themselves. This one is the RECLAIM path: recovered.gaps has no reader, the seam and its content already exist, and it is frontend-only. nocx-22k1c.4 is a follow-on defect discovered by doing this work (its own text: 'Found while giving recovered.gaps its first reader (nocx-fz4qa)') — the number this bead will draw is one round-trip stale, and a second reclaim cannot report a hole at all; a discovered-from edge now records that. nocx-k6p18.29 is the LIVE path and a different mechanism: it says in its own description that a client which READS THE RECORDING BACK — a reclaim, session.output — is already told what is missing, and that a LIVE tab is not, because internal/transport's ringToConn steps over the hole and keeps sending. Fixing it needs a mid-stream reset shape that this carrier does not have at all, across contracts, transport and the renderer. Same concept, three different behaviours and three different mechanisms — which is exactly the merge AGENTS.md's rule forbids. No edge was added to nocx-k6p18.29 because that bead was named do-not-touch for this sweep; the owner may want one.

title: Re-summoning while an answer still streams consumes the chord and shows no composer
description:
## What a person sees

Ctrl/Cmd+Enter over a running program, ask, then press Escape while the answer
is still streaming. The screen thaws, which is correct. Press the chord again
before that answer reaches a terminal state: the frame freezes, the grid goes
read-only — and no composer appears. Escape gets them out, and the composer
returns by itself the moment the answer settles, so it self-heals; but a
deliberate gesture that freezes the screen and then shows nothing reads as
broken.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `top` in a pane.
2. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, ask a question, and let the answer start streaming.
3. Press Escape while it is still streaming — the screen thaws, the answer
   stays on screen and keeps growing.
4. Press Ctrl/Cmd+Enter again before the answer finishes.
5. The screen freezes and the grid is read-only, with no composer to type in.

## Why

`summonEditor` sets `_summoned = true` and calls `_syncLifecycleOwnership`,
which computes

    const answerInSummon = this._summoned && this._currentSummonedAnswer() !== null

`_currentSummonedAnswer()` returns the newest NON-terminal answer, and Escape
(`_endSummon`) deliberately keeps the answer nodes — it only clears `_summoned`.
So the still-streaming answer from the previous summon is found by the new one
and hides the composer it just opened. `editor.focus()` on the next line then
runs against a hidden editor.

nocx-7l4ex.8 narrowed this: before it, `_summonedAnswer` stayed non-null until
the command ended, so the window was the whole life of the program. It is now
bounded by the streaming turn, which is why this is a follow-up and not a
re-opening.

## The thing to decide, not to assume

Whether the second summon should adopt the orphaned turn (show the composer
below it, as a follow-up in the same stack) or refuse the chord with a spoken
reason while a turn it no longer owns is still in flight. Adoption is closer to
what the person asked for; refusal is closer to "one summon owns one turn".
Say in the commit which and why.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pressing the summon chord while an Escaped turn is still streaming either
  shows a usable composer or speaks a refusal — it never freezes the screen
  into a state with no input surface.
- editor shown <=> grid read-only holds at every step.
- Asserted from the state a person is in, waiting on observable state and never
  on a duration.

title: Nothing proves a transport binding does not acquire a domain gate the operation already holds
description:
Half of the gate-ownership invariant is proven and half is not, and the split is worth recording because the unproven half is the one that can actually break.

TestOperationOwnsDomainGate (internal/capability/disposition_test.go) shows that a capability operation acquires its domain gate and lane itself, in the same order, whether invoked directly or through a wrapper. That establishes the operation OWNS its gates.

It does not establish that no transport binding acquires the same gate a second time. A methodSpec handler that wrapped op.Run in its own gate acquisition would double-queue or deadlock, and nothing would catch it. The worker that wrote the capability half reported this limitation itself rather than claiming the invariant proven — the brief forbade it from touching internal/transport, which is where the missing assertion has to live.

Why it matters beyond tidiness: internal/capability is about to become the projection surface for the assistant, so every operation gains a SECOND caller. Two carriers entering one domain gate by different routes is precisely the shape that produces an unmetered path around the backpressure the renderer is subject to.

## Acceptance Criteria

A test in internal/transport drives at least one real methodSpec handler for each domain that has a domain gate, records gate acquisitions, and asserts the domain gate is acquired exactly once per call — by the operation, never by the binding. A binding that adds its own acquisition fails the test.
close_reason: Test drives real methodSpec handlers across seven gated domains and asserts each domain gate is acquired exactly once per call, by the operation. Verified by breaking it: a double-acquiring binding was written, watched to fail, and removed. Landed as e13d3961.

Seven stale comments replaced with what is true. Three transport tests corrected as a record of mutate-reversible gaining its first tool. Landed as 7e1fd595.

title: TestLocalPty_SignalForegroundReachesTheExecution is flaky on ci-mac: it waits on a duration
description:
TestLocalPty_SignalForegroundReachesTheExecution failed on ci-mac, then passed
on a rerun of the SAME commit with nothing changed:

  sha            98a94c17baf0c62fb57860a1d19d486b3c950f2a (PR #122, a frontend-only diff — no .go file in it)
  run            33204387749
  job 98961600383  FAIL  4m46s
  job 98967428821  pass  5m4s

  --- FAIL: TestLocalPty_SignalForegroundReachesTheExecution (5.13s)
      signal_foreground_test.go:80: timed out waiting for the execution group to
      end or foreground to return; the execution's process group 10864 survived
      SIGINT (or the shell never resumed)

The test waits on a DURATION — roughly five seconds for a process group to die
after SIGINT and for the shell to resume — which is the thing AGENTS.md forbids
by name: "a test may not depend on timing. Wait on an observable state change —
a frame, a record, a DOM state — never on a duration. A spec that needs a slow
machine to pass is broken on a fast one too; it has only not been caught yet."

So this is not "the runner was busy". The signal either reached the group or it
did not, and that is observable: the group's exit, or the shell's prompt coming
back. Whatever the test polls for, it currently gives up on a clock instead of
on evidence, and it will keep costing a red PR at random on somebody's unrelated
diff — which is also what teaches people to rerun a red job without reading it.

internal/pty is already the package AGENTS.md names as the one where a developer
Mac and the runner disagree (it hangs to its 600s panic locally while green on
CI, nocx-58gq). This is the same package failing the other way round.

Standalone: it arrived from an unrelated PR and belongs to no live epic.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open any PR and let ci-mac run.
2. Occasionally "Test (the OS-specific packages)" fails as above.
3. Rerun the failed job on the same sha; it passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] The test waits on an observable state change (the process group is gone,
    or the shell has resumed) rather than on elapsed time
[ ] Its failure message names which of the two it did not observe, so a future
    red says what actually did not happen
[ ] It passes 20 consecutive runs on ci-mac, and 20 under NOCX_CI_CPUS=1 or an
    equivalently starved runner
notes:
2026-09-02, second recorded occurrence, and again on a diff that contains no .go file under internal/pty at all: PR #177 (feat/agent-policy), run 33664621320, job 100363177494, FAIL 8m15s. Same test, same shape — 'timed out waiting for the execution group to end or foreground to return; the execution's process group 11423 survived SIGINT (or the shell never resumed)', signal_foreground_test.go:122 (the line has moved from :80 since the first report). Every other job on that run was green, including both ci-e2e legs, both ci-backend keyring variants and both ci-linux variants. The branch's diff against origin/main touches internal/pty in zero files. This is the cost the bead predicted in as many words: a red PR at random on somebody's unrelated diff, which teaches people to rerun a red job without reading it — I reran it, having read it. Priority is worth revisiting: two occurrences in five days on unrelated PRs is not P2 behaviour.
2026-09-02, confirmed: the rerun of job 100363177494 on the SAME commit, with nothing changed, passed in 11m7s (job 100372243829). That is the second time this test has been shown to pass and fail on identical bytes, and it is now the whole of the evidence anybody needs — the test's verdict is not a function of the code.

title: A worker died mid-task when the disk filled: 51 GB of Go build cache on a 197 GB volume shared by every agent worktree
description:
2026-08-28: an omp worker running golangci-lint over two packages died with 'compile: writing output: write $WORK/b436/_pkg_.a: no space left on device'. Its work was complete and intact in the worktree; only the agent was lost.

Measured immediately after:

    /dev/sda1  197G  168G  21G  89% /
    ~/.cache/go-build        51G
    ~/.herdr/worktrees       14G   (about 40 worktrees, most from finished sessions)
    ~/go/pkg/mod            2.1G

So the volume was not permanently full — 21 GB free when measured — which points at a transient spike: three workers compiling at once, each with its own $WORK under /tmp, against a build cache that has grown to a quarter of the disk.

Why it is worth a bead rather than a cleanup: a coordinator running parallel workers has no signal for this. The worker does not report 'out of disk', it reports a compile error, and a coordinator reading the pane sees a failing gate rather than an environment fault. The next wave will hit it again, and the failure will look like the worker's fault.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run three or more agent workers in separate worktrees of this repo.
2. Have each run go test / golangci-lint over several packages concurrently.
3. Observe a compile step fail with 'no space left on device' rather than a compile error.

## Acceptance Criteria

Either the build cache is bounded (GOCACHE trimmed on a schedule, or a smaller cache dir per worktree), or stale worktrees are collected, or both — and whichever is chosen, the failure mode is written down where a coordinator will meet it, so 'no space left on device' inside a lint run is recognised as an environment fault rather than attributed to the worker's change.

title: AGENTS.md says the CI cpu caps are off by default; f93ba326 turned them on
description:
AGENTS.md still says "So the caps are off by default" and describes NOCX_CI_CPUS
and NOCX_E2E_CPUS as an on-demand debugging tool, in the long paragraph about

Both halves now mislead. A reader is told the caps are off when they are on, and

carries the argument for why capping is wrong ("it does not produce the runner,
it produces a third machine", and it keeps timing-dependent tests alive) — which
f93ba326 evidently overrode on purpose, for laptop survival. Whichever way it is
settled, the document should say what the code does and why the earlier argument
no longer wins.

Not fixed inside nocx-fwsw2 (the pre-push change): that commit touches the same
section of AGENTS.md, and rewriting a neighbouring paragraph about somebody
else's just-landed decision inside it would hide that decision in an unrelated
diff. Filed instead, in the same minute, per AGENTS.md.

## Steps to Reproduce

2. Read scripts/ci-linux.sh and e2e/run-in-container.sh on main after f93ba326.
3. The default is 4 cores; the document says there is no default cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] It states the current default (4 cores for ci-linux and e2e) and what

title: Params contracts for the 81 methods outside vault, secrets, api, git, files and agent
description:
Continue the sweep the mechanism proof started. The mechanism, the naming convention and the registration-driven agreement test all landed in 2a8e69f4 for notes.* and snippets.*; this task applies them to a bounded tranche.

In scope: app, backup, connections, dialog, endpoints, fs, groups, history, ledger, lifecycle, notify, policy, ports, profiles, roles, session, sessions, settings, shell, tunnel, uistate — 81 methods, listed in contracts/params-unswept.txt.

Deliberately out: vault.*, secrets.*, api.*, git.*, files.* and agent.*. The first two are sensitive enough to deserve their own pass; the rest are being touched by other work or classified Adapted in docs/assistant-ui-action-capability-map.md.

Files: contracts/, internal/transport/. internal/agenttools, internal/assistant, internal/hashline and internal/filesystem are owned by another worker this wave.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A params contract for each of the 81 methods, additionalProperties false plus an explicit required list.
- isParamsContractScope in internal/transport/params_contract_test.go widened to the tranche, so the existing bidirectional agreement test covers them: every schema-rejected payload is validator-rejected, and every schema-accepted payload is validator-accepted.
- Where a schema turns out to be more permissive than its registered validator, the SCHEMA is tightened, never the validator loosened. Every such case is named in the report — those are the findings, not the file count.
- Any registered validator that accepts what its schema forbids is reported rather than quietly worked around.
- contracts/params-unswept.txt updated to exactly what remains.
- go test ./internal/transport/... -count=1, npm run contracts:check, and golangci-lint over changed files all pass. No repo-wide gates.
close_reason: 81 params contracts, in-scope unswept to zero, three validator/schema disagreements fixed by tightening the schema. Decoders unified with specific diagnostics; the 15 layout methods audited as the real out-of-tranche behaviour change. Landed as e9c22b2c.

title: A remote session survives a dropped network, and shell integration stops travelling as a script
description:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-28-the-nocx-server-design.md B, section 8. The session service the remote-helper design reserved and deliberately did not build (D15; internal/helper/host/host.go:85 still panics on the name). The helper spawns the shell itself and owns its PTY, so the session outlives the SSH channel — and integration no longer needs rc-file editing or SFTP delivery, which is a family of open bugs disappearing rather than being fixed.

D2: B reuses the coordinator's ring/ack/reset contract rather than minting one. AD-9's ring, offsets, acks, replay and reset are implemented in the transport today (ring.go, ws.go:64, ipc.ts:403) while internal/helper/proto only RESERVES seq/ack. A second notion of resumability here is the delay-fused regression AGENTS.md names. Hence this epic follows A.

AMENDS AD-5, deliberately: architecture.md:139 says Tier B augments and never replaces the remote shell. A helper that spawns the shell replaces the substrate. The amendment lands in docs/architecture.md, it is not routed around.

Keeps ADR-0034: consent stays keyed by machine identity, not by helper connection or daemon instance. A durable session outlives the SSH channel, so 'the channel is closed' stops meaning 'no helper is running' — consent inventory, stop and uninstall need a daemon-aware liveness protocol or the reversibility the helper design promises becomes false.
acceptance_criteria: On a remote host: start a long command in an SSH tab, break the network long enough to cross the ring bound, restore it, and reclaim the session — the process ran throughout, and the reclaim either replays exactly or states its gap per the D6 decision. Shell integration is present in that session without any rc file having been edited and without any script having been uploaded. Uninstalling the helper from that host stops the running session and leaves nothing behind, with consent still keyed to the machine.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-09-03. Merged to main as a04c4e2f (PR #163, merge commit, 116 commits
preserved). The gate ran on the MERGED tree at 6d619340: all eight CI jobs green,
including ci-e2e in both chromium and webkit.

DONE WHEN, watched end to end: e2e/remote-coordinator-reclaim.spec.ts. A person
starts a build on a remote host, the client goes away ENTIRELY (browser context
closed AND backend restarted), and on return the build is still running, its blocks
are there, and the output lost while nobody listened is NAMED rather than silently
absent. Four green runs unmodified, and falsified in four directions (lifecycle
socketpair removed; ExitOutcome's exit-code branch deleted; the host-window hole
recorded under the wrong reason; the adopted lifecycle carrier resumed at the
window's base) -- each turns it red at a named assertion.

SEVEN P0s, none found by reading code. Each came from chasing a specific assertion:

  .24  AttachedSession.Write put the session frame on the wire with NO outer
       envelope, so a helper-hosted tab rendered output and accepted no input.
  .30  NOTHING in the coordinator re-adopted a live helper-hosted session across a
       restart -- the epic's central promise had never been built. Found by this
       epic's own acceptance test before it could go green.
  .31  The lifecycle capability is minted by the dead process's kernel, so a
       re-adopted pane went markerless: every restored block built, in the DOM, and
       display:none, with no editor to type into.
  plus: the helper embedded its own binaries (make helpers doubled them until the
  linker refused); the helper linked the coordinator's SSH client (25% of its size);
  Reg.Adopt dropped the SSH options, so a helper-hosted session probed as root with
  no key; and no lifecycle channel reached a helper-hosted session, so a remote host
  produced zero command blocks while OSC 133 markers were being delivered.

THE LAST THREE were caught by CI on specs this branch does not touch, and they share
one shape -- a decision taken before the thing it depends on exists:

  nocx-07cf4  onCwd/onTitle subscribed AFTER the bind that replays the OSC 7 they
              exist to receive. A reclaim carries no cwd by design, so the replayed
              scrollback is the ONLY statement of where the pane is -- and .6's
              awaitWriteBarrier made losing that race deterministic.
  nocx-ht15k  the block-projection port refused every callback while this.renderer
              was null, and LifecycleProjections.pump had ALREADY recorded the
              attempt in _bound -- so the refusal was final and the block never
              opened. Same window, third subscriber.
  nocx-bzac4  helper selection (OpenHosted) probes by dialling the destination
              itself, with the interactive rung attached. On a password profile the
              probe raised the ask, released the only pool reference, closed the
              connection, and the session's own dial raised a SECOND ask -- so the
              answered password authenticated a connection that was thrown away.

VERIFIED BY THIS COORDINATOR, not taken on report: nocx-07cf4 by mutating tab.tsx to
an empty span (both new tests red, revert byte-identical); nocx-ht15k by reading the
diff and confirming the renderer is built at terminal-content.ts:1844, the port wired
at 2742, and the field published only at 3366 -- one object, no second owner.

DELIBERATELY OPEN, detached to standalone: .14 (macOS cwd needs cgo; the cost is the
build), .29, .32, .33, .34, .35 (every remote open still dials twice), .36.

KNOWN NARROWING, not a regression: a host whose password is not yet REMEMBERED no
longer gets a helper -- the probe declines silently and falls back to a plain shell.
Before this epic there was no helper at all. .35 is the real fix and needs the
transport's open handler, which is why it was not smuggled into the bugfix.

PROTOCOL DEVIATION, recorded on purpose: the merge was made WITHOUT the merge slot.
It had been held by feat-agent-policy for over two hours while that branch iterated
its own red CI, with a second waiter queued ahead. No slot was forced or released.

DEPENDENCY EDGE REMOVED, not forced past: nocx-k6p18 was blocked by nocx-p2q1q (the
cmd/nocx-server split). That dependency is satisfied in fact -- this epic ships ON
that backend, and its acceptance spec drives cmd/nocx-server headless. The edge was
removed explicitly rather than overridden with --force. nocx-p2q1q itself is left
alone: it is another epic's status to correct, not this one's.

title: An update no longer costs you your sessions
description:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-28-the-nocx-server-design.md A2, section 8. A1 may kill the old coordinator on a version mismatch and lose its sessions, saying so out loud. A2 removes that cost: drain or hand over sessions across an update instead.

BLOCKED ON ADR-0043 before any design work: it says multi-process safety of the encrypted store is unproven, and that nothing stops two backends reaching the same application data directory (0043-one-connection-to-the-encrypted-store.md:140). A handover must therefore either be strictly sequential with a proven handoff of content.db, or this epic starts by resolving that boundary. Overlapping two full coordinators against one store is not an option that may be assumed.
acceptance_criteria: A running session survives an application update: start a long command, take an update, and after the new coordinator is in place the same pane is reclaimed with the process still running and its output continuous. No point in the sequence has two coordinators holding content.db.

title: An over-bound line during setup is reported as a connection that ended
description:
A far side that writes more than `maxBootstrapLine` (4096) bytes with no line
ending during setup made `ReadLine` return a bare error
(`ssh_bootstrap.go:251`), which the writer's `awaitToken`/`awaitOutcome` treated
as "the stream ended" and reported as `bootstrap-interrupted` — so the card said
"The connection ended while nocx was still setting this session up" about a
connection that never ended.

This is the reason the owner actually hit, and the wording sent the diagnosis at
the network instead of at the far host's output. Nothing about the bytes was
recorded either — not even how many arrived — so the next occurrence would be as
undiagnosable as this one.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have the far side write 4097 bytes with no `\n` during the bootstrap window
   (a stale carrier doing something else with the terminal will do it).
2. The session degrades with reason `bootstrap-interrupted`.

nocx.log 2026-08-28T17:32:45.302 and 15:57:54.257, both error="ssh: bootstrap
line exceeds the bound".

## Acceptance Criteria

- An over-bound line is reported as what it is — output that is not nocx's
  protocol — and not as a connection that ended.
- The log names the byte count and the bound. The BYTES are never logged: the
  backend does not read the user's stream (AD-6), and a bounded prefix in a log
  file is reading it.
- Both readers (channel and local pty) are covered by a test that writes
  bound+1 bytes with no line ending.

title: 23 tests fail on a Linux dev machine before any change, so a merged gate here cannot be read without a baseline run
description:
Running `go test ./internal/... -count=1` on this Linux workstation fails in three packages BEFORE any local change. Measured 2026-08-28 by running the identical set at 64244ad4 (pre-change) and at the tip of feat/agent-tools after three merged commits: **the two failure sets are identical, 23 and 23, with zero difference in either direction.**

Failing packages:
- internal/app — 5 tests
- internal/shellintegration — 17 tests
- internal/notify/wailsadapter — [build failed], the same missing gtk4 / webkitgtk-6.0 pkg-config packages that make `go build ./...` exit 1 here

The full list is in the acceptance section so a future run can diff against it mechanically instead of by eye.

This is NOT the same as nocx-58gq or nocx-65v6: both of those are macOS workstations, and they name internal/pty, internal/git/local and the child-environment probe. This is Linux and a different set of packages, and nothing in AGENTS.md warns about it — its paragraph on local-versus-CI disagreement names only the macOS cases.

Why it matters beyond annoyance: a coordinator integrating parallel workers is told by AGENTS.md to run the merged gate and to send a red gate back to the worker who caused it. Here the gate is red before anyone touches anything, so without a measured baseline the correct action — accept the work — looks exactly like the incorrect one. It cost a baseline run to establish, and the next coordinator will pay it again.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On this Linux workstation, check out a commit with no local changes.
2. go test ./internal/app/... ./internal/shellintegration/... -count=1
3. Observe the failures below. They reproduce on a clean tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

Either the three packages pass on an ordinary Linux dev machine, or the shortfall is documented where a coordinator will meet it — AGENTS.md's local-versus-CI paragraph — naming the packages and the reason, so a baseline run is a known cost rather than a discovery. Whichever is chosen, the list below is what a later run diffs against.

Baseline at 64244ad4:

TestAPlatformThatCannotObserveStillOpensTheSession
TestBashChannel_AcceptNeverComesKeepsVisiblePrompt
TestBashChannel_AnswersRefreshWithSnapshot
TestBashChannel_CapabilityNeverInAnyEnvironment
TestBashChannel_ChildFrameWithoutCapabilityProducesNoAcceptedEvent
TestBashChannel_ChildProcessCannotReadTheCapability
TestBashChannel_HandshakeAndLifecycle
TestBashChannel_HelloNeverArrivesKeepsVisiblePrompt
TestBashChannel_LocalDescriptorTransport
TestBashLauncher_RunsUnderDash
TestBashNested_AnAcceptedSSHGrantRunsTheBootstrapInsteadOfTheLine
TestBashNested_ARefusedSSHGrantStillRunsTheUsersCommandExactlyOnce
TestBashScript_ParsesUnderBash32
TestBootstrapProgressBlock_RunsOnEveryBashOnThisMachine
TestClosingAnEnhancedSessionEndsItsWatch
TestLaunchCarrier_GoodManifest_PosixExecsIntegratedShell
TestLiveSshd_ZshAdapterReachesAcceptedDomain
TestLocalEnhancedSessionIsWatchedForReplacement
TestLocalEnhancedSessionReportsWhatItStarted
TestPosixLauncher_EmitsMarkersFromPS1
TestStartupFidelity_HushloginSuppressesTheBanner
TestStartupFidelity_MotdPrintedExactlyOncePerTier
TestStartupFidelity_SystemProfileObservableOrDeclared
notes:
BASELINE IS STALE BY ONE TEST, re-measured 2026-08-29 on the merged
feat/agent-tools tree.

This run failed 24 distinct tests where the recorded baseline lists 23. The
arithmetic of the difference:

- TestLocalZshSession_AZprofileThatExecsStillRuns is GENUINELY NEW to the
  list, and it is not new breakage. It arrived from main in 04ecf07b
  (fix(shellintegration): a local zsh tab runs the user's login phases,
  nocx-2ka0), which postdates the 64244ad4 baseline, and it fails for exactly
  the reason the rest of the list fails:

    launcher_local_zsh_test.go:1114: timed out waiting for the program the
    user's ~/.zprofile exec'd; output=".zprofile:1: no such file or
    directory: /bin/echo"

  Same class as TestLocalEnhancedSessionReportsWhatItStarted's "fork/exec
  /bin/bash: no such file or directory". THE CAUSE IS NIXOS: there is no
  /bin/echo and no /bin/bash on this workstation, and the fixtures hardcode
  absolute paths under /bin. Anything added later that shells out to /bin/*
  will join this list automatically.

- Three further entries looked new and are not: /unknown subtests of
  TestStartupFidelity_HushloginSuppressesTheBanner,
  TestStartupFidelity_MotdPrintedExactlyOncePerTier and
  TestStartupFidelity_SystemProfileObservableOrDeclared. The baseline records
  parent names only, so a mechanical diff reports the children as additions.
  WHOEVER DIFFS THIS LIST SHOULD NORMALISE SUBTEST NAMES FIRST, or the
  baseline reports four discrepancies where there is one.

- Nothing on the baseline passed. The set only grew.

Also worth recording for the acceptance criterion: TestPosixLauncher_
EmitsMarkersFromPS1 fails for a DIFFERENT and self-describing reason -- dash
is missing from PATH, and the test deliberately refuses to skip ('The
launcher's riskiest paths must not silently skip'). That one is provisionable
where the /bin/* ones are not.

title: pre-push stops running the containerized suites; the gate is CI and the integrator
description:
pre-push runs the whole Go module under -race and the whole vitest suite, each
in its CI image, on every push. Measured cost on the owner's machine: minutes
per push, and it is paid by whoever is pushing a branch — not by whoever
integrates.

That is the cost AGENTS.md already argues nobody should pay on a branch: "The
gate belongs to whoever integrates, and to nobody else. A worker on a branch
runs the unit tests for the files it changed, and stops there." The same
section records three measured costs of running the containerized jobs per
branch — they serialize on one Docker daemon, they mount node_modules as named
volumes with no worktree in the name so concurrent runs break each other's
dependency tree (nocx-x6z3), and a full gate per branch was also a keychain
dialog storm per branch. This repo now routinely has five or more worktrees
live at once, which is exactly the shape those costs scale with.

So the containerized suites come out of pre-push. What remains protecting main
is unchanged and is where AGENTS.md already puts it: CI is the source of truth,
and `make ci-full` on the MERGED tree is the integrator's, every time.

The owner asked for this directly on 2026-08-28.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `git push` from a worktree runs no container and no test suite, and still
  pushes the issue tracker (push_beads_state must survive — a push that skips
  it leaves collaborators on a backlog days old).
- AGENTS.md's "How we work" and "Git authority" sections describe the gate the
  hooks actually run: a reader must not be able to find the containerized
  suites documented as a push-time gate that no longer exists.
- `make ci-full`, `scripts/ci-linux.sh`, `scripts/ci-frontend.sh` and
  `e2e/run-in-container.sh` are untouched and still runnable on demand.

## Out of scope

Moving the suites somewhere else (a host-side pre-push, a lighter subset). If a
branch-time net is wanted later it is a separate decision with its own measured
cost; this bead removes the one that was measured to be too expensive.
close_reason: Done on main by nocx-fwsw2 (ee17a2f6), from worktree-clear-valley-0dba. Same outcome: pre-push publishes the tracker and runs no suite; AGENTS.md and the hook prose follow. Two differences, both theirs better: containerized-tests.sh is KEPT as the by-hand entry point rather than deleted, and the diagnosis is sharper — the old hook's scoping never fired at all, because git hands pre-push the REMOTE's sha and a branch the remote has not seen is forty zeros, so every first push ran both suites whatever the diff held. My chore/pre-push-drop-containers (692f7498) is dropped unmerged and never pushed; nothing to revert.

title: Step 7: spec self-review (placeholders, consistency, scope, ambiguity)
A tool can return more than the run can hold, and nothing says when it should have stopped
description:
Every tool needs an explicit byte or result limit, a deadline, defined cancellation behaviour and DETERMINISTIC truncation that states what was dropped. Today only files.read has a window (a fixed 64 KiB, internal/assistant/execute.go:26) and it is that tool's own return contract rather than a property of the registry.

Baseline tool-execution safety, and a precondition for projection: renderer results are component-shaped and can be large because a component can render them — a model tool must not ingest them automatically. Shared execution does not imply identical serialisation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant to read a large or unbounded source through any tool other than files.read — e.g. `run` on a command producing megabytes.
2. Nothing in internal/agenttools bounds the result; only files.read's own executor windows its output.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every declaration states its result bound, its deadline and its cancellation behaviour; truncation is deterministic and the result says what was dropped and how much remained; a row omitting them does not assemble. Raised by an adversarial review (codex, 2026-08-28).
close_reason: ResultBound, Deadline and Cancellation are required declaration fields; filesReadWindowBytes removed so there is one bounding mechanism. Landed as e7483014.

title: The assistant replaces a whole function by pointing at its first line, in languages where that is exactly right
description:
MEASURED, 2026-08-28, before deciding anything. A pure-Go tree-sitter runtime exists — github.com/odvcencio/gotreesitter, MIT, v0.51.0, 206 grammars as compressed parse tables, no cgo, cross-compiles everywhere. Binary cost, built on this machine: baseline Go binary 2.41 MB; + runtime with one grammar 13.05 MB; with six 13.56 MB; with all 206 31.84 MB. So the runtime is ~10.6 MB and each grammar ~100 KB — grammar SELECTION is not the interesting cost, the runtime is. Still to measure before committing: decompressed table memory, cold start, first-parse latency, behaviour on pathological files.

AND THE ALGORITHM IS NOT PORTABLE AS WRITTEN. Ported crates/pi-ast/src/block.rs ('climb to the outermost named ancestor still beginning on this row') to Go against gotreesitter and ran it on a thirteen-line Go file. Line 6 (a func opener) resolved 6..11, correct. Line 13 correct. A blank line and a lone closing brace correctly resolved to nothing. But line 7, an `if` ending on line 9, resolved to 7..11 — because gotreesitter's Go grammar interposes a `statement_list` node that ALSO begins on row 7, which upstream tree-sitter-go does not have. So `PUT 7*:` would silently widen from 'replace the if' to 'replace the if, the return and the function's closing brace'. THE RESULT STILL PARSES, so a post-edit validity check would bless the corruption.

Therefore 'we have a parser for it' is NOT an acceptance criterion. The unit under test is the triple: grammar version x resolver policy x source construct. A parser gives exact syntax nodes; it does not answer the product question 'what span did the person mean by this line'.

BUNDLED and ENABLED are separate concepts: all 206 grammars may be bundled while the locator is enabled for two. Maintain an explicit allowlist of {language, grammar version, resolver policy, corpus version}.

CORPUS CONTENTS, per enabled language — human-authored expected spans, with upstream/pi-ast/gotreesitter outputs recorded as DIAGNOSTICS, never as the oracle:
- A nested construct followed by a sibling in its parent (the if/return regression above), with sentinel statements immediately before and after the expected span.
- Every construct promised: function, method, class/type, conditional, loop, switch/match, case arm, exception branch, anonymous function, module.
- Transparent grammar wrappers beginning on the same row: statement_list, block, body, declaration lists.
- Multiline headers; opening delimiter on the same line vs the next; headers preceded by attributes or decorators.
- Decorators, annotations, doc comments, ordinary comments — inclusion stated explicitly, never inherited from tree shape.
- Single-line constructs, bare statements, blank lines, closing delimiters, continuation lines, interior body statements — each with an exact span or a mandatory null.
- if/else and try/catch/finally: decide whether anchoring a branch means the branch, the whole compound statement, or refusal. Grammar ancestry will not make that product decision.
- Strings, regexes, templates, heredocs, macros and comments containing fake delimiters.
- Temporarily invalid source, missing closers, error nodes — default null, never best effort.
- BOM, CRLF, no final newline, empty file, huge lines, Unicode identifiers, mixed indentation.
- Markdown headings inside fenced and indented code, varying fence lengths, Setext headings, an unclosed fence. Markdown needs a small deterministic state machine, not 'no parser at all'.
- TS vs TSX, JS vs JSX, aliases and misleading extensions.
- Real-source fixtures mined from repositories alongside the adversarial microfixtures: microfixtures find algorithm defects, real files find grammar shapes nobody anticipated.

UPDATE GATE: any output change after upgrading gotreesitter or a grammar requires review. A widened span is a failure even when the file parses.

BlockResolver stays an interface: tree-sitter for enabled languages, a markdown state machine, and an explicit refusal for everything else.
acceptance_criteria: For each ENABLED language, a corpus of human-authored expected spans passes exactly: every must-resolve anchor returns the exact inclusive range, every must-refuse anchor returns null, an unresolved structural locator produces ZERO writes, and the resolved concrete range appears in the preview, the approval and the result. A language without a passing corpus does not advertise the block locator to the model at all — not 'offered and erroring'. Deliberately out: proximity recovery, any degradation of an unresolved locator to a line-relative one, and syntax-guided repair of a mismatched edit.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-29, and it overturns this bead's own diagnosis. Read this
before proposing block operations again.

THE DIAGNOSIS IN THE DESCRIPTION IS WRONG. It blames gotreesitter for
interposing a statement_list node "which upstream tree-sitter-go does not
have". Upstream HAS it. Ported the pi-ast climb ("outermost named ancestor
still beginning on this row") to Go against github.com/tree-sitter/
go-tree-sitter v0.25 + tree-sitter-go v0.25 -- the same grammar version
oh-my-pi uses -- and ran the thirteen-line file from the description:

  7  "\tif n > 0 {"   ->  7..10   [if_statement -> statement_list]

Identical widening. The defect is in the ALGORITHM, not the library: a
transparent wrapper that begins on the anchor row and ends later swallows the
following sibling. oh-my-pi carries the same latent bug; its passing test
resolves_inner_if_block is TypeScript, where statement_block begins on the
brace row, so no widening occurs and the test is green while the policy is
wrong.

NO UNIVERSAL CLIMB POLICY EXISTS. Tried the obvious fix -- climb only to a
parent whose end position equals the child's:

  policy      Go line 7 (if)     Rust line 1 (pub fn f)
  loose       7..10  WRONG       1..6   right
  strict      7..9   right       1..1   WRONG (visibility_modifier alone)

Rust's `pub` is also a named node beginning on the anchor row and ending
earlier. Each policy is correct for one language and corrupting for the other.

BINARY COST WAS MEASURED AGAINST THE WRONG LIBRARY, and cgo is available:
the desktop app already builds CGO_ENABLED=1; CGO_ENABLED=0 is load-bearing
only for cmd/nocx-helper, which imports git/hostsvc, git/local and
helper/host and neither hashline nor agenttools. Upstream, cgo, stripped,
against a 1.51 MB baseline:

  runtime                 +0.27 MB   (gotreesitter runtime was +10.6 MB)
  json ~0.00  go +0.20  javascript +0.39  python +0.44  c +0.59
  rust +1.06  bash +1.29  typescript+tsx ~+2.75
  nine grammars together: 8.50 MB binary

So the cost objection dissolves and the correctness objection does not. Note
the inversion: with gotreesitter the runtime dominated and grammar selection
was free; with upstream the runtime is free and grammar selection is the
whole cost.

WHY IT IS CLOSED ANYWAY. `PUT 7*:` is one anchor plus one silent resolver,
and one line does not carry enough information to distinguish if_statement
from the enclosing statement_list from the function body from the function.
No parser recovers intent that was never expressed. The failure is silent by
construction: the widened result still parses, so a post-edit validity check
blesses the corruption.

And the feature buys little. hashline.Read already bakes line numbers into
the text it hands the model ("1:one\n2:two\n" in hashline_test.go), so the
model does not count -- it reads `6:func f(...) {` and `11:}` and writes
`PUT 6.=11:`. The locator would only save it from finding a matching closing
delimiter by eye.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, so they are not proposed again:

- Context-anchored patch with fuzzy matching (hermes-agent V4A + 1187-line
  nine-strategy chain). Directly contradicts nocx-q4so4's shipped invariant
  that a stale edit is refused rather than applied. Their own comment records
  the near-miss: thresholds of 0.10/0.30 were "dangerously loose -- a 10%
  middle-section similarity could match completely unrelated blocks."
- Exact old-text replacement with mandatory uniqueness and NO fuzzy fallback.
  Safe (every deleted byte appeared in the request) but costs the model the
  whole block in output tokens, and the model can still copy the wrong unique
  block.
- go/parser for Go only -- no new dependency, exact positions. An honest
  single-language helper, but it does not generalise and still needs a
  per-language policy for comments, directives and decorators.
- LSP folding ranges: nondeterministic (depends which server the user has
  installed) and folds are presentation, not a syntactic contract.
- Lexical brace matching per language: Go tractable; JS needs regex-vs-
  division and template re-entry, Rust variable-length raw strings and nested
  block comments, shell heredocs. A naive scanner terminates early and
  silently.
- Python indentation: silently drops a decorator or leaves a `finally`.

WHAT SURVIVES is the verification half, filed separately: name the anchor and
the byte-exact first UNTOUCHED line, and refuse on mismatch. It is not a
convenience -- it strengthens the refuse-don't-guess invariant.

Sources read: oh-my-pi crates/pi-ast/src/block.rs (1199 lines, ~55 grammars);
hermes-agent tools/patch_parser.py + tools/fuzzy_match.py. Second opinion via
codex agreed independently that the feature as specified should not be built.
close_reason: Won't do. The premise fails independently of the library: on upstream tree-sitter-go v0.25 the pi-ast climb widens 'the if on line 7' to 7..10 by swallowing statement_list, exactly as the pure-Go port did, and no universal climb policy exists (the fix for Go resolves Rust's 'pub fn' to the visibility_modifier alone). Cost is no longer the objection -- upstream costs +0.27 MB of runtime, not +10.6 MB -- correctness is. One anchor line does not express which construct was meant, and the widened result still parses, so the corruption is silent by construction. hashline.Read already numbers the lines it shows the model, so the locator would only save it from matching a closing delimiter by eye. Full measurements, the rejected alternatives and their reasons are in the notes. The verification half survives as nocx-ynbb5.

title: The composer's cursor is a bar where the terminal's is a block
description:
The composer drew a bar caret while the terminal one row above draws a block, so one product had two vocabularies for "where your typing goes". Asked for by the owner (2026-08-28): "можем заодно курсор сделать квадратным, как в других терминалах?" xterm already owns the answer: a block filled with `--terminal-cursor`, the glyph under it painted in `--terminal-cursor-accent`, and nothing at all when the surface is unfocused (`cursorInactiveStyle: 'none'`, renderers/xterm.ts). This is that answer extended to the prompt, with the same two tokens and the same unfocused rule, rather than a second one beside it. ## Shape The block is drawn two ways, and the split is the design: - ON A CHARACTER — a mark decoration (block-cursor.ts), which paints behind the glyph and recolours it. A block laid over the text would hide the character it stands on, which a terminal never does, and which costs more in a box you move around in than in one you only type at the end of. - AT THE END OF A LINE — CM6's own cursor element, widened to `1ch` in style.css. Both alternatives are wrong there: an inline widget brings back the `cm-widgetBuffer` image of the height defect, and a line-level `::after` renders after everything on the line — including the completion ghost — so the cursor would sit at the end of the suggestion (`unam[e]#`) rather than at the caret (`unam#e`). Also measured: on an EMPTY line an `::after` lands behind the `
` CM6 gives that line and the card doubles, 16.797 → 33.594. No blink, because xterm does not blink, and it is turned off through drawSelection's `cursorBlinkRate: 0` rather than in CSS: the cursor layer writes an inline `animation-name` on itself, so no stylesheet rule can outrank it. ## Checks - block-cursor.test.ts, six cases through a mounted CommandEditor. The end-of-line half is deliberately NOT asserted there: CM6 places that element by measuring coordinates and jsdom computes no layout, so an assertion would pass against any implementation. - Verified in a browser on the dev stand, five states: empty, end of line, mid-line, with a completion ghost (block before the ghost, at x=158.9 against the ghost's 159.5), and unfocused. Line box and card height 16.797/76.797 in every one. No blink: animation-duration 0s, opacity 1 sampled over 2.6s. ## Acceptance Criteria - The composer's cursor is a block of one character cell, painted with `--terminal-cursor` — the same token and the same shape as the terminal one row above, in every theme. - A character under the cursor stays readable: it is recoloured to `--terminal-cursor-accent`, never hidden. - An unfocused composer shows no cursor at all, matching xterm's `cursorInactiveStyle: 'none'`. - With a completion ghost on screen the cursor is at the caret, BEFORE the suggestion, not after it. - Neither form changes the height of the line box or of the card, in any state — including the empty document. - Exactly one cursor is on screen in every state.
close_reason: Done in 22c42429: the block is a mark decoration on the character under the caret and CM6's own cursor element at the end of a line, with xterm's two tokens and its unfocused rule. Verified by the owner in the macOS app.

title: internal/app tests inherit NOCX_SHELL_INTEGRATION from the nocx tab they run in, and one of them fails because of it
description:
TestLocalSession_UnsupportedLoginShellRunsItAndSaysWhy asserts that a shell with
no tier is NOT told it is being integrated. Run from inside a nocx tab it fails:
the fake shell reports GATE=[1], because NOCX_SHELL_INTEGRATION=1 is in the test
process's own environment and reaches the child through os.Environ().

So the test reports the environment it was launched from, not the product. It is
red on a developer's machine for a reason that has nothing to do with the code,
and green in CI where nothing exports the variable — the exact shape AGENTS.md
warns about, because a test that is red for the wrong reason gets read as a
known-red and stops being read at all.

pty_local.go scrubs launcher session variables (scrubLauncherSession) but not
this one; whether the product SHOULD scrub it for a nested local session is a
second question this bead should answer rather than assume.

## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-28:

1. From inside a nocx tab: go test ./internal/app/ -run
   TestLocalSession_UnsupportedLoginShellRunsItAndSaysWhy
   → FAIL: "a shell that will not be integrated must not be told it is:
     FAKE_SHELL_STARTED argv=[-l] MODE=[marker-only] GATE=[1]"
2. env -u NOCX_SHELL_INTEGRATION -u NOCX_PROMPT_MODE -u NOCX_SESSION_ID
   go test ./internal/app/ -run <same>
   → PASS

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test passes when run from inside a nocx session, and still fails if the
  product actually tells an unsupported shell it is integrated.
- The question it raises is answered in the code or the bead: whether a nested
  local session should inherit the parent tab's NOCX_SHELL_INTEGRATION at all.

title: when the local lifecycle bootstrap fails, the fallback starts zsh without -l, so the session loses the login PATH
description:
internal/app/app.go:2300 falls back with cfg.Args = []string{"-i"}. Forty lines
above, the no-tier path for fish/tcsh uses []string{"-l"}, and the zsh enhanced
launch uses []string{"-l", "-i"} for a reason LocalEnhancedLaunch states: the
login startup files are where a GUI-launched app gets a usable PATH at all.
pty_local.go:143's library default is "-i" too.

On macOS the app inherits launchd's PATH. Without -l neither /etc/zprofile
(path_helper) nor ~/.zprofile runs, so a degraded session degrades twice: it
loses shell integration AND the PATH every other terminal gives the user. That
second half is exactly nocx-2ka0 — `command not found` for a tool that is
installed — arriving by a different route.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS with a zsh login shell and a PATH entry set only in ~/.zprofile
   (the Homebrew shellenv eval is the canonical case).
2. Make the local lifecycle bootstrap fail (LocalEnhancedLaunch returns an
   error — e.g. an unwritable TMPDIR).
3. The tab comes up conventional, as intended, and the ~/.zprofile entry is
   missing from PATH. Terminal.app on the same machine has it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The conventional local fallback for a zsh login shell starts a LOGIN shell,
  and a fixture ~/.zprofile PATH entry is present in the session.
- The bash fallback is unchanged: a bash user must get exactly what they got.
- The two fallback paths in localPTYFactory.NewPTY agree about -l, or the file
  says why they differ.

title: The tab strip's menu offers New note
description:
The tab strip's caret menu offers Quick connect…, Insert a secret…, Snippets… and
New workspace…. A note is not there. Until now it was reachable two ways: ⌥⌘N, which
is only a shortcut once you know it exists, and the Notes panel, which a person has
to find in the activity bar first. So for anybody who has met neither, "make me a new
note" was not offered anywhere they look for "make me a new thing" — and the row
beside it, New workspace…, is exactly that shape.

Not a contradiction of the notes spec §6.3 (.internal/specs/2026-08-16-notes-design.md).
That paragraph says the CHORD reaches a note with "no panel, no menu, no dialog" —
it is about the chord's distance, which this does not lengthen. The spec's three
surfaces (panel, tab, chord) gain a fourth door onto the one the chord already opens.

The row calls the same createAndOpenNote() the chord and the panel's + call — one
owner for "make a note and open it" (AD-8), not a second creation path.

Also gives Notes its own glyph. TextQuoteIcon meant BOTH "saved phrase" (snippets)
and "a note" (the Notes panel's activity-bar entry), which would have put one mark on
two rows one apart in the same menu — the failure tab-strip.tsx already records for
LayersIcon. StickyNoteIcon takes the note half.

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] Opening the caret menu in the VERTICAL strip finds a row reading "New note";
    clicking it calls onNewNote exactly once
[ ] The same holds for the HORIZONTAL strip — a strip replacement does not lose it
[ ] The row's label contains no "…": nothing further is asked, the note and its tab
    exist by the time the menu has closed
[ ] The row's glyph shares no path with the Snippets row's glyph
[ ] With no callback wired the row is inert rather than throwing
[ ] main.tsx wires it inside wireQuickConnect, so it survives an orientation change
[ ] frontend/src/ui/README.md has a row for StickyNoteIcon and for TextQuoteIcon
    saying which meaning is whose

title: secret-panel-position asserts a pixel number, not that the panel is anchored: 17.5 <= 16 fails on a tree that passes four times out of five
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

e2e/secret-panel-position.spec.ts:209, inside expectAnchoredToField:

  expect(gap).toBeLessThanOrEqual(16)

where gap is Math.abs(panel.top - field.bottom).

Run the e2e suite on 490517a6 (the v0.3.0 tag commit) enough times. Observed on that
exact tree, 2026-08-28:

  RED    CI run 33173357366, ci-e2e (chromium), first attempt:
         expect(received).toBeLessThanOrEqual(expected)
         Expected: <= 16    Received: 17.5
  GREEN  the same job, rerun, no change to the tree at all
  GREEN  CI on PR #117 (both browsers)
  GREEN  the ci.yml run inside the v0.3.0 release (both browsers)
  GREEN  e2e/run-in-container.sh locally, 456 passed

Same commit, five runs, one red.

## What is wrong

The assertion states a NUMBER where the property is a RELATIONSHIP. What the spec is
about - and what its own helper is named for - is that the panel is anchored to the field
a person is typing in, rather than floating at the top of the window. 17.5px of gap
satisfies that as completely as 16 does; nothing a person can see or do differs between
them. What the test actually measures is whether this renderer, at this font, at this
device pixel ratio, rounds the same way the author's did.

That makes the threshold a magic constant with no derivation. 16 is presumably a spacing
token, but the assertion does not read the token, and a half-pixel of subpixel rounding
puts the measured value outside a bound that was never meant to be exact. AGENTS.md
already warns that layout-sensitive specs behave differently between the container's
Linux WebKit and CI's runners; this is that class, and it now has a measurement.

Two other specs failed the same run and passed the same rerun, both on 30s locator
timeouts rather than on geometry - api-secret-in-path.spec.ts:163 waiting for the
'Change where this goes' button, and vault-sealed-probe.spec.ts:191 on webkit. They are
recorded here as context for how loaded that runner was, not as part of this bug: the
browsers failed on non-overlapping specs, which is what said 'flake' rather than
'regression' in the first place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The assertion states the relationship the spec is named for, not a pixel count. Either
  the bound is derived from the spacing token the layout actually uses (read, not
  retyped), or the check becomes the qualitative one: the panel's top is below the
  field's bottom and within the same screenful, so a panel anchored to the window rather
  than the field still fails.
- Whatever replaces it, removing the anchoring logic from the component makes the spec
  fail. Demonstrated, the way nocx-y47mi's fix was: break it, watch it go red, restore it.
- No bare numeric literal is left in expectAnchoredToField without a comment naming where
  the number comes from.
- The spec is green on chromium and webkit, in the container and on CI.
close_reason: Shipped. The bare pixel literal is gone from e2e/secret-panel-position.spec.ts: the bound is now the derived constant ANCHOR_GAP_PX = readAnchorGap(), which reads the value out of floating-panel.ts rather than retyping it, and the helper branches on the three placements with the whole Measured object in the failure message. The only 16 left in the file is inside a comment explaining the old assertion. That is this bead's acceptance verbatim — no bare numeric literal, the bound derived from the token, read not retyped. Commit 78657366, subject 'test(e2e): the panel spec asserts anchoring, not a pixel count (nocx-brf45)', verified present during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh. Its sibling nocx-rthz7 closed as a duplicate. NOT covered by this close: nocx-sa1pk stays open, because its webkit half is a different assertion in the same file (#endpoint-header-0-value not visible after the Add header click, still waiting on a fixed budget at :366).

title: TestAPIRequestCancel_ASecondCancelAfterItSettledChangesNothing accepts a cancel the settled token should refuse
description:
internal/transport, ws_api_cancel_test.go:161. The assertion that fired:

  cancelling a settled exchange was accepted; the token stops resolving when it settles

## Steps to Reproduce

Load-dependent, so it needs the whole suite under contention rather than the package:

  go test -race -tags gtk3 ./...            # in .githooks/images/go-tests, or `make ci`

on 490517a6 (or 41ccebe2 - the tree changes zero Go files). Seen twice on 2026-08-28:

1. The pre-push gate on the first push of docs/release-v0.3.0-refresh. That push ran the
   whole suite only because the branch was new to the remote - .githooks/pre-push
   classifies an unknown branch as CLASSIFIED=0 and tests everything. Reported as
   FAIL internal/transport 233.902s. The test NAME was lost: the output was read through
   `tail -30`, which cut the --- FAIL lines. That is why this bead is a round later than
   it should have been.
2. `make ci-full` on the merged tree, host-side `ci` job: FAIL internal/transport 253.927s,
   name captured this time.

Does NOT reproduce:
- ./internal/transport/ alone in the hook's container: ok 191.7s
- -count=1 ./... in the same container: ok, 80 packages, 0 failures, transport 252.4s
- CI on PR #117: ci-backend x2 and ci-linux x2 green, identical tree.

So it is load-dependent, not environment-dependent. It is NOT the missing-/bin/bash and
missing-bash-3.2 class that reddens internal/app and internal/shellintegration on a
NixOS host - those tests say so themselves and name the container fixture to use.

## What is wrong

The property is a state, not a moment: once an exchange settles, its cancellation token
must stop resolving, and every later cancel must be refused. The run saw a cancel
ACCEPTED after settle. Either the token outlives the settle by a window, or the test
proceeds on a reply that precedes the token teardown and observes the gap. Either way
the assertion rests on a moment rather than on the closing event, which is the shape
nocx-td6d4 exists to remove.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The settle path in the API cancel handler is read, and the bead records WHICH end of
  the interval was missing: a token released after the reply, or a test proceeding on a
  reply that does not imply the release.
- The test waits on the observable state change that closes the interval - the token's
  release - and on no duration. No sleep, no retry budget standing in for a wait.
- The fix is demonstrated the way nocx-y47mi's was: the guard is removed and the test is
  watched to fail, then restored and watched to pass.
- `go test -race -tags gtk3 -count=5 ./internal/transport/` is green, and one full
  `./...` run under contention is green.

title: secret-panel-position.spec.ts is flaky in both browsers on ci-e2e
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Push a branch and let ci.yml run. Observed on run 33153950875, commit
   165b2f51, both e2e jobs failing at once and both inside this one spec.
2. Re-run the failed jobs: both pass (98796417918, 98796418032).

## What happens

Two DIFFERENT tests in the same spec, one per browser:

- chromium, e2e/secret-panel-position.spec.ts:213 "a field panel is inside
  the viewport, and its rows own their own point" — expectAnchoredToField
  measured a gap of 17.5 against a hard-coded tolerance of 16.
- webkit, e2e/secret-panel-position.spec.ts:291 "a field further down the
  form opens its panel at ITS OWN offset" — expect(locator).toBeVisible()
  failed, element(s) not found.

The chromium half is a 16px tolerance the panel misses by 1.5px under load
— a layout race dressed as a geometry assertion. The webkit half is the
panel row not being there yet.

Both belong to the panel-anchoring work (nocx-le5ic); the spec reached main
through PR #110, after the last green run of the branch that caught this,
which is why it looked like a regression from an unrelated frontend change.
Worth deciding whether the anchoring tolerance is the right assertion at
all, or whether the spec should wait on the panel's own settled state.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Both tests wait on an observable settled state of the panel, not on a
  numeric slack that a loaded runner can exceed.
- The anchoring assertion states what a user can see — the panel touches
  its field — in a form that does not change verdict with 1.5px of layout
  jitter.
- Ten consecutive e2e runs of this spec in both browsers pass, and the
  evidence is on this bead.

title: TestLiveSshd_SSHChildAssembly_ExitFreezesTheChildBlockAndCompletesTheParent is flaky on ci-linux
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Push a branch and let ci.yml run. Observed on run 33153950875, job
   98792195482, ci-linux (no-secret-service), commit 165b2f51.
2. The same test passed in the with-secret-service variant of the SAME
   commit and machine class, and passed on a plain re-run of the failed
   job (98796418056). Nothing in that commit is Go.

## What happens

    --- FAIL: TestLiveSshd_SSHChildAssembly_ExitFreezesTheChildBlockAndCompletesTheParent (30.05s)
        ssh_child_assembly_test.go:884: timed out waiting for child domain Established via its own hello
        composed-line terminal: Warning: remote port forwarding failed for listen port 40185
        child attempts published: []

The composed line names the cause: sshd refused the remote port forward
because the listen port was already taken, so the child never announced
itself and the test spent its 30 s waiting for a hello that could not come.

Two things to decide, and the second is the one AGENTS.md cares about: the
port is picked in a way that can collide with something else on the runner,
and the wait is a 30 s duration rather than an observable state change. A
test that needs the port to be free and the clock to be kind is already
broken on a busier machine; it has only not been caught yet.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- The remote forward's listen port cannot collide silently: either it is
  taken from the OS and read back, or a refused forward fails the test
  immediately with sshd's own message rather than after a 30 s wait.
- The test waits on the child domain reaching Established, never on a
  duration.
- The reasoning is recorded on this bead: which of the two causes was the
  real one, shown from the run, not assumed.

title: Placement stops delivering a viewport for a DPR-only change
description:
Review finding on PR #115 (nocx-cwnz0).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On the merged tree (main + PR #115), call
   `content.viewportChanged({ width: 800, height: 400, devicePixelRatio: 1 })`
   on a mounted TerminalContent, then the same rectangle with
   `devicePixelRatio: 2` — the delivery panes.ts makes when a window moves
   between displays of different scale.
2. Count `renderer.fitViewport` calls: one, not two. The second delivery is
   accepted by `viewportChanged` and dropped by the shared guard.

## What is wrong

nocx-cwnz0 gave XtermRenderer its own resolution media query and made it
refit inside the last authoritative viewport on every DPR change (design
§B.5: "the renderer may still observe things placement cannot express ...
device-pixel-ratio changes"). It also put one shared width/height guard in
front of both fit drivers.

Together those left a dead surface. panes.ts `_deliverViewport` still treats
`devicePixelRatio` as a delivery trigger: the same rectangle with a new DPR
is delivered to content, and `fitUsableViewport` — which compares width and
height only — silently drops it.

That is the shape AGENTS.md names: two surfaces owning one input, and the
loser goes on advertising what it can no longer deliver. DPR is also not
placement's quantity — placement owns the CSS rectangle, and B.5 assigns DPR
observation to the renderer. `ContentViewport.devicePixelRatio` has no
consumer anywhere in the frontend; it is read only by the panes.ts dedupe
that produced it.

## Two smaller things from the same review

- `refitIfResized`'s "no loop" docblock still argues only about height; the
  guard now covers width too, and why width cannot oscillate
  (`scrollbar-gutter: stable` in Chromium, overlay scrollbars in WebKit)
  is not written down anywhere.
- The DPR refit is a rare event on a user's second display and leaves no
  trace at all. `logDecision` exists for exactly this and costs nothing
  when `nocxDebug` is off.
acceptance_criteria:
- A DPR change that leaves the pane rectangle unchanged produces no
  viewport delivery from the presentation layer, asserted by a test in
  panes.test.ts that fails before the change.
- `ContentViewport` carries no quantity without a consumer.
- Design §B.5's payload line matches the code.
- The renderer's DPR refit emits one decision trace behind the existing
  seam, and nothing when tracing is off.
- The width half of the shared fit guard has its loop-safety argument
  written down.
notes:
Implemented on PR #115's branch (fix/resize-vertical-oscillation), commit
015a1225, on top of nocx-cwnz0.

What changed:
- ContentViewport is { width, height }. `devicePixelRatio` is gone: it had
  no consumer in the frontend, read only by the panes.ts delivery dedupe
  that produced it.
- panes.ts `_deliverViewport` no longer compares the ratio, so a display
  move over an unchanged rectangle produces no delivery at all. The ratio
  stays the renderer's, watched through the resolution query nocx-cwnz0
  gave it.
- Design §B.5's payload line amended, plus a paragraph on why the field
  left — the alternative (teaching the shared fit guard about DPR) puts the
  ratio back under two owners and fits with cell metrics xterm has not
  re-measured, which is the stale-metric fit that helped produce the
  oscillation.
- refitIfResized's "no loop" docblock now argues the width half too: the
  scroller's width comes from the pane, never from the grid drawn in it,
  and the vertical scrollbar cannot move it in either engine (Chromium
  reserves the gutter, WebKit's overlay bar occupies none).
- The DPR refit emits one `nocx:decide dpr refit` line with dpr, cell
  width/height, the cached viewport and the resulting cols/rows. Behind
  isDecisionTracing, so it builds nothing when off.

Tests:
- panes.test.ts "a display move that changes only the pixel ratio is not a
  delivery" — verified red before the panes.ts change (viewportChanged
  called 1 time), green after.
- xterm.test.ts "traces the refit behind the decision seam, and nothing
  when it is off".
- Using DECISION_PREFIX in that assertion made a baselined dead export
  live; dead-exports baseline regenerated, 150 -> 149.

Gates run on the branch merged with origin/main (b6f066f4):
frontend vitest 5355/5355, lint-fixtures 48/48, tsc both projects, npm run
lint (frontend + root), prettier, contracts:check, and the whole pre-commit
hook. NOT run here: make ci-full, the Go -race container, e2e — those are
the integrator's on the merged tree before main.
close_reason: Placement stopped announcing the ratio; the renderer keeps it and now traces the refit

title: TestLoader_EOFMidFrameNamesBootstrapInterrupted fails only in the full module run, and the symptom does not look like a race
description:
Seen once, 2026-08-28, in the pre-push hook's containerized 'go test -race -tags gtk3 ./...' on feat/ai-assistant. A retry of the same push on a quieter machine was green, and the push went through.

    --- FAIL: TestLoader_EOFMidFrameNamesBootstrapInterrupted (0.02s)
        carrier_exec_test.go:429: the session ended without emitting "NATIVE_LOGIN_RAN"; output:
            NOCX1 LOADER_READY
            NOCX1 OUTCOME interrupted
            /bin/sh: 4: id: not found
            /bin/sh: 4: [: Illegal number:

## What was measured before filing

- The test passes on ORIGIN/MAIN in the same image (nocx-hook-go:1.26-bookworm), run alone.
- It passes on feat/ai-assistant in the same image, run alone, -count=3.
- It only failed inside the whole-module run.

So it is neither this branch nor the image, and the image is not missing 'id' — a run of the same image finds it. Recorded because the obvious reading is wrong: 'id: not found' looks like a missing binary and is deterministic-shaped, which is exactly why somebody will otherwise spend an hour on the Dockerfile.

## The likely shape, not established

Something the full run does to the environment the spawned /bin/sh inherits — a PATH, or a fixture that another test in the package mutates and does not restore. That is the same shape found today in the Playwright fixture for e2e/ask-about-full-screen-program.spec.ts, where sentinels leaked between repeats until per-test cleanup was added.

Related: nocx-98fhn and the family before it (nocx-1s8re, nocx-vhxtn, nocx-josaw) are 'wait for the fact, do not assume the order'. This one may not belong to that family — the symptom is a degraded environment rather than a lost race — and saying so matters, because filing it under the wrong family is how it gets 'fixed' with a retry that hides it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not reliably reproducible. Run the pre-push hook, or the containerized whole-module race suite, on a loaded machine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either the leak is found and named — which test mutates what, and where it is restored — or the test is made independent of whatever it is inheriting.
- Whatever is decided, the fix is NOT a retry: a retry on this symptom would hide a real environment leak rather than tolerate a scheduling difference.
- The whole-module containerized run passes repeatedly on a loaded machine.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-l9le4: the same test, the same single assertion and the same failure text — TestLoader_EOFMidFrameNamesBootstrapInterrupted, 'the session ended without emitting NATIVE_LOGIN_RAN', and internal/shellintegration/carrier_exec_test.go contains exactly one such wait (the s.waitFor(nativeLoginMarker) that this bead cites at :429 and l9le4 at :432 are the same statement). l9le4 survives as the newer bead naming the mechanism visible in the code. This bead's distinct evidence is NOT discarded — it is copied into l9le4's notes, because its captured output carries /bin/sh: 4: id: not found and Illegal number, i.e. a degraded environment inherited from the whole-module run, which is a different mechanism from l9le4's lost event and is recorded nowhere else. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: The in-flight-token test asks once for a release that is not ordered against the reply
description:
`TestAPIRequestSend_ATokenAlreadyInFlightIsRefused` (internal/transport/ws_api_cancel_test.go) closes the sender's gate, waits for the FIRST send's reply, and then asks once whether the token is free. The reply and the release are two events and nothing orders them: the handler answers, then lets the name go.

It held until a loaded machine put them the other way round. Caught by the pre-push gate on a full container run — 0.00s, so not a timeout, a genuine lost race:

```
--- FAIL: TestAPIRequestSend_ATokenAlreadyInFlightIsRefused (0.00s)
    ws_api_cancel_test.go:283: the token was still held after its exchange settled:
      &{Code:-32602 Message:a request is already running under this token (token "run-1")}
```

The same package passes alone in the same image, twice, both keyring variants (192s, 198s) — it is company, not the code.

Fixed in passing because it blocked a push: the second send now retries until accepted or `wantWithin` elapses, which asserts the far end of the interval the comment above it already claimed to be asserting. A token that never frees still fails; it just takes the deadline to say so.

Filed rather than left silent because this is the fourth sibling in one family — main fixed nocx-1s8re, nocx-vhxtn and nocx-josaw the same way this week, all 'wait for the thing, do not assume the order'. Worth asking once whether the shape can be found rather than met: a helper that waits for an observable release, or a rule that no test asserts a second fact off the back of one reply.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the whole Go module under -race in the container, on a loaded machine (a full pre-push or ci-linux run).
2. The test fails at 0.00s with the token still held.
3. Run `./scripts/ci-linux.sh -- ./internal/transport/` alone — green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test states the interval rather than an order, and cannot pass by luck of scheduling.
- Whether the family has a shared shape is answered — either a helper the four can share, or a written reason why each waits differently.

---

## A second reading, from the feat/ai-assistant session (2026-08-28)
