ascend independently, no family is mixed WITHIN a run), and the ledger prose
matches whatever the fake actually streamed. Only the fake's attribution is
wrong.

This is AGENTS.md's "a test may not depend on timing" — the test waits on an
ordering the code never promises.

Fix: key the script by the ask rather than by arrival. Ask receives
assistant.AskParams, whose Messages carry the question ("first?" / "second?"),
so the fake can select deterministically and drop nextScript entirely.

PRE-EXISTING ON origin/main — reproduced on a clean origin/main worktree
(0aa521e6), not a defect of the feat/orchestration merge. Filed standalone.

## Steps to Reproduce

On origin/main, host, 2026-08-27:

    go test -race -tags gtk3 -count=60 \
      -run TestAgentAsk_TwoConcurrentStreamsInterleaveWithoutCorrupting \
      ./internal/transport/

    --- FAIL: TestAgentAsk_TwoConcurrentStreamsInterleaveWithoutCorrupting (1.28s)
        ws_agent_gap_test.go:884: run 1 (first ask) received "bbb1bbb2bbb3" — text from the other run
        ws_agent_gap_test.go:887: run 2 (second ask) received "aaa1aaa2aaa3" — text from the other run

2 failures in 60. Also seen once in a full `backend-linux` container run of
the merged feat/orchestration tree, which is how it was found.
acceptance_criteria:
- interleavedAskClient selects its script from the ask itself (the question in
  AskParams.Messages), not from a call counter; nextScript is gone.
- `go test -race -count=60 -run TestAgentAsk_TwoConcurrentStreamsInterleave...`
  is green.
- Deliberately out: the assertions themselves. What they check — independent
  seqs, no family mixed within a run, prose per turn — is right and stays.
close_reason: fixed on feat/orchestration: the interleave fake keys its scripts on the ask's question, not on arrival order (4693d721); -count=60 green

title: A panel row activates on mousedown, so a press cannot be aborted
description:
FloatingPanel binds its row activation to mousedown (floating-panel.ts:511 in the current
tree; the row's handler calls onPick). Press a row, drag off it, release somewhere else —
the action has already happened and there is no way to abort it. Every menu-like surface
on every platform activates on release, and this kit's own rows already do:

  ui/suggestion-field.tsx:412-413  role=option row: onMouseDown preventDefault + onClick
  ui/text-field.tsx:427-429        the lock itself: onMouseDown preventDefault + onClick

That is the established idiom for a control over a focused field, and the load-bearing
half is the preventDefault on mousedown, which suppresses the focus shift so the field
keeps focus and nothing closes underneath. Acting ON mousedown is a separate choice that
preventDefault does not require.

It was an accident, not a decision: git log -S mousedown shows it arrived in b9c5cc7a
with the first completion dropdown, with no comment and no bead, and travelled into
FloatingPanel wholesale in 401c23dc.

Found while diagnosing nocx-vzdna: it is also why Playwright's locator.click() could not
drive a row. click() is hover, mousedown, mouseup; the panel closed on the mousedown, so
the element detached mid-action and Playwright retried and reported a stale
'<html> intercepts pointer events'. That message misdirected three rounds of
investigation. e2e/secret-field.ts now presses the way the panel listens; that helper
keeps working after this fix, because down+up with no move between them is also a real
click.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Focus any value field and press the lock, or type '@', to open the secret panel.
2. Press the mouse down on a row and, without releasing, move the pointer off the row.
3. Release. The row's action has already run — a secret was inserted or a create ask was
   raised — and nothing the person did after pressing could stop it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Row activation moves to click; preventDefault stays on mousedown. One place,
  floating-panel.ts, so all four variants (secret, completion, recall, grant) change
  together.
- A test presses on a row, moves off, releases, and asserts NOTHING happened.
- A test presses and releases on the row and asserts it did happen — the paired case, so
  the fix cannot pass by disabling activation.
- The field keeps focus across the press, which is what preventDefault is there for,
  asserted rather than assumed.

title: agent-ask.spec's pointAt loses the Mark block affordance on containerized WebKit, and which test reports it moves
description:
The helper at e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts:302-304:

    const offer = block.page().locator('.mark-affordance .ui-button')
    await expect(offer).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 })
    await offer.click()

`toBeVisible` PASSES and the click then times out at 30 s with the element
resolved but not visible:

    locator resolved to <button ... aria-label="Mark block for the question">
    2 × waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable
      - element is not visible

So visibility flips between the assertion and the click — the shape of a hover
affordance losing its hover, or of the node being replaced under the locator.
Playwright reports "not visible", not "intercepts pointer events", so it is not
something covering it.

## Steps to Reproduce

    PW_PROJECTS=webkit ./e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts

## It is pre-existing, and the reporting test moves

Measured 2026-08-27 while gating a merge:

- full containerized suite, merged tree: 416 passed, 1 failed —
  agent-ask.spec.ts:578 "a second ask while the first streams lands its deltas
  on the right entry" [webkit], 30.3 s. Chromium ran the SAME test in 2.6 s.
- the spec alone, merged tree: failed at agent-ask.spec.ts:371 — a DIFFERENT
  test, same helper.
- the spec alone, CLEAN checkout of 163c0d48 in a detached worktree: failed at
  :578 again.

A clean tree fails it, and which test loses moves between runs. That is one
shared condition, not three test defects — the shape nocx-2h08 named in
internal/transport, in the e2e suite this time.

Related: nocx-6wayi asks for exactly this — each surviving containerized-WebKit
failure split into its own reproduction bead with evidence. This is one of those,
and it is not among the four that bead lists.

AGENTS.md's standing warning applies and is why this is P2 and not P1: the
container is Linux WebKit at a container-default viewport, the shipped app is
macOS WKWebView, and layout-sensitive specs fail there and pass in CI. Confirm
against CI before believing the product is broken.
acceptance_criteria:
- The reason the affordance stops being visible between `toBeVisible` and `click` is named. Not "added a wait" — either the hover state is lost (and the helper must not depend on hover surviving), or the element is re-created under the locator (and the helper must anchor to what survives).
- `PW_PROJECTS=webkit ./e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts` passes 5 consecutive runs, and the full containerized suite passes agent-ask.spec in both browsers.
- Whichever fix lands, it does not sleep: the wait is on observable state.
- If the conclusion is that the container's WebKit is lying and CI is right, that is written down WITH the CI evidence, and the bead closes on that — a documented divergence is an answer, a shrug is not.

title: The e2e container's npm ci runs --silent, so a failed install ends the whole suite with no output at all
description:
`e2e/container-entry.sh` runs

    echo "=== npm ci (root + frontend) ==="
    npm ci --silent
    (cd frontend && npm ci --silent)

with `bash -euo pipefail`. npm's `--silent` sets loglevel=silent, which
suppresses its ERRORS as well as its notices, so a failed install aborts the
script having printed nothing, and the entire e2e job's output is two header
lines.

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed twice on 2026-08-27 while gating a merge. The whole captured log of a
failed run:

    === building nocx-e2e:local (cached after the first run) ===
    === npm ci (root + frontend) ===
    e2e exit=152

and on the next attempt the same two lines with exit 1. Two different exit codes,
zero diagnostic either time. Both installs then succeeded when run by hand in the
same image against the same volumes, and the third scripted run got through to
`Running 430 tests using 1 worker` — so the fault was transient, which is exactly
the case where the message is the only thing that could have told anyone what it
was.

Cost: two full container runs plus a hand reproduction to establish only that the
step was not deterministically broken. A gate whose failure carries no
information cannot be distinguished from a gate that is lying, and the reflex it
teaches is "just run it again".
acceptance_criteria:
- When either npm ci fails in e2e/container-entry.sh, the reason is on screen. Whatever the mechanism (drop --silent, or keep it and print the captured output on failure), the run never ends with the last line being the step's own header.
- The quiet of a SUCCESSFUL run is preserved — the reason --silent is there is that two clean installs print ~40 lines of funding and audit notices before the suite starts, and that is worth keeping.

title: TestScheduler_PromptDebounceCoalesces paces its five hints with sleeps inside a 15 ms window, so load splits them into two samples
description:
Seen 2026-08-27 in ./scripts/ci-linux.sh on the merged feat/ai-assistant tree,
in the no-Secret-Service variant:

    --- FAIL: TestScheduler_PromptDebounceCoalesces (0.11s)
        schedule_test.go:225: exec count after 5 prompt hints = 3,
                              want exactly 2 (settle + one debounced)

## Steps to Reproduce

    ./scripts/ci-linux.sh          # on a loaded machine; internal/discovery, ./... run

It is not the change under it: the merge touches ZERO files in
internal/discovery, and the WITH-Secret-Service variant of the very same run
reported `ok github.com/shady2k/nocx/internal/discovery 2.162s`. Run alone in a
container on the same tree it passed 5/5 in 0.10s each — which is the point, not
a reassurance.

## The mechanism, in numbers

`testScheduler` sets `WithPromptDebounce(15 * time.Millisecond)`. The test then
delivers five hints spaced by `time.Sleep(2 * time.Millisecond)` — about 8 ms of
pacing inside a 15 ms window, so on an idle machine all five fall in one window
and coalesce to one sample.

Under load a single 2 ms sleep dilates past 15 ms. The hints then straddle two
debounce windows, the scheduler correctly emits two debounced samples, and the
count is 3 instead of 2. The scheduler did exactly what it should; the test's
notion of "rapid" is a claim about the machine's clock.

That is the AGENTS.md rule inverted: usually a test needs a slow machine, this
one needs a fast one. Both are the same defect — an assertion resting on a
duration rather than on an observable state change.

Family: nocx-mgevc, nocx-qqhsm, nocx-sf4kx, nocx-8b47. nocx-s8df was the same
file losing a different race and is closed.
acceptance_criteria:
- The test no longer depends on how long a `time.Sleep` actually takes: whether five hints are "rapid" is decided by the code under test or by an injected clock, not by the scheduler of the machine running it.
- It passes with the whole package under load — the shape that produced this report is `./scripts/ci-linux.sh` on a busy box, not the test run alone; a green run in isolation is not evidence here and 5/5 alone has already been observed while the full run was red.
- The sibling tests in schedule_test.go that pace with sleeps inside a window are audited in the same pass and named: fixing only the one that lost this round is how this recurs under a different test name (nocx-2h08).
- The debounce behaviour asserted is unchanged: five rapid hints still mean one sample.

title: Show the whole plan to the person when a plan step asks for approval
description:
The plan carrier (graphcarrier.go) exists to be compared against the program
carrier on ONE axis: what an approval can honestly show. A program is
Turing-complete, so an approval prompt can state the resolved effect in front
of it and whatever bounds are readable off the source. A validated plan can be
shown WHOLE before anything runs — every effect site, its tool, and which
earlier steps it depends on — because those are structural facts rather than
consequences of running it.

graphCarrier.Preview() already computes exactly that, and today it reaches only
the model: it is the "what ran / stopped here / never started" report a failed
step returns so the model can repair a half-run plan without repeating an
effect. The person, who is the one being asked to approve, sees the same single
call any other carrier would show them. So the carrier's whole distinguishing
claim is currently unverifiable in the product.

WHAT IS IN THE WAY, verified 2026-08-26 rather than assumed: the question
reaches the renderer as agent.approvalRequested, and contracts/
agent.approvalRequested.schema.json is the single declaration of that shape.
Carrying the plan means the schema gains an optional plan member, the
renderer's type is regenerated from it, the Go side is validated against it
(both the _DTOConformsToContract and the _OverTheWireConformsToContract tests),
and the approval surface renders it. That is why it is not a footnote on
nocx-d6gn4.8.

DELIBERATELY OUT: showing a plan before it starts, with nothing asking. That is
a different question (consent to a plan as a whole) and it would change what an
approval MEANS, which is ADR-0028 territory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A plan whose second step needs approval shows the person the whole plan when
  it asks: every effect site, its tool, and the earlier steps it reads.
- Asserted end to end — off the real socket, not off a payload the test built —
  so the schema, the Go side and the renderer are all party to it.
- The same run under the program carrier shows what it can honestly show and
  does not pretend to a plan. The contrast is the measurement nocx-d6gn4.10
  reads; a prompt that looked the same under both would erase it.
- One rendering of a plan, not two: whatever the person is shown and whatever a
  failed step reports to the model come off graphCarrier.Preview().
notes: Depends on the plan carrier, which is being removed (nocx-d6gn4.14). Close or rewrite when that lands.
close_reason: Moot. There is no plan step to show: nocx-d6gn4.14 removed the plan carrier, so no approval interrupts a plan mid-flight. The person sees the one invocation being approved, which is the whole of what is running.

title: The Secrets page loses the value the store row was holding
description:
nocx-3o0ed.2 gave the field's lock a store row that carries the typed value into the
create ask. That works wherever a vault client is wired: api-pane.tsx's
createSecretInPlace passes the value into openSecretCreateAsk.

The no-mint-seam fallback in main.tsx cannot. Its destination is the Settings Secrets
page via openSettingsPane().startNewSecret(name), and that page owns its own value
field (settings-content.ts) while startNewSecret takes a NAME only. The name travels,
the value does not, and the UI says nothing about the difference.

Escalated by the T2 worker rather than dropped silently; documented in a comment at
the call site in main.tsx.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Reach a surface whose SecretTextField has no mint seam — the main.tsx fallback,
   where requestCreate hands off to the Settings Secrets page.
2. Type a credential into the value field, e.g. Bearer t.Yixxxx.
3. Press the lock and activate the store row.
4. Settings opens with the name proposed and the VALUE EMPTY. The credential must be
   copied out of the field by hand and pasted in — the detour nocx-3o0ed removes
   everywhere else.

## Acceptance Criteria

- startNewSecret carries a value as well as a name, and the Secrets page opens with
  the value already filled in.
- A test drives the fallback path end to end and asserts the value arrives, not just
  the name.
- If a path genuinely cannot carry the value, the person is told before they leave the
  field rather than discovering it in Settings. A soft degrade must be visible in the
  product (AGENTS.md), not only in a code comment.
close_reason: startNewSecret(name, value) through the pre-mount queue, newSecret and a value signal; fallback source moved to vault.tsx as createVaultSecretSource so it exists once and is test-reachable. settings.test.ts 39->45, 574 tests green on the merged tree. Landed 95201f45.

title: Close waits for the auto-seal goroutine with no ceiling, and that goroutine can park in a provider's Lock()
description:
internal/vault/vault.go:752. Close() calls autoSealWG.Wait() unconditionally. On its
way out the auto-seal loop calls v.Seal(), which takes the provider's lock; a provider
whose Lock() never returns parks Close forever, and with it every caller of the
composition root's shutdown.

This is no longer the nil-channel shape — nocx-td6d4.7's second reading closed that
constructively with a WaitGroup whose zero value already returns. It is the older shape
AGENTS.md rule 3 names: an external call with no test for its failure.

## Steps to Reproduce

Give the vault a provider whose Lock() blocks forever, unlock it so auto-seal is armed,
then call Close(). Close does not return.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test drives Close() with a provider whose Lock() never returns and asserts Close
  still returns (or reports), rather than parking.
- The invariant is written with both ends: from the moment Close is entered until the
  goroutine is joined or the wait is abandoned, and what is true on disk and in memory
  either way.

title: T4 One control everywhere: SecretSource dies and three surfaces adopt the field
description:

It also carries the duplicated label the owner photographed — SecretSource renders a Field labelled 'Token' and the TextField inside newControl renders its own.

With T1 and T2 in place the control has nothing left to do, and removing it is what collapses two vocabularies into one rather than adding a third.
acceptance_criteria:
- frontend/src/secret-source.tsx is gone, and the connections editor, the endpoints page and the Auth tab all place the same field.
- The Auth tab shows its label ONCE. Asserted on rendered text, not by eye.
- The standalone 'Store' button on the Auth tab is gone: it was a crutch for a field that had no '@'.
- A bound field still renders its chip and still names the secret rather than its handle, on all three surfaces.
- The narrowable chooser from nocx-7mfwb.5 either moves inside the panel or is retired. Whichever it is, say in the code which, and do not leave both.

title: TestBroker_FailedDeliveryIsNotARecipient loses its pending id under load: the wait it stands on does not mean what the next line assumes
description:
internal/transport/request_broker_test.go:1138 fails as

    resolution by the delivered recipient refused: Unknown request id

The test waits for broker.Pending() == 1, then takes the lock, reads the single
key out of broker.pending, unlocks, and resolves it as c2. Under load the id it
read is no longer pending by the time Resolve sees it, so Resolve answers
"Unknown request id" and the assertion fires. Pending()==1 says a request is
registered; it does not say the request will still be registered on the next
line, and there is no second end to that interval anywhere in the test.

The same shape is one line further in TestBroker_WrongResolveMethodIsRefused,
which reads its id the same way.

## What was measured, and what it does NOT establish

On 2026-08-26, host, -race -parallel 8:

    w-waitfor (after the sleep sweep)   1 failure in 600 runs
                                        plus 1 in an earlier 300-run pass
                                        plus 1 in a containerized pre-commit run
    6106c6fe (main, before the sweep)   0 failures in 300, 0 in 600

That looks like a regression and probably is not one. The sweep's only change to
this file is three swaps of a package-local waitFor for testwait.WaitForTimeout,
and the two are semantically identical: the old helper polled every 10 ms
against a deadline and fatalled on expiry, which is exactly what testwait does,
and wantWithin is 30s on both sides. request_broker.go itself is untouched. At
roughly one failure per 600 runs, 900 clean baseline runs is not enough to
distinguish "the sweep opened it" from "the branch runs happened to be the
unlucky ones". Anyone re-measuring should interleave the two revisions under
comparable load rather than run them in sequence, which is how these numbers
were taken.

## Steps to Reproduce

    go test ./internal/transport/ -race -parallel 8 -count=600 \
      -run TestBroker_FailedDeliveryIsNotARecipient

Expect roughly one failure per several hundred runs on a loaded machine; a
single run passes in about a second.

## Acceptance Criteria

The test resolves an id it still holds, or it stops depending on the id
surviving between two statements — for instance by waiting on the condition it
actually needs (the request is pending AND both delivery seams have been
called), or by resolving under the same lock acquisition that read the id.
TestBroker_WrongResolveMethodIsRefused gets the same treatment.

Whichever way, the fix is a wait on a state the next line can rely on, not a
longer timeout: this is the epic's own rule applied to the epic's own output.

Deliberately out: changing request_broker.go. Nothing here says the broker is
wrong.

title: A settled exchange can still be stopped: the token is dropped after its answer is on the wire, and only one of the two paths knows it
description:
handleSend registers the cancel token before the send and drops it with

    defer h.cancels.drop(h.conn, p.Token)

on line 335 of internal/transport/ws_api_handlers.go. The function's last
statement is

    _ = h.r.TryResult(req.ID, mustMarshal(wireExchange(...)))

so the answer reaches the socket FIRST and the name is released afterwards. A
caller that reads its own result and immediately sends api.request.cancel for the
same token can be inside that window, and handleCancel then finds a live
registration and accepts the Stop for a run that already came back.

## This is not news to the code — one path already fixed it

Twenty lines above the final TryResult, the sealed-vault branch drops the token
explicitly, and says why:

    // The token is dropped HERE rather than only by the deferred
    // drop below, because the renderer re-sends the request VERBATIM
    // — the same token — as soon as the vault answers. The defer
    // runs after this response is enqueued, so releasing the name
    // first is what makes the replay's registration certain rather
    // than merely likely.

"The defer runs after this response is enqueued" is exactly the defect on the
ordinary path. One branch of one function was corrected with the reasoning written
out; its neighbour, which is the common case, was left.

## And the doc comment states the invariant the code does not hold

ws_api_cancel.go opens with "THE INTERVAL, BOTH ENDS ... until the exchange has
SETTLED, whichever way it settled, because the drop is deferred in the same
function. Never after". The deferral is offered as the reason the interval closes
on time, and it is the reason it closes late. This is the interval-with-two-ends
shape nocx-rtg0.6 names, with the far end placed after the event the client uses
to know the interval ended.

## Steps to Reproduce

Pre-existing on main, not introduced by the sleep sweep — measured both sides on
2026-08-26:

    # main before the sweep
    git worktree add --detach /tmp/base6106 6106c6fe
    cd /tmp/base6106
    go test ./internal/transport/ -race -parallel 8 -count=300 \
      -run TestAPIRequestCancel_ASecondCancelAfterItSettledChangesNothing
    # FAIL, ws_api_cancel_test.go:160

The same command on the sweep branch fails identically at line 161. A single run
(-count=1) passes in about a second on an idle host, which is why this reaches CI
as an occasional red rather than a standing one; it surfaced in a containerized
pre-commit run at 247s under load.

## Acceptance Criteria

The token stops resolving no later than the moment its answer is written, on every
path out of handleSend — so the drop happens before TryResult rather than after
it, the way the sealed-vault branch already does. A test that fails on the current
code and passes after: -count high enough to open the window, or the ordering
asserted directly.

The comment in ws_api_cancel.go either becomes true or says what it now means.

Deliberately out: rewriting the cancel registry, or changing what a refused Stop
answers.
close_reason: Fixed by commit 39d223df under nocx-f9har — internal/transport/ws_api_handlers.go:515 drops the cancel token before enqueueing the result, which is this bead's first and main criterion — and a duplicate of nocx-dbqmx, closed alongside. Its SECOND criterion is not silently dropped: the comment in ws_api_cancel.go:15 still explains the interval as closing because the drop is deferred, which is no longer true, and that two-line correction is filed as nocx-co4ao rather than kept as an open P2. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: git.status is described to nobody: a declared tool with no executor, and the policy branch it was the only path to
description:
Found while landing nocx-751xy, 2026-08-26, and recorded because it is a product fact rather
than a test detail.

`git.status` is declared in the tool table with no capability constructor — `Narrow` is nil —
so `policy.go` refuses it at execution with "declared but not executable". Before nocx-751xy
it was invisible: the run grant carried no path scope, so a path tool was never offered to
any model. That bead gave the grant the whole filesystem, which would have put a tool that
can only fail into every request, so `Registry.ForGrant` now omits any declaration with no
constructor — the registry's own rule, "the strongest refusal is the one never proposed".

The consequence: `git.status` is the ONLY declared tool with an empty `ResourceArg` (files.read
names `path`; session.list, session.read and run all name `sessionId`). So the policy's
"declares no resource" branch — `namedResource` returning declares=false, and the scope
check's unconditional true — has NO reachable production tool at all until `git.status` gets
an executor. It is not a regression: the branch was previously reachable only through a tool
that always failed. It is now unreachable honestly rather than dishonestly.

The test that covers that branch survived by moving to a synthetic registry: it assembles the
real table, takes session.list's real schema and executor, and empties only that copy's
`ResourceArg` (internal/assistant/policy_test.go). So the branch is still pinned; what it is
not is exercised by anything a person can cause.

## What to decide

Either wire `git.status` — it is a small tool over `internal/git`, which already exists and
is used by the Git panel — or decide deliberately that nocx ships without it and say so
where the declaration lives, so the next reader does not find a described, undeliverable
tool in the table and assume it works.

Wiring it is the obvious answer and it is cheap; the reason it is a bead rather than a line
in nocx-751xy is that an executor is a capability, and a capability needs its narrowing
decided (which repository, and what happens for a pane whose cwd is not in one) rather than
assumed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -n "git.status" -A8 internal/agenttools/registry.go` — the declaration has no
   `Narrow`.
2. Ask the assistant anything: the tools array carries files.read, session.list,
   session.read and run. `git.status` is described in the table and offered to nobody.

## Acceptance Criteria

• `git.status` either executes or is gone from the table, and whichever it is, the table says
why in one line.
• If it executes: what repository it reports on is decided from an owner that already knows
it, never guessed, and a pane that is in no repository gets an honest answer rather than an
error.
• The "declares no resource" policy branch has a reachable production tool again, or the bead
records deliberately that it does not and what that costs.
• The synthetic-registry fixture in policy_test.go is revisited: if a real no-resource tool
exists again, the test uses it.

title: SecretValueField has no caller outside its own test
description:
frontend/src/ui/secret-value-field.tsx describes itself as 'the one control in this product a secret VALUE is typed into'. It was put on the API Auth tab by 5d636b55 (nocx-m4cyq) and taken off by 113e1f26 (T5 of nocx-0khco). Since then its only importer is its own test.

This is the exact shape AGENTS.md names — a package that is reachable with a dead half, found only because somebody looked — and the reason it went unnoticed is worth writing down: the deadcode ratchet is Go-only. Nothing in the gates reports an unreachable TypeScript export, so a kit component can lose its last caller in the same commit that claims to have wired the feature it belonged to.

nocx-7mfwb.3 puts this component back in service, so the instance is being fixed there. What is filed HERE is the missing gate.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. grep -rn 'SecretValueField' frontend/src --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts
2. Every hit outside ui/secret-value-field.tsx is in ui/secret-value-field.test.tsx.
3. Both frontend gates are green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The frontend gates report an exported symbol whose only importers are test files, the way the Go ratchet reports an unreachable function — or, if that is judged not worth its false-positive rate, the decision is written down with the measurement that justified it rather than left as an absence.
- Whatever is chosen runs in ci-frontend, not only in a pre-commit hook, so a --no-verify commit cannot skip it.
- The check is proved the way the Go ratchet was (nocx-re6gk): a deliberately orphaned export IS reported, and the same export with one real importer is NOT.

title: T5 Choosing an existing secret can be narrowed from both doors

The recommendation is text first — it is the one that is missing, and a filter nobody applies is a control that costs a row of screen. Record the answer here.

- The person never leaves the request: no navigation to Settings, no losing the request they had open.
