title: Three secrets.* contracts are theatre: two schemas nothing validates, one method with no schema
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. grep -rn 'secrets.captureSave.schema.json' internal/transport/*_test.go — zero hits.
2. Same for secrets.captureDismiss.schema.json — zero hits.
3. grep -rn 'secrets.paneClosed.schema.json' internal/transport/*_test.go — one hit, the DTO case only.
4. ls contracts/secrets.usage.schema.json — no such file, though the method answers on the wire (ws_secrets.go:515).

## Expected

A committed schema is validated by at least the over-the-socket case, which is the one that proves the SERVER sends the shape (AGENTS.md rule 5).

## Actual

Two schemas are committed and nothing loads them; one has the DTO case only; one method has no schema at all.

Found while closing nocx-zqce.3, which added the missing DTO and over-the-socket cases for secrets.savePassword and secrets.saveKeyPassphrase. For contrast, the three that are complete after it — savePassword, saveKeyPassphrase and saveKeyMaterial — each have a schema plus both cases.
acceptance_criteria: secrets.captureSave, secrets.captureDismiss and secrets.paneClosed each have a …_OverTheWireConformsToContract test validating the real result off the real socket; secrets.usage has a schema in contracts/ with both cases. Each schema keeps additionalProperties:false and an explicit required, and pins the shape of any row handle it carries the way secrets.savePassword now does (^secrow:[0-9a-f]{32}$) — a bare string type lets the server send an empty row and still pass.

title: Several transport tests wait a fixed duration by design, which is the rule AGENTS.md forbids
description:
Found while closing nocx-2h08. Measuring where internal/transport spends its wall time turned up several tests that are slow because they WAIT A FIXED DURATION by design, which AGENTS.md forbids in as many words:

  "a test may not depend on timing. Wait on an observable state change - a frame, a record, a DOM state - never on a duration. A spec that needs a slow machine to pass is broken on a fast one too; it has only not been caught yet."

Measured 2026-08-25 on the post-fix tree, 1040 tests in 143.9s of test time:

  TestWSServer_FairnessTwoFloodingOneQuiet                5.09s - collects a five-second streaming window
  TestLineage_AParentMayNotCloseDriveOrObserveItsChild     4.00s - two two-second observation windows
  TestFilesChanged_DirtyPathsDeliveredOnceOnReattach       3.02s - drains a three-second bounded window
  signal and lease tests                                  ~2s each - exercise signal escalation grace periods

Deliberately NOT in scope: TestWSServer_CreditStopsSendingAtBoundary (8.13s) and TestWSServer_CreditDropAndReattachKeepsSequence (7.71s) are slow because they process 25,000-line PTY floods. They do work rather than wait, and that is legitimate.

These are the same class of defect nocx-2h08 turned out to be, one step earlier: a fixed window is a bet that the machine is fast enough, and the bet is what produced a timeout reporting under a different name on every run. Each of these is currently winning its bet, which is why nobody has noticed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each named test waits on an observable state change rather than a duration, or states in a comment why no observable event exists for what it is asserting and what bounds the wait instead.
- The package wall time falls, and the before and after are reported from the same machine.
- No assertion is weakened to make a test faster. A test that stops asserting what it asserted is not a fix.
- A grep-based check, or a note in AGENTS.md, makes the next fixed-duration wait visible when it is added rather than when it fails.

title: AGENTS.md's known-local-failure list names three tests; a clean main produces about twenty in other packages
description:
AGENTS.md tells a developer to read a local red against a named list before believing it:

  "internal/pty hangs to its 600 s panic here while green there, and three tests in internal/app and internal/git/local fail here and pass there (nocx-58gq, nocx-65v6). Until those are closed, read a local backend red against that list before believing it."

The list names three tests in two packages. Reality is roughly twenty across two DIFFERENT packages, so the advice cannot be followed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out an untouched main (verified at 6847d257) on a NixOS dev host.
2. go test ./internal/app/ -count=1            -> FAIL, 5 failures
3. go test ./internal/shellintegration/... -count=1 -> FAIL, 18 failures
4. Compare those names against the list quoted above: none of them appear.

The failures are the shell-integration suite - bash 3.2 parsing, dash, a live sshd, PS1 marker emission, MOTD and hushlogin fidelity - which need a shell environment this machine does not have. internal/git/local was not observed failing in this run.

## Why it matters

A developer following AGENTS.md compares their red against a list containing none of the tests they see, and has no way to separate an environmental failure from one they caused. The safe-looking reading - assume it is environmental - is the habit that lets a real regression through. This session watched four workers make the same mistake in the other direction, reporting their own failures as pre-existing; the only thing that caught it each time was measuring the baseline.

This is not a request to fix the tests. It is a request to make the document match the machine, or the machine match the document.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The known-local-failure list in AGENTS.md matches what a clean checkout actually produces on a supported dev machine, and names packages rather than a count.
- The list is generated or checked rather than remembered - a hand-maintained list of environmental failures rots exactly as this one did.
- Where a package cannot run on this host at all, the target says so when invoked rather than failing as though the code were wrong.
- If NixOS is not a supported dev host for the shell-integration suite, AGENTS.md says so plainly.

title: golangci-lint cannot load a wails internal package, so the host-side gate never reaches the other three jobs
description:
golangci-lint cannot complete on this machine, on ANY commit including an untouched main.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. cd to a clean checkout of main (verified at 6847d257).
2. Run: golangci-lint run ./...

Observed, identically on main and on feat/ai-assistant:

  level=error msg="Running error: cant run linter goanalysis_metalinter
  buildir: failed to load package webview: could not load export data:
  no export data for github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/internal/assetserver/webview"

Consequence: make ci-full stops at lint-ci (Makefile:422) with Error 3 and the other three jobs never run, so the host-side gate cannot be used at all here. The containerised jobs are unaffected and remain the real signal.

Baseline was measured before filing: the same command on main produces the same error, so this is the environment or the wails toolchain, not any branch.

AGENTS.md already records that backend is the one job where local and CI disagree, and lists nocx-58gq and nocx-65v6 as known local-only failures. This belongs beside them - a developer running the documented gate gets a red that means nothing about their work, which is how a gate stops being read.

## Acceptance Criteria

- golangci-lint run ./... completes on a clean checkout on this machine, or the Makefile target states plainly which environments it cannot run in and why.
- Whatever the fix, a developer following AGENTS.md gets either a working gate or an honest refusal naming the cause - never an error about a wails internal package they did not touch.
- If the cause is the wails dependency needing a build before lint, the target does that build itself rather than relying on the developer having done it.
close_reason: merged; lint-ci now passes the host-derived WAILS_PLATFORM_TAGS to golangci-lint, so it analyses the GTK3 package the product builds instead of wails' GTK4 default. Nothing excluded. It immediately found a shadowed err in a test merged earlier today, fixed in 35b03460.

title: vision.md never mentions API testing, though a pane of it ships in this branch
description:
## Context

`docs/vision.md` is one of the two sources of truth (AGENTS.md: "what & why").
Epic `nocx-h8jzd` is labelled `phase-2` and ships an entire new product surface
— a collection tree, a request workbench, import from Postman/curl/URL, send
through an SSH connection, and secret binding. `grep -iE 'api testing|postman|
collection|http request' docs/vision.md` returns nothing.

So §5 PHASE 2 and §6 Strategic roadmap both describe a Phase 2 that is
"Splits/panes + scrollback search + the semantic command line" and omit the
largest thing Phase 2 actually grew.

## Acceptance Criteria

- §5 PHASE 2 carries a line for API testing naming the epic.
- §6's Phase 2 one-liner mentions it.
- No claim there that is not already true of shipped code.
close_reason: vision.md §5 PHASE 2 now carries an API testing line naming nocx-h8jzd, and §6's Phase 2 one-liner mentions it. Both describe only shipped behaviour.

title: Folder variables save themselves
description:
Owner's call, 2026-08-25: the folder page's Save button goes and the rows persist on
their own.

The button was there because the environments page has one and the request has one, so
it was the shape at hand. It is the wrong one here: a folder's variables are three
fields in a table, there is nothing to compose and nothing to review before committing,
and a person who types a value and walks away has said everything they mean to say.

## What to build

- The Save button is removed from the folder page.
- An edit is written after a short pause once typing stops, coalesced so a row typed
  character by character costs one write.
- Leaving the folder page, or opening another folder, FLUSHES a pending write. A debounce
  that loses the last edit because somebody clicked away is worse than the button.
- The page says which state it is in — writing, or written — because a save nobody asked
  for and nobody is told about is a save a person cannot trust. The refusal stays a
  danger toast, which is the surface that is still there when the table is not.
- The success toast goes: one per keystroke-batch is noise, and the status line says it
  more quietly.

## Deliberately out

- The environments page and the request keep their explicit Save. They compose something
  a person reviews before committing; this does not. If that should change it is its own
  decision, taken deliberately rather than by drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Typing a name and a value writes them without any button being pressed, and the write
  carries exactly the rows the table holds.
- Two edits in quick succession cost one write, not two.
- Navigating away with an unsaved edit still writes it.
- No control named Save exists on the folder page. A test asserts that, because the
  button's absence is the feature.
close_reason: Committed as ff2c2a1d. No Save on the folder page: edits are written 400ms after typing stops, coalesced to one write, and flushed when the folder or the page changes. The pending write carries the path and rows it was scheduled for, and its answer is discarded if the page moved on. Feedback is a quiet Saving…/Saved line rather than a toast per keystroke-batch; 'written' is deliberately not 'nothing left to write'. Three tests: it writes with nothing pressed and offers no Save to press, two edits cost one write, and typing then clicking away still writes. The environments page and the request keep explicit Save deliberately.

title: The folder page puts its editor above what the page is about
description:
The folder page opens with FOLDER VARIABLES — a caption, two lines of prose, an empty
state, Add variable and Save — and only under all of that comes the list of what is
actually in the folder. So the page a person opens to see a folder's contents shows them
an editor for a thing most folders do not have, and pushes the contents down the screen.

The variables section was appended to the page because that was the smallest change that
made nocx-x3cax.2 reachable. It was the wrong shape and the owner said so on sight.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a collection and click a folder that holds several requests.
2. The first screen is the variables editor. The requests start below it, and in a folder
   with five of them the last is off the fold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The page uses the kit's Tabs — the same component and the same horizontal orientation
  the request surface already uses for Params/Variables/Body/Headers/Auth, so the panel
  has one vocabulary for "views of one thing".
- Contents is the first section and the one a folder opens on.
- Variables is the second section and carries its own Save, its loading state and its
  refusal card.
- The Variables tab says whether the folder declares any without being opened, in the
  same words the request's own tabs use for the same fact.
- No new CSS vocabulary: the page places kit components and repaints none.
close_reason: Committed as 39ceab54. The folder page uses the kit's horizontal Tabs — the same component the request surface uses for Params/Variables/Body/Headers/Auth — with Contents first and Variables second. The tab carries its count through 'counted', now exported from request-form rather than restated. The suite's folderTab helper is scoped to .api-folder because the request form has a Variables tab too and an unscoped query would have driven the wrong surface while staying green.

title: A pin whose environment is gone says so rather than sending somewhere else
description:
The failure path of the pin chain, and it has to be answered deliberately because both
silent outcomes are bad. A pin names an environment by relPath. That file can be renamed,
deleted, or never arrive on this machine at all — a colleague's collection pulled from
git carries the environments the repository holds, while the pins are this machine's.

Sending under the next level up SILENTLY is the dangerous one: a request pinned to `dev`
whose dev environment was renamed would fall through to the collection's stand, which may
be production. Refusing the send outright is the other extreme and makes a dangling pin
block work it need not block.

## What to build

The effective environment is still resolved by the chain, so a dangling pin falls through
— but it is VISIBLE: the picker says the pinned environment is missing and names it, and
the run says what it actually went out under. A person can clear the pin or re-pin from
there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pin naming an environment that no longer exists does not send under it and does not
  silently pretend the pin is fine.
- The surface names the missing environment and offers to clear or replace the pin.
- The send still happens, under the level that actually answered, and the run says which.
- A test for each: a dangling request pin, and a dangling folder pin with a request under
  it.

title: A refusal is silent while the environments page is open
description:
The workbench's generic refusal card is suppressed whenever `anyAskOpen()` is true, and
that list includes `envOpen()` — the environments PAGE, not an ask. The reasoning holds
for the modal asks in the list: they take the screen, so the only failure that can arrive
is the ask's own, and the ask shows it under the field.

The environments page does not take the tree. Delete, Rename and Move stay reachable on
every row while it is open, and `void store.deleteRequest(...)` in api-pane.tsx has no
local failure handling at all — `store.error()` and the generic card are the only surface
a refused delete has. So a delete the backend refuses while that page is open fails in
silence, which is the soft degrade AGENTS.md forbids.

Found while reviewing nocx-x3cax.2, where a worker extended the same suppression to the
folder page and introduced the same hole there. That one was fixed by keeping the folder
page's own refusal out of the store's global error channel rather than by suppressing the
card, and there is now a test watching a refused delete with the folder page open. The
same shape is the fix here.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a collection and open the Environments page from the sidebar.
2. From the tree, delete a request in a way the backend refuses (remove write permission
   on the collection directory, or delete the file underneath the app first).
3. Nothing is shown. The refusal is in `store.error()` and no surface renders it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A refused row action is visible to the person whatever the right half is showing.
- `store.error()` keeps one meaning — the last failure nobody else is showing — so a
  surface that displays its own refusal does not publish into it.
- A test drives it through the seam a person reaches: with the environments page open, a
  refused delete is on screen. It is the sibling of the folder-page test added in
  nocx-x3cax.2 and belongs beside it.

title: A request reaches a service that has no network path except its cluster
description:
ADR-0038 (docs/decisions/0038-a-forward-is-a-route-blind-to-the-name.md) is this
epic's design and was written before it. Read it first; the summary below is a
pointer, never the decision.

WHAT A USER CAN DO THAT THEY CANNOT NOW: send a request to a ClusterIP service
that is reachable only through its cluster's API server -- no ingress, no route
from the bastion -- without ever typing a port number, and afterwards read from
the saved run WHICH CLUSTER answered.

Today the only way is to run `kubectl port-forward` by hand and write
http://127.0.0.1:8080 over the `direct` route. That works and is exactly the
accident the route-on-environment design exists to prevent: the URL identifies
no destination, so one collection hits staging or production depending on which
forward happens to be running; the ephemeral port leaks into a file meant to
travel to a colleague; and APIRunRoute cannot say afterwards which cluster
answered.

THE THREE DECISIONS (ADR-0038):

1. A third route kind, `forward`, BLIND TO THE NAME. The environment names a
   machine-local forward by opaque id and carries nothing else. The forward's
   own definition fixes the destination; the hostname in the URL contributes
   exactly `Host` and TLS SNI, and the URL is never rewritten to loopback.
2. A CLUSTER is a machine-local entity BESIDE a connection profile, not a kind
   of one, and may reach its API server THROUGH a connection (SOCKS via
   internal/tunnel/dynamic.go, handed to kubectl as HTTPS_PROXY). The pool
   already keeps `jumpRoute` inside its key for exactly this figure (ADR-0023).
3. kubectl is BOTH THE ORACLE AND THE CARRIER -- ADR-0015's decision arriving a
   second time. Exec credential plugins (EKS/GKE/AKS/OIDC) are why a library
   does not remove the subprocess, only our worse copy of it.

FIRST MEASUREMENT, BEFORE ANY CODE: are the target services reachable from the
bastion's own network? Where they are -- the common arrangement -- https by name
already works today on the `connection` route with nothing built, and the only
real gap is plaintext http by name, which ADR-0038 deliberately does not open.
This measurement can cut the epic substantially and belongs in its first child.

DELIBERATELY OUT: pod-versus-service identity strictness; named service ports;
IPv6; adopting a forward the user started by hand (identity scraped from a
command line cannot be trusted -- though nativeports+procwatch make a fine
on-ramp for OFFERING to define one); any reconnect policy richer than "fail
closed, the next send re-establishes".
acceptance_criteria:
Written as assertions rather than prose (AGENTS.md testing rule 4).

END-TO-END, the one check that watches a user do it (rule 2). A fake `kubectl`
on PATH prints the readiness line and proxies to a local test server, so the
whole path runs with no cluster:

1. An environment routed at a named forward sends and reads a 200, and the
   request URL in the collection contains NO port number and NO localhost.
2. The `Host` header and TLS SNI the test server observes are the URL's logical
   authority, not 127.0.0.1.
3. The persisted run names the forward id, provider, context, the cluster's
   server identity, namespace, resource and remote port. Two runs against two
   clusters are distinguishable from the record alone.

FAIL-CLOSED, each its own assertion and none of them a direct dial:

4. With `kubectl` absent from PATH the provider reports unavailable IN THE
   PRODUCT, and a send through that route returns a refusal naming the forward.
5. With the forward's process killed after readiness, the next send either
   re-establishes or refuses; no request is silently replayed.
6. A redirect that changes authority on a forward route is REFUSED, and the
   test asserts the new Host never reached the old resource.
7. A cluster declaring `via` a connection whose SSH connection is then dropped
   reports THE CONNECTION as the thing that broke, not the forward.

BOUNDARIES:

8. Two environments naming one forward share one route and one forward; a
   cancelled run tears down nothing (AD-7 -- reference, never ownership).
9. Two forwards on two clusters never share a cookie jar or a pooled
   connection, asserted by a cookie set through one being absent on the other.
10. `deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive` on the forward provider's Dial prints a path
    from main, and the same run on a knowingly-unwired symbol prints the
    reflection-only answer. The contrast is the evidence, not the empty output.

title: A refusal is silent while the environments page is open
description:
The workbench's generic refusal card is suppressed whenever `anyAskOpen()` is true, and
that list includes `envOpen()` — the environments PAGE, not an ask. The reasoning holds
for the modal asks in the list: they take the screen, so the only failure that can arrive
is the ask's own and the ask shows it under the field.

The environments page does not take the tree. Delete, Rename and Move stay reachable on
every row while it is open, and `void store.deleteRequest(...)` in api-pane.tsx has no
local failure handling at all — `store.error()` and the generic card are the only surface
a refused delete has. So a delete the backend refuses while that page is open fails in
silence.

Found while reviewing nocx-x3cax.2, where a worker extended the same suppression to the
folder page and introduced the same hole there. That one was fixed by keeping the folder
page's own refusal out of the store's global error channel instead of suppressing the
card; the same shape is the fix here.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a collection and open the Environments page from the sidebar.
2. From the tree, delete a request in a way the backend refuses (make the file read-only,
   or delete it underneath the app first).
3. Nothing is shown. The refusal is in `store.error()` and no surface renders it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A refused row action is visible to the person whatever the right half is showing.
- `store.error()` keeps one meaning — the last failure nobody else is showing — so a
  surface that displays its own refusal does not publish into it.
- A test drives it through the seam a person reaches: with the environments page open, a
  refused delete is on screen.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-nxokg, same day and same title, both parentless, both P2 bugs, same defect (api-pane.tsx firing void store.deleteRequest and the refusal being suppressed by anyAskOpen() including envOpen()), same fix shape and same acceptance. nocx-nxokg survives because its text is a strict superset: it adds the note that this is the soft degrade AGENTS.md forbids, records that a test already watches a refused delete with the folder page open, and adds the acceptance clause placing it beside the folder-page test from nocx-x3cax.2. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: The import's report is a toast, not a panel under the tree

The property that must survive is AGENTS.md's: a soft degrade is visible in the
PRODUCT, not only in a log. A toast keeps that — it is raised where the person's
attention already is, at the moment they pressed Import — provided it is STICKY.
The per-level default for a warning is eight seconds, which for a degrade is a
slower way of being invisible. duration: 0 keeps it until the person ends it,
which is what the panel's dismiss control did.

One report at a time, as before: a new import dismisses the standing toast
rather than stacking a second under it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The "Not imported" Section, its report record and .api-workbench__foot are
  gone from the workbench.
- An import that dropped something raises ONE sticky warning toast naming the
  import — the request a curl line became, or the folder an export went into —

title: session.read is session-scoped, so marking a block narrows nothing
description:
The chip will say "отмечено для вопроса" rather than "модель может прочитать", because today the grant does not narrow: narrowSession (agenttools/narrow.go:34) builds a SessionReader from ResourceSession scopes only, so session.read reaches every item in the session regardless of what the person marked.

That is honest but weaker than the epic promises. Narrowing means a per-block scope kind, or a per-run allowlist of item ids carried alongside the session scope, so a session.read naming an unmarked item is refused the way an out-of-scope sessionId already is.

Until then the marks are ADVISORY: they tell the model where to look, they do not stop it looking elsewhere in the same session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A run whose person marked items A and B is refused a session.read of item C in the same session.
- The refusal is the same shape as the existing out-of-scope sessionId refusal.
- With nothing marked, the default grant is explicit and the chip states it.
- The chip wording moves back to naming the read scope once this is true.
notes:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-25, and it corrects this bead's premise.

Asked whether to implement the narrowing so the chip could name a read scope,
the owner answered: «Выделение нужно не для того, чтобы ограничить скоуп, а
сказать модели что именно интересует пользователя.»

So marking a block is ATTENTION, not permission. The concept this bead was
built on — that the chip understates a restriction which will become true once
narrowSession honours per-item scopes — is the wrong frame. The mark's job is
to tell the model what the person is asking ABOUT; it was never meant to be
the fence around what the model may read.

Two consequences.

1. The acceptance criterion 'the chip wording moves back to naming the read
   scope once this is true' is withdrawn. Whatever the wording becomes, it
   names interest, not scope, and it does so NOW rather than after the
   narrowing lands. That is a separate bead.

2. The narrowing itself is no longer justified by the chip's honesty, because
   the chip stops claiming to narrow. If per-item scoping is still wanted it
   is wanted as a security bound in its own right, on its own argument. This
   bead needs re-deciding on that basis before anyone takes it.

title: The TLS switch is named for one refusal and covers them all
description:
The environment control reads "Accept self-signed certificates". What it sets is
route.insecureTls, which is InsecureSkipVerify: it accepts EVERY refusal a
certificate can draw — self-signed, an authority this machine does not know, an
expired one, a name it was not issued for.

The owner met the gap from the other end: a run refused with "x509: certificate
signed by unknown authority" (a corporate MITM chain), read the only switch on
offer as being about self-signed hosts, and asked for a second option for an
untrusted authority. There is nothing to add — the switch already does it,
proved end to end in internal/apisend/trust_test.go and
internal/transport/ws_api_trust_test.go — so the defect is the words, and a
second switch would have been a second owner of one input.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a request to a host whose chain this machine does not trust for a
   reason other than self-signing (a corporate proxy's own CA).
2. Read the failure: "tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate
   signed by unknown authority".
3. Open the environment. The only control on offer says "Accept self-signed
   certificates", which names a case this is not, so the person concludes the
   product has no switch for what happened to them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The control names what it turns off — the verification — rather than one
  refusal it forgives.
- The refusals it covers are readable BEFORE it is on, not only in the warning
  that appears once it is.
- A test mounts the environment editor, finds that control by its label, turns
  it on, and asserts onRoute carried insecureTls: true — the control had no
  test at all.
notes:
Fix is written and green (frontend/src/api/environment-view.tsx + its test, 12 passed). NOT committed: the pre-commit hook fails on gofumpt for four files belonging to other in-flight work in this worktree — internal/apicoll/folder_variables_test.go, internal/content/api_run.go, internal/content/api_run_sqlite.go, internal/content/api_run_test.go. Committing needs those formatted by whoever owns them, or the two files taken across to a clean tree.

Also established while diagnosing: the switch itself is not broken. Probed against the reporting host through apisend.Client — Key{InsecureTLS:false} fails at the handshake, Key{InsecureTLS:true} answers 404 with trust unchecked-untrusted — and the saved environment file already carries insecureTls: true. The failing run in the report is a STORED run from before that save (runs now survive a restart, nocx-kpl58), not a fresh refusal.
close_reason: Shipped. frontend/src/api/environment-view.tsx:274 renames the control to name the check it turns off, and lists the refusals it covers under the control rather than only in the on-state warning. Tests in environment-view.test.tsx assert both the rename and the route call. Commit 38d8f6de, on origin/main. The bead NOTES claiming it was not committed are stale. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

description:

title: The block shows what was taken, and the input line says how much
description: Design §'What is shown'. Today referenceChipLabel (terminal-content.ts:4149-4161) builds '<command> · row N' from the term-line index — the person selected a word and the chip talks about a row they never counted. The mark is the half the chip cannot do: the chip says how much, the mark says which.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every term-line a live attachment covers is highlighted in its block: a left rail plus a faint tint from existing tokens. It must not look like a selection, and it must survive a block re-render for another reason (a wrap toggle).
- The input line carries ONE small counter, however many attachments there are — no per-attachment badge, no preview text, no row numbers. It sits in the SAME row as the cwd chip (owner, 2026-08-24), never in a row of its own.
- Clicking the counter scrolls to the first attachment and flashes its mark, so 'what will be sent' is always one click from being seen.
- Dismissing one attachment is done on its mark, in the block, where the person can see what they are removing. The counter dismisses ALL.
- The marks are repainted from the chip list by ONE owner on every change to it.
- Marks and counter follow their attachments: a question consumes them, clear takes their blocks.
- Attaching still does not move the input target, with the counter on screen.
notes:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-24, replacing the label design in the approved spec.

The owner's complaint was that the per-attachment chips look wrong. They do, and the cause is that the chip is built from .nocx-chip (frontend/src/editor.ts:1161) — the SAME component that draws the cwd chip, the model name and the status badges. That vocabulary means 'a small fact about this thing'. An attachment is not a fact about the prompt; it is CONTENT that will be sent with it. So it reads as one more label in a row of labels, while being the only thing there that carries text. The spec's planned change — the label becomes the region's text — would have made it worse: a preview does not fit in a badge.

The owner proposed highlighting the rows themselves. Right instinct, one objection: the assistant design §2.4 says context is never invisible — everything that will be sent is on screen before it is sent. With only a mark in the block, a person can attach, scroll away, type and send content that is nowhere in their field of view; with two sources they have no single place that says how much is going.

So the two halves split the job: the MARK says which rows, the COUNTER says how much. One element regardless of count, in the cwd chip's row (owner: no separate row). Coordinates disappear entirely — with no label to put them in, the question of row numbers does not arise, and the mark shows what a number was standing in for.

Known cost, accepted: without hovering, the person cannot tell WHICH block an attachment came from when that block is off screen. The click-to-reveal is what pays for it.

SUPERSEDED IN PART, 2026-08-25. The counter this bead designed is being replaced:
under the grant reframe an attachment is a FACT about the question, not content
going out, so the chip vocabulary this note argued against is correct after all.
The block mark survives; the bare-text counter and its bare x do not. The
replacement design, owner-approved section by section, is in the notes of
nocx-5u3oz.9. Nothing here was wrong about the copy frame — the frame changed.
close_reason: merged into feat/ai-assistant; gate green

title: Two more doors to the same function: Attach output in the ⋮, and the chord

title: A fenced code block is one formatted unit, and it can be copied
description:
Fenced code is on answer-markdown.ts's deliberately-unrendered list (:19-26) because markdown expresses it ACROSS lines and the renderer paints one completed line at a time — the contract that keeps selection, copy and chips working. This task adds the minimum multi-line accumulator for fences alone and does not reopen tables, setext headings, rules or images.

The kit's CodeBlock (frontend/src/ui/code-block.tsx) has no copy button today; add it there, not in the scrollback — the export page shows payloads through the same component. Read frontend/src/ui/README.md before touching the kit.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fenced block reads as ONE code unit: the ``` delimiter lines are not visible as content. The container, the unwrapped body and the shell highlighting already exist (scrollback/answer-body.ts) and must keep working.
- `Copy output` on the block still returns the answer with its fence markers INTACT — that is the contract answer-body.ts:160-167 states and nocx-juau bought. Whatever hides the delimiters must not take them off the copy path. A test holds both halves at once.
- A copy button on the code unit puts exactly the block's code on the clipboard: no fences, no info string, no surrounding prose. It is the KIT's button on ui/CodeBlock so every surface using CodeBlock gets it.
- An unclosed fence at the end of a streaming answer does not eat the rest of the answer, and does not flicker while the fence is legitimately still open mid-stream. Say what it does and test it.
- Selection and the reference chips still work over an answer containing a fence — the row model is what they stand on.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-08-24 by the coordinator. The original bead said fenced code is unrendered, citing ui/answer-markdown.ts's header, which lists fences among the things it deliberately does not paint. That is true OF THAT MODULE and false of the product: scrollback/answer-body.ts owns fence regions above it (fenceLanguage, FENCE_MARKER, a fresh code container per fence, paintShellInto for shell fences, a second fence after prose getting its own container). The visible delimiters are deliberate, not missing: answer-body.ts:160-167 says neither delimiter is painted because leaving them as plain text is what keeps Copy output returning the answer with its markers intact.

So the work is narrower and better defined than first written: hide the delimiters without taking them off the copy path, and add the kit's copy button. The first worker (wfence) escalated rather than guessing, which was correct — the brief had not given it answer-body.ts and the task as written could not be done without either editing it or building a forbidden control inside the scrollback.

title: A client that is not the active one renders at the session size, not at its window
description:
Two clients see the same screen only if they render the same bytes at the same size. The active client gets that for free — its window IS the size. The other sets its terminal to the session's size and pads or scrolls within its own window.

This is the one place the user sees a cost, and it is the same cost herdr has: a smaller window crops or scrolls, a larger one shows margins. It applies only to the client you are not currently using.

Layout around the terminal — tabs, sidebar, splits — stays each client's own and needs nothing: our UI is DOM, and every window already lays itself out. herdr has to do this explicitly because its clients re-emit into a host terminal (src/server/clients.rs:288 carries each client's own terminal_size); we do not.
acceptance_criteria:
With two clients attached at different window sizes, both show identical terminal content.
The inactive client pads or scrolls rather than reflowing to its own width.
Its own tab strip and panels lay out at its own window size, not the session's.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text: Carried from nocx-eidfb.2, so it is not lost: two behaviours there are verified only by reading and have no test naming them — (1) monitorExit removes an exited session from connState and tombstones its lane before any teardown could ask for a resize, which is why a dead session's detach logs a debug line rather than a warning; (2) announceDisplacement removing the session from the loser's connState is what stops a displaced connection's own teardown firing a spurious return-to-default. Both are covered indirectly by the passing suite. If this task touches either path, give each one a test that names it.

title: A session with no shell integration says it has no blocks, in the product
description:
Block boundaries come from the authenticated lifecycle channel, and first-class shell integration exists only for bash and zsh (internal/... launcher_local.go:29, ReasonUnsupportedShell). Everywhere else there are bytes and no attempts — which is true today too, so nothing is lost.

What must not happen is the silent version. AGENTS.md: a soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log — a feature that quietly does not exist is how one survives a release. The user is told the pane is recording output and not producing blocks, and why.
acceptance_criteria:
A session in an unsupported shell records output and produces no blocks, and the pane says so in the product.
The message names the reason, and does not appear for a session that is integrated.
