Merged into feat/nocx-server. A pane in an unsupported shell now says, in the product, that it is recording output and producing no blocks, and names the reason — the silent version is what AGENTS.md forbids, and now that the backend records for every session that silence would have been new.

The assertions I checked hardest are the ones that keep a notice honest: 'draws no card at all for a session that integrated' and TestIntegration_AnIntegratedSessionCarriesNoReasonOverTheWire — without a negative, a message appears everywhere and means nothing. And 'is the kit StatusCard, not a private one', which asserts the component came from frontend/src/ui rather than being hand-rolled; two epics in this repo were spent unwinding exactly that.

Run by the coordinator: the three frontend suites, 102 tests, all pass. Deadcode measured by the worker with the new test file moved aside and back — 85 all baselined, before and after, nothing baselined away.

Stated honestly and worth carrying: the notice depends on internal/app's local factory reporting ReasonUnsupportedShell for a login shell with no tier (app.go:2229-2250). That package was outside this task's ownership and the transport test emulates the factory in-package — so if that reporting call were ever removed, these tests would stay green and the pane would go silent. Recorded on nocx-22k1c so it is not lost. No e2e run, so nothing watched a real fish session end to end, and macOS is unverified.

title: Accelerators: the vendor inbox socket and hooks, measured against the general route
description:
Claude Code binds a per-session inbox socket and exports its path and token to that session's own children, and its documented delivery rule is exactly what this design wants: a message is read between tool calls during an active turn, and when the session is idle Claude Code STARTS A NEW TURN with it. No screen reading, no modal hazard, acknowledged by the vendor.

It cannot carry the invariant, for four reasons that are all in the vendor's own documentation: it exists only for one agent; it is behind a feature flag that several ordinary privacy settings switch off; between machines it travels through the vendor's servers rather than ours; and the receiving session's inbound controls can hold or drop a message, which for a session that bypasses permission prompts is the DEFAULT unless we stage crossSessionInbound: accept ourselves.

Three traps, all documented: identical repeats inside a short window are dropped, so every wake must be distinct and coalesced; a wake counts as usage like a typed prompt; and bare-mode headless sessions bind no socket at all.

A Stop hook is the other accelerator and a much weaker one than it looks — it fires when a turn ENDS, so it can stop a coordinator falling asleep with unread mail, and can never wake one that is already asleep. In a wave the facts almost always arrive after the coordinator has gone idle, so the hook catches a narrow race and not the case.

Value is measured against nocx-dkawo's escalated fraction, not asserted.
acceptance_criteria:
With the socket route enabled, an idle coordinator takes a turn on a fact without any keystroke being sent.
Disabling it falls back to the keystroke route with no loss of correctness, only of latency.
A session whose inbound controls would hold our message is detected at enrolment and reported, not discovered when a wake vanishes.
The escalated fraction with and without accelerators is reported side by side.

title: Drag a request row into a folder: the accelerator on api.request.move
description:
Deferred by nocx-8aczn, which says so in its own description and its acceptance criteria — 'Drag is an ACCELERATOR on the same call and is deliberately out of this epic: a drop grammar is its own design (into a folder versus between rows, the highlight, autoscroll, what a drop on another collection means) and it would need this menu as its keyboard equivalent anyway', and 'Deliberately out: dragging a row (an accelerator on this method, filed separately)'.

It was never filed. Asked by the owner on 2026-08-24 — why is there no drag — and a search of the backlog turns up nothing for an intra-tree drag in the API workbench, open or closed. The only drag/drop beads are about files arriving from the OS into the import ask, which is a different currency entirely.

That is the shape AGENTS.md names: 'A reported blocker becomes a bead with a dependency edge in the same minute, or it evaporates between rounds.' Without this bead nocx-8aczn closes at 5/5 and the deferred work exists nowhere, so the deliberate decision reads as an oversight to whoever looks next.

State of the product, checked at 98d96821: there is no drag handler and no draggable attribute anywhere in frontend/src/api/. The kit's DropZone is not the primitive for this — it accepts files dropped from the OS (the native half hands Go absolute paths; the browser half carries File bytes) and knows nothing about moving a row within a list. So there is no intra-tree drag vocabulary in the kit either, which is what nocx-8aczn meant by the grammar being its own design.

The backend needs nothing: api.request.move already exists, is one rename under apicoll's path rules, and refuses a collision by name (nocx-8aczn.1).
acceptance_criteria:
DONE WHEN a person can drag a request row onto a folder row in the collections tree and find the request inside it — the same api.request.move the menu already calls, the same refusal on a collision, the tree redrawn from the same re-listing.

The drop grammar is the deliverable, and it is decided BEFORE any of it is built:
- onto a folder row versus between two rows (is reordering a thing here at all, given the tree is sorted?)
- what the row under the pointer looks like while a drop is legal there, and while it is not
- a drag near the top or bottom edge of a scrolled tree
- a drop onto another COLLECTION, which nocx-8aczn put explicitly out of scope for the method itself — so the answer here is a refusal, and it has to say so rather than doing nothing
- a drop onto the row it came from, and onto the folder it is already in

The menu stays. It is the keyboard equivalent, and an accelerator that replaced it would take the act away from anyone not using a mouse.

Deliberately out: dragging a FOLDER, and dragging between collections — both are out of the method, not just out of the gesture.
close_reason: Drag a request row onto a folder row moves it through the same api.request.move the menu calls; no backend change. Grammar decided and documented: folder rows only (no reorder call exists), row-level drop feedback, cross-collection refused aloud, same-folder drop is a no-op. Menu untouched, its 11 tests pass unmodified. 12 new tests. b9b64c14.

title: Four SSH-dependent e2e specs fail in the container, and nothing says so
description:
Measured 2026-08-24 on feat/api-testing.

The full containerized suite reports 193 passed / 4 failed / 3 skipped. The same four fail identically at d308aa97, before any of that branch's four commits — baseline taken by detaching to that commit and re-running exactly those specs. They are pre-existing and environmental, not caused by the change under review.

  api-secret-in-path.spec.ts:99
  nocxify-journey.spec.ts:341
  ports-row-width.spec.ts:307
  shell-mode.spec.ts:145

All four depend on an SSH connection coming up. The one inspected in detail fails at its precondition, not its subject:

  ports-row-width.spec.ts:357
  expect(locator('.pane.active .nocx-editor-input')).toBeVisible() — Received: hidden

which the spec's own comment calls the connection being up. It never reaches the row-width assertion its name is about. The spec also notes in a comment that this container has no probe tool, so discovery says unavailable — suggesting the image is missing something these four need rather than the product being wrong.

Why this is worth a bead rather than a shrug: AGENTS.md tells agents to iterate in the container and confirm in CI, and warns its failure set is not CI's — but names LAYOUT-sensitive specs as the difference (scroll ownership, tab-strip roving, label centring). These four are not layout. So the documented exception does not cover them, and a person following the documented workflow meets four reds the documentation does not explain, on every branch, forever. That is a standing tax on every worker who runs the container, and it teaches the habit the repo can least afford: reading a red suite as noise.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From any commit on any branch: PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh
2. Four specs fail, all SSH-dependent.
3. Detach to any older commit and repeat — the same four fail.
acceptance_criteria:
- Either the four specs pass in e2e/run-in-container.sh, or the container path declares them out of its scope the way it is already declared to differ from CI — a skip with a reason, not a silent red.
- Whichever way, the container's own README/script header says which specs it cannot run and why, so the next person reading a red run does not have to bisect to learn it.
- If the cause is a missing tool in the image, the fix is the image, not the specs.

title: isUnknownBinding treats every -32602 as an unknown binding
description:
Found by a worker mapping the git panel's mutation errors to sentences (nocx-8sudy, commit for the tenth site).

frontend/src/git/git-store.ts:264 — isUnknownBinding treats ANY -32602 as an unknown binding, so the store re-resolves through git.open before storing the error. internal/git/errors.go maps several distinct domain refusals onto codes, and the ones that share -32602 are therefore indistinguishable to the renderer.

The observable consequence found while writing the mapper: a conflicted-entry refusal, a 'cannot amend' and a 'nothing is staged' can never reach the panel's error path at all. The worker classified them, then discovered the branches are unreachable and said so rather than leaving them looking live.

Two costs. A refusal a person should read is swallowed and replaced by a silent re-open that cannot fix it — the operation appears to do nothing. And the renderer now carries mapping branches for reasons that cannot arrive, which is dead code that reads as live.

The fix is not to delete the branches: it is to make the predicate ask what it means. Whether that is a distinct code, a sentinel on the wire, or a field in the error payload is the decision this bead is for — internal/git/errors.go and the contract for the git methods are where it gets made.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Put a repository into a state where a mutation is refused for a domain reason carrying -32602 (a conflicted entry).
2. Trigger that mutation from the Git panel.
3. The store re-resolves the binding through git.open instead of surfacing the refusal; nothing tells the person why the change did not happen.
acceptance_criteria:
- A -32602 that is not an unknown-binding refusal is not re-resolved through git.open; it reaches the caller as the refusal it is.
- The predicate distinguishes them by something the backend actually says, not by the code alone.
- A test per refusal shape that shares the code: unknown binding re-resolves; a conflicted-entry refusal does not.
close_reason: The wire carries a fixed reason vocabulary (contracts/git.error.schema.json, six values, additionalProperties false) so the renderer can tell six refusals apart that share -32602. isUnknownBinding now asks the declared reason, mirroring the dispatcher's isSaturationData. Three over-the-wire tests. Mapping lives at the transport boundary like the vault's reasonForError. b9b64c14.

title: The e2e container run leaves root-owned files in the worktree it ran from
description:
Observed 2026-08-24 while running the wave for nocx-stf7j.

Two directories were left behind in /home/dev/.herdr/worktrees/nocx/w-tree-e2e after 'PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh':

  <root>/node_modules            empty, owned by root — a bare mount point
  <root>/frontend/node_modules   REAL packages, owned by root

The consequence is that the worktree cannot be disposed of. 'herdr worktree remove --workspace w8Q --force' failed with worktree_remove_failed after having already dropped the workspace, so the workspace record went and the directory stayed — an orphan git no longer tracks. 'rm -rf' then failed per file: 'cannot remove .../node_modules/yallist/package.json: Permission denied'. Cleaning it needs sudo, which an agent should not reach for on its own.

This bites exactly the workflow AGENTS.md and the worker-wave practice encourage — a worktree per worker, removed when the worker is done. Every worktree the e2e suite has ever run in is undeletable by the user who created it.

One caveat on reproducing it: in this case frontend/node_modules was a SYMLINK into another worktree (the coordinator's, to avoid three 219 MB installs), and the container replaced it with a real root-owned directory rather than following it. So the exact shape may be specific to that setup. The bare root-level <root>/node_modules mount point was NOT a symlink and was still left root-owned, which suggests the general case holds. Confirm both before fixing.

Not a data-loss risk: the coordinator's own frontend/node_modules was checked afterwards and is intact, dev-owned, with zero root-owned entries at its top level — the container's named volumes did not write through into it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. git worktree add a fresh worktree.
2. Run 'PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/<any>.spec.ts' from it.
3. ls -ld node_modules frontend/node_modules — owned by root.
4. rm -rf the worktree — Permission denied.
acceptance_criteria:
- After e2e/run-in-container.sh, every file it created in the checkout is owned by the invoking user, or it creates none there at all.
- A worktree the suite has run in can be removed with 'herdr worktree remove' / 'rm -rf' without sudo.
- Whichever way it is fixed, e2e/README or the script's own header says what the run writes into the checkout and what it does not.

title: No surface prints an error into the document flow, and a gate keeps it that way
description:
The rule is already written and is already being broken. frontend/src/ui/README.md, 'Telling the user something happened: Toast':

  Toast is the only notification affordance. An operation's outcome is raised
  with showToast(...) and rendered by the single ToastHost in App.tsx —
  surfaces do not render a status line of their own. [...] What belongs on the
  field instead is field validation [...] The rule this replaces a pattern for:
  a message about an action does not live in the document flow.

Nine surfaces grew a private one anyway, each with its own class name and its own colour. That is the shape AGENTS.md names in 'Look for the existing answer before you write a second one' — two vocabularies for one concept, agreeing everywhere anyone looks.

Raised by the owner, 2026-08-24, from the API tree's red paragraph: 'нужно запретить отображение ошибок инлайн во всем проекте, за исключением валидации и некоторых редких случаев'. The exceptions are the two the kit already names.

Sequence: nocx-stf7j does the API tree first because a screenshot is already open on it; this epic sweeps the rest and installs the gate. Without the gate it is a cleanup that grows back.
acceptance_criteria:
A person doing something that fails is told by a Toast, wherever they are in the product. What stays in the flow is only: field validation (the kit Field's own error), and a StatusCard standing in for a surface that has nothing else to show.

Every private error element below is gone or converted, and a gate makes a new one fail:

  api/api-pane.tsx:2214,2220   .api-tree__reason      (owned by nocx-stf7j)
  api/environment-view.tsx:410 .api-environments__refusal
  api/move-dialog.tsx:157      .api-move__refused
  settings.tsx:1088            .ui-settings-error
  backup-restore-section.tsx:284 .backup-restore__error
  ports.tsx:624                Badge tone=danger for a failed listing
  about-section.tsx:93         .ab-failed
  key-material-input.tsx:190,220 .cm-key-file-error   (split it: the local check is validation and belongs on the Field; the read failure is an outcome and belongs in a Toast)
  connections.tsx:2499         .cm-forwards-error     (validation, but hand-rolled — move it onto the kit's RowList/Field error)

The gate: the kit already has an eslint fixture gate (frontend/src/eslint-fixture-gate.test.ts) and nocx-pp3y owns 'the kit owns how controls look'. Add the rule there, not a new mechanism.

Deliberately out: run-list.tsx:315 — a run's outcome is the RECORD, and the run list exists to hold records; StatusCard is right there. git-panel.tsx, folder-picker.tsx:241, integration/notice.tsx — StatusCard as a surface's empty/failed state, which is what the component is for.
close_reason: Ten surfaces' private error elements gone; each decided on its own into one of three homes (kit Field for validation, StatusCard for a surface's failed state, showToast for an outcome) plus the row-hover treatment for a persistent per-row defect. No backend string reaches a person unmapped. check-error-vocabulary.mjs is the gate, with a negative fixture gate.sh asserts in both directions and three baselined entries each carrying its reason. 7ce9b934 + 98d96821. Also fixed on the way: four lint-fixture checker tests that had never run (48 tests where 9 ran).

title: Show in Finder is a dead menu item: no revealer is wired
description:
internal/transport/ws.go:993-998 defines WithFilesRevealer. grep across the repo finds exactly two callers, both tests: ws_contract_test.go:2916 and ws_files_test.go:717. Nothing in internal/app or cmd calls it.

So s.revealer is nil in the shipped app, handleReveal (ws_files.go:863) takes the nil branch, and files.reveal answers -32601 'files.reveal not available'. The Files panel offers 'Show in Finder' (files-view.tsx:442) unconditionally for local origins; choosing it raises a danger toast with that message.

The code says this was known — 'the Wails runtime seam is a later wave, and a reveal that did nothing would be a silent lie' (ws_files.go:834). The refusal is honest; the menu item offering it is not. AGENTS.md: 'A soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log' — here the degrade is visible only after the user clicks.

Found while scoping nocx-stf7j, which wanted to reuse reveal for a malformed request file and cannot.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Files panel on a local tab.
2. Right-click any file. 'Show in Finder' is offered.
3. Choose it. A danger toast reads 'files.reveal not available'; nothing opens.
acceptance_criteria:
- WithFilesRevealer is called from the composition root, with a real implementation, or 'Show in Finder' does not render.
- A test proves the seam is reached on a normal machine, not only that it errors when absent (AGENTS.md: 'For every returns-an-error-when there is a paired and-on-a-normal-machine-it-succeeds').
- deadcode -whylive on the Reveal implementation shows a path from main, not 'reachable only through reflection'.

title: e2e/api-secret-in-path asserts a compact body the response pane no longer renders
description:
The spec's last assertion reads the response body as text and expects the server's exact JSON, `{"ok":true,"result":{"message_id":42}}`. The pane now lays the body out for reading and puts line numbers beside it (nocx-6hg2w.17/.18 era), so `textContent` comes back as `9123456{  "ok": true,  "result": {    "message_id": 42  }}` — the gutter's digits, then the indented JSON. The substring can never match again.

Same class as nocx-6u2gz: a spec asserting the shape of a surface that has since been redesigned, and it fails in BOTH browsers, deterministically, so it is not the container's layout.

WHAT IT COSTS, which is the reason it is P2 and not P4: this is the spec that proves a secret in the URL path crosses to the server and NEVER to the screen. It dies before its final assertions, so the thing it exists to guard is currently unguarded — the same way nocx-6u2gz hid the literal-is-sent pair.

Measured on d308aa97, the merged tree, in ./e2e/run-in-container.sh: 8 failed / 381 passed, and this is 2 of the 8. It also failed identically on 7f981475 the night before, so it predates today's work.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. PW_PROJECTS=chromium ./e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/api-secret-in-path.spec.ts
2. It fails at line 221 on toContainText.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The spec reads the body the way the pane presents it, and still proves the same thing about the bytes.
- Its final assertions — the ones about the token being on the wire and nowhere on the screen — actually run, and the report says so.
- The line-number gutter is not asserted as content: a test that pins the gutter would break on the next body that is one line longer.

title: The pane says what it is doing, and three workers stop collapsing into one dot
description:
Three workers — one finished, one asking you a question, one dead — collapse into a single
dot that activating the tab erases. frontend/src/panes.ts holds ONE boolean per pane — Pane._hasActivity, whose markActivity()
returns early while the pane is active, because setActive() clears on activation and not on
deactivation (this cited tabs.ts:52 until 2026-08-25; nocx-ehkvy renamed that file on
2026-08-17) — and agent-status.ts derives
working|idle from OSC 0/2 with no provenance and no history. That is the whole of what nocx
knows about what a pane is doing.

## What this crosses, and what those documents already decided

docs/vision.md §11 founds orchestration on OSC 133 answering "did this command finish?",
"which is the same question as 'is this agent done?'". THAT IS FALSE FOR AGENT TUIs, and
this repository already knows it twice: the git-manager design's D13 rejected OSC 133
command-end because "an agent is one long command", and agent-status.ts says the same in
its header and reads the title instead. §9.1 of the orchestration design owes vision.md
that correction, and this epic is where it gets paid.

D11 of that design decides the model: state is EVIDENCE, not a value. Observations are
appended with their provenance and REDUCED; a single `status` field with source priority
produces a stuck `done`, because the hook fires at end of turn, the agent resumes without
firing, and a stale high-ranked value outranks a fresh low-ranked one forever. Ordering is
not solved by a clock — there is none shared — but by binding every observation to
`session epoch + lifecycle domain (ADR-0024) + attempt (ADR-0020 §4) + output offset
(AD-9)`, which is the thing nocx knows that no orchestrator does. §5.2 fixes the
provenance table and which classes may wake a phone: `known` and `declared` yes,
`declared-anonymous` (the terminal title) no by default, because a file containing
`ESC]0;Action Required BEL` would otherwise push a notification from a `cat`.

D12 decides that detection rules are LOCAL, user-editable settings with shipped defaults,
switchable off per agent, and accompanied by a live "what is this agent emitting" view —
against herdr's network manifest catalogue, which is right for a public product and is a
network dependency for correct behaviour here (vision.md: no cloud, ever). The emitting
view is not optional: a rule the user must write blind is a dead rule.

AD-6 governs the hard boundary: the renderer owns VT state and the backend never sniffs
the byte stream, so every `inferred` observation is derived where the grid already lives
and crosses as a typed fact under AD-1's ledger-facts amendment, never as bytes.

## Why it is not first, and why it was refused twice before

nocx-taehg records the refusal in its own words: attention counts need the liveness rule,
and a second spelling of live-work.ts for the sake of a decoration is "the AD-8 defect
bought for a badge". nocx-edhcu.2 shipped the overview's cards and left the same hole.
Both were right to stop. What was missing is an owner for "what is this pane doing".

ORDER CORRECTED 2026-08-25. This paragraph used to end "what makes the owner testable is a
wave to point it at — which is why this epic follows nocx-dkawo rather than preceding it."
f5ef47e1 reversed that edge: nocx-dkawo now depends on THIS epic, because the wave consumes
the driver and building the wave first would leave it reaching for a driver that does not
exist. The edge moved and this prose did not, so for a day the two said opposite things.
What makes the owner testable is not a wave — it is three panes with agents in them, which a
person produces by hand today. A wave becomes one more producer of such panes, never the
precondition for having any.

## What it unblocks, and does not contain

nocx-edhcu.1 (the overview's cards and the strip's rows), nocx-taehg (attention counts in
the switcher) and nocx-ms7v.4 (the attention queue) each consume this and stay where they
are. nocx-hz94 (a notification catches you on your phone) gains the eligibility rule it
needs from the provenance table.

## Deliberately out

The attention queue itself and any durable retention of attention events (§11 item 10).
A remote manifest catalogue or any network fetch of rules. Delegation and authority.

## Success Criteria

With three AGENT PANES running, one finishing, one blocked on a question and one dead, the
product distinguishes all three at a glance and says of each which source it learned that
from — and a late observation from a previous attempt does not overwrite a current one.
One automated check watches a user with three panes in that state — started by hand, no wave
required — read the correct answer
for each, and watches the stale observation arrive and be refused.

Falsified if any of the three renders the same as another, if activating a pane erases the
fact rather than acknowledging it, or if the terminal title alone can push a phone
notification without the user opting that agent in.
close_reason: 8/8 children closed. DONE WHEN watched by the three-pane check in 74272f8b: PaneManager mounted against the real WSClient over the mock socket, three real session.observationChanged notifications produce three distinct statuses with three distinct sources, activation preserves all three, and a stale observation from another incarnation is refused (assertion ordered, not timed; verified by removing the incarnation guard and watching it fail). Work lands on main with feat/orchestration.

title: A wave of workers runs inside nocx: a coordinator starts them, waits on all of them, and reads what they did
description:
Replace herdr. The owner runs worker waves in herdr every day, from a Mac against a
server on vm-agents, and wants that workday to move to nocx. This epic is the piece with
no manual workaround: every other gap can be covered for a while by opening a tab and
looking at it, but a coordinator agent that cannot address anything does not exist at all.

## What this crosses, and what those documents already decided

AD-1 splits the wire into a binary data plane and a JSON-RPC control plane, and says
nothing may be added to it without its own decision. AD-8 puts every module behind one
interface at one composition root. ADR-0020 records authority per RUN, never per session.
ADR-0028 keeps the agent loop ours and narrows by grant rather than checking after the
fact. .internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-lineage-and-orchestration-design.md decides
the shape in §6 — ONE dispatcher, TWO callers: the built-in agent in-process with a grant
minted per run, an enrolled external CLI over a private local channel, differing only in
how the grant was sourced — and in D13/D14 decides how the external caller is
authenticated: enrolment of a process TREE, pinned by a non-reusable handle, approved once
by a human, with NO bearer material in the environment. D9 makes spawning a child the
`delegate` effect over the resource `environment`.

ADR-0024 decision 2 already built the carrier, and this is the fact that makes the epic
affordable: an authenticated channel that is not the tty, local through a descriptor
handed over at spawn, remote through a reverse tunnel on the pooled SSH connection the
shell reaches with `/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/<port>`. Nothing about that transport confers
authority — the per-epoch capability does, and it never enters the environment.

Two consequences worth stating before anyone designs against them. First, this reaches
FURTHER than herdr can: herdr's socket is local and mode 0600, so its own operating notes
require the coordinator to run on the server, while nocx's carrier rides the session's own
SSH connection and a coordinator may sit on any host nocx has a session to. Second, and in
the other direction, AD-6 forbids the backend to sniff the byte stream, so herdr's
`pane wait-output` — a regex over the pane snapshot — has NO legal translation as a
backend screen match. The renderer owns the VT state. How "wait until this pane prints X"
is answered without a second VT owner, and whether it can be answered at all while no
renderer is attached, is the first thing the spec must settle.

## What exists today

nocx-dw3 is CLOSED: an in-process agent that acts under a grant checked before it touches
anything — the first of §6's two callers, already built. Workspaces, tabs and panes are
backend-owned rows (nocx-isoph, closed) with contracts. Epic A (nocx-ebl4) gives every
session an identity, an immutable parent edge and a liveness projection. internal/helper
carries a framed protocol, a service dispatcher and a deploy path.

What does not exist is any method an external process may call, and any way for one to
prove who it is. D13 designed the authentication and named no call.

## Deliberately out

Agent lifecycle classification and anything that reports what a pane is DOING — the next
epic owns that, and this one is built so a sentinel over output is a sufficient completion
signal without it. Durable sessions and the relay (nocx-1p1h4). Worktree creation as one
call (nocx-kdccc). Delegation as a revocable object beyond what a single wave needs.

nocx-98rn ("the control plane cannot dispatch an unvalidated call") is NOT a blocker and
NOT out: the new surface lands validated from its first method, because a second caller
onto an unvalidated dispatcher is how that epic's defect doubles.

## Success Criteria

A coordinator agent running in a nocx pane creates three workers, gives each a task, waits
on all three with ONE wait that returns when the first settles, reads what each produced,
and closes them — with herdr not installed and not running. One automated check watches
exactly that, end to end, against a real backend.

Falsified if any step needs a herdr command, a screen scrape by the backend, or a bearer
token in a child process's environment.
notes: SCOPE ADDED 2026-08-24, owner's call, when nocx-ebl4.1 was split. THIS EPIC PRODUCES THE LINEAGE EDGE FOR THE PANES IT OPENS. nocx-9hu9d built the record, the full-identity Ref, validateParent and the wire; nothing ever sent one, and that was filed as nocx-ebl4.1 and deferred as a UI decision. The UI half really is undecided — a split, a new tab from the strip, an activation with nothing focused. The dispatcher half is not: a pane opened by a run has exactly one possible parent, the session of the run that asked. So the dispatcher is the first and least ambiguous producer, and nocx-szb40 reads that same edge to group a wave under its coordinator rather than inventing a second grouping. Constraint carried over from nocx-ebl4: the edge is IMMUTABLE, no addressability follows from lineage alone, and a parent's death never closes its children. And there must be ONE producing seam — if this epic writes its own, nocx-ebl4.1 must later write through it, not beside it.

title: One entry's clocks and status describe different attempts
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Run an entry whose intent is attempted twice — the shape ADR-0020 decision 4 makes ordinary,
a tool call refused and then approved — and read the entry row afterwards.

## What happens

`FinishExecution` writes all three facts in ONE statement, with three different rules:

    UPDATE entries SET
      status      = ?,                                   -- unconditional: the last finish wins
      started_at  = COALESCE(started_at, ?),             -- the FIRST attempt's start survives
      duration_ms = COALESCE(?, duration_ms)             -- a non-null new value wins: the LAST

So one row shows the start of attempt 1, the duration of attempt N and the outcome of
attempt N. The three look consistent and describe different intervals: `started_at +
duration_ms` is neither the entry's end nor the last execution's end. Nobody decided this —
it is three operators in one statement.

Second half, and it is worse: "the last finish wins" is only correct while attempts finish in
order. Nothing enforces that. An attempt 1 that finishes late would overwrite the outcome of
an already-finished attempt 2.

Found while reviewing the kind/source split (nocx-dc2fr.8). Pre-existing, not caused by that
epic; surfaced by looking hard at the table.

## What should happen

The entry's times mean one thing each, stated and enforced:

- `started_at` — when the intent was first executed.
- `ended_at` — when it was finally resolved, after which no further attempt is expected.
- `duration_ms` — the wall-clock span between them, and NOT any attempt's own duration; an
  attempt's duration already lives on the execution, and copying one onto the entry is what
  produced the ambiguity.
- `status` — the intent's final aggregated outcome, chosen deterministically from the
  authoritative attempt rather than from whichever UPDATE ran last.
acceptance_criteria:
- An entry attempted twice reports `started_at` from the first attempt, `ended_at` from the
  resolving one, and `duration_ms` equal to their difference — asserted with two attempts of
  genuinely different durations, so a wrong rule cannot coincide with a right one.
- An attempt that finishes OUT OF ORDER does not overwrite a later attempt's outcome:
  driven directly, with the paired case where in-order attempts do settle the entry.
- Summed active time is not stored anywhere: it is derivable from the executions, and a test
  asserts the entry does not claim it.

title: The remote helper reaches the orchestration tree: merge feat/git-manager
description:
feat/git-manager (nocx-457v, 17/17, PR #90) sat 35 ahead and 248 BEHIND main since 2026-08-15, so
the remote helper — cmd/nocx-helper, internal/helper/{proto,host,client,deploy,consent} — was on a
branch and not in the product. The orchestration work needs it in the tree (the session service the
helper reserves is what makes a worker survive the client), so it merges into feat/orchestration,
cut from feat/notifications, rather than into main: PR #106 stays about the notification centre.

Eleven conflicts and THREE silent auto-merge defects — files that merged with no marker and did not
compile. Side chosen deliberately per axis: the desiredMode axis to the branch (auto is a real
addition, nocx-7iisi; relay integrates, nocx-7k8ma), the bootstrap carrier to main (ADR-0035 is
newer and supersedes the branch on that path), noPane from main plus the deletion of the ssh
refusal from the branch. Two second-owner pairs collapsed to one owner each: the e2e sshd fixture
had startSFTP and serveSFTP, and internal/transport had two openSSHSession helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria

go vet -tags gtk3 ./... clean, tsc --noEmit clean, go test and vitest green on the merged tree, and
no conflict marker or duplicated behaviour left behind.
close_reason: Merged as 340126b8 on feat/orchestration. Verified on the merged tree: gofumpt, golangci-lint, prettier, eslint, the fixture gates, contracts:check, tsc on both frontend configs and e2e, containerized go test -race and vitest, scripts/ci-linux.sh green in BOTH keyring variants, and the deadcode ratchet at 87 unreachable functions all baselined with no internal/helper entry — so the helper is reachable from main(), not merely present. Host-side go test shows 23 failures that are the NixOS host's (no /bin/bash, no bash 3.2 fixture): the same 23, name for name, on the base branch, and green in the container. Not covered here and not coverable here: ci-mac and the e2e suite.

title: A typed /sandbox command replaces the active tab
description: Design and implement a shell-owned /sandbox command that applies or removes filesystem sandboxing by replacing the active terminal tab through the same grant-aware conversion path as the activity-bar shield. The slash command must never be written to PTY, must require a local terminal with verified cwd, and must preserve transcript/draft while remaining fail-closed.
design: Exact argument-free /sandbox toggles apply/remove before PTY/history/ledger and delegates to the shared replacement controller. Applying always confirms the effective workspace/standard profile; design §5.
acceptance_criteria: Typing /sandbox in the command editor toggles the active local terminal between ordinary and sandboxed replacement sessions through one backend-owned grant flow; invalid surfaces explain refusal; no PTY bytes or renderer-authored policy cross the control contract; automated tests cover apply, remove, refusal, duplicate submit, and failure preservation.
notes: Implemented exact argument-free /sandbox editor command. It is consumed before secret planning, PTY, history, ledger or block creation; apply confirms profile, second invocation removes via replacement; tests and Chromium e2e green.
close_reason: Closed

title: The tree misleads twice: the open request is invisible and an open empty folder looks like a parent
description:
Two reports from the owner, one surface.

THE SELECTED ROW WAS PAINTED WITH HOVER'S OWN TOKEN. tree-row.css gave data-selected the same --color-surface-hover the row takes under the pointer, so the open request was drawn exactly like whatever the mouse happened to be over. On a collection of fifteen rows nothing said which one was in the form.

AN OPEN FOLDER WITH NOTHING IN IT LOOKED LIKE THE PARENT OF THE ROWS BELOW IT. Those rows are its SIBLINGS, drawn at its depth with their icons in its icon's column, so a folder made a minute earlier appeared to have swallowed every request in the collection. Indentation cannot answer it and neither can an indent guide: there is no deeper level to draw, because there is nothing at it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a collection with a dozen requests at its root and make a folder.
2. The folder is expanded and empty; every request below it reads as being inside it.
3. Open one of the requests: nothing in the tree says which row is the open one unless the pointer is elsewhere.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The selected row carries the register the rest of the product uses for the current choice in a list, and is distinguishable from a hovered row.
- An expanded folder with nothing in it says so, at the depth its contents would have had.
- A collapsed one says nothing; a collection holding only malformed files is not empty.
- Under an active filter nothing claims to be empty — holding nothing that matched is a different sentence.
close_reason: Selected rows take the ghost Button's --color-tab-active (the rail's register), without the 2px accent marker — the owner asked for the colour and a tree row's leading edge already means something. An open folder with nothing in it says so through a new kit component, TreeEmpty; flattenCollections gained an explicit 'narrowed' so a filtered tree claims nothing about emptiness. 4 new kit tests, 14 in api-tree.test.ts.

title: A request's FILE can be renamed, from where the request is named
description:
The second act of the same method. The header renames the NAME inside the file today and says so; what it cannot do is rename the file, and that is the half a person expects when the tree row shows a basename nobody chose.

Where it goes is a decision this task makes and records: beside the name in the header, or in the same row menu as the move. Whichever it is, it is ONE call — the move method with a destination differing only in the leaf — and not a second minter of paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- A person renames the file of a request from the panel, and the file on disk is at the new path.
- The name INSIDE the file is untouched by it: two acts, two controls, and the code says which is which.
- A name that is not usable as a path is refused by the one owner of that question (nocx-9a22b), with the reason on the field.
- A collision refuses and names it.

title: The Files panel has the same open-empty-folder ambiguity the API tree just fixed
description:
Both panels render the same kit component (ui/tree-row.tsx) and neither of them said anything when a folder was expanded and held nothing — so the rows below it, which are its SIBLINGS at its own depth, read as its contents. In the API workbench that misled the owner about a folder made a minute earlier (fixed in api-tree.ts: an expanded folder with nothing in it emits an 'Empty' row at the depth its contents would have had).

The Files panel flattens its own rows (files-store.ts), so the fix did not reach it. One rule, two flatteners: whoever takes this should decide whether the row belongs in the kit rather than in each surface — two implementations of 'an empty folder says so' would agree everywhere anyone looked and disagree on the one case that mattered.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Files panel, expand a directory that is empty.
2. The rows below it are its siblings and read as its contents.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An expanded empty directory in the Files panel says it is empty, at the depth its contents would have had.
- A collapsed one says nothing.
- Under an active filter it does not claim emptiness — holding nothing that matched is a different sentence.
- The rule has ONE owner across the two panels, and the choice of where it lives is stated in the code.

title: The curl import door stands on the URL line instead of with the other two doors
description:
Owner's request of 2026-08-23: put it where Save is, between the plus and the three dots.

The import button sat between the address field and Send — a control about WHERE A REQUEST COMES FROM inside the row a person edits the request in. Making a request, importing one and acting on the open one are the same kind of act on the same subject; they belong in one group at the trailing end of the crumb trail.
acceptance_criteria:
- The button is in the crumb trail's trailing group, between the New request plus and the More menu.
- It keeps its id, title and mark, so tests reaching it by accessible name still find it.
- It is offered with no collection and no request open — a curl line becomes a draft with no file behind it, so that is the state it is most needed in.
- Nothing is left behind on the line: the prop, the wrapper and its CSS selector are gone.
close_reason: The door is in the crumb trail between the plus and the menu, keeps its id/title/mark, and the trailing group now also stands when only it is there — a curl line becomes a draft with no file, so an empty workbench is where it is needed most.

title: A secret can be chosen or made from the body editor, not only from the fields around it
description:
nocx-5dfa5 names the body editor as deliberately out, and says why: CodeMirror owns its
own input, so a picker inside it is its own shape rather than the same control placed
again. It also says the case is real, and it is — a token in a JSON body is what the
owner's own `POST broker-access` holds today, in clear text, because there was nowhere
else to put it from that surface.

This is that follow-on. It is an OFFER, not a rewrite: nothing here refuses, moves or
sanitises a credential somebody typed into a body, per the owner's decision of
2026-08-23 (nocx-tg9l8's closing reason). What it adds is that from inside the body a
person can insert a variable the active environment already holds, or make a secret on
the spot, without leaving the request and without typing a name from memory.

The write goes through `store.bindSecret` — the same call the Auth tab and nocx-5dfa5's
picker use. A second minter would be a second answer to "what does storing a credential
mean here", which is the thing AD-8 and the kit rule both exist to prevent.
acceptance_criteria:
- From inside the body editor a person can insert a variable chosen from what the ACTIVE environment holds, and the inserted text is `{{name}}` — never a value.
- From the same place a person can create a secret: a name and a value, written through `store.bindSecret`, the same call the Auth tab and the field picker use. Not a second minter and not a second scoping rule.
- The list says which entries are secrets and which are plain, in the vocabulary the environments page already uses.
- Absence is the capability: `SecretTarget` already distinguishes no-collection from no-environment and says which; no control is drawn that would fail when pressed.
- Nothing here rewrites, refuses or sanitises a credential typed into the body as text.
- The saved request file contains `{{name}}` and never the value — asserted on the bytes on disk.
- Kit only: the surface inside CodeMirror is a kit component or a new one added to `ui/`, placed and not repainted.

title: Cancelling the curl import's new confirmation throws away the line that was pasted
description:
Reported by nocx-86wvw's worker, which could not reach the file (another
worker held api-pane.tsx that wave) and named it rather than abusing error()
to force the ask to stay open. That restraint is why this is a clean bead.

Since nocx-86wvw, importing a curl line over unsaved work asks first. Cancel
means "let me save that request before I do this". But api-pane.tsx around
1248-1256 closes the curl ask whenever `store.error() === ''`, and a declined
confirmation is not an error — so the ask closes, and opening it again clears
`curlLine`. The person has to go and find the command again.

Nothing is destroyed and no criterion of nocx-86wvw is broken. It is the
difference between "refused" and "declined", which this surface cannot
currently tell apart.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a saved request and change something.
2. Import a curl command; the confirmation appears.
3. Press Cancel. The ask closes and the pasted line is gone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Declining the confirmation leaves the ask open with the pasted line still
  in it, so the person can save and press Convert again.
- A refusal from the backend still closes or reports the way it does today —
  the two are told apart by something that means it, not by the absence of an
  error.
- A test presses Cancel and asserts the line is still in the field.

title: The renderer mints a request name a third time, so a name the backend now refuses is written silently
description:
Found by nocx-9a22b's worker while making internal/pathname the single owner
of "is this name usable as a path component". It reported the gap rather than
growing the duplicate, which is the right call and the reason this exists.

frontend/src/api/api-paths.ts:18 `slugify` is `[a-z0-9]+ → '-'` with no length
bound and no device-name check, and `freePath` (api-store.ts) builds request
paths from it. So the renderer is a THIRD minter of path components, beside
the two that were just merged into one.

Since 55d5e4f4 the backend refuses those names. Naming a request `CON`, `PRN`
or `COM1` now gets a refusal from `api.request.write` where it used to write
`con.json` — which is an improvement, except that the surface does not say so:
the person typed a name and the save fails with whatever the generic error
path shows.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Make a request and name it `CON` (or `nul`, or something ending in a dot).
2. Save it.
3. The backend refuses; the sentence it returns is not shown beside the name.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The refusal's sentence is shown where the name was typed — the header's
  rename field — naming the name and the remedy, not a generic failure.
- The renderer does NOT grow a copy of the device list, the bounds or the
  character rule. A fourth owner in TypeScript is precisely what nocx-9a22b
  removed two of; the backend already returns a sentence naming the name and
  the remedy, and showing it is the whole fix.
- A test types a refused name, saves, and asserts the sentence appears beside
  the field and the request is not left believing it was written.
- Considered and rejected in the code, in one line, so the next person does not
  re-decide it: minting through a TS twin of pathname.Portable.

title: Retention evicts a run's prose as one unit
description:
ADR-0019 §7 evicts bodies and leaves entries. With the answer split across N blocks, a
partial eviction would render as a complete answer missing its middle — worse than an
answer that is plainly gone. ADR-0037 makes the unit the RUN.

AGENTS.md: a soft degrade must be visible in the product, not only in a log.
acceptance_criteria:
- Evicting under the budget takes every `text` body of a run or none — asserted by driving
  retention against a turn whose pieces have different sizes.
- A turn whose prose was evicted says so on screen, once, and still shows every child block
  it had.
- A command's VT body still evicts independently of the prose around it.
close_reason: Landed in 62e5ffbc. The unit is the RUN: a sweep that takes one prose body of a run takes all of them, so a turn never renders a complete-looking answer that is missing its middle. A command's VT body still evicts independently of the prose around it, and every block a turn had survives — only bodies go. The receipt is a flag on the dropped body rather than an overload of truncated/gaps, which describe what the CAPTURE got and not what the store later chose to drop; Entry.ProseEvicted is derived from those receipts, so one stored fact and one reading of it. Tests are mutation-checked by the worker: reverting the run-unit rule fails three, dropping the pin exemption two, hard-coding the flag false two. Verified by the coordinator on the MERGED tree, not the worker's: internal/content, internal/transport and internal/assistant green, lint clean; the one conflict with nocx-dc2fr.2 (both added a field to Entry) was additive and both fields kept. Worker's escalation accepted and rehomed rather than dropped: the sentence stops at the store, and carrying it to the screen needs ledger.get plus the renderer — nocx-dc2fr.4 owns it and its brief now commissions it explicitly. Also reported and left, deliberately: the budget is checked on Submit only, so a command body growing via CaptureOutput is accounted at the next submit rather than as it grows; and EvictionResult.Evicted now counts prose rows, which changes what that number means and is documented on the field.

title: The conversation is assembled from the turn's children
description:
The follow-up question needs the previous turns as messages. The answer is no longer one
string: it is the `text` children of a run, in `pos` order. Related: nocx-0s2gh.2, which is
the same direction at larger scale — do not build a second assembler.
acceptance_criteria:
- A follow-up after a turn that interleaved prose and calls sends the model that turn's
  prose whole, in `pos` order.
- A turn with TWO agent executions (a suspended run that resumed) does not interleave the
  attempts' prose: the assembled message is one attempt's.
- A turn whose prose was evicted sends the turn without inventing text for it, and says so
  rather than sending a hole silently.
close_reason: Landed in 197c5583. The brief's premise was false and the worker said so instead of working around it: there was NO conversation assembler on this tree — nothing ever constructed an assistant-role message, so a follow-up question reached the model knowing nothing of what had just been answered. Built rather than repaired, in the one existing assembly. PriorTurn is a ledger read and the three-step join lives there (AD-8): which turn came before in the pane, which of its runs stands, what that run printed in what order; the transport only maps it to Messages. Which run: the latest agent-lane execution, the attempt whose text the person actually read; a superseded attempt is neither merged nor reported missing. Attribution is deliberately two rules — with one run every text child is that run's and the payload is not consulted, so a block written by anything but OpenProse still assembles; with several the recorded runId separates them. Evicted prose goes to the model saying so, a cut-short run is marked partial. Worker's second correction, recorded in the commit: an approval resume is the SAME execution here (nocx-igu4y checkpoint resume), not a second attempt — the multi-attempt mechanism was built and tested anyway because StartExecution permits a second agent-lane row by design (ADR-0020 decision 4). Mutation-checked by the worker: ASC run selection, no run filter, reversed pos order, dropped partial marker and a nil assembly each fail their own tests. +7 transport, +14 content. Verified by the coordinator on the merged tree: content, transport, assistant, capability all green; full pre-commit hook including the containerised go test -race and vitest.

title: apicoll validates path components but not the names Windows refuses, and there is no depth bound
description:
`internal/apicoll` validates a path component for the things that make it dangerous — traversal, an unclean path, a name that is not a single component — and does not check the names Windows refuses outright: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9, a trailing dot or space. Nor is there a depth or total-length bound.

Surfaced by the folder-creation work (nocx-8v1fu): its brief expected the check to exist already in `apicoll/names.go`. That file is `apiimport/names.go`, it belongs to the importer, and it MINTS names rather than validating them — so reusing it is not possible and copying its reserved list into apicoll would be a second answer to one question, which is the thing the rule forbids. The worker left the gap where it found it and said so in the commit body rather than growing the duplicate.

The gap is not new and is not about folders: every path apicoll accepts has it — a request file, an environment, a collection name. A collection made on macOS with a folder called `con` is a collection a colleague on Windows cannot check out.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS or Linux, create a request or a folder in a collection named `con` (or `nul`, or a name ending in a dot).
2. Commit the collection and check it out on Windows.
3. The checkout fails on that path; nothing in nocx refused the name when it was typed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One owner for "is this name usable as a path component on every platform we ship to", reachable from both apicoll and apiimport. Whichever side it lives on, the other calls it; there is no second reserved list.
- Windows-reserved base names, a trailing dot and a trailing space are refused by name, with a sentence a surface can show, and are not silently rewritten.
- A depth bound and a total-path-length bound exist and are stated, so a deeply nested import cannot produce a path no filesystem will take.
- The importer's minting and the store's validation agree by construction: a name the importer mints is a name the store accepts — asserted with a test that runs a minted name through the validator.
- The existing refusals are unchanged; this adds cases rather than restating them.
close_reason: 55d5e4f4 on feat/api-testing (w-winnames). New internal/pathname is the single owner, called by apicoll (CheckComponent/CheckRelPath) and apiimport (Portable), landing with its callers so the deadcode ratchet is satisfied. Refuse and mint are two sides of one rule; agreement asserted by running a minted name through the validator. Bounds stated with their arithmetic: 128 bytes/component, depth 32, 200 bytes of relpath (sized under git-for-Windows' 260). Verified on the merged tree: go build -tags gtk3 ./... clean, go test on pathname/apicoll/apiimport all ok.

title: The e2e ssh fixture forwards no TCP, so a connection-routed fetch cannot be watched
description:
The URL import can fetch through a chosen connection (nocx-7fopj asserts the route reaches the table and that a dead connection refuses rather than dialling around the bastion), but no e2e can watch a person actually do it: the suite's own ssh fixture cannot carry the traffic.

`cmd/e2e-sshd` rejects every channel type but `session` (cmd/e2e-sshd/main.go:237) and forwards no TCP at all. A connection-routed fetch needs a `direct-tcpip` channel — that is how apisend's connection route dials the far side. A spec written against the fixture today would watch the fixture refuse and call it a product failure.

Reported by the worker that wrote e2e/api-import-url.spec.ts (nocx-4g0e5), which watches the DIRECT route end to end and says in its header comment which half is unwatched. Closing this gap means teaching the fixture a direct-tcpip channel, which is outside e2e/.

## Acceptance Criteria

- cmd/e2e-sshd accepts a direct-tcpip channel and forwards it, refusing everything else it refuses today.
- e2e/api-import-url.spec.ts gains the connection case: import through a connection the fixture serves, and assert the collection's environment carries that connection's route.
- The fixture's refusals stay refusals: a channel type it does not serve is still rejected by name, and the test asserting that still passes.
- Nothing in the fixture reaches the developer's own ssh agent, keys or config — the suite's isolation rules hold.
close_reason: landed in 1342b677: the fixture forwards direct-tcpip, so the routed import is watched

title: Unsent edits live in a signal, which is why Save feels compulsory
description:
Edits that were never SENT live only in a signal: switch requests, close the tab or restart, and they are gone. That is what makes Save feel compulsory even though Send already writes the file when the draft is dirty (api-store.ts:1098) — the person is insuring against losing an experiment, not deciding anything.

With runs persisted (nocx-kpl58) anything SENT is recoverable, so this covers the remaining case: what was typed and not yet fired.

Deliberately not autosave-into-the-file: the request file is what a colleague sees in a diff (§6.2), so an experiment on a shared collection must not land in the working tree until the person chose a moment — Send or Save.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Edits to a request survive switching to another request and back, closing and reopening the pane, and a restart of the app.
- The request FILE is unchanged by any of that: reading it back shows what it held before the edits, asserted on the bytes.
- The surface says a request has unsaved edits, in the tree and in the header, so "unsaved" is never a surprise at the moment of loss.
- Saving or sending clears the draft; discarding is possible and says what it is discarding.
- A draft for a request that was deleted or renamed underneath does not resurrect it, and does not wedge the pane.
close_reason: 0ca67708 on feat/api-testing. Owner overruled the bead's own 'deliberately not autosave-into-the-file': the draft is written 500ms after the last edit (the note tab's rhythm, idleMs injected for tests), and the Save button is gone. Every act inside the write window is answered — open flushes, delete cancels, move flushes to the old path first, Send cancels — and a failed write says so and stays dirty. Criterion 'edits survive a restart' is met by the file rather than by a draft store, which is the owner's call; criterion 'the surface says a request has unsaved edits' is void, there is no such state to say.

title: [bug] The generic approval lead says the assistant is ASKING to call a tool that has already run
description:
Found by the nocx-n7xha worker and left deliberately, out of that bead's scope.

nocx-njn8s fixed the TENSE for the `run` tool: a policy question is asked before the
call, so "the assistant wants to run this command"; an egress question screens a tool
RESULT, so the command has already run and saying "wants to" would misreport what has
happened to the machine.

The generic lead never got the same treatment. For an egress question on any tool
other than `run` the window still reads "The assistant is asking to call X" although
X has already been called and the thing being decided is whether what it returned may
leave for the provider.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Make a non-`run` tool return something the egress gate holds (a secret-shaped
   result from `files.read`).
2. The prompt's lead is in the wrong tense for a call that has already happened.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The lead's tense follows the GATE, not the tool: a policy question is about a call
  that has not happened, an egress question about one that has. Asserted for a
  non-`run` tool on both gates.
- ONE derivation of the tense, shared with the `run` lead njn8s added — not a second
  conditional beside it.

title: A running command's body says nothing for 33 seconds, while an assistant turn shows it is working
description:
Raised by the owner, 2026-08-23, alongside nocx-92gfl: «Давай показывать лоадер, как
и для агента в командах.»

An assistant turn that has asked and not yet heard back draws typing dots in its BODY
(`cmd-answer-typing`, blocks.ts ~1930, with its CSS at style.css:849) as well as the
pulse and word in its header. A command running on the normal buffer that has printed
nothing yet draws only the header pulse and its ticking duration; the body is empty.
So the two states — "the model is thinking" and "the command is working" — report
themselves differently, and the quieter of the two is the one that can last minutes.

This is the same family as nocx-hoeq3 (the header's right group) and should be read
with it: the answer flow built an in-progress vocabulary for the body, and the command
block, which had the state first, never got one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A command that is running and has produced no output yet says so IN ITS BODY, with
  the same component the answer flow uses — one owner for "this block is in progress",
  the way nocx-ex636 already made the header's pulse one owner.
- It goes away the moment the first byte lands, exactly as the typing dots retire on
  the first delta. Asserted — dots left running under real output is the defect this
  would otherwise introduce.
- A command that finishes having printed nothing does not leave a loader behind, and
  is still distinguishable from one whose output was evicted (ADR-0019 §7): "printed
  nothing" and "output is no longer kept" are different sentences and must stay so.
- Nothing here reads the byte stream to decide anything (AD-6). The running fact is
  the lifecycle's, which the pane already holds.

## Deliberately out

The header's chips — that is nocx-hoeq3. This bead is the body only. They touch the
same file and should be sequenced, not merged.

title: snippets: the refusal notice is not found under full-suite load, and the spec passes alone
description:
e2e/snippets.spec.ts:179 ("a multi-line body is refused when the program has not
enabled bracketed paste") failed on chromium inside a full ci-e2e run and passes
in isolation. The assertion never sees the notice element at all:

  Locator: .nocx-dialog[open] .quick-connect[data-variant="snippets"]
           .quick-connect__notice
  Expected substring: "bracketed paste"
  Timeout: 10000ms
  Error: element(s) not found

MEASURED, not assumed:

  full ci-e2e run, chromium   FAIL  13.9s
  the SAME test, same run, webkit  PASS  3.4s
  PW_PROJECTS=chromium on that one spec file, alone   PASS  2.5s (3/3 in file)

So it needs the whole suite running to reproduce, and one browser in that run
was fine. It is the WAIT that is failing, not the claim: element-not-found at
10s rather than a notice reading something else, so the palette dialog had not
reached the fire-refused state in the budget.

NOT nocx-8rtr.1, which is the reason this is a separate bead. That one is the
bracketed-paste-ON branch, which cannot be arranged in the e2e stand at all,
and it records that the OFF branch "is covered end to end and passes". This IS
the OFF branch, and it is the passing one that intermittently does not.

NOT caused by the notifications branch: the merge that surfaced it (f3aebbec)
touches nothing under frontend/src/snippets or e2e/snippets.spec.ts, and the
spec is green alone at that same commit.

Related in class to nocx-j41jx (two tests that fail under load and pass alone)
but not in mechanism: that bead is Go tests under -race in the containerized
gate; this is a Playwright wait in the e2e job.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. make ci-e2e (the whole suite, both browsers)
2. Sometimes: chromium e2e/snippets.spec.ts:179 fails with the locator above
   not found inside 10s, while webkit passes the same test in the same run.
3. PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/snippets.spec.ts passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The spec waits on an observable that is actually reached — per AGENTS.md a
  test may not depend on timing, and a budget raised from 10s to something
  larger is not the fix, it is the same defect with more slack.
- Whatever the wait becomes, it survives a full two-browser ci-e2e run
  repeatedly, not once.
notes:
A SECOND SPEC OF THE SAME CLASS, 2026-08-23, and the name moved again.

  full ci-e2e run, webkit  FAIL  e2e/vault-sealed-probe.spec.ts:147
                                 'a sealed vault raises the unlock and the probe
                                 completes after unlocking'
                                 expect(unlock).not.toBeVisible() -> visible
  the same spec alone, webkit, same commit  PASS 7.5s (2/2 in file)

So this bead is not about snippets. Two different spec files now, two different
assertions, same signature: red inside a full two-browser ci-e2e run, green
alone at the same commit, one browser only. Both are waits that never resolve
rather than assertions about a wrong value.

Worth noting for whoever takes it: the vault case is a DIALOG that does not
close, and the snippets case is a NOTICE that never appears. Both are 'the UI
did not reach the next state in the budget', which is what a starved renderer
looks like from a spec's side -- the same shape nocx-2h08 has on the Go side,
where a 30s timeout reports under a different test name every run.

2. It times out at api-testing.spec.ts:186 waiting for a visible button named

api-testing.spec.ts:185 does getByRole("button", {name: "Import", exact: true})
and then asserts aria-expanded becomes "true" — the collapsible Import section

(import-dialogs.tsx says so in its own header comment), so the button it waits

deliverable has no end-to-end proof.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The spec drives the import ask that exists — the dialog — rather than the
  disclosure that does not.
- It still asserts what it was written to assert: the export becomes a collection
  with no credential in the files, Send answers 201, and the raw view names the

close_reason: Merged as d308aa97. The bead's own account of the cause was STALE and is worth recording: the collapsed Import section it named had already become a dialog in this tree. The real break was two doors further in — the auth field sits on a Tabs panel that stays in the DOM but hidden, so the read-only assertion above it passed while a fill could not reach it; and runs are newest-first, so the literal run is .first() and the old .nth(1) asserted the token run's status and never saw the 401. Consequence of the break, and the reason this mattered: the literal-is-sent pair added for nocx-6hg2w.20 was written but never executed. It runs and passes now.

title: [bug] make lint-ci runs golangci-lint without the platform build tags, so it cannot pass on Linux
description:
Found running the epic-end gate on feat/ai-assistant, 2026-08-23, and BASELINED
before being blamed on the change: the identical failure reproduces at 9c730ed3, in
a detached worktree, before either wave of the work under test.

    === golangci-lint ===
    golangci-lint run ./...
    level=error msg="Running error: can't run linter goanalysis_metalinter\n
    buildir: failed to load package webview: could not load export data for
    \"github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/internal/assetserver/webview\""
    make: *** [Makefile:422: lint-ci] Error 3

The cause is two lines apart in the Makefile. `test-ci` passes the tags:

    $(GO) test -race -count=1 $(if $(WAILS_PLATFORM_TAGS),-tags "$(WAILS_PLATFORM_TAGS)") ./...

and `lint-ci`, immediately above it, does not:

    $(GOLANGCI_LINT) run ./...

Without the platform tag cgo cannot resolve wails on Linux and the linter dies
before it reaches any of our code. This is the same shape AGENTS.md already records
for the dead-code ratchet — "note the `-tags gtk3` too, without which cgo fails on
Linux before `deadcode` reaches our code at all" — and the pre-commit hook gets it
right, running `golangci-lint --build-tags=gtk3`. Only this target is missing it.

Related but NOT the same bead: nocx-ql23 is about AGENTS.md instructing a gate that
cannot pass on a dev box, and its worked example is `go test -race ./...` wanting
dash and zsh. This is a different command failing for a different reason, and it has
a one-line fix.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Linux, in any checkout: `make lint-ci`
2. Error 3, before any of our packages are linted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `make lint-ci` passes on a Linux dev box, and still lints the same packages it
  claims to. The obvious fix is the one `test-ci` already uses two lines below —
  apply the platform tags — but check against what CI's own job runs before copying,
  because `make ci` is the job AGENTS.md warns is the one place local and CI disagree.
- A green `make lint-ci` and a green containerized lint do not disagree about which
  packages were actually linted. Say in the target, or in its output, which they are:
  a linter that silently skips half the tree is worse than one that fails.
close_reason: Shipped by the same commit that closed nocx-ekj7a, which names the identical behaviour: lint-ci ran golangci-lint with no build tags, so on Linux the wails assetserver/webview export data could not load and the target died before linting any of our code. Makefile:20 now defines GOLANGCI_BUILD_TAGS from WAILS_PLATFORM_TAGS and Makefile:497 passes it, with the comment at :496 recording that it is empty on macOS so that runner keeps running exactly run ./... — which is this bead's macOS-unchanged criterion verbatim. Commit 4d2f2f3d. Verified in the tree during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.
