title: A tool call the assistant made is invisible, and its block lands after the answer it produced
acceptance_criteria:
A person reading the scrollback can see WHAT the assistant did and WHEN, in the order it
happened.

## What happens

Owner asked "what command did I run?". The assistant read the screen (empty — see
nocx-5u3oz), then ran `tail -20 ~/.bash_history …` through the run tool and answered from it.
In the scrollback, the command's block sits BELOW the finished answer that was written from
its output — so it reads as "answered first, ran the command afterwards". The readScreen call
before it is not shown at all; the only trace of a tool having run is the raw JSON result
leaking into the answer text (nocx-bshm2).

## Cause

Two halves of one shape. submitAgentCommand (frontend/src/terminal-content.ts) opens an
ordinary block through submitShellCommand, and a new block is appended to the scrollback tail
— but the ANSWER block was opened when the question was asked and is still streaming above
it, so anything the run does lands after it. And a tool call that is not a shell command
(readScreen) opens nothing at all: the transport notifies agent.runDelta and nothing else.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant something it answers by running a command.
2. The command's block appears below the answer that used its output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- What the assistant did is visible in the answer's own flow, in the order it happened —
  a tool call that ran is a thing on the wire, not an inference from a stray JSON blob.
- The ordering criterion is asserted, not eyeballed: a test drives one ask that calls a tool
  and asserts the tool's appearance precedes the answer text written from it.
- An ask with no tool calls renders exactly as it does today.
- Decide deliberately whether the agent's shell run stays a top-level block as well (it IS a
  command that ran in the lane, and the ledger says so) or becomes part of the answer flow —
  and write the reason down. Two surfaces may not own it (AGENTS.md).
close_reason: Landed in a18cead9 (merged 9f5d5655). A tool call is now a fact on the wire (agent.runToolCall, sent once per execution immediately before the tool runs) and an element of the answer's own flow, drawn where it happened — so the ordering fixes itself rather than a block being moved. The agent's shell block stays, with the ownership stated: the block owns the command (text, output, exit status, ledger entry), the answer's tool-call line owns WHEN and restates nothing the block holds, so they cannot drift. Schema in contracts/, generated renderer type, asserted over the real socket; an ask with no tool calls renders as before.

title: The model's reasoning is dropped on the floor: the engine reads Content and never ReasoningContent
acceptance_criteria:
A reasoning model's thinking is visible to the person (or deliberately hidden), rather than
silently discarded because nobody read the field.

## What happens

Owner ran deepseek-v4-flash — a reasoning model — and saw no reasoning at all.

## Cause

internal/assistant/engine.go's event loop emits onDelta(msg.Content) and nothing else.
eino's schema.Message carries ReasoningContent ("the thinking process of the model, which
will be included when the model returns reasoning content", schema/message.go:527) and the
streamed parts carry a reasoning part kind. We never touch either, so it is decoded off the
wire and thrown away.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Point the answering role at a reasoning model (deepseek-v4-flash over openrouter).
2. Ask anything. The answer arrives; the thinking never does.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reasoning reaches the renderer as its OWN thing on the wire, never mixed into the
  answer text — an answer block that concatenates thinking with the answer is the defect in
  another shape.
- A test drives a fake provider that emits reasoning parts and asserts where they land.
- The renderer decides how much to show; the decision is deliberate and written down.
- A model with no reasoning is unchanged — no empty section, no placeholder.
close_reason: Landed in a18cead9. ReasoningContent was decoded off the wire and dropped; it now travels agent.runReasoning into its own collapsed note, never concatenated into the answer text. A Go fake provider emitting real reasoning_content SSE frames covers it, and a model that returns no reasoning renders nothing at all.

title: A permitted tool's raw result is streamed to the person as answer text
acceptance_criteria:
Found while building nocx-igu4y and deliberately left alone there: a permitted tool's return
value reaches onDelta and therefore renders in the answer block. The person sees
{"path":"…/a.txt","total":10,…,"text":"hello file"} above the model's prose.

Measured pre-existing: the worker compared a clean HEAD tree against its own and the behaviour
is byte-identical, so nothing in the checkpoint-resume work caused it.

The tool result is the MODEL's input, not the person's — the answer block is what the model
says, and a JSON blob in it reads as the assistant having answered in JSON.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant something that makes it call a tool (readScreen, files.read).
2. Approve it. The tool's raw JSON result appears in the answer block before the prose.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts the deltas a run emits for a tool-calling ask contain the model's text and
  not the tool's return value.
- Whatever the person SHOULD see about a tool call that ran (that it ran, on what) is a
  deliberate answer, not the raw payload leaking through the delta path.
notes: Cause found 2026-08-22 while triaging the owner's live run: internal/assistant/engine.go's event loop emits onDelta for ANY message with content and never checks msg.Role. A tool result is a message of role tool, so its raw JSON goes down the delta path as though the model had said it. The fix is a role check at that seam — and what a person SHOULD see about a tool call is nocx-shxv0, which owns the visible form. Related: nocx-s92so (ReasoningContent is dropped at the same seam, for the same reason — only Content is read).
close_reason: Landed in a18cead9. The event loop checked no role, so a tool result — a message of role tool — travelled the delta path as answer text. The run's stream now carries typed events (AskAnswer / AskReasoning / AskToolCall) and only the model's own prose is the answer. The tool's result is deliberately not sent to the renderer at all: the attempt's outcome is in the ledger, the run tool's output is in the block the command opened, and a second copy would be an egress path around the gate.

title: ADR-0028 says checkpoints are encrypted; the store built for them is a plain in-memory map
acceptance_criteria:
ADR-0028's Consequences say a checkpoint is "encrypted, deleted on terminalization, swept at
startup". nocx-igu4y built the store and two of those three hold: it is deleted on every
terminal path, and it is born empty, so a restart sweeps it by existing. Encrypted does not:
internal/assistant/checkpoints.go is a plain map[string][]byte.

The worker declined to edit the ADR to match, which was right — the coordinator decides which
of the two documents is wrong. The argument for leaving it plaintext: the blob sits in the
same address space that already holds the run's messages, the question and the model's answer
in the clear, so encrypting it protects nothing from anyone who can read the other. The
argument against: the word is in a binding document and a reader takes it at face value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either the ADR's bullet says what is actually true and why (one sentence on why an
  in-process blob is not encrypted while the ledger at rest is), or the store encrypts and a
  test proves the bytes at rest in it are not the messages.
- Whichever way it goes, the ADR and the code say the same thing afterwards.
close_reason: ADR-0028's bullet now says what the store does: in-memory, keyed by run id, deleted on terminalization, swept at startup by being born empty — and states why the word 'encrypted' was struck rather than implemented (the blob shares an address space that already holds the run's messages in the clear; encryption is a property of the ledger at rest, and a checkpoint is never at rest). It names the condition that reopens the decision: a checkpoint that becomes durable. Commit 5ae124b2.

title: The ask block's status word lands right of the ⋮, so two block kinds have two header grammars
acceptance_criteria:
Every block header reads the same left-to-right, whatever its kind: chips, then the status,
then the ⋮ overflow button last.

## What happens

Owner's screenshot, 2026-08-22: an ask block's header reads "⋮  failed" while the command
block under it reads "50ms  ok  ⋮". Same header, same row, two orders.

## Cause

frontend/src/scrollback/blocks.ts: the overflow button is appended to .cmd-header-right when
the block is BUILT (:810, :887). The command kind's duration and exit chips are built before
that, in buildBlockHeader, so they land left of it. The ask kind's terminal word is appended
by the answer flow's close() (:1729-1740) — after the build — so it lands right of it.

The waiting chip is fine (built at build time), which is why only the FINISHED ask block
looks wrong.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant anything; let the run finish or fail.
2. The answer block's header shows the ⋮ to the LEFT of "completed"/"failed"; a command
   block above or below it shows the ⋮ to the RIGHT of "ok"/"exit N".

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts the ORDER of .cmd-header-right's children for both kinds: the overflow
  button is the last child in each. Failing before the fix.
- The fix places the chip, rather than making close() know about the button's position by
  luck — a third kind added later inherits the right order.
- No CSS repaint of the kit's chips to compensate (AGENTS.md: a surface may place, never
  repaint).
close_reason: One owner for the placement (placeHeaderChip): chips go left of the ⋮, whether or not the button exists yet. The test asserts the order of .cmd-header-right's children for the command kind and a finished ask block in one case — red on the ask half before the change. Commit 958b81fe; all pre-commit gates green.

title: A run never says what the name resolved to
description:
A run says which address answered the dial and never said what the name
resolved TO. The two are different questions: a host with four A records
answers from one of four, and a name resolving to a stale address is the whole
explanation for a request that went somewhere nobody expected.

The resolver's answer is a fact about the ATTEMPT, so it rides the attempt —
looked up again later by whoever reads the run, it can legitimately differ.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `api.request.send` answers `dnsAddresses`, in the resolver's own order (the
  order the dialler tries), declared in the schema, never null.
- An address literal and a failed lookup both answer `[]`.
- The run's connection block prints the answer when there is one.
close_reason: landed in 95d5e26b

title: The timings are a line of numbers, not a reading
description:
The run's Raw tab printed one line — `dns 97.278ms · connect 0ms · tls 0ms ·
ttfb 0ms · total 97.337ms`. It is exact and it answers the wrong question. The
question a person asks of a slow request is WHERE the time went, and five
numbers in a row make them do the arithmetic, including a subtraction that is
nowhere written down: `ttfb` is measured from the start of the request, so the
far side's own thinking time is `ttfb` minus the three phases before it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The elapsed time is drawn to scale: resolve, connect, tls, waiting,
  download, in the order they happen.
- `waiting` is `ttfb` minus the phases before it and `download` is `total`
  minus `ttfb`; both are clamped at zero, and a clamped phase is not drawn.
- A phase that did not happen is absent from bar and legend alike — no
  hairline that reads as "instant".
- The numbers stay, under the bar, because comparing two runs needs them.
- Every drawn span is named in the accessible label with the measured total.
close_reason: landed in 95d5e26b

title: TestBootstrapWindow_QuarantinesTheUsersInputAndNotItsOwn is timing-dependent and flakes under container load
description:
Failed once in scripts/ci-linux.sh and passed in the previous run of the same script on the same commit. 15 host runs green on the branch and 15 green on main, so it is not the diff — internal/session is untouched by feat/file-upload.

The assertion is about scheduling order — a refused keystroke must not be delivered later — and it loses under container load. AGENTS.md: a test may not depend on timing, and a spec that needs a fast machine is broken on a slow one; it has only not been caught yet. This one has now been caught.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. ./scripts/ci-linux.sh, repeatedly. It fails intermittently at bootstrap_window_test.go:113 with: a refused keystroke was delivered later; the terminal received their passwordNOCX1 ... abcdtyped.
2. go test -count=15 ./internal/session/ on the host: green, on both the branch and main.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test waits on an observable state change rather than on ordering that a loaded machine can reorder.
- It fails when the quarantine is genuinely broken — prove it by breaking the quarantine and watching it go red, not by watching it stay green.

title: Context menus have no icons at three of four call sites, and nothing catches the fourth
description:
Reported by the owner: the Files context menu has no icons. Diagnosed: not a kit defect. ui/context-menu.tsx accepts icon?: Component and reserves the icon column whether or not one is passed, deliberately, so a menu may mix rows with and without. Three of the four call sites simply never pass it — workspace-menu.ts does (PencilIcon, ArrowUpIcon, ArrowDownIcon, CloseIcon) and is the one that was fixed before; files-view.tsx and tab.tsx do not.

There is no global FIX, because the kit cannot know which icon Copy Absolute Path wants. There is a global GATE: frontend/lint-fixtures already carries check-row-grammar, check-two-owners and check-css-integrity in exactly this shape.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Right-click a row in the Files panel: Copy Relative Path, Copy Absolute Path and Show in Finder all render with an empty icon column.
2. Right-click a tab: same.
3. Open a workspace chip's menu: icons are there, because workspace-menu.ts passes them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every item in the Files and tab context menus carries an icon from the kit's set; none is invented locally.
- A lint fixture rule fails a context-menu item literal with no icon, so the next call site cannot omit it silently.
- The rule is baselined only where an omission is deliberate, and each baseline line says why.
close_reason: Merged as 180cae03. Measured rather than assumed: 15 context-menu item literals across four call sites, 3 bare — all three in files-view.tsx. My brief claimed tab.tsx was bare too; it was not, and the worker checked instead of believing me. CopyIcon on both copy rows (one verb, two objects, the label separates them), ExternalLinkIcon on Show in Finder because it leaves nocx. The gate is the real deliverable: check-menu-icons.mjs in the house shape — baseline, growth-guarded updater, negative fixture, 12 unit tests, its own vitest config, wired into gate.sh. The baseline is EMPTY and the updater refuses to grow, so nothing is suppressed. It scans .ts as well as .tsx, with JSX parsing only for .tsx, because a .ts file's generics would otherwise fail closed as a permanent parse violation. Proven both directions: marking the fixture's bare row makes the rule stop firing, un-marking a real call site makes it fire.

title: Upload from the Files tree context menu, on the row you meant
description:
Owner asked for upload/download in the Files tree context menu. Download is nocx-9le.8 and does not exist; a menu item for it would advertise what nothing can deliver, so this bead is upload only and download joins the menu with its own epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An Upload item on a directory row uploads into THAT directory, reusing the existing flow rather than a second one.
- The item joins only on a remote origin, the way Show in Finder joins only on a local one (files-view.tsx:263,281) — R1 by absence, not by a disabled control.
- It does not contradict section 4's refusal of drop-on-a-folder-row: that refused a GESTURE with a third target rule, not a folder as an explicit target.
close_reason: Merged as e019d79f. Upload on a directory row, destDir is that row's path, reusing upload-flow and the existing picker passed down as a prop so both placements raise the same one. Absent on a local origin and present on a remote one, mirroring Show in Finder's opposite condition — R1 by absence, tested both ways. Directory-ness comes from isExpandable, which already owns that question in the file rather than a second predicate. No download row, stub or TODO.

title: make ci is unusable on a machine without /bin/bash, and says nothing about why
description:
Distinct from nocx-58gq, which is about a macOS workstation. This is a NixOS-class machine: there is no /bin/bash, and the shell-integration and bash-channel tests fork it by absolute path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a machine without /bin/bash, run make ci at any commit including main.
2. internal/app and the bash-channel tests fail with fork/exec /bin/bash: no such file or directory.
3. The same go test ./... is green inside scripts/ci-linux.sh, which has /bin/bash.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either the tests resolve the shell the way the product does rather than hardcoding /bin/bash, or they skip with a stated reason on a machine that has none.
- A developer running make ci on such a machine is told which failures are the machine and which are the code, without having to baseline against main by hand.

title: The request header changes height when a request opens
description:
`header.api-crumbs` measured 32.5px with nothing open and 48.5px with a request
open, so opening a request pushed the whole right half down.

The row already declared a floor — `min-height: var(--control-height-md)` — and
could not reach it in either state. Two causes, one under the other: the floor
named a control height while `min-height` on a border-box element also has to
carry the row's own padding, and the tallest child was a ghost Button, the one
kit variant with no height of its own (its size came from its padding plus the
inherited line-height, about 32.5px, which is not any control height we
declare).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the API workbench with no request selected — measure the header.
2. Click a request — the header is sixteen pixels taller and everything below
   it moves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The header is the same height with and without a request open.
- The ghost Button's height is a token like every other variant's, and a
  `data-size` ghost still honours its size.

title: A variable in the URL is not marked as one
description:
A `{{variable}}` in the URL field was plain text: nothing said which part of
the address is a reference the environment answers and which part is typed
literally. Postman marks them, and the mark is what makes an address with two
references readable at a glance.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a request whose URL is `{{baseUrl}}/zen`.
2. The braces read as ordinary characters; nothing distinguishes the reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reference is painted, the rest of the address is not.
- The scan mirrors `internal/apicoll/substitute.go` character for character —
  `{{"a":1}}` is not a reference, `{{ name }}` is, `{{secret:X}}` is not.
- The mark changes colour only: the ink layer holds the same characters as the
  input, so the caret and the glyphs cannot part company.
- The kit owns the paint (`TextField.marks`), the surface owns the grammar.

title: Download: a file from the host of the active tab lands on this machine
description:
The reverse direction of nocx-9le.5. It reuses that epic's shape — the sink's io.Reader seam inverted, the same binding addressing, the same progress and done notifications — and is its own surface: a save dialog, a local write path, and a different set of failures.

## Success Criteria

- A person picks a file in the remote tree and it lands on their machine, with progress and cancellation, watched end to end by one automated check against cmd/e2e-sshd.
- Deliberately out: directories, resume after a broken link, and a queue of concurrent transfers — the same three the upload epic deferred.

title: The import ask's Browse floated beside the sentence, not the field
description:
The picker button was aligned to the input by a hand-measured 1.625rem top
margin, copied from key-material-input.css where the field carries a label and
nothing under it. Both API path asks put a DESCRIPTION between label and
control, so the button sat level with the sentence rather than with the field it
belongs to. On a 480px dialog panel it also took a third of the row from the
path, which is the one value that must stay readable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the API workbench, collections menu → Import collection…
2. Look at "New collection folder": the Browse control is level with the
   description text, a line above the input it fills.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The picker is inside the field (TextField's `trailing` slot), so its position
  is the kit's and holds for any label, description or error.
- `.api-path-row` and its 1.625rem constant no longer exist.
- The same treatment in `collection-dialog.tsx`, which shares the layout.
- The export field's description is one line, not two sentences.

title: Parallel worker gates starve each other and report timeouts as defects
description:
Measured three times in one session (2026-08-21) while running four workers in parallel worktrees on a 6-core box, load average 9-29:

1. nocx-avogl.4 pre-commit hook: 14 vitest specs failed, every one "Test timed out in 5000ms", no assertion among them, none in files the diff touched. The run own numbers showed the starvation: collect 645.84s against a 345s wall clock, environment 339.79s. Same tree, same hook, unloaded machine: green in 1m32s.
2. scripts/ci-linux.sh on the merged tree: TestLocalPty_SignalForegroundReachesAChildNotOnlyTheShell failed at 5.03s in the with-Secret-Service variant. The epic touched no file under internal/pty (git log bbe89639..HEAD -- internal/pty/ is empty), and the same test passes on the host in 0.103s. Re-run on an unloaded machine: both variants green, internal/pty 1.7s.
3. TestAgentAsk_SlowConsumerBoundsTheDeltaPath flaked for two different workers in two different worktrees (nocx-5j8z3).

The common cause is not three tests. containerized-tests.sh starts the vitest container at --cpu-shares 512 IN PARALLEL with the Go container, and AGENTS.md removed the CPU caps from these scripts on the argument that "a test may not depend on timing". That argument is right and the caps were removed for good reasons. What was not costed is that a COORDINATOR running a worker wave makes every worker gate compete with every other, so the gate poisons itself and reports defects that are not in the diff.

The damage is not a red run — it is that a worker reads a red gate as its own defect and starts fixing a test that was never broken. Two workers this session correctly refused to, and both spent a round proving it instead of building.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start 3-4 workers in parallel worktrees, each running its pre-commit hook.
2. Watch load average pass ~2x cores.
3. Observe timeout-shaped failures in specs no diff touched, which pass on the host and pass again once the machine is idle.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worker gate either does not compete with other worker gates, or says in its own output that the machine was contended, so a red run is not read as a defect in the diff.
- Whatever is chosen is written down where a coordinator planning a wave will see it, not only where a worker reading a failure will.
- The three observations above are cited, so the next person does not have to re-measure them.

It was NOT among the five failures of the previous full run on a tree differing only by the settings fix, and the epic touches no ssh, pty or block code. LIMIT OF THE EVIDENCE, stated rather than glossed: I did not re-run the FULL suite a second time to watch it pass there, so 'flaky under suite load' is the best-supported reading, not a proven one. title: Brainstorming: upload a file to the server in the active tab
description:
Design session: how a person puts a local file onto the host their active tab is connected to.

- A design doc exists in .internal/specs/ and the owner has approved it.
- The transport shape (who carries the bytes) is decided, not left open.

title: The API panel asks you to press refresh for something files.watch already does
description:
The API panel carries a refresh button whose tooltip is "Re-read the open folders". It
exists because a collection is a folder on disk that changes underneath us — a git pull, a
neighbouring editor, a colleague's branch. The intent is sound; the answer is not.

files.watch already answers this question, and the Files panel already uses it. Its
contract even carries a mode field that exists, in its own words, "so the UI can say why
refresh may lag" — so the product can both watch AND admit when watching degraded to
polling.

So two panels answer "how does this surface learn the folder changed" two different ways.
The button is not a stray control; it is the symptom of the missing watch.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the API pane with a collection open.
2. Change a request file outside nocx.
3. Nothing happens until the refresh button is pressed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The open collection roots are watched through files.watch, the way the Files panel does.
  The watch set is REPLACED on change, per that contract — collapsing or closing a
  collection must not leak a watch.
- A change on disk re-lists the affected collection with no user action. A test asserts the
  new state is on screen without anything being pressed.
- Where the mode says refresh may lag, the panel SAYS SO rather than looking current. A
  soft degrade the UI does not admit to is how a stale tree becomes an hour of confusion.
- The manual button survives only if there is a case watching cannot cover; if there is,
  name it in the bead. Otherwise it goes.
notes: Fixed in 654910a2. Watch through files.watch with the set replaced rather than added to; refresh button moved into the pane header mirroring files-view.tsx; and the polling badge became a KIT COMPONENT (ui/watch-badge.tsx) with Files migrated onto it — Files' own 23 tests pass unchanged, which is the evidence the migration was faithful. What moved into the kit is the judgement (polling AND a reason AND a local binding is one warning; every other combination is a designed mode and says nothing), not the markup.
close_reason: Done and integrated in 5e731bd3 / 654910a2. Verified on the merged tree: typecheck, lint (dead-exports all baselined, shrunk by 4), 3612 frontend tests green.

title: The assistant can look for work that is no longer on a screen
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-21-searching-the-ledger-from-the-assistant-design.md (approved by the owner, 2026-08-21).

The assistant cannot look for work that is no longer on a screen. Today it is shown nothing it was not handed: readScreen sees the live screen, and there is no way to ask what was run or printed before. The person has to find the block themselves and attach it — which is the thing the attach design says the assistant should be asking for with a tool instead.

This epic is the TOOL ONLY: a row in internal/agenttools (effect observe, resources [environment], resourceArg environmentId), a params schema under contracts/tools with additionalProperties:false and an explicit required, a Narrow that hands it a reader scoped to the grant environments, and the model-facing sentence. It has NO predicate, index or ranking of its own — ledger.search (nocx-rtg0.21) is the one owner of search and this is its second consumer beside the recall overlay.

The one non-obvious decision, from design section 2: the tool MUST name the environment it searches. A tool naming no resource takes the branch in policy.go inScope that returns true — its scope becomes the grant own scope for the kinds it declares — so a search that named nothing would read the whole machine recorded history under a grant a person gave for one session.

## Success Criteria

- A person asks about a string printed three weeks ago and on no screen now; the assistant calls ledger.search, answers, names the environment, and states the coverage hole when retention has evicted part of the window. Watched end to end against the real backend.
- The tool carries no predicate, index, ranking or coverage computation of its own: a test or a review note shows the search logic lives in one place.
- A call that names an environment outside the run grant is refused by the scope check, and the refusal reaches the person as a sentence they can act on (depends on nocx-avogl.3).
- The schema is in contracts/ with additionalProperties:false and an explicit required, and the result is validated over the real socket.

## Deliberately out

- ledger.search itself (nocx-rtg0.21).
- Any index over output before nocx-jrdy is closed.
- Deciding the FTS indexing unit or the substring promise (nocx-ms7v.7).
- Widening the grant beyond one environment: the policy surface for that is its own bead.
- Search over the live screen (readScreen already exists) and cross-pane conversation memory (out by the what-the-model-is-told design).

title: The autonomous run: a mode it declares, a lease it obeys, a goal it states
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-21-what-the-model-is-told-design.md section 5, over assistant-surface design 4.2 and ADR-0028. The loop itself is NOT reopened: eino runs it, and the two modes are decided.

Today the mode is an accident rather than a fact: tools are declared whenever the grant permits anything, so 'explain' and 'agent' are not distinguishable on a run. A loop nobody can bound, cancel or read the purpose of is not one to leave running.

## Success Criteria
- A person gives the assistant a goal, it works through several tool calls under the policy and stops when it is done — and the block says throughout what it is trying to do. Watched end to end.
- The run records its mode; an explain run declares no tools.
- A lease bounds it, cancel ends it, and both are visible on the block.

## Deliberately out
- Anything that widens authority. The grant is still per run and immutable (ADR-0020).

title: The second model is actually consulted: classifier, then advisor
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-21-what-the-model-is-told-design.md section 4. Finishes the missing half of nocx-kpy23.

profile.RoleClassifier is assignable, internal/assistant/classifier.go is written, and ResolveClassifier has NO production implementation — only test fixtures. So the second model is declared and never consulted: the auto-approve, the prompt-injection defence and the judge for a stalled run all rest on a seam that is not connected.

The advisor omp ships (docs/advisor-watchdog.md: own context, own model, read-only tools, may object and may never authorise) is the same seam with a wider remit, not a fourth subsystem.

## Success Criteria
- A proposed tool call is judged by the classifier model resolved through the roles surface, and the verdict is visible on the run. Watched end to end against a fake endpoint.
- The classifier may only ever raise suspicion (permit -> ask), never lower it, asserted.
- An auto-approve is a decision the POLICY makes on the classifier's evidence when the person has said so — never the classifier acting on its own authority.

## Deliberately out
- The advisory note channel until the per-call verdict ships.

title: You can ask about the program that is holding the keyboard
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-21-what-the-model-is-told-design.md section 6, over assistant-surface design 3.1-3.4.

While a full-screen program owns the terminal the editor is hidden, so there is no way to ask about what is on the screen. The mechanism is already decided — the assistant is a state of the machine that already owns keyboard routing, and it does not overlay the program, it gets the room back — what is missing is the door.

## Success Criteria
- A person runs a full-screen program, opens the assistant from the strip menu (mouse) or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+/ (keyboard), asks what is on the screen and gets an answer naming what is actually there — with no keystroke sent to the program. Watched end to end.
- The chord and both menu rows call ONE function.
- No new floating surface over the terminal, and no new mark in the activity bar.

## Deliberately out
- Driving the program (keystrokes) — that is nocx-x8s2's drive rung.

title: Settings: the person adds their own paragraph to the system prompt
description:
Design section 1, item 6. A free-text field in Settings, appended LAST to the assembled prompt, under a heading that says it came from the person.

Last, because a rule of theirs that contradicts a line of ours should win. Under a heading, because the model must be able to tell our standing rules from theirs, and a prompt that silently merges the two cannot be debugged by either of us.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The field writes on change like every other settings screen (no Save button), through the settings document that already exists.
- The assembled prompt ends with the person's text under its own heading; a test asserts both the position and the heading.
- It is bounded in length, and the bound is stated on the screen rather than enforced silently.
- It is NOT authority: a test asserts the policy path never reads it — it cannot widen a grant, name a tool, or turn an ask into a permit.
close_reason: 64173be3 plus the regression fix 4451a77d. A bounded free-text setting (2000 chars, counted in runes) appended LAST to the assembled prompt under its own heading, written on change through the settings document, rendered by a multiline VARIANT of the kit's TextField rather than a sixth ControlKind. TestPersonalInstructions_HaveExactlyOneReaderAndItIsThePrompt asserts the policy path never reads it. The first commit turned four proof-matrix e2e specs red: cause was NOT the new control but hidden sections living in the DOM, on which 'the last row in the document is visible' held by coincidence until a section registered after it. 4451a77d stops rendering sections nobody is looking at; measured 57/5 to 61/1, which is the baseline.

title: Hide the policy rows for effects nothing can produce yet
description:
The Agent policy page drew all seven effect classes: the two a declared tool carries, and five more behind a disclosure headed "Capabilities the assistant does not have yet". The owner read that group and could not tell what it was for — fair, because a row saying "Ask every time" about an effect no tool can produce is a control that does nothing.

Drawn only for the live classes now. `live` is the backend's list (agenttools.LiveEffects), so a row reappears the day a tool carrying that effect is declared — nothing is removed from the model, the wire or the store, and nothing has to be remembered later.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The page draws a row only for an effect class in the backend's live list.
- A dormant class carrying a non-default answer still draws its row, visible without a disclosure, and can be set back to Ask.
- Nothing is deleted from the policy model, the contract or the store: liveness stays the backend's answer.
close_reason: shipped on feat/ai-assistant: 95b314ba

title: Four identifier mints outside the lifecycle family still tolerate a failed random read
description:
Enumerated while closing nocx-s16k8, which fixed every tolerant random read in the
lifecycle family: the per-epoch capability, the recovery fence, and the transport, lane,
domain, request, attempt and generation identifiers in internal/lifecycle,
internal/lifecyclepub, internal/lifecyclechannel and internal/lifecycleremote. Four
tolerant reads remain, all OUTSIDE that family, and each is a prior deliberate decision
with its reason written next to it -- which is why they are a bead and not part of that
fix. AGENTS.md: re-deciding a settled question inside a bugfix is how it stops being
settled.

  internal/session/session.go:316   NewID      -- the session id (AD-7, server-authoritative)
  internal/tunnel/tunnel.go:215     newID      -- the forward's backend id (spec 7.3); its
                                                  comment states the decision outright:
                                                  "crypto/rand failure is treated as
                                                  unreachable, and a deterministic fallback
                                                  would mint colliding ids"
  internal/profile/profile.go:1120  newUUID    -- the profile id suffix
  internal/vault/system/system.go:173 randomProbeID -- the keychain probe id

None is an authenticator, so none has the capability's failure mode: no equality check
authenticates a caller against them. What a zero value does is make every id the SAME id,
and each of these is a value something else tells two things apart by -- two sessions, two
forwards, two profiles. The consequence is a collision, not an intrusion.

The question this bead answers is whether that is acceptable, ONE way, for all four --
and if it is, whether the reason belongs in one place rather than restated four times.
internal/content/ledger_agent_sqlite.go:41 is a fifth shape and already loud: it panics
with "rand.Read never fails on supported platforms".

## Acceptance Criteria

Each of the four sites either fails loudly on a failed or short read, or carries a comment
naming what a zero value would collide and why that is acceptable here -- decided once,
recorded once, and referenced by the other three rather than re-argued. A test exists for
whichever answer is chosen: a failure injection for a refusal, or an assertion that the
colliding value cannot reach the thing it would collide.

title: The Agent policy description is flush against its heading rule, and the dormant section does not say what it is for
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Settings -> Agent policy.
2. The sentence under "Agent policy" touches the heading's rule — no air at all —
   while the note under "Capabilities the assistant does not have yet" a few rows
   down has 24px.
3. Read that note. It does not say why the section exists or what setting a row in
   it does.

## Cause
settings.css halves PageSection's flex gap (`.ui-settings .ui-page-section { gap:
var(--space-2) }`) so the heading does not float above the first row. The kit pulls
its description UP to the heading with `margin-top: calc(var(--space-2) * -1)`,
sized against the kit's own 16px gap — so under this surface the pull cancels the
gap exactly and the description lands on the rule.

The dormant note read "Nothing the assistant can do today falls under these.
Answering one now is allowed and does exactly what it says — nothing, until it
gains something that does it." Every clause is true and the paragraph is a riddle:
it never says the answer is SAVED, which is the only reason to set one.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The section description clears the heading rule by the same distance the
  collapsible Section's note does.
- The dormant note says three things: the assistant has no tool with these effects,
  an answer governs nothing today, and it is kept and applies the day one arrives.
close_reason: fixed on feat/ai-assistant: a93154c7, 829b4626

title: A header value picker prints the literal text \u2014 None \u2014
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Settings -> Endpoints -> edit an endpoint, add a custom header.
2. Switch the header value source to "Use existing secret".
3. The empty option reads `— None —` — the escape, not two em dashes.

## Cause
endpoints-section.tsx:907 passes the placeholder as a JSX STRING attribute:
`placeholder="— None —"`. A string attribute is not a JS string literal,
so the escape is never interpreted. Every other call site spells it as an
expression — secret-source.tsx:74, key-material-input.tsx:245,
authentication-editor.tsx:113,168 — and renders correctly.

The prop is also redundant: SecretSource already defaults to the same text
(`props.placeholder ?? '— None —'`), so the fix is to delete the line.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The header value picker's empty option renders as an em-dashed "None", asserted
  by a frontend test that reads the option's text.
close_reason: fixed on feat/ai-assistant: a93154c7, 829b4626

title: apicoll path safety has a narrowed but open TOCTOU between lstat and open
description:
The symlink refusal in internal/apicoll/path.go checks each component with lstat and then
opens the path. Between those two steps the component can be replaced by a symlink, so the
window is narrowed, not closed. Reported by the T1 worker rather than found in review, and
left deliberately: closing it needs openat2/O_NOFOLLOW per component behind a build tag,
which is a per-OS problem this repo already solves elsewhere (internal/contentkey) and not
a thing to invent inside a collection reader.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a collection whose request lives at users/create.json (an ordinary file).
2. Between the lstat of "users" and the open of the request, replace "users" with a symlink
   pointing outside the collection root.
3. The open follows the replaced component. A test that loses this race deterministically
   needs a hook in the walk; add one for the test rather than sleeping.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test that wins the race with the current implementation, and cannot win it after.
- Per-component open with O_NOFOLLOW (openat2 where available), behind a build tag, with a
  portable fallback that states what it does not guarantee.
- If the fallback is weaker, the product says so — not only a code comment.

title: A hard-killed multiplex master can leave a socket that silently disables multiplexing
description:
Raised while integrating nocx-m8jwn and deliberately left unanswered there.

The typed path's control root is a fixed name shared across sessions, and %C makes each socket per-destination. OpenSSH's behaviour for a control socket that exists but has no listener is to refuse to use it -- 'ControlSocket ... already exists, disabling multiplexing' -- so a master killed hard enough to skip its own cleanup leaves a file that turns the typed path's integration off for that destination, silently, until somebody removes it.

defaultMasterProbes already watches the three loss events of the design's section 6.2 -- the socket, the master process, the transport -- for a master this process made. What is not answered is the socket it did NOT make: a leftover from a previous run, or from a session that died with the machine.

## Steps to Reproduce

Bring up a typed ssh so a master and its control socket exist. Kill the master with SIGKILL so no cleanup runs, leaving the socket file. Confirm with ss -lx that nothing listens on it. Type the same ssh line again: ssh finds the existing path, reports that it already exists, and runs without multiplexing -- so nocx cannot own the connection and the session comes up unintegrated, with no indication that a stale file is the reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

A control socket that exists with no listener is detected before the line is wrapped and either reclaimed or refused with a named reason a user can act on -- never silently degraded. The check distinguishes a dead socket from a live one owned by another session of ours, and from a path owned by a different user, and does not remove a file it cannot prove is dead. A test drives each of the three cases.

title: Task 5: policy.get reports which effect classes are live
description:
Plan Task 5. contracts/policy.get.schema.json, internal/agenttools/registry.go, internal/transport/ws_policy.go, frontend/src/policy-client.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- live lists exactly the effects at least one declared tool carries, in the lattice's canonical order, deduplicated. Today: observe, mutate-destructive.
- policy.get's top-level object gains additionalProperties:false (it lacks it today) and live is required.
- Adding a declaration carrying a new effect changes live with no other edit. Asserted.
- An over-the-wire conformance test validates the real result.

title: The 24 new refusal reason strings have not been through owner agreement
description:
nocx-m8jwn.5 widened the refusal vocabulary from 7 members to 31 -- one per row of the section 6.4 matrix and one per bootstrap outcome -- so that a user is told which refusal happened instead of reading 'conventional, unknown'. The coverage is not optional and is not in question here.

The wording is. Twenty-four product strings were written by the implementing worker and have not been read by the owner. AGENTS.md's nocx-viil records that user-visible wording is the owner's, and a sentence a person reads at the moment their session failed is exactly the kind that should not be settled by whoever was closest to the code.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every one of the 24 new reason strings has been read and either accepted or rewritten by the owner, and the accepted text is what the product renders -- asserted at the wire seam the renderer consumes, not in a Go enum. A reason whose wording changes does not change its enum member, so the change is text only.

title: A t.TempDir cleanup race fails TestBootstrapProgress_AClosedDescriptorCostsNoTerminal on a first run
description:
Seen while integrating nocx-m8jwn, in a file that epic never touched.

The test fails on a first containerized run and passes on re-run and five times in isolation. The failure is in t.TempDir() cleanup rather than in the behaviour under test, so the assertion is not what is flaky -- the fixture's teardown is.

It is worth fixing rather than tolerating because a test that fails once per cold run trains everybody to re-run instead of read, which is how a real failure gets waved through.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the package in the repository's containerized Go image on a cold cache: .githooks/containerized-tests.sh's go_test_containerized, or scripts/gotest-pkg.sh style invocation against the package holding the test. The first run fails in cleanup; a second run in the same container passes, and the test passes 5/5 when run alone with -count=5.

## Acceptance Criteria

The test passes on a cold first run in the containerized image, five consecutive times, with no retry wrapper and no raised timeout. The fix names what the cleanup was racing with -- a file handle still open, a child process still writing, or an unlinked path -- rather than reordering statements until it stops reproducing. If the race is in the code under test rather than the fixture, that is the finding and it outranks the test change.

title: Brainstorming: the Agent policy surface — a person cannot tell what it does or how to use it
description:

3. Its description is ADR-0020/ADR-0028 language pasted into the product:

The surface is REAL, not a placeholder: GlobalPolicyStore -> WithAgentPolicy

title: A healthy state narrates itself on three assistant surfaces
description:
Owner review pass on feat/ai-assistant, 2026-08-21. Three surfaces reassured a
person that nothing was wrong, in three different places, and one of them
blocked a button for a condition the backend was already built to handle.

THE RULE, now held by tests on both surfaces: a status line speaks only to
REFUSE, or to answer a check the person asked for. A healthy state is silent.

Also in this pass: the endpoint dialog put custom headers AFTER the models,
below the Test button — but headers ride on every request the probe sends
(ws_assistant.go resolveProbeHeaders), so they are part of the CONNECTION, and
a header typed after a green test was never part of what went green.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings -> Roles, with a default set and no role assignment of its own:
   every role renders a green "As default: <endpoint> · <model>", restating
   the Default model control twenty pixels above it, once per role.
2. Settings -> Endpoints, with a resolvable credential: every row renders a
   green "Key saved".
3. Lock the vault, reopen Settings -> Endpoints: every row renders "The vault
   is locked — unlock it to use the assistant" — a global condition narrated
   per row, about something the row is not about — and every row's Test
   button is disabled.
4. Edit an endpoint: custom headers sit below the models, under the Test
   button they are part of.

## Acceptance Criteria

- roleStateLine returns null for a role resolving through a healthy default,
  not only for a role naming its own healthy pair.
- The endpoints row renders no status at all for 'resolvable' and for
  'sealed'; 'none', 'deleted' and 'unavailable' keep their sentences, and a
  probe outcome still renders (it answers a button the person pressed).
- rowTestDisabled no longer refuses 'sealed'. Pressing Test on a locked vault
  raises the unlock and then runs the check — ws_assistant.go
  resolveProbeCredential raises vault.ErrVaultSealed, sealedNormalizer
  rewrites it to the canonical -32001, and the renderer's dispatcher raises
  the unlock and re-sends verbatim (ADR-0032). The comment there already
  calls a probe RESULT naming the sealed state "the dead end this bead exists
  to delete"; the frontend was greying out a path the backend kept open.
- The endpoint dialog reads name, base url, key, headers, Test, models, held
  by a DOM-order assertion rather than by eye.
- No e2e assertion treats a caption as evidence that a secret landed. The
  proof is the probe through the fake endpoint, which reports the material it
  was sent.
close_reason: Shipped in bfb9163c on feat/ai-assistant. Roles line and endpoints row are silent when healthy; Test stays live on a sealed vault and raises the unlock through the ADR-0032 seam; the endpoint dialog puts headers above the button that tests them; two e2e sites stopped reading a caption as proof a secret landed. 3569 frontend tests green; agent-ask + assistant-readiness green in the container (8/8, chromium).

title: Reopen this tab sandboxed, and restart it when its grant changes
description:
Landlock is monotonic and Seatbelt applies before `exec`, so applying a policy can only ever mean relaunching. That makes "restart with these rights" and "reopen this ordinary tab sandboxed" ONE operation, and it wants the grant persisted so it can be re-issued.

A tab context-menu entry covers the real scenario — already in the directory, decide to cage it — without amending AD-11's promise that `+` and `Cmd/Ctrl+T` are untouched.
design: Profile changes never mutate live grants. Relaunch is explicit replacement through the shared conversion controller; design §3.1, §5.2, §6.2.
acceptance_criteria: From an ordinary tab's context menu a user reopens it caged in the same cwd; from the panel a changed grant offers a relaunch that says the process will be replaced.
notes:
Implemented explicit relaunch with updated profile through the shared controller: source terminal is reactivated, permissions reconfirmed, replacement created, transcript preserved, live grant never mutated.
Implementation complete; closure blocked only by prerequisite nocx-a0qhd.1.

title: The activity bar shows the active tab's grant
description:
A sandboxed tab can only state its policy through a hover tooltip today. `SidebarViewDescriptor` is scoped to the active tab by contract (`activeOrigin`), which is exactly this shape — Files, Ports, Git and Notes are all per-tab panels.

Shows backend, workspace, both root classes, HOME projections, and the denials seen in THIS tab. `ShieldIcon` already exists. The action stays in the palette: it opens a NEW tab, which is what `Local shell` next to it does.
design: Superseded shape: no separate sidebar grant view. Active grant/profile statistics live in the singleton Sandbox statistics tab opened by a distinct global activity-bar action; see design §6.
acceptance_criteria: With a sandboxed tab in front the panel names its grant; with an ordinary tab in front it says so plainly.
notes:
Implemented dedicated Sandbox statistics activity action and singleton tab. Source-tab grant/provenance and effective profile are backend-read; button retargets the singleton from each terminal.
Implementation complete; closure blocked only by prerequisite nocx-a0qhd.1.

title: A workspace carries a filesystem policy that its tabs inherit
description:
The default a sandboxed tab is minted with should come from its workspace, not from two global settings lists. `workspaces.payload` is already declared "sparse extension only", so the workspace half costs no schema change.

The pre-launch dialog changes shape with it: from "edit two global lists" to "here is what the workspace grants, here is how I narrow it once".
design: Approved design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-23-sandbox-command-statistics-and-workspace-profiles-design.md §3, §4, §7. One optional profile per named workspace in workspaces.payload; missing inherits standard whole; always confirm grant.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a sandboxed tab in a workspace with a policy needs no global list; the dialog shows what was inherited and what this launch narrows.
notes: Implemented one optional named-workspace sandbox profile in workspaces.payload with standard fallback, strict path validation, revisioned get/set/delete RPCs, stale-open gating, tests and profile editor.
close_reason: Closed

title: The agent policy's second scope lands in the label column and is squeezed
description:
Reported by the owner from first use (screenshot, 2026-08-21): in the Agent
policy matrix, the Observe row's first scope renders at full width while the
second is visibly narrower — a squeezed `path` select and a `/works` field
cut off mid-placeholder.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings → Agent policy.
2. On the Observe row, press `+ Scope` twice.
3. The first scope sits beside the decision select at full width; the second
   wraps to the next line under the effect label at 12rem and is squeezed.

CAUSE, read rather than guessed. `.st-policy__row` is a three-column grid
(`frontend/src/styles/surfaces/agent-policy.css:6`,
`grid-template-columns: 12rem minmax(8rem, 14rem) 1fr`), and the `<For>` over
the row's scopes (`frontend/src/agent-policy-section.tsx:121`) emits each
`.st-policy__scope` as a DIRECT CHILD of that grid. So the children flow into
cells: label, decision select, scope #1 — then scope #2 wraps into the next
grid row's FIRST column, which is the 12rem label column, and the add-scope
button takes the second. A third scope would land in the decision column.

Rows with no scopes look correct only because their third child is the button,
which is the one element the third column was sized for.

WHY IT IS THIS BUG AND NOT A WIDTH TWEAK: widening the first column would move
the squeeze rather than remove it, and the row would still put a scope under
the effect label — which reads as if that scope belonged to a different row.
The scopes and their add control are one group and must occupy one cell.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A row with three scopes renders all three at the same width as the first,
  under the decision select's column, never under the effect label.
- The effect label and the decision select stay in their own columns; adding
  or removing a scope does not move them.
- A row with no scopes still shows `+ Scope` beside the decision select.

title: [bug] The pre-commit gofumpt gate reports a permission error as a formatting failure, and the e2e container's output triggers it
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `e2e/run-in-container.sh` (or leave one running).
2. `git commit` anything.

Observed:

    FAIL: gofumpt — the following files need formatting:
    open .e2e/home: permission denied

    Pre-commit hook FAILED. Fix the issues above and try again.

No file needs formatting. The commit is refused until the developer works out
that the message is not about formatting and runs `sudo chown -R` over a
directory git is already ignoring.

## Root cause

`.githooks/pre-commit:113`:

    UNFMT=$(gofumpt -l . 2>&1) || true

`2>&1` folds stderr into the list of unformatted files, so any error gofumpt
prints becomes an entry in a list whose every line the hook then presents as "a
file that needs formatting". `|| true` discards the exit status that would have
told the difference.

The trigger is ordinary: the e2e container runs as root on a bind mount and
leaves `.e2e/home` root-owned with mode 0700. `.e2e/` is in `.gitignore`, but
`gofumpt -l .` walks the working tree rather than the index, so the ignore does
not reach it.

This is the shape nocx-z9s9.8 already recorded once — `eslint .` and
`prettier --check .` dying on EACCES against the same container's root-owned
output, where a crashing gate reported nothing and 19 lint errors accumulated
behind it. Here it fails loudly instead of silently, which is the better
direction, but it fails with a diagnosis that is not true.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gofumpt run that ERRORS is reported as an error, with its message, and is
  never presented as a list of files needing formatting. Separate the streams
  and read the exit status.
- The walk does not descend into the e2e container's output, so an ordinary
  container run does not block the next commit at all.
- The same reading applied to the other whole-tree gates in this hook, since
  the cause is the tree walk and not this one tool.
- A test or a scripted check that a hook run with an unreadable ignored
  directory present still passes.

title: [bug] The snippet body editor never wraps: a long line runs off the box instead of onto the next
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings -> Snippets -> New snippet.
2. Paste a paragraph with no newlines into Body.

Observed: one line running off the right edge, the box scrolling horizontally,
and the text clipped at the edges of the frame.
Expected: the line wraps at the box's width, the way a body of prose does.

## Root cause

`CMHost` (frontend/src/cm-host.ts) builds its CodeMirror view with no
`EditorView.lineWrapping`, and CodeMirror does not wrap by default. The only
place in the app that adds it is `src/editor.ts:342`, the command editor — so
the command line wraps and every other CodeMirror surface does not. That covers
the snippet body (`EditableHost`, snippets-settings.tsx) and notes
(`note-content.ts`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A line longer than the box wraps onto the next line in the snippet body; no
  horizontal scrollbar and no clipped text.
- Notes wrap too, or it is stated in the code why that surface wants otherwise —
  one decision about wrapping, not one per host.
- The command editor keeps the wrapping it already has, from one place rather
  than two.
- A test asserts the host mounts with wrapping on.
close_reason: EditorView.lineWrapping added to CMHost's editable bundle — it follows from the mode (prose), and the read-only modes deliberately keep lines unwrapped. Unit tests on both modes plus an e2e that types a paragraph into the real dialog and measures. Commit 9fc4cd8f.

title: [bug] Two hidden notices still occupy 48px at the head of the tab strip, and the macOS traffic-light inset is stale
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the app on macOS with no update pending and the socket connected.
2. Look at the gap between the traffic lights and the first control in the tab
   strip (the layers glyph).

Observed: the glyph starts ~137 CSS px from the window's left edge, while the
green light ends at ~59.5 — about 77px of empty chrome. Measured twice and they
agree: from the owner's screenshot (the red light is 24 device px wide, so the
scale is 2, and the glyph's left edge is at 275 device px), and in the container
against the real stylesheet.

## Root cause, and it is two things

FIRST, and it is most of the gap: `.tabbar`'s first two children are anonymous
wrappers around `.update-notice` and `.connection-notice`. Both notices carry
the `hidden` attribute, and both stylesheets declare `display: flex` on them —
which BEATS the UA stylesheet's `[hidden] { display: none }`. So neither notice
is hidden at all: each is an empty flex box wearing `padding: 0 12px`, and the
two of them own 48px of the row at all times. Measured in the container:

    children of .tabbar: "" @78 (w 24), "" @102 (w 24), .tabstrip-lead @126

SECOND: `--titlebar-inset-start: 78px` was calibrated for
`mac.TitleBarHiddenInset()`, which insets the traffic lights. 4c430dcf dropped
it for `mac.TitleBarHidden()` to fix nocx-dqg and touched only main.go — its own
message says "only the extra inset of the traffic lights is lost". The lights
moved left; the padding reserved for them did not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An element carrying `hidden` occupies no space, whatever `display` its
  component declares. Fixed once, where every component gets it, rather than per
  notice — the next component to pair `display:` with `hidden` must not be able
  to reintroduce this.
- The leading inset matches the traffic lights the app actually draws
  (`TitleBarHidden`: they end at ~59.5 CSS px), not the inset variant.
- Tests: the hidden notices take no width in the strip; the inset token is
  applied only under `data-platform='darwin'`.
close_reason: Two causes: [hidden] was beaten by display:flex on both notices (48px of permanent dead space on every platform), fixed once in base.css instead of a fourth local answer; and --titlebar-inset-start was still 78px from the TitleBarHiddenInset era, now 66px to match the lights the app actually draws. e2e measures both in a browser. Commit 1001353d.

title: [bug] The 'Previous session' boundary stays on screen when a program takes the pane
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a tab whose scrollback was restored from a previous session, so the
   `Previous session` rule is drawn above the restored blocks.
2. Run an alternate-buffer program in that pane (htop, an agent TUI, vim).

Observed: the blocks and the separator go, and the words PREVIOUS SESSION with
their rule stay painted over the program's screen.
Expected: the pane belongs to the program; nothing of the block chrome remains.

## Root cause

The alt-screen rule enumerates the child kinds it knew about when it was
written (frontend/src/style.css):

    .scrollback-inner.inner-fullscreen-mode > .cmd-block,
    .scrollback-inner.inner-fullscreen-mode > .scrollback-separator {
      display: none;
    }

`.scrollback-restore-boundary` was added later (nocx-m3fqk) as a third kind of
child of `.scrollback-inner`, and nothing added it to that list. A hide-list
that names what to hide has to be revisited by every future child, and this is
the first one that was not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Entering the alternate buffer hides the restore boundary along with the blocks
  and the separator; leaving it brings all three back.
- The live region (`.xterm-live-container`) stays visible — it is the thing the
  program draws into.
- The rule is written so a FOURTH kind of child is hidden by default rather than
  needing to be added to a list, because the failure being fixed is the list.
- A test asserts the boundary is not visible while the pane is in alt-screen.
close_reason: The alt-screen rule is an exclusion now (everything but .xterm-live-container) instead of a two-name hide-list the restore boundary was never added to. e2e in restore.spec.ts after a real restore, asserting visibility; green in chromium and webkit. Commit a0918a55.

title: ports-row-width guesses a port and hopes the listener started, so a busy port reads as a broken panel
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run e2e/ports-row-width.spec.ts when something already holds the port the
   spec happens to pick out of its hundred candidates.
2. The spec waits out its 30s timeout and reports:

   Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed
   Locator: locator('[data-testid="detected-row"]').filter({ hasText: '38228' })
   Error: element(s) not found

Observed on CI (ci-e2e webkit) on PR #100, whose diff touches only release
packaging, docs and scripts — nothing the ports panel can see. The same job had
passed on the same branch minutes earlier.

## Diagnosis

The spec started its fixture by typing a shell command and then waiting on the
UI, with nothing in between asserting the fixture existed:

    const port = 38200 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 100)
    await page.keyboard.type(`node -e '...listen(${port},"0.0.0.0")' &`)
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter')
    await expect(row).toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 })

Its comment claimed the randomness avoided colliding with a leaked listener from
a retried run. It does the opposite: a hundred candidates is a hundred ways to
land on a port something already holds. listen() then fails, node exits, and the
spec waits thirty seconds for a row that was never going to exist.

The failure text is identical for four different causes -- the panel is broken,
the port was taken, the keystrokes were dropped, or node never ran -- so the one
signal the spec produces cannot distinguish a product defect from its own setup
failing. That is the actual defect: not that it is flaky, but that it is
uninformative when it fails.

## Fix

Two changes, in e2e/ports-row-width.spec.ts:

- reserveFreePort() asks the kernel for a port via listen(0) and closes it. A
  port the kernel just handed out is free by construction; nothing is guessed.
- Before touching the panel, the spec polls until it can itself connect to the
  port. The test process shares the container's network namespace, so that is a
  direct observation rather than a proxy for one, and it is a state change
  rather than a duration (AGENTS.md: a test may not depend on timing).

A timeout after that point is the product's fault, which is the only thing that
makes a thirty-second wait worth having.

Verified: PW_PROJECTS=webkit e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/ports-row-width.spec.ts
-- 2 passed, the target test in 8.0s, layout measurement intact (sw=217 cw=217).
acceptance_criteria:
1. The spec never picks a port by guessing; the port comes from the kernel.
2. A run where the listener does not start fails with a message naming THAT,
   and does not spend its panel timeout on it.
3. The layout measurement the spec exists for (nocx-4wbx) is unchanged: the
   address element's scrollWidth <= clientWidth with the pointer away.
4. PW_PROJECTS=webkit e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/ports-row-width.spec.ts passes,
   and so does ci-e2e (webkit).
close_reason: Fixed and merged in #100. The port now comes from the kernel via listen(0) and the spec polls until it can connect to the listener before asking the panel anything, so a setup failure can no longer be reported as a panel failure. ci-e2e (webkit) green on the merged tree.

title: Containerized WebKit full suite has four sequence-dependent failures
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `./e2e/run-in-container.sh` on a warm e2e image/module cache.
2. Let Chromium and WebKit execute serially in the shared container stand.
3. Observe the final WebKit failures.

## Observed

On the merged PR91 integration tree the warm-cache run completed with 342 passed, 8 skipped, 4 failed. WebKit failures: backup-restore missed the download event; completion's graphify-output fixture returned `No matches`; focus-after-reorder had `uistate.set` refused `Control plane busy`; restore kept the active editor hidden. A first cold-cache run failed more broadly through devharness WSTOKEN timeouts, supporting a sequence/resource/shared-state symptom rather than four established product regressions.

title: The -R bind port for an ssh child is picked blind, so a live-sshd test fails on collision
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Run `internal/app`'s live-sshd suite enough times, or watch CI. Seen on
2026-08-20, PR #96, `ci-backend (with-secret-service)`:

    --- FAIL: TestLiveSshd_SSHChildAssembly_ChildEstablishesOverComposedLine (30.20s)
        ssh_child_assembly_test.go:602: timed out after 30s waiting for child
            domain Established via its own hello
        composed-line terminal:
            Warning: remote port forwarding failed for listen port 41046

`ci-backend (no-secret-service)` ran the same tests on the same commit and
passed, so it is not the change under test — PR #96 touches one CSS file and
two Playwright specs.

## Root cause

`internal/app/childdomain.go::randomPort` picks the `-R` remote bind as
`40000 + rand(20000)` and never checks that it is free. Its comment is honest
about the consequence — "a collision with an occupied remote port makes the
forward fail and the child fall back conventionally — the honest degrade" —
and that degrade is the RIGHT production behaviour.

The test is what has no answer to it. It asserts the non-degraded path (the
far shell's hello arrives over the reverse forward) and cannot force the
forward to succeed, so a collision is indistinguishable from a broken product
and reads as a 30-second timeout.

Two things make the collision likelier than "one in twenty thousand": Linux's
ephemeral port range is 32768–60999, which covers [40000, 60000) entirely, so
any outbound socket on the runner can be holding the port; and the package
grants several child domains in one run, each drawing again.

## What this is not

Not the timing-dependence AGENTS.md forbids — the test waits on an observable
state change, not a duration. A slower machine would not fix it and a faster
one would not hide it. It is a resource the test needs and does not reserve.
acceptance_criteria: The live-sshd child-assembly tests cannot fail from a bind-port collision: either the -R port is reserved before it is offered (bind, hold, hand the number over), or the test detects the refused forward from the terminal it already captures and reports THAT rather than a 30-second timeout. Demonstrated by occupying the port the run would pick and watching the suite say so.

title: A kit icon slot that does not size its svg is a lint failure
description:
The kit's icons are inline `<svg viewBox>` with no width/height of their own,
so the SLOT states the size. Twelve slots in the stylesheet need that rule and
eleven had it; the twelfth (`.ui-context-menu__icon`) shipped without one and
the glyph rendered at 0x0 in WebKit — every context menu in the packaged macOS
app had an empty icon column (nocx-8830c).

Nothing could have caught it short of a rendered browser: the element is in the
document either way and only its box is empty, so jsdom reports a healthy icon.
The e2e case added with the fix guards the context menu and nothing else; the
NEXT slot added to the kit will arrive with the same omission and the same
silence.

`frontend/lint-fixtures/check-css-integrity.mjs` is where this belongs — it
already reads the kit's identities out of `src/ui` and holds eleven rules of
this shape. The rule: a class that wraps an icon component in the kit's JSX
must have a companion `... svg { width; height }` (or size the svg some other
stated way, as `.ui-icon-button > svg` does). Needs a negative fixture, the way
`lint-fixtures/gate.sh` requires of every rule — the gate asserts all rules
fire.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run lint` in frontend/ fails on a kit icon slot with no svg sizing rule,
  and the fixture gate reports the new rule as fired.
- Removing `.ui-context-menu__icon svg` from context-menu.css makes it fail;
