title: SSH session reconnects when the connection is lost, with an ask/auto/never setting
description:
No bead covers this today. nocx-2ho.3 is closed and is the AD-9 byte-offset replay layer (WebSocket drop, backend session survives); nocx-bwzg is a bug about two reconnect subscribers on a live session. Neither is 'the SSH connection died, get it back'.

Surfaced by the file-manager design (.internal/specs/2026-08-01-file-manager-design.md, nocx-gglz), which CONSUMES this: a dropped session leaves the Files panel and its viewer tabs readable but unrefreshable, and they rebind on reconnect only when the attested endpoint matches. The file manager works without this bead — just with no way back — so this is a dependency in the product sense, not a blocking edge.
acceptance_criteria: When an SSH session's connection is lost (not a WebSocket drop — AD-9 already covers that), nocx surfaces it and offers to reconnect; a setting chooses ask / auto / never; a reconnect that succeeds reports the endpoint it actually reached (resolved host, port, principal, jump route) so consumers can tell whether it is the same filesystem. Tested with: connection lost mid-session, reconnect to the same endpoint, reconnect after the profile was edited to a different host.

title: Verify the focus-drift keystroke lands exactly once, in a real browser
description: Split out of EDITOR-W4 (nocx-87o) on 2026-08-01 after a worker diagnosed the code rather than assuming a defect. terminal-content.ts _globalKeydown has two redirect paths that LOOK inconsistent and are not. Block-selected: preventDefault + focus + insertText, exactly one char, deterministic, asserted in jsdom. Focus-drifted (body has focus): focus() only, NO preventDefault — the event target is fixed at dispatch so CM6 never sees the keydown, but the browser's native default action runs afterwards against the then-focused contentDOM and lands the character once via beforeinput. jsdom CANNOT observe this: it performs no native text insertion, so a zero there is a harness artifact and asserting it would encode a falsehood. Hence a real browser. IMPORTANT for whoever takes this: the naive 'make both paths call insertText' fix DOUBLES the drift character (native default plus programmatic insert). The binding spec's framing would have produced exactly that regression.
acceptance_criteria: In Playwright against the real build: with focus on body and the editor visible, one printable keystroke puts exactly ONE character in the editor document. Same for the block-selected path. Both assertions present — the second is what keeps the first from being 'fixed' into a doubling.
close_reason: e2e/keystroke-lands-once.spec.ts: both rescue paths assert exactly one character in a real browser; the doubling was confirmed by mutation probe and reverted. 14/14 chromium+webkit.

title: Remove graphify from the repo — index, skill, hooks and docs
description: Owner decision 2026-08-01. Measured over one design-and-review session: five graphify queries, zero answers — it returns symbol names ranked by graph proximity, truncated to a token budget, while every finding that mattered came from grep (blocks.ts:671's serializeRange call, which made an entire byte-stream output-capture mechanism unnecessary; the absent z-index:20 that three comments still claim exists). Cost: 91MB of generated output committed across 16 commits, a PreToolUse hook making a graph query mandatory before EVERY file read and grep, and workers regenerating it unasked — one dropped 326k lines into a diff under review, which is how the question got asked. Removed: graphify-out/, .claude/skills/graphify/, .claude/CLAUDE.md, both settings.json hooks, and references in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README.md, .gitignore. AGENTS.md keeps a Code search section recording the measurement so nobody reintroduces an index or a pre-read hook without beating the grep baseline.
acceptance_criteria: No graphify files tracked; no hook fires before a file read; the only remaining mention is the AGENTS.md record of the removal.
close_reason: Removed in 6ca29c4: graphify-out/ (48 tracked files, 91MB), .claude/skills/graphify/, .claude/CLAUDE.md, both PreToolUse hooks, and the references in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README.md and .gitignore. AGENTS.md gains a Code search section recording the measurement so the decision is not re-argued from scratch.

title: Reindex is an operation the size of years, and must not resurrect what was excluded
description: Design §5.2, §9.1. FTS corruption, a tokenizer upgrade, a schema migration or a change to the redaction rules all force a reindex of gigabytes of text. That needs: a schema version for the FTS projection separate from the main schema; a resumable rebuild with progress and cancel; a disk-space precondition; and search coverage that states the rebuild is in progress rather than answering as if complete. The trap worth naming, because it is silent: a reindex that re-derives from stored text can RESURRECT output previously excluded as sensitive. Exclusion must be recorded durably, not re-decided by re-running the matcher.
acceptance_criteria: Interrupt a rebuild at 40% and restart it: it resumes rather than restarting, and search says it is incomplete throughout. An artifact excluded from the index by a §9.1 decision is still excluded after a full reindex, without re-running the matcher.

title: An explicit target chip — never a magic prefix
description: Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §8.2, §8.3. ADR-0004 rejects magic prefixes in those words: 'an explicit command/agent switch plus a keyboard shortcut, never a magic prefix such as ? — prefixes collide with valid shell syntax'. It is right on the merits: > is redirection, / begins an absolute path, @ is valid in arguments. A visible target chip with a shortcut to cycle it, and the current target rendered at all times so Enter is never a surprise. And when the shell target is unavailable, Enter does NOT silently become an agent question — a surface that reinterprets a keystroke by rank has broken the contract that makes a terminal usable.
acceptance_criteria: The active target is visible before Enter. No prefix character changes the submission target. With the shell target unavailable, Enter does not submit to another target without explicit activation.

title: The editor surface is reachable when the shell cannot vouch for it
description: Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §8.1. Today shouldShowEditor(m.owned) ties the editor's existence to shell input ownership, so sshing to a box without our hooks removes the application's whole input surface. Three-way split: inline as today when the shell target is owned; reachable by a deliberate shortcut as an overlay in every other state; NEVER inline in alt-screen, where a persistent editor competes with vim and a debugger for keys and screen space. input-state.ts keeps its states, transitions and fail-open semantics untouched — what changes is who consumes owned. ADR-0004 §1 survives word for word.
acceptance_criteria: With no shell integration, the overlay is reachable by shortcut and no inline editor appears. In alt-screen the full viewport and raw keyboard behaviour are unchanged. PROMPT_READY behaviour is byte-identical to today.

title: Outcome annotation while typing
description: Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §10.3. 'This failed here twice; the variant that worked was ... REGION=eu', shown as you compose, scoped to the environment and saying which rung it means. This is the recall data rendered at composition time rather than only inside the ranker — showing it is cheaper than being subtle about it in the ordering.
acceptance_criteria: Composing a command that failed in this environment shows the count and the successor. The annotation names its scope. A command with no history shows nothing — the annotation is silent by default.

title: Passive context, always; confirmation only when the situation is unusual
description: Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §10.2. The affected facets appear next to the pending command — no modal, no keystroke, no interruption. Confirmation escalates only on criticality != routine, privilege elevated relative to the session norm, or a key facet at confidence=unknown.
acceptance_criteria: Local rm -rf node_modules in a routine environment: context shown, nothing blocked. The same command on an environment marked critical: confirmation required. Turning the passive display off is a setting; the escalation is not.

title: The terminal warns you where you are, before Enter
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §10.2, §10.3.

Most of a terminal's memory is spent showing you what already happened; the leverage is in what it can tell you while you can still change your mind.

The rule that keeps this from becoming wallpaper is the whole design: SHOW ALWAYS, CONFIRM RARELY. A guardrail that fires on the verb alone gets trained away within a week and then fails to fire on the one that mattered — which is exactly the failure mode of a generic 'are you sure?'. The escalation condition is not about the command, it is about where you are, and that is a sentence only a design with Environment can write.
acceptance_criteria: A destructive command in a routine environment with no elevated privilege shows the context and asks nothing. The same command with criticality=critical, or elevated privilege, or a key facet at confidence=unknown, requires confirmation. Both halves are tested — the first is what keeps the second effective.

title: A destructive-shape classifier over the composed text
description: Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §10.2. Recognise commands that destroy something — rm -rf, drop table, kubectl delete, terraform apply, redirection over a device. Runs on the composed text in the editor, where CM6 shell mode already parses it. It classifies shape only; it never decides whether to interrupt (that is the escalation rule).
acceptance_criteria: Known destructive shapes are recognised, including through a leading sudo and inside a simple pipeline. A false positive is a logged, tunable rule, not a code change.

title: History that remembers outcomes, not just text
description: Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §10.4, §3.4. If make deploy failed twice here and 'make deploy REGION=eu' is its successor that worked, recall offers the successor and annotates the failure. Frequency alone systematically promotes mistakes, because a command you got wrong three times is frequent. Needs the rerun-of/supersedes edges written when a user edits and re-runs, plus the outcome feature in the scorer.
acceptance_criteria: Given a failed command and its edited successor that succeeded, recall ranks the successor first and the failure carries its annotation. A command with no successor ranks unchanged.

title: Doubtful text is retained but not indexed, and 'forget this output' is the escape hatch
description: Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §9.1. When a matcher fires with low confidence the entry keeps its output and stays out of FTS — search that cannot find something is a smaller failure than search that surfaces a token by substring. And because rule-based redaction is allowed to be imperfect, a one-action 'forget this output' must exist: it drops the artifact and its index row in one transaction, and the entry survives.
acceptance_criteria: A low-confidence match retains the artifact and produces no FTS row. 'Forget this output' leaves the entry, removes the artifact, and leaves no index row behind — verified after a forced crash mid-operation.

title: do-not-record: a scope, not a vague promise
description: Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §9. Per-session, toggled from the surface, does not survive a restart, suppresses ledger.open and artifact capture together. A global default lives in settings as public config. The earlier design mentioned the mode three times and never said what it covered.
acceptance_criteria: With the mode on, no entry row and no artifact is created for that session. Restarting the app clears it. The global default is a setting, not a hardcoded constant.

title: command-ledger.ts becomes the live cache, not a second writer
description: Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §4.2, §6.2. The in-memory ledger stays as the frontend's render cache and ShellDriver's backing store. It must not grow its own path to the database, and it must never answer a recall query with its own ordering — ledger.query is the only ordering implementation, or the same keystroke returns different results depending on which tab it came from.
acceptance_criteria: grep shows exactly one caller path from the frontend to ledger.*. A recall query issued from two different tabs returns identically ordered results.

title: The file picker is native where the platform has one
description:
## Success Criteria

Wails v2.13 exposes runtime.OpenFileDialog(ctx, opts) (string, error) and runtime.OnFileDrop(ctx, cb) — both Go-side only, both returning absolute paths. The renderer reaches them through a new control-plane method rather than directly, per AD-1.

Path mode gets a chooser that yields a real absolute path. Where the runtime is absent — the dev-web harness has no Wails at all — the method reports itself unavailable and the surface falls back to what it does today: typing the path by hand, and reading contents in choose-file mode.

Drag-and-drop of a key file onto the connection editor is in scope if OnFileDrop is wired; say so if it is deferred.
acceptance_criteria: A control-plane method opens the native dialog and returns an absolute path; Path mode offers a chooser that uses it; the absence of the runtime is reported as unavailable rather than failing, and the surface degrades to manual entry; the method has a schema in contracts/.
close_reason: Landed in 758eed5

title: The Secrets page has no gutter and does not look like Connections
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Settings → Secrets with the vault unlocked and secrets present.

## Expected
The page reads like Connections: a pinned toolbar with a filter and the create action, rows below, and the same gutter.

## Actual
Content sits flush against the rail and rows run past the right edge. The page is declared scrollMode 'contained' — the mode for surfaces that own their own scrolling, like Connections — but unlike Connections it is not built on CollectionView, so it gets neither the page gutter nor a toolbar. The store name was also bare text running into the row's edge.
acceptance_criteria: Secrets is a CollectionView with a filter and the add action in the toolbar; the add action is present on an empty vault; a filter that matches nothing says so rather than claiming the vault is empty; the store is a Badge.
close_reason: Landed

title: Rotating a secret overwrites the name the user gave it
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Rename a secret on the Secrets page.
2. Rotate it (save a new password on the connection that owns it).

## Expected
The user's name survives, or the user is told it will not.

## Actual
Rotation writes a freshly generated user@host name over the one the user chose. Reported by the worker implementing ADR-0016.
acceptance_criteria: A generated name never replaces a user-supplied one; decide and record whether rotation carries the old name forward or asks.

title: vault.resetPreview undercounts secrets nothing references
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a secret on the Secrets page with no connection using it.
2. Settings → Vault → Reset the vault.

## Expected
The confirmation counts it among what will be destroyed.

## Actual
It is not counted. vaultreset builds its preview from CountSecretReferences, which walks credential records — and an ownerless secret has no reference to walk. Reported by the worker implementing ADR-0016, whose change is what made ownerless secrets possible.
acceptance_criteria: The reset preview counts records the vault holds, not only references the credentials carry; a secret with no owner appears in the confirmation.

title: A secret owns its name (ADR-0016)
description:
## Success Criteria

See docs/decisions/0016-a-secret-owns-its-name.md. The ADR reverses the secrets-and-vault design spec §4.1; this epic is the work it implies.

Deliberately out of scope: changing the SecretID grammar, accepting a name as an identifier from the renderer, and storing secret values anywhere but a provider.
acceptance_criteria: The vault persists a display name per SecretID and is its only owner; a password saved on a connection gets a generated name; the Secrets page can add a secret with no connection using it, and rename one; a secret whose name did not land still renders, never blank and never as its id; '+ New Credential' is gone from the connection editor while selecting an existing credential remains; the design spec's 'No display name' clause is amended to point at ADR-0016.
close_reason:
ADR-0016 shipped; the epic was never told. All six acceptance criteria verified in code on 2026-08-25:

1. The vault persists a display name per SecretID and owns it: vault.SecretMeta{Name,Kind} (internal/vault/meta.go:18), persisted as Document.Secrets []SecretRecord (internal/vault/document.go:28), written only through setRecordLocked / RenameSecret (vault.go:1135, 1505) — one path, as the ADR's cost section demands.
2. A password saved on a connection gets a generated name: connections.tsx:2634 secretNameFor(...) feeds savePassword; the same at :717 and :1644 for key material.
3. The Secrets page adds and renames: frontend/src/secrets.tsx createSecret (:333) and renameSecret (:408), covered by secrets.test.tsx 'adds a secret by name and kind' (:417), 'renames a secret by its row handle' (:465) and 'renders a secret with no connection using it' (:504) — that last one is the state the ADR says was previously unreachable, so it is the epic's happy path under rule 2.
4. A nameless secret still renders: deriveLabel where an owner exists (inventory.go:269), kindLabel otherwise (meta.go:47) — never blank, never the SecretID.
5. '+ New Credential' is gone from the connection editor, asserted absent by connections.behavior.test.tsx:843 together with the creation form.
6. The design specs are amended: secrets-and-vault-surfaces-design.md:172, :183 and :306 point at ADR-0016; vault-storage-backend-design.md:157 and its section 10 do the same.

Closed with zero children on purpose: the work landed through nocx-9ib6 and the Secrets-page wave, which is why it never appeared in bd ready. Remaining hangover stays as standalone bugs (nocx-fyyf, nocx-gqzg, nocx-cx03, and nocx-25k9.21 under its own epic), per the AGENTS.md rule that a bug arriving from nowhere gets no parent.

title: The dialog sizes to the section it is showing, and the change is animated
description:
## Success Criteria

Tabs stops sizing its panel box to the tallest section and sizes it to the active one, so the New Group dialog's General section no longer sits in a box measured for Connection-with-Paste-key and the footer no longer floats hundreds of pixels below the last field. The panel height animates between sizes so the footer moves visibly rather than teleporting, and the animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

This reverses the sizing half of the Tabs decision recorded in ui/README.md ("every section is rendered into one grid cell, so the box is the size of the largest"). That decision traded emptiness for stability; the animation buys the stability back without the emptiness, so the README section must be rewritten rather than merely contradicted.

## Constraint that decides the technique

Transitioning to and from height:auto needs interpolate-size/calc-size, which is above both declared browser floors (WebKitGTK 2.40, Safari 16.2 — ADR-0013 §3). So the animation is measure-and-transition in JS: read the current height, pin it, set the target, transition, release to auto on transitionend. Dialog already owns the panel and its max-height, so it is the right place for it — not the surface.
acceptance_criteria: Switching sections or auth methods leaves no empty space below the footer; the panel height transitions rather than jumping; prefers-reduced-motion disables the transition; the panel never exceeds its viewport max-height mid-animation; ui/README.md's Tabs sizing section states the new trade.
close_reason: Landed in 3c952d2

title: A dialog names its width but not its height, so revealing a field moves the footer
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Connections → New connection → Authentication.
2. Choose Public Key.

## Expected
The dialog does not change size.

## Actual
It grows: Public Key reveals a Path/Choose file/Paste key control and a field under it, and the footer buttons move down from under the pointer reaching for them. Tabs measures its sections so switching General/Authentication/Advanced is stable, but a control changing what its own section renders is outside that guarantee. The panel names its width via data-size and left its height to the content.
acceptance_criteria: The lg panel names a min-height bounded by its existing viewport max-height; choosing any auth method leaves the panel the same size.
close_reason: Landed

title: Copying a one-time recovery code reports nothing, including when it fails
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set up vault protection.
2. On the recovery-code step, press Copy.

## Expected
The user knows whether the code reached the clipboard.

## Actual
Nothing is shown. Both copy handlers swallow the rejection — one with a bare catch, one with an empty rejection arm — so a denied or unavailable clipboard is indistinguishable from a successful copy. The code is shown exactly once, so the user presses Done believing it is saved and it is gone for good.
acceptance_criteria: Both copy handlers report success and failure; the failure message says to write the code down before closing; tests cover both outcomes.
close_reason: Landed

title: Diagnostics rows touch, and Secrets floats a description line above every state
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Settings → Vault → expand Diagnostics.
2. Settings → Secrets with the vault locked.

## Expected
Diagnostics rows are spaced like every other row group on the page. The locked Secrets page shows a locked state and one action.

## Actual
The diagnostics rows are a bare div, so nothing spaces them and they sit flush against each other. The Secrets page draws a standing line of body copy above every state, so a locked vault shows a paragraph with no heading over it and a centred plate floating below — contradicting the surface spec's own rule for the sealed state.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostics rows are spaced by the Stack primitive; the Secrets explanation is the Secrets section's description and does not appear in the locked or empty states.
close_reason: Landed in b25db08

title: Every JSON-RPC method the renderer calls has a contract in contracts/
description:
## Success Criteria

Filled in as methods are touched, not in one sweep — the rule in AGENTS.md is that a method you add or change gets its contract in the same commit. This epic exists so the remaining surface is visible and can be swept once the touch-driven pass stops finding new ones.

vault.status landed with nocx-nfld.5, together with the Go and TypeScript harnesses both sides reuse.
acceptance_criteria: Every vault.*, profiles.*, settings.* and connection.* method the renderer calls has a fully-populated sample in contracts/, a Go shape test and a TypeScript key-list test; a method added or changed without one fails review. Deliberately out of scope: the binary data plane, which has no JSON shape to pin.

title: Diagnostics states values as badges at readable size, not fine print
acceptance_criteria: Badge gains a success tone; every diagnostics value is a Badge; the block is not set in a smaller type size than the page.
close_reason: Landed in 13d6ea9

title: Test reports what it found, instead of quietly stamping a timestamp
acceptance_criteria: Pressing Test raises a toast naming the store and its result; the timestamp stays as the record of when.
close_reason: Landed in 13d6ea9

title: The Secrets page anchors its locked and empty states instead of floating them
acceptance_criteria: EmptyState takes an optional icon and fills the height it is given; the Secrets rows are built from kit components rather than .sr-row markup with emoji.

title: The backend's log is written into a mktemp dir nothing surfaces
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. `make dev-web > somewhere.log 2>&1`
2. Exercise anything that logs on the backend — unseal the vault, save a secret.
3. Read somewhere.log. It contains vite's output and not one line from the Go process.

## Why

scripts/dev-web.sh:115 runs the backend as `"$work/devharness" >"$work/backend.log" 2>&1`
where `$work` is a `mktemp -d`. Nothing prints that path, so capturing the script's own
output captures vite and nothing else.

## Cost

Several hours of one night. Diagnosing nocx-25k9.20 proceeded entirely by elimination —
ruling out a race, a stale frontend status, the idle timer, a second vault instance — while
the answer sat in that file the whole time, one WARN line:

    msg="provider put failed" provider=file error="vault is sealed"

which names the culprit immediately.
acceptance_criteria: make dev-web prints where the backend log is, or tees it to a stable path. A developer can read the backend's own INFO and WARN output without first reading scripts/dev-web.sh.

title: Every vault.status call writes to the OS keychain, though the spec says probe once
description:
Found while verifying a worker's caveat about the new "Test" button on the Vault page. The
worker reported that it could only wire Test to a status refresh because no re-probe RPC
exists, and worried the button therefore does nothing. The opposite is true, and that is the
defect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Settings -> Vault. The page fetches vault.status on mount and after every operation.
2. Each fetch reaches system.Provider.Status(), which delegates straight to Probe()
   (internal/vault/system/system.go:122-124).
3. Probe() writes a random entry into the OS keychain, reads it back, compares the bytes and
   deletes it (:128 onward) — a real write per call, every call.

## Why it matters

- The spec is explicit and the code does not follow it. Vault design 5.7: the probe's
  "outcome is cached for the process lifetime with an explicit re-probe action". There is no
  cache and no re-probe action; there is only an unconditional probe on every status read.
- On macOS a keychain write can raise an OS authorisation prompt. A settings page that
  probes on mount can therefore prompt the user for merely opening it.
- A failed delete leaves an artifact. The spec accepts that as the price of a truthful probe
  ("preferable to a false positive") — but it accepted it for an occasional probe, not for
  one per page render.

## The two halves are linked, so fix them together

Adding the cache without an explicit re-probe RPC breaks the Test button, which is honest
today precisely BECAUSE nothing is cached. So: cache the outcome for the process lifetime,
add the re-probe method the spec already assumes, and point Test at it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two vault.status calls in a row perform exactly one probe — asserted with a fake keyring
  that counts Set calls.
- An explicit re-probe path exists, is what the Vault page's Test button calls, and a test
  asserts it does perform a fresh probe.
- The cached outcome is invalidated when the process would otherwise report stale readiness
  after a store's state changed — state which case you chose and why, in the code.

title: The Tabs status marker distinguishes states by colour alone
description:
Found reviewing the worker diff for nocx-0v7z before merging it. The mechanism is right and
the screen-reader half is correct; the sighted-but-colour-blind half is missing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Render a vertical Tabs with three items whose statuses are ok, warning and error.
2. View it with a red-green colour vision deficiency (or desaturate the screenshot).
3. The three rows are indistinguishable.

## Why it happens

`styles/components/tabs.css` gives `.ui-tabs__status` an 8px circle whose ONLY difference
between tones is `background`: `--color-success` / `--color-warning` / `--color-danger`. The
accessible name is handled properly — a `.ui-visually-hidden` span inside the row's Button —
so assistive technology is fine. A sighted user who cannot separate those hues has nothing
else to go on.

That matters here more than it usually would. The marker exists so the broken store can be
spotted WITHOUT selecting its row (the Vault page's store rail, spec §7). Selecting the row
shows the state in words — which is exactly the step the marker is supposed to save.

WCAG 1.4.1: colour must not be the only visual means of conveying information.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The three tones differ by something other than hue — a glyph, a shape, or a fill pattern —
  and a test asserts the distinguishing attribute reaches the DOM per tone.
- The `.ui-visually-hidden` accessible name stays as it is; this bead does not change it.
- The kit README's Tabs row records how tones are distinguished, so the next variance does
  not reintroduce colour-only.

title: Quick connect sits 80px narrower than its own dialog
description:
Reported from the running app: the quick-connect palette's filter field and rows
stop well short of the dialog's right edge, leaving a band of dead space beside
them.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the quick-connect palette (the connection picker).
2. The panel's border is at one width; the search field and every row end ~80px
   before it.

## Why it happens

Two owners for one dimension, which is the exact thing dialog.css:32-38 forbids in
words: "The size prop names the width; the content never gets a say."

- dialog.css:86 — `.nocx-dialog__panel[data-size='lg'] { width: 640px }`
- quick-connect.css — `.quick-connect { width: 512px }`

640 minus 24px of panel padding on each side is a 592px content box; the palette
declared 512. The stale comment above the dialog rule preserves the history: it
still describes the content as "512px + the 24px padding on each side", i.e. a
560px panel. Someone widened the panel to 640 and neither the content width nor
the comment followed.

## Fix

quick-connect.css stops naming a width (`width: 100%`), and the comment on the
dialog rule now says the number is declared there and only there. The fixed
HEIGHT stays: it is what keeps rows from moving under the pointer while filtering,
and that argument is about the list, not the panel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No stylesheet outside dialog.css declares a width for a Dialog's content at
  any size.
- The quick-connect filter field and its rows span the dialog's full content box.
- Verified in the running app, not only by reading the rule.

title: The settings-page gate names Vault instead of walking the page registry
description:
Follow-up from nocx-d3mr, recorded because I accepted a weaker gate than the brief asked for rather than closing over it.

The brief required a test that walks the registered settings pages, so that a NEW page opting out fails it. What landed in 7272280 (frontend/src/settings.test.ts) is two tests: one mounts the generated pages, one mounts VaultSection by name. A page added tomorrow is not covered by either.

Why this is P2 and not P1: after nocx-d3mr the protection lives in the DEFAULT — a horizontal Field is primary unless a caller explicitly passes labelProminence='secondary', and no surface passes it. So the gate guards against a deliberate opt-out, not against forgetting, and forgetting was the original failure mode.

Cost to do it properly: the component pages need clients (ProfileClient, VaultClient, VaultController), so the test needs the same mock scaffolding settings.test.ts already builds for VaultSection, applied over the registry instead of one name.

title: You cannot see what the vault holds
description:
Asked by the user looking at the Vault page: "how do I even see what is in my
vault?" There is no answer in the product today.

The transport exposes nine vault methods (internal/transport/ws_vault.go:112-128):
status, setup, unseal, seal, changePassphrase, regenerateRecovery,
setDefaultProvider, setAutoSeal, activity. None of them enumerates what is stored.

The closest thing that exists is `credentials.list` + `credentials.hasPassword`
(frontend/src/profiles.ts:397,417), on a different page, answering a different
question: which credential records exist, and whether each has a password. That is
a view of the credential list, not an inventory of the vault — it cannot show a
secret held for a profile that no longer exists, which is exactly what nocx-2x8x
(orphan collection) is about.

## What this is not

Not a request to reveal secrets. Reading a secret back in plaintext was ruled out
deliberately (nocx-ggja verified "no Reveal or plaintext read-back path anywhere").
The inventory is metadata only: what is held, for what, in which provider, when it
was written.

## Open question for whoever picks this up

Whether this belongs on the Vault page or on Credentials is a product decision, not
an implementation detail. The Vault page currently shows plumbing — default
provider, per-provider Writable/Not ready badges — which is a maintainer's view of
the subsystem. An inventory is the first thing on that page that would answer a
user's question rather than an implementer's.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can see, without leaving the app, what the vault holds: one row per stored
  secret with what it belongs to, which provider holds it, and when it was written.
- Nothing in the path returns or renders a secret value.
- The list distinguishes a secret whose owner still exists from one whose owner does
  not, so an orphan is visible rather than inferred (see nocx-2x8x).
- A test walks the path a user walks: from an empty vault, save a secret, and assert
  the row appears with the right owner and provider.
notes:
CORRECTION to my own acceptance criteria, found in the KB check before any work started: the criterion 'the list distinguishes a secret whose owner still exists from one whose owner does not' is NOT achievable as written.

internal/vault/provider.go:16-28 — Provider is ID/Status/Get, WritableProvider adds Put/Delete. There is no List anywhere. And per the stored memory constraint-nocx-secrets-zalando-go-keyring-v0-2, zalando/go-keyring v0.2.8 exposes exactly Set, Get, Delete and DeleteAll — the system provider CANNOT enumerate what it holds, at any level.

Spec 4.1 is the reason it is not merely missing: a vault catalogue document mapping SecretID to provider/name/kind/timestamps was proposed in the first draft and killed in peer review on three counts (two persisted owners for name and kind, the all-or-nothing metadata guarantee from nocx-y910.1, a third crash gap per write). SecretID is deliberately 'not promoted into a durable user-facing entry identity'.

So an inventory must be DERIVED from metadata that already exists (credentials.list + hasPassword, profiles holding references), not read from the providers. That view can show everything a user owns; it cannot show an orphan, because an orphan is by definition the thing metadata no longer names. Orphans stay nocx-dm0's problem and would need a List capability on the file provider plus an accepted blind spot on system.

title: The file provider tells you to unlock a login keychain it never uses
description:
On the Vault page the `file` provider renders: "Your login keychain is locked.
Unlock it and try again." The file provider is nocx's own encrypted blob. It has
no login keychain, so the remedy named is not merely unhelpful — it is impossible
to act on, and it sends the user to an OS dialog that cannot change anything.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings → Vault with an uninitialized (or sealed) vault.
2. Providers section, row `file`: badges "Writable" + "Not ready", message
   "Your login keychain is locked. Unlock it and try again."

## Why it happens

internal/vault/file/file.go:62-69 — `Status` returns
`vault.Status{Ready: false, Reason: vault.ReasonLocked}` whenever `p.dataKey == nil`,
i.e. whenever the vault is sealed or not yet set up.

frontend/src/vault.tsx:35 — `REASON_MESSAGES.locked` is written for the OS keyring:
"Your login keychain is locked. Unlock it and try again."

So one reason code is carrying two unrelated meanings — "the OS keychain is locked"
and "this vault is sealed" — and the UI prints the first for both. The truthful
sentence for `file` is that the vault is sealed and unsealing it is the remedy,
which is a different action in a different place.

## Relationship to nocx-25k9.6

Same family, different instance, and they must not be merged: 25k9.6 is the SYSTEM
provider's probe classifying a locked collection as no-service. This one is the FILE
provider borrowing a keychain-specific message for an unrelated state. 25k9.6 is
being worked now; whoever takes this should expect to touch the same message map and
coordinate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The `file` provider's not-ready state is distinguishable from an OS-keyring lock:
  either a reason of its own or a provider-aware message, decided deliberately.
- The rendered sentence for a not-ready `file` provider names an action the user can
  actually take on this machine, and a test pins the sentence to the state.
- No reason code carries two meanings: a test asserts each Reason maps to exactly
  one user-facing remedy, per provider.
notes:
Widened after an independent review (codex) and my own verification: this is a LAYERING defect, not a wording one, and it has three faces.

1. provider.go:9-10 states the contract in words: a Provider 'knows nothing about sealing, routing or policy'. The file provider knows about all three — file.go:192 has its own Lock(), Get/Put return ErrVaultSealed, and Status() reports the vault's seal as its own unavailability. The implementation contradicts the interface's own doc comment.

2. file.go:117-141 — when no blob exists yet, Unlock deliberately starts empty and the doc comment says the provider is 'ready to accept writes; the first mutation creates the blob lazily'. But dataKey stays nil, so Status() (file.go:62-69) reports Ready=false Reason=locked for exactly that state. The comment and the status disagree about the same moment.

3. provider.go:42 puts ReasonUnknownProvider in the same enum. That is not a status a registered provider can ever report — it is a reference-ROUTING failure. Registry state, external-service health and vault lifecycle are collapsed into one bag of strings.

Suggested shape rather than a patch: separate provider availability (available/unavailable/unknown + why) from vault lifecycle (uninitialized/sealed/unsealed) from reference-resolution errors (unknown-provider/secret-missing/corrupt-store). The spec justified the binary Ready on the grounds that CI cannot exercise a third value (design doc 269-274); that is a testability argument erasing a distinction that drives different user remedies, and it is what produced the impossible 'unlock your login keychain' advice.
close_reason:
Landed in f2c41f5. file.Provider.Status() probes the document store and answers about it; a sealed vault with a readable store is Ready. ReasonUnknownProvider left the provider Reason enum for vault.go as a routing error, wire value unchanged so the renderer mapping still resolves. go test -race ./internal/vault/... green including the invariant this could have broken — a sealed vault still refuses Get/Put/Delete, proven by test.

ACCEPTED WITH A KNOWN WART, recorded rather than closed over: any docs.Read error is reported as ReasonDenied, which overclaims — a corrupt document and an I/O failure are not access denials. There is no store-level reason in the current vocabulary to say it honestly, which is precisely the wider split the design asks for (spec §5, and codex's four-way separation of provider availability / vault lifecycle / reference-resolution errors). Fix it there, not by adding one more string here.

Second wart: Status now reads and parses the whole blob under p.mu on every call, where it used to be an in-memory check. Harmless at today's call rate, wasteful at any scale.

title: Probe reports no-service when the Secret Service is running but its collection is unusable
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Found by accident while verifying nocx-25k9.2 with a deliberately incomplete recipe:

    nix-shell -p gnome-keyring dbus --run 'dbus-run-session -- bash -c "echo -n test | gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock; go test ./internal/vault/system/ -run TestRealKeyring -v"'

That starts the daemon and registers org.freedesktop.secrets but never creates a usable login collection. Result:

- SecretServiceAvailable() returns TRUE — the D-Bus name has an owner — so the integration test runs instead of skipping.
- Probe() then fails its write and reports Ready=false, Reason="no-service".

Both halves are wrong in a way that matters.

## Why it matters

The reason codes exist so the UI can offer the right remedy. 'no-service' tells the user to install and start a keyring they demonstrably already have running; the truthful answers are 'locked' or 'denied'. This is precisely the misdiagnosis the machine-readable discriminator was introduced to prevent, so it is worth fixing even though it is not release-blocking.

Secondly, the guard and the probe disagree about what available means. The test skips on SecretServiceAvailable and asserts on Probe, so a half-working store produces a FAILING test rather than a skipped one — noise that looks like a real regression.

## Note for whoever picks this up

The full CI recipe (gnome-keyring-daemon --daemonize --login, then --unlock) works and the integration test passes all seven subtests against it. This bug is only about the partial state, which is a realistic thing to hit on a user machine — a running daemon with a locked or missing collection.
acceptance_criteria: With a Secret Service whose bus name is owned but whose collection cannot be written, Probe reports a reason distinguishable from 'no service at all' — locked or denied, not no-service. SecretServiceAvailable and Probe agree on what 'available' means, or the integration test guards on the one it asserts against, so a half-working store makes the test skip rather than fail.
notes:
Reproduced against a real locked collection on 2026-07-30, and the reproduction is not reliable — both facts matter.

Recipe (probe = a tiny main calling system.New().Probe):
  nix-shell -p gnome-keyring dbus --run 'dbus-run-session -- bash -c "
    eval $(echo -n nocx-ci | gnome-keyring-daemon --daemonize --login)
    echo -n nocx-ci | gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock
    <probe>                # READY=true REASON=""
    dbus-send --session --dest=org.freedesktop.secrets --print-reply --type=method_call \
      /org/freedesktop/secrets org.freedesktop.Secret.Service.Lock \
      array:objpath:/org/freedesktop/secrets/collection/login
    <probe>                # READY=false REASON="no-service"   <-- the defect
  "'

So a locked collection is reported as 'no system keyring available' and the user is told to invent a master passphrase instead of being told to unlock their login keychain.

On a second attempt the same recipe gave READY=true after the Lock: a daemon started with --login holds the password and re-unlocks on the next access. Any test built on this needs a daemon that cannot self-unlock, or the arrangement will pass by accident.

Note also that classifyReason (internal/vault/system/system.go:282) guesses from error text — strings.Contains(s, "locked"). The raw error for the locked case was never captured, because the run that reproduced the defect did not print it and the run that printed it did not reproduce. Fixing the classifier against a string nobody has seen would be guesswork; the robust alternative is to read the collection's Locked property over D-Bus rather than infer it, which is a real dependency decision and should be made deliberately.
close_reason: Reason is now observed over D-Bus rather than guessed from go-keyring's error text. Verified against a real gnome-keyring: locking the login collection turns READY=false REASON="no-service" into REASON="locked", and SecretServiceAvailable now means usable so the integration test skips instead of failing. Confirmed the stricter guard does NOT make Linux CI skip: under the full CI recipe AVAILABLE=true and both TestRealKeyring tests run and pass.

title: Two app instances would silently lose each other's writes, and not only in the vault
description:
Raised by the vault core review but NOT vault-specific, so it is filed outside that epic.

Every DocumentStore consumer loads its document once into memory and later writes the whole thing back atomically. Atomic rename prevents a torn file; it does not prevent last-writer-wins loss between two processes. profiles.json has had this property since it was written — the vault simply makes the consequence sharper, because losing a journal entry or a key envelope is not the same as losing a profile edit.

A second app instance is not exotic: a user double-launches, or a stale process survives a crash. Wails runs one backend per process, so two instances are two writers.

Options, in rough order of cost: document the invariant and add a startup check that detects an existing instance and refuses or hands off; or take an inter-process lock over the config directory for the lifetime of the process; or accept it explicitly and say so in the ADR. What is not acceptable is the current state, where the behaviour is undefined and undocumented.
acceptance_criteria: Either the single-backend-process invariant is documented and enforced with a startup check that refuses or defers to an existing instance, or an inter-process lock guards the config directory. Whichever is chosen is written down and covered by a test.
notes: Backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh: moved from in_progress (untouched since 2026-08-01) back to open. Partially addressed under a DIFFERENT bead and not for this store: internal/coordinator/lock.go acquireLock returns ErrAlreadyRunning for the coordinator RUNTIME dir (tested at coordinator_test.go:537), not for the config dir this bead names. The tree still records the defect as live: internal/storage/appdir.go:44 says two instances still overwrite each other's writes because every DocumentStore consumer loads its document once and writes the whole thing back, naming this bead, and calls a per-run state directory the next step. Still missing: the documented invariant (no single-instance or last-writer-wins statement in docs/architecture.md or docs/decisions/) and any test tying a lock to the config directory.

title: Step 7: spec self-review (placeholders, consistency, scope, ambiguity)
close_reason: Self-review found five under-specified points, all fixed inline: how the ctx-free SecretStore supplies a ctx to providers; that passphrase/recovery envelopes exist only once created; what unseal actually looks like on a keychain machine (one click, no prompt); that the sealed visibility rule is realised in V2 while V1 ships only the backend refusal; and that a locked system store reports 'unavailable' rather than earning an untestable third Status value. No placeholders, no contradictions found.

title: Step 9: optional stress-test if selected at the spec gate

It overturned four positions: the vault catalogue (second metadata owner, and a second document breaks AtomicImport), the dropped journal (ADR-0011 §4 requires one), Set vs a Vault-owned Create, and two overclaimed guarantees (ctx cannot cancel a go-keyring call; seal cannot revoke an already-issued Secret). It also surfaced the open Reveal-vs-ADR-0011-§2 question. Spec revised and committed at 79f06a6.

title: Names and minted ids have no length cap
description:
slugify (profile.go:775-789) is allow-list-by-construction - it lowercases and keeps [a-z0-9_-], replacing everything else with a dash - so "../../etc" becomes "-----etc" and traversal through an id is not reachable. Confirmed separately that no renderer string reaches any filepath.Join in internal/: documentStore joins only its own fixed name (storage/document.go:111) and profiles, groups and credentials all live in one JSON document (store.go:93-97).

What is missing is a length cap. A 10 MB name yields a 10 MB id through NewProfileID (profile.go:745), NewGroupID (profile.go:755) and NewCredentialID (credential.go:194). No Name field has a length or charset check anywhere, and the ids are stored, exported, and echoed back.

Filed as a task rather than a bug: nothing is exploitable today, the store is the only consumer, and the fix belongs with whatever nocx-98rn establishes.

## Acceptance Criteria

Name and id length are capped at the point they are minted and at the point they are accepted, with a test at the boundary. The cap is one constant, not one per call site.
close_reason: Review fix: bounded slugify again applies Unicode lowercase semantics before the ASCII allowlist; spec and regression coverage updated.

title: Three smaller unvalidated inputs: keyPath, empty host, unowned ack
description:
Three smaller holes found in the same audit, grouped because each is a couple of lines and they share a fix shape.

1. keyPath reaches os.ReadFile with no restriction. credentials.create/update accept it verbatim (ws.go:1383, ws.go:1481); it flows cred.KeyPath -> cfg.KeyFile (connection/resolver.go:185) -> resolved.identityFile (ssh_config.go:76-78) -> os.ReadFile (ssh_auth.go:193), with only ~/ expanded. connections.test then reports the outcome, which makes it a file-existence and parse oracle over the filesystem.

2. profiles.create stores a profile with an empty host. ws.go:1194-1223 goes from json.Unmarshal to JSONStore.CreateProfile, which checks only that the id is non-empty (store.go:164-167). ProfileService.SaveProfile:70 does require a host and is not reachable from this method.

3. ack does not check the session belongs to the connection (ws.go:1003-1021), unlike resize and close which do.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a credential with keyPath /etc/shadow and run connections.test; the error text distinguishes "cannot read" from "not a key".
2. Call profiles.create with no host; the profile is stored and appears in the list.
3. Call ack with another connection's sessionId.

## Acceptance Criteria

Each of the three has a test that fails without its fix. keyPath is either constrained to a base directory or the failure text stops distinguishing cases; profiles.create requires a host on the same path SaveProfile does; ack checks connection ownership the way resize does.
close_reason: Review fix: ack authorization now requires the current session subscriber, not historical connState membership; reattach regression proves stale-owner ack rejection.

title: The rollout has a surface that shows what is true
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Staging a candidate, choosing a canary, watching a rollout, and the three transitions are
  reachable from the Credentials section.
- Per-endpoint status distinguishes accepted, rejected, unreachable, host-key problem and
  needs-interactive — the taxonomy the probe already returns. Do not invent a second one.
- The blast radius of a transition is shown before it is applied, the way group changes do
  (nocx-uxs5.11). Emergency revoke closes live transports; that must not be a single
  unqualified button.
- Rollout status is operational evidence, not profile configuration. It reads as a run that
  happened, not as settings.
- Accessibility is acceptance criteria: destructive confirmations announced, focus restored.

## Deliberately out

Anything that starts a real rollout without the user asking for it.
close_reason: Rollout surface in credentials section: staging, canary, run, per-endpoint taxonomy with exclusions and not-attempted apart, impact preview before every destructive transition. Coordinator repaired a broken Dialog tag and an invalid role=list.

title: Save as connection adopts an external host
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

Spec section 4.

- After connecting to an alias that came from ~/.ssh/config, the user can save it as a nocx
  connection.
- The saved profile stores the ALIAS, not the resolved hostname — the point is to keep
  following the live source, not to freeze one evaluation of it.
- Once saved, the system duplicate is suppressed (the rule from the palette bead).
close_reason: Save as connection stores the ALIAS, not the resolved hostname, so the adopted profile keeps following the live config and the palette's suppression — which compares alias to profile host — removes the system entry for free. user and port are carried only when the config supplied them. Coordinator fixed three things at integration: the renderer minted a profile id again (nocx-uxs5.10 removed that; the backend mints on profiles.create), the caller discarded the returned record and logged an empty id, and a restored test asserted the old minting behaviour. The report also claimed to have fixed a broken alias session path; the branch shows the path was sound and the actual change was port plumbing.

title: A terminal hint offers the alias the user is typing
description:
## Scope, and its honest limit

Spec section 4. The hint is FRONTEND-only. AD-6 forbids the backend interpreting the byte
stream, so it cannot be built there.

nocx knows the command text only while its own command editor owns input — submission runs
through ShellInputTarget (terminal-content.ts). In raw terminal mode it does not: OSC 133
marks prompt and command boundaries but does not expose the shell current editable line, and
reconstructing `ssh <host>` from keystrokes is unreliable because history, completion, cursor
movement and pasted control sequences are handled remotely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Typing `ssh <partial>` in the nocx command editor offers matching aliases.
- Raw terminal mode is NOT promised. Do not attempt it; supporting arbitrary native shell
  input needs cooperating shell integration (AD-5 Tier B) and is a separate decision.
- The limit is visible to the user rather than felt as flakiness.
close_reason: Typing ssh <partial> in the nocx command editor offers matching aliases, fetched live per keystroke generation with stale-response gating — no cached snapshot, so the hint cannot go stale behind the palette. Raw mode degrades transparently. Coordinator rewired it onto the shared contract: the worker built its own SSHConfigAlias types and listSSHConfigAliases method in profiles.ts despite the brief giving that ownership to the palette worker, so there were briefly two client methods for one RPC. Its private wildcard filter was deleted rather than renamed — the backend already excludes patterns in containsWildcard, and the two copies had already drifted, the frontend regex covering brackets and braces while missing '!'. 994 tests.

title: Aliases from ~/.ssh/config are a live source in the quick-connect palette
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

Spec section 4.

- Aliases appear in the quick-connect palette as a LIVE, read-only source — never copied.
- They do NOT appear in the connection manager, which lists only nocx-owned records, so an
  empty manager honestly means "you have not saved any connections".
- **Priority is ours**: when a saved profile targets the same alias, the system duplicate is
  not offered. Alias identity must be defined precisely and in one place — a profile named
  differently but pointing at the same alias is the same target and must also suppress the
  duplicate. Write that rule down where it is enforced, not in two places.
- The source is visibly distinguishable from a saved connection, so the user knows which one
  nocx owns.
close_reason: sshConfig.aliases enumerates Host patterns from ~/.ssh/config and resolves each one's values through the ssh -G resolver — enumeration and authority are deliberately separate, and the narrow scan says so in its own comment so nobody mistakes it for a second parser. Wildcards are excluded on the backend, in one place. A saved profile whose host equals the alias suppresses the system entry, and the profile's NAME plays no part, so a differently-named profile targeting the same alias suppresses it too. An unreadable config surfaces through the unavailable field rather than looking like an empty list — the failure nocx-n7yv was. Coordinator fixed three lint findings the worker reported as clean: an unchecked defer Close, an unjustified G304, and 0644 fixture permissions on an ssh config.

title: Creation starts from one field
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Creating a connection starts from a single field accepting deploy@10.0.0.1:2222, a bare
  alias, or ssh://...
- parseQuickConnect (frontend/src/profiles.ts) already does this parsing and is currently
  reached only from the palette. Reuse it; do not write a second parser.
- What could not be parsed is stated, not silently dropped.
close_reason: Creating a connection starts from one field accepting deploy@10.0.0.1:2222, a bare alias or ssh://. parseQuickConnect was EXTENDED for the ssh:// scheme rather than duplicated — the constraint that mattered, given three earlier revisions in this epic were sent back for a second implementation that had to agree with a first. Unparseable input is stated, not dropped.

title: TextField composes Field, so the kit stops carrying two label implementations
description:
## What is wrong

frontend/src/ui/text-field.tsx implements its own label, and frontend/src/ui/field.tsx
implements another. Spec section 5 names the consequence: the required marker exists in one
of them, so it appears on some controls and not others depending on which the surface reached
for. Two vocabularies for one concept is the defect the kit migration spent two epics
unwinding.

## Acceptance Criteria

- TextField composes Field rather than duplicating it. The required marker, label, error and
  description come from one implementation.
- Every existing caller keeps working with no change at its call site, or the change is
  mechanical and applied here.
- The kit README inventory table reflects the composition.
- Identity classes stay stable: the CSS-integrity and kit-identity lint gates must still pass,
  and the raw-controls / inline-markup baselines must not grow. If a baseline entry becomes
  stale that is fine; growth is not.
- Existing kit tests still pass and the composition is covered.

## Why this is its own bead

It is the one piece of wave 6 that touches only frontend/src/ui/, so it runs in parallel with
the backend without colliding with the surface rewrite that follows.
close_reason: TextField composes Field; one label implementation, so the required marker is everywhere at once. Coordinator fixed an accessibility regression the composition introduced — label={props.label!} silenced a real case and emitted an empty <label for> for a field with only an error. Field.label is now optional and the element is omitted when empty; both directions pinned by tests. Commit d01ca47.

title: Wiring global defaults must extend the credential-usage contract
description:
## What this is

`ComputeCredentialUsage` (internal/profile/usage.go) reports where a profile got its
credential: `source: "profile" | "group"`. Those are the only two values the renderer
switches on, and they are the only two the effective-profile engine can produce today.

`FieldSourceGlobal` (internal/profile/profile.go:245) is documented as "not yet wired to a
store", and the transport passes an empty `SparseSSHOptions{}`. `FieldSourceDefault` cannot
supply a credentialId — the hardcoded defaults are port, user and behaviorOnSessionEnd.

So a profile whose credential comes from a global default is impossible now, and the
computation skips that case rather than emitting an undocumented third source value into the
wire contract.

## Why this is a bead and not a comment

The day global defaults get a store, that skip becomes silent undercounting: a credential
used by every profile through a global default would report "not used by anything", and the
delete confirmation would show an empty blast radius for a credential the whole fleet uses.
Nothing would fail; the number would just be wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Whoever wires global defaults to a store extends the usage contract with the third source
  and ships the renderer's handling of it in the same wave.
- The skip in usage.go is replaced, not merely widened, and a test covers a profile whose
  credential arrives from a global default.
- The contract change is reflected wherever it is written down (the wave-5 briefs and any
  ADR that carries it).
notes: Resolved in part during wave 5: the third source value 'global' now exists in the contract (ProfileRefSourceGlobal, internal/profile/usage.go) rather than being silently dropped. What remains is what the title says — wiring global defaults to a store, and the renderer's handling of the third value. The coordinator's first attempt was to skip the case entirely; the backend worker's TestComputeCredentialUsage_GlobalDefaultsInherited caught it, which is why the skip is not what shipped.

title: ADR-0006 describes the credential model that shipped
description:
## What is wrong today

`docs/decisions/0006-reusable-credentials.md` documents a model the code stopped having,
and it has been contradicting itself since wave 2 landed:

- Line 27 still carries `Host string // Optional: bind to specific host (empty = works for
  any host)`. `nocx-mon` made an empty host a refusal at connect time, and wave 2
  (`nocx-j685`) then deleted the field outright. Go's `Credential`
  (`internal/profile/credential.go:20`) has no `Host` at all.
- The "UI Changes" section describes a "Saved Credentials (УЗ) button" that opens a form.
  Wave 5 deletes that button — an entity switch disguised as an action — in favour of a
  Credentials entry in the settings rail.
- The storage section predates credential versions (wave 1): `Versions`,
  `CurrentVersionID`, `CandidateVersionID` do not appear in the ADR at all.

An ADR that describes a model nobody implements is worse than no ADR: it is the document
the next agent will believe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Data Model block matches `internal/profile/credential.go` as shipped, including the
  version fields and what each is for.
- Authorization is described as computed from the profiles that reference the credential
  (spec section 3.1). The host binding is recorded as **removed**, with the reason and the
  work that removed it — do not silently delete the paragraph. An ADR that quietly loses a
  decision destroys the only record of why the decision was made.
- The UI section describes the Credentials settings section and the one shared form
  component that both it and the wave-6 dialog host.
- The amendment is dated and attributed the way ADR-0001 records its 2026-07-26 amendment;
  the header's Status/Date reflect it.

## Deliberately out

The vault-versus-keychain question (`nocx-25k9`). Where secrets physically live is not what
this ADR decides, and guessing at it here would create a second contradiction to unwind.
close_reason: ADR-0006 now describes the shipped model: versions, no host binding, computed authorization, CredentialPatch, and the settings-rail section. The removed host-binding rule is recorded with its reasoning rather than deleted.

title: Changing a fleet password is a rollout, not a hope
description: Wave 8. Spec sections 3.9 and 6. SAFETY: never try several passwords against one host — it triggers account lockouts and is indistinguishable from password spraying. MaxAuthTries is finite. Verify the host key before probing. Built on the probe primitive from wave 4 and the version model from wave 1.
acceptance_criteria: A credential holds current and candidate versions; a canary selection is probed with a forced-fresh pool-bypassing connection sending only the intended method; per-endpoint status distinguishes accepted, rejected, unreachable, host-key problem and needs-interactive; rollout proceeds in bounded batches with per-bastion concurrency limits; promotion, retirement and emergency revocation are three distinct transitions; there is never a silent fallback from candidate to current during an ordinary connection; a straggler pin is keyed by profile provenance, not by endpoint.
close_reason: All five children closed. Criterion met clause by clause: versions model (8.1); canary probed first through a forced-fresh pool-bypassing single-method probe (8.3 + ssh_probe.go); five-outcome taxonomy in ssh.ClassifyProbeError and rendered as such (8.5); bounded batches with global and per-bastion concurrency (8.3); three distinct transitions (8.4); no silent candidate-to-current fallback (ResolveWithVersion, tested); pin keyed by profile provenance, tested that pinning one profile does not pin another on a shared endpoint. NOT run against real hosts — that needs the owner present.

title: Hosts from ~/.ssh/config appear where they are looked for
description: Wave 7. Spec section 4. The terminal hint is frontend-only and works while nocx's command editor owns input — OSC 133 marks command boundaries but does not expose the shell's editable line, so raw-shell support needs cooperating shell integration and is NOT promised here. AD-6 forbids building any of it on the backend.
acceptance_criteria: ~/.ssh/config aliases are a live read-only source surfaced in the quick-connect palette and in a terminal hint inside the nocx command editor; the connection manager still lists only nocx-owned records; a saved profile targeting the same alias suppresses the system duplicate; Save as connection adopts an external host storing the alias; a one-off importer exists alongside the Tabby one, labelled as producing a detached copy; the supported ssh_config subset is declared and conformance-tested against ssh -G.
close_reason: Wave 7 landed in five commits (6ce3063, f519d28, 234fbfd, 01a4463, f4a1bd2). nocx stopped parsing ~/.ssh/config and asks ssh -G instead (ADR-0015), which closed nocx-n7yv — a single Match directive had silently disabled every alias. Aliases are a live read-only source in the palette and in the command editor's hint, suppressed when a saved profile targets the same alias; Save as connection adopts one by storing the alias, and a separate importer produces an honestly-labelled detached copy storing the resolved hostname. The supported-subset and conformance-fixture task from spec section 9 item 3 dissolved: the subset is whatever the user's ssh supports, and make conformance checks the parsing against the real binary.

title: e2e/proof-matrix.spec.ts: unused initialId fails npx eslint . on the branch
description:
\`npx eslint .\` at the repo root reports one error on the branch, introduced by
bbd8723 and unrelated to any work in flight: e2e/proof-matrix.spec.ts:573 assigns
\`initialId\` from the active tab's data-tab-id and never reads it. The assertion
that followed it was replaced by one that reads the first tab directly, and the
binding was left behind.

It matters because AGENTS.md makes \`npx eslint .\` part of the gate that runs
before every push, so a single dead binding blocks every unrelated change until
someone removes it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. \`npx eslint .\` from the repo root.
2. One error: '@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars' at e2e/proof-matrix.spec.ts:573.

## Acceptance Criteria

- \`npx eslint .\` exits clean at the repo root.
- The ArrowLeft focus-movement assertion in that test still checks what it checked.
close_reason: Deleted the unused initialId binding in e2e/proof-matrix.spec.ts; npx eslint . is clean at the repo root. Commit 2245418.

title: Theme catalogue: ten ported palettes behind a parity + contrast gate

close_reason: Ten themes ported (Ayu Dark, Catppuccin Latte/Mocha, Dracula, Gruvbox Dark, Nord, One Dark, Rosé Pine, Solarized Dark/Light), each registered in all four places and held to WCAG 4.5:1 text / 3:1 border by frontend/src/theme-catalogue.test.ts and internal/settings/theme_catalogue_test.go. e2e/theme-switch.spec.ts reads a resolved token out of the running bundle so a missing @import cannot pass. Fixed one pre-existing AA failure found by the gate: light.css dim-on-chrome 4.43 -> 4.57. Commit c000b28.

title: e2e activity-bell waits on the app alt-screen class that nocx-6w4z deleted
description:
nocx-6w4z moved the fullscreen live region inside the pane and deleted the
`#app.alt-screen` class it replaced (the class existed to blank the window
chrome that the old viewport-sized xterm painted over). e2e/activity-bell still
waited on that class, so it timed out 5s into a spec whose actual subject — a
bell lighting the tab indicator from the alternate buffer — was never reached.

Retargeted at `.pane.active .xterm-live-container.live-fullscreen`, which is
what `enterFullscreen()` writes on the same alt-screen path.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run e2e/activity-bell.spec.ts on main at 6efb1bf: it fails with
`toHaveClass(/alt-screen/) ... Received: ""`.

## Acceptance Criteria

e2e/activity-bell passes in chromium and webkit, and asserts alt-screen through
a class the product still sets.
close_reason: Spec retargeted at .xterm-live-container.live-fullscreen

title: DocumentStore path capability does not confine names to its root
description:
DocumentStore.pathFor blindly filepath.Join values supplied by callers. Absolute paths and parent traversal can escape the configured root, and the symlink check is separated from rename by a TOCTOU window. Current production callers pass constants, but the capability boundary is weaker than ADR-0011 states and becomes unsafe for future plugins or importers.

## Steps to Reproduce

Construct a DocumentStore rooted in a temporary directory and call Write with an absolute name or a parent traversal name. The resolved target can leave the configured root; a concurrent symlink replacement can also race the pre-rename check.
acceptance_criteria: Document names are validated as root-relative basenames or an explicitly documented safe relative form; absolute paths, traversal and symlink escapes are rejected. Tests prove writes cannot leave the configured root under hostile names and symlink replacement.

title: Session output pump can busy-loop on a zero-length successful read
description:
realSession.readPump immediately calls the output handler after Read returns n=0, err=nil and repeats without blocking or yielding. A legal but misbehaving Channel implementation can consume a CPU core and flood the handler with empty slices.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use a Channel fake whose Read repeatedly returns zero, nil. Start output and observe the loop repeatedly invoke the handler without waiting.
acceptance_criteria: A zero-length successful read cannot spin or invoke the output handler repeatedly; the policy is documented and tested with a channel that returns consecutive zero-length reads before data or EOF.

title: Validation: move focus to the first invalid field and announce the count on submit
description:
ui/validation.ts covers the rules and the show-it-yet decision, and the Connections
form refuses an invalid submit with a per-field message plus a toast carrying the
first one. Two things nocx-74cn's design section asked for are not built:

- On a refused submit, focus does not move to the first invalid control. On a form as
  long as the profile editor the offending field can be scrolled out of view; the
  toast names it but the caret stays where it was.
- Nothing announces how many fields failed. A screen-reader user gets the first
  message through the toast region and no count.

## Two findings from reading the code, 2026-08-13 — both change what this bead is

1. THE SUBMIT GATE IS ALREADY DUPLICATED, so writing focus-and-announce on top of it
   writes them twice. connections.tsx wraps valid() -> revealAll() -> toast(firstError)
   in a private gate() at 1560-1570; secrets.tsx repeats the same three lines inline at
   250, 334 and 378. THIS BEAD STARTS BY LIFTING THAT GATE INTO THE KIT, beside
   createFormValidation, and both surfaces call it. AD-8: one owner per behaviour, and
   the kit is the owner of how a form refuses a submit.

2. THE TARGET IS OFTEN NOT IN THE DOM. The profile editor is a Tabs surface:
   keepaliveInterval, keepaliveCountMax, readyTimeout and forwards live on panels other
   than General. With the user on General and forwards invalid, revealAll() marks a
   control that is not rendered, focus finds nothing, and the outcome is exactly today's
   -- a toast. So "focus the first invalid control" is not implementable by the kit
   alone, and a gate that silently fails to focus is worse than one that does not try.
   Proposed: the gate takes an optional reveal(field) hook, called before focusing, and
   the surface uses it to switch tabs -- the surface owns its tabs, the kit owns the
   sequence. Whatever is chosen, the no-hook case must be honest rather than silent.

Focus needs a control id, and the rule keys are logical names (host, port); the ids are
profile-host, group-name. So createFormValidation gains an optional controlId mapper,
defaulting to the key.

The announcement has an owner already: ui/toast.tsx renders its host as
role="status" aria-live="polite". Do not add a second live region.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A refused submit focuses the first failing control and the live region states how many
  fields need attention.
- No surface calls revealAll() itself: connections.tsx and secrets.tsx (four call sites)
  all go through the kit gate, asserted by grep in a test or by the absence of the
  private helper.
- A failing field on an unopened tab: the surface's reveal hook is called with that
  field before focus is attempted, and the field ends up focused. Without a hook, the
  gate reports that it could not focus rather than pretending it did.
- The count is announced through the existing toast live region, not a new one.
- A form whose first invalid field is already focused does not re-announce on every
  keystroke.
close_reason: Kit owns the submit gate: createSubmitGate reveals, focuses the first failing control via an optional reveal hook for Tabs surfaces, and announces the first failing rule's message (plus a count when several fail, plus an honest 'could not focus' when it could not). All five call sites migrated off their private copies; connections.tsx no longer defines a gate. Proved against the real profile editor, not a fixture. 2fab1f76.

title: Export page: manifest, backup payload and status all had surface-only styling
description:
Follow-up found while fixing nocx-kjjs. The export surface owned the appearance of
three things the kit should own, each with its own type size, colours and spacing:

- the mode manifest (`.st-export-manifest` + five sibling classes) — the page's main
  reading matter, sitting two type steps below the text around it;
- the backup payload `<pre>` (`.st-export-backup-details`) — background, border,
  radius, padding, size and scroll cap declared on the surface;
- the outcome line (`.st-export-status`) — see nocx-4clc.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings → Export / Backup / Import.
2. Compare the manifest text size against the summary line above it.
3. Show Backup Paths and look at the payload block.

## Acceptance Criteria

`MarkerList` and `CodeBlock` exist in `ui/`, the export surface imports them, and
`export.css` holds only placement plus the page's own two text styles.

title: Export page: native file-picker button, tiny manifest text, stretched buttons
description:
Three visual defects on Export / Backup / Import:

- `FileInput` renders a bare `input[type=file]`, so the platform draws its own button
  ("Выбор файла" on a Russian browser) inside an English form. ADR-0014 accepted this
  trade; it reads as pasted-in and the kit now wraps the input instead.
- The manifest list (`.st-export-manifest li`, incl. `.st-export-carries`) is at
  `--font-size-xs` — smaller than the summary above it for the page's main content.
- Buttons inside a `Stack` stretch to full width, so Import and Decrypt and Import
  are page-wide slabs while Export Configuration (not in a Stack) is button-sized.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings → Export / Backup / Import.
2. Compare the Configuration Export section with the Import section at the bottom.

## Acceptance Criteria

FileInput shows a kit Button plus the chosen file name; the manifest reads at the same
size as the rest of the page; action buttons size to their label everywhere.

title: Settings: heading floats too far above the first row
description:
The section h2 in the settings surface carried `margin-bottom: var(--space-2)` on top of
PageSection's flex gap (`--space-4`), and `.ui-settings-row` adds its own `--space-3` top
padding: 8 + 16 + 12 = 36px between the heading rule and the first control it names.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Settings surface, pick any section (e.g. Clipboard).
2. Measure from the h2's bottom border to the first row's label.

## Acceptance Criteria

The heading rule sits one gap above the first row: h2 margin 0, and the flex gap on
`.ui-settings .ui-page-section` alone owns the distance (`--space-2`).

title: Switching strip orientation marks every inactive tab as having activity
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open four tabs and let them sit idle at a prompt.
2. Switch the tab strip from vertical to horizontal.

Expected: nothing changes about the tabs. Changing how the strip is drawn is not
something that happens IN a tab.
Actual: every inactive tab lights its activity indicator.

## Cause

Not a state-storage bug in the strip — the flag really is being set. Switching
orientation resizes every pane at once, `renderer.onResize` sends the new
geometry to the PTY, and the shell answers by redrawing its prompt. That redraw
arrives on `session.onData`, where `terminal-content.ts` calls
`host.requestAttention()` for any output in the normal buffer.

So the output is real; what is wrong is the meaning attached to it. The activity
flag means "output arrived that you have not seen", and output the app provoked
by resizing the window is not that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Switching orientation leaves every tab activity flag as it was.
- Resizing the window by dragging does the same.
- Output that genuinely arrives on an inactive tab still raises the indicator —
  the suppression is bounded to the shell response to a resize we sent, not a
  general mute.
close_reason: Output that follows a resize we sent is no longer read as unread activity. Switching orientation resizes every pane, the shell redraws its prompt, and that redraw arrived on session.onData looking exactly like output nobody had seen.

title: Active and inactive rows in the vertical strip differ by two percent
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Switch the tab strip to vertical.
2. Open three tabs and look at which one is selected.

Expected: the current tab is obvious.
Actual: the rows read as one undifferentiated column. The only thing separating
them is the 2px indicator on the left edge.

## Measured

Inactive row: `--color-surface-sunken` = #24283b.
