title: [bug] 23 shellintegration and app tests fail on a Linux workstation and pass in the container
description:
The host-side Go run — `make ci`'s test-ci, the target that stands in for
ci.yml's uncontainerized `backend` job — is red on a NixOS workstation with 23
failures across two packages, while the containerized `ci-linux` job on the same
tree is green. This is the Linux counterpart of nocx-58gq and nocx-65v6, which
record the same shape on macOS.

Measured 2026-08-25 on feat/ai-assistant at 7dc673e4, and again on a pristine
`git archive origin/main` tree on the same machine. The two failure sets are
BYTE-FOR-BYTE IDENTICAL, so the cause is the machine and not any branch:

    internal/app              5 failures  (101.9s)
    internal/shellintegration 18 failures (110.8s)

Two of them cannot pass here whatever the code does, and they are the lead:

    TestBashLauncher_RunsUnderDash      — this machine has no `dash`
    TestBashScript_ParsesUnderBash32    — bash here is 5.3.15, not 3.2

The rest are the bash channel handshake, the nested-SSH grant pair, the POSIX
and carrier launchers, the startup-fidelity trio and the live-sshd zsh adapter —
all of which spawn a real shell and depend on what that shell is.

## Why this is worth a bead rather than a note

A developer running the documented local gate is told 23 things are broken and
none of them is. AGENTS.md already warns that `backend` is the one job with no
container and the one place local and CI disagree, and it names the macOS list
so a red can be read against it. There is no such list for Linux, so the next
person to run `make ci-full` here has to derive it the way this was derived.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a Linux workstation without `dash` and with bash newer than 3.2:
   `go test -race -count=1 -tags gtk3 ./internal/app/ ./internal/shellintegration/`
2. Observe 23 failures.
3. Extract a pristine tree — `git archive origin/main | tar -x -C /tmp/base` —
   and run the same command there. The failure set is identical, which is what
   establishes it is the machine.
4. `./scripts/ci-linux.sh` on the same tree: green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Linux host-only failure set is either FIXED (the tests declare and skip on
  a machine that lacks the shell they need, rather than failing) or WRITTEN DOWN
  where AGENTS.md writes the macOS one, so a red can be read against a list.
- If skipping is the answer, a skip states which shell was missing — a skipped
  test reporting success is the failure AGENTS.md's testing rules exist to stop.
- `make ci` on a machine with the shells present stays red for a real defect:
  whatever is done here must not turn the shell-integration tests into no-ops
  in the container, where they are the only coverage the feature has.
notes:
THE CAUSE IS CONFIRMED, and it is the image, not the code. `.githooks/images/ci-linux`
installs the shells this workstation does not have — its apt line reads, in part:

    dash zsh openssh-server openssh-client

So the container has `dash` and a zsh; the NixOS host has neither dash nor a
bash older than 5.3. Same tree (7dc673e4), same command, opposite results:

    host          internal/app               5 FAIL   (101.9s)
                  internal/shellintegration 18 FAIL   (110.8s)
    ci-linux.sh   internal/app               ok        97.4s / 98.4s
                  internal/shellintegration  ok       133.8s / 126.6s
                  (both keyring variants, exit 0)

That is the whole diagnosis for at least RunsUnderDash and ParsesUnderBash32 and
is strongly indicated for the other 21, every one of which spawns a real shell.

WHAT A FIX MUST NOT DO, restated because it is the trap: the container is where
these tests are the feature's only coverage. Skipping on a missing shell has to
be conditional on the shell actually being absent, never on a build tag or an
env var a CI job could acquire by accident — otherwise the 23 become no-ops
exactly where they are load-bearing.

title: The agent wrapper's no-channel branch is the one path nothing exercises
description:
__nocx_agent_run has three exits and two are tested on a real pty (nocx-szb40.5): an
enrolment that is granted, and one the backend refuses. The third — the channel is
not active at all, so the wrapper prints 'not orchestrated' and runs the agent
conventionally — is asserted nowhere.

It is the path a person is MOST likely to meet: a pane whose handshake never
completed, a shell that lost its domain mid-session, a tier that is marker-only.
The two tested exits both require a live channel to reach, so the harness that
proves them cannot reach this one; it needs a shell sourced with the script and
no accepting kernel behind it, which internal/shellintegration already knows how
to build (startChannelShell without the accept).

Both shells, because they are two implementations of one branch.
acceptance_criteria:
A bash pane with the integration sourced and no live lifecycle channel runs the agent and says it is not orchestrated, asserted on a real pty.
The same for zsh.
The agent runs exactly once on that path, like the refused one.
close_reason: Both shells prove the third exit on a real pty: no lifecycle channel, the pane says it is not orchestrated, the agent runs exactly once. The first draft's withdrawal assertion searched the rendered pane for a protocol frame — a condition false for every possible run — and was replaced by a comment saying why nothing is observable there, pointing at the refused-enrolment test where a kernel records frames and the assertion can fail.

title: The Module Map in architecture.md still lists only the original six backend modules
description:
## Context

`docs/architecture.md` §Module Map is the binding spine's inventory, and it
names `pty`, `ssh`, `session`, `transport`, `config`, `shellintegration` — the
original six. Every backend module added since is absent. Measured by grepping
the table (lines 76-95) for each package name, all of these score 0:

    vault  content  git  files  update  settings  capability
    apibind  apicoll  apifetch  apiimport  apisend  pathname  reveal  httppolicy

This is repo-wide staleness, not a gap any one branch introduced — which is why
it is filed rather than patched inside a feature merge. Adding only the `api*`
rows would leave the table wrong in the same way and newly inconsistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every `internal/` package that owns a module-level responsibility has a row,
  or the table says explicitly that it is the spine and not an inventory.
- Each row states an SRP responsibility in the voice the existing rows use.

title: Drag a request onto a folder to move it
description:
The accelerator on api.request.move, deliberately kept out of nocx-8aczn: that epic ships the act and its keyboard-reachable door, and this is the faster way to do the same call.

It is its own design and that is why it is separate. The product has NO intra-tree drag today — draggable appears on the tab strip, the snippets list and the dialog, and nowhere in a tree — so this invents a grammar rather than reusing one: dropping INTO a folder versus BETWEEN rows, what the highlight says, autoscroll on a long tree, what a drop on another collection means (the epic says moving between collections is out), and what a drop on the row's own folder means. Whatever it decides, it calls the same method and adds no second path.
acceptance_criteria:
- A request dragged onto a folder row lands in that folder, through api.request.move and no other path.
- The drop target says what will happen before the pointer is released, and a drop that would do nothing is refused visibly rather than silently.
- The menu item stays: this is an accelerator, and the keyboard door is not replaced by it.
- The grammar is written down where the next tree can read it — a drop on a folder, a drop between rows, and a drop on something that cannot accept it.

title: Save's enabled state re-derives the store's unsavedWork predicate inline
description:
Reported by nocx-86wvw's worker, which introduced the owner and could not
reach the caller (api-pane.tsx belonged to another worker that wave).

api-pane.tsx derives, inline, for Save's enabled state:

    store.draft() !== null && (store.dirty() || store.selected() === null)

That is character for character the question `unsavedWork()` now owns in
api-store.ts, where it is named, commented and covered — it exists because
`dirty` alone misses the case with no file behind the draft at all, which is
exactly what a converted curl line is.

Two derivations of one question agree until they do not, and this repo has
measured that shape five times in one session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `unsavedWork` is promoted onto the `ApiStore` interface and api-pane.tsx
  reads it instead of re-deriving it.
- No third caller appears; grep for the expression and say what you found.
- The existing tests for Save's enabled state pass unchanged — if one has to
  move, the predicate changed meaning and that is a different bead.

title: The terminal's contextmenu listener is added without a signal and never removed
description:
Reported by nocx-8v1fu's worker while writing a test that asserts a tree row
suppresses the platform menu.

terminal-content.ts:2642 attaches a `contextmenu` handler with
`target.addEventListener` and no `AbortSignal`, and nothing removes it. In
`api-workbench.test.tsx` the API pane reuses an element that listener was
attached to, so `event.defaultPrevented` on an API tree row answers about a
neighbouring surface rather than about the row.

The worker did not work around it by weakening the assertion into a lie: it
asserted the user-visible property instead — that no menu of ours opens — and
wrote down why. So nothing is blocked; this is the underlying cause.

In the real app the panes are separate, so the observable symptom is probably
a harness artefact. A document-level listener that outlives the thing that
added it is not, and it is the shape that produces "two surfaces own one
input" — this repo's most recurrent defect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mount the terminal surface and then the API workbench in one document, as
   `api-workbench.test.tsx` does.
2. Dispatch `contextmenu` on an API tree row.
3. `defaultPrevented` is true even where the API pane did not prevent it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The listener is removed when the thing that added it goes away — an
  `AbortSignal` tied to the pane's lifetime, or an explicit removal on the
  same path that mounts it.
- A test asserts it: after the surface is torn down, an event on that element
  is not touched by it.
- Whoever fixes it checks whether the same file adds others the same way; a
  single one fixed in isolation says nothing about the file.

title: A block can be seated under itself, and nothing refuses it
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Seat an entry under its own id — `AddCause(x, x)`, or an UPDATE writing
`parent_id = id` — on a database built by schemaV1.

## What happens

It is accepted. `entries.parent_id` has no self-reference guard, so a block becomes its own
parent: a one-node cycle that no read can terminate on and that renders as a block
containing itself. `tabs.parent_id` in the same schema DOES carry
`CHECK (parent_id IS NULL OR parent_id != id)`; entries does not, and the omission is an
oversight rather than a decision — ADR-0037's brief enumerated the CHECKs it wanted and this
was not among them.

Found by the worker on nocx-dc2fr.1, which correctly declined to add a constraint the brief
had not asked for.

## What should happen

The database refuses it, the way it refuses a taken seat. Nothing in the code can currently
produce one, which is why this is P3 and not P1 — but "no caller does this today" is not a
constraint, and a deeper cycle (a under b under a) wants thinking about at the same time:
a plain CHECK cannot see it, and a recursive read that meets one must terminate rather than
hang.
acceptance_criteria:
- `UPDATE entries SET parent_id = id` is refused by the database, with a test that asserts
  the refusal and a paired test that seating under a DIFFERENT block still succeeds.
- A read that walks the tree terminates on a cycle it did not create, rather than
  recursing — asserted by writing one through a raw statement if the CHECK cannot prevent
  it, and saying in the test which of the two defences caught it.

title: The terminal pane's drop affordance is a second vocabulary beside ui/drop-zone
description:
Discovered writing .internal/specs/2026-08-23-import-collection-ask-design.md.

That spec adds ui/drop-zone.tsx to the kit for the import dialog, because
frontend/src/ui/ has no drop zone and file-input.tsx is a picker. terminal-drop.ts
already hand-rolls its own dragover/dragleave/drop with a data-drop-active
dataset on the pane element. Once the kit component exists, that is two
vocabularies for one concept — the defect the kit rules exist to stop.

It was left out of the import change deliberately rather than missed: the pane
half is entangled with the pane lifecycle and with the DOM half of the browser
drop, which the dialog does not have.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The terminal pane renders its drag affordance through ui/drop-zone; the
  ui-drop-zone identity class and data-drop-active are the only state the pane
  declares.
- No dragover/dragleave paint rule remains in the pane surface CSS.
- The existing local-drop and upload e2e specs pass unchanged.

title: e2e: the sshd fixture is copied into a fourth spec
description:
startSshd / trustHostKey / rpc / bindings are duplicated in e2e/shell-mode.spec.ts, e2e/nocxify-journey.spec.ts, e2e/ports-row-width.spec.ts and now e2e/notification-centre-grouping.spec.ts. Four copies of one arrangement: they agree today and will disagree the first time one of them is fixed. e2e/harness.ts is the suite's fixtures module and is where a shared one belongs.

A second, smaller duplication rides along: quietBell / backToTheTerminal / run are copied between notification-centre.spec.ts, notification-osc.spec.ts and the grouping spec.

Reported by the worker that wrote the fourth copy (2026-08-23) rather than extracted quietly, because the extraction touches four spec files and was outside its brief.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One sshd fixture, in e2e/harness.ts or a module it re-exports; the four specs use it and carry no copy.
- The extraction is behaviour-preserving: each of the four specs passes before and after, and the report names the runs.
- The notification helpers (quietBell, backToTheTerminal, run) are shared the same way or the report says why they should stay per-spec.
- No spec gains a longer timeout as part of the move; if one needs it, that is a finding to report, not a line to add.

title: A Field's label reaches no Select: SelectProps has no id
description:
frontend/src/ui/field.tsx renders <label for=...>, and frontend/src/ui/select.tsx accepts no id, so the association is to nothing. Every Select consumer is affected -- vault.tsx, connections.tsx, settings.tsx, secret-source.tsx, key-material-input.tsx, and now the notifications panel's host filter. A screen reader user gets a labelled group with an unlabelled control inside it.

Found 2026-08-23 while building the notification panel's narrowing (nocx-ikkbe). Pre-existing and not caused by it; the panel follows the established pattern rather than hand-rolling a label, and its tests locate the control by the label's text so they do not depend on the broken association -- which is exactly why nothing has caught it.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Render any Select inside a Field, e.g. the Vault page's provider select.
2. Click the Field's label text: focus does not move to the select.
3. Read the select's accessible name: it is empty, not the label's text.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A Select rendered inside a Field is programmatically associated with that Field's label: clicking the label focuses the control, and the accessible name of the control is the label's text.
- The fix is in the kit, once, not in each of the six consumers.
- A kit test asserts the association through the accessible name rather than by asserting the attribute -- an attribute test passes on an id that points at nothing.
- The other Field children (TextField, Checkbox, SearchField) are checked for the same gap in the same pass, and the report says which of them already had it right.

title: One ledger field means both who wrote a row and what the row is, so a question says its author is the agent
acceptance_criteria:
Every row says who wrote it, and nothing has to read that field as two answers at once.

## What is true today

internal/content/ledger_command.go:79-88 states it plainly: "Author is WHO
submitted the command, and it is the entry's own kind". So entries.kind carries
the AUTHOR — shell is the person at the keyboard, agent is the assistant's lane.

But the same column also carries WHAT THE ROW IS for every writer that is not a
command: a question and an answer are written kind='agent'
(ledger_agent_sqlite.go), a frame capture is kind='agent' with intent=frame-capture,
a tool call is kind='action'.

The visible lie: a question the PERSON typed is stored with kind='agent'. Read as
the author — which is what the field is documented to be — the row says the
assistant wrote the person's question.

## Why this is filed and not fixed

nocx-4em1z needed to tell a command from a dialogue on restore and considered
splitting author from kind. It does not need to: the block's grammar comes from
what its BODY is (a terminal body is application/vt with the plain copy marked
derived_from it; an assistant turn has a text/plain original and never a vt body),
which is stored and never inferred. So the conflation costs nothing there, and
widening that bug into a ledger refactor was the wrong trade.

It still lies, and the next reader of that column will believe it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant anything.
2. Read the question's row: kind='agent'.
3. Read ledger_command.go's doc for that column: it says the column is the author.
4. The person wrote the question.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One field per meaning: who wrote the row, and what the row is. Name both in the
  code where they are written, not in a comment that explains the overload.
- Every writer sets both deliberately — no default that means "the ordinary case"
  for the field that says what a row is.
- The readers that exist today keep working, and the check is theirs: history,
  recall's rungs, the restore read and the assistant's own block tools all still
  answer what they answered before, asserted.
- Greenfield: replace, do not shim. There is nothing to migrate.

title: The OpenAPI fetch can carry a credential, so a spec behind auth is reachable
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A spec behind `Authorization` can be fetched: the dialog offers a credential for the fetch, resolved through the vault, never typed into a collection file.
- The credential is dropped across an origin change, as `httppolicy` already does.
- Until then the 401 message from nocx-l1hat is what a person sees; this bead replaces it rather than adding a second path.

Deferred deliberately in the OpenAPI epic (nocx-ttrlr §2, §4.2).

title: Swagger 2.0 imports too, instead of being refused by name
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A Swagger 2.0 document imports into the same collection model: `basePath` folded into `baseUrl`, `definitions` where `components/schemas` is, body parameters, `consumes`/`produces` as `Content-Type`/`Accept`.
- The refusal added by nocx-67ug8 is replaced, not left beside a second path.
- Same bounds, same hostile-input rules, same `Unsupported` discipline as the 3.x path.

Deferred deliberately in the OpenAPI epic (nocx-ttrlr §2): a second document shape, and 3.x is where the value is first.

title: RendererRequester now carries a seam the renderer has nothing to do with
acceptance_criteria:
The interface a run's tool seams arrive on is named for what it is, and its name does not
say "renderer" while carrying the ledger.

## What happened

nocx-5u3oz.6 delivered the block seam (assistant.BlockSource) by embedding it in
assistant.RendererRequester, which the transport already satisfies. The alternative — a new
AskParams field — needed edits in internal/assistant/engine.go and internal/transport/ws_agent.go,
both owned by the worker on nocx-shxv0 at the time, so the worker escalated instead of
crossing the boundary. That was the right call and this is the follow-up it asked for.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The interface carries a name that covers what it now delivers (the worker suggested
  ToolSeams / RunSeams); the doc comment says the transport is the single adapter for
  everything a tool cannot reach from internal/assistant.
- Rename only. No behaviour change, no new seam, no new field — if the rename turns out to
  want a shape change, that is a different bead.
- Do it AFTER nocx-shxv0 has landed, or the rename collides with it.

title: Directory upload: a folder dropped on a tab arrives whole, or says what did not
description:
Recursive upload on the mechanism nocx-9le.5 built. Blocked by it because it moves the same files.

## Success Criteria

- A person drops a folder on an SSH tab and the whole tree arrives, with a partial failure mid-tree reported as what arrived and what did not.
- One automated check watches it against cmd/e2e-sshd.
- Names the decisions the file case did not have to make: mkdir collisions, symlinks, modes, and what happens when a directory disappears mid-walk.

title: TestAgentAsk_SlowConsumerBoundsTheDeltaPath waits on a 10s duration, and flaked once
description:
Seen once by the worker on nocx-avogl.3 during a full-package run of internal/transport; not reproduced in 3 subsequent full-package runs, and green in isolation. A clean-tree baseline run of the whole package was also green, so it is not the nocx-avogl.3 change.

The test waits on `case <-time.After(10 * time.Second)` at internal/transport/ws_agent_gap_test.go:432 and failed at exactly 10.00s. That is the class AGENTS.md names outright: "a test may not depend on timing. Wait on an observable state change — a frame, a record, a DOM state — never on a duration. A spec that needs a slow machine to pass is broken on a fast one too; it has only not been caught yet."

Filed rather than fixed inside another task: the fix is to find the observable this test is really waiting for, which is its own piece of thinking.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. go test -tags gtk3 ./internal/transport/ -run TestAgentAsk -count 5 (the failure needs the full package under load, not the test alone).
2. Watch for TestAgentAsk_SlowConsumerBoundsTheDeltaPath failing at ~10.00s.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test waits on an observable state change rather than on a duration, and the 10-second time.After is gone.
- It still asserts what it asserted: that the delta path is bounded for a slow consumer.
- It passes under NOCX_CI_CPUS=1 (the cap AGENTS.md keeps for exactly this kind of bisect).

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text: Seen a SECOND time, independently, by the worker on nocx-avogl.4 in a different worktree: 'TestAgentAsk_SlowConsumerBoundsTheDeltaPath (10.01s): stall count = 2, want 1; timed out waiting for 257 delta frames written'. Green on its two other full runs and green at -count=3 in isolation. That worker's diff does not touch the delta path either (it drives newGapHandlers, which never reads the settings seam). Two independent observations in one afternoon, on two clean trees: this is load-sensitivity, not either change.

title: A tool name the model invents lands on the default sentence: eino rejects it before our middleware
description:
Measured by the worker on nocx-avogl.3 while writing the three product sentences for a failed run.

ErrMalformedModelOutput has an unknown-tool branch that cannot be reached through the engine: a tool name the model invents is rejected by eino own index lookup ("tool %s not found in toolsNode indexes") BEFORE the policy middleware runs. The failure therefore lands on the default sentence. Nothing framework-shaped leaks onto the screen, so this is not the nocx-avogl.3 defect returning — but the cause is not named, which is exactly what nocx-avogl.3 argued against: one message for three causes is how a cause stops being findable.

Naming it needs a handle eino does not offer today. Options not yet weighed: match eino own message at the boundary (brittle, and it is the framework text we just took off the screen), or declare the tool set to eino differently so the lookup cannot fail first.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant a question with a grant that declares tools.
2. Get the model to emit a tool call naming a tool it was never offered (a stub model in internal/assistant tests is the practical route).
3. Watch the answer block: the run fails with the DEFAULT sentence ("the model failed to answer. The details are in nocx log."), not with a sentence naming the cause.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A model naming a tool that does not exist produces a sentence that says so, distinct from the default failure sentence.
- The test drives it through the real engine, not through a hand-built error: the whole point is that the engine intercepts first.
- No framework identifier reaches the screen (the nocx-avogl.3 invariant still holds).

title: e2e connection-password: the remembered second open times out on a click, rarely, on the runner only
description:
Seen once while integrating nocx-m8jwn, on CI, in ci-e2e (webkit): e2e/connection-password.spec.ts:195 'first open prompts and connects; after remembering, the second open does not prompt' failed with 'locator.click: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded' at 30.1s, alone among 178 cases.

It is filed as a flake rather than fixed because the measurements say so and are recorded here rather than summarised: five runs of the spec alone in the repository's own e2e container, all green; one full webkit suite in that same container under the load CI runs it in, 178/178 green; and four real CI runs of that browser on this branch, three green. The epic did not touch this file, and its most recent change (05cc398f) was itself a fix for the suite racing its own settings load -- so a race in this area has a precedent and a shape.

That is enough to say it does not reproduce here and not enough to say what it is. It wants an owner who can get more than one failure: the artefact of the failing run is the place to start, and the question to answer is what the click was waiting for -- a panel that had not settled, a backend that had not finished remembering, or a prompt that had already gone.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the full e2e suite for webkit in the repository's container: PW_PROJECTS=webkit ./e2e/run-in-container.sh. The failure is rare -- it did not appear in six local runs -- and has only been observed on a GitHub runner, so reproducing it locally may require running the whole suite repeatedly rather than the spec alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

The failure is either reproduced and its cause named -- what the click waited for and why it never arrived -- and fixed by waiting on that state rather than on a duration, or a measurement over enough runs establishes a rate and the wait is made observable so the next occurrence reports what it was waiting for instead of only that it timed out. A raised timeout is not a fix and neither is a retry.

title: A tracked empty file named 1 sits at the repository root
description:
git ls-files finds a zero-byte tracked file named 1 at the repository root, committed in 0d167c43. It has the shape of a shell mistake -- 2>1 where 2>&1 was meant -- captured by a git add -A.

It is harmless and it is noise: it shows up in every listing of the root, and the next person to see it has to work out whether anything reads it before they can remove it. Flagged during nocx-m8jwn by two separate workers, which is itself the argument for removing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

The file is gone from the index and from the working tree, and a search of the repository -- Go, TypeScript, shell, Makefile, CI workflows and githooks -- shows nothing that reads, writes or names it.
notes:
2026-08-21: the tracked file was removed by 17483de9, so the INDEX half of this bead is done. The working-tree half is not, and the reason is now known: something recreates ./1 during a containerized e2e run, as root, in the bind-mounted repo root. Observed twice in one session -- 15:51 and 17:36 -- each time immediately after e2e/run-in-container.sh, owner root, zero bytes.

Ruled out by reading: nocx's own shell scripts (nocx.bash, nocx.zsh, nocx.posix), the carrier loader and stage-1 (carrier.go's template redirects stderr with 2>/dev/null and 2>&1 and writes dd's output to a mktemp path, never to a bare 1), and every *.sh, Makefile, githook and workflow in the tree -- a grep for a bare '2>1' or '> 1' redirect finds nothing but numeric comparisons. So it is the container toolchain (npm, playwright, or git inside the entry script), not the product.

That matters for the fix: deleting the file does not close this, because the next local e2e run puts it back, and the harm the bead describes -- a git add -A committing it -- is live again every time. Two candidate answers: find the writer inside e2e/container-entry.sh's install step, or add /1 to .gitignore so it can never be committed whoever writes it. The second is a defence rather than a diagnosis, so it is the owner's call.
close_reason: Fixed, and the residual has its own bead. The tracked file named 1 was removed by commit 17483de9, whose subject cites this bead; re-verified during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh — ls ./1 reports no such file and git ls-files does not list it. This bead's own NOTES already recorded the index half as done and named the working-tree half as the live question: something recreates ./1 during a containerized e2e run, as root, in the bind-mounted repo root. That residual is the open nocx-qkid5, the e2e container run leaving root-owned files in the worktree it ran from. No stray redirect exists in the e2e scripts today. Duplicate sibling nocx-su4g closed alongside.

title: Running the containerized e2e leaves a root-owned .e2e/home that breaks make ci
description:
AGENTS.md tells you to run e2e in the container and to run `make ci` as one of
the four gate jobs. Doing both in that order fails, on a machine where the
container runs as root:

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `./e2e/run-in-container.sh` (any spec).
2. `make ci`.
3. `lint-ci` dies: `gofumpt -l .` → `open .e2e/home: permission denied`.

`.e2e/home` is the disposable $HOME the suite gives the backend. The container
creates it as root, so the host user cannot read or delete it:

    drwx------ 5 root root 4096 .e2e/home

`.e2e/` is gitignored (.gitignore:82), so nothing surfaces it and the failure
reads as a lint error in the repo rather than as a leftover from the previous
gate. The order the two gates are run in decides whether the second one works,
which is the kind of coupling nobody remembers a week later.

Observed 2026-08-21 on Linux while gating the model-selection epic. It cost a
confused minute and a workaround; it will cost the next person the same.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the containerized e2e and then `make ci`, in that order, succeeds.
- Fixed at the cause rather than by teaching `gofumpt` to skip a directory:
  either the container writes that tree as the invoking user, or the suite
  removes it as root before exiting. Say which and why.
- If the host-side gates must skip transient directories anyway, the skip is
  stated once in the Makefile, not repeated per tool.

title: Settings -> Developer -> Sandbox access folds into the activity-bar panel
description:
Once the panel is scoped to the active tab, a global page duplicates it in a worse place. Its unique properties are cross-tab history for a memory-only inbox, and promotion to the global baselines — the second belongs in the panel.

The backend half stays needed either way: the seccomp USER_NOTIF observer, the unified-log consumer, and the `sandbox.access.*` methods.
design: Clean cutover: remove Sandbox access from Settings and re-home the bounded inbox in a non-restorable singleton statistics tab opened by a global activity-bar action; design §6.
acceptance_criteria: There is one surface for denied access, and it is the one scoped to the tab that saw them.
notes:
Removed Sandbox access from Settings and re-homed the bounded denied-access inbox in the singleton Sandbox statistics surface; promotions now target backend-owned workspace profiles.
Implementation complete; closure blocked by nocx-a0qhd.3/nocx-a0qhd.1.

title: The answer block records which model answered but never shows it
description:
Found while reviewing the model-selection plan (nocx-rikz5), 2026-08-21.

The attribution required by nocx-e6kn2 — "a person must be able to tell which
model answered" — is RECORDED in two places and VISIBLE in neither:

  content.RunFacts (internal/content/ledger.go:703) persists EndpointID and
  Model on the run, so a later endpoint change never reinterprets what the run
  used.

  agent-ask.ts:241 sets `handle.el.dataset.answeredBy = ask.model` on the
  answer element, in a comment citing nocx-e6kn2 by name.

Both are data. A person reads `data-answered-by` only by opening devtools.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE AFTER nocx-rikz5, and why it is filed rather than folded
into it: once a default model exists, a role the person believes is unassigned
still answers — through the default. The editor chip names the model BEFORE
the question, which is most of the answer, but it shows the CURRENT resolution,
not the one a scrolled-back answer was produced under. Those differ the moment
the default is changed, which is the whole point of having one.

NOT a reason to reopen nocx-e6kn2: the decision's mechanism exists and works.
This is whether the recorded fact should be legible without devtools.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A person can see, from an answer block alone and without devtools, which
  endpoint and model produced it.
- The value shown is the one recorded ON THAT RUN, not the current resolution
  — changing the default must not retitle old answers.
- Asserted through the seam a person reaches, not by reading a dataset
  attribute in a unit test.

title: The generic settings surface knows two sandbox keys by name
description: settings.tsx maps sandbox.allowedWritablePaths / sandbox.allowedReadOnlyPaths to a path class by literal key, and internal/settings carries checkSandboxPathConflict plus a sandboxPathKeys set called from six write paths. A declaration-driven registry should not know a feature's keys: the class and its peer belong on the declaration, so the renderer reads them off the wire and the guard has one choke point.
acceptance_criteria: No sandbox key appears literally in settings.tsx or in the generic Registry write paths; settings.describe carries the class.

title: PR 91 leftovers: a dead App field, a truncated comment, an unexplained report argument
description: App.UnlockRequester is declared and never assigned or read. The SSH-config-resolver comment lost its first line and left the next one dangling. f.report switched from p.Shell() to shell.Path on the ordinary enhanced path inside a sandbox change, with no comment.
acceptance_criteria: The dead field is gone, the comment reads, and the report argument is either reverted or explained.
close_reason: Fixed on PR 91 (feat/sandbox-current) in the review-fix pass.

title: Native Linux packages (AUR, deb, rpm) as a second channel, where the WebKit helper problem cannot exist
description:
The AppImage is our only Linux artefact, and ADR-0007 makes it the only
self-updating one deliberately. But it is also the format that forces us to carry
somebody else's WebKitGTK and patch its baked helper path to make it work off
Debian (ADR-0035, nocx-azxe.7).

A native package does not have that problem by construction: webkit2gtk-4.1 is an
ordinary dependency, the system's own library finds its own helpers where its own
distribution put them, and we ship only our binary and its assets. For an Arch
user an AUR package is also the more native way to install a program than
chmod +x on a 100 MB file.

wails v3 already generates these: `wails3 task linux:create:deb`, `:rpm`, `:aur`,
with nfpm metadata under build/linux/nfpm/. We do not use wails' packaging path
(release.yml calls linuxdeploy directly), so adopting it is a decision to make,
not a switch to flip.

Explicitly NOT a replacement for fixing the AppImage, and the two must not share
code: self-update stays AppImage-only, a native package cannot repair an AppImage
already on a user's disk, and the byte patch must never reach a build that links
the host's WebKit.

Open questions for whoever takes this: who signs and hosts the repositories (the
AUR is a PKGBUILD pointing at a release asset, deb/rpm need a repo or bare
downloads); whether the in-app updater must learn to recognise a packaged install
and stay quiet (it already refuses without APPIMAGE, so possibly nothing to do);
and whether the version/manifest pipeline in release.yml grows these artefacts or
they are built separately.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A user on Arch can install nocx from a PKGBUILD and start it, on a machine
   that has never had an AppImage on it.
2. The package declares webkit2gtk-4.1 and gtk3 as dependencies, and the
   installed binary loads the host's WebKitGTK — assert no bundled
   libwebkit2gtk/libjavascriptcoregtk is shipped in the package.
3. Nothing in the native package path applies the AppImage byte patch: assert
   scripts/appimage/ is not reachable from it.
4. The in-app updater stays silent in a packaged install (no APPIMAGE), and says
   so in the UI rather than only in the log.

title: The README opens with a wall of text and no mark
acceptance_criteria: README.md opens with the nocx icon and a link to the landing page, and the icon file is the one the site already ships rather than a second copy.

title: A Mac dev run is unbundled, so notifications can never work in it
description:
## What
`make dev` runs `go run .`, which produces a bare executable in a temp directory with no .app bundle. macOS notification APIs need a bundle identifier, so on a dev run the service refuses to start and every banner is unavailable — correctly reported since nocx-l21ib.7, but never testable by hand on the platform banners were written for.

The v2 `wails dev` used to build a bundle; v3 has no dev CLI without a Taskfile and this repository has none (see the Makefile's dev target).

## Options, none chosen
- A darwin-only branch in `make dev` that assembles a minimal .app around the binary (Info.plist with a bundle identifier) and launches that.
- A Taskfile after all, scoped to the dev loop.
- Leave it, and test banners only from `make build-release` artefacts.

## Not urgent
The product's behaviour without a bundle is now correct and stated: the service reports unavailable, the host is born PermissionUnavailable, and banners fail with ErrUnavailable instead of aborting the process.
acceptance_criteria: Given a macOS dev run started by the documented command, when the notification service starts, then it has a bundle identifier and a banner raised from the product appears — or the documentation states plainly that banners are not testable from a dev run and names what is.

title: docs/frontend-state-ownership.md still models sidebar persistence as localStorage
description:
Found while implementing nocx-mqie (ADR-0033, commit c38b4a91).

docs/frontend-state-ownership.md is the design for nocx-ycet (one authoritative frontend store). Its section 3 models the sidebar's collapsed flag as living in localStorage under 'nocx.sidebar.collapsed' at sidebar.tsx:19,98-100,221-233, and specifies a one-shot MIGRATION that reads that key at first boot. Both are now wrong:

- The key is gone. ADR-0033 settled that localStorage may not carry facts; the collapsed flag and the active sidebar view are in the UI-state document (internal/uistate, uistate.json) and reach the renderer over uistate.get/uistate.set.
- The migration is moot, and this repo does not do migrations (greenfield).

Left alone rather than edited in nocx-mqie because the document belongs to a different epic and rewriting another epic's design mid-flight is how two plans end up disagreeing. But a design doc that instructs its implementer to migrate from a key that no longer exists is a trap with a fuse on it, so it is filed rather than mentioned in prose.

The same paragraph appears in .internal/specs/2026-07-27-ui-shell-kit-and-theming-design.md (lines ~611 and ~672, the latter as a risk row 'Persisted UI state lost on upgrade -> migration test from the existing nocx.sidebar.collapsed key'). Fix both, or state in one place that ADR-0033 supersedes them.
acceptance_criteria: docs/frontend-state-ownership.md section 3 names ADR-0033 as the owner of sidebar collapse and active view, and its localStorage migration step is removed rather than left as an instruction; the ui-shell spec's two references say the same.

title: Drag a card between workspaces in the overview
description:
The overview (nocx-edhcu) ships READ-ONLY: it reads the application through
`OverviewPort` and expresses exactly one intent, `activate(paneId)`. Dragging a
card from one workspace's area onto another is deliberately out of that first
slice and is this bead.

WHY IT WAS SPLIT OUT rather than done with the surface. A move is a WRITE
against a lifecycle the backend owns (workspaces-ux design §4.4: one lifecycle
authority, and the two ends of the invariant are in two processes). §4.5 also
says a drag moves the WHOLE LINEAGE SUBTREE and that a lineage child may not be
dragged out on its own — so the drop target is a subtree, not a card. And §4.4
is explicit that the atomicity model for a subtree move is NOT YET DESIGNED: a
snapshot boundary taken at drag start, a compare-and-swap on session epochs so
a child spawned mid-drag is neither silently included nor lost, and either an
atomic commit or a recoverable journal. Until that exists a partial subtree
move must FAIL CLOSED — the move does not apply.

WHAT THIS BEAD HAS TO DO
- Extend `OverviewPort` with a move intent, keeping the port the only thing the
  surface knows about the application.
- Make the drop target the SUBTREE, and refuse a drag that starts on a lineage
  child.
- Decide, with the backend, what a partial failure leaves behind, and prove it
  with the crash cuts §4.4 enumerates.
- Keep the DEFAULT workspace a legal destination even though it renders no
  header (§4.2): dropping onto the ungrouped area is how a pane leaves a
  workspace.

Do not start by writing drag handlers; start by settling the atomicity model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A card dragged onto another workspace's area moves that pane there, and the
  overview shows it under the new workspace without being reopened.
- Dragging a pane with lineage children moves the whole subtree, asserted by a
  test that names the children.
- A drag that starts on a lineage child is refused, and says so.
- A move whose backend call fails leaves the overview showing the pane where it
  actually is, never where it was dropped.
- Dropping onto the ungrouped area moves the pane into the default workspace,
  which still renders no name and no header.

title: The workspace switcher shows no attention counts, so a workspace with a finished run looks like an idle one
description:
Carried out of nocx-isoph.7, which shipped the create/rename/reorder
affordances and deliberately did NOT fake this one. The reason is worth
keeping and is why it is a bead rather than a TODO: attention counts need the
liveness rule, and a second spelling of live-work.ts for the sake of a
decoration would be the AD-8 defect bought for a badge.

Workspaces UX design §4.3 sketches it. Nothing depends on it — the switcher
and the vertical headings both work without it — so this is a P3 that should
land WITH or AFTER whatever next touches liveness, never by reimplementing it.

WHAT IS MISSING IN PRODUCT TERMS: a window shows one workspace at a time, so
work finishing in another workspace is invisible until you switch to it. The
per-tab attention signal already exists; nothing aggregates it per workspace.

STANDALONE ON PURPOSE. It was first filed as nocx-isoph.8, under the
workspaces epic. The epic's acceptance is met and proven end to end, and
holding it open for a P3 decoration would turn a deliverable into an area of
code that can never finish — the failure AGENTS.md names for "Persistence" and
"Quality gates". bd derives parentage from the dotted id, so the bead had to
be re-cut rather than reparented; nocx-isoph.8 is closed as superseded by
this one.
acceptance_criteria:
- A workspace whose tabs hold attention says so in the switcher and on its
  vertical heading, and one test drives a run to completion in a workspace the
  window is NOT showing and watches the count appear.
- The count comes from the existing liveness owner (live-work.ts). A second
  derivation of "is this work live" is the defect this was deferred to avoid,
  so the test that matters is the one proving there is still one owner —
  grep for a second spelling and find none.
- Zero renders as nothing, never as a zero: a badge that is always present is
  a badge nobody reads.

title: The agent's question history does not survive a restart
description:
nocx-4ff.7 gave each input target its own recall corpus. The shell's is the persistent command store with the ledger fallback; the agent's is renderer memory (source: 'session'), so a tab's questions are gone after a restart while its commands are not.

That asymmetry is deliberate for now - a question is not a command and must not enter the command store, and giving questions a durable corpus is a backend surface (a table or an entries kind, a query method, a schema), not a renderer change. It is filed rather than left as a comment because a user who reopens the app and finds half their recall missing will read it as a bug, not as a boundary.

Where it probably goes: ADR-0019 says one authoritative ledger with entries.kind IN ('shell','agent','action'), and an agent turn is already an entry. So the likely answer is that recall reads the agent kind from the same ledger the shell reads, not that a second store appears.

## Acceptance Criteria

Ask a question, restart the app, open recall in agent mode: the question is there. Asserted end to end, not by reading the store.
Shell recall is unchanged - a question never appears in the shell corpus and a command never appears in the agent one. Both ends, asserted.
The agent corpus is served by the same query shape the shell's is; no second history method on the wire.

title: Every race test binary sleeps 1s at exit: TSan atexit_sleep_ms is the floor under 37 of 49 packages
description:
Every race-instrumented test binary sleeps one second at exit, doing nothing.
This is ThreadSanitizer atexit_sleep_ms, which defaults to 1000.

Measured 2026-08-16, host side, on internal/version — a package with ONE test
that asserts link-time defaults and touches nothing:

  go test -race -count=1 ./internal/version/     ok  1.010s
  go test        -count=1 ./internal/version/    ok  0.001s
  the -race binary run directly:   real 1.013s   user 0.003s   sys 0.007s
  the same binary, GORACE=atexit_sleep_ms=0:     real 0.008s

One second of wall clock against ten milliseconds of CPU: the process is
blocked, not computing. 37 of the 49 packages in the backend-linux job sit at
that 1s floor, which is what the floor IS.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY BUYS, stated honestly rather than as 49 x 1s. Packages run
concurrently, so the saving is not the sum — a sleeping binary still holds a
scheduler slot but burns no core, and the run is bounded by the slowest package
(internal/shellintegration at 111s). Expect the floor to matter most on the
tail of small packages and in the pre-commit hook, not on the critical path.
It should be MEASURED before and after rather than asserted, and this bead is
not worth doing before the two that are on the critical path.

AND IT IS NOT FREE. atexit_sleep_ms exists so that threads still running at
exit get a chance to have their races reported; setting it to 0 can drop a
report from a goroutine that outlives main. A middle value — 50ms or 100ms —
keeps almost all of the saving and most of the safety. Choosing 0 for a
correctness gate is the wrong end of that trade.

## Acceptance Criteria

- GORACE is set once, where the race runs are launched (.githooks and
  scripts/ci-linux.sh), not per developer shell.
- The value chosen is NOT 0 unless a measurement shows 50ms costs materially
  more, and the comment beside it names the trade — that the sleep exists to
  let a late goroutine report its race.
- Wall clock of scripts/ci-linux.sh and of the pre-commit containerized run is
  recorded in this bead before and after, from the same machine.

title: The snippet clipboard destination lost its affordance when the palette became a quick-connect variant
description:
Found while the owner reviewed the surface swap (2026-08-16).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Save a two-line snippet.
2. Fire it into a program that has not enabled bracketed paste.
3. The refusal says the fire was refused — and offers nothing.

Before the swap the old floating panel offered the alternative the design names (§9.4, §11.1): the multi-line body the terminal cannot honour can be COPIED, and a secret that must not reach the clipboard can be inserted into the pane instead. That was ⌘↵ on the panel plus alternativeFor(); both went with the panel.

What survives: the fire adapter still takes destination: 'input' | 'clipboard' and still refuses a secret to the clipboard (§11.1), so the policy is intact — nothing can offer the alternative.

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] A multi-line refusal offers 'copy instead' from a surface a person can reach, and taking it copies the resolved text
[ ] A secret-to-clipboard refusal offers 'insert into the pane instead' the same way
[ ] SnippetDestination has a caller for BOTH of its values outside tests

title: Spec self-review
close_reason: Self-review: fixed criterion 3 (assert the narrowing, not a behavioural negative); made the rendered-lane consequence explicit

title: Delete the disconnect overlay's temporary lost-sessions toast
description:
The disconnect overlay carries a temporary toast — shown only when lost > 0 —
because until nocx-ictcq lands it is the only place in the product that says a
session's work was lost. By then the tab has already been destroyed
(terminal-content.ts:1902 on onExit, reached both from the backend's exit
notification and from a failed reattach at ipc.ts:290).

Once a lost tab SURVIVES and carries a visible mark, the toast is a second voice
for one fact and must go. One condition and one showToast, deleted in one move.

This bead exists so that deletion is scheduled rather than remembered. AGENTS.md:
a TODO in source is not a task.

## Acceptance Criteria

The lost > 0 toast and its condition are gone from the disconnect overlay, and a
test asserts the surviving tab's own mark is what tells the user, with no toast.

title: notify.raise's params bound and availability were decided in a merge, not deliberately
description:
The merge of main into feat/notificcations (f0faaf9f) had to give notify.raise a
params validator, because main's nocx-q27y sweep made one a required field of a
control-method registration. Two things were decided there under merge pressure
rather than on their merits, and both are cheap to settle.

1. maxNotifyTextRunes = 4096 bounds title and body in
internal/transport/ws_notify.go. The number is invented. contracts/notify.raise.schema.json
declares no maxLength at all, so the wire contract and the Go validator now
disagree about whether a bound exists -- and the schema is the party to the
contract (AGENTS.md rule 5). Either the schema grows the bound and the renderer's
generated type carries it, or the Go side drops it and says why.

2. notify.raise still answers -32601 from inside handleNotifyRaise when
s.notifyRaiser is nil. main now has whenAvailable(spec, available, message) for
exactly that, and every other optional-domain method uses it. The handler check
predates the idiom and is covered by a test, so this is a refactor with a test to
move, not a behaviour change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The bound on title and body is stated in ONE place, and contracts/notify.raise.schema.json
  and internal/transport agree about it; npm run contracts:check passes.
- A payload that exceeds the bound is refused with -32602 over the real socket,
  asserted in ws_notify_test.go's over-the-wire test rather than against a
  struct the test built.
- notify.raise declares its availability the way the rest of the surface does,
  or a comment in ws_notify.go says why whenAvailable does not fit.
close_reason: Closed

title: Gate acquisition order has two owners: composite and sessionTargetOperation
description:
control.NewComposite owns 'acquire in declared order, release in reverse, exactly once' (internal/transport/control/composite.go). capability.sessionTargetOperation.Run re-implements that sequence by hand because it needs a STAGED release — the session gate ends after the snapshot, the ordinary lane is held for the callback — which the composite cannot express.

It is justified and commented, but the ordering rule now has two owners, and the second one is a hand-written sequence that no test compares against the first. AGENTS.md: extend the existing answer rather than write a second one.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read internal/transport/control/composite.go TryAcquire.
2. Read internal/capability/session.go sessionTargetOperation.Run — same order, released in two stages.
3. Change the canonical order in one and nothing tells you about the other.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The staged release is expressed through internal/transport/control (e.g. a composite that can release a named part early) rather than by re-acquiring the parts by hand in capability.
- ForSessionTarget keeps its observable contract: session gate released before the callback, ordinary lane held for its duration (TestSessionTargetOperationReleasesSessionGateBeforeWork stays green).
- No caller outside control re-implements the acquisition order.

title: frontend/package.json.md5 has no consumer and should be deleted
description:
Nothing in the repo reads frontend/package.json.md5 — .internal/reports/w3-deadcode-ratchet.md already recorded it as stale with no consumer. PR #87 refreshed its contents instead of removing it. Clean-only (AGENTS.md): dead artefacts get deleted, not maintained.

## Acceptance Criteria

- frontend/package.json.md5 is gone.
- grep for 'package.json.md5' finds no reader anywhere in the repo.
- All four CI jobs are green without it.

title: sudo --help probe runs on every nested sudo launch
description:
__nocx_sudo_supports_preserve_fds (scripts/nocx.bash, scripts/nocx.zsh) shells out to 'sudo --help' every time the user submits a sudo command. The answer cannot change within a shell's lifetime, so this is one extra process per sudo invocation on the interactive path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an integrated shell and run sudo repeatedly.
2. Each submission spawns 'sudo --help' before the launch decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The probe result is computed at most once per shell instance and cached in a shell variable.
- The unsupported-sudo fallback still runs the user's exact command exactly once (TestBashNestedSudoWithoutPreserveFDSRunsConventionally stays green).
- The bash tier still parses under bash 3.2.

title: A worker survives the network, and an upgrade never strands one
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-lineage-and-orchestration-design.md, D4, D5 and
section 4.2. DEFERRED by D5 — at stage 1 workers die with the backend, which is herdr's
behaviour and was accepted deliberately by the owner. This epic exists so the requirements are
recorded where they were learned, not so it is scheduled.

WHAT IT SPENDS. nocx-457v already paid the expensive half for the Git panel: cross-compilation,
SFTP install into ~/.nocx/helper/<platform>/, the platform in the directory name, hash
verification, the sentinel handshake with a nonce, exit 42 on version mismatch, consent
(nocx-8d6e), uninstall (nocx-aggw) and pruning. Its helper-D15 reserved exactly what a worker
needs and did not build it: seq/ack in the frame header, an instance id in hello-ok, the
`session` service name, and the rule that a helper's lifetime is not tied to one channel.

SHAPE, from the design's D4: a THIN daemon holding PTYs and the AD-9 ring and nothing else — no
drivers, no classifier, no policy, all of which stay in the local backend. A unix socket in a
runtime directory keyed by HOST IDENTITY, not merely by platform: helper-D7 already found that
one $HOME can serve two architectures, and a shared $HOME can serve two hosts that would
otherwise fight over one socket path.

WHY NOT tmux/dtach: it is a second VT engine, and rendering modern agent TUIs flawlessly is the
product's table-stakes claim (vision.md section 4) — inserting another emulator with its own
$TERM, colour and mouse handling is the degradation nocx exists to remove. It is also a second
replay owner against AD-9, and a prerequisite we cannot install ourselves.

THE OPEN MECHANISM, and it must be answered before the first durable helper ships. The design
decides the invariants and deliberately not the mechanism: mismatch may refuse CREATION and must
never strand a LIVE session. Candidates are version-matched adapters retained at install time
(the reviewer's preference: an old generation and its adapter are removed only after its last
session terminalizes, so compatibility is isolated in immutable version pairs rather than
branching current code), PTY handoff between generations (which needs a transactional transfer
of master fds, ring offsets, seq/ack and writer ownership, plus a recovery protocol when it
fails halfway — generation supervision in a more dangerous form), or a frozen rescue protocol
(insufficient: a rescue often needs to answer a prompt or save and exit an editor, not just
read).

Whichever is chosen, it needs the owner's decision on a narrow exception to AGENTS.md's
"Clean-only: no backward-compatibility shims" rule — see section 9.4 of the design. The helper
is the first nocx component for which "break freely" can destroy someone's running session.

THIS EPIC ALSO OWNS durable session records and the prepared -> active interval of section 4.2,
which were removed from the foundation epic: internal/session/ has no restore path today, and
under D5 there was nothing yet for persistence to preserve. Here there is.

DELIBERATELY OUT: nelix's GenerationSupervisor as such — its generations exist because its
daemon carries drivers and session state, and ours carries neither; the rejection is of that
machinery, not of the durable-ownership problem, which this epic must solve. Also out: Windows
remote hosts, and any service beyond `session`.

## Success Criteria

See acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
Watched end to end: a worker is started on an SSH host, the link is dropped for longer than any
timeout, the app is restarted, and the user reattaches to that worker with its output intact
from the offset they had already acknowledged.

- A session survives a dropped link, a client restart and a logout of the launching shell.
- Replay after reattach comes from the AD-9 ring by offset, or an explicit reset — never from a
  second replay mechanism.
- An instance id distinguishes the helper the backend was talking to from a fresh one, and a
  reattach against a different instance is refused as such rather than silently accepted.
- A client and helper whose protocol versions differ MAY refuse to create a new session and MUST
  NOT kill an existing one, nor leave mismatch as its terminal state: the user retains an
  actionable path to the live session. Asserted by running a mismatched pair against a live
  session.
- With no live sessions and no client, the helper exits rather than lingering.
- Uninstall closes the channel first and removes nothing that a live session is using.
- A partial install is never used: a directory without its completion marker is removed and
  reinstalled.

title: Worktrees are a list you can work from, and it never hides without saying so
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-lineage-and-orchestration-design.md, D10, D15 and
open questions 8 and 9.

Spends the exclusion at line 251 of .internal/specs/2026-08-06-git-manager-design.md —
"Multi-repository, submodules, worktrees as a list. nocx has no 'project' concept" — whose
stated reason the workspace epic removes. The plumbing is already there: that design's
sections 471-486 resolve a linked worktree separately from an ordinary repository and record
that linked worktrees share history but are different working trees.

THE INVERSION THAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM orca. In orca a worktree is normally created
through the UI, so one created outside it is the exception and gets an explicit inbox with a
visibility policy (src/shared/external-worktree-inbox.ts). We are a terminal: `git worktree add`
typed by hand is the NORMAL path, and a button is a convenience on top of it. So the thing we
need is the opposite one — a rule for which worktrees NOT to show.

WHICH ONES TO HIDE IS DELIBERATELY UNDECIDED and is to be settled by using it. orca's prior art
runs in both directions: a prefix list (.claude/worktrees, .gsd-workspaces) plus bug #9388,
"broader matches can hide legitimate user worktrees". The owner's machine currently has ~25
worktrees under ~/.herdr/worktrees for one repository, so an unfiltered list is unusable on day
one and an over-filtered one hides real work.

What is NOT deferred is that the deferral stays honest: discovery returns everything with a
reason, the surface filters, and the count of hidden rows is always visible. Deciding the filter
later is cheap; shipping silent hiding meanwhile is the invisible degrade AGENTS.md forbids.

THE LIFECYCLE HAZARD THIS INTRODUCES: a session open in a directory that is being deleted. orca
fences PTY and watcher installs during removal and has the renderer RECOGNISE the fence, so a
doomed pane does not surface it as a terminal error
(src/shared/worktree-removal-fence-error.ts). We have no such situation today and will after
this epic.

DELIBERATELY OUT: multi-repository and submodules, which the git-manager design excludes for
reasons this epic does not touch; creating worktrees from the UI beyond what the list needs;
anything about branches beyond what the git panel already derives from the active session.

## Success Criteria

See acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
Watched end to end: in a repository with a main checkout, two hand-created linked worktrees and
one created by a tool under a scratch path, the user opens the workspace and sees the two
hand-created ones as rows, with a line stating that one more was hidden and a way to reveal it.

- A worktree created by `git worktree add` in a terminal, outside any nocx UI, appears without
  the user doing anything else. This is the normal case for a terminal, not the exception.
- Discovery returns every worktree with a reason attached; the surface decides what to show and
  ALWAYS states how many it hid. A test asserts the count is reported when the filter is
  non-empty — silent hiding is the failure this criterion exists to prevent.
- A linked worktree resolves to the linked tree and to <main>/.git/worktrees/<name>, not to the
  main checkout — the distinction the git-manager design already draws.
- Removing a worktree that has an open session does not surface a raw terminal error: the
  session reports that its directory is going away, and the pane is not left showing a fence
  message as though the shell had failed.
- The git panel still follows the ACTIVE TAB and is unaffected by which worktree row is
  selected.

title: pre-commit demands the whole toolchain for a commit that will run none of it
description:
The hook classifies the staged set into RUN_GO / RUN_FE / RUN_E2E (.githooks/pre-commit, the block after 'what does this commit touch?'), so a docs-only commit runs zero gates by design. But the binary precheck above it is unconditional: gofumpt, golangci-lint, deadcode, go, node, npm, docker and frontend/node_modules are all required before the classification is even read.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. git worktree add a fresh worktree; do not run 'cd frontend && npm ci' in it.
2. Stage a file matching none of the hook's cases — e.g. .internal/specs/anything.md.
3. git commit.

Observed: 'FAIL: frontend/node_modules not found' and the commit is refused.
Expected: the commit succeeds, because the classification sets RUN_GO=0, RUN_FE=0, RUN_E2E=0
and no gate would have run.

Found 2026-08-15 committing .internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-lineage-and-orchestration-design.md.

The cost is not the inconvenience. It is that the only ways forward are 'npm ci to satisfy a gate that checks nothing' — and nocx-x6z3 says concurrent installs across worktrees break each other's dependency tree — or --no-verify, which is the habit AGENTS.md most wants not to form. A hook that makes bypassing itself the reasonable option trains the wrong reflex.

Fix shape: move the precheck below the classification and demand only what the enabled gates need.
acceptance_criteria: A commit touching only docs/ or .internal/ succeeds in a worktree with no frontend/node_modules and no docker running. A commit touching a .go or frontend/ file still fails there, with the same message it prints today.
close_reason: Fixed as 64439133. The precheck moved below the classification and each demand is scoped to the gate that needs it: Go tools only when RUN_GO, frontend/node_modules only when RUN_FE. node, npm and the ROOT node_modules stay unconditional because prettier and root eslint are unconditional. Added the root node_modules check, which nothing demanded, so its absence used to surface as a prettier failure rather than as the line saying what to install. Proved on itself: a docs-only commit went through in a worktree with no Go tools and no frontend/node_modules.

title: Four surfaces each carry their own copy of the group-caption register; the kit now owns it
description:
nocx-dgsp added the kit's Caption component (frontend/src/ui/caption.tsx, .ui-caption) because the settings rail needed the app's group-caption register and writing a fifth copy was not allowed. The four existing copies were deliberately left alone in that pass — changing them was not what the bead was about, and touching four surfaces to prove a component works is how a focused change becomes an unreviewable one.

They are now a consolidation debt, and the debt is the same shape the component exists to prevent: five declarations of one look, free to drift.

  frontend/src/styles/components/sidebar.css:48-56        .sidebar-title
  frontend/src/styles/components/floating-panel.css:90-99 .ui-floating-panel__group
  frontend/src/styles/surfaces/connections.css:242        the group header
  (quick-connect.css:138 was checked and is NOT one of these — it is an item badge, a different register)

## What to do

Each site composes the kit Caption and keeps its own PLACEMENT — floating-panel's hairline and padding, sidebar's gutter — in its own wrapper. Placement is the caller's; the register is the kit's. Two of these are vanilla-emitted components rather than Solid, so the shared thing may have to be the identity class and its CSS rather than the JSX component; decide that deliberately and write down which, because a component that only half the callers can use is a sixth vocabulary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every remaining site renders the kit's caption identity, asserted per site.
- No site declares font-size, letter-spacing, text-transform, font-weight or colour for its caption; each declares only placement, asserted by the existing check-css-integrity surface-paints-kit rule rather than by eye.
- A change to the register in one place moves all of them, asserted by one test that reads the identity from two different surfaces.
- The vanilla-emitted callers are handled explicitly, and the choice between sharing the class and sharing the component is recorded in the component's doc comment.

title: The pre-commit hook lints frontend/ but not the repo root, so e2e/ reaches CI unlinted
description:
The `frontend` CI job runs eslint in BOTH `frontend/` and the repo root
(`scripts/ci-frontend.sh` — "node 24 — frontend/ AND the repo root"). The
pre-commit hook runs only the `frontend/` half. So anything under `e2e/` is
committed unlinted and fails in CI instead.

Caught on 2026-08-14 integrating nocx-x8s2.2: `e2e/agent-ask.spec.ts` committed
with an unused variable, every pre-commit check green, and `ci-frontend.sh`
red on `'blockB' is assigned a value but never used`. Cheap this time — one
line — but it is a gate that reports green on a tree CI rejects, which is the
property that makes a gate worth having.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Introduce an eslint error in any file under `e2e/` (an unused variable).
2. `git commit` — the pre-commit hook passes.
3. `./scripts/ci-frontend.sh` — red.

## Expected behavior

A tree the pre-commit hook calls green passes the `frontend` CI job, or the
hook says plainly which half it did not check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The pre-commit hook runs the same eslint scope as `scripts/ci-frontend.sh`,
  or names the gap in its "NOT covered here" footer the way it already names
  macOS, Ubuntu and the e2e suite.
- A deliberately broken `e2e/` file is refused at commit time, asserted.
close_reason: Fixed, and a duplicate of the already-closed nocx-s3cu3 rather than of nocx-pvjj. .githooks/pre-commit:235 now runs host_gate 'eslint (root)' npm run lint unconditionally beside the prettier gate, where the root package.json lint script is eslint . and eslint.config.mjs:37 covers e2e/**/*.ts, playwright.config.ts and the root *.ts/*.mjs/*.js. Commit 3955e3c4, which is what nocx-s3cu3 was closed on. This bead's own trigger case is closed too, as dda940d3. Closed during the backlog sweep nocx-e1xzh.

title: Generated nested types are permanent dead-export debt: 27 baselined, and every new nested schema object adds one
description:
Raised 2026-08-14 while landing nocx-utbm, and deliberately kept OUT of that commit.

## Context

frontend/scripts/gen-contracts.mjs emits one exported interface per nested schema object. Consumers import only the top-level result type and reach nested shapes through it, so each nested interface becomes an unused export the moment it is generated. check-dead-exports.mjs gates that as a violation, and update-dead-exports-baseline.mjs refuses any violation not already in the baseline — set membership, not count — so the sanctioned escape is closed for anything new.

dead-exports-baseline.json already carries 27 entries under generated/, including three in one file (backup.preview.ts: ItemCounts, ProfileRef, SettingsCounts) that are the same artifact.

## What was done instead, and why it is not the general answer

backup.preview.schema.json referenced snippetCounts from $defs exactly once, so it was inlined and the named export disappeared. That is the right fix for a single-use $defs entry and it shrank the baseline by four. It does not generalise: a nested object referenced twice earns its $defs entry, and inlining it would duplicate the schema.

## The decision to make

Either generated nested types are API debt worth gating, in which case the 27 stay and every future schema pays this tax; or they are a projection whose liveness is owned by contracts/ and contracts:check, in which case check-dead-exports.mjs should report but not gate 'types' violations under src/generated/ — and all 27 baseline entries come out in the same change.

Rejected on inspection: making the generator stop exporting nested interfaces. Several are imported directly and legitimately (Snippet from snippets.list, Status and Entry from the git schemas, FilesListEntry, HistoryEntry), and the generator has no way to tell those from implementation-only declarations. knip's ignoreIssues suppresses findings entirely rather than reporting them without gating, so the wrapper is the right layer if reporting is wanted.

Keep the 'files' kind gating under src/generated/ whichever way this goes. It caught a real defect on 2026-08-14: five generated wire types with no renderer consumer at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The question is decided one way and written down where the next schema author sees it
- [ ] If the policy changes, all 27 generated/ entries leave the baseline in that same commit
- [ ] The 'files' kind still gates under src/generated/

title: A shared $def re-declared per contract file forces a consumer to union identical types
description:
`contracts/endpoints.list.schema.json` declares the endpoint shape once in `$defs`, and `endpoints.create` / `endpoints.update` reference it cross-file. The generator emits a SEPARATE `Endpoint` type into each generated file, so `frontend/src/generated/endpoints.{list,create,update}.ts` each export their own structurally identical `Endpoint`.

A consumer only ever needs one of them. But the dead-export ratchet counts the other two as dead exports in files that may not be hand-edited, so `frontend/src/endpoints.ts` had to write

    export type Endpoint = ListEndpoint | CreatedEndpoint | UpdatedEndpoint

and say so in its doc comment: "This union names all three declarations so the dead-export ratchet sees every generated file consumed". A union of three identical types is a no-op at the type level, which is exactly why it is bad: it is a type whose shape was decided by a lint tool rather than by what it means, and the next reader will believe the three can differ.

The right owner is the generator, not the consumer. A `$def` referenced cross-file should be emitted ONCE, into a shared generated module the referencing files import. Then each generated file has exactly the exports it needs and the consumer names one `Endpoint`.

Until then, every new method group sharing a `$def` reproduces the same union — this is the first, not the last.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `frontend/src/generated/endpoints.list.ts`, `endpoints.create.ts` and `endpoints.update.ts` each declare `export interface Endpoint`.
2. Import only `endpoints.list`'s `Endpoint` in a consumer.
3. `cd frontend && node lint-fixtures/check-dead-exports.mjs` reports the create and update `Endpoint` exports as NEW violations, which the ratchet refuses.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `$def` referenced across contract files is emitted once, in a shared generated module the referencing files import; no generated file re-declares it.
- `frontend/src/endpoints.ts` names one `Endpoint` type imported from that module, and the union — with its comment about the ratchet — is gone.
- `npm run contracts:check` and `node lint-fixtures/check-dead-exports.mjs` are both clean with zero new violations, and the dead-exports baseline shrinks rather than grows.

title: The toolbar menu: findable without the chord, through the same fire path
description:
Plan Task 11. tab-strip.tsx, tabs.ts, main.tsx, settings-content.ts, settings.tsx.

CORRECTIONS: tab-strip is a presentation port — add onSnippets as a nullable public field beside onQuickConnect/onInsertSecret (lines 66-69), never pass it the store or the palette. main.tsx re-wires REPLACEMENT strips through a helper (line 782); miss one and the menu works until the strip is replaced. The class is ui-context-menu__item and ContextMenuItem.onSelect takes NO event, so a modifier cannot be read there. 'Manage snippets' needs a queued page-open that settings-content.ts does not have yet.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The menu lists the library in stored order plus 'Manage snippets...' last
- [ ] Picking a row goes through the palette's accept path, not a second copy of the fire logic
- [ ] With the store unavailable the menu shows the reason and no rows
- [ ] The callback survives a strip replacement
close_reason: The tab strip's snippets action opens a kit ContextMenu: the library in stored order plus 'Manage snippets…' last; picking a row goes through SnippetPalette.fireChosen (the palette's own accept path — the menu has no fire logic); an unavailable store shows the reason and no rows, with a retry; the callback is wired in wireQuickConnect so it survives a strip replacement. Settings gained a general openPage(id) beside its three bespoke openers.

title: Snippets in the one dropdown: resolved at acceptance, never as ghost text
description:
Plan Task 12. suggest/candidate.ts, providers.ts, rank.ts, controller.ts, plus the composition chain main.tsx -> TabManager -> TerminalContent.

SIX CORRECTIONS: the contract is SuggestionProvider with applicable(ctx)/suggest(ctx,signal), not a candidates() method (providers.ts:98-106); createShellProviders is built INSIDE TerminalContent (terminal-content.ts:724) so the store must be plumbed through; resolution belongs at ACCEPTANCE not at suggestion (spec §8) because a candidate carries static insertText and cwd/branch go stale; merge.ts has no weights and rank.ts:134 takes its exact-match bonus from insertText, so a snippet body can outrank a real command; the whole-line replacement range must be defined after a pipe or a semicolon and asserted; and ask snippets must NOT be silently dropped from the surface — spec §10.2 disables ghost text only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Answers in command position only, matched on the title, ranked below command names
- [ ] eligibleForGhostText is false, always
- [ ] The resolved text is produced at acceptance; a branch change between query and acceptance is tested
- [ ] A command-versus-snippet ranking collision is tested, not a snippet in isolation
- [ ] The unique-completion path cannot auto-apply a sole snippet candidate on Tab
- [ ] The row carries its source word
close_reason: The snippet provider ships: command position only, matched on the title, ranked below command names (tested as a collision, not in isolation); eligibleForGhostText false always; the candidate carries the title and the library id, and the body is resolved at ACCEPTANCE through the palette's fire path (a branch change between query and acceptance is tested); the unique-completion path excludes snippet rows so Tab cannot auto-apply one; the row carries its source word in the dropdown. The store gained ensureLoaded so a per-keystroke provider is not a per-keystroke wire call.

title: The submit gate acts on a validation snapshot taken before its async reveal hook
description:
Found by an adversarial review of 2fab1f76 (codex, read-only, 2026-08-13).

frontend/src/ui/submit-gate.ts:58. The gate reads firstErrorField(), firstError() and
errorCount(), THEN awaits options.reveal(first), then focuses and announces. It never
revalidates after the await.

The hook's own documented contract is `void | Promise<void>` -- "may be async — focus waits for
it to settle". So the gate promises a window in which the world can change and then acts on
what it read before that window. With a genuinely async reveal (a lazily loaded panel), the
user can fix the field, or reactive validation can move underneath it, and the gate still
focuses the old control, announces the old message, and refuses.

Today every reveal hook in the tree is synchronous (setProfileSection, setGroupSection), so this
does not currently misbehave. It is the promised contract that is wrong, and the async test only
